reviews.comment: Dr. Sakis is very nice and loves to answer questions whether that's in lecture or in office hours. He's always looking to help his students. That said, the course is very fast paced and so are the lectures, which focus heavily on proofs. Exams are hard, but you can do well on them if you do all the problem sets. Grade curve at the end is generous

He is not good at lecturing, only going over definitions and proofs. Your grade is determined by 3 exams, and there is no homework or practice exams, only some problem sets with solutions that are difficult to understand or read. The class is extremely difficult on its own, but he doesn't make it any easier. You have to teach yourself the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sakis's class was the toughest that I had this semester. That being said, I really enjoyed having him as a teacher. He is a bit intimidating in lecture, but he is very nice and helpful in office hours. His lectures could be a bit confusing at times, but he is always willing to answer questions. His tests were difficult, but he genuinely cares .
Nice guy.
She is not very genuine. And she treats us like little kids. She is over the top in an unauthentic way that feels forced. And her lectures are mostly repeats. I just cringed the entire time.

She's nice and that is it. Lectures made the same points every class. Had to write a 1000 word essay, which is more than my required history class. Made us introduce ourselves to our groups every class for multiple months. Cried in the middle of a lecture once over a hypothetical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. PH was truly a delight. I recommend her to everyone. She is emotionally intelligent, caring, and wants to see us succeed. The other review for this class is a gross misrepresentation of Dr. PH.
This professor is so disorganized. did not understand why I felt like I was in elementary school in so many ways, other than the way we are graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You are missing out if you don't take a class with Dr. PH. She is easily my favorite professor. She is so engaging, caring, and funny. Her class was the highlight of my day; she always greeted students with a smile and made them feel welcome. There were many extra credit opportunities (not that you need them  though, because she grades fairly!)

I cannot believe Dr. Durbak's rating is so low. She is an amazing professor with the know-how and the passion for her students. THERES A REASON SHE WON THE KEMPER FELLOW!! The best professor in BIO_SCI and its not close
Yappaholic!!!

I am not a STEM person at all, and I truly understood everything I learned in this class. Professor Durbak is KIND and wants you to succeed. She basically hands the A to you. You just have to show up to class and try. She gives so many bonus points, you have to put effort into getting them, though. I LOVE THIS WOMAN SO MUCH.
Take this class

She is a very no-nonsense professor and is clearly passionate about what she teaches. She is genuinely interested in seeing willing students succeed in the course. Intimidating for sure, but she was always helpful when I met with her one-on-one and responded to emails promptly. If you put effort into her class, she will put effort into you

Dr Durbak was the most caring and thoughtful professor I have had at Mizzou. She is very passionate about the content and it explains it very clearly. I have testing accommodations and didn't fill out the form on time to qualify but she made sure my testing plan was met even though she didn't have to. I highly recommend her!

Durbak was a great professor. Not too much homework, not a really tough grader for projects as long as you did what you were told. Attendance wasn't really mandatory but we had to come to class 9 times throughout the semester. Practice exams were just like the real ones, and in the videos (and class) she did a great of job of explaining material.
Flipped classroom style you have to watch videos online to be somewhat informed on what you're learning.

Super nice and cares about her students. Really helpful video lectures. Interesting lectures, and she's passionate about what she teaches. The tests and assignments are easy too if you just pay attention and take notes in class.

I love this professor!! You definitely will need to study for the tests but she gives you a practice exam and study guide that will help you a lot. You also can use a cheat sheet on the test! So much extra credit given too. You can also drop a test at the end of semester, so you can skip the final and just drop that.

Dr Durbak is an excellent professor. She goes over the material well, but you do need to do the at-home videos so you know what is going on. There is a group project and a case study in every unit. She lets you bring a note card to tests. She drops your lowest test score and hw. She sets her class up in a way that makes it hard to fail.
Dr Durbak is my favorite professor she is so awesome I look for classes she is teaching just so I can take them

Dr. Durbak is one of the sweetest professors you will ever have. She really wants everyone in the class to succeed. Her tests are pretty easy if you study and if you put in effort you will learn a lot. For honors, she does a big group project at the end instead of finals which was really fun. Much rather do this instead of a big final
If you aren't religious, pick a religion and pray.

Dr. Durbak is incredibly passionate about biology, and it shows. She is a very animated lecturer who honestly reminds me of Mrs. Frizzle. Her cell bio class is fun, and I learned a lot. If you're just trying to get that Pre-med requirement, don't worry, the exams are easy, and there is extra credit galore. Remember to be respectful to educators!
She is a passionate professor who deeply cares about her subject, but she does not consider the needs and recommendations of students with disabilities.

Dr. Durbak was a great Extended One Read professor! I believe it was her first time teaching this class, but you couldn't tell. She allowed for great comprehension of the book and used her biology background to bring in an alternative perspective. She was very caring and understanding about late work due to illness. Overall 10/10 professor
She truly cares and could easily gotten an A if effort put in.

Not the worst but would avoid. She's demeaning and will treat you and your ability to be an autonomous learner like they're mythical cryptids--never to be seen. She has no outside resources, just her and her lectures, which can be self-contradicting and unhelpful at best. If you have a solid biology background, you'll be okay. Just annoyed.
Amazing teacher. Loved going to her lectures and you get a dropped exam so a little less stress.

I loved Dr. Durbak's cell bio. Her lectures were so interesting and she related everything to real-world applications. Tests were pretty difficult, but with studying and a test notecard, it was very doable. There are a lot of possible points from discussion and ICA. I wish she taught more classes! You could tell she cared for all her students.

Only annoying thing about the class is that you're asked to watch at-home lectures, but then go over the same content the next class. It does force you to understand it though! Durbak is friendly and accessible in office hours. Tests are straightforward and you're allowed a notecard. Overall, great course!

Probably the most understanding and caring professor I've had at Mizzou-- Dr. Durbak really values her students' learning and wellbeing. The tests aren't hard in my opinion, especially because she allots a notecard. She also allows one dropped exam and 11 absences. Very fair class and she is a great teacher.

There are ample opportunities for extra credit (can raise grade ~2%) and discussion points are easy to get if you pay attention in class and show up. Lenient attendance policy and you get a notecard to use during the exam. Love the memes and iClicker to reinforce concepts.

Professor Durbak is a good teacher. She cares about her subject which helps a lot. It is definitely an intro course. Super easy if you do all of the assignments. You get plenty of skip days and some extra credit opportunities. Lots of group work. Easy A.

She's not as nice during office hours. She got angry at my friend for missing class for health reasons even though she lets you have 12 drop days. But, she's entertaining during lecture. Likes to hush people talking in the back so beware. The group projects are easy but obnoxious we're still doing them in college. Lab doesn't 100% match.

Very energetic professor, and you can tell that she loves what she teaches! I wasn't a fan of her teaching style. Uses iClicker for attendance and it isn't graded. You have the same group the whole semester, and there's lots of group projects/days. Workload got heavy and exams could be difficult at times but overall it was a pretty average class.

Very good professor. Made content clear for everyone and did not expect too much from us. Actually cared about us and was understanding when things would come up. Would definitely take this class again!

Flipped classroom style, the things we need to learn at home aren't posted until 12 pm/right before class starts. Not told what we're supposed to be learning on our own, it's not very clear online. Uses iClicker so attendance is important. Uses jeopardy iClicker game the class before an exam but the questions aren't really based on what we learn.

Biochem majors will have an easy time, but others might not. Some questions can be worded a little strangely IMO, so be careful. Uses iClicker, but has a generous attendance policy. Watch the lectures before you take the quizzes, not all the info is on the slides so you can't cheese them. Flipped classroom format isn't for everyone, so be warned.

Prof. Durbak's lectures were very interactive with iclickers and participation does receive a grade, but you can miss a few classes. she offers a lot of bonus opportunities which is nice because her exams are hard! She did let us make a notecard for the exam which was super nice but the exams were still hard.
Dr. Durbak was a really easy professor for me. She was nice, and the grading was precise and clear. Lots of exams. You only have to go to 21/33 classes to get your attendance grade. Super easy

Really easy class. Only have to attend 21/33 classes before iClicker starts dropping your grade. Skipped 12 classes and got an A+. She does a flipped classroom but I never watched the videos before. By far the easiest bio 1010 teacher.

I love Dr. Durbak! She is funny and passionate for what she teaches. The lectures are flipped-classroom style, so there are videos to watch before class and the material is discussed & clarified in class. If you love memes, Dr. Durbak's class is for you! The honors component of this class wasn't too bad either- just a paper and group presentation.
Just is a weird teaching method. I basically had to teach myself with notes outside of class, so going to discussion felt unnecessary.

I liked her teaching style it was a flipped classroom. Plenty of in class activities to make sure you understand. Lots of opportunity to get extra credit. iclicker is for attendance. Tests were pretty easy as long as you study and they aren't worth an absurd amount of your grade. There are a lot more points to earn that aren't tests.

She was such a nice professor! I ended up with a B+. I never went to class, all tests were online and she dropped the lowest one. She was always very understanding. I would take a class with her again!
lots of pointless busy work. is not very sympathetic as well.

Dr. Durbak was an awesome teacher! Made things funny and I love Woohoo Wednesday! Exams are open note but make sure you study too because they can be a little tricky! Very approachable and caring! Love her

Dr. Durbak is so caring and loves her subject! Notes are easy to follow and a textbook is required, but I never needed to use it. Tests are pretty easy and open-note. There is homework but it's very easy, along with plenty of extra credit opportunities. I've always struggled with science, but I understand it in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: No homework which is a good and bad thing. Difficult and very specific material. Does give extra credit. Fun to listen to, but lectures do not align with exams. You have to work for your grade and teach yourself outside of her notes. Nice woman, tries her hardest but it is just hard material to teach. wish tests weren't so hard and matched lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Durbak was great! Yeah it was a challenging class, but I really felt supported in the class and she was always accessible. She had reviews for tests outside of class and was always helpful. I felt like the class was straight-forward and the material followed what we were tested over. P.S. she has a gel electrophoresis dress. A true Ms. Frizzle.

Dr. Durbak is a really amazing professor. I never felt like I was lost in her class. It is very structured and easy to follow. She really helps you when you need it. There are plenty of options for extra credit too! Dr. Durbak truly wants you to succeed and she makes that very clear in the way she treats the students!

Very nice and understand but the tests are very hard. The information on the tests is not mentioned in the lectures. However, homework assignments and quizzes are fairly easy because you get multiple chances on each. She also does a lot of extra credit. Pretty work heavy, but it helps you learn the material.

I had Biology with Dr. Durbak. She has an attendance policy for about half of the lectures, so if you go to half you'll get full credit. Homework and tests could be a little tricky, but for the most part, they're not too bad. Don't expect to do well if you don't try. My test scores definitely reflected when I paid attention and didn't.

One of the most frustrating classes I have ever taken. The content explained during the lectures is not difficult, yet the exams are. The questions asked on the exams do not correlate to the lectures and have multiple right answers. She will put a question on the homework and then ask the same question on the test with a different answer.

Durbak is fine. She doesn't give out a lot of homework, and the class is easy. But, she puts some questions on the exams that weren't discussed and has pointless Zoom sessions for review. Isn't incredibly helpful when you ask her questions. You'll be fine if you can learn on your own, but if you need any help, the internet will do a better job.

There is a lot of content to cover but she is very good at teaching as long as you are willing to pay attention to lectures. She recommends doing textbook readings but you can get all the info you need for her exams from lectures. Exams aren't too bad and are more application based. She also gives a lot of opportunities to boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Please I urge you do NOT take her class . Her exams are hard, discussions are pointless . Her review sessions are pointless . She makes EVERYTHING hard for no reason . We are in a pandemic and she still is grading hard and giving out 0 if you do the hw wrong. She is not lient nor caring . REGRET TAKING HER CLASS I SWEAR TO GOD I DO .

Lectures are kind of boring and pointless since they're posted on canvas. There was a test every 2 or 3 weeks but little to no homework. It's an easy class as long as you get the credit for showing up and answering polling questions and gloss over the lectures right before the tests.
She was awful. The test were hard and not like the practice exams. She didn't round my 79.5 to an 80.

Made biology super easy to understand and her lectures were engaging. She records attendance but it's easy points to get. Tests were difficult, but as long as you study they're passable. Gives great feedback, gives extra credit opportunities, and is easily accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed her class. I was nervous because I hate science, but she made BIO really easy to understand. The class is very lecture heavy and you need to be there to fully understand, but she does put up panopto videos and lots of extra credit opportunities. I studied by reading the lecture notes and got an A on almost every test. Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Biology 1010 was probably one of the harder classes I took this semester. I tried my best on each exam, but they were extremely hard and the wording was really confusing. The workout problems did not match what I reviewed for and overall just confusing. I thought she was a nice professor, but this class seemed too difficult for a general class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is really helpful outside of class, but during class I found her lectures to be boring and hard to follow. Overall, the tests are hard but if you study a lot it is a manageable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is very lecture heavy and makes Biology way harder than it needs to be. Doesn't ever curve tests and makes her multiple choice exams confusing and easy to get tripped up on. Least favorite class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cell Biology isn't easy, but she gave lots of ways to earn points that boost your grade. Clicker questions are extra credit, so go to class, reading the assigned text before class and sitting next to smart people helps, because you are allowed to work together. Tough, but doable. Exams were average, except the take-home, which was killer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is not hard, it is just that I'm personally not a fan of her teaching style. Many lecture notes were incorrect and screwed me up on tests. Speaking of the tests, some of the weirdest worded questions I have ever seen. It's like she's trying to get you to mess up. I thought she was a very nice lady, but I just wasn't a fan of her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is super passionate about the class material and is very engaging and easy to listen to! Her lectures are quite entertaining, she always finds ways to offer extra credit, answers emails timely and posts super helpful study guides for the exams! Strongly recommend!

Dr. Durbak is passionate about what she teaches, and she tries to make us be passionate as well. Her lectures were always interesting even for someone that is not a huge fan of biology. She's one of the only teachers that I have ever gone to office hours for.

Dr. Durbak has been my favorite teacher ever. She is super helpful and willing to take the time to meet with students to make sure you understand the material. Go to her office hours and she'll become your friend. Always says hi to me outside of class a year later too because she got to know me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a great class and I wouldn't have taken it with anyone else. Durbak is very nice and tries to do as much as she can to help you succeed. The optional homework problems she posts are pretty challenging, but if you know how to do those then you will do fine on exams.
Intimidating at first but really nice if you get to know her. Read the textbook and study if you want to do well on the tests. Lots of quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is a good teacher. you have to study alot. But she wouldnt round my B+ of 89.56 up to an A-

Caring & knowledgable professor! You definitely have to work for your grade. There are five exams that are strictly based off of lectures & your ability to apply the information. Exams aren't easy, so be prepared to study A LOT for this class. She offers many extra credit opportunities. Pay attention in class, work hard, and you'll be just fine.

Durbak makes you work for your grade because all of her exams are not very straightforward. She makes you think and apply your knowledge rather than just memorization. Attendance is not mandatory BUT she does clicker questions almost every class and all in-class assignments are given at random. She made class interesting and was extremely helpful.

Wonderful professor! Really nice and super easy when explaining concepts. If you want an A, you can achieve it, you just have to read the book (buy the physical copy) and show up for lecture. Online quizzes are a pain, but the exams is whats gonna get you that A. And she will drop you from the final if you have 90% exam average.

Pretty simple and straightforward class. She tests you based off strictly her lectures. Exams are short, yet she now included 5 exams during the semester instead of 4. She has plenty of extra credit opportunities and drops your worst exam score/hw score. Class was super easy and anyone should be able to get an A if they put in a little effort

She makes her class way too difficult for what the material is. Her test questions are not straightforward and they are way too in depth. Unfortunately, she is the better option of the cell bio professors
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Durbak is fine. Her class is not easy, you actually have to work for your grade, but if you put the work in, you'll do fine. Also, her class really helped me in biochem later.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I find her class stressful. The lectures are very basic, but her questions on clickers tests and homework are detailed application probs. She gets a lot of her questions from the MCAT test banks and expects you to know all about molecular bonding but never goes over it. Extra credit and in class assignments, so go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tons of material on each test. Don't fall behind. Biggest gripe is this is supposed to be cell biology, it's really loaded with Chemistry, with no prerequisite for it. Take it after Chem 2. Clickers are extra credit, but many are application problems with no time to think through. Very unfocused, difficult to know what will be on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Teaches like a high school teacher but her class is really easy as long as you actually go. She uses clickers all the time and you get extra credit if you get more than 75% right over the whole semester. TONS of in-class assignments and quizzes and homework. Tests aren't too hard if you study
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She made the class very entertaining and interesting to learn. Even though it was a 9 am class she always had my attention. It is important to be in class because she has clicker points that give u extra credit and she has in class assignments. Also, if you have an overall A grade in the class you dont have to take the final!

Overall, Durbak was a pretty solid cell bio professor. The class material is going to be hard no matter what professor you have, but Durbak's style (while sometimes difficult to earn an A from) really helps you learn the material. You just have to be willing to put in the work! She gives good opportunities for easy points & extra credit, too!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You have to go to class because of her clicker questions. Lectures were seriously boring, and tests were pretty easy if you study. Would not take a class with her again.

Taking Cell Bio with Durbak I received my very first C in a Biology course (from previous A's).  I had her when it was her first semester teaching, so she was still getting adjusted to the course. Exam short answer questions were unclear. Student gave constructive criticism and exam averages skyrocketed on the last exam
The tests are hard but she is always available to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Show up to lectures and there is no way you wont at least get a B-

Very easy if you come to class and take notes. Clicker questions in class give you a lot of extra credit at the end of the course, and she makes the lectures interesting so it's worth coming to class. Best part about the class is that she lets you drop the final if you have a 90 avg on all other tests, which was awesome. Def reccomend!

Dr. Durbak is an awesome and genuine professor, she cares about students more than she should. The class can be difficult at first to get a hang of but if you stick with it good things will happen. The tests are difficult although if you show up to class and complete the homework assigned online you shouldn't fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She uses clickers for bonus points, with a possible 2% grade boost at the end of the semester. There was a decent amount of in-class assignments. She posts her lectures on tegrity, but I suggest going to class. Her slides were very helpful and relevant. She offered great study materials, and one class dedicated to review, for the 4 exams + final.
Tests are harder than they should be but she balances it out with lots of homework and in class assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I have not had a teacher that cared more about her students! The tests are difficult and more conceptual.  The book is only useful for the homework, so if you pay attention in class and actually know the material (not memorize!) you will be okay. She is very nice and approachable for help.  One downside is lectures are boring.

Go to class and participate and you'll receive easy extra credit. There are in class and out of class homework assignments. There is a way to get out of the final so if you study hard and read over notes you can get out of it. All lectures are online.

Dr. Durbak is a pretty good professor. She is very clear in when she is available for office hours - utilize those and she is always willing to help. Because she posts all of her notes and recorded lectures online, it makes it hard to go to class, but she does give a lot of in-class assignments. She is personable and uses college student humor.

I skipped so many of her lectures because I couldn't tolerate the way she taught. You have clickers and index card assignments. Attendance is mandatory. You have online work, quizzes, difficult exams with multiple choice/short answer, sometimes essay. Her voice is awful. Her examples are boring. Would not recommend.
Best teacher I've had so far. Great lectures and clicker questions are extra credit for the final. Responds to emails in less that 24 hours. Very nice woman and great professor.

Tests are only the information from her lectures which she gives before every class-everything posted on tegrity. Need to come to class for clicker questions because they are extra credit. 4 tests and a final, drops the lowest one unless you get an average of 90% then you are exempted from taking the final.

Professor Durbak is such a great professor! You can tell she really cares if you understand the information, and she explains concepts clearly.  I'm usually terrible at biology but she helped me understand it!

Dr. Durbak is a great professor; you can tell she cares about her students. She puts all her lectures on tegrity and provides practice exams for all the tests. She is very invested in helping students succeed and is constantly asking for feedback on what students don't understand. Tests are completely based off lectures; book only to supplement.

She's a really sweet person but a horrible teacher. She will make side notes during lectures that will be on the tests, and the only grades for the class were tests that were incredibly hard. She will expect you to memorize every slide and every word.

Attendance is mandatory but she just reads from the slides without giving anything else. I took this class because I thought it would be a fun, chill way to get a science credit, but it was so boring and poorly structured.
Do not recommend this class at all. The teachers voice is very annoying and the lectures are extremely boring. Be ready to memorize almost everything even the stuff you don't think is important.

She knew her info, mostly. She blamed the class for lab samples being placed in the incubator incorrectly when it was her TA, was rude when answering questions, told us about a group project 1 week before the last day, & gave us a quiz after stop day. Her exams & lab assignments were also unnecessarily specific & difficult for a 2000-level course.
Do not take this class or this professor, she doesn't know what she is talking about, is not good with technology, and it is honestly really boring.

She is a really sweet person, but the assignments are very unclear. Although there are only a couple, I ended up having to rewrite one of the essays because the directions were very unclear. You are expected to memorize almost all the information given to you on the slides, including which dishes come from which country and how to make them.

Dr. Mustapha is among the most intelligent professors I've ever had. Her exams are difficult but they prepared me for upper-level STEM courses. There's a curve at the end of the semester so don't panic over a bad grade. She did class recordings which were convenient if we were absent. Despite dense textbooks and PowerPoints, she was very invested.

Do not take her class!!! I mean it, the lectures are over an hour long and her voice is so annoying and she is just plain mean. Ask her any question and she will make you feel stupid and humiliate you. There's only 3 tests and most of your grade is "participation points" where half the time the technology doesn't work and she doesn't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Still working on a book he started over 27 years ago and got years of funding. Just can't get motivated to finish anything.

Andre is very passionate about the subject of philosophy. You are only graded on attendance and assignments, and if you pay attention in class, the assignments are easy. Despite what others say, there are 0 exams or textbooks for this class. I think he mentioned this is his last year teaching, which may be why this class is easier than years past.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely would not recommend Prof Ariew. His lectures turn into him rambling and you have no idea what to take notes over. The only reason I had a decent grade is because the TA's were helpful. Weekly quiz's make up 90% of the grade which may seem nice but its very hard to bounce back if you have a bad quiz or two. Try and get a different prof.
Andre is very scatter-headed at times but the class is pretty easy. The lectures were pretty thought provoking and the discussion section wasn't too bad. Show up to class and the exams are very easy.

Not an introductory course nor taught in an introductory manner: the concepts have considerable depth and rightfully so. Make an earnest attempt to understand the problems of Science and the grade will follow. Very challenging work. Phil of Sci will ask why we model the world the way we do and there is no guaranteed answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought this class was unnecessarily difficult. Because prof Ariew is disorganized, he doesn't remember what he's taught from week to week. And because he doesn't understand what it is like to be unfamiliar with the material, he is unable to explain things in different ways that might make the material accessible. I thought he was a terrible prof
interesting and helpful

I was not interested in this class at all- I only took it as a requirement, but I hated it. The material is confusing and there is no text book so you have to go to class in order to pass, but even then you still don't have anything solid to refer to when you need extra help. He's very unorganized and jumbled, but very passionate on the subject.

He confuses himself and then confuses you to the point that you don't know what's going on in class. When you ask him to clarify he repeats what he just said, still leaving you confused. There is a quiz every week.

He barely provides enough points in the class, you do bad on one exam and you automatically will fail his class. He is very disorganized and never really knows if he is doing anything correctly and looks at the class for clarification, when we do not understand at all. He does not give you anything to study in advance with. He is awful
Boring guy, super disorganized, but I still got an A. So yeah, he's the worst prof I've had at MU. But if you are just looking for a grade, he's your guy.
This guy is a complete dolt.  He's disorganized and dumb.  The combination is absolutely lethal.
I guess Ayer said it best when he said "Bottom"
Interesting.  Fair grading and almost as hot as Waddington.
Myself, I am puzzled about the explanatory structure of the theory of natural selection.  Ariew made it all crystallllllll cleahhhhhh!
This class is incredibly easy and he conveys the information well. highly recommend this class

Feels like we've been talking about the same topic all semester and I still have no idea whats going on. Sweats profusely and  rambles a lot. The TAs are absolutely no help either. Pointless topic, so save yourself some sanity and avoid this class.

Professor Ariew is very passionate about philosophy and knows his stuff, for the most part. This class is a walk in the park. I ended up playing games on my phone most of the time during class. I used the textbook only once during the class, and not even then was it necessary. I'd recommend this class to anyone who wants an easy A.

While he is a very intelligent man who obviously has a passion for philosophy, Ariew greatly fails in conveying information to his students in a simple and didactic manner. You will have to turn to outside sources to help yourself understand the course material. Also, his tests and quizzes are very poorly written. I don't recommend this class.

Dr. Ariew's lectures are very unorganized and hard to follow. He clearly knows what he is talking about but has a difficult time portraying it to students. He waves his hands around and sweats profusely during lectures. TAs teach discussion classes every Friday which is also a joke. The TA admitted to the class she was clueless about the topic.

I've always wondered where all the senile, crazy old philosophy professors come from. What are they like before they go completely nuts? Now I know. Take this class if you're really interested in abnormal psychology.
Was a very smart man but was not well prepared and did not communicate with students very well.  TA's where usually in the dark about everything that he did, which in turn, made the students suffer.

I was initially really excited, but I ended up hating the class. It's difficult to follow his lectures, and even though he's enthusiastic and obviously knows his stuff, he doesn't communicate it well to the students. Even the TAs had a hard time helping us. The textbook isn't helpful, either. I definitely recommend choosing another professor.
Agree with the previous post. Rambles, unclear, unprepared and self congratulatory.  But seemingly a nice guy.
Rambles about nothing. Worse than a pre-school teacher.

Ariew is a very energetic teacher, but he jumps around a lot during is teachings.  It is easy to get lost and left behind, so make sure you go to class and take good notes.  It's crucial to read the book.  He stresses that he wants everyone to get an A, but the tests are terribly written so it can be hard to.  Study, go to class, ad you'll do fine

Dr. Ariew is a good teacher, but very scatterbrained. He's very intelligent with Philosophy and is very concerned with student learning. He wants everyone to get an A, but for quite a few of us it didn't happen.  Think outside the box and you should be fine.
This class was so easy.  Prof Ariew was so disorganized so he never taught us anything week to week.  Definitely take it if you want an easy A.
The class was disorganized and scattered. He lectures in a very boring and arrogant manner.

This was probably the easiest class I have taken so far. But I have learned or seen probably 2/3 of the material previsouly. He is very scatter brained during lectures and tends to talk to his class like they are 5, so it can be annoying. He also makes you attend class, lame. Just do and understand the homework and hope that you have a good TA.

This class seems pretty easy to me. His lecturing style is somewhat erratic and energetic. The notes are helpful and if you do the reading you should be fine. I have/will get an A in this course and I only study at exam time.

It can be difficult to understand his lectures. He is scatterbrained and goes all over the place when lecturing. It's hard to take notes b/c he lists everything that pops into his head and doesn't organize the material very well.  Tests are tricky! A lot of "Both A & B" and "All of the Above" questions.

He is quite funny, nice, and knowledgeable. However, he erratically changes the syllabus, including the grade distribution, and has an apathetic approach to the course layout, assignments, and grading. I learned a lot, but stressed a lot more because of these things.

Great professor and is passionate about meteorology. He is one of the funniest professors I have and he cares about everyone in his class. The only things that could be difficult could be the exams and projects but his lectures make it up since he has a tv guy voice when he speaks! Don't get on his bad side though since he can be serious >:(
Very good class. He is great at lecturing and has lots of opportunities for extra credit.

Dr. Aldrich was an absolutely stellar teacher. He cares for all of his students, he's funny, engaging, and AMAZING at responding to emails. Office hours were amazing and accessible. I will say that the tests were challenging, and I did have to fight for this A, but overall the class taught me so much, and I feel better for it.

Very sweet man who clearly cares for his students. Lectures were engaging and projects were so helpful. Makes material very easy to understand. Don't talk in class though. Saw many a group get called out for being loud.

Ahh, the online class of Meteorology and it's an extension of the lecture version of the class but it's a super easy lab class and you can do it your own pace. The class is reading articles, watching videos, and mapping. Not bad  class and you get 3 tries but the questions are easy if you did the material. It's a class to learn before lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great class!

Such a wholesome man who genuinely just wants everyone to do well. Clearly passionate about Meteorology. The TAs did great too, they created very helpful study guides for the exams this semester. There were three projects which were all pretty fun to work on. It's a good, easy course where you'll learn some cool weather stuff!
The course I took was very easy. All online tests and almost no homework. The professor is great!
I LOVE HIM WITH ALL MY HEART AND I WOULD TAKE HIS CLASSSSS AGAIN AND AGAIN. I WOULD CHANGE MY MAJOR FOR THIS MAN. HE IS THE GOAT AND I TAKE EVERY CLASS HE TEACHES.
Number one in the world
Great class and great professor. Really nice to take a class that has such real world connections. Exams are easy if you study, come to class, and use the resources provided. 100% taking this class!
The absolute best professor that this university has to offer!!

Extraordinary Professor clearly loves his work and his students and makes time even outside regular office hours to meet with them. Every lecture was engaging; you could tell he wanted everyone to understand and appreciate what he does, and he sets up his lectures so that even someone with no meteorological background can comprehend every concept

Professor Aldrich was one of my favorites. This class was entertaining, and you can tell he really enjoys teaching others about weather events. I did say attendance is mandatory because he does IClicker, and he does it on random days. Overall, I would totally take another one of his classes again

Really engaging class and a very genuine guy. He's a former weather broadcaster for COMO and has a crazy background for the stuff he teaches. Very fun too. All the resources you need to succeed are available.

Genuinely so engaging. He is so passionate about meteorology and you can tell with his lectures. He is a master at using metaphors to explain complex topics. If you pay attention in class you'll have no problem with the tests, and if you can answer an odd question in class he might give you extra credit. 100% recommend.
Great guy!

if u r not an amazing test taker, don't take this class. u will not receive more than a B. Exams are 40% of ur grade and one bad exam will keep u from getting an A in the course. great guy tho. allegedly.
So awesome 10/10 recommend taking his classes

One of the best professors at Mizzou. His class was moderate. The coursework wasn't hard, but you really have to understand the concepts to do well on the exams. He is super caring, and I really like how personable he was throughout the class.
I've never liked science classes very much but he's a funny and nice professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally the goat. If you fail his class, thats on you. Offers so many opportunities/resources for extra help outside of class, and his lectures are interesting.

Hes the best. Yes, there is Iclicker but if you miss a few days it wont drop your grade. Material is pretty easy and has a lot of projects that are super easy and that are worth a lot of points. His classes are fun and tests are not difficult. If you just need a phsycial science class this is the one to take.
Fantastic professor, especially for someone who is really invested in learning about the weather.
Excellent prof! He has been one of my favorite professors at Mizzou and this class was fantastic! Would highly recommend!
Pretty good professor overall. A few in class crash outs when people were talking but they were valid. Tests are easy enough if you study, enjoyable lectures.
He is actually the best. Gives easy extra credit after tests to boost grades and knows that people aren't necessarily ATM majors

Professor Aldrich is one of the best professors I have had. He makes every student feel welcome in his class. The best part about him is how fun he is. He makes every class engaging. This is the type of class that you are excited to go to. All of the assignments are easy and as long as you study for exams you should get a A. I recommend this class.
He is a good and engaging professor, I enjoyed the lectures. Provides a good basis of understanding. One of my favorite professors.

I really liked Professor Aldrich, but I felt a bit misled by advisors when I was signing up for his course. They made it seem like it would be an easy A, but I ended up having to dedicate quite a bit of time/energy to studying just because of the amount of course content on each exam. That being said, he's super passionate about the subject!
Literally the best teacher that Mizzou has to offer and it's not even close.
Eric is an engaging and funny professor who makes learning enjoyable. Do the homework, study for exams, and participate in class - you'll do well. Unstuckstudy was super helpful for prep too.

Funny guy who made it easy to follow during lectures. If he asks questions during lectures and then answers, he sometimes gives out extra credit for speaking up. Also, he shows up to class after exams; he likes to give out free test points to people who show up. Love this guy, and he is a good teacher.
absolutely loved this class with him. always willing to help and making sure his students understand the materiel and succeed especially by giving multiple options for extra credit. heavy on clicker.

Lectures were so easy to follow and fun to go to. It's really easy to take notes and the lecture notes is basically the whole tests. There is a lot of content for each test so make sure you give yourself enough time to study but easy to understand concepts. Would 100% take again!

Amazing professor with easy exams, but if you need it he gives tons of opportunity to make up for poor exam performances through projects, quizzes, and discussion boards. Hilarious guy, engaging lectures, I only got 50% on the iClicker (attendance) and still ended with an A. Stopped recording lectures a week in, but other than that almost perfect.
The man can yap for sure, but he keeps lectures interesting. Also he will call out students in a 400 person lecture, just don't be rude and you're fine.

Aldrich clearly is very skilled at what he is teaching and it shows during class. Exams were a bit difficult for me but if you study you shouldn't have an issue at least getting an 80% on them. If you are respectful in class you'll have no issues but he has no problem calling out people who he views as disturbances in a 400 person lecture.

professor aldrich was a great professor. I took this to fulfill the A & S science requirements. I took BIO 1010 and really did not like it but professor aldrich's meteorology class was a lot more interesting and not as tough as Bio 1010. Would recommend this for non-majors.

Whatever you do during your time at Mizzou, take a class with Eric Aldrich. The funniest, kindest man and most incredible professor. His class was fun, and he made learning the course content enjoyable to the point where I wished I had his class everyday. Make sure to do the homework on time, introduce yourself, study for the tests, and participate

He is a very lecture heavy professor but they are all super interesting. I took this class as a science credit and I'm glad I took this instead of Chem or Bio. The exams can be kinda tricky but most of the questions come from the Unit Quizzes on Canvas and iClicker. The class is very heavy on iClicker but TA can adjust your grade. Would take again!

Absolutely amazing! Eric is engaging and knowledgeable in his field and you can tell he just loves to teach. I was able to learn a lot without being overwhelmed with information. As long as you pay attention to the due dates you should be fine
While there were some difficult materials, Aldrich was an incredible professor. Very easy to talk to and a fair grader depending on what TA you are given. Understanding with absences.
Prof. Aldrich keeps his lectures interesting. Our 2 projects were fun, tests can be somewhat difficult.

I never wanted to skip his class. He is the funniest teacher I have ever met. He will work with you to improve your grade if you go to office hours. Study for exams, do the weekly homework, and you'll pass easily.

Professor Aldrich is highly qualified, and cares deeply about what he teaches. I took his Severe Weather class, and LOVED it! Homework load was light, tests open note but quite difficult. He uses iClicker for attendance as a part of your grade, but attendance isn't required. Very lecture heavy course, but with interesting material. I recommend!
awesome guy

He has been my favorite professor at Mizzou so far. You can tell he loves his job which makes the lectures much more enjoyable. The class itself is somewhat hard but he throws in extra credit. Attendance is mandatory

Prof. Aldrich is so funny. I loved his class and the examples/anecdotes he used to keep students engaged. The content was interesting. Sometimes he uses iClicker, so I always go to class, but he doesn't take attendance. Definitely recommend if you're not into science but need to take a course for Gen Ed!

Professor Aldrich was a former meteorologist so he is highly qualified! He is very nice, but doesn't tolerate disrespect. Topics are interesting, but style of class is strict lecture. Little homework load with easy assignments, but tests are rather difficult. 95% assignments are online. I would recommend his Severe and Hazardous Weather class.

Eric Aldrich is one of the best professors at Mizzou. If you're looking for an easy way to get your science & upper level credit, take this class. He does use iClicker sporadically, so go to class every once in a while. The only homework he gives are discussion posts & in-class activities. The quizzes are online and super easy as well.
Super helpful and knows what he's talking about. iClicker is taken for accuracy but you get some points if you do it. Tests are a little hard but nothing terrible.
He called students out in class. Exams were not super tough but there were weekly DB and chapter quizzes. No final exam
Cool guy.

The content was pretty easy but I found the tests extremely difficult, even with studying. They were extremely annoying and tedious, but other than that, it was fine and there a bunch of chances to get a good grade.
Overall great professor, but the lectures would get boring at times.

9/10 really liked it! fill-in-the-blank lecture notes, recorded lectures, interesting content, all around great!

Aldrich is a great professor and lecturer- his lecture pace is great, he adds jokes and anecdotes- truly iconic

Professor Aldrich is great! Makes meteorology a lot of fun with little work outside of class. There are weekly discussions, two projects (one group, one solo), and 4 exams. The online textbook is optional but it was helpful at times. Attendance is important with random iClicker questions.

You don't need the textbook or even to show up to class as long as you monitor iClicker. Aldrich is very kind and makes sure the tests and assignments are as easy as possible. He wants everyone to get an A.
My favorite professor at Mizzou. Hes a great teacher and Meterology is an easy class

I'm glad I was able to take this class with Professor Aldrich! It's not always an easy class, so you do have to work hard and hold yourself accountable for your own performance--it is a 4000 level course, after all. He's always available in his office to go over certain topics, grades, and so on. Overall, a really great class with fun material!

Eric would rather watch you fail than help you succeed. As an upper level atmospheric science student, I was expecting to learn challenging concepts in this course. Whenever we would approach those concepts, his explanations would only be surface level and push it off for "another class." This is a 4000 level course, what is the "next class?!"
He is super fun and nice! i never thought i would be interested in this class but he makes it fun to learn, will help a lot before exams and gives extra credit!

Aldrich is a great professor, his lectures are interesting and he is very nice. Easy A if you put in the effort. Go to lecture! A couple times he will give extra credit points for going to lecture. Very easy honors credit, it's the same lecture as the non honors section, same content and tests as the regular section, and barely any extra work.

Prof. Aldrich was a great professor. A really nice and engaging guy who really knows his stuff. The lectures were most of the class, but he managed to make the note taking process more enjoyable, as his lectures were always informative and not boring. Would absolutely take again

Aldrich will give you real life experiences and examples. I laughed at least once every lecture and he was very easy to follow along to. Lots of little grades throughout the semester, but they are super easy to complete. Great professor and knows what he is talking about!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Super passionate about Metrology which makes class more interesting. Grades are based on weekly quizzes & discussions, 4 exams, and a super easy project. Many of the questions can be found in notes/online/textbook. It's not necessary to purchase the textbook. Attendance isn't necessary, but he does iClicker most classes that counts towards grade.
He's a good professor in my opinion, I just hated the course because I don't want to learn about clouds and stuff but, still passed even with me not attending the zooms.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Aldrich is an amazing guy. He is very passionate about the weather, and you can tell he loves what he does during lectures. iClicker questions during class so attendance is mandatory most of the time unless you're okay with missing points for those. Some quiz and test questions come from the textbook. I loved him and this class.
AMAZING guy and teacher. So passionate about the subject and it doesn't matter how little you care about weather, he makes it fun. If you can, take this class FORSURE! don't buy the textbook btw

The BEST professor I've had in my entire lifetime. He made me want to come to his class. There are quizzes after each chapter but can be found on notes/book/quizlet. I recommend going to every class especially right after tests b/c he gives extra credit to those who showed up. He was flexible with the pandemic and posted lectures on canvas.
Prof Aldrich is the best professor I have had so far. If you have the chance to take one of his courses... DO IT

Eric is hilarious. You probably don't need to go to lecture every time but you will because he makes it entertaining. Test will be word for word out of the powerpoint. Gives a lot of extra credit for just showing up to class.

Material isn't super hard if you are willing to study, but don't take this class with him. My iclicker worked all year and right after i took his final, he told me he did not ever receive any of my answers even though it worked for me and i never skipped class. He ended up failing me which nearly cost me my college education. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: do NOT take this class. It's so difficult. I'm a straight A student, and I got a B in his class. The lectures are elementary level science, and the exams are at a college level-- soo hard. I went to every review session and studied for hours, and still ended up with a B. he is nice, but the class SUCKS. do NOT take. it's not worth it.

Great teacher, I loved him for all of the classes I have taken. He wants you to suceed but requires the least amount of effort, like seriously you have to try to fail his classes. He is a wonderful resource for anything Meteorology and also has the most interesting lectures. Highly recommend

Aldrich is the best professor I have had so far. I had to take ATM1050 for my major and I was not looking forward to it, but I ended up actually loving it. Easy if you study for the exams and come to class. Notes are really important because he gives extra credit. Dude is super passionate about what he's teaching which makes it much more enjoyable

Nicest and most understanding professor ever. Two easy projects and open-note online quizzes. Tests are decently hard and weighted heavily. He holds reviews where he pretty much gives out answers. Gives random extra credit points if you show up to class. Always wants to help students improve their grades. Go to class and study for tests to do well!

Aldrich is the best teacher that I have had so far! While there are a few projects, he is so funny that every class flies bye! He brings in his daughters occasionally and has extra credit throughout the semester. Great guy who never failed to make me laugh!

Aldrich is an amazing professor who knows what he is talking about. You will have to go to class because he does clicker questions. The tests are hard if you don't study, but I got a D and C on two of them and still have a B+. Their are two major projects, but I completed them both in under an hour and got an 100% on both. VERY funny!

Aldrich is really passionate about what he does, he used to be the weatherman for Columbia! Even though I'm not very interested in meteorology, I looked forward to going to class. Take notes & study a little and you will be golden.

Eric was an enjoyable teacher, he is very enthusiastic about meteorology which made the lectures fun. He gave extra credit two times during the semester. all you had to do was show up for class on that day but he didn't tell you the day. the class was not super easy but it wasn't super hard either.

Aldrich is very funny and caring. His class is note-heavy and not necessarily an easy A, but with a proper amount of studying before the exams and attendance for notes and REEF questions, it shouldn't be hard to get a good grade in the class. Aldrich makes it interesting with his humor and stories connecting to the subject in class.

Very interesting class. Professor Aldrich is very funny and wants his students to succeed. It helps a lot to reach the textbook but you could most likely get by without. I definitely recommend taking this class if it is for a needed credit.
Goofy.
If you show up to class and participate, he'll generously round up your grade if you ask for it. He often gives EC for answering questions in class too.
Eric is a great guy who makes the lectures very interesting and funny. If you have any interest in weather I suggest taking this class!

Professor Aldrich teaches the ins and outs of meteorology in a pretty captivating way. His lectures are large, therefore, students on their computers, etc. can be distracting. Attend class to get easy REEF points and sort out any issues you might have with that early. His tests are definitely challenging. Use quizlet, office hours and study guides.

Great teacher, i took this for science credit and it was a great choice. I studied and went to class, but if you do that you will get an A. Him and his staff have helpful reviews i recommend going to before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Subject isn't super interesting, but he clearly knows a lot about it and has a passion for it. Lets out class early daily, gives lots of extra credit opportunities. Tests are somewhat difficult; you should read the textbook and study the PowerPoints to do well, but if you come to class & get the extra credit, you don't need to study too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: What is not to like about this guy. He's hilarious, tells great stories, occasionally lets out early especially when weather is nice. He's extremely approachable, cares about the students. Tests aren't bad, solid guy.
Professor Aldrich is funny, to the point, and always there to help (if you ask). If you show up and pay attention you'll have no problem.

Professor Aldrich is amazing! I loved his class. He's very funny and makes the material understandable. His stories are great and I highly recommend the class.  The 2nd Exam was the hardest, but don't give up. Do the Homework, Chapter Assessments, and Quizzes and you will be fine.

If you go to class, you will be better off. He gives out some great lectures and has hilarious stories about his time at KOMU TV when he was a meteorologist. Exam 2 is tricky, but you can go to his office hours and he will help you a TON. Textbook was optional, and overall great class.
I absolutely loved this class. Aldrich is a great guy. His lectures are clear & his tests are based off of his lectures. Would def take again.

Eric is a very personable, funny, knowledgable professor. His analogies are odd at times, but they somehow make sense. I liked having professor that shared some of his personal life with his students.

Professor Aldrich is a great person and very entertaining at times. His class was fairly easy but the material was boring. You must attend class in order to get clicker points and to fill in the blanks on his ppt slides. Be sure to review these before exams and you'll do well. I never looked at the ebook and passed with an A-.

Professor Aldrich really tries to make lectures entertaining, and most of the time succeeds, but sometimes the material can get a little dry. He is very good about answering in class questions despite the large class size and it was over all an enjoyable class. Lots of clicker points and you can't opt out of purchasing the ebook, however.

This class was hard for me because science is not my strong suit. Eric is a great, funny guy though who has made our entire lecture hall laugh out loud many times. I would suggest always going to class because of clicker points, studying to the best of your ability, and utilizing office hours a lot. He is very passionate, be ready to work though!

He's a good instructor and teaches like he enjoys meteorology which is always a bonus. It pays to go to class, participation points can help or hurt your grade. As long as you keep up and complete the study guides the exams shouldn't be too complex.

He's such a nice and funny guy! For sure my favorite professor. He used to be a weatherman, so his lectures are like listening to weather reports. He gives such clear and accurate lectures and the tests are mostly easy. Just make sure you check the syllabus regularly and you'll do great.
Eric was a great professor who made class fun and interesting. Highly recommend the class, and would take it again for sure.

By far one of my favorite professors that I've had thus far. There are Iclicker questions in the majority of questions but participation is the majority and the questions are usually easy. The exams are doable if you're going to lectures (which are actually fun), and EC is sometimes offered when attendance is low. Definitely a great professor!

Professor Aldrich is great!! He is so helpful and his lectures are interesting and easy to understand. GO TO OFFICE HOURS BEFORE TESTS. He will help you out and possibly give you extra credit. There are iclicker questions but not every class. Online assignments are super easy. Tests are easy if you spend some time studying! Overall great teacher!

Eric a great guy! He loves what he does, and it clearly reflects in his teaching. He cares about all of his students, and he wants everyone to be successful. I learned a lot of practical knowledge from his class. My favorite professor at MU by far.

He was very fun to listen to in lectures. Tests were not exactly an easy A, but with time put in to studying you will do well. Homework and quiz grades help overall grade a lot. Very helpful during office hours. You can tell he cares about his students and loves to teach.

Professor Aldrich has been one of my favorite professors at Mizzou. He really breaks down the lectures so everyone can understand what he's talking about. He's also really funny, and tells a lot of funny stories throughout his lectures. But the class is pretty easy, just take good notes and study for the exams and you'll do fine!

First, go to class. Trust me it will make your life easier come exam time & attendance points are huge! But, the class is pretty great. Eric is actually hilarious, and he makes weather interesting! Quizzeshmwk are basically free points, but exams are harder than you'd expect. Not an easy A, but with a bit of effort you'll walk away happy.
Aldrich is hilarious and you will actually want to go to lecture. 2nd test is kinda tough but nothing unbearable.
aldrich is a great guy. you will need to study for the tests, but there are other points to help you out. all in all an enjoyable class
Funny Guy, Easy set up class, makes it simple for the students, and the exams are very fair.
Definitely not a throw-away class. If you study hard and work hard, you will do fine in the class.

I was really excited for this class but it got pretty hard in the end. I thought the tests were unreasonably hard, there was no way to know all the answers. But the information is interesting and fun to learn.

He is a great professor! I learned a lot in in class. If you attend ALL classes, you will do just fine.  Besides, his classes are actually fun to attend!  He has some great stories to tell. My only other advice is to not get the textbook, since we never used it. Great teacher, great class, you can't ask for anything better!

Great, very knowledgable professor! He's really passionate about the weather and you can tell he enjoys coming and teaching class. iClicker is used fairly regularly and is a decent chunk of your grade. He had us by the online textbook but I never used it once. Straightforward multiple choice tests, final was not cumulative.

Eric is the bomb. As an atmospheric sciences student I loved his class, it was very basic for me but I understand not all the concepts are something other people will get right off the bat. He's funny, keeps class interesting, and will help those who don't understand something. He is very forward about the class and there are not tricks. I loved it

Class is not always enjoyable but it is recommended you attend because he uses iClicker and a lot of points come from that. Office hours are a must, especially before a test because the TA hold awesome review sessions which they have the test right in front of them. Tests seem basic for the amount of information he gives, but still A achievable.

He is a pretty good teacher but there is a lot of information for such a basic class. You don't get full i clicker points unless you study online which is irritating. He pulls info from the book and his notes for tests

Very cool teacher, probably one of my favorites! Tests were based off of lectures and reading so make sure you study both! Take advantage of his office hours! He gives you bonus points for asking for help! Attendence is important bc he uses the iClicker to ask questions during class and a huge chunk of your points come from it!

AWESOME TEACHER! he does a great job teaching and keeping your attention. does not have a final. only 4 tests. quizzes and homework are online and they are soo easy. does use a clicker. highly recommend this class if you are looking for an easy science class!!

AWESOME TEACHER! his presentations go exact with test so def attend class. keeps you interested. test can be somewhat challenging, but studying one night will probably get you an A. homework and quizzes are a piece of cake. looking for an easy science class, TAKE THIS!!!

Overall it isn't too hard.  I'm a meteorology major, so I found the material more interesting than most people.  Opened the book one time.  Really isn't that necessary.  Test's are kinda tricky, do the study guide.  He wants you to "apply" your knowledge so  some questions are dumb.

The class itself is huge and Eric does a really good job of holding your attention. Attendance is not mandatory and everything you need to know is on blackboard or in the book. Eric himself or the TA's are always looking to help you and will spend as much time as you need to understand the material. WOULD RECOMMEND, EASY A!

All lecture powerpoints available online. Quizzes can be completed with just those notes. Book was opened once and still received A's and B's on tests. Follow study guides given but still look over all notes, not everything is laid out to you he wants you to apply what you learned

He is a good teacher but my grade did not reflect that. He even says he makes hard tests. I suggest Googling quiz answers when you do the online quizzes because some will take you to online sites that have test questions & answers. Know the study guide really well.

I made this class harder just because it was easy not to go to class since most of the notes are on-line. To make it easier I suggest going. I agree you're not always sure what will be on the tests so you have to study a lot more than you think. Not too bad though.

The class is decently hard. The quizzes are online so you have the abilities to look up the answers. Tests are difficult because you don't exactly know what he wants you to study. He gives study guides  but half of what is on the guide is not covered on the test.
This really shouldnt be a hard class but Eric makes it difficult.  Do not think it is an easy class.

Intro to Meteorology is a joke. The class is him doing a slide show but he never actually knows what are on his own tests. Only half of his study guides are correct and although the material he teaches is simple, it is a nightmare trying to scramble through the junk he says and the junk the book throws at you to find what is actually important.

For a one thousand level class, this was much too difficult. Quiz and test questions did not reflect the level of instruction in class or the textbook. I'm a journalism major who took the class thinking it would be a relevant, easy way to fulfill my science requirement. I hated this class and it brought down my near perfect GPA.

I love Professor Aldrich! He's really a funny guy and the class is as easy as you make it. He gives easy assignments and quizzes to boost ur grade so its practically impossible to fail! Attendance isn't mandatory, but sometimes he has attendance quizzes and he'll give extra credit points.

at least he tries... but I didn't like this class. His tests were terribly written and he doesn't seem to know what's on his tests, don't bother paying attention during review because most likely 50% of it won't appear on the test. Make sure to read the book, and even do your own research on the topics outside of the text
He is a good guy, you do have to go to class or you will not get all of the notes, also reading is nessissary, read before you take quizes!!
Pretty funny.  Go to class and take notes on the small things he says.  Make sure you do the readings in the book because a lot of test questions come from that.
Funny teacher. If you go to class you will have no trouble getting an A or B. Don't by the case studies book, you will never use it.  Waste of 45$
Very handsome. Not very tall
Eric is a cool guy!.. local celeb!... class is interesting if your curious about the weather... not the easiet class but if you just go to class and take decent notes you should get an A
It is a pretty easy class as long as you attend lectures and keep up to date on material.
Class is stupid.  The test are difficult-He also made us buy a completely useless book for two assignments.  It takes forever to get grades back.
Great Teacher. very interesting!
Intro. to Meteorology ATMS 1050
No Comments
Took the leadership development class and learned a lot. Lectures were interactive. Class attendance is important so don't plan to miss a lot.

I had her for MNGT 3000W and she was terrible, TA did all the grading, had to remind her to post grades, class was a snooze fest, exams were impossible to study you just had to wing it, SO MANY GROUP PROJECTS, She would take at least two days to respond to emails and when she posted grades, revisions were due like 5 hours later. wouldn't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had her for Management 3000W and she has no idea what shes doing, youll do papers and shell expect you to revise them without releasing the grader you got, and then shell release it like 5 hours before revisions are due. The TA does all the grading and then finals week shell come in and drop your grade by like 4%

The most unorganized class I have ever taken. Her TA's do everything and she does nothing. The grading is not made clear to the TA's so they make it up as they go. Your groups participation will affect your grade and they do not care if they did work or not. Her lectures are pointless and she uses iClicker. She will give no direction.

Professor Brengarth is not a good professor and I did not like BA3500 with her at all. It all felt very unorganized and like a waste of time if being honest. The lectures were pointless, and I couldn't wait to be done with the class. I can't recommend this class with her to anyone. Stay away.
Good class but a lot of group work.

Great experience getting hands on real-world experience working with a team and REAL client (not just a case study). Dr. Brengarth clearly cares about her students. Students who don't want to put in the work will complain, but those who show up end up with an awesome resume builder.

BA 3500 was the worst class I have taken at Mizzou. Completely unorganized, would ask TAs for help and they wouldn't know either. Big assignments would seemingly pop up out of no where. Important information about our project was held back until deep into the semester for some reason. Not really sure what brengarth does when TAs do all grading.

!AVOID! The worst class I have taken at Mizzou as well as the worst professor. Everything is disorganized. This class is a dumpster fire. Essentially you do free work for companies and it is as time-consuming as a part-time job. I should be paid for taking this class, I shouldn't have to pay for it. No notice of assignments and everyone's confused

This has been the worst class I have taken, taught by the worst professor I have had. It is a 3 credit hour class that is VERY time consuming that consists of only busy work. We were told when big assignment were due less than a week in advance, if that. She does not know how to work canvas and puts things under the wrong module. TA's are also conf

The assignments are all over the place. Grading is inconsistent. No help from the professor. Very little feedback. Overall the worst class I have ever taken at Mizzou. The fact that it is this poor of a class and is mandatory for business majors is crazy. A horribly structured class with ridiculous standards.
doesn't teach and doesn't give any information

Very unorganized. Impossible to reach. TA's never know what they are doing. Lectures are pointless to go to. She is very unclear in her grading scale. Sends out meeting links a minute before we are supposed to start. Does not actually really do anything. Saw her salary, makes too much. Puts all the work onto the TA's. Not sure what she really does.

The class is very unorganized. She randomly assigns homework due by the end of the day (completely screws any chance of working students to do the assignment correctly). She will add assignments midweek with no warning. TAs didn't communicate until about a month into the class (TAs are necessary for this class).
Worst class I have ever taken. It is basically an unpaid internship filled with busy work with no clear grading criteria.

This is single handedly the worst professor in the college of business. Been here 4 years and haven't taken a class as poorly organized as this one. Lauren Brengarth is a joke. She is teaching a professionalism class, yet she is the most unprofessional professor I have seen. She also tells her T/A's to not give out A's.

The professor is highly disorganized, which has made it difficult for many of us to follow the course. Assignments and materials are often unclear, and she rarely provides feedback or guidance. It feels like there is a lack of concern for the students' success, many of us have reached out with questions and received little to no response. AWFUL!!

Does not respond to emails. Relies on TA to respond to emails and grade all work. Points get docked for little to no reason. Class meetings were pointless. Little to no guidance and the TA is just as confused most of the time.

If you can choose any other professor, do it. I have never had a professor choose to give me bad grades even when they are not justified until now. Her and her TA will find any flaw in your work that they can to justify taking off a ridiculous amount of points. Quite possibly the worst class I have taken at Mizzou and it is not the courses fault.

Honestly, just a standard EDGE program class. Lots of red tape and hoops to jump through. If you miss any little thing written or not, you will definitely get points off. She was ok, but the class content was awful. Just hard to sit through and attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst course I have taken in my academic career. The class is completely unorganized, and there is no leeway for students. We had a group project with a client, there were no guidelines for what we were supposed to be doing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

One of the worst classes I've ever taken at Mizzou, changed my entire outlook on Cornell because I could not believe how well respected she was as a professor, but how awful she was as a teacher. The group project is HORRIBLE, there is almost no grading criteria, she posts things late/pushes back due dates, and the TAs never know what's going on.

Genuinely one of the worst professor I have ever had. She is not only unprepared to teach students, her teaching assistants don't even know what is going on. She repeatedly posted things late and wasted class time on panels instead of going over the necessary assingments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.B gives you a client and expects you to give 100% of your time to help them. Very unorganized and agenda is unclear. Lectures were pointless and most of the time had nothing to do with course content. Waste of time and money. Didn't learn anything.

Lectures are mandatory but have nothing to do or help with the group project at all. Lauren is the worst professor I've ever had at working with students and trying to help them. Its her way or the highway. As mentioned by others, the amount of homework and how tough its graded is insane for a 3 credit hour class. Mizzou needs to change this class.

Honestly the worst class I have ever taken at Mizzou. Lectures are pointless yet required, no organization, and assignments are worth way more than 3 credit hours of time. Feels like you are taking 2 classes at once. Hour long lectures but spends no time elaborating on the group project, the biggest part of your grade. Only hope is your TA.

As others have said, heavily TA dependent. While many students have easy projects in the class, if you are unlucky enough then you will struggle while others get 100 in the class. The project and the in person aspect are basically two completely unrelated classes, and it's bizarre how this is set up. Mizzou should not require it.

Students get points off for the most impractical reasons. Class attendance is required for classes with little to no educational instruction.
