reviews.comment: I took this class with this teacher my freshman year, one of the first college level classes I've taken and my experience has been nothing but positive. She was a great teacher and her lectures clear and concise. The bad reviews I've been reading only makes me think of students who were lazy and wanted an easy A. You NEED to go to class to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really don't understand why her rates here are so low. Maybe all the bad feedback got to her but she has been really good with answering questions when I was in her class last semester. Also, the tests are pretty easy if you study. If you just read the lectures once or twice, then obviously you won't do well. Just study, it's not bad at all.

Took it for my mandatory bio science credit. For the love of god, do not take it with this woman. She will set tough deadlines for you, but then she will break her own deadlines constantly. I hope you don't like asking questions, because if you ask one she will make you feel stupid. The only positive side to this class is that the tests are easy.

This class isn't hard as it is made out to be. Natalie is very clear with what you need to know for exams. I would recommend going to class as she gives hints about word problems on the exams. I just studied my notes from the class, and did really well on exams. I only looked at the book if I wanted to know more about something. At least a B.

Tests aren't too bad if you have developed critical thinking skills by this point. You really have to apply information rather than regurgitate. Not bad from a lecturingtesting perspective, but she can be very rude and make you feel dumb for asking a reasonable question or challenging her. Go to recitation for help!

Horrible. Do not take this class with her as your professor. She does not care about her students nor is she helpful in anyway. She is very rude and disrespectful to her students. This class is not worth taking if she is the teacher. RUN.

Downer is terrible.  She is incredibly rude.  If you ask any questions, she'll act like you're stupid and not answer the question.  Her lectures don't portray what will be on the exams.  For your own good, PLEASE get a different professor.
Downer was never helpful to any of her students and always made you feel stupid if you asked a question. I would not recommend her to anyone in the future

People make this class out to be much harder than it is because they want to be handed an easy A. Show up to lectures, take notes, and memorize your notes before tests. All I did was look at my notes and glanced at my book a few times before tests. Ended with a 98 and didn't have to take the final. If you talk one on one with Downer she is helpful.

PLEASE do not take this course with Downer. On review days she will ask if anyone has questions and someone asked a question and she told them that they should of prepared more and that she wouldn't take the time to go over the answer. She makes you feel very dumb. Her exams are very difficult, while the homework is easy. Get a tutor.

Downer was the worst professor I had at Mizzou. She is extremely unorganized and unclear. If you want to do well you have to go to office hours and talk to her. If not, you'll probably get a C or below.  Don't ask questions in class because she will make you feel stupid. 45 of her test averages were failing grades. Throughly unimpressed. SWITCH!

Professor Downer is definitely passionate about what she does. It's frustrating because the content is not that hard, but she is very unclear. If you don't go to office hours, consider yourself screwed. Her lecture slides are very unorganized and confusing. I would recommend getting tutored every chance possible because otherwise it'll be difficult
Very rude when you ask questions, makes you feel stupid easily.
Teacher has strong accent, and it's a lot of content, but I really liked Natalie. She is super nice and is very passionate about what she does. While class was hard I enjoyed her a lot.
Semi-easy class, definitely need to study for exams, and attend all RSDs and Labs. Overall not a "hard" class.

Reads directly off slides in a mind numbingly monotone voice. Easily the most difficult class I've ever taken in my academic career, and unfortunately also the worst professor I've ever had. This combo makes for a GPA-detrimental course that either consumes your entire semester or has you accepting a C.

He just reads off slides, which are just stuff from the textbook. Test averages never went over 65. You CANNOT cram studying in this class. I liked having the physical book, highlighting what is discussed in lecture. My advice: consistently review, TRULY memorize pathways and cycles, draw out concept maps.

Doesnt know what he is talking about, goes on tangents that do not make sense, he mumbles. He's strict and his study materials are 50/50. Lectures/slides are confusing.need a lot of background information to try to understand this course. He is honestly rude. He is not helpful during office hours.PLA's are nice and really do try to help you though.
Doesn't even try to teach. Read off of slides and refused to answer questions in office hours. Degrading
horrible. horrible. horrible. DO NOT TAKE

It seemed like he was learning the material as he was presenting it to us. He also talked painfully slow and stumbled over every word. Lectures were genuinely so painful & I never knew what he was saying. The exams were impossibly long and so hard, averages never got above 62%. He seemed like a nice guy but truly a terrible professor.

reviews.comment: Professor Van Doren is currently stumbling over his slides as I'm writing this review. Every slide is word vomit and impossible to follow and learn from. Mizzou, please fire this man.

reviews.comment: He seems very knowledgeable about biochemistry, but he uses recycled slides. This class has made me seriously reconsider changing my major because of its difficulty and stress. This is by far the worst professor at Mizzou. Do not take a course that is taught by this guy.

This was the hardest class I have ever taken at Mizzou, I have never struggled like this in a STEM class, I met with this man every week trying to understand the material, and I simply could not. reviews.comment: The content itself is interesting. He gives extra credit for you showing up through iClicker & for submitting extra discussion posts. He is also a bit rude in emails.

Honestly the worst and hardest class I have ever taken at Mizzou. Class averages were always a D. He does not teach you have to learn everything on your own. His exams are also ridiculous because he intentionally tries to trick you. Do not take this class with him.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I have never had such a horrible professor prior to taking this class. None of the material is organized and it is impossible to study and do well on his exams. His class average was a D. Save yourself the struggle and take this with another professor

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable of subjects but ineffective in teaching it.  Secondly, he is unwilling to help any students in his class that do that do not work for his lab, and at times, gossips about his students to other teachers.  When you summarizes all that has been said, it is no reason why Dr. Van Doren is also nicknamed, "Dr. Van Douchebag"

I love Dow! His class is really fun and I enjoyed all of the essay prompts. The discussions are great if people feel like talking, so just get him to like you through talking when he goes quiet and you're basically set. He says essays should be 500 words but doesn't check, so just keep your writing generally concise and you're good.

Dr. Dow is great! He's super funny, has a ton of energy, and really cares about all of his students. He makes what should be a very boring class fun and overall brings a great vibe to class. While his grading can be a little confusing, if you meet with him and discuss what you did wrong, his feedback is very helpful.

Dr. Dow is a nice person, but a difficult professor. The class was graded on 4 exams and attendance, with optional seminars for extra credit. You won't pass the exams without almost perfect attendance or reading the required book. Exam questions also felt abnormally difficult. If you aren't a good test taker, I wouldn't recommend this class.

All and all, he's a great guy, lock in for his class though.

reviews.comment: Prof. Dow is a clear instructor. A lot of the work is done in class, and he lectures in a very easy to follow, articulate style. He stays in the intellectual mainstream — you'll read for standard interruption, and very rarely encounter critique of the Founders.

reviews.comment: Dr. Dow is a very sweet guy. He also is the most confusing grader in the world. There's a lot of reading, but as long as you pay attention in class its fine- I suggest annotating

reviews.comment: Professor Dow's class is intense, but engaging. Attending lectures is a must - he moves quickly, but his passion shines through. Utilize the textbook and study tools like unstuck AI to stay on top of the material. Manage your time well, and you'll do great.

I'm taking 4190 with Professor Dow right now and it is a really interesting class! He is a good lecturer and explains things well. There are a lot of papers and you will not get a rubric unless you go to his office hours. Attendance is mandatory and you will not do well on the papers if you don't go to class

If you don't show up to lectures, you will not pass. His humor during class comes off as rude occasionally and I found myself afraid to answer questions... I have to emphasize you must read every single thing assigned and come to class. I've heard other 1100 teachers are a lot easier so I'd avoid his if you're not going to try!

Professor Dow is phenomenal. The class consists of members reading the necessary texts out loud. Beyond that, there is one test concerning Constitutional knowledge and then 4 essays and participation. Dr. Dow brings awesome stories and good humor to the class. If you are still concerned about a high grade, literally just go to his office hours...

Okay, he is a really easy professor IF he knows you. Go to his office and talk with him, become friends with him. You do not have to go to all of his classes but when you do go talk a lot. If he knows your name you will get a good grade. Just show or at least pretend you care about what you are learning.

reviews.comment: he is rude and disrespectful. his tests are nothing like what you have learned. dont take his class.

reviews.comment: Jay is really a personable guy. Is super passionate about history and cares for each one of his students, even though being in a lecture hall full of 300+ students.

Jay Dow is one of my favorite professors at the University of Missouri, as he is engaging and knowledgeable about his field. I understand that many people perceive Dow as a strict, but this perception is most likely from students who he taught in large lecture halls, in which being strict is oftentimes required. In small classes, he is a great guy.
Study and pay attention. He has been doing this for years and hundreds of students have passed his class. It is doable, trust me, you just can't wait to the last minute to study for exams

reviews.comment: You have to be there for every lecture or else you will miss a lot of notes. I would just skim through the chapters we were supposed to read the day before the test and that seemed to work for me. I think the class had 3 or 4 test, but I can't remember exactly. Almost all questions on the test came from lecture with a few coming from the book.

I like professor Dow's lectures. It was really interesting to take his class while an election was going on, so if you have the chance to take the class during midterm elections, I would recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dow is very intelligent and gives good lectures if you listen closely to everything he is saying, although it can make you sleepy. Read the assigned readings and don't skip because all of the exams are based off the lectures, which he doesn't post online.

reviews.comment: Lectures are absolutely terrible to sit through and he walks around like he owns the place.  Very smart guy, but very arrogant and cocky.  Never know what he'll test you over so if you take this class you should study 5-6 days in advance of an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is a tough class, but Jay Dow knows his stuff. His lectures are interesting and he really is interested in what he is teaching.

reviews.comment: He's a fine professor, but definitely expects a lot from you. The reason I find the class difficult is because of my lack of interest on the subject. History classes have never been my thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Boring and arrogant. He gives off the feeling that he believes he's superior to all of his students.

reviews.comment: Jay is not a cool guy. He is self-absorbed and extremely arrogant. You can tell he feels as though he is extremely superior to the students of his lecture. Disrespectful to students during class and inconsiderate of effort. He doesn't use tegrity so if you are sick I would recommend attempting receive multiple students notes if you miss a lecture.

reviews.comment: Very passionate about his research and teaching but overall just a jerk. Jumps right into all the topics and provides us with little background knowledge to help us follow along. Grading is based on 4 exams and that is it. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dow really knows what he is teaching and his passion for the material is obvious. He comes across at tough because he really wants you to learn what he teaches. I use the material I learned in his class frequently, he's a great teacher.

Dow can seem intimidating and uncaring at first, but he is just passionate about what he does.  Won't care if you come to class, but should because most material is in lecture and slides are not posted to blackboard.  If you need help with something serious he is extremely helpful.  If you are confused about materials see a TA.

Funny guy, makes lots of bad jokes but they're usually worth a laugh  clearly passionate about what he does. Didn't think it was a horribly difficult course. finished with a B by only going to lecture. Would recommend reading.

his lectures are almost impossible to understand, but you have to attend because he lectures about things that aren't in the readings that will be on the tests. tests include an essay. whenever I've gone to him for help he wasn't too helpful and treats his students like they're idiots and is super arrogant.

really knowledgable of the material. lectures are just reviews of the reading. there is a lot of reading but you don't need to read them if you pay attention in class. only 3 test and a final. seems intimidating at first but is just a review of high school government with a little more detail and focus on the constitution. The TAs help more.
toughest class I've ever taken. do not recommend to anyone

As someone with an interest in political sciences I really enjoyed this class but it was tough. Its very important to go to the lectures and to ask questions for clarity. Dow knows what he is talking about but can be very pompous at times. Personally I did well without reading but thats rare. If you pay attention in lectures you should be fine.

if you love yourself and value your livelihood in any capacity, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Only 3 tests and a final exam but the exams cover weeks of info and are only 35 questions and he never does reviews/lets you know what will be on the test. no notes or powerpoint online either. PP slides are vague so u have to be pretty engaged to get good notes

This has been the hardest class that I have taken thus far. His tests are insane, you have no clue what exactly is going to be one them, besides what you've gone over in class (which is everything). I didn't care for politics or government but after taking this class with Dow, I have come to appreciate it very much. He is a truly passionate teacher

Tough class. Come to class take notes and pay attention. If you do that, you'll do fine. He has a zero tolerance policy for technology use that is not used for note taking. So no facebook. Learned a lot.

Stay Away! I honestly have no clue how you could like this class. He is very knowledgeable but is an awful teacher and a jerk. Tests are insane and studying for his tests are hard as well. He has no clarity on what he wants you to know. Only class I received below a B on in college.

Hate this class so much. Dow is incredibly conceited and often degrades his students. He honestly doesn't care about their grades. Take the class, just choose a different professor. Listen to me. The worst college course I've ever taken.

Go to every class, take notes by hand, at least skim the readings, pay attention, and you'll be fine. Dow knows what he's talking about and is interesting to listen to. I've learned a lot and am now more interested in government. Tests can be difficult, but if you really pay attention, you'll do fine.

Jay Dow knows what he's talking about, and enjoys talking about the government. As someone who wasn't originally that interested in government, he made it interesting. Definitely go to all the classes and at least skim the readings, especially bolded terms and the quizzes at the end of chapters. Taking notes by hand helps a lot. Pay attention.

annoying and arrogant teacher.  Him and his TA's told me to study "word for word" what the constitution says.  I bombed the first test after learning what his tests are all about.  Go to class and study readings.

Dow is very full of himself and annoys me more than anyone. This is not an easy class but as long as you go to class, take good notes and read everything you should do fine on the tests. There is a lot of reading in this class and its hard to keep up with it. This class requires a lottttttt of studying.
Reading and attending the lectures are a must. Take notes because the tests are 50% lecture and 50% readings. He may come off as sarcastic but he is nice if you come knowing your stuff.
Lectures are interesting, but the tests are difficult and he does not give out study guides. There is a lot of material, do not expect higher than a B, class averages on exams were low B range.

Definitely more of a workload than I expected with this class. You are required to read ALL of the assigned readings. As long as you take good notes and do the readings tests are fairly easy. Go to class- gives occasional quizzes.
He explains things well the class is just hard as hell

What I consider my first class, Dow was a pretty cool guy to have it with. Most important thing is going to class and taking notes;got a C- on my first test and still ended up with an A. It taught me how to prepare. He will  let you fail, but also keeps it loose.The textbook is expensive but needed; try to share one with someone. Lectures are key.

Class is not that exciting but you should go whenever you can manage to wake up at 8am because of his pop quizes. His tests are somewhat challenging but if you put in the time, you will be fine. Overall, I would say that he loves what he teachs. I would take this class with him again.

Hard tests for me, but that is b/c I cramm 2 days before. Keep up with the textbook, b/c he won't tell you but then put it on the test. Class is boring b/c it's at 8am. Tries to be funny and sometimes is. He rolls a die every morning and if it's a 1/6 your in luck b/c there is a quiz and I don't study everyday so I get 1 out of 3's on those. Study!

Tests are very hard compared to what is covered in lecture and the book. Pop quizzes are apparently not only over politics, but also over anything and everything in the New York Times. Thinks he is funny but isn't. Quite possibly the worst thing I have to get up for at 8.

My first university class. I thought it was a pretty good experience. I like that he puts a strong emphasis on knowing the constitution. Its a core of American politics and many don't completely understand it. Go to class because he will give a quiz if he see attendance is low. Pretty funny guy, but i can see why some might not like him.

I know Dow can seem arrogant at times, but he knows the material very well. And he has a great passion for teaching American Government. I had him in American Government, and now I'm currently taking my capstone with him. He may be arrogant, but that's life, get over it and learn from someone who knows what they're talking about.

HATED THIS CLASS WITH A PASSION!! Dow is an arrogant **** and does not give two****s about anyone but himself. His tests were terribly hard. The only good thing about this class was that his final was the EASIEST thing I have ever taken. Around 80% of the final were questions from the 3 midterms word for word.

He is really arrogant and gives pop quizzes on days that no one shows up. His tests are really hard, I even studied old ones from sororities/frats and still came out with a C average. He assigns readings from a book that is completely irrelevant to the lectures but puts it on the test anyway. I loved Poli sci in highschool but he made me hate it.

AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS, I was very good at poli sci all throughout highschool and was qualified for a way higher course than this. Jay Dow will ask the most random questions on his tests that pertain to nothing he ever talked about or was mentioned in the book.

For my first semester of college. I enjoyed this class a ton and sparked my interest in political science a ton so much so that i have added a poly sci minor. He may talk over the heads of some students but its college, and was very easy to comprehend. the tests were easy, i got an A- with no effort at all.

This class was fine, not hard at all. If you get an old copy of the test, you'd literally have to TRY to fail. Went to class, got extra-credit, was let out early on nice days and got an A. Dow was cool, too. As a first-semester freshman, probably one of the easiest classes I took.

Yes, he's arrogant but he knows his stuff. His lectures can be a bit boring and you have to attend if you're taking one of his upper level classes. Tests are fair- his election campaign class if worth taking

Quite possibly the most arrogent, bias professor at Mizzou. Ironic that he teaches political science. Turned me away from pursuing a minor in political science and made for a HORRIBLE first semester class freshman year. Go find someone else who will actually care about your education. Jay Dow is a joke.

Was extremely knowledgeable, interesting and funny professor. Best class I have taken at Mizzou so far. Don't understand what the difficulty was, studied night before the test and got the highest grade. I highly recommend Professor Dow.
He's a very smart teacher with the tendency to talk over the heads of an 1100 class. Seems pompous but knowledgeable. Study hard and do all the reading if you want a good grade, this guys tough.
He made you work but it was a good class.

Class is hard. He expects you to learn a LOT of information and doesn't give you much direction on what specifically is most important. Comes off very very very very very arrogant--so much that it makes me not stand the guy. I would pick another teacher..

He definantly expects you to learn the material he presents to you. His test are only are hard if you do not go to class or read the readings. They can be alot easier if you can obtain and old test and use it for a study guide. He was a good professor that knows what he is talking about.
While he may be a little on the strange side, hes a great guy who knows ALOT about what hes talking about.

Dow's a good professor who knows what he's talking about. When you see people complaining about not being able to take notes, he gives a lot of things that you can easily sum up in a few words. The class is pretty easy if you get into a study group with people who go everyday. His old tests can be found at any frat/sorority with similar questions.

His class was so difficult and you had to keep up with all of the reading and try to write as quickly as possible b/c I swear he could be a great auctioneer. He talks so fast so if you have any other options for a professor, TAKE THEM!
he sux!

READ THE TEXT AND GO TO CLASS! His tests are pretty hard but it all comes from lecture and the text. This class was much more difficult than I had expected. He's a smartass and wont' stand for talking in class, cell phones, or any thing besindes notes on a lap top. I suggest you find someone else as your poli sci professor!
material is quite interesting. however, although he seems like a really nice guy, tries to act too smart. doesn't realize the capacity of his audience. book should help with this.
Hard

This class was much harder than I thought it'd be. He's very easy to talk to during office hours but doesn't give you much advice on studying. I learned to read chapters and take notes on them as well. I ended up w/a B in that class luckily. This is definitely not a class you'll breeze thru unless you're a poly sci major!

Dow is not a bad teacher, especially if you keep up with the readings throughout the semester.  His tests are a little difficult, but you can get an A if you have read in a timely manner and then skim through before tests.  He can be dismissive during his office hours, though.
No Comments

Dow is not as bad as many of the people list him to be. He is extremely smart in this subject which can intimidate some people. His language is hard to follow but you get used to it after a few classes and can follow pretty well. I appreciated Dow when he was sick and we had a crappy replacement when compared to him. Overall, hes a decent teacher.

This is the hardest class ive taken in my 1 1/2 yrs at mizzou. He talks way over everybody's head and usess big words just so he can sound smart. I studied harder for this class than i have for any other class i've taken and i have a C avg on his tests. AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS IT WILL RUIN YOUR GPA! Jay Dow is the devil incarnate.
He is sooo hard and can kinda be a jerk. If you take his class, watch out for the way he words his tests...thats where he gets ya!
Horrible, Tests are very hard, they cover so much material, and you don't know whats on the test and what isn't!

Professor Dow is a great teacher. I think this has been my most interesting class this semester. Although it's a little tough, if you pay attention and read all that's on the sylabus you will do fine. Lectures are interesting and he's very intelligent. I enjoyed this class.

He's pretty random, but the class isn't that hard.  Just show up, take notes and pay attention and you can't fail...unless you're just stupid.  I've never read for the class and I'm still doing OK, just b/c of good notes.  Lecture DOES get boring, but the class overall is not too bad.
Class wouldnt be so bad if he told us what was going to be on the midterms. I hate studying 20 hrs for 50 questions and realiziing I studyied the wrong stuff...
Thinks he is funny.  And, well, he isn't.  Basically, I hate this class, and I WAS excited with it.

This guy knows a lot.  His classes are hard but its COLLEGE, do a little studying!  I was a screw off and still got a B by being interested in what he said and listening.  Just make sure to show up or you will miss a lot of info!!!!
He thinks he is hillarious, and he definitely wants everyone to fail.
He's so funny but not, but really knows what he's talking about
yeah this class or professor really is just ridiculous
AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!

I didn't think it was that bad. He just goes wayyy too fast. He doesn't get things either. People were coughing on cue today. In big groups. So he quotes Animal House. What?

His class wasn't too difficult.  He's a nice man but just an average lecturer.  I felt like he repeated the same points over and over throughout the semester and could have summed up everything in a couple weeks worth of classes. Just not a very deep thinking type of person.
Gah.                                               Just Gah. Class format doomed it from the beginning; his style doesn't help.
Worst. Professor. Ever.
I did not like his class. I did not like his readings. I did not like his lectures. I did not like him. Go figure.
mumblin', bumblin', stumblin'
This was one of the most enjoyable classes I had all semester.  Although I fell asleep a couple times it wasnt because of him.  Keep up the good job Jay. You rock!
jay dow is hotttt
"i should get started"  his microphone blow to test it out.  what is there not to love about jay dow.  i even named my chia pet after him.
A little boring, a little bland...but the class is pretty easy.  I've seen much worse.
I CANNOT stand this man. He tries to sound so intelligent.

Yikes!  What a waste of money this class was.  The material was exciting and the books well chosen, but Jay was about as unhelpful and uninsightful as he could be.  It wasn't his politcs that bothered me,  It was his seeming desdain for this students.
He talks all in jargon, trying to sound smart, and posts far too many useless notes.
o.k.
I guess I'm in the minority, but I thought his PS305 was pretty interesting.  But easy.

An overall terrible class.  He taught what he thought was important.  Even if he asked for your opinion, he really didn't want it.
Rush Limbaugh with pretensions of science.
I'm not sure I've ever known someone more arrogant for less reason than this guy.
He'll like you...as long as you share his opinions about everything.  And don't expect to get a good grade unless he likes you.

Somewhat arrogant and very obviously biased.  The course is relatively easy to get through, just not exactly enjoyable.
It's a pretty one-sided class. All his opinion, all the time.

Good professor. Not the most tech savvy and a bit slow on grading, but very willing to meet and is good at teaching the material. Very monotone voice and can be a bit dry, but lectures are useful. I didn't like the class, but not because of him. Probably the best professor you can have for this class.

Great professor! He explains things very well. Gives great review problems, just the right amount of homework, and a great formula sheet to use on all of the tests. Tone can be a bit dry in lectures but that is outweighed by how good he is at teaching the material. I would definitely take his courses again!

In a quite dry subject and class, Professor Deming makes the class tolerable and quite enjoyable. The example problems given are very similar to the ones given on the exam. He is a caring professor and will make sure you have ample resources to do well in the class.

The formula sheet allowed on all tests made this class a breeze; it tells you just about everything you could need to know. 
He was very responsive and asked for suggestions on timing and grading to make sure kids were able to do well. 
When things sometimes went wrong with the software, he was also gracious and quick to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were a little boring most of the time. Homework was never too bad. Exams were all online so they weren't bad either.

I took this during the summer of 2020. While COVID-19 is still apparent, I think that this class was well worth the studying and tests. It was a hard transition, but his Panopto lectures were detailed and he explains very well. The class was very test heavy, and he did not have any quizzes for us to learn from. Strictly online is very tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Professor Deming's two-week statistics class over Christmas break, and it was a really good decision. He is arguably the best math teacher I have ever had. I have always struggled with math, but he explains it so clearly and makes sure his students get practice with the material in class. Would definitely recommend this class if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is very good at explaining with simple and easy examples. Little bit more homeworks but they are very helpful when preparing for the exam. Overall he is amazing. I would like to take course with him again.

I took his 2-week stats class, and it was a great decision. Thought it'd be a lot of work, but it really wasn't. If you pay attention in class, do the suggested homework and the suggested practice exams, you will easily get an A (or at least a B..) He gives you a formula booklet so that you just have to know how to do the problems and not memorize.

I took the 2 week winter term with Dr. Deming and he is hands down the most helpful and clear stats teacher. I originally took the 6 week version of this class with Perkowski--it was very less than stellar. You can tell Dr. Deming actually knows how to teach stats. He gives points for attempting to do the Q correctly, even if the outcome is wrong.
He is amazing.

I would strongly encourage looking at the MU grade Dist. Demming is a WHOLE letter grade lower than some of the other stat teachers you can take. Only 50 min to complete exams and very tough homework. I would suggest Fresen or Zaniletti they consistently stay above 3.5 overall. This information IS statistically significant.

Dr. Eiffert is very respectable and a fine professor. Skip out on the textbook; I didn't open it once. Go to class for iClicker points, do the assignments on time, and make sure to check your grades. I went to the TAs a few times for grade mistakes and got the points back. Exams can be difficult or confusing sometimes.

Her lectures were engaging and easy to follow along. The content seems easy and comprehensible until you get to the exams. Why this woman insists on making the exams 10x harder than the lectures is beyond me. She grades assignments pretty harshly and takes off points for things that weren't even in the rubric. She's fine at her job.

Dr. Eiffert was such a good professor. I am not a morning person, but she was able to keep my attention and keep me engaged the whole time. The textbook is needed and matters for her assignments. IClickers are used and attendance is mandatory but she does good going over the answers. There is an opportunity for extra credit, and I suggest doing it.
She was very easy to follow and made it clear what exactly you need to know for the exam. Lots of extra credit offered.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was a good professor. I had no problems with her, and the class was fine. The class wasn't bad unless you were taking it with a hard class as I had. The exams are more difficult than the lectures in my opinion. But not a bad experience.

Dr. Effiert was an amazing professor who really cares for her students! There are a few out-of-class but clearly graded assignments. I recommend using her guided notes to take notes in lecture. Study the objectives she gives you, and you'll be golden for the tests! She records the lectures but you get attendance IClicker points by going in person.

Kristin was an awesome professor to have! I really enjoyed this class and learned a lot. I personally didn't use the textbook, so if you need to save money don't purchase it. She is very fair on grading and you just have to make an honest effort to learn the material and you'll be fine!

Dr Effiert is so nice and makes it clear that she cares about her students. This class had a lot of interesting new information but wasn't a huge source fo stress either. You don't need to use the textbook other than for like one assignment, but you should go to class cause you get iClicker points.I feel if you go to class the tests aren't that bad

Dr. Eiffert's class was pretty easy-going. You need to go to class to get the iClicker points. They help your grade tremendously. She split the exams up into 5 different ones this semester and they weren't super tricky, but you do have to study. I only used the book if I was unclear about something. she gives guided notes & records lectures.

She is a real dietitian that really knows what she is talking about. You have to come to class for the notes and if you listen to what she says and the class is easy and super interesting. The test questions go off of what we learned but if you cant apply it to simple patients youll do poorly. The assignments are fast and easy only 4 and 4 tests

The tests were very difficult for a 2000 level class, but everything else was not too hard. She is clearly passionate and knowledgeable about the content. I would highly recommend using the objectives as a study guide for the tests.

There is a lot of information covered in this class. If you study the objectives it helps. She does not go over all of the objectives during class and some things that she says you don't need to write down are in the objectives. This year she did not post any of the slides. There were two extra credit assignments. The tests are the hardest part.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super nice teacher! If you study the objectives you will do fine on exams. She really cares about her students and puts a lot of time into making sure everyone understands. I would highly recommend this professor!
As long as you go to class you should be fine. She's super nice, if you have any questions don't hesitate to ask her.

Told her I had to miss a few lectures for sports and she met with me outside of class to do a mini teaching of the lectures I was missing. Seriously the nicest person to ever exist. Sometimes goes a little too in-depth on some topics but will warn you that her tangents will not be on the exam, so you can turn your brain off a little.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Eiffert's class is quite possibly the easiest class I have taken at Mizzou so far. She hands out extra credit like candy so its almost impossible to pass. I currently have an 114% in the class and I have gotten two A's and a B- on the 3 tests so far. Easy class.
I absolutely loved her. I recommended her to all of my friends. Truly one of the most caring and best professors I have ever had
She is amazing

She is really sweet and caring! While you do get some attendance points, it does not impact your grade significantly. She literally said that if you're sick, DO NOT COME, so she cares way more about your well-being than you attending class. If she taught other classes here, I would take them again, every time.
Amazing Teacher

This class was honestly so easy if you just wrote the papers. She would give our class extra credit for just showing proof you submitted your paper to the writing center. It was super easy, definitely recommend it for an easy A.

Erin is so amazing and you can tell she genuinely cares about each student. There is no homework and you only write 4 easy papers throughout the semester. This was my easiest class and I never felt stressed about it. She also loves her cats so be prepared to see many pictures of them.
Honestly a great and easy English 1,000 teacher. She shows that she cares and understands sometimes if you aren't able to make it to class if you email her ahead of time.

Prof. Regneri is so genuine, laid-back, and overall amazing. Attendance is mandatory, but class goes by pretty fast and attendance is a bulk of your grade. Only 4 papers assigned for the entire semester.

Erin is truly one of the best professors. She really tries to get to know her students and connect with them, which is super amazing. There are three papers and a project at the end of the semester that is super fun. As long as you submit your assignments you are guaranteed an A in this class. Would 100% take a class with her again!

Professor Regneri is quite literally one of the sweetest and most caring people on the planet. She only has 4-5 real assignments, gives plenty of time to work on each paper, and is a lax grader. She cancels class often to allow students to work on the paper outside of class. However, the content of this class is similar to high school content.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Love her cats! She was an easy grader and only had 4 or 5 real assignments. Every other grade (ex. peer reviews) were for attendence and participation. Show up to class and you will get an A!!! 

(If you don't do good on the essays she offers extra credit if you use the writing center on the paper.)

As long as you try just a little bit, you will pass the class. She tries to make the class as engaging as possible with the material, and always loves to show off her pets. Lots of time givin to complete each assignment.
Erin is great for this class. She does as much as she can to make this class the least stressful thing in our lives, and to be accessible to talk to at any time. I'm so glad I chose her!

This professor was so so cool. Her class was extremely easy she was a super easy grader and there was literally no tests or homework outside of the big essays/projects which I believe there was only 4! Also Regneri is such a caring and sweet individual, I recommend her to literally anyone who needs to take English 1000!!
The most amazing teacher of my college career. She's a wonderful woman and if you have the chance to take her, I definitely suggest that you do.

Erin goes out of her way to make this class the least stressful part of your semester, and she makes an effort to make all of her student's feel welcomed and comfortable. I originally dreaded taking English 1000 because I normally feel super uncomfortable in a small class setting, but this class is the best part of my day!

She's honestly the nicest professor/person I have ever met. The class environment she creates is extremely welcoming & as a student you feel very comfortable! I love her & I've never seen anyone who didn't.
Love her, gives one on one help. Theres no reason you won't pass with a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I unfortunately cannot recommend Dr. Holberg. The only information I learned was from the textbook. The lecture slides (and overall class) were very disorganized, and it made taking notes impossible.
Dr. Holberg was very disorganized, and it made it a very difficult environment to learn. Please, take this course with a different instructor if you want to learn anything.

Her slides are extremely disorganized, and it makes her lectures are completely uncipherable. Her slides convey exactly zero of the topics in a clear and organized manner, and it made learning in this class unbearable. I got secondhand anxiety from how disorganized everything was. Would not recommend if you want to learn well.

disorganized notes and lectures, takes points off things with no explanations, not accessible outside of class/ does not respond to emails, posted our online final exam 4 days late with no change to the due date, purposely misleading test questions where one small technicality changes it from a true to false statement, got an A+ but wouldn't retake

I hated attending this class every time I had to. Towards the end of semester, I ended up just checking into iClicker from my car and going back home. It's not a hard class whatsoever, just do the homework and all the tests are super duper easy. It was the boring yapping, unrelated lectures, and unnecessary political views that bothered me.

Dr. Holberg's class is quite interesting, and I look forward to going every time. But, the tests were pretty exceptionally bad. They are all online and True/False but the wording is clunky and unclear at times. The written portions of the exams yield essentially 0 feedback which is frustrating.

Shes chill but the lectures are just basically discussions. Tests are on cavnas and you have a while to do them, can use your notes and work with other people. Its boring but go to class because you get iClicker points for being there and it can affect your grade if you skip a lot like i did LOL. Honestly just go and work on other stuff

I had 2310 with Professor Holberg, and one thing I would say is that she is very lecture-heavy, and some lectures are a bit unclear in what she is trying to teach versus what she is trying to make a discussion. Tests were very easy as they were online tests that you had a week to complete. Overall, pretty simple class, just wouldn't take it again

This class was insanely easy, anyone who got an A- or lower simply was not paying any attention at all. You get several easy extra credit options, there are plenty of easy homework completion grades, tests are easy and you can work with people on them, and they aren't even due until like 2 weeks. This was 10x easier than my high school psych.

Lectures can feel very long and boring. There's weekly homework that isn't hard, textbook is mandatory as the homework relies on it. The tests are open note but low-key difficult to understand. There is also an essay part of the test that she doesn't really provide any feedback on so it is hard to know what you did wrong.
This class was not a fun class. The professor talks and talks.

Prof. Buckingham is a fantastic professor and her Ancient Tech class was very interesting. She's very kind and open to questions and creates a homey environment in class. The civ building project and final were also great. I actually enjoyed them and looked forward to the assignments. Definitely the most fun I've ever had doing a college assignment
Worst humanities offered at Mizzou

reviews.comment: Lectures are not interesting, the test questions are very niche.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor expects you to spend 10 hours a week on this course which is actually insane for a HUMANITIES course. The class is genuinely so boring it is not even funny, essays every other week (not a writing intensive) on top of discussion posts, 10-15 lectures, textbook readings, discussion posts, and a quiz. Don'ttakethiscourseyouwillhateyourlife.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lancaster is a legendary professor. Truly an inspiring person, his lectures are always fun and he'd very passionate about his subject. If you want to learn Japanese, Lancaster is a fantastic professor.

The best class which is basically outside! Yeah, I talked to him in person during a casual dine in at a sushi place and it surprised me that he took a lot of gap years. My friend said he travels and researches because I want to study abroad in asian countries and be like him someday.

Yes, this professor is actually the best. He's funny, he's smart, he's a good teacher, if every person in the teaching field was like him I would have better classes. He never gets mad and is a father, I know his because he is actually my father, don't tell him I did this…

This professor is the best professor I've ever met. He's funny, caring and never gets loud or angry. He teaches well and is an interesting person with a lot of background. He is a dad and a husband and it clearly shows as he is gentle. Best professor.

Lancaster was my favorite professor all throughout my time at Mizzou. A genuine, caring, hilarious guy. As for classwork, put in the work and you will pass. If you get to take a class with Lancaster, I recommend it.

Lancaster is truly a stellar teacher. His work and teaching ethic are far beyond your average professor and it seems like he actually, truly cares about his students (crazy stuff!!) Always made class a joy to be in, despite the very difficult workload. I would take any class this man would teach.
super cool genuinely so much fun

Japanese is a hard subject no matter where you go, but Lancaster is a great person to study under. Clear objectives and well paced lectures, which included a lot of really funny asides that helped to remind me why I was studying the language to begin with. Very good teacher.

One of the funniest professors I've had. He came in after the original professor for indigenous religions had to go on medical leave. He's hilarious but always stays on topic and is very knowledgeable about what he is talking about. Always made the lectures interesting and made you think. Not sure if he will teach REL_ST 2300 again.
Hard classes, but great professor. Willing to restructure as needed and very funny and encouraging.

What can I say? It's Lancaster-Sensei, the man, the myth, the legend. He made our summer class asynchronous for a week to go complete in the national taekwondo Contest of Champions. Japanese will be hard. It's Japanese! But he makes it fun and will genuinely be one of your favorite instructors ever. Every class is at least 10% comedy show.

I took a semester of Japanese to fulfill some credits and also just because I have always been interested in the language, but this man made class legitimately enjoyable by relating it to other things we knew and enjoyed and was always in a very bright mood. Constantly joking around but still gets through lectures without making them confusing.

Professor Lancaster is both a great character and a great teacher. He really drills in participation to solidify that everyone understands the material, yet homework is very light (maybe 1 per week). This class was very difficult but thats how languages are. Always go to class! If you missing one class you can miss a huge section of importance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Lancaster is AMAZING hes been everywhere around the world he is also a father. I know because I have seen him bring in his daughter he is funny and a great teacher Im proud to be in his class

This guy is amazing! He has been all around the world (including Japan) and by extension knows a lot about culture, history, and religion in addition to his extensive knowledge of Japanese language. Japanese with Professor Lancaster is very easy if you just study a little outside of class (most people are too lazy to do this).

Lancaster Sensei is the most humble person Ive ever met. He will always be willing to help you out and will even remove certain bad grades if he sees that you understand. His tests are extraordinarily fair and he is always happy to see you. If you dont like him, odds are the problem is you.

Lancaster is an awesome professor. He makes the content understandable, and encourages everyone to participate in a friendly manner. The course itself is pretty challenging, so if you want to do well on tests, you'll need to put in an effort to understand the material. Overall, I was thoroughly pleased by Lancaster and found myself having fun.

Professor Lancaster is extremely passionate about Japanese. Albeit a challenging language to grasp, he's accommodating to various learning styles. He's also very approachable both in and outside of the classroom. In two semesters I never felt like I couldn't ask him for tips or further clarification on the subject---would recommend.

I've taken this man's classes for several semesters and plan on taking many more. I've only had his Japanese classes, where he acts more like a TA with lots of class participation to make sure that you understand what is going on. He's lived in Italy, Japan, China, and Alaska, so he's very worldly and speaks like seven languages.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great funny teacher, must take for Italian.
Professor Lancaster really helped me a lot when everything started to get overwhelming, especially in the second semester. I totally recommend his class for your foreign language requirements!

Calc II is very challenging, but she moves too fast and is hard to reach for help. She skips key details yet focuses on less important ones, which makes topics more confusing. She often pauses class for minor noises or side conversations. Homework is extremely difficult, leaving students more lost than helped

Calculus 2 is a very difficult class, no matter the professor. Elena has done her best to teach us what she has learned in her time at college. Given that, the averages were very low, and the class was weighted very fairly. I would see if another professor is open before signing up, but she is very knowledgeable in her field. The exams are not easy
Lectures are not good. Does not explain stuff in class at all. Very inconsistent with new material. Does not use a mic in lecture.

Not a good professor, also says that we're all doing bad and not learning because of “the acoustics in the room”. 
Seems like a nice person I guess but not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like this professor.

Frequently lectures will derail into lengthy proofs, but fear not because she makes the tests relatively easy for the variety of content covered. Test reviews are close to identical to the exams themselves, if you cover those problems and are well versed with them you will have literally zero difficulty getting triple digit scores.
She makes a lot of mistakes and goes into pointless textbook stuff, but she curves hard, so it's not that bad. Lectures aren't that useful, definitely attend recitations though.

I found her to be a very caring professor. She was always ready to help students after class and during office hours. Im not even a math or engineering major and did just fine; test curves are generous, and if you complete and understand the reviews (which are just harder versions of the test), you're golden. I promise, the class is not that scary.

A bit hard to understand sometimes and doesn't always explain things very well, but if you show up and take notes you'll for sure pass. Curves final grades very generously. Her tests are difficult, but fair. Very nice and her lectures are very straight forward
Bro, this semester you needed a 40% to pass and a 90-96 for an A. This is the free-est class you could ever take.

reviews.comment: Her exams were pretty easy if you just did the review. Her lectures aren't really needed. She is kind of hard to understand at times. I think you'd be fine just doing the homework + review to pass.

You won't do well if you aren't very active in discussion, watching YouTube videos on the topics she presents, and doing practice problems. This is a 5 credit hour class, but it should be 7.
Recitation is a far better source of learning.
actual beans

I just skipped lecture and looked at the posted slides. The smaller discussion on Tuesdays and Thursdays was most helpful to me. The tests aren't too hard.

Pretty good lectures that have a good amount of examples and practice. If you do the homework and practice problems provided in class you will do well. Test aren't too bad and you are provided a good amount of studying resources. The class is very well organized. Professor is kinda hard to understand sometimes and speaks quietly.

reviews.comment: This prof was very hard to understand during lecture but discussion really pulled into clutch in understanding the basic concepts. A tip or two about this class is to do a lot of practice problems and ask your TA, idc if you think you're being annoying but it really does help

She gets a bad rep as she isn't the best at teaching; however, her lectures are at least helpful to learn the topics. She is a fairly lenient grader and her exams are easy, but be prepared to have to teach yourself a lot of the course material as her teaching style is somewhat difficult to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She gets a lot of bad ratings but she is honestly not that bad of a professor. A lot of the time the lectures are over proofs that aren't necessary. She makes mistakes a lot when doing problems. If you follow along in class and do some studying on your own, it is definitely a manageable class anyone can do well in.

she is extremely passionate about teaching and gave really good advice about studying and preparing for the tests. calc 3 is obviously really hard, and she was not afraid to assign homework and quizzes. I  liked the workload, however, becuase it didnt give students a second to slack off and need to cram for exams. grading was fair and predictable

Very kind professor. She frequently went over class time and only showed up on time on exam days or quiz days. All of the work generally makes sense. The homework is harder than almost all the tests and quizzes, but going to class will at least mildly help you understand some concepts.

If you go to the lectures and do the homework (especially the exam review) you will do just fine in her class. Usually the exams are a step down from the review and she is not a tough grader by any means. Some lectures were proof heavy but overall the important content was communicated well

Worst professor I've had at this school by far. She was late to class nearly every day and was quite rude about note-taking. Her lectures were either extremely drawn out and pointless or far too fast for us to gain anything from them. Gave us about 10 minutes per quiz and spent the whole time harping about how easy it should've been. Awful class!
She really loves math and is super helpful in office hours! She gives ample resources to prepare for the tests and quizzes.

miserable professor. so frequently were we behind in content, even though words were pulled directly from the slides. often times found ourselves having to correct her in basic algebra. quizzes were difficult and often you were needed to stay 5-10 after class. tests are incredibly difficult, and long. i will never take another math class b/c of her

Her teaching style is disorganized and rushed despite the lecture slides being drawn straight from the textbook. Expect to be a week behind the projected schedule and for lectures to go past class time. Quizzes are always rushed as they are given out the last ten minutes of class. Expect to teach yourself everything in the textbook yourself.

Vast majority of lectures spent on proofs. Does not give quizzes or exams back (intellectual property). Quizzes and exams had the most difficult problems. Office hours are useless, as it turns into a shaming session. Extremely pedantic and overly formal. Criticizes choice of and how you write notation. Get another professor.
Her lack of enthusiasm for teaching leads to lectures that come straight from the book. She is difficult to understand, unclear in her teaching style, and grades harshly.

Late to class, lectures ran long so quizzes were always rushed. A week behind in content always. Lectures were powerpoint, did not seem to know the contents beforehand. Textbook's terrible, long+uninformative, neglects proofs. Tests were easier, hw 8% of grade. Said "Not hard you shouldnt take so long" during a difficult, rushed quiz

Just a grade F professor overall. Pretty sure she just reads off the power point slides made by Cengage and actually doesn't know what she is talking about. I had to take Calc. 2 twice because of her and history is repeating itself once more in Calc. 3. HW is a pain to do and tests are short but problems are long; makes no difference in the end.

I feel like the course material makes it impossible to teach Calc 2/3 well. It is a fast course. However, Koucherik was often stressed about keeping up with the pace. Lectures are very proof-heavy, which often goes over our heads. Be ready to teach yourself Calculus on your own. Going to TA help hours is a must.

Calc II is a very difficult class, and Elena does a great job teaching it overall. At times she seems stressed or unprepared for lecture, but she grades fairly and if you complete practice exams and reviews, you will be in good shape.

Her accent is hard to understand at first, but you get used to it. However, her style of teaching in general is unhelpful. She made algebraic mistakes VERY frequently, and didn't clearly communicate with the TA who led our recitation section. Be prepared to study and still not understand. The only saving grace is that she curves at the end.

Although lectures are sometimes difficult to understand due to rambles or her accent, it's clear she cares about teaching. As long as you're trying, she seems accessible outside of class and very willing to help. Grading on tests is fair or even generous if enough work is shown, but it's very important to do all optional review for a good grade.

Can not understand the way she and teaches the content AT ALL. The grading process is VERY harsh. She took points off of my answers even though I got them correct. I looked at what my grade would've been if she didn't count the correct answers wrong and it was an almost 20 point difference to what I did get. Also she gives no review days for exams!

This was by far the worst "learning" experience I can say that I've ever had. Where to begin...
She tells the class multiple times per lecture that "you will not be able to learn the material from coming to class, and if you feel like you understand the material you are incorrect"

you are better off teaching yourself not even joking. -100/10

reviews.comment: There is so many other great professors to choose for calc 2 at Mizzou. reviews.comment: Dr. Koucherik is a wonderful professor and lady. She really does care about her students and their success. Calculus 2 is EXTREMELY difficult, but she even says herself, if you work hard and study, she gives you all of the tools and materials you need to get an A. Some exam questions are straight from her notes, so make sure you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very strict professor. Very little room for mess ups. Goes over class periods making you late for other classes and does not fully explain topics. Convinced she has the slides memorized and just writes then on chalk board.

Amazing professor. She is so kind and understanding, but a strict grader. She always emphasizes that success in math is about hard work, and as long as you put your best effort in, she is always happy to explain the concept if you do not understand something. She is by far my favorite math professor that I've had so far.

I got locked out of a test before it started. (Online) I emailed her immediately (she said she would be checking to see if students had any issues) and she genuinely took 3 weeks to get back to me. I had already contacted my advisor before her response and was allowed to drop the course. will not respond to a single email if her life depended on it

Showed up late to class every single day. Gave 0 partial credit on exams so even if you knew the material you couldn't do well. Spent half the class period trying to figure out how to use technology and refused to work with students. Avoid at all costs.

First off this is a very difficult course. It is definitely not easy. She is a really nice person, but her accent can be difficult to understand (especially with masks), and she is horrible at technology. She really cares about her students, and offers as much feedback as possible, but really struggles with technology. Avoid if possible, but solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She was late to every single class and then sped through the lecture, nothing is recorded but her lectures are right out of the book, so don't bother writing down any of the words, just the practice problems. reviews.comment: Very unorganized, often muttering to herself while writing on the board and constantly makes mistakes. Takes attendance when she remembers to but says that attendance is mandatory. She works through problems very fast making it difficult to understand what is happening if you are writing it down or just listening.

very good professor. cares about her students and there are no surprises on exams. the class itself is extremely difficult, but she makes it much easier on the students by having a clear example of what she expects. the reviews are much harder than the exams, but still do every problem. very friendly & makes an effort to make students understand

Elena was incredible. Absolutely loved her. I hope I get her again in the future. People who complain about her simply didnt take the time outside of class to master the material. She was always available in office hours and eager to help. Shes also pretty funny. Just dont get on your phone, pay attention, and put in the work. Take it w elena

reviews.comment: Professor Koucherik taught a quite challenging class, but was very helpful and available if you had any troubles with any of the content. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is probably at the top of my list for favorite professors of all time. Amazing is the best word to describe her. Open to helping students and actually cares that you learn, very patient and enjoys teaching math. I struggled with Calc2 but she made it all the better. The quizzes and tests are very similar to the practice problems and study guide

The lectures are so slow. Which is nice for people who struggle with this class but it's really not challenging. I honestly didn't touch the homework or anything until 2 days before exams and I got an A. She gets so overwhelmed when she makes an algebra mistake. She's adorable though. Tests are straight forward.

She was always very clear about what content would be on tests and quizzes. The small amount of hw that was collected was a grade booster. Class was unnecessarily slowed by technical difficulties and algebra mistakes once in a while, but she was still able to cover a lot of the content in the semester. Consult textbook if lectures are confusing.

There's only 3 tests and all of them are only 15 questions so if you make a little mistake you're screwed. You're going to have to do ALOT of extra problems on your own. Calculus is hard, and it's even harder when your teacher is confused on the material and the english language. She's really nice, but the language barrier was difficult for me.

I had Elena for calculus 2 and absolutely loved her as a teacher i even emailed her to see if she was teaching more courses required for my major. You have to do the suggested problems and complete her reviews to succeed. She doesn't expect you to know anything she hasn't taught, but this course does require tons of self-study because its calc 2.

She is Russian so she has an accent but she is clear and easy to understand. However, she makes sooo many mistakes it can be very frustrating so you have to be patient. You'll get used to her teaching style and she'll be easy to understand. She grades tough but before every test, you get a review which makes things much easier.

Calc2 is a complicated subject, and taking the class with Elena makes it even more difficult. She makes a lot of mistakes on the board, and her accent is hard to understand at times. She also repeats the easy stuff (not the hard) 4 times before moving on. Her tests are easy, but don't take this class with her if you want to understand the material
Tests and Quizes match up pretty well with her practice problems that are assigned to study. Overall she is a fairly decent teacher.

I'm someone who already likes math a lot, so I think I enjoyed the class more than most but I found her to be very helpful.  She's intimidating but once you reach out she cares about her students and appreciates students who come to her office hours.

She is nice as a person, but not as a teacher. She makes lots lots lots of mistakes during the class. Even in her practice exams, sometimes she doesn't know how to solve the problem she wrote or doesn't give you the right answer. However, her exams are so easy, sooooo silmilar to the practice ones. As a junior she is the the long shot winner for worst professor or teacher I've ever had in my life. She makes a lot of mistakes every singe class and she's downright ridiculous. If you care about your health and stress do not take her class, Lectures have nothing to do with any assignments you will be forced to listen to her talk about her knee replacements and college days with both beginning class and end of class attendance taken at random times. Literally as bad as every other review. He has a passion for teaching this class! I always found the content to be interesting and would recommend it for anyone interested in the content! If you do not need to take this class, DO NOT! It is a very hard class for someone who is not interested in the subject at all. History majors would enjoy this more than I did for sure.

reviews.comment: 3 exams each lasting 5 hours. It is so important to show up for every class and take detailed notes as the questions on the tests directly relate to the lecture outlines he gives you. Overall a very knowledgeable and funny professor who cares a lot about what he's teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are difficult and time-consuming, but this professor is extremely knowledgable and relatable. His lectures were one of the best I heard from a history teacher, and he often sprinkled in fun examples that helped you immerse into Euro History. As long as you show up to class and take detailed notes, you should get an A or B.

Overall, Prof Frymire is a pretty good professor. His lectures are full of useful stuff and he throws in some jokes which makes it easy to engage. He worked with me on deadlines and was pretty forgivable as long as you attend class.

Class was pretty reading heavy, but overall the readings were interesting. Tests were a bit long, all together five hours, but sections can be taken at separate times. Frymire is very chill as long as you do what you are supposed to. Doesn't respond well to slackers.

5 hour exams for an intro class. Three hours to write 2 essays, hour and a half to write 5 short answers, and 30 minutes for multiple choice. I'm not saying intro classes should be blow off classes but needing to block of 5 hours of my day for an intro class is crazy. Also attendance it mandatory it's honestly just a lot so be ready

reviews.comment: Expect to read a lot and come to class prepared to discuss the material. Books are usually pretty interesting. There is one major research project that makes up most of your grade, so do not slack around on it. If you work on it throughout the semester you should be good. Just read the books, take notes, show up, and try not to procrastinate!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading, but the books are interesting and helpful. Great class and good instructor for learning about the history field. Also, always attend class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't listen to the two previous ratings for this class. Yes, he does expect you to arrive to class a lot and read a lot. However, this is a seminar-level class for history; you can't just not show up and pass. If you do show up, he will be extremely helpful in helping you become a better writer/student. He is also incredibly funny and passionate

Professor Frymire is one of my favorite Professors at Mizzou. Not only is he extremely knowledgeable on just about everything that happened in Middle Centuries, but he is also hilarious. If you are not a history person, his lectures could be a bit dry but rarely does a class go by without a ridiculous joke. Take his class, you will not regret it!
Dr. Frymire is the Elden Ring of professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Frymire has offered me some of my most positive experiences at Mizzou. He is a fantastic academic, teacher, and above all he is a wonderful person. The lectures were easy to grasp and engaging. The assignments were also reasonable for the course level, and I got great feedback on all of my assignments (shoutout to Mia Edwards, great TA).

I normally hate lecture heavy courses but Professor Frymire is one of the most knowledgeable and hilarious professors I have ever sat in class with. I will say, you will have to read a lot of historical text and it takes HOURS to do so, but he explains what parts of the text are important in easier terms to understand.

For starters, I would like to say that he is a great teacher, who really knows the subject and care a lot about it. However, I would strongly advise against taking his online classes. He took over a month to grade things, he was hard to contact, lectures were sporadic. I know he would be a great teacher in person, but avoid online.

reviews.comment: He is super funny and genuine. Do not skip this class though, he says in the syllabus that if you skip class he will not grade you leniently. You'll take about 6,000 pages of notes but he really makes the subject material interesting. If you make a good impression and he knows you care about the course, you'll get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took 4 week intensive course over the summer. Was a lot of work, but Dr. Frymire easily made it worth it. He was extremely knowledgeable, entertaining, captivating, and hilarious during lecture.

I love Professor Frymire! Being a history major, I can safely say he is a huge asset to Mizzou's History department. Although he is a busy guy and can be slow with grading, he is approachable and willing to help students understand material.
