Never gives clear instruction on labs or homework. Very easy to miss many points because the questions can be interpreted different ways.

Fang Wang's class is possibly the worst class I have taken at Mizzou. Assignments and Labs are very old and badly worded. The class needs a major update and not to use assignments given from 2013 or earlier. Technology changes quickly but her class doesn't. I honestly have gotten nothing out of her class and seems like a waste of time.

She talks so quietly during the lectures and there's not many people that show up to class as a matter of fact. The assignments are so worded weirdly and the instructions for the labs and exams don't make any sense... I had to go to office hours a lot for this class so far... It's too bad her class is required...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Alright, you can't avoid taking her class so here's what you need to do. Find someone who has already taken her class. Ask them for strategies for the exams, write as many notes as you can because she lets you use notes on the exams, and have a very good understanding of how to use the software. The assignments are easy, but the tests? BRUTAL.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly just a terrible professor, one of the worst classes I've had at Mizzou. She assigns homework due sometimes the same day, and her lectures are worthless. Prepare to do a lot of work on your own if you want any chance of passing her brutal exams (which are worth 40% of the final grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I truly wish that I could give her a 0 star. Dr. Wang is terribly hard to understand and you gain little to nothing from her lectures. The best lecture all year was done by her TA. The test are very hard and cover 5% of the material. Very hard to study for. If she didn't have quizzes everyday, you are better off staying home and teaching yourself.

Fang Wang was hard to understand with the language barrier. I do not understand the content to this day. She reads off the slides and doesn't explain much. Test are somewhat hard but similar from year to year so if you can get them from previous year it won't be too bad. The assignments are time consuming and confusing but my TA always gave me A

Worst teacher ever. Feel bad for her because of the language barrier but she is still an awful teacher. Gives ridiculously hard labs over material we barely (or never) even cover in class. We had labs in assembly language that  way surpassed even our C knowledge from the pre-req 1050. TAs are bad too and super unhelpful (except for Cody). AVOID
Avoid at all costs

I changed my major after this class! In class lectures were useless, hard to understand, and boring. You still had to attend class, since attendance points saved my grade! Online video lectures just as boring. Labs were poorly written, and "homework" was just busy work. There is midterm and a final (40% of your grade), was extremely difficult.
The worst class I have taken on campus so far

If only I knew what was going on in this class! We turned in two 100 point assignments and got a midterm assigned before any grades were handed out. I thought I was doing well until she just now graded some of the stuff and I have a C there isn't enough time for me to fix my grade. Terrible Class!

Worst class I have ever taken. She just reads from the notes so there's honestly no real teaching involved. No one else in the class even knows what they're doing. This current assignment that I'm working on includes writing in Java, which is an elective class and isn't even required for this class either. Pretty ridiculous.
Very personable, just kinda frazzled. Don't procrastinate on homework, it's a lot of reading articles and watching videos. Grading took forever. Engage with the content, come to class, easy pass imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Trust me. So much homework and stuff to do. Gets upset if you say something one way. Extra credit is available, but may not give it to you. She takes so long to grade assignments. Needs faculty review so she can restructure this course, it's a mess. Take any other class if you can, 
She is a great professor for knowledge, but a terrible facilitator
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is actually insane. There are so many discussion boards and the professor expects us to reply to every classmate and then reply AGAIN to what the classmate says to you! You will then be docked points if you don't reply to people. Which is honestly ridiculous because I am not going to wait up until 11:59 pm to see if people will respond!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just don't take this class. The assignments are ridiculous, and it's just repeating other info from lower-level classes. Up to 10-minute video assignments, handwritten citations, and no outside sources.

i loved this class but i also participated like a crazy person. you have to to be successful. she cares if you care. only complaint is the final being a group presentation that we only had 2 weeks (4 class periods) to work on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely slow grader takes literally months to grade things so you have no feed back on anything so if you do one thing wrong over and over youll know by the time the semester ends. You cant use outside resources for the papers so you have to read all the book and all the lectures instead of just quickly finding your own study to reference.

The overall course was very discussion heavy, with outside reading every week. Exams were highly specific (and quite challenging), but they were open note. Overall, the class was really boring. However, Professor Flynn Peters is a great person, and very nice, just not the most fun class. I'd take a different elective, if at all possible.

My colleagues and I refer to her as "the third grade teacher" because she treats the students like children and cares a bit too much about the trivial content. This is not a complex class and does not have enough true material to work with, yet she stretches the minimal material to create an uncomfortable learning environment.

This class was easy, but literally the most boring class you could take. If you missed more than either 4 or 5 classes (don't remember), you couldn't take the final. She probably only made attendance mandatory because she knew people wouldn't come to her boring hour and fifteen minute long lecture when you can get A's just by reading the book.

I loved Dr. Flynn-Peters! Her class requires lots of participation to be successful in. If you make sure to do her pre class materials, you will be just fine. There was a quiz, a midterm, a long paper, and a final. Those things can really impact your grade, but there are many other factors that do too. She really does care & has extra credit too.

Don't take this class unless you absolutely have to. 
Assignments = ridiculously long
Reading = mostly irrelevant 
Grading = not a tough grader, but you have to actually answer all the questions and cite things correctly every time. Takes FOREVER to grade anything. I didn't get my grades for each assignment back for 6+ weeks after submission.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is mostly based on discussion from outside reading. The reading can get overwhelming, but she is very understanding. We only had two exams in this class that were open note and a couple of short papers that had clear expectations. If you show up to class and read the assigned readings there is no reason you shouldn't end with an A.

The discussion postings are ridiculously long. The instructions she gives are overwhelming and it just makes the class hard. The material is easy but the workload she gives makes the class harder than it needs to be. It feels like a writing intensive course but its not

This professor truly cares about her students and the topic! I would recommend actually reading the material the quizzes are over, otherwise they can be hard. One project is very time consuming. Only one exam (the final). I would recommend this class. Easy A/B.

Too many overly-involved discussion postings. Essay only exams. She will leave comments that she can tell you understand the material, but then on the same assignment, will say she can't tell if you understand the material if you haven't used enough quotes from the textbook and supplemental materials. Grading makes no sense.

Dr. Flynn-Peters is passionate about the topic of this class and imparting her knowledge on future health professionals. She is very understanding of adversity that students may be facing outside of the classroom. However, she is trying to operate a flipped classroom. You can pass without putting in much work, just show up.

This class was easy imo. If you watch the lectures and read the books you'll be fine. Be sure to double check all discussion posts and papers. This class is a bit time confusing, but not difficult by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: A very passionate instructor with a very good soul. Class can be repetitive and sometimes go into tangents that are not very helpful to class material. Very, very few points and lots of work to do. If you miss 20 points over the course of the year, no more A. Grading is frustrating and be prepared for half and quarter points that dont make sense
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very engaged teacher, but some assignments are questionable and very few points in this class.

Dr. Flynn-Peters makes her class interesting! It is more of a high school size section & she requires participation from everyone to get the conversation of topics going. She is very kind and considerate. Her assignments take both time and effort! Put the time into the class and do all of the readings & attend every class- you'll learn & get an A.
I liked the class.
She is a caring person, but you need to reach out to her with your needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would never take a course with her again if I can avoid it.

Her grading system is completely unconventional and confusing. She uses multiple trick questions on every single quiz. I will have my textbook open for the quiz and I'm rereading the same paragraphs or pages repeatedly to ensure that I am answering the question correctly, but no. I'm always tricked by one word being missing, added, or rephrased.

If you want to do good in this class then you HAVE to go to lecture. There are a lot of things that make up your grade, attendance points, smartbook readings, homework, case studies, and extra credit, if you do not get a good grade on the exams. The lectures are very boring and it seems like a review. Go to class and you'll get a good grade.

While Dr. Faheem is such a nice lady, this is a class you HAVE to be active in to succeed. Exams every 3-4 weeks with tedious McGraw Hill work every week to boot. Course material is dense, almost overly so for a non-major gen-ed class. Do your due diligence and you'll pass, but it'll challenge you.

Commonly does not have any words on lecture slides and have to take notes based off what she says. She goes insanely fast while lecturing and expects you to know everything she is already teaching. Her exam reviews don't have an answer key and she puts out very little questions related to her tests.

I wasn't in this class for the first 2 weeks of school, those assignments the first 2 weeks were graded a 0 by the end. I asked her many times to open the assignment, and when she did it was open for 2 days about 4 months into the year. Missed that, then she said we'll see how it affects your grade after the final, which it did. + She reads off sli
She is super nice, but definitely go to class and get your homework done and you will do just fine in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Keeps students to the very last minute and gets upset if you pack up before she allows. She will stop talking for long periods of time either waiting for answers or for it to be completely silent in the auditorium. Claims she does not know how to explain terms and says she will review it then never does. Posts assignments last minute, not for sem.

The class itself is easy if you have a basic understanding of biology, but the professor herself is the worst part about the class. It feels like she's always in a bad mood and taking it out on us. She often yells at the students for making noise, closing laptops, but other than that the grading is pretty lenient and makes for an easy A.

This class has way too much group work for a lecture class. A lecture hall of 300+ people and she expects everyone to talk and respond back. She definitely doesn't lecture enough for the material covered, you basically have to teach yourself the material outside of class.

If you genuinely study/pay attention you'll be fine. I had a couple bad grades on exams and still ended with an A as the lecture and lab/discussion grades are combined at the end of semester + 1 exam dropped. She talks fast in lecture which can make it hard sometimes to get notes down, but overall as long as you put in the effort you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly was a huge hater on her since the tests felt pretty hard but then realized how she set up the class its easy to get a good grade. Just do somewhat decent on the test and make sure to try and do really good in lab since both grades combine.

She is very kind and clearly cares about students but lectures tend to feel rushed. She often states that students should only listen during lectures and take notes on their own time since the slides are posted. Lab doesn't correlate much with lecture and exams are based on solely lecture and homework material

I read her reviews a week before classes started and they were so daunting I tried to drop but couldn't. Turns out lecture and discussion were not bad, but lab was boring. Weekly readings and homework but it's doable. If you study and prepare for exams outside of class you'll be good. She really cares and responds quickly. It's easier than AP bio.

Everyone hates on her, but I genuinely thought she was a very kind professor. You can do well on the exams if you study, there are a certain questions that can throw you off, but with all the easy assignments/grades from lab and discussion, you can get an A.

I think she's nice, I will admit I did bad on a lot of tests. But like if you just spend time on the homework and do well in the lab you could get an A or a B+ if you just put the work in. I think it's more of an effort thing. I never went to office hours but I'm sure if you just try your best you'll do fine. Also don't memorize everything apply it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Faheem is really friendly and passionate about bio but her lectures could be improved. Going to lectures is mandatory but the lectures are only the introduction to the material, you're going to have to do a lot of studying own your own. The tests are mid-difficult, they're written weirdly so even if you know the material you might get it wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class requires a lot of outside work. The homework assignments were often long and made concepts more confusing. You will spend a lot of time teaching the content to yourself. The exams were often poorly written. I was also very frustrated with the weighting of the exams given how poorly written they were.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The test questions were not well written and you will have teach yourself a good portion of the content. Some of the homework assignments were extremely long and just made things more confusing. I also was not a fan of how grades were weighted.

I thought Dr. Faheem was very supportive and taught the class very well! She always posted lecture slides and provided test resources. Concepts were difficult, but she provided student hours and answered emails quickly. The class is very fair and even drops the lowest test score. However, you do need to put in effort to do well.
Short and sweet the lectures left you feeling lost, the tests were overly tricky, test became more of a challenge of reading than actually figuring out an answer, and over all just not a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: find a different lecture teacher
Lecture is ass

Lectures were not good. Always rushed and talks super fast. Crammed so much material into a short amount of time. Homework was simple, but a lot of reading. Be ready to study for test, but they aren't difficult. You have to teach yourself a lot, as the lectures are too fast.
Ummmm so I have an A in this class but let me tell you the sleep I lost. This was by far the most test heavy class and attendance is MANDATORY
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Faheem is a great professor. She provides a lot of resources, listens to student feedback and obviously cares about her students success. As long as you put in the work you will do well in this class.
She definitely cares, but I would never retake this class. You teach yourself everything, and she just reads off a slideshow at an insane speed during lecture ( impossible to take notes ).

Dr. Faheem is a great Professor who gives good analogy to her students and puts aside time to put them first. She is super sweet and you can tell that she cares about her students. Helps understand biology in a different way and is supportive throughout the entire course.
She's horrible

Dr. Faheem runs a “flipped” classroom, meaning you have to watch up to 3 videos twice a week every week. Homework, labs, discussions, and lectures never correlated. Entire class was very disorganized. Often times it seemed that Dr. Faheem didn't know the content super well. She also never listened to students feedback. Do not take this class.

This could be one of the worst classes mizzou offers. The time commitment is absurd, and they politicize half of the course material. 

Notice how I said “they”. She co-professes with an old German who cries about how he used to be racist in class.

Most of the grades in her class are participation, don't need to be right just get the work done and you'll get credit. With that, the amount of work she assigns is insane and tons of your time will be taken up studying and doing homework for this class. Additionally she's strict on some strange rules but nothing deal breaking.

For BIO1500. Dr. Faheem is very nice, but I do not like the way the class is structured. Lots of online work at home, and group work in class that's unhelpful. Attendance is mandatory. Lab and discussion don't relate to lab. Tests are difficult. I don't think Faheem is the problem, it's the class structure. Time consuming, unhelpful, and exhausting

I had to put A LOT of time into this class. I got an A, but basically taught myself everything. She was hard to understand and had lots of iClickers. Exams every couple of weeks made the class feel so rushed. She yelled at my class once for a C average on the exam, and was passive-aggressive towards me in emails, or didn't respond at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She responds to feedback really well and really cares about her students. There's five tests but the lowest score is dropped and she gives a lot of resources to help study. She does use Iclicker a lot so make sure to come to class. If you do that and do your homework you should be able to pass pretty easily.

Its clear she knows a lot about biology, but is not great at conveying that information in an educational setting, or sometimes it seems like she just wasn't knowledgeable about that particular topic, which can feel weird since its a introductory course. Faheem herself is fine, its the class structure that is absolutely horrible. Honestly the worst

Dr. Faheem was a pretty good teacher, especially if you are willing to put in the time and effort. She is very encouraging when it comes to providing resources for exams. She is very knowledgeable and know how to transfer that knowledge to he students. She can blunt sometimes. The inquizitive assignments required each week can take long though.
If you study hard for tests you will do well

She is super helpful one on one but her lectures are all over the place. She talks about the most random things that just don't line up with the class. Make sure to read the book (it's online) and do the extra credit she assigns. You are able to drop one exam grade, including the final. She talks very fast and can be hard to understand.

She was a very nice lady. However, all the lectures were hard to follow, and the class involved a lot of outside-of-class work. I would only take it if you have a lot of free time and were really into biology topics as a non-major.

Dr. Faheem was a great professor, and passionate about what she taught. The class took A LOT of in and out-of-class commitment. Study ALL materials she gives u to prepare for the exam or you won't score well (especially practice exams). As nerve-wracking as it is, ask questions and engage in the class. She does work with you and is understanding.

She goes through lectures quickly and is hard to understand. She cares about the students and wants people to get good grades, but is impossible for non-bio major students. Just do all the online homework and get 100% on them and do half decent on tests and you will get a B. Iclicker is required so make sure to go to class.

Professor Faheem clearly cares about the subject she is teaching, she just doesn't understand that this is not a class for bio majors. She expects us to dedicate a lot of time and effort to a class I am taking purely for the natural science credit. If you are able to make yourself care, then she is a decent lecturer and the work given isn't hard.

She talks so fast during her lectures that you almost have to just scribble down what you can and rewatch an hour+ of lecture materials on your own time. You also can't understand what she's saying half the time even when she is trying to engage with the class. There are 5 exams each one every 3 weeks with a final and 3+ assignments every week
She kind of sped through the first month or two, but people expressed this to her. She changed how she did things so she listens which is important.

Dr. Faheem was very kind and put in a lot of effort to insure we had good resources and information. Lots of tests and they are pretty difficult, so be sure to study often. Participation and attendance are very important, you really don't want to miss too many classes, or you won't know what's going on. There's a lot of course content.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class doesn't make much sense to me. I can understand the material during the lectures for the most part, but the assignments and exams are completely different questions than you would expect. I always feel unprepared for the exams no matter what.
She's super sweet

The class started with content that was difficult to understand, and homework assignments start in the first week so beware, but you get used to them quickly. She talks fast in class, but she posts slides before class and records the lectures. Attendance is required to pass and expect multiple iclickers a lecture (if you pay attention, it's easy).

I genuinely thought I was loosing my mind. It is so hard to understand her and she speeds through lectures on top of that. It is super test heavey (I think we had one every other week?) A lot of homework. The tests were always unpredictable and the study guide she gave us never matched what was on the test. You have to go to class to pass
Tests seemed nearly impossible to pass ... after studying for three weeks my friends and I still failed.
worst class everrr

Deborah Finke is clearly extremely passionate and caring about her work. Her excitement about the material is contagious and I thoroughly enjoyed lectures with her. She offers a lot of resources to meet outside of class if you're struggling or just interested in learning more. Absolutely recommend taking Intro Entomology with her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nothing but positives for Dr.Finke. She is one of the most caring professors i've had at Mizzou. Go to class and pay attention and you will do great. She gave me such an appreciated for insects!
Wonderful, wonderful instructor. It was a privilege to take her class!
As long as you do the work and come to class, you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Finke is possibly the best professor in the AG department. She is unbelievably understanding and caring. I would happily take her class again. Exam materials are obviously outlined in lectures. It would be nearly impossible to fail her classes.

She's a Chad.
Her class is interesting. And her tests cover things in the class but aren't hard in my opinion. She's a very nice and understanding person too. I'd recommend taking entomology with her.

Dr. Finke cares about her students and gives good lectures about the diversity of insects. I enjoyed this class because I love bugs, but to others it can become boring or a lot to remember if you aren't engaged. Our big projects were a Pest Presentation and a Digital Insect Collection that should not be put off. I recommend her class!
Insect Pest Management was a great course. Dr. Finke explained all concepts and offered great guidance for exams and quizzes. I thoroughly enjoyed her class.

This is a difficult class but it would be difficult with any professor. In my opinion Dr. Fritschi is a very knowledgable instructor who has great lecture slides and is genuinely interesting to listen to. It will require studying to get an A in his class but the information is valuable and it is possible with class attendance and decent studying.
Save yourself.

The worst professor that I have had at Mizzou. Started the semester by saying in the first class “this class is really boring, I don't really like teaching it”. The most monotone person I have ever heard speak. Took two months a piece to grade the first tests. Didn't grade the quizzes for at least a month as well. Didn't respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: each persons test is different- different questions for each person. they aren't different orders but different questions. stupid hard
So disorganized and can barely hear her talk in lectures
No technology allowed, sped through notes during lecture which has no definitions of any terms, reads off a script, canvas page has no grades or dates. Very disorganized. Save yourself

She doesn't allow technology in lectures, making note-taking harder. Her Canvas page is disorganized, with no clear due dates and grades split across 2 different Canvas pages, so it's difficult to track progress. Staying organized is challenging. I recommend choosing a different professor if possible.

Not 4353 (it's 3326) but great professor. Extremely difficult class with very little room for error. I wish the quizzes could be padded by having other graded assignments. If you bomb one exam or 2 quizzes, your grade is toast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have taken multiple classes with KG and she is definitely one of my favorite professors! She is super easy to talk to and extremely helpful. She does a great job explaining the topics and gives out many practice problems with clear explanations. She is the best!
This lady is truly evil.

Had an A all the way up to the end of my sophomore year last year. I had to go home as my brother was in a terrible accident. I told Kari during office hours and explained the situation, asking if I could take the final exam THREE days later. She said no, accused me of faking it, and showed no sympathy. Was penalized for late exam resulting in a B-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very helpful to read the textbook and do EVERY practice problem (of which there were many). She is really great at explaining concepts and has clear criteria and focuses on grading things quick and being fair. Tests took a lot of prep, but the material was covered in class well.

Prof. Gingrich was one of the best teachers I had at Mizzou. I failed Accounting 1 so I had to take that again and received another poor grade on it. But then Accounting 2 was so easy if you just go to lecture. Trust me, do not miss a lecture.

Decent professor. GO TO LECTURE. Also lab is not mandatory but I suggest you go. She does a pretty good job of getting the content across but the content is boring as all get out and the lectures are a drag.

Kari is an amazing teacher. The class is set up for your success. She lectures at a good pace and is engaging. Lab is optional (you can either do the assignment with your TA in lab or alone at home) and once an exam she gives extra credit for lab attendance. Kari is by far my favorite prof I have had and her class is well planned and thought out.

Gingrich did a good job of giving students every opportunity to succeed in this class. She explained the content well and gave the on your own problems as well as practice tests which were great for studying. I think that some of these reviews were a bit harsh, the class really doesn't take much effort to do well in and was easier than 2036.

I really wanted to give her a good score, and maybe the outcome was purely my fault, but I feel like the lectures and labs did not set me up for success. I was in the top 10 percent of the class in Accounting 1 which is supposedly harder, and I struggled in this class. Do not skip lecture, you will need it.

Her lectures are slow which I don't mind. Extra credit really isn't worth much in this class. Exams could be pretty difficult and unclear on how to study. Easier then accounting 1 but not much easier.

Great professor, but goes through the notes very slowly which bored me sometimes. Very easy class, going to Friday lab is not mandatory which is a plus, although she gives a couple extra credit points throughout the semester for going to lab and lecture. She has video lectures from the past in case you miss, and a notes sheet on the test is a plus!

Tries to dumb everything down but too extreme. Problems seem simple in the workbook but then more difficult on exams and something we've never practiced before. Doesnt release how to solve the practice exam questions.Extra credit throughout the semester in lectures. Gives us opportunity on the final to make up something we missed on previous exams.

Professor Gingrich is a diamond of a professor. She is always there to listen and help when you need it even though you have several TA's. She is someone who wants to see you succeed in life and is a very caring individual. I would recommend anyone to take class with Professor Gingrich.

This class was really not hard at all. Show up to class and follow along with her and you should not have any problems. Going to lab is also really helpful. Study what you get from lab and in class worksheets. Gingrich provides many opportunities to help you succeed in her class, even quite a few extra credit points.

If you don't go to class don't expect to get a good grade. Plain and simple, you will get lost if you don't attend lecture. Also, the friday discussions often give out extra credit. The class has three main tests, each allows a cheat sheet. Make sure to make you cheat sheet amazing, this is how to do well on the tests.

Gingrich explained subjects well but what made the class a lot easier was lab. I missed over half the lectures for the section 2 but I went to every lab and I ended up getting a 94 on the exam. Attendance isn't mandatory but it's a lot easier to understand the concepts if you go, if not you will just have to study a lot more when exam time comes.

Super easy class. Attendance is not mandatory, but you wont pass the class if you dont go to lecture but other than that there isnt a ton of homework, tests are straightforward, and she curves a lot and has extra credit throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super easy class so far. All you have to do is show up and take the notes in your notebook that she gives you. The multiple-choice questions on the exams are always not known before, but the write out questions (a majority of the test) are the same questions from your notes with a different prompt. Super easy, currently have a 99%.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kari is the WORST. She doesn't know what she's talking about. Don't take her class!

Super fun class, if you're scared because of your experience with chemistry don't be, it so much better. Furrer is a really engaging professor brings in real world problems to keep students engaged. There is opportunities for extra credit which is helpful. Of course the doggies and candy is a huge plus!!

Dr. Furrer is extremely passionate about teaching which made Micro2800 so much fun for me. I'm not usually someone who enjoys science, but Micro was easily my favorite class this semester. a true king

Dr. Furrer WANTS his students to be successful!! I have never had a professor who was as caring and respected in their field as he is! You can tell how much he cares on the topics he teaches as well as your performance in the course.
Love him and the way he teaches
Dr. Furrer has been my favorite professor so far. I would take his class 100 times over

The best there was whoever did it.

Dr. Furrer is an incredible professor who genuinely cares about student success. While the class requires effort, the content is fascinating and useful. unstuckstudy was a game-changer for my exam prep.

Amazing professor who makes learning fun!! His dogs Luna & Chewy make lab more enjoyable too!!!

Dr. Furrer is the best college professor I've ever had. He has such a deep passion for microbiology which shows in his lectures and motivates you to learn more. He is such a great professor who really cares about your success. Always tells you you're going to do good and encourages you. Definitely go to lecture and lab, very helpful. I LOVE DR.FURRER!

Loved this class and his flipped style!

I wish that you could select more than 3 for the tags. This has been by far the best class I have taken in all three years at Mizzou. I cannot say enough good things about Dr.Furrer.

Literally the best professor/teacher I've ever had in my life! He is so passionate about what he does and he wants everyone to succeed. He's great at making class fun and interesting. Dr. Furrer is great! You can tell he is passionate about the subject and wants you to learn as much as possible.

Absolutely loved this class, and I wish Dr. Furrer was my professor for every class. He cares so much, and I learned SO much! Favorite class so far for sure. Absolute favorite professor - he is super passionate and truly cares about the subject, the medical field, and his students. By far my favorite professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and makes the lecture material make sense. I wish I could take this course again

LITERALLY THE BEST TEACHER/PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD IN MY LIFE. He genuinely cares so much about his students, and is a fantastic teacher. I learned so much in micro 2800 from him, I wish I could retake the course. 10/10 would recommend

he didnt necessarily require you to attend class, but to understand the material it was vital that you attend class. he is good at explaining things in a way that is easy to understand them and he makes the lectures interesting and related to nursing.
