He has a whole team of TA's, but they are slow graders and unresponsive. His lectures wont prepare you for exams, but he'll waste time talking about bridges or his research.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If he could lecture with half of the passion, knowledge, and organization he has on his love for bridges he'd be amazing but he genuinely cannot teach/lecture. 90% of the work is busy work AND WILL NOT HELP ON THE EXAMS. I'll give him credit however for being able to speak English unlike 99% of Engineering Professors here

I hate this class! The professor doesn't know how to lecture, and doesn't even know what's going on ever, the TA's run everything. Lots of busywork homework that takes a lot of credit off if you get small things wrong in the algebra, and there's 90% algebra with 10% actual work. I would love to drop but it's required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Although this class is not too hard, it requires a lot of time spent studying outside of class. Lectures are virtually pointless to go to, but also required. Jeff Hanson on YouTube is an amazing resource that I used the entire semester and helped A LOT. Exams are fairly easy and get curved/graded very leniently if everyone does the poorly.

Washer just so clearly doesn't care about this class at all. Also the grading was all over the place. I would make one very tiny mistake and lost 9 points then mess the entire problem up and lose 5 points. The terrible and nonsensical grading ended up being to my benefit overall though.
No choice but to have him as your professor. He's the Keller for mechanical and civil engineering. Good luck.

If you did well in statics you will be fine in this class. There are so many online resources and ways to do well that you cannot blame the professor if you're failing. My only complaint is that it would take about 3 weeks to receive exams grades back.

The class was very disorganized, and the lectures were hard to follow. Dr Washer was not very good at explaining complex concepts, and the test questions were much harder than the examples he gave us. He actively tells students not to reach out to him, and his TAs run the whole class. Exams take forever to grade. Class needs to be restructured.

This class was disorganized, overloaded, and poorly paced. The TAs handled almost everything, grading was slow, and examples were too simple compared to the homework. The exams were too long for the time given and I had to teach myself the material to do well. This course needs major restructuring, especially considering how many people dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Glen Washer spends too much time in class ranting about bridges instead of really teaching at all. The textbook is well written so get ready to read, you won't get much out of him. Everything is doable with the textbook, though lectures aren't much help. Overall Dr. Washer seems annoyed to be here, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Washer's a very sweet guy but not great teacher. Way too much HW. Lectures have lots of pop-quizzes and oftentimes felt like wastes of time with tangents completely unrelated to the material itself being a common occurrence. Test grades took longer to come back than any other class I've ever taken despite the army of TAs the class has.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The steel class was difficult unless you had the steel manual. While you don't have to buy the $150 book, the class is significantly better if you do. He teaches pretty much straight from the book and his practice problems rely on using formulas that are not common sense.

Washer is a chill dude but doesn't really care how students do in his class.Tests take about a month to grade and are graded by the TAs. Get ready to do about 3-4 hours of homework a week. He's not very good at explaining problems during class. Getting through his class is a big accomplishment. Strengths and Materials is not an easy class. Lock in.

The professor is horrible and the class is torture, but you know that already. The TAs were nice and curved several exams including the final by 5 percent each, even though the professor said there was no curving (shows how little he's involved).  There was multiple typos or missing info on nearly every exam and no extra time was given… good luck

Dr. Washer is one of the worst professors I've had so far in engineering. His lectures are long and boring, and have little to do with the exam problems. He rambles about bridges 90% of the time. You still have to go to class however, as attendance is mandatory (iClicker). His army of TAs take a while to grade exams— and the grading is very harsh.

My biggest issue with the professor is that he doesn't write his exams which makes up most of the grade. The exams are made by his TA's and he claims he trusts his TA's. He isn't there when the tests are being taken either.

He just talks as if we can peer into his mind. Pulls variables out of thin air and formulae that he has never talked about before. Having him elaborate is just a similar mess. There is nothing you can understand because he is not a teacher, he's just a good student. He thinks we all have a background in it and has no ability to teach.

Took this class as an 8 week online summer course. While Washer is professor for this class, it is ran entirely by the TA. With this being an 8 week course its extremely fast paced. There are 4 proctored exams worth 70% of your grade. The exams are difficult but resemble the past exam problems he posts on canvas. If you study you will be okay!

i purposely stopped wearing my seatbelt  because of this class. glen himself hasnt known what hes talking about since roughly 1995. he cant even get his own test questions right. he is a sad excuse for a professor. many of my friends have quit the program as the whole strictly due to how horrible this "professor" is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Washer is nice, but this class was awful. TAs are nice but grade the exams horribly. I've never had an exam regraded before, but I've had each one regraded in this class. MC on exams are 5 points each. There are random pop quizzes in lecture. SO MUCH homework & reading quizzes every week & each time you put the wrong answer, it takes off points.
Dr. Washer teaches a very difficult class, and part of that is due to the class material itself. As for the other part, Dr. Washer can be a little difficult to talk to if you have issues in class.

. Washer is a nice guy, but terrible of teaching this class. He knows what he is doing, but the lectures are dreadful. his test does not line up with the lecture. Test problems comes directly from the homework. There is an overwhelming amount of homework. Be prepared to spend 2 hours doing homework. Exams take forever to grade. He does not curve!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I have never had a professor who so clearly does not care about their students as much as Glenn Washer. While he has a lot of experience in the industry, his lack of problem-solving skills shows when he stumbles through examples in class. He has a strong team of TA's who do 90% of the work, but the grading is EXTREMELY harsh.

Dr. Washer knows what he is talking about but is very difficult to listen to during lectures. Moves very quickly. It is very hard to contact Dr. Washer when you need to ask a question. Review sessions held by the TAs are awesome and TAs don't grade too harshly. Hardest class I've taken but if you study and go to lectures you'll do fine.

Dr. Washer was not my favorite professor to take this semester. He did not seem to care too much about the students. Neither he or his TAs answer their emails. He would get confused during lectures and create the wrong solution. Tests were very difficult to study for. Only positive was that the random in class quizzes were a guaranteed 8/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was not clear in expectations. Class was test heavy and confusing and impossible to pass. He was also very demeaning when asked a question.

Honestly a pretty cool guy, easy to work with. Good lectures, very chill, and the exams are super fairly graded (there's a hidden curve that the TAs or professor won't say). The class is not that bad if you can actually learn the material. Worst part were in class quizzes to track attendance and the online material, but Washer is the good!
The worst class I've ever taken. A test every other Monday for the entire semester. Final and tests are 85% of your grade. Good luck.
Pros: Ummm... Yeah none Cons: Everything I have never seen a professor care less about students. Not exactly sure how he has a job teaching the worlds future engineers. Goodluck.

Work load is insane. A given week had 1 exam, 2 quizzes, 2 HW assignments, 2 online lectures, 2 in person lectures, and text book reading (way too much for a 3 hour class). I truly do not think the professor could solve the entirety of a problem correctly without his guided notes. Lots of questions asked during lectures receive useless answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are just him reading off slides out of the book. If he's not reading the slides, then he's staring at the floor. He will only respond to emails that don't require him to do any work and you can always expect him to take the easy way out. Steer clear of any of the classes taught by him if you can.

Class is 3 credit hours but structured like a 5+ hour course. (1 exam+1 quiz+2 assignments+ 4-5 lectures per week). Exams are extremely difficult and no not represent any problems that you will have on homework (80% of them are on chegg though). The quiz's are given early on in the week so you are expected to know material before being lectured.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bi-Weekly exams, alongside the most homework of any class I have ever taken leads this class to be extremely time consuming.
He is a terrible professor, but thank heavens the textbook was exceptionally well written. If it weren't for the textbook, I probably would have failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is horrible. You're pretty much expected to teach yourself. The exams are ridiculous and are graded harshly. He just reads off slides and really doesn't teach you a thing. I'd give this a worse rating if I could.

Class is structured in a way that almost sets students up for failure. There are quizzes due the day after the first lecture each week, before you get a chance to finish the homework and insane amount of textbook reading to adequately understand the material in order to do good on a TIMED quiz, plus there is NOT enough time given on biweekly exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst, ever. Gave a quiz on the second day of class. Sometimes assigned multiple quizzes AND homeworks in one week. Most of the exams I did not finish in time. I would give negative rating if I could

There was a quiz on the second day of class. Exams every other week but don't expect to get your grade back for over a month. Docked points with no explanation. If I could have rated him 0/5 then I would have. Honestly worst professor I have ever had. Does not care about students at all.

Washer was the worst teacher I have ever had. He reads lecture notes from already written notes and does not care about whether or not students learn the actual material. Exams are usually problems that you have never seen before and you can expect to run out of time on all of the exams. I would never take him again.

Glen Washer was a great professor. I really enjoyed the quizzes and homeworks and believed they were great at allowing for you to understand and master the concepts. There was enough material to prepare for each exam and the exams were similar to the homework and in class problems. I would take Washer over almost all my Engineering Professors.

Absolutely awful. His lectures are barely lectures at all, just talking about random stuff. Theyre absolutely useless. Extremely difficult exams every 2 weeks. Hes also apparently rude to students in class, ignoring their questions etc. I would trust a kindergarten teacher to teach me this course more than I trust Glen. Thanks Glen.

Doesnt care about you or want you to learn. He knows everyone in the major has to take the class and it seems like his goal is to make you take it more than once. Exams every two weeks and they are all extremely difficult. Not enough time to complete them. If youre enrolled in this class, find a coping mechanism. I cry.

Took this class online during the summer. It went alright. Quizzes, multiple hw assignments, and exams every single week. The more practice problems you do, the better off you will be. This class is pretty demanding. Grading was pretty lenient and he dropped your lowest exam at least.

This course was incredibly rough. Dr. Washer looks at the floor when he lectures, and his lectures consist of problems on slides then he just flips to the answers. Nothing is really ever solved out in class. Quizzes every Friday, reading quizzes, 3+ homework assignments a week, and 3 VERY hard exams that were unreasonable. The final was fair.

He's horrible at lecturing. This class involves solving physics types of problems, yet his lectures do not consist of him actually going through and solving problems. He simply has a powerpoint of screenshots from the textbook. I stopped going to lecture and had much more success just reading the textbook (since you have to anyways for quizzes).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: At least 3 homeworks a week and a quiz every Friday and Tuesday. Test have nothing to do with the review session and study guide is miss leading. Homework and quizzes carried me in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Washer does not prepare you for exams. Get ready to hit up any and every resource outside of lecture in order to help you master each topic. Not a bad guy, but his lectures do not prepare you for the difficulty you will face on the hw, quizzes, and exams. Btw, he assigns a ridiculous amount of homework each week, so be ready.

Really tough guy. Although if you do homework before quizzes and exams, you can pass. However it is not easy to get A. He didn't explain much in class and talks really fast. Gave me really hard time mastering it all by own. Grades were all based on quizzes and exams scores. He didn't care much other than grades. No curves.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you do the homework before tests, you will do well on them. So, if you don't do the homeworks, you will fail. He shows the material ok and explains it but it's all on you pretty much to master the material through the homework.
The class isn't too difficult except sifting through the manual to find what you need. Teacher doesn't explain the greatest or thoroughly. Seems unorganized.

Can't select my course but it was LINGST 4600. Do not let these intro class ratings fool you. Once you get past 1060 he isn't all sunshine. Mysterious 95s and 96s with feedback about how amazing you are and zero insight as to why you lost points. And blunt/rude when you ask clarifying question about homework over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Gordon was amazing!!! I looked forward to his class every week. Even if you're not studying linguistics I would still recommend taking his classes because he's so engaging and funny. It's a project-heavy class, but all of the projects were fun. A lot of "turn and talk to your neighbor" in class but never had a group project, which I liked.
Matthew Gordon is a great professor who genuinely cares about his students. He is clear in explanation and lectures, as well as always being open to helping or working through problems.
He is just awesomeeee
I messed up by not doing my assignments but Prof. Gordon was super understanding about my situation and did everything he could to help me pass. Love this man.

Matthew Gordon inspired me to acquire a double-major in linguistics because his class was so much fun. He is an open-minded, kind man who cares about his students individually. I recommend all of his courses and recommend becoming his bff!! :)
He's very funny, and he loves to teach. If you want an A, there are enough resources for you to get one
the goat fr. the class is really interesting and pretty easy to follow along with if you do the (minimal) work outside of class. such a good professor i added on a linguistics major

Makes you buy the textbook (that she wrote)....and then says not to use it half of the time because there are parts that are wrong with the textbook (that she wrote). Content was not very difficult, but you need to put the work in.

Professor Ivey was amazing! She makes what may seem to be pretty complicated material at first very simple and prepares you for the tests, which aren't too hard to begin with. She'll teach you all about personal financing, and test you over pretty easy math problems. Great class!

She's a great teacher who will answer any question and help you in any way. Her class is tough if you don't study or make an effort. If you go to class and do the homework and the reviews, I guarantee you will get an A

I only took this class for my math proficiency requirement so I was surprised when I found myself enjoying it. It's a useful subject, and Dr. Ivey explains everything really well. Remember to do the online hw, I forgot half the time.

I loved her class. It was not easy, but if you pay attention and give effort, you will do well. She is very easy to talk to and her lectures are actually fun and interesting. Probably one of the best Professors I've had! Great Professor!

Extremely easy. All you have to know is formulas and apply them on tests, No definitions or terms on test. Received a 103% on most tests. Recommend this class for sure. And I wouldn't even buy the book for the class only uses one page from it and she posts it on blackboard so you can print it off. But you should definitely go to class.
Great class

Professor Ivey is a wonderful teacher who goes out of her way to help her students. She uses repetition to make sure you know how to solve the math problems. Her tests are straight forward, and the material you will learn in this class is invaluable. Great class.

Seems like a hard class, but it isn't. Dr. Ivey is down to earth and teaches you exactly what she tests you on. Extra credit available. Provides lots of homework opportunities. Be early to study sessions, they fill up quickly. One of the best (and easiest) classes I've had here.

This course is extremely demanding, with quizzes every week and multiple assignments each week. The workload felt excessive alongside other classes. It often seemed like there was little consideration for students' overall course loads. Homework did not clearly align with quizzes, making it hard to feel prepared.

Definitely a very strict, drill sergeant teaching style. From my experience, this approach works better for accounting majors. I ended up switching professors and doing so much better. During exams, rules were loudly announced the whole exam. Overall, this section felt needlessly difficult compared to other sections of the same class.

(Online FIN 4010) Assigns multiple homework's every week, even on breaks. The Exams are comprehensive, with exam 1: chptr 1-8 and last exam covering all chapters. Even for an upper level course, she makes it unnecessarily hard and wont allow cheat sheets or even scratch paper on calculation heavy quizzes. Miss one packback and your grade will tank.
Dr Griswold is one of the best professors at MU. Yes, the class is hard, but just study the workbook and review the problems and you will get a good grade.

Avoid Professor Melissa Grissald at all costs. She expects you to already know everything about finance and just reads homework answers without really going over them. Homework isn't graded, but she'll kick you out of class if you don't do it. She won't answer emails saying “That's the TA's job.” Her drill sergeant style makes the class stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most knowledgeable professor I have ever had. It is clear that Professor Griswold's life experiences have led to her abundance of knowledge in Finance. If you go to class, and watch her posted videos in Canvas, you should have no problem in this class. I liked her no electronics rule. I felt it contributed to my learning.

I've taken two classes with Griswold now, and I don't think she deserves the hate she gets. I think that she is great. Just study the workbook, and you'll get good grades on the exams. She also often tells you what to expect on the exams. It's not hard if you put in a little work.

She's abit tougher compared to most MU Business Professors, but she is 3x better than the alt. choices for FIN3000. Just do all of the homework, do the quizzes, read abit of the textbook, and average a 50% on the tests and you'll pass. You'll walk away with a solid beginner foundation for finance knowledge. I never had any trouble contacting her.

Reached out to professor multiple times and never got a response. Example, my power went out mid Exam 1 and I sent her proof and let her know that the timer ran out by the time my power came back and she didn't care. Won't allow scratch paper for writing out equations. Makes us use crappy BA II calculator. Overall awful experience. FINANCE 4010.

Mrs. Griswold is not accommodating at all to documented disabilities. If you have ADHD or any other disability, you'd best "pull yourself up by your bootstraps". Also, she talks way too much about herself and her family. I paid for this class to learn: I am really not interested in her life story or what her kids do for work. Very unprofessional.
Horrible..

Lectures are a waste of time but required. When she actually covers material it is LITERALLY NOTHING like the homeworks or quizzes. She writes her own exams, so good luck studying with the quizzes and homeworks. When she writes exams she definitely sits there with a glass of wine and her feet up trying to find the worst way to word problems.

Weekly online quizzes and homeworks aren't bad. Except the Sunday of spring break she assigned double the homework (seriously what a lame move). I've been trying to like her all year but that was the last straw for sure. The exams are hard and the study material is misleading. Lectures are absolutely pointless but you are required to attend.

She would go on tangents or go over the calendar for 40 min then expects us to know the stuff she didn't teach. Would be upset if someone left to go pee and call them out in front of the class and wouldn't give you attendance points if you were on a phone. Kicked the half the class out of her lecture for not doing optional assignment, not hw.

She is a great professor who truly wishes everyone success. The content is pretty hard, so attend lectures and try to absorb the content. She sometimes gave the class extra credit on days of low attendance, so go. I always found that having a study group helped me prepare for exams. Finance majors should pay attention because it's a great intro.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams were hard. She truly gave everyone room to succeed. She grades very fairly towards every student and is always willing to help. It was a harder class, but I would still take her again.
Thanks Professor Griswold, with your amazing teaching skills and ego, I have decided to commit suicide.

Yells at students to cover exam with hands @ Busch Aud's little baby desks. Does this to "prevent cheating" like we don't have backpacks confiscated, 2 seats apart, and 6 test versions. She is ridiculous and her way is absolute, don't email her for anything: passive-aggressive & uncompromising. Got tricked bc she was cool in 1000. NO TIME ON EXAMS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: By far one of the worst professors I ever had. She makes you use a BAII calculator for everything (horrible calculator) and you won't be able to finish your exams on time. Does not curve and blamed everyone for not doing well on her 2nd exam. Super strict for nothing and 100% thinks shes better than all her students. Ego on this woman is insane too

Spends a lot on time in class complaining about how lazy we are.I get it but I don't think she realizes that most people in the class are not finance majors and they will not be busting out their BA calcs at work IRL. Exams are insane, no one has time to finish. Due dates are changed around a lot- confusing. Shes smart but she made this class awful

Avoid if you're not a finance major. For exam 2 I talked to ~20 people and the highest score anyone had heard of on the Exam was a 50%. She hid the average grade for once & scolded us to just get better in class. No curve and it was 20% of the grade. Most work of any class at Mizzou just to learn outdated techniques. 

FIN 1000 is good with her tho

Griswold is one of the few professors I have had that actually knows what they are talking about. She has a strict way of teaching at some points but it is all with good intentions. If you show up to class, take notes, and do the homework all in an efficient manner, you will do good in this class. Also, does not tolerate any BS that goes on

Could use class time better. Don't like the flipped classroom style I wish we did more problems in class. Talked about exams in class instead of going over material for the exam. End of chapter problems are weird because you do them before class and then don't really go over them except to review answers I'd rather be taught a section and do after.

This woman is so smart and accomplished. She tells you exactly what will be on the test, how to study for it, and how she will grade it. She does use scare tactics from time to time which usually invokes many eye rolls from students, but she is truly a great teacher. If anyone hates her, it is most likely because they don't go to class or study.

A big part of grade is based on your ability to remember outdated facts from 2015 and using a handheld financial calculator. This class will not prepare you for a career in finance as the info is outdated and I assure you, not a single person on any trading desk is using their trusty baii calculator. FYI not correct course code. gg

She taught personal finance to our Graduate school. Class was tailored to post-graduate students.
Here's the deal: 
if you don't like her, you under the age of 20, have never had to handle your own money, and want your parents to do everything for you and probably sleep during class
If you are mature and care about learning, you will love her.

Idc how bad the other finance professor is, that doesn't make her a good one. If you don't read the textbook and do a ton of additional problems (which aren't for a grade) you won't pass, she doesn't actually TEACH you anything, just talks using vocab no one knows. Don't bother asking questions in class, you'll get a passive-aggressive response.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is unbelievable. Griswold talks down to students with a condescending tone that frankly, makes her sound whiny and unprofessional. On top of that, I had to take quizzes/exams while she is yelling at students to move desks in the lecture hall for the sake of "Fairness". Lastly, the TAs are worked to the bone dealing with connect homework issues.

No idea how Griswold has gotten this many good reviews. She is not a very good professor. Although she is extremely knowledgeable, she hardly teaches in class and constantly talks down on her students. Her poor TAs do just about everything for her including fixing mistakes. Be prepared to get yelled at as a class, told bad jokes, and to suffer.
Griswold is extremely smart and scary. Her class isn't too difficult and her exam averages between 75-80. Most of the content on the exams are from the book or math based questions from her book.

Yes, she assigns things to do outside of class, however it was all beneficial and helps you to do well in her class. She is an amazing teacher and very passionate about what she does. I never found the work she assigns to be overwhelming. Like any class, if you do not put in any effort, you will not get a good grade.
There is a reason she will no longer be teaching undergrads. What a terrible class. Hilarious that she probably wrote the most recent positive review.

Great person, TERRIBLE INSTRUCTOR. She clearly knows a lot, and is too knowledgeable to be teaching an intro level class. In class she constantly refers to concepts we have never heard of and expects us to know what she's talking about. She expects you to read the textbook cover to cover, while also completing all the problems in the course book.

This is my favorite class at Mizzou so far, and Dr. Griswold has been an amazing professor. Attending class, reading the online textbook, and pushing yourself are key to excelling. Dr. Griswold, an experienced entrepreneur with an inspiring backstory, teaches valuable, applicable skills. It's disappointing to me she's done teaching undergraduates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is basically a female finance bro. While she may be the least worst option, ALL finance professors at Mizzou are terrible.

By far the worst professor I have had at Mizzou. Be prepared to be called out and publicly humiliated during class. Does not explain things during lecture and expects you to do 8+ hours of homework for no credit. Expects you to know how to do homework before talking about it in class. Is not considerate of students having other classes.
You have to put in work to do well but she is a great professor and sets you up for success!

Melissa is the best professor i've ever had. She makes every lecture a fun learning environment. She is incredibly knowledgable and someone I look up to. One of those professors that you can talk to after class about anything and they will always take time to listen. She is the BEST!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Just go to class. None of the material is hard and there are 3 exams (no final during finals week). Pop quizzes occasionally but she never takes the textbook questions for a grade. I'll definitely take her for finance 3000
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I have taken. The way the class is set up, you learn a lot about current financial events and about things like mortgages and tax brackets, as well as other financial topics. Dr. Griswold was so interesting to listen to and had great financial advice.

The only professor who I've actually learned from. She tells you exactly when there will be a quiz and what will be on it. Goes back to things previously learned and makes you review in class. One time she had everyone count out loud how many people there were and then kicked out the extra people on iclicker. Curves the exams.

One group of tests were graded differently than others based off suspected cheating so she gave credit to the second group who took test and not the first. Interesting to listen to and very intelligent teacher, but she does not set you up to do well on these tests with how little she covers the test concepts. Find a different professor.

She's a great professor. One of the most prepared professors I've had. Very interesting to listen to, and likes to keep things interesting. Exams are a little intense and have a weird three-paper system to hide answers which is odd since there are 5 different exams.  would take again!

Professor likes to go on tangents. Often aggressive for no reason. Goes too fast in class. Assigns in class work/exam reviews then does not post answers or explanations. No partial credit on assignments or exams. Exams are overly difficult, not given nearly enough time to finish the exams. I would highly suggest the other professor for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She set this class up as a flipped classroom. We were required to read the chapter and know how to do things before our first class of the week. She doesn't cover everything in the lecture, just a few main points, so make sure to do your work. She is very fast in lectures and hard to keep up with sometimes. Hard to follow. Lots of quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I dont think I have ever met a teacher or professor who cares more for her students than Dr. Griswold. She is so kind and sweet, and understanding about the problems life throws at you. Shell make you work for an A, but her knowledge and wisdom of finance is second to none.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her class. She teaches you information that is useful outside of class and really challenges you to retain the material. If you go to lecture and study for exams, you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Generally inconsiderate professor, but easy to get an A in the course. Attendance required, I got singled out in front of everyone for missing a day due to family emergency. Easy class though

this guy is not it... class content is common sense though. online quizzes, mandatory attendance. fairly low maintenance class, he is just annoying that's all. not the best elective, but it's okay for a requirement if you need it
Bad professor, super easy class though.
Great professor, extremely motivational.

This class is super easy but the professor is AGGRAVATING... Attendance is mandatory so you have to sit through an entire semester of listening to him talk about absolute nonsense. No phones, no laptops, just him talking at you very loudly

He has a small amount of graded work, so make sure to do your best on the few quizzes there are. Easy A but the class was insanely boring. The content is very interesting, yet he barely taught any of it. You'll learn more about his love life than anything communication-related. For credit, this class is fine. For an elective, don't waste your time.

While the class content itself is interesting, taking it with Dr. Hales felt like a let down. He didn't appear to have much knowledge in the subject, and honestly could benefit from some constructive criticism. He tended to divert questions about the content into a motivational speech about nonsense when he wasn't sure of the answer himself.

didn't enjoy his class very much due to his teaching style. other students saying he gets off topic is very true, and classes are tough to sit through. if you just smile and nod when he talks to you, you'll do just fine. just a heads up don't take this early class in the morning - he's a yeller.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, but very boring. Lacks emotional awareness and fails to engage the class in a professional manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hales has an easier class but his class content isn't very relevant to Communication. He tends to pull up videos that have no relation to the class quite often. I will say it is an easy A though, just beware of many distractions. i'd recommend only taking this course if you need it for credit

Dr. Hales is by far the best professors I have had the pleasure to learn from. His lectures are informative, hilarious, and relevant to today's political climate. If you sign up for his online class make sure you have comfortable headphones. Please know that students who refer to him as "racist" obviously didn't pay attention to lectures.

Dr. Hales is by far the best professor I have had. His lectures are informative, hilarious, and relative to today's political climate. If you plan to take his online class make sure you have comfortable headphones. 

Side Note: Anyone who calls him a "racist" obviously didn't pay attention in class.

Dr. Hales can be "funny" sometimes, but his jokes are racist jokes that typically only one or two students laugh at. His class is insanely hard to sit through and he has a strict no laptop policy, regardless of whether or not you have disability center accommodations. His poor teaching mannerisms are disguised as "dark humor". I do not recommend.

While it's quite easy to get an A in this class, the lectures are a bit hard to sit through. He discusses offensive topics with little empathy, lacks professionalism/authority, and makes inappropriate comments towards students. Gets very distracted during lectures and is inefficient with his time. Overall quite disappointing and not worth it.

Hales is one of the most interesting people I've ever met. Some might say he's weird, and he may be an acquired taste, but he cares for his students and wants them to succeed. The class is so easy (most of it is common sense), and yes he does ramble about topics that are often strange, but most of it can be connected back to what he is teaching.

makes jokes about dep0rting students out of the country. won't teach a thing, just blabs the entire class about things that have nothing to do with the class content. if you're going to drop the course, do it early so he can't belittle you. in terms of nonverbal comm, you won't learn anything.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. You will learn absolutely NOTHING. Goes off topic the ENTIRE class, shares his political beliefs constantly. Puts empty terms up on the board with zero explanation, even when asked for clarification. He just googles random images the entire time. Waste of money. Take this class with a different prof.
Best Professor I ever had. I actually looked forward to attending his class. Super funny, but he cares about his students more than any professor at the school.

This was an easy class. Short lectures, some extra readings other than the textbook, two quizzes, and 5 tests (including final). Hales was laid back and there was no busy work. I really liked this class and the subject. It may not be everybody's cup of tea but the easiness of this class made it to where I could focus a lot more on other classes.
This class was very easy. However, some of the tests were poorly written.

Attendance is mandatory and affects your overall grade heavily. He only puts up terms on the board with little to no explanation. He goes off topic nearly the ENTIRE class and talks about random things that have no correlation to nonverbal communication. He shares his political beliefs constantly and it never has anything to do with the class.
He is the best professor ever! Whatever you do, take his class! He is so passionate and he truly cares about every student.

Seth is an amazing professor. He is passionate about the material he teaches and cares about his students. You will be challenged in his class (because it is a class where you read material in another language), but he understands that it is difficult and will help you out. He's supportive of his students, one of the best professors you can have.

Howes is a celebrity at Mizzou. I have had the pleasure of working with him for three semesters. He is a very engaging professor and always exceeds expectations. He is known for helping students with graduate school and fellowship applications with a ton of success. He genuinely cares about your wellbeing as an academic and as a professional.

Seth is honestly one of the best teachers I've ever had in my life. He is so incredibly thoughtful and really cares about his students. He's helped me through various side projects and continues to offer help as I apply to grad school in Germany. I've had him for numerous classes and loves all of them because of him. 10/10, a great guy.
Dr. Howes is an outstanding professor, I recommend his classes to everyone.

No need to attend lectures. However, labs are mandatory and there are weekly lab assignments, some of which are very long and tedious. Practice exams, which are extra credit, are close to the real ones with guides to solutions.

Huy Nguyen is very kind and friendly, and he's very knowledgeable about his field. However, he's extremely difficult to follow in lecture, and the structure of the class means that you'll spend half your week learning almost nothing. Plan for at least 10-12 hours of work per week on this class.
Most of what people complain about on here has nothing to do with him, just based on what TA you have

A lot of people complain about his lectures but he's probably one of the best engineering professors I've had. He actually likes his job and he's easy to follow.
He's also pretty chill when it comes to exams too, he gives opportunities for lots of extra credit and if you just do that then you'll know stuff for the exam.
Very long lab assignments due every week, so plan accordingly. Very long wait for grading as well.

Labs were intense and lectures didn't reflect on labs/exams. Lectures were not mandatory but labs are. You'll have to spend time outside of class to work on lab assignments, and grading was also sketchy and inconsistent (done by different TAs). Big group project at the end too, can make or break your grade. Also a fair amount of extra credit.

I hate to say it but he is really not easy to understand at all. Going to the lectures is pretty much pointless, the quizzes are online and the theory parts of the exams are open note. I feel bad for him because no one was listening during the lectures, but you really don't need to anyway.

This engineering department is a literal joke. They made a math PhD teach the first 8 weeks and then after he quit his job they through professor Nguyen in for the last 8 weeks… He taught MAE 2600 well compared to MAE 1100. His lectures were full of helpful examples. But it's a shame how disorganized and silly this MAE department is…

Lectures were borderline incomprehensible because of his teaching style, and the information presented could have been an email. The labs were helpful and understandable, but that was because of the TA's. Massive spikes in difficulty in the labs and exams seemingly out of nowhere, but came out of it knowing SolidWorks and AutoCAD very well.
this mf cannot grade an assignment in a timely manner to save his life

The spring break assignment is absurdly longer than usual, fundamentally impossible to finish in just 2 hours. Lectures serve no purpose, exam grades remain unreleased, assignments are unhelpful, graded late, and unrealistic to complete within the lab time. Lab work takes usually 4-6 hours, often 2x to 5x the scheduled lab period.

He is not good. Plain and simple. If there is ANYONE else take them instead of this guy. You can tell he's only teaching because it's required of him to continue doing his research at the university. Have more respect for yourself, you deserve better than what Huy can give you.

In 1100 the lectures are hilariously unrelated to the course material so you don't have to go. I felt that overall his grading was def reasonable but there was a LOT of work. My group got a 100% on the final project too which lowkey we def shouldn't have so don't stress it. He clearly cares too much about his research to give that class any worry.

Very strong accent and is extremely hard to understand. By first exam, no assignments were graded.  By final exam, no exams were graded and there was still a ton of work that was ungraded. Had an A in the class the whole semester, thought I was doing good. Final grade dropped to a C because he finally graded everything.

He has a strong accent and relatively confusing lecture slides, so its a little hard to fully understand the material. Really nice dude, super smart too, but the entire course was just a little confusing. Pretty lenient with late work and retakes which is nice. Labs were pretty straight forward and the lab instructors were always a great help.

Dr. Nguyen is a chiller. It's hard to understand him tbh, but he cares about how students do in his class. Dynamics is a challenging course with lots of online assessments, such as reading quizzes, concept quizzes, and additional homework/study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very slow grader, just read off lecture slides made from the textbook

Can't understand a thing this dude is saying, the lectures are entirely irrelevant to the labs, the only reason to attend them is the off chance he might have a lecture quiz on them. but the class itself is pretty easy because you learn the material from a website that you pay 80ish dollars for (SolidProfessor).

He's a nice guy and he's an easy grader. But he could not teach a monkey how to peel a banana. I couldn't learn anything from him and it sucks because he's the only professor for some classes. He's a really nice guy and you can tell he's passionate about engineering but with his accent and him just using below average slides he is not a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand, and often would teach the incorrect ways of doing things. Very understanding when it comes to turning in assignments late. Emails are basically riddles, good luck.

His lectures were very repetitive, and most students found him difficult to understand. Fortunately, all the coursework could be done on your personal laptop, and he never took attendance. Overall, his teaching style was poor, but he didn't make the class overly difficult.

MAE1100 - Intro to CAD is a joke of a class. If anyone else teaches this class, take them. Huy is so hard to understand during his lectures. Only good thing about this class is that you can do everything remotely on your laptop or PC instead of going to the labs to work on the assignments.

I took eng1100 not mae3400, it would not let me choose the correct class. Nonetheless, the class was pretty easy. As long as you do the labs and the tests you should be good. However, make sure to pay attention to the graded test review quizzes, not all of them are graded. But I missed one and it took my total grade down 8%.

Seems like an alright guy. His lectures are a great sleep-aid. If you have him for MAE 1100 you'll have a fine time. 

He is the textbook definition of MID. A true block of tofu in man form.

Professor Nguyen is my favorite professor at MIZZOU. He gives extra credit opportunities to really push you to learn the material better. I like that he was quick to grade, didn't grade too harshly, responsive, easy to follow lectures, organized, always prepared, several types of assignments to ease impact of exam grades, good exam prepping.

Nate is a great professor, and for an intro course, he does a great job of making geology interesting for everyone, even if they had no prior interest in the subject. You really don't need to worry much about your grades, as long as you try your hardest in the labs.

Dr. Hopkins is a master of his subject, unfortunately he expects you to be one as well. I studied for many hours just to get ≤90 on many exams. I'd guess that 85% of the class cheats on exams. If you are like me and do not cheat, I encourage you to attend office hours. He is, kind, helpful, funny, great lectures, studying advice, overall good prof.
Very average class. Lab section can be difficult/tedious, but exams are online so you can definitely pass if you need a science credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Nate is a great professor who cares about his students. The lectures are entertaining because of his jokes. The tests and quizzes are very hard, but because they are online and open note, it's manageable. 

The labs are interesting, but that also depends on the TA and how much you like rocks and Earth's processes.

Actual lecture was really good and this guy tried to keep lecture fun and engaging, very funny. Lab was graded very tough by the TA and felt super long. iclicker attendance mandatory. All quizzes and exams are online which is nice.

He has great lectures and very nice. However, quizzes/tests are waaay harder than lecture material. Most of the time I felt completely unprepared for the them, and despite no one else I know having any clue what they were doing either, the avg grade is somehow still incredible (which MAY have to do with the fact that tests are entirely online...)

I truly loved Dr. Hopkins. He's very engaging in his lectures and makes lots of jokes. He really cares about students if they put any effort into the class. I thought that the material was somewhat difficult but I don't like science that much. Super interesting class and a good choice to get your lab credit out of the way
I personally did not like the materials covered in his class. However, he was a very caring professor who was always willing to go the extra mile to help his students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To call Heiss an subpar professor would be a huge understatement. Lectures/discussions amount to nothing, she hands out readings she gave us weeks before, she once forgot she what lecture she gave and started the next class the EXACT same way. Students showed up when she canceled class bc she is bad at tech. She just should not be teaching anymore.

Tough grader and not really good with tech. Pretty old-school, but provides feedback on assignments. There's definitely a decent amount of work outside class but it wasn't a huge overload. Her learning process of the AP Style with weekly quizzes really helped me. In-Class Writing is worth a lot, so make sure you turn in assignments on time.

She's a very nice woman but when it comes to teaching she's just not a very good at it. She spends majority of class just reading off the assignment page that you fully have access to yourself and she goes on long tangents about nothing. I was lucky to have journalism experience going in otherwise I would've been totally lost on the assignments.

She is actually the sweetest woman ever on earth. I had her freshmen year and she still stops to talk to me as a Junior. Definitely a harder grader but she's willing to work with you to do good. If you get on her good side and are just kind to her and talk to her she will love you and she even bumped up my grade at the end of the semester!

She is very good at NOT teaching. She's very bad with technology, can't even navigate Canvas well.Very tough grader and no extra credit opportunity and no resubmission.I only remember her reminding due date and word limit for assignments.Every time I asked for help she couldn't give any useful advice.Worst professor I ever took.

Heiss is such a sweet lady! J1300 is a fairly boring class to be quite honest, but she tries to make it fun and engage with you. The class is not at all hard, and she is very willing to work with you all the way through the semester

Heiss is wonderful! If you come to this class, you WILL succeed.  All of the assignments, except for a few will all be completed during class time. She will look at each person and give them advice on how to make it better. I always got above a 90 on each assignment. Assignments are not hard, ap tests are annoying, but it's nobody's fault.

Professor Heiss has been the most amazing teacher. I can not say enough good things about her and how caring she is. She is a bit of a hard grader but that shouldn't stop you from getting a good grade in the course.

Such a sweet professor! She brought us pizza on our last day of class. Heiss values connections with her students and loves to chat! She spoke about her experiences abroad, which were interesting, so ask her about them. The workload is manageable and organized clearly. There's time in class to work on assignments, and it is discussion-based.

Professor Heiss is very sweet and knowledgeable! Her experiences outside of class proves why she is teaching in the first place. Her grading is pretty easy I would say, but make sure you turn everything in by the deadlines and really ask about instructions for assignments. Otherwise, I totally recommend taking another class with her!

She is generally friendly and kind, but not when she is grading your assignment. She seems to know a lot about journalism, but her knowledge is outdated.She does not allow resubmission and no extra credit to earn back points you lose, so if you miss an assignment or skip a class, your grade is toast, so you think twice before taking her class.

She is a good person , but not a good professor.She always welcomes you outside the class, but don't get surprised if you get a bad grade for the work you did doing your best.If you skip a few classes, your are already on her bad side.I got A teaching myself and talking to class coordinator about my grade.She is friendly though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She should not be teaching anymore honestly speaking. She does not teach or give clear instructions about assignements and plus gives you very bad grades. If you miss a class, your grade just drops. Very bad with technology, she couldn't even organize a zoom session when campus went online,my friendly advice - just avoid her class.

She shouldn't be teaching anymore. Doesn't know how to work canvas or help with instructions. basically she doesn't know whats going on at all. She doesn't set this up but the grading scale doesn't make sense: 10% for quizzes and 65% for in class writing. If you miss one in class assignment, your grade is toast and she's a very tough grader.

Shouldn't be an instructor. Won't teach or explain/clarify instructions. Uses students to teach other students. Barely able to work Canvas (I've physically watched her struggle countless times). Stayed after class once to get two grade discrepancies sorted out...took her 45 min, and she couldn't even fix both. Friendly, but you won't learn a thing

Prof. Heiss is so kind! She brought us cupcakes after Halloween. The workload is honestly not too bad, especially for being a writing intensive course. The only thing that bugs me is that I will do my assignments and get points off w/out constructive feedback. Overall, though, if you stay on top of the assignments it is an easy and manageable class

Heiss is very old school to say the least. Although I feel like she is educated when it comes to journalism, she does not always provide clear instructions. Attendance does matter heavily in this class! If you start missing classes she will call you out on it. She grades kind of tough especially towards the latter part of the semester.

Dr. Heiss is awesome. Just talk to her once and she'll remember your name and everything you talked about! It's so easy to be on her good side. She loves journalism and yes she is old fashioned but she rocks. So chill.

She is the nicest woman. I had pneumonia and other illnesses all semester, and she personally reached out to me about missing work and let me take it on her time. She is so understanding, and honestly loves what she does. There is a lot fo work but I'm pretty sure that's just the course. Awesome professor and would recommend.

I had a really special relationship with her, she was so kind. Some may say she is old-fashioned, but I don't think it is a bad thing. She is incredibly wise in the world of journalism, seeing it's evolution in real-time during massive historical events. You get what you give in this class, show her care and effort and your grade will reflect that.

She is old-fashioned and bad with technology. Her teaching methods are outdated and her lectures are rambles rarely relating to assignments. She is a very tough grader considering her poor attempts at educating us on our assignments. I wouldn't have her as a professor again. She makes attendance mandatory even though the lectures are pointless.
She is very caring and willing to help you outside of class. One of the nicest professors I have ever had, her lectures are usually interesting too.
I love her so much she is one of the nicest professors I have ever had.
A long way from Lafayette School. Very impressive.

He is an amazing professor and person overall! He is there for your success and he brings in guests to help better inform us on real life examples!! If i could have him as a professor again I totally would and recommend this class to everyone!

This course is relatively really easy! Attendance is "required" since he does random attendance check assignments, but you can sometimes predict when he is doing them and he does excuse 3 of them. His exams and lectures are easy, but he does tend to talk a lot during lectures about other topics. Overall recommend this professor though!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved him so much. Attendance is technically mandatory but he only takes attendance 16 times throughout the semester and we met 3 times a week, also some of them get dropped so missing 1 or 2 isn't a big deal. He taught almost directly from the textbook and exams were online so it was super easy to get an A. Only complaint is he talks A LOT.

Dan is an awesome professor. I encourage all to read about his background and how he currently serves the people of Columbia. This is a very people oriented class and Dan really takes the time to talk a lot about the justice system and how to understand it better...he is my favorite professor I have had at Mizzou. I had him jun/sen years.

Criminal Justice was THE easiest class I've ever taken. He teacher verbatim from the book so missing a class is no big deal. Attendance is technically mandatory but he rarely took attendance. The assignment answers were also verbatim from the book, so I barely went or studied and still did very well. He's SO boring but its worth it for the easy A.

Loved Hanneken! Only complaint is that his lectures could be shorter. He likes to talk a lottttttt. But he is a great professor who is passionate about his work. His assignments aren't worth a lot of points, but they're not difficult and he isn't a tough grader either. He took attendance almost every class.

Mr. Hanneken is very passionate about social work and criminal justice. He goes off on tangents, but they're very engaging and allow for a more human perspective. There are no tests, just 25-point quizzes, and the quizzes are online, open-book, and very easy. He takes attendance with random in-class assignments but they're only worth 3 points
this dude was honestly super cool and even though hes got these class quizzes at the end of class to check for attendance sometimes, hes super chill and funny

Professor Hanneken was very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. He always answered questions and took them all seriously. His coursework was easy to follow and understand. He posts the notes online. 10/10 would rec.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This teacher was super laid back and chill, but be prepared to read the textbook to do well on quizzes (they are online tho)

He is a super cool dude, he does tend to talk a lot about things that don't seem relevant to the material but he keeps it interesting. The class is easy, there are 4 quizzes that are open note and the homework is all easy. He does randomly do in class assignments that are taken for attendance points.
Very nice and understanding, with a caring heart.

He does random "In class assignments" 1-2 days a week and that's how he takes attendance. He is a talker so he goes off into tangents a lot and sometimes it can be really frustrating because most of it doesn't pertain to our course materials. Overall a very easy class.

Overall easy class. Hanneken cares about his students as well and that is what I liked about him. Sometimes he would go off on little tangents during class but he is fun to listen to. He brought in lots of guest speakers as well which was cool. No exams in this class, only quizzes and attendance points which was also nice.

I liked this class. It was fairly easy and Prof. Hanneken's lectures were good. He would tell anecdotes that kept class interesting, brought in guest speakers, and obviously is familiar with what he teaches. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he does do in class assignments so I always go.

He leads very interesting lectures. He has great experience in the justice/social work system, and he relates a lot of class information back to society. He brought in people from the justice system as guest speakers which really helped us understand the topics in class. Honestly a great professor and I would recommend him and this class to anyone!

He very clearly does not have training in education. His syllabus wasn't published until halfway through the semester. We would find out about big assignments 5-7 days before. Enough people would email and ask for an extension, which he would grant. He never read any of the several papers assigned. I got an A on everything. Prepare to be frustrated

Does random in class assignments. Don't need the textbook but it's helpful for quizzes and assignments. No tests, just online quizzes every few chapters. Brought in some guest speakers which were very interesting.
I took this for humanity credit and enjoyed this class. Attendance is required with random in-class assignments. The class is very easy and interesting. Be sure to attend class!

I had Professor Hanneken for SW1200 (which convinced me to become a SW major) and this course. Both courses I really enjoyed. Professor Hanneken has experience in the field that relates to the content of the classes, so he's a great resource for questions. I loved that he had us read Just Mercy and the discussions about it. Informational lectures.

Amazing professor! The class I was in had an in person lecture but he also gave a virtual option for students. First couple months went to the lectures everyday. Lectures were good, talked more about real life events and relating them to the course work. Tests and quizzes are easy if you read the book sections assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dan is great. He cancels class sometimes and his lectures don't always pertain to the material, but he is such an interesting man. I highly recommend his criminal justice course. The quizzes are super easy and open book as well as there only being one homework assignment a week which is very simple and takes about 15min to complete.

I only used the book to prepare for quizzes, they are pretty easy and all the questions from the final are from the quizzes. You have a couple one line answer in class assignments here and there to mark attendance. Hanneken is a great and passionate teacher. Definitely recommend to take this class at some point at Mizzou.
One of my favorites so far in the MSW program! You can tell he loves his job and cares about his students! Loved the content of the course!
He is so nice. 10/10. Class isn't mandatory but I'd go just because he is so nice.

this class is super easy. just show up and listen and you'll be fine. the tests are online and you can use your notes. he does exam reviews and tells you what to study and what images to know. super easy would recommend to anyone looking to pad their G.P.A

One of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Quizzes were online and quizlets were easy to find online. Attendance is taken randomly and is worth a substantial amount of points, but a few absences aren't detrimental. Projects are easy, but I wouldn't recommend putting them off until the last minute.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Easiest class I have ever taken. 10 in class quizzes worth 15% of your grade, so if you show up you get the points. 4 quizzes each worth 10%. Final worth 25% and 2 other assignments make up the rest. No homework. Would highly recommend. Material is actually somewhat interesting too.
Very entertaining but the class is pointless, you won't learn anything, and the professor goes off on random rants that do not pertain to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is an easy A and the material is actually very interesting. 10/10 would recommend. The guest speakers make it worthwhile and there are attendance points so dont skip often.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: all answers on quiz let. be resourceful. cheers. show up to class too to easy to ace with 100% if you just go.

Lectures in class were boring and were usually not relevant to the quizzes. However, there are in-class assignments to check attendance. Dan is very nice and seems to care about his students. The quizzes are online and are very easy, even without reading the book ahead of time. There are two main assignments but they are not very hard.
Tests are online.  Two projects which are kinda tedious.  Couple in class assignments, if you show up you'll get the points.  Cool teacher, laid back.

Very easy, interesting class. Dan is a nice guy who seems to genuinely want his students to succeed. Quizzes/final are online, open book, whatever. Not many points possible, but if you use your resources and go to the reviews, you will get 100%.

I loved Criminal Justice with Dan! The prof is super chill and laid back, and is hands down one of the nicest professors I've had. The quizzes and final test are online and open book, there's the occasional in class assignment, and 2 projects. Take this class, you won't regret it. It's really interesting plus it's an easy A.
Lectures can get boring and there are occasional in-class assignments. One of the easiest classes to take. He is very laid back and understanding.

I had to take this class for my major and I would hope a bus would hit me as a crossed the street on the way to her lectures. Her lectures are genuinely so pointless. She just reads off of her slides and then makes you take a mandatory attendance quiz. I know more about her personal life than I do my own best friend. Exams are rough. Good Luck!

Lecture being online was really nice, lab once a week wasn't bad. I was glad to learn excel until we got to the Macro section and then it became pointless. I wanted to learn excel, not learn how to code. Besides that, it was good.

You don't actually have a lecture to go to, but the lab is required for attendance. The first two tests are pretty easy, but the last one is hard. It's basically about nothing you've ever learned or will see again. I didn't even watch any of the lecture recording until I needed to prepare for the last exam. Overall, not too bad of a class.

Videos for 2018!!!! lmao, she doesn't even teach the class they are just old videos getting re uploaded and her office hours are always changing. I was playing prime fort in 2018 without a care in the world, so much has changed... anyway don't take this professor if you have a choice, chatgpt is 20 a month for premium and is better.
this "professor" sucksssssss so bad holy

She is nice, but not the best professor. Spends at least 15-30 minutes of each class discussing her personal life, her dojos, etc. Lectures are graded for attendance through iclicker quizzes but I personally went to about 5-6 lectures total (because they are useless) and still did very well in the class. HW is easy, the only hard exam is the last.

The class is useful in theory, but your grade depends on exams, each exam in a different format. If you're not a strong test taker, it's tough. Attendance in lecture and lab helped me pass. The last exam required memorizing code and was much harder than the practice exam.

I didn't find the class to be particularly helpful, but Professor Hockman didn't help. She wasted most of lecture talking about anything other than the course material. Professor Hockman is super sweet, but the lecture is close to pointless. She mostly rambles about stuff that we later (actually) learn in lab. Unfortunately, we have to attend lecture for attendance :( A lot of this class is very useful except for the last unit where we learn about macros (which is a coding language almost no one uses anymore)

Her lectures were usually hard to follow as she would go on about simple things like how to access the practice exam for half the class and then have to rush through course content. Lab was helpful to learn more. Exams took some preparation but not that bad if you put in the effort

Iclickers during lectures so you have to attend but they arent very difficult. I feel like I didn't learn very much from the lectures and I think I learned more doing the homework and during the lab, and the lab is held by a TA who basically just does the lab assignment for you. She said she would round A-s up to As so they don't hurt our GPA,.

This course uses the flipped classroom style. You go to class and she rambles on about pointless concepts and hardly talks about the content you were supposed to learn. Makes you learn a coding language you will never use. There are in class i clicker quizzes about very specific concepts you were supposed to read. Try and take the other professor.

Prof talks about herself constantly in lecture to the point where she can't get to key concepts because she is talking about nonsense. The course content makes it extremely hard to learn since you are basically hand held in lab, lecture, and homework, so the exams kind of feel like being thrown into water. Would learn excel better on your own.
na

I really do not have an issue with Professor Hockman herself, but the way this class is designed is not ideal for the material we are learning. You will teach yourself all of the material as the lectures seem to be pointless. You will honestly learn more from your TA.

Horrible in lectures. Only talks about herself and will go in circles on information not even needed. Usually can't finish necessary information during lecture. Only your lab TA can help but good luck with this course you'll need it.

This class doesn't prepare you well for exams, and it felt like follow the leader. Even in lab we weren't able to answer problems for ourselves. Hockman was nice and open to questions, but the class org. is poor

Lectures and labs are mandatory. She uses iclicker and waits till the very end of class to use it. You will need to use school computers. This is not an accounting course. Lectures/labs are mandatory but were boring and I didn't really learn much in them. Most of your grade is based on three exams which you have to teach yourself most of the content. Labs are just students following along with what the TA does on the projector. I didn't really like the class content but she did seem like a nice enough person.

Very nice lady, but goes off on tangents way too often in lectures that she has made mandatory. I really only ever played games on my phone in lecture, cause labs are what helped the most. Study the simbooks, and practice the coding.
She's super nice, but the lectures are just pointless for this class. They are mandatory though :(

Nice professor, class was not that bad if you put even a little effort into it. The first two tests were easy and the last one was hard, but certainly not a nightmare. Did not like this class, the content is useful and if taken the time to study isn't an issue to pass, the prof is very bad at lecturing and talks mostly of her personal life rather than lecturing.

3 exams. Each gets much harder. Third exam you write code on a paper which was pointless. Lecture was mandatory and mostly pointless. Overall you need to study to do well.

Hockman is a nice person, but runs a bad class. She is very disrespectful to students and does not want to see student succeed. Prof Hock is really sweet and the class is not terrible except for the last exam. Labs are important, you do not want to miss them. The exams get progressively harder, with the last one being much harder than the first. Lectures are optional and really not necessary.

The TA's truly carry this class. The lab instructors walk you through everything that the lecture goes through. I didn't attend one lecture after the first one. If you aren't tech-savvy the lectures could prove useful.

reviews.comment: Spends the first 20 minutes of class telling us we will get out early, goes on a tangent, and then crams all the info into the last 30 minutes of class and says one more quick thing at least 5 times each class.

Governmental was hard to take in the summer as we didn't meet at all for class, but she was very helpful when I emailed her.  However, I would definitely recommend taking this class during the regular year as it was difficult to teach yourself from the book.

this is a hard class to go and set through but it is important to go, the TAs are good and hockman can come off as not caring but her test are fair, some questions are really easy and some are hard, do good on the excel test and the project and the homework, cause the final is just crazy hard! Dr. Herzog is an amazing lecturer and her slides are very engaging. There is a good amount of work but the assignments are not hard. Dr. Herzog doesn't take attendance, but if you miss class you will struggle on tests and assignments. Overall, her class is super interesting and well-organized.

QUEEN! Dr. Herzog is amazing and so educated on the things she's teaching. I have so much admiration for her and hope to grow into a powerful woman like her.

Super interesting class and lectures. Go to class because there are semi random activities for points. She's very knowledgable and uses relevant real life examples. I learned a lot for my personal life.

Had high expectations, but graded fairly. Tests were a little difficult, you definitely need to study.

Caring professor who is very organized and sets clear expectations. The course includes take-home quizzes and opportunities for extra credit on exams. Content speeds up towards the end of the course, which Ian discloses numerous times in the early weeks of the semester. genuinely, he was the best professor i have ever had. always willing to help with problems, his lectures are great, and the problems on quizzes/exams are difficult but always within the scope of what he has taught you- there are also usually a few bonus points on quizzes/exams. he is very witty and super nice

Aberbach is a great guy, and a great professor in general. The dude knows his stuff, and knows exactly how to lecture the material. She's awesome

Extra credit points just for filling out the scantron properly. Seriously take this class if you struggle with math like I do. You can't fail if you go to lectures.

Decent enough professor for the content, just hated how her lectures notes went up with just questions and no answers filled out. If you suck at taking in-class notes, skip this professor, she expects you to print out the slides (annoying) and prattles on while lecturing (so confusing). TAs are the only reason I got a B. Would not take again.

Confused about something in class? Don't be afraid to ask,  she will answer your questions best of her ability with no judgement!  She makes her lectures fun and provides easier ways of learning the material! I would recommend her classes to anyone! She is an amazing professor!

Go to class and you'll do fine. Extremely nice and helpful. You can tell she loves her job. I missed class a few times because I'm in a club sport and catching up was difficult for me (math isn't my strongest subject). You cover a lot of material but it's very useful for life.
Going to this class isn't necessary, it feels like a waste of time. It was always easier to just learn the material from the work book. Not super difficult.

I loved Dr. Ivey! She was awesome, I was really nervous about this class but I can see why it is mandatory for most majors. She really prepared me for real life. The assignments were pretty easy and the tests werent too bad if you just look over the given practice test! Definitely recommend her!

I'm changing my major to Financial Planning!!!! And that says a lot being an English Major!!! This woman makes learning about numbers so fun!!! She's very knowledgeable and friendly, never seen her have a bad day!

Very attentive, makes sure students know what is going on for class, ensures exam reviews happen and are available for the entire class. Make sure you do every homework assignment and pay attention in class. She drops subtle hints about what's going to be on the exams.
Very inconsiderate and rude. Does not like students asking questions because they expose her incompetence. If you have to take her joke of a course find another teacher.

Professor Ivey was awesome!  She's extremely clear and makes the class easy to understand.  Very open to comments from the class, willing to help with any and all questions, overall a nice lady and great professor.

Dr. Ivey is really nice and her lectures are easy to understand.  Class is mandatory and attendance accounts for a chunk of your final grade.  The tests are not too bad.  If you have any questions about them, she invites you to her office hours.  Nice teacher, class recommended.

this class is pretty easy if you attend the lectures. the test are not hard if you study a couple of hours before the exam. she really wants every one to do well in the class. i highly recommend her class.

Assigns a LOT of readings per week, if it wasn't for ChatGPT to summarize all of them.. idk what I'd do. 3 papers that weren't terrible, although had to write first draft in person on paper.. Was clear on what was going to be on exams. Didn't think I'd have to put in as much effort in this class compared to my other classes, but I was wrong.

Prof. Ireton is incredibly knowledgeable,he explains everything very well .He returns your paper with all mistakes identified and lets you revise it untill it's perfect so that you get the highest grade possible, which is really great.He is a good person and a good professor , plus has a good sense of humor.Totally recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback
