reviews.comment: Professor Ireton was a great professor for 2310. His lectures were engaging, and you could always tell that he was passionate about the subject matter. He always made sure to let you know what was going to be on tests and how they would be graded. We had to write 5 papers, but they were relatively short. Take this course if you need a WI credit.

Sean is a pretty cool professor. I didn't think I'd enjoy the reading selection that much cause a lot of the stuff was super old, but he made it manageable. He was also pretty good at balancing Zoom and in person teaching. He made everyone feel involved. Just do most of the reading and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: We had two professors, and he was far better than the other guy. Kept lecture interesting, even while talking about architecture. Tests were tough, but he was available for questions after class.

Worry when he doesn't make fun of you. He cares if you care. He likes writing in his style, but you can usually fight him on some of it. Generally really nice and a great professor. Would have many more classes with him if I could.
His grading will make lesser men quit. His German speaking is really standard and easy to understand.
Grades hard on the essays. Speaks easy-to-understand German and isn't afraid to re-explain things in English.
He will give you a hard time, but it is usually if he knows you can take it. He is pretty picky about writing in the way he likes best, but you can fight him on it sometimes. Generally a good class.
Very good teacher, interesting readings that weren't too hard. We went over any difficult passages in class. All tests were take home. Overall an easy class but you do learn something.
Excellent teacher. Ein Liebe aus Nichts was a difficult read, but he tried his hardest to help you understand this existential work.

I took 4580 because I really loved Dr. Gizer in 2510. He's funny and really cares about his students. The class is hard though, I would recommend it for upperclassmen because I was a sophomore and was kind of thrown in head first. However, Dr. Gizer does understand that his material isn't easy to understand, as you're reading lots of research.

He is a very nice guy and the material is interesting and easy to follow. However, exams are poorly worded and confusing. The questions differ significantly from how concepts are explained in lectures, so studying the lectures alone isn't enough—you need strong inference and interpretation skills to do well. Average on exams is usually C's or D's.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture-heavy class, attend them, read the textbook & take notes. Tests are asynchronous, so not hard to get a good grade. Difficult due to the sheer volume of info.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Gizer is engaging and creates a safe and welcoming learning environment. While lecture heavy, the exams are online and open-notes. Attendance is (kind of?) mandatory, he takes a grade for attendance on iClicker but it's not a very heavy percentage of the grade. Literally if you just show up to class and pay attention you will do great.

Loved having him as a professor and Psych2510 with him is such an easy class. The lectures can feel long sometimes, but the homework isn't difficult and the tests are all open note with one lowest test score being dropped at the end of the semester. Overall, super easy and I'd recommend this class for sure!

Dr. Gizer is very knowledgeable about psychopathology and I learned a lot from his class, but his lectures just drag on forever. He tends to spend a lot of time on each chapter because he puts in so many slides, but most of what you need for tests is from the book. Tests could be challenging, but open note and book so that makes it better.
i love this man so much, his lectures are interesting and entertaining and the homework is easy. tests are open note

Professor Gizer is not very good at lecturing, because his class is an hour and fifteen minutes its very hard to stay engaged. The tests can be difficult, so notes are important, but his slides aren't very in-depth, and you'll need to study the textbook too. On the upside, he is a very nice and approachable guy!
really nice

Dr. Gizer's PSYCH 4580 class is extremely dense and very quick-paced. Slides have limited info, making it difficult to gather any info you may have missed. Be prepared to read empirical articles for each class ranging from 10-30 pages, then be prepared to KNOW all of that information for the exams. Do NOT take if you're looking for an easy class.
Only have to attend 8 classes for credit. But the tests can be hard so make sure you at least take notes from the slides.

Dr. Gizer is very smart but is a bland lecturer. The exams were all online and there was online homework due at the end of each exam period. Pretty easy class if you are engaged during the lecture which can be hard considering it can be pretty boring. He is nice though and would be a great resource for those pursuing a career in psych (I'm not).

This class is really hard tbh. You have studies that are 20+ pages long that you have to read before each class and some have pop quizzes. Study guides are like 27 pages of questions that you need to know, and tests are 7 essay questions (only answer 5). He grades with LOTS of partial credit. Rubrics aren't easy to understand AT ALL, very confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gizer did a great job teaching this class. While there were a lot of homework assignments, I felt I learned quite a bit. He is a truly nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is a good psych class to take, as Professor Gizer keeps it interesting! He is great, and seems to care about his students. He uses an online homework program (cengage mindtap) and if you stay caught up and read the material/do the homework, you will do fine. I recommend reviewing heavy for tests as they are somewhat difficult.

He posts a lot of lectures, but I never had to watch them because I learned all of the material from the textbook and its quizzes. You get three tries at each of the reading quizzes which is nice. Tests are pretty easy if you make sure that you did all of the reading and review a little before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gizer is great & I learned a lot. His exams are pretty normal in difficultly, weren't too easy or too hard. Attendance wasn't taken but when I didn't go it reflected on my exam grade. He does online self paced textbook quizzes which helps lift your grade. They are time consuming but pretty easy. Class can get boring but topics are interesting

A little lecture heavy so it can get boring, but he's genuinely interested in the subject so it's a nice class to take. Tests are a little hard but you can make up for it with the online quizzes. If you actually put effort into studying, his exams are passable. You get to drop your lowest exam, no cumulative final. I'd recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dope professor, attendance isn't mandatory and he puts his slides on canvas. Tests were kinda tough for some reason, but you get to drop one and the rest of the assignments are all online quizzes through cengage (super easy). Super interesting learning about mental disorders and all that stuff. I totally recommend taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Gizer is very knowledgable and enthusiastic about psychology - extremely nice guy. Externalizing disorders is pretty difficult - 3 essay tests in which there are 7 essays and you choose 5 to write about. He is very leniant in grading though as long as you can show you put some effort into studying.

The material is interesting but dense, and Dr. Gizer tends to go through it quickly. The slides he posts after lecture aren't always comprehensive enough to make up for anything you might have missed in class and there's no tegrity. His tests are very difficult, but if you study hard, you can do well. For how hard the tests are, he's a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Isby's SOC 101 course through MACC, although it was not listed. She is a very intense grader, with a rubric that goes into the 100th decimal place, discussion posts 6.35/10 for example. Super late getting graded stuff back, but when it comes back late, she seems to just give full credit as a "completion" grade. would not take again.

Ashley Isby is very kind, she made sure that all of her students got exactly what the needed from the class. She's always available whenever you need her. Personally, she's been my favorite instructor i've ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES!!! She is the worst professor I have EVER had. She is the worst at getting back to students and she takes 6 months to grade assignments. On top of that, she assigns projects every single week and the instructions are not clear at all. AVOID HER CLASS AT ALL COSTS!!! If there was a 0 I would give her a 0.

Her main downsides seem to be based in organization, typos on tests are common, grades can take a while to come out, but I don't think it's because she's lazy, she definitely cares and works hard. There isn't too much homework, although there was a group project, and she is easy to contact and often willing to work with you
Stay away. Biased professor and takes forever to grade. Strict on grading and brings her political views into assignments.
i dont want to be mean lol

she had a lot of bad feedback on here and I am unsure why. I took her social inequalities class online and didn't really love my first two essay scores so i just met with her before submitting the others and she was so helpful, informative, and i ended up doing a lot better once i started doing that. just show you want to learn and she is 5/5
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like sociology and was so disappointed with this class. Isby does not know how to manage a lecture hall full of college students. She treats her classes like children, has a nonsensical participation system, and is unclear on grading criteria. Her tests are long reading quizzes riddled with errors. Sometimes in lecture we'd get through one slide.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She has a weird and time consuming attendance policy (flash cards), we never got through all of the slides in class, she makes multiple errors on tests and takes forever to grade. Shes the worst professor Ive ever had honestly. Had an A the entire semester until the final (GROUP) project where the average score was around the 75% mark.

Worst professor I've ever had. There's participation credit, which actually results in there being 25 minutes of "productive" lecture and then 25 minutes of people asking dumb questions. LOTS of readings. The readings are the only thing on the test because we don't do anything in class and the questions on the exam are very badly written.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: THIS IS THE WORST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD! I cannot express how terrible this class was. Isby expects you to read upwards of 4-5 hours a week AND retain the tiniest details from the readings on the test (which is full of grammatical errors) and the readings don't even apply to lecture content. I'm premed and this is the worst class I've ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I have had wildly different Instructors at MU, all with diff styles, but this one is by far the ABSOLUTE WORST! Very politically biased, yells at the class, has a dysfunctional way of taking participation points, assigns insane amounts of readings, gives tests with improper grammar and repeated questions, tells us to shut up &so many other probs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever. She gives her test online and you are supposed to take the test within the 24 hour window BUT she lets some people go as long as 2 weeks before they have to take the test. It's kind of unfair to those who took the time and took the exam within the 24 hours on the day the test went up. Will never her for any class again

I am a junior and have attended 2 different schools and this is the worst professor ive Had yet. If I went to class Id leave angry. She teaches bias, acts like the world owes her something, brings political views into her lectures, and doesnt know how to teach. The class is set up awfully with a group paper and off topic class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There is a ton of reading in this class, bout 50 pages a night and sometimes more. lectures are packed with information and exams are hard as well. However, if you go to her office hours and talk with her and show that you have knowledge of the information you can receive points back on your exam. She is also very passionate about her subject area.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easily the worst teacher I have ever had. She is unprofessional, yells at the class, leaves students in tears, assigns ridiculous group projects, teaches little to nothing (we could cover 1 slide with two points in an entire class), tests are basically alien from little that we do learn, seems uncaring about student feedback, tells us shut up, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Awful teacher for large classes.

Attendance is graded, otherwise no one would go to class. I finished the course with the exact same knowledge I had prior to taking it, as lectures are superficial and incredibly basic for a 3000-level class. The assignments were juvenile and a waste of time-- why she had us do financial planning in a sociology course, I'll never understand.

Long lectures. She's very passionate about WWI but I would only recommend taking this class if you have previous knowledge! Grades were based on 3 assignments so if you bomb one you're screwed. She's a decently tough grader and expects you to include material from all of the weekly assigned readings in your paper. She uploaded the textbook, no cost
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked professor Karthas, but I found her paper grading to be pretty strict. I do think that if classes had been in person her class would have been much easier and more enjoyable so I do not blame her for my struggling in her class. She is caring and a good professor I just would have liked a little more understanding when she graded things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Even though my class with Doctor Karthas hasn't finished yet I can definitely say she is my favorite person in Mizzou so far! I am an international student who judges professors very strictly, but Doctor Karthas just blows my mind with her energy, ideas, inspiration and eager to help us to do our best! Love her!:)

Karthas is extremely passionate about the course, which makes her fun to listen to. However, she is a very tough grader and expects her students to know the information forwards and backwards. If you go to class and make an effort to get to know her in office hours, she'll love you. Don't take this class if you're expecting an easy A.

I took Dr. Karthas capstone class on Interwar Paris. She is by far one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. She is so kind and it is obvious that she cares a lot about each of her students. She didn't just teach history, she encouraged discussion and taught critical thinking skills that could be applied to any study. I really enjoyed this class.
Professor Karthas is a pleasure to have for a professor. She is clear in her expectations and provides excellent feedback to her students.

She is one of the most knowledgable teachers I have ever had. That being said, she expects her students to understand the information as well as she does. Her lectures are so detailed that it is hard to get the gist of things. The French Revolution class is a lot more boring that what I read online. She is helpful in office hours though!

One of the best teachers I have ever had.  So nice and accommodating - she is genuinely passionate about her students' learning. Always willing to talk with her students and help them any way she can. Her History of the French Revolution class is one of the coolest, most interesting classes I have taken in college.

Karthas is probably the best professor I've had since I came to college. Her history of the french revolution course is extremely engaging, and you can tell she's passionate about the material. I hate missing this class, and only do so when I absolutely have to because the course is so great. I'm not a history major, but she makes me wish I was.

She is a phenomenal teacher for 17th and 18th Cent. European Thought. No textbooks were required...all readings were through BlackBoard. She is extremely flexible but grades very strictly. I loved the class and put my heart into it and got my A. Readings range from 50-100pgs a week. Material read can be difficult but that comes with the territory.

Great Professor, Probably the most flexible Professor I've ever worked with. Very helpful to students. Always give the student the benefit of the doubt and loves what she does. Not to mention, she's good looking.
She didn't require a textbook but she did provide many required readings.  Overall she's a pretty great and she's nice and easy to talk with.

Ivan is a kind/funny professor. I enjoyed having him as a professor but I didn't like this class very much because it was graded based on 3 tests and attendance. If you did bad on one test, it was hard to raise your grade. I stopped reading the super long chapters because you only had to pay attention to what he talked about in class. SO much info.

Great guy. Glad I studied abroad with him. He's the kind of coordinator available at a moment's notice, even at 3am, and will be nothing but happy he could be there for you. You will learn so much and he will advocate for you whenever I need it. Was conscientious of my accommodations and I wouldn't have felt safe doing Machu Picchu without him.

Dr. Reyna was a fantastic Spanish professor! We would read a textbook chapter, listen to a lecture about it, then have a group discussion and group presentation on that chapter's topic. Dr. Reyna is super sweet and funny; he created a safe and welcoming space to improve your Spanish-speaking skills. I highly recommend taking one of his classes!!

Profe Reyna was easily my favorite professor this past semester. He truly wants students to succeed and learn Spanish, so he offers great feedback and creates a safe space where students want to learn and don't feel pressure when they make mistakes. We had a lecture, small-group discussion, and group presentation over each topic we covered.

A good professor, but is not forgiving in terms of extraneous circumstances. You must not miss a single assignment or day in class because he WILL NOT allow you to make it up, or any of the points missed, and it will drag your grade as it did mine. Mind you, this was during COVID-19 and the absence should have been excused bc it was due to COVID.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Reyna was one of the most compassionate Spanish professors I've ever had. Despite occasionally being preachy, he was open to hearing new opinions in class. His assignments were short stories that were very entertaining and didn't even feel like homework a lot of the time. If you are entering SPAN 3420, make sure to pick one of his sections.

My FAVORITE Spanish professor! Attendance is mandatory, but he doesn't actually grade participation. Keep up with the readings for pop quizzes. Some stories are tricky, but he's very helpful in walking through and explaining what he wants you to get out of it. Fair grader, not hard to do well if you put in effort. Very sweet and funny professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Tests, quizzes and essays are open note and he lets you use your phone for a dictionary. By far the best Spanish class I've taken at Mizzou. Comprehension of the short stories we read is pretty difficult for everyone in the class, but he's really good about walking through the plot and helping you understand details about the language.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's the best professor ever!
Professor Reyna is a very intelligent man and excellent professor.  He is helpful and the class is always interesting.  I have taken three courses with Professor Reyna and I highly recommend him.

This professor is really helpful and nice! He's one of those professors who cracks jokes, but at the same time wants to be clear so that you understand everything! He wants you to learn. I love this guy, I would recommend taking his course. I'm just a bit worried about his upper level courses, but I'm sure with much effort I should be fine.
A lot of participation and effort needed to do well in this class. Its not impossible but definitely is time consuming and a LOT of studying to do well.

Ivan is awesome! A really fun guy that cares about his students. You will get to use and improve your Spanish a lot but in a fun way. Every other Friday we had a free day to talk about whatever wanted. His tests were talking tests that were pretty easy, and you got to redo your essays. He loves to talk about his life and yours in class- take him!
Best Spanish prof/teacher ever!!!!!! This guy is funny and really cares about his students learning! Seriously, everyone should take any of his classes. He's awesome.

Survey of Spanish American Lit I. All I can say is he's probably the fairest professor I've had in terms of grading. Not easy, but not impossible. Also beware: always be sure to do your reading on time - you never know when he'll hit you with a pop quiz! That's what brought my grade down. :(
AWESOME professor. Take his class if you have the chance. He's very bubbly and interested in student learning. Makes coming to class fun.
He explains things very well and seems genuinely interested in people understanding Spanish language and culture.

In 3-D materials, Ian was a great professor. The class was getting restructured and he made sure we were happy with the projects he was proposing. He was semi laid back and always made sure to check in with us during our projects. I thoroughly enjoyed having him as a professor.

I have never had a worse professor in my life. He allowed no technology in class, assigned more homework than any 4000 class ive taken and was a horrible teacher. I hope he is never allowed to "teach" aka torture students again

Just a genuine kinda guy. Could sit back and crack open a cold one with him, you know? Does he ramble? Yes. But it's about the journey, not that destination. And, boy, did we go on a journey! Shout out to my man!

He does IClicker and questions throughout class. There are itnquizitives due twice a week but they are pretty easy. His tests are multiple choice. My only complaint is that he doesn't allow technology in class. He does have field trips though to art studios on campus and guest lecturers.
Lectures are hard to sit through. Make sure to attend class as 5% of overall grade will be deducted after 5 absences, sick or otherwise. No study guides and tests are hard to prep for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Intro to visual arts was unorganized from the start to finish. Lectures were very hard to sit through as they seemed to not get to the point. The iclicker questions were said to be the questions on the exams, but many questions were not or not even out of the textbook itself.

Class was always disorganized & Ian would ramble the entire time. It's difficult to study for the exams as he rambles the entire class period & doesn't provide a helpful study guide. You can study your homework & iClicker questions but you're still going into the exam blind. He provides lecture notes, but then doesn't cover what's on the notes.

He covers a lot of interesting topics like AI and cybersecurity. Tests are challenging but he has prep sessions beforehand and lets you use a sheet of notes during exams. You can also earn the right to drop a low exam if you complete enough optional assignments.

Class covers a lot of ground but his exam prep guides and pre-exam classes are useful. The assignments are optional but if you complete enough of them you earn incentives that help your grade. He worked in business before teaching and is really knowledgeable.

Personal opinion:

Quiet.
Nice guy.
Unhurried energy.
Voice made for nighttime audiobooks.

This class is structured super easily. All of your grade is based on exams, but you can do extra 'power-up assignments' to boost your final grade. You get a cheat sheet, and the tests are fairly easy.

He has a "reward system" of sorts through extra assignments that can help boost your grade - the course grade is based on exams. The exams are not difficult and you get a cheat sheet for each of them. Attendance is not mandatory and he posts lecture recordings but attendance does add up through the reward system.

He is a really good professor and gives a lot of opportunities to do extra assignments for power ups but they only affect your grade if you get a certain amount of points. No homework, all tests. He seems very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches.
He is awesome! Not a hard class at all.

Pelikan is a kind person but doesn't have an engaging class. The class is 400 people, but only about 100 people show up for class because attendance doesn't count. Tests are the only grades in the class, but a point system allows you to drop exams, get extra credit, etc. The points come from attendance, optional projects, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pelikan is incredibly knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about what he teaches, which makes me even more eager to learn. Out of all my classes this semester, his has been the one where I feel I've retained the most information. The topics we cover are super relevant to what's happening in the world right now.

Very flexible and understanding. Class is only graded by 4 exams, but you get a double-sided notes sheet and it's not super difficult content. There is a thing called Power-up Points where you can complete a certain number of assignments and get an exam dropped or an automatic 100% on the final (or both) if you get enough points.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Nice guy. Worked in business. Gave good advice.

Do not ever attend M3300's Lectures. Jack Pelikan is quiet and does not take command of the class at all. 100% of the grade for this class is based off of the 4 exams throughout the semester and they are rather easy.

Several lectures were certainly controversial with several opinionated points that could be found offensive given the seeming lack of evidence to them. Other than that the content of the class was beyond simple and easy, hardly relating to appropriate college journalism at some points.

Professor Porter is very passionate about the topics she teaches, and her lectures are very entertaining. The class is heavy on readings, but they don't matter a ton. Quizzes and tests are pretty easy and it's mandatory attendance twice a week (she will ask a question in class and you will answer it on Canvas).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Porter's lectures are very fun to attend and she brings in a variety of high valued guest speakers. The weekly quizzes are easy if you pay attention in class.

Professor Porter is very intelligent, but I feel the class was incredibly heavy on readings and videos. This typically wouldn't be an issue, but for a student taking 17 credit hours, I didn't always have time for a two hour podcast. Aside from this, Porter is an excellent lecturer and also had compelling guest speakers in class.

By far the easiest journalism class and professor I've had at Mizzou. Although she said things that were questionable at times, she is knowledgable and very kind. Attendance is mandatory, but as long as you show up and do the weekly quizzes this is an easy A.

Professor Porter was great! The class would be better as a smaller class, and the readings were many, but I loved her energy. Professor Porter did a great job handling the difficult task of explaining her lived experience and getting people who can explain what she hasn't experienced and handled people speaking without thinking with grace.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Porter did her best to manage a class with a difficult structure. We had a huge lecture hall with little opportunities to discuss nuanced topics, so discussion usually fell to particularly vocal and often bigoted voices.  Dr. Porter is very intelligent and assigns valuable readings and other materials.

This class was really important but Porter does rely heavy on outside reading and videos. I know she created and found the material but I don't think she was the one that taught the class. She was an easy grader on most things IF you give in-depth answers. The more thoughtful and in-depth you are, the better you'll do on weekly quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: gupta accent.

Had him for a lab and discussion last semester and he was absolutely horrific at explaining anything. He hasn't even taught a course yet (only TA), so not sure how others have formed an opinion on his teaching (hint: they haven't). He tried, but his English was almost impossible to understand and in lab everyone was confused constantly.

Professor Jayswal was very good at explaining the material thoroughly and giving real world examples to help describe the physics formulas. He helped to solidify the course material by applying it to the problems we had the most trouble with.
His lab sections were informative and he gave good feedback. He was also available to answer any questions about the course and was very helpful.

The course was a little tough at expected periods. As such, this instructor walked through step by step both a universally used and personal approach in his lessons. Making the example problems easy to process and learn. He is also really kind and talked to students personally when he saw struggle to encourage office hour visits.
Was excellent tutor.

Professor Jayswal instructed my physics discussion course, and it was evident that he is passionate in physics and wants us to succeed. He was very friendly and caring, and encouraged us to ask questions. He was also extremely thorough in explaining the concepts and problems.
Really got surprised with the great technique of teaching style and the details explanation makes it more valuable. I would like to learn more in the future too.

Professor Vishal was an excellent instructor. He explained concepts clearly, ensured we understood the experiments, and was always willing to help if we had questions. His feedback was constructive, and he made the lab sessions much more manageable and engaging. Highly recommend him for this course!

Professor Jayswal was an absolute pleasure to learn from. He was thorough and meticulous when teaching; his style makes it impossible to forget anything you learn. 

As a person, he is friendly and personable, and bent over backwards any time I needed extra help. Absolutely would take again!!

I might be a little different because I have some security background, but I didn't learn anything from this class. Weekly in-class quizzes for attendance, exams with strange wording, and the occasional homework assignment made the content really easy, but still made me miss some random points for things that didn't make sense.

Its a totally online course, so I never met the professor, so I can only give them a three. Use all your resources and this class will be a breeze. I never used ChatGPT to do the assignments, but I wouldn't go through this course assuming that they have a way to tell the difference between AI coding and human coding when grading. Just saying.
This has quite possibly been one of the worst and most challenging courses I've taken in 4 years of college, absolutely horrible. Avoid at all costs
Good class, I learned how to code in python better than I could have ever imagined. Not too heavy of a workload only one quiz and one homework assignments per week plus midterm and final.

Easy enough class, but the final and midterm projects were a bit tough. She's really smart and will always answer any questions you have. Didn't always teach exactly what you needed to know for the assignments, but it was usually stuff that was easy to look up, and the PLAs are always there if you need help.

I had a terrible experience with this professor. The video lectures she posted were not useful when it came to the homework assignments. I felt ill prepared for every assignment, including the midterm project and final project. I feel as though none of the information was taught and I had to get help from my programmer dad or the internet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
**this review is for IT2910 - CyberSec**
The class is difficult, but Prof Jiang is great. Lectures are not too hard to understand and she is very willing to help. Met with me on Zoom multiple times to help me with specific problems and graded fairly.

Her lectures can be a bit slow and boring at times, but the slower pace helps when you're not understanding something. She is always available after class and can help you with the homework. I came in having never written code before and didn't struggle. Everything can be done online, at home, which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Jiang was a decent professor, but her class was only easy for me because I had some prior experience with Python. If you are coming into it without any experience, then you might be far worse off. She doesn't explain programming logic that well, and often defers you to online resources instead of trying to explain something herself.
tough, hard prof. but also very knowledgeable. you will have to work for your grade! but i have learned so much

Jurczyk is one of the few professors teaching Comp Sci at MU who knows what he is talking about. He teaches the content great. The one caveat is that he is harsh and unforgiving on grading, refusing to answer emails inquiring about regrades. Get ready to study hard and turn things in on time. You have to work for your grade here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: no. just no.
Tough teacher. Lectures are dense, homework is difficult, project takes time. On the bright side, you will learn.

He is an amazing lecturer and is extremely knowledgeable on all of the topics and their associated history. He tries to keep the class engaged with little jokes and posing things as questions to the class. He is far and away a highlight of the CS department so enjoy the few classes you will have with him.

He is a terrible grader and is extremely rude to students. Fails to realize that his lectures are boring and awful at communicating material and blames it all on students, and seems to think of himself as some sort of immortal who does no wrong.

Jurczyk cares quite a bit about this class. The lectures are always good and well explained, and at a good speed. There is a Homework or Lab every week, but not too difficult. 
Courseload is pretty light overall.

Really chill teacher. Hes a nice guy but very strict on deadlines. In this CS1000 Course 80% of the grade was determined by attendance, and 20% was based on a singular HW Essay. Overall really great professor, though the class can be a bit boring if you aren't into the topic.

Blames average course grade of B- and many F's on "attendance". Doesn't post extra examples/lecture videos despite having them (even during tornado warning), HW much more complicated than lecture. Mentions how students lose their post grad jobs because of his class without any sympathy. TA does everything. Easy content made hard for no reason.
Jurczyk single handedly saves the CS department. If you can get a class with him it'll be the best decision you make all semester.
The lectuer is very confusing which make it also very hard to work on the homework.

Pretty filler class there's one writing assignment that is graded pretty easy on as long as you put in effort. Attendance is required a letter is put on the screen and you have to put it into Canvas for attendance grade. Be careful if you skip bc if he notices he might throw another letter in for the people skipping. Overall easy class.

Dr. Jurczyk wants you to come to class, and for good reason. His lectures are engaging, easy-to-follow, and helpful. Assignments, projects, and exams are relatively straightfoward as long as you come to class frequently.

Professor Jurczyk is an excellent lecturer. He makes the lectures engaging and covers what would be difficult material in a very understandable manner. I would take any class he teaches in a heartbeat. Favorite professor I've had so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Jurczyk is a great guy, his lectures are very engaging and he clearly outlines important topics to take note of in regards to assignments and exams. Lectures weren't mandatory and he does post lectures from past semesters on Canvas, but I'd definitely recommend attending them, he recommends that pretty heavily as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Jurczyk is a great professor. For CS1000, all you do is sit and listen to lectures, with one paper. He did his best to make this class fun. You'll mostly be hearing from people from the Engineering department, and Professor Jurczyk. Attendance is mandatory, and is 80% of your grade. Overall great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jurczyk is a great professor and even though there are some boring topics, he does his best to make them engaging. Exam questions are pulled straight from homework or slides with different values. Labs and HW can be difficult, but guidelines are laid out clearly. Class isn't mandatory, he posts videos of his lectures, but it definitely helps to go.

Jurczyk is amazing at making lectures feel like discussions. Assembly is confusing, but he legitimately cares about making you understand it. No office hours kinda sucks, but the TA was helpful. Labs are tough, so get started on them very early. 3280 is a rather difficult class in general, but all grading is fair and expectations are always clear.

Definitely a challenging course, but Dr. Jurczyk manages to answer any and every question in class. Exams are somewhat difficult, but he tells you which homework questions they'll be similar to beforehand. I HIGHLY recommend doing the extra credit project halfway through the semester, as it will give you up to an extra 12% in the class.
CS 1000 is just showing up to lecture and turning in the single assignment. The lectures are generally interesting enough and probably helpful to some people.

The class is only worth one credit hour and is therefore very easy. You only have one assignment and the rest of your grade is attendance based. The one assignment is a paper that is graded very easily (everyone got a 100). The professor is fun and active but it can be hard to understand him at times.

Dr. Jurczyk is hands-down MU's best CS professor. He is amazing at answering questions and it is clear that he has a strong understanding of the material. He is great at asking questions that encourage learning and make students think deeper about the content. A couple of tricky questions on the final exam but other than that the class was fair.

Professor Jurczyk is really good at keeping the class engaged in the topic. He really knows his stuff and is good at relating everything back around. He is a bit of a harsh grader, but if you follow the lab documents to the T then you should be okay. All covid lectures are posted online, and empty slide decks are posted if you want to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jurczyk has an amazing ability to know anything and everything about the tiniest details of what he's teaching. Sometimes it's not the most interesting material, but he's quick to answer questions whenever ppl have them. The only tough part about this class was the project, but other than that Jurczyk continues to be one of the best profs for CS.

Hes a fantastic teacher. Hes extremely engaging, and if you find the subject interesting youll love the class and things you learn will stick with you. Ill never forget the sliding-window-protocol! Speak up in class, participate and ask lots of questions. If youre confused, just ask!

Hes fantastic, not just as a teacher but as a person. He cares about his students, and their learning. This class was tough, but you can tell he meticulously plans each lecture, when the class is following along hell finish right on time, and you can pretty much always ask a question. At times his lectures are conversational. Speak up if confused

I remember sitting in this class as a fresh transfer student, a 22 year old surrounded by freshmen. I was definitely a pain at the time, so frustrated to be stuck there. Honestly, the class was frustrating because like that other review says in some ways it does play like an Ad, but the guy teaching it was amazing.

Michael Jurczyk is one of my favorite professors because he makes every class exciting and does a great job of answering questions. CS 3280 was challenging but I appreciated how he made it clear what content would be covered on exams and had fair grading on the labs/homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Jurcyzk will give you everything you need to succeed as a Computer Science major and onward. You will need to attend class to succeed in this class, but if you attend and take notes you will depart with a solid understanding of CS fundamentals.

Professor Jurczyk is very chill and easygoing. CS 1000 is inherently a boring class but he made the best of it. I took this online and his soundboard was hilarious. Also he can absolutely SHRED on the electric guitar...

I like Prof. Jurczyk. He's very knowledgeable of this course and pretty funny sometimes in lecture. But this course in itself is just fairly boring. The labs are okay but can be challenging and the homework is not the easiest as well. But he does upload his lectures so you can reference them anytime. Overall it was an okay course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy material, but also very trivial material. Almost like an ad for the major that you have to pay for. You get one paper but if you just follow directions you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best CS profs at Mizzou. Assembly is a really cool topic if you get into it and Jurczyk's lectures make that easy so long as you put in a bit of effort. Always willing to walk through answers to questions. Pay attention and ask questions and you will understand what's happening in the course which means homework & labs won't be bad.

Great teacher. Takes dry material and makes it interesting and engaging. Very fair in grading, tough class, but communicates everything effectively and tells you exactly what will be covered on each exam. Go to office hours for help on all the lab assignments and labs and youll make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really good professor who makes engaging and fun lectures. The homework and labs were evenly and fairly spread out. The test were homework questions with numbers changed (also he tells you exactly what questions from the homework is on the test). Really makes an effort to be a good professor.

CS1000 is a requirement by the COE to get a CS degree. It's a complete joke, and I honestly think that it's just a plan by the COE to get their enormous course fee from freshmen who have no idea what they want to do. This class is 80% attendance & 20% hw based on ONE paper that if turned in, you get 100%. Easy A, bad class & professor. Switch to IT
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only thing that matter is attendance. Class is solely graded on attendance and participation, with only 1 homework assignment. Classes are mostly people from industry or related fields coming in to give a presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going to lecture AND office hours in mandatory for this course. There are many labs and homework assignments that are take home, but there is absolutely no way to look up questions that you have when you get stuck because of how specific and outdated the assembly language used in this class is. Tough class but not bad if you don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Jurczyk is a tough grader Hes demanding and detailoriented Learning Assembly requires close attention to registers and processorbehavior and he will take points for missing anything However the class is interesting Hes obviously enthusiastic about the material-he makes an effort to learn students names and ask the class questions Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Jurczyk is exceptionally knowledgeable about the assembly language and shows it in his lectures. His lectures contain all of the information you will need for the course and are as entertaining as possible given the course content. The grading is tough, but reasonably so, and has clear criteria. He clearly enjoys teaching this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jurczyk's class will be very challenging if you don't easily grasp the material. He explains the concepts very well, but Assembly is very difficult. Very tough grader, but curves the class in the end. Be careful on labs/homework, small mistakes will cost lots of points. Exams are like the homework, but on a time limit. Take thorough notes!

His lectures are boring but you have to show up or you'll fail. The homeworks and labs are worth a lot and they require lots of time but you can always ask for help and he will help. The exams are jokes: he gives you the questions in advance (in class only)

Networks was one of the most tedious classes I have taken. The material is incredibly interesting and Dr. Jurczyk is a decent lecturer, but all of the assignments and tests were awful. The problems weren't relevant, the grading was incredibly inconsistent, and he didn't give enough time to finish the midterm. Try to get someone else for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Would not compromise on disability accomodations, and changed prior agreements halfway through the semester
Grading is based almost entirely on tests. Lectures are extremely boring.

Jurczyk is a great guy. CS1000 is taught by mainly guest speakers, so I didn't get to have him for many classes. This course is really an introduction to computer science, so it is an easy A+ if you go to every class and do the work.

Dr. Jurczyk is a great professor, I really don't know why he's teaching CS 1000, the most boring class ever. 70% of the grade is attendance, and there's only one 2 page homework assignment. The class is mostly taught by guest speakers, and can get really long and boring, but Jurczyk really has a passion for what he does and cares about his students
funny kinda awkward teaching
Dr. Jurczyk was my favorite professor while I was at MU.  There is no comparing to a teacher who describes computer operations in terms of beer factories...!
Jurczyk ('ur-chick') rocked!!  Always very helpful and humorous.  Sure, I had this course 5 years ago, but he is one of the ones I remember!
This class is not very useful. I enroled in CS, not EE.

Attendance made mandatory half way through course. No clear grading. Gives extra credit but it's not actually extra credit and affects final grade. Many students went the whole class thinking they had an A but extra credit inflated  curve to needing an above 110% to receive A. Waste of money, I was looking forward to learning excel based stuff.
Very good researcher

The absolute worst professor I've ever had at Mizzou. Her class is absolutley impossible and taught at a graduate level. You can attend the lectures. You can study. You can ask questions. And you will still have no idea what is going on. There are 3 tests and 1 project all extremely difficult to understand with no help. You won't know your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE. Trust me. Entire class is 4 exams (22.5% ea) and 1 project (10%). Both are impossible and get no help from her. Not helpful with questions over email. Not sure how she is still employed here. Thick accent (can be hard to understand her) Dont know grade until the end curve. Do yourself a favor & take it with a different professor.

Such a sweetheart, but as of December 11th she has only graded ONE assignment from the first week. She reallyyyyyy needs to grade more efficiently. Readings are incredibly dense but I had good class discussions. The class honestly became a family despite the difficult readings and lack of grading.

Kathryn was nice but literally took 2 months to grade things. By the time a paper was done, it was finals week and I didn't know how to improve my last two papers that were already due. The feedback is also confusing. Solely on the way she grades and the fact that it takes forever, I wouldn't take her again
I fell behind in this class for personal reasons. Dr. Kat was extremely understanding and super flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: I have never felt passionately enough about a course to write a review but this class was awful. For an entry level sociology course the workload was insane. Every week was somehow worse than the last and no matter how good your work is or how much time you spent on it you will not get an A. She is a really tough grader, doesn't respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took SOC 4240. She's passionate and loves student discussion, but very slow with grading. Weekly reading quizzes were easy, and journal assignments were every few weeks. Midterm was multiple choice with a couple short answer. Not too bad. Random attendance checks with 5 freebies. Loved her, but the grading delays were frustrating.

The papers you have to read are nothing short of esoteric. If that's not bad enough, then you have to compare 2 of them. Weekly. 100% should be writing intensive. 
Other than that, she's pretty engaging during lectures. Class was interesting as well. The papers really suck the fun out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Posted the final assignment the Thursday OF finals week. Does not respond to emails and has graded three assignments total (it's finals week). Although this course was relatively easy week to week, Kat's lack of communication and complete off-hands method of teaching for the first 7 weeks made it incredibly difficult to know what was expected.

She is nice and helpful with feedback. However the directions on a lot of her assignments were confusing and vaguely worded. This class is also writing and reading heavy compared to many other 1000 level courses. There are 4 essays (the last one being a 6-page group essay) with 1 page-long reading response every week and discussion every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This teacher was hard to communicate with but flexible and clear with class expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lectures were an easy length and interesting info. However... the amount of writing and timely assignments per week was NOT WORTH IT. There were 2-3 required readings/ week that added up to be pretty lengthy. There also is a group paper worth 35% of your grade. To be honest, if you are looking for an easy elective this probably isn't for you!

I genuinely enjoyed each unit & watching the documentaries, but it was challenging to stay on top of assignments because the course load was extremely overwhelming. Additionally, she must have copied every announcement/assignment description from a spring semester because all the dates were wrong for my fall class... very confusing and frustrating
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very relaxed, flexible, and knowledgeable. When I got behind, she was very forgiving. The lectures and readings are pretty straightforward and easy to follow. She allows for lots of class discussion as well. There are a lot of short papers, but they are mostly just reflections. Overall, I really enjoyed this class and the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Each week there are min. 2 lecture videos (~30 min), they can be confusing as she speaks in complex terms + an occasional documentary. Min. 2 readings (often 20+ pgs) and a weekly assignment, requiring you to reference readings, lectures and documentaries. plus a research paper. Very time consuming. Learned a lot but I was overwhelmed weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Rittenhour cares about her students and is very knowledgeable. The class did not have as much structure as I would have liked, things in general were often unfocused and tense. The readings were very good and I still reference them. The class was more difficult and writing intensive than higher level Miz Soc classes. Grading was convoluted.

I took her 3300 class (queer theory and identities) and I really enjoyed it. I learned so much about the LBGTQ+ community, and I would recommend this for anyone who wants to learn more about the community through an academic lens. We also had meaningful discussions about real world issues that affect the community.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Some lecture but also several activities and videos throughout the semester. She is very flexible and cares a lot about her students.

Very knowledgeable. Assigned reading/lectures every week with weekly assignments. Grading rubric is available and easy to follow. Add'l assignments throughout semester and one research paper. Easy class if you do the work/readings and grades fairly (follows rubric). Gives add'l resources with each module. Allows late work but pts deducted each day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took her SOCIOL 1010 course and its a writing intensive course even though it is not marked as one and you do not fulfill your writing intensive credit taking it. She assigns a paper every week, a huge group paper you must revise and then write another paper on, and even more papers on top of those.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kluever is a very helpful professor! His class structure is great, with four smaller quizzes rather than big exams. Sometimes, you are left in the dark about what will be on the quizzes. Graded homework is kind of tedious, but besides that, it's a great class and a great professor!
GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was extreme about not using phones or laptops in class.  Unfortunately, MAE 1000 didn't really give Kluever a chance to shine because the class was really stupid anyway and shouldn't be taught.

Your grade is just Lectures, HW, and Quizzes. The quizzes lowk irritated me bc you never rlly had much to study before hand, so you kinda just had to know. The last two quizzes are review quizzes as opposed to a final, but again you have no review content. Not a difficult class at all, but a lot of busy work and something I just never wanted to do.

This class was extremely hard for me, but I am also not good at math. The lectures were vague, and the professor didn't explain how to do things well at all. I asked for help and he said to work practice problems and when I said I have been working them he didn't seem to know what to tell me. I felt like I had to teach myself all of the material.

Dr. Ries didn't really seem to care about the student's education, and rather expected us to know how to do things already. VERY TEST HEAVY, but there are 12-13 quizzes throughout the semester that are 80% of your grade. Very overwhelming, especially in the beginning if you don't do really well on the first test.
Pretty good professor.

Overall good professor. No feedback on any assignments other than a few notes on the exams. The material in this class is easy if this isn't your first exposure to statistics. The final project was not graded harshly at all.

Dr. Ries is a good lecturer and his slides are straightforward. There's a 10 question homework every week/every other week. There are quizzes 1-2x a month, but they're short (12 questions) and reflect the homework. There are no exams or finals (but there are 2 cumulative quizzes). Textbook is optional, but he posts the key terms from each chapter.

Great class, homework, and quizzes are both due online. Participation is graded by watching online lectures or showing up in person. Make sure that you are prepared for doing quizzes, as they hold A LOT of weight when they're graded. He's easy to get a hold of outside of class, and was very attentive.

Dr. Ries is a pretty good professor all things considered. I'd say that more than anything - at least if you plan to take STAT1200, whether for major or as a gen-ed, study - the grades are mostly based on quizzes, but should be pretty simple. Watch the lectures on Canvas as they're posted there too and you should do OK.

This class is a breeze if you've taken AP stats in high school; they're exactly the same. The homework is fairly easy and can be used as a study guide for the exams. No quizzes and only one final project at the end of the semester. Exams are worth 75% of your grade and are pretty short which sucks.

Dr Reis not only talks in slow motion, but also describes things in a very confusing way. However, the material itself isn't super hard. I just had to teach myself different ways from YouTube. The hw tends to be harder than the quizzes. You can show up or watch online for attendance. Textbook is optional, but definitely get the workbook!!

The class focused almost entirely on tests due to the professor's worries about students using AI to cheat, and I ended up learning almost nothing. We barely used R, and the 3 HW assignments didn't actually teach the material well but were only for test prep. Don't take this class unless you have to or until they improve the content and structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer, his quizzes are incredibly easy, easy to follow lectures, in person attendance is optional as you can watch the same lectures online for full credit, and not a lot of homework assigned. love this guy fr

I struggled in this course because the lectures did not provide support for students who need material broken down clearly. There were limited opportunities to ask questions or revisit confusing concepts. I believe the course would benefit from teaching methods that recognize different learning styles.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall good professor! I was signed up for his in person lecture but after a while I just started watching his lectures online still got full attendance points. His exams are very very easy.

The content in the class itself was fairly easy, my only issue was the way it was graded. 9 quizzes are basically your entire grade, and doing bad on one of them can easily ruin your grade for the entire semester. Quizzes are also only 12 questions so getting a few questions wrong can really mess you up.

Quizzes are graded 85% of your entire grade,100 points for 10-12 questions. I scored a 60 on a quiz and had to ace several quizzes to finish with an 87. No quiz drops, no extra credit, everything is online. He doesn't even teach in class; he stands there and provides surface-level explanations on slides that also fail to clarify anything.

Very easy class: 3 exams very similar to 3 corresponding homeworks, & a simple project comprise your grade. There really isn't much coding involved; it's mainly simple statistics. The prof is nice but the lectures aren't super interesting and he spends a lot of time going over not much content. There isn't attendance and he records lectures

I took DATA1030 the first time it was offered so the class was a little rough around the edges but it was good. I think Larry expects us to have some statistics knowledge before the class. Lots of lectures about statistics and a few R assignments+labs. Labs/tests are not open book but the HW before it is so similar you can use it to study.

He has timed quizzes which should honestly speak for itself. He gives you 24 minutes to complete 18-20 questions. His lectures are so painfully boring and he is not flexible with late work whatsoever. Would only tell someone to take this class if they actually needed it.
Grades very easy but he is pretty rude and unhelpful
He is great! The class can be taken fully online, but make sure you watch the lectures! Tests are worth a lot of points so make sure you study and don't miss any!
There is a textbook, but do not get it. He posts his lectures online so you do not have to go, but he only mentions one useful thing in each lecture. Tests are 80% of the grade, but they are online.
This class was super easy. Watch the lectures and you'll pass easily.

Professor Ries' STAT1200 is a manageable class if you stay on top of the weekly quizzes and use resources like unstuck AI alongside the lectures. Attendance is required but the material is straightforward, and you can get an A with minimal effort.

He wants you to get a good grade, so he is there to help. However, your grade is based on homework and quizzes (which are weighed like tests). You fail one quiz and your grade will drop significantly. Dr. Ries is laidback and knows how to push info out to students electronically. If you are taking the "in-person" section, he doesn't require you go.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Honestly, I never went to lecture and you aren't required too, I only ended with a B because I did badly on one quiz. Quizzes are taken online anytime between noon-midnight and are open book. Could easily end with an A if you do a little prep before each quiz. Only homework and quizzes.

Easy A. Watch the lectures, take notes, and use the formula sheet like your life depends on it. There was homework like every other week that took 15 minutes and quizzes every 2 weeks that took 5 minutes. Put the lecture in 2x speed and you won't spend more than 2 hours on this class a week. So easy and well-taught.

I took it online so I just watched recorded lectures, but he seems like a great prof and person. His class is the first time I've ever laughed in math class because he tells hilarious stories. Very easy as long as you read the slides, but quizzes are worth a lot so try hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, it was pretty easy, you don't have to go if you don't want to but at least watching the recorded lectures is helpful. All tests and homework are open note, and all tests are weighted the same including the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's pretty much there just to get you out with a passing grade. The system he uses for homework and quizzes is weird but they are pretty easy until the end where you will have to work just a little bit harder than what you were doing before which is most likely nothings. His lectures are super boring just watch the lecture at home or read the book

He was very clear and really had his format down. Class could be attended live or online, and he covered what was on the tests and quizzes. Somehow statistics wasn't my most boring class thanks to him!

I've never really been good at math and this was a pretty easy class. Homework covers what you learn in lecture and theres quizzes every two weeks that are very similar to the homework. Quizzes are also open note/book and taken online. Take good lecture notes and you'll be fine.

It has been some time since I had the professor, but I have vowed to give him a proper rating. He is very cold and unempathetic to his students. Had to go on a deployment that semester. My schedule conflicted with class. I asked for consideration in this. He said he was not able to and the only advice he could give me, was to withdraw.
If you have dealt with any sort of trauma growing up do not take his class as his emails are aggressive and rather triggering. Went to ask for help and was met with rudeness as well.

He posts his lectures online and is good about sending out reminders for deadlines. He is a pretty snarky guy, so I can see why he rubs some people the wrong way, but I don't find him that off-putting. This class is also super easy. If you are able to complete the homework without problems, there is no need to go to discussion.
Likes to talk a lot about things that aren't important to the class and tends to get off topic
Lectures are easily accessible and easy to understand. Quizzes were straightforward and followed the class examples and homework.

Dr. Ries has got his format of teaching down. He clearly states every due date in the syllabus and makes an announcement every week to ensure students know what will be going on. He is very positive and easily approachable.

Dr. Ries is a great professor. He has simple expectations: a homework assignment and short quiz each week over a couple of chapters covered in lecture, using the online website Webwork. They are all open-note and quick, and you can use his formula sheet for them. If you watch his recorded lectures, or attend the class in person, you should be ok!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stat 1200 was a very easy A. I rarely went to class and did fine. Your grade is entirely webwork homework and online quizzes, both of which are open book and have a formula sheet with every formula you'll ever use. Lowest homework and quiz scores are dropped. TA's are there to help you in discussion if you don't understand anything.

Dr. Ries made his lectures pretty easy to follow, but if you don't go to class you'll be able to catch up. There was a homework assignment for each chapter but most of the time you get unlimited attempts. Rather than big exams, there are quite a few mini-quizzes (3-10 questions) if you need help the TA's are there for you.

Dr. Ries's STAT 1200 class is one of the easiest courses I've ever taken. Homework was due once a week (on Monday nights) and quizzes were every other Tuesday. These are the only things you will be graded on, so you'll want to prepare for them, but if you did the homework and wrote down the lecture notes you will be completely fine. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class, requires minimal effort. As long as you do the webworks and understand how to do all the problems, you should not have any issues with the quizzes. Never read the book or did the recommended practice problems, but good if you need some extra practice.
Pretty easy class just make sure to do the webworks. The quizzes are similar to problems on the webworks.
Easy if you put in the work. He's kind and takes class slow so that it's easier to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He makes it clear in the beginning your lowest test score gets dropped and the two lowest homework gets dropped, but there's no extension on dates at all. He explains that's his "built-in" flexibility for emergencies. His classes are really easy. If you watch his zooms or recordings you'll be fine. I barely used the textbook.

He definitely knows what he's talking about when he's teaching stats. He could work on being a little more personable. His lectures are hard to watch since he talks like a game show host and yells the whole time. The one time I reached out w a question and a personal situation he sent me the link to a canvas reminder. Very happy to be done.

Professor Ries was a good teacher, but didn't have the best personality. He was rude to students for their internet going out during a test and needing to retake it. Elementary-level math course for me. If you watch the lectures and did the online homework, you'll be fine. Barely used my textbook. Drops the lowest test score and two lowest homework

There is no one worse at math than me. Going in to this class, I was terrified, but ended up getting an A! The class is truly not very difficult and Ries seems to understand that this is just a required intro level course for most people. He makes the content easy to understand and explains it slowly and deliberately, which was so helpful for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: nice guy really funny, posts lectures to panopto so no need to go to class just watch and make sure you understand examples, online homework is pretty easy, dont really need to read online textbook, 4 tests are multiple choice & written but super easy if you understand workbook practice test, discussion is optional only go if you have questions

As long as you keep up with the work and lectures, youre totally fine. He posts everything on canvas so you dont actually have to go to class. Just try to keep up with the lectures because they can feel long if you have to do several in a day. Read the emails he sends and syllabus and youll stay informed but he does respond to emails quickly
Pretty standard stats professor. Not great, not bad.

Larry was a fun professor. His lectures were pretty boring but he cares about his students. In high school, I couldnt do math. I got an A- in this class. Big tip: do webwork during your discussion class. I did that and always finished within the hour. The TAs are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You don't have to read the textbook or do any of the optional homework problems. All of the past exams are on eRes, and he changes the numbers in the problems but that is it. It's kinda funny how easy it is actually. Like I think if I took it in high school it would be more difficult.

Ries is not that bad of a professor. He does lecture really slow and boring, but he posts his lectures online, so really you don't have to go. He tries to make the class interactive which makes it better if you do go. If you suck at stats it's not the easiest class but he gives lots of resources for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Can't say I actually learned a lot from this class, felt like the content itself is pretty basic. Easy to watch lectures on line (on double speed - he's a slow talker) and get by just fine. Never went to discussion; if you put in the time with homework and practice times and make sure you understand the content you'll be good for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Larry is one of my favorite professors. He is rather knowledgeable, and he actually makes going to lecture quite fun and entertaining. Some may say his pace is slow, but its actually better because he allows time for you to grasp the information. He wants you to succeed and he holds you accountable for all your work.
Lectures are heavy and he talks really fast, but he's a really funny guy and makes coming to a non-mandatory attendance class worth it.
Really nice teacher and very helpful. I got the feeling that he just wants to help the kids learn and have an enjoyable time. No doom and gloom like a lot of profs.

Larry is a pretty cool guy, even though I personally struggled with his class since I've always been bad at math-related courses. He does try to set his class up to have help available as much as possible from TAs, etc. The formula packets help too. If you're like me and struggle with math, watch his tegrities as MUCH as you can! Tests are big too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He will post all the lecture slides and recording online so just view them at home at x2 speed since he speaks really slow. Exams constitute 90% of the course but they are really easy as long as you do the practice papers that are uploaded online! You will surely get easy A as the practice papers are very similar to the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Voice is monotoned and boringggggg - makes going to class really hard, but fi you go to class and pay 1/2 attention, you will get an A
SOOOOOOOO BORINGGGG. Talks extremely slow, takes super long pauses for no reason, and goes off on random tangents that have nothing to do with classes all the time.

Excellent class, math is fairly straightforward, concepts are easy enough to grasp. Watch the videos (can be watched at 1.5x speed), do the practice question. You will get a good grade. Exam is the same exact format as the practice questions with different numbers. I used a $3 calculator and got an A!

I hate math and everything to do with it, but Larry was amazing. The way he explains concepts makes them SO easy to understand. Yes, he does Panapto but I would really recommend going to class. The discussion section was useless and I went maybe twice. Unless you have questions, it's not worth attending.
Dr. Ries explained things pretty well, and has a good voice. Kind of hot in an offbeat way. Funny.

Dr. Ries explains concepts very clearly. He sends lots of canvas announcements for reminders. Do the practice tests when studying for the exams; they help a ton. The hmwk assignments are online and easy to get 100s on. If you put in some work, youll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--Clear grading criteria--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Larrys lectures are enjoyable and they are all posted online so you can watch them later and not go to the lecture. Class grade is mostly made up of tests so make sure you study! As long as you watch the videos or go to class you will do fairly well.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I've sucked at math, but I've thoroughly enjoyed Ries' stats class. However, it's a very dangerous class in the grading sense. Three exams (60% of your grade), one cumulative final (30% of your grade), and the homework (10% in total) make up your total grade. You cannot afford to do poorly on the exams. It's an easy class, but you need to study it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Math isn't exactly my favorite class but he made statistics very understandable. Everything was on powerpoints that were easy to read. Also puts his lectures online in case you miss class. I recommend going to lectures though and studying for the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: don't have to go to class, but make sure to watch tegrity. I struggle with math but this class was extremely difficult. Practice tests are somewhat helpful, but exams are way harder. Rude prof and TA's aren't much help. Do attend discussion classes tho. that attendance will help for bumping grade if needed. would recommend taking at comm college.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Ries is great. He makes the lectures interesting. There are weekly quizzes and homework but they are not hard and if you are struggling you can go to the discussions and if you can't understand your TA you can go to a different TA for help. I did NOT think his grading was hard, its math you either get the right answer or you don't.

Ries' class is the hardest math class I've ever taken. I usually do very well in math and have no trouble but in his class, I struggled. Even after getting continuous help from my TA and acing all of the homework and quizzes, I still did awful on his exams. His exams don't reflect what he teaches in class or are significantly harder. Do NOT take!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do not take his class. He is a terrible teacher and the tests are worth 80% of the grade. Homework and quizzes are extremely easy but nothing like the exams. He is very rude and is unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is very simple as long as you bother to listen in. You don't have to actually go to lectures - they're also posted online if you can't make it.
