You only need to show up for the labs once a week which are usually just used as time to do the weekly homework assignments. As long as you pay attention, it's pretty simple.

Class is almost exclusively online, so you don't even have to go to class. I went to the first week of lectures and never went again, and I got an A. Study for the exams, and take the practice tests so you know the format. He's very vocal about office hours and meeting with him for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm not good at math, so I had to work especially hard in this class. Tegrity wasn't cutting it for me and there were distinct verbiage differences between him and the book and an entire unit outside of the text. That being said, I emailed him for help and he was very off-putting, unhelpful and rude. Also left for a week the week before the final.

If you have a question, it's better to ask the TA's than Larry. He wouldn't always answer people's questions in class with the utmost respect. He talked negatively of his ex wife a lot, but the material was fairly easy to grasp if you watch the Tegrity videos or go to class.
Great class, you dont always have to go. Easy A if you watch the videos, and a lot of practice exams that are just like the test and finals.
Super easy class with a professor who gives you all of the information that you need.

Class wasn't mandatory, all lectures were on tegrity however i do recommend actually going to class. Homework once a week, quizzes once a week. I thought i wasn't going to do well bc im not math oriented but i finished with an A in the class. He's very thorough and made me understand stats easily. Can be a little boring but solid class.

lectures are available online so going to class is optional. discussion classes with teacher aids really helped clarify questions. there is a homework and quiz every week but lowest quiz and homework grade are dropped. easiest math class i have ever taken for sure

He is a super easy teacher. His lectures are clear and if you still don't understand him you can go to your discussion and the TA will help too. He also has tegrity and gives out tons of practice exams for each test. If you have to take stats take his class. Also attendance in lectures is not necessary unless you're struggling

I am pretty good at math and found this class hard just because there is a ton of work into it. I didn't find the information as hard, but his tests were really hard and had to study a ton just to get a B on tests.

Meh. Material is boring. Study for the exams and know how to work out all the formulas. You get a formula sheet for exams. Weekly quizzes and homework. Dr. Ries lectures via tegrity, so you don't have to attend class. It's honestly just a boring class and Dr. Ries doesn't make the material interesting.

Professor Ries talks really slow, so I recommend skipping class and watching Tegrity. The homework and quizzes aren't hard, and with the provided formula sheets the exams are pretty easy. My only complaint is he wasn't very friendly or approachable. Attendance only counts in discussion section if it will help your grade. Don't buy the textbook!

Pretty chill class. Tests aren't to bad at all... Basically exactly the example in the work book. Tegrity for every class. Theres some homework online but its not too bad if theres a group of you that can work together on it

You legit don't have yo go to class, just discussion. He posts everything online. Make sure to study with friends and do your best on tests. Easy B and most people will get a B+ in the class. Larry is really weird and may come off as rude, but he's very fair.

So let me preface this by saying I never once meet Larry.  The course I took was exclusively taught by a TA which I found to be ridiculous.  I personally believe he should had been involved in the class somehow, but this was not the case so watch out for getting a TA that does not speak English as their first language

LARRY RIES IS THE BOMB WOW I have never had a math teacher as AWESOME as he is. You literally never have to go to class if you watch his super clear tegrity videos, and you get an INCREDIBLE formula packet for every test that helps you out so much. Leaving this class with a new found respect for statistics. YOU ROCK LARRY RIES KEEP DOING YOU!!!!!!

You don't have to go to the original class you signed up for, you can go to any of the ones that he teaches or watch on Tegrity. You are given a formula packet that you can use on the exams. He is very easy to understand, even on the Tegrity, which is straight from the morning lecture.

Lectures are on Tegrity and textbooks are not needed. It doesn't hurt to go to lectures though- I took his class my 1st semester and now I am a junior and he is still one of the best professors I've had at lecturing. Very easy to understand. Get familiar with formula packets and do the sample exams. Easy A for me (a journalism major).

Lectures are online and you'll want to watch them that way because he talks SO SLOWLY. I watched every lecture on 2x speed and he was speaking at a normal pace. The formula packet will be your best friend! It makes the exams a breeze. Pro tip: print the practice exams the week before the test!! If you wait till too late, the server gets overloaded.

He posts his lectures online, so you don't have to attend lectures. 1 homework and quiz a week. He drops the lowest homework and quiz grade at the end of the semester. He posts exams from past semesters online. There are 3 exams and 1 cumulative final. Use those exams he has posted because they help a lot!

All lectures are posted online, so it's not mandatory to go to class. There's 1 online quiz and 1 online homework assignment a week, which are fairly easy. There are 3 exams, and 1 cumulative final. He posts past exams online and if you review those for the exams, you will be extremely prepared. Don't buy the textbook. You dont need it. Easy A.
Makes things easy and simple. Don't have to go to class, posts all lectures online. Gives practice tests from former years that are really helpful.

Ries is good.  It's an easy A--literally all you have to do is take a few of the practice exams that he posts on eRes, as all of his tests are the same thing, just different numbers.  Makes stats simple.

He's horrible to go to for one-on-one help. I thought I should've had a different grade on an exam, and although it ended up being my own fault (which I accepted) he spoke very rudely to me and pretty much forced me out of his office. Other than that, lectures are okay but he doesn't give many examples.

Larry clearly realizes that most of the students taking this class are not math or statistics majors. The material can be hard if you aren't used to it, but the formula packet is the holy grail. Also you don't have to go to class because all lectures are recorded on tegrity. I would also say the labs are pointless so don't go to those either.

I hated this class. Larry is extremely strict and will make no exceptions. Don't bother going to the discussion as  they're lead by foreign TA's that don't speak a word of English. You don't need to go to class either since he posts lectures online. Also DO NOT BUY THE BOOK!  I literally did not open it and I am still mad I wasted $120 on it.

Well the group weekly meetings you have with TA's are completely useless. None of my TA's spoke a word of english and couldnt help answer any questions I had when confused. His test suck because they are multiple choice which is fair than switch to show your work and its hard to gain any points when the TA's grade those parts so tough.

He is a very good at his lectures. Everything is clear, everything is posted on Blackboard, and he religiously records on Tegrity. However, he is terrible to go to one-on-one. He makes you feel completely ignorant and speaks with a rather hateful tone. Luckily, this class is probably easy enough, you won't have to ask many questions.

I think I would do better in this class if the test-taking time were longer; it is 25 questions in an hour and I always run out of time before the main writing portion. I'm very disappointed with the "discussion" section because there is no discussion, they just sit on the computer instead of actively helping students. you have to go to them.

Whenever you have to wake up 7 in the morning to go to class at 9, Dr. Ries is the best choice.  He is very interested in the subject that he is teaching to students and that he will awaken and entertain you to listen to his lectures as if you're enjoying his class.

Ries is a pretty good teacher. You can watch all of his lectures on Tegrity ( and speed up the pace because he talks so slowly). But I've found that the best way to learn in his class is to actually read the chapter in the book before and then watch the lectures to help clear things up. In lectures, he doesn't go as in depth as the tests are.

He posts all his lectures on Tegrity, so it was a lot easier for me to go at my own pace, and if I needed to pause or rewind I could do so. I never really went to class and still got an A. He explains stuff pretty well and I heard he gave out m&ms to the entire lecture class once. Pretty awesome teacher

Larry is one of my favorite professors at Mizzou. He records all his lectures on tegrity, so you can easily get an A without going to class. There is a purple formula packet, as long as you know how to use it, you'll get an A.

Cancels lectures after big events on TV (Emmys, Super Bowl, etc.). Does not cooperate with regard to moving exam dates, passive aggressively barks at you through mass emails, very unpleasant. You will get an A, but you will not like it.

Unless you learn easily with just the book, you will not understand a thing he says. In lecture, he reads his slides to you and just tells you the answer. Isn't much help at all. He doesn't explain things well and never explains how he came up with his answer.

Larry Ries is the reason I changed my major to Statistics! He is a super great teacher and MU couldn't have hired a more knowledgeable professor. You can tell that he cares about making sure you learn the material. He breaks it down to a science and uses PLENTY of examples. He's funny and you never have to come to class because everything's online!

Easiest course I've taken at Mizzou but would not recommend if you have any interest in Statistics. You won't learn any more than what you might have learned in high school classes and will be bored by the professor's lack of enthusiasm and monotonous tone. You don't need to attend classes either as he posts everything on Tegrity.
Such an easy class, never went to any classes and got an A.

Ries explains well and is pretty nice. Sometimes it's difficult to understand the statistics TA's English, so I mostly skimmed his powerpoints and tegrity lectures which were well organized and developed.
If you fail this class with this prof drop out of college. If you haven't taken stat make sure you take this dude when you have to enroll in it. Guaranteed A-B
Larry teaches a SUPER easy class. if you go to class, or watch the tegrity, you should pass. Study off of previous exams and you should do well!

No need to to actually go to class. All you need to do is study old/practice tests and your fine. Especially for the final. I thought the weekly homeworks and online quizzes were harder than the exams.

No need to to actually go to class. All you need to do is study old/practice tests and your fine. Especially for the final. I thought the weekly homeworks and online quizzes were harder than the exams.

Loved it. He is a very smart guy and a very good teacher. He has a bit of a dry voice, but don't mistake it for him being mean. He also puts all the lectures, slides and audio, on tegrity so if you ever miss class you have nothing to worry about.
Ries posts all of the lecture contene online as well as an entire archive of past exams.  Therefore you never have to go to class; the course is very easy to self-teach.
Never went to class but watched all the lectures and did a lot of practice tests and got an A.

I asked him for help after trying tutoring, group tutoring, and talking to the discussion TAs (none of which have any sort of proficiency in English) and he had no other options.  He does not make himself available for help near the end of the semester, when people need it most. My advice is to get a tutor you can really work with.

Discussion class was not helpful at all. All discussion leaders are foreign. Mine hardly knew English. When I came to pick up my test from her, it took her three tries to say "what's your name"! I tried to get Ries to help me find a new discussion class, but he was not helpful. The tests are not hard except I never had enough time to finish.

Absolutely hate math, but loved this class! Ries makes it interesting, and easy to understand. I didnt even go to discussion section because he explained everything well enough in class. Take previous semesters exams as practice for tests and you should do just fine.
I would've had to tried to fail this class. Lectures are all online, plus sample exams. I hate stats and math, and this class was still a breeze for me.

Professor Ries does an excellent job of keeping students interested in stat. He also post all the classes and review online just encase you miss. The quizes are short only 15 mins to complete them though.

He is a complete jerk and will not work with you on anything no matter the circumstances. Doesn't matter if you have a completely legit excuse for not being able to take a test, he won't care. He is the biggest jerk I've had for a teacher ever!!

Larry is really entertaining and tries to joke around to make class worthwhile for those who do attend his lectures (his powerpoints and lectures are also online). Quizzes are very easy, though they're only 4 questions, and tests are easy as well. The best way to review is by taking practice exams online!

if you go to class, it will be the easiest class you ever take. i studied the night prior for about and hour for every exam and got A's on all of them. he answers your questions after class if you want to ask them and the online quizzes are SUPER easy. great teacher.

Very easy class. Records and posts all lectures online along with past exams for practice. No attendance is taken at all. If you go to the lectures or watch them all online before an exam, youll do well. RSD's are pointless unless youre having trouble with the material.

RSD's are pointless.Just about everyone I talked to quit going after the first few weeks and still have a good grade in the class.If you listen to lecture(he posts them all on blackboard)and go through the workbook problems as he does them in lecture.Also,I've found the best way to study is by using his old exams, which he posts.Great formula chart

He doesn't encourage his students to come to class because he puts them up on Tegrity. He was a good teacher however. He used real life applications and made learning statistics not so complicated. The formula sheet was a lifesaver too.
NOT A NICE GUY!!! DOESN'T ENCOURAGE STUDENTS TO GO TO CLASS! AND MAKES IT INCONVENIENT TO ATTEND HIS OFFICE HOURS! AND NONE OF THE TA'S SPEAK ENGLISH!

This class is pretty easy. Take the previous years exams from practice and you should do fine. Lecture is boring, but somewhat helpful. RSD is often taught by grad students that are difficult to understand. Lectures are boring, but effective. You will do well if you attempt to apply yourself, professors corny jokes aside.

Go to class, takes notes, and use the old tests he provides to help study. If you do good on the practices tests you will do good on the actual test. If you don't figure out what you need to study cuz chances are it will be on there!!
Always opens with "Gooood morning class," and tries to relate his life to something he finds interesting/funny. The material can be boring and may induce slumber.
Larry is a very easy teacher. If you go to class, he makes it almost impossible for you to fail. He gives you all the things you need to get an A! Class can be somewhat boring, but its not bad.

Very good teacher. Gives you all the resources you could need to succeed - posts power points on blackboard, comprehensive book problems, LOTS of practice exams (and answers). He's funny and maintains interest. Take his class. It's easy to get an A if you do the homework and tests. Didn't go to RSDs though, not necessary.
Great teacher! Funny lectures, helpful examples, straight forward tests, optional homework. I never thought I'd get an A in math! Go to class and do the practice tests and you're set.
Really enjoyed this teacher.  Was great for explaining things and kept class very interesting.  Old tests are offered for study guides which were great because tests were almost identical
Funny as hell. Has perhaps the best voice I've ever heard from a professor, at least in terms of being able to pay attention.

Probably the most fun you'll ever have in a math class.  Go to lecture and everything will become clear; lots of examples, moves slowly, surprisingly funny for early in the morning.  Watch out for the Isle of Capri and angel dust jokes; he's an odd duck, but that's what makes him a great teacher.

I am absolutely horrible at math...barely passed pre-calculus...and I got a 97 in this class. Go to the lectures (going to section doesn't really do anything, most of the TA's are foreign, hard to understand, and not helpful) and do the practice tests he puts on Blackboard and you will be fine!

My grandma passed away during the semester I took his class and he was not willing to help me out in any way. I ended up getting a C+ which I was NOT happy about because I could have done a lot better if he would have had a heart.
funny professor. listen in lectures and do many  practice test and will do fine

Even though it may not seem like going to lecture is necessary, towards the end of the class you will be very confused if you don't go. Also, I didn't go to RSD but two times the entire semester and was fine. Just do a bunch of pratice tests before the exams and you should be fine.
Dr. Ries is a very interesting professor.  If you take the initiative, he is very helpful.  Some of your grade really depends on which TA you get.  He puts a lot of faith in them.
if you come to class and work on his practice quizes/exams, you'll be fine.
No Comments

I thought he was an easy teacher. The things I would recommend are to practice in the workbook and the exams. Also the review sessions before the test are vital. Attend them and your grade WILL improve.
easy class; states exactly what is expected; refer to his practice tests to study for the exam
Very easy class, he knows what he is talking about, and as long as you practice the exams you will do great in this class!
Easy class. If you took high school stat and did well, you don't really even have to go to class (except lab), as long as you look at the notes online and do a few of the practice problems.

the class was extremely easy. He started posting the notes for the first time in my class which made me not ever go to class. I didn't go since the second week of classes and I passed every test with flying colors. All you have to do is practice ALL of the seven tests he gives you online and the questions on your test will look almost identical.

Professor Ries is a wonderful Statistics teacher and one of the best math teachers I've ever had.

Good teacher, seems to love his job. The class was pretty easy, but I actually looked forward to coming to class.

Dr. Ries is quite a character.  He comes in and does his job and does it well.  He provides lots of supplements to help you out.  But if you feel like you have to be babied and accomodated, don't take this class.

Dr. Larsen is an awesome professor. He makes lectures entertaining and does a great job tying the lectures to real life. You can tell that he truly loves what he teaches. Notes are really easy to do, he gives a packet out that will guide your notes throughout the lectures. You do have to write five country reports, but they're only a couple pages.

Dr. Larsen is the bee's knees. The cat's meow.
Lectures are imaginative and delivered with enthusiasm, and if you have him in your discussion section, you will be delighted at the energy he brings into the room. This man is radiant. So knowledgeable, so down-to-earth.
Do beware that the packet for notes is a pretty big high school throwback.
Seriously one of the best professors I've ever had. Great guy. Super passionate about what he teaches.

I have seriously considered sitting in on some of his lectures even when I'm not taking one of his courses -they are interesting and passionate and clear. He is always willing to help students and his coursework is engaging and useful.
His passion for teaching and strong command of geography made his lectures one of my favorite classes I've taken here at Mizzou. Cannot recommend enough, he's the best.

Dr. Larsen is an amazing professor. His lectures are entertaining, informative, and useful. His grading schema are clear and reasonable, and he makes the class interesting for everybody. I highly recommend any of his classes.

Lots of assignments for this course but they weren't too hard. He's really passionate about teaching this topic and it made his lectures really enjoyable. Overall a pretty easy class, just quite a bit of busy work.

Probably the best professor I've ever had. He makes learning really fun and is super insightful. He's always smiling and is a joy to be around. A very kind and caring person. I recommend taking his class, even if you don't need it or aren't interested in geography. Gives great feedback & All around awesome guy, and he's a musician

Dr. Larsen is probably one of the best professors you can get at Mizzou. He very clearly loves what he teaches and wants his students to experience that same excitement. He always provides good feedback and has very manageable coursework. If you have the opportunity to take one of his courses, do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. He's very engaging and animated and gives lots of good feedback. He's extremely approachable, so ask questions if you have them. The work is pretty easy and straightforward. I took this course for honors credit and it's become a class I really look forward to.

I adore Prof. Laresen. He is my favorite professor at Mizzou, and he's the one who convinced me to seek a geography minor. He is a very engaging, intelligent teacher, and he is a great person to go to with questions. Larsen also plays in a band that performs around Columbia, which is pretty legendary.

One of the BEST profs I've had. Took his class as an honors elective and ended up being something I looked forward to going to. No exams, genuinely cared about students and made lectures engaging. Points come from participation, online quizzes (very easy), and a few papers. Would highly reccomend this class if it's an option.

Soren gives very engaging lectures and makes coming to class enjoyable. Even if geography isn't your thing he makes every topic interesting. The included discussion section is kind of a drag, but the lectures do a great job at preparing you for the exams which are fairly easy. Highly recommend.

Soren is by far the best professor I've ever had. He not only cares about teaching geography to his students, but he is always willing to learn more about the topics that he discusses. He's TRULY passionate about what he does. Also, his story is pretty inspirational. I'm hoping and praying I get to have him in another class later on.

Dr. Larsen is the best teacher/professor I have ever had.  Not only is he passionate about what he teaches, but he is easy to communicate with.  He also leads extracurricular trips.  For GEOG 1200, read the pages with vocab discussed in class.  The exams are vocab heavy, and there are no trick questions.

Professor Larsen is a very nice guy who seems to really care about student learning. He uploads presentations to Canvas with blanks in them that you fill in during class. If you don't go to class, you need to get this information from someone else because most of the tests are based on lectures. Some reading is required but overall, it's easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've never had a professor more passionate about his subject - he LOVES geography and knows SO much about the world. Tests are super easy if you come to class/discussion and study the PPs - he underlines the things you need to know, everything else you can forget about. Very fascinating class, very nice/compassionate/genuinely good person.

Dr. Larsen is easily the most passionate and invested professor I have ever met. His enthusiasm makes just about any topic he covers in class enjoyable and engaging, and his collegial mentality of seeing students as peers really helps to add an extra injection of lively debate into his classes. Tests are easy and content is very interesting.

Soren Larsen is the bomb.com! I never thought geography would ever be that interesting but he changed that. He's very knowledgeable of what he's teaching and explains it with so much clarity. He will ALWAYS mention what he wants you to know for tests. 3 tests which are easy if you study. The book isn't too important. Mostly for discussion

Soren Larsen is the best instructor I have ever had.  He is truly enthralled with Geography and this makes his class entertaining and easy to pay attention in.  He is animated, excited with the topics in class and extremely well-read.  The tests are tough but not too tough.  He challenges you to look around you and LEARN. 10/10 professor.
Very enthusiastic and easy to understand. Textbook helps further clarify--would suggest buying it. Best Geography teacher at Mizzou by far.
Personally never read book. Only used powerpoint slides and his lecture talks for test. 3 tests with a map portion. He was very interactive and tried his best to make class enjoyable.

REALLY nice guy, completely evident he cares whether his students are retaining the information.  Can be a tad unorganized at times, but again, makes up for it in clarity.  Homework assignments are really easy and I got high 80s and low 90s on test without studying for more than an hour or two.  Got an A in the class.
Awesome teacher, one of the best at Mizzou

Soren is one of the best professors I've ever had at Mizzou. He is amazingly enthusiastic and clearly passionate about both the subject matter and his students. From the beginning of the lecture to the end of class, this prof is so high energy that he sucks you into caring about it as well. He also makes really great power points that help out A LO
A really nice guy with a passion for what he does. He will help you with whatever you need! Take his classes!
He is a great professor. Taking his classes made me switch to a geography major, plus he is easy on the eyes :) which never hurts.  Over all he is an extremely knowledgeable and charismatic person.
Very Helpful and passionate guy. Interesting material and a great class.

Professor Larsen's lectures were extrememly interesting. He taught with the utmost knowledge of the subject. His assignments were also beneficial to furthering my understanding of the course. Would definately take class from his again.

The best professor I've had in college. Not only is he full of knowledge on many subjects, he loves to look at issues from all sides. He's a spinning top - his passion ignites early in the lecture and he goes deep into the material but it's fun and keeps you thinking. Tests are hard but you are encouraged to be a serious thinker and grow with it.

Dr. Larsen is a fabulous professor. He knows a lot and really wants to share his knowledge with students (plus he knows how to effectively do so). He's energetic and a really nice guy in addition. He learns names quickly too, which is always nice. I would highly recommend any of his courses.

This guy is one of the best professors i have had in college. His teaching style is energetic and up-beat making the class tolerable. He is constantly blowing me away with his knowledge...very very smart man.  Test are a little difficult, but he sets you up for success.
No Comments
Knowledgeable, interesting, and definately active in the field of geology.  Many goegraphy nerds in the class make getting an a more difficult than it should be.  Pretty easy class though.
No Comments

Moves deadlines up on Canvas as they approach but not lenient with student late work... Class attendance could be worth 0.5 points one day but 3 another and you don't know until day of, so if you can't make it one day, better hope you're lucky! Condescending towards students with questions; sometimes it's funny, but it mostly makes people not ask.

Took Thermo 1 and Fluids with her. Thermo was a little better, but it was her first time teaching fluids. Impossible to know the type of questions coming up on the exams in Fluids. That was tough. Thermo 1 or 3261 was more manageable, but a lot of studying is required to keep up with both.

The homework is very different than what is covered in class. The grading is very inconsistent on the homework. She also assigns group assignments and gives a short time window to do them and they are outside of the classes allotted time, but due before the other classes end

Different material covered on lectures, homework, and exams. Impossible to know what's important or expected to know. Opposing feedback from professor and TA's. Did a homework problem set with her in office hours, proceeded to get my lowest homework grade of the course.

Only 2 midterms 1 final and 2 quizzes. Tells class when quizzes are and exam not set time for either. Class was very easy. Practice problems are same as on quiz/exam with numbers changed. Best diff eq professor you could possibly take.
Do the online videos and their practice problems and you will do great in class

This is the easiest math class you can take at Mizzou, there is no homework and the quizzes and homework are very similar to the lecture notes so take good notes. Don't get behind on the lectures and you'll be ok.
Take math 4100 with him, I promise you won't regret it. Best math class I've ever taken at Mizzou.

Professor Li was an outstanding professor. He would write out the notes with us during our zoom calls so we weren't rushing to copy PowerPoint slides down plus his own notes on top of it like other professors. There is only two quizzes and two exams and a final exam for the grades but he makes it so that if you watch his classes you're fine.

He is also very good at explaining the proofs over topics in diffeq. He actually makes learning the content enjoyable because he hasn't formulated the class as a "stress fest" like your typical math course/professor.

reviews.comment: Very Straight forward Teacher who wants to make sure that you do well. Professor Li is very helpful and can explain almost every problems that he give in at least 3 different ways. Unintentionally hilarious  and his notes and examples are the best I've ever encountered at Mizzou, which made Differential Equations a breeze.

Dr. Li is the best professor I've had at Mizzou. He made Differential Equations, a difficult high level math class, a breeze. he gives "pop quizzes" but always alerts you a few days in advance. He grades very easily and the quizzes and exams are not difficult. Attendance is pretty important. Also, he is hilarious. definitely recommend to anyone

Li is phenomenal, once you get used to his straight to the point lectures. There's no intro, he just goes straight in on the first day. Makes this class incredibly easy though. Show up and you have an A
Charles Li makes what could be a very stressful class a breeze.
Go to class and you'll get an A in the class, it really is that simple. Professor Li knows his stuff and as long as you are there you will learn.

Charles Li is the most amazing math professor I have had at Mizzou.  He is easy to understand, and his exams reflect the material learned in class.  Homework is nonexistent, and exam averages are always above a 90.  He is very entertaining and genuinely cares about student learning.  If you have to take diff eq, he's the professor to have!

So easy! All his exams are just questions from the notes, so as long as you go to class you'll get an A. If you don't go to class, you'll probably get a D or F, which is why the curve evens out and he can be so easy.

Great professor. His quizes are all "pop" quizzes, but don't let that deter you from choosing his section.  His exam problems are as simple as can be, and very similar to the examples in his notes. If you have to take diffeq, choose his class.

As a professor, Lever incredibly difficult to work with. The lectures weren't very helpful. If you want to do well in this class, you need to study a lot outside of lecture. I found myself relying more on the textbook, which was very useful for teaching yourself the content.

The exams weren't too bad overall, but even so, the class averages were below 50%, which shows that many students struggled.

reviews.comment: Should not be qualified to teach Orgo. Emphazied that students should have to read the textbook in addition to lectures and homework. Barely tought the content that was required. Exams are tough but if you study enough and do lots of outside work it is managable. I read Ochem as 2nd language as additional learning-can find on reddit. Very helpful

This class was horrible. The lectures didn't match the book, the homework, or the exams. She does not explain anything clearly. Exam averages were 50%. Exams are mostly trick questions. If you take this class you'll have to put your heart and soul into it and probably still get a B or C. Would not recommend.

Dr. Lever is very intelligent & passionate This class is brutal. Absolutely is lecture heavy, lots of material. But, she does a very good job explaining things.  YOU HAVE TO STUDY.  YOU HAVE TO WATCH THE LECTURE VIDEOS. STAY ON TOP OF IT. Using secondary resources really helped me, like youtube videos or even tiktok.
worst ever. exam averages were 50%. don't take this class

Dr. Lever is probably the best professor I have ever had. She is incredibly helpful and truly cares about her students. I highly suggest utilizing her office hours and reading the textbook. She makes a incredibly difficult class mangeable.

She is a fun teacher and uses examples you'll remember. She repeats questions on exams so make sure you look over past exams. She curves the whole class so it's easy to get a good grade. Gives multiple attempts on HW problems, penalizes for late work. If you do the HW & study you'll be fine. She cares about her students & wants to get to know them.

I strongly urge you to take orgo with a different prof. Dr Lever allocated her class time to bizarre metaphors and ramblings yet expected you to magically learn the content. She also provides little guidance as to what you will be tested on so it is difficult to self-teach using the textbook. I got an A but it took everything out of me.DONT SUGGEST

Dr. Lever was very kind and good at communicating with students. Homework assignments aren't particularly difficult, and you get ten attempts for each question. Tests are pretty tough. Reading the textbook and lots of practice is how I earned the grade I did. Overall, I think Dr. Lever is a good professor to take organic with.

By far the worst professor I've had. I went to her office hours at the beginning of the semester and she acted annoyed when I did not understand a concept and I got nothing out of it. I went to Tiger Tutoring for the rest of the year and that was way more helpful than her office hours. I highly recommend choosing a different professor for orgo.

Reading the textbook got me through this class. I didn't find lectures helpful, but Dr. Lever provides lots of study materials on canvas. Exams are multiple choice, but still tough. Study the textbook and the summary of reactions at the end of chapters and you'll do decently. The adaptive quizzes are also very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures make no sense and are hard to follow. She goes off topic sometimes and writes everything together so it is hard to know what is going on. I visited her office hours once and got no help whatsoever, so I went to tiger tutors and they explained things so much better. You are expected to memorize everything. Choose a different professor!

Doesn't explain concepts well. It's not useful to go to class because she doesn't explain things, puts extra information in her slides that isn't in the slides she gives to you, and then tells you to read about it. You may as well watch the lecture later to get all of the information. She's nice but she expects a lot from students outside of class.
is not good at explaining concepts

She is the sweetest teacher I have ever had. She was so helpful and so fantastic. You are able to understand everything even if you did not do great in orgo 1. Has homework and tests were pretty good and not too bad if you just study and do the homework.

Dr. Lever is a wonderful person, but I personally had a hard time with her teaching style. I think for the most part she is good at clearly explaining the basic principles of organic chemistry. I took her Organic chem 2 class to further understand organic chem, so when the lectures cover basics while tests are about more specific topics, its rough.

Prof Lever is so sweet! You can tell that she genuinely wants you to do well, and she's very passionate. She gives a good balance of homework that doesn't feel like busy work, and I like that she emphasizes the bigger picture. Considering the circumstances with it being an online class, she did well.

Dr. Lever is definitely one of my favorite professors, she is super sweet and genuinely wants you to do well. This class has several exams and the homework is useful for tests. Be sure you do the book problems! Honestly, it's the reason I was able to secure the grade I did, don't take them for granted. There are a lot but they're worth the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Professor, very caring, and yes, motherly, but I found that endearing. She cherry-picks the chapters, and homework assignments are reasonable. Make sure you do all the assigned problems, they might show up verbatim on an exam. Exams multiple-choice and average difficulty. Homework and short reports boost your grade. Low exam dropped.

The messiest teacher ever which isnt okay when learning organic chemistry. Youd think for 200 students paying 75$ per class she would have an Apple pen to draw with but she literally uses her finger and you cant understand a word of whats written. People try and speak up and ask her to be more clear and concise and she doesnt care to adapt
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Warmest of the Chemistry Professors. Cares a lot about her students and if you go to office hours she does her best to help. I like that she only used relevant portions of the text, so you have less reading. Homework is distilled to relevant questions and do the assigned probs because one or more can show up on exams. HW and papers boost grade.

This was the hardest class I've taken but the final grade is really curved. She really cares about her students and takes the time to really make sure you understand the material, but her tests are multiple choice and really hard. You have to study a lot and get a lot of outside information to really understand it. Make sure that you do practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Test questions were ridiculously hard/nothing like what we went over in class. She is very smart but it makes it hard for her to explain anything where students can understand. I've been a straight A student and ended up with a C in the class. All her test averages were 60%. Definitely take this class with Ganley if you can.

Orgo 2 with Lever has been the best chemistry class I've had at Mizzou. Obviously it isn't easy, but she makes it as easy as she possibly can. Her lectures are straightforward and she tries to keep it simple for you. At times her tests get tricky, but she'll even try to prepare you for exam questions

Lever is one of the nicer professors I've had. She's very accessible out of class, easy to talk to, and responds to emails incredibly fast. Her lecturing is solid, but sometimes she strays and doesn't convey the overall concept that well. Exams are sometimes not great, but stay with the covered material for the most part. Good for Orgo overall

Dr. Leaver is my favorite chemistry professor I have had at Mizzou. The course material is definitely difficult but she made the course as clear as organic II can be. Go to class she will get to know you and is an all around wonderful person.

Oh Susan.  She is so friendly and wants nothing more than to be your friend.  In my experience, however, she needs to be corrected on problems (which she will humbly admit she made a mistake on) and has a problem conveying information in a way that doesn't leave you as confused as when you walked in.   If you can understand her, awesome professor.

Dr.Lever is a very sincere professor. Organic in general is a hard course so in terms of 'easy' tests she's your best bet. I didn't find her lectures helpful but I recommend going to class anyway and especially her office hours. She's really good at remembering names and faces.

Just finished taking organic with her and it was definitely a challenging class. The tests are not easy so be sure to study. The review sessions helped a lot though so go to those. There isn't really any extra credit, basically the homework is used to boost your grade in the end and she curves it a little bit.

Taking organic with her now.  She is very nice and caring--super helpful, readily available outside of class.  The course is tough but she provides a ton of resources.  Go to class, study lectures and reading the book helps.  DEFINITELY do the practice exams--sometimes has old q's verbatim.

This is a really hard class and I don't think she makes it any easier. Her lectures aren't very helpful. She is a nice caring teacher though and the EC is nice. It is important to read the book and do practice exams. Make sure to study previous tests for the final.

Lever makes organic chemistry not too bad. Her lectures are kinda boring, since she talks to us like we are 10, but she is very clear what will be on her tests, and if you study your stuff, you will do well. Go to lecture and it helps to read the book to get the overall organic concepts that will only help you when you move onto organic 2.

Dr. Lever is alright. She talks to the class like we are 7th graders which really turned me off to getting interested in the material. In class examples were also oversimplified to the point that they started to be confusing. But she was really helpful and cares that her students do well. Tests were always fair and there was even some nice EC.

VERY nice person, but I can see why some ppl may not like her. Her style doesn't match everyone's, but her tests are fair and on the very easy side for a class like this. That said, you do still need to study. She offers extra credit, so that's awesome but don't rely on it. You basically get what you put into this class.

Dr. Lever is great! For the most part her tests are pretty reasonable and she doesn't try and trick you. She doesn't stress out over math and nomenclature. She also offers extra credit. She's also great if you go to talk to her in her office. She genuinely cares about her students. I loved her class.

She's annoying to listen to because she talks to the class like we are 3 year olds. She does little to NO example problems in class. She understands the information but instead of teaching information she makes horrible annalogies and explains things like how to open a text book. Go to the review sessions instead of lecture. Always.
Horrible Lecturer.
Dr. Lever was an amazing teacher.  She wants everyone to do well in her class and makes it possible to do so.  I really enjoyed taking her class
Great professor.  Very enthuastic and cares about her students' learning.  The class will be very difficult no matter who teaches it though.

Dr. Lever is the best Prof I've ever had, ever!  She's very concerned about her students and wants us to learn the material so we can be successful in 2nd semester OChem.  One MUST STUDY to do well in this class!

her class made organic seem a lot better than i expected. The tests are decent and she is really nice and approachable. The lectures are pretty good sometimes they are a little hard to follow when she has the models and everything out but overall its a good class.

Lever does an excellent job of teahing organic which isn't easy. Her tests are very fair and she gives a lot of partial credit. Make sure you start memorizing the reactions right away!!! And the final was relatively easy.
Very difficult tests, but she is nice, helpful, and has well organized lectures.
Graded a project four months late that tanked my grade.

Very confusing lectures, she gets off topic a lot, and then adds those random things to the tests. Harsh grader and does not have clear intentions with the projects, tests, or assignments. Good person, but not meant to teach.

Rambles a lot in lectures and often veers off topic. Goes through slides pretty fast and is a little unorganized. Grade is based off exams and a few 100 point assignments, which aren't too hard just heavy. Has a small assignment every day for attendance. Overall very knowledgeable and knows what she's talking about, she's just not for everyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was harder than expected. Exams were open-note but in person, with questions based on what the professor said ONCE aloud, and not on slides. Attendance was mandatory due to in-class assignments and the grading scale was strict, as only three major projects made up most of the grade, and was graded super harshly by the professor and TAs.

I would take 1,000 more classes from Dr. Lancaster!  She is knowledgeable, comes to class prepared, and really cares about her students.  Writing assignments are reasonable, and solid feedback is given for each one.  When I was going through family struggles, Janna was so kind and compassionate.  I wish all of my professors at Mizzou were like her!

Janna is a great professor. She's passionate about what she does and teaches and it shows. I always get sad when everyone starts packing up early and leaves before she can finish what she's saying. She deserves more respect than that. She is the most wholesome and caring person I think I will ever meet. Highly recommend taking her classes!!!

Amazing teacher! I will be taking as many of her classes as possible. She comes to class with well-prepared lectures and is easy to talk to. Homework is easy as long as you pay attention and take notes.
Boring lectures and is always telling the class to close their computers and phones lol. Easy midterm and final. Projects were kind of fun but sometimes it kind of felt like a high school class.

The lectures consist of 4 videos each and each quiz is over 2 lectures so I have 8 lecture videos to do for one quiz. Half of the questions are poorly written (sometimes not even in the lecture) and meant to confuse you and trick you. A true or false will seem obviously true but she changed one word in the question so the answer is actually false.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lancaster is amazing
Janna did not give us any incentive to come to class. Class was not as interesting as it could've been. Only thing that mattered were the midterm and the final.
Dr. Lancaster is amazing. She is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic.

Not an architecture major, just took for fun. Skipped a lot, but be careful because there will be unannounced in-class assignments that will help determine your attendance grade. Read the book and you'll do fine. Exams were relatively easy and projects weren't graded super harshly. Enjoyed the class a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a great fine arts class at Mizzou. First, it is extremely easy. You can not show up and still get an A. Everything is open-note, online tests. However, Dr. Lancaster is a great professor. She is very passionate and caring. She is funny and you will get more out of the class if you do show up to lecture. Great elective class!

Horrible. DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HER!!!! She will make your life hell for 16 weeks. The class is only worth 100 points and its all group projects. She doesn't answer questions and creates a very negative learning environment for her students. I'm warning you, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't take a class with her again. interesting classes and course materials but you're as good teaching yourself the stuff. Group-heavy. very adamant on never giving full points.

Entire class is one group project; had a group that didn't contribute, & after countless emails asking for help one unhelpful email was returned. Ended with a B as a result of poor course design & a teacher that knows her stuff & teaches (interesting) material well but doesn't know how to be a good person. Am not excited to have her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: New class. Professor was relaxed. During lectures, told what would be on the quizzes. Had guest lecturers who provided quality, real world information. The class focused on applicable public health in current society. Would take class(es) with her again.
She really knows her stuff!!!

Wow!  For a 4 credit hour class she requires a TON of work, 10 hours a week of clinical time  plus 20+ hours a week on completing assignments.  The most frustrating was not knowing until the last minute that we had to make a conference style poster as a final project.  Turned an interesting subject into a nightmare.
This professor is a harsh grader and will report you to disciplinary board for any reason that he might think your work is ai generated.
just no to this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Participation is mandatory - Quizzes every day at the end of a class...
Grading scale on exams never really expressed/explained on exams, and on assignments to the point where he reluctantly had to make one to show the class.

Worst part - as of Spring 2026, a group project is assigned for a big part of your final grade...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Both him and his TA's are VERY harsh graders. Docks points off for very small things and it can really tank your grade. Lots of studying and only short answer questions on his tests!
Don't take this class. He grades VERY tough for literally no reason. I think he tries to make his class seem more important than it is. Hate this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. McLaughlin is a nice and organized instructor, but do expect lots of written assignments and very boring readings/lectures when taking his class. He can be very stingy with grading, but it's pretty easy to earn an A if you attend class regularly and complete extra credit assignments. Definitely relies on in-class discussions to pass time.
Professor grades horribly if you have a differing viewpoint than him.
His class was really easy, he just really likes to talk. Also has very liberal views and is pretty closed minded.
Just don't take his class LOL he is so tragically boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is extremely nice, but attendance is mandatory and lectures are not great. Assignments are relatively easy, and you get one dropped. You can get extra credit by attending office hours, and he is very understanding. The main problem I have with this course is the lectures not being very interesting.

Very nice professor, but very tough when it comes to grading. Followed the rubric exactly on every project, but still ended up getting many points deducted. Also not super accessible outside of class and office hours, so it is hard to get feedback before submission.
Class is called Global Religions, but not many different religions were talked about. You'll also learn about other groups that aren't religions. Not what I led to believe the class would be about.

TA does all the grading and is inconsistent throughout the semester. I was missing many points at the end of the semester and was on the verge of an A- and an A. He offers the opportunity to go to his office hours for extra credit points throughout the semester, but on more than one occasion he wasn't even there so I could get the extra credit.
boring
lectures are very boring, is a very ticky tacky grader.

Lectures are very boring and I found I didn't really learn anything because they were so hard to follow. McLaughlin encourages participation in lectures and occasionally will have us break into groups. McLaughlin is a very kind, young professor, and he encourages you to go to office hours, and will give you extra credit if you do show up.

Lectures are boring and attendance is taken, so if you miss too many days you will get points deducted. Assignments are easy but he has an obsession with AI and making the class revolve around that. I think he's a nice guy though.

Dr. McLaughlin's lectures are boring, which is impressive as the topics are interesting. His obsession with class participation is quite strange and it doesn't help that he asks super open-ended but oddly worded questions. I understand wanting to embrace AI, but making it part of the assignments halfway through the semester was more confusing.
Just read the textbook, but she also typically goes over the content in class. Super sweet and loves getting to know her students.
Definitely not as hard as other reviews are making it seem. If you can write, put in some effort, and go to class, you'll get an A. She knows a lot, is energetic, and willing to help if you ask.

I'll start by saying she is a good-hearted professor; however, my compliments end there. She is unbearable to listen to. Whether or not this is just because the content is incredibly easy to comprehend, or just the fact that her voice is like a fork on a chalkboard, is up for debate. Nonetheless, everything about this class is a joke.
u better know how to write business style
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Good Professor, Personable and understanding while keeping things fair for other students. Not an easy class but if you do your best to apply yourself you will be okay.

Christine is a fantastic professor. I was not a big fan of this class because it's writing intensive, but if you are required to take 3000W do everything you can to get her as your prof. Highly recommend.
One of if not my favorite professors at Mizzou

She's really nice, the in class assignments are kinda busy work, the class is a bit random but I would recommend this class. She doesn't call on people by random, so you won't have to talk out loud in class if you don't want to and I felt her assignments were not graded too hard. I just can't get behind in the class but otherwise you'd get an A.

Okay professor, worst personality. Class is kinda pointless to go to; she mumbles on and on about random information, as you make table tents. Yet she still declares that she doesn't give out busy-work, while half of the class is a PowerPoint of reiterated information in the book. Class isn't bad, but the ego on this woman is crazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory, and if you show up to class and participate in lectures you get extra credit. Two tests and three case studies throughout the semester with a packback and quiz over the chapter every week. Christine is amazing and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She has been my absolute favorite professor in my time here. I would highly recommend this course as it is incredibly useful. She takes the time to make sure students understand the material and genuinely cares about her students. Assignments are clearly explained and tests are very straight forward. I plan on taking her other courses.

Her style is different in a good way. I like the creative projects, even tho I cant draw. She does reminders on canvas but not in class, so you have to check canvas as sometimes they are due before class and midnight. She gives effort to make class fun, but sometimes your group has a bad attitude, which sucks. She is super nice/understanding.

The highlight of my day is going to class with Dr. Sabrina. You should read the announcements that she posts because sometimes she won't mention an assignment in class but it will be posted in the announcement and module.
Great at using Canvas!

One of my favorite professors! I hate science and kept putting off taking my science req until my junior year. If you hate science then take her planet earth class. I actually enjoyed the class. There are some rando assignments that require you to draw which I didn't love and more work than I thought, but I didn't feel it was a lot of busy work.

She is such a nice person, just really bad at using Canvas. Really read everything she posts with the date and time it's due, sometimes things are due in the middle of the day for no reason. The tests aren't bad and the field trips are fun, just be ready to send emails when things online don't work correctly.

Amazing professor. Very discussion based class, and she had us meet in a different place on/off campus every week so that was really nice. Very chill grader -- frequently gives late credit and extensions for assignments. Also is very open to feedback and takes course evals seriously. No complaints overall - if you can get her, then do it!

Just finished planet earth! Downside: you will leave class wishing all your other professors were like this, and they are not. 10/10 would recommend. Take her class. Your GPA, mental health, and serotonin will thank you. I also hate science but somehow loved this class.

Dr.Sabrina is such a nice professor. She makes class exciting, and she makes learning fun. She is super interested in what she is teaching, and that definitely shows in her teaching. She is also a very approachable person and a fair grader. I always knew what was expected of me in her class.

Hate to be that guy but she showed up in a striped sweater and white Vans and I spent 20 minutes trying to figure out if she really our teacher or a grad. When she teaches it's like a jump scare, she explains things so well and is well spoken but looking like she wants a ride to target. But she's smart and a good teache so don't judge from looks
Don't be fooled by the eyelashes and sweet smile she will assign something every time she gets a new idea, which is unfortunately every 14 seconds. I ruined shoes in this class. But I

I really like Dr. Sabrina. She was really fun, and I liked all the field trips that we took! Especially because I've never had a teacher who would take us on fun trips like that! The grading can be a bit subjective at times, but it's really easy to earn points by putting in effort, so it balances out.

I would give a 5 but I am pretty sure I developed arthritis from the amount of writing I did for this class so 4/5. Best class to take for a science w lab credit if you are not a science major plus get the H credit. Field trips are fun but so random.

Dr. Sabrina Michael = GOAT  Her classes are hands-on, organized, and never boring (well sorry sometimes a little but only some days). You can tell she loves teaching and cares about her students for real. Some labs you are literally sinking in mud so make sure you have old crappy shoes before taking her class. Easily one of the best at Mizzou

Dr. Sabrina is such a slay prof 😭 She actually makes science make sense and fun?? Every class feels like a mini adventure. Super chill, kind, and genuinely cares about her students. Take ANY class she teaches she's that rare prof who makes you want to show up and learn. Real life Mrs. Frizzle

Dr. Sabrina made me see the world differently. She's incredibly passionate about what she teaches and puts so much effort in. She genuinely cares about her us and treats everyone with kindness and respect. You can tell she wants you to succeed. Her classes are organized, creative, and surprisingly relaxing even though you still learn a ton.

I was hesitant to take Dr. Sabrina's course after some bad reviews, but they couldn't be more wrong! She's incredibly caring and her classes are so much cooler than any others at Mizzou. Yes, they're challenging, it's a biology course! But if you put in the effort, it's one of the most rewarding and memorable classes you'll ever take.

Dr. Sabrina is the coolest professor I have ever met. Her course set up is so unique it makes learning easy and fun. For labs, we went on trips to caves and aquariums! What other professor does that?! She is so caring to her students and gives her all to teaching. You cant leave Mizzou without taking one of her classes!

Dr. Sabrina put us in groups and did activities that made us become such good friends. I know that isn't the point, but it seems to be a reoccurring thing that happens in her classes. I feel like the class was easy but only if you show up and pay attention. She was always willing to help. I'm taking two more of her classes this semester!

Best professor ever. She was very passionate about the topic and motivated to teach. You can tell she truly enjoys it. Very understanding and generally if you didn't like her it's because they tried to cheat and things so syfm. Overall very nice and is worthy of taking the class if you enjoy the topics or need the credit.

I love Dr. Sabrina! I learned more in her class than I have in any other class! It was low pressure, but she still had high expectations for us. You do need to attend class to do well, but I honestly found myself never wanting to miss. If you can, take her science sequence for your honors credits!!!
Dr. Sabrina is a wonderful and caring instructor whom I have had the pleasure of working with

Dr. Sabrina is super sweet and genuinely cares about her students. Several extra credit opportunities exist & we went on a ton of field trips and did dissections. She also made us cookies for the end of the year. You do have to read the syllabus for assignments b/c she won't mention them and some things are hard w/o a biology background

NOT 3400!- Dr. Sabrina is an amazing professor with an enthusiastic teaching style. I took her Honors Marine Biology course and loved it! We went on fun field trips, did multiple dissections, and I learned more here than in any other class. It's quiz-heavy, but manageable if you pay attention. Some topics can be tricky without a science background.

She didn't submit anything into the grade book until midterms and then gave everyone 75%. She would miss class frequently yet gave no leeway for students to miss class. Her rubrics were very unfair and often she would deduct 15+ points without giving any explanation. She was disorganized and gave poor feedback.

I was compelled to write this review because I never wanted someone to take her class again.Overall her class was structured in an elementary school setting. The issue with her test was that she NEVER graded it correctly. I had to go to office hours to get it regraded. I would get back10 to15% on her tests. TA was from a diff major and was useless.
Super test heavy, test were fair but made careless mistakes in grading. Final was comprehensive, and required a 95 to get an A. Wouldn't recommend.

The class was relatively easy. I attended every class and always participated in my group. But Dr. Sabrina expected you to raise your hand and ask/answer questions in class in a lecture hall of 180 people. This is not something I have ever done in college. She counted off points in my total grade and then it dropped me from a A- to a B+.

This class was decently easy but more than anything Dr. Michael was engaging and kind. She had lots of extra credit opportunities and is super passionate about her research. Tests were only 20 pts so super low pressure but were frequent.

This class was fairly easy, but we had exams every 3 classes which was a huge pain. There isn't much leeway for missing classes either-- if you miss more than one ICA (given at random) you are kinda screwed. She's pretty good at clarifying concepts and clearly passionate about what she teaches. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

Very, very good professor. Lots of concepts on test but very similar to review assignments (progress checks). Accessible outside of class, very caring and good at clarifying concepts. Attendance to class required and some long readings, but very understanding and relatively easy grader.

If you aren't taking this class for the Neuroscience certificate, I don't really recommend it. This professor was absent past the first day. Each week, Matthew Will and a guest presenter talked about new topics, making the class feel like it lacks structure. However, homework and quizzes are very easy if you need the 1 credit hour.

I took the online section of this course which was completely put together by the TA. Many of the prerecorded lectures and lecture slides were outdated, some spanning back to 2018 and 2020. This made information of how to access homework difficult as there was a lot of conflicting information. Confusing lectures lead to confusing homework.

Where do I even start… He admitted he uses ChatGPT to make his exams, which explains why they feel nearly impossible. He drags out the same topics for weeks, then suddenly rushes through the rest. The only mercy is a 10-30% curve at the end. Anyone taking this course… you'll need luck.

This prof does not grade for partial credit. So, If you get one part of a four part question wrong, you earn no points. Very stressful. Also, the correct answers for Hw, quizzes, and exams are not revealed. There is no guidance. Also, hours before grades are due, an extreme curve is applied. Your grade in canvas does not reflect your final grade.

I have never had a professor this bad in my entire life. Assignments take hours with unclear instructions and the necessary material frequently forgotten. All of the learning for the course consists of online videos that either under-explain content or have zero correlation. Assignments and labs also have no correlation. DO NOT TAKE.

This class is the worst I've seen during my time at Mizzou. Satish is very adamant about sticking to his style, which consists of never answering student's questions, not teaching things himself, and assigning unreasonable amounts of homework. This is a glorified teach-yourself course, but it lacks the necessary structure and guidance. Stay clear!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This guy is a joke. Genuinely awful. First day of class he'll tell you there will be no feedback on homework and it's completion and it takes hours upon hours to complete it and it often serves zero purpose for the class. This is the worst professor I've ever had. I took the elective because it sounds interesting but he completely ruins it.

This class wasn't awful but it's a lot of work. I took the online version so there were less opportunities for content review, but it's still doable and tests were alright. The TA was a big help (and also basically ran the whole class). Taking it in-person might be better for concepts to be cleared up, but overall I still learned a lot.

He had a unique lecture style, which could be fine for other professors but for him it involved asking questions that made no sense and then berating students that didn't give him the answer he wanted. What we were meant to learn over the semester was unclear, the TA did pretty much everything. This class made me not feel sane.

This class is so poorly run it's almost impressive. Lecture videos are posted to be watched before class time each day and have little actual correlation with lab or homework assignments. You will question your sanity if you take this class.

His work load is INTENSE and you will not know if what you are doing is correct because there is no rubric. He will expect you to read an entire textbook in a week and summarize it all. If you are not taking other classes, this might be doable. He posts random youtube videos and articles and you are to learn from those. There is no class. STAY AWAY
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. This is the most unorganized course I have ever taken. Getting an A is not hard as homework is for completion but you recieve very little feedback. His teaching method is to essentially make you learn all of the material outside of class. Any questions you may have he will tell you to ask ChatGPT

I took Psych2017, it took 5 weeks to get a response from either my TA or my Professor. This course only had 4 questions quizzes, which allowed me to get 3/4 every time and have a not ideal grade in this course. Furthermore, I did not know my grade in the course until 2/3 through the semester as it was not posted. This prof and ta were so god awful.

Please do not take this course!! This is the most unorganized class i have ever taken and the professor is not accessible, the class itself is mostly led by the TA. I did not learn a lot from the couse and it was a time not well spent

Dr. Nair has an unpopular approach to teaching. He doesn't really teach the class. Instead, he calls on students to answer questions and essentially teach for him. Most assignments and projects are not connected to what is discussed in class and are time consuming. If you sit in the front of class and participate, you'll learn some things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is an extremely mismanaged class. There is little correlation between the in-class lectures, labs, homework, and quizzes. He frequently can't be bothered to teach the class himself, and other reviews are accurate in how students teach. Over halfway through the class, he made all lectures mandatory by having students physically sign-in on sheet

Do not take this class with Dr. Nair. He's a nice guy but he cannot/refuses to teach. He does not teach the material in lectures. He also made the course way more difficult than necessary, lab assignments were impossible. It is May and assignments from February are still not graded. If you want to learn about neural models take a stats course.

Avoid at all costs. Never truly teaches or clearly answers questions. Has unprepared students sub in for him. He's incredibly degrading when you don't understand material. His grading is incredibly subjective and unfair. So many unclear, impossible assignments that don't teach you anything. If you want to learn machine learning, do it on your own.

If you take a class with this professor, you will regret it. He is extremely unclear, often has other students teach his classes without guidance. Yes, you read that right. The class workload is also larger than any other class I have ever taken. He talks about how grades don't matter but gives out crappy ones. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES.
He does not give clear answers for questions. You have to teach yourself by yourself. Huge homework.
Very kind.

This professor was extensively unorganized. The class relied on the readings, which were not posted before the quizzes, sometimes not until like 2 in the morning the morning before the quizzes. She was also constantly showing up late for class, and we didn't have a single grade until after spring break in the gradebook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor assigned so many readings that were crucial for the quizzes and exams, yet she would not post them until days before the quiz, or even at like 2 am the morning of in one instance. The syllabus was also wrong so nobody knew what they were reading. Also, we didn't have a single grade until nearly after spring break.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Never take her class, she put in grades very late like not until march, and is extremely disorganized. I have a harder time in school but I still try my best and she has not been supportive what so ever. You have to hand write notes in this class too which isn't an issue but she moves so fast for so many words in the screen.

She mixed me up with other students that weren't attending class and gave me a bad grade because she didn't know who I was. She also offered extra credit, but did not make the extra credit out of 0 points, therefore these assignments dropped my grade. Nothing was graded until 2 months into the semester.

Easy class made hard by professor. Was late on many assignments, but did extend the deadlines. ALOT of reading, most required to do well on quizzes. Exams - DO THE PRACTICE QUESTIONS - she grades tough but when class average was low, she gave opportunities to fix mistakes for more credit. Try to find different class, but if no choice it is passable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I have her online course and she is very sweet. However, her online lectures and readings that were due for the week would be posted late frequently, but did extend the due date sometime. She is not specific with what she wants/grades in the rubrics for heavily graded exams which is scary. LOTS of reading, quizzes and discussions every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: NEVER take her class. She was disrespectful to feedback and questions, lacked communicated and was incredibly disorganized, and a very harsh grader. The course load was ridiculously difficult for a 2000s level course and she was not kind to questions about grading. Lectures are heavy, required and unorganized. Tanked my gpa

The worst ever. This professor constantly showed up late but expected perfect attendance whenever she was on time. She showed up to the in-person midterm 35 minutes late and tried to pass out the exam with 15 minutes left before the entire class yelled at her. Posted quizzes over the weekend and then made them due by 9am Monday morning. DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the best math teacher/professor I've ever had. She teaches in a way that is easy to understand, and goes through plenty of practice problems. She gives out plenty of extra credit. The workload is decently high, but it really does help with understanding in the end. She is also a very fair grader. I would take her again if I could.

I can't recommend Professor Xuan enough! Gives plenty of extra credit opportunities, ample amount of time on homework, and prepares you well for quizzes/tests. Professor Xuan wants you to succeed and is ALWAYS willing to help. Just ask. One of the sweetest, caring professors I've had. I highly recommend her for Trig.
Her heavy accent didn't affect her teaching. She's super sweet and kind. She is awesome about giving extra credit. We have weekly quizzes, but most of them only had two questions.

I cannot stress how much she has helped me with math. She is very caring and is willing to help students with anything they are struggling with. She offers a lot of extra credit to help your exam scores. I had a hard time with math in high school and she made learning this new information a breeze. She has an accent but she is easy to understand.

She does have a heavy accent but it doesn't even matter she is a very good teacher and she is very neat. If you pay attention you'll be fine. There is a lot of homework but it's fairly easy. She's sweet and a very good math teacher.
Hard to understand and uses no helpful images or methods and rather just does the examples quickly. Very heavy accent

Have you considered that you do not deserve a professor as good as Monnier? Have you considered that you, unworthy that you are, might combust in the presence of a Divine of the Humanities? If you have not so considered, if indeed you are a worthy student, then prepare for a semester of Olympian triumph.
Never criticize Monnier in my presence. She, along the rest of the Russian faculty, is the lone bright spot in the otherwise Stygian night of the humanities at Mizzou. Give her more money.

Tough grader. At the same time no clear grading criteria. Most of the time I didn't even understand why I received such a grade. A lot of materials to read and 0 explanation in class. High expectations and no help. Got C (average) for participation even though I talked in each class. Makes me wonder what others who never said a word got.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Monnier is awesome!! She really cares about her students. She's actually a Russian Prof so she just teaches this class on the side, but she's obviously really interested in the material. The class does require a lot of reading, but in general, I think she tries to make the books we read really accessible. Aweomse gal!!
Dr. M is amazing!

Dr. M is the best teacher to have when you want someone to nerd out with over the best works in literature, art, and music. She truly cares about her students and isn't afraid to tell you when you're obviously slacking in her class.   If you're lucky, you'll get to see her pug, Buddy!

Best teacher I've ever had, hands down, in high school or college. Give your best effort, and she will give it back and then some. Always willing to help, whether through email, office hours, or in class questions. Having Dr. Monnier as a professor is a privilege by seeing how much a professor can truly love their subject, as well as their students

worst class to sit through. not sure how she got so many reviews. lectures are awful and boring, great for catching up on work for other classes though. she makes you read like 20 pages then gives you a 5 question true/false quiz each week... why. doesn't keep grades up to date. we are 6 days away from my final and grades from january aren't in.

Russian with Prof Monnier was probably the most fun I've had in a class in college. She is really passionate about what she's teaching, and makes it fun for her students.
