The class is time consuming , but I feel like because the actual class was so fun, the homework wasn't as bad as it could have been. She really goes above and beyond when helping!

She's awesome! She teaches well, will give you a hard time to show you that you can relax around her and she's very willing to help! Even if you haven't been trying in the past, she will help you no matter what! A+

I absolutely LOVE this lady. Russian is hard but if you go to class and try she will give you a C to insure you pass the class. She knows students struggle but she does what she can as long as you work with her on it. I would major in Russian if she taught every single class in the major. She doesn''t. You''ll love her.

Best professor I've ever had!! Hands down makes me want to be a russian professor. Professional, flexible but hard, you will learn anything you've ever wanted to know about Russia and more. She made language learning easy. She keeps things interesting every day in class and makes you want to give your best effort.

Dr. M is amazing! She is without a doubt the best professor I've had during my time at MU. I've had her for several classes now and she is also my adviser. I strongly suggest everyone take a class with her.

Quite simply the best and most professional educator I have ever worked with. I am a better student and a more enriched individual thanks to her teaching, patience and compassion. PLEASE come to her with questions, concerns, etc - all it takes is politeness and she will bend the world for you. Just make sure you give back the effort.
THE BEST.
She is very kind and grades fair! Monnier taught my first college discussion class and while I was very nervous to speak in front of so many intelligent students she was very patient and encouraging.

I took a few of her classes at the beginning of my college career.  After having very many professors throughout all these years, I know she is very smart, helpful and fair.  She really wants you to do well and will help in any way she can.  Great professor!
She loves Russia! She got on tangents, but she was pretty fun. I had her for GNHonors, so you have to go the readings, or you will be utterly lost during class.

Having taken French and Spanish in high school, Prof. Monnier provided the best foreign language instructional experience I have had. Amazing teacher! She is very understanding of the difficulty of Elementary Russian, study guides were provided, etc.

interested in student learning not for grades, but actually learning the material.  She wants you to come to class and if she can tell that you're thinking about the material then she'll give you good participation even if you don't talk in class.  class is easy if you are interested and even so if you're not. she was great.
Not my first or last class with Dr. M.  She is probably the greatest teacher of anything I've ever had.
Wonderful teacher.  I've had her a couple of times now and look forward to her classes.  She definitely requires participation and doing the work is necessary.
Discussion was always interesting, and she was very accessible outside of class.

She will call you out on any mode of laziness, which will make you recollect your elementary school days. I felt at times she wanted to grab me by the ear and send me to the principle. Though, these are not flaws, and reassure you there are still profs. at Mizzou that care about student interaction and academic success. Great overall professor.

I had her for Early Modern World- part of the honors humanities sequence and she was awesome. While she does like discussion (especially small groups which sometimes don't go so well) and expects you to work, she is fun, enthusiastic, and there's a good chance you'll see her at a bar one night!
Great teacher!!!  Energetic and excitable.  Invites student ideas and participation.  She's tough, but only because she expects the best from everyone.
The most accomadating professor ever!!!
No Comments
She is smart and she is hot!! Brains and sex appeal all rolled into one!

i dreaded going to his class everyday, lecture wasn't great and attendance was mandatory. tests were easy and only had 3 grades in the class (quiz, midterm, final). study guides are the exact test and tests are open note but also all open ended
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy history class. open note tests and quizzes with the exact the exact questions on the review guides as the actual tests. very knowledgeable professor as well. great course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are mandatory, exams and quizzes are essay based but he lets you know what to expect.

Do not take this class, so lecture heavy with a lot of information (typically unnecessary info) thrown at you. If you miss 3 classes, 20% of your grade is immediately removed. The only graded assignments are 2 exams, and 2 quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He talks way too fast and throws a ton of information at you in every lecture and doesn't post the slides after. There's two open note tests based on the lectures, a midterm and a final which are a few short answer questions and an essay question. There's also three quizzes based on assigned readings. I'd take another class if you can.
Best professor I've had yet.

Very lecture heavy, notes move SO FAST, I couldn't type fast enough. Lectures & notes aren't uploaded. Attendance is required and PASSED AROUND through the class. It got to a point where reading the actual constitution was easier than his notes. I filled out an entire bluebook during one test and extra credit is only 10 points for a two page paper.

His class is the worst I've taken in college. He makes you buy around 10 books for the class, only for us to talk about them for a week before moving on. He centers the class material around the topics he wants to write about for his next book rather than what the class says it will in the course description. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Benner is extremely kind, helpful, and supportive to all of his students. Even though students need to learn how to use different kinds of software alone, he is very flexible to work with; if you need extensions or help with projects, Mr. Benner is always there, and he tries his best not to make students feel bad for being behind or messing up.

Professor Benner is a genuinely good teacher and an understanding + kind person. Lets you turn in projects a little late if an interview fell through. Lots of group work + interviewing required (it's journalism.). Let us out of class early often. Lectures might be a little boring, but just do whatever and then answer when he asks questions.

My only genuine complaint is how often I walked all the way to class, for it to end 10 minutes later, classes could have been an email. You will have a new project every week, but Nic was amazing, and if he weren't my professor, I would not show up to this class, but I did every week. He's very understanding of late work and was an easy grader.
Great professor. If you are interested in film or photography, specifically, he would be a very good person to know. Thoroughly enjoyed the class and learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nick was a nice teacher. He was always available if you needed help. He grades fairly and gave good feedback.

Just had Nic this semester for J1200. He's talented & a great explainer. Went into the class with 0 knowledge about any of the software, but he helped all of us. He made the class fun and interesting, and he's overall just a really nice guy. Once freaked out because I turned in an assignment 5 minutes late- emailed him and got full credit.
Yeah don't take this class if you have other options

I am fighting for my life to hopefully end with a B-.  Homework, lectures, practice and previous tests have zero correlation to exams. He doesn't answer questions clearly. I would rather wake up for a 6 am lecture with anyone else than be in this class. If you have plans for grad school, do not take this class- it will tank your GPA and sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He teaches to students like everyone is a Chemistry Scholar. Be prepared to teach yourself everything.

He talks and riddles and you leave every lecture wondering what he was even on about. Then the exam is full of questions he never went over so unless you absolutely have to, do not take this class with him

Took this garhsart in the fall of 2016. 1 of the tsrow professors ever and sadly at the time I didn't know that you could drop classes.Don't waste your time with this gabmucs with a foot in the grave, if Idk how ylroop Mizzou ran things and delddoc their faculty I'd be surprised he still had a job

0 correlation between lecture/homework material and exams. It is impossible to know what is to be expected of you on each exam, and the practice exams are misleading. Class average generally falls between 55% and 65%. Your best bet is to take this class with a different professor.

Never in my life have I felt such dread for a test. He doesn't do any problems in class similar to the ones on tests, nor are they on the ALEKS. Lectures are almost impossible to follow, and have little to no correlation to whats on the test.

If you can, take chemistry with a different professor or at another school. Keller is passionate about chemistry but struggles with teaching and exam design. Practice and old exams don't match the current tests, which often include material not clearly covered in class and heavy interpretation of concepts. Proceed with caution.

Keller was the reason I changed my career course. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but on some Fridays he would sit us with our lab groups for a participation project. His homework took up most of my time. The honors kids who were in my lab said that we were learning the material more in-depth than they were. So if you want to pass, take honors.
Do NOT take his class. point blank.

He is very nice and really wants all of his students to learn and enjoy chemistry, but the tests are way too hard, and there's really no good way to study for them. Your best bet is study groups. Do the ALEKS homework.

He taught you nothing on the test in the lectures. You're gonna have to read the book yourself to survive.I would rather go to an 8 am chem class with another teacher every day than take a class from him.
I truly believe that Keller
i wished i got hit by a car every day.
Lectures were hard to follow

This class was very hard and lecture intensive, even though the lectures never had any correlation to tests or assignments. Very hard to study for tests, you are basically just guessing when studying, I would study the textbook or smart book assignments, which would help more than the lecture material. I fought for my life to get a B- in this class

You know that surfer dude vine where nothing mad enay sense? that exactly what having a class with keller is like. He is one of the most interesting people I have ever met in the worst way possible, he cannot answer a question, stay on task, or teach. It is honestly shocking he is still employed by the university. Even his own TAs hate him.
DO NOT TAKE IF KELLER IS YOUR PROFESOR. he does not stay on task and doesn't teach what is actually on the exams. I shit you not everything I have learned that is chemistry related I taught myself.

You are literally teaching yourself everything and doing a puzzle to try to figure out what he is even talking about and how any of this relates to the test or materiel  He goes off on tangents in class that make no sense so you are really just shooting in the dark when studying. genuinely find a way to talk this online or over the summer
DO NOT DO IT!!!!!!!!

Every time I would have a problem I would email him about hey times are tough and stressful and I accidentally missed the first assignment can I get an extension by one day and he never responded tried again and silence so when I wrote he was a bad teacher he then emailed me telling me to try his office hours and guess what not even there to help.

Genuinely if there is any way to NOT take this guy please do. Taking this course is like paying to teach yourself. The lectures and studying for his test is like putting together a puzzle, you are constantly guessing what is going to be on the test. He rambles on and on and dances around topics without ever fully covering them.
He is not a good educator.

Dr Steve Keller is so over hated, likely because chemistry is the only stem class many people have to take and is a very difficult subject. He is a deeply passionate professor and extremely accessible out of class. The ALEKS homework is brutal but is the only way to guarantee success. If you don't do the work the right way you will not pass.
Avoid at all costs.

Everyone says this class is so hard and Keller is a super tough grader. To be honest if you pay attention to what he says in lectures and actually show up, its not that bad at all. You have to study and actually put effort in, but it is possible to end with an A.
he is a terrible teacher and expects you to already know the subject. was put on probation a few years ago and somehow they hired him again. take anyone else but him

He is awful, I went to 4 different tutors for what was supposed to be a Chem 1 class. But in those meetings they informed me, They didn't know how to help, and that I needed a bio chem tutor instead. No student should have to feel the way they do in Kellers class. Please take my suggestion and get a different professor you will thank me later.

I had Keller for Chem 1 and 2; his class is hard but not impossible. The effort I had to put in to earn a good grade set me up for success in future courses. Go to office hours and lecture!!! On the practice exams, make sure you understand why an answer is correct. Use the learning center!! Keller picks the tutors he feels are best for the job!!

I took this class last semester and was scared because all that I have heard. I am now in orgo and Dr. Keller set me up extremely well. If you are wanting to go on and take much harder science classes, Dr. Keller gives an amazing chemistry foundation. I can see how people think he is hard, but hard work pays off! Also go to office hours.

Do not take a class with Keller. I promise you are better off waiting a semester if needed and changing your schedule around to avoid having him. He gives you practice exams you can understand then makes the entirety of the actual exam a trick question compared to it. You will at least one question on the real exam you've never seen before.

Absolutely one of the worst professors at Mizzou hands down. Unfortunately he's a very kinda man and I know he's intelligent but he is NOT a good teacher and can not clearly communicate ideas and almost never has his lectures be helpful for his exams.
Lectures and homework did not correlate at all to anything on the test. Very hard to follow, went to very many tutoring sessions and studied for hours, ended up with a C. :(

Dr. Keller is such an awesome professor and is super passionate about chem. My advice is to read the textbook information before lecture and then after lecture go to Dr. Keller's office hours with any underlying questions you have. If you just try in this class and study you will do great and don't be afraid to get extra help if you need it!

This class is extremely difficult and the tests make up a huge portion of your grade. The practice tests are a joke and the lectures are hard to follow. The homework takes hours to complete and has nothing to do with what you learn in lecture or on the test. Take Ganley if you can.

He should not be nicknamed "killer Keller"... he is kind, caring, and at the end of the day just wants you to be able to learn. Haters just don't like him because chemistry is a difficult subject and he is just the one who teaches it sometimes.

There are a lot of bad reviews on keller but truthfully he is a great professor. his class is not that hard and he even adds extra points for the many people who complain and do poorly. If you listen in lecture, do the ALEKS, and put some preparation in for the exams you will be fine. Some people aren't prepared to actually have to do work

Keller is a great professor. The homework you can complete till you get a 100%, and the tests are not very difficult. They are mostly word problems which use the same exact formulas mentioned in the lectures and practice exams. I didn't study too much and still ended with an A+ despite never having experience with anything past the first two weeks.
I hate chemistry and wouldnt take again. Keller was NOT the worst but this class required heavy outside of class work load that often became unmanageable

Do not take this professor for chem. He is passionate but his lectures are almost impossible to follow, his system of note taking isn't helpful, there are exams every 2 weeks it feels like and no matter how hard I study I always did poorly on exams. I would not recommend this class to anyone.

No extra credit. Grade is only tests and homework. I worked so hard and studied for days before each test and went to tutoring and barely passed the class. This class is set up for you to fail do not take it. Keller is a nice person but not a good entry level teacher. Don't recommend.

Very passionate about Chemistry and loves to teach it. A lot of things that he teaches are useful for further chemistry classes past Chemistry 1, however a lot of it is not needed for the Chemistry 1 class. If you put in the time to understand the homework and practice tests you will do well in the class. Attend lecture and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was scared to take this class at first because of the reviews. This class is definitely not easy, but if you do the supplemental readings, ALEKS problems, and practice exams you will have a better chance at the tests. Go to class even though attendance isn't mandatory. Dr. Keller is great and very easy to reach outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was legitimately one of the worst classes I've ever taken in my life. The practice tests are nothing like the exams so don't even try to study from those. I had friends in a different professor's class (Ganley?) and the exams were all homework problems and they got cheat sheets for all exams. Please do whatever you can to not take his class!!!

Legitimately one of the worst classes I've ever taken in my life. The practice exams look 1000% different so don't even try to study from those. I had friends who had the other professor (Ganley?) and their tests were exactly like homework problems and got a cheat sheet for exams but we got none of that. Do whatever possible to not take the class!!

Unlike what most people say this class was hard but really not that hard. I'm a stem major and it really isn't too bad for a stem class. Keller is passionate about chemistry and willing to help you so show up for office hours. However, I suggest taking chem 1 in the fall instead of spring with another prof because it doesn't have to be this hard.
Don't take a Keller class. It's absolutely terrible. He is not good teacher. He just talks to entertain himself and you will be lost 90% of the time. Also, he doesn't think he is the problem.

This professor is passionate, but not a good teacher. His material doesn't relate to the exams, which can be random and confusing. Practice exams were unhelpful, and I often failed despite studying. If you must take this class, consider online or community college options. I won't take another chemistry class with him. Beware of a lot of ALEKS hw!

I did not receive a single exam grade back that was accurate to what was put onto Canvas. Additionally, we are allowed a drop for our lowest exam. Instead, my HIGHEST exam was dropped putting me in a situation worse than before. I studies weeks before each exam but each question was unpredictable and no where near what was put on the practice exam.

Keller's class is extremely test-heavy—there are four exams (with the lowest one dropped), and the final, which constitutes about 70% of your grade. While some questions are related to the material covered, many feel random. Always have your tests reviewed by Keller, as they are often graded incorrectly by the TAs.

Will never understand the hate towards Professor Keller. He can be a bit fast-paced and a little condescending at times, but those are my only complaints. Do not go in thinking you are going to have a tough time, or else you will have a tough time. Practice tests give good idea of how actual tests will be.

Not good professor. Wait until you can take the class with a different professor. His lectures are disorganized and random, often not relating to test content. Save yourself pain and suffering and take it with a chemistry professor that teaches in a way that promotes learning, rather than confusion and anger.

He is extremely passionate about chemistry. He isn't a good lecturer for a College Chem I course. I feel he would be a better graduate professor. I taught myself everything in his course because his lectures are everywhere. The homework isn't hard, but the tests are hard. A 72 is his highest average for his tests. Study hard and get a tutor.

He never responds to emails and always has a line of people asking questions after lectures, so it's hard to reach him. Hard to study for exams and do homework when topics are not discussed in lectures. Showing up for class matters even though he doesn't take attendance, as you will be clueless otherwise.

His lectures are... confusing at best, the only good thing about them are how clear it is that he is passionate about what he does. His "office hours" are worse, he answers questions in a very roundabout way where you forget what you question even was by the end of him answering. Class is very ALEKS heavy, rely on your TA's and classmates instead.

I only took this professor for lab, not lecture. Holds about twice as many labs as other chem professors. Ridiculous grading criteria, expects professional level accuracy, and if you do not do everything perfectly, good luck getting a good grade. Labs are also not useful for the class; essentially a waste of 3 hours a week doing busy work.

Seems like sweet guy, but he cant teach. He skips foundation info, youre confused first day of the unit. He is too involved in chemistry and expects gen chem students to understand much higher level material. The exam grade averages are always either low D's or F's. Neither the homework or practice exam prepared me for the difficulty of the tests.

Don't bother attending his lectures, there is no structure to them and he explains literally nothing. Do the ALEKS homework, it's worth a lot but don't think it'll prepare you for the exam they are nothing like what you do on the homework. Do the practice exam diligently and pray

His lectures are disorganized and useless. He lacks any ability to take accountability. He typically blames the students for their poor performance without being able to acknowledge that he might have taught a subject poorly. Wait to take chem 1 through Ganley or just take it through a community college to avoid having to interact with this man.

I know know why he is called killer Keller.I went to office hours with my TA & him 3 times a week on top of meeting with an outside tutor who had taken his class before.I struggled immensely and I never had before in any stem class.His tests way so much on your grade same with his final which is worth twice the amount the bimonthly tests combined.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the worst class I've ever taken at Mizzou. Keller rambles during his lecture, and never come full circle with the point. I was confused af. The exams are not multiple choice and you will struggle.

Don't be intimidated by "Killer Keller". This is a big misconception about Keller. He loves what he does and is very passionate about chemistry. If you focus in lectures and study for the tests you will do fine. He has very enthusiastic lectures that are important to attend and stay caught up in. Great teacher for students who care.

I went into this class knowing that Dr.Keller was a tough proffessor and mentally prepared for that but i wouldent say there is a ton of hw. I use the hw as a studying tool and that helps. The test are much more indepth then what he teaches therefore you may want to take those extra steps on stuying.

If your major does not REQUIRE you to take this course, for your own sake do not take it. After hours spent in office hours and tiger tutoring, my test grades still have not improved. Everything on the test is application based, and a majority of the tests do not correlate to the lectures.
he has been on probation bc he struggles to teach and you basically have to teach yourself and his writing in class is just a bunch of scribbles
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult and he wasn't very helpful outside of class in office hours. I spent many of nights and mornings worrying and studying for his course. I used all of the resources he gave us and yet still got a C-.

Worst teacher ever. If you've never had chemistry, avoid this class. Tests have nothing to do with his lectures, and practice exams are useless. A test every three weeks is crazy—you won't learn. Attendance isn't required, but group projects are graded, so it basically is. Unfair grading, unclear expectations. Avoid!

Tests are nothing like the textbook, lectures, or homework. Be prepared to teach yourself everything and study for days just to leave the test feeling like you failed. Calculation test questions barely give you any info to work off of.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steve Keller has been on probation before and Im not surprised by this at all. He deserves to be fired, he doesn't provide/teach you any of the tools you need to pass his tests.
Been suspended for academic issues before absolutely do not take

The class is disorganized, and lectures are disjointed meshes of whatever Prof. Keller feels like talking about at any given point. He is extremely passionate about the topic, which could make him highly engaging but in this case only makes him struggle to be accessible to students who are not advanced in the field. Do not take this class.

This class is extremely disorganized. He jumps from topic to topic without building a foundation at the beginning. The tests have nothing to do with what is talked about in class and there is no structure. He does not teach but rambles. You will be teaching yourself most of the time. Kahn Academy and YouTube taught me everything.

I'll keep this as straightforward as possible with the limited word count:
Lectures are unorganized and difficult to follow
Tests are more difficult than the material learned in class
Lab is absurd and it seems like Keller and the TAs don't communicate
If you want to learn BASIC chemistry, you will not learn it in this class (i.e. use Khan Academy)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have not even finished this man's class yet and I am pissed. When I tell you Steven Keller does not know anything about teaching. Yes, he is a smart guy who knows chemistry, but he cannot translate this for beginners. I have never been so enraged by homework because he has never taught us the problems, nor does he acknowledge this.

I thought he seemed really nice and seemed to be a good professor. Turns out he just going on tangents in class and doesn't talk about what is actually important information. In class seems easy and understandable yet the tests are about stuff he never even mentioned once in class. ALEKS is not a good resource or teacher either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aleks is nothing like in-class lecture problems and his Test are very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I know a lot of people think that he is a horrible teacher and the class was bad, but if you really put in the work, it is possible to do well in class. I suggest using outside resources and Khan Academy if you are struggling. The tests are only five multiple-choice questions out of 30 I think, and the rest are free-response or solving.

A lot of people dislike Professor Keller and while I didn't think he was the best professor, I think he really tried and people that emailed, reached out, and went to the study hours did totally fine in this class. There's a lot of teaching yourself. Lectures were confusing and tests were hard. If you took high school chemistry you'll be fine.

Oh my god do not take this class unless you want to walk in to lecture and feel like u just go slapped in the face. I wouldn't even call his lectures “lectures” I'd call them rambles. The only thing that got me a decent grade was getting access from previous years tests and studying for 10+ hours for each exam. Prepare to be stressed out.
very nice guy, lectures could use some work he does ramble but still gets his point across. the tests are definitely difficult but with studying and paying attention in lectures it pays off.

worse professor r Ive ever had, every time I emailed him he always had a very smart remark and gave me attitude when I asked for an extension on an assignment to go to a funeral. Didn't give me an extension. TA was absolutely awful and I missed one lab and he bashed me in front of the whole lab about how I didn't go. Made me not want to come back.

Be prepared to have no idea what's going on and most likely rely on YouTube. Half the time you don't even know what you're learning because the notes do not correspond from day to day. He also grades assignments very differently. I don't know if it's the TAs or him, but they're a lot of test discrepancies

Between him rambling and trying to read his awful handwriting it is almost impossible to take any helpful notes. There is no point in studying the practice exams he provides because they never turn out to be like the actual exam. The only reason I am barely passing this class is because he gives assignments that are easy points.
If you take this class you better know how to follow along to tagents that dont go over anything thing on the exams.Also don't try and study the pratice exams they are nothing like the actually exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Horrible prof, doesn't even teach relevant content and study guides do not relate to any of the text content.

If you are able to take this class with anyone else you should. Extremely hard and test heavy and not very helpful during office hours. Lectures are hard to follow along and the tests are like 20 question MAYBE so you have to get so many correct. Also does not provide a study guide so hard to know everything for the test.

Yes this class is very hard. If you study and take vigorous notes on the lectures and participate, you should do pretty decent on all the tests. A lot of the people that drop this class only study before the test, you NEED TO BE STUDYING DURING THE WHOLE UNIT! I can be a lazy student too, and was just fine. Labs are pretty easy.

reviews and labs don't relate to the exams, he rambles on during lectures and jumps from topic to topic, his handwriting looks like literal scribbles most of the time. He seems like a nice guy but a HORRIBLE teacher for an entry level chemistry class.

-Harsh grader
-Labs don't correlate with lecture
-Test has nothing to do with lecture
-Doesn't explain things well
-You and your TA will be confused in the lab
-Only grades the hardest questions in lab and gives no credit for the easier ones

His class is tough, but if you go to office hours when you need help, start the weekly homework early, and read the text book BEFORE lectures, then you will be okay. Going to lectures is only helpful if you have some background knowledge of the material that will be covered, hence read the textbook. He is so nice and will answer questions!

Keller is extremely disorganized, making everything more difficult. Youll teach yourself everything in this course, because of careless errors in everything. Exams are nearly impossible, with errors and questions on content you haven't learned yet. Youll second-guess everything in here like you are being gaslit. Youll spend 300+ hours on homework.

Keller is completely unfit to be teaching this class. His lectures are incomprehensible and he only covers content a week after you already taught it to yourself from doing the homework. The ALEKS site is frustrating and he assigns a ridiculous amount to do each week. Tests never have anything to do with class. Do not take here.

He is nicknamed Killer Keller for a reason. Tests are horrible and make no sense and include none of the material he rambles about in class. Honestly don't know how he hasn't gotten fired because of how many students fail his class. This is an entry-level class and he acts like everyone is a chemistry major and knows everything. horrible.

This is my first time having Keller in any of my classes, and thought that everyone was just lying. I came from a background of harder classes in high school and a heavier workload with only one or two Bs in my life. WRONG. Exams are nothing, literally nothing like the lectures. ALEKS system has insane amounts of homework. DO NOT TAKE.
If you can take this class honors or with literally anyone else, do it. This caused way too much unnecessary stress. The TAs and homework points are the only reason I have a decent grade.

His lectures consist of him drawing arrows, circling, and scribbling all over the place.  It is impossible to read let alone understand the notes by the end.  If you have to take any of his classes, take them online somewhere else.  Topics on the exams are often introduced the week AFTER the exam.  The textbook and youtube are the only way to pass.

He literally told me he didn't know how to do the quadratic formula. THAT LITERALLY THE BASIS OF ALL THE MATH ON EXAM 2. He also "doesn't like power point" and scribbles down his notes on the projector. That is personally not my jam. But seriously, if he would just use powerpoint slides or something similar for his notes, he would be much better.
This class is extremely hard. The exams have questions over material that hasn't been covered yet. The wording of exams make it difficult to understand what is being asked.

I would sooner drop a class that he is teaching than give it a try. HE DID NOT TEACH THE FUNDAMENTALS OF CHEMISTRY WHATSOEVER! Unless you have already taken a chemistry course, can read his mind, and are able to sift though his disorganization- do yourself the favor and do not take any class he teaches. Tests would have new material on them too...

Yes, his tests are insanely difficult and he's unorganized. However, if I can do it, you can too! I HIGHLY recommend reading the textbook and taking notes. Try to do this before his lectures too, since they can be super confusing. I studied so many hours for this class and yep, it was horrible. But it is possible, you just have to work for it.

As you can see by his ratings, he's not a fan favorite... I personally thought he was very knowledgable and passionate about chemistry, but kind of too much. His tests and quizzes may seem easy to him, but not to his students. This was my hardest class by far. Keller is sometimes funny and is probably a good person, he's just too smart.
I've never met someone more condescending and rude in my entire life. Killer Keller lives to his name again. Absolutely slaughtered my GPA.

Professor Keller is so smart that some times it is difficult to understand what he is saying. He also throws a lot of information at you at once so you have to take pristine notes to understand what is going on. He records every lecture so it is important you go back and watch them before the test. His test are also very difficult.

Dr.Keller is incredibly brilliant. He's genuinely my favorite professor. He has a lot of passion for what he does. My only complaint is that the study guides don't seem to have much to do with the exams. The exams are extremally hard. However, he always gave us 10 mins to discuss the exam while having the a copy of the exam first.Chem is just hard.

Dr. Keller is incredibly intelligent, has dope fits, and he genuinely loves chemistry. However, it should be illegal for this man to write exams. Some things I saw for the first time on exams. He also is so disorganized that it is somewhat impressive. If you didn't have to take any of his classes, I am sure he would be awesome.

This professor stands true to his given nickname of "Killer Keller". He often leaves his students and TAs confused about what they are supposed to do in the lab. His exams are over things that you are either taught about the class before and are presented in ridiculous ways that makes it hard to understand what he's asking you to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor does not actually teach. He talks at you in a rambling way and makes fun of the few brave students that actually ask questions. The entirety of the school, including people not taking the class and other professors, know him as "killer Keller" -- and with good reason. Calling the man a teacher is offensive to teachers everywhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has the name Killer Keller for a reason. His lectures you learn nothing pretty much and the best way to do good on the test is by reading the textbook on your own before the test. The test questions are terrible too, he shouldn't be aloud to write a test. Also at the end he hits you with a group project to work on outside of class which sucks.
He rambles too much and doesn't provide sufficient explanations on topics. He is very unclear on what is going to be on exams. If you want to learn you have to teach yourself outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will "learn" the material for the test the class before. He doesn't follow any section of the book and leaves you wondering what the test is even over. His lectures jump all over the place. He is a kind man, but a really bad professor. There are multiple opportunities to contact him through office hours and other times however.

The rumors about him are 100% true. His lectures make zero sense and his tests do not follow his lectures. He is an extremely hard grader and will take off points if key words aren't used. He does not give you any time to study, as he teaches new material a few days before the tests. Goodluck.

Keller is honestly the worst professor I've ever had. It's like he wants us to fail. He gives us no time to study for exams, is not helpful when asking questions, and will quite literally laugh at you when handing back an exam if you don't do good (happened to me this year). Overall, do not take his class if you want to keep your sanity lol

This class is awful. Keller is the absolute worst. Half the material he presents is hypothetical and will fly over your head. The exams are completely unfair, the lab rubrics are constantly being revised and handed out right before it's due, there is ZERO communication between him and the TA's. Our test average had to be curved 20% so we could pass

Even in an upper level class he was an awful teacher. I'm sure he knows his stuff, he seems like a very smart many, but he cannot teach for his life. The practice exams included topics that were sure to not be on the exam, it was never clear what would be asked of us on the exam, and he would do theoretical problems that made no sense.

He teaches the class as if we have doctorates in chemistry, even though this is an entry level class. Anyone that doesn't have background knowledge in chem, good luck to you. Practice exam is nothing like the actual exam. Very last minute as well, not enough time given to learn topics. He teaches stuff the day before the exam.
This man just speaks words, half of the time doesn't even make sense

He is hated on a lot on campus because the class is difficult. However it is the only class I have ever had where I feel like I learned and knew what was happening. Material after tests wasn't forgotten. He is very nice and a wonderful person just shouldn't be making tests!

He clearly cares about research and wants you to care about chemistry. Unfortunately, he struggles greatly with the entire teaching aspect. Tutoring alone got me through. Once told me in response to a question "It's not magic, its chemistry. I put the numbers on the board bc they made sense" Do not recommend
Amazing guy and super smart, but his exams are ridiculously difficult.
Keller is not this big bad guy students try to make him. His class is difficult, but it will teach you a ton and it is very doable. Study as you go and you will be in good shape.

Don't let other scare you about Dr Keller. He got me interested in chemistry even though I'm a bio major. He can be aggressive in some aspects but his class isn't impossible, just time consuming. His tests are difficult, though you'll do fine if you studied a week in advance. Complete and learn from the homework

Keller doesn't make chem accessible, especially for an intro course. Tests aren't impossible, but require heavy studying for a week before each one. Lectures aren't mandatory but attend every one or you'll be completely lost. What saved my grade was reading the textbook section and taking notes before the lecture over that section the next day

Dr. Keller originally scared me. His tests are hard, but if you're good at thinking on your feet they are definitely doable. He is very good at what he does, and is extremely knowledgeable and willing to help you. His voice is loud, enthusiasm is high, lectures are enjoyable. Looking back now I WISH he could teach the rest of my chemistry courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Before I took any class with him I heard a lot of negative things but after two semesters I thought he was not bad at all. His lectures are pretty engaging and he is very willing to help. The one negative thing I'd say is that his tests are very difficult, but with all the other components that go into the final grade most people easily pass

No doubt that Professor Keller is very passionate and intelligent within his field, however, the mental turmoil this class caused me is unmatched. Tests are extremely difficult and nothing like the lectures/homeworks. You're left to do difficult labs with little guidance. No curve at end.

Safe to say the ones that made it through are trauma-bonded
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller, although he knew the material, struggled to explain it efficiently and often gets sidetracked when teaching. He is very bad at updating grades on time, and his tests are nothing like what you get in the lectures. Good luck to anyone taking his Chem 1 class.

This class was by far the worst class I have ever taken in my life. The tests are near impossible. The labs are ridiculous. Dr.Keller is quite possibly one of the smartest people I have ever met. However, that does not make up for the disaster this class is. This may be the class that takes me out of STEM. Does not update grades.

Professor Keller is very passionate about chemistry, and it shows. It is very important to apply yourself, read the book and complete the homework/practice tests. He gives many points out besides test points to help your grade and grades with 1/2 credit as well. This is a tough class, but we are not in high school anymore.

Keller is amazing! I was intimidated by his reputation at first, but it is not accurate. Tests are 100% manageable, just make sure you truly understand the material not just memorize notes. He is super accessible outside of class and is a great lecturer. Chemistry is just a difficult subject. Attendance is only required for certain classes.

GO TO LECTURE! The tests are hard and if you skip lecture you will not succeed. Study hard for the tests, go to his review sessions and ask questions, and do the practice tests. The class average on all the tests is a failing grade, but he curved them 5 points. Be prepared. He is very passionate, but the material in class is not what is on the test
Lectures were helpful.  Manageable amount of homework.  Difficult exams if you don't go through the practice exams.

It is clear that professor Keller is extremely passionate about chemistry, however I definitely do not recommend taking his class. The exams are awful and look nothing like the homework or material discussed in class. If you like crying take Keller's class.

Professor Keller makes lectures interesting and makes you feel that you understand the material... Until you take the exam. When I took the practice exam, I realized I did not understand the material to the extent that he required. To study, I read the sections of the textbook that the exam was covering. DON'T TREAT THIS CLASS LIKE HIGH SCHOOL.
Worst teacher I have ever had. DO NOT ever take chem with him.
Everyone loves him until the first test... Incoming freshman beware
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everyone loves him until the first test
Dr. Keller is very considerate of his students. I am glad I took his class.
The worst teacher I have ever had since I have been in school.

Keller is knowledgable but horrible at conveying his knowledge. 100% the worst professor/teacher I have had. He over explains things that are too complex for the class to grasp and then skims over the foundations for these concepts. I feel cheated paying for this class because I am teaching myself everything and hiring a tutor to pass.

Dr. Keller is a really understanding guy and gives a lot of resources. You just have to apply yourself. He's pretty old fashion too, but he records all of his lectures and gives his students a lot of ways to succeed.

I think taking this class as a freshman was definitely a learning curve for a lot of people. Though he is a passionate teacher, his passion doesn't make up for the lack preparation he gives us for the exams.

I feel like I can't complain because I ended the course with a grade higher than most of my friends; however, this class was the absolute worst. The tests were unnecessarily difficult and while Keller is very knowledgeable, he doesn't always do the best job at describing concepts. I recommend tiger tutors and doing homework before he lectures on it

If your gonna be an engineer, I do NOT recommend this professor!! No matter how many times you can go to him, he will not curve your grade or give you points for anything. I got all Ds and Fs on the tests and failed with a C- but his tests are so stupid! The tests are mostly stuff you didnt learn. To pass this class, take it at community.

if you're considering taking this class at MU please take it else where. The amount of stress this class brings as a 1000 level course is absurd and not worth it. Good professor but with the exam averages being F's and low D's it speaks for itself. Its not an impossible course but I wouldn't recommend it.

He explains what formulas are and not how they relate to each other and references concepts for other classes constantly rather than staying on task, so be prepared if you are someone who learns this way to form study groups or hire a tutor. He is very intelligent, but he can't bring it down to an introductory chem level.

I took his honors tutorial on climate change, so my experience is very different from those who took his CHEM 1320 or 1330 sections. In this smaller class setting over a subtopic that he's very passionate about, he was very sociable and easy to get along with. I didn't have to take one of his infamous exams, but up-close he's a really genuine guy.

I put in more work for this class then the rest of my classes for the YEAR combined. Extremely hard- spent every free second on this class and still couldn't get an A... Tests are not weighted and the averages are all 55-60%. You can study every single line of notes and practice exams for days and still will struggle ot get above a 70% on exams.

While a lot of people bash on his teaching and difficulty of tests, I found that if you do more than the bare minimum and you really prepare for his tests using the textbook, you can get A's and B's on them. I think he is a really nice guy but loves chemistry a little too much to be teaching an intro class. His knowledge is unmatched.
extremely difficult.

Tests are very hard. Lectures are all over the place, and during the week of a test there is a huge workload. You have a lab due, about 5 homework assignments due, lectures, and a test to study for. His lectures are all over the place which makes notes hard to understand and study from. Tests are hard, lab does not go with lecture until weeks later

Keller has a reputation throughout mizzou and it is well earned. His tests are extremely hard. He is very passionate about chemistry but sometimes that can lead to him skimming through certain topics which results in the whole class being lost. Be prepared to not have an A. And go to all of the labs, that's your only hope for improving your grade.

If you have this professor here is what you need to do: TRY TO TAKE ANYONE ELSE. When that doesn't work pray you get a good TA and rely on your lab and homework grades. These tests are impossible it doesn't matter how much you study he will throw in topics not covered in lectures. Lectures are sporadic and don't help on tests.
Broke my heart. I was a pre med major... wanted to be a doctor. Now I'm a business major.

Keller is known for his extremely tough tests, however, they are not unreasonable. I was able to get an A on every test with a day of studying beforehand. You just have to REALLY understand the chapter, not just memorize facts. He is a great lecturer and you are able to miss most classes, as he posts lectures online as well.

Keller is a nice guy overall but his exams are horrible. I only got a B because I made sure to stay on top of my labs, small group, and homework assignments. The average for the tests never goes above a D. How you know his tests are hard is when you go to tutoring and they don't even know the answer.

I would prepare for his exams up to 5-7 days in advance, studying everything that I possibly could. Even though all the time and effort I put into the class meant nothing. Keller doesn't set his students up to succeed. I do not recommend ever taking a class with him and if you have the option to take it over summer then do that.

I stayed up and spent the night in Ellis so many times. Studied for HOURS and way too far in advance just to get 50s and 60s on the exams. If you get Keller just give up and get plastered instead. Better living your life at Willies instead of at your dorm crying!
You thought this was an intro class, lol.

His lectures are so abstract and hard to follow because of how 'passionate' he is. He will never give you a direct meaning of anything -- even questions if you ask them. The lectures don't give you clear material to reference in the future since they are so broad and ramble-y. Tests are basically mind games for him. Prepare to learn from Youtube.

Keller is a great professor that really cares about students actually understanding material and not just the regurgitation of it. There are multiple times a week to get help on material and homework with either TAs or the professor. The tests are brutal, but he gives old tests as study guides and drops the lowest grade which helps a lot!

I honestly don't know why the university still allows this guy to teach. It's an intro level, yet he makes the tests more difficult than anything you'd see in a 4000 level class. He's all over the place in lecture, so it's frustratingly difficult to know what he's talking about half the time. Take chemistry at a community college if you can.

Keller has crushed my dreams of continuing my career in stemThis class is like nothing else. His lectures are all over the place, he never finishes a topic and you have to teach yourself all of the content. He seems to be very passionate about chem but forgets that this is an intro class. Tests are hard and dive deep into concepts barley covered
Very very tough professor. Loves what he teaches and is a good person but not a good professor. Even with perfect attendance it is easy to find yourself lost in what he is teaching.

Professor Keller's tests are going to be hard. The test average was under 60 percent on all three tests. He grades on a total points system so it is hard to determine your grade mid-year. Make sure to try hard and do well on all labs and homework assignments. His lectures are interesting but reading the textbook to understand ideas is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take any other professor. If all other professors classes are full, wait a semester. You cannot trust this man. He holds review sessions where he misleads students on what to know for the test, but the tests are very abstract. You will be tested over very specific questions which you have never seen before. Heads up - first test is insanely hard.
Awful tests, decent lectures. If you took ap chem youll get an a, if youre a stem major youll get a b, if youre anything else, good luck.
Hes a very smart guy but not a great teacher. Look for outside resources for better explanations on topics and rewatch lectures.

Keller is very passionate about chemistry, but not a good teacher at all. He uses random problems and numbers which makes lectures every confusing. Labs dont correlate with course material. Homework isnt helpful. He didnt even respond to my emails. Basically, learned his whole course in the first three weeks of chem 1330 easily. Horrible teacher
Exam's will be unclear and nothing like previous semester tests. Note taking is hard to follow.

This class seriously stole all my passion for science as a science major. Left me feeling inadequate, frustrated, and like a failure. I've always been an A student, studied about 10+ hours for exams, and still failed. Literally sent me back to therapy. He's a passionate lecturer but gets off on making his tests have nothing to do with his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exams are unnecessarily hard. These kinds of professors crush dreams and work ethics.

Keller wouldn't let me turn an assignment in late when I had a death in my family. My family member died on a Sunday when our Aleks was due. He told me that "I had all week to do it so it should have been done already." Terrible professor and terrible person honestly.

Keller seems like a nice guy and the material seems understandable until you take the first test and realize it has hardly anything to do with the material at hand. Thinking about this class makes me nauseous and discouraged me greatly
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Test averages were all Fs and he didnt do anything about it

Keller is a super nice guy and he's clearly enthusiastic about chemistry. But the lectures/lab/homework don't help for the tests. Don't take this class. If you can wait until another prof is teaching then I highly suggest that. You'll be fighting to save your grade the entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The exams are pretty unpredictable because the lectures, labs, and homework are all different levels. The labs hold a lot of weight in your grade, so do well on those and it'll help outweigh your exam scores. I struggled through the class but somehow ended with an A. He curved some exams and a little bit at the end, but nothing is set in stone.

Keller makes his tests very difficult, but it isn't impossible to do well. the best way to study is to find old exams, fully understand each of the problems, as well as doing good in labs to boost your grade. Keller does have interesting lectures and doesn't seem bad at first, but his test averages are low so you will have to work for a good grade.
DO NOT TAKE!! I repeat, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!

Every single bad review on here is spot on, and this is by far the worst class I've ever taken. The tests are killer and will leave you fighting to save your grade and sanity. You will not be given any kind of material that even comes close to the test material so take the practice tests he gives you with a grain of salt. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a horrible person and a worse professor. Do whatever you can to avoid this class. He was so rude and shamed me in front of other students during office hours for not understanding a concept we covered in class. This class was detrimental to my mental health, and I advise anybody considering taking this class to STAY AWAY
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Keller clearly loves chemistry and did a good job at keeping people engaged during lectures. The labs were enjoyable and the content never seemed unbearable. But then we would have a test. The tests were everything he had ever talked about in lecture but on steroids. Its a good class to take to learn how to study for a stem test.

professor keller himself seemed nice and his lectures werent bad but outside of this, the class is terrible. i relied heavily on hw assignments to teach me the lessons that would actually be tested. exams are extremely difficult if you didnt know chem before and i failed every single one. if youre taking this class, good luck youll need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Keller is the worst professor imaginable for a chemistry ONE course. The topics are simple yet the way he taught it and the way he forms his test questions are nearly impossible to understand (even the TAs agreed). Hes a great guy and passionate about chemistry , just the worst professor Ive ever experienced, and completely unapproachable.
A a lot harder than an introductory level chem class should be.

This is by far the worst class I've ever taken. I had 100% in labs and assignments, but couldn't pass a single exam. If you can take this class with anyone else definitely do it because this was not worth it at all. Really regretting not taking it in high school.

Pros: 1. Nice and enthusiastic guy 3. TAs were helpful Cons: 1. Tests were bad (Lots of unnecessary trickery) 2. Pre-labs were bad (labs were better) 3. Poor at teaching (Highly irrelevant conceptual topics) I took this class 4 yrs ago, and I can safely say it was my hardest class. My only C+. I still love chemistry, but that was a huge blow.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Keller gets a bit of a bad reputation for his class being extremely difficult, but I disagree. His class teaches you time management and forces you to learn how to study quickly. Keller's lectures are engaging--he goes into great detail, so you have to pay attention. He is a really nice guy too. Be ready to work! (it is really worth it!)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is not what you would think an introductory chem class would be. Very difficult and teach yourself most of the material. If you have taken previous college chem classes you will be okay, but still struggle some. Try to find previous test other than the one he gives. Haven't figured out how to study yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst chemistry teacher at Mizzou. Tests are hard af and he gives so much homework and the labs are so time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures bounce from topic to topic and don't follow the structure of the textbook. The only positive thing was that the textbook was online and easy to access. Not helpful with study materials for the test and the tests are not usually about the material discussed in class. Lectures were however posted online which was helpful.

Nice guy but his class sucks. I don't find lectures very helpful. If you want to pass practice the homework problems in the textbook. Very challenging course for myself and my friends in the class. Beware: the tests are very difficult, so start studying well in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Is the worst professor that I have ever had. Makes everything so much un needed work. This class was my thirteenth reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Keller is bad at lecturing, and the tests always seem like they have things that are never taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Seriously so disappointing. I was really excited to learn at the beginning of the year. I only have to take Chem1320 for my degree, but he treats this class as if it's a 4000 level class. Tests aren't weighted, study guides are useless, and communication is very poor. Lectures are dry, and his tests are created with no regards to the student.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Keller is a nice guy but his lectures are all over the place and dont cover everything you need for the exam. For me i practically live in the building where the TAs and Keller had office hours and Im still barely passing right now. The labs are very time consuming so is the homework. I spend about 6 hours a day on this class.

I've had professor Keller twice now and both classes I've had have been horrible. His lectures are all over the place and there's a lot of homework that takes hours to do each week. His tests are even worse. I hope I never have to take his class again as he has been the worst professor or teacher I've had. The labs are horrible with no instructions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unless you've already done college-level chemistry, don't expect to breeze through this class. Go to lecture/lab, take notes, read the textbook, do the homework and go to office hours and you'll be fine. Be ready to settle for your grade in this class, he doesn't do extra credit and everything is "point based only", meaning there's no curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Keller gets a bad rap because his tests are hard, but if you show up to class and go to office hours you should get at least a B in the class. He is bad about responding to emails and putting homework in the gradebook though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Keller is by far the worst teacher I have ever had. I am a transfer student so I have had my fair share of hard teachers. His lectures are dull and boring. Exams are very hard there is no way to actually prepare for one. This is a weed out course! Avoid Keller!! Good luck you need it! All the other negative reviews are true! BEWARE!

Chem 1320 was the first chemistry course I had ever taken. The homework assigned was reasonable and you could use your textbook to help figure out homework answers. When it came to exams the questions were written at higher levels and it felt like there was no way to properly prepare if you are someone that prefers to use study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You need to know more than just the basics. When studying you have to know things inside and out. Most students take this class twice.

I liked Professor Keller but his class was very difficult. You will be fine if you take it and devote lots of time outside of class working on strengthening your knowledge. I did have to teach myself or go to TA office hours often to make sure I had a firm understanding of concepts after lecture.
he was an absolutely horrible professor and I feel as if I got nothing from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He poured a lot of passion into his lectures. I really loved learning the basic materials that he covered. Unfortunately his tests are beyond complex and cover far more than what he offers to study. Youll have to do more than just studying homework, having good notetaking skills, and attending lectures to be able to pass his tests.

Holy hell. He is the worst professor I've ever had in the entire time I've been in college. He goes over the basic portions of his material and tests you like you've studied it for WEEKS UPON WEEKS. I'll tell you why you have a large amount of people dropping chem. It's because you make students put in so much work for a 100 LEVEL CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are just amazing, he teaches everything in detail! He is passionate about his field. You can find him easily and ask a question. His exams are bit difficult, this gives you the motivation that you should study harder. He is so caring and inspirational.

Professor Keller gets a bad rap. The class is difficult YES, but he's trying to challenge you to make you a better student. He's passionate and explains things well, and he posts lectures on ponapto. Just do the OWL homework and study and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy and clearly loves what he teaches but I feel like he expects you to already know what is going on. Exams were very difficult and I feel that the practice exam did not help gauge how well you would do. He offers lots of outside class help so definitely attend those if needed. I just wish he made it easier to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: He's honestly a great professor, I blame my grade on my lack of motivation and not showing up to lectures. You HAVE to show up and do practice problems on your own or the exams will be very difficult. He teaches everything that is on the exams and is super flexible on adjusting the material if the class as a whole needs it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was warned about Professor Keller but he turned out to be a great instructor. He is very passionate about this subject and is also very approachable if you have any questions. I never found his tests to be overly confusing or full of trick questions. The only thing I had a big issue with was his inconsistent grading schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved and hated this class. Keller is a hard professor to like because he seems like a great person but it is difficult to actually learn from him.
