ONE OF THE MOST CHALLENGING CLASSES I'VE EVER TAKEN. PROFESSOR KELLER IS A GREAT PERSON AND DECENT TEACHER BUT HE ASSUMED WE KNEW FAR MORE THAN WE DID COMING INTO MIZZOU. I'VE NEVER TAKEN HARDER TESTS IN MY LIFE.

I would study for a solid 2 days & its a lot easier when u have a group of people just talking out the material. When taking notes, be sure to note what he repeats bc thats test material. His tests are mostly essay, thats why talking about the topics helps bc then i always wrote that down to get credit. Don't be lazy with labs bc those r easy pts
Okay-ish class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not going to lie, this class is very hard, you will have to study and put in a lot of work. Keller is a very good teacher, he genuinely will do everything he can to help you. If you take his class, add him on facebook, Prof. Keller.

So here's the deal with Keller. He teaches honors chemistry so he's used to being a harder teacher. He's a really nice guy and very enthusiastic about the class, but the tests are not what you would expect from an entry level course. Keller loves essay questions and seeing how you think. This class is tough, so no cutting corners with Keller.
Tests are impossible. They are all essay questions. You really need to read the book in order to pass the class. The teacher is very nice and super into chemistry.
Do not expect to do well in this class, he provides practice exams but they are not at all helpfull
Taught me a lot about chemistry and being a scientist

Kellers lectures are PAINFUL and the exams are impossible. My only saving grace was my amazing TA in lab section. With such a huge class, it is very hard to get one on one time with him to ask questions and if you are lucky enough to meet with him, he will give very vague answers. The exams somewhat follow lecture but READ THE BOOK.

Keller is sooo enthusiastic about what he teachers.  Lectures kind of pertain to the tests but  you really HAVE TO READ THE CHAPTERS in full detail.  If he talks about something in class, you better make sure to find it in the book and read about the fine details, because the fine details will be on the test.  Learned so much!

Wonderful professor, his exams are very difficult but as long as you put something logical he will give you some points for the answer. Make sure you attend class and lab and you should be able to pass with a B. He is also willing to go out of his way to help you out so make sure you reach out to him.

Although he seems to be a nice guy, his class is impossible. No matter who hard you study or try to prepare for his tests, most everyone in my lab section has failed. The assignments, labs, and quizzes are the only things that saved me from total failure.

Be prepared to study for days and still only get a c or d on the test. Great professor, but he does not take his class lightly. His tests consist of about 15-17 questions that are from lectures, the book, and random online assignments. Definitely not an easy class.

Dr. Keller is an amazing professor. He really cares about his students and their success. The class was really hard, but not impossible. It takes a lot of time outside of class to be good at it. I took his honors course two semesters in a row, and I'm glad I did. I feel like I learned a lot more taking his class than I would with another professor.

First things first, Dr. Keller is a super friendly guy. However, the class is much too difficult for a course made for non-chemistry majors. The exams are extremely hard & they are mostly short answer.  He does not go over many things that are on the exams in lecture. My TA apologizes to us every week for how hard he makes it. Nice guy though.

I just finished my second semester with Dr. Keller in three separate classes. You will never find a more enthusiastic professor. While his test may be "impossible" it is still possible to get a good grade. I received a B my first semester and found out how I needed to study (in all classes). Great professor who interacts with the students. 1010

Good Professor. Effort will need to be put in though to succeed! He makes Honors more challenging by adding extra projects that sometimes work and sometimes don't. The toughest part of this class is probably the tests, which really test your knowledge on the subjects and are not simply recall.

If you can avoid Dr. Keller, do so at all costs. His students either admire or loathe him & there's no in-between. His tests are unbelievably challenging for an introductory chem course. He talks in circles & the rare times that we have assignments he tears the class apart and says everyone's wrong. Apparently, that's his definition learning.

He's a tough professor. You'll need to go the extra mile by practicing on your own. Luckily my TAs were fantastic. You must keep up with the chapters, and DO NOT underestimate his tests. He talks in a circle, and class will run over 80% of the time. Unless you excel in chem, I would take regular, and get your honors credit elsewhere.
Super difficult tests and they're usually pretty long.  However, he is super helpful and willing to meet with you to answer questions. His TA's are also very helpful and super friendly.

Dr. Keller is always coming up with new ways to help you learn (help sessions, study groups, small assignments), and you do learn, but you still will likely do poorly on his tests.  The tests are nearly impossible, and people cry during them.  "Honors" to him means harder to get an A.  He held attention well for an 8 am, and was quite entertaining.

He will make you work hard  but in the end it's worth it. I understood chemistry so much better than I ever thought possible in high school. He offers a ton of time outside of class for help. However, you have to be willing to put in the work. Definitely get the book for this class and READ IT even though its not mandatory to do it. Saved my grade.

interesting lectures as in he could keep me awake at 8 a.m. I was impressed by his availability; he has regular office hours and even responds to texts after 10 p.m. However, his tests are ridiculously hard, and his idea of "honors" is to assume the class has already mastered the first five chapters. Don't do honors unless you know and love chem

Dr. Keller is all over the place in his lectures. He jumps around from different sections of the book and always says things like "well- nevermind, I wont explain that now, we'll see this later on in chapter 6" or something like that. He is very passionate and excited about chemistry, but unless you have a LOVE for chemistry, 1330h is not for you.

This class is very challenging. The test are extremely hard and are full of questions that do not have a straight forward answer. He often cancels his office hours and is not very approachable. You better be prepared to do a lot of studying and teach yourself.

Prof Keller is a very interesting guy who tried to keep class fun! But be warned the class is hard and requires a lot of study time but it is totally possible to get an A! Read the textbook and the problems in it, sometimes he uses problems from the book on tests, ALWAYS go to lab!

Definitely a hard class. His tests are nearly impossible and very hard to study for. They are hypothetical questions that he makes up himself, so you have to know the concepts very well and know how to apply them to everyday life. Going to class helps a lot. He doesn't email back and isn't has his office hours half the time.

I'm sure he's a good guy, he's just too smart to be teaching a beginning chemistry course.  The final grades are on a curve and I thankfully came out of that class with a C.  Very difficult class and I can honestly say I learned almost nothing new, not that I knew anything beforehand about chem, but still!  Just be careful with the course!

Very funny and enthusiastic guy but boy does he make you work for an A. Do good on labs and quizzes and homework because his test averages are around a 60%. Very hard and inconsistent with lectures, he likes to throw curveballs. Dont take it if your looking for an easy A, but if your interested in chem hes a good teacher
One of the best professors I have ever had.  Not a pre-med killer if you're willing to work hard, and probably one of the best people to know on campus.

While I wanted an A, Keller made me work hard and taught me how to study better than I ever would have learned here. once you've had keller, everything else seems easier and you're probably more prepared than those who didn't have him. good guy for a recommendation letter too

Dr. Keller is absolutely the best professor I have ever had. His class is definitely a challenge and the exams are very difficult, but you will learn so much from it. I got an A both semesters by doing and thoroughly understanding every book problem and practice exam. Prof. K is also extremely easy to access by email, facebook, or office hours!!!

One of the most impressive science teachers I ever studied with. Pushes students to learn and go beyond memorization and regurgitation, something I feel is lacking in most instructional institutions these days. I would gladly take another course with this professor. Those who just want an "easy A" don't realize what they're losing in the process.

Dr. Keller is by far one of the most available professors on campus. ALWAYS there to lend a helping hand. He's knowledgeable about the material as well as enthusiastic. If he doesn't know something he will find out and get back to you promptly. Tests are hard, but fair. You get as much out of a class with him as you put in.

Keller is one of the best professors I've ever had. He will joke constantly in class and is always willing to help you. His tests are very impossible but I've learned more about chemistry in a semester then I did my entire two years in high school. He will definitely prepare you for years to come.

Keller will kill you with his "nice guy" persona. He will talk to students on facebook, joke during lectures, even keep up with students at games. However, speak to any upperclassman and you will learn why he is dubbed the "pre-med" killer. He has been on probation for failing students, he will give you tests that have no relevance to class. Switch

This was the hardest honors class I have ever taken. His lectures and notes are easy to follow but they have nearly no relevance to the test. His tests are absolutely impossible. They are 20x harder than in-class examples. People cry during the test. If you want to have a decent GPA at all DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Take regular.

Dr. Keller is absolutely the best professor I have ever had. He is extremely passionate about Chemistry and knows the topic frontward and backward. His exams are very difficult, and he will thoroughly test your understanding of the subject. However, he makes himself extremely available all the time and is extremely helpful and fun to talk to!
He is super nice and helpful and smart and he is a fantastic person and fun to talk to. His tests are crazy.

This guy is one of the teachers that you can tell loves Chemistry. He is very passionate about it and is extremely willing to help if you go get help. But his exams are the most ridiculous tests I've ever taken. I hardly passed. I would study for 2 weeks in advance and still get a low C at best. If you want to be successful, GO TO LECTURE.

He is very passionate about chemistry and is a great lecturer - maintaining student interest at 8 am is very hard. He has high expectations of his students' ability to problem-solve on tests which makes them hard. It will take a little while to get used to the way he writes tests but once you do, it's a bit easier. DON'T MISS LECTURE!!!

All I can say is: Do well on all of your labs and quizzes because those will be the only things saving your grade. Tests are quite impossible. They don't have anything covered in lecture on them. So if you hate chem, take this with someone else. Your GPA will not look so pretty afterwards.

This guy is really nice, wants students to learn, &is passionate about chem. However, his exams were way out of the ballpark of what was lectured. Insanely difficult. Avgs were usually 60%. He is on probation & I understand why now. GPA Killer at its finest. Please take heed if you don't like chemistry. Even if you do, his tests can be impossible.

By far worst professor I have ever had at Mizzou. Yes he may be passionate about Chemistry but his test are absolutely ridiculous. I read and did every problem and understood the material very well until I went to the exam and knew nothing!. I recommend never to take this class it will ruin your GPA.
Really hard class. He is a great teacher but makes his tests very challenging. You will be lost if you don't go to class or watch the tegrity.

Prof K is one of my favorite professors! He genuinely cares about his students- he holds help sessions and made a facebook group to help keep us updated/connected with things. The material is a little difficult and he makes it slightly ambiguous as to what you need to study, but if you attend lectures and go to his help sessions, you will succeed!
Stay AWAY! He made the tests the complete opposite of what you learn in class to see how you can apply what you "learn" to different material. WHAT?? not okay..

2 midterms and 1 final. He tries to trick you on all the tests and does not test over what he lectures about in class. However, he is very helpful and available. I nearly failed all of the exams but still ended with a B in the class because the labs and quizzes bring your grade up (if you do good on them)
DON"T DO IT. Worst teacher ever, worst class ever. Material won't match tests and it will kill your GPA

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!! It is my hardest class out of everything I'm taking, it is a gpa KILLER and his tests don't reflect the notes or lectures. He always puts random topics on the test that we HAVN'T talked about in class or in the notes or book and just expects us to know them! Take it with another teacher and save yourself!

Let's just say his exams have absouletly NOTHING to do with anything he teaches in class. He will lecture on and on about one subject and it will be nowhere to be found on the exams. When you ask him for help, he makes you feel like a complete idiot for even asking. Avoid this professor at all costs!
Do not take this class with this teacher. He is so difficult and he is no help at all even if you go in for extra help.  this is a gpa killer. take it with a different teacher.

Keller seems like a really nice guy however I dreaded going to this class everyday.  this class was very hard and the TA's were not helpful at all.  All the labs that we did we a joke and pointless.  Not a class that you can cram for the test the night before.

Definitely a challenging course. I did terrible on the first test but got a tutor and ended up finishing the semester with a solid B. Know how to apply the equations to different situations than the ones he gives you in class, because the ones on the tests are more challenging.

Keller is very enthusiastic and knows what he is talking about. He tries to do too much during the semester. I lost a lot of respect after our third test: the class average was 20 points lower than tests 1 and 2 and many students? grades dropped 6-7%. He admitted that there was material on test 3 that was not covered in class. Good luck.

Keller's a great teacher. He aims to challenge his brightest student, so don't think this is a walk in the park. Go to his office hours. I wish I went more. He helps you out, you get to know him really well, and he's a really cool prof. Become more than just a name on blackboard. Add him on facebook and become besties. Hahah. Seriously.
Keller is very passionate and engaging. He also cares about student learning. The class is difficult and requires a lot of studying, but as long as you put in the time, you will succeed.

Keller enjoys teaching but he tries to do a million things at once. He would cut lab recitation short for the TA by performing "mini labs" and we would never work out homework problems. He did not include everything that was presented on the test in lecture. It was an awful honors class to take and would not recommend it to anyone.

Professor Keller is very passionate about what he teaches, and cares very much about student learning. However, his tests are very hard, and you have to put in the amount of study time that this class deserves. Go to the review sessions before the test! Do practice problems and check out previous exams. Overall, he's a great professor.

Gen Chem 2 with Keller is very tough.  Chemistry is beyond memorization (you actually have to *learn* concepts), if you want to memorize your way to an A go enroll in a biology class.  Keller was extremely interested in student learning, and willing to go out of his way to help for those students with a genuine interest in learning.

This was for sure the worst class i have ever taken. Run away while you still have time. The tests were impossible and related very little to the class and even the book. I studied for days before the tests and in the end, I failed every one. The only way I managed a C is by doing good on quizzes and labs

Difficult course. I failed the first test but ended up with a B+. You can do this if you work hard! He is a very helpful teacher, and if you want to pass this course do exactly what he recommends (ie STUDY QUESTIONS, tutoring, office hours) and you will be fine!

I had Keller for Chem 1320 and it was very difficult. I had a hard time learning from the lectures and often taught myself through the book and from the internet. The tests are very difficult. The lab helps though (and the curve) and I got a B+ in the class. Don't give up! Keller does offer a lot of help, however. I give him credit for that.

Definitely a hard class, but Keller takes a sincere interest in student learning, despite the large class sizes. He's always trying to come up with new ways to learn the material, and often sends e-mails/facebook messages with surveys. Get used to getting horrible grades on tests- they are HARD. but the lab section is a good grade buffer.
Class is ridiculously hard, but there are plenty of sources like tutoring to help. I failed 2 of the exams and got a D on the third and still ended up with a B-.

Dr. Keller is extremely hard! This is my hardest class ever. But the guy did know what he was talking about and was very interested in student learning and teaching his profession. His moto are "tests are suppose to be. They're meant to make you think."

Hardest class I have ever taken in my entire life. He is serious about letting his students have the ability to learn and likes to be very involved with them. BUT!! If you do not need an advanced chemistry class. Do not take it with him.

By far one of my favorite teachers of all time, He is more on the ball than any other professor and really cares if you learn. Yes the class is difficult he will make you work and earn your keep, that is kinda what college is... Do the homework go to all the classes and read the chapters and you'll be fine. Sink or swim... you decide.
This class is terrible, the averages for Keller's tests are F's. He doesn't really care about the grades of his students. Plus I have not been to a lecture yet when his voice did not crack.
This class is terrible, the averages for Keller's tests are F's. He doesn't really care about the grades of his students. Plus I have not been to a lecture yet when his voice did not crack.
While he's interested in student learning and very enthusiastic, this class is nearly impossible. I've never worked harder in a class, and I'm expecting a C-. This course will kill your gpa.

This class is so difficult to the point where people will cry during the test. Get out while you can, because if you don't you may have the same fate as those who cry during the test. Also, do all your labs and google the answers for your quizzes and you may pass with a C-!

By far the hardest chemistry class i ever took in my life. This class will ruin your GPA. Everyone on the website will tell you that he is willing to teach you etc. However, this class is freaking impossible. DO NOT TAKE IF YOU HATE CHEM. Keller + Chem 1320 = You studying for no reason, failing, hating your life and surely  hating chemistry.
did not like him at all!

He really loves chemistry so it's great to see a teacher be so passionate about his subject but..he kind of makes you feel bad for not knowing everything or loving everything to do with chem. Students that raise their hands to ask questions in class....keep those hands down!

Very difficult exams, but it's very possible to get an A if you put in the fairly large amount of work to get one.  Very interesting lectures, Prof. K. cares about his students success and understanding of concepts he teaches.  If you want to work hard and learn the material, take this class.  If you're wanting an easy A, look for another professor
Overly helpful and explains concepts very well.
He is very helpful and wants you to understand the information.  He is accommodating to your schedule.

Don't even bother taking this course with Dr. Keller! Save your money for somebody who will actually teach you! His exams are OFF the wall ridiculous! He only WANTS 15% of the class to get any of his questions right. My TA couldn't even do some of the problems on the tests because they were so difficult. TAKE THIS WITH ANYBODY ELSE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. K was the worst professor I ever had.  His tests had nothing to do with the notes he gave us and didn't reflect the time we spent on topics in class.  Though interested in student learning, I did not learn anything.  Lets just say that I used my HIGH SCHOOL notes to scrap an A.
Although this course was very difficult, I found that Prof. K.'s lectures were very interesting. He was very interested in student learning.

Dr. Keller was the worst teacher that I have EVER had! His tests had nothing to do with what he taught in class! The tests were problem based, but we would only do a very easy problem in class and theories. Then you get to the test and the problems are nearly impossible.During tests I would hear people crying.Don't even bother going to office hours

This class is chemistry so of course it wouldn't be easy, but with keller it was easy to get topics. He set aside many opportunties for help sessions and was always willing to see you when you needed help. Most labs related to class but were off by a week sometimes. His exams were to hard if you did past exams. One of the best chem teachers for sur

This guy is great if you love chem. Extremely interesting and helpful, he will devote as much time to you as you do to chemistry, but the test were WAY to hard. I thought I had a firm grasp on the concepts of chemistry before, but he completely blew it out of the water. He writes his test from his head and there is no barrier for what is on them.

I am in 1320, questions on the tests have nothing to do with the lectures. And some of the labs have nothing to do with the lectures. This class has been very frustrating!! I would not recommend taking it in the Spring with Keller.

Prof K is a great instructor. His classes are very difficult and require alot of effort, but he is veerry helpful and has alot of review/help sessions. I've had him for chem 1 and 2 and hopefully for chem 3!

Nothing Keller ever lectured about correlated with the labs. Nothing in the labs or lecture ever seemed to be on the exams. Things I've never even seen or heard from Keller's lectures appeared on the exams. Luckily I had an awesome TA who basically told me what to study otherwise I would have been screwed. I can't name any professor I disliked more
Prof Keller is my favorite prof on campus. He's always willing to help you and has the best lectures. his tests aren't easy, but you can do well if you study.
Very good teacher and very helpful. Definitely a 2 thumbs up. Real easy to get a long with. One of my favorite teachers.
if you dont like to study and ur not a chem major dont take his class.  his tests are really difficult and his lectures are not the best.  he is willing to help you if u need it.

The tests in this class are very difficult. But that he curves the class so people dont do too bad. If you do pretty good on your labs, its still possible to  earn a decent grade. This class requires a lot of work!

His tests are difficult and require a lot of studying, but he is such a nice guy and honestly cares about his students. I wouldn't recommend skipping any of the lectures because he covers a lot of material each day.

Professor Keller was one of my favorites last semester. Like other comments, he was always willing to go above and beyond the call of duty to help his students. A great guy, actively involved with other MU stuff. He even offered to jump my car when it was dead outside of Plaza (he laughed at me first, of course). DO WELL ON YOUR LABS!

Had I not taken two years of high school chemistry, I wouldn't have had a chance in this class.  Keller's tests bore only the remotest resemblance to the material covered in lecture or in the book.  When the class ended, Keller asked me how I did so well - I told him I had a fantastic high school chemistry teacher, simple as that.
This was an extremely tough class. The tests had averages of 50-60% every time. It was interesting and he was helful, but it was just really hard to keep up with him.
He was an awesome, but his tests were SO hard.  I don't even know where he got some of it from.

Keller is a great teacher. He really goes out of his way to be available to students and tries to explain things more than one way so everyone will understand. He is very lively and passionate and I really liked his lectures. His tests require ALOT of studying and chem is not the easiest subject in general, but A's are definitely possible!!
If you have any problems, he's more then willing to help out

Keller is utterly awesome, enthusiastic, and cute.  His tests would probably confound Einstein, but Keller is highly available to his students. His lectures are surprisingly entertaining and down-to-earth; he uses great analogies to describe atomic and molecular phenomena (ocillating jump ropes become an example of e- cloud nodes). I'm in geek love

My class, "paradigms and paradoxes a history of science", was mostly a discussion group.  There wasn't much homework. I think he mostly liked to see that we were paying attention, and he made it interesting enough that that wasn't tough to do.

I learned about things that apply to the world, like global warming and the ozone hole. However, the tests were the hardest I've ever taken. I recommend this class to people that have already had a lot of Chemistry experience, otherwise you'll be completely lost. Dr Keller is an enthusiastic teacher, he just needs to lighten up on the tests.
Very fun, crazy teacher
good teacher, very interesting in class experiments, entertaining

The hardest tests I have ever experienced.  I took his class in the Spring of 2004 and I enjoyed his teaching technique.  He made the class very interesting, but I don't think what he taught during the lecture helped you at all for the tests.  I don't know where he came up with some of that ****!

One of my favorite profs at MU. He completely goes out of his way for students. His tests can be really hard though. But he makes Chemistry fun, and I felt like I could go talk to him anytime. Great overall professor.

his lectures are straightforward and not too complex.  they are deceiving when preparing for exams as the tests are much more difficult than anything ever even discussed in class.  however, he was an extremely interesting teacher who didn't mind answering even the dumbest of questions.
He's a great teacher, and he makes chemistry really fun.
hes awesome
Sometimes I find his explanations kind of elementary, but I keep interested because he's so cute :D
Dr. Keller is THE BEST profession I've had for any science-based course, hands down.  His tests are challenging, but he's very passionate that his students actually learn.  I have a crush on him.
Awesome professor, one of the best I have had.   His exams can be pretty tough though.
Tough course but Keller is awesome. enthusiast teacher, very helpful and open door policy is not a problem. easy to approach and always willing to help you understand the material!
Pretty good teacher. Tries to make himself seem really cool, like he's trying to pickup the freshmen girls.
One of the best!  He goes so far beyond the call of duty, always available for extra help.  I can't wait to take another one of his classes.  Highly recommended!

Great professor...one of the best I've had in my 3 years here. He gives difficult exams, but spends an incredible amount of time helping students prepare. Really enthusiastic, makes you really want to learn.

Chemistry 32 is challenging, and likewise Keller's exams reflect the complexity required to prepare you for later material (i.e. he is hard, but fair). He is an interesting lecturer and does lots of out-of-class/online stuff to ensure his students do wel

Dr. Keller is an awesome person! He may be a difficult teacher, but he is the best best professor I have had so far. He is passionate about Chemistry and science in general, and in addition, he has great character and personality.
been here 3 semesters...coolest prof i've had
Nicest guy!  Has a passion for wanting his students to do well.  He is awesome!
this man is the devil!! didn't grasp that chem.15 was supposed to be basic chem.

Brian is a wonderful professor, if you come to class and have even a loose grasp on class content you're set. He is an engaging lecturer who clearly cares about students, and exam expectations are not ambiguous whatsoever. I intend on taking any other courses he offers whenever I can fit them in my schedule. His teaching style makes the learningfun
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Ott is awesome. His lectures are fun and engaging, and as long as you show up to class, you will do just fine. He gives extra credit for attendance, has review sessions before every test, and gives very clear guidelines for exams. I would recommend this class to anyone, even if taken just for fun. I intend to take another of his classes!

GREAT dude, his class is very manageable as an elective. I've taken two classes with him so far and both were so worth my time. Not hard at all, just show up and you'll do fine. (his lectures are engaging and fun anyway)
If Ray Romano was real and taught Sociology. 10/10.

If you go to class and put any effort in you will do amazing in the class. Professor Ott is hilarious and makes sure his lectures are incredibly entertaining. I highly recommend him and this class to everyone I meet.
His lectures were so engaging and his personal examples and stories added so much to the reading and lecture material, seriously and amazing professor and really nice person!
Brian Ott is one of the best professors at Mizzou, simple as.
Great guy, easy class

Professor Ott is one of the best professors I've had class with. He makes the class very easy. There is no test or quizzes in this class, only lectures. He gives extra credit and even brought us coffee in one of the lessons. I'd definietly take another class with him. He is a very good person overall. Totally recommended.
Brian is so funny and he makes learning very fun!
Dr. Ott was very informative, and his lectures are fun to follow. Class is very easy with no exams, only papers. He's a very nice guy and I recommend this class to everyone.

I had brian my first semester here and I still talk about him very fondly and meet others who liked him a lot too. It was his first semester when I had him too and he was super nice and excited that people liked him. He cancelled class a lot too which was cool

Lectures can be boring, but he does everything he can to make them interesting. Exams are extremely easy, and quizzes are open note. He offers participation as extra credit. He gives test and quiz answers if you attend class. If you go to most of the lectures, the class is extremely easy and he is an extremely understanding and nice professor.

Super easy class. Go to the reviews and listen because those helped so much for the test. As long as you do the study guide and put in some work for the tests you will be fine. No homework. The quiz's were easy and helped boost your grade. Attendence was counted for extra credit. Super nice teacher who wants the best for his students.

An AMAZING professor. He is so passionate about what he teaches and cares deeply about his students. Brian is always very understanding and allows many opportunities for extra credit. I took this class as an elective, but now I'm adding a sociology minor-that is how great he is at his job! He's also the funniest professor you'll ever have. 10/10

Dr. Ott is the best professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about your success as a human and as a student. There are plenty of opportunities for extra credit. If you just come to lecture and pay attention, you will get an A. His dry humor at the beginning of lectures makes my day.

His class is so great. Lectures aren't mandatory, but he's really funny so you should go. He's also very knowledgeable and his tests/quizzes are a direct correspondence to his teaching. Honestly not hard at all, and he's super caring.

His class was so much fun. He takes attendance through google forms and multiple times throughout the semester he would tell us what days he was taking attendance and even gave us the option on what day we would rather him take attendance.

Brian is such a nice, funny professor. Lectures are easy to stay engaged with as he adds his own sense of humor to lectures. He's extremely understanding, and gave days off as breaks for students which was greatly appreciated. As long as you keep up with content and use his study guides on exams you'll do well.

Brian was a fantastic professor and his class was one of my favorites. His lectures are funny and engaging despite being primarily powerpoint presentations. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you do get extra credit the more you show up and Brian often gives away quiz/exam answers in class.
Super chill guy.

He was a great professor and his lecture's although slightly boring, attending those and taking notes are all you need to pass the class with a good grade. Warning: he says um at least 5 times a minute
only lectures, but attendance not required. he gives extra credit, curves tests, and exams are mostly memorization

Such a great professor! Definitely recommend going to his review session before the exam, he gives you all the answers for the exam and utilizes the outline he posts on canvas when studying for the exam! Very funny, relatable, and down-to-earth professor! If you need to take sociology 1000 I 100% recommend him!

Brian Ott is an exceptional teacher! The course comprises three exams, including the final, along with several quizzes. Expect a significant amount of readings provided via Canvas by Professor Ott. Active participation in class is highly recommended, as well as diligent note-taking since video lectures will not be posted on Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall Brian is a fine professor. The class looks the same every day with him reading off the slides so it's pretty boring. easy class if you review before the test, you don't really need to go to lectures if you look at the slides he posts online. 2 exams and 1 final. He has 6 quizzes that are online.

I loved professor Ott! He is so funny, he always starts class off with something to make the class laugh. Lectures can be boring because it is always just a powerpoint, but class is relatively easy if you study. There are only two exams so study! He also gives a couple opportunities for extra credit and hints at answers during class so attend class
Brian is the best! So glad I had his class, he's hilarious and very accommodating. Lecture slides are posted on Canvas but still come to class because he gives hints on exam questions.

I LOVED PROFESSOR OTT! He was seriously an amazing professor who is a great lecturer and knows his information very well. I never felt unprepared for exams or quizzes. He always posts his slides after lecture so you can review the information before tests and quizzes as well. I would recommend him for anyone in need of an intro to sociology credit.

He was a great professor! You really just had to show up to class and he would sometimes very heavily hint at test answers. Posts his slides after every class and does not take ICA's which is great. Very chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy, a few quizzes and a few exams made up the grade. He gives you insight as to what is on the tests and all you have to do is put the work and study the vocab and you will get a good grade. He is entertaining, hilarious, and cares about his students. Definitely would recommend the class and professor!

Loved his lectures, made sure everyone understood what he was talking about. Great sense of humor. I recommend going to class even though it's not required for the lectures, the at home reading isn't enough for the exams.

I actually hate the way this was taught. 90% of her material she teaches she does not give reasoning on why she is doing it, it's “just because you can”. The lectures aren't like the exam. The amount of quizzes is absurd. I have never had this hard of a time in one of her classes. So good luck!

THIS REVIEW IS FOR REINFORCED CONCRETE. Example problems are often incorrect and are very difficult to follow. Nothing is explained intuitively and you're expected to know everything based on slides with very minimal information. Slides just provide equations and don't provide explanations on when to use them. Final project took 30+ hours.

I've enjoyed my time in materials. Dr. Orton is a great lecturer with very clear expectations. Grading is very fair and she is always open to explain her reasoning for taking off points where needed. I would highly recommend this class. There is a lot of material, but if you pay attention during class it should be an easy B if not better.

Dr. Orton was very knowledgable about the topics she was teaching and set up the class and the labs very organized. Although the class was difficult, she would do her best to provide chances to make up missed points.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken. Every lecture is either a powerpoint or a guest speaker. She expects you to know material that she did not teach and expects homework to be submitted in specific formats but does not tell you until she counts points off while grading. Outside of class she will ignore you or be rude and cold. Do not take her classes.

Dr. Orton acts like she cares but in reality it seems like she doesn't. If you see her outside of class she acts like she doesn't know you. She is condescending towards student in class and will guilt you into asking questions. For a one credit hour class, she gives a lot of busy work and requires attendance, I would not recommend taking her class.

This was a new class, but I got a lot out of it for not being a degree requirement. There was a lot of work that was usually busywork, but the lectures were interesting because of guest speakers and simple design problems. She would always give feedback and communicate exactly what was expected. She was also quick to respond to questions.

CV 3600 was by far my favorite class taken at MIZ. Dr. Orton does a good job teaching and is one of the better professors I've had. It's the kind of class that if you work hard, you will be rewarded. Labs are every week (which is a grind) but really interesting compared to some of the other mundane labs at Mizzou. It's Excel heavy in lab analysis
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Read the other reviews before this semester and was expecting the worst. Dr. Orton was fantastic in my opinion. She is clearly very excited about the material which is difficult because it all seems pretty dull. The course is heavily based on memorization of the material covered in long powerpoints, however her energy made the class enjoyable

She is the type of professor that presents the material ok but then states a vague question about it either in a quiz or exam. I would recommend to become certified in ACI because then you don't write a 20 page paper on a material you have learned.

The worst professor in the civil department. Very unorganized and slow with grading. She has one way of thinking and is very condescending toward students. The class is basically memorizing useless information in hopes she is specific on the tests with what you studied. She would not know what to do at all in an actual civil engineering job.

Not an ounce of educational skill in her body. Condescending towards students questions when at the same times she requires each student to ask ten questions per semester. Presents way too much material in fly-through-as-fast-as-she-can lectures (all boring PPT), then tests on obscure specifics on her exams. MU should be embarrassed to employ her.
Nice to look at.
Not awful, but she has never actually worked in the field and has only done research on the subjects. Questions for clarification on a subject sometimes won't be answered well because of this.

His reviews are very similar to the exams. He has a policy that you can replace your exam scores with whatever you get on the final, so most people recover their grades on the final. All homeworks are participation, but he does go over them in class so you can check yourself on whether you got the right answer. I highly recommend his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes on material he hasn't even taught,I know hes trying to force students to do the reading but this is very detrimental to students who learn from being verbally/visually taught,The exams were 10x harder than anything ever seen in the class,You'll never know your performance in the class until after finals,Also makes annoying mouth noises 24/7
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: O'Connell is a tough, but motivating professor. The fast pace lectures, difficult content and structure of this course is overwhelming to say the least. This class is the ultimate grind for understanding, and you will be in the same race with the rest of your classmates for the final exam at the end of the semester worth 70% of your grade.

Professor O'connell is a great teacher. The course content is naturally difficult so no matter what this class takes a lot of work. He does a good job of breaking down the textbook and making it clear. In order to make the classes more effective you do have reading assignments/problems to do before lecture, but they never took more than an hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff, but you can tell he used to be in the military. He didn't have set office hours, which made it somewhat inconvenient to meet with him. His notes were pretty hard to follow because he jumped around the board a lot. His grading scale was very generous though.
Has a different approach to teaching which is really helpful for this class in particular. Really cares about his students and their learning. He's a little blunt, but he knows his stuff.

Awesome teacher, actually cared about students and if they learned. Has a different hands on approach to learning which is great. Speaks english which is rare for engineering, and is just an all around fair teacher.

The material in this class is kind of difficult but Dr Shahvari teaches it decently well. The tests are open note and open book, and they were all very similar to the practice tests. So just print out the practice test solutions and bring them to the exam. Make sure you show up to class, the participation bonus points are percentage points.

Very hard to understand the lectures as he goes through them very fast. I seems as if he does not care about students learning the material, but rather students copy his examples exactly the way they are. His TA's are pretty much an extension of him and when I didn't understand lectures, they seemed pretty condescending in their explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He teaches with slides but will actually go over the problems with you. At the end of class he makes you do an in class problem but you can do it with others so sit with someone and become friends. You also have to do a group project and you get to pick the people.

As an online student, I wasn't aware of who was in the class or what outside materials others were using. I would recommend choosing a different course or professor unless you're prepared to defend every step of your work... word for word.

Unless you do the problems structure by structure, almost word for word, you risk being accused of academic integrity violations. If you miss a minor step, instead of docking 1-2 points, the issue is escalated to an integrity report. Even after annotating the work, explaining the reasoning, and citing literal lecture timestamps, it didn't help.

Bring your tin foil hats to class! She has no concept of real world economic/finance problems and it makes sense why she is stuck in academia. Unbelievable some of the answers she would give that would absolutely be rejected in the corporate world. Easy class, don't take anything she says with you to your job. Take Industrial Organization instead!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny and personable! A study group makes this class very doable.
Bad person!!!!
She treats grad students like 5th grader. No respect or trust whatsoever. Tries to ruin students' lives.

Run away!
She accused me with 13 others saying that I cheated despite she had us do the exam on old style pen and paper. How do you accuse someone of cheating in mathematics only because you find similarities? 2+2 is always 4 and we all use the same method to calculate that. She is a saddist and avoid her at all cost.

Worst professor ever! I see previous comments from my class who also got violation for integrity, they are all right. She could have at least warned us before reporting. We all are garduate students & she didn't even think twice before ruining our record. I won't recommend her even to my worst enemy. Do not take any class witj her. U are welcome!!!
She filed academic integrity for 13 students even though I didn't cheat. Now I can't even withdraw. She doesn't care about her students. Please avoid her even if it means late graduation!

DON'T take her!
Taking her game theory class now and she accused the whole class of using AI and gave a 0 in midterm and filed an academic integrity complaint without first consulting with the students. I had to terminate my degree because of her action. STAY AWAY FROM HER.

I took this class in person attendance wasn't mandatory but I highly recommend it, that was the best way to understand what was going on. One homework assignment dropped, but your grade is only made up of 6 HW's and 3 exams. She keeps lectures relevant and doesn't waste anyone's time. Just a heads up, at the end of the semester there was no curve

Loginova was a fun prof for Game Theory. I wish I would have taken it in person, as I've heard she's even better there. Class is only based off 3 tests and 6-7 homework assignments, so make sure you do your best on every assignment. The online course is well structured, and you can slack a bit as long as you get each bi-weekly hw done in time
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was amazing online, but I believe it would've been even better in-person. She is a MUST TAKE at Mizzou. She throws in random Russian time to time and makes the content super understandable and interesting. If you do the homework and practice exams, you will do great in the course! Dr. L is incredibly kind and always available

Professor Ola was a nice and understanding teacher. It takes a bit of work and proper understanding of the content, however as long as you show up and make an effort you will have the ability to do well. just make sure to do the readings and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Osman has such incredible, in-depth knowledge of black studies. She also brings in gender perspectives on peace which really opened my mind. Some of the material was challenging at first and you won't keep up if you don't do the reading assignments but once I followed her instructions I was able to make my way through it better.

Prof. Osman was fantastic! She was so caring and helped me learn how to think more critically. She gives solid feedback. Be prepared to work hard and think critically during her class. I would recommend her course. Also her marking is very fair.
Ola Osman was the best professor! She taught the class with great enthusiasm and was very well versed in the topics!! Highly recommended taking a class with her!!

Pros
Professor Osman is very sweet
She'll class if she gets sick

Cons
Minimal feedback on papers. Things like "This is wrong" or "change this"
Point of the readings are unclear
The class discussions are just dissing America
Feedback took a month to get
Information and readings are extremely forgettable

There's more but im out of characters to use

reviews.comment: Only students teach this class by presenting through reading peer reviewed articles. She talks very little and it's usually when she tells us that participating in class is worth a part of our grade. She told us that at the beginning of the semester that she will not answer emails and that all emails should be sent to the TA. Don't take this class.

This professor is very unorganized and unprofessional. She makes the student teach a lecture that some of us don't even understand the topic enough. There was a mix up with my group and another group and instead of giving us an alternative assignment she makes us redo the whole presentation with a different topic. Do not take this class.
The way the professor is "teaching" this Peace Studies could easily make it an online course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Pros:

*Sometimes engage in discussions

reviews.comment: Osman did not teach, instead made the students teach with presentations. Did not leave clear instructions for essays (the only grades). Also doesn't grade or answer emails. TA does that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While his lectures are a little boring, I believe it is the fault of the topic not the teaching. He is very kind, and even if you do not attend class he will still treat you the same. If you are concerned about a mistake you made effecting your grade, just respectfully talk to him and he will almost certainly allow you to rectify it.

He is a very calming professor. His lectures are a bit slow sometimes but I enjoy his classes. He gives a lot of examples when learning new topics so you understand how it works. He is genuinely a nice prof. One of the few good comp sci professors at Mizzou. Posts lectures online as well.

Boring class, but did provide a good study on relational databases and SQL, and the professor knew what he was doing. Exams are straight forward, but be prepared for a semester long project that's worth more of your grade than the exams. Also be prepared to present said project to the TAs at the end.

The grading for assignments and the three-part phases of your project are very reasonable. Very up to date with the news, such as new AI models. A few extra credits comparing Deepseek to GPT. Does his lecture seem boring? Yes, but you can tell that he's very passionate while lecturing on each topic. Ask questions, he's good at explaining.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and passionate. The only negative is that the lecture is boring and drawn out.

The lectures were pretty boring, but it was an interesting topic and an easy class. Lecture videos were immediately posted, and he would respond to emails. 
The final project was not totally covered in class, which made it hard to implement, but he was willing to help.

One of the better profs in CS department. You can tell he cares about the topic. There's very little homework, so the only way to really learn concepts is to do your own code outside class. Tests are pretty easy as long as you understand the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rao was an amazing professor and passionate about the material. The project was probably the best part about this course. Because you got to design a database and a application that uses the database.

If you are good at Computer Science and Math then CS3380 is a blow off class. I skipped about 70% of the lectures and currently have a 102% in the class.

It is pretty easy. Keep in mind though this may not be the case for everyone. But based on the grade distributions on assignments, it seems people are doing well in the class.

CS3380 got boring sometimes, and lectures were pretty slow, but that's better than the alternative. The final project was confusing, but the TAs are very forgiving with grading. There are lots of extra credit points on exams. It's definitely possible to score well in this class without attending every lecture if you've worked with SQL in the past.
Quite a nice guy and good test giver

This class was definitely not as bad as it was made out to be. Dr. Park's lectures may not be the most entertaining, but he really wants students to learn and pass. I think at times the material was overcomplicated by many lecture slides which made it difficult to study for, but it wasn't too bad.

Prof was super passionate about the content but couldn't teach at all, e.g. would just read off of the slides. Might give out pop quizzes, but only gave one. Exams are in class and he allowed an one-sided cheat sheet. The exams are basically the homework assignments, it's the same exact format/pacing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class material is not too difficult itself, but the professor is extremely unmotivated to help his students at all. Does not not care to aid students when they ask, and is one of the worst professors I have had during my time in engineering at Mizzou. Also has homework due on the Friday after Thanksgiving, just to add salt to the wound.

terrible professor. I've gone the entire semester so far and it feels like the only thing I've learned are the millions of different equations. We barely talk about anything else. The book that is used doesn't provide an answer key in the normal sense so youll have pay some website to actually see the way to soove the problem. what a joke
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Listen very closely. This class will probably be the worst, most unorganized, worst taught class you'll take. You are required to go to class, but understand that when you go to class you will not understand anything. The lectures consist of snipping tooled equations vommited onto a slide. You will have to learn everything yourself.

his class is graded on only two midterms and the final which itself is worth 30 percent of your grade. also, he has pop quizzes that he announces the class before said quiz, then pushes it back by a few weeks to a month until you forget about it. gives no practice exams or study materials.TA doesn't help at all either
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst course I have ever taken. The Intructor does not how to teach at all. It seems like he hates to teach, is condescending, and not at all helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I hate to be negative, but professor Park is simply not a pleasant or helpful instructor. He does not explain very difficult concepts clearly (the textbook is much more informative), he frequently makes demeaning comments about the performance of the class as a whole, and his exams are a logistical nightmare, with barely any time or desk space.

Reads off of lecture slides straight from the textbook. Not very helpful when asking important questions on the material. Even worse TA who could not help with homework assignments himself. Absolutely suggest taking such a core engineering class with another professor if possible. While i passed, i do not have a solid foundation of thermodynamics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He reads off lecture slides that are copied from the textbook. People ask him questions and he doesnt know how to answer. He is generally rude to the class. Wish I had a different teacher since Thermo is important. Take a different teacher if possible. Test average was a D and he blamed it on the class.

He just reads off the slides and doesn't really teach. Definitely just expects you to get it by reading a chapter. Do not recommend at all. Kinda rude too, after a bad average on the first exam, he decided to blame it on us instead of his teaching.

The good: I dont have to take the class again. The bad: his teaching. Reads formulas off of Powerpoint without explaining what they represent. Also, never does example problems. The ugly: his character. He goes out of his way to be unnecessarily rude to his students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Does not do examples whatsoever. Expects you to learn the material on your own. The book is a better teacher than he is. He's Pretentious. You will not finish the exams in scheduled class time. Worst taught class I've ever experienced in college. Take the other professor if you want a better time. He will not give you any respect.
I enjoyed her class, the material was great and presented in an organized way. The tests were pretty easy, but there are a lot of group work assignments. She is honestly pretty funny too.

Very inconsistent in grading and feedback. Often gives out identical grades to all member of a class with the same blanket feedback. Be prepared to read a fair amount and also be ready to share and discuss things in class. She lacks explanations in most things she says in class. Sometimes she is unprepared and ends classes early.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Raonka is a very knowledgeable person, just not the best professor in terms of organization and giving helpful feedback. She mostly relied on her TAs when it came to grading assignments, which were often left ungraded until weeks after submission, and her quizzes were difficult. Just pay close attention and don't skip--you'll do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor!!

Dr. Ouda is good for CS 3330 and 4050, but I recommend taking 4320 with JimR (fall semesters). His teaching style is pretty good and the assignments are reasonable in theory, but the TAs are incredibly nit-picky on the grading of assignments. The exams test memorization of the slides, so literally memorize everything he says is important.

Ouda is one of the most overhated profs in the CS department. He is very well organized, with lots of detailed slides that lay out the content very well. He gets excited any time someone has a question in class. He's a tough grader for attention to detail on homework. Tests follow examples from the slides and require that you write code by hand.

Good Luck. You can't understand what he is saying half the time, he covers hundreds of slides and then doesn't post the examples that are test relevant. Does not test over understanding of a topic, but your ability to copy and paste code from his slides. Then gets mad at the class for performing poorly instead of taking any of the fault.

Dr. Ouda is a pretty good teacher for OOP. This is the first CS class where I've been able to understand all the content really easily and score high scores on all the quizzes and exams. My only complaint is his TAs grade pretty harshly for things that are not significant such as messing up a print statement. Other than that this was a good class.

The group assignments were graded harshly, made worse by the fact that no one ever explained how we were supposed to complete them. He insists the class “isn't based on memorization,” yet every exam demands exactly that. Honestly, there are far too many issues to list here. I do NOT have a grasp on software development practices after attending.
Dd not grade based on any rubric for a single assignment, and scoring was never transparent. In fact, ta made several mistakes on different assignments and exams/quizzes.
The class, being a 3-credit course, should be a crime itself with the amount of workload in his SWE class.

Lectures are a nightmare of unending slides, yet you're required to attend since he doesn't most many slides that are on the test. It's hard to understand what he's saying half the time. I appreciate project-based learning, but in 4050 it's a 1 person problem for a 3 person group vs 4320 requires everyone to do 20-40 hrs/person for the last project
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
4050: HW was all group projects despite being a 1 person job and irrelevant to the class content. not terrible class.
SWE: HW was overwhelming and class was a slide memorization game, with over 1000 slides. bad class
4410: He's great as a lecturer for this one, but he hides info about HW problems behind the TA's
I took CMPSC3330 (OOP) with him in Fall 2024 and enjoyed it so much that I decided to take three more of his courses in Spring 2025. He is definitely one of the best professors in CMPSC!
Ouda seems like a nice dude, but man you cannot understand him. His lectures are tough to follow and TA's are not very good. Not a good experience overall and I'll be glad when its over

Exams and projects must be made to exactly as he discusses in the class slides, which he refuses to post online or let you take pictures of, no announcements are online. Extremely tough grading, and TAs are told very little about exams and projects, so they are not much help. Just wait until he's done teaching the course or find another section.

Perfectly fine person but a terrible teacher did a review slide where we went over potential problems but didn't post these questions for studying and wouldn't let anyone take pictures. Assignments are ambiguous and have awful pacing. Slides are absurdly long and could undoubtedly be trimmed. Slides also have multiple typos and are confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor but it takes a lot to do well in SWE. He cares about students, but assignments are unclear. Go to every TA office hour you can for feedback--basically if your answers don't match Ouda's solution perfectly, you'll get points docked. He says in class what to memorize for tests, so as long as you pay attention you'll do fine.

Attend class and pay attention during lectures as there was a lot of content covered in the slides. He lets you know what will be on the exam which is very helpful. I liked the projects and assignments because I thought it was applicable to real jobs. Make sure you like your group members because this will play a role in success in the class.

Tests and assignments are very difficult. If you want to pass you have to go to the TA's and his office hours to learn information that 'could' be on the test and assignments. Hundreds of slides per lecture and he doesn't post them all so highly recommend going to class and listening for 'key' information that probably will be on the test.

The exams and quizzes are unnecessarily difficult. They are do-able but I don't see the point of having us write the code on paper. He is passionate about what he teaches but also very hard to understand. So get ready to read your slides. DON'T TAKE HIM UNLESS YOU ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO!

The professor is disorganized, with poor communication with TAs, leading to confusion. Projects have short deadlines, and TAs deduct excessive points for minor mistakes while being unhelpful in required office hours. Exams heavily on memorizing slides, which adds little to learning. The workload is excessive for a 3-credit class and poorly managed.

The professor shames the whole class during lecture when he believes the class didn't perform as well as they should have on an assignment or an exam. Sounds like a teaching issue not a student issue. Exams are super long and don't assess the students' actual knowledge at hand. TA's don't grade projects by the rubric whatsoever. Good luck

While not an incredibly difficult class content wise, the way it is organized and managed makes it much worse. Assignments are vague with many of the important requirements being mentioned in passing during lecture, sometimes only mentioned the day before it was due. Overall poor communication between him, students and TA led to many issues.

He intentionally makes it hard on his students! Everything is vague from his exam content, to the grading criteria on any of his projects. On top of this, the grading is picky. A minor flaw will result in a 5-10 point deduction on 100 point assignments ( a mistake as little as an image not being to the size preferred by the TA ). Avoid at all costs

Do not take this course with its current professor, poor communication between prof and TAs results in poor/unfair grading, unclear and vague assignments and frustration between students, TAs, and professor, at the latter's fault. Additionally, exams will be covered by ~500 slides of material where > 20 slides matter and need to be memorized.
This class is so bad, if you can avoid taking him I highly recommend it.
Not a good teacher but good person. Can't understand him a lot and says important info during class so go.

I do not recommended taking this course with him. Ouda is a nice guy who is willing to help, but half the time you can't understand what's even being said during lectures, it sucks when he gives important information for upcoming quizzes or tests and you're trying to understand what he's saying at the same time.
Do not recommend. Hard class and bad teaching. Don't be suprised if your always confused

Project you work on throughout the semester is divided very poorly...given two months for making class diagrams and not even two weeks for implementing the entire project. He is a clown for thinking this is a good project, especially with the timeframes given. His choice in TA's are horrendous, they can't even help with the project half the time.

He tells you everything that will be on the exams, so failing to study the right things is entirely your fault. ATTEND EVERY LECTURE AND LISTEN FOR WHEN HE MENTIONS SOMETHING WILL BE ON THE EXAM. He won't remind you later. If you do this it's an easy A. If you don't you'll have a very bad time. Really though, he does care and is pretty fair.

Assignments are confusing, no clear grading criteria. Says key information in class so make sure you take notes. Exam was very difficult, lots  of memorization of diagrams just to put a few on. Had multiple choice questions that seemed super difficult

I'll be honest, the assignments and quizzes aren't hard and I feel as if I have a good understanding of Java now. The issue is the exams, not sure why he thinks writing full codes in paper and pencil would be a good idea especially if you're taking other classes that utilize other languages. Overall don't take him if you have the option.
The test are very difficult as we have to handwrite java. his teaching style is ok but the ability to express the material is blah (i can't understand him half the time)

Professor Ouda sounds like he understands what HE'S talking about, but does not do a very good job explaining or teaching it to the class. You currently have to receive a 50% or higher on each exam, which is 100% written code or you will just not pass the class. I would avoid having him for class, unless you love coding/writing in Java daily.

What is there to say, don't take him... Doesn't review for test, lots of assignments. However, the assignments aren't to difficult. The people who say his English is good, are liars do not listen. He stutters a lot which makes it hard to understand and follow. He seems like a good person though, just not a teacher.
Ouda and TA's are never in sync with how they grade homeworks, which makes it hard to know what they want. Also his lectures are a snoozefest. It's not a hard class but you will hate taking it.
The Professor is a good human being who always smiles. However, his lecture is tough to read because he usually gives a huge but he notes the important topics. His grading is very fair.

Professor is a mess, changes mind all the time. If you don't go to class, will miss out on "important" information from hundreds of slides. The communication between TAs and professor is not good, as you will lost points on assignments.

Listen... Ouda is not a bad professor, I've seen worse. But the miscommunication gap between him and the TAs is terrible. I can tell he wants the best for his students; however, the class is unnecessarily stressful for what it is. Mind you this is coming from people who have had Software Engineering Internships.

Professor = Fine.
TAs = :/.
Tests = :(.
Everyone I know and don't know complains about this class. I better be paid the salary of a therapist with how much mental support I provide for these unfortunate souls.

Professor Ouda's lectures are very fast and require you to review the slides.  He does point out important slides.

His English is perfectly fine, I have no trouble understanding him.

My single biggest complaint is that his TAs never seem to be on the same page as Professor Ouda, and this causes the grading criteria to be incredibly unclear.
I took CS8050 with him. Amazing professor and personality!

Seems like a nice guy, but can't stand the way he teaches lectures. Be prepared to read the slides from class yourself as it's sometimes difficult to understand what he's saying and goes through the slides fast.
Ouda is tough but good guy with not the best English. Lots of slides for the tests so be prepared to study. Recommend to go to class, otherwise it will be rough.

Ouda is a good person, but his lectures can be tough to follow. Slides are very important for the test, so make sure to study them. Like way too many slides... Go to class, can be hard to follow at times.

Dr. Ouda does an "okay" job during lectures. I'll start off by saying he's not a bad guy at all, he wants people to succeed and seems pretty passionate about teaching the material/content. But when my brain is trying to understand what he is saying and the content at the same time gets frustrating. It would be nice if he would record the lectures.

Dr. Ouda provides great slides that go into a lot of detail. His lectures, while fast, were very helpful in understanding the concepts and knowing what to study for the exams. We did a lot of in-class examples to enforce grasping the material, and the assignments are done in groups.
Very helpful mentor, who made a lot of effort in guiding me through every step of my research.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: His English is not good, repeats hundreds of slides for exam. Need to memorize a lot of things. Go to class otherwise he will make you
Helped a lot in my research! Very on top of things, and caring.

Attendance isn't mandatory but highly recommended. Learned about a lot more algorithms than I have in any other algorithms class which was fun. Unfortunately, I had unexpected events arise before the final so I didn't do very well, but as long as you put time aside for this class's hw / studying you will do fine. Taught me time management for sure.

Attendance wasn't mandatory, but doing so is highly recommended especially because he notes the "important" slides. Great class, you will definitely learn a lot because he pushes you to learn unlike a lot of other professors who are more laissez-faire and don't care about how much / what you learn. Learned lots abt software development lifecycle!
Really good homework assignments that relate to the lecture content.

The homework, while it was involved with programming, was a bit out of scope.

However, the lecture content was superb. I am appreciative of the depth and complexity given. Hard but rewarding

Dr. Ouda prioritizes quality in his slides.
There was a lot of information on the given topics

The exams are rigorous, practicing a considerable amount of time before such is paramount

Very kind professor who explained all the concepts very clearly. He gave us a lot of problems to solve in class to build on our intuition, rather than only giving out of class labs / assignments. He tells you what concepts are going to be on exams when he goes over them. His slides are very detailed and organized, making them ideal for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ouda was super responsible for his class and his students. I like the way he represented the slides. He knew what he was talking about. And he can make the course so easy. It was such a fun experience to have class with him.

Very kind, can tell he cares about his students. Also (unlike any other comp sci prof) he actually answers questions during tests. Also he gives actually code most times and not just pseudo code in case you struggle with that. He is one of the only prof that actually entertains me during lecture

Super nice professor, and fair with grading typically. Only complaint is that the lectures were sometimes not explained very well and I had to supplement with YouTube, and that the last assignment about machine learning seemed out of scope of the class. Other than that, great class.

Quackenbush is an amazing historian but a horrible teacher. If you want to talk to someone about history he's the one but if you want to save your GPA do NOT take his class. For a 1400 level class it should not have been as difficult to follow along with what he says. I spent more time teaching myself after the classes his slides are HORRIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor was nice but just read off of slides and didn't always know what he was talking about. Final grade is mostly weighted by exams so you have to do good on them, but there are only 3 tests. Attendance was supposed to be taken randomly, but was never actually taken. Class should have been much more engaging and easier than it was.

This was easily my least favorite class this semester. Dr. Quackenbush is a great guy with a lot of knowledge to offer, but the lectures were very hard to follow along with and quite boring. There are not many assignments/help offered in this class, extremely test heavy. Do not recommend/would not take again.

This class was easy in the sense that there were minimal things to submit, however, lectures were not great. He would read off slides and it was hard to follow along with him. He does not give study guides for exams and there is a lot of content to remember for them. Be prepared for exams since there's few other assignments. I would not take again

He knows a lot about the course material, but lectures are very hard to stay engaged with as it just consists of him reading off the slides. Study guides are not provided on exams, so studying for exams can be tough. He's nice enough, this class just wasn't enjoyable.

He is a good guy and very knowledgeable in his field, but the lectures leave much to be desired. The lectures were long and he just read off the slides. If you ask questions he will go more in-depth and that might help more. If you are more of a hands-on learner this class may be difficult for you.
Pretty easy lectures. Tests are all multiple choice and pretty easy. He makes study guides and crosswords for you. Total WW2 nerd

This class is a breeze. Most lectures get out early and we watched videos online. Biggest complaint is that Quackenbush does not reply to emails. Ever. About anything. Maybe he would if you asked about tanks? Nothing class or test related though. Tests are straight forward so as long as you know some information youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I like Dr. Quackenbush. He's a bit awkward at times, but he's a genuine guy who knows his stuff. There's nothing to not like about him. The class was a bit test heavy with tests pretty much determining your grade, save for one paper. But overall, I liked him and I would take another class with him.

Kind of an awkward guy, but knows his stuff. He doesnt respond to emails though. Go to class or read the book, both are not necessary. He literally lectures word for word from the book. Many lectures are just videos of wars. Entertaining and easy A

The class is interesting, but you have to keep up with notes and reading to do well on tests (which are really the only grades, along with a paper). He does a few random attendance roles to make sure you attend class too. Note: PowerPoints don't hold specific information, so missing lecture means missing lots of crucial information for tests.

Quackenbush is a pretty weird guy, but he also has a good sense of humor. His voice is monotonous and he is easy to tune out, so the lectures are semi-boring. He gets you out of class early almost every class period, often with 15-25 minutes to spare. The only grades are 3 tests, a paper, and he very seldom takes attendance.
Dry humor and super cutie!

I like this guy. He's enthusiastic about the material and doesn't bog the subject down; the academic approach makes warfare cooler, in many regards. The paper and tests are great. He tests understanding without being too harsh about knowing a bunch of tautology. One con, though, is that the content could have been taught in a much shorter timespan.
I'm probably the only one, but I thought he was pretty funny. Just very dry. The class is pretty easy. I got a B but I hardly ever studied. Three multiple choice exams make up most of your grade.

Oh my, where do I begin? Well, if you like boring people, take this class. He talks with a very monotone voice, reads straight from the powerpoints(I can do that myself), and he sucks at answering/explaining questions you have.
