I'm sure he means well, but his class honestly sucked. It was really hard for me to understand at times.
Not the worst but far from good

class is really boring. he reads from the powerpoint which is from the readings. he has not original thought. tries to be funny but just comes out to be lame. has a hard time answering questions. and the lab class seems to have nothing to do with the lecture at times. so try and avoid getting him if you can.

Course was politics and war. Class not very interesting. He talks about the readings in class (so don't really need to read them) Seldom have discussion in class. He is sometimes humorous, but the class is too sleepy to laugh. Tests are easy, just need to define 10 terms from a list he gives in advance.
Dr. Quist is incredible. He cares about the students growth not just academically but personally. He believes each student's life can impact their writing and pushes his students to understand that.

One of the most caring and intelligent people you will ever meet. Don't take him for granted. If you have the opportunity to learn from him, take it! He is always willing to answer questions, even the ones you wouldn't expect him to.
Great guy, easy grader, and has a lot of flexibility when it comes to due dates for assignments.

Quist is one of the most spectacular teachers I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. The coursework was understandable and he was very clear on due dates and assignments. It was all easy to understand and he is just the most likable man, very understanding of everyones situation and very lenient if something comes up.

Donald is the best, most accommodating person on the planet. He is so good at connecting and making things engaging. This man brought Childish Gambino into analysis and storytelling. Truly cares and is always willing to go above and beyond. If you aren't taking his classes, do it now.
great teacher, he cared about his students and when it came time to turn in papers, we conference with him and he will tell you what to do to get an A on your paper and how to make it better.
Donald was my favorite instructor. He went out of his way to help all of his students. He made each class interesting and also taught life lessons.
One of the most amazing teachers you could ever have for English. He is so inspiring and really cares about his students. He is a super cool guy and makes his class fun to go to!!!
Unfortunately he is very hard to understand which makes the lectures extremely hard to sit through and understand the material.
Exams are open note, no final but there is a final project that you have to do in groups. Do the homework and what is asked of you and you'll be fine.

Dr Yu is a great person and good professor. That doesn't mean he's giving everybody an A though. His exams are decently difficult and his writing assignments are not free As. He only gives the best performing groups 90s and above. You need to earn your A with effort.  Hard to fail class though if you show up and do work. There Are Pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Yu is a very respectful teacher who cares how you do in the class. There are pop quizzes at the end of lectures, so go to class. Course material is pretty challenging, but if you study, you will be fine. However, this course is not a breeze. Be prepared for lots of homework, and know people in your class for the papers he assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Yu is one of the nicest teachers I've had in a long time. However, his English is not good and that made it almost impossible to understand him in class. The hardest part about this class is the exams (there are two of them). If you don't study and prepare according to the homework, you will fail—one bad exam score can tank your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yu is an amazing professor and genuinely great person. I had him for MAE 2200W and his class structure was very reasonable. He would print out the notes for us, which was super helpful. Most classes had quizzes at the end that were very easy and the answers were found in the notes. I would highly recommend taking MAE 2200W with Dr. Yu.
Fantastic professor! Really cares that his students actual learn the material instead of being overwhelming

I respect Professor Qin a ton, he is very accessible outside of class. At first when I thought only zoom office hours it wouldn't be productive but it's the complete opposite. He is very good with screen sharing his iPad and computer screens so you can easily follow his steps on problems you don't understand!

Dr. Qin was great. The course itself I regret taking, but the lectures were his personal notes with plenty of definitions, explanations, and examples. He does not post lecture notes regularly, so although attendance is not taken it is important. Assignments are infrequent but long, due at 8 AM. Very professional.

Review for 2320** Professor Qin did an amazing job of explaining the class in a clear and concise way, and managed to keep me understanding everything going on throughout the course. Very easy grader, and the exam questions come from the reviews. Somewhat boring during lecture and can be hard to stay focused, but he does a great job of explaining.

Disclaimer: Had him for 2320, not 2300. It did not give me the option to select 2320. He was lecture-heavy, but if you took good notes and practiced examples from class and homework you will do fine on exams. He was very communicative and always would answer any questions you had outside of class. Overall a great experience with this professor.

Dr. Qin is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is a phenomenal lecturer and very fair grader. He makes it very clear from the start what his expectations are and he never tries to trick you on exams. His exams are a great knowledge check and as long as you do the work and come to class you will do well. I highly recommend Dr. Qin.
He was great! I took him for 4100 and I felt like I learned a lot despite the class being online. Definitely made math fun for me, despite the material being hard.

Best professor I ever had, even with an online format. Was super available to give help outside of class any time you emailed, graded exams and quizzes same-day, and was just a super nice guy. Exams and quizzes were very reasonable.

Hes one of the best math professors Ive had. Even with courses being online, I feel like Im learning in just a regular math class. His exams and quizzes arent out to get you; theyre just there to make sure you understood the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Qin was one of the best math professors I have ever had. His lectures were very clear and organized. Lots of examples every class and he knows how to answer student's questions. Study your class notes and you will do great on the three midterms. However, he surprised us and made our final extremely hard, so study a lot. He makes the class easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Qin is by far the best math professor I've had yet! He is very nice and always thanks someone who answers a question. The dynamic of my class was awesome and we all had some laughs over the semester. He teaches the content well and clearly answers questions. His tests can be hard, but if you pay attention in class you'll be fine!
Qin is the Math God.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An absolutely phenomenal math teacher.  His lectures were long and moved quickly, but every ten minutes or so, he asks "Any questions?" Web Assign homework due every week, pretty difficult but if you could do the homework, the tests would be extremely easy for you because they were much easier than the homework.  Had a funny sense of humor, too.

Great teacher. Very interested in student learning. Explains things very well. Exam are very strait forward, all problems just like examples from class. No surprises on exams. Very easy for such a high level math class.
Great teacher.
Nice enough guy, good sense of humor. Gives very well-structured lectures, though sometimes a bit dry. Overall a good teacher.
Dr Qin is a very good teacher. The book we are using for this class is so borrible, and he found a way to make the material attainable. Very helpful, too.
he isnt too hard, but he doesnt give enough time on the exames and stingy about giving partial credit
Great at keeping you interested. Explains things very well.
The best math teacher I've had in a LONG time. His english isn't the best, but he writes everything on the board. Even tells jokes when the material gets really hard.

Professor Zhang is an amazing professor that cracks some jokes when needed, but can also answer any questions that will arise during the class. The class is graded with 5 HW assignments that you turn in and 3 tests (1st, 2nd, and the comprehensive final). Be prepared to study because the tests are worth a majority of your grade. You will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is awesome. He's hilarious, kind, and approachable. If you're taking discrete math, I'd highly recommend him, as he's been teaching the class for 10+ years and really knows what he's doing. The class is a little weird, but I found it interesting, and if you study like you do for other classes you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand. If you've never taken calculus before, I wouldn't recommend this class at all. He doesn't explain anything very well and always puts 3 extremely tricky questions on the test. To study, definitely just go over all the problems he's done in class like 3 times. He gives a generous curve if you show improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang had what seemed to be a thick accent at the beginning of the semester, but very quickly became understandable. He has over a decade of experience with the class and will cut unnecessary material. His class progresses fast and covers a great amount of small sections.  None of them were individually hard, but all were required.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Homework every day. Make sure to show up to class because lectures have all the material for the tests, including the exact problems on the test. Only 2 midterms and a final and he's available for help. Material is very basic and the class overall is nothing compared to its prerequisites.

This guy is seriously one of the best teachers I have ever had. He made the material super easy to understand and retain. The homework is participation based, and the tests are a bit challenging, but doable. His accent is definitely noticeable, but he's very understandable and after a weak you won't even notice. On top of that, he is hilarious!

Very straightforward math class. Be warned it is deceptively easy at times. The easy concepts combined quickly make challenging concepts so always pay attention. However on a few days you've already learned everything so you can sit back and relax. The professor himself is a warm person. He tells jokes and is very approachable.

This class was so fun! My first film class at Mizzou, and was very enlightening to types of films I otherwise would not have known. Transnational/migrant films are more important than ever. If you're a film non-major and want a film class, this is the one!

She is awesome! I'm surprised to see negative ratings about her. From my experience, she's super understanding and brings great energy to class. The coursework is challenging, but she's a great instructor and will re-explain until you understand. I wish I could take another class from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't think there was a single assignment in this course that wasn't docked. Professor grades harshly and unfairly and will think of any excuse to knock your grade. The reading material is impossible to find or watch videos on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She grades very partial and not fair. Do not expect to get full credit on any assignment.. EVER. Always has a comment to make about something you did not answer correctly, but the class is difficult to understand.

She's a really nice professor, the lectures can drag on a lot though. The class is based on reading books, a few online assignments, a presentation (group), attendance, and papers. She can grade kind of particularly but it's really hard to get below a B with everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Had her for Woman and Gender Studies, she was a great teacher. She was helpful and had a very open mind when listening to students. She would also review over all important material before the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class!
Quizzes are open book. Essays are very important to do well on.  Reading the assignments isn't necessary but is recommended if you want to do good on the midterm and final.

I thought the content in 2160 was kinda boring, but not rlly his fault. Dr. Scott is a great prof, very accessible outside of class. Participation def matters. You really just go over HW in class, have a couple essays, and like 2 group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Taylor is fantastic! Dude is super caring, organized and clear. There is a reason that he's the coordinator over some of the other professors. You genuinely could not ask for more!

Very very kind professor-I would absolutely recommend him for any French class. Prof Taylor fostered excellent and insightful discussion while teaching course content. Doesn't really get better than him.

really couldnt ask for a better french teacher. really expressive which helps with comprehension, and he understands that all students are at a different level. gives feedback on ALL writing assignments which is hard work with a lot of students. easy grader, awesome teacher, and super funny. cares about his students and makes class fun.
boring lecture
The lecture is torturing boring.

- Lectures are mind-numbingly boring.
- Occasionally does random iClicker checks, and you must be in class to know the answer.
- Exams are very easy and are the exact same as the practice exams.
- The content is interesting, but he makes it uninteresting.
- One homework assignment per week. The homework is very easy.
- That is basically it.
This dude is actually the least enthusiastic person to ever live. Puts me to sleep every class> I would much rather learn the material on my own.

Last week I got home from class and was dumped by my long term girlfriend, so as one does, I went to the bar. I met this chick and spent over $100 on a bar tab just to find out she was a dude. This class has been a worse experience by far. Do not recommend.
Lord Help me

This is for Finance 3000, but there is no option for that yet This Professor may only speak about 3 words per minute during these lectures. Im trying to comprehend how this man got past any interviews with the university speaking at a literal sloth speed. I was really excited for Finance but its hard to be when you have 75 minutes of slow lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I rather get my legs blown off in WW2 then sit through this class and its the second one.

You will probably have to teach yourself this class if you are not a business / finance major. He is a nice guy but I attended every class and took notes but I did not understand the class.He's super quiet and monotone so it's hard to stay engaged and attentive.

he is very monotoned when he speaks. he also speaks exprtemly soft even sitting in the fron the the class i have trouble hearing him. he doesn't explain the problems very well. watch the videos posted on canvas they help. he also does put your final grade average in till the final is over. the exams are worth about 65% of overall grade.

He has no personality, no inflection in his voice and talk at like level 1 volume. I sat in the front and could still NOT hear him. During lecture he just reads from the slides. He gives you no real outline of what will be on the tests, so the average for all of them was like 50-60%.
Lectures are very boring and the way he weighs grades makes it difficult to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very homework and group project heavy. He grades very very graciously and if you ask him for help he will give you a lot. He is a super nice guy, but a bit boring during class.
He is a very nice guy. If you show up to class and do the work he assigns, his class is not bad. There is not that much homework, and he does a good job at giving you practice problems for the exams.
Lectures can be very boring and class is graded mostly on tests. Would not recommend but also a good dude.

Professor Trick is a really nice guy and really cares about everyone, but his class is so boring. He talks very slow and isn't really engaging. His practice tests are exactly the same as the tests just with the questions randomized. Iclicker questions also count towards your grade, so you have to be present.

While he is a caring person, I could not follow along in his lectures because his speech was incredibly slow. When it comes to exams, they are all written, not multiple choice, and require a lot of remembering formulas with no cheat sheet. Fortunately, exams are not too heavily weighted.
Cares about the students but talks soooooooooo slowly and presents the information in a pretty boring way.

This class felt like a struggle always. Test every 2-3 weeks which were most of your grade. Tests had so many concepts that it felt impossible to every really learn everything. None of the content really correlated either which made it hard to study. Test questions were lengthy and were confusing to understand. Overall felt pointless and hated it.

Uses a flipped classroom model with completion-based homework and mandatory "active-learning" sessions twice a week. This class takes a lot of your time, but Dr. Schul does respect students and will work with you. Hard to adjust to the different course structure, it's not for everyone (including me), but it's you have to try to fail this class.

Labs are basic discussions are pointless. Lectures only contain 10 minutes of content. They have a political questions in their tests which aren't need for the content. They also gave people a hard time for having vehicle problems and not making it to class once because apparently that is not "excused." Really frustrating and interesting experience
Poor course structure

Overall a very frustrating experience. The professor often came across as condescending, especially when students asked questions. The flipped classroom felt poorly executed, and the course was disorganized and unclear. Exams had multiple “correct” answers where you had to pick the “most correct,” which felt confusing and subjective.

Overall, not a difficult class, but it feels very disjointed—lectures, discussions, and labs often don't align with each other. He also occasionally includes random political topics on exams that don't seem relevant. That said, he is very helpful and accommodating, which makes the course more manageable.

The class just feels so pointless. The actual learning is online and then I travel a mile across campus for him to yap about the same subjects over and over again. Lecture, lab, and discussion material have nothing to do with each other, and it makes it feel so irrelevant. Hardest thing is navigating trick questions and boring material.

Bro yaps for 15 minutes about political issues like every other class. Like bro no one cares just teach the class im not paying to hear you talk about how the US president is like we all know. The lectures could be 20 mins max if he didnt yap the whole time about nonsense.

So boring the lectures can be almost completely ignored besides the fact he will test on something he said one time in lecture. He consistently keeps teaching past the 50 mark holding up everyone. The lecture worksheets can be done in 10 minutes yet somehow he stretches it to 53 every time. Only reason people take this is cuz its required.

If you have the option of taking this class with literally anyone else. Do it. The assignments are never-ending and class averages for tests are always in the C range if that tells you anything. Honestly half of the stuff we had to do could've been in an email but I was doing stuff for this class at least 10 hours a week. SAVE YOURSELF!!!

This guy formats his class in a way that no learning is done inside the lectures, only outside on online learning assignments. Disscussions have literally nothing to do with what we're going to be tested on, and will prove ultimatley pointless. Lab has nothing to do with course as well. Might as well be an online class with mandatory yap sessions.

His lectures were confusing, and he cherry-picks some BS questions for them. Why the hell was a question about what people look for in a job on an Intro to Biology test? 

Other than that, he was a bit boring, but his class was engaging at times. I didn't care for the lecture types. (One big picture about whatever, then delving into it).

7 tests and one final. testing every other week is not too much fun. you are put into a group that you have to sit with every single lecture, which in the lecture you do not go over new material, you have to learn everything outside of class. Labs and discussion have nothing to do with the course material. you have lab quizzes every week. stupid

I liked the course content, but his teaching style is not great. The labs and 50% of discussions have no relevance to the lecture/class content. There are 2 recorded lectures to watch outside of class a week. In-class time is for reinforcing learning but attendance is very necessary. Usually throws out a couple questions when grading tests though.
Terrible structure. Teaches nothing in class and has us learn it outside. The content is barely even biology its so useless and wont help you in future.
Don't take, topics are not useful for future. Find another biology class.

Dr. Schul is a nice guy but the class structure absolutely sucks. A test every other week, a quiz on the weeks you are not doing a test. Meeting almost everyday with the same group and going to discussions that aren't useful. Labs were very unrelated to class but had more biology topics than the class. The content is so useless for future classes.

The guys is Nice, but his class structure sucks. Almost meeting everyday and participation is required. We also have to fill out worksheets almost every day. Labs have a quiz and worksheet points. Overall try not to do this class its too much work for the same reward if you do it with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Dr Schul he cares so much about his students, all work is done in set groups during lectures, labs and discussions, attendance is mandatory, test every other week, study to do good on them

The lectures are all online, lab covers material completely unrelated to the lecture, and there are 7 exams total. 

The exam questions are applied version of what you learn, they questions are the "word problem equivalent of a math problem". Dr. Schul is a great guy, but the class makes simple concepts confusing and harder than it needs to be.

Dr. Schul makes it his number one priority that students participate in lectures and get to know the people in the class. You have to go to a lecture and it's graded on attendance.  tests and labs every other week
Inverted learning. You learn nothing in class. Takes a lot of time.

Class had a lot of information and the lectures are really fast but she records the lectures so I always watched them on my own time. She is very nice and understanding if you have situations outside of class and allows you to catch up easily

He is excellent at his job, and I really enjoyed this class. The labs were very interesting, and the content was unique and not quite what I expected to learn about. Schul is very kind and helpful as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This was the first class where I liked having group work. Dr. Schul cares a lot about making sure everyone feels included, which was a breath of fresh air for me. He was very approachable in office hours and I felt like he really wanted me to do good on the tests. The labs are annoying but the lecture and discussion are useful.

The class itself is not bad, but the course structure is horrible. Dr. Schul is a great guy, but his teaching does not match up with the tests (which are unnecessarily hard and do not correlate with the assignments given). I would suggest taking a different class if possible. He relies on groupwork, which is not very useful in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, and understanding. Overall average difficulty of the class. Do your homework and attend lectures and labs and youll be fine.

Overall his class is OK. He co-teaches with Dr. Bush. If you can, try to get her section. They're both great professors, but her lectures I've noticed are much easier to follow. You are stuck with the same lab/discussion group all semester, so if your group doesn't do the work (like mine) you get stuck doing all the work. Tests are relatively easy.

If you really enjoy science, chances are you will enjoy his class.  For being a 6 credit hour class, it did not seem like that much.  He does lots of group work.  Unfortunately, discussion sessions seem pointless.  Labs are enjoyable.  Tests are not too difficult.  Most homework assignments are not graded for accuracy.  Few complaints.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: A lot of group work in this class, he makes his lectures interesting and you can tell he is passionate about Biology. This was my favorite class this past semester.
He won't teach you anything you need to know for the next level bio courses. If you are planning on taking genetics or cell bio after this class, take a different professor.

Johannes Schul isn't a bad professor but he's a very nice person. The class content was very boring and the same topics were reiterated all semester. The exams were not too tough but you need to study to do well. The class relies to heavily on group projects and the groups are assigned to you. The lab section of this course although is awful

Professor Schul was overall a great professor. At the beginning of the semester, it took me a while to get used to the test format. They are pretty difficult if you do not study beforehand. You need to be able to apply what you've learned and truly know what's going on. He was always available during office hours listed on the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Schul is overall a really kind professor. The class is somewhat difficult but it is the material not the professor. Dr. Schul is typically available whenever you need help and truly wants his students to succeed. Studying before tests is a need.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Good professor, but lectures didn't match up to the work given. Tests didn't make any sense compared to everything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's not a bad person or a terrible professor. The class is very group work heavy which is annoying. The labs and discussions are full of busy work and group work but they're an easy A and pad the grade quite a bit. He repeats himself and doesn't move on from topics for weeks at a time, also relates everything back to one or two big topics.

Schul's a really great guy and cares a lot about his students and what he's teaching. There's points for showing up every day but he gives you so many opportunities to earn points it doesn't matter much. Don't think you can skip RSD though, he multiplies your lab and RSD grade in the end. (which is worth a quarter of your final grade.)

Classes seem weird at first like "Why am I learning about dragonflies?" BUT then as each unit goes on everything makes so much sense. There is a short exam every other week so no cramming! such a cool dude

All of the reviews say that some of the topics were too specific, but the information you learn about dragonflies and geese are really just a platform to make basic information about genetics, proteins, etc. easier to remember. He also is super available and will always e-mail you back.

Really enjoyed his class. He focuses a lot on group work, which isn't always great, but as long as you participate and do the homework, it's not hard to get an A. He very obviously cares about his students learning the material.

Dr. Schul isn't as bad as he's made out to be. Despite teaching hyper-specific topics such as geese and dragonflies, the biological concepts are pretty useful for upper-level STEM courses. However, he forces people into randomized groups, and my initial group was horrible. In general, the material is easy enough as it's introductory.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was so scattered, it felt like we werent even learning anything. There are tests every two weeks and it was pretty easy to get a good grade but I dont feel prepared for upper level classes at all. Class is graded on participation so you have to show up to get a good grade.
Talked too much about things that didn't matter like dragonflies and geese. Learned almost nothing that I should have. If possible, take with ANY other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of group work, which is awful only because they pick your groups for you. You are forced to sit with these people for the rest of the semester in lecture, lab and discussion. Labs are easy but don't match the class at all. Lots of small tests which are nice because it breaks up the material into more manageable sections. Overall not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Schul is awesome!!! Great guy, tough class but he is awesome!!

He splits the class up into groups, then you must sit by them the whole semester. I hate group work, but it was super easy and you get 10 points just for showing up to lecture everyday. He does tests every other week, but I actually like that because its easy to remember just a few topics. It's basically just a beginning genetics class. Pretty easy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class is easy for the most part but the labs dont go w/ the lecture at all. And it is really heavy in group work, which i hate. I dont want to depend on other people for my grade, but that's just me. Lots of homework. And lots of small tests. We learn a lot about things that aren't really general bio, its more about bugs and their research.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: You have to go to every class. Attendance ends up being like 30% of your grade due to group projects in class every day(not hard-just for attendance). A test every other week. Not a bad teacher, but he's all over the place. I got an A and don't think I learned anything. Just retained enough for the tests. Only take if you can attend every day!

Christiansen is so sweet, but the class is difficult and everything is done using excel. Four timed exams make up 80% of your grade, though cheatsheets are allowed for exams and retakes. My discussion TA wasn't at all helpful, so I stopped showing up for those. Watching the videos Christiansen leaves on discussion quizzes is more than enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took STAT2200 and Dr. Christiansen was the lecturer for it. Her lectures were easy to understand and she gave a lot of examples on how to do the problems. As long as you keep up with the lecture quizzes and lectures, this class is an easy A.

Tests are worth 80% of the grade, making all other assignments pointless. If Teri was as concerned about the structure of her class rather than catching people cheating in her class, then the course would be tolerable. DO NOT RECOMMEND! Class needs a new professor.
Not easy class. TA aren't very easy to reach.
Do not take her class

Incredibly well organized course, if you prepare excel files before taking quizzes you'll secure yourself an A for sure. Any qualms can be answered by Teri, she's very kind and cares a lot about students understanding her subject.
Super clear lectures, always knew what was expected on quiz and homework. Great Prof.
Super nice, class isn't hard if you follow along and make the excel files for the quizzes.
Would not recommend this teacher at all.

Way too difficult for an Intro class. Asked for in person help through my T/A since I could not understand what they were saying on Zoom, and was told no. Honorlock is required on all quizzes. DO NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the most psychotic professor imaginable with her new quiz procedures. If at any point a new professor is available for stats jump on it. Otherwise get ready for a semester of hell.
Gives no resources, spends every waking minute trying to catch people cheating. She's horrible and mizzou needs another stats professor

Honestly, I genuinely liked her. After the first discussion class, I stopped going and watched the videos she uploaded online and it helped me understand more. So long as you pay attention to the iClickers and actually take time to make your cheat sheet for quizzes (a whole excel file with screenshots), there's no reason to get lower than a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This teacher is awful, convincing herself she is doing the right thing with insane quiz procedures in an intro stats class. Not a surprise that so many kids dropped. It sucks that this is a required course for business majors, but if a new teacher comes along, take them instead!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Do NOT take this class unless you're ready to study 15+ hours every two weeks.

The quizzes cover material barely mentioned in class, make up 80% of your grade, are timed, and use Honorlock (which pauses your already under-timed test for any movement they deem unnecessary). 

This class is NOT worth the hassle.
No sympathy, 80% of grade are quizzes that are completely honorlocked with no scratch paper or calculator, she watches all the recordings

Honorlocks everything and gives you no resources (calculator, scratch paper) to help you with the 20 quizzes you have to take. Genuinely think she should take the class herself to see how hard she makes it for us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes are extremely difficult and account for 80% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are 80% of grade, everything is Honorlocked and she quite literally goes through every single test and watches you. Half the class dropped it when I took it because she was so insane about the exams yet made them worth 80% of our grades.
She is great and makes concepts and R/ Excel sound super easy.

Very kind professor, and probably provides the most preparatory material for assignments/quizzes for any class I've had to date. On top of that, her slides look nice and are comprehensive. No exams either, just quizzes and homework -- no complaints.

So nice and caring! Her lectures were informative and she applied them to real life and made them interesting. It is clear she has been teaching this class for years and knows just about everything there is to know--not only about the material but about Canvas and the homework and quiz software.

She posts all the lectures online. I would just watch the lectures online after she posted them so that I could pause/fast forward at my own pace. Stats2500 is pretty much all excel, and she was really good at explaining how that works for intro level. Bi-weekly quizzes that were online, so no big exams. Fairly easy class but I still learned a lot

Teri is great! Stat 3500 is so much easier than 2500. You learn how to use a software this is much more intuitive than using Excel in Stat 2500. There are no exams and only online quizzes. One quiz can be dropped. Lab and Lecture can both be accessed via zoom, its a very flexible class.

I have more than enough nice things to say about this professor. She was really great and responded quickly to questions. You will use Excel and Posit cloud but she helps you get used to them first. All around amazing!
Amazing professor. She cares a lot about the students and does a wonderful job! Class is quite easy just make sure to watch lectures and do the practice quizzes!

Great professor! Took 3500 as well, even though I didn't need to, because I enjoyed and truly learned useful things in her classes. She's extremely flexible and has a course built to work however you need it to. Fair deadlines and tests you can take, relatively, on your own time. She wants you to be successful.

Teri is a terrific professor! I took this course online and everything is in a set-and-stone routine which is amazing!  It can get a little difficult but Teri is no stranger to helping you out! Every week consists of notes, homework, and "discussion" which is like another homework assignment. Quizzes are scattered around so be prepared!
Great class, if you show up and pay attention you will pass. All of the work is done on Excel, and it is easy to learn, especially if you have a discussion class.
She's very nice and gives you everything you need to succeed. (templates, recorded lectures, tutoring, etc) Gives great lectures, makes it straight forward and easy to understand

Christiansen is very kind and good at teaching. Her slides are strait forward, and she explains and does example problems in class. A lot of the class is online, including tests, and is very excel heavy, but if you follow her slides and lectures she gives you equations/outlines you can copy and paste to use for the test.

Mrs. C was awesome. Her lectures are interesting and she tries to keep everyone engaged. She's intelligent and cares about the subject. Quizzes every other week, they aren't hard but make sure to take notes and do the homework.

Teri is very nice and understanding of everything. For the class, it was nice as it was all online kind of. Although you still have to do the HW and know what you are doing or the quizzes will drop your grade.

Good professor, just hard material, easy to get behind, also some people found it easy to cheat on the tests (because online), so they did and got reported, so don't do that. Also I heard cheating on the tests proved to be very difficult since you don't have enough time and you have to take a picture of all your problems worked out and send it in.
8 quizzes that were pretty easy. I didn't go to one class and got an A. If you can use excel you will excel in the class :)
Had Teri for 2500 and again for 3500, you won't be disappointed. Fantastic lectures (go in-person), material can be a little daunting at first but there are numerous resources available.

Dr. Christiansen's lectures made statistics straightforward and easy to follow, even if it's still a hard subject. While the tests can be hard, there's generally opportunity to recuperate from a bad test and improve your study habits. The lectures are also recorded, which gives great accessibility if you're ill/something else preventing attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teri is the best prof in the stats department, she is very willing to help and genuinely wants you to get a good grade. I've taken both stat 3500 and 4710 with her and she is beyond reasonable in every way. She often lets you make up points on quizzes and exams, but you have to earn them, it won't be easy makeup points, but at least it's offered.

professor Christiansen is easily the best stats professor you could take at MU. I had her for 2500 and am currently taking 3500 with her. Her lectures are very clear and concise, she posts her excel sheets that she uses in class, and her quizzes and homework have no surprises on them. If you need a stat 2500 credit definitely take her!

Mrs. C is a great professor! Attendance is not required, and she posts a recording of each lecture on her Canvas. The lectures are easy to follow and specific about each topic. The homework and graded excel tutorials mirror pretty much what will be on the quizzes, so if you do those and understand them, you're pretty much set.

Mrs. C is a pretty average prof. Her lectures aren't interesting but they'll get you through the homework. She constantly expects you to use excel spreadsheets. If you do the homework, its not that hard to earn an A.
She has great lectures and explains concepts well. I recommend taking her class for Stat 2500.
In-depth, specific lectures. If you have a problem with grading she will sort it out, she is very responsive and flexible.

She is absolutely amazing professor. Her lectures are engaging, her communication in the course is clear, she gives very detailed feedback that perfectly makes sense, always open to meet outside class and you really learn the content in her class. She is perfect example of a good professor. Definitely should take the class with her if you can.

Tracy is just the absolute best professor I've had in the past three years at Mizzou. Her lectures are super easy to understand, and she makes it extremely clear which topics from the textbook you need to read for the exams. Her grading on group projects is extremely fair, and her feedback is detailed. She's awesome!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was a significant introduction to an 8-week group project, and she was amazing in teaching and providing everything necessary for it. Her feedback is excellent and really helped me; it never discouraged me, and that's what I love about her as a professor!

Dr. Brown was seriously my favorite journalism professor in my years at Mizzou. I'm a 3rd-year strat comm student, and her lectures are so informative. There are a lot of group projects, so as long as you score well on those you'll be set. and the exams are pretty straightforward.

Tracy was an amazing professor! She encouraged us to meet with her outside of class and when I did she remembered a detail I had included in an assignment weeks prior, even though she has hundreds of students. The assignments and in-class quizzes for attendance are very straight forward and she has clear feedback to give.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good class, you can tell she enjoys teaching the provided material, I enjoy all of the lectures as well.

if you can, definitely take her for Intro to Strat Comm! she made the class super straightforward and as long as you follow the rubric, the assignments are very simple. Also -- there's no lecture on Fridays, which rocks. assignments are: attendance quizzes, bi-weekly-ish group projects, weekly chapter quizzes, and two tests. awesome lectures too!

Tim Hill is a chill guy and he seems to be very engaging. I don't think he is a bad professor and does do interactive stuff in the lectures. The downside might be that lectures can feel pointless at times since you can skip a few and get a good grade. Overall, Tim is not bad but the homework is what counts towards most of the grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Perfect class! Really kind professor and has lots of great material in class.
He was a chill guy, however, the class itself was a joke and was taken way to seriously for being a class that teaches you to smile when you meet new people.

Make sure you're following the rubric and listening to the lectures. He's a great guy and makes lectures interesting even though the topic isn't. Prepare to be called on and participate in-class activities. TAKE NOTES! IT'S AN OPEN NOTE EXAM!
Chill guy, makes his classes fun
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good professor, Really caring and it's an entry level class, some of the work can be hard but it gets you up off your ass and makes you start doing stuff. Final exam is dropped if attendance is high enough so just dont skip and you'll be fine.
The lectures and professor was ok the class is very end-loaded though so you have to lock in the last few weeks.
super nice guy
If you need BA 1500, I highly recommend taking it over the summer. Besides a few projects and assignments, this is a very low commitment. He's a lenient grader and offers extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty standard, don't have to be too engaged to know whats going on.
Don't take him if you can
There's a lack of empathy or flexibility, even in legitimate situations.
I do not recommend this course if you're looking for a supportive or engaging learning environment.
Would rather transfer colleges than have him as a professor again.
Hands down the worst professor at Mizzou, not sure who hired him.
Was very inconsiderate when it came to matters outside my control.

Professor Hill had great, easy to follow lectures and lots of opportunities to raise your grade. There is a lot of homework, but most are short assignments. He makes it easy to stay engaged in the course and there is a pretty good policy with attendance and the final exam!
You can tell he loves his job and enjoys helping out students

He seems very passionate in his lectures and tries to keep students engaged by having fun. Very easy to get an A, just go to most classes and turn things in on time. If you don't turn something in by the deadline, your grade will drop drastically.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tim was a great instructor. I feel, however, that this class could've been more beneficial as an online course. Besides that matter, the class was engaging and allowed us to have a little fun. No tests, but plenty of projects and discussions. Tim is very knowledgeable and understanding; make sure to always talk with him if you have concerns.
Good teacher who seems passionate in his lectures and easy class
Tim is very friendly and engaging. Attendance is mandatory, and the class was offered at an unfortunate time (5pm on Mondays), but other than that, I can think of no complaints.
Tim Hill is passionate about the subject matter. Lectures are usually interesting and are made exciting even for the undesirable timeslot.

Professor Hill is very nice and gives great lectures. But the information wasn't something I felt I needed. This course could have been 100% online and I would have gained the same thing I gained by taking time out of my day to attend a 5pm lecture. Only good thing was I learned how to structure a nice looking resume :)

Tim Hill was a great professor. Do I think some of the content we went over was middle school level? Yes. Did I still like this class? Also yes. The most annoying part about this course was that it was only offered during Monday evenings. Overall the class was super easy, and my TA (Mikala Vaughn) was super great too! Attendance was very lenient!
Great teacher

I liked Prof Hill, but BA1500 was mad annoying. The classes offered are only at 5pm and 6pm which by itself sucks, and the lectures just feel like a waste of time. We are in college so we don't need to still be learning about basic concepts like "teamwork." TA of your lab grades your work, so sometimes it can be a little picky or harsh. It's ok.

Despite BA1500 being a joke of a class, he made these lectures worth going to because of his enthusiasm about business. Most of the curriculum is useless and common sense, but the resume and mock interview were helpful.

I didn't like how much he made us interact with other students in the class. Gave a few bigger assignments which take some time, but overall very easy. You volunteer somewhere for the semester which is great for your resume. Will pick on random people in class to explain their iclicker.

BA 2500 is so pointless the business school is getting rid of the course. I had to stand up and touch my eyes, ears, and nose one day. However Tim is very nice and understanding. Class did give me volunteering hours for a resume at leat

The class content is common sense but Tim did a good job making it interesting. Each week we had a Smartbook assignment, online assignment, and discussion lab. Very easy class but it's a bunch of busy work. You get 4 excused absences for both lecture and lab, so if you push through to Halloween, you should be able to stop going after that. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Tim Hill talks a bunch of nonsense and honestly nothing is helpful besides creating a resume.
Good professor and TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very easy class, just have to participate in the iclicker every class. You have to show up and participate in the once-a-week lab. Very easy to schedule a meeting during office hours even for things not related to class.

Tim, despite being on paternity leave nearly all semester, made it a habit of being easily accessible by email and still taught his class. BA1500 is stupidly easy, but Tim does make it interesting, engaging and does a good job presenting information which could put people to sleep with a bad instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Freshman level class Makes it an easy class for freshman in business Stupid easy class

Professor Hill might be the friendliest guy on the planet, but his class is mostly common sense. The one helpful assignment is the Resumé assignment, but besides that this class is difficult to justify putting a bunch of effort into. It is an easy A though, which will take some pressure off of you.

Professor Tim is STELLAR. He's responsive to his students, he breaks concepts down, he's never condescending or prideful, he exudes compassion and understanding, equips you with the tools needed to be successful, gives out effective reminders, etc. Make sure you show up to class 'cause attendance and participation is part of your grade.

I took the transfer student combo course for 1500 and 2500 which I really recommend for transfer students going into the business school. Its faster paced than taking both classes separately and doesnt have the freshman orientation bit the lecture has. This class is also smaller than the lecture option in Busch making it easier to get help.

Professor Hill cares about his students' wellbeing. However, I feel like this class size is way too large and prevent students from doing their best. It's super distracting to have over 400 students in Bush Auditorium, and I'm doing better now that this course is online. It's not his fault that he only gets one section of 1500 per semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tim is a good guy but he teaches a class that doesn't mean anything. It's pretty much a show up and do your work class where you don't learn anything but it boosts your GPA. Only one class a week once you start doing you volunteering (part of the class) and late in the semester he makes it once every other week.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tim Hill has never been in the business world, and as such, has no knowledge on the subject. The lectures are borderline painful to attend because of how long he drones, on plus the lecture hall being way too small for only one section. The only thing this class prepares someone for is dealing with paperwork and unnecessary garbage during finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tim truly cares about the students' wellbeing and their understanding of the content. He is a great speaker, so it's not hard to pay attention to lectures. He also does a really nice job of coming up with new ideas for the class like holding a Q&A panel rather than a lecture. Quizzes and exams are open book/note/laptop, whatever, so it's not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lecture is boring but gives extra credit for attending. Lots of case studies and essays but if you follow the rubric youll do fine. Would probably recommend taking the class online over the summer if you dont have time for the 15 hours of volunteering the class requires (but I enjoyed the volunteering, it wasnt too bad)
just take someone else

Incredibly helpful and kind professor. Expectations were clear for all assignments and class was structured in a way where you could learn from your mistakes instead of being punished for them. Also extremely helpful in office hours and walked you through how to solve the problem.

I loved this professor, while DiffEq is a very difficult class, Christiansen cared about her students and wanted us to do well. She had very helpful review guides and review sessions before exams. The review guides are pretty much questions from the exam. She has us participate during class, which is also nice.

Tanya Christiansen is one of the worst professors that I've had at Mizzou. She gives nearly no partial credit on exams. I once did a question almost completely right and she gave me a 2/10 because the final answer was wrong. She was also incredibly rude and made you feel stupid for asking a question. Take this class with literally anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher. Basically calls you stupid and laughs at you with any question you bring to her in office hours. Exams were close to the reviews, but she only posts the answers and no work so you need to know how to do it on your own. She writes a lot on the board and it is hard to write everything and understand it. Take someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Christiansen was one of the worst professors I have ever had. Your grade is based almost only off of exams. Her reviews are nothing like the actual exam and the review answer key is only answers with no work to see how to solve the problem. She makes you feel stupid for asking questions and has no interest in helping you once start to fail.

Lectures were pretty easy to follow and she gave extra material outside of what was required for extra help. Office hours were semi-helpful, although if it was crowded you could only ask one or two questions.

Professor Christiansen is really good at explaining difficult material. She does not assign excessive amounts of homework but gives you plenty of practice problems. Calc 2 with Christiansen is still difficult, but not unbearable.

Mrs. C was great for STAT 2500! One of the best professors I have had. Caring and easily accessible outside of class. She responded to my email after 10pm one night! Attendance was taken, so make sure you show up. Be careful, this class is 80% exam and 20% homework, so if you don't do well in exam settings, be prepared to struggle.

I usually go to her 2pm section of Statistics when I need to listen to a lecture again although I am enrolled in the 9:30AM - 10:45AM section taught by a TA but she explains concepts very well and gives you very good resources to study for exams. Be sure to study for the exams the most because they take up the most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Christiansen was a very good Calculus 2 Professor. She was amazing at teaching the concepts and explaining how to solve problems. If you study and do practice problems you will be fine for the quizes and especially the exams. I thought the quizzes were fair and the exams were really easy. She is by far my favorite professor at Mizzou so far!

The class's grade is basically all exams. She won't ever tell you what your grade is either. It's impossible to know how you're doing in her class. The exams are really, really hard as well. The class material is hard, but she makes it much harder than it has to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't take any class from this prof. It's impossible to get an A or B unless you want to spend endless hours outside of class. She expects you to do at least 100 practice probs/week on top of the hw. Her exams are incredibly hard and she trys to run you out of time and trick you constantly. She also won't ever tell you your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very clear cut lectures with average difficulty exams. She really knows what she is talking about and makes calculus seem less complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She rocks
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Teri Christiansen is the best math teacher I've ever had. She explains every topic in such a clear way that it's very easy to understand. We go through a lot of examples in-class, and she's always offering extra help to those who need it. It's probably a good idea to attend class, because she gives quizzes almost every day.

Dr. Christiansen is an insanely intelligent woman. Very helpful, and her lectures were CLEAR and to the point. I didn't do well in Calc II in high school but nailed it at MU because of here. Just make sure you GO TO CLASS. I definitely recommend taking her class. She's strict, teaches class like a nun, but it's for a good reason.
Best math teacher I've ever had.

Teri is such a nice teacher. She really cares about her students. This class was tough for me (College Algebra 3x a week) and she made it the best it could be. I didn't go for extra help, but I could tell she really helped a lot of people. She is easily the best math teacher I have ever had. Just a fair warning: calculators are not allowed.

Dr. Christiansen is excellent. She makes complicated Calc topics fairly easy for everyone to understand. She keeps lectures interesting and she always answers questions. Quizzes and tests will be difficult if you don't do the practice problems, but she does post old exams online for extra practice and gives partial credit.
SUCH a good teacher. My class was daily but with her as my teacher I didn't even mind going. So willing to help and really wants you to do well. Definitely take her if you can!

Great class and professor! Very nice, knows when to avoid being too "technical" when explaining the theory behind things and isn't too hung up on "mathspeak"/theory specifics. Exams are meant to test your mastery of the material, so homework is a MUST. One of the best professors ever!!!

She is an excellent teacher. Her notes are pretty clear. In order to do well, show up to class, ask questions, and DO the suggested homework problems and practice exams. It is possible to do well. One of my favorite classes this semester.

Dr. Christiansen is a great professor! Thorough explanations, open for any questions and is concise with her teaching. Exams can be tricky...if you don't practice the old ones she gives out, which makes them far easier!

Christiansen is an amazing teacher.  By far the best professor I have yet to encounter.  She knows what she is doing and she is great at explaining the material.  You will have more than enough resources to do well n this class.  If you have her take advantage of the opportunity.  She is your best bet.  If you do bad its COMPLETELY your fault.

Best math teacher I've ever had. She is very nice, VERY helpful, and she makes everything very easy to understand. You can tell she really cares about students, and she's funny. I highly recommend this teacher!!
WONDERFUL teacher! She is super sweet and helpful. If you have to take college algebra, definitely take her! She constantly makes an effort to make sure you're doing well. choose this teacher!!!!
Clear, and easy to follow lectures.Good explanations. Course content was boring for me, but made tolerable by her lectures. Very difficult exams, though. Study hard, lol.

AMAZING teacher. Goes over news and announcements several days in a row in case you missed, is very organized (makes available a handbook of her slides), gives study guides, has a lot of office hours, uses CPS clickers to get feedback and maintain interest, good speaker and humorous at times. I wish i had all my math classes with her
Excellent instructor!  Very clear, and is ALWAYS avaliable for help if you need it.  No suprises on the tests.  Definitely take one of her classes if you have the opportunity.
She was very easy to understand, as well as very nice!  The tests were hard, but she gave us ample time to prepare.

She was a great teacher, and from what I know, she was brought to MU to TEACH, not RESEARCH.  She has a lot of positives, grades fairly and knows her stuff.  She tells you everything you need to know, homework was not mandatory, but it helped.  If you have never had a math class at the college level and you get her feel privileged!

Instructor is very clear in presenting information to the class and is always willing to put in extra hours to help students in need. Her tests are hard; however, you can do well in that class as long as you apply yourself and study, study, study!
No Comments

She was really interested in you actually learning the information. She didn't throw curves at you just to see what would happen. If there was a hard problem, it was always something she had gone through in class or made sure you understood. Explains things multiple ways. You have to study, but she is a great teacher.

Teri is one of the best teachers I've had at any level - take her class if you can.  She really wants students to learn the material and succeed. Her explanations are easy to understand and she can explain things in multiple ways. Teri makes herself available for help outside of class and even outside of her office hours if needed.
Very easy to follow, but sometimes gets overboard on exams.....Good teacher though, actually learned something without feeling like everything depended on exam scores
Very clear and very effective. Always there for help. Really showed concern that ALL of her students pass her class. Great teacher.

Mrs. Christiansen's tests are wayyy too hard.  18 q's worth 7 pts a piece, no partial credit, is ridiculous!  But I forgive her because she is very easy to look at.  Not hot at first class, but after a semester, you might change your mind.
She did a good job of teaching the material...sometimes the tests were harder than the reviews, but it wasn't that bad.  She does speak fluient english, which is rare in MU's math department.
Amazing teacher, knows the material extremely well and can actually teach unlike most of the professors.  I would label her by far the best teacher I have had in the math department.
Great teacher.  Really knows Calculus and how to teach it!  She is pretty serious and takes control of the class.  Take her class!!!!

Take her class if you can!  Rare combination of solid knowledge of the subject, great teaching skills and willingness to impart her knowledge.  Willing to schedule extra hours to go over material you don't understand.  Drops lowest quiz and homework scores and also curves at the end of the class.  Very friendly and extremely helpful.
The course material stinks, but the professor presented it in such a way that made it much easier to understand. Hard tests, but generous curves. Very approachable.

Attendance isn't mandatory but if you get a certain grade on iClicker questions you don't have to take the final. 3-6 assignments a week all due Monday but not to difficult. As long as you pay attention and take notes over lectures and homework you should be fine.
all in all one of the best speakers for a teacher I've ever had. Don't be afraid to ask questions.

Tabitha is interested and passionate about what she is teaching. It is very fast-paced and lecture heavy, but if you show up to class, pay attention, find class buddies, and do the homework you'll be just fine. You don't need to read the textbook. Don't feel too bad about low test scores because they won't ruin your grade.

From what I've heard from other Econ 1014 students with different teachers, it seems she was the best. Lectures are always informational, and she knows what she's talking about--but don't be surprised when she starts to guilt the class for petty stuff

Also, participate in the iClickers if you can get out of the exam. Extreme lifesaver.
Tests can be difficult but it's weighted to where you could bomb every test and still have a good grade. If you pay attention and do the homework you will do just fine in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Purposeful trick questions and takes pride in no one getting 100% on her exam/ quizzes. Ive reached out to her over various ambiguous questions but never admits she's in the wrong. However, i have caught multiple mistakes of hers in her algebra and uploading wrong assignments. In summer session she uploaded assignments midweek (bruh). Save urself
The lectures can go a little quickly, but Tabitha is great at making connections between the lecture and the real world, and she'll answer any questions either in or out of class.
She just talks really fast and does not explain anything
This class was very difficult, but Juneau was the entire reason I passed. As long as you participate, she is willing to help. She met with me for tutoring and took a lot of time to help her students.

Class lectures move very fast and sometimes can be confusing, but Tabitha is good about answering any questions and is engaging. Her lectures are posted on Canvas but attendance is still mandatory for grade. Tests are just like the practice exams. 3 extra credit opportunities. Honors micro is harder than normal micro so keep that in mind.

Tabitha is such a sweet, knowledgeable instructor! Her lectures are very important to understanding the material but are very engaging. If office hours don't work for you, she will make time to schedule an in-person meeting with you and will respond to emails very quickly. She is very clearly passionate about economics and is always open to chat!

This class could have been great. it seems like you are learning a ton and you will be prepared for the test. For tests, the wording is purposefully difficult to trick you so you don't know which answer is correct. It's as if she tries to make sure you get the question wrong. You could do well on the practice exam and really bad on the actual exam.
Overcomplicates material and poorly words tests so that the concepts are less-recognizable for no reason. There are lots of holes in her explanations and examples that easily confuse students.

Lectures are sometimes fast paced and material can feel monotonous at times, but overall a great class and professor. Grading is very fair, material isn't too hard (but isn't trivial either), and there is adequate extra credit. Professor is very willing to help students on class material or economics education overall.
She knows her stuff but the lectures can move extremely quick at times. Showing up to class is vital if you want an A as iClicker is a huge part of the grade. Weekly quizzes are usually pretty fair.

She is very open about wanting to help her students and is willing to go the extra mile. She is very knowledgeable in the topics and can answer pretty much any question. Lots of extra credit that isn't too hard, but it boosts your grade a lot. Highly recommend!

Unal is not a bad professor but there are some small issues. Calc 3 is paced very fast and is very difficult if you miss a single lecture. I think my class had an abnormal experience with Unal because he always seemed upset with everything from my class and said we are not like his other classes. He can be hard to understand at times.

Great professor and a class that really goes the extra mile in ensuring that you are prepared for calc 2. As long as you show up to class every day and attend the occasional review session you will NOT fail this class. 

Cons:
Pacing is a lil fast

This class is pretty tough but Unal makes it decently digestible and is a nice guy that you can tell likes being a professor. My best advice would be to not try to hard to understand the meaning behind the concepts and just focus on learning how to do the problems. He is pretty helpful if you need help.
Took a second to catch on but after a bit his lectures were great. Doing practice problems out of the textbook was a big help as they were harder than what was on the exams.

Dr. Unal is great! His lectures encourage you to try and learn and will have you attempt concepts in class! The exams are kind of tough but are easier than the homework problems. He grades fairly tough and small mistakes will cost you, but he genuinely cares and wants you to succeed!

Unal is very nice and caring, but he is a little bit eccentric and his lectures take time to be able to understand well. Once you get a feel for his style though, his lectures are amazing and you will understand everything very well. His review sessions for exams are VERY important, never miss them.

The first test was challenging. There are exam concepts that we didn't over in class (and no review guides). His teaching style is outdated and easy to get lost in. Online notes don't correlate with lectures  (where he makes mistakes and changes variables/numbers in examples). Calc123 was easy, but it felt complicated when he reviewed the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very difficult to understand and often rushes through explanations. Most of my class thought the course was regular Linear Algebra which it is NOT, take Matrix Theory if you want to learn about Linear Algebra topics. Isn't always clear on what grading criteria is and docks points for the smallest of errors. Class average for HWs and Exams was a 49%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Unal could have been a lot better. Went to his office hours atleast once a week, but his grading is just weird. Good luck if you have him but he doesn't always answer email. Also reviews are strictly in person and there are NO practice tests, all you can do to prepare is study notes which don't even always cover everything.

Dr. Unal was awesome. His lectures were super helpful and he responded super well to questions without making you feel dumb for asking. He creates a welcoming environment in his class and tries to make sure everyone understands. The material was not too bad but make sure you have a strong foundation on calc 1 and 2 and do the homework.

Dr. Unal is an amazing math professor, his lectures are very conversational and his classes feel comfortable. His class did require some work, but if you put in the work and study what he teaches you will not have a difficult time being successful. Overall, he was my favorite math professor that I have had yet at Mizzou.

Dr Unal was not an effective professor. The class average on our first exam was a 55%. He told us that he did not deserve for his class average to be a 55%, but if the whole class fails, that's his fault. He changes problems halfway though solving both in class and during exams and quizzes. Students had to correct his many mathematical errors daily

Diff Eqs is a tough class, but Dr. Unal makes sure that every student understands the content. He is very friendly and I cannot recommend him enough. He knew every students name, and made me look forward to class everyday. The exams were tough, but if you pay attention in class you can get through them with little trouble.

Lectures were definitely dry, but the syllabus was more to blame than her teaching. She took feedback and did her best to make sure we were happy with how she ran the course, which is all you can really ask for. Exams were never a surprise or a curveball, last two labs are super time consuming but lab is ran by TAs, not the prof.

Deniz is a very kind professor and cares about the success of her students! Make sure to show up for the biweekly quizzes, she'll cover the material on the quiz right before it. The labs are a good portion of your grade, but it's easy to get 100s on if you put in the work. The exams are all multiple choice with 10 built in bonus points.

Fair and kind professor. She genuinely wants you to succeed and is happy to meet with you to help. Lectures are not the best, but you can understand enough to easily do well on exams. She offered extra credit too. The labs are a different story as the manuals were not clear about what needed to be included, and the TAs are on a power trip.

Good professor, expectations were clear. Grading system is great. She's not great at lecturing and the lectures are pretty dry, but the class was overall somewhat easy if you have any prior knowledge of programming in any language. Exams have some trick questions, similar to the other professors of this course. But otherwise an overall good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not bad, I knew exactly what was expected of me. Very poor at lecturing incredibly dry but attendance is not mandatory and the class pace is so brutally slow you can learn it all in a few hours on your own before the exams and do well. Gani, one of the TAs, is on.a SERIOUS power trip, don't let him touch anything you need graded.

This class relies on C, which is not beginner friendly despite this being a 101 class. She writes quickly, which is a double-edged sword. I really like that she drops the lowest 2 labs, and the adjustable grading system. If you are not a CS major, take CS-1700, its the same concepts in a friendly-ier language. I wished the lectures weren't as dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor extremely confusing to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good and worthwhile class if you put in the work. Tim is an excellent professor too
Homework is nothing like what we see on the exams. Tim forgets the fact that in real life we can just google something, so one would think a one sided cheat sheet on exams would be acceptable.

He is a good person, but not a good teacher. I clicker is for attendance but not multiple choice, so if you put even a wrong decimal in, you do not get attendance credit for being there. He likes to repeat himself. His life's mission is to make the exams hard, and for us to memorize dozens of formulas. The lectures are also disorganized.
The expectations for tests are insane
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Howald is a good person, but his ADHD-ridden lectures and inability to finish thoughts make his lectures nearly impossible to comprehend. His lectures do not pertain to the exams in any sort on the bright side. He usually provides a 200-question test bank, so I recommend memorizing formulas instead of listening to an "um ummm uh" filled word salad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tim was a great professor in my book. The class was hard but felt like it was worth it. Prepare those tests at least 2 weeks in advance!!

Tim is a great professor I've had him for four classes now and he really doesn't care about his students and wants to see them succeed. If you need help he is always willing. Know all of the problems on the practice exams he gives and you will get in A in all his classes, he doesn't try to trick you he gives you everything you need to be successful

He is nice, but genuinely one of the most unhelpful professors I have ever had. He talks way too fast and goes on about pointless information while barely working problems or explaining the complex concepts. He prides himself on making the tests unnecessarily difficult, like 180 page practice test and making you memorize 25+ ratios without notes.
Had for both 3000 and 4356. Both have the exact same issues. Talks too fast, self proclaims his exams being hard, lots of textbook work.
Speaks unreasonably fast, tests are brutal (his own words), Requires tons of memorization and textbook work.
He posts all possible questions that will be on the test. If you are a good student willing to put in the work you will have no problem getting an A.

Professor Howald cares about his students, I found the videos he makes before each exam to be EXTREMELY helpful (you'll 110% see a similar question on the exam). His lectures can drag at times and he does use iClicker.

The class is set up well (you get a dropped exam & some assignments). If you study the guide and watch the vids you'll be alright

This class depends on your learning style. Lectures are unhelpful, and exams are based entirely on memorizing a 200-question practice test, with 50 questions pulled at random. If you like memorization, it's fine, but if you want to actually learn, it's frustrating.
He is not very good at lecturing or explaining complex topics. He works though examples too fast without doing a good job of making sure students are understanding.
