Good professor, holds two hour zoom meetings before the exams to answer questions and is really caring, I would def take him again and you can tell he really likes his job and what he does. Exams are 50 questions but has 200 question answer key where he pulls exam questions from. Study and you'll do fine.

Professor Howald is a very nice guy, and an overall good professor, but his exams are hard and all cover a ton of information. 
Maybe this is just because his only section this semester was at 8am, but I found his lectures sometimes yappy and hard to follow. Overall, Tim is a caring professor with a long and successful career in this field, a bonus
Lecture heavy class with mandatory i clicker. He's Super difficult to follow during lecture, Would not recommended.

Currently taking this class. The videos for exam prep are awful and although it's a 200 question study guide similar to the exam the material is a ton. I survived griswold with an A and I still feel like this class is harder.

Great professor but the class was WAY too hard for a required course. There are other finance professors that don't make you take a 50 question exam, I would recommend taking those if you are not pursing finance. However, Tim would make a fantastic professor if you're going into finance/accounting.

This class is structured very simply. He gives you a 200-question practice exam, and 50 of the questions are on the test. If you attend the lecture, you can eventually get extra credit once you meet the attendance requirements. There is no reason you shouldn't be doing well in class when he practically gives you the exam and offers extra credit.

He will say that he is never wrong, that if there is mistake than its probably your own fault. I cannot even count the times he was wrong. The amount of emails and announcements sent out saying "a student caught this mistake". His lectures are graded over clicker but you will end up teaching yourself the material. avoid this professor if you can.

Not a good teacher. Excel-based homework but handwritten exams, so do the practice exam repetitively. His lectures and assignments do not correlate to his tests. 
However, he's a nice guy. Definitely would take with Griswold if you're looking to emphasize your major in finance because he does a bad job with the foundational knowledge.

homework is exclusivly on excel, which you cannot use on the tests... lectures arent great, felt like we covered about 30% of test material in lectures. Definitly take a dif teacher for finance 3000 he is bad

Tim isn't the best. He's average for Mizzou finance profs, but that's not saying much. Attendance is mandatory iClicker. Lots of easy homework, 3 tests, 1 final. He drops some grades, which helps. Lectures are useless, he rambles and doesn't prep us for exams at all. TAs don't help and you'll end up teaching yourself most of the stuff but its a ton

his only redeeming quality is that he is somewhat funny. he always talked way too fast and sped through lecture. His questions on simnet are wrong all the time but he won't admit it. Do not take a class with him if you can avoid it.
he's one of the best professors I have ever had. He made my finance class journey interesting. absolutely take his class. he teaches so well. HE DOES CARE ABOUT EVERY STUDENT!

He lectures well so that you get the topic. He has much experience in finance, he really knows what he's teaching. Attendance is required, there are 2-3 easy iclickers daily,class starts with music, the first iclicker is- how you like today's music. Exams  gonna be easy if you study. He's super caring professor. I'd love to take his classes again.

As a senior undergrad, Dr. Ekin has easily been my favorite professor. He is very knowledgeable, and does an excellent job at sharing said knowledge with his students. The homework assignments can be a bit tough, but Dr. Ekin is always readily available to help you out. He is also a nice and funny guy, which makes lectures enjoyable to attend!

Positives:
Labs are very well set up and explained. I was never confused.
Engages with students and is good at taking questions.
Tests are intuitive and don't seem unfair.
Negatives:
Just reads off slides a bit too much. Need more examples
We never get our tests back. Just goes over the whole test.

Ekin seems like a great guy who is very knowledgeable about the field. If you have any sort of coding experience in any language the class will be cake for you. Attendance isn't "mandatory" but are often pop quizzes that are only accessible in the classroom. Grades are largely made up of just a few exams that are all 40 question multiple choice.

I wish there was more material put out for exam specific review rather than just the lecture slides, I understand that is our job to create guides and such but the slides themselves seemed so hard to pull information off of without the context of the lectures. Great guy and very understanding of uncontrollable circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ekin knows what he's doing, but it's hard to take notes during lectures because he goes so fast and mainly focuses on coding examples.  If you make an effort to know what you're doing, then you'll be fine.    Attendance is important, so be ready for iClicker quizzes.

Labs and tests can be hard sometimes but honestly I think the first exam and some of the earlier labs purely exist to weed people out. Ekin uses JimR's exams so be prepared for some annoying questions. The final was quite a bit easier compared to all the exams so just stick with the class and go to office hours if needed and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not a hard class but not an easy class either

Overall, I think Dr. Ekin is a good professor. He is very passionate about computer science and you can tell he loves languages like C and C++ and is always willing to answer questions. The labs are pretty fun and engaging. The tests are pretty difficult but not impossible. I prepared for the tests by testing random questions I had about C.

Ekin is a good teacher, but the class setup itself makes it extremely difficult. The exams are designed to trick you. Everyone fails them. Be prepared to grind or else you will fail or get a bad grade. If you can get out of taking this class by doing it online through UMSL, I would. I plan to do that for 2050.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ekin is good at teaching the topics of 1050, and the labs were, for the most part, easy. However, the tests are full of trick questions that assess your ability to be a compiler rather than your ability to understand coding principles—a very hard intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are terrible

Overall his lectures are pretty good. They aren't too difficult to pay attention too and in that regard he is a pretty decent professor. However the exams are a big part of your grade and don't grade you on the material as much as your ability to act as a compiler. The material he gives you to study for exams is often not actually on the exams.

Ekin is an enthusiastic professor who gives good lectures on the material and seems like a cool guy. It's too bad that he believes the class is easier than it is, with the tests having an F average. The lectures can be long sometimes, but it's a consequence of how the class is set up more than anything. He is still better than JimR for CS 1050.

I have learned coding languages since I was 7 and I took CS 3330 already but needed to take this class because the starting course at the school I transferred from didn't meet this school's requirements. This teacher is bad at giving lectures and this is by far the worst class I have ever taken. It almost seems like it is designed to make you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ekin is a nice person, and definitely the best option for CS1050 profs at Mizzou, but he is convinced his class is significantly easier than it is. The exams are ridiculously hard and the average is always a failing grade, but he still doesn't curve. This class is insanely difficult especially if you are new to programming. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went into this class already knowing everything, only taking it because it was a requirement, and I still felt like the tests weren't very good. They don't test real knowledge as much as if you know weird quirks of the language. However, he was super enthusiastic, the lectures were good, and it's not like the other CS profs are better...

Went into this class not knowing not knowing how to code, and left with a very good understanding of C. Dr Ekin is a great professor. It's important to go to every class and do all the prelabs. The labs were sometimes ahead of what we learned in class, making them difficult. Tests were more focused on finding mistakes in code, not coding ability.

He clearly enjoys teaching and coding. His lectures are long and boring, but that's more the fault of the course material then his lecture ability. Labs were fairly simple. The exams were confusing and aimed to trick you, but if you take your time and pay attention to his in class examples, you should be fine

bro does not check his email or give support to his students in need... if he does then he does a bad job at it because ive emailed him 3 times and still not even an answer. He barely tells you what to study from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does a very good job at teaching the new programmers in 1050. If you pay attention, the lightbulb will click and computer science will be easier. Otherwise, it will be very difficult.

Like most CS classes at Mizzou, his tests are a joke and do not evaluate ability to code, or problem solve. Instead they reflect your ability to see through his trick questions. His lectures are often base level and he dodges questions about more complex things. Overall he is a nice guy, who should not teach.

The professor is enthusiastic about his material, he demonstrates code that is relevant on tests AND to real-life programming foundations. Since the professor has worked in Computer Science jobs outside of academia, he is always able (and happy) to provide current industry-standards/trends, real-life problems, and other useful insights.

Ekin is a good professor. It is clear he cares a lot about what he teaches. I like how he encourages student input during his class. Wish he would start and end the class on time though. I think the hardest content is actually at the beginning with the Regular Expressions and the CFGs. The exam, final project, and assignments were not bad at all.

Good professor overall. Sometimes lectures can be a bit confusing. Overall, just put effort into the class and understand the material and you should be ok. Cares about your success in the class. There will be quizzes most lab times, so be prepared. Labs will also get challenging at the end of the semester, so be ready to put the hours in.

I took micro-processing from him and it is not so much hard as it is time consuming. The difficulty of the class jumped 2/3 the way in due to the involved, multi-step labs. He is the most friendly and approachable professors I've had at Mizzou. The homework assignments and exams were mild: study the practice exams and you'll be fine.

Dr Ekin was a super chill guy, and as a person, he couldn't be better. Unfortunately, there were a lot of times where he straight up taught us wrong and we had to correct him. Frustrating to not even be able to rely on lectures to teach the right content

Felt somewhat like the class needed more background information, but once we got into topics, lectures were good and I learned a lot. Coding homeworks weren't hard (grasping the languages was hard though), but regex and cfg required more work. Group project at the end of the semester. Exams had 10 points extra credit built-in, which was super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr Asuroglu is an exceptional teacher with an extensive knowledge for orchestration. His enthusiasm is infectious and he creates an engaging class. He offers extra guidance and resources (including his huge library of scores.) While he expects your best effort, he's understanding and approachable. Highly recommend his classes!
Great class! I learned a lot from Dr. Asuroglu. His lectures are energetic and fun and he will teach you a lot!

Dr. Asuroglu is an amazing teacher! He is very knowledgeable with electronic and acoustic composition and his classes were very engaging and fun (he is very funny!) He expects attendance but is understanding if you have a circumstance. I learned a lot from him and would highly recommend his class!

I had Dr. Ullrich for 3150W. Dr. Ullrich is a very knowledgeable and thorough lecturer and is a fun guy in general.  He is very excited about answering tough questions anyone has about the content. I'm sure he would be great to have in any higher-level physics class. Not a tough grader in my experience.

Senior physics major here, by far my favorite physics professor. I didnt have him for anything earlier than mechanics, but from then on hes really helpful and kinda funny lol. Tough subjects but I still like the dude. He chill.
Don't listen to this other reviewer. Ullrich is the man. I wouldn't want any other professor for mechanics. He talks slow, but he teaches well.

He talks so slow, I have to watch him on Tegrity at 1.5 speed just to keep from zoning out. He over exemplifies the simple stuff and breezes straight through the new, important stuff. You need a basic understanding of physics before taking his physics 1 course or you'll be completely lost.

Dr. Wentz is the most boring professor Ive ever had. She speaks with no charisma and its hard not to fall asleep during her poor lectures. I think she means well, but sometimes people are just plain boring. Our group assignments in class are just meticulous busy work, with no true purpose.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having her. Just get on her good side by answering questions in class and putting in an effort and you'll be just fine. She wants you to read the textbook but she puts everything on the powerpoint slides. She also has you do what she calls concept guides after every chapter but she doesn't actually look grade them, just skims.
She's a nice person, but I hated her as a professor. She grades hard and doesn't give good feedback. I hated the class and their are a lot of group assignments.
She grades based on her own idea not by criteria. The first test is the worst and always ready to take off your points.

Dr. Upah is a real point-shaver. She makes it impossible for students to earn great grades. If you need to miss class or make up quizzes, etc; don't expect her to keep her word! Upah does little to benefit students and cares more about her admin status than teaching. Her courses are $$$ scam set-up for MU-PRT. PRT's best Profs are leaving b/c her!!

Terrible professor. Told us the entire week before her final that we would be able to use a notecard on the exam, then as she's passing out the final she tells us we're not allowed to use it. Terrible person and doesn't belong anywhere near a university. Her lectures are terrible and she steals all of her info, but won't hesitate to write you up.

Spends entirely too much time wasting away talking about examples that only consist of swimming experiences. If you need help, don't expect her to be there. Get ready to waste time listening to stories that don't matter and assigned seats. She also assigns group projects (with members that she assigns) which is so fun.

Yes,  go to class if you want a good grade. She uses clickers. But it really was not that hard of a class. The first exam usually surprises the class. I will admit, that first exam did not go well for myself, D+ I think. But everyone got something like that. But then you know what is asked on the test and study accordingly. Really not hard..

Upah does not use recreational examples in recreational based classes. What does working in a factory have to do with municipal recreation? Don't worry, she won't tell you. The worst professor I have had in a recreation based class.

Always confused on how to do an assignment.. Half the class failed a test and she took no responsibility for the way she taught the material. She told us that we didn't answer the questions correctly... Assignments are late if you're late to class by 1 minute.. Go to class, be on time, and love group assignments in any class she teaches....
bad with technology, but means well. she is funny when she wants to be. pay attention

Had him for 2239H, he is my GOAT. If there's one professor you should have while at Mizzou, it's him. He is not only passionate and incredibly educated on the topics, but also genuinely cares about his students. He'll always work with you to help you out. I'm going to miss having him as a professor!

By far my favorite class and professor. His lectures are engaging and insightful and he allows for just the right amount of student discussion, participation, and feedback. Super understanding and caring, reasonable expectations, fair grader, and genuinely taught me a lot. Take his classes!!

I've taken a few classes with Dr. V, and he always makes it an amazing experience. There's a lot of reading, but it all contributes to the content and he brings a lot of his own insights too. It feels like he really cares about the class and his students, and genuinely cares about having everyone share and participate.

he is so awesome!! Doug approaches teaching with compassion and flexibility, and is genuinely interested in his students' well-being. if you're having a difficult semester, he'll work with you and encourage you to communicate, and wants to help you succeed. the books are also super interesting, and he's really understanding about deadlines.

Took the honors American Way of Death class. Excellent teacher, very interesting class. Lots of outside readings, but all interesting. Emphasis on participation and student-led discussions each week. Three essays and a final paper. Fun, engaging teacher and very understanding. 10/10 would take again
An excellent professor all the way around. Amazing lectures, accessible outside of class, and makes sociology an interesting and dynamic subject even for non-majors.

Literally my favorite class I have ever taken. Valentine is such a good teacher and his lectures are actually interesting. He gives out a ton of extra credit and the tests are very easy. This class genuinely changed my perspective on the world and was so interesting to take.

Doug is the only professor I enjoy learning from in the Honors College at Mizzou. He makes learning easy by providing examples of tough-to-understand concepts. He fosters a welcoming environment for all students & opinions. He is a genuinely good person. Readings due every class with synopses & 1 discussion lead. 3 exams, 1 essay. easy grader.

Doug is a GEM. By far my favorite professor at Mizzou. He cares about his students and he is so real. He loves discussion and its always inspiring. He has great examples in his lectures. The discussions arent bad because he normally has good fillers for awkward silence. I would take him every semester if I could. 11/10 would recommend.

You have to take Dougs intro sociology class or you didnt go to Mizzou. His lectures were inspiring and informative. I found myself not having to study as hard for exams because I felt he had taught the material so well. You have one day of discussion (about 30 min), but its actually really helpful to break out of your shell. Doug is worth it.

I enjoyed taking Sociology 1000 with Professor Valentine. It was an interesting class, but the exams can be a little rough at times. His lectures were really good and he makes concepts very easy to understand. Definitely go to his office hours if you are struggling with a certain concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Doug was a great professor. His lectures were amazing and I didn't dread going to class. Plus he was very clear and easy to understand. His tests were fairly easy if you do the study guide and know the terms he gives you on there. He did random attendance and provided extra credit opportunities. I recommend this class greatly.

I'm a nursing major, a solid A student and try hard in all of my classes. I took the online class and I would not recommend. I'm sure in a classroom setting he is a great teacher, but I spent more time on this class than I did for my major specific courses. Very reading heavy, and expect MANY assignments outside of the weekly assignments.
He seems to care about his students. Respects everyone's opinions. Tests were extremely easy to me. His lectures were great, had powerpoints and talked loud & clear. Great guy.

VanPool is a very kind and smart professor who's quite reasonable. Offers in depth and interesting lectures, I'd go even though attendance was optional. Gives you a 1-1 copy of the test as the study guide, and while assignments are scarce, none are overly tedious and difficult, and expectations are clearly laid out. Highly recommend.

Really enjoyed the class, lectures were interesting but sometimes dragged a little long. Dr. Vanpool was readily available after classes and always interested in student contributions. He goes over test questions the class before the exam, and often gives out extra credit on random days of lesser class attendance. ASK QUESTIONS IF NEEDED!!

You can tell how much he genuinely cares about students and the content. Assignments are very straightforward, just discussion posts and weekly quizzes over the content. I maintained a 100% the entire course so it's not bad at all. There is a lengthy term paper but it is basically a completion grade. I loved his class and his teaching style.
Wonderful and insightful lectures. A bit unclear when it comes to grading requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Would not recommend this unless you like anthro. Took it as a gen ed and professor is passionate, but wasn't interesting to me. The 2 tests are easy. Reading textbook is important- heavily tested on but not gone over in class. Term paper was graded easily. At the end I got 40/50 on participation which was odd because I don't think he knew my name.

Dr. Van Poole is literally the best teacher I have had at college. He is extremely understanding and one of the only teachers on campus that truly cares about his students. His class is also really interesting!
Great teacher
Really cares about his students and prepares for class.  His classes are in no way bird classes but I promise you will learn a lot - more than worth the effort!!!
No Comments
She had minimal resources in canvas and it was hard to study for tests because of it. She would also talk AT you and yet her directions were bad.
A great professor, she gave great feedback on projects. The projects were fun to do, and the class was great overall.

As a filmmaker, she's really good, and some of her work has helped me reflect on my own.

As a teacher, she can't teach.

Feedback shouldn't take up an entire 3-hour class.
Grades should be put in regularly.
Questions shouldn't be met with backhanded remarks.

I just hope moving forward things change for the better for future students.

Worst professor I've had at Mizzou. She didn't upload a single grade to Canvas all semester which left many people with surprise D's and F's. Coupled with feedback that was only given verbally it was difficult to know your progress. She was rude and condescending at times and was hard to approach with questions. Classes and Canvas were disorganized

Viviana is a professor that is all about getting students to take their own accountability.  She provides resources, while allowing students to be creative and independent.  You can do well as long as you stay committed to getting the assignments turned in.  She gives feedback in class rather than online, but the critiques are fantastic and useful.
So frustrating I spent half my semester crying. Minimal feedback at screenings, no grades as of yet and it's Dec 5. This class and teacher almost made me change majors.

In December, zero grades for the semester have been put in. Syllabus was constantly changing without warning. Promises were made and not kept, and Canvas was incredibly unorganized. Unrealistic expectations for students as far as group work and time that is possible to dedicate to assignments. Minimal feedback, which was frustrating in a film class

Dr. VanPool is outstanding. As a Wiccan, I appreciated how she handled topics related to religion and witchcraft. Many professors are dismissive or uncomfortable with non-Christian traditions. Dr. VanPool was respectful and her discussion of these topics was thoughtful and inclusive.

While she is knowledgeable about the subject, she gets off track easily and is rude to confused students.  Also, she is quite conservative politically, and it shows in her course material, and she even said a few things directly to me about my identity that were inappropriate, offensive, and completely out of nowhere.

Dr. Chris encourages students to ask questions and explore the topics covered in class. She has a lot of publications and provides good examples in class. I liked this class and will take more classes from this professor. The tests are okay and pretty standard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor

Dr. VanPool was great and this was a fun class. The student led discussions were okay. I wish some of the other students were a bit more motivated, but that isn't he professor's fault. Good class and good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a good teacher with lots of experience. She know a lot and gives good lectures. The readings are okay. This was a good class.

Class was boring. Very rude to students who were confused, asked for help, or just disagreed with her answer. Takes points off of long answers when you don't state the answer in the first sentence, even if you state the answer a sentence after.
In my experience, she was super nice and very understanding! You either need to go to class, or read the textbook but don't have to do both. I would definitely recommend for Intro to Archaeology!
Disorganized, unwilling to admit error (happens frequently), quite disrespectful to students who disagree with her, discriminatory, unprofessional. Avoid.

This was a fun class. It covered a lot of material since it dealt with all native groups in North America, but I came away feeling like I knew something about the topic. She expects you to read the material, because she can't cover everything in lecture, but she is a fair grader.

Professor VanPool is an expert in her field and proves that in her classes with her depth of knowledge on the subject she's teaching. If you want someone that shares your passion for anthropologyarchaeology then she's a wonderful Professor. If you are a slacker, don't bother wasting her time because she's tough, but fair!
She is very disorganized. Did not provide an assignment sheet for a massive book review. Talks very quickly and is difficult to follow. She doesn't make her expectations very clear.

This professor is an absolute expert in her field, unfortunately she is not good teaching. I had an extremely difficult time keeping up in this class. She does not clearly state her expectations and gets frustrated when students don't do what she expects.

Neat class.  I learned a lot about language and human culture.  We read real articles about the subject, not just a text book.  Class discussions were great.  Professor actually expected class to think and keep up, which is a nice change.

I came into this class actually liking Linguistics, thinking it would be fun and interesting. No. If you like reading and writing weekly responses to incomprehensible articles, or sitting through stunningly boring and confusing powerpoint presentations, or listening to lectures by a horridly grating voice, then this class is for you! If not, I woul

As a linguistics major, I thought we were going to study what the course description said: different non-indo european languages. Nope. We basically just talked about anthropology the whole time, and how to integrate culture into things. That is not bad, but not what was promised to the class. Anthro majors will love this class, others will hate it

She's a sweet lady and her tests are usually just like the practice exams/quizzes. The grading criteria is clear. My only complaint is her slides are super math heavy, whereas her exams/quizzes are more theoretical. Overall, she's a good teacher and good explainer. Just show up to class and do the quizzes. Lot easier than intermediate micro!

Yajie is SO GOOD! She makes a really challenging course very easy to understand. After taking intermediate micro...intermediate macro was like a walk in the park. She is so funny and a little quirky, but seriously cares about her students.

Yaijie Wang is an OK professor. Her lectures are very boring and she only focuses on the formulas of concepts. The way her class is set up is extremely convenient. Homeworks are due every week but are super easy. The exams are just like her practice exams. She often jokes that she does not know whats going on. Which for me seemed true lol

This was Dr. Wang's 1st semester and she's still learning. That being said her lectures lacked clarity and I felt like her and the TA weren't on the same page. She focused a lot on the formulaic aspect of the material and not enough on the practical application/concept. She did provide a lot of extra credit though and was receptive to criticism.

Dr. Uhlmann was an extremely good professor for CS_2010 (int. property). The course was paced very well, allowing for proper retention of the material. Exams are heavily based on lecture notes, so attending class is very important. Also, Dr. Uhlmann has a dry sense of humor/sarcasm, which I came to enjoy a lot!
Don't bother showing your code to him for help, as he will refuse to look at it.

Uhlmann doesn't seem to enjoy helping students and expects a high level of retention from his lectures. He makes the course very easy to succeed in. Low lab scores can be replaced by exam scores and absences from labs can be replaced by the following lab. In short, Uhlmann is a below average professor with an above average class structure.

Uhlmann's teaching style can be hit or miss. While the slides are helpful, he's often disconnected from students. unstuck study was a lifesaver for lab prep. Avoiding this class if possible is recommended.

Easy class if you've taken other programming courses. Extra credit on all of the tests. Majority of grade comes from weekly labs. As long as you do the prelab the lab is easy. Lectures are engaging and funny, makes you want to go to class everyday.

This is the worst professor I've ever had the misfortune of encountering. He will encourage you to drop the course before giving an ounce of help. His presentations are word walls, usually filled with filler phrases and will no significant importance on anything, making exams an utter toss up of what he could ask.

Not very gracious-thought if you had too many questions you weren't trying hard enough. Labs weren't necessarily like pre-labs and were graded harshly. His slides were all conceptual, he never coded and sometimes didn't even have code on the slides, and then would expect you to turn around and do it on your own. Tests were easy.

This class was a nightmare. I used to be A+ student, but the lack of support and constant dismissiveness ruined my confidence and affected all my other classes. When I asked for help, I was told to drop instead of being guided. My TA ignored me, and the atmosphere felt judgmental. This class took a toll on my mental health a terrible experience.

TERRIBLE PROFESSOR. He is not a good person. He does not care about his students; he will tell them to drop out if they are struggling. This guy spends more time talking about gibberish than teaching factual information. Avoid this guy at all costs he only has some five-star reviews because he begs the class to give him good reviews. 0/5 AVOID!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His teaching skills and ability to assist students is quite lacking. I went to him for assistance throughout the semester just to be told to "do better" and for him to agree with me that I was going to fail the class. Does not give you the materials to adequately prepare for labs. When you are paying insane tuition you expect much better.

He may be good at Kalman filter but a TERRIBLE TEACHER. He will tell you to drop the class nonstop. If you used to study the day before the test then pass like smart don't take this. Need a shit ton of memorizing. The TAs are just mean do not help at all and have no office hours. Just take it somewhere else and transfer the credit.
Just wait for Jim Ries to teach the class and take it then.

As a senior in IT taking for a minor, I can say that this class is clearly meant to weed out anyone interested in CS that wants to give it a shot. Course material wasn't hard, so there is no need for the structure to be as difficult as it was. While Uhlmann is accredited in research, he doesn't shine in much other places, so take that as you may.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Uhlmann seemed disconnected from the students and material. One student asked what percent of our grade was labs; lab pts / total pts. Uhlmann said the labs are not weighted; he didn't answer the question! Any questions about lab concepts or grading he would tell us to ask the TAs. The TAs were responsible for so much, and it went to their heads.

Professor Uhlmann isn't particularly great but I didn't find him as bad as most. This might be because I didn't try and talk to him outside of class, which my friends have had issues with him in that regard, but he's pretty alright otherwise. The slides he makes are so good you won't need to actually attend class. Prepare for weekly labs though.

I understand that CS 2050 was going to be hard since a lot of people passed CS 1050 but GODDAMMNNN what was that?? Half of the students dropped, the professor is harsh, it's difficult to ask for help and some of the TAs are just mean.

Uhlmann is the worst professor I've ever had. Objectively, he is just a bad person. Asked him to spare some time to go over my wrong answers in an exam and said that my request was "unreasonable". Lectures make no sense and don't teach you anything, do the pre-labs and go to tutoring instead.

If you are trying to go into computer science or any other major requiring this class, avoid it like the plague. The only lecture material he uses is a couple of short slideshows that mostly just repeat the same information. There has been no live coding at all on any material we've learned. Beware a nightmare of a semester if your have this prof.

If you are wanting to go for a computer science or any coding related degree at Mizzou avoid his classes like the plague. His teaching style is outdated and there is no live coding or explanations on how introduced material works. Just the other day in class, after the first exam, he says to the whole class if your below a certain grade to leave.

He is a horrible teacher stay away if you actually want to learn computer science do not take him. When asked for help he simply will respond that he has given you everything to succeed in cs2050. Also the grading system is horrible the fact you just get a 0 on a lab after you coded it for 2.5 hours to get a 0/20. We are not master coders yet.

You're grade is going to be weighted 50% exams (3), 50% labs (12-14). These labs are every week, proctored (some in person, most online), and very trivial. If you do not know coding practices like the back of your hand, you will not easily succeed, you will most likely have to drop or barely pass. Do with that what you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Topics felt slightly disjointed, but he's an engaging lecturer, clearly knowledgeable in what he discusses, and very reachable outside of class. Assignments were pretty interesting and their structure was more realistic to real-world problems than those given in other CS courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I've ever had the misfortune of encountering. He will encourage you to drop the course before giving an ounce of help. His presentations are word walls, usually filled with filler phrases and will no significant importance on anything, making exams an utter toss up of what he could ask. Don't take him if you can avoid it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Uhlmann is nice and tries to engage class even with boring topics. Very few assignments/exams, but did offer some extra credit. Some assignments were very difficult and he wouldn't allow questions after a certain date, but he gave us over 2 weeks for each one. He's informative and shares a lot of personal experiences that tie topics to real life.
I wouldn't recommend taking him if you aren't very savvy in coding

I thought the professor created fairly engaging lectures given the material and was generally straightforward with expectations. However, labs were always a mess. The proctoring software adds a lot of unpredictability and TAs were not helpful when it created issues for students. Lab specs were occasionally overly-vague as well.

Terrible professor, as a CS major you will have to take his class. If you tell him you are having a hard time with the class he will tell you to drop. If you reach out to him for help he will not assist you. The TAs do not help at all during labs and do not offer any office hour, all they say to assist you is to refer to the manual. Good Luck.

Not the hardest class ever, but it is very easy to slip up on labs and exams and lose a huge percent of your grade. Learn pointers inside and out before exam 1. Lectures were slow and the content is dull (it's an  algorithms class) but Uhlmann has a good sense of humor. Follow his algorithm for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the greatest man to ever live. He created a movie trilogy of unmatched talent and taught the most important class in my degree program.

This is so amazing! I am taking his CS4995, and this is just a project-based course. The last time I took it, it was a guarantee A, though I needed to do a lot of work. And he can reply to your email really fast about questions!
Even though the material for this class might be difficult for some, he does an excellent job of teaching it. One of the classes that I actually had a interest in attending. funny guy too :)

Dr. Uhlmann is a great professor for a class where a lot of students are only just learning about concepts like data structures for the first time. He has a very dry and witty sense of humor which might throw you off at first, but which you will learn to love. And for the love of Kernighan and Ritchie, do the prelabs! They make the labs much easier

Uhlmann was a really fun lecturer, managing to keep things interesting even for pretty dreary algorithms and such. He always explains things multiple ways (sentences, pictures, pseudocode) so whatever clicks best with your learning style is there. Labs were a little difficult sometimes but not too bad. Plenty of extra credit on exams

Professor Uhlmann was a great, his lectures were not the greatest but he tried to make them fun and tried to get the class involved. The class has less than 20 things in the grade book all semester which makes the class tough but it is not impossible.

Not as bad as everyone says. 2050 is not an easy class; you have to go to lecture: but then again, CS is not an easy degree. Uhlmann is serious but passionate about the class, and if you put in the work he will not leave you hanging. However, if you don't give it 100 percent then you should not expect him to either.

This class was much better than CS1050, even if you don't have much coding experience. Lectures were well-structured and there was always time for questions. Exams had lots of extra credit which is helpful. Tutoring is also useful. The class did require some effort, but if you do the prelabs, show up to class and go to tutoring you can do well.

Uhlmann is a great professor. The class moves pretty slow which allows most of the class to fully understand each concept. As long as you have a good understanding of pointers the class will be pretty easy. Be sure to do the prelabs as they really help for labs which are a big part of your grade. Tests are pretty easy. Average was usually a high B.

Professor Uhlmann is a great professor and a great guy. At the beginning of the semester he lets you know what you should know for the course. The class expands on a lot of the topics covered in 1050, such as pointers. Sometimes the lectures move a little slowly, but he explains the topics so in depth that it is beneficial if you pay attention.

Much more enjoyable than CS1050. This is genuinely one of the best professors and teachers I've ever had. He is very knowledgeable and explains pretty complex topics from the ground up and ensures his students understand him, offering time for questions too. If you complete the little things he asks of you, the class isn't difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For being the second course in the CS major, he sure does expect you to fully know C. Will degrade you if you ask for any sort of help. TA's aren't allowed to really help unless it's something extremely simple, that could be found online. Constantly says that if you don't understand, sucks for you, you should understand something "simple as this".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My fears about Uhlmann were definitely unfounded. He's a great prof. He explains everything at least three different ways (conceptually, then image-based, then code-based). Follow his "Algorithm for Success" and DO THE PRELABS. Exams are fair and labs are usually easier than prelabs. Lots of dry humor. Sit in the front row and ask about his movies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took his CS 2050 first and I think it is easy, but that could be because I took similar courses before. But he is a nice person, wrote me a LOR, gave me research opportunities, etc.

I enjoyed his class. The topics were more conceptual but he does a good job explaining them, maybe even overexplaining them at some points. I really didn't have any interactions with him outside of class, but the grading was fair and the tests were very forgiving. The labs each week can be tough but as long as you do the prelabs you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Okay teacher, decently funny, but is not helpful at all. Emailed him when I was struggling at the beginning of the semester and he told me to drop the class... finished with an A- thanks to an awesome TA. Curves his exams like crazy which is very helpful but labs are difficult.

First impressions from a welcome email was that he is a jerk. Tells you if you don't know how to do these things off the bat, "why even be an engineer in the first place?" Yes, that is taken from the first email from him. Teaching style is horrific and most of learning came from outside class. My grade came from outside experience before this class

Difficult course. Lectures are over-explained; he would only go over 2-3 slides from a slideshow per lecture, yet there are few practical coding examples that you'll need in labs/at a job. If you do poorly, he will shame you during lectures, saying "you're not good enough" and "you should drop my class". Keep a high grade and he'll leave you alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took uhlmans class in the fall and was forced to retake it. Sure he can be rough around the edges, but he is passionate about what he teaches. I am glad that I retook it as I now have a far better understanding of C as a result. Sure it's a hard class, but that's the point. As for his unwillingness to help, CS is learned best through practice.

I have never met such a terrible person in my life. The class is hard yeah. But Uhlmann is a monster. He gets enjoyment seeing his students suffer, will continuously say in lecture that you are probably "not good enough" to code. There's a rubric for the labs, but for what? I got points taken off for not being "efficient" enough. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Incompetent, has no real knowledge of what coding is like in the real world. If he knew how to code he wouldent be a professor becuase he could get paid more literally anywhere else. This past exam he had us take it on the sidewalk in downtown Columbia.

Compared to the other CS professors Ive had? Hes doing swell; at least hes got a sense of humor. The coding practices left something to be desired - some of my class got laughed off stackoverflow for asking questions about them - and the lectures were somewhat dry. Prelabs were dumb - keys werent released before labs, so you better not mess up.

Dr. Uhlmann has dry in his lectures, partly due to his monotone voice, but makes it interesting to listen to with his occasional joke. He will over explain something which makes the rest of the lecture boring after you understand the topic, but thats better than not getting something explained fully. Very fair grader and assigner.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It is quite easy to get weeded out of this class. You have to stay focused the whole time and do every prelab the best you can. You cannot rely on your friends, the TAs, and especially Uhlmann to save you. Do not think that you can just show up to lecture and succeed. You will have to work for everything: there is no mercy when it comes to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The only resource students are given in this class is a weekly PowerPoint. Pre labs are vague intentionally and there aren't resources available to know if you completed the prelab correctly, in turn, students who complete the prelab with a bug will also put that bug in their lab for the week thinking they are correct. Highly recommend not taking!

This guys logic is flawed beyond resoning. Hes not a good programmer even, his code is sloppy and he does stuff the hardest way possible. He claims you shouldent get help with coding which is the exact opposite of what every programmer ive evere talked to has told me.

This has to be the worst professor on the planet. Everything in this class is not weighted, so if you miss a SINGLE lab, your grade is going down 5% buddy! You can miss up to four classes but highly not recommended you will miss a pop quizzes that are essential to passing. The entire class is 500 points. Going into office hours will surely help!

Yeah he can be sarcastic and a bit condescending, but he's honestly one of my favorite professors. Get him alone and talking about something other than class and he's absolutely wonderful! He's passionate about you really leaning something, so he does grade hard. He basically gives you what you need to know for tests, and if you read you'll do fine

Professor Wilson is a funny, sarcastic guy.  I actually didn't like him at first in the beginning of the semester, but he grew on me and he tries to make the class fun by sharing stories and being a jokester.  As far as the class, I ended up with a low B.  He is VERY SPECIFIC to what he wants on essays, which I guess makes it easier to do well.

This is the WORST. TEACHER. EVER. PERIOD. I took AP English Comp in high school and received a B- but was unable to take the AP test. EVERY PAPER I HAVE GOTTEN BACK HAS BEEN A D OR LOWER despite working my ass off. Grading is totally unreasonable. When you want help he's not there. The writing lab is useless for this class, as is he. He's awful.

I really enjoyed English Lit with Professor Wilson. He is very intimidating at first, but once he gets used to the class and you get used to him, he is very entertaining. You have to go to class, and you have to do the readings because he gives lots of pop quizzes. And participation is big! But don't be afraid to speak up, he likes it! Good luck!

He is a great teacher. Very sarcastic and makes the classroom a fun place to be in. He is a tough grader and makes you work for a good grade. Doesn't just let you get by easy like most English teachers do. He is challenging but taught me so much. Highly recommend

Yes, Professor Wilson is sarcastic, arrogant, and a tough grader. However, it is not impossible to do well in his class, as long as you put the work in. I attended every class and paid attention and participated. That's what he expects of you and it is rewarding at the end. He will notice your hard work.  Not a bad class IF you put in the effort.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! He is an awful teacher. Grades way too difficultly for a 1000 level course. I am a decent writer and I got a C in his class. If you want to keep a good GPA listen to me and NEVER TAKE WILSON'S CLASS. You will regret not listening to me...
Wilson's a beast, he's a tough grader but that's because kids come to expect easy A's on papers. He's a funny guy and is down to talking sports with you after class. Definitely Recommended.

NOTHING YOU WRITE WILL BE GOOD ENOUGH, EVER. He is VERY sarcastic and negative which makes all classes extremely uncomfortable.  Makes no effort at professionalism and acts as if teaching is a prison sentence he is forced to endure daily. Sarcastic, demeaning remarks at students are daily. Very harsh grader.  No grades posted all semester.  AVOID.

He's extremely sarcastic, but it can be funny. Hard grader. Got a D on the first test, did everything he told me to do to prepare for the next test and still only got a C. He's also moody. You can easily tell when he doesn't want to be there.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Professor Wilson takes English 1000 way too seriously for a freshmen level course. I got As in English all through high school and got a C in his class. Although he knows what he's talking about, he should be an honors teacher or a higher level course. If you do not like English listen to me and DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE!

Professor Wilson was the best professor I had at Mizzou. I was in his freshman English class and he essentially taught me everything I know about writing. His class is hard, but SO worth it. Not to mention, he will write a hell of a rec letter later in life. He is a great guy, take ADVANTAGE of his office hours, he WANTS to help you.
You will learn a lot, but your grade won't show it. Sorry... Nice enough guy if you try to get to know him.
PLEASE. PLEASE. PLEASE, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH CHRIS WILSON. He takes Eng 1000 way too serious... be ready to throw out any prior knowledge youve learned.
Difficult class but hands down I have learned the most from Chris.  He is a great guy that will help you if you ask for it.  Definitely worth taking.

Professor Wilson has been my absolute favorite teacher since I've been at Mizzou. His class is interesting and he is hilarious. He genuinely cares about his students if they put in the effort, and wants you to get a good grade. You have to put in a good amount of work to get the A, though. Beware.
tough personality, funny, but hard to get along with. hav a walking discussion with him to your next class and youre on his good side. be a good student and youll be ok.

This guy is definitely not for overly sensitive ppl, his humor is mean but awesome. Easy class if you do the reading and show up, he likes pop quizzes. If you embrace his humor, you'll love it. Though he even says himself that he's rough on ENG 1000 students.

He seemed to know what he spoke about, but I took World Lit, so there was little writing. He is a smarta** but it actually gets my attention. He doesn't use the Internet for anything, but explains everything pretty well in class. He is verbatim from the text book, so do the reading assignments. He makes you actually work and you begin to appreciate the value of an actual A. If you start the class slacking, just drop-you will probably not pass. Be on your toes! Good class.

He was the most ridiculous teacher ever. No matter how hard you work or how many times I took my paper to the writing lab, I would get it back with a C.  The writing lab people were always as shocked as I was. I learned more from my writing intensive than this class. I ended up with a B in this class and an A in my writing intensive. Don't take him

Ridiculous. I felt no matter what I did or how much help I got, it was never good enough. I would to the writing lab 4 times for each paper, and the tutors would become just as exasperated as I was.  He tries to help your papers, but you will end up with a C no matter what. At least you get to read Vonnegut...
He definately taught us how to write but the class is extremely difficult.  Would not take another english teacher, just expect a drop in your GPA after the class.  Great learning experience though.
He scares me
doesn't return papers very fast and gives 3 essays but no tests or quizes. I had basically no clue what my grade was until it was on myzou.

This class was horrible. He uses the worst examples that basically just confuse you more than you already are. He drifts off topic to pointless things and treats you like you are an idiot if you don't understand him. Horrible teacher, made me hate writing, don't take his class!
Great Teacher, Very nice Guy. Very understanding and interacts with the students

I took his survey World Literature class. The only grades in a class are one paper of a very unclear topic that only makes sense to him, some quizzes (easy if you read the assigned reading), written tests, and participation points. Speak up in class(you get points automatically)but you better have something constructive to say or he'll tear you dow
He made the class interesting.  Was sarcastic and merciless, but fair. If you did the work, he stayed away from you, but if you didn't, watch out!

I had Chris for freshman English in Fall '99 and he was the one who taught me how to write a paper!  The knowledge I got in that class helped me every single semester of my 7 years at MU.  He was the best teacher I ever had.  If your grade on a paper is poor, speak with him at office hours and he will help you earn that A.  He wants you to succeed.

Chris is/was an ****. His class is hilarious, I loved his sarcasm and wit. He wants you to do well in class, just ask for help. He won't bite off your head, even though he seems like he will. If you work hard it shows if not he'll make fun of you.
Exceptional teacher, but a challenging class. Take this class if you want to learn how to write well. His sarcasm and wit make for a very fun class room experience. Cheers to Chris

He was super specific on what he wanted in each paper.  Which actually made it easier to write.  Just fill in the blanks of what he wanted.  He is extremely helpful on papers and wants all his students to do well.  I got an A.  Go into this class expecting to learn how to write.

He does give everyone C's on their papers and no matter what there is always something that he wants you to fix.You cannot get an A!He made me feel like an idiot and yeah he makes fun of everyone, I did not like going to that class!

Most people don't like Chris, but this is only because they are still used to high school half-ass work.  He is gonna make fun of you and he is gonna be harsh, but this is his motivational tool.  He knows you aren't gonna learn if he babies you.  The class isn't easy, but hard work gets decent grade

He's arrogant and pompous but most of the time he's right about papers. If you take this course it WILL demand work not the average BS that is acceptable with most other teachers. Advice if you like a challenge go for it if not switch teachers.

If you want to ruin your GPA take this class. Like someone previously said on here, your paper will never be good enough. Class time is wasted with non-pertinent issues being discussed not even relating to english. Don't expect to get a good grade.

Prof. Wilson is a very demanding teacher.  Some of his in class comments might seem rude, however, he seems to be a nice guy.  He is very good at making time for individual help and if you decide to talk to him individually about a papper he is extremely helpful.
Grading of papers is extremely stiff.
straight up jack A** it so hard to look forward to a class when you know you're just going to be bashed on.

at the beginning of the year I hated him, but you've just got to learn how he thinks.  He will make fun of you. He will give you C's on all your paper even if you work your ass off.  But if you really need help, he'll help you.  He's not THAT bad, but he CAN make people feel like crap.
Any professor who lets me write a paper on the movie "Dazed and Confused" gets a good vote from me. If you know how to write a decent paper you'll have no problem in his class.

hes a good writer and i think he tries to make it simple but your papers will never be good enough. hes incredibly cynical, and yeah he had one person he always made fun of in our class too. don't expect this to be the easy A freshman english class
His arrogance is surpassed only by his inability to explain the informat
i don't even think he reads the essays he grades. and he's not a very good writer. his sample essays look like they were written by a 12 year old.
biggest waste of star dust, time, money, and chemical bonds ever
The second best butt in the department!
No Comments

She requires you add the editing history for your essays which is just annoying for innocent people who actually do the work. Just because you are worried about AI I don't think it warrants that you add a whole extra step for people who are doing the work.Never have I had this required. Just do your job...
While the course is generally manageable. She does like to trick you with hidden text.

Everything is pretty set in stone take notes on the lecture slides, complete a discussion board based on either notes, a video, etc. There'll be occasional quizzes the class is very online friendly. The "toughest" part for me was the 3 papers in the semester. The papers were not hard, but I spent a couple of hours on each paper! Overall good class!
Gives good feedback on papers and grades them fairly

Professor Warzinik was so engaging even with being in an online class. This was all self-paced, but she was so helpful no matter what problems you were having. She was always willing to help. Lots of reading and busy work - but none of the work is really that hard. Overall, it was a great class!

Overall, I liked her! She is nice and doesn't assign too much work. There are three papers that did not take me too much time and a final project. My only problem is sometimes she doesn't give the clearest instructions, I had to email her multiple times for clarification. Other than that, it's a good course, she drops grades at the end too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though this was an online class, she made it interesting and interactive. Every week there's a small discussion board but only have to post on 10 of the 15 boards. Very understanding and willing to help. There are 4 papers due throughout the class but she gives lots of prompts and questions to answer and they're no more than 3 pages.
Loved this class! The papers were amazing to make you think! I enjoyed how much this class made me think differently!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Good professor that always gave great feedback on papers and assignments. I felt as though she tried her best to connect with her students.

Professor Warzinik is really helpful and understanding! I had several family emergencies this semester and she worked with me through very generous extensions to allow me to turn my assignments in for full credit.

First of all, the first class of the semester he started lecture by reading his negative rates on this site and told us all why they were right or wrong. The class can be tough, but Walensky was great. There is a lot of work right before tests and the tests are stressful, but if you sit down and work it is possible. I did enjoy this class.

Even though this class is lecture focused, the lectures fly by with the way he explains the material! This was his first year as a professor and he did great! Study guides are clear cut, grading system is fair, and overall a great class!

Walensky is a good Professor, and if you attend lectures it is clear what questions will be on the exam. Since the class was online, tests were open note and you could use things from Canvas. Due to this there really isn't any reason to do worse than a B-, so you should really learn your way around his canvas. It will save you Alot of trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's probably one of the most sarcastic teachers I've had, but he does explain throughly what the concepts are. Tests are average you really just need to pay attention in class which can be long. He also gives grade boosts through other assignments (but they can also hurt your grade) so do them early so you don't fall behind.
Dr. Walensky is beyond amazing. His sense of humor makes the class even more enjoyable and he is very helpful when approached with questions. As long as you study the material, its an easy A! :)

I took Dr. Walensky's class during the pandemic, which I thought would be a real challenge. However, I somehow found myself looking forward to a chemistry class (not usually my thing). His jokes provided a break in my hours of online lectures. Tests weren't too hard, and he posted plenty of practices. Highly recommend any class Dr. Walensky teaches

Chem 1330 was the first chem class I actually enjoyed including high school chem. He convinced me to minor in chem and the class is super interesting. It's a bit fast paced and the tests aren't the easiest but they're not hard if you do the practice problems. Super accessible outside of class and generally a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Walensky is a good professor. He can be sarcastic at times but that is just his sense of humor and an attempt to keep everyone entertained. He does a very good job in lectures and will provide all the information you need to succeed. But be warned, you will get no slack if your grade suffers because of a lack of effort/attendance on your part.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Walensky can be sarcastic, but that is just his sense of humor and an attempt to keep himself and us entertained throughout the course. He is a solid choice when you can take him and he does a really good job in lectures. But be warned, you will not receive slack if your grade suffers because of your lack of effort or attendance.

Walensky is one of the best chem professors that Mizzou has. He jokes that he only cares about his research but he is actually very helpful and cares about his students. His lectures got boring sometimes but he was very funny and entertaining. He won't hand out A's tho and you won't do well if you don't study.

Dr. Walensky is a great professor. His personality is cool dad, so hes very sarcastic and blunt. He is incredibly understanding of family emergencies, illnesses, etc and his class offers a large amount of easy points from homework. Most of the homework is graded on participation anyways. If you want to do well on the exams, do the practice test!

Seems like the only Chemistry Prof worth a crap at Mizzou. Can be funny, pretty sure he made a joke about sexual relations with his grandma. I just hope I heard him wrong. But practice problems are helpful and I managed to have a great TA for the confusing labs. Clicker questions and attendance taken which actually helps your grade fairly well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is good at teaching chemistry and you will do well on his tests as long as you do the practice problems. Nothing on the tests were unexpected, they were all formatted the same as his in class and practice problems. Keep up with the lectures and put in some time to do problems on your own and you will succeed in his class.

Justin is a very fair professor. In my opinion, if you don't attend class you will not do well. Justin is very lecture heavy and we did not have a textbook, so what you get in lecture is what you get. He is hilarious and may make jokes, but never let that prevent you from asking serious questions and seeking help when you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Walenky is a person of depth and layers, but unfortunately, laziness is the layer that wraps it all up. The very first day he clarified that his #1 priority wasn't to teach. Basically research >/ department affiliation > academic advising > anything else > teaching. Overall he will help his best and turn you away when he doesn't know the answer.

Walensky is the best professor to take for a Chemistry class - he is available for extra help and wants you to succeed. His lectures are entertaining (makes going at 8am not so terrible) & he's actually funny, not lame-professor funny. He offers literally 50+ practice problems and explains how to do them - somebody give dis man a raise!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: BEST chem teacher you can get. everything makes perfect sense when it comes out of walensky's mouth and plus he is the funniest most sarcastic person. 8 am lectures are not too bad when he is the professor
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I had Walensky in my first semester at Mizzou. He's head and shoulders above any other chem professor I've had since. Smart, funny, and genuinely cares about his students. Far better alternative than the harshly graded non-honors 1320 class. Material is pretty tough, but that's just chemistry in general.

Walensky was my absolute favorite professor this past semester. That being said, if you expect him to hand you an A, it's not going to happen. However, he is accessible through email and after class. He loves chemistry and keeps class interesting. Def take his course if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: On first glance, he honestly seems awful. However, working with him through the semester he has easily become one of the best teachers I've ever had. He genuinely cares about chemistry and it's infectious. If you come to him with the right mindset, that is "I want to learn and do well" he will make that possible for you. A great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Walensky is overall a pretty good guy. He kind of struggled with teaching 1320H for the first time this semester. He could get kind of unorganized and go off on tangents above the average students' head. He's accessible through email and after office hours. My biggest complaint is the lack of a decent textbook. The online book used was terrible.
He's a very good teacher with well prepared lectures. Definitely go to class and office hours. The only problem with him was the lack of example problems/homework.

He's a great teacher & keeps the class really interesting, even at 8am. Very transparent and good about communicating changes with you. The class itself is hard but seriously, GO TO OFFICE HOURS- esp b4 tests, he will help you so much!! There's also labs to help pad your grade. He put the notes online for lectures but I would still go bc he's great

Walensky is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are super clear, offers lots of practice problems, and he is quick to reply to your emails. He's well known for using lots of "college humor" in class. He tells the same super inappropriate joke on the first day of class, & puts these reviews on the board for everyone to see.

Love this man! He cuts right to the chase and tries not to bore you because he knows that this is just a gen ed for most students.  He gives tons of practice problems. Most of the TA's are really good.  Beware of the 3rd test, it sucks.  He pads your grade with homework and the labs, so if you don't do to hot on the tests, you could still get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Walensky is a great professor. He's clear from the beginning about the class and is ALWAYS there to help. He gives so many practice problems and tons of opportunities to come to him if you need anything. He's hilarious and makes lecture interesting. Best professor I've had so far. Keep doin you Dr Walensky.

Walensky was awesome. I'm not a huge fan of chemistry, but I throughly enjoyed his class and Walensky as a person. He's very fair with his grading scale, sets you up perfectly for the tests, and is hilarious. As long as you do the practice problems and listen in lecture its easy to do well. Beware of ALEKS homework!

Walensky is by far the best chem teacher I've had so far. He gives plenty of material to help you prepare for the exams, and there are no surprises. Although his lectures are long and at 8 AM, he makes them entertaining to listen to. He assigns ALEKS, but honestly that helped me prepare for the exams even though it's a pain to finish. Great class!

Dr. Walensky was a phenomenal professor. He is so helpful and he holds sessions to help his students three days before the exam. The third test was very hard, but you can drop one exam and the class is very doable. The TA for this course was phenomenal and she is another reason why the class was so tolerable.

Make sure you get a good lab TA. THE LAB CAN MAKE YOU OR BREAK YOU. He is a good professor. He doesn't curve the class, lowest test grade is dropped. The third test is HARD. it's almost everyone's dropped test. But the first two and the final are pretty easy. The homework sucks. It's a system that makes you keep going until you get 3 in a row right

His expectations are clear and there are other ways to bring grades up besides exams so he's fine in that end. However, if you need help, don't go to him. He always says how he's willing to help, but he is super judgmental and belittling if you don't understand right away. If you need help, go to tutoring where they're NICE and PATIENT (unlike Wal)

He's generally a good professor, makes expectations crystal clear and the grading is definitely fair and makes other opportunities to bring up your grade instead of just exams. There's only one con with him, and it's that he's judgmental. He always talks about how he's willing to help, & he is, but he's super condescending if you don't get it asap.

He is so funny! He definitely knows he's funny though, haha. A little arrogant but makes up for it by being incredibly smart and incredibly helpful. He explains things so clearly and really makes me understand chemistry. Really wants his students to do well. Said he wouldn't do tegrity but then did- which personally was a lifesaver with an 8am!!

Ehhh. He's not the nicest of people. Acts like a know-it-all often and I never felt comfortable enough to ask him a question. His multiple choice portion of his tests are bogus. Each question is worth around 4 points each so if you miss just 3, you already have a C on the test. Hated every second of this class and I regret taking it.

He is a great teacher! He goes over practice problems in the beginning of each class. He's hilarious and if you go to office hours he tells you whats on the test! Tests are straight forward and if you study, you'll do fine. 3rd test is the hardest but it isn't that bad. If you average 90+ on the tests, you don't have to take the final!
Probably the best chem 1330 professor on campus just study and do well on labs and you should be fine also a test gets dropped which is nice.

The class just the exams, labs, and online quizes. He might be the only professor so you have to take him for 1330. Hes nice, tries to be cool, has lame jokes, and is just average. He reads off the slides and is difficult to hear, even if you sit up front. one of our tests had an avg of 55. he didnt curve it. If you do well on the labs you'll be ok

He does several examples from the previous lecture to refresh your memory and has plenty of practice problems posted on blackboard. Whenever you go to office hours, he actually WANTS to help you. Plus, he's hilarious and makes you want to go to class (even when it's at 8 am). He wants to know his students and makes an effort to do so. He rocked!

This professor was very clear that you need to come to class. He even said something like "if you don't come to class and think you can pass, then you are sorely mistaken." Still, less than half of the class showed up. If you went to class and asked questions, a good grade is very attainable. A very fun teacher and I advise that you take him.

He's an okay professor, but somehow has turned this class from an "easy A" into a "I just need to pass". Averages on his tests range between 40-60100. You can still do well in this class but you'd have to spend way more time than you should!

Waleksy is a great professor! It is not an easy A, but he is very eager to help his students. Just put in the work and do a lot of practice problems, and you will be fine! I highly recommend printing off the notes before class, and that way you can actually follow the lectures instead of scrambling to write everything. Overall, very funny, nice guy
Very Good professor.  Does practice examples at the begining of every class.  Encourages questions.  Knows his materials and is very enthusiastic about the topic.

Awesome teacher! Relates to his students and does everything he can to set his students up for success. The class is a little harder than 1320, but definitely manageable. The TA's grade much harder. Getting 100% on the hw isn't hard, just tedious.

I would probably recommend finding another prof if possible. He is a really nice guy and decent professor, but the tests are just way too difficult. Wants everyone to take notes his way, and rushes through slides while reading them verbatim. The fact that the class was at 8am didn't help any (not his fault though).

Walensky set his students up for success this spring by putting the ppts online. Also he seems to truly care about his students. Going to class wasn't always necessary because it went along well with the book. But understand the book/hw well! I did put in some time reading/understanding hw problems for this class and it paid off.
Best professor ever. If you attend class, read the notes, and do his practice problems, you will breeze through this class.

Well, he is a new chemistry teacher on campus, and it unfortunately shows.  He's fun to listen to and get to know, and he is passionate about teaching.  He is helpful, really. But his expectations are entirely too hard for a 1000 level class, even with prior experience.  Just be warned and use your textbook, study hard, and go to class.
Wants you to succeed but very passive tone to beware.

She has no idea what she's doing in her class. She doesn't communicate well and changes the rubric every day and her TAs do not know what she wants. She puts you in groups, and even if one of your teammates does nothing, she doesn't care and gives them full credit, after you explain your situation.
Just awful
Save your time and your GPA. This is a really hard class that you actually have to try very hard in. The TA does all the grading and is super strict and not helpful. Jennifer does nothing.

For an intro class, this class was terrible. You rarely have class, once every two weeks, but if you miss one day you'll regret it. Tests were super hard and she doesn't teach in class, you need to teach yourself.

I thought this 1000-level elective would be easy, but it's packed with busy work and weekly reading quizzes under Honorlock. iClicker is weighted way too heavily for a once-a-week class, and she never replies to emails. Exams even have “ChatGPT traps.” Not an easy A—wouldn't recommend if you have other demanding classes.

Xu is better than David from what I hear but I simply cannot pay attention in his boring, rambling lectures. Exams are not bad but no dropped exam and no dropped attendance makes it tough for a lot of people. Make sure you make your own grade calculator because canvas will not display the correct grade. Overall it was meh.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class isn't bad, besides the fact that you never know what your actual grade is. Chapter homework is put into the gradebook even though they only count as bonus points for the exam, which inflates your grade in Canvas. He also doesn't give any drops for attendance.

Dr. Xu clearly does not take his class very seriously. He spent the first day of class talking about prostitutes in the red light district. He grades completely inconsistently and makes you turn in everything handwritten, even though he frequently loses track of your assignments. He provides no feedback on your assignments. You will get screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Sen for genetics and it was almost the same as evolution, except no exams. Evolution is very reading heavy, with 9-15 page papers you needed to read every week for discussions on thursdays. Quizzes are not difficult, and there are no exams. Overall an easier course out of the evolution classes, and I would take this again.

Seems like his summer class improved significantly. Whole class is straightforward.
