Watch the lectures and you'll have everything you need for homeworks, but you definitely need to be good in MATLAB for the "lab" piece. No coding on exams, and questions are similar to homework/notes. However, exams are 2 hours with many tedious questions, so study.
The class is do-able if you work hard. Be prepared to dedicate a lot of time to this class, but he is approachable and helpful if you do choose to attend office hours.

Takes weeks to grade homework and lab assignments and wont give you any feedback on them. Wont have exam review until a day before the exam, but the exam will cover material not in the review. Most lecture material is just copy pasted from the textbook (which is awful). Don't use a pen to take notes because he messes up in lectures a lot.

Had to take his Comp. Methods Class online, probably the worst 8-week class I've ever taken. The amount of work due in such a small amount of time is astonishing. Have a question? You better have a friend in the class, bc questions will be met with a condescending demeanor, and answers still don't help. If you have to take this class, good luck :)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was the hardest class I've taken towards my major so far. The MATLAB and homework assignments were very lengthy and difficult. If you are not good at MATLAB you better teach yourself quick. The final project was ridiculously hard and time consuming. He lectures straight from the textbook without explaining many of the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Comp Methods with Ming Xin in Spring 2018. Brilliant, hard-working teacher who expects an equal amount of work from his students. Be prepared to write pages of notes for each class or else you'll be unprepared for graded work. The path to an A is clearly laid out, but its requires a fair amount of effort with Ming Xin.
He is very open to helping his students, but you really have to work hard to understand the material because he gives a lot of work, although it pays off in the end.

Took his Computing Methods class. Worst class I've taken in college so far. So much work with so little purpose. It's supposed to be a programming class and we spent almost all the time in lecture learning mathematical derivations. He's a very knowledgeable guy, but terribly out of touch with what engineering students actually need to be learning.
Her quizzes/homework assignments are exactly like the exams, which was very helpful in learning and studying.  She posts the slides online and definitely listens to feedback.

This professor is great and always goes the extra mile to accommodate you and help you understand/pass this course. I also want to note that any other comments about her accent and not being able to understand her are blatantly racist. No one in the entire class had any issues understanding her bc she is fluent in English.

Professor is nice but she is not good at teaching at all. To me, her accent did not seem to be a problem, however she is just not good at conveying the material. She gives lots of unnecessary derivations which makes it hard to see what you really need for tests. She is not very good at answering questions when you are confused either.

Zou wasn't supposed to teach our course and it shows. The first two exams did not correlate with the course material which was aggravating. She had no clue how to explain any concepts, meaning you have to attend your recitations to learn anything. The labs were complicated since lectures were poor. Do the practice exams & go to recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Xiaoqin Zou is a nice lady but she isn't built to be a teacher - I truly don't think her accent hinders her but it is her speech patterns and stuttering which divides the communication between her and the class. Even the smartest of students often left her lectures perplexed by what she was attempting to convey.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She seems like a very nice lady but she has no idea how to teach this class. Expect to be learning a lot on your own because her lectures are very unstructured. At times hard to understand because of accent.

I dislike the structure of her classes. She speeds through a lot of content in one session trying to fit as much in as possible, but spends 10-15 minutes (or once the whole class) repeating the same slides from the previous session. She throws up a lot of extra formulas and information than what is needed, making it difficult to know what's needed.

She is a little hard to understand sometimes, but she's a nice lady. Her practice exams are like her real ones, but the exams are a little tougher. Be sure to come to class/RSD (attendance pts) and to do the online homework-it will help your grade. Also, when studying, focus on the problems done in recitation class. That helped me.
The GOAT !!!!!!! Very nice guy and very accomdating
Outdated teaching style. Lectures were also very difficult to understand and in order to understand I would have to look up a youtube video/websites to understand the topics.

Lectures were amazing, but not necessary to attend. The textbook also does a great job of explaining the algorithms and data structures in this course. Tests aren't overwhelmingly difficult, but the time limits can be a crunch. Not a lot of homework. Lots of extra credit are provided at "Mock Interviews," which are just a glorified trivia bowl.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is breezy compared to 1050 and 2050, because it's barely even about coding, just algorithms. The professor does a great job stepping through every algorithm shown to make sure everyone understands.

From what I've heard definitely the better professor to take for this class (3050) but still may be a tough course for some people. Goes more in depth into theoretical concepts than you'll have had in previous classes, but that's part of what CS is. Homework isnt bad if you pay attention, definitely helps to read the textbook in addition to lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very straightforward and he's willing to help.

He is the best math professor I have had at Mizzou thus far. Passionate about mathematics and his students success, he is very inspiring and wants you to do well. He gives you practice problems that are very similar to exams, so do the practice problems a few times. Take his class!

He is super passionate about Differential Equations and demonstrates a very clear understanding of this subject. He is helpful and welcome to any questions. His exams are very, very similar to the practice exams he gives as preparation material. I definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great teacher- able to break down complex topics multiple ways to give greater understanding. Really seems to care about students understanding and wants to make sure that his students know the subject material. Passionate about his subject matter.

Xiofei is very nice & funny, but is hard to understand as he is Chinese. Notes are taken but sometimes don't make sense bc of language barrier. Expected to read LOTS for weekly pop quizzes. Ask a question and he probably won't give you a straight answer. He seems to get baffled when someone counters his arugments. BTW, it's LOGIC, not just philo.

This guy is extremely hard to understand. His grading standards are not at all presented in the initial syllabus. He was constantly giving extra assignments that he forgot to mention there would be, and it took some intense prodding to get him to grade my final essay fairly. Course materials were interesting but take the class with someone else.

The major problem with this course is his grading scale. There are only 100 points available for the whole semester, so every point missed is a percentage lost. He clearly knows what he is talking about, but it would help if his notes during class were clearer and we knew what to look for while reading the assignments.

very nice, and very intelligent.  His accent isn't bad.  However, it would be nice if he outlined the reading for us so we know what we're looking for.  It's is pretty difficult to understand, and I think that would help everyone out, and probably increase class participation.
very nice guy, i was able to understand him fairly easily although his accent is fairly thick. interesting class (intro to logic) but probably a bit more technical than you'd think
Attendance is not mandatory, and before exams there is a class review period. But the structure of this class was all over the place. Most lectures seemed like manic rants.

Easiest class you will ever take. There will be 2 weeks where you literally just watch a basketball movie. The other weeks are just Dr. Brekhus reading off of a google doc, so pretty boring. Other than exams you will have very low-weighted Packback assignments that you will undoubtedly forget about. Just do them in class.

This class was based primarily off tests. You had 3 tests which were all 20% of your grade. There is only a few assignments so if you do bad on the tests, you will fail. He doesn't answer emails and his lectures are all over the place, he just goes off topic. Good news is attendance isn't mandatory!

Your grade is based off three exams and the final with very little else being graded, if you don't do well on one of the exams your grade is done. Says "um" after every single sentence and the lectures get hard to listen to when you notice just how many times he says um. Very passionate about the topic but can get boring and hard to pay attention.

Dr Brekhus is a very silly guy. His lectures are unforgettable because of how engaging he is, and you can really tell how passionate he is about sociology. I definitely recommend Soc 1000 with him since he is an easy grader. His tests are not complex at all, I never read the material I just showed up to class and took notes and really listened.
He is a super funny guy, but I found it hard to pay attention during the lectures. Lectures are recorded, and the course is super test-heavy. overall just do the work and study hard for the tests.
I love this professor!!
he was super cool and took a humorous approach to sociology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is overall a wonderful professor. However, study for the tests and keep up with the topics! homework isn't really worth anything and you rarely have in class assignments. but overall it has interesting topics in the class and the packbacks are due every Thursday and are not put into canvas as assignments so check them regularly!

Professor Brekhus Sociology 1000 course is an overall very fun course. The majority of your grade will be based on 3 quizzes, but the study guide he gives + quizlet resources means you will always get an A if you study. Professor Brekhus is very animated and passionate and his lectures are very fun if you choose to go.

Brekhus is a funny and engaging professor, though the class can be challenging. Focus on the exams and use resources like Unstuck study alongside the textbook to prepare. He's willing to help if you communicate with him.

Brekhus is really nice and funny. Good guy!! Class is only graded on 3 exams-while he does do in class review, the tests are somewhat difficult and the wording is odd. Packbacks due every week and worth 5 points, but do not really do anything to your grade. Tests are really important!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Brekhus was incredibly funny, and his lectures were always engaging. That being said, it is a somewhat difficult class. You need to do well on the tests; otherwise, you will fail. But he does want to help people with their grades; just talk to him!

The whole class was based on 3 exam grades and a few 5 point-pack pack questions due every week. I would say this class was hard, but Brekhus was one of the most caring professors I have had so far. He knew I cared about my grade, and helped me to raise my grade at the end of the semester.

Class was pretty easy. It's true that you have to do well on your 3 exams in order to get a good grade in the course. Besides the exams theres one discussion post due each week. Going to lecture isn't mandatory but I highly recommend going to the review session before the exams, it basically covers everything you'll need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading and you're pretty much screwed if you fail the first test because hw is barely worth anything and his lecture's are boring at most times -- although the subjects are interesting. He does have a genuine passion for sociology but he makes it so difficult to get a good grade if you didn't do as well on the first test.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a chill dude
Professor Brekhus is funny, but the only grades are 3 tests and weekly 5 point assignments. If you do not do well on the first test, you are kind of screwed with your semester grade.

This guy was so funny.He really cares about his students and everyone loves him. his class has no hw pretty much but also means you need to do good on tests if u want a solid grade. they are not too bad but still need to study. Yes, sometimes the lectures were boring but at least once a lecture he would say something out of pocket and made them fun

Brekhus is a great guy but his lectures can be boring. The readings he assigned were very interesting and informative. Your grade is mostly just three tests, but they are very easy if you show up to the review section and fill out the review sheet along with him. I showed up to nearly every class but you could easily pass without attending.
Grading set up is AWFUL. I got a 100% on every assignment. Failed one test and ended with a 78. He is very nice and funny but not a good speaker. he truly cares about his students though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are only three tests and weekly homework assignments worth minimal points, so you have to do good on the tests. Tests aren't very difficult and the review sheet covers all the info. He is absolutely hilarious, but his lectures drone on and on and get boring. Overall a funny and passionate guy and I would take again.

There were 3 tests and 12 5-point assignments so you have to do well on every test to do well in the class. There is ~100 pages of reading a week but I never did any of it and I did well. If you go to his review session and read over the notes you will be fine for the tests. He is very funny in his lectures but they are Boring. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Brekhus! Keeps lectures interesting and funny. Tests are just like the reviews and he goes over the review very explicitly. Attendance isn't mandatory but you won't survive if you don't show up.

Dr. Brekhus is such a funny guy. His lectures are funny and full of real-life examples that keep you engaged. His word choice in his jokes is unmatched by most professors on campus. I laugh every time he is teaching. There is some reading but it is all very interesting.

Lectures are a bit repetitive, but he does try to make them fun. Attendance is not mandatory as long as you do the reading, and you probably won't have to do the reading if you go to lecture. Exams are all multiple choice and pretty common sense. Just don't forget to do weekly discussion posts and it's an easy A.
I couldn't listen to him talk because he was so monotone and boring.
I liked him.

He is very kind, and honestly tries to make his lectures entertaining, but to me his voice seemed monotone and made it easy to zone out to, making me end up skipping class a lot. If you take his course I highly recommend going to lectures, and if you don't: do the reading! Most of your grade revolves around exams, which range in difficulty.

He only gives the online discussion post grades and then exams. If you get awful grades on both, you won't pass. He'll make you buy his books at the beginning of the year, you do not have to. I never read them one time. Waste of money. His exams follow a study guide, but I got Ds and Cs on his tests. Most boring lectures, but funny person.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brekhus was a great professor! He posts the notes for each chapter online before you start discussing it. Attendance is not mandatory, and lectures are sometimes pretty boring. He puts out a study guide before each test and goes over it in class. The tests are the only thing you get graded on so as long as you know the study guide, you'll be fine.

Super easy and relaxed class. He's a really fun and caring guy who has a passion for sociology. The 3 exams were really easy as long as you went through the notes beforehand. Definitely not a class you have to show up to. I recommend going to class the day before the test because he'll give some answers out and go through the study guide.

Dr. Brekhus was a pretty bland professor. I could tell he knew his material well, because he never had PowerPoints, instead opting for writing keywords up on the board and talking away for all of the class. His tests were a joke, partly because the answers were half of the time literal jokes. Less than 30 people would show up out of a class of 350.

You dont even need to show up to class to pass. Just read the notes he posts on Canvas and you can get an A on every exam. I highly recommend this class for anyone looking for something easy with little commitment needed for a good grade.

The only 3 grades you will see in the grading book is your exams. Its so stupid and this is the worst teacher by far that I have ever had. At least create more assignments and dont be lazy so the exams arent 100% of your grade.

I loved Brekhus!!! He made class interesting and fun, even online. He is one of the few professors i've had that seemed like he actually cared about his students. I def recommend taking his class. Pay attention to lecture and do your homework and you'll get an A.

I loved the course because of him. Such a great person who cares about the wellbeing of his students, super funny as well! I honestly didn't read any of the books/textbook but got an A+ bc I showed up to every class. He throughly explains each concept and basically gives you the answers to tests in his review sessions. Interesting topics as well :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Super funny and passionate dude who makes the classes interesting. I had him on an internet class and he always loves to show off his cats. Zoom attendance isn't mandatory but his lectures are incredibly helpful and he posts them on Canvas after. If you pay attention and do the readings it's a solid A+, & his review sessions are incredibly helpful.

He is a super funny guy who loves mountain dew. He talks and talks but his humor and personality make up for it. Tests are somewhat easy, make sure you do the homework and go to class for easy points.

Wayne was hilarious, and he made his lectures entertaining. There are only 3 tests. His tests were difficult for me, but easy to others. I recommend going to his office hours before a test. He will give you Q&As. He rounded my final grade up, since I went to his office hours. Altogether, an interesting class.

Smart, Knowledgeable, and passionate about sociology. Lots of reading, but he goes over it, so show up to class, and you don't have to read. Graded on 3 tests, but he gives out study guides for each test and goes over the answers in class. If you know the study guide material, the test is super easy and straight forward. Attending class Easy A

There's a lot of readings but as long as you show up you shouldn't have to read them. His tests were easy for the most part but some questions made you think and multiple answers made sense to be right. You only get graded for a few things so if you bomb the test there's nothing to really help you. Lectures could be long and boring but he's funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Brekhus is a very funny little man with a light Northern accent who also doubles as a wonderful teacher. He explains big-picture ideas with simpler examples and I enjoyed his course so much I'm picking up sociology as a minor. As long as you attend the majority of lectures you should be fine.
He is a great professor and taught me a lot about the world and myself.

I really liked him as a professor because he's an awkward funny which made it bearable. Most of the lectures are pretty boring in general. You can either go to class and not read and get an A or not go to class and do all the reading and get an A. Everything on the review is on the tests.

Brekhus is HILARIOUS. I didn't mind going to class at 9am because I looked forward to hearing him speak. The material isn't very challenging, and he explains all the readings in lecture, so I didn't have to do a lot outside of class for an A. 10/10 would recommend.

Brekhus is the funniest professor I have ever had. His lectures always kept me interested because of his passion and his humor. Though he "assigns" a lot of reading in the syllabus, he explains every reading in class/lecture, so you never really have to read. His tests are just like the study guides, & if you show up to class the class is an easy A

A little crazy, especially about Mountain Dew in an early class. Check him out on youtube if you want to have a good laugh. Tries to be funny but comedic timing and delivery. Knows his stuff (wrote one of the books for class) Overall he sets you up to pass even if he can go on and on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very logical and the reason i decided to minor in sociology!

Literally this man was my favorite professor Ive had at Mizzou. If you have the chance to take sociology with him, do it. He is hilarious. I had a separate page of notes full of just weird quotes from him. 11/10

Very knowledgeable. Not the most interesting lecturer though. He tends to speak slowly with a lot of pauses which bothers me personally. He has a good sense of humor just poor comedic timing so I always felt slightly annoyed during lectures, but the class isn't too hard because all the tests are multiple choice.

He is great! This class is super easy and actually pretty interesting! I suggest going to class because he explains all the readings so you don't necessarily have to do them. As long as you try in the essays, he gives good grades! He's super easy to talk to and really funny. You'll do great in this class as long as you do what he asks. Easy A!
Great professor, need I say more?
Great professor! He was intelligent in lectures and got me interested in sociology. Would definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: My man Wayne is my favorite professor this semester. You don't need to read for the class because he thoroughly explains all of the readings in lecture. I look forward to his class every Tuesday and Thursday because of all the laughs he causes. He is hilarious, and is often not even trying to be.

I love him! He is so funny during lecture and talks/explains exactly what the reading assignment was, so you can choose to do both or one or the other. Attendance isn't mandatory for the sake that you can have a classmate sign you in whenever you can't go/don't want to. Exams are 30 questions multiple choice. Will be taking another class of his!
He assigns a fair amount of reading but he explains and summarizes the readings each day so its not the most necessary.

His lectures are really funny and he makes the material as relatable as possible.  When you're in class you almost feel like your having a conversation with him.  Attendance is mandatory (5 free days), and I suggest you go if you didn't get the books because he goes over most of it in class.  Tests make sure you know the material but are funny.
Lots of reading. It's very easy to skip class, or show up and not pay attention. As long as you read and pay some attention, it's easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wayne is the best. He really makes college do-able. I loved going to his class. I would always laugh. The entire class showed up every day just to get a dose of Wayne. People who weren't in his class would show up to his lectures. If you take his class, you will not regret it at all.

Brekhus is the kind of professor who stands up in the front and talks & talks- sometimes it's hard to pay attention, but if you don't feel like reading the books, you have to make some sort of effort in in-class note taking. He goes over the study guides in class and even gives the class answers to a few questions, so be sure to have a pen in hand.

Wayne is a great teacher. He tells jokes, shows movies, and tries to make the material relatable. Tells you the material for tests in lectures, so you shouldn't fail if you come and take notes. Exams are short answer and short essay but not hard if you go to class.  It's writing intensive so there's a 15pg term paper, but it's very do-able.

This was my first sociology class ever and I loved it! Wayne is a beloved professor at MU. He really enjoys teaching, and you can tell by his lectures. Some lectures were a little long, but he got his point across. The content is very easy and the exams are easier. He goes over the study guides with you in class before exams.

Brekhus is the man, his lectures can be boring at times but he's hilarious and makes it fun. He's very enthusiastic and gets excited when his students do well.  Show up to class and take the notes he writes on the board, and you're golden.

Takes attendance, but lets you skip up to 4 classes. Attendance is pretty much mandatory, but if you listen to the lectures, you don't need to do the readings. You'll want to listen anyways, since Brekhus is hilarious. Would absolutely have him as a professor again in the future. Only three tests, and doing the study guides before makes them easy.

He's a pretty good professor. His lectures are very, very long and he pretty much only talks about exactly what we read, so sometimes the lectures feel pointless. I never really know what to take notes on in lectures since he pretty much only gives examples of the topics instead of the topic itself. Other than that, he's quite the character.

Definitely recommend taking this class with Brekhus!!!! As long as you come to class and somewhat pay attention, tests will be a breeze. I barely ever read the books but paid attention in class and I got A's on every test. He's super funny and always keeps the class laughing.
Wayne Mellow Yellow Brekhus has been my favorite professor for my gen eds. Do the reading and go to class and you should get a good letter grade no problem.
He is a wonderful teacher and very understanding and caring. One of my favorite professors ever.
Brehkus is hilarious and keeps the class interested. If you come to lectures, you'll rarely have to read the books. Do the study guides, they are extremely helpful for the tests.

His lectures are always entertaining and he uses goodmemorable examples to illustrate ideas found in the reading. The class is easy if you do the assigned work and show up for lectures, the tests aren't hard.

The lectures and the assigned readings greatly overlap, making lectures often feel long if you do the assigned reading. However, the professor is great and his jokes are pretty funny. Minimal note taking required. His tests are not incredibly hard.
Very descriptive teacher that comes up with many stories. He drinks a lot of soda (usually mellow yellow)  and keeps trying to drink it even when there is none left

Wayne is an awesome guy. His lectures are fun to listen to and he is always willing to meet to help you better understand something. One of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had at Mizzou. I took SOC1000 with him as well as SOC3300 (Queer Theories) and SOC2300 (Me&Society). All great classes & received good grades.
LOVED this professor! He's hilarious and keeps lectures interesting. If you do the readings and go to class you will definitely get an A.
AMAZING professor. So funny and class was fairly easy. Would love to have him for another class.

Dr. Brekhus is GREAT teacher. He is very knowledgeable about his stuff and he makes his lectures interesting to listen to. He is also really FUNNY and NICE. I definitely recommend this class. Advice: If you read the articles you can miss class, if you don't, go to class...
This is hands down the best teacher Ive ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and wants the best for them. He is always available to help and ask questions. Take this class
Awesome profession, amazing to watch and great to learn from!
Takes attendance. Very entertaining and interesting lectures. No homework, just three tests. Very friendly and helpful
Dr. Brekhus is devoted to the subject and gets really excited in class. Super fun professor to have, enjoy!

Best professor I have ever had. I would take another one of his classes in a heartbeat. He really pulls you into what he is saying while always adding humor.  You will never catch this guy without a mountain dew.  He is such a character and a fantastic teacher.  He explains concepts very clearly and his tests are fairly easy. Strongly recommended.

Great lectures for the most part. Good at working in humor to keep interest. Explains concepts through several examples so its easy to understand. Make sure you do the reading. The tests cover both reading and lecture so know your material.

I'm an Economics major and yet this Sociology professor is my favorite teacher I have ever had at the University. I love him. So much. Best teacher ever. He is hilarious. Pretty much gives you an A (obvious answers - an example being one where you just pick the one that insults KU) but somehow you end up paying attention and learning anyways.

Favorite professor thus far at Mizzou. Very enthusiastic, witty, and quirky; I've never laughed so much in one class. Tests are very straightforward and easy; even include jokes. Takes attendance, gives 3 free absences. Class readings aren't really necessary if you take notes. Exam review sheets give you all necessary info. You'll love him/class.

I took his Self&Society Soc. class and I really enjoyed it. He's truly a GREAT teacher. There is a LOT of reading in his class but if you do the reading&go to lecture he reiterates what you need to know. His tests are incredibly straight-forward. If you come to class&do the reading you'll make an A+ easily. He's also incredibly funny and quirky.

I recommend ANY class with this guy. He is hilarious, and really good at his job. It's obvious he loves to teach and his enthusiasm really makes this class worth it. And I've never taken an exam with more jokes sprinkled into the questions. You'll love him.
Awesome teacher. Leactures were extremely interesting. I have never laughed so much in one class before! The class was in Engineering West and it was definitly worth the walk.

Professor Brekhus is extremely nice and intelligent. He obviously loves sociology and teaching. The exams aren't very hard, and the study guides he gives out before each exam tell you exactly what you need to know. Sometimes it helps to do the readings for clarification, but I wouldn't say it's necessary. This is a great class to take.

An amazing professor that will help you and give you some incredible worldly knowledge.  He manages to stay politically neutral despite the ease of straying to one side or the other.  BEWARE! You may die of laughter before the end of the semester!

Great teacher.  Prepare for a lot of writing assignments and lots of reading.  If you don't do it your screwed you will be in left field.  The class is very interesting.  Just keep up with the work load and you will get for sure an A. I would highly recommend taking this class.

Brekhus is my dude....point blank. Such a nice guy who cares about his students. It wasn't the easiest class I've ever taken but it's fair. Take this class and you'll enjoy a professor that cares about you...unlike most people in that profession these days.

Professor Brekhus is a wonderful and funny guy.  He likes to use extremely funny examples to keep the class interesting.  This class is also extremely fair and should be an easy A if you attend class and pay attention to the lectures.  Though I did do most of the readings, I would say they are not necessary.  Most of what you read he goes over.
He's such a great professor!! Really easy class, you dont even have to read. I recommend taking any of his classes, he's so adorable :) !
Great Professor!  Kept class interesting the whole time.  Very funny guy!  Highly recommend taking any of his classes!
I HAD BREKUS FOR SOCIOLOGY 1200 HE WAS AMAZING I DIDN'T EVEN HAVE TO READ THE BOOK AND I ENDED WITH AN A- SO THAT'S PRETTY MUCH ALL YOU NEED TO KNOW. PLUS THE GUY IS FUNNY AS HELL
Great class with a great professor!
Brekhus was a wonderful teacher! Very entertaining!.. Would suggest taking any of his classes.  He has a great sense of humor!

WHAT AN AWSOME TEACHER! so far, he is definitly my favorite! he has a great sense of humor and is extremely goofy! there is a lot of reading, but i hardly ever read and just took decent notes and got an A+ on all of my tests! i would definitly recommend this class to anyone!

Lots of reading but he repeats it all in class. Big lectures and sometimes he repeats himself with lectures from earlier in the week. Test was a bit difficult if you didn't read. Notes are taken but not much. He's energetic, funny, kinda goofy, but the class is not the worst one out there and is definitely passable
AMAZING TEACHER who truly cares about students learning, a hard to come by quality in education at Mizzou. I have taken three of his classes and would take another if offered!
I LVOE BURKEYYY! He is extremely funny & the class is a sinch if you come to every lecture and take good notes (you don't even have to read) <--although the books are interesting.

I absolutely love this man! He is a fantastic teacher. The material in the class is really easy, and really applies to life. I would recommend taking a class from him, because it is so easy and you learn so much :)

Absolute ACE prof. I've had him for two classes and I can't wait for the next. He's the reason I switched my major to Soc. and maybe the reason why I'm still in college. AMAZING guy take his classes Soc. 1000 and Soc. 2300. Hope he teaches my capstone!
Good teacher, teaches everything he assigns as reading so I didn't read any assignment the whole semester

TAKE THIS CLASS. Not only will you learn a lot about things that are actually interesting & relevant to life (McDonalds, what makes a person attractive in society, the sociology of Christmas cards) the tests are really straightforward and easy to ace. Do the reading, the studyguide & go to class because he tests over what he talks about in class!
Great Guy. Makes the class really fun.
He's an awesome teacher and i loved taking his class because it's actually interesting!
Great class.  Funny and interesting, good readings, and easy tests.  Take a class with him!
He's a cutie and a great advisor/professor

If you pay attention in class (which is pretty easy because he is hilarious at times) then his points are very easy to understand. Tests are 30 mc questions and not hard at all! even if you're confused on a question, if you write what you know to the side he might give you credit!
Very funny and goofy. Effective at conveying his lectures in a conversational manner. Easy exams, likes getting students involved.
Wayne is may be the greatest Sociology Prof ever!

Funniest teacher EVER. When a cell phone rings in class, he breaks into the funniest dance. His tests are not hard if you go to class and take notes. The lectures are really interesting too. There is quite a bit of reading though but it's not always necessary since he talks about the readings during the lecture. I'd recommend this class to anyone
He is an awesome teacher, and if you go to his office hours with questions about the test, he will explain everything.  If you bring up a valid point as well he might give you the points!
i've never had a better prof.

Mr. Brekhus is the best, most entertaining professor I've had yet! He is so helpful and nice, and really shows that he cares about his student's grades. If you don't like your test grade, go talk to him. When taking tests, if you're unsure on an answer, write what you know out to the side! He just wants to know that you studied. He's a good person!
we love Wayne
He's the nicest, funniest professor. I loved having him in class.

I love Wayne Brekaus he is a wonderful teacher and knows what he is doing. He is extremly helpful with everything and a very understanding teacher. He presents his concepts clearly and is always willing to help a student succeed.Take his class if you get the chance!!!!
He's amazing!! HOt Bod, funny, very good professor
No Comments
this guy is amazing. he really loves what he does. he's hilarious, plus he's really easy. take as many classes with brekhus as you can.  i changed my major to sociology because of him.
Best Soc class i ever took, and I've taken a lot. He has a way of making everyone really love the field of Sociology, and creating an atmosphere for people to get to know each other (like over beer)
An awesome professor.  Extremely nice, funny, and energetic.   He really loves his subject and it's apparent during his lectures.  Great class, I'd recommend it to anyone!
He's the reason I changed my major to Sociology.  I've taken two classes w/him and look forward to when I can take the next one.  He's super fun and has great ideas!
lots of fun

Great professor!  He is very energetic and enthusiastic.  He cares about students and is very easy to approach for help.  Subjects that are discussed are very interesting and he has a good knowledge of them.  Tests are all multiple choice and pretty easy.
Very nice, very easy
good
No Comments

A great sociology professor.  His enthusiasm is contagious, and as long as you pay attention in class and at least skim the readings you should do fine.  My first semester in college, he did what none of my other teachers managed: he made me look forward to going to class.
Dr. Brekhus is amazing! He makes what could be a boring class fun. Especially when hops around and gets excited. He's absolutely adorable, and obviously very interested in what he teaches.

Wayne Brekhus clearly loves his field and is incredibly knowledgable, always full of exampls and stories and excited to teach. The tests are easy, class isn't too bad, and he always lets the class out early.
GREAT professor. Funny, interesting lectures and tests are fairly easy if you go to class. Easily one of my favorite professors, take any class he teaches!

Professor Jung is one of the most thoughtful and engaging instructors I've had. The class was clear, challenging, and rewarding. I still think about what I learned. Highly recommended if you ever get the chance.

Prof Jung is fairly nice and does care about her students a lot. However, she is not the greatest teacher. Whenever students ask her questions, she often rambles and does not even answer the original question. The lectures are very dry and repetitive. The culmination of this course is a research project so prepare for that.

She's very smart. But uses iClicker for each class & if you miss more than 4 classes, she drops your overall grade by 10%. The content of the class is very lecture heavy, & there is a reading for each (however I did not do these) No assignments other than a final group prj and the exam

In larger classes, Dr. Yaw is effective at maintaining a balanced and fair class that pushes people to try their best. In smaller classes, he is much more personable and easy to hear back from if someone is having issues with their grade.

Yaw is my favorite prof I have had so far in college. His lectures are clear with a lot of examples, the homework problems are useful for quizzes and exams, and he gives a ton of extra credit opportunities. Pay attention to the types of problems he says will be on the exam and find them in the book and the exams will be so much easier.
Good lecturer and gave lots of opportunities for extra credit

Dr. Yaw is a great professor for a very challenging course. The material for this class can be very challenging as a first engineering course for many students; however, Dr. Yaw loves to answer any and all questions you may have, and either himself or his amazing TA's are available for outside help, which you will need at some point.

Good professor, good class. Sometimes material is tedious and very difficult (3D moments, friction, bending moment diagrams), other times its not that bad (vectors, trusses, strength of materials). His lectures are solid, but the class was at 8AM so good thing they were recorded online. Gives extra credit but won't curve a tough grading scale.

Best professor I have had at MU so far. Its a tough class, but he knows how to teach it well. You need a good calc and physics background. Make sure you do all the extra credit, it pays off. He is flexible on attendance but dont skip class..

First off, it was a great class for the majority of the semester. However, that changed when shear force and moment diagrams came about. To put it bluntly, he did not teach it well nor did he have a good, COMPLETELY correct complex problem and solution for us to look at. He gave outrageously difficult questions for some test questions also. Unfair.

Kind of a hard teacher but not too bad. He gives out a lot of extra credit so pay attention to emails and announcements. Go to office hours, hes always willing to help. Even though attendance isnt mandatory, I strongly recommend going because this class is tuff and he gives extra credit for attending!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good choice for 1200. You will have to do a lot of math and work. But do all the extra credit you can, show up to class, and your grade will quickly fall into place. Watch out to minimize losing points. Better to do so so on all the quizzes than to bomb one quiz because you can never fully recover from it.

Great teacher. Material for statics starts easy and ramps up after a month or two, but doing the homework and showing up for lectures makes the exams doable. So much extra credit and partial credit on exams that even doing rough on quizzes/exams means you can keep an A. Held lots of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He doesnt try to trick you. Hes very straight forward about what will be on quizzes and exams, and gives tons of opportunities for extra credit. You can tell he really cares about the students. It was difficult at points. Just be prepared for long homework assignments.
Super great professor! Tests and homework are really hard but he offers a lot of extra credit which makes up for it. My test average was like 70 and I ended with an A.

Yaw is always willing to help on anything. He is really good at explaining things one on one and wants you to succeed. He always had a positive attitude every morning when he showed up. We also knew what to study for exams and quizzes, which was helped for Exam 3 and the final. Don't skip classes, read his ppt slides and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Purposefully put wrong answers on the Exam 2 review key and only told the students in his office hour the day before the exam. I wasn't able to go & wouldn't have known I was studying incorrect info unless my friend told me. Yaw also changed the rules on his Integrity Points & grading policies multiple times during the semester. Not fun at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Never have I had a professor that cared about students as much as Yaw did. He literally gives you a possible additional 20% added to your overall grade. The class is not even that hard if you study the in class problems and know how to do all the homework. It sucks how I will not have him as a professor because his class was the easiest A+ ever.

Very friendly guy but he will make you work for your grade. He doesnt take attendance but skip class at your own demise.. Hand writing is poor so you wont be able to read his notes if you keep skipping class.. He is very caring though. He grades very fairly.. Prepare for pop-up quizzes, review his note regularly and go to his office hours

Yaw was a friendly guy, goes through class examples way too fast. Handwriting is atrocious, go to class because you won't understand when he posts the notes online. Lots of opportunity for EC with in-class tests and answering questions. The 2nd exam was pretty tough, final was very hard, 50% avg. Understand all homework Q's and examples from class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great! Guy.. He good

Professor Yaw is amazing. He is a new professor but you won't even notice it. His lectures are very simple and straightforward. Pay attention to his reviews before exams. He is very patient with students. I struggled at the beginning of the class because of his accent but I caught up with time.
I found Dr. Yang's lectures pretty uninteresting. Expect tangents and tough grading. He's not the worst professor by a long shot, but I found his class boring and unengaging.

Prof. Yang is really knowledgable and passionate about his studies, which was nice to see in a history class. Yes, he does sometimes go on long tangents, but I still enjoyed the class as he offered a different perspective on Chinese history. He is a tough grader, but provides a lot of feedback that helps you improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is pretty relaxed, definitely one of his easier classes content-wise but still super cool learning about Taiwan. It's pretty lectured based. However, Dr. Yang is a great lecturer and despite tendencies to run over time and get sidetracked, he is very caring and passionate about teaching. Assignments are straightforward and easy to do.

Dr. Yang is a fantastic teacher who is incredibly passionate about his subject. He went through a lot personally this semester, but he never quit being a fantastic professor. Textbook is interesting to read and he provides great feedback on your exams and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yang is a fantastic professor. His work made me change my focus to East Asian History. Yes, he does get on tangents during lectures. Additionally, he can be a bit of a tough grader for an introductory history course,  but he gives incredible feedback. This might not be an easy A, but the skills and lessons learned through the class are valuable
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't feel like he was a very good lecturer, he was always going off on some sort of tangent and we didn't spend much time on the actual material. Super tough grader too. He was accessible, but never very helpful if you did talk to him.

Phenomenal professor with a lot of passion. One of my favorite classes I have ever taken at any level. His lectures are awesome and you should attend them as they will help your understanding of the class. Lots of readings but they are worth it as they tie in well to lecture. Overall a great class that expands your knowledge of the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing guy. He legitimately made me love a course that I had no real interest in taking. He is more than fair with grading, and he is always willing to have a meaningful conversation with you. Do your work and you will get along better than most any other professor.

Wonderful professor! Super smart and obviously loves what he does. Makes the class interesting and really nice to everyone and accepting of all comments/questions without making you feel dumb. He is a bit of a harsh grader (though he says he isn't), especially for a 1000 level class, but you do end up learning a LOT. Made me want to visit China!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You are better off teaching yourself the material over anything she can teach you. All of her lectures are rambling nonsense that waste everyone's time. An hour for an exam that a normal prof would give 90 minutes for. I can confidently say I have learned nothing from her, all of the physics I have learned are from the TA or self taught. NEVER TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take the class asynchronously and don't watch the lectures. Instead, use that time to understand the homework. I learned more gaining through the homework problems. I thought discussion was useful as well. I would recommend going. Labs were super easy. Use old exams to study. She is nice, but get ready to teach yourself. Canvas page is also a mess.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take the class asynchronously and don't watch the lectures. Instead use that time to go over the homework. I learned more from the homework and the discussions. Go to the discussions they are helpful. Also make sure to go over the practice exams. Labs were super easy. She is really nice, but can't teach. Get ready to teach yourself.
take the class somewhere else and save your sanity

Pretty hard for a 1000 level class, she's very hard to understand at sometimes, and lots and lots of homework. HW represents the exams pretty well so they're pretty predictable. You will spend lots and lots of time outside of class trying to understand the material. Exams way too short for all of the content on it.

Anyone who says this class was insanely hard just didn't keep up with the homework. You are assigned a maximum of 4 assignments per week all of which are self explanatory if you do the problems she goes over in lecture. The key to getting an A in this class is literally just doing the homework every week since her exams use the same problems.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This course was at best, bad. I am a 3.9 GPA and a hard worker, yet a B was all I could pull. The lectures were incredibly difficult to understand -- it took me half of the semester to understand her speaking. There is at a minimum,10 hours of homework a week and the exams are much too short for the amount of problems. Avoid if you can!

The worst course I have taken at Mizzou. You will spend hundreds of hours on homework. Tests are impossible. She is very unorganized. If I had to drop out or deal with this hell of a course again, I'd drop out. Inability to improve the course despite teaching it for decades is inexcusable. Avoid at all costs.

This lady is evil. She went to Tsinghua for her undergrad, which is the Harvard of China, and Peking for her masters, which is the Yale of China. That should be all you need to know. She is very nice but oh my god you will have so much homework. It will take up all of your time. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit. But she is evil.

I just took Physics 1 and all of the reviews are pretty much the same. Course itself is pretty simply IF you spend time learning the material. I did the online lectures/in person labs and tests. SO MUCH HOMEWORK! Heaviest courseload I've had. If you study the practice exams you will be fine, and she offers a lot of extra credit.

I can't believe she has been teaching this class for so long and this is how she chose to structure it. She expects you to learn material from recorded lectures before class and just does problems in class. So many filler words I almost can't listen. I have never seen so many people stay until the last minutes of a test because there's no time.

DO NOT take this class hybrid if you are not self disciplined. There is so much homework and although there are due dates there is practically no late penalty so it is basically all self paced. Overall the professor is very nice.

Not a crazy hard class to do well in, the exams are almost identical to past practice exams she posts on canvas. So much homework, so you have to do a lot to stay on top of it. Just memorize the practice exams and you'll do fine. Also has opportunities for extra credit which is nice.
if you aren't religious, pick a religion and pray

Prof Zhang floods you with homework and problems, if you are a stem major I suggest taking this course on an easy semester - it will have to be your life for a good understanding of physics with the style Zhang teaches with. Also if you don't like hearing people lick their lips and make other mouth sounds - lec recordings will be ur worst nightmare

I genuinely hated this class and it caused me so much anxiety so I dropped it. Everyone you talk to will probably tell you it's awful. If you do take it, get ready to make it your life or you won't survive. The tests are hard and she doesn't give near enough time. The final is cumulative and only 2 hours long.

Took online summer course. Way easier than in person somehow. Still way too much HW. 2-3 HW per week that take anywhere from 3-6 hours to complete (many times due on test day), labs (quick) and quizzes (redundant, but use the slides and you're fine). Tests are way too long, you need at least 2 1/2hrs to finish comfortably but only 2hrs are given.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was sweet, but not good. He just read off the slides that he posted after. Lectures are about the concept and maybe include a rushed through example question. I failed my first ever exams in this class. The concept isn't hard but the way you have to teach yourself makes it very difficult. Chegg is the only reason I passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang was very kind, but the class is a logistical nightmare. There is just way too much content in each lecture, and only one brief review for each exam (20-30% each). He only lectures about the theoretical and practical side of thermodynamics. He expects you to figure out the problem solving (what you're tested on) in the homework.

Lots of resources and leeway for homework and quizzes. Sometimes hard to follow along in lectures. Doesn't have all the formulas on the formula sheet. She has some, but not all, which makes it very difficult to do tests and homework. Timing for tests is extremely hard.

Probably my favorite professor in at Mizzou engineering. He's accessible out of class and encourages you to ask for help without making you look stupid. The class is test heavy, but he lets you use resources. He's very passionate about thermodynamics. I withdrew from thermo last semester with a different professor and its a night and day experience
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thermodynamics is one of the most inefficient classes taught here (ironic, huh) due to its vast and difficult content size, but Dr. Zhang did his best. He's a very kind guy and is passionate about teaching thermo. The lectures are long and 95% of the class never shows up, but you should go to them. He shows you how to use the formulas and tables.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Biggest thing is get ready to spend lots of time studying material, completing homework, and watching lectures. It's one of those courses where if you get behind you stay behind. The material itself is not incredibly difficult, especially if you have a math background. Plus, there's extra credit and practice exams that are similar to the real exam.
Always behind and doesn't finish lectures. Crazy amounts of homework.

I had Yun for Physics 1 and 2
She has a distinct teaching style, which seems to be replicated every year. She cares and adheres to your worries, but her exams are pretty hard. 
I cannot stress this enough: STUDY PRACTICE EXAMS AND DISCUSSIONS FOR THE ACTUAL EXAMS. 
The homework will not help you for exams but will help for content. 
Good luck

Lots of homework, boring lectures, and an unorganized canvas page. She never gets through the lectures on time and we are always behind so you never learn stuff in discussions. Crazy amount of homework

Weekly:

x2 Weekly Short Assignments - (~1hr each)
x1 Weekly Comprehensive Assignment - (1-5hrs)
x1 Weekly Quiz - Doesn't take long but feels redundant (10-15 mins)
x1 Discussion Section Work Submission (~30 mins, impossible to keep up during the section)
x1 Lab Work Submission (~30 mins)
This is all homework, not done in lecture or discussion time

I took the online class during the summer, so I had to spend a lot of time listening to lectures. Lectures are quite monotone, but do get across the necessary points. Make sure to take notes of the equations and know their application to problems, of which was pretty straightforward on homework and tests.

You will drown in homework that is nothing like what's on the exams. She has set amount of points for homework and quizzes with more points above that amount that don't count. Very dry and monotonous lectures. Exams are hard to finish within the time given and count for half of the grade. Avoid if you can.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. If I had not taken calculus and chem 2 before hand I would have been lost. She is not very good at explaining concepts and the quizzes are not relevant at all! Nothing on the quizzes appears on the tests. Her grading system is weird but it does help you. Watch lectures and do the practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The HARDEST class I have EVER taken. So much material is thrown at you every week. So MUCH homework. I spent about 15 hours each week doing homework, quizzes, and studying. She does offer some extra credit (DO IT)! It is possible to get an A, but you will have to work so much for it. Labs were annoying but could be helpful. Discussions were boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She gives out a lot of extra credit and the penalty for turning in things late is really low. The only reason class is hard is because she has so much hw if you get behind its really annoying to catch up. However, because I had to always do hw I didn't really need to study for exams.

One of the worst professors I've had. Her lectures are pointless to go to because she is so hard to follow. I ended up teaching myself the entire class by reading the notes and going over the homework. The homework was grueling and so time-consuming, definitely use online resources. The exams are long and tedious, most people don't even finish.
Professor does a decent job at teach tough material. I am convinced the people failing this class are going to drop out of college because she gives lots of extra credit and resources to do well.

Passing this class is a breeze, and getting an A is really easy. Anyone who has issue passing this class isn't putting in the effort they're paying for to attend university. Do homework and take the quizzes and you're guaranteed 50%, go to office hours/tiger tutors for homework problems and if you don't pass then I suggest applying for disability.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hard, but if you do your work, you'll be fine. Exams are doable if you truly master the homework. She's very accommodating with deadline homework. However, you will do poorly if you don't do the homework and do your best to truly learn from it. Go to TA review sessions for exams. Exams' partial credit will save you, too.

If you read the other reviews you may see that it is a very hard class, It isn't, on the other hand it is very time consuming. There is at least 5-7 hours of HW every week. On the other hand everything on the test is from the HW. While yes the exams are hard the practice test she gives you are the exact test, but with different numbers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i want to kms
She is certainly a smart person, but she would be better off in a lab than teaching students.

The homework takes 2-3 hrs per assignment and are typically worth less than 15 points in a 1000pt course. So many assignments every week, along with discussions (plural), quizzes, labs, and exams. Material can be overwhelming at first, even if you took physics in hs. If you can take with someone else or another school, you should. do not recommend

Lots of homework, but there are multiple attempts to get points and they really help as a buffer for exam scores. Exams (for me) were the most difficult part so do the homework points, quizzes, and labs. I recommend keeping track of all the points you earn in each section, you won't have to do every homework question/assignment to get full credit.

Having gone to the lecture every day for this class, I can confidently say you do not have to go to the lecture every day for this class. He reads off the slides, while maybe explaining slightly beyond what's written on the screen. There was also a quiz after every lecture which can be solved through the lecture slides. Overall, the class was avg.
I failed this class and I have to retake it.

Dr. Zhang is a nice teacher, but there is so much work. There are multiple quizzes and homework assignments due each week, labs. Exams are every few weeks, and attendance lectures is required. I highly recommend watching the video lectures and utilizing resources like Tiger Tutors, or becoming involved in the physics community with Dr. Zhang/TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So much work that it's hard to keep up. Multiple quizzes and homework assignment due each week, lab report each week, exam every few weeks, mandatory lectures.

500 of the 1000 points are pretty easy to get as long as you complete the homework. You get several attempts at each problem before you get it wrong.  If you do the homework and the practice tests they are the same format and you will be set for the test. The final is worth 200 points and was the most challenging part of the class.

Though the class was a lot of work, Dr. Zhang was easy to contact and get help from. Practice exams generally reflected the exact format of each exam. Physics covers difficult content, but knowing what variables stand for on the formula sheet is 80% of what you need to know as exams are written mathematical questions.

The class has a lot of homework but she prefaces the course by saying this. This course helped me tackle some harder concepts I will need for the future. She was accommodating for me when I needed to take an exam early.  I would recommend making an Excel sheet to track your points if you want to know your grade all of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class put me in a psych ward. always been a straight A student till now and i just lost all hope of ever getting into med school.

The class was a lot of work. The homework would take hours to complete and I found that it was not very helpful for studying for the exam content. In the end, all the points for homework, discussions, labs, and lecture did help my grade. Yun Zhang tries her best to help set you up for success even if you do poorly on the exams. The class is doable
She was hard. Had to retake the course

The labs are the only easy part about this class and will probably save my grade. I do not see the relevance of the course unless you're a physics major or going into engineering. Grade is locked all semester and homework take HOURS then are not worth much. Take the online lecture section to save yourself. only upside is a few extra credit offered.

Ungodly amount of homework that takes forever to do and then it's hardly worth any points. Also she has it to where Canvas doesn't show your grade so you will have to calculate it yourself or wait until the end of the semester. Exams are rough, but at least the labs are relatively easy. She does offer some extra credit.

taking this class was the worst decision ive ever made. I spend every waking second trying not to fall behind. I don't have free time anymore. 3 "short" homeworks, a quiz and 1-2 LONG homeworks per week. also makes them due test days. If you can take any other class or teacher im begging you do it. Ive never struggled more in a class in my life.

Terrible class. I don't think she realizes how much HW she's giving us, 1 assignment per MWF (1 hour each) + weekly assignment (2-3 hours) + labs. 1 hour to do a test which is essentially a weekly homework assignment with half the questions. In lecture, she's terrible, starts speaking clearly and starts to mumble as she goes through the question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've never spent so much time on homework for a class in my life. I'm doing well in the class, but I spend 15-20 hours a week doing work for this class which is ridiculous for a 4 credit hour course. Also, sign up for the online section and teach yourself because the lectures are not helpful.

Zhang is a much better professor than people give her credit for. I think a lot of the dislike for her is simply because this is a general intro science course that many people take and really dislike the content. Its really not that hard or bad. Zhang gives lots of leeway with points. WATCH THE VIDEO LECTURES they're helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Extremely disorganized, the homework is just a ton of busywork instead of meaningful work. I should not have to do 9 different complicated equations to be able to earn 1 point. She does not understand her class is not our only class. Nothing is clear. Also very poorly translated.

This class is tough due to the subject. But professor Zhang does a good job of covering a ton of difficult information well. There is a bunch of tutoring and review sessions for each test. She provides several practice exams & a TON of homework that helps tremendously with the exams. Do all the assignments and study and you'll get an A.

Homework heavy but you don't have to do it all (60% of short/80% of long assignments). Half of your grade is the hwk, quizzes (2 attempts), & lab. Other half is 3 exams & final. STUDY THE PRACTICE EXAMS. Time crunch on exams. Really just need to know how to use the formulas from the lectures. Take lecture online if you love yourself.

While the homework takes an ungodly amount of time, she is lenient on late submissions. The tests however require you to know the material like it is second nature. If you have to think about a problem at all you will run out of time. Maybe 5 out of 70+ students leave the test before time is up. Expect to spend a lot of time outside class.

Do NOT take this class with Ms. Zhang. With the amount of homework she assigns, you would think she's unaware her students have other classes to manage. If you're not a good test taker, you will be miserable. This is the first class I've ever withdrawn from. If you're forced to take this class with her, godspeed. Wish I had more space to write...

Do NOT take this class with Ms. Zhang. With the amount of homework she assigns, you would think she's unaware her students have other classes to manage. Tests were very difficult. If you're not a good test taker, you will be miserable. This is the first class I have ever had to withdraw from. If you are forced to take this class with her, godspeed.

Took three times to pass this class. Do not take this class with another hard class or you will fail. Read the syllabus and her grading scale. As long as you reach the counted points, you will pass. She is very lenient with due dates for hw! Submit the labs & assignments even if they are late. Enroll in the online lect section if you love yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you plan to take any other science course simultaneously, rethink that. This class is so brutal and time consuming. It is also highly disorganized. The homework is not manageable either. The only good thing about this course is that exams only make up 50 percent of your grade. Find a different professor.

She had so much homework that was honestly not super helpful for the exam but the points matter so do it. She's very lenient on late work. The study session were very helpful and doing the study session problems was a great way to study.

This class is extremely difficult. I am taking it online (in-person lab/discussion), so I am lucky enough to play it back at my own speed. There is a billion homework assignments each week. She offers minimal EC so don't count on that. The homework takes hours to complete and it is multi-step....oh the best part is you get like 2.5pts on those ;)
Poor online organization, enormous homework load and ineffective teaching style

I like Zhang personally but not a good professor. Her lectures did not correlate to the criteria and were not helpful with the exams nor completing the large amounts of homework. I went to tutoring about 20hr a week and the tutors taught me everything. When I asked her what else I could do, she said that she did not know bc I was doing everything.

The teacher is nice. I didn't find her accent difficult to understand. However, she gives the most ungodly load of homework I've ever experienced. There are 2 short assignments (by short they usually take an hour) and 1 or 2 comprehensive assignments (sometimes over 6 hours of work). She also locks the grade which is super annoying.

Zhang doesn't really teach the content at a deep enough level to where you actually understand it, or repeats the stuff you already know over and over. If she's running out of time at the end of a lecture, she breezes through slides and expects you to know it instantly. You mostly learn on your own through homework, which isn't bad/just like tests

I've taken 4 credits before, and they aren't as heavy as this. That being said, she is A LOT better from 1210. She made an effort to let you know your grade this time around and the obsessive amount of homework is easier once you get used to her. I dislike physics, but I learned it and her tests are pretty easy as long as you do the practice ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Anyone who struggled in her class just didnt put in the large amount of effort this class requires. Lots of assignments but do them and the exams are a breeze. Worst part is you wont know your exact grade until the end of the semester just a ballpark unless you actually calculate it yourself

Very difficult class. She gives A LOT of homework which is a blessing in disguise because if you finish those assignments, it helps your overall grade IMMENSELY. Let's you take quizzes twice and keeps the best score. You get multiple tries on hw problems. Labs aren't too bad, but go to your TA's office hours for help. Final exam not cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take your time to actually do the homework and quizzes. Save your work on assignments for the exams, they're literally the same problems. She reopened quizzes for those who missed, drops a lab score, and gives you 10-20 total pts to be missed on hw and quizzes each. Everyone who struggled prob thought a 4 credit hr course wasn't time consuming.

Worst professor I've ever had. She overloads assignments during the week. You never know what your grade is & she doesn't care. Email & her response is she "doesn't have time to answer questions." Students typically fail the second exam, which she says is bc they don't understand the concepts but its because she doesn't teach it well. Nice lady ig

I had Professor Zhang for physics 1210. A few pieces of advice- PRINT the lectures. Do not write your notes down. It is impossible to write all the notes and stay on top of things. I would recommend going to class for attendance. Finally, keep track of the caps on points. You can miss some homework and do fine- put in the work and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken. So many assignments - be aware that only 25 points from the short assignments count toward your grade and focus on the quizzes and weekly comprehensive assignment, which have more weight. Labs are awful and always run over. Take this with another prof or at another school. Avoid this professor.

Nightmare class. 3 short assignments, a long assignment, a quiz, discussion problems, a pre lab and lab report every week. Bad accent, can't understand her in mandatory lectures. Worst prof I ever had, dropped class. Stay away from this teacher unless you are looking to suffer and not learn anything.

3 short assignments 1-2 Long assignments, quiz every week, pre lab and lab. Lecture is a mandatory waste of time because can't understand herbut so many assignments it's impossible to find time to work from the book. Ridiculous work load, esp for a freshman class. Avoid this professor, worst I have had at MU.

80 homework questions (for credit) due each week, quizzes due every class, has two different "due dates" for every assignment and you have to learn which ones are actually the TRUE due date? It's a complete nightmare. She dosen't put ANY grades in until EXAM WEEK so I had no idea what my grade was until the class was over.

Assigns excessive hw assignments. She drops them at random times with no announcement, no consistent due dates, and no schedule to outline the work. Lectures are dull and repetitive. Grade distribution is unclear, grades are locked, labs put in the gradebook on the last day of classes. Hw has wrong answers and quizzes leave out important info

You will attend lecture MWF and a lab (2 hours long) and discussion (1 hour long) per week. There are roughly 3 short assignments, 1 long assignment, 1 long extra credit assignment, Pre-lab, and Post-lab write-ups due EACH week. She's difficult to understand and it can be challenging to follow along in lecture/office hours. I am retaking the class

She's a good professor at heart (and very friendly), but her accent can be challenging to understand at times. Tests are incredibly challenging for the time allotted, and many people don't finish. She doesn't curve, so unless you're pretty decent at physics and math, be prepared for a rough time.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Had Zhang for Physics 1 & 2. Not the best professor, but definitely not bad either. Lectures are slow; I suggest watching at home on 2x speed. Keep up with homework and take advantage of extra credit. More than enough points available to get a good grade, and homework/discussion problems do wonders for test preparation. Very doable class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A lot people give Dr. Zhang a bad rap, but I honestly loved her for physics one. She gives you hints in class about what people miss most on tests. Tutoring and discussion helped me understand what I was learning so much (some test questions came from those)! If you go to tutoring you will get an A.

Class was initially tough for me because I'm really bad at math and I didn't take physics but I got an A+ with lots of hard work. I put in 5 to 10 hrs / week and go for most tutoring sessions. You must set aside lots of time for this course because of there are ALOT of homework and 3 exams + 1 comprehensive final. Do strategize your timetable well
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Required to go to at least 25 of the lectures but they are useless and boring. Her accent is tough to understand at times. Tons of homework that is generally harder than the tests. Lab is simple and weekly discussion is generally most helpful. Tests are fairly easy if you study practice exams and discussion questions. Homework and EC boosted grade.

Lectures are very boring and class has a lot of homework. If your program allows, I would take the class online (I've heard its easier). If not, the best way to go about studying is lecture notes and discussion problems. Homework problems are harder than the ones on the exam
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Imagine reading a paper with misspelled words, no spacing, or punctuation. Welcome to lecture. EC is 15 points, so it helps a little. Assignments due per class period, a weekly homework set, and a weekly quiz. Worst instructor I've ever had. Lectures are simple, tests complex. Find a different instructor, even if it's at another school. No curve.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The amount of work you have to do is insane. And if you plan on studying don't rely on the practice exams their useless. She has no Idea how to prepare students for the test nor does she know how to measure her students abilities to take her tests. Avoid her she is not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: 1210&1220 Grading is very fair. A middle schooler who tries hard could get a C. There are 1000 points in the class and tests are 500. You can fail every test with 40s and pass the class. The book isn't necessary to buy at all. Save your money. Big HW and quizzes are online and due at 9pm Tuesdays. She's an ok prof. The subject isn't for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a nice person, but very hard to understand her accent and her tests are really tough.
