I find her somewhat lazy for using pre-made slides from the textbook company and reading off verbatim. I can do that home. Does give extra credit so that'll help your grade. Had her for 1210 and 1220. TAs in lab were great. Avoid this professor.

She's downright rude in office hours. I got on the unlucky cycle of taking her for 1210 and 1220 and she is just not a good teacher. She doesn't understand physics is tough, and doesn't care about you or your grade. I barely swung a B for the class and have a 3.9 if that tells you anything. If you can, wait to take the cycle with the other teacher.

She is not helpful. Physics is a difficult class and the teacher should be more prepared to help students. There is no curve in the class and don't expect her to help your grade at the end either. I would say take it with another teacher, but the options are slim. She's hard to understand and always seems to be on the fence about her teachings.

Lectures are really dry, and you need 25 attendances to get full attendance credit. I took Physics in high school, and it was roughly all the same material, but much faster pace and more emphasis on the little things.  Make sure you do all of the online homework, extra credit, and labs, because they'll really boost your grade in the end.

Dr. Zhang's lectures are long and can be very confusing to understand. The tests are tough, but she does give extra credit. Make sure to do the homework and do good on the labs because they will save your grade.

I don't really have a lot of nice things to say about her. She really screwed the class on the final, it was way harder than she acted like it would be while reviewing it. The class has no curve at all, or if it is there, don't count on it, it was maybe 2%. Which is ridiculous considering the class,and that almost everyone I know got a C+ or lower.

Her tests are very reasonable and many problems are  pulled straight from the homework.  I've never heard a complaint about her, and she's always willing to help her students during her office hours or through email.  Make sure you learn the concepts and do the homework to gain practice before the tests, and you'll be fine
The class was pretty easy as long as you keep up with the homework and do the practice exams before the tests. Go to class because she does random clicker questions as participation points.
Definitely not a blow off class, but if you study and do ok on the exams its curved a ton at the end.

As long as you study the lectures and recitations before the test, you should be able to do fine, as they are nearly the same. Her lectures are dry (but that could just be the subject material). She is also a very nice person and very willing to help.

She's pretty easy to understand but the material is just hard. She is better at explaining if you go to the office hours she holds. I did pretty bad on all the exams except for one and got a B in the class. Exams aren't that hard you just don't have time to get them done at all. Not a horrible class but you reallllllyyyy have to keep up with it!

You need to keep up in this class even if you're bored in lecture. It's hard to understand her at times, but as long as you get the help you need this class isn't too difficult. I got a D-,D and an A on the three exams and still had a B+ in the class. I'm usually a straight A student. She's just average in lecture, but helpful in office hours.

Horrible teacher, and a terrible class. The exams aren't too hard if you study, but the final COMPREHENSIVE exam at the end of the semester is just mean. She expects way too much out of her students, and she's really hard to understand. She's also the TA for most of her classes, so you don't even get another person to help you understand. AVOID.

Great class! She builds in a lot of extra credit so even if you get B's on all the tests, you can come out with an A. Labs are fairly easy and somewhat interesting. Print off the power point slides prior to class. Go to her office hours if you need help! She's patient and very helpful.
Can't understand anything!!

This professor appears to have brilliance and vitality in his knowledge of thermodynamics.  He may not have the most interesting of lectures but like a true professor he can answer most any question in his field with expertise.

I agree with the previous poster.  Her exams are very similar to the practice exams.  Also, the extra points throughout the semester (homework, RSD attendance, lecture attendance, and lab) are really good at boosting your grade.  Basically you would have to not study at all to receive a poor grade in this class.  She is very nice in person.

The lectures are pretty boring to go to, but you get points just for clicking in.  The exams are EXACTLY like the practice exams.  The people that are saying that it was the hardest class ever and not to take it are crazy; they must have not studied at all!  If you do your homework and study, you will do great!Everyone I know got an A or A+!

Very hard to understand, her English was a little broken.  Test questions were random and poorly worded. Did not make learning easy.  That being said she was VERY nice and tried to build some extra points into the system to make up for low exam averages.

This Class is ridiculously hard and the professor made it even harder. She's hard to understand, her exams and extremely hard. You can study your ass off and still fail the exam. FREAKING PIECE OF CRAP!!! Highly recommend not to take it because this class is honestly gonna make you kill yourself. HATE IT!

Aside from getting attendance points going to lecture is useless. She's hard to understand and all the notes are online. The tests are pretty hard, but get curved.  If someone else is teaching the class take it with them, but its not all that hard to get by with a B.
Professor Zhang is a decent teacher, but pretty boring.  There is homework due every week.  If the homework is kept up with then the tests aren't to bad since the tests and hw are so similar.
Very hard class, avoid this professor if at all possible. Very hard to understand, class time was pointless. This class ruined my semester and my GPA. STAY AWAY!
Very hard to understand and follow lectures, but can print off power point slides and use them. Tests were pretty easy but final was a curve ball - VERY hard.

This class sucked. Id heard she was easy from fellow classmates but I dont know how they got that impression. Besides going to class for attendance points, it was pointless to be there. Dr. Zhang reads from the powerpoint with her green laser and doesnt acknowledge the class. Tests were hard, but curved and grading was fair. I squeaked out with a B

Those first 2 people that left comments must have been CRAZY!  She is hard and horrible, don't take her!  She would give practice exams which were fairly easy, but all our tests were SOOOO HARD!  The average on our 2nd test was a 47!  But she did curve it to a 70, so I have to give her that.

She made physics VERY easy. Many people in class got an A+ or A. As long as you make a halfass attempt at understanding the material you can do well. She is very helpful, but class is also very boring.She also has a tough accent to understand. I thought most material was beat into the ground, so even if you're not good with physics, it's an easy A.
Very willing to give extra help whenever needed.  This is a difficult class for most, but she grades very fair.  Can't ask for anything better from a physics teacher.  Very good prof overall

Somewhat rude, and harsh with his course. Kind of aggressive with his grading. Miss any class for any reason whether it is sickness or school sanctioned events and he deducts from your total participation 5 points each time. (Post Normal Biochemistry)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yokom's lack of student engagement makes this course very difficult for students.

Professor Yokom is knowledgeable about the subject, he cannot convey it in a way that is understandable to non-major students taking a lower level Biochemistry course. Weekly quizzes online. Group assignments once a week also. No homework which sucks because it would make the class better to understand. You MUST pay attention and study HARD to pass
I had to drop

i took this course (extra-galactic astronomy) last semester and liked it a lot. dr yan was one of the two professors in the department who inspired me the most. his lectures were well organized and he asked deep questions. i also liked it very much that he set aside time in class to work out the past homework problems. he is awesome.

I took his Galactic Astronomy last semester. He is an extremely knowledgeable professor and a caring person. He teaches in the classic way but I did learn a lot, basically what astronomy is really about. Not an easy professor though, and to do well you must come to his lectures. But he would give you many opportunities to make things right.

Missed a few assignments due to family issues after the spring break and thought I'd fail this one. I explained my situations, he was sympathetic and gave extensions. A highly recommended teacher. The class was fun, the lectures were organized nicely through canvas. just did the hw on my phone because i had to travel a lot.

I took this online course instead of a bio class to fulfill the science course requirement. Being a history major I found this course a bit different from what I'd expected. But overall the materials were great and inspiring and I'd recommend it. Dr. Yan was very quick in answering my emails. Had I not forgotten two homework I believe I'd got A.
Absolutely terrible teacher. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. SO BAD SO BAD SO BAD.

All of these reviews are 100% true. One of the online quizzes (worth 75% of grade) closed out before the due date for me, and I had to basically argue with him over email to get him to open it again. Expect no leniency with assignments, even though they are 3/4 of your grade. Very lazy class layout and seems like an excuse to get research funding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst teacher I've ever had. His homework answers are not anywhere in the notes, and are not accurate according to legitimate online sources. He can barely speak English in the lectures and skips over important information needed to succeed in Astronomy 1200. Will not ever take a class with this teacher again.

Class had lecture vids./slideshows posted every week. I just used the slides. Textbook is required but I didn't really read it. Weekly hw assignments that are ~22 questions and multi. choice (took ~45min-1h). The final exam is all the homework questions & answers. There is no final paper, that was a mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As many others have said, beware if you are looking for an easy science credit, as this is the opposite. The lectures hardly add anything to the class, as he only reads directly off the slides and doesn't explain anything in layman's terms. The homework is tricky and frustratingly specific, so be prepared to spend several hours on 20 questions.

This class only had 15 quizzes each worth 5-pts that make up 75% of your final grade. If you miss any (which is easy to do since quizzes are due at noon) your grade will drop a lot. No extra credit or late work. The other 25% of your grade is a 100 question final which you're given 2 hours to take. Expect to spend ~7 hours a week on notes/quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is not the easy A you might be expecting! If you're wanting to succeed, this is not the class to slack off on. The comprehensive final makes up a huge amount of the grading portion, so don't take this class unless you're ready to dedicate significant time to it. The material can be very confusing, but Yan tries his best to make it work.

Only took this class bc I needed a science credit. It is way to difficult to be considered a 1200 level course. Every week it takes me about 10 hours to complete lectures, reading, and the assignment. The assignment alone is 20-25 questions and takes me ~2hrs. He has refused to meet with me multiple times and left many emails unanswered. STAY AWAY

Please save yourself. I didn't look on rate my professor before I took this class. That was a mistake, it is all true. I don't care about those "Easy A" classes, but this is absolutely the opposite. He just announced the final to be 100 questions in 60 minutes, with what the homework is like, I don't know how that will even be possible.

Worst professor ever. Gives you homework you will need to spend hours trying to solve. Too lazy to make a canvas page. Just honestly the worst professor ever. It will be hard after this professor to say that you still want to be an astrophysicist. If you want your GPA to tank take this class.

This man is horrible. I wish I dropped this class when I had the chance. He barely gives any feedback, which you have to explicitly request. Sometimes it will just be "not really..." or "no..." with no additional help. This class was way too difficult to be classified as a level 1200 class. Nevermind the 7 page SINGLE spaced paper for a final...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures make little to no sense and make the hw difficult. Feedback is provided upon request, but is minimal and provides little help. Sometimes will just say "no" with no other info to help learning. Too many tears shed over an intro class that has nothing to do with my career path. Only provided extra credit once course evals came out

This class is online so it may be different in that regard, but Yan is a good instructor who presents the material in a way that is easy to understand. The class does mainly consist of listening to lectures and doing homework (which may not be the most engaging). But he is willing to discuss outside of class if you have questions/want feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He only reads off PowerPoints and doesn't have a rubric for anything. He never gives feedback and grades harshly. The class is only a 1000 level class yet I have to put in more work in this class than my 3000 level classes. I would never recommend taking any class he teaches.

I don't want to touch astronomy with a ten-foot pole. This class drains the life out of me every time I even think about it. The homework is worth a lot and there is no clear rubric for anything. The lectures are boring and he just reads off the slides. I have no idea how to improve my homework scores because he never gives feedback. Stay away!

This class made me hate astronomy. His lectures are not specific and confusing, and he doesn't actually explain anything he just reads over the slides. I have taken three notebooks worth of notes and I am not even done with the class yet. I haven't learned anything and I never want to take an astronomy class again because of him.
Strongly advise against taking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I need to do my part... His teaching style is dull. He's never prepared for lectures. Goes through slides willy-nilly so that it's impossible to take notes. Exams cover literally every possible thing that can be covered in the field of astronomy or physics and they're 40% of your grade.  As Ackbar would say, "It's a trap!"
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was the worst teacher I've ever had. Never take a class from him. Everyone in the class did poorly on the midterm and he still refuses to give study guides, curve, or round up grades. I emailed him and he never replied to me. He is rude to students. He asked the same question twice on the midterm ON PURPOSE so you get double points wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Quizzes are almost impossible to prepare for, tests are difficult. Homework long and not helpful.

The worst professor I've had to date. Yan flies through the slides at an ungodly pace. His exams are incredibly hard, and there are pop quizzes. He won't tell you about anything coming up, so watch the syllabus. I have written a notebook's worth of notes and I don't think I've learned anything. The guy is in his own world. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You have to listen very hard to understand what he is saying. He spends no longer than 15 seconds on each slide, and it isn't even worth your time to try taking notes. Everything you learn will be from using Quizlet on homework and quizzes. He doesn't cater to students' concerns with technological difficulties & you get 30 seconds per quiz question
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Yan lectures on one whole chapter per day and goes very fast. Our first test was on 14 chapters of the book (literally half of the book) and we didn't get a study guide, even though many student asked for one. The homework is all online, very long and difficult to do, and can't learn much from it. He says the class average on tests is 60%.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The most tedious professor I have ever had- takes attendance way too seriously, does way too much. Lectures are pointless and hard to sit through. I'm exploring the PRST major and he has made me not want to be a PRST major. Talks way too much about himself, literally cannot stand him as a professor but the class is easy.
This guy is an absolute dawg. Cares about what he's teaching and has a lot of background in the field. Highly recommend this guy if you're intrested in the degree!

The work he assigns you is the most tedious, pointless, time consuming things you will ever do in your life. He makes you do journals about YOUR experience at work, and then will take points off for whatever reason he thinks as if he was at the job site. Just get out if it while you can.

Easy class but his work is very outdated would post post links that were old and had templates of professionals in the field that no longer worked for the company he had posted, overall easy class but his work is old and he seems to be very outdated with his knowledge of the industry.
He was very light on grading and pretty funny and easy going. Topics in this class were very simple with minimal homework. I hope to take one of his classes again throughout college.

A very easy class with points for showing up! Professor Young was very passionate, but personally lecture could get boring when it was all stuff that's kind of obvious. If you attend each lecture, you don't necessarily need to read the textbook closely.

His class was very easy and ended with an open note final. It is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory, and doesn't factor into GPA. His lectures do heavily revolve around using iClicker, which he puts a location lock on so you do need to attend class. He was very nice, and was open to answering questions regarding your major after class.

He assigns like 30 homeworks throughout the semester, with each one taking at least an hour to complete. Make sure you do all of the assignments—even if it seems optional—because they're not, & if you don't do them your grade will drop significantly. He also will never respond to your emails so don't even bother trying to contact him about issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super friendly with great vibes and happy to see his students.

Passionate about what he lectures but as a non-business major the content is extremely boring but easy. The homework is awful and dreadful (2-3) hours each, it consist of 100-200 questions that you must get correct to move on -- which just incentives you to chatgpt the entire assignment because if you make a mistake your progress pauses.

He is AMAZING! I love showing up to class and always get a good smile from the lectures. Grading isn't bad the homework is a little heavy but if you know what you are doing it goes by pretty fast, and its all online you get to retake the questions unlimited times until you get it right. I would attend lectures whether its mandatory or not!!

Classes can feel quite long, however Professor Zumwalt always tries to make lectures interesting and interactive. He encourages questions and explains them in a way that doesn't make you feel stupid. The assignments can be very long but are easy. On tests you're allowed to use notes, one sheet front and back. Overall informative class.

Lectured very fast and gave a lot of homework. On average HW would take me roughly an hour to an hour and a half to complete. On another note, the exams were very easy. The first one was online and open notes, and the final was only over the second part of the semester and we were allowed one sheet of paper, front and back.
He was super fun to have and explained everything very well! Missing a day wasnt a big deal, but he does do in class assignments. He taught me a lot about managing my personal finances

Zumwalt is a great professor, and i think he does well teaching this course. There were four exams, and two essays as well, but they weren't difficult. The good this about his course is the way he structured the due dates with his assignments, which was pretty helpful.
He was very helpful and explained concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, very knowledgeable of the basics of financial planning, overall, this course was amazing to take!

I did not love Dr. Zia's teaching style due to the lack of clear example problems that often left me struggling on my homework for hours because I did not understand the problem. However, she is very generous with extra credit and participation grades and seems like she wants you to succeed. Overall wouldn't take her again but a nice person.
Judgmental and mean spirited. Violated ferpa. Asked students to come to office hours for no apparent reason.
I genuinely could not believe how every question I'd ask her she would take personally like I offended her honor. I'm appalled by her ego
He is such a nice and passionate professor! Make sure you go to lectures because they are a big part of grade, but if you go to class it is such an interesting class and an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best prof i've had at Mizzou. He's very educated and enthusiastic about his lectures, and really cares about his students. I was sick for about a week and messed up one of my reading quizzes and he was very open to fixing it. The course is not hard, it is all covered in lectures and the reading quizzes are very straightforward
a pretty cool class, interacts with class sometimes during lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zambito is a fantastic professor. The  lectures are informative and engaging. You can tell that he is a very cool and knowledgeable about his craft and has dedicated plenty of time to perfecting it. I am so glad that he is at the University and I hope that he stays forever.

Lectures aren't mandatory but very engaging. The content is fun and really interesting. Quickly turned into one of my favorite classes. Online tests and weekly quizzes are based on lectures and part of the readings but are very fair.

Very fun to listen to! Engages students in lectures in a fun way (but not required to participate). Grade is based on weekly quizzes and exams every three weeks, all of which are online and open note/open book.

Class was easy, but be warned if you're taking the online version of this class. The class switches between two professors as the course goes on, and only one knows how to properly set up zoom. Aka, you will be able to read the lecture slides for one half of the class, and the other half the lecture is unreadable and completely useless.

Enjoyed Dr. Zambito. He was energetic and made this class enjoyable. Quizzes are almost entirely from the lectures, but reading quizzes are a bit tedious. Overall, I would certainly recommend Dr. Zambito for anyone who wants a chill elective/humanities credit.

He is honestly a great professor, I wish he taught more classes so I could take them. He LOVES to give partial credit on quizzes and exams and also offers a large amount of extra credit. You can tell he loves to teach and is passionate about his job. Attendance is not required but is helpful and he gets frustrated when no one shows up for class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit and an easy grader. Every exam and quiz had bonus questions. Exams, including the final, are NOT cumulative. Talk to Dr. Balboula if you're having issues and he'll actually help you. He is very quiet so try to sit close to the front, but otherwise very straight to the point and doesn't waste time with small details.

Very slow lectures which get a bit redundant if anyone asks him to repeat information more than once, but he really seems to care about everyone doing well and is by far the most lenient grader grader in AnSci I have ever heard of. Labs are interesting, and assignments and exams are super easy and very clear what you should study if you go to class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Balboula is one of the best AnSci professors I've had, especially in upper level courses. He simplifies concepts and repeats complex topics if we ask. He genuinely wants his students to learn and succeed in his class. The written assignments are only based on participation. What's on the quizzes is on the exam, and no trick questions!

Dr. Balboula is an amazing professor who you can tell really loves what he does. It was really refreshing to take his course and be reminded that learning can be fun. I came into the course with no care for reproduction and came out really considering it as a potential career choice. Take this course if you can!

Amazing professor. His tests were all written, which was great because if you hit key points even if you didn't know everything you'd get decent grades in the course. Made it really easy to learn and would print his slides for everyone before class. The labs were always interesting and he cared most about understanding rather than memorization

Dr. Balboua is the most amazing and caring professor I have experienced at Mizzou! He really does care about his students and just wants you to understand. If you are struggling on a quiz ask him about the question and he will help you out a lot! He offers 2 extra credit writing assignments that will bump your grade up a lot! Make sure you study!

Most outstanding professor you'll likely ever have! Not only an amazing teacher but an amazing person as a whole.  He will do whatever he can to help you out and is very sincere.  Absolutely take his class.

Ahmed is the best professor I've ever had. When Ahmed says don't worry about grades, believe him. I've taken two classes with him and both times I got the grade which I felt like i deserved, and even if the points didn't add up. Ahmed's classes are a joy to attend. I'd suggest going to office hours and getting to know him, he's a truly a nice guy.
Passionate about teaching and will helps anybody that asks.

Ahmed is a very enthusiastic professor, which is important since this class is usually only offered at 8am. He does a great job of explaining everything and all assignments and exams are very straightforward. The only drawbacks are the class times, mandatory attendance, and two to three homework assignments a week. It's a big time commitment.

BEST professor I have ever had. I wish there was another course he taught because I would take any class with him as a professor in a heartbeat. Could care less about just testing you and grading you. He make sure that you understand the material. Made a 8:00 am class my favorite class that I would not have ever missed even if it was non mandatory.

Dr. Abu El-Ela is an amazing professor. He is taking care of all of his students. Honestly, he is very fair with everyone. His main concern is understanding the topic, critically think about all aspects as engineers, and finally, students success.  He is great and so far he is the best professor I ever had at MU.
Ahmed is a great teacher and pours his heart and soul into it. Unfortunately, he's an incredibly sexist man. I felt bad for the girls in our class because they were treated so differently
I loved this class because he cared about the subject and has a passion for everything.

I thought that 8:00 am in the morning will be an awful class but because of him, I was always waiting to go to the class. Learned a lot of lessons for the class and for being a successful Engineer. I really appreciate what he did to me. Great Professor.
Make sure every student understands material being taught, will go above and beyond with help opportunities. Challenges the student to become better
This professor is great in teaching concepts and he ensures students understanding. Always willing to help and reexplain points different ways to make them understandable.
Great teacher.  The lectures are at 8:00 AM, but going to them will really make this class a breeze.  He teaches the subject very well and the in class examples are usually exactly like the homework.
He is very willing to help and very enthusiastic about what he is teaching.
No doubt! Great teacher.

The class as a whole wasn't too bad. There was a semester long project, which was actually very fun towards the end. Getting there was a pain, but as long as you don't procrastinate (like we did), it really wasn't bad. There was basically homework every class, but it was explained really well the class before, and the teacher is awesome!
Great professor! He explains everything very well and will always make time to help students.

Ahmed is undoubtedly the best professor I've had and definitely one of the best teachers I've ever had. His expectations for his students are clear and completely reasonable. He is always there for help and wants everyone to succeed. I would take another one of his classes in a heartbeat.
Amazing teacher. Comes to class eager to teach and has a great understanding of the subject matter. Motivates you to work harder and is willing to take his time to make sure you succeed.

Really good teacher,  he wants you to do well and the class is very fair.  He is willing to help at all times and always answers his emails with any questions quickly. Class is interesting and he knows all of his students.

Great Teacher. He is always taking care of his students and their understanding. Ask questions. He knows every student in his class and always remember their questions and the points they did not get and try to point them out every time to make sure they got it.
The class is very tough, but he is an overall great and helpful professor.

Ahmed is a great teacher and truly does want to see the students learn the material. I feel he was very clear on the material and that the tests were fair. Also there is a big group project over the semester with which my group had overlooked some important details and Ahmed was nice enough to give us a small extension to complete it properly.

He is extremely enthusiastic about teaching and truly wants to see each of his students do their very best and succeed. He is very helpful outside of class and students should never hesitate to ask him for help. Without a doubt one of the best professors I have ever had, I truly hope to have the chance to take more classes from him in the future!
He is young and really enthusiastic about teaching. Some of the content is not easy but Ahmed is always available and willing to help you. Overall, one of the better teachers I've had.

Ahmed is a great professor. He may be strict during class it is for your own good. He really cares about his students and is always there to help you. Use his office hours whenever you need it and don't be scared to ask questions.

Ahmed is one of the most well-prepared instructors I've ever had. You will need to go to every class but he will help you understand the material very well. He truly wants you to do well, and will reward hard work.

Ahmed is probably one of the best professors I've had so far. The material could be challenging at times but he took no short cuts and was genuinely determined to make sure the class understood each concept. Would love to have him again

Ahmed would always make time for students outside of class. Very quick with email replies. He gave students every chance to be successful, those who were not chose that path on their own. Ahmed's passion for not just engineering, but also for education is palpable. This is the quality that makes him special compared to most other university profs.
Ahmed is a great professor. Really gets to know his students. He is always there when help is needed.

I enjoyed having Ahmed as a professor. He genuinely cared about the success of his students and was very easy to get in contact with. If you had a hard time understanding something he would take the time to help you out. The class can be difficult, but with him as a professor you will learn a lot!
Ahmed really made the class exciting! He was very knowledgeable and was able to break down the tough material to where anyone that applied themself could understand.

Very willing to help any student out and very easy to get in touch with. Always responds to emails and requests for help in a timely manner. He is very enthusiastic about the material during lectures and constantly keeps the class involved by asking questions. Furthermore, he is more concerned with the students learning the material than grades.

Excellent teacher-very enthusiastic- excited about teaching- taking care of all of his students- the class is at 8:00 am but he will keep you focus- Exams a little bit long and sometimes tough but his point is how much did you learn. I really enjoyed that class and hope to have him as a teacher for other courses.

EASY EASY EASY class! Did not have to use the book once! Passing with an A! And she makes the topic of Roman  Culture interesting! 1 ten point map quiz and 3 tests make up the grade. No papers! Chance for extra credit with  random attendance quizzes!

Latin is not my favorite subject, and the fact that I actually *enjoyed* it this semester is testament to Dr. A's teaching style; the course was interesting, and most importantly she *explains* the material thoroughly and without confusion. We were able to move through the text at a steady pace without rushing through important topics. A+ class :)
I liked Dr. Acton she is very nice and if you go to class you should pass. I ended up with an A
Honestly, she's a nice woman, but she bores me to death. Relatively easy though and I skip class every so often.
Is very hands off for this class. Also doesn't really try to help students out much.

The first half of lectures was reviewing information we had already learned and reviewed every lecture before, then she would "run out of time" for the information we needed to know for foal watch, so we started in April. She is disrespectful, and sometimes unprofessional, but she did make it very easy to feel comfortable calling her on watch.

she was a terrible person and a terrible professor, she would get angry if you don't know everything about horses straight out of the gate. She uses favoritism and makes your life a living hell if you don't know horses. she has even thrown fresh horse poop on me on purpose because of her not liking me.

I love all my equine classes, but Makayla does make the class intimidating and unfair as she does not respect some students as I was one of them. She is terrible at reading emails and had often misread what I said and turned it around. Does not email back fast which is reasonable but inconvenient. Doesn't try to know her students.

The foal watch shifts and mare checks are long, but they're worth it if you enjoy the content. Mikaela always seems stressed and it makes her unapproachable at times. Respect for your time will go out the window. Grading takes forever. You will not know your grade in this class most of the time because there are too many ungraded items.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although this is a 300 level class, she has no awareness of the fact that a majority students taking that class needs it as an elective. I know the stereotype of being a STEM major having a strenuous workload is annoying, but the time needed to succeed in this class is unreasonable. Would not recommend unless interested or majoring in this subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took her at USCA. Stay clear of her class. She is very unclear of what her expectations are, and gets upset when you do not understand the Few assignments that she gave. If you can take it with someone else DEFINITELY do, and if you can't take it with someone else, take it SOMEWHERE else if you don't want your GPA to be messed up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took her a USC-Aiken and highly regret it. Very unclear in her expectations. Only had 2 exams and 3 assignments, so they count very heavily. Nothing but lectures, but get ready to read and discuss in class. Course focused mainly on international relations rather than US politics. Seems like a fine person but not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was very nice by rounding my B+ up to an A- but I showed up at her office hours and took her advice for my papers. She is a tough grader and does not have clear grading criteria. Tests were very hard and broad. I spent many nights studying more than necessary for this freshman level course. If this class is required for you, stay clear of her!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cletzer may be a QUACK, but he is a pretty good guy overall. Sometimes he is too smart for his own good, so if you need something rexplained or an assignment adjusted, just ask him. He is a rambler and talks fast during lectures, but provides good info. Class is pretty good as long as your assigned small group and TA is not horrible.

You'll easily get an A if you do all of the homework. There are weekly reading journals that cover 15+ pages of scholarly reading. Every class period involves group work. Don't take this class if you're busy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Cletzer is such a fun professor. He really works hard to help every one and is very respectful in terms of feedback. Really awesome guy, 10/10 would take again

Professor Adolph is a good professor. He grades his papers thoroughly and grades are not handed to you.  His style of teaching is very interesting. While giving you a lot of excitement through hip-hop songs and short stories, he also knows how to keep the class professional. I'd recommend you take Professor Adolph's course.

Mr. Adolph always brought a lot of energy to class and kept his lectures interesting, but his grading had extremely high expectations.  He uses Skype which is cool and allowed for help on the go.  I ended with a 79.8 in the class, he lets you re-write your paper if you get a C+ or lower, but he usually gave me an 80% to prevent that.
I really liked Jessie! He kept the class really interesting. He's a hard grader but he gives you a chance to rewrite your paper if it's less than a C. The books he picks are also really interesting.

This class was great! You have a chance to rewrite all of your essays and the topics are very interesting. As a journalism student my research skills greatly improved, thanks to this class. Also he'll like you more if you don't cry during your conference with him.

Awful. The first paper I turned in in this class received the worst grade I had ever gotten on a paper. Essentially, when we discussed it, we figured out that the main reason I got a C was because he disagreed with the point I was making in my thesis. If you would like a good grade in this class, simply write papers entirely on his opinions.
HE IS THE WORST!!
I took Jesse's Hip Hop English class, it was very interesting, the discussions were always good. But he is a difficult grader. You have to put in the effort and attend class.

My favorite class and favorite professor thus far! It focused on hip-hop and was very interesting and fun! Laid back prof who cracks a lot of jokes, gives extra credit, and doesn't give many assignments. As long as you put in effort to the assigned papers, you'll do fine and he helps out a lot if you visit him during office hours! Take this class!!

My absolute favorite class and favorite professor! We focused on hip-hop which made the class really interesting and fun! He is a cool guy, he cracks a lot of jokes, and he is very intelligent! He does not assign a lot of work and, if you put in effort, his class should be relatively painless! He also gives quite a few extra credit opportunities!

I took Jessie's English 1000 hip hop class and absolutely loved it. I learn about a culture and art, which was very inspiring. The trick with Jessie is to take the material seriously and put forth EFFORT. He only comes down hard on the kids who don't try. And he's always willing to help you out.
Class was interesting and fun. Does grade papers hard, but lectures are very interactive. Gives plenty of time to finish assignments. Not as difficult as everyone claims.

Worst teacher I have ever had. He is rude and completley useless when it comes to trying to help you improve your writing. If you have him DROP the class immediately. If you dont you will just be wasting your time and energy for nothing. BY FAR THE WORST TEACHER AT MIZZOU.

WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD!!!  He would recommend going to the writing lab, but going would not improve your grade. I'm a journalism major and had to ask for a B- in the class because I would've had to re-take it with the grade I was going to get based off my papers (a C+). DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. TAKE IT WITH ANY OTHER TEACHER!!!

English 1000 with Jessie was the worst class I've ever taken at Mizzou. I spent countless hours on papers and took them to the writing center several times and never got higher than a B. The worst part about the class was that I feel like my writing did not improve at all. If you are stuck with Jessie, try to take another class.

Grades way too hard on papers. He recommends the Writing-Lab but this does not improve your grade!!! In fact, he marks off for things that the Writing Lab tutors correct. He belittles students in class, often laughing at the papers he reads during revision periods. His corrections on the paper are petty, and he marks off for EVERYTHING! Bad teacher
Very challenging, but makes all writing classes that follow seem petty.

TERRIBLE teacher. None of us had higher than a C+ before midterm... he kept telling us to go to the writing labs in the student success center, so we did. when we fixed our papers with the advice he gave us and the student center gave us, he still didn't give us a better grade (the same grade as first draft)...

Really knows what he's talking about and fosters a productive creative environment. He's also very understanding about life things if you reach out to him about it, and gives great, constructive feedback. His classroom is a very positive learning environment! I have very little bad to say about this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: He's a rather new professor to Mizzou, but I think he will do really well here. His class was engaging and well-structured; he facilitated class discussion very well and gave everyone wonderful writing advice. If I wasn't a senior, I would look to take one of his classes again. Definitely pick him if you get the chance.

He really cares about what he's teaching and you get a lot from lecture time. I loved the way class was structured and I enjoyed all of the readings. There are several books you will need, but each of them are good and useful in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: worst class ever it was super boring and too much pointless She is foreign and hard to understand sometimes.

I am a poli sci major and honestly I regret not dropping this class. Her lectures are very general and random, and test are very specific and difficult. Only have two tests, and a final, and three map quizzes. Very dry lecturer if you love poli sci, sorry but don't take this class. This class just needs some clarity on what she wants you to know.

Good teacher, she knows what she's talking about. Also good at explaining things, but somewhat hard to understand. The tests are hard with lectures being so general while questions are VERY specific. Study guides would be helpful for this class, but she doesn't offer them

Mrutu is nearly impossible to understand. She is quiet and has a heavy accent. In addition, she just goes over the powerpoint in lecture which she sends to you, so attending class is not necessary. She also has trouble understanding questions, but she generally gives good examples.

Her door is always open. If you put forth effort and go to her office hours, you should do pretty well. By going to office hours, she works with you on a more personal level and will help you understand things from all aspects.

She is so nice and willing to help if you go to office hours. She expects you to put in the effort and go to class, but is so willing to help if you actually take the time to know her. Go to her office hours and she is lots of help and a really good person!!

She is so willing to help and really cares about you if you actually take the time to go to her office hours. Its all about getting to know her on a personal level. You actually have to put effort in to going to lecture and coming to her office hours, and not just hope she will take it easy on you. She is so nice and really cares if you give effort

HORRIBLE teacher. I think she learned English a week before teaching and learned chemistry even after that. So hard to understand and literally reads the slides word for word, and then e-mails them to you. Going to class is completely worthless; you just have to teach yourself from the book.

Very hard to understand.  She emails us notes and reads them word for word in the class.  Pointless to attend the class because she can't answer the questions you have anyways.  Strongly recommend taking this class with another teacher.  Tests are fairly hard, but all teachers give the same test.

Do not take this teacher. You won't learn much of anything in class. I learn mostly from the book and videos on the internet. I expect to be paying for quality education, not this. I'm very disappointed.

she didn't really teach us at all. she just took slides from the book and read them in the lecture hall. i am basically learning chemistry half way from the book and half from the internet. avoid her at all cost!!!
Reads everything out of the textbook, does not explain a thing. Worst teacher I have ever had.

do NOT take her. She reads everything word for word from the slides. You can't understand her, and she gives out, absolutely NO materials to help you study for exams. I am very upset with her poor quality of teaching.
Her door is always open which is helpful and is willing to go over any of the material. I don't think she's taught much before this because class seems a little "clunky" (best way I can describe it).

Pretty much useless to go to class. She reads the notes word for word off the slides that she then emails to you. Not to mention not the best english. I can easily stay at home and read the notes better than she can. There is constant stumbling over words and confusion. You really have to teach yourself in this class. People walk out during lecture
She is very hands-off as an editor. It is difficult to go to her if there are issues or if you have questions, I have found that I leave frustrated or still confused.

She's very hands-off with the students she edits for. She never clarified her expectations during editing for RW 2 and would try to cut my stories to half their content. She didn't understand that assigning extra sources would make my story take longer and then tried to cut an entire source after telling me to talk to someone else.

Abbott may seem ditzy, but she really knows but she is talking about and I have lots of respect for her. Her class may have little direction and be difficult, but If you go to her outside of class about how to improve, she is very helpful. At the end of the semester, she even published some of our assignments, which was really generous of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She's passionate and brings valuable firsthand experience in humanitarian aid. Lectures stay engaging, even when content leans dry. Encourages class discussion and welcomes diverse perspectives. Only complaints: essay rubrics were missing, so expectations were far from clear and canvas page was confusing to navigate and lacked a "grades" tab.

This class was very boring and the professor seemed somewhat unqualified and unprepared. She was pretty unprofessional and I would say it was one of the worst classes I've taken so far here. Not really sure how this course was greenlit. I wouldn't recommend it.

Professor Abousalem is amazing. Since she works in humanitarian aid she has lots of experience in the field that relates directly to the class. You can tell she is passionate about her work and getting to know her students. Show up to class, take good notes, ask questions, and no matter your major it will likely be one of your favorite classes.
Great professor! Really cares about his students learning.

Rabbani did a good job teaching this course, but he isnt the most organizing. Lectures move slowly. There were a good number of assignments given, and he gives random top hat quizzes. I did learn a lot in this class and I overall had a positive experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He abuses his academic freedom and deviates from his own syllabus. Very unclear grading criteria. He is very approachable at the beginning of the course, and very difficult to work with during the last month of class. His lectures are slow and unclear. He maybe covers 5 slides in one class. He's a nice person, but a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bing needs to make up his mind. First 3 months of class he degraded everyone for "not studying" for his extremely difficult and specific tests, then saw everyone was barely passing so he's salvaging the class grade by making tests easier and allowing more drops. Not once was there an apology for the disorganization of structure. Do not recommend.

Dr. Zhang has a very hard to understand teaching style. He provides you with many resources and offers lots of help but somehow the material still doesn't make sense. The lectures feel so unorganized, assignments aren't worth any points so the only thing you are graded for is test and lab. I think he really does try his best though.

Degrades his students! Almost impossible to get over a 60 on exams. He uses trick questions and ChatGPT to write them. He will make time to meet with you whenever BUT he spends that time interrupting and going into tangents completely unrelated. Uses a lot of graphics/images instead of words/definitions for exams. Shows emails to class with names.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang does not offer much support; Instead, he usually states that the topic has already been covered in class (They're unrecorded and he frequently doesn't use slides). He responds rudely to emails and has frequently shown student emails to the class. Test questions had many grammatical mistakes, and he refused to answer clarifying questions.
Avoid this guy. He is absolutely toxic. I cannot believe that he is still a professor there.

I graduated with a double major in biology and nutrition and a 3.77 GPA (and 3.92 GPA in grad school). This is by far the hardest class I have ever taken. It is very different from any other course in that he doesn't really test over concepts, but instead seemingly unimportant details. This is one of 2 classes that I ever had to withdraw from.

Sample tests are helpful for exams, but don't rely on them. His grading system is kind of weird. Stay on top of the case studies and active learning because they are on the exams. I don't like this professor, he is kind of rude 
in more personal settings, and his class is hard even with labs to boost your grade.

As a senior, this is the worst professor I have had. Expects you to teach yourself material and does not provide study guides, not technologically capable (the class is primarily online), insults students, does not provide answers, expects extensive memorization, and uses intentionally misleading trick questions. Seems to enjoy confusing students.

I took Dr. Zhangs animal physiology course in the Spring of 2022. I came into his class reading these reviews and being terrified. The course is challenging. My advice is to do his study questions, go to his office hours WITH Questions and you will be fine. Stay on top of weekly quizzes and study material often. I had the class in person. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bing is fairly knowledgeable but has very poor teaching and interpersonal skills. But he will not own up to his faults; instead, he will blame his students for not working hard enough. Do not bother going to his office hours either because he will just belittle you. Strongly recommend taking this class with another teacher for a fair chance.

The worst professor I have ever had. Incredibly degrading, disrespectful, and the worst manners. He told a student they were unteachable in office hours. His teaching is unclear and he expects you to teach yourself 90% of the material. I was excited for this class, but he made me hate it. Mizzou needs to fire him. Would give him a 0 if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang knows alot about biology, but when it comes to teaching he seems to value degrading and berating his students more than helping those that need more assistance. He claims to be here to help the students because they pay for him to do his job, but i guarantee not a single soul would talk to their boss the way Dr. Zhang talks to his student
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Horrible professor and class. Tested on irrelevant topics that are not focus of the class. Furthermore, I personally know several students he has essentially harassed and demoralized. Blames others and finds fault in everyone but himself. Stay far away if you want to maintain sanity and confidence.

Great class if you love random trivia because there is no structure whatsoever to his teaching material and what he puts on the exams. Every exam is a surprise and the questions are vague. If you ask for clarification on the questions, though, he will state "the question is very clear" and not help you beyond that. Extremely rude professor too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor of my life, do not take his class at all costs. The take home tests takes 2 days. The multiple choice are completely random and doesn't go off of what he lectures. TAKE ANOTHER PROFESSOR
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: As a 3.7 science GPA student with my lowest grade a B in biochem4270/7240, getting a C+ in this class really does prove how awful Bing is at teaching. He can't properly evaluate student effort and knowledge of the material. His lectures are unorganized, and he could care less about you. Ask him a question, and he is demeaning. Worst professor at MU
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: All I have to say is what MyZou says for his student evals: 77% "disagree" and 6% "strongly disagree" that he taught effectively. NOT ONE PERSON (0%) agreed or strongly agreed that they would recommend the class based on the instructor's teach style. It's no secret, Bing shouldn't be teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Horrible. Get ready to do 14 page long take-home exams toughly graded only worth 40% of the total exam score, and sometimes he is so generous as to make a take-home quiz and a take-home exam due on the same day! His logic: it's take-home, so you MUST have time. Also teaches nothing, just talks about his research and WILL TEST YOU OVER IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took this class a while ago, when he first taught it, so I'm not sure if things have changed. I wanted to go back and reflect on it since it is the worst class I've probably ever taken at Mizzou. His tests are very random. He grades very tough and is unwilling to give back points that you should have earned. Tests over specifics, not concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Every exam I have took was a curveball. His lectures aren't relevant to exams, you can read the book like I did but still be lost on oddly worded exam questions. His take-home exams are 12 page papers that are over techniques in biology and unfairly graded. Very unreasonable and unavailable during office hours (he was out of town every other week).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang has been one of the best professors I have had at Mizzou. His class is not easy and he will make you work, but there is no reason to get below a C. He is funny and smart and is willing to go out of his way to help students. I would recommend Bing over any other bio teacher! I would take cell bio again for fun if Bing was the professor.

Dr. Bing's a good professor. His test are hard, but he substituents in take home portions which are basically free points if you do them and it counts towards the test. Since the test are hard he does give lots of extra credit. Helps out with curves at the end of the course. Genuinely cares about the students.

Bing is enthusiastic about his lab work and he is more interested in teaching you the newer techniques as opposed to the fundamentals. He changed how he taught this semester, offering a total of 32 bonus points, had 2 take home exams and one open note exam. Do the study questions, just copy his slides. Really easy for me I got an A+
An absolute embarrassment to the University.

This guy is a joke. Mizzou needs to get rid of him, as he truly makes the University look bad. The least sympathetic teacher you will ever experience. When the entire class fails a test, instead of taking responsibility, he will email everyone stating that the entire class isn't trying. Taking this class with Bing is a huge waste of time and money.

I feel really, really bad for anyone taking his Cell Biology class next semester. Along with just about half the class, I was forced to drop his class with a W. I just finished retaking Cell Biology with a different teacher and received an A with ease. Dr. Zhang has by far the lowest grade distribution of all Cell Bio teachers and the worst reviews

I feel really, really bad for anyone taking his Cell Biology class next semester. Along with about just about half the class, I was forced to drop his class with a W. I just finished retaking Cell Biology with a different teacher and received an A with ease. Dr. Zhang has the lowest grade distribution of all Cell Bio teachers and the worst reviews.

This class was really interesting and useful for anyone interested in learning about neurodegenerative diseases (Alzheimer's, ALS). There is a lot of reading, but there are no exams. Dr. Zhang knows what he wants in the presentations and provides great feedback. If you go to class and are prepared for the presentations you will get an A.

Set up like a grad-level course where you read a article for each class and the students present it. No tests, one term paper, and reading articles, so as long as you do the work, you will get an A. I really liked the set up of the class and it was very easy to get to know Dr. Zhang. Now I will get an awesome rec letter.

Bio 4002 - Neurobiology of Disease.  Lots of reading, lots of class presentation, but not a heavy workload outside of class. Much easier than other 4000+ level classes.  Dr. Zhang takes student feedback seriously and changes his teaching style accordingly. Be sure to attend every class. If you do your work, you will get an A.

Probably the only reason there are good ratings for him on here is because he bribes students with extra credit to give him a good rating. Dr. Zhang is very bad about staying on topic during lectures. He often ends up spending most of the time talking about former Nobel Prize winners and how he knows them personally. Tests are unreasonable.

Anyone who has rated him more than 1 star in helpfulness obviously hasn't ever been to his office hours. If you actually go to his office hours, he will become frustrated and will often yell at you for wasting his time. He encourages you to ask questions on exams but if you do ask a question, he won't answer it, stating "the question is very clear"

I just got an A on the first exam with a new professor by putting in half the effort it took for me to get a D on Dr Zhang's first exam. Exams consist of questions concerning small details that he may have briefly mentioned in between bragging about himself in lecture. PowerPoints only have pictures, so they are no help. TAs agree that he is unfair

Not even worthy of 1 star rating. Was cussed out multiple times after going to his office hours for "wasting his time" asking questions. Powerpoints are composed of pictures. Has the lowest grade distribution on record at Mizzou for the class (and that's AFTER more than half the class dropped). Very rude, unhelpful, and AWFUL at teaching. AVOID HIM

Class is tough. The test are over study guide. Do all extra credit, no curve. If you do not understand something, he will discuss it with you. Wants you to succeed but have to put an effort in it. Go to class, pop quizzes and quizzes are often. Plus explains some stuff that is not in the book or powerpoint but on the test.

The tests are really tough. You have to go to class in order to do well on tests since everything on it comes from lecture. I recommend taking good notes and recording the lecture. Study way ahead of time for the tests and quizzes. He does answer questions in office hours, so he is helpful. The class only has three tests so study hard.

You have to teach yourself everything outside of class via the internet. He doesn't teach you much. Just gives you study guides. But unfortunately if you don't write down exactly what he wants on the test you'll fail. He expects you to know what's in his head. Even the TAs complained with us. I didn't like his class.

Professor Bing has an intense interest in what he is teaching. In his own words, "nothing gets me off more than the brain." He loves cell biology and I would honestly recommend him as a professor. If you are Pre-Med, this is the teacher you want.

Professor Zhang  wants you to stay current with hot biology topics, which includes reading research papers, learning new molecular techniques, watching videos, and much more.  He is a very tough grader when it comes to quizzes because he is looking for specific terms and phrases listed in the answer.  This class is not easy, but  the help is there.

He was an absolutely horrible teacher. unfortunately he was new to our school so i was not warned. All he does is talk about how amazing he is and all the awards he has accomplished, but can't can't seem to teach his students anything related to the class. His tests are ridiculous and you have to teach everything to yourself.... aka read the book!

People who take this course... LISTEN TO WHAT HE HAS TO SAY AND DO IT!!!!!! If he says do the practice questions, do them because they help so much. Just do what you're suppose to do and you will be fine.

Professor that is really interested in teaching and tries to stimulate your learning. Be prepared to take lots of notes! His slides are put together in a matter that doesn't explain too much and he does not use tegrity. His tests and quizzes are on the smallest facts that he only explains quickly. He does give ample extra credit opportunities tho

Nice guy but get ready to work. His lectures are extremely dull and are unorganized, making it hard to follow. To make the problem worse, there are no video recordings to go back to and take notes.  It makes TestsQuizzes even more difficult. I would definitely recommend getting another professor for Cell Bio.

He taught some interesting extra subjects that can grab your attention, however this extra material usually dealing with diseases can be pretty advanced and hard to understand and you will be tested on it. The class averages were not so great for almost all exams and quizzes. Anice guy who wants students to develop. Into application over big pictur

This dude is awesome! definitely better than most bio professors at MU. Show up to class and take notes on things he says not the slides. you can look up the slides later. Do as many extra credit assignments as possible and you will get an A.
Hard to understand. Unsure on criteria for test and quizzes a lot. Doesn't redll make topic interesting.

Pros: He's funny and knowledgeable  Cons: Tests and quizzes are tough and the material you are tested on is somewhat unpredictable. Consistently low (by low I mean F to D range) test and quiz score averages do not make him reconsider his teaching style, but rather he'd put blame on students for not trying. Persistently lusts over nobel prizes.

This was by far the most stressful class I have taken at MU. I like Bing as a person but those tests and quizzes, WOW. They had ridiculous questions on them that were only geared towards one specific topic in GREAT detail vs. the study questions he gave us as a guide. Waste of time to study because the test will look like a foreign language.

Dr. Zhang is one of the nicest most interesting professors I've ever had. Don't let the angry posts on here dissuade you from taking his class. Although you will have to study hard and keep up with the class, it is well worth it. I have learned more from this class than any other I've taken.

The class to take if you're interested in research. There is extra reading, he ties everything learned in class back to research topics and in the last lectures, combines topics learnt throughout the semester. Tests and exams are HARD!!  Do the study questions he gives you,he mostly tests on that. Definitely recommended, teaches you how to think

You can tell he loves teaching but was the toughest professor i've ever taken. Extra assignements, hell lotta extra material (half the stuff for exam 2 wasn't even in the book). Extra work but teaches you how to assimilate info.  Advice: DO THE DAMN STUDY QUESTIONS!!! He likes to test more from them than the book.  Verdict: Definitely worth it!

Go to class. Learn the definitions and memorizeunderstand pretty much all of the information that he talks about in class. Dr. Zhang challenges his students to do higher-level thinking, so if you are unfamiliar with research topicsideas go to his office hours. He is very friendly, and more than willing to help you LEARN. This is college.

Ive never been a complainer about teachers and usually support them when others  put them down. Not this time. He is by far the worst teacher I have had in my academic career and everyone I have talked to agrees. His lecutures are pictures, doesnt go over them and then asks test questions about stuff we never talked about on tests. Dont take him.

His lectures are a little confusing, he is particularly interested in Nobel Prize winners, If i were you I would definitely get the book because sometimes the lectures can be hard to follow. Make sure you PAY CLOSE ATTENTION. Many of his quizzes come from things that he said in class, so if you don't go to class chances are you won't do well at all
The worst thing about this class that the quizzes are very broad and they only have one question.

I have never taken a class where I was more confused on what was going on. He is horrible at explaining anything. All I can say is thank God for having a decent TA. If I didn't I would have failed this class miserably. If you can take this class from another teacher do it you won't regret it.

His lectures are hard to follow, he gets off topic very easily, and is very unclear of what he wants you to take away. He is a very nitty gritty professor where he tests on minescule details instead of major concepts. The quizes and tests were absolutley ridiculous. He expects you to do ten times more work than other classes. Never felt so defeated

This class was the hardest class I've ever taken. He is the toughest grader that looks for the exact specific answer that he wants or else you get no credit at all. He just cares about getting a Nobel prize and ties it into his confusing lectures. If you wanna depress yourself then go ahead and take it otherwise AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

This was the first time I've taken a class where I have felt like no matter what I do I can't succeed. You can't tell what you're supposed to be learning Because he goes off track so often. His test are hard as well as his quizzes.

He was rude I emailed him and asked a question in his face about assignments because somethings wasn't clear and he was rude told me it was clearly stated and I just felt like if I'm asking a question then apparently it's not too clear to me. Also it's hard to follow his lectures and you just need to go in and study study study everything

This is the worst class I've ever taken. I felt like the entire semester I was unprepared for everything.   Instead of trying to understand where the ENTIRE CLASS was going wrong , he chose to believe that we were all incompetent and put in no effort.  Most discouraged I've ever felt in my life.

Do take the time to go through the lectures and make sense of them. Do the study questions and make sure you understand them fully. Don't underestimate the quizzes as they will stump you if you haven't prepared before hand. Come to class because sometimes the quizzes will be over something that he stated in class but not in the notes.

I enjoy a course where I'm motivated to perform well out of respect for the professor and his passion for learning. The only course I've taken at MU like this was Keller's Chem 3 H. Only take this course if you know how to study, but I think that goes without saying for Bio class? Standard difficulty for class at MU. Do u even lift? welcome to RL!

Dr. Zhang is a nice professor, and if you put the time in to learn the material you will do well in his class. On the other hand, if you are just looking to get an easy A this is not the class to take. Dr. Zhang is very passionate about the material he teaches about, and expects his students to understand the material well.

Extremely hard class, definitely not one to be taken lightly. Takes course very seriously & runs it on more of a graduate level than an introductory cell bio course. Tests are brutal and detail specific. Quizzes are also hard. However open-note pop quizzes and bonus points are offered as a saving grace for easy points. No curve.

You have to pay really close attention in lecture to get the test information.  He treats it more like a research topics in cell biology class instead of an introductory cell biology class.  I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you don't have to take it.  It's not an easy class.  He isn't very clear on what information will be on the tests.
The exams and quizes were difficult and graded very tough.

Dr. Zhang is honestly the best professor I've had since I been in college. Even though  its a little difficult to understand him, he still finds a way to explain the content very well. If it wasn't for time and money. I would enroll in all of his classes.

He provides Powerpoints in advance, but he gets off topic, so you cannot understand there are also less words and more pictures, so it is hard to follow along during the lecture. His exams are tough as the questions are nitty gritty and challenging. His lectures go over the littlest details, but you're tested on the major concepts in detail.

You definitely have to work hard in this class. Lecture is essential to doing well in this class. He has PowerPoint notes but will sometimes ask questions on the tests that were only discussed in lecture. Also, he has some pop quizzes, but you are able to use your notes on them. Most examquiz questions are from his study guide questions though.

Ok, here we go.  Dr. Zhang tests over nitty-gritty details that he either covers briefly and verbally in class or does not cover at all. He does not test over concepts, but would rather have his students memorize definitions. I have taken 4000 level biology courses and passes with ease, but this is by far the hardest course I've had.

Does not emphasize the material that is talked about in the booksyllabus and the material that will be covered in the exams. Instead spends class discussing "important" topics that you will most likely not be tested on and talks about Nobel Prizes in almost every class. I'm very disappointed with this professor.

Never felt so discouraged and hopeless before. I love to study and love the subject of Cell Biology, but no matter how many hours you study, you will not be even close to prepared for his obscure quiz and test questions. He is hard to understand and his expectations for what is important to learn are unclear. Avoid if at all possible.

You go into this class expecting an awesome semester. Zhang is funny and tries to make his class interesting with stories, but that's the downfall. The majority of lectures he goes off on tangents and doesn't say what we need to know. Tests are difficult and test you over the littlest details possible. TAprofessor communication is non-existent.

To pass: Attend all lectures, he asks questions ONLY verbalized  Fill out his study guides COMPLETELY, they cover 90% test. Other 10% is lecture  To be safe, write out EVERY bio process in a map and memorize major parts in order, a cellbio duh  You do not need a book, wikipedia! E.C. is work, needed for A Plight lvl high if u do not study.

Great guy who really wants students to succeed. I don't know if this is his first time teaching a larger more basic level, but his style doesn't totally work. Uses specific examples without explaining the broader concepts which makes it hard to get much out of them. Willing to help but high expectations. Nice guy and hopeful he'll adjust soon!

Great guy who truly wants his students to succeed. However, he's very vague about what information from lecture is most important. This makes studying for exams kind of a nightmare because the course covers so much information and his questions require thorough comprehension of specific topics. No multiple choice. Tough class. Don't underestimate.

I am a senior engineering student and Dr. Zhang's class has given me more of a headache than any of my other classes. I signed up for cell biology with the expectation that I would be learning about how cells work. I've instead learned nothing but specific, irrelevant facts about diseases and listened to countless stories about his famous friends.

While Dr. Zhang is an extremely good guy and wants to make your tuition dollars worth his class, he falls short of his goals. The biggest nuisance is his tendency to ask for very specific details on his testsquizzes that were barely mentioned. If you think you'll be fine knowing the main concepts of his lectures like in other classes, you're wrong

He's a really great guy, and really easy to listen to. The problem is that his lectures just kind of wander about, and when test time comes, he wants you to be very, very specific. He'll tell you to learn 10 different drugs, 10 different enzymes, and 10 different experiments. On the test he'll ask what Nobel prize winner used what drug in what year

This is the hardest class I have taken at Mizzou and I have taken many advanced 3000 and 4000 level courses. The things he tests on are incredibly specific so if you think you'll do fine by just understanding the main ideas, think again. He does not stay on topic during lectures and it is a complete guessing game sometimes to understand him. Beware

What's difficult about this class is that he expects test answers to be very specific while the questions could be vague (especially fill in the blank).  He has an accent but it's not crazy bad and i think if you put a lot of work towards it, your grade won't suffer too terribly.

-Large number of points for each question. You don't know a single answer, you're screwed! -Exam questions VERY vaguely written. Questions do not ask for specific answer. Yet, he wants you to write a 1 sentence answer when the question is not clear. -All over in place in lectures. Irregularly shifts from point to point. Don't know what to write.

Dr. Zhang is a great professor and really wants his students to succeed. If your the kind of person who doesn't go to class, you will probably fail if you take this class. I would definitely recommend him if you are interested in research.

I definitely recommend getting the book. His lectures are hard to follow and just relying on the lecture slides won't help. His slides are mostly pictures and you sometimes have to play a guessing game of what scientific term he just said. It's difficult to expect what you will be tested over. He gives plenty of extra credit and you'll need it.

Although many people complained about Prof. Zhang for many reasons, I disagree with most of them. Yes, his class was hard; but hard only if you are used to having everything perfectly outlined for you. We are in college, which is supposed to prepare us for real jobs, where we will be given guidelines and expected to figure out things by ourselves.
