I recommend taking the class with another professor. Seems like a nice guy with a sense of humor, but teaching is not his forte. Has great knowledge of the material, but explains it poorly. Everything I learned was from the book and the Internet. Studying is a guessing game. Random questions appear frequently. Extremely harsh grader. Good luck!!

The tests have a lot to do with small details and not so much the big picture. However he really does want you to succeed and does his best to help you out. Throughout the semester there were numerous extra credit opportunities. That being said you really have to study hard, it is not going to be an easy A but it is definitely possible.

Learning anything in this class is a joke. Awful english. Can't stay on topic when teaching. Impossible tests. Extremely rude, sending out degrading emails to students, tells us we're stupid. Did all of the bonus, still didn't help. Thinks he's teaching us important things for the MCAT, but no help. This class makes me want to do bad things. AVOID!

Dr. Zhang cannot stay on topic during lectures, and will often spend entire class periods talking about Nobel Prize Winners in other topics like Chemistry and Physics. He says you don't need a textbook, but YOU DO because he does a poor job at teaching. EXAMS ARE TOUGH - over the smallest details. Do not come into this class expecting to do well.

Taken 3000 and 4000 level science classes with top grades, so not unprepared. Lecture slides are sparse and lectures unorganized and hard to follow, but expected to know details mentioned once. Hard to study for but not undoable if willing to work. Very hard to know what info is expected to know. Quizzes ask one detailed question for lots of points

He changes exam questions during the exam, does not accept any criticism. His grading is hard and inconsistent he will say we do not need to know something and then test on that in very specific detail, the list of complaints just goes on. Over half of my class dropped and the rest did not preform well due to his methods.
Very informed and knowledgeable, but sometimes hard to follow.

Awful lectures.  Ridiculous grading system--when people did poorly he sent an email saying "we weren't working hard enough." I am a junior used to challenging courses, but his lectures are so off-topic and his tests so random it is impossible to succeed.  Also as a pre-med this did NOT prepare me for my MCAT, so even more a waste of time.  AVOID.

Can't stay on topic through a lecture to save his life. Extremely tough grader. Even if you PROVE to him that you are right, he won't listen. Tests cover small details instead of major concepts. I went to his office to talk to him after I failed his first test, but he told me to get out because I was wasting his time (not including the curse words)

Confusing. Lots of weird projects and papers. Really chill and informal though, which is nice, you don't have to worry about being professional and on edge the whole time. But like, you gotta read a lot and do lots of things. Participation is important.
Abrahamson isn't a bad teacher. The course was really quite easy for a college level class. Pretty informal and she grades really lightly.
She's a great teacher! Attendance does matter. Papers aren't too long and she grades well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Don't be quick to judge; he's a great teacher (and guy) and is very personable once you get to know him. His classes are very relaxed, but not boring. As long as you pay attention and do your work, while also doing a little bit of studying, you should do fine in his class. He also grades fairly, often giving grading criteria ahead of time.

He is an exceptional teacher who provides insightful guidance and consistently exceeds his teaching goals. He teaches far more than French, offering valuable life lessons that extend beyond the classroom. I believe he is often unfairly overlooked. I would gladly take his class again and highly recommend him.

Amazing professor, he is an extremely personable guy and he is clearly very passionate about the class that he teaches. I learn something new every day and I'm so thankful that he was the one to teach me French. 11/10

He is a great teacher who cares about his students. He may seem a little cold at first, but later on, he opens up and is a cool guy. He gives homework but gives you multiple days to do it. Not many tests, but he grades homework accurately and precisely. Good luck, he is amazing yet tough.
Great teacher.  Very willing to help if needed.

Great teacher. Had his outlines clear and what he taught was right on. Other than the syllabus he had a lot of other information that wasn't in the book which I thought was rather interesting. Overall I enjoyed his teaching and he was a nice guy. I learned a lot from him because all of those verbs and tenses are hard to keep up with and he did well

He was an awesome teacher and despite what others say he really DID CARE. He was a GREAT teacher. I struggled big time in the class and what he taught was easy to get I just had to go over it more and more to get it. Overall I enjoyed him. He is very smart and knows A LOT. GET TO KNOW HIM.. he is a nice guy. People rag on him because they judge.

I did not have any problems with him, because I know french pretty well already.  However, he is a cold person who makes it quite obvious that he only cares about himself and grades pretty strictly.  Avoid at all costs!!!
He could be abrasive and pretty tough, but the freedom he had with the course he used to do more fun learning activities and he was always helpful if you visited during office hours.

Koehnemann is difficult but I learned more in his class than in French 1 and 2 combined. He speaks mostly in French during his lectures but is extremely easy to understand. I had a hard time during this class but if you go to his office hours, he's very eager to help. If you want something easy though, take Wetzel.

Super boring, and my pronunciation/language skills definitely got worse during his class.  However, if you are only taking this class for the credit, and you have some skill in french, it's super easy, and he cancels class on occasion.

Very easy to ask questions to. Encourages his students to come to office hours. Cares about students actually learning the material and doesn't like to move on until everyone understands a concept. Grades fairly. I think he is a great french professor. better than the woman i had last semester that's for sure!!
worthless. horrible teacher, he definitely plays favorites.
I had him for a tutor, VERY helpful, got an  A in my french class. however, when i had him for a teacher, he was terrible. his class is ridiculously boring and he knows it.
difficult to approach, creepy
No Comments
No Comments

I think that Mr. Koehnemann is a wonderful teacher.  He possesseth a superior knowledge of the French language and culture, and that showeth through in class when he teacheth said topics.  I learned a lot and really enjoyed htis class.
Ron is lovely. He's a real journalist and gives amazing feedback. He cares so much about his students and will support you in any way he can.
He goes on a lot of tangents about his experience in the field, but is very interesting to hear from. The class dynamic is very relaxed.

The class is interesting, but engaging most of the time. He usually ignores what the class period is planned to be about and what the assignment is in Canvas and talks about whatever he wants for at least the first 30 minutes, which is a little odd but fun. Prof. Stodghill is a very nice man and cares about making students good at what they do.
Awful...Terrible...Beware....NO

Wasn't responsive to emails. There are assignments from August not graded and it is the last week of the semester (December). When assignments were graded months later feedback was given that was no longer helpful but I was unable to get any points back because it had already been so long.

I would shy away from any class that this man teaches. The entire semester, he was ill prepared for class. He only gave 1 grade the entire semester until the final. Then he gave random grades at the end of the semester. He did not notify students of the grades they received on their final. He did not notify students that final grades had posted.

Professor Sullivan is one of my favorite professors. He is incredibly nice and he genuinely cares about your well-being. He talks about his life a lot which is really nice because he feels more like a genuine human being rather than just a professor. He doesn't check homework for accuracy just asks that you do it. Pay attention to Truth Tables.
Professor Sullivan is great and was my favorite professor. He makes the class interesting and easy to understand. If you have to take a Philosophy class definitely take it with Aaron.

He is the funniest professor ever. He doesnt mind in you skip class. There homework and quizzes but you cant fail the quiz and he doesnt check homework. He is absolutely hilarious and nice. Not difficult at all and the work was easy to understand.

best intro philosophy prof anyone could ask for, is very attentive to student's needs if something comes up and tries to explain concepts as best he can. Tests are straightforward and exactly what was taught in class

Best ethics class ever! Super fun, not stressful, relevant, and Sullivan is super nice! Only 3 tests and a few pop quizzes he grades generously. Just read the assignment or watch black mirror and discuss!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: dope philosophy teacher that cares about his students and their knowledge about philosophy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Sullivan is the absolute best. Love his class. He is very caring and gives extensions when you need them. While there isn't really a penalty for missing class, I highly recommend you go as it helps on the tests (which are entirely multiple choice). The lectures are also really interesting. Half the homework is watching Black Mirror.

Prof Sullivan's class was always interesting. He always expanded on questions and didn't make anyone feel bad about asking too many. He was respectful of different perspectives. He had a few pop quizzes to incentives us to come to class, but if you missed a class/ quiz he would let you retake it if you asked. Tests were online which was nice.

PLEASE TAKE THIS MANS CLASS. You will love going to class, seriously. This course alone is amazing and worth it but Sullivan MAKES this class. He is one of the best professors I have ever had. This man deserves a fat raise for the way he teaches. He loves teaching and it shows. You will not regret taking him

Dr. Sullivan is an awesome professor. His classes are very straightforward: do the readings, come to class, and he breaks down the material for you. He understands what it is like to be an undergraduate student, and understands his course may not be the top priority for some people. Take Aaron's class!!

This is the class you want to attend if you're in the MU IT program or any degree! Absolutely fun to attend and he has a deep understanding in how life is tough as a college student. Very informational and passionate in cyber sec and loves to help you out when possible.

Loved this class! Professor Scantlin has a huge passion for infosec and his passion shows throughout the course and makes the course that much more enjoyable. Very understanding of his students and also is very approachable and helpful. Brian his TA is incredible as well and was available almost 24/7 for help. Highly recommend this course!
He was good for Cyber Sec. I enjoyed his current events portion of the lectures. Kind of a slow class if you already have some experience in cyber sec.
I took him first semester freshman year, four years and a new school later he is the most memorable professor I've ever had. No filter what so ever, but very refreshing. Not for the overly sensitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Halvor was a culture shock coming straight from high school. He is the craziest teacher, maybe person I have come across. He has A LOT of stories and isn't afraid to tell them, no filter. He's genius and hilarious. He talks like he belongs on the Office. Noooo filter lol. Great teacher though, class was always fun and he helped me improve!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is insane and rude. He is also the most inappropriate person I've come across. He may know what he's talking about, but I don't know for sure because I dropped. Don't take his class. He is unpredictable and mean. He says his goal is to make you cry. I pay a lot of money to go to class, and I don't ever want a teacher like him.

Halvor is one of the craziest teachers I have ever had. All of the stories he tells you are unbelievable but make class worth it to listen to. I don't think any of his classes are structured the same but read the assignments and definitely participate in class so he knows who you are (but he will never call you by your real name). Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor and his notes are easy to follow and organized. He also recognized me as his student in the engineering building one time even though I never went to office hours

He gets mad if he is asked about his logic during example problems. Essentially, prepare to watch him do only example problems that aren't near as challenging as the exams, while rarely explaining his logic during the example problems. Only one person out of 200 in the class got full points on a problem (25% of exam pts) and he blamed the class.
His lectures were very good and if you were able to follow those then you'll do fine on exams.

He is a very good professor teaching a pretty difficult class. The way it is set up gives you no excuse not to pass other than a lack of effort. Anyone can get a good grade in this class but you have to work for it for sure. The second test was definitely the hardest, so beware. Also, weekly quizzes, so stay on top of things.

Aaron's a good professor. Lectures are just practice problems the entire time. Once a week in class quizzes. Review sessions held outside of class multiple times a week and Aaron was always available for questions or help. Statics isn't the easiest subject but there are so many resources available to succeed in this class if you want to.

Dr. Saucier was good at explaining problems. Held review sessions with himself or the Ta's. Lots of Ta office ours during the week and 2 weekly review sessions with them are held. Ta help session before each exam too. Tells you what will be exactly on the exam. It is just like the homework and in class stuff, just a little harder on the exams.

Saucier was a cool professor who explained concepts well. Posts notes online, posts practice exams, and exams were a little tough but he curved the lowest grade. Only issue is he could come off as a little derogatory when answering questions for students who were really confused. Slightly more homework than usual but still a reasonable amount

Saucier is the goat!! He has great lectures that are really easy to follow. The exams are always straightforward and he and his TA's are very accessible if you need help. Probably the best professor I've had at MU so far, definitely take his class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Probably the best class I've taken at mizzou. Dr. Saucier is very organized and goes through example problems very well in lectures. The class is pretty hard, but if you go to class and pay attention, you will be fine. He is approachable in office hours for the most part, TAs are helpful too.

The class was pretty well structured, but the teacher could sometimes come off as eccentric when explaining things. Like when you messed up on a quiz or ask a question he'll make you feel incompetent.

Probably the most efficient class you'll take at mizzou. There is a lot of content, but if you utilize the resources given to you and practice the problems, your grade will reflect it. You will know what you're expected to do. However you need to be disciplined to wake up for the 8 am classes. especially for those dreadful 8am quizzes.

Very good experience. Gives you all the resources you need to succeed from exampes in class, homework/quizzes that looks like the exam problems, and a full week's worth of office hours from either him or his 6 TA's. Also seems to enjoy teaching and engaging with the students. just make sure you wake up for the 8AM's and avoid Chegg or gpt for hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aaron was an overall really good professor! He was super helpful in office hours. It was very evident that he was passionate about the material and cared about the students actually learning the material. Exams very similar to homework and problems gone over in class. Just do a lot of practice problems and you'll do fine in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Aaron saucier is a king

For an 8 AM course it really isn't the worst. Quizzes every Wednesday at the beginning of class, sometimes with the same or very similar problems you'd see on one of the 4 exams. Grading was fair, he replaced the exam 2 score (class average was low) with the average of exams 2 & 3 plus the final. Good lectures, make sure you do the homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 8 am Wednesday quizzes are brutal! But this is definitely the most efficient class that I have ever taken. The homework is crucial, even if it does seem like a lot.

he's a nice guy and is very concise. he doesn't get off topic and gets through a lot of material during class. there's a lot of hw (3 assignments per week) and quizzes every week but he offers to go through questions during class. he gives a few practice exams and holds review sessions. overall, he shows that he cares abt his students
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Aaron is a great professor. He genuinely wants his students to do well and pass the class. There is homework every lecture, but he and the TAs are always available during office hours or by email. Lectures are sometimes a little slow because he handwrites everything, but this gives you time to take good notes.

Lectures were straight forward and really helped me learn the material. Also, pop quizzes sometimes so I definitely advise going to the lecture .The tests themselves weren't bad at all and there was a study session the night before every test. Overall, a very easy class made easier thx to Aaron's teaching. Worst part about this class is it's an 8AM

Amazing Professor! Aaron's notes were super organized and always posted to canvas. Homework's are posted after every lecture. TA's are sometimes hard to reach out of their office hours. Exams are fair and follow the practice exams and homework. Overall great class and experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Saucier is a great professor. He was available outside of class, and genuinely wanted his students to succeed. Perhaps most importantly, his lectures where clear and easy to follow, and posted online afterwards.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aaron was an awesome professor because he wants you to succeed. You have 3 exams and then a comprehensive final exam. I failed my first exam because I had no idea what I was doing, but if you did better on your 2nd and 3rd exams, he took the average of all 3 and changed the first exam score to the average. He also gives random extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Saucier is one of the best engineering professors I have had in awhile. His lectures are clearly explained. He and his TAs are always available for help via email or in person. He has a sense of humor and wants people to do well in his class. He does the work on screen while explaining so you have plenty of time to understand and write.

He handwrites the notes while giving lecture which is helpful because most professors just read off slides and give us no time to consume/write the notes. Makes mistakes sometimes in class but is always a good sport about it. Weekly quizzes, but they really aren't that bad. Take the course, even though it might be an 8am.
Statics is a tough class. Professor Saucier is a good professor. Make sure to attend each class to get the extra credit he gives out.

His lecture is about a page of notes per unit then about 2 days' worth of examples. He clearly lays out the course material using color coding, explanation and example. There is a lot of homework, but it is kind of necessary to wrap your head around the more complex subject matter. Very responsive and makes an effort to be available to students.

super chill dude. Funny. goes off on tangents sometimes. he writes down his lecture notes as he teaches so you have plenty of time to copy them down. super accessible outside class and accommodating. he even made an extra final because too many students wanted to take it early to be done with it. super chill and nice.

This professor is great! The lectures were great, he was funny, engaging, and knowledgeable. I would 100% take another class with this professor. There was a class of 200 people and he was memorising peoples names, amazing teacher!

Super easy teacher. Takes too long on some examples in class but he's making sure everybody understands. Will give quizzes and extra credit out sometimes at random so show up! Super easy grader. Tests were usually like practice exams but he never gave answer keys for practice exams so you had to go to the review if you wanted the answers.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Aaron is one of the most demanding professors I've ever had; but he has kept me accountable as a student. Three semesters in a row with him has left me broken, but I can say that I've come out better because of it . He has a good sense of humor and is always accessible via email or office hours. Be prepared to grind though - his tests are too long!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good dude, lectures are very interesting and engaging asks a lot of questions and make sure everyone is confident.

If you have an opportunity to not take this professor, do yourself a favor. He acts like he would rather be anywhere else than teaching your class or dealing with you. His tests were fairly predictable but excessively long.
There are weekly quizzes, and he takes attendance randomly, so go to class! He honestly is a great professor and makes the class easy. Practice exams are like the actual exams.

A lot of homework but it helps you learn. Go to lecture. Tests are just like practice tests. Tests were worth 80% of total grade, but there were only 2. This makes you think that doing the homework doesn't matter, but it does!! Long lectures but it went by fast because they are easy to follow and he's really good at teaching. Don't afraid to ask!
Tough class, need to go to class. Will not pass expecting to cruise through like you have youre whole like. First real engineering class, just stay on top of material. Lots of in class quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You have to show up to lectures. He posts his notes, but without context they are very hard to follow. He is very accessible outside of class though. I went to his office hours several times. He also cares about his students. He knew the names of most of his students. However he could be a bit condescending at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Saucier is a great guy, very understanding when circumstances come up. I don't usually rate professors but wanted to rate him well because he is an all around great guy and effective professor.

He gets mad if you ask him questions during lecture. He is not good at explaining what he is teaching and expects too much from students. He gave my structural analysis class a class average of 2.3 gpa (which is the first time it's been that low for this class). He is mean outside of class to, don't go to his office hours. Avoid him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Saucier can be kind of rude sometimes when people ask questions, but if you get to know him more, he's actually extremely helpful and caring.  He's a great teacher with fair tests and quizzes (tests are almost identical to practice tests), but there is homework assigned every single class.  Personally, I love him after two different classes.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: In my opinion, Aaron was a great professor. His class focused heavy on example problems rather than lectures. Homework every Mon, Wed and Fri made the course a heavy workload. If you don't go to class or don't do the homework, your grade  will suffer tremendously. Questions on weekly quizzes and exams often come from in class and homework problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Comes off as if he's trying to have low grades in the class. Excessive homework weekly (Mon,Wed,Friday due dates all semester). I understand you have to work for your grade but this guy has pop quizzes the same week as exams. Lectures are not thorough and he does not explain concepts really well, just sort of shows you that he can do the problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Was not pleased with Aaron's teaching at all. He did not go into detailed explanations unless asked about. When people would ask questions like why something was done the way it was, he would get angry that we even asked. I never wanted to ask questions because of this reason and was left confused on several aspects and was never prepared for exams

Aaron is only a phd student and is out to prove he has it all figured out. Don't expect to learn much, be prepared for tests, or enjoy the subject matter. Rough semester. Has a funny sense of humor though.

Dr. Harstad is a very good professor. He is very compassionate and understanding towards students when they need help. Lectures are insightful and can become a great place to learn. Don't need textbook in IO course and attendance is optional. Bottom line, Dr. Harstad understands the dynamics of students lives and looks to help not hurt students.
The course is structured correctly and the professor is intelligent. Great course I would recommend.
Great pofessor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Participation both in-class and especially online discussion (via Sakai -- like blackboard,  but simpler), was critical. Exams are tough, and "don't always have a right answer", but participation bonus points make up for it. Classes are discussion-based and usually quite interesting as he explains concepts based on personal experiences.

I took this class last year, and since have taken another class with Dr. Harstad. This class was amazing, Dr. Harstad teaches this at a higher level than other teachers, but provides extra credit. I think all econ majors should take this class and game theory with Dr. Harstad, he really cares about the material and his students.

Dr. Harstad is the best professor I have had while at university. Dr. Harstad really cares about his students and the material he teaches, and he really knows what he is talking about and can give real world examples. I would never take game theory with another professor, and any econ major should take this class with Dr. Harstad.

Dr. Harstad is an extremely intelligent and kind professor. He specifically teaches his classes at a higher level than other professors. His test are difficult but there are points available to make up for a low test grade. It is clear he highly values student learning. Expect a strong focus on game theory and its applications.

One of the first econ teachers I ever had who was able to relate real life stories to economic theory.  His tests are hard, but I would suggest not leaving anything blank, no matter what!  Expect a lot of self teaching, long "discussions", and as noted elsewhere, posting on sakai for "participation" is huge (points) and helpful (learning).

Dr. Harstad was great.  He told our class up front that he was going to have a family issue to deal with later on in the semester, which I thought was extremely transparent.  Postings on Sakai are extremely beneficial, both for your grade (you can get unlimited points) and for pure knowledge.  His test are tough, but there's a fair curve.
Hardest tests I've ever taken, but the biggest curve I've ever received.

Lectures are boring, but the grading system allows you to get many extra points. I attended class twice and got a 105 on the midterm. Discussion board posts are also very helpful. If you read the book and understand what he wants on the tests you will pass easy.
lectures are extremely boring and he makes no sense. The text book is "harder than the honors textbook" as he says. Overall very bad, the only good thing is the class is curved so that is nice.

An odd class, but one I thoroughly enjoyed.  Prof. Harstad doesn't seem interested in the administrative aspects of the class; You're virtually guaranteed a pass if you don't drop.  It's very easy to get an A in here, but Prof. Harstad is also VERY knowledgeable with respect to the subject matter.  You can learn alot in here if you pay attention.

He has been unfairly judged on this site. The vast majority of people rating him here are for Econ 1014 - a class that all people complain about their teachers in (try to find a Mizzou Econ 1014 professor rated highly). Some people are just not smart enough for Econ and take it out on the teacher. One recent comment: "your retarded" -- Enough said.
Really hard class but the all the extra credit makes its  a joke, if you don't get an A your retarded.

Horrible teacher and horrible class. First of all no one goes if they do most are asleep.  He is boring and just goes over slides that come from the book. however just doing this does not help because the tests are all about how to apply the concepts which you do not learn how to do in lab. In lab all you do is play a computer game that doesnt help

Harstad is an interesting teacher. He only gives you 30 minutes to do the tests and expects you not to finish but then gives everyone a huge curve. This class has unlimited extra credit though so take advantage of that. I got over a 100% easily.

Tests are extremely hard,  Reading the textbook and also going through and understanding practice problems are useful.  Although the curve is high, don't plan on relying on it too much, he uses a formula that includes your raw score. So people who received a 50% may get a 90 with curve while those who received 30% may only get a 50%.
I get over a 100 on everything, including the exams. PZ and L8. Oh and don't bother going to class, just read the slides.

basically we just go over general information like what so and so means. but on exams he expects to apply information pertaining to alot of math, which is the majority we go over...and he doesnt even go over how we can apply that kinda information. just definitions and stuff.
This mans tests are absolutly insane. However, the curves make a 30 percent an A somehow. This class is not informative and is a major waste of time

Worst class of my life.  I really wanted to learn econ, but he made it so confusing it was near impossible.  Like someone else rated, I came out knowing less about economics.  His tests are way harder than the TAs say they are at review sessions.

DONT BOTHER WITH LECTURES! his curves are huge and basically he is kinda crazy. He is hard to follow and hear even when I sat in the first three rows. Overall, one of the better econ teachers usless you actually want to learn it.

Harstad is the man, don't get me wrong, but he's not the greatest teacher ever.  Give the man his tenure and be done with it!  TA's in Micro Rock my world though...absolutely phenomenal!  Oh yeah, gotta love the curve and the extra credit...how often is a 60% an A+, seriously, how sweet is that!
worst class of my life. huge curves, but he's still a horrible teacher. lecture is pointless.

This guy is so WORLTHLESS. I mean you know something is wrong when less than 80 people go to lecture out of a total of 500 students. I honestly couldn't tell you if the class was hard because the curves are RIDICULOUS. The average for the 2nd exam was a 38. I could teach this class better than Harstad...but then again that's not saying much.
thank god it's over. don't know how i got an 'a' cause i think i know less about econ than when i started.

I have never had a class be so worthless in my life.  He seemed like a very intelligent guy but he just couldn't teach the material....i never knew what we were studying in class....the TA saved me on this one.
Probably the worst class ive ever taken. Im not sure why i ever went to class.

How worthless was this class?  I went to a grand total of 3 lectures, all before the first exam and ended up with an A.  This proves that Harstad's lectures are terrible, unclear, and disorganized, as well as sleep-inducing...as well as completely useless to passing.  There was a huge curve in the class, the average was around  50%. Glad its over.
Horrible teacher. Stopped going to lecture because it taught nothing. I only did well because of my T.A. The only plus is big curves.

horrible teacher!!!  his lectures make no sense, his grading procedures are confusing, and he has an annoying/strange sense of humor.  You wont think it is funny when you are trying to do good in what he has made a worthless economics class.

Lectures weren't informational at all.  If you are stuck in this class, just go to labs and forget lecture.  He is horrible at explaining and lectures are of little relevance.  Terrible terrible class.
Lordy, this man mannot teach.  I think he knows his stuff, but damned if I know, because I did not learn a single thing in his lecture.  Thankfully, I had a wonderful TA.
Worst Professor I've ever had.
Don't mean to reiterate what the other posts say but yeah.
DO NOT TAKE HIS LECTURE, the TA's have to do all the clarifying and his lectures are an absolute waste of time.
If you get Harstad as your teacher drop the class ASAP b/c you will not learn anything from him. The little info I did get out of the class was from my TA.
I agree completely.  The TAs had to make the tests because nobody would take notes during lecture.  There is a huge curve in the class though!

I noticed that no one has rated Harstad, so I've taken it upon myself to inform the community. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS MAN!! DO NOT!!! His lectures are confused and disorganized, there are no notes nor even a workable textbook. Personally, he is pompous, boring, and scatterbrained. STAY AWAY!!

Aaron is one of my favorite math teachers. His class was laid back and incredibly interesting. He is a major math nerd and it shows, but he makes complicated topics easy to comprehend. He hosted review sessions before every exam that covered all of the topics covered. All homework and exams were useful and fairly straightforward. Take him for math!
One of my top 3 professors at Mizzou by far! Very funny, keeps class chill, and tests are based off exactly what he goes over in class, in homework, and from review work.  Get him if you can!

Aaron was an awesome professor! He took time to hold review sessions before midterm exams as well as the final exam. You knew exactly what you needed to know for the tests. He also was very available for help on homework or anything else during office hours. Going to class was entertaining and very helpful with Aaron. Best professor I've had!
Really great teacher, makes material easy to understand. Does a review before tests which is super helpful. Very charismatic and funny. I'd like to take an upper level course taught by him.

Great professor! Really enjoyed the course material compared to previous math classes. He made it fun and interesting to learn. Told you what was expected on exams. Took out personal time to have review sessions before exams. Cracked funny jokes and kept it light. I wish I could have taken all my math courses with him!

Dr. Wood is a great teacher. He is very funny and loves his students. He really does want you to do well, but doesn't make it super easy in doing so. If you pay attention in class and do the online homework you should get an A in his class. One of my favorite professors so far in college.
Best teacher ever! He always has a good story, but can still make the daunting task of understanding Calculus manageable.

Nice.
Likes math.
Good vibes.

He's a little shy but a very nice guy, made math understandable. He wears fun shirts. My personal favorite is his "Hot Salami" shirt. He's always thankful to those who come to class and has a good grasp at the classroom level of understanding. I would recommend taking this course with him.

Aidan was a great instructor. The course material is fairly easy when it comes to mathematics and he does a decent job at teaching it. Overall just focus and show up to class and you'll do fine in this course. He has office hours as well if you are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I have had at Mizzou. She gave me extension on assignments and allowed resubmissions.. She is very caring and cares about students mental health.She is very understanding and kind professor and also teaches her subject well, you can tell she know well what she teaching.Take her class, you won't regret.
Very flexible with due dates and late assignment submissions.

She understands everything you are going through. Never forces you to work on something you don't like, or affects your mental health. If you have ADHD or you prefer to work individually, she allows even everyone is working in groups. She gives the best rubric ever, so you never miss even a point.

Ainsley Kelly is an amazing English teacher. As long as you show up to class and get your work done, this class should be a breeze. She has super clear grading criteria for essays and assignments. She is also very forgiving if you miss the due date by a day. Overall an amazing learning experience in her classroom.

Dr. Guhlincozzi's class is what made me declare a WGST major! Discussions in her class were amazing, and her research focus of feminist geography is so interesting. She is also funny, approachable, and listens to her students.
Doesn't seem to have a grasp on what she's teaching, I would 100% stay away from this course if you value your sanity

Dr. Guhlincozzi was excited about Feminist Geography and had decent lectures. However, the weekly quizzes you took were insanely difficult and based entirely on unclear academic journals. They were only 4-5 questions but took between 30 minutes to an hour to complete. The written final was also insane and took 3.5 hours to complete 15 questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is nice but she does not understand that this class is an ELECTIVE. It took more effort than my major classes. You take a quiz every which which takes you over an hour to do and are expected to read 20+ pages of academic journals. Don't take it thinking it'll be an easy A because you're an woman. If you don't learn by reading, don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is nice but her class is bad. This class took more effort/time than my core classes because we had to read 20+ pages of academic readings and had a quiz every week that would take me around 2 hours. She was sometimes late to class and would easily get off topic. She didn't explain concepts well enough. Projects were time consuming and not fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Li is a bit eccentric but a really cool professor. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about astronomy, which means you learn a lot but sometimes in a meandering way. Super easy grader.

I took Astrobiology (4102) with Dr. Li. Definitely the easiest class I will ever take in college, I could have easily gotten an A in this class in high school. Dr. Li is a great guy who is a lot of fun to talk to and makes his lectures very interesting while encouraging conversation. Homework is completion graded, and exams were HW problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Li is knowledgeable about his field. He knows its difficult and doesnt demand much. He handed out answers for homework, just so we could rework the problems quickly. The midterm was open note, though the final was closed. Not a difficult class, but meandering and occasionally confusing if youre expecting a clear progression of topics.

Hands down the easiest class to pass. He's very hard to understand. I think I opened my textbook once, but you need the online codes to do the labs (which he didn't explain at all). I only went to class when he handed out "homework" and on quiz days. FYI, the homework is the quiz and he gives you the answers to the homework...

Aigen Li was the best teacher I had! He assigned homework early in the week. Then he'd give us ALL  the answers to the homework before it was due. We would take a quiz over the homework and the questions were very similar. Then after the quiz he would collect the homework. The tests were a combination all the quizzes. IF you didnt get an A you suck

I took this class because it was four credits and counted towards my physical science credit. I could NOT understand him no matter how hard I tried. Didn't feel like any of his lectures were relevant. All the labs he just thrusted upon us at the VERY end of the semester without explaining a one of them. Quizzes were easy. Attendance was infrequent.

Easy course. Although he is somewhat hard to understand, if you do the work required it is easy to get an A grade. Textbook was hardly ever used, and all in class lecture notes were put online (therefore I hardly ever went). To people who are not interested in Astronomy or let alone science, this will be the most dry class of your life.

Seemed like a nice guy but cant understand anything he says because of his accent. Class has no organization, no refrence, the textbook wont really help. Do not take this class. One of the worst classes i have had at Mizzou.

Got an A in the class but hated attending (clickers were used so need to attend) He was very difficult to understand even though I sat in the second row and the material never seemed to relate from one day to the next.
She was not helpful, tests were difficult no matter how much you studied. Her teaching style made it to where it was pointless to attend class and you were wasting your time.

Professor Ruth has lectured on subjects such as the thoracic cavity and heart in Gross Anatomy. Her lectures in comparison to other professors we have in the course are extremely dense, hard to understand unless you have significant background knowledge, and poorly organized. I have had to spend 2-3 times relearning her material in comparison.

Lab itself is very easy, info is straightforward. Attendance not mandatory, but the same models from class are used in exams, so you have to show up and be familiar with them to do well. Dr. Ruth is very nice but not always the most helpful; the TAs often seemed to answer questions better than her. Lots of info in a short time; must keep up! Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lab complements the lecture very well. But you must prepare in advance. Do the online labs and pre-lab quizzes before lab. Going to lab allows you to interact with the material and apply it by filling out the lab packets as you look at the 3D models. Dr. Ruth does a good job answering your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Ruth is good. I feel like the assistants she has could be better. I found lab to be really helpful while taking lecture at the same time. Go to the labs and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Anatomy lab is ran by grad students. While the units line up with the lecture, they're very different. I wish the lab and lecture were taught by the same person. Poorly structured class and don't feel like I've gotten much out of it at all. You mostly teach yourself the material. No real guidance at all.

One of the best professors I've personally ever had! Jambul cares so much about his students and genuinely wants them to succeed. By the end of just one semester you'll be able to speak basic Russian. Mizzou is so lucky to have Jambul. Take his class!

He is an amazing professor. I am seriously considering pursuing a Russian minor based on the sole fact that he is the teacher. The more you get to know him, the better class will be. He makes Russian fun to learn, even if there is a good amount of homework. The tests can be quite tough if you don't do the homework, so keep up and ask questions!
Amazing instructor!!! Would 100% take the course again!

He is very nice and genuinely cares about his students. Tries to make learning Russian fun with videos, activities, and jokes. There is a lot of homework, but it's understandable for a language class. Be mindful that he does tend to cold-call on people, which can be daunting, but if you studied and are prepared, it is not bad. Overall a great time

Jambul is a fantastic professor, one of the best I've ever had. He genuinely reignited my desire to learn and inspired me to pursue a Russian degree. He is an asset to Mizzou, and his presence at Mizzou raises its quality as a learning institution.
Jambul is the best professor that I've had at Mizzou. I cannot say enough great things about him and his classes.
He is our prophet, our priest, our king. Joseph Smith was not one tenth the revelator he is. His teaching is like unto the discovery of a third tablet at Sinai.

Jambul is a very engaging teacher and he cares so much about his students, he takes the time to get to know them each individually. Thats pookie fr

love you jambul MIZZOU YOU NEED JAMBUL

I cannot speak highly enough of Jambul! He has hard shell, but truly cares about his students. He is a true instructor and is more than willing to help students understand the material. I am loyal to him to a tee, and hopefully will have him for the foreseeable future. Lots of homework, but very well paced and actually helps if you aren't lazy.
Dzhambul is a new Napoleon of Caucasia. We are deathlessly loyal to him. At his word we will do anything. Take every class possible with him.

Really interesting lectures, and keeps them pretty brief with the asynch format. Be prepared to watch about 4-5 hours worth of movies and lectures each week, but as long as you connect your work to the themes in the lecture and use specific examples you'll do well on most assignments. Interesting and creative final group project.

An amazing professor, he often says (in MATH 3000) "I wish for you to enjoy and learn in this course, do not worry about your grade". He is very accommodating and open to extending deadlines, and the exams are straight forward. He is a very kind soul and his lectures are easy (as easy as they can be given the topic) to follow.
Jacob is a great professor. I struggled in the class because I did not enjoy the topics presented, but he is very accommodating and is very kind. if i could take him again I would.

He is a great teacher who truly does want you to succeed and aids you in any way that he can. There is an abundance of course materials that can be used and he makes the exams as simple as possible; they are purely conceptual. Also, there is one extra credit question per exam.

Such a caring professor. Lectures are easy to understand, gives clear/concise steps, and homework/quizzes directly resemble tests. He's quick to respond to emails and his tests are typically easier than the homework questions. His canvas page is very easy to follow and the class was overall great!

I took Calc 2 online, because the in-person professor was terrible. I ended up getting Jacob as my professor for the online class. Although taking calculus 2 online was very challenging, you can tell he really cares about his students. He goes out of his way to help you if you ask, and you can tell he enjoys doing so. Highly recommend.
simply the goat.

I took Math 1700 in the fall and had an amazing experience. He is a super friendly guy, and you can tell he truly cares about his students. Every test had extra credit. I found out I am in his class for Math 2300. I am ecstatic!

One of my favorite professors this semester by far. If you can take Calc II with him, do so! While the nature of Calc II is inherently challenging, he was very helpful during office hours and answered any questions I had. Really caring professor who wants to see his students succeed. 10/10 recommend.

Super caring guy. Such a loose grader and his tests were extremely easy. Easy to talk to, fosters a fun environment in class, and lectures aren't hard to follow. Calc II is hard but he made it enjoyable and manageable. Homework is a b it annoying but thats out of his control.
Great class! Assignments and grading were clear. Rahmet was kind, helpful, and easy to reach. Course content was interesting and connected well to real life.

Rahmet clearly communicates expectations and everything is laid out well. If you stay on top of the work you'll learn a lot. She genuinely cares about her students and she was always willing to help when I reached out.

Without question the worst professor I've had at Mizzou. Lectures are as captivating as watching paint dry. Tests are written to trick you. Between the two quizzes, the discussion posts, and the "engagement activities" you have to do each week, you'll spend 80% of your time in this course doing busy work. Couldn't possibly recommend her any less

While this class is very interesting, the grading sucks! There are very few items to be graded on, and the tests dictate your grade, so it is difficult to come back from a poor test score. While Rahment herself is very kind, this class structure was very strict for a 2000-level course. I personally would not take from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was a really good and straightforward class. Writing and reading heavy but there're interesting/entertaining commentaries on each topic that help you grasp the material better. would definitely take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There's a lot of writing involved in this class but the assignments are all explained well with clear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is not understanding at all. I received a A+ on all assignments in the class. I accidentally submitted the wrong assignment and did not know until she graded it, so I received a 0 and could not submit the correct version. There are no lectures. You have to get 3 expensive textbooks and teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never taking this professor again. She will accuse anyone of plagiarism if their Turnitin score is above 1% and gives students a 0 if a source isn't cited in her own way. She also makes you buy 3 very expensive textbooks and doesn't post video lectures. Sorry, but I'm not paying tuition to teach myself through textbooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's strict about citations and plagiarism, but she pushes you to learn and do your best. There are 8 assignments (3 pages each) and a final paper (analysis of a film).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you do the work it's fairly easy. Try to submit assignments on recommended checkpoints and don't fall behind. She is willing to work with students just communicate with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was not expecting this class to be an easy A, but I also was not expecting to write 3 page essays every week. I'm all for self-paced classes, but I almost have to drop this class because it interferes with my other classes. Also makes you buy 3 textbooks!! If you want a social life out of this class, I would recommend choosing another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is online/self paced, requiring a lot of self discipline. There were no lectures but it was well-structured with textbooks and lecture commentaries. Rahmet was great!! She really cared about her students' success and was extremely helpful whenever I had questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The teacher is so rude and a really tough grader. You also have to buy a ton of expensive books for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ive never heard her voice (because she doesnt teach at all and expects students to teach themselves from the 3, yes 3, very expensive required textbooks youre required to purchase for the course)but her emails are so mean. She expects students to write 3 pages a week and uses a very confusing database to turn things. Just take another class :( !

As you've seen in the other reviews, this isn't a blow off class. Halfway through semester I thought I might have to drop. I went to his office hours and went through some things with him, and realistically, he helped me graduate. He's a great guy and a great professor who cares that his students learn. I hope you payed attention in Finance 3000.

I had Dr Kern for Finance 4020. He's easily my favorite professor. If you are looking for a blowoff class/looking to get by without understanding anything, this will not be the class for you. He genuinely cares about our learning and prepares you for the industry. Great class if you're driven and intentional about a finance career.

Professor Kern's class is not easy. If you're looking on here for a blow off class, definitely do not take this one. However, being that I learned more in his class alone than every other class I took in college, I would recommend it. He is very helpful outside of class, so if you feel behind, stop by his office hours. It makes a difference.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Andy was my favorite professor during my time at Mizzou. I had him for multiple courses, and it's clear that he wants his students to do well in class and be prepared for the industry. I hope he continues to be interactive with his students as that's where I got the most meaning during lecture. Go to class and ask questions and you'll do well.

Professor Kern genuinely cares about our education. He makes sure to focus on the topics we need to know rather than just go through what the class is about. He is very knowledgeable and entertaining. He is extremely smart and if you go to lectures you will learn a lot. I went to office hours a lot and he was very helpful. Test heavy, final was 40%
Dr. Kern is a breath of fresh air. His expertise and insight shines through in subtle unexpected ways. I recommend his class to anyone who wants an awesome learning experience.

He spent more time making jokes and chatting than he did lecturing. He once sent us home early from class because he didn't know how to do a homework problem. I emailed him about the final and he told me he doesn't know how to help me and that I should just look over my notes.
Dr. Kern is an all round good guy. He cares about the students He wants them to succeed in class (and in life).  If you ever get the chance to have Dr. Kern as a professor, take  it!

Dr. Kern could be the best professor that I've had at the University of Missouri. He is very passionate about finance, which shows everyday in his lectures. His office door is literally always open and he is more than willing to help and assist where he can.

Overall, a great teacher.  All the explanations are really clear.  The homework is tough but you get three chances to get it right and will walk you through it if you have difficulty.  Always available to help in his office.

Andy is the man.  He will help you in any way he can and his exams are challenging but also very fair.  His office is always open and he is always available to help explain things you don't understand or simply talk about the stock market.
all of the readings for this class are about taylor swift. it's an easy A but Dr. anderson makes it a cortisol spike
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson takes a introductory English class and makes it entirely about Taylor Swift. Her lectures are boring and unengaging. She's a pretty easy grader on papers, but assignments if you do one think incorrectly you lose credit for the entire assignment. I would take this class with another instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ashley is very kind and willing to work with you, however I felt like I was in hs again taking this class. She gives okay feedback, and grades fairly. I did not improve as a writer in this class. Lecture is VERY boring and the in class activities are childish and feel arbitrary. If you show up and make a moderate effort you'll be fine
don't take this class with here

I felt like I was in high school again. She would make you stay in class for work time—if you left or weren't there, you would be penalized. The lectures are long, and almost all of them are on slides. She is a nice person and gives good feedback, but I would recommend choosing a different professor.

I've heard bad things about this prof but honestly as long as you stay on top of the weekly assignments and follow the criteria for each assignment you'll be fine. Her feedback with every paper is really helpful with getting good grades as well. She really does care about her students and their well-being and is super understanding!

Weekly participation grades, weekly discussion boards with lots of reading, 4 total projects. If you are in a hard major, I recommend looking for a different professor. Unclear Canvas organization. Boring lectures, unhelpful feedback, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take her English 1000. She does not communicate things you need to have done by class and WILL greatly deduct your grade due to this. When you ask her she will brush it off and not take responsibility. Not helpful when writing papers either, don't bother meeting with her just go to the writing center they are much more help. Worst professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Particpation is heavy. She was a tough grader esp for a level 1000 class, she treated it more like a 3000 class. Lots of essay drafts and class activites. Went to 1 on 1 meetings with her & she said my essays were good but I would get 60-70% on them. It was frustrating, however I think it was her first class ever so things couldve changed by now.

this guy grades sueor generously but the class is built such that you have to parcipate bc he makes some of the assignments interacting w your classmates and he does actually grade these. hes super chill and forgiving, also super chill and straighforward assignments.

As long as you stay caught up you will do fine. I hate writing more than anything and got a 95 on the first paper. His expectations are reasonable. He has lots of really cool stories and is very nice. There is homework but mostly discussions and easy grading. There is extra credit to make up for missed attendance too.

He is amazing. He knows his stuff and really enjoys what he does. I would 100% take a course taught by him again. The homework can be a fair bit but he makes the rest of the class enjoyable, balancing it out.

WORST class ever. I have so many negative things to say about it, but honestly one of the worst parts was how extra credit was given out for dressing up at movie screenings (Example : cowboy). We are talking +20 points which could boost you almost an entire letter grade. Alot of people arent willing to dress up in silly costumes for extra points.

Prof Kazakov's class was disorganized and unhelpful. Assignments lacked guidance, and feedback was vague. He seemed unprepared and uninterested in engaging with students. It felt more like I was teaching myself than learning from a professor. Would not recommend his courses.

A very realistic and entertaining teacher. Show up because there's an attendance grade but if you watch all the free movie screenings you'll be fine if you miss a few classes. Lectures are explained to teach us how film correlates to live. Having a creative mind, this professor listens to everyone's opinions and are valued for participation.

The guy is great. Funny, reasonable, cares about the subject but doesn't expect every student to be a film nerd. Class has a really chill atmosphere but there's still a clear understanding that this isn't a blow off class. He's not a super strict grader and he's understanding if you have genuine reasons for things to be late or miss class.

This class is not very hard. As long as you do the papers and projects, you can get a good grade. He is an easy grader and will give you super long extensions. I really did not get anything out of this class though, it is obvious that Proff Kazakov does not want to be there. He is a really awkward guy and makes cringey jokes and comments.

Overall his class is fine. He wants AMA format and is really picky about it. Everything is due on Fridays. Some of the discussions felt annoying, but they help if you do bad on a test. The final assignment is annoying because you get very little time to make a 15 minute presentation. He does grades fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class isn't bad but he won't respond to anything you send him.

The quizzes were pretty easy and there were weekly discussions or assignments. His powerpoints were very useful for all class assignments and the textbook has some information needed for quizzes. If you look over the powerpoints and textbook you should do fine in the class.

Great PPT lectures. Listen to those lectures at 1.5x or 2x fast because he talks slow! Most quizzes and test questions come from lecture, but a few questions come from the book. Just need to skim the chapters. Most answers on quizzes and tests can be found on quizlet. Highly recommend this professor!
A lot of content. High expectations.

The class can be a drag at times, especially if you take the afternoon timeslot. Her lectures are at best tolerable, at worst agonizing. I was fine putting up with this course, as it's a prerequisite to the more advanced photo classes. Not the worst experience ever, but certainly plenty to improve on.
critiques.

Angela is very understanding and accomodating. You can tell that she is passionate about photography and her work, and she brings in a variety of references to the class that are helpful for developing your own style. Assignments are not very focused on technical aspects of photography, but expectations are clear. The course is engaging overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A nice teacher who was easy to talk to. All assignments were laid out with specific grading points. If you do the work, you will get a good grade. Critiques are long and you are required to find the hidden meaning behind others work. It was a little too much at times because not every piece has a super meaningful background.Overall nice class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really light grader, you can be given an A for taking a photo of a toothbrush on a toilet as long as there's some “deeper meaning” behind it. Doesn't really know a lot about photography and the assignments are not based on technical skill but if you can stand around and “critique” people's half-ass attempts at photography. Really boring class.

This teacher ruined photography for me, I will never take another art class at this school. Giving a decent compliment is beyond her, providing feedback on work is non-existent, and she does not tell you your grade until the end of the semester. Does not know more complex information on Adobe or cameras (both which are required for this class).

do everything perfectly, get a B (it says in the syllabus); teacher doesn't know much about cameras (could never help with anything technical); you also don't know your grade until finals week and no feedback is provided
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Senora Placeres is AMAZING! I have never felt like I understood or enjoyed Spanish before taking her class. She made it fun and enjoyable in a way no other professor has before. She came to class everyday so positive and genuinely cared about your understanding of the content. She is the best Spanish professor I've ever had.
She's just the best. There isn't much more to say than that. She makes the environment very comfortable even if you don't know what you're doing. I wish I could have her for every spanish class ever

She was very helpful in helping out every student and knew their name within the first 1-2 months. Class could be scary at times because she randomly calls on students, but it does engage everyone in the room, as much as I disliked it. She's very easy to reach outside of class and is always understanding and talks you through wrong answers.

Professor Placeres is a genuinely pleasant person. She facilitates the learning of her students by not chiding them or deducting points in ways other professors would. At the end of the day, she cares about your learning, do her a favor and care for your own performance and she will be a great aid to have.

I understand that the Spanish department is mainly controlled by the director, but I did find this to be the most difficult I have had to get a good grade and connect with a professor. If you are doing poorly she thinks you are lazy and doesn't offer sympathy. She rolled her eyes and scoffed in class. Spanish is hard; she doesn't make it easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was so kind and took the time to help and/or get to know each student. She would encourage, but not force participation from every student and meet them where they were at. The course itself is pretty content and test heavy, but she prepares you well.

She's very kind and quickly learns everyone's names. She forces class participation in a good way and always gives constructive feedback. She supports a lighthearted mood and laughs at her own little mistakes.

She was my favorite professor this semester by far! She is so caring and wants you to understand and love Spanish and Spanish/Latin American culture as much as she does. Even though I won't have a class taught by her next semester, I am very excited to see her out and get the chance to say hi to her again. She's just a wonderful woman all around.

She was more than helpful. She would take the time to set you aside and make sure that you understood the material. Very nice, funny, embraces her mistakes. I would totally take any class offered by her. Don't drop this course. Just ask for help. It will be given to you.

She is extremely helpful. She really cares about each student and does help you out and gives you the benefit of the doubt if she knows that you are trying really hard. This is my first time taking Spanish ever and she was so helpful throughout the semester.
She showed authentic concern for her students ability to understand the material. She was very patient and understanding.

Dr. Ali's lectures are a little slow, but he is extremely easy to work with and very caring. He's also very passionate about helping students, and is an extremely knowledgeable advisor for capstone projects.

He's the worst professor I've ever had. He's got a ridiculous attendance policy and then will send a TA to teach when he doesn't want to. On the plus side all of our midterms were online. It's like he knows he bad at his job so he lets us take most of the exams online. His handwriting can be illegible. I want to give a shoutout to Wayne the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sichani is perhaps the most disorganized and disrespectful professor at the university. Lectures were incredibly messy & information on the slides often was wrong. It was clear that he did not plan his lectures ahead of time. Practice problems were made up on the spot & not helpful. He clearly did not communicate with his TAs. Labs were helpful

Dr. Ali is a good lecturer, but paired with his very difficult to read handwriting and the fact that everything came from the textbook, it was hard to really take the class serious. The textbook and other resources would explain the concepts better than him. One of his TA's, Wayne, was also a very good aide for the class. Avoid if possible.

A very weird experience.

I want to give positives, because it's clear Dr. Sichani cares, but a lack of organization and chaotic teaching style make it very difficult to learn. The course concepts are simple, but he makes them feel more difficult. 5 minutes of YT taught me more than 10 lectures unfortunately.

Great guy, lenient grading, horrid TAs

If you have a pulse, you'll get an A in the class. However, if you actually want to learn something, his lectures are unorganized and his TAs are never around. Try to follow along with channels like "UConn HKN" to learn each topic and "Electrical and Electronics Engineering" to get good at solving problems quickly.

This professor is the worst I have ever had. You'll get an A in this class if you do ANY work at all but you won't learn anything. He assigns homework WAY above the expectations for a typical circuits 1 class, can't explain concepts well, grades very slowly, and has borderline unreadable handwriting. Nice guy, but shouldn't teach. TAs are bad too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had, and that is saying a lot because I have had really bad professors. Where do I even start. For starters, attendance is mandatory and if you don't show up you lose some of your grade. Super disorganized professor, and irrationally strict for no reason. Almost seems like he gets a power trip, if you read his syllabus.

Helpful and kind professor. He is extremely disorganized and receives flack from students for it. He makes his courses easy to succeed in with online exams and ample time to complete assignments. Attendance is claimed to be mandatory but is not from my experience. A professor that wants his students to succeed. I believe he is just overworked.

Gets more flack then he deserves from students who expect the professor to do all the learning for them. This is college, you have to teach yourself, everytime I did have a question Dr. Ali was always helpful and explained concepts well in his office hours. Was a tad bit unorganized but I guess that is to be expected from a newly minted professor.

This is a mess of a class. Super disorganized lectures and class schedule. There is not a weekly schedule so if you miss a day or want to see what we will cover during any week, good luck with that. His policy stated each absence would result in a -1%, so many people came to just to avoid that. Examples in class rarely helped with homework or exams

The lectures were unorganized, seemed improvised, often had mistakes, and were mostly tangents on subjects unessential to the class. Gave very little other resources to reference. Topics were often over complicated and made more confusing than necessary. If you are forced to take this professor, do not use him as your primary resource.

ECE 3830 with Dr. Sichani wasn't a good time. You could honestly just read the textbook, never attend lecture and still end up with a good grade. For a subject that has both a lot of practical applications and mathematical abstraction, I learned neither of them in detail. If you actually want to learn, take this class with another professor.

Linear Systems and Signals are hard, so instead of paying attention in lecture I watched MIT open course ware for the class that was made in the 80's. The online tests took more than 2 hours to complete. Had Matlab questions on the homework, and the only direction were marginally understandable pdfs uploaded to canvas by the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Altman isnt the worst professor ive had but she wasnt the best. For 3700 she was decent. She refuses to post slides on canvas so coming to class is key. As long as you take good notes and get paired into a good group you should be fine. Tests are straight forward

Her Research Methods 2 course was difficult, but informative and rewarding. It was one of the best courses offered throughout the MPA program because the knowledge is useful long-term, and despite the course content being a little more challenging her lectures made research methods understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: HlthSci 3700! Lecture is main portions of class, attendance isn't mandatory but she doesn't post the notes or let you take pictures. Pretty strict grading on homework-which is given weekly almost but if you build rapport with her she's very kind and will help as much as possible. Very nice, course is just boring and complex so hw just takes time
Awful and aloof! Pretend to be professional.

She is a very hard grader and her assignments require a lot of time. She is not very helpful when you ask for help and her lectures are so lengthy that it is hard to stay focused. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grades really tough, not a fun class at all. Boring lectures and a teacher who doesn't place her students in the best positions to succeed particularly in the way she goes about helping you. Offers little helpful advice and then rips your grade to shreds afterwards regardless

Hard to do well in her class when taking other tough classes on top of it. She grades harder than a good amount of my science professors and is not helpful when you approach her for help. She always finds something to take points off of during her long drawnout assignments and has some of the most boring lectures I've been in. Have fun in this one!

Supposed to be an easy class, She sees it differently. Notes every class that she will refuse to send to any student regardless of the excuse. group projects that she gives zero information on how to do. HATES phones a LOT. Extremely bias view on the entire Healthcare subject. If you don't agree with her, you are wrong. Wouldn't recommend

Bring your laptop, and get ready to take notes. She's a bit of a stickler about phones being out, so put them away. Would recommend bringing a pillow too, cuz her lectures are a snoozefest. Very reasonable and understanding person. Group projects will be a nightmare if u have a bad group. Tests will go smoothly if you study a good amount.

Everyone told me that this class would be an easy A. She is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. She is not open to anyone's opinions other than her own and makes points for things that are not on the syllabus. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. You will regret it!!

The course doesn't have a textbook, rather Alicia sends out readings weekly, similarly to her other courses. She gives a lot of feedback, but is a very nice grader, and she makes sure everyone in her class is heard and a part of the conversation. Easily one of my favorite professors at Mizzou, I had her in two of my other courses, 3150 and 3160.
One of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. Please take a class with her if you get the chance, you wont regret it.

Alicia is the best Spanish professor I've had during my time here at Mizzou. She makes every lecture fun, wants to get to know every student and facilitates great conversation. She is understanding and is accessible outside of the classroom as well. Fairly easy grader, but you have to put in the work. I highly recommend this class!

Alicia is the best Spanish professor I have ever had. There is a lot of homework, but that is how you learn Spanish. If you don't care about learning the language, then don't take Alicia's class. But if you do, you will learn so much from her. She is super caring and easy going. I loved getting to be in her class.

The sweetest Spanish professor I have ever had. She would randomly call on people but she didn't single anyone out and understood if you didn't understand the question. I wanted to take my next Spanish class with her but the section is full :(

Amazing! I loved taking Spanish with Alicia! She really helped me improve my Spanish grammar. Reading the textbook really hopes as we focus on exercises based on the readings in class. Overall, she gives good feedback and makes sure everyone is putting in effort.

Super funny and always happy. She gave lots of pity points on tests and essays. Forced lots of class participation. She did everything she could to give you a good grade. However, I'm a mech. engineering degree and this one class had more homework than all my other classes combined. It was at least 7 pages of notes almost every night.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers
