reviews.comment: Alicia is great! She may seem intimidating at first, but she is very caring and also super funny. She gives good feedback on assignments, and is a relatively easy grader in my opinion. Come to class prepared for the compositions, it will make them so much easier.

Professor Avilones is one of my favorite Spanish teachers ever. It is clear that she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed in her class. The material is also explained very well and concepts that are not fully understood by the class are retaught. I can not recommend her enough.

Take her class! She can seem intimidating at first, especially if you are unsteady in your Spanish, but she really does want to help you. Try your best and go to office hours if you're having a bad time. Alicia is one of the main reasons I decided to pursue a dual-major with Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Profesora Alicia is an AMAZING instructor. 3160 was a zoom class this semester, but if you attend class and participate, you will succeed. It was laidback and discussion-based, where Alicia would call on students based on the homework grammar concepts. She sets clear expectations for the few exams and compositions, with reviews to use for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Alicia both semesters last year and she has been one of my favorite professors. She cares about the students and creates such a fun environment. If you try and do your homework, you will pass with an easy A. One thing I will say is that YOU have to want to learn, she will not push you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty much just attend class and participate. Alicia makes it easy by calling on students & cultivates a relaxed & fun environment. A few tests and compositions in the class but all very manageable as long as you put effort in class. Homework is basically optional. Very reasonable workload and you'll learn a lot and enjoy yourself!

Great teacher, super nice. Attendance is mandatory but I was late everyday and she never said anything. Participation is pretty important when you go to class. Tests are easy and she prepares you well. You'll have a good time in the class and you probably won't have to work very hard for a good grade.

Best professor I've ever had. Had her for two semesters in a row, and now having her write a letter of rec for me. She's funny, genuinely cares about her students, is passionate and honest, and makes students smile every class! She may sound a little harsh at times, but she wants you to succeed and is trying to help you!

There will be homework assigned to every class. If you do it, you will be better prepared and will succeed. She loves to hear from everyone and will engage you in conversation. She is light-hearted and is very passionate and an awesome teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Alicia is an amazing prof! She's not afraid to tell you what she thinks and that's a refreshing thing coming from a professor when it's from a good place (and with her, it definitely is) Participation is important, her syllabus and structure are flexible. She's willing to talk about anything in class as long as it's in Spanish.

Alicia was an interesting professor. She hardly uses technology so she doesn't use Canvas. Her class schedule is super loose and relies mostly on conversation. Can get too political at times, but that's mostly to foster discussion. Easy grader. Goes extra mile for students. Really funny and easy to talk to.

This was my first college-level Spanish class and I really enjoyed it. Three presentations throughout the semester, two recorded interviews, and a group project at the end. Go to class to participate, it will help and you can't get better if you don't go. Alicia is very nice but is a little too political at times. Otherwise, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I thought I actually enjoyed Spanish until I took this class. The material wasn't helpful (study the book all the time if you actually want to remember the grammar) and the students were all idiots and didn't even try (not sure why any of them are taking the class) so she hated the whole class and made us feel like idiots. It's a great time. 2/10
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Alicia just wants to see improvement in your writing and wants to help everyone succeed - everyone I know got at least a 90% on every composition. You have to go to class, but you'll want to because she makes it fun. One class we literally discussed which celebrities we thought were attractive and argued over it (in Spanish obviously)

She just wants to have fun and make sure you know how to speak the basics. Talk about anything you want, as long as you're talking in Spanish! Never did a homework assignment, all we had to do was find one relevant news article to discuss during class.

Not a lot of homework, mainly just read the news and show up ready to talk to classmates. Usually doesn't call on people but do receive a participation grade. Mostly presentations about different topics, but not too bad if you prepare! Usually a really fair, easy grader.

She is dope!! Super easy class, pretty sure everyone in my class (who showed up) received a B or higher. As long as you show up you'll be fine. She grades presentations/projects extremely easy. You do not need to do the textbook homework - she didn't check once- but do look at the news beforehand, she'll ask every day. Joke around with her too!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Although I don't feel like my Spanish improved that much over the course of Span3150, Alicia is a kind professor who is funny in class and has really reasonable expectations about where everyone's Spanish abilities should be. Virtually no homework besides some class presentations and group projects. Overall a great professor to have for 3150.

She has everyone sit in a circle. Doesn't tend to call people out but be prepared to share out reactions and analysis on the readings daily. The material is abstract and difficult-all Borges, all semester. Her tests are essay questions. She doesn't grade very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the most thoughtful and engaging professors I've had at Mizzou! Tests were easy and based on exactly what was learned in class. Professor Quiñones was always understanding if you had to miss class for a reason. She is always there for her students and willing to help if you do not understand something. Would definitely recommend!

Alicia encourages you to participate in class discussions. She didn't lecture much, but sometimes she taught us grammar that was very helpful. She has a great sense of humor. Projects are not hard as long as you take some time to prepare and she gives out very good grades. Would definitely take her class again.

Quiniones is awesome...She is very engaging with students. Helpful when needed. She is funny and very interesting to listen to so there is never a dull moment in class. Class is definitely mandatory so I suggest not missing any classes.

Prof. Aviles-QuiÃ±ones is very helpful and very passionate about literature. She encourages classroom discussions and genuinely wants to help each student succeed and learn as much as possible. She adds a little humor to each class and is very accessible when students have questions or need help. All of her assignments are writing-intensive.
Great professor.  All stories in book are thoroughly explained by her in class.  Exams are based on discussions of short stories, very easy.

Dr. Petry covered the Swine section in BAP II; you must attend the lecture to learn what will be on the exams and quizzes. Her slide decks have few words, and the important things she says and will say are "this is on your exam". She provides a study guide and review section for her exam—sweet but strict overall good prof.

She cares and values students time. If you communicate with her, she can help out with anything! The group projects helped me gain confidence in working collaboratively and taught me the importance of asking for help when needed.

Dr. Petry is such a kind person who is truly interested in what she is teaching and it shows. Group work is heavy in her classroom so come prepared to work with others and share your ideas! Focuses more on projects that display your knowledge and less test heavy. Would absolutely take a course with her again.

Dr. Petry is a great teacher who truly cares about her students. Projects are detailed, but if you stay on top of them and check in with her before they're due, you'll get full credit. There are only two exams, and the study guide covers everything. Replies quickly to emails and will always help if you ask. She WANTS you to succeed. LOVED Dr. Petry

Dr. Petry is very knowledgeable. I had her for the swine section in Ani-Sci 1175. She doesn't have a lot of words on her slides, but uses a lot of pictures and graphs. Some of the slides were a bit disorganized, but that is the only critique I have. Other than that, she was nice, she had bonus points, and a study guide.

During her lecture for the swine section of BAP, she spoke to us like we were idiots, and constantly told us to "star" information that we would need to know, which seemingly felt like the entire presentation. She was very passionate and her lecture style was nice, but she needs to learn how to do her makeup, speak to us like adults, and condense.

Dr. Petry expects a lot from her students, but her expectations are never out of touch with reality. Her assignments are relatively straightforward, and the study guides she gives are helpful for the tests. She is willing to help with any issues that you might have in an understanding/nonjudgmental way, and she does care about her students.

Reversed classroom so you'll spend more time watching lectures outside of class than working in class. Very dry and not helpful in explaining things. Lectures are very slow and monotonous. Labs can be fun but are mostly math-based. Problems are generally easy if you like algebra. Extra credits are LONG but boost your grade a good bit.

The class is one big group project so the people you are with all semester will make or break the class. She is super helpful and she is almost always available outside of class. You can tell this is her passion and that she wants you to understand the material. Dr. Petry is a super fair grader and you will almost never fully miss a question. Slay.

Amy Petry is an amazing person. She makes connections with all of her students and wants to be an active part of their learning experience. She never hesitates to answer questions, even late at night. She wants you to be able to apply the things you learn in her class to the real-world. She and Dr. Spain are the gems of CAFNR.

When class starts, Dr. Petry makes it clear she wants you to write down what she is saying, not necessary what is on her slide. At one point when the class asked her to go back, she was like 'The slides are posted, this is recorded and continued. She knows her stuff and a lot about it, but makes it very hard to keep up. She did give a study guide

Taught the lab section of 3242. The lectures were easy to follow and understand, but if you struggle with math, lab is hard. Luckily she gives out a lot of partial credit and that saved my grade on the lab calculation exam. My one complaint is that she was never really present during lab and her TAs were the ones to answer questions and help us.

Dr. Petry get negativity from people who don't care and end up struggling. She is the queen of partial credit, putting something down is likely to get you some points. She is encouraging in class, projects, and your professional career. She is concise about her teaching. She expects the best from her students and you'll thank her in the long run.

Dr. Petry wants you to write down what she says and not what is on the slide and then will only test you over the material on the slide. She zooms through her lectures and yells at students when they ask her to slow down. She knows her stuff but doesn't know how to communicate it to students. It is always the student's fault and not hers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: took this online event planning class as an upper-level area course for my major. we were thrown into a semester-long group project, having to meet virtually, even when our schedules  didn't align. we also had to meet with a community partner, which felt like an unpaid internship in a career field i wasn't pursuing. overall, communication lacked.

I've taken a couple classes with Amanda and always enjoy them. She can be a little strict with late/missing assignments, just communicate ahead of time and you'll be fine. Big presentation at the end of the semester, start early. She's a little intense with questions, but it's to help your final submission be great. Will happily take again.

I previously left an amazing review for her, however having her for more classes, my original rating does not reflect her current teaching. She is nice, her low level courses are easy. Higher level courses are horrible. Everyone dreads presentations with her. She will tear into you. She rarely responds to emails and provides little feedback.
Excellent teacher who cares about the subject and her students. Easy to talk to outside of class. Attendance through iClicker. Tests were open-book and open-note.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Alexander is by far and away the worst professor I have ever had at Mizzou.  She is a horrible communicator.  Gives no guidance on the semester long group project.  You also for some reason have to volunteer for 24 hours at a “community partner”.  Stay far away from this class if possible.
the easiest class i have ever taken. all homework assignments and exams were on quizlet. attendance does count for a grade

I took this as an asynchronous class and was surprised to find out we would be doing a semester long group project and meeting with Dr. Alexander multiple times. Communication was lacking at all times and the syllabus for the group project was very unclear. She is kind and forgiving, but it's overall been a very irritating experience.

This class does give great information but every lecture Dr.Alexander will try to call on the class instead of just teaching which can be frustrating. This class also counts attendance and makes it mandatory to do more out-of-class work than my 4000 level classes. You will be forced to do multiple volunteer events on top of the class for a grade.

Dr. Alexander was a great professor, I took her intro to hospitality class in the fall and it was great. An easy A as long as you do the 1 weekly assignment and exams. The only complaint I have was that she would open iClicker for attendance and close the class within 2 mins of opening it, so if you were late you pretty much missed out on that.
Super easy class. Test questions pulled straight out of the book, and the tests were open note open book. All your grades are quizzes, but it doesn't matter because the quizzes are so easy.

She takes attendance every day using tophat. It was a Mon,Wed, Fri class but she cancelled all Friday classes the first day of school. All exams are open note/book and online outside of class. Make sure you show up and take notes on the lecture and guest speakers and it will be an easy A.

You sometimes use the book, you will need it. The test are online, not that difficult if you go to class. You get points for attendance so go. Take notes during class and look over the power points and you'll do fine. She is always there to help and is very nice.  Easy class to take, I recommend if you're looking for a class.
so sweet and will do whatever she can to help you. Tests are super easy online and as long as you come to class and take notes it's the easiest A you will get. No final and mostly guest speakers.

Pretty much the most adorable teacher ever.  With that said, she also is supper involved.  I've had her as a teacher and a faculty advisor, and she is selfless and genuinely cares about all of her students.  She is the only teacher that I actually enjoy listening to in class.  You can learn a lot from her as a teacher and in general

One of my favorite professors I've had here at Mizzou. Made the class interesting and was very clear on what was expected. Also was very understanding if you make a mistake. Also the online homework was a little childish but easy points and interesting as well. Great class with a great professor

Amanda is an awesome teacher! She truly cares about her students and wants to see them all succeed. Her class material is very good, there are many interesting guest speakers, and the test aren't very hard at all. Great class and teacher!

Amanda is sooo nice. She tries really hard to keep interest in the class even on low-attendance days (which there are a lot of). She has a lot of guest speakers-some aren't the best, but some are really impressive. Homework is online, pretty easy completion points. Only 3 online open book tests and no final. Well covers the basics of hospitality.
She's one of the nicest teachers out there. She actually cares how her students do and gives multiple chances of extra credit with online exams. Easy class and a good teacher!

Loved Amanda! she's a young girl who is passionate about the hotel/restaraunt industry. she will go out of her way to make sure that you are headed down the right path as you further your studies in hospitality. very easy class, tests are a little difficult but there are other assignments to cushion your grade. i highly recommend her and this class
Attendance matters, no homework, in class participation, online tests, group work, and lots of notes. would take her class again

She loves to involve her students in what she's teaching and won't lecture at you the whole time. Fun group activities in class. Exams are online open note, few assignments. Final project she is STRICT about the use of AI and has strict guidelines. She is very nice, and very acedemic.

I adore Professor Elkhalid! She made contemporary theory so much fun at UARK and I want to have her again for another class. She also appreciates feedback on the assignments and lots of it is group work or a paper, but she makes it fun! Attendance is mandatory but didn't affect my grade for the days I did miss and homework is due before class!

Amnee is GREAT! This was her first semester at the University of Arkansas and she was fabulous. She's extremely kind and cares for her students. If you turn in your work on time, completed to your best ability, and show up to class, you will do great in her course. She is always open to feedback and makes the classroom a fun and safe environment!!!

Amnee is a great professor because she's always super excited about the material that she's teaching, even if the material itself isn't super exciting. She's also a fair grader and you should do fine if you follow the rubric.

Amnee is amazing!! I would highly recommend having her as an instructor. Awesome learning environment and this course was one of the most "real life" application classes I have taken in college. She is so kind and organized too.

Most of your grade is determined by attendance and speeches. If you miss more than three classes Amnee reduces your grade by a letter grade. She is a super cool professor that makes the class feel personal and also making it know that she cares greatly about the subject as well as her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amnee is an awesome teacher!! She's easy to talk to and cares about her students. I learned SO much from her! You do have to read, so be prepared for that but if you follow instructions, put in effort, and actually do what you are supposed to, she's super understanding. I can honestly say I enjoyed going to this class every day!

She's a super hard grader for no reason. Like everyone got points taken off of their first speech for MINOR reasons. She is cool and interesting, and you can tell she cares about her students and the class, but her grading is the downfall of that class.

Amnee is genuinely one of the best teachers I have ever had. She actually cares about our success and is incredible warm and open. She loves teach, and this shows through her incredibly easy to understand her lectures. Plus, she's awesome to talk with! I consider her more of a friend than I do a teacher.
Amnee genuinely cares about her students well-being and education. Id recommend a class with her.
Do not take! Doesnt take grading seriously. Entire class did poorly speeches without explanataion.
Dr. Knopps is genuinely the nicest director I have ever had. You can tell she really cares about her students, and absolutely no one could do as good of a job as she does.

Dr. Knopps is very passionate about music as a whole and she makes marching band feel very special and not so much as a class. She does a great job managing an ensemble this large. I had an amazing experience with all the games and the bowl trip, and I'll definitely be coming back for a second year.

It was an ensemble so there isn't a lot to say. Expectations were pretty clear but use of rehearsal time was questionable at times. I think the band pulled the last concert together pretty well but beware that the pieces you really need to work as a group may get sidelined by whatever the TA is conducting.

Truly THE BEST band director in the land. Dr. Knopps cares so much for M2. She so frequently advocates for her students, and makes an effort to know all 350+ of us. She holds M2 to a high standard so that we can be truly great, but also inspires fun. She is highly organized and professional, and by far the best professor I have ever had at Mizzou.

I would highly reccomend doing band with Dr.Knopps.  She cares alot about the band and their health and she truely does show that on the way she welcomes everyone to M2.  She truely does make the band seem more like a family.

Literally the greatest of all time. She clearly cares a lot about the band and the people in it and wants us to succeed. She gives plenty of breaks and is understanding when the weather is poor. Marching band is tough in general and can be a lot of work at times, but Dr. Knopps makes it feel like home.
She hurts future music educators more more than she supports them. Which is just ironic and sad

There aren't enough words to say how much I absolutely love Dr. Knopps. She is organized, fair, precise, and just wonderful in every way. I have her for marching band, and there is no one who could do this job like she can. She sees everyone in a 340+ person organization, and she is understanding and also very funny.
super caring and super hard-working -- and expects you to be, too

Dr. Knopps really cares about students and Marching Mizzou. She works really hard to make sure that the band looks and sounds good. She can be a bit much but that's what it takes for M2 to be as good as it is.

Dr. Knopps is such a gem. Love her to death. She really loves what she does and the students she teaches. She plans out her Marching Mizzou and Symphonic Band rehearsals down to the minute! She is easy to contact--replies to emails within 30 minutes to an hour. Dr. Knopps was one of my absolute professors and I can't wait to work with her again!

Dr. Knopps truly cares for each of her students. She cares for their health, mental state, and their academics. She makes the course and each rehearsal enjoyable, which makes everything easy. She is a very organized, detailed, and respectable person as she holds her head up high and proudly represents the University of Missouri.

You can tell Dr. Knopps really does cares a lot about M2. But unfortunately, her crave for perfection has turned a fun activity into a dystopian nightmare. She has an overarching tendency to micromanage every little thing & completely ignores constructive criticism. Band is supposed to be a "family", she says - but in reality, it's a business.

Dr. Knopps is extraordinarily organized, highly professional, and passionate about Marching Mizzou. She plans each rehearsal down to the minute and sends detailed information each day about the upcoming rehearsal, future performances, and other events. She respects every student and listens to feedback very well. She loves Mizzou most of all. <3
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took Archst 4325 (Energy Efficient Building Design) and he was an amazing professor. While the homework assignments were a little lengthy, there were only 3-4 throughout the whole semester. His lectures and quizzes were also not too bad, and you have a couple attempts if you didn't understand on the first one.
Aman is great! He is very strict with his standards, but also very clear about them. Everything he has you do is for a good reason, he has good intentions. He wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good. Started off harsher but accepted criticism and became very sweet.
Not an open minded professor; always had comments and was always docking, no matter what.

This was a great class to take! Very informative and relatively easy. Prof. Rose is super nice and very helpful if you need to reach out although she can take a little while to respond sometimes. You do have to read research papers which can be tough but she really eases you into it. Definitely recommend!

Professor Rose is great! There are quite a few writing assignments over the articles you read for the class, but she gives you time in class to go through each one and really understand it before you write the paper. The material is interesting, and the grading is pretty easy, as long as you do the work.
awesome professor! super nice and easy to approach! always willing to stay after class or meet up to help with whatever you need.  Really easy and interesting! Amazing capstone!!

She reminds me of a kindergarten teacher, but not in a patronizing way at all - just caring and informative, although quiet.  Her research is very interesting, the class was fun, and she's pretty open students presenting their own views and ideas or discussions.
Be ready to take notes, she is a very fast talker, and that's not just how she lectures, she is the same in her conversations.  Be attentive, and take good notes, and you will be fine.

She's a terrific teacher, and she does interesting research centered on children's friendships.  I loved her class (so did my non-psych major friends), and she's a caring, interesting, and dedicated teacher!

Dr. Appold is fantastic. He was willing to round my grade at a 84.5 to a 85 and I honestly really appreciated it. This put me at an A- in the class and I cannot be more thankful. Geology was hard, but I learned a lot and am very content.

This class expects you to be heavily knowledgeable in the field. The class really is only two grades. The homework is long, but only 2 points for each assignment, so it does not really help you in the end. Terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade in this class rest only on two test: the midterm and the final. Labs take hours to complete and are only worth completion grade. The grade scale should speak to how hard this class is. A 60% is considered a C. DO NOT TAKE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I only have 350 characters to let you know how much I hate this class. That isn't enough. I'd need a billion word count just to scratch the surface about how much I hate this class. But I'll start by saying I am only four weeks in, and I felt the need to come on here and warn everybody. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Everything is done through Canvas, but the class page couldn't have been more confusing. Everything is uploaded into one module, lectures are disorganized and not focused on specific chapters, and there is very weekly minimal communication. Only saving grace is the grading scale which has a C- at 55%, which should speak to how rough the class is.

Absolutely loved my experience with GEOL 1050 online. Appold does a great job of bringing real-world examples into the lectures to help you understand the concepts. The biweekly quizzes are challenging, but the instruction is very clear and the expectations are straightforward. Definitely recommend as an elective if you are interested in rocks!

If you enjoy mind numbing lectures and someone reading off of a powerpoint slide then this course is for you! This class was incredibly boring and Appold is more or less just going through the motions of teaching. He uses an artificial intelligence program (Packback) to grade your discussion which shows how much he actually cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is actually a fine teacher and is passionate about the material, but his grading/test/quizzes are so ridiculously hard. He has a generous grading scale (90-100% is an A, etc) but he makes his quizzes and lab exams so difficult it's almost impossible to even benefit from the grading scale. Material isn't extremely difficult he just tests HARD.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Appold's lectures are phenomenal if you are interested at all in physical sciences. He provides the background information and evidence to what he teaches, making them seem more "real".  The exams and quizzes are somewhat difficult and you'll have to study. He posts old ones online.  The lab part of this course is mediocre though. Waste of time.

By far the most boring class I've ever taken in college.  He repeats him for 50 minutes until he runs out of time to talk. Class is easy for the most part but he makes lecture unbearable. Nobody shows up and the people that do are usually half asleep. Wouldn't recommend.

Boring class, he teaches the same thing over and over until he finds something new to say. The Lab portion of the course is terrible. There is no instruction on how to complete the assignments and you'll be lucky to get above an 85% on the lab assignments. Do not take this class.

I really like his class. His teaching style is very easy to get along with. If you don't go to class, you won't have trouble with the material. He posts slides on Blackboard right after the class. The is not really difficult; just come to class and review the slides carefully, you will get A from this class.

The books are very hard to find, the lab manual is impossible.  The course seems pretty outdated.  You will be frustrated by each assignment, digging through lots of text to end up getting a C.  If you're not careful, you will lose points very quickly.  I wouldn't recommend this as an easy class to take online.  There are other, better classes.

Knowledgable but talks at you for most of class. Patronizing and often blatantly disrespectful to students. Assumes student time revolves around her and never gives a direct answer to a question. Assigns hundreds of pages of reading per class and will require that you buy 10+ books. Really wanted to love this class but regret taking.

Dr. Langley so clearly cares about her students and the material she is teaching. Yes, you have to work for it but that's how college should be anyway. I ended the class with over 100 percent. Do your work and show up to class. It's worth it and she's awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Really condescending. Treats students like they're 5 years old. Wastes a lot of class time rambling on about how we shouldn't waste class time. 50+ pages of reading per night. Participation in discussions is mandatory. Gets off topic a lot and rambles on about nothing. Don't take a class with her, you'll regret it.

Awesome professor. She is very clear about what she's looking for so if you read the syllabusrequirements then there is no reason for you not to get an acceptable grade. Ive taken her class online & 1 n person, she knows what she's talking about. She might delve deep into the conversation but id rather do that than only read textbooks & lecture

She never returned a single grade throughout the class, so you were left wondering what your grade was until you got it, and most of us were not amused. She also speaks on a soapbox about a lot of things, and is usually late to class. Avoid.

This was a great class for me. She talk a lot and often went to deep into discussion of topics, but overall she is a great teacher. Make sure you NEVER mess up her format or deadline requirements or you will be screwed!! Enjoy her class!! And make sure you participate.

Hands down, the absolute BEST Professor I've had in my college LIFE! Her syllabus is crystal clear, this woman is thorough and intelligent! I believe only the STRONG will survive in her class, and the WEAK ones who only want a degree are exposed from the little effort that they put into the work. She gives extra credit, so how can 1 not get an A?

She's awful. I don't think there's a better word to describe her. She lectures on her own soap box, she grades impossibly hard (and half of her comments are opinion), and she thinks she's outstanding. Avoid this class at all possible cost--the reading material is interesting but this class is impossible and dreadful, all thanks to Dr. Langley.
She was horrible. She is just a nasty person. I have had a lot of teachers here, and she is the only one i didn't like. She treats people like kids, and shes always late

i had her for African American Hist (beginning to 1900). The class wasn't overwhelming but she is an incredibly difficult person. Most of class time was wasted while she stood on her soap box and talked about things irrelevant to the class material. She treated us like we were children at times, which was very demeaning.

This was a new course and Bass did a wonderful job setting it up. There was a lot of reading and writing, but she pushed back deadlines all the time. The class was not ready for all of the requirements (over half of us were not ANTH majors) so she dropped the final exam and spent class helping us finish the papers. She cares!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Caring

reviews.comment: She definitely cares about the material. And she taught through cancer!
Not my major, but the class was pretty interesting.

I came into this class excited because i was interested in the field, but after this class, i never want to talk about anthro again! Her exams were unbeliveably hard (half from lecture/half from book) and the book was so big that even if you read it, you would have no idea what parts would be on the test. I recommend you don't take this course!

I have a mixed feeling toward this class. While the topic was explained thoroughly, the tests were ridiculously hard. You definitely have to do all the readings and study for each test. She was absent, due to illness, which added to the difficulty. Switching between her teaching style and guest speakers was no fun.

Professor Bass is extremely hard. I was very excited about taking this class and now i hate it. Her tests are impossible. You dont know where the material is coming from. You have to read very carefully and make sure you remember details because her tests are very detail oriented. If you can take this class with a different professor, do it.
Best teacher I have ever had/will ever have! Overall just a great person and she is someone that needs to be a teacher!

By far the best prof i have ever had! So much fun in class and always willing to help and go out of her way to help any student! Supper funny and knew her stuff! She is the best prof to ever teach at Westminster College has done amazing things for the college!
She was one of the best teachers I have ever had.  She was funny and knew what she was talking about.  I would recommend her to anyone!
My favorite proffessor during my first semester of college.

She scared me a little at first, but she's actually really cool. If you do your readings and stuff you will be fine on the tests. She knows you don't care about Bio so she makes it applicable to the modern world. If you have to take a science, she's a good one to take.

I am not a Biology fan but Mrs. Potterfield made this class interesting for me. She introduced modern topics for subject matter when applicable and was always on top of questions and suggestions to keep class interesting and easy to learn in.
Really good teacher, interesting class. I don't like bio, but it was a good class to get my gen. ed. out of the way. She makes sure she's on top of current issues.
just like highschool biology, quizes are harder than exams
very fun teacher, likes to use up to date examples
Best teacher ever. Granted, it was a super easy class, but she was amazing.

I was genuinely kind of suprised to see many bad reviews. I thought that she really put in a lot of effort and was quite involved which a lot of professors aren't. As long as you do the work, I can not imagine why you would be getting anything less than an A in this class.

Amy was the class coordinator for my J1400 class. She would often interrupt our class time to 'inform us' on information that was already sent in emails and was often blatantly disrespectful to myself, my peers and my professor. I would never recommend taking one of her classes and try to get a J1400 professor that has a class far away from amy.

She is blatantly disrespectful towards all of her students. She always treats the students like they are embarrassing her and will correct them harshly in front of others, so she looks like the hero. She is insanely disorganized in a meeting when everyone was supposed to be able to ask questions; she missed 5+ groups.

I found this class to be pretty easy. I only got a B because I didn't do a lot of the discussion boards. There are quite a few assignments every week, but some are as simple as taking a 5 question quiz. There are SO many extra credit opportunities that are also fairly simple. Overall, I enjoyed the class, but it does take some time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She took 10 points of an essay bc i called it a PHOTO instead of a SNIPPET and when i emailed her very kindly asking why i lost points, she literally called me by the wrong name, so she has standards she cant even hold herself to.

If you can, avoid taking ANY classes with Amy Simons. She takes things from level 1 to 100 all the time. It seemed like her goal was for us to fail her class. She gave us all these loop holes to jump through with no sympathy or leniency of any kind. She wants up to think outside the box just to criticize us for doing so. The worst prof I ever had.
Very harsh grader, and is always looking for you to do more. Does offer extra credit, allowing you to keep your grade up, but definitely expects too much out of you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I was honestly surprised to see so many bad reviews here. I had a very easy time taking this class and ended up with an A+. I would say the only downside to this class was that it took a lot of time, but it is an 8-week course after all. If you take this class, make sure to follow the modules in order as it makes it a lot easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was honestly so easy. Do the work and get an A+. If you do the 3 extra credit assignments, you don't even have to do the last 3 assignments. All these other reviews are misleading. Take this course for an easy A+.

This semester was filled with rude comments and countless pointless emails. The last straw was in the final week when she posted a quiz for the wrong week on Canvas, then blamed 125 students for not submitting it because they needed to study the paper calendar and refused to give them makeup points.

Amy's emails are constant, critical, and condescending. If I wanted this attitude, I'd just text my ex. Her grading makes no sense—expect to lose points for things not on the rubric, and don't ask for clarification unless you enjoy being made to feel stupid. Want real investigative journalism? Figure out why she's still employed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I chose "online savvy" as a tag, but I meant "online SASSY" because Amy is rude and condescending. Expect 5+ emails a week, most of which are unnecessary complaints. One of the worst was her Monday gripe about low assignment submissions due Friday—hello, we're college students! This class felt unnecessarily stressful. Amy Simons do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: By far the rudest professor I've ever had. I've heard from several people she views her low rating on this site as a point of pride and I'd just like to say - Amy, if you ever see this, you are failing your students and your school as a matter of selfishness. You have spoken to me in ways I would scream in your face for if you weren't a professor.

I took the 8-week journalism class for non-majors. It was a heavy workload, but it was not necessarily difficult work. She was a little harsh on the grading sometimes and gave aggressive feedback. However, if you complete the homework ahead of time, you will be fine in this course. It felt like I was writing papers weekly. Lots of extra credit.
She was very rude. Rude when adding comments to papers.
Don't take her class if you don't have to, you're welcome.

The class itself was easy to the point I felt like I was wasting money. On the extreme opposite side of things, the professor was incredibly rude and approaches any sort of conversation as conflict. As a communication professor, you'd think she would understand how to bring up topics with a calm and cooperative approach. I would not recommend.

All Amy Simons does for this course is send out rude announcements. This class hasn't been updated in years, I assume. X is still called Twitter, and there were links to posts that have been removed on the final. This course is a waste of time and a money grab for the J-School.
Truly the worst communicator I have ever met. I have many bad things to say about Amy, but believe me when I tell you to never take a class offered by her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I might be the odd one out but I enjoy Amy! She's giving my feedback where you can tell she actually enjoys her job! It's so in-depth and almost conversational. The class is pretty easy as long as you follow the material more stamina then difficulty in my opinion!

I didn't realize how big of an issue other people had with her like I did. Her TAs were good at critiquing and were always nice (Amy herself rarely graded my stuff). But she was always incredibly demeaning in her announcements and made things harder on us than needed. Work wasn't that hard, but she made it so stressful and blamed all issues on us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I wish that I could say something different about Amy but unfortunately I cannnot. After several interactions, she belittled me and others during a press conference and pitch meeting for one of our projects. Simply put, as an educator, Amy spends her time demeaning students instead of actually teaching them solutions to be a better journalist.

So little information was given to our class, yet so much had extremely specific rules and requirements for grading. During our first project she came to our class and spent the hour lecturing us on everything that we had been doing wrong and how stressful this was making her life. She was rude answering our questions and often spoke down to us.

Just finished the J1400 press conference, and I am in complete awe. Amy was ruthless during this entire process. First off, there was no reason for her to be speaking during the interview, but she chose to be extremely belittling and disrespectful to every single student in the room. Hope no one has to experience the shame and embarrassment I did.

First of all, I have never received such a rude and belittling email until Amy sent a course-wide email threatening to lower our project score by 10 points for simply communicating when she couldn't. Secondly, she attacked my group and others at the press conference and treated us with no respect. Relieved she's only my course coordinator.

She has a very harsh typo/spelling policy during quizzes and would not allow for alternate spelling (like UK) even if a source of spelling was attached. She was also course coordinator for another class I had and yelled at everyone during group projects for doing them "wrong" even though she created vague directions.
One word rude

In my experience, Amy DOES NOT suffer fools. Meaning, if you're a student who is just trying to slide by and put in as little effort as possible, Amy will sniff that out and will be tougher on those students. For those who really care about journalism and have enthusiasm about the actual profession, she's your biggest advocate and supporter.

The class and content were easy but I wouldn't recommend Amy as a professor. She grades discussions way too subjectively. She will always find a way to take points off even when you technically meet all the rubric requirements. The assignments are also tedious, due at weird times, and don't make sense when it comes to journalism.

I've NEVER had this many issues with a professor at Mizzou before. She is the rudest professor I've ever had, both in class announcements and personal communication. She sets weird due dates for assignments and will NOT accept late work. I heard this class would be an easy A. The content isn't hard, but it's so much annoying busy work.
Lots of tasks due at odd times, very little flexibility on deadlines. Class felt a bit pointless.

Professor Simons's assignments often felt tedious and unnecessarily rudimentary. This fault may be more on the class itself, but the presentation was monotonous and grating. Prof. Simons is not understanding of external circumstances and emergencies, and is quick to put policy over her students.

Took the online journalism for non journalism class. Class was a free A. The assignments were easy but extremely tedious and often useless. Absolutely no extensions unless for religious/medical reasons. didnt watch any of the lecture videos, just did the assignments and finished with a 108. Felt rude through class announcements and emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's kinda tough in terms of grading and doesnt take any late work, but as long as you turn in your work on time its not too bad

Professor Simons took over my J1400H course midway through the semester. Yes, she is a stickler for late work, Her critiques can be blunt, but they come from a place of love/wanting her students to thrive. She prepares her students incredibly well for the world post-grad, and has lots of knowledge to share. I would take a class of hers again 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you need an easy humanities credit, take this class. As long as you do your work on time and follow directions, you'll get an A. Beware that she doesn't accept late work though, so if you are the type of student that doesn't turn work in on time, don't take this class. Professor is a total pain and very unfriendly, but the course is easy.

Disrespectful and overbearing. As the course director for J1400, she attended one of our classes to critique our branded website final project. She took the "constructive" out of constructive criticism, loudly ripping into another group for not understanding the project, even though her expectations for the project were unclear on Canvas.

She wasn't even the main teacher of this class, but just one day with her was enough. Just all around disrespectful and just mean. She didn't really seem like she wanted to help us students, moreover, it seemed like she just wanted to be correct and discourage us.

She refuses to work with students. She blames a lousy quiz grade on my computer, even though I sent proof of work and turned the quiz in over a week early. Obviously does not want to see students succeed.
She was very rude and non understanding. Seems like she does not care about students. Only seems like she cares about being right.

She is straight up one of the meanest professors I've ever had. If you act like you hate your job and hate all your students you're in the wrong profession. If you give your students no respect I don't understand how we are supposed to give you respect back. Just awful professor I highly don't recommend.

There was a misunderstanding with a project I did where I should've received credit where I didn't. I emailed her about it and she was very dismissive and refused to give me points even when I pointed out that the rubric matched the work that I submitted. I wouldn't have minded if she was willing to work with me but she wasn't.
This professor was just mean sometimes and seemed unwilling to work with students. I have a feeling she is a nice person outside of class but as a teacher she is condescending and unreasonable.

This class is an easy humanities credit. She makes it seem like you are going to learn way more than you actually do. The group project may suck if your group members don't help and you actually have to put effort into the discussions, but I still recommend it. Easy 8 weeks.

class was easy but Amy was the worst professor I've ever had. This is an easy J1000 class and she acts like it is the most crucial class you will take in your entire life. The group project sucks because some people won't pull their weight and everyone gets penalized for it.

This class is a journalism class for non journalism majors and it was easy. If you followed the directions you would get a 100%. She also gives extra credit which is helpful. Truthfully if I did the extra credit that was worth like 40 points I wouldn't have had to do the final paper which was easy as well.

I'm not sure what people disliked about this professor! Her online J4160 class was great. It was easy if you did the work and also very fun! I loved the projects. I also really appreciated that she reached out to me to congratulate me on my high performance. This teacher is also very knowledgable of journalism. She does not allow late work.

At one point we had to do some reporter game online and it literally wouldn't work on my computer. Tried 3 times and had to resort to my phone and best response we got when the entire class was having problems was "Whelp, should've let me known 12 hours in advance to get an extension." Outstandingly horrible teacher. Class is easy tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class was an easy blow off. Simons on the other hand is the worst professor I've ever had to deal with. She does not care about your circumstances and try's to make everything a teaching moment, she thinks her class is so important when it was mind numbingly easy. Do the work her way and you'll be fine

She's alright. Never turn in anything late. Only problem I had was during our group assignment, I got penalized like 10% for one of our group members not responding which I literally couldn't do anything about so that sucked

Listen guys. I've had many many professors throughout my academic career, and trust me when I say Amy Simons was one of the worst ones I have ever had. She seemed very annoyed any time there was an issue regarding course-work, and even when she gave feedback, I felt like it was more berating than it was actually helpful. BE AWARE.

Simons is terrible and I wouldn't recommend her if you're wanting to major in journalism. I thought this class would be inspirational and promote students to want to become a journalist but her grading and feedback is terrible. The assignments are doable but she doesn't care what you put down. She'll email you her opinion then give u a lower grade.

Worst experience with a human being ever. Failed me for one late assignment (my fault ik) and I immediately emailed her. She told me I couldn't make it up, and that I should drop. Then adds me to next semester canvas before seeing if Im enrolled. I wasn't. Had to take 3 TIMES. Condescending, full of herself, god awful. Not for the easily offended.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely no chance you can submit late work. She is a little condescending and thinks she's the sh*t but it doesn't really affect the class. DO THE WORK ON TIME, that is what messed my grade up. Other than that, if you do the work exactly how she asks you will get 100% on every assignment. Turn everything in on time and its an easy A.

I took this class for a humanities credit. The class was totally online, but I learned more about the field of journalism. She is very strict when grading, so make sure you follow the directions EXACTLY. There were tons of extra credit opportunities as well. If you do your work and the extra credit you will get an A incredibly easily.
I loved Amy! She is very understanding and wants her students to succeed. If you ask for help, she will always give you feedback and help you understand the topic better.
Amy Simons was very rude and condescending throughout the whole course. 0/10. Literally transferring schools.
worst professor ever

I learned everything for this class last year in my first semester of journalism classes. The class is easy, nothing to worry about. Simons says she wants you to ask questions, DONT! I asked a question about one of our assignments and was responded with an informal email with horrible attitude. Many of my friends have received the same treatment.
There is a ton of extra credit. I didn't even do the final paper and still received an A. This is a great course to take as a humanities credit.

Amy Simons claimed, after me being in her class for several weeks, that she had never seen my service animal, and tried to kick me and the service animal out of class. She then tried to force me to show proof of disability, all of this in front of the entire lecture hall. The class itself was easy but Amy was a big downside.

Although she may seem very condescending or full of herself, it doesn't have any effect on her actual teaching ability. She recognizes when students succeed and gives them a pat on the back. She makes herself available to students on the other side of the spectrum. Assignments are very easy and there are only two papers instead of any exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: J1010 is the easiest class you'll ever take. Amy Simons is the only downside of it. Luckily, it's mostly guest lecturers, because she tries way too hard to be funny and relatable. Also, she can be kinda condescending and rude to students. Go to class to get the quiz points so that you don't have to do the final paper.

She takes things very personally and as a result isn't empathetic to many students' struggles. She can be very passive aggressive and not professional. Felt like walking on eggshells in her in class. You never know what you'll say that will make her angry. If you're late to class for an understandable reason she'll berate you in front of the class.

VERY full of herself. She thinks very highly of herself and of no one else. She talks down to everyone and makes them feel less of a person. I only had her for an online class and I hope to never meet this woman in real life. If you like being treated like a dog then highly recommend
Very full of herself. Thinks she is miss prima donna of journalism. She is just rude and condescending. Also her lectures are super repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Very inaccessible. Very loud. Highly cocky and arrogant. Disliked her a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you like to be coached, you will like Amy Simons. She is very passionate about journalism. She did well to prepare our section for the real world of journalism. The class is getting out what you put in. If you work hard and engage, you will do well. She is very critical, but it is to your benefit. Also extremely willing to help outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Attendance quizzes every day and three papers are the only assignments. Guest speakers were usually good and interesting in this class. Professor Simons, on the other hand, was rude and often lowered herself to the level of her students with negative comments. Write extra length on papers if you want full points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you go to class and do ALL the assignments & online quizzes you'll be fine. She won't remind you, pay attention to the syllabus. Pro - You get assigned to 1 newsroom for the semester and do online audience development stuff for them. Con - Didn't leave the class w/ much skills. Felt like I could've learned most of it in a few lectures.

She treated the class as if it were a room of pre-schoolers. Her arrogance and condescending nature was unpleasant. The course was not difficult, however, a lot of the lectures were uninteresting and repetitive.

She is very inconsiderate and extremely conceited and cocky. She does not express concern about her student, but rather complains about her own personal problems to her students making us feel extremely uncomfortable. She preaches on not interrupting and being respectful, but she cannot practice her own ways. She picks on students publicly.

She's a very tough grader but also a very reasonable person and relatively fair. She's approachable and available outside of class. Overall, her class was tough but fair, and I worked hard to receive a pretty good grade. Also she's a solid 7.5/10.
Seems like a nice person, but is  really really tough
What can you really say about the quality of mathematics in missouri

He is overall not an awful professor but he is not great by any means. He does not care about his students instead he cares about his attendance sheet and taking petty points off of quizzes and test. Has a shirt temper and yelled at a student because they missed class because their car died. If you take his class every lecture is essential.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aritro seems to worry more about the attendance sheet rather than teaching mathematics. He is unable to teach material in a way that anyone can understand and he does not foster any class participation. Do not under any circumstances choose him for a class.
Aritro Pathak does not explain material in a way that is easy to understand. Does not foster any class participation and does not seem interested in the subject matter at all. Avoid at all costs.
Has the best attitude and makes it easy to enjoy the class
Great teacher my favorite

Doesn't respond to emails quickly, takes awhile to grade. Doesn't post any of her own course content, the class is entirely someone else's including lectures. Isn't always clear about expectations on assignments. Pretty decent amount of work considering she doesn't put any into the content.

Mara is a great professor. She is passionate about her work and accessible outside of class. Same expectations each week (2 lectures with a quiz, 2 video quizzes, 1 reading quiz). Class was interesting. Graded by a few things so be sure to maximize points.
Mara is a great professor. The class itself is a bit hard but there are the same expectations weekly (2 lectures 3 quizzes). She's accessible outside of class and passionate about her work.

I LOVED professor Aruguete. She is an amazing lecturer and doesn't emphasize big tests or papers. This style allows you to watch her lectures, take notes, and learn. There are quizzes every week, a midterm, and a final. However, her lectures are very enjoyable, and she is accessible by email. I would take classes from her again in the future!
Super easy class and seems like a nice professor! Interesting content and easy to follow along
Amazing professor, so kind and caring. She has a great personality and is so understanding. Her class was so well structured and easy. Highly recommend you take her class,
Literally loved her so much I struggled at the beginning but if you actually do this class and work in it its not difficult and the information stuck so easily

This class was pretty fun. There is a good amount of work (5 assignments) each week. But once you get used to the schedule it's really easy. The lectures were interesting, not very long, and she was very flamboyant.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easiest and most understanding professor I have had, allows extra credit which boosted my grade a ton, there is iclickers and if you miss 4 your grade will go down, overall super easy laid back professor.
Probably the easiest class to take for this credit. Show up, do the online work and you will do very well. No exams given out for this course or final.

Catherine is very nice and cares very much. Uses IClicker for attendance. Probably the easiest A I have ever gotten. The problem is her lectures are insufferable. Visual Studies should be moved to a political science class because politics is all she talked about. Its ridiculous how narrow viewed someone can be.
Highly recommend taking this class (coming from someone who had no prior interest in art history)

I took Armburst's Intro to Visual Studies lecture class. The content was very interesting, and the class was overall very easy to do well in as long as you came to class and did the simple online homework assignments. I think it may be meant as an easier course for freshmen getting used to college life. If that's the case, it was very good.

Shes very nice and very passionate about art. but i feel like she definitely made known her political view and i just dont think that needs to be brought up in my art class. for example In one of my lectures she had a guest speaker that was showing KKK hats that had " make America great again" sewed into the hat. just not appropriate in my opinion.

Every single day I went into Intro to Visual Studies I wanted to do a dance of joy. Her lectures were always a treat to go to. She was truly passionate about her lectures and would just throw in stuff to study for fun, like Kendrick Lamar's Super-Bowl halftime and Beyonce music videos. It's truly so rare to find a professor as passionate as her.

Easiest class I've ever taken - lectures aren't referenced in assignments and no tests. All the points are in short homework quizzes which are very easy, a couple discussion board posts and a very easy final project. You get four absences so you do need to show up but you don't have to take any notes. Great way to get some honors and gen ed credit.

Professor Armbrust is extremely kind and knowledgeable about her subject. Some of her lectures are more interesting than others, but they don't really count towards anything except participation points, which are important since you only get 4 absences. Homework is extremely easy.

She is one of the nicest people you will ever meet. If you are ever having a problem you can just go up and talk to her and she is very understanding. Class is an easy pass as long as you go and get your clicker points. She also gives out lots of extra credit! Would recommend!

She's okay. Lectures for this class sometimes felt like I wasn't learning anything and her politics definitely find their way into the class. Easy grade. Overall okay class probably just not my kind of thing

Easiest class I've ever taken, because all you have to do is show up for the attendance quizzes (which she gives the answer to at the end of class). There were a couple of other easy assignments as well. My one gripe was that she leaned on Sarah Green's Youtube way too much, but in general her lectures when I paid attention were interesting.

All of the lectures were incredibly compelling, and it was clear that Catherine always wanted to expose her students to as many perspectives as possible. She brought in multiple guest lecturers, and gave her own artist lecture as well.

Professor Armbrust is a great professor and I enjoyed her class because we got to talk about so many different topics on art. She tries her best to make a big lecture hall engaging and pulls examples from her personal life to try to connect with students. She made attendance mandatory about halfway through, but otherwise the classwork was light.

I only received a B+ because I missed the deadline on a few assignments but overall she's a super easy grader, very kind and understanding, and it's an easy A class if you need the credit. At one point she started to make attendance mandatory since she got too lazy to read assignments. She gives extra credit too.

Professor Armburst is the best Professor I have ever had. She turns a classroom into a fun environment that you look forward to going to. Other of being a great professor she does inspiring things in her personal life, always focused on how she can help others. Lectures are laid back & the homework is very light. I recommend this class 100%
Professor Armburst is very nice and has interesting lectures. The class itself is a very easy A. There are no exams, papers, or large projects so the class requires very little time outside lecture.

I loved taking this class and learning more about art. However, the class did not meet on a constant basis. Due to this, I felt like I did not get my moneys worth. She usually would not let us know if we had class until the day of, which mixed up my schedule. None of the classes were required, however.

I have learned so much in this class! All about art history and seeing things from a different perspective I feel like my life has changed. The material is fun and the professor works hard to make sure her students are on track and having a good time. Definitely recommend this for any major!

My favorite professor so far! Her class was such a nice break from others I was taking. We left the classroom a lot and had valuable real-world discussions everyday. I always looked forward to this class, and I can honestly say that having her as a teacher has changed my worldview. She's wonderful. I would recommend her classes to anyone.
Catherine is awesome. SUPER funny, very engaging, really cares about her students. Very non-judgmental regardless of your interests. Her senior seminar class was an absolute blast. She's great.

Dr. Fried is an amazing professor and person! She is very caring and understanding. I took WGST 2005 with her and absolutely loved it! Turn in your stuff on time, participate in class, and read the readings and you'll do well in her class.

Fried is really kind and very understanding.Very approachable if you need help with assignments or the readings.The reading is required to engage in class and participation is a decent chunk of the grade.Would recommend for Fried but didn't love the class material, it was a bit boring at times.Lectures can also be pretty dull if ppl don't engage

One of the nicest professors I have ever had. She is super caring and understanding towards her students. There was a lot of reading, but the readings were always really insightful and I use the knowledge I have from those readings in my other classes. The class I took (WGST-2005) was organized really well too.

She is a pretty good English teacher for ENG1000. You will pass her class no problem. There are 4 papers nothing awful. Just make sure you do the work and you'll get an A. There is 1 group project that is a 10-13 page essay, so make sure you pick good group members
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved her class. She really cares about her students, and gives really good feedback to make you a better writer.

Took this as a summer class and it didn't feel rushed at all. We were given plenty of time to do the work and readings. Papers were mostly "informal" but still took effort. I was never confused about what the prof wanted from us. She was very understanding and willing to work with me when I was having difficulties.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Ariel is super chill and personal. the class is smaller, maybe 25 people in it. She is fantastic about communication as far as papers and assignments go. She gives fantastic feedback and really cares about the student learning to write at a collegiate level. the reading sometimes feel a little pointless but she makes up for that with good lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Avery is great! She's very approachable during office hours, even for an online class. She's so cool I want to be her when I grow up.

I'm writing this to hopefully warn some people about SOCIOL3000. It's an engaged learning course and the entire class is a group project. This would be fine but the prof is extremely disorganized and expects students to have extensive background knowledge. She also got extremely defensive (almost hostile) when concerns about the class were raised.

She is an amazing professor! I took the course online, there was 1-2 video lectures each week and a discussion. There was two exams over the lecture content and a couple of easy projects. The course was organized and very clear about the expectations. She always worked with me if I had any problems, it is obvious that she cares about her students.

Easiest class. She gives you 2 weeks to do hardly any work, and the material is so simple, you definitely already know it. Occasionally, one week you'll get two 20-min lectures that you can watch on double speed and knock out assignments real fast. Dr. Avery doesn't do much for the class at all. This class is a joke.

Criminology is a fun and easy class. If youre interested in the topic and need an easy A, this is the class for you. Tests make up the majority of your grade, but if you know the lecture then they are the easiest tests ever. Only 10 attendances are accounted for, but they are crucial. She doesnt seem very confident in her teaching or material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a very boring lecturer. She does not use a mic and does not project her voice. Very disorganized in speaking and thought. I think her exams were all very poorly worded and written. It was required to do volunteering service hours, which was rewarding, but she had no idea what was going on with that for the entire semester.

Knowledgeable but lectures are not helpful. Reading the textbook is more effective. Practice exams offer some guidance, but each real test includes a very difficult surprise in at least one question. Heavy exam curves are the saving grace.

I found Professor Aura's teaching frustrating. Classes were just lectures where Professor Aura frequently rambled. The content was hard to follow, and he did not check in to see if we understood what he was teaching. More class participation and structure would've been helpful. Having our grade dependent on three exams did not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are just regurgitating the textbook word for word, so they were extremely useless if you simply did the reading. In fact, the reading was better than his lectures because he went over formulas extremely fast without explanations or relating it back to economics. Sample tests never reflected his actual exams.

Honestly...this class sucked. I just didn't really mesh with Saku's style of teaching. It's a very unorganized class and I felt that I didn't have what I needed to succeed. BUT an A is possible. Honestly get a good study group, teach yourself the material if you don't understand, and memorize the practice exams.

Worst professor I've ever had, but a nice person. His class consists of 3 tests (only 3 questions on the tests), and homework where only half counts for the grade. He said in class he hasn't taught 4315 since the 2000s and it shows in his poor teaching and tests. I've always gotten As and Bs in classes, this class was extremely hard for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very chill online class, a lecture or two a week over the material, definitely to be supplemented by the textbook. Then a few multiple choice quizzes pretty directly over textbook material and a 10-page case study that was graded easily. He was friendly, even through an online course, and accessible.

Worst prof EVER. Its ridiculously hard with 86% tests and the rest homework, which are easy but half do not count. His tests are incredibly difficult and he admits they were too hard after and heavily curves. Things he never taught are on exams. His lectures are not mandatory and he rambles a lot. While trying to discuss my grade he was very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: saku aura genuinely means well, but he rambles often and the exams are worth 84% of your grade and are rarely designed well. my advice is to skip the lectures, and use that time to study the textbook (especially the terms and graphs (and their corresponding math,)) homework, and lecture notes. attendance isn't mandatory, and exams are curved a LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't take the writing intensive version of this class, so my grade was made up of 6 proctored quizzes (2 dropped) and one 8-page case study. You'll need to read the textbook because his lectures are difficult to watch/listen to and very outdated. He responded to emails fairly quickly though and seems like a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Aura is a very knowledgeable professor and Urban Econ is a strength of his. He does have a fairly long and intensive writing assignment for the class that I really enjoyed. The tests could be considered to be difficult. He is very understanding when it comes to what we all "should" and "shouldn't" know. So, if homework is too hard, tell him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Aura makes himself available through the online forum readily. The material covered and testing were fair. I would really like take a lecture class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Teaching style is okay. Hard to attend at 8 am. No multiple choice on exams which is tough for the content. Final is comprehensive. Instructions very vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His PowerPoints don't make much sense if you don't attend. Doesn't have much homework and the grades rely heavily on the two exams. Will not give a clear direction on how to study for the exam. It's easier to score a better grade for the writing section. Knowledgable but only a few will like his teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Austin was an incredible TA, very helpful and wanted his students to succeed.
Dude was moved way too fast in the notes and just expected us to understand everything.
He's chill. Our class average is the highest of any other class.
Austin was my TA and he was funny. I would take his class again.

Austin Spratt is a TA. I had him for Math 1100 this past semester and he made it so enjoyable. He's hilarious and genuinely cares about your success in his class. He teaches at a pretty fast pace, but will always go over things if you don't understand. Austin literally made college students excited to go to math class. 10/10 would recommend.

Class was very discussion based and student led He will jump in I'm necessary to keep the conversation flowing in the right direction. Just be willing to share some opinion or thought on the reading. And be prepared to step out and have fun with the roll playing exercise at the end of the semester. Overall he is a professor that is there to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is almost entirely discussion based save for the final two weeks being a historical role play experiment. What this means is that you need to read and and speak in class. While there are essays that he will grade mercifully, you really only need to convince him that you are participating erego he is just there to help YOU do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 2 lecture days and 1 discussion day each week. Lectures are fine, he tends to go fast, so take pictures and just pay attention to the key terms. Don't join the honors discussion class unless you are ok with doing historical roleplays. I hated them, but whatever floats your boat.

While his lectures could be more engaging, you can tell he really does care about his students and enjoys teaching. Very passionate, great sense of humor. The class is pretty easy if you pay attention and study. I do wish the tests were slightly less weighted but other than that, great professor and a great course!

I cannot say I enjoyed his class at all. It was boring and he didn't give engaging lectures. I didn't speak to him once and he seemed to lean somewhat unfairly on his TAs to do everything for everyone but the Honors students, who he personally worked with. He gave bad vibes generally and I never heard anyone besides him talk in the class.

He'll either take ages on one slide or flip through five in thirty seconds, and he doesn't post slides so be ready to take pictures of them. He's monotonous and boring, although to his credit he posts the definitions you need to know for the tests, but I've heard post civil war profs are better so just save yourself the trouble and take that.
