Assigned reading can be initially over whelming, but Dr. Stewart does a great job of breaking down the readings in class. The class is almost entirely discussion based, and Dr. Stewart can be a bit hands off at times. However, he frequently jumps in and adds good humor to the discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Stewart is a good person and is alway available to help you outside of class. Having said that, this was a difficult course so be prepared to be challenged if you want to do well. H2100 is a discussion based class and you will be expected to do a lot of reading and a lot of talking, as well. I learned a lot though and I stayed engaged!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: HIST 2100 with Dr. Stewart is super discussion based. The vast majority of the class is discussion-style, led by students so if you never show up or never talk (plus never read the hw), your grade is not going to be good. However, Dr. Stewart does a good job of jumping in and helping discussions while being relaxed and nice and funny to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best history professors I've had at Mizzou; great lectures, knowledgeable about a variety of topics, and makes a point to talk about minorities and women throughout the class.

Excellent professor! Super passionate about the history, dating back to 10,000BC, of the western civilizations. Lectures/readings definitely pair together nicely but there is A LOT of reading.  In discussion sessions the TA would allow us to flesh out questions/concerns about the quick lecture pace and reading intensity.
She was amazing and I wished that she would teach more classes! You HAVE to go to class though, her powerpoints, if posted, don't even begin to cover what she says in class.
she is a good teacher, just necessary to be at class and pay attention.
Great professor...the class is difficult but she is available for help when needed. Do not be afraid to ask questions! Going to class is a must.

Aurora Meyer makes me not hate this class. It's an incredibly hard class and the grading is harsh but reasonable. She's incredibly nice and sweet and if you ask for help, she will give it. Honestly, this class is stressful and I"m not getting the best grades in it, but you can tell Professor Meyer is experienced and I am learning a lot from her.

DO NOT TAKE NEWS WITH AURORA MEYER. She is by FAR the worst news professor. She is new so she has no idea what she's doing. She's rude, grades terribly, and unhelpful. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH HER.

Make sure that you go to class or have someone who can get you the notes. She discusses things that aren't in the book and tests are heavily based on lecture.  Also, read the book and do the reading questions.  Dr. Aubrey is really nice and helpful.  Extra credit is given at the end of the semester that helps.  You'll get an A if you do the work.

I really liked Prof Aubrey, I thought classes were interesting enough, and the grading is really straight forward - there are quizzes, one paper and a final project - all fairly straight forward, if you read and can write semi-decently, you'll probably get an A

Definitely an easy A if you just do the work. Take notes over the lecture, read the chapters, make some flash cards, and you're golden - 100%'s on the tests are easy to come by if you really try. The downfall to the class is the ridiculous lab work - doesn't help with what's on the tests, it's essentially glorified busy work.

Uses clickers so attendance is necessary. The subject material is interesting, but she's not the most exciting teacher. It's an easy A. Best described as "meh". Gives study guides. Practically serves you an A if you just do that and study. Too much lab work though.

I loved this class. I didn't miss a single one. She is extremely organized, assignments and tests are very reasonable. She gives great lectures and the material is very interesting. I'm taking her Contemporary Issues in Mass Communications class next semester. Yay! :)
Great professor! She keeps class fun and interesting, and material is pretty self-explanatory. Take this class if you can!
I had him for finite math, which I am NOT a math person but he kept me very engaged! He is super funny and by far my favorite mizzou professor yet!
He is extremely hard, doesnt talk to his TA's and if your struggling he expects you to figure it out.

Hilarious guy with a very off-beat sense of humor.  He is a helpful teacher and enjoys what he does, which makes a huge difference in how people teach.  If you have an option for your Math courses, be sure to take one of his classes.

DO NOT TAKE HIS ONLINE CLASS!  He won't email you back if you are having problems and only has the exams available from 2-330 on Fridays, so if you actually have a job like I do you have to take off work or miss the test, which missing one drops you 100 of the 600 points offered for the class. If you have ANY other responsibilities DO NOT take!

Really good teacher and really funny. He allows you to miss 9 classes a year. As long as you do your online homework (you can keep answering the questions until you get them all right) every week you'll be fine.
Great professor, really is willing to explain things and help you out.  Do the online homework and the homework in the text book you should do fine.
Go to class and make sure you know how do all of the homework for the tests.  In his 1160 class, the tests are multiple choice.  If you go to him for help, he is very nice and helpful.
It is a clicker class and it is very hard. don't take if you haven't taken trig before.

I have never disliked a professor before, and Atuhura is very kind, passionate and generous, but she is not a good lecturer. She jumps from topic to topic so quickly that I can't follow her at all. Incredibly unclear in her expectations. Also if she learns your name be ready to be cold called on every single day. No joke, all the time.

She offered to take everyone in my class out to lunch and I was the only one who took her up on the offer. She paid for my meal, asked about my mental health (the day after election day), and asked if I had any questions about my assignments. She cares a lot about her students in and out of class.

Dr. Atuhura is very considerate; she is always approachable and understanding regarding outside circumstances. Unfortunately, this class was based on participation, something that Dr. Atuhura struggled to incentivize. Maybe a different group would have been able to create better discussion.

While she may call on you randomly, she is a very easy professor to communicate with and you know what is expected of you when you join the class. she repeatedly asks if anything can be changed with the class and the way it is ran, she also poses great discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is taken daily. While the assignments are necessarily difficult (content-wise), professor Atuhura lacks personal communication skills. Students often feel uncomfortable in her classroom as her tone is very demeaning especially if you do not answer the question asked in the exact way she wants it answered. I rarely dislike professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I have ever had in my life. Doesn't really follow the book and there are no other resources. Tests are BS and random questions.

Horrible -- doesn't teach at all. This could be a really interesting class, because it focuses on how chemistry relates to environmental issues. However, Dr. Atwood completely ruins it by being a useless teacher. Most of my answers on the tests were based on knowledge I already had of chemistry. I haven't learned a single thing. Avoid Dr. Atwood.

His subtle jokes keep class interesting.  Usually about 5 min late every day.  He's helpful when you can catch him, but being the director of the Chemistry Dept. he has many obligations.  We never used a textbook.

Dr. Atwood is friggin awesome.  Every single word that comes out of his mouth has meaning and relevance, and he talks slowly unlike most profs.  If you love chemistry and the THEORY behind things, you'll love him as a teacher, but if you don't, get someone who'll spit cookie-cutter problems at you instead, you'll probably do better

Atwood is an alright guy. He rips out pages from the book during lecture so we know it wont be on the test. One annoying thing is he was usually 3-4 minutes late to his own class every time. His explanations are helpful. He also dropped out lowest test which was awsome. Overall good guy

Prof. Atwood is a great guy.  He teaches the important info, skips the stuff that isn't important.  He keeps things interesting and makes you want to come to class.  I also really enjoyed the lab portion of this course.
Great teacher.  Pours soda on the floor and pretends it's acid.  If you don't know a lot about chemistry, I recommend this teacher.  If you GO TO CLASS everyday, it should be a breeze.
No Comments
old, lazy, worthless. He works hard on his research and prepares for class 10 minutes before it starts
The dude looks like Charles Darwin...

He made class very fun while he was teaching.  Unfortunately, a diff. teacher took over after only a few lectures.  I learned more in the few days Dr. Atwood taught than I did the entire rest of the semester.  He makes quant/analy. fun, if that's possible
Not a good teacher, not helpful either.  Always showed up 5-10 min. late to class.

I had to take this class 15 years ago and she booted me out after the first exam (made an A) after finding out that I had to audit math 5.  the dean gave me 100% refund and allowed me to take algebra at a juco over summer.  i highly recommend doing the same thing I did.  she is completely biased and useless as a teacher.

Worst class I've ever taken. Put material on test that was not covered. Very difficult to work with. Was never in her office during office hrs. She was incredibly rude and condescending both in person and via email.  Class is too demanding for a 1000 level course. Very difficult to understand. Did not communicate with TA's regarding teaching.

Such a horrendous class. She often put problems on tests that weren't included on the review, a truly deplorable act. Miss Fabulous is very staunchly difficult to work with, and I'm thrilled not to be taking her class anymore. Don't let her goofy demeanor fool you. There's a fierce, unwielding lioness lurking beneath those benign eyes.
sucked.
Extremely hard class, she doesn't communicate clearly with her TA's only leaving you with an awful grade on your homework, quiz or exam.

Her tests are ridiculous. Her TA's are good. She isn't good at communication to her TAs. To get even a decent grade you have to put a lot of time and energy into the class, which is stupid because its a lower level required class. The bar shouldn't be set so high. If you can get out of taking it...DO IT!

I never actually took a course directly from her - instead I was with her TAs.  I had to take Math 5 because I was one point away from entry into Math 10.  No one has ever made me more frustrated than this woman, as she refused to allow me to enter Math 10.  She is an ice queen - I saw three people leave her office in tears before I went in!

i had her for college algebra, i failed the class the first time and with her help i made an A the second time around. i personally had a wonderful experience with her. you really just have to immerse yourself in the class and be okay with working hard and keeping up with the material and you will do fine.
Unfortunately there's no way around her. She is THE weed out teacher at Mizzou. There were many many nights my fellow dormmates and I cursed her name....
her tests are impossible!!! it sucks!
She sucks.  I got an A in this course but she is very strict and insensitive.  She is a battle axe.
Sandy is the most evil professor...ever!  Avoid her like the plague!!

I failed Sandi's class. This semester I have a t.a. and am doing much better. Sandi will call people out in the middle of class without any remorse and her accent can be difficult sometimes. She requires a lot more work than the other t.a.'s and makes the class much harder than it should be. I never got above a C on any of her tests.

She is so far the worst teacher (if you could even call her that) I have ever had.  The tests are ridiculously hard, she is extremely unhelpful.  And the fact that you get 3 credits for a five-day-a-week course blows.  Even the TA's think she's nuts.

Sandi is a great college professor.  There are times when I hate the class becuase it is so demanding, however I love the class when her students exam average is higher than all of her TA's students exam average.  You might hate it while your in the class.  When you look back on it, you will be a much better math student.  Prepares you for exams.

Sandi is an amazing prof, get in her class specifically and you can't lose. She WANTS to see you succeed, and offers reviews like crazy and will spend hours with individuals. For non-math people, she is the best, but won't go out of her way if you don't go to class, skip homework, and wait till the day before a test. Got my first A in math ever.

My mother passed away and I took a incomplete in the course.  Sandy was not willing to work with me to let me finish the course and when she did, she gave me a different test than what the final was that she gave in class and gave me a fat F.  She's difficult to understand, quite often not on time, and makes mistakes when trying to teach you the materials.  Not helpful at all!

Sandy knows her math, she is a great professor and dedicates her free time before and after class hours to help her students, but you have to be willing to put in your side of the work, you definitely wont get by just by simply showing up for class.
No Comments

Sandy should not be the coordinator for lower math or anything for that matter.  Typos on tests that a child could see, unclear directives that only confused students.  Thank god my TA was cool.  Even the TA thought she was out of her mind.
If you are willing to work to get the grade, than this class is great.  If you are hoping to skip or not do any work, don't expect an "A" or possibly even a "C".  She is a great professor.

Almost everything you read below this comment is incorrect.  Most of the Math TA's speak English as their native tongue.  Sandi is fair, and she is a great teacher.  If you are you have her as your teacher, AND you are willing to work hard, then you will do fine.  If you have one of her TA's, then you can also do fine.  It's up to you.
This class sucked.  Sandy never even taught the class, and had her TA's do it for her.  I hadly understood anything.
Who is Sandy and what in the hell does she do?? All of her TA's hate her, so why is she even here? She doesn't really actually do****.
SHE IS A HEARTLESS WITCH!!!!  It doesn't matter what is happening in your life, she doesn't care.  Besides, her math is hard and quite honestly she doesn't give a**** if you learn or not.

If you get in her class, you are definitely going to do fine. She goes very slow to let everyone understand and when I went in for help, she spent 3-4 hours every time and didn't let me leave until I knew everything. If you get a TA and you don't understand, go to her! She'll help you!

just do the problems in the book, you'll be fine on the tests.  and go to the reviews even though they're long- they really help!  i never actually met the woman since the class is taught by TA's but i had a cool TA and i did fine
she is a witch and wants you to fail.

This woman is the worst professor I have EVER seen! Only 1 of her T.A.s I've seen speak good English, she is extremely arrogant, and there are errors in the study material she drafts. Her standards for students to learn are ridiculously high, and her teaching quality is extremely inferior!
hate her, tied for coldest witch alive with Wilma King
No Comments

This class is very difficult because the class is taught by teacher's assistants, most of whom are foreign.  I was stuck with a chinese TA who spoke poor english.  Every TA is foreign expect for one. Good luck.

Although the course was very structured, a lot of things fell through the cracks due to graduate student teachers. Getting clear help is very difficult because you will receive a million different instructions from other people and probably be counted wrong for it.

Great professor. Had her for calculus 3. Her lectures are full of information so don't miss them, but she does have the material on canvas. As long as you attend and do homework, you'll be fine. If you do struggle, she has accessible office hours or can be flexible for your schedule. She is very good at teaching the material.
She is very nice and easy to work with. Always responded to emails and provided excelent study materials for exams.

Lectures felt slow but honestly are helpful if you miss a day because she'll go over everything from the previous lecture before new material. Tons of practice problems. Go to review sessions before exams, super helpful. Sit close to the front because sometimes her mic doesn't pick up her voice and she uses the chalkboard a lot.

The lectures are poorly paced, spending most of class on an easy topic and then the last 10 min on the hard part. Luckily the slides are easy to learn from on your own and she posts A LOT of practice resources online.
The tests are formatted well. You get a note card, and they look exactly like the practices.
Probably the best calc II option at MU.
Moves way too fast. Reads off of slides and writes on that little board that you need to be at the front to read
Very hard to understand her and she just over-explains things and runs out of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very sweet lady who I really enjoy as a person, but her lecture style sometimes felt like a 50 minute sorta monotone rambling of difficult, high-level math concepts. I genuinely almost fell asleep every class. If you talk to her outside of class for help she is great, overall not terrible.

I took this course at another university and got an A. I then attended MU after a lengthy absence. My first attempt at MATH 1700 was with Tanya Christiansen but had to withdraw because of poor exam performance. My mid-term exam performance averaged to an 89%, and my final exam grade was a 93%. Overall my grade was a 93%. Loved the exam/quiz format

Probably the best option out of all Calculus II professors at Mizzou. Allows you to have notecards for each exam, and won't try to trick you with unfamiliar questions on quizzes or exams. She also curved all exams. The only complaint is that her lectures were very boring and she spent too much time over-explaining simple topics.

Prof. Harcharras is a fine choice for a Calc professor. She does have a slight accent but it does not detract from her teaching style. She does use a weird hybrid cursive writing style that can be difficult to read. She makes up for this by posting her lecture videos and slide to the canvas. She provides a LARGE amount of good resources on canvas.

She was a fairly decent professor however, it was difficult to pay attention in lecture as she would talk in a monotone voice for all 50 minutes. She is a difficult grader but it is known the expectations for each quiz and test beforehand. All homework was typically more difficult than the tests. Discussion attendance is mandatory, not lecture.

Dr. Harcharras is perhaps one of the best professors I have ever taken a math course with. Her ability to involve students in lectures was honestly wonderful. Her love of mathematics shines through in her passion during class. She is not the easiest grader, and will certainly challenge your abilities. But as a teacher, she is truly unmatched.

Dr. Harcharras is really intelligent, and wants her students to genuinely learn. The class can move slow at times, but it means you get a really good understanding of the topic. Her homework and practice problems are much harder than the actual quizzes/exams which is nice. Just make sure to study because exams are a huge part of the class.

If you don't take Asma for calc 3 you are doomed. Her english isn't very good but she tries hard to get you to understand the topic which is great. Every test has a note card where the practice exam is very close to the exam. On the final you get 5 note cards and every test is curved. You will do well in this class it is easier than calc 2.

Asma is the best Calc 3 professor. Note cards on each exam + 4 on the final was a lifesaver in a class that has a lot of content and things to remember. Calc 3 can be stressful but she does her best to right extremely fair exams and hosts help sessions before each exam that I would suggest attending. Very kind lady.

Professor Harcharras is probably the kindest professor I have ever had. Lectures move pretty slow at times, but the expectations on quizzes and exams are extremely clear and a good grade is not too difficult to earn.

She was definitely the best professor that I've had! She cares more about you actually learning the material, then trying to throw tricky things at you. She gives practice exams that are almost identical to the tests, so you always knew what to expect. You can also have a notecard during the exams. An excellent teacher!

Dr Harcharras is an incredibly sweet lady. She graded fairly and you can always reach out to her after class or even over email. Practice tests help to review material for the test very well! Go to her lectures; she makes it easier than the textbook!

Probably the hardest grader I have ever had. She is very difficult and if I were you I would just go for a well known teacher like Dustin Belt. Please do not take this class. She make calculus impossible and it is a lot harder than what it needs to be. She does teach the class however she teaches in a way that graduate students would understand.

Best Calc 3 professor. Let us use notecards for all exams and made sure we knew what was going to be on them. She lectures extremely quickly and doesn't take many questions; it took a while to get used to her style of teaching but it was 100% worth taking her class in the end.

I'm taking calc 1 for the first time this fall in a class full of students who have already taken it in high school. Regardless, she spends the time carefully explaining each new concept and proof so that students are able to understand the reasoning behind most of the math. She's also super easy to reach out to and will respond to emails quickly
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Harcharras was very excellent, especially given the difficulties of teaching virtually. This class is very tough, but not impossible. The practice problems arent very helpful due to the lack of solutions, but she provides extensive reviews and the homeworks are quite beneficial as well. The exams were take home and open book, so not bad!

She is clear lecturer, but very dry. She is not super friendly and has high expectations. My biggest problem with this class was the practice problems had no solns and the textbook isn't popular enough to be on slader/similar, so I had no way to check, so practicing from tb was useless. Go to class and turn in all assignments on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good teacher for a difficult subject. If you passed Calc 2, the material is more relaxed but still challenging. The pace is much faster for this class and she hustles. No quizzes so you have to maintain your understanding between exams. She's clear and enunciates well, just is usually crammed for time and lectures until after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I did not listen in lecture, taught myself everything using the online textbook practice problems. Got an A on every test, and did better than my friends who listened in lecture. She explains concepts several times over which makes it awful. Prints out notes for you. All quizzes are take home. Unnecessary amount of hw. Notecard can be used on test

Great teacher. Gives you her notes to go along with lectures and study guides are similar to the tests, which are super straight forward. (no tricks)  You also get one side of a flashcard for every test, and 2 full cards for the final.  Difficult class, but she makes it manageable.

She's a great teacher, she lets you use notecard on her tests but thats balanced out by  super hard exams and tricky questions that the notecard might not always save you with. She's just a very tough grader which she thinks is balanced out by her curve but again, its not. She was there for help whenever you needed it and is very helpful however

Very nice and helpful when asked. During lectures she can be hard to understand but she is always willing to explain more. As far as testing goes she makes them relatively easy but can be hard on grading, but she curves well it's nothing too bad.

Very in-depth professor. Does speak with an accent but she is still able to clearly understand. Does alot of proofs only because she wants you to understand what you're actually learning and not just know how to work out problems. Lectures are about 52+ mins long.  Took Calc 1 twice and struggled.  With this professor,  I passed Calc 2 with an A.

I took Calculus in High school and loved it. When I came here however I acquired a new hate. She overcomplicates things and only focuses on proofs which don't help students' solve problems. Rarely ever does she go over practice problems and she assumes that you should "just get it." If you have an option, take calculus from another professor.

Her tests are crazy.. But more so the Final I just took. It basically tested you over everything if you were a genius and could do all the most in depth questions in the book. Good luck, i had an A in the class, until the Final.
This was my 1st time taking Calc & it was horrible. She was hard to understand. She over complicated the concepts with extravagant proofs. I didn't learn anything.

She explained things in a way that seemed out of the ordinary and hard to understand. The material wasn't difficult, but I actually benefited from not going to any of her lectures and having a friend teach me out of class. Also, she was hard to understand unless you sat in the front half of class.

The entire class consists of examples that aren't helpful to actually learning the content. Beyond that it is sometimes hard to make out what is being said, and she has recently used a mic which has made it impossible to understand.

I took the Honors section of the class.  The tests were easy if you attended class, took notes, and were good at keeping up with the suggested homework (a lot of practie problems).  She is always ready to help you understand concepts but class attendance is neccessary!

She was very helpful and there for you when you needed it, but she grades tests ridiculously hard, she curves them pretty good but you got to keep an eye on what the final grade is going to look like.
She was amazing! She explained things in a way that was easy to understand conceptually. I would recommend her to my friends if they were thinking of taking this class.
The best math teacher I have ever had
She gave us practice test, but they were nothing like the tests that she actually gave.  The take home quizzes are hard, but at least you can work with someone

Asma is the best professor to get for math2300. Her practice exams give you the exact wording to every question that will be on the real exam, the only difference is the functions used. Ohh yeah, most of her quizzes are take home.
The class itself is difficult due to the homework which all sections have to do.  However, she let you know exactly what to expect for her tests and quizzes, so if you studied, you did awesome.
she prepares you really well for the tests and she is more then willing to help you outside of class.  great teacher!
Calculus 3 is pretty hard, but her tests make it even harder. Shes a pretty good teacher, but her tests suck because she makes them rather difficult. Other than that, I would recommend her.
Calc 2 is hard, this course is not for weaklings a lot of the people in my class took this class for the second time.  I know this sounds stupid, but do EVERYTHING on time so you DON'T fall behind.
Very nice guy and will offer help when needed. As long as you go to class and do homework and study, you will get a fine grade!

I had Benjamin for MATH1400, not 0110, but it won't let me select that course :(
Benjamin is a great instructor. He makes the content understandable, explains topics thoroughly, and does lots of practice problems so you can see how the concepts work. There's weekly homework but it's not long, and the quizzes/tests are very similar to the homework.

MATH 0110 is a basic math class, and Benjamin does a great job teaching the concepts of it. I struggled with math for years, but he is an excellent instructor and helped me get my highest grade in a math class since middle school!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is one of the best I have ever taken at Mizzou. Dr. Lester is a delight to work with and shows up to every class with a positive attitude and genuine excitement for what she is teaching. The class is lecture-heavy, with many turn-and-talk discussions and group activities. TAKE NOTES!! And read the textbook because it will be on exams.

I always look forward to class with Dr. Lester! She is so passionate about what she teaches and really makes the class engaging. It is a hard class, and a lot of information, however she is so willing to help whenever needed! She also is very supportive and provides great feedback! 100% would take any class she teaches again if I have the chance.

Dr. Lester is one of my favorite professors I have had. Each and every class she comes in so happy and excited to teach, and you can tell that she really cares about what she is lecturing. She connects everything into real life scenarios and makes her lectures so interesting. Would absolutely recommend her, and her Intimate Relationships class.

Lester was very difficult and her class about took me down.. So many assignments but only ten points given her tests are very hard as well.. and she gives you little to study from. She also goes till the VERY end of class and does to many clickers you can't keep up. Her ta Karen Talley is awful and horrible at her job and is a pain to go to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course-long paper prompt is chosen too early before enough information is learned. Despite focusing on a narrow prompt, the professor insists on note-taking for unrelated lectures. Instructions are vague, yet grading is strict, with points lost for minor details that are not said. Avoid this class; the online section is a much better use of time.

HDFS 2400W with Dr. Lester has been one of the worst classes I have taken. The essays assigned for the class often make no sense and not much time is given to write. The examples provided are awful and the rubrics for essays are confusing. Although she is really passionate about the field, you should take the online section if you have the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There's a lot of extra assignments I feel that there is no need to be done. There is a lot of content in this class I feel very overwhelmed.

I took Dr. Lester for my HDFS 2400 Writing Intensive course. She offered a live zoom of her lectures, which a lot of kids used, however, her lectures were super interesting and fun to listen to. She truly is passionate about what she teaches and makes the content interesting! The big paper you have is no joke, but she offers lots of help!

she had us do in class assignments at the end of lectures, but gave an option to attend via zoom which was nice. I didn't like how we had to take reading tests on content in the textbook that had not yet been covered in class. Dr. Lester is super nice and likes to ask questions in class. Writing intensive section is lots papers and revising
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: mrs. lester was a pretty good professor. clicker points but interesting lectures! tests are hard so study and look at chapter summary in textbook! Shes a caring person but a hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lester is clearly passionate about what she is teaching so her lectures were really interesting to listen to. She takes lecture time to go into detail about the assignments which I found really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the things I didnt like was how she set up her due dates. In a masters program, people have real lives outside of school including full time jobs and families. She didnt seem to understand that. She was also a VERY difficult grader and very critical. Its like you couldnt win with her. She would take off points for small, silly things.

Be prepared to read between the lines. Take more notes than what is necessary. The tiny details that weren't discussed in class? Yeah, those make up a good chunk of the exams. Don't let this deter you, though. This class is incredibly fascinating and if you're self-motivated, you will learn a lot of things that will surely enhance your worldview.

Dr. Lester is one of the best teachers I have ever had.  She is so passionate and dedicated, yet so sweet and down to earth. She definitely works with you if need be, and will encourage you to be the best writer! Her lectures are AMAZING. I always looked forward to going to class. She is tough but well worth it. I changed my major because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took her online class, and she is a very tough grader. Doesn't give A's on papers, and tests have 9 chapters on each.. which makes it impossible to do well. Book is a necessity

She is a very good teacher and clearly loves what she does. If you go to class every week you will get an A. Her tests are tough but straight forward. There are 4 unit tests and a final but she drops a score so you can choose one not to go to. Overall I really liked the class

Ashlie is great! Not only as a professor, but as a person too. She is very energetic and you can feel her passion in every lecture. I was a little iffy about a class about intimate relationships, but it has become one of my favorite classes! Ashlie is happy to be in class and see everyone every single day. I can tell that she wants me to succeed.

Ashlie was so much fun to have as a teacher! I have recommended this class to everyone I know and used more information learned in this class than any class I have taken.  Ashlie is great and uses clips from Modern Family and The Office in useful ways, not just for entertainment.  Only advice, don't forget to do your journals every week.
One of the best teachers I've had at Mizzou. She's very energetic and helps you stay interested in class. The tests aren't too hard but there are clicker questions and you can drop one of your tests.
Ashlie was super fun! She definitely enjoyed what she was teaching. Tests weren't terrible, but the questions were very comprehensive. Class is mandatory because theres a clicker. Super fun though!

Firstly, She is super hot. She is funny and really cares about helping you. You have to go to class but her lectures are entertaining and easy to follow. take lots of notes. But its all pretty straight forward from there

Super fun class! Ashlie makes the class so interesting by relating it to everyday life. Tests are extremely straight forward if you attend lecture. If you take HDFS 1610, definitely try and get her section.

Amazing teacher!!! She uses awesome examples, really cares about students and learning. Tests are pretty straight-forward from lecture and the book. Besides tests, there are short and easy weekly blog entries and inclass assignments. Loved her and Loved the class!! Favorite class I've taken and favorite teacher. It made me consider changing majors!

The Class was TOTALLY AWESOME!!!! She uses alot of video clips that are easy to relate to. No homework assignments or papers. Very simple in class assignments. The tests aren't too challenging as long as you attend every class. Class was very interesting.

Ashlie Lester is amazing! She makes the class so interesting & uses celebrities & tons of clips from The Office as examples. She gives easy participation points, there are no assignments either. The tests are super easy. This class made me change my major to human development sciences! love her!

The TA's do everything for the bio1020 labs. The lab topics aren't complicated, but my TA wasn't great so I always was confused in lab and then had to teach myself the concepts later on by myself.The pre-lab resources were also often never posted before class, so I couldn't prepare even if I wanted to.

My issue is that I contacted her regarding my TA, and nothing was done about it. It resulted in 3/4 of my group members dropping the course, including me. The TA was beyond terrible and claimed that since we were the first lab of the day that it would always be messed up. UH WHAT! A TA with a PHD told us to use Google if we needed help.What a joke
Literally have never seen or met her, a TA runs the whole class, there was a quiz and worksheet everyday, material was all over the place and instruction was not clear.

Does not give clear instructions, and will subtract major points from participation for very little things. The TA's lead the class, and are extremely unhelpful and rush the class to just get things done instead of thinking and understanding.

Dr. Asgari is a nice person but a bad professor, her instructions are very unclear, and often she is difficult to understand. Most of your learning takes place outside of class and she goes over the same stuff you learned repeatedly.

This is done as a flipped classroom which isn't my favorite but Dr. Asgari wasn't the one to decide that and she's super nice. The class overall isn't super hard, there's just a lot to do. There are tests every other week and two homework assignments/week but graded for completion not accuracy. It was a little tedious but not super difficult.

Nice professor, clearly passionate about the subject. She explains things well in lectures. Attendance is mandatory and there are two homework assignments per week (not graded, participation points). Tests every other week, lots of group work. Not a difficult class.

Good class and prof to learn about linguistics and a different aspect of Spanish language not considered in other courses. It is a hw heavy class, with reading and practice exercises due most classes. Extra credit opportunity, hw revisions, and a fairly generous grader. Only two exams; midterm and final (which covers the second 1/2 of course).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: High workload, but also, don't overthink. Do the work, do your best, and ask for help when needed. He's open to feedback and is incredibly kind and accommodating if you communicate your needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: profe alcazar is amazing. he is kind and really wants you to do well in his class. he knows so much about these topics and has really helped me improve in my spanish skills. i wish he could teach me for the rest of my classes. there is a lot of homework but it is pretty easy to do. grades are very fair and you can improve after an assignment.

By far the best Spanish class I've taken at Mizzou. Topic was very interesting, and Prof. Alcazar gave great feedback. I knew exactly what I had to work on and how I could improve. I learned a lot from him and saw a major improvement in my speaking skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Since the pandemic, Prof. Alcazar moved all of his classes online. While the course content was both dry and difficult to understand, his lenient deadlines and grading offset it. He also gave us the chance to revise our homework to get full credit. His lectures are pretty rushed and monotone, but usually the linguistics topics were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course is clear and easy to follow. He has a set schedule that cycles through three different interactive lecture types; all of which are engaging and a light workload. There's homework for each class, but it comes from the textbook and it's not very much. He's very laid back and approachable. My best professor this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Second time taking his class, I will say that during the pandemic he has changed. This class used to be a capstone, so lots of homework. Still dry as usual, but gives good feedback. He is a lenient grader, so if you put some effort in, you will at least get a 80% on homework. Sometimes he recycles material (puts homework questions on tests).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Asier was the best professor I've had yet; he is kind, caring, and intelligent. He gives 110% in teaching, and I learned how to speak Spanish much better in this course. Homework due before every class that will probably take you an hour- make a GroupMe with your class. Zooms are optional attendance- you can watch the recordings later.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While his class was very organized, it was rather very boring & hard to pay attention. His lectures are very dry. He has no emotion or enthusiasm. Difficult to get connected. Gives a lot of assignments, etc. However, he only wants all assignments turned in by email, no exceptions. There was homework twice a week. So it's very easy to fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Alcazar is probably the best Spanish professor I've had so far. He helped me so much with my pronunciation. He gave me constructive feedback, practiced with me, and was easily accessible for help. You can tell he really cares for his students and wants each one to succeed. I would highly recommend taking if you are serious about Spanish.

Asier is all business during lecture. The material can be dry, but he does an OK job of teaching it. Make sure you pay attention/take note, it will be easier when you review the slides online. The homework is a lot, don't wait to do it. He sets clear deadlines-meet them or he'll dock you. DEFINITELY revise any HW/tests at the end-boosts your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: While there was homework assigned for every class, it never got to be too much at much at once, not to mention there is good feedback given. Most class was spent going over the textbook, with him correcting our pronunciation. While we were corrected often, I never thought he came off as rude- everyone was regularly corrected and seemed to improve.

Sometimes can be rude to students and often is not clear in his assignments. However my spanish improved greatly especially with my pronunciation. I would recommend him if you really want to improve conversation skills

He is very straight forward and he is not afraid to be blunt so sometimes he will say things that may seem a little bit rude or mean.  However, he is one of the easiest graders i've ever met.  Basically, if you attempt to do the assignment you will at east get a b.  For the most part his class was very time consuming, but over all, not really hard

The worst professor I have ever met! He is extremely rude and disrespectful to his students (unless you are one of his few favorites...just wait in the end everyone hates him). He thinks he knows a lot & probably does however he lacks any ability to communicate it to his students.  Only positive side was a good grade but not worth being around him.

His grading's a little weird and unless you talk to him about where you stand & why, your final grade might come as an unpleasant surprise. He's not terribly difficult as a grader though - but to get a B or higher requires a fair amount of work. Overall, I think he's a good, non-boring, non-confusing teacher, and I would be happy to have him again.

His grading is simply arbitrary. He will never return anything, and if asked, will be unable to give a breakdown of your final class grade. Several students have had problems: save all of your stuff and hold him accountable for your grade!

Dr. Givens is passionate about her work but the structure of the course made the information meaningless. Lectures were short and did not go in-depth. Honestly, I did not learn much. The most interesting material comes from classmates' presentations. Too tough of a grader in my opinion, but lax on due dates. Approachable, but this class was a mess.
Dr. Givens is great and wonderful. She is doing amazing research and lectures very passionately. However, she is a tough grader.

Dr. Givens is a very knowledgable and passionate individual. Dr. Givens' lectures are very entertaining because she knows how to have fun. I'm thankful for the content we discuss in this class and the book choice. Dr. Givens gives very useful feedback on assignments that truly teach individuals how to sharpen their skills.

Aycan was really fun - parts of her class focus on guest speakers and learning about types of engineering work. Her methods set you up for success in CHE2225 so make sure to pay attention and learn them well. She was available often for extra help outside of class.

She's very nice and caring, always asks us how she can help or make the class easier. You don't do anything for the first couple of months, then it hits you out of nowhere. A lot of homework, projects, and group projects too. Only 2 exams and no final and the exams are super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: LOTS of homework. And she threw it at us all at once right at the end of the semester which was annoying because that's when I was studying for finals. She really seems to care about her students though and she's a super nice person. It's just frustrating to do 3 projects, HW, and a quiz all the week before finals
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is a little hard to understand sometimes, but she seems really passionate about chemical engineering. She seems to care about her students, and she's always willing to help.

She was not very helpful with her lectures, she would just read from the slides and didn't care about students understanding the concepts. The couse was very test heavy and tests were difficult.More than 60% of the grade was based on tests. There were also too many concepts and formulas in the course and it was hard to remember all that.

Doesn't really do much to make the class interesting and there's little to no in-depth explanation on topics. It kind of felt like she just simply read what was on the slideshows without explaining them any further. Exams were relatively difficult, but the practice exams did help a lot when preparing for them. Homework is due by the week.

She is funny and lecture is very helpful to go to. She makes the slides funny while still being able to teach well. Mandatory icliker attendance but if you get over 60% the final is optional to take. Lots of homework and packback's due every Monday but they aren't worth much. exams are very difficult. Do the homework and study and you'll be okay.

Gavin did a good job teaching a difficult subject. I personally would not take calc 3 again but it's not his fault. He's open to questions and his office hours are really helpful. His handwriting can be difficult to understand and he goes fast but he will stop for clarification. He definitely cares for you as a student; you're not just a name.

(For MATH 4100) Dr. Ball had extremely detailed and in-depth lectures. His office hours were super helpful, and he was very accessible even outside his office hours. However, his exams were graded out of 30 points, and they were unnecessarily difficult and punishing. He was a great guy, and there was a huge curve at the end. Sweats too much tough.

He frequently explored topics in great depth, sometimes at the expense of clarity and conciseness. Exams were exceptionally challenging and occasionally included material not covered in class. Exam averages were consistently below 70, and our class received a limited formula sheet compared to the notecards allowed in other sections.

I don't even know if this guy is alive. Everything is graded by canvas and online. The class is extremely easy and doesn't require much effort. The lectures and content are pretty enjoyable if you have interest in the field.

Dr. Deng taught this class online, which I think limited potential to clear up any problems students had during the lecture, but as for the actual content of the class, it is enjoyable and a good introduction to Environmental Engineering.

I did not like this professor, none of the class knew their grade until the end of the semester. Furthermore, the lectures were long and there was no enfasis put on any of the information. This made studying for the tests very hard. The labs were very good, however these were put on by the TA's not the teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a bottom tier teacher who isn't the most coherent speaker - yet you can still learn a lot in CV 3200. The labs/site visits helped to visualize what we were be learning in class. He's not a bad guy, and has plenty of opportunities for extra credit by attending research seminars that are actually interesting. If you work hard you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very kind man but has no business being in the classroom.

Honestly had to teach myself this entire course. It was pretty difficult and you have to study extremely hard. He just talks in lecture, there was no explaining and you need to memorize everything on every slide basically.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really interesting course. Definitely difficult and lots of material in the course. It is possible to do well just be prepared to work for it. Though the course is amazing, 10/10 recommend if pre-health. Extra credit if you go to lecture and do the iClickers.

This is easily the hardest class I've taken at MU so far. Lectures are a bit dry and very, very dense. Be ready to study 10+ hours if you want an A on the exams. There are quizlets pre-made by past students that you can use. I learned a lot taking this course and if you're pre-med it is a good course to take, just be ready to put in a lot of work.

This class is extremely dense. Lectures are very detailed and made for med students. This class is NOT just memorization, you have to be able to connect ideas and apply knowledge. The TAs are extremely helpful and enjoy helping, just reach out to them. Extra credit helps a LOT. Spend the time studying and an A is possible.

Probably the hardest class I've taken and is extremely test heavy with multiple choice, application questions. Go to class when Baldwin is lecturing two get EC, but don't bother if it's another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Baldwin does a great job of presenting information in a concise manner! However, this class is VERY information-heavy so you have to study quite a bit! I studied on average 10+ hours for each test. Exam 3 is the hardest one so be prepared and the final is cumulative! Overall, it's an interesting class and an A is definitely possible. LOTS OF EC

understanding but doesnt communicate much, lectures are long & hard to get though, interesting info for pre-health, can do HW until get 100%, proctored multiple choice exams are very detailed & difficult but possible if study a lot & do practice tests, labs are pretty easy(can redo until 100%) & can do whenever, 2 other professors do some lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is definitely pointed towards medical students. It is very in depth and detailed. The lectures are long but they are only twice a week. There is a lot of information to learn so it does take time to study, but the information is applicable and useful. I studied probably 10+ hours a week outside of class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting info for med nerds, but lectures are long and lots of info is covered in a short time for each exam. Some exams cover LOTS of detail; not a class you can do without some studying. Baldwin's not the best lecturer, but the info is straightforward. Gives lots of extra credit for attendance w/ clicker questions. An A is definitely possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was ruined by the difficult exams. They were so specific to random details that it was difficult to actually learn and remember anything at all. Each powerpoint slide is packed with information, it's like reading a textbook. Study for weeks in advance to do well on the exams.

Baldwin seems like a nice guy but his lectures can be pretty boring. It's important to go to class and take good notes though because the tests have a lot of material that he points out during lectures. He offers a decent grading scale and a couple of extra credit opportunities too. The lab part of class is pretty fun, but make sure you study!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bartow is the best. She will teach you anything you want to learn and work with you until you know it. She puts a lot of time and effort into the class. If you are able to apply for UAP 100% do it.

Professor Bartow is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. She makes it very clear that she cares about her students well being and wants them to be successful in her class. She goes above and beyond.
My goat Spanish teacher, other than Ivan. He's really funny when you get to know him, and it's easy to get an A as long as you pay attention and do the readings.
Best Spanish teacher at Mizzou. Easy class. He is funny and sweet. Read the things right before class and did great on quizzes.
He seems to be biased against men as a whole in his lectures and covering stories and asking questions that are biased against men. He seems to bash men as a group.

He isn't the most consistent of professors, but I honestly think that's better. He changed based on how the class performs. Everyone keeps making a mistake? He'll start taking points off for it. Nobody does the readings? Quizzes are back! It is easy to do well as long as you so the homework and understand it. This is advanced Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: the class is so boring at times he is disorganized, doesn't follow his own course calendar he grades really easily allows you to make up anything you miss takes attendance every day, is part of your grade doesn't give you more than like a 2 hour notice for quizzes, check canvas regularly

Prof. Badiane is very passionate about the course material but his style is pretty disorganized. He's a pretty easy grader and a really understanding guy. I would recommend taking his writing-intensive section if you need it for your major. It's one of the easier options. Having it on zoom was rough but same goes for any discussion-based class.

Was told this class would be an easy A so I took it, but for some reason he refuses to give anyone in the class 10/10 points for participation despite showing up and speaking at least once every class period. Not sure why he is being so difficult this semester, but I would not take this again his grading criteria is too tough and unspecific.

The class is a little monotonous but there are no surprises and you know what to expect each time! Professor Badiane was really kind and flexible with online class and was one of my more forgiving professors relating to covid circumstances which I know we all really appreciated. Overall, I would definitely recommend him!

Great professor! This class is really easy. If you complete readings and show up to class you should have no problem getting an A. He really cares about his students and is also super knowledgeable about hispanic literature. I'd highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Best teacher I have ever had. Has more experience than anyone in the department and cares a ton about students. He follows up and has kept in touch as a valuable reference. TAKE HIS CLASS!!! Amazing.

From Senegal, but his accent is very easy to understand. There is a lot of reading in this course, but he makes sure you fully understand every text. Very kind and sympathetic professor, funny and approachable. Clearly very passionate about his job; definitely the best Spanish professor I've had at Mizzou.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor, hands down my favorite Spanish professor I've ever had. Easy to get an A if you read before class and complete writing assignments on time. Gives great feedback and is willing to help whenever. Really enjoyed the class and actually felt like I learned something. Highly suggest taking Dr. Badiane's class!
Excellent teacher. Speaks slowly and clearly; able to understand in Spanish. It's easy to get an A if you read the homework before class. Super nice guy too.
Professor sticks to the textbook and goes through a power point or sometimes group discussions. Class quizzes are easy if you read the poems and plays and are what raise your grade.
Best teacher and class ever, even if you don't have an interest in law, this class is amazing and will make you interested in law.
I loved having him as a professor! One of the best teachers I've ever had, and I learned so much! He is also super understanding and easy to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors my freshman year. If you have any interest in law I would strongly recommend taking law-1100 with Trachtenberg.

Professor Trachtenberg is good at not making lectures to repetitive and makes it easy to engage.  There is an assignment between each class but they are much better than reading multiple chapters in a text book per week.  He brings a very good variety of speakers.  If you are considering a career in law this is a great class and professor.

Enjoyed his class so much and learned a lot!  10/10 recommend this course with him.  Lots of participation homework with big papers due every other week, but is very forgiving with late work and resubmissions.

Amazing class and professor and, despite having a lot of homework in the class, I highly enjoyed taking it. Overall, it provided a great outlook on many types of law. A great course to take if you're considering Law School.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great teacher clearly cares about his students. Clear about what is expected he is very helpful. Just read! and go to class you will be fine.
Awesome teacher. Difficult class.

I've had Professor Bereskin for Financial Investments, and he's one of the nicest and most supportive professors at Mizzou. He makes tough finance topics more enjoyable with his jokes and friendly style. He gives great advice, sees the best in his students, and wants everyone to succeed. Exams are hard, so attendance matters if you want to do well!

I took investments with Professor Bereskin last semester. The course was challenging, but he was knowledgeable and passionate about this subject. Great guy, very approachable, and he made class fun and worth going to by looking at real-world topics. If you want a good grade in this course you have to attend every single lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! Very enthusiastic and encourages student participation. Lots of memorization for the class, but relatively easy exams.
She is a good professor. Gives a lot of room for improvement and offers many opportunities to improve your grade.

Professor Bauer is very kind and constantly offers information and resources to help her students succeed outside of class. She made sure her class was accessible to everyone. She also seemed to have a lot of experience outside of Mizzou, which I thought was cool!

Professor Bauer is a very kind individual that clearly cares about her students. She provided so many resources to everyone that she had no obligation to. Attendance is not mandatory after you reach a certain number of points for in class activities.

I took Forensic Psychology online to complete my minor, and it was very straightforward and easy.  Weekly discussion posts and 4 exams total, lowest one gets dropped. Dr. Bauer and the TA's were very approachable for questions or help.  Interesting content and an easy A.

While learning about research methods may not be the most interesting topic Dr. Bauer manages to make it interesting. She keeps you engages in lectures. Dr. Bauer is also the nicest professor I have had. She is always willing to talk and cares about her students.
I loved this professor and how caring she was. The lectures were a little boring but not bad, they could just feel a little bit long. Overall, I would love to take her class again.

Dr. Bauer is nice and cares about her students, but the course is boring. Presentations are usually close to 100 slides long and there's a lot of redundant content. The assignments are exactly the same every single week - even the discussion questions. If you want to be interested and engaged with the material, take Psych1000 with someone else.

I love Mrs. Bauer!! She is such a great professor and makes it easy to know exactly what is needed to pass the exams and go onto research methods II. She has a few in class assignments, but you don't need to go everyday if you don't want. She has her slides online with some definitions and examples blank that she reveals in class.

I enjoyed taking Psychology 1000 over the summer with Professor Bauer!! She explains things very well, gives great resources to study for the exams, and really cares for her students! Go to class, because she gives in class assignments.

Lisa was by far one of my favorite teachers, if not my #1 fave while attending Mizzou. She was very sweet and also knowledgeable on psych topics. (I had her for multiple classes) But don't try to take advantage- she'll put you in your place real quick if you try to pull a fast one on her. Get ready to read and actually learn in her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lisa is an absolute gem. She provides several resources for your success and is probably the most caring and down-to-earth professor you'll ever have. She managed to turn a subject that I feared and wasn't confident in into something that I love and am naturally curious about. The online homework is fun, too!

Definitely liked taking Bauers class! Shes very nice and wants all of her students to succeed. Very good at explaining material. Takes attendance via random participation activities during the semester. Liked how the final exam is optional and can replace your lowest test score.

She is a sweet professor and cares a lot about the subject she's teaching. Her lectures are heavy but in general, the class was interesting. The assignments were very time-consuming and difficult. She is a tough grader and attendance is mandatory.

I am a senior at Mizzou, and she is by far the best teacher I've ever had. She's so sweet and really cares about how well you do in the class, and tries to help all students. She's also very clear on what she is looking for when it comes to assignments.

Shes a clear grader with fair assessments and you can tell she cares deeply about the subject and her students. However, as someone who finds it hard to concentrate on one thing for very long, her lectures can be a bit tedious and repetitive.

Bauer is one of the better professors you can get on campus. Exams closely followed her lectures, so there were no surprises & its easy to get an A if you show up. Easy homework assignments, quizzes, and in-class activities to help your grade out too. Lectures can admittedly get boring sometimes, but the information is at least mostly interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lisa is a great, enthusiastic professor. She cares about her students and their learning. Make sure to go to class to get the random attendance because if you're a couple points from the next letter grade at the end of the semester, she'll round you up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr Bauer is sweet, helpful, and knows her stuff! She is always willing to help her students conduct and publish research, apply and get into grad school, etc. She really goes the extra mile. Her lectures are clear and her online slides are posted the day before to print. She  is relatable, personable, and easy to talk to and get ahold of

This class is mandatory for psych majors, so don't take this if you don't have to. Bauer is an awesome professor but there is just so much information to learn in this class. Pretty dry lectures too. She has a ton of online study material that was very helpful. Would take her as a prof again. You need to actually attend class w/ all info
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bauer has difficult tests which account for most of your grade.  Basically, study hard and often and you'll be fine.  She is more interesting than she seems at first and she loves to talk about Psychology and research.

She is awesome. I didn't think I would like Psych 3010 but she made all the boring concepts so understandable and in the end this class had become one of my favorites. Her lectures are well organized and the way she explains all the terminology of research method has always been very concise.
ICA's are legit. Leaves online lecture slides blank mostly so you have to come to class to get the examples that will be on the example. She reiterates herself often.

Dr. Bauer is a great teacher who knows the material can be difficult. She gives multiple examples and has funny anecdotes that help solidify tough ideas and concepts. There were 3 homeworks, 3 quizzes and 4 exams. Lowest exam score is dropped. She does an item analysis on each exam, which is honestly a fantastic way to understand student learning.

Dr. Bauer's lectures are amazing - she adds videos and stories that break up lectures & help you remember. She's so nice and always available for help. Tests are a little tough even if you study but the optional final allows you to drop 1 of 4. Writing assignments are easy. Attendance not mandatory but helpful for notes

Dr. Bauer is fantastic and super sweet. I love her personal stories. Truly cares and wants to be helpful (occasionally too much but she means well). I'm not good with research and APA writing but she broke the class/project into segments and made it very manageable.

Dr. Bauer is the sweetest! She is very helpful so visit her office hours frequently. I had her for cognitive psych and Research methods 3010. A lot of the material overlapped. You have to study for the tests but she gives lots of notes.

Oh, how I hate research methods. But Lisa made it bearable, and dare I say fairly easy. Read, read, read, go to class and labs, do your homework, and you'll make it out alive. She's so friendly and relatable and kept me from pulling my hair out because math.

Dr. Bauer teaches so many different classes, yet she still makes time for every single one of her students that asks for help. She truly cares about our learning! Exams can be difficult, but if you study her lectures you will have no issues. She grades fairly and her lectures are always interesting. Would definitely recommend!

She was very nervous in the first class so I didn't know what to expect, but it just made me like her more. She is super nice and knows her students by name. I think the information on the tests are mainly what is gone over in class. The lectures are very interesting! I think Lisa is extremely intelligent and I feel like get a lot out of class.
Dr. Bauer was very personal and very helpful. She truly wants to see her students succeed. As long as you attend class, you shouldn't have a problem making a good grade. Totally would recommend her!

Took this class twice. Not b/c it was hard but b/c I didn't attend class & that is essential. Classes feel long but you learn a lot & a majority of what you learn is tied to a memorable example in class. I would advise printing out the slides ahead of time and filling in the blanks in class. 4 exams, one dropped. 2/3 papers due.
She is super super sweet i was extremely nervous for this class and i had heard it was horrible and she is super sweet and clear about everything
Good. Doesn't tend to go into the math of how the methods are derived.

She is SO helpful, easy to understand, very involved in student learning and success. There is weekly homework, but plenty of time in lab to work on it and get help. There are MC tests in lecture and computer tests in lab.

She is the nicest most helpful teacher I've ever had. Research Methods II is a bit of a challenging class and she gladly answered any questions I had. She made the time to help me with my homework almost every week. Ask her for help and you will definitely get a good grade.

Loved her! She made the class very interesting and always gave great examples. If you ever have any questions she is happy to answer them. Final is optional which was nice. Her tests were based mostly on power point notes so make sure you go to class to get all of the notes.

Very effective teaching method. Recaps the previous class in the first few minutes of each day, which helped me retain what she said. Also puts powerpoints online before class so you can add your own notes to her slides. It made studying easy provided you put in the effort to show up and take notes.

She is SO nice! She really wants you to succeed in this class. Attendance isn't mandatory but her posted powerpoints leave info out, so its VERY beneficial to go to class. Her tests are very detailed but manageable if you go to class and pay attention. Her lectures are pretty interesting and she makes an effort to give fun examples. GREAT professor

Very good teacher!! Classes are very interesting and you will learn a lot. She also shows some videos which are fun. She is a very nice and helpful professor and is willing to help with anything you need. Tests are harder than you you will think going into them but not terrible. Just be sure to read the book it helps a lot.

She's a very nice lady, but this is not the easiest class. I'd say it's an easy B. Class isn't mandatory, but she leaves gaps in her ppts so you should probably go. Her tests can definitely be a little tricky but she does her best to try to make sure everyone understand the difficult concepts. Take if you dont mind a challenge.

The class was very straightforward, no tricks. Tests are directly from lectures and the book. She is very willing to help. She is so sweet and makes classes interesting with side stories and helpful examples. She also makes an effort to get to know her students. I highly recommend taking her classes.

Elise was an engaging teacher for me in ENG1000, and made a connection with the majority of the students of her class. Everyone loves a cool and laid-back professor, but I don't suggest putting any real effort into the projects as she was a very easy grader which felt unfair compared to others definitely using AI and other methods...

Super chill, flexible with you as long as you communicate. Yes there was lots of writing but its an english class and she is also a very nice grader. 10/10 love her and would take another class with her any day compared to other prof. i've had here
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Gives 4 essays + a final project, but they're pretty easy. You have assignments, but they will be posted in the monthly calendar. I never went to class, just did the assignments that were posted. She's a nice teacher, but attendance isn't mandatory to get a good grade. Takes forever to grade tho.

Dr. Broaddus is really nice and I enjoyed her classes. You have 4 essays and they aren't too hard. She does take a good while to grade the essays. You have little assignments due pretty often but they aren't too hard. I would recommend.

Didn't learn a single thing in her class. She is super nice and caring and loves to know her students. She just talks about unimportant things. Never replies to emails, grades up months later, no feedback at all. Turned in my 1st out of 4 essays in early February and didn't get a grade until late March after the 2nd essay was due.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved professor Broaddus! She made this class super easy to understand. She does give almost daily readings and one or 2 pop quizzes if she thinks you didnt do the reading. Some of the assignments took more thought to complete but she is super helpful in and outside of class! I ended with an A as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Honest to god waste of time. Took English 1000 as a mandatory class, and was SO disappointed with her teaching. We spent most of the class talking about instagram/emojis/pop culture and though literacy has always been my favorite subject, she managed to not teach a single thing all semster. Easy A but the topics felt extremely unimportant
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: A totally beautiful human being, inside and out.   I'm not a huge literature person but I loved her class!!

Ms. Broaddus has an exquisite taste in clothing, carries herself so gracefully, and I don't think her sense of quiet dignity is matched by any other instructor at Mizzou, to be honest.  Despite her youth, she has so much knowledge to impart, both about literature and about life!  She is challenging, kind, and exquisitely unique and wise.

Class is pretty tough but if you show her that you will put in effort, then she will help you a ton.  I am a terrible writer but put in hours of work with her and tutors for every paper and got an A in the class. She hands out many B's and C's but if you want the A you really have to work for it.  She is a very nice and understanding person

Amazing prof. She can be intimidating as she is very direct, but she cares an incredible amount for her students and the work they produce. She is receptive to student feedback, provides a wealth of information about the industry, and motivates students to do well. She is a true storyteller. I found myself hanging on to her every word in lectures.

Exceptional teacher! She reignited my passion for writing. She was great with every single student and ensured we had good opportunities for publishing. She was very supportive. Great teacher! I really hope I get to take another one of her classes!
It's so easy to be on her good side. Get to know her and you'll love her.

The class was redesigned this year and should keep being redesigned. You will need to have time outside other classes and work to come in and get clips for the paper. Your grade is dependent on work outside of GA work. If you want an A, you have to make yourself more available. Liz is nice but direct.

Liz is one of the most amazing professors I have ever had and I think I will ever have. She is so quirky, fun, and cares so deeply about all of us. Her love for journalism is so clear but her love for her students is even more clear. If you have the chance to meet her or take her class do it!

Liz is a great journalism professor with real-world experience. She is one of the editors at The Missourian so she'll bring real stories from that to class to teach with. She cares about the learning and not so much about the grade. This way you can take risks and not have the pressure of being 100% perfect just for a grade.

Liz Brixey was my favorite my professor during my 4 years at Mizzou. She was kind, understanding, and extremely passionate about what she teaches. Every morning shed have an incredible energy that made you want to do well in her class. Best of all, she has compassion for her students and doesnt have an ego.
super understanding and helpful, great person, relaxed vibe in class
She is such an engaging professor to have. She really cares about her students. Most of that class was based on news releases and profile stories, so she gave great feedback to those.

Liz is great, and an inspiration. She gives lots of good advice, and makes sure to help you as an editor and as a friend. That being said, don't expect an easy edit. If your writing sucks, she will tell you to fix it. Overall, the friendliest, and most honest editor.
Fun instructor who stands up for her reporters-- against anyone (even you know who...). Difficult to read sometimes, but she really does want everyone to excel.
Intense personality, but fun

I'd heard horror stories about this class before taking it. None of them were true. Liz is one of those professors who actually cares that her students are learning, and will go to bat for them, even to Tom Warhover. Really got the best out of me.

I came into this class not really liking journalism but within the first week she reminded me why I enjoyed journalism.  She takes an honest and sincere interest in her students and goes out of her way to help as well.  She is a little quirky but that makes the class even more fun.
