I came into this class not really liking journalism but within the first week she reminded me why I enjoyed journalism.  She takes an honest and sincere interest in her students and goes out of her way to help as well.  She is a little quirky but that makes the class even more fun.

Her class lectures do not make any sense (poor organization); writes on a chalk board as if people in the back of the lecture hall can read it; doesn't use a microphone in a large lecture hall (even though someone asked her to); she's a boring lecturer; made everyone buy a top hat subscription when we have MAYBE 1 question per class.
You are going to have to study but it's not bad. She's generous with a curve.

She's a kind professor and you can tell that she's interested in criminology (she's very well versed), but her lectures are awful. She reiterates what you read in the book and reads straight off the powerpoint. The only benefit of showing up is for extra credit, but you could definitely get an A without showing up once.

sooooo boring. everyone is always falling asleep in her class and no one ever knows what she's talking about. reads directly off the powerpoint and makes us try and do online participation while in class but the internet never works so we just waste time. super frustrating

I didn't learn a single thing in this class. Bin Wu is a pretty funny professor but he pretty much talks in circles for the entire class. You can tell he knows a lot about what he is talking about but hes not great at sharing what he knows. I made a total ChatGPT mess for the final and got an A. I don't think he actually graded anything at all.

Show up to lectures and participate. If you form a relationship with him, he will help you out if you need it. Make sure you email the TA if you have any questions. Only three assignments were graded all semester, so do them well.
He is a good guy and a decent teacher. When he talks about the stuff he's known for, i.e. energy efficiency, then his class gets really interesting. Doesn't require a lot of work.

A terrible lecturer, class is very easy. Grading is random. He is the author of the textbook which sucks too. Learned nothing, need refund. He assignments are very simple. Since he is tenured and has been in the school for a long time, I think he is waiting to retire. Absolutely not inspiring at all. I will rate negative if the system allows.

Bin Wu is a great guy. Had lots of fun in the class. Didn't learn as much as I would have liked to though. 3 assignments and a group project, all a lot of work. Start early and work hard. Otherwise, the class is fairly easy going. Lectures could drag as he tends to talk in circles. Some topics are very interesting. Pretty easy class all around,

Dr. Wu is such a friendly & funny guy.  The material has the potential to be very dry, but Dr. Wu does his best to keep it interesting and get the students involved in a discussion.  As long as you do the assignments, you will get a good grade.  My only complaints are that his handwriting is difficult to read and his class is not on Blackboard.
Honestly I really enjoyed taking this class. It's a super easy one. I promise you will end up with an A. However, You won't learn so much about systems. it's a really really basic class.

VERY SIMPLE CLASS. Literally the easiest class I've ever taken... Except English 1000 with Galenas. His TA was worthless and graded poorly. Don't be surprised when you get a bad grade for doing GREAT work. Somehow, you still end up with an A, or I did anyway haha.
Difficult to understand, fairly easy class
It's an easy A. You don't need to show up to any of the lectures, they're useless. The papers and the final project are all complete jokes. It's a sign up and pass class.
TA does everything. His information is not updated and his research is so-so. Papers are published in unknown associations.
No Comments

This guy is awesome. He's a genuine teacher who is there for his students and wants them to succeed. There aren't any quizzes unlike most calculus classes and notecards are allowed on exams. The exams themselves have easy problems and as long as you have good notecard and you understand what you're solving for, its basically a guaranteed A.

prof banks is one of the greatest calc professors i have ever taken and is extremely nice. he is willing to answer any question and values connections with students during lectures. his exams were pretty similar to the practice exams he gave out, and as long as you do the homework and do the practice exams, you're bound to do well in the course.
He cares about the students. Great professor, he's always there to help. Seems like a very genuine professor who loves math and teaching it. Highly recommend him.
One of the best Calc Professors I had. Related Calculus to everyday life, made lectures fun with jokes in between. Despite having him for an 8:00 Am lecture, I thoroughly enjoyed the course.

Super chill guy. Really cared more about you understanding instead of memorizing formulas so he gave you formula sheets. Practice tests were usually like the exams but not always. Can easily get off on tangents during lecture and isn't the best at explaining hard concepts. Gave an easy term paper instead of a final.

Dr. Banks is an awesome professor! By far the best math professor I've ever had. Managed to make the material not seem too intimidating and is always cracking jokes. We were allowed notecards and/or a page of notes on exams and there aren't pop quizzes. He really wants you to succeed and gives you all the tools you need to do so.

This man is so funny and nice. He is passionate about Mathematics and making sure you understand it. He truly cares and is very genuine, and is always available for extra help if you need it. He taught me Calculus while reducing my stress about it, and I definitely recommend taking a class with him.

I was so glad I had Prof Banks. His lectures were usually pretty easy to follow, but the practice exams were the best way to study for exams. He is very understanding and gave extensions on quizzes/homework and would curve if needed. The homework was much harder than the exams but would be available for questions if we had them.

12/10 professor, made number theory extremely interesting and fun. Grades are mostly based on completion, and he will do everything in his power to get you a good grade. As long as you participate and care, you are set.

I was afraid to take this class since I had not taken calculus in many years. However, Dr. Banks is incredible at explaining complex topics, so not only was I able to do well enough in his class, but he helped me really succeed. His assignments are helpful, and his exams are very manageable. Take a class from Dr. Banks if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy. He told us day 1 that as long as you show up and participate, you'll get an A. His lectures are funny in an intentionally-awkward/nerdy sense and he's really helpful. He doesn't use online Canvas a lot, so take good notes if you need them. Participate in class, it makes it more fun!

Bill is a really cool guy, probably the best professor I've had at mizzou. He goes over the material in a way that is example heavy so you actually can do the problems instead of just copying down a theorem. He tells you exactly what is going to be on the tests and takes questions from the practice tests. Dude also has a sick tattoo on his arm.
Really nice guy.  makes you want to try hard in his class because he is very nice to his students

Prof. Banks is a really great professor. He made Calc. 3 very easy to understand and follow. His tests are extremely straightforward and not too difficult if you do the practice exams he posts online. He prints out a lot of his notes. He may talk with a monotone, but he is the professor you should have for Calc. 3.
great guy and very easy going and solid grader.

Hey's a great guy who cares about you learning and your grade. He allows you to have a notecard for the test and actually curves the tests a little bit so that helps your grade. Definitely learned Calculus 3 better than I thought I would.
He teaches very well. His methods of teaching are relaxed and relate-able . He makes the complex concepts in Multivariable Calculus seems trivial and obvious. I definitely recommend this guy!

Dr. Banks was extremely helpful! He held my attention well! Calc 2 with Banks is an easy A because of his articulate teaching style and nearly flawless presentation; I learned the material with ease. Tests actually tested my knowledge and aren't excessively difficult.
He has a low somewhat monotone voice which makes it very easy to sleep if you take his class in the morning.  he is very willing to help his students.
he is really boring but he tries to help...did i mention really boring.  He will occasionnally print out his notes.  Oh, and really boring....Try not to take it in the morning you will fall asleep
No Comments
No Comments

He tries to be funny/nice but at the end of the day he's still an old white man who frankly refuses to make his class more accessible. He refused to record lectures despite the pleading of many students. He also refuses to share grade cutoffs so you never know where you stand. His tests are also nightmarish. The curve saved me though 🙏

DO NOT TAKE HIM. His class is 100% test based and there are hardly any practice problems. On exams, he gives you half the alphabet to choose from to "eliminate guessing" (The last exam had options A-J and took up half the page). The only bonus is the gigantic curve, which hovers around 60-65% is an A, because everyone needs it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: James Birchler is one of the best professors at Mizzou.  Not only are his lectures fun and engaging, he saved my semester.  I failed multiple tests and still got an A, and there was not an attendance grade to worry about.  I would recommend Dr. Birchler to anyone and am very sad to be done with his class.

Just. Ew. Avoid at all costs. This is a class you luckily have other sections available for. Take them. This man is incredibly unhelpful in preparing you for his exams and the TAs can't save you. Studying is irrelavant at best and academic dishonesty is the only way I've seen people guarantee an A--regardless of how much work one puts in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are the only grades. Huge curve however (above 65 is an A). I took notes outside of class so I can pay attention in class better, it helped me. Go to every lecture. Discussions are mediocre. Also does review sessions with TAs before each test outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. B is a great guy but has a very specific lecture style. You will only succeed if you participate in class and do the recommended problems. If you don't do well in traditional lecture type course take it with another prof. Tests are the only thing in the grade book besides two 10 page paper extra credit opportunities. Curve is huge though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Like other people said, Dr Birchler has great motives as a professor, but struggles to put it into action. Final grade is made entirely of multiple-choice tests that have up to 8 or 9 choices per question. I felt like I learned more in discussion, but then again, the TAs can only cover so much. There is an extreme grading curve for a reason
This class was very difficult, I worked hard outside class to get an A. Exams were basically the entirety of the grade. With that being said, his office hours were helpful and he's a goofy guy.

Had no idea how hard this class would be going into it and I usually get mostly As or Bs in my STEM classes. His lectures are very boring as they are read off of slides and the tests are the only component of your final grade. There's an extra credit opportunity but I personally didn't think it was worth it. I also had no idea how to study for test
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take with anyone else. I went to class, studied hard, did all the ungraded homework and felt like the tests were a guessing game - all this time learning the material on my own only to be given a test question with 8 mutule choice options that seemed impossible to answer. TAs said we were SOL. Dr. B is a great guy, not so great intro genetics prof.

Dr. Birchler is a very nice guy and cares about his students. Use his course pamphlet, it has all of the lecture information and study guides that have the content covered on the exams. The exams are tough and have many answer options, but if you put in the work outside of class then you can get a good grade with the extreme curve that is applied.
He is a nice guy, but really not a good professor. He speeds through lectures that don't really make sense and I barely learned anything this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No homework so all grades are from 5 tests although he drops the lowest score. Covers anywhere from 30-60 slides per day and speeds through the slides to get through them all. Studying is a requirement in this class and if you don't it will make things much more difficult. The good thing is he uses an extreme grading curve. Wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. B is a really nice guy, but this class was just not good. He goes very quickly through lectures (just reads off slides). You're only graded on tests which are near impossible with very low averages. Only plus is the ridiculous curve. I ended with an A but don't feel that I learned anything. Class was a guessing game.

BIO 2220 was probably one of the hardest classes I have ever had to take in college. The tests in this course seemed nearly impossible. Dr. Bichler is a really nice person, but not the best at teaching. His teaching style was something that caused me to struggle in his class. You are only graded on tests. Tough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. Buzzes through his lectures reading straight from the slides. Very quiet even with a microphone and hard to hear and understand. The only thing you are graded on are exams and there is such a large curve on the exams it is almost impossible to fail the course while still not learning anything from the course. My best advice is to not take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Due to COVID Dr. Birchler struggled to balance more difficult problems due to exams being open note, and reinforcing basic topics through exams. This showed through final average 30%. Although he curved and made it fair. Regardless Dr. Birchler is an amazing person and I would of loved to take this class in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. B is a great guy. He cares about his students and curved the class grade so much that a test with a D average was turned to a B average. He is very intelligent and the only reason I wouldn't take him again is because the genetics class itself was boring, but Dr. B is very monotone which did not help the boring class. Great guy, just boring.

Birchler is an amazing prof and very caring. Definitely wants the best for his students and rewards improvement. He does curve the test which are helpful. Read the book and practice problems but can still pass by if only listening to lectures. He made class intriguing and definitely one of my fav prof especially in the pandemic

I would rather take Organic Chem over 3 times then take this again. Tests were curved a lot but I learned nothing. Just guessed and was lucky to get an A. TAs didn't even know how to do the problems (they tried their best). Unnecessarily hard & lecture material/practice & books problems were much easier than tests. Only graded by 4 tests & final.

Only five grades were put into the grade book for the whole semester which were the tests. The tests were horribly hard with only 10 questions on them with up to 8 choices per question. He would never truly explain anything and would just read and click through up to 50 slides in a PowerPoint. Didnt learn from him. Class was simply a guessinggame
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was unbelievably difficult. The test averages are abysmal and there was a ridiculous curve but it was not enough to make up for the impossible questions in the exams. Dr. Birchler is a good guy and cares about his students but it does not make up for how awful his tests are. Avoid him and take genetics with the other professor
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a really sweet guy and is very knowledgeable but not the best at fully explaining what you truly need to know. Everything seems to get muddled in the lectures. You can also get caught in the loop of falling behind so keep up with the lectures! Consult the biology handbook he gives you as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class while its online. Exams are near impossible, and were made even harder due to the fact they were online. Not to mention some exam problems would take three TAs approximately 20 minutes to complete. No HW grade, only 10 question exams with impossible questions. prepare to see class averages dip in the 35%-55% range per exam
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Birchler is a great professor. The class was entertaining and the material is really interesting. That being said, the tests were almost impossible. But dont let that scare you away completely, because he curves them HEAVILY. There were multiple instances where a 60% was an A in the grade book. Honestly, it was a good class

This class is unbelievable and not in a good way. He tried to make it hard due it being online and because of that he made the concepts impossible to understand. Never have I EVER saw a class as big as a joke as this class was. He also has a VERY monotone voice. Would NEVER take again. Better hope he curves be class average is like around 60ish%

The only reason I got an A is because he curves the exams so much. There are NO other grades besides exams (all worth 100 points). I learned absolutely nothing from this class. Take it with anyone else but him. Trust me.

As indicated by many other reviews, this was the most unnecessarily burdensome class that was made exceedingly more difficult during a pandemic. Was definitely not an introductory level genetics course if the TAs struggled on problems. Take this class with the other professor and save yourself from the stress and pain this class brought us.

One of the worst courses I have ever taken at Mizzou. lectures were very informational heavy that at times it was extremely difficult to retain any information for exams. Even the TAs said this course was too difficult for a 2000 level class. Class averages for exams were very low. Birchlers class made dealing with the pandemic even more stressful

Dr. Birchler is really intelligent, he just has a tendency to be monotone and drone on a bit. Covid made the class entirely online and the only points came from tests which sucked but he curved the grades so much that it was nearly impossible to fail. Good guy, just a bit boring.

This was the most pointless and difficult class I have ever faced. Just take Genetics with the other professor. He is very nice and cares about his students but that does not make up for his exams. Only 10 questions and each of them were impossible to do. He gives a really big curve but it pales in comparison to the stress and pain you will suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the hardest class I've ever taken. The only thing students are graded by is the tests. The tests are so hard that sometimes the TA's struggle to figure out the answer. The tests are all online and not proctored, so there's no way to prove if other students are cheating. It hurts students who are being ethical because the tests are curved.

Absolutely terrible. No matter how much I prepared it was never reflected in my test exams. Im normally a good student but this class was honestly impossible. I have had so much stress over exams, that even the TAs said were extremely difficult for a 2000 level course. He is a nice guy ig but has really made a hard period of time so much worse.

The hardest class I have ever taken. Harder than orgo, gen chem I and II etc. He has restructured the class during the pandemic, and made it much more difficult. Tests are around 9-10 multiple choice questions with approx. 8 options each, with a very restricting timeframe. Has a great personality but has done his students a disservice this semester

If this class is online, do not take it under any circumstances. The grade in the class is 100% based on exams, and he will lecture over almost nothing on the exam. I feel like I haven't learned anything despite going to every lecture and doing all the review because I open the exam and only know how to do about 2/10 questions.

Deliberately made tests impossible during a pandemic. Reason being the class is online and thus open book, but it doesnt make sense. Tests are 100% of the grade, and the study material is rainbows and sunshine compared to the tests. Its unnecessarily stressful in an already stressful time, and the class average is so low, the curve is huge. 0/10
Really nice guy, but tests are impossible. I watched every lecture, filled out the study guide, and still would fail the tests. Nothing he teaches is on the test.

Dr. Birchler is a great teacher, he made genetics very enjoyable. If you can try to get ahold of past exams, lots of questions are similar and they make great study materials. Also, really pay attention and study the blue book as well as problems from his lecture slides. A good chunk of his tests are vocabulary so take memorizing those seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult. The course is lecture heavy and the only "book" available is a handout written by Birchler. This book is supposed to be the best thing ever but turns out only includes 1/2 of material needed. TA's were unhelpful and exams were overly difficult. Grades were not clearly defined. TAKE GENETICS WITH SOMEONE ELSE!

Dr. Birchler is honestly a very kind and caring man. However, his teaching is not wonderful, and his tests are quite awful if you do not have access to old exams. Get the old exams and you will pass this class easily. Study the old tests but study the new material as well since not every question is the same as the old exam.

A bit monotone but quite the character; never fails to surprise. One of the most respected professors at MU. You'll be glad you took a class with this legend! Some of the most memorable lectures I've had. His blue book is a true gift; literally all the info needed for exams. Willing to curve grades if you participate & show effort/improvement!

Dr. Birchler is AWESOME. His class is interesting, he makes a boring topic fun. I never missed his class because I wanted to be there. His tests are difficult but very straight forward. He gives a study guide and there are never any surprises on his exams. There are old exams online that are similar so if you do take the course look over old exams

Dr. Birchler is great and always willing to help. Study the blue book and nothing else. That was a little nerve-wracking for me, but I got 90 and above on every test and you usually only need a 65-75 for an A. If you don't understand everything in the blue book, go to office hours. As long as you just memorize the blue book, it's an easy A.

You definitely have to work for a good grade in this class. Get his blue book at study it! He throws a surprise in there every once in a while, but for the most part everything comes from that blue book. His lectures are a little confusing if you're not paying complete attention.
Dr. James Birchler is an excellent professor. It is not difficult to get an A for his class; I got an A plus.

I don't know why people don't like him. He is very helpful and so are the TA's. They answer emails all night before an exam. The tests are not hard at all if you just follow the study guide. He will never give you a question that is not on the study guide. What more can you ask for.

This class is awful. Dr. Birchler tries to make it interesting but he talks so monotone and still uses the overhead projector from elementary school. Tests are HARD. TA's don't help. Take this class with a different professor if you want an A.

Lectures are really boring.  Going to lecture isn't even required to do well on tests.  But, you should go to know if you're in the "big 12" or not.  You need to know EVERYTHING in the blue book, know how to do all RSD problems, follow the study guide and know all the definitions in each "study questions Test # Whatever and you'll get an A!

He is rediculously intellegent and tries to make it interesting, however his voice is rather boring. Read the blue book like the bible and it will help you. I would say he is affraid to give A's. Went to his office seven times to fight for my A, and never got it, deffantly deserved it, you will need to study hard core for exams  to do well at all.

Fell asleep in lecture once or twice and I'm a good student. He dresses up like Mendel and tries to make things interesting. His voice makes you pass out though. Go to rsd. Do what the blue notebook says like it's the bible. Tests are graded with a HARD hand, quite frustrating. The TAs are frightened to give us partial credit for frear of Birchler.

Birchler is a great guy, and a great researcher, but his lectures put most students to sleep.  I went to all the classes, but I never felt as if I gained much from going.  His tests are not hard, but they are really tricky - you get everything you need to know for the tests in the notebook.  Virtually no student-prof interaction.  Go to RSD!

Already graduated and heading to med school. Still remember Genetics with Bircher as my hardest biology class in undergrad. Goes really fast, assigns lots of problems. Felt like I just memorized stuff without ever understanding. Wonderful man, but horrible teacher. Go the TAs for help!
Dr Birchler is an extremly caring man who is more interested in his students learning, than his own ego.  The things he does to help his points sink into his students is commendable.

He can be a funny guy, but mostly, he's extremely boring. Everything is right out of the notebook, so going to class is worthless. Be prepared to memorize more info than you ever thought possible. It's a hard class, but if you study, you'll be fine.
Very boring lectures.  He only goes over info. already given in packets.  Hard, long, written tests
Good class. Interesting.  Hard tests.  Funny lectures!

Dr. Coleman facilitated a hands-on and approachable classroom. He made sure that no question would go unanswered, and created a very in-depth discussion environment. It is a fantastic way to understand political strife, violence, and change. It is an engaging and entertaining class, and I cannot recommend it enough.

This class is entirely discussion based and you have to read 30-50 pages every two to three days. However, Dr Coleman leads wonderful discussions, he is hilarious, great at feedback, and so passionate. All of the Kinder classes are very participation-based, so if you don't honestly enjoy the topic, do not take. If you do though, Billy is fantastic
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class Fall 2021 and would highly recommend Billy Coleman. He is a caring professor that provides a great classroom environment. Be sure to attend as many classes as possible since participation is a huge part of grading. Big projects are the main grades such as a couple presentations and the final paper/creative history project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great Professor, he is always willing to meet outside of class. There is a lot of reading and a large project due at the end of the semester, don't let this scare you the class is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgeable professor who is very polite. She will literally spend time with students outside of class, and kindly imparts knowledge. Clearly loves what she does and is passionate. Take her.

As long as you watch the lectures, the tests are a piece of cake. There's daily reading, but I didn't personally find it necessary. There are weekly quizzes but they aren't too bad either. Teacher is very sweet and even sent out emails to let you know you're doing a good job.

Being a big fan of mythology and the ancient world to begin with, this class was really enjoyable and Professor Binek's lectures were fun and easy to follow. If you attend lecture, take notes, and do the assigned readings you will succeed in this class and have fun while doing so.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I never read but I went to every single class. She is very passionate but quick to talk so you have to be fully focused or might as well not even go to class. Getting an A is very possible but get ready to work and study. I thought it was gonna be a blowoff and its not . Weekly quizzes based off readings :/ tests are so hard if you're not prepared.
Binek was great! I loved learning about the content and stories, and she did a great job explaining the stories. She was positive and upbeat. The way she taught made me want to come to class.
very knowledge; kind and always willing to help or discuss; great use of TAs; lectures were well structured and highly effective; course work wasn't boring; her slides were phenomenal
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Binek presented everything extremely clearly, showed what was important & her lectures were entertaining with plenty of images & bit of humor. She was very helpful when I saw her during office hours about an issue. Textbook was sometimes confusing so the lectures were a must. Overall, I liked learning about myth & might take more AMS courses.

***She was not very personable or friendly, relied heavily on TAs. Good: -lots of opportunities for extra credit -5 point quizzes each week online were pretty easy Bad: -study guides were unfathomably vague and unhelpful -Its ALL lecture -all test based, if you fail one test, you're pretty much screwed -NOT engaging during lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: great professor, knows her stuff and presents the material in a way which makes clear whats important in the many, many stories, gods, and people of mythology. the textbook jumps around a lot, but the lectures put things in order. the quizzes are easy if you do your readings and come to class. she posts a review aid for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think her lectures are nice blend of images & stories, and interpretation of myth (she keeps bringing up the question what is myth?). Her organization makes sense, it works well with the textbook. I really enjoy the course.

She jumps around in lecture a lot, and the tests are difficult but it comes down to if you read the book and pay attention in class. Also showing up in class is important. She post summaries of the slides but not the full presentation.

She isn't a bad professor, she just doesn't know how to handle all of the students and her class in general. She kind of talks down on her class (treats us like elementary students). The way she does her notes and lectures is very confusing because there is no structure to it at all (she jumps back and forth) which makes mythology very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: her lecture structure is super super weird. she jumps around all the time which can be confusing, and super tough for tests. She has maybe 12 quizzes for 5 points each which are difficult but online. and she has 3 legitimate tests that are LONG and tough, all on paper. i would NOT recommend her for AMS 1060, take anyone else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Stone was very welcoming and made an easy transition into college. Attendance was very important for daily in-class activities and notes on lecture. You can walk away from this class with multiple basil plants and maybe African violets, would definitely recommend.

Class is pretty easy as long as you pay attention and study. The content isn't difficult to digest, but can seem off-topic at times. Class is structured around small groups and there is a lot of busy work during class, which attendance is part of your grade.

Dr. Stone is the greatest! She is so kind, smart, and funny. If you come to lecture and use the study resources given to you, you will do great. She wants each and every student to succeed. She once got on to me for being on my laptop lol. Later in the semester I realized she really just wants a class full of attentive students who will do great.

She is such a lovely woman and she genuinely cares about your learning. You have to go to class every day to get a good grade. If you show up to class and actively study you will do well. Generous drop policy. Great choice to get your biological science with a lab credit! The labs are not that difficult and you will have to do a group long project.

Dr. Stone is a very smart and enthusiastic professor who cares very deeply about her subject. I would not recommend this class if it is not required for your major or you do not have a big interest in botany. It is very test heavy and there is an exam every 3 weeks. She likes to put in confusing word questions so I would reread everything.

The tests are very difficult to understand. She uses AI to write them, and student made questions. I personally knew the subject, but when I go in for exams, I feel dumb because of the way they are written. She is not very forgiving with attendance. This class is very group-heavy, and if you don't have good teammates, be ready to do everything.

Bethany Stone was an excellent professor. She breaks things down well, and really only focuses on necessary topics that you can connect with other topics in later classes. Bethany is very considerate of your time, and is willing to work with you if you can't make a deadline. 
I didn't love the group project, but that was more because of the group.

Aside from the semester long project with strangers and a random lecture about AI in place of an exam review, I have really enjoyed Dr. Stone's class. She is kind and grades fairly, plus she is extremely understanding when her students are unable to attend class or submit an assignment on time for unexpected reasons. I would definitely recommend!

-will keep you late everyday
-does not talk about anything worthwhile in class
ex. she spent the entire 50 minutes of last class talking about how to use AI opposed to helping us review for our exam two days later
ex2. spent the ENTIRE first two weeks trying to convince us why a harvested apple is alive... that is just incorrect and wastes my money

Dr. Stone is a super nice women who teaches botany in an easy to understand way. She will talk to you about plants all day long and will answer any questions you have. I thought her lectures were entertaining and interesting and very easy to follow and take notes on. I would love to have her again!

What an amazing professor and person Dr.Stone is. She always came to class with a smile on her face, no matter what she was going through. The lectures were easy to follow and interesting. The labs were well thought out and participation made your grade. The only downside is a semester-long project with random partners.
She's a great lecturer, makes the material interesting with her passion
She does a wonderful job at making lectures interesting and is super kind and respectful to all her students :)

She's very difficult to work with for disability accommodations compared to other professors I have had. 
Attendance is mandatory despite a lot of the content being very basic concepts that I've learned in high school biology courses. There's a lot of work outside of class including growing a plant, a grow log for the plant, and a group project.

Dr. Stone is an engaging professor who genuinely cares about her students. While the group work can be a bit annoying, it's not too difficult if you put in the effort. Using unstuck AI along with the provided materials made studying much easier.

Lecture is heavy and even the smallest things will be on all exams. Tests are a little hard to prepare for as random things mentioned in class and small "non important" details are involved. Good professor though, you can tell she cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

You can tell she really wants her students to succeed in this class. She makes it as easy as it can be to pass, as long as you show up and pay attention. There was a group research project, but if you put in effort and follow instructions it's pretty easy to do well on. She leaves feedback on the group submission, which is also helpful.

Dr. Stone was a good professor however, she made this class hard for non-majors. I heard the professor that teaches this course in the fall is far easier. If you are a non-major like I was I'd recomend taking this course in the fall semester. Attendance is mandatory and you have assigned seats. Overall, not a bad class but content was rough.

Dr. Stone is a very caring person and you get "free" points for doing ICAS if you just show up to class, so that's nice, it boosts your grade. But, you do get an assigned group (and group project) + assigned seats which felt very high school to me. My biggest issue is that she requires paper notes unless you email her and ask to use electronics...

I LOVE DR. STONE!!! People often complain about her mandatory group work, which can be annoying, but really isn't difficult. Most of the in-class assignments with your group are easy review sheets that get you "free" points as long as you show up. Dr. Stone is so engaging and kind, and I know she cares so much about her classes. Totally recommend!

While 1010 was a huge class and I never actually talked to her outside of answering questions in class, I found her to be a pleasant teacher and seemingly a pretty solid person. She clearly cares about her students and their success (she does a ton of studies on how to get the best results, apparently). Would recommend.

Dr. Stone is a great professor and genuinely cares about your success as long as you work with her to achieve that. She does assign a team and team project as well as making you sit with your team during class, and she has a lot of in class assignments but if you pay attention and do what you're supposed to its all super easy.

Dr. Stone genuinely cares about her students and what she is teaching. Be prepared for a seating chart and mandatory semester team project. She does a good job of making things fair though and always explains information very well. If you don't think you will attend class every single time, don't take this class as it will hurt your grade.

Dr. Stone's class is very interesting and will help you learn a lot. Beware of seating charts, mandatory group projects outside of class, mandated paper notes, and participation. She definitely cares about her students, but you have to attend class in order to pass. Prepare for 6 exams and a lab practical over the semester.
Super similar to a high school class, with mandatory attendance, seating charts, etc.
great

I loved Dr.Stone. She was always enthusatic, well prepared, & is one of my fav prof I've ever had. Attendance is mantatory but at 9am she still made fun/intersting. She had practice exams that were close to the actual exams, encourgaed participation, & was very helpful if you had a question. I loved her slideshows and the organzation of her class.

The class is ran like Highschool. Assigned seating/Group projects and ICA's EVERYDAY
That being said, if you pay attention and show up to class you will do great. She is very clear on what will be on the exam and its obvious she wants all students to succeed. Lectures are very comprehensible and I ended the year understanding every topic in detail.
She is a fun professor.

I liked how this professor really cared about teaching. The only thing I didn't care for at all was the group project. It lasted the entire semester and was frustrating. Other than that she is very approachable and never thinks that there are stupid questions. All the TAs are amazing.

I had Dr. Stone for genetics and it was her first time teaching the course, so my experience may not be indicative of her as a professor. If you do have to take her, my best advice is not to get complacent. Lots of reading, lots of homework, test criteria aren't clearly communicated, and whether you have a good TA is rolling the dice. Hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved professor stone! She was very clear in lectures about what we needed to know and what we didn't. She was always available for help outside of class and would try several different methods to help you understand the content. The only bad thing about this course was the TA never seeming prepared for discussion.

Some of her teaching methods could be a bit annoying but she truly cares about her students. As someone who's immunocompromised her decision to separate the class by masking habits was highly appreciated and helped keep me safe. Overall her class was more accessible than most but it is necessary to attend in-person lectures most of the time.

Prof Stone can be reminiscent of a high school teacher but is very engaging during lectures. However there are seating charts, and assignments in class every single lecture. Tests were either a breeze or oddly difficult but it's manageable if you study a bit. Just show up to class and take good notes and you'll be fine.
Super easy class, attendance matters tho. Lots of extra credit opportunities and group work.

If you want to feel like you're in high school again, this is the class for you. Seating charts, mandatory attendance, and group projects with people you don't choose are just a few of the things you'll see. The class in general isn't hard but it can get very frustrating when it comes to the class dynamic.

BIO 2150. This class did not cover many genetic diseases. It spent most of the course reviewing basic biology with the last 6 weeks of class going over genetic diseases. You do a group project for the entire semester and the class mostly consists of busy work. Class felt like a writing intensive with how much you had to do. Lots of researching

This class is easily my least favorite in-person course I've taken at Mizzou. The professor acts like a high school teacher and expects people to sit in groups, attend every lecture, and participate in group projects a lot. Short answer? Too much emphasis on ICAs and group participation.

Dr. Stone is a very kind professor, and does seem to genuinely care about her students. However, only take this class if you enjoyed high school. If you are ready to be treated like an adult, then this is not the class for you. She assigns seating (ew) and even has done the "I'll wait.." in response to light chatter. It is just so annoying

She was a great professor. Except we had assigned seats which was stupid because were in a lecture with 200 plus people. Felt like I was taking a course from a highschool professor. Separated us in people who no joke will wear a mask in class and then people who wont wear a mask in class. Even sent out. survey asking if I was vaccinated.

This class is easy if you attend. She has in class activities that are graded, but she drops the lowest 3. Final is also optional. She provides so many helpful materials to help study for exams, such as like 3 past exams and a study guide with tons of helpful video links. She genuinely wants you to do well, and her exams are not written to trick u
Great teacher, if you study you'll do fine, really kind
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Stone is everything you want to see in a professor. Shes understanding, caring, funny, and good at teaching! She never makes you feel stupid for asking a question. Love Bethany Stone!
She was awesome!!

Dr. Stone has been my favorite professor by far. Her canvas site is extremely well organized which makes a normally difficult class pretty easy to do well in as long as you put in the effort. She breaks up the lecture videos into individual topics so it doesn't get boring. If you are interested in plant science at all, this class won't be too hard.

While the class seemed daunting at first, I was able to utilize her Canvas in order to stay organized. Everything Dr. Stone does is in order to help her students learn, and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. She was always enthusiastic and used real-life examples in her teaching. Stay on top of your work, and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Stone! She is an amazing example of what a professor should be like. Incredibly caring and understanding, she was flexible with the pandemic and was available during office hours outside of class every week, and is willing to help you. There is group work in lab, and a decent amount of assignments. Relatively easy if you study well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Stones Bio 1010 class. She is so nice and is great at teaching the course content.

Very sweet person. Felt like I was back in a high school classroom with the way she taught. That being said the material in the class is mostly high school AP material so it's incredibly easy. There is a group project of some sort but with the COVID-19 pandemic we just didn't do it.

Professor Stone is the best professor I have had at Mizzou to date. She cares about how well her students do and strives for them to succeed. She offers many opportunities for extra credit and is always willing to create office hour times for you to come in and get ideas on how to improve. I highly recommend her for BIO.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Anyone who gives Professor Stone a poor score just doesn't want to work for a good grade. Stone is funny and relatable, applies all material to real life, and truly cares about how well her students are learning. She is extremely passionate about bio. Tales awhile to answer emails, but thats about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I would never take one of her courses again. I am an education major that was forced to take this as a class for credits and it was horrible. She was not that caring and did not respond to many emails. It was way too difficult for an entry level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really easy class for a gen ed science. You do have to sit with "teams" that she assigns all semester which can be annoying. Participation assignments every class- easy points but you can't skip. Tests are a breeze if you study and she ends up offering almost 50 extra credit points. Group project at the end but she grades it easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the class! Interesting lectures, and I already find myself applying some of the concepts we discussed in class to everyday life. I especially liked being able to take home each of our exams and immediately have access to the answer keys to review.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: NEVER take a class with this professor. Gives out in class assignments almost every class, that can really hurt your grade if you miss class frequently. Horrible teaching style that involves readings and videos to watch before class and poor lecture. 6 exams, and ridiculous group work/projects make this class one of the worst I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is an excellent teacher, but enjoys fitting political agenda into classes.

Dr. Stone is the best biology professor Ive ever had! I was really dreading having to take science gen eds, but she makes every topic interesting and important. I just couldnt understand protein synthesis before this class, but now its a breeze. She also really cares about her students actually learning the material :)

She was a wonderful speaker with an easy going personality, the labs were usually pretty easy but the lab reports were really long and you depend on your labmates to succeed. The readings weren't too hard and the exams were fairly comprehensive. Nothing too bad, but you did need to put in the effort.
She gives very interesting lectures. You need to go to class to pass because she does not put the power points online. She is very easy to get ahold of and very helpful when in need of help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had so far. I wish she taught other classes that I could take. She's extremely good at explaining new ideas and wants her students to understand the material.

She is very passionate about what she teaches and is really engaging in her lectures, throwing in some corny jokes here and there also! There is an in-class activity every day, so if you skip class your grade will fall, but she's very lenient on exams and such and drops the lowest few quizzes, in-class assignments, and lowest test score.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Stone was incredible!  She enthusiastically taught each class, throwing in some cheesy botanical jokes as she saw fitting.  You can tell she's a passionate and seasoned educator!  I recommend her classes.

I really loved this class. Dr. Stone is both knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. This class is partially flipped so it does take a little more time for you to be successful. I don't think it's very difficult, she gives a lot of resources to help you out for sure.

Professor Stone rocks! My major was nowhere near botany, but I highly enjoyed this class and loved 1) the real-life application of the elements of her teaching and 2) her approachability. I highly recommend taking her classes and would definitely take a class of hers again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Stone provides many materials to study for exams such as study guides, old exams, and worksheets. She makes you work for it though, it is a flipped class so you watch videos before hand and do assignments in class. 1 group project, and 5 exams plus optional final... tons of work but offers about 30 extra credit points through the year.

Gives a lot of in class work and opportunities for points, but will grade an easy extra credit very hard. She is very rude. She talks to her students like we are in a middle school health class. She will probably end up screwing you over with points due to her lack of organization/clarity at one point in the semester.

be ready to put a lot of work into this class and come to EVERY CLASS. There are in class assignments almost every class but it's a nice boost to your grade. The tests are SUPER hard but there are other assignments to bring up your grade. There is also a group project at the end of the year. Be ready to work!!
Beware of ICAs, quizzes, and a huge group project!

Don't be worried of this class being too difficult. You will have to do group activities which get annoying but if you find people you like it will be fine. Going to class is important. Only short weekly quizzes for homework. Lots of note taking.

Dr. Stone tends to spend a lot of time focusing on in-class assignments and awkward group work instead of actually teaching us the material. Since there is no textbook required for the class, she posts links to material online (some of which are outdated and/or don't work). Her tests are fairly difficult and she rarely lectures in class.

Dr. Stone is always helpful when you need it. Her office hours are flexible and is willing to schedule other meetings if needed. As long as you study you'll do fine. She's very clear on what you need to do to get a certain grade

Bethany is a great professor. She really cares about her students and walks you through everything that is going on. Class can be a little tough at times. It's all about how much time you spend outside of class studying. As long as you follow along in and outside of class you should do well.

She is a wonderful professor that knows what she's doing. She's been here for a long time and she's amazing at teaching. There are activities for points during class, so you need to go. There is a test every other week but she does this so you don't have to have as much information on each test.
She rocks! She is so helpful and I love her flipped friday activities! Can't wait to take her plant pathogen class
very helpful if you go into her office hours. lots of points so one or two bad test grades won't hurt your grade. notes are very well organized but you do have to study to get a good grade

I absolutely loved Professor Stone. It is very clear that she loves what she does, and she cares about her students. There is a lot of material to memorize, but she provides plenty of resources for students to use for studying. If you spend the time, you should't have a problem getting an A.
A lot of course material but class itself isn't too difficult-just tedious. Beth Stone is always very friendly and concise, office hours are very helpful
Great teacher. Lotttts of material to help prepare for tests. Didn't like the Friday group activities though.
Felt like I learned a lot from this class, although tests were somewhat difficult she kept the lectures interesting.

She does a lot of tegrity expecting you to learn a lot on your own. Is a tough grader, and has a test every two weeks, while the other bio 1010 classes have one per month. She isn't very flexible when asking for extra help.

The class is a large lecture class but rather than teaching during lecture, she expects you to learn the material outside of class through Tegrity (which doesn't work half the time) and gives you an assignment to complete with a partner instead. It's unbelievably frustrating.

Dr. Stone was one of the professors I liked my first semester of college. Biology is not my best or favorite subject but she finds ways to make the lectures interesting. Everything is posted to tegrity but she does do in class assignments randomly! Tests could be difficult, it just depends on your knowledge. I liked her a lot and am glad I had her!

Professor Stone is easily my favorite professor! As long as you go to class, take notes and pay attention, you will have no problem with passing. She really does a good job of making sure every has a good understanding of biology.
I went to her and inquired about my exam score being lower than I believed it should be. Mrs. Stone recommended disability services to me. Avoid her at all costs!
uses trick questions

Dr.Stone is one of the best teachers at Mizzou! She's very organized in her lectures and makes sure we all learn something. Bio has become one of my favorite subjects thanks to her. Make sure you take notes and use tegrity. If you ever need help Dr.Stone will be willing to help you. Theres no way you could fail the class!
She is a wonderful professor. I can tell she puts just as much if not more time into this class outside of the classroom as we do. She is clear, helpful, and happy. AWESOME

Definitely the best teacher I had at Mizzou. Her lectures are very organized and help a ton with the tests. She is a very fair grader. Always willing to help and goes out of her way for students to succeed. Definitely take Dr. Stone for bio!
Yes there are a ton of points for her class but her tests are nothing like her lectures.  You will do well on everything but the tests.

Best teacher I've had so far at Mizzou. I took her botany class and she was an extremely helpful teacher. Like they all said, she has a lot of points available so a bad test doesn't hurt you much, and the tests aren't that bad. No book required thanks to her use of tegrity. But go to class. Highly recommended for almost a guaranteed pass.

Took her my freshman year and LOVED the class. Hands down my favorite class. she is very clear and presents the information well. She is more than happy to answer any questions students have. Test are fairly easy as long as you go to class, take notes, and pay attention. Holds study sessions the night before exam to answer any last minute questions

SUCH a good teacher. Always willing to help and teaches things in a way that makes sense. NO TEXTBOOK NEEDED. Lectures always available on Tegrity if you miss a class. It's a lot of work (weekly assignments, multiple tests, readings before every class), but I left the class feeling like I actually learned something. Highly recommend her.

She cares about her students, but you need to attend class. She has A LOT of assignments (2 per week) plus in class assignments and in class projects. Also you will have to do a semester long project. If you lose points on ICA or ICP by missing class your grade could suffer-- they add up. However, she does offer some extra credit. No book required!

She really cares about her students and wants them to do well. Notes are extremely organized and easy to follow. However, tests can be difficult and never a curve. TONS of points, but also tons of homework. I have gotten bad test scores, but I have enough other points to make up for it. Overall a good class, and a super nice teacher.

Professor Stone is an amazing teacher! She is all about the students! Lots of points available in her class to cushion a bad test grade! If you're a non-bio major and need a bio class or are just needing an extra class I HIGHLY recommend taking a class by her!!!
AMAZING TEACHER. She is one of the best professors at Mizzou. Go to class and you'll get an A. She will do whatever she can to help you.

By far one of the easiest classes. If you go to lecture and study your notes the night before an exam there is no reason you should get more than 2 questions wrong per test. There are so many ways to earn points in her class it's not even funny!

She's an awesome teacher. Gives great examples and explanations. It would be very difficult to fail this class as long as you show up and pay attention. All of her classes are recorded on tegrity but she has in class assignments. These assignments are good practice for the test/quizzes.

She is so helpful! I'm not a science-oriented person at all, but she made the class so much fun. She wants everyone to learn and feel comfortable with what they're learning. Attendance is essential because she has in-class assignments all the time, but they are good to build up a solid grade.  I would definitely recommend any class with her!
Absolutely loved this professor. She loves what she teaches and makes learning fun. She is very student oriented. I would highly RECOMMEND her!
She really makes it her goal to have everyone in the class succeed.  Also, she makes everything relatable and constantly tries to work into her lecture what students want to learn about.

Great teacher, tests are mostly multilevel choice. There are in class assignents are easy points. All notes are by PowerPoint. Don't need textbook!! Makes bio interesting and easy. Homework every once & a while also boosts grade! Really nice! Best bio 1000 level lecturer! Take it! Easy A (or at worst B)
were clear teaching and tests are straight forward
I thought I would hate Biology, but she made it interesting. Everything we learned was applicable to everyday real life. It's a super easy class if you go to lecture.
Such a great professor! Makes coming to class fun. Tests are difficult - be sure to put extra effort into studying - but the class is completely worth it. You will learn a lot.
GREAT TEACHER! The tests are HARD but she does so many in class assignments so, if you go you can easily get at least a high B! FUN CLASS!!!!

Awesome teacher! If you go to class pay attention and take notes you will understand the material. Study for the test and use the study guides and you will be fine! She seems to know not everyone is a bio major and has to take this class so she makes it intersting for everyone.
Go to class, you'll get an A

Class was awesome.  She made it interesting, and her notes were really easy to understand and follow.  I did not like how lab and lecture did not flow together.  She also had some technical difficulties w/her laptop, but class was just canceled early.  She's a great teacher, and I am sure you will enjoy the class as much as I did.
Very easy Just go to class for the IN class assignments. Non-cumulative exam. Just lot of fun.

If you go to class and do all the work there is no reason you shouldnt get an A.  Her notes are easy to follow and she gives you a study guide for every test based on the notes.  She is very helpful and knowledgable
LOVE HER!!! She makes science (for non-majors) so much fun. I understand it and she gives great examples! Definitely one of my favorite teachers. It should be a decent grade.
One of my most memorable teachers ever here @ MU. She's very outgoing, and fun to have.  She's extremely nice, helpful and understanding (always willing to help!) Definitely reccommend her!

Dr. Stone cares greatly about her students understanding of the material and wants to help everyone achieve the grade they want. She offers lots of online resources for further understanding beyond the thorough notes she gives during class. No textbook, and lots of points in the class. Remember when weekly assignments are due and you should be fine
The BEST teacher I have EVER had so far in college. I thought the online questions were sometimes difficult but it REALLY helps for the test. Also, the online review sessions were GREAT!
Incredible lady. Best teacher I've had this semester, made the transition to college a wonderful experience.
very helpful and even drops some of your lowest grades, i felt confident in getting a good grade in the class because she's very fair
Great teacher...I enjoy the class
Great professor.

Bethany was the best teacher I've ever had. PERIOD! She made biology interesting and relevant to our day-to-day lives. I will truely miss her class. If you have the opportunity to be one of her students...take that chance!

Awersome professor. Made class fun, interesting, and very accessible for everyone with very easy to understand notes and well-designed lectures. Tests and assignments were very, very straightforward. Demonstrates a true passion for Biology and for educating students about it. Very helpful as well during office hours.
Loved her! she made class fun and prepared us well for the tests.
very nice, helpful, wonderful notes, easy to understand, not difficult, and easy to get a good grade

Dr. Stone provided online chats the night before exam days where she would often ask identical questions to the ones on exams. She was very easy to get ahold of and provided multi-media in class to help understand concepts easily.

prof stone was very good in lecture. she simplified things extremely. the online assignments are very helpful and boost your grade, so do them! and she posts practice tests and previous tests, which are great for exam review. wording on some test questions are confusing, but if you ask, she may through it out! very fair prof!

She is an awesome teacher.  She is organized, clear, interactive and fun.  Her tests are easy and if you study and do the reviews you will get an A no problem.  Very fair teacher and an interesting class!
Offers a lot of good study tools.

Dr. Stone is a great professor! I recommend her to anyone needing to take Bio. Her class isn't easy but she's willing to help you out at anytime in anyway possible. She gives you lots of oppurtunites to get easy points and very understanding when things come up.

Dr. Stone is a very good teacher and she thoroughly explains what she expects out of her students, but her tests are extremely difficult. However, there are a lot of overall points in the class so it is possible to get a good grade in the class, even if you haven't done so well on the tests.
No Comments

Dr. Stone is super nice and treats this like a class for non-majors as it should be. Her notes are concise, easy, and clear. Very, very organized. She is very friendly and willing to help. The group work is annoying but easy points and she is understanding; offering easy points and occasional extra credit. If you have to take bio, take it with her.

Mrs. Stone did an excellent job this semester...just watch her tests some can be sneaky, but the good news is there are a lot of points in her class so you can screw up a couple and still keep an A.  Trust me i know from experience...if your taking the class i'd say go with stone she made it fun.

BIO 1010 is supposed to be a non-science majors class. Dr. Stone teaches it like it is for science majors.  I found the tests to be nearly impossible and the group work made me feal like I was back in kindergarten.  She is a very nice lady but do not take her class unless you love science.

If you want to get an A in this class, you can easily. She offers tons of help and tests are strictly from the notes.  There is a lot of little assignments, but they're graded easy and are good for bringing up your grade.
Class is easy, tests are easy, teacher is annoying
Great teacher, always available for help, You can get an A if you work at it, and she'll definetely help you. Great study guide that tells u exactly whats on the test
good class, good teacher, if you try you can get an A

I took her class two semesters ago.  She was an excellent professor.  She was available for help when needed, her tests were reasonable, if you studied.  The group work was worthless but what can you do about that.
Easiest class I've taken in college, but I had to work at it.  She's very helpful and caring.

Bottom line:Class lectures are somewhat interesting,outside work is horribly complicated and groupwork is confusing.Take Stone's class if you like mind-numbingly difficult and tedious assignments and exams.
Very easy and elementary class/teaching style

Dr. Stone is an awesome professor. She really makes herself available if you have questions. She also gives everybody feedback on how they're doing. I would definitely take her class if you need to take Bio 1.

The main problem I had with the class was that certain questions were on the test, but you had no idea from the study guide. Also, some of the wording of the test questions were confusing. This was the only class were people were asleep after 5 minutes.
Bio 1 was the easiest science class I have ever taken. Didn't need the book because her tests went with the notes.
A decent teacher.  Tests aren't too bad.  Just keep up in class and you will do fine.
The class could have been a nightmare, but she made it easy to understand and take notes in.  A little boring at times, but overall, I liked her a lot.
class was so hard.  she taught me nothing and her lisp made me want to jab sharp things in my eys.  i hated her class and i now hate science comepletely.  never take her class.
Just keep up on the notes and go to class.  She's fun.  And it's interesting.
WOW this was bad

Worst professor I ever had, she grades terribly and expects you to word things the exact way she did. She says she's willing to help, and in reality, she's not. I recommend avoiding this class at all costs. The subject is amazing, and I love reading about Asian philosophy, it's just the professor that makes a great subject dreadful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Never again. So incredibly difficult. She nickel and dimes you for points and does not give you a clear explanation for the grade you receive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: awful....

Grades and gives feedback for assignments very quickly and reliably. I find the feedback to be thorough but unhelpful. Very very very tough course. Extremely detail oriented. If you take the course whip out evernote and write down ever term and date and memorize them. Also try submitting all assignments to OWL.

The professor had a clear lack of interest and investment in her students. Her "synthesis" of the material was very difficult to understand, and when I asked her for advice on how I could improve my performance, she "had no suggestions". In addition, she didn't even respond to 2/3 of my emails. WORST ACADEMIC EXPERIENCE EVER. TERRIBLE.

Crazy based grade reductions based on grammatical errors. Seems to want you to restate every piece of information given. Doesn't seem to care much about thinking critically in your answer. Extremely high expectations for essay answers. Wants highly standard, precise, boring, formal, uninteresting writing.

Her Intro to Ethics class does not introduce ethics, it has too much of an emphasis on the background of Indian theology. The only actual ethics we covered was a brief definition. She is condescending, expects students to orally answer questions in essay format. I'm no more knowledgeable on ethics for having taken the class than I was before.

Her courses are certainly difficult, but she knows the subject matter and is willing to invest her time/energy into students who care about the subject matter. If you do philosophy (or perhaps religious studies, though don't bring any of that post-modern stuff to the table in class), then you should take any class she offers.
SHE IS AWESOME! She definitely knows what she is talking about. She has written several books on a variety of philosophical points. This is not a blow off class, you must be interested in the topic!

She's really funny and a good person, but a terrible professor. I almost failed this class because of her inability to answer e-mails. She gets very hung up on how you word an answer, and completely ignores whether you've comprehended the concept or not. I wouldn't take another class with this professor if you paid me.

She expects you to regurgitate every tiny detail that you have ever learned concerning the class material for all quizzes and tests.  Class discussions are all over the place.  There is no systematic order of topics.  Don't expect to have any idea of what your grade is until it is submitted as final.  She gives only straight grades A,B, etc

Gupta is a wonderful person and a great professor to know.  She actually wrote the textbook we use in class, which is great because we only need to buy one paper-back book and not four or five from different philosophers.  She has a pretty thick accent and is confusing at times, but if you can get through this class it will be worth it!

Prof Gupta is one of the most caring individuals I have ever met. She is a tough grader, true, but she also wants you to learn and grow as a student and will challenge you beyond just reading a repeating information. I enjoyed her class very much and recommend it to anyone interested in Philosophy, S Asia, or both.
AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS. Unless you are a mindreader, there is NO HOPE.
Her classes are not for slackers.

She was pretty unapprochable for such a small class. Her notes are all over the place, and she does not really tell you what will be on the test. Be prepared to study a lot and decipher your notes. Only for those who really like philosophy.
Very confusing, her notes and lectures are not organized and she jumps all over the place

I had a small class so there were no TA's, and she did a great job of handling the class herself. She was approachable in office hours, and did a great job of explaining the material (and responding to questions) so that it was very clear. A little tricky to understand at first, but you get used to it. And she's pretty funny too.
No Comments
Kinda scary at first, but really not too bad once you get into the course. She can be pretty funny, and the tests aren't that bad if you just pay some attention in class.
No Comments
No Comments
I couldn't understand a word she said, and she didn't allow recorders for later clarification....and her TA's were just as useless...
Does not have time for her students!!! Ushers them off to the TA's...

Dr. Blodgett is a nice person and willing to help students outside of class. Class could use some restructuring, though. Labs had all the instructions available online, so no need for TA to go through them step by step. The book covered the same topics as the lecture, so those book quizzes felt repetitive. The semester project was fun to complete.

Blodgett is an excellent professor. He respects his students and wants them to fully understand the material. This means that his courses are not easy -but you actually learn and grow as a student. He is always available to help out and is an extremely caring and kind person.
This class is a lot of lab work and work on your end of semester project. Your best tool for success is going to lab in person (I'd avoid the online section) and asking the TAs for help.

The exams were a little difficult, but there were plenty of extra credit opportunities on exams and projects. The semester project also seems intimidating, but was super easy and not very time consuming. BEWARE of mandatory cumulative final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors I had at Mizzou. Knows how to teach the material while being entertaining(a lot of professors can't do both at once). Taking notes and studying for exams is so easy the way he teaches! As a senior, this was just a fill in class but I wish I would have been able to enjoy Dr. Blay for more classes while I was at Mizzou!

Professor Blay is incredibly laid back in class and delivers really interesting lectures. His exams are hard but fair, and the assignments are long, but you have a while to complete them. His pop quizzes are easy if you pay attention, so try and do so! The semester project is fun and isn't too difficult! Also, super funny! BE RESPECTFUL!

Dr. Blay has been one of my favorite teachers so far at Mizzou. His lectures are interesting, and he grades fairly. You will need to go to class and study for tests, but if you put in the effort, you can definitely get a good grade. Would highly recommend for Vertebrate Biology!
Great professor, cares about students and always willing to help. Has pop quizzes in class to take attendance. Not a lot of homework but test are HARD.

Great professor who cares about his students. He wants us all to understand, which is why he gives pop quizzes (controversial but they are not hard if you pay attention). Tests come directly from slides. Accessible outside of class and hilarious. You have to go to class because he doesn't record his lectures and quizzes are at the beginning.

His lecture slides are the worst. They never line up with his outlines. I have never had a class with him where he actually teaches the things on his slides. Basically none of the content he teaches is relevant to his exams.

Great professor who pays attention to where students are at in order to best explain the material. Easy going and his lectures aren't boring. Multiple choice can be tricky, but he gives back points for questions that are frequently missed. Doesn't record lectures and has pop quizzes, but they are like 3 points, so missing 1 or 2 is not a big deal.

Beware of this teacher, extremely hard class. I passed Biochem with a better grade than this class. Would not recommend this teacher. Lectures and tests do not match at all and he does pop quizzes in class to check for attendance and it is a big chunk of your grade. I would wait to take this class with a different professor.

Bases tests off obscure snippets from lectures, which aren't recorded so be ready to read notes over and over. Also does surprise quizzes to ensure attendance. Rounds to the 0.01 percent. Would not reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Buzz is the best!!! I took Sociology 4620 Drugs and Society. He's so chill and understanding if you need help. There is some reading to do for the class but it isn't exorbitant and it's pretty interesting. I thoroughly enjoyed this class and wish I could take another class with him. If you have the chance to take any of his classes, do it!

Slides are like FOREVER LONG, at least 50-60 slides which are covered over 2 lectures. He goes super fast over content, it's overwhelming. If you are looking for a nice intro level into sociology, don't take it with him. The tests are in person, which is challenging because they cover 6 chapters, and there is quite a bit of extra credit offered.

Amazing professor. His stories and examples are interesting and sometimes even humourous. If you attend the lectures and pay attention to the questions he asks students during class, you will pass with flying colors. There is a small book you need to read but the stories in them are easy to remember because they keep you interested.

The lectures are really interesting and if you go, you'll pass all the tests no problem. If you don't, you can read the texts and still pass. You will need the books, because that's what the homework questions are based off of. Really intriguing class, helped me learn a lot even as a non-sociology major

He is a very straight forward teacher. The tests are written by students based on weekly homework questions you submit for points. The questions are based off the lecture so you have to go to most classes. But he teaches straight from the book, word of word so its easy to catch up on missed classes. He also offers a TON of extra credit!
