This is for Precalculus class. Bushman is a tough grader on exams. Attendance is not necessary mandatory as he does not do Iclickers. He does encourage people to go to his office hours which do help for this class. Hw is not hard and you get a week to do it.
Super nice guy with great math lectures. This is a review for a PreCalc Class, it is not available on rate my professor.

He was very difficult to work with! His emails were kinda rude. Doesnt care about your situation if you miss and assignment or something its on you and dont ask him for leeway because theres no such thing in his books!
I really enjoyed this class, JBC always answered any questions you had on WebCT, posted lecture outlines before class, and had genuine knowledge on the subject and related well to the class.
Her powerpoints and lectures have NOTHING to do with the material on the tests...buy a book, read it, and dont waste your time attending class!

Great Professor! She is really intrested in the subject making it more interesting. She puts the class notes (powerpoint) on WebCT so your able to print them off before class. Test can be tricky, so you really need to study notes as well as read the book.  She puts review online so have an idea of what will be on the test. I really enjoyed the clas
No Comments

She is a very good professor. She knows the material very well. You get a cheat sheet for test that are very helpful. There are also Kahoots randomly given for extra credit. As long as you study and pay attention, you will do well.

Good lectures, great class to take for your own learning. Her aim is to help you improve your own nutrition, and I've learned a ton through her class. High volume of reading & quizzes, but the content itself is not difficult. She is understanding of absences and not too difficult to make up tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Peterson is genuinely one of the best professors I have had in my college career. Her lectures are very engaging and very helpful. There is a decent amount of homework but it is very do-able, she is a very fair grader and makes it very clear what is expected of you.
The class was pretty easy, and she was fine. Nothing extraordinary.

I really enjoyed taking nutrition with Professor Peterson. She is very engaging and clearly knows a lot about the subject and cares about her students. The class was super easy and really interesting. I feel like I could apply these things in my real life.

Professor Peterson is extremely knowledgeable about her subject. Lectures are long and can get boring. Gave extra credit in class. Full page cheat sheet allowed on every test. DO NOT take this class if you have disordered eating. It will almost definitely stress you out.

She might come off as a little rude or uncaring but she's great. McGraw Hill homework 2-3 times a week that look anywhere from 30 minutes to an hour, but they were fairly easy. Exams were easy and you're allowed a cheat sheet. She does random in class extra credit which is just a kahoot with a few questions. Would love to have her again.

Shes pretty chill but the lectures are really boring. Class is very easy though and you get a cheat sheet on the test so its very manageable but the homeworks do take a little bit so its a easy A but you gotta do some work yk. Prof really nice though

Super nice professor that cares about the students and is always willing to answer questions. She gives a lot of homework but it's really easy. She also gives tons of extra credit, I passed with over 100%. You get a half page cheat sheet on the tests too which is nice
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Peterson is amazing professor, gives good lectures, participation is not mandatory, she gives extra credit for attendance, only thing to consider about this class is that four exams that are not very easy if you don't read the material and attend lectures, but a small cheat sheet is allowed, there are also extra credit assignments.

She is very passionate about her class. This class gets easier as the semester goes on, but be ready for a lot of homework through McGraw. Attendance is optional, but she does occasionally give extra credit for attending. If you are needing a biological science credit, this is a great option that isn't too horribly difficult.

Great Teacher!! She taught me so much!! I always walked out of her class feeling smarter, so sweet and patient!! I would say the only downside is a ton of Mcgraw Hill, also lots of independent learning!! Always gave time for extra credit and was a easy grader!!

Peterson makes notes easy and straightforward and really seems to care about students, but
SO MUCH MCGRAW HILL- with up to 90 concepts, and takes at least an hour. 4 major exams, with only a 4x6 sheet of notes. 
PSA: if you have any food issues - DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. One assignment was to calculate your BMI and Portion sizes, be warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She couldn't have made this class any easier. She provided extra credit ALL the time, so much that I was able to skip the last exam and still finish with an A. I genuinely enjoyed going to class and learning.

So kind and passionate about the topic, lots of extra credit opportunities and I actually learned a lot. She honestly just wants you to learn the material so it's not an unnecessarily hard course at all. No final and allows a cheat sheet on the exams!!!

Dr. Peterson is a super nice person, and she is really passionate about what she is teaching! However, her lectures are very boring. Lots of busy work - but overall, not too bad. Attendance isn't accounted for, and she posts everything on Canvas. Textbook is online - there were 2 of them.

Dr. Peterson is amazing! She is clearly very passionate about the topics she teaches. There is a fair amount of work involved, especially for the honors discussion, but she is a lenient grader and allows late work. Allows test cheat sheets, has 8am review sessions before the test, and offers extra credit Thursday classes and other EC opportunites

Dr. Peterson is very knowledgable about what she teaches. Lenient about late work, and attendance isn't required. Extra credit 8am session if needed. The tests are difficult but she allows a cheat sheet. The homework is easy just time consuming and busy work. I highly recommend if you need an easy science credit.

Dr. Peterson is passionate and knowledgeable about the course content. She is generous with extra credit opportunities & sometimes gives credit if you just show up. Her course is challenging, but you learn a lot. If you study and do the online prework (which takes the longest time), then you will do well in the course.

Very solid professor. In my opinion, a good amount of the test questions seem a bit extraneous from the study guides, but you do get a 1-page cheat sheet so I can't complain much at all. Very informative professor and guaranteed to learn something new every day. Would take it again, also good for non-nutrition and nutrition majors.

Professor Peterson was an amazing professor. Her tests can be a bit challenging but she posts a guide before every test that gives you all the information you will need. She also records all of her lectures so that you can watch them outside of class. She does give out lots of extra credit. There are plenty of TA's in her course as well.

The lectures are not particularly engaging and there were multiple times when someone (even in the front row) would raise their hand and Dr. Peterson would look past them and continue talking as if they weren't there. All the lessons are recorded. It's easy though not particularly fulfilling.

You didnt have to show up to class but I would recommend doing so because she randomly gives extra credits and she covers lots of material. She was very nice and accessible outside of class. As long as you do the work and study for the exams you'll pass the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 1034 is essentially graded on completion quizzes, the application assignment and the four exams. She posts all the lectures online but I would recommend going into lecture for the content. Peterson is clear and knows what she's talking about so I would recommend her. Write a good cheat sheet that follows the criteria for the exam and you'll be fine

Really enjoyed this class! She really sets you up for success to get a good grade as long as you do the assignments which are typically easy. Going to lecture isn't mandatory but I recommend at least watching them online so you are prepared for the exams. Overall an easy and interesting class as long as you keep up with assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I am not a food science major, but still found this class really interesting and pretty easy. Exams could be a little hard, but there are so many other grades so they don't tank your grade. Lectures aren't mandatory but I'd suggest going to as many as you can - it makes tests easier.

Dr. Peterson is such a great professor and you can tell she really cares about what she is teaching. All assignments are very straightforward and overall she is very organized. There are so many opportunities for extra credit and all lectures are posted online, so you don't need to attend class as long as you watch the lectures at some point.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are posted online. 4 exams in the class, don't make a significant impact on your grade. I received no higher than an 85% on all exams and did all extra credit and assignments and still ended with a 92% at the end of the year. Gives 1-2 extra credit assignments before each exam. It gets boring after a while but provides good material.
Hard but fair… learned a ton.

Dr Peterson is awesome! Her grades are based on homework, projects, and tests. There is extra credit opportunities spread throughout the semester. Her tests are lots of memorization and recall out of her lectures, textbook readings and assigned readings. This class covers a lot of material in one semester, so get ready to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class! The tests are very lecture heavy but she gives out note outlines! She also offers a study lecture before the test that literally tells you everything that will be on the test. Sometimes the lectures get a bit boring but I would definitely take her again!

Love love love her. She presents her material in lectures very very clearly and you can tell she really loves what she talks about. She gives exam hints before each exam so you know exactly what to study, and as long as you put in the work to study hard, you will get an excellent grade in her class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson is fantastic! I cannot recommend her class enough. She loves nutrition and its obvious she loves teaching others about her passion. I think she strives to impact every student. She has tons of extra credit opportunities that you should take advantage of; don't complain about your grade if you don't do the extra credit...

Dr. Petersons class was great. Though the class material itself is relatively challenging, there are great study tools that make passing very easy. There are weekly extra credit opportunities.... GO TO THEM! I know they're early, but I swear, they make a huge difference in your grade, and she does NOT bump. She knows EVERYTHING abt nutrition too.
Class was easy and I would have ended up with an A- but instead I ended with a B- because I was not able to take my last exam online even tho I couldn't because I had the flu.

Overall, the class was easy. She was a good teacher and I received high A's on each test. The position paper for the honors portion was hard. I do not struggle with papers, and have always been told I was a great writer, but I received a C on the paper which brought my grade down a letter grade which was extremely frustrating.

Really recommend intro to nutrition! I had a lot of fun. Most of the time I would procrastinate and do all the lectures the night before a test and I did okay! WOuld definitely take this class again very interesting

The class will be easy as long as you do the work. In my semester, we started in-person and then went online. You can be successful in either format, though it is tempting to not go to the live class or zooms and just watch the recording. Don't. The videos add up quickly. Do the completion homework and pay attention in lectures and you'll be fine.

This woman is absolutely one of the most intelligent people that I've ever met. It's a bit intimidating at first, but she is so approachable outside of class and really does her best to help you learn. I can absolutely say that she gave me the utmost confidence to be able to read and analyze research, which will be a great asset in my field. 10/10

This class was very easy to get an A in, as long as you do the work. For every chapter there were learning curves (which as long as you finish them you get 100%), a test, and an application. The class was given in a hybrid format, due to COVID I believe. There were TA office hours almost every time of the day, and they were always willing to help.

NEP is an easy A. The "homework" consists of 3-4 learning curves and one assignment per section (4 sections because of 4 tests) which you can use the online book/Quizlet to find answers and are pretty easy to do. For tests, you can easily use Quizlet/Socratic or take some notes to make the tests faster. Peterson is very nice as well.

I enjoyed this class a lot, although lectures were sometimes long and boring, Im glad I took this class because I feel like I actually learned a lot from it. Shes a really nice person and good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class wasn't too bad. At times it felt like information overload. It was manageable if you keep up, but falling behind would be hard. Tests were kinda hard, but there were enough homework assignments to balance out the load.

She is a highly intelligent woman. She truly cares about her students and is readily available outside of class for help. Her classes can be hard that I took, as it involved a lot of writing and research, which was new to me. She really taught me how to read research, how research studies differ, and how to sniff out good sources.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson is so kind, passionate, and knowledgable. The class is interesting and can be applied to your life since it is human nutrition. The tests are not difficult if you study using the review sheet and the homework is easy too. She records the lectures and uploads them on canvas so you do not have to attend class if you do not want.

The class was very easy. The study guides for the exams were really helpful. Attending the review sessions the night before the exam is a good idea. Also Dr. Peterson had a section that offered extra credit every week so it is easy to get extra credit
I never went to her class. If you to the review sessions they basically give you the answers. Take the notes and do the homework and you'll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy course - tests were entirely multiple-choice, and there was a review the night before each test of everything on the study guide, so if you showed up to that, you're pretty much golden. She even answered a nutrition question I had over winter break after I was finished with the course. As long as you attend lecture, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. She definitely seemed passionate about nutrition, and I thought her class was really fun. It was also definitely an easy A.

I took the honors section of this course. I really enjoyed it, but the final research paper was tough! As far as the regular class, the tegrities are very helpful and you get to do them on your own time. Tests aren't bad if you keep up with the notes/online activities
Peterson is so knowledgeable, and her class is very insightful.

I had this class at 8 am so I never went. She puts the lectures on Tegrity but I never used those either. I would just do the homework and use Quizlets people already made to study the night before the exam. The material is not hard, and some of the chapters are common sense. The exams are exactly what is on the study guides, no surprises.

You need to either go to class or watch the tegrities. Her tests are heavily lecture based. Her tests are not easy, but she does curve each test depending on the averages. There are online assignments that are grade fluffers, so make sure you do them.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Petersons class. She is very well spoken and easy to follow. All of her lectures are posted in Tegrity so you don't have to go to class if you watch those. There are no quizzes and she will never take attendance. I watched the Tegrity videos the night before the exam and did well. All test questions come from her lectures.
Don't have to show up to class because she records it but the class is difficult and the learning curves are very time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Its hard to listen to Peterson sometimes. Her lectures are literally just her reading the infographics out of the textbook that shes copy/pasted onto slides. Its easy to get an a if you do the homework assignments, which are almost always participation points. Boring, but not hard.

Dr. Peterson is very knowledgable about the subject. I took the honors section, and I would highly recommend that. The discussions are very interesting and I learned a lot about nutrition controversies. The tests are hard, but if you study your notes, then they are not too tough. She gives lots of extra credit, so take advantage of it.

She's a tough teacher but Dr Peterson really loves her subject. Sometimes her teaching is somewhat dry but she's very understanding as long as she knows you're trying. I forgot to turn in two of my online assignments on time and she adjusted it for me. She does take attendance so go to class. Ended up with an A in the class.
Basically just reads the book to you.
Yes, her tests are hard but you will do fine if you read through the notes several times and read the articles on Blackboard. The book is not necessary to get an A, I promise.
Professor Peterson is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic.  She will help you if you go to her office hours.  READ THE TEXTBOOK!

Took her Human Nutrition I class. She is a hard teacher, but you will learn a lot. The only things you're graded on are 6 online quizzes, 2 projects, 4 tests, and a final, so you have to study HARD for the tests. Also, she expects you to know EVERY little detail about nutrition, so if it isn't your passion, you may not want to take this class!

Dr.Bush is great! She's very nice and understanding. But if youre someone that doesn't want to show up to class/participate you may not like her class. And I would consider myself one to not like showing up and being engaged, but I learned from her more than any other professor at Mizzou. I took 3 different courses with her, all were my favorites!

Uses a flipped classroom model with completion-based homework and mandatory "active-learning" sessions twice a week. This class takes a lot of your time, but Dr. Bush does respect students and will work with you. Hard to adjust to the different course structure, it's not for everyone (including me. You have to try to fail this class.

i love love love her - I've had her for 2 biology courses and she teaches super well along with making sure you understand the material. She also gives easy points - such as attendance points, group work, and small assignments in order to help your grade if tests go bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Poor course structure

I was nervous going into this class because science wasn't my thing in high school but Dr. Bush was great. Make sure you go to class and take advantage of stage 2 of the tests and you'll be fine. Just don't turn in your scantron late!

We had assigned seats in a lecture hall. Horrible with getting grades in on a timely manner even when asked in person or emailed. Tests every wednesday worth 35% of your grade and questions were never clear and you often left the class more confused than when you walked in. Consistent snarky comments and acted as though she was better than you.

Attendance is 10 points every class. As well as a test every wednesday. Weekly homework assignments and every once in a while a more time consuming homework project (4 total). She was nice and I did not have to try super hard just show up and you will be fine!

I absolutely loved her class.  Her lectures are always clear and interesting. She cares a lot about her students and was willing to meet with me outside of office hours for help. There's a short test every week, which worried me at first, but it was actually helpful for keeping me on top of everything.  Just make sure you go to class.

I really like her! She is very witty, and I find her lectures to be very engaging. Weekly quizzes, but if you attend class everyday and rewatch the lectures or look over your notes the night before, you can do great! There is classwork on that you work on with an assigned group on days there are not quizzes.

This is one of those professors with many low ratings here. But when you take the class, it's just because the professor actually wants you to come to class and learn. Weekly quizzes that are very easy (if you attend class). Attendance is not mandatory but there are daily assignments. Overall, her class is very interesting and well-structured.

A lot of the wording she does from tests to assignments is unclear. Directions are often misinterpreted and multiple-choice answers to test questions can sometimes be ambiguous. She does not own up to these mistakes and instead puts them back on her students. Narcissistic attitude in lecture.
group projects, treats students like children, and forces students to participate.
Doesn't care about students, virtue signals all class, boring, requires group work, acts like she's better than you.

I've taken her class my first year and thought since I've taken it I would be fine, but after her second test/quiz my grade immediately dropped from an A+ to a C-. Her tests are nothing like the lecture slides she provides for us to study and there are always trick questions. Every person I've talk to says the same thing about her. WOULD NOT REC.

Dr. Bush's class can be challenging, but engaging lectures and helpful group work make it manageable. The homework load is heavy, but completing it is key. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for study prep.

This class has a lot of exams. The exams are also pretty challenging. Dr. Bush had good lectures, and did explain material well, but this class requires a lot of time. You also have to do worksheets in class, which are a waste of time, and not at all helpful for exams. Overall, the formatting of the course was far from ideal.

Class set up was really nice. The online lectures gave a guided opportunity to really learn topics well. If you study a day in advance for tests you will be fine. Just actually put effort into this class and you will get an A.

Professor herself isn't bad. Nice, lectures aren't bad, it's the way the class is set up that is confusing. You watch lectures online, and then complete worksheets/quizzes for those, and then lectures are mostly group work. Lab/discussion is confusing, with topics not related to those in class. Be prepared to put a LOT of time into this class.
showing up matters. tests were very hard and there are 7 of them plus the final

She uses a flipped classroom (discussions in class, lecture videos outside). Had 7 small tests per semester, 2 assignments per week, 1 lab per week. Being an active participant really helps with understanding. She is an amazing freshman teacher as she helps build helpful study/test skills. Easily available outside of class and very understanding.

Dr. Bush uses a flipped lecture style and there's 2 out of class lectures + assignments, 2 in person lectures, and a lab/discussion per week. However, if you put in even the slightest bit of effort, this class is very manageable. I found the class difficult the first few weeks but once you figure it out it isn't awful.

I LOVED having Dr.Bush as my professor! You can tell she cares a lot about her students and enjoys getting to know them during office hours. Studying is very important for this class as there is a test every other week and more so application-based, but they're short so it's manageable as long as you're organized. Don't be afraid to ask for help.

Dr. Bush sincerely cares about her students. She is a great teacher and will help anyone who is struggling in or outside of her class. The tests were kind of hard and there are many of them, but because there are a lot of tests you can bomb one and your grade won't be hurt too bad.

Class has 7 exams and a cumulative final, so 8 exams total. Pretty excessive but it's a freshman course so there isn't many ways around it. Attendance is required, definitely can help or hurt your grade so just go to class. Final exam isn't really anything like the other 7 exams which was a little unfair. She uses a "flipped classroom"

She was very unorganized, and the structure of the class made very little sense. The content in class, homework, lab, and discussion was never the same thing. Lots of tests and homework. I love biology but she made me hate the class.

Dr. Bush cares so much about her students. Participation and attendance are very important for this class. Homework assignments can feel extensive but they are very helpful. The biggest downside to this class are the evening exams, but thats just because I'm lazy.

This class is a flipped style classroom. There are two homework assignments a week, and they can be lengthy but they aren't terrible. Lab and discussion are apart of the final grade. STUDYYYYY hard and take notes because the tests are a lot of applications to the material. You are paired with a lab group and do like everything with them. No ex cred

Dr. Bush is a great professor, and she excels at a tough job. Teaching introductory biology is a tough feat, but she thrives at it. I think this comes from a deep passion for the subject and hope for her students to succeed. Get cozy with your lab group because you'll see them a lot, in and out of class. Most homework assignments are simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class can be difficult if you don't pay attention to the HW, it is participation. Class has 7 tests, however everything from the tests is directly from the HW and videos she puts out at the start of the week. She is a very nice and respectable professor.

Bush was a good prof, you can tell she loves the subject and very knowledgeable. Homework is usually online, graded on completion. Wish she would post study guides earlier in the week but you can find premade quizlets from previous semesters lol. Also sucks how she has clueless TA's for labs, which dont make them that fun

pretty good professor. 1500 had many homework assignments, graded on completion. be ready for lots of outside work and study as much material as you ca before tests. I wish she would post the learning objectives sooner in the week rather than the friday before, but i found that many students have premade quizlets to study from online lol

The only negative about Dr. Bush is that she kind of talks to you like you're a third grader, but she does make sure you have a very wide introductory knowledge about everything, just be prepared to get really cozy with your lab group.

The course itself is fine, but you can totally tell it hasn't been updated in awhile which is fine if Dr. Bush was more approachable. At least from my experience she seems distant from students and always moving on to the next thing so you can't ask her anything after class. You can also tell she shoves most of the work on mildly unprepared TA's.

Two times a week you have a HW assignment based on completion, not correctness. Bush operates a flipped classroom. At the beginning of the semester, she splits you into groups that you're with for the rest of the semester. Exams are every other week outside of class time and are a little difficult. Watch the lectures and go to office hours

I struggled literally so much in this class even when I showed up and watched lectures and did all the notes. All of my friends also thought she used confusing examples and the amount of homework is also a lot more than it needs to be AND the labs didn't even match up with what we were doing in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush's class is easy to follow, but there is a lot of homework- graded on completion. Her lectures may seem redundant, but if you listen that's exactly what will be on the test. Attendance is CRUCIAL to doing well in the class. An easy A if you watch the lectures and take good notes. Don't blow off the homework just because it's completion.

At first, she might seem she repeats everything again and again during Active learning sessions, but during exams, you will see the benefit. She does not add anything extra to the tests, only the most important concepts that are covered. Questions in the exams will be similar to the questions on the active learning session papers, so keep them.

I actually learned quite a lot this semester, and overall it was a pretty good class! I do feel like the class is slightly micromanaged though, and the structure is a little confusing. The tests questions were also often not very clear and she takes a very like infer off the information approach, so don't just memorize the stuff and learn it!
Dr. Bush herself is a carrying professor, however the class set up is annoying. She has always made herself available
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The semester group was actually REALLY helpful in understanding content. Her lectures are engaging. Those who complain about the workload forget that this a 5 credit hour class and simply don't try. Get along with your group, come to lecture, and do your homework and it's an easy A.
I like her.

By far the best professor I have had. While there is a lot of content, it isn't too confusing. There are many opportunities for participation points. Dr. Bush is also super approachable during office hours and is sure not to leave students behind when they don't fully understand something. I have nothing but respect and admiration for Dr. Bush.
Dr. Bush is very passionate about what she teaches. She knows a lot about the class and is a very good lecturer. The structure of the class can be annoying, but she herself is always very sweet.

I love this class and this professor! Everything taught in lectures directly relate to assignments and tests, you're never left searching for answers or explanations. Showing up and participation is huge, do it and you'll pass easily. Those who complain in my class about their grades are those who don't show up or use resources Dr. Bush provides.

Group assignments don't assist with the learning experience at all. Questions on homework and tests are poorly written and worded. Little to no actual learning is done in class, which is unfortunate since attendance is mandatory, and a large percentage of your grade.

Every test she makes has at least 4-5 questions worded in the most confusing ways possible. That is 20% of the questions on the test. OH! and each question is five points!! Sadly, this is the only biology class you can take as a freshman, so good luck. Basically, all I want in this class is to learn about biology, but that's apparently hard to do.

...And none of the learning material is connected. So, when test day comes, we somehow have to scrape up all the information we get from SIX DIFFERENT CLASSES into one study session. Also, she claims that her test questions are not trick questions... literally a college professor is lying to your face. CONTINUED...

This class is one of the most inefficient learning environments ever made. She claims that her completely ridiculous "flipped schedule" is proven to help us. I do not see this at all, we have online learning, online labs, in person lectures, in person labs, in person discussions, and outside of class assignments with lab groups. Continued...

Dr. Bush was really great at making the class fun and helping students build a scientific mindset. She pushes the boundaries of traditional teaching and focuses more on empowering student to learn for themselves by thinking scientifically.

Dr. Bush is very educated and passionate about what she teaches. The way the class is set up is interesting. You're put in groups of four for the semester and you do in-class activities together that are worth points, so attendance is absolutely mandatory. Also, there are weekly small quizzes every Wednesday and no big exams except for the final.

Attendance matters. Puts you in groups in a giant lecture hall, but does it so you have people to work on assignments with. Tests every week so theres no big exams. Curates assignments for a class full of non majors, so we did get to learn about things that affect our everyday life. Very nice professor, knows her audience, wants you to succeed.

Tests every week and she assigns points for filling out worksheets every day, so make sure you go to all the class periods. Material is not too difficult and you can resubmit your tests for extra points. It was one of the better classes I've taken at Mizzou.

Gave us assigned seating in a lecture hall of over 250 people, and took attendance with in class assignments that she would wait until the last 5 minutes to do. The content was not hard at all which was nice. Tests every Wednesday no exams
test grades do not make sense. We have seven tests and a final, but all the tests are graded out of a different number of total points, making them weigh different amounts. Also there is no curve.
Have to attend every lecture, but get points for participation  in literally everything except tests. A lot of tests. Works well if sick

We have tests every other Wednesday night at 8 pm. She is understanding of personal issues, but she basically makes you teach yourself and doesn't actually teach during the given class time. You and your lab group will have to meet outside of class to finish your labs if you don't have time to during your lab once every 3 weeks.

Dr. Bush is a very cool person in general, but don't expect this to be an easy class. She gives plenty of quizzes, exams, and homework. MAKE SURE YOU GET ALONG WITH YOUR LAB GROUP. You will be with them every day for the entire semester. She assigns the lab group. You'll have discussion with them, lab, and lectures with them.

She needs proctoring software. Tests are unproctored and ~20 mult choice questions. I was wrongly accused of cheating. She assured me before that I would not be able to prove my innocence. Luckily the other girl and I scored the same when she watched us take the next test after. In a ~400 person class it is not hard to get the same score.

Lots of group work. Lectures are off-topic and don't cover the harder-to-understand topics. Tries to be a "different" lecturer but it seems disorganized and does not help people who need to continue course work in biology.

I thoroughly enjoyed her class. She wrongly accused me of academic dishonesty and basically said I could appeal but had no chance of winning. I felt threatened in the conversation and wish she used a proctor browser for tests to prevent these issues. Now I am having to retake the class and do not look forward to it. Very difficult to reason with.

Dr.Bush has been an amazing professor, while in her class I had a lot of family issues going on and she worked very well with me, which was much appreciated. 

All in all, Dr.Bush has all my respect, while her tests can be somewhat difficult, she is amazing to work with, very caring, and loves having office hours with students. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush is awful. She is very rude and condescending. Her way is always right; no other opinions are considered. So much group work and tests over concepts that were taught with few, very specific examples that do not help with learning broader topics. Online lectures were slow and boring. This class was very micromanaged and taught like Pre-K.

The course is a lot of work but its not too difficult. There's a lot of group work and a test every other week. I had some family issues this semester and Dr. Bush was really helpful and understanding about letting me make up assignments.

Dr. Bush is amazing. I loved this class. The format is different - we watched recorded lectures online and then did activities in the classroom. The material was really interesting and different from what I learned in high school biology. It's easy to get a good grade as long as you study for the tests.

Sarah Bush was a good professor. She is knowledgeable about what she is teaching and cares about her students. It is a flipped classroom where during class there are no lectures, just team activities. The lab and in class grades are combined and you get points for going to each class. The lab TA and the professors are never on the same page.

I found this class to be a huge disappointment. I was very excited for my first biology class, but the structure and content of this class are extremely dry, repetitive, difficult to understand, and frustrating. Tests are much more in depth than what is taught, and there's no textbook. I found lectures to be a profound waste of time, too.

Very self absorbed way of teaching. Constantly using social experiment type logic to steamroll her way. Mandatory teamwork, mandatory participation or your grade will significantly suffer. She makes her class the center of my semester and I think its a bit much for a level1 class. The lectures are uninteresting and repetative and do not captivate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The profs work very hard to make sure you learn in this class and their lectures are very good. With that being said, the 7 tests are difficult and test questions are lengthy and tend to ask about topics that weren't taught, but should be "inferred" based off of the general info that was taught, so not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Was great at making sure we understood how different levels of biological concepts related to each other. Sure the geese and dragonflies got annoying to talk about but she formatted it in a way that helped you understand the content better. Would definitely recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The style of the class is really different from most classes, but it turned out to be a fun way to structure the class. I loved my lab group, which made the class something I actually looked forward to.

Dr. Bush and Dr. Schul are amazing! They used dragonflies and geese as a means to incorporate the concepts of biology. Although unusual, it was effective and thorough. There were 7 small tests and a final that were very specific to lecture. They're doable if you study.

Theres about 2 outside of class worksheets per week which are always easy if you pay attention to the lectures. The material was made easy to understand to where I would hardly have to study for each test and the professor is very approachable and fair. I was never worried about my grade in this class.
she does talk about dragonflies and geese but with context
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her and Dr. Schul's BIO 1500 class. A lot of people complain about their topic choice and teaching methods, but I thought it was fine. However, they do force students into randomized groups due to some random psychology study. The material isn't too challenging but is pretty useful for STEM majors later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush is an amazing professor. She is passionate about what she teaches and cares about individual students. Yes, we did talk a lot about birds and bugs, but only as examples to explain concepts in class. As long as you do all of the homework and show up to class, you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I put off my science requirement until my senior year because its really not my thing but this was one of the best taught classes Ive had at MU. I never needed to study because Dr. Bush explained everything so well I understood it in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVED Dr. Bush's class even though I've always hated biology. Of course, everyone has different preferences, but I never got bored. There are weekly tests, but they're very easy and she gives you a chance to earn back points if you mess up. She also drops the lowest test score. It's hard to do poorly if you attend class every day.

Gives excellent and entertaining lectures. Be prepared to attend every class as the slides are not posted and there is no text. All exam material comes straight from the assigned reading and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting, she doesn't just read from the slides bu actually explains the material very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class was taught with Dr. Schul, and the entire thing was focused on dragonflies and geese. Lecture was mandatory (and extremely boring), and your grade would tank if you missed one. There were 7 exams and a final, and the test questions could be extremely unclear and confusing. I don't recommend these professors for BIO1500.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yes, we did talk a lot about geese and dragonflies, but they were used as context. People are making it seem like we learned absolutely nothing about important biological concepts when that is not the case. Their teaching style is unique and beneficial to those who actually want to LEARN and UNDERSTAND biology and not just memorize it for a test
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Learned virtually nothing in this class. Talked too much about dragonflies and geese than the things that you're ACTUALLY supposed to learn in biology. Waste of time. If possible, take with ANY other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring and pointless, information hard to maintain

I would highly recommend taking bio with Bush. Lectures are accessible outside of class. You have to go to class though because she has clicker questions for points and will occasionally do in class participation papers. She has a 10 question test every week that you should not blow off! They are pretty easy as long as you study the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush is a really fair teacher. She has quizzes every Wednesday so there are no large exams, except for the final. The homework helps prepare you for the quizzes really well. I am not a strong science student but I would definitely recommend taking Bio with her
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush makes the lectures interesting and easy to follow. However, there are class activities that allow you to get credit for showing up to class. The activities are not announced beforehand. I missed one and my grade dropped 5%. Her tests are way harder than they need to be and I did all the readings and classwork.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There's a test every 2 weeks and lots of reading assignments but if you go to class and do the readings its not hard to get an A. The lectures are interesting and shes a nice lady. Just don't skip class if you want a good grade because she gives points for showing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Not a hard class, just a bad teacher. Seems nice and like you get the material and then you get 20 minutes to complete a test that comes from left field (even if you read the assignments and come to every class and take all the notes). Just not great.

She's a good teacher. There's a 10 question test every week, and lectures are what's directly on the the test. She answers any questions and tell you whats on the test. easy to no homework. She posts lectures online so there's no need for class. She does questions for point for attendance but its not a big part of your grade.

Every class period was worth 10 points which was a pain because things come up. There were exams every other Wednesday. At first it was scary but it was great in the end. Having less material to cover each test made it much easier to do well. Lots of group work and your groups are chosen for you which is very annoying. Overall not bad though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush is really awesome. She is a nice lady and definitely cares about you/your grade. She makes the material interesting. I didn't like how she puts you into your lab groups as I was stuck doing most of the work. Overall, I would take her again.

I found Dr. Bush's lectures really interesting! I also really liked how she had shorter, pretty straightforward tests every two weeks; I think it helped reinforce the material better because I was able to really study my notes instead of cramming. It wasn't an "easy" class, but I feel like Dr. Bush makes it easy to do well with some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: I really liked the class, the lectures, the readings and I liked Dr Bush, I did not, however, care much for the group project. The people in my group showed up to meetings but did little to nothing on the project. Professors - look at/ask for edit logs - so you know who actually worked! Want to do well? Do all the readings and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Everything in her lectures is what is on the tests. It's nice that you have 2 chances to complete the homework and improve your score. Same thing goes for the tests, since there is a stage 2. As long as you go to class and pay attention, it's pretty easy. There are also a couple extra credit opportunities which are pretty easy to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bush is a really cool gal. She makes the class easy to understand, and her test set up is great for your grade and your knowledge. I would take this class over and over.

I dont like the way she and Johannes Schul set up the class. Instead of just teaching us the material they go over their teaching methods a lot. No student wants to learn about how they are being taught, they are there to learn the material. They also base the class around their research a lot, so if you like insects they're the professors for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class is easy for the most part but the labs dont go w/ the lecture at all. And it is really heavy in group work, which i hate. I dont want to depend on other people for my grade, but that's just me. Lots of homework. And lots of small tests. We learn a lot about things that aren't really general bio, its more about bugs and their research.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Bush's evolution class last year and recently realized that it really changed the way I think. Now when learn about something in one of my other classes, I wonder how it evolved and sometimes I think I figured out how it happened. I wanted an A and was annoyed I didn't get it but I learned a lot in that class, so I would recommend it.

Her class material comes off as really easy and interesting, but the tests are harder than expected. She has a test once about every 3 weeks, but each question is extremely heavily weighted (one problem wrong will take you from an A to B). You have to go to every class because she doesn't post slides or do tegrity and she uses tophat clickers.

I took this last spring and am a bio major that ended up in this class because my advisor is an idiot. If you're a science person this class is a joke. If you're not I still don't imagine it would be too hard. She gives lots of little tests so it's easier to do well on them and she's really cool but GO TO CLASS because there's (easy) in-class work.

This is possibly the best biology class I have taken here at Mizzou. Dr. Bush gives an "exam" every other week, but they are only worth 30 points a piece. That way, the lessons are broken up into smaller chunks that you can truly learn. She uses TopHat, so going to lecture is pretty important. She is a phenomenal professor and I highly recommend!
She's a cool lady and I found the class really interesting. It''s also great that she gives small tests every other week. She's really set it up so you can actually learn. Highly recommend.

Great teacher!  I'm so glad that she opted out of using a book.  Her lectures, movies and examples are always interesting.  Having tests every other week make the class stress free allowing you to really learn the material.  Take her and you wont be sorry!

Dr. Bush is absolutely fantastic! She keeps the material interesting and you don't get bored. I wasn't really interested in taking this class, but now I'm really glad I did. There is an exam about every other week worth 30 points, so if you do bad on one it doesn't impact your grade as badly.

Dr. Bush is so easy to pass as long as you come to class and take the tests each week. She even gives the same test online later the same day to help you make up for any missed problems. She is amazing and so good and knowledgeable at everything she does. loved having her!
Great teacher. Made the class so easy with tests every week. Loved her
Very good teacher. A lot of outside work to do, but weekly tests really help your grade. Not interested in Bio but thought class was interesting.

Powerpoint lecture are very clear on everything you need to know. class is based on homework grades, one quiz a week which you can go back online and take again with notes to boost your grade, and modules which you can use your notes and peer groups. very easy if you go to class and complete all work

Dr. Bush is really clear in her lectures and gives plenty of real life examples that correspond to the lessons. The tests are kind of difficult because they're only 10 questions but they are every week and she gives you plenty of opportunities with homework points and modules.  She can be very funny at times and tries to keep the class engaged.

I'm not relatively interested in Biology at all but Dr. Bush makes it interesting. If you study for her tests you can do well. I've gotten an A on every test just studying my notes carefully the night before! Plus  she drops your lowest test score! Her class is clear and she goes slowly enough for you to hand write notes.

Bush is a horrible professor. Her tests are ridiculously difficult for a level 1000 introduction to biology class... a class made up primarily of freshman. She says a lot of really dumb things and relates every lecture to something way outlandish. The only good thing she does is has stage 2 exams, but the exams are so hard you can't even get 100%!
It is an annoyinjg class but overall easy.
Dr. Bush is an excellent professor. Her lectures are actually interesting and she can be funny at times. The exams require a lot of studying. I would definitely recommend her!
I'm LOVING this class.  There's no stress since there's no major exams, Dr. Bush's grading is fair, and you can tell that she's really into the topic.  I never skip class.  highly recommended.

In contrast to the previous commenter, I find Dr. Bush's quizzes to be challenging - you need to know your notes, but just memorizing them doesn't help much.  I agree with that commenter that the course is interesting, though.   I recommend it.

Didn't miss a point in her class. Quizzes every third class come straight from the notes. There is some pretty annoying homework now and then that is easy, but time consuming. Definitely a GPA booster... and sometimes its even interesting.

Dr. Bush is a fabulous teacher.  She explains the material with so much enthusiasm that you end up being just as excited about it as she is.  Honestly, I wasn't looking forward to this course, but it ended up being one of my all-time favorites.  Just make sure you go to class.

Excellent lecturer. She was extremely organized with her content and methods of teaching. Class was not stressful because we had no big tests, just quizzes every 3rd class. Class is easy if you go and take good notes. Dr. Bush really knows what shes talking about.
GREAT professor.  The lectures were very well organized and we covered a lot of fascinating stuff.  My favorite class so far at MU.

Anything on a test is in her lectures, so you have to go to class.  She liked to re-word things to the test to be tricky tho.  She was a great teacher and you could tell she loved her job.  Pretty easy all in all.
Very intersting and reasonable!

Well organized and taught. Going to class is very necessary, but if you pay attention and write down the notes (which is ALL on powerpoints) you don't even need to study much. I was nervous about this class, but she is fabulous! I totally recommend her!

Prof. Bush was the best teacher I've had at MU.  I was nervous going into this course, but her lectures were engaging, the homework wasn't too bad, and her exams were actually fun.  She emphasizes critical thinking skills, rather than memorization, which is a breath of fresh air for an intro class.
Very well taught class.  She conveys the material and responsibilites of the student very clearly

Sounds as if it is harder than other bio 1 classes but not bad at all. You have to study but if you know the material you will do good.  I got an A+ and only studied the night before basically by memorizing the notes.

Knows her stuff, but truly has no idea that Bio 1 is non-major.  If you love bio she's great.  If, like me, you need a science for your non-science degree, avoid this class.  It pulls way too much time from classes important for your degree.

I think that she is a great professor.  Her tests and homework aren't the easiest things in the world, simply because she expects you to study.  She really stresses understanding concepts as opposed to just memorizing them.

she's great, don't listen to the other jackass who thinks she sucks..if you have an interest in bio, you will defintly like her lectures. she is extremely knowledgable and she uses subtle humor that most people don't understand.  she's a great fresh prof

This is one of the most difficult professors I have ever dealt with. She is not receptive to any student feedback, she is negligent to the fact that every student in her class took around 4 or 5 weeks of classes to understand her course material and organization, and with talking with other classmates has consistently made rude remarks to everyone.

Prof. Brock is incredibly knowledgable and passionate. However, this class was miserable. The work is monotonous and resembles "busy work." You are given three essays to complete, but each essay requires an outline and a draft. The instruction page for the final essay was 7 pages long. The instructions are often confusing and repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a writing intensive class, some people don't realize that. It's not a guaranteed easy A, but if you do the work, you'll do well. Only two main papers, with lots of feedback and support. Professor is kind, always available to talk, and offers plenty of office hours and extra credit opportunities. Ended up with a 108% in the class.
She often doesn't really make sense but the class really isn't that hard especially for a writing intensive
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sometimes a lot of work and she can be confusing at times. Not a hard class but she can be aggravating. Gives a lot of extra credit though which is helpful. Has a lot of office hours too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Can be a lot of work but overall the class isn't that hard. If you are a good writer and go to class you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There is work you have to do outside of class which can sometimes be aggravating but overall this class is really easy. She has a ton of office hours that are helpful and she gives a lot of extra credit which is nice. She's a really nice lady and has helpful TAs.
Horrible grader and makes no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While she gives a lot of pre-class work and readings, she provides a lot of feedback on assignments and is always willing to answer questions and meet with students. As long as you apply yourself and listen closely to directions, you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is a very doable writing writing-intensive class to take at Mizzou. The class is front-loaded, which is nice, and there are only 2 papers. There is stuff to turn in after every class, but all of the questions write your paper for you.

Dr. Brock is kind, thoughtful, and knowledgeable. The class can be somewhat heavy workload especially early in the semester, but all of the homework feeds directly into the papers and is really not that difficult. She is always available outside of class during office hours and she is very flexible and willing to accommodate.

If you are taking this class I would drop it as soon as possible. Dr. Brock is a god awful professer that only cares about herself and nobody else. The TA's also do not even know how to answer a question and even say the professer is bad. She is a terrible professer as a whole and I would stay away from this class as much as possible.

She is a horrible professor and does not care about the students in class. she does not explain things and grades things horribly with hardly any explanation. She does not explain of what we are doing in the actual classwork and more on the Amish as a whole.
Very confusing class.

Get ready for the worst class of your life. Pro tip: never bring up opposing views in class or in essays that is an extremely easy way to fail this class. If you want to learn how to write an email for 15 classes in a row this is the class for you!!!! Seriously this is the worst class with the worst teacher in the worst department.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor is the worth that Ive ever had and I'm on my last semester of senior year. Most of the learning is done outside of class lecture is used to explain assignments and it's a waste of time but attendance is required. Teaches students how to write an email for multiple classes but then tells you to not email her. AVOID AT ALL COSTS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Brock seemed like a nice lady at first but she is very passive aggressive as she constantly belittles her students all class. Get ready for many many many microaggressions towards all groups of people. She is an extremely biased grader, favoring students who suck up to her weird agenda. Grading scale is weird, she can't even write properly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class ever. Do not take any class taught by her ever. I spent more time writing non-sense papers than actually studying for my major and it tanked my GPA due to her biased grading. I hope she is happy for how much she dropped my GPA, she clearly needs something to be happy about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: WORST PROFESSOR EVER. Do NOT take this class. Only take this class if you like to get belittled for 3 hours a week and not learn a single thing. I wish I was lying but we did not learn about the Amish once during lectures. Lecture consists of her pandering about how to write an email or how to use Canvas. How she has a job is beyond me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The most confusing and weirdly organized class I've ever taken. Attendance is mandatory although nothing is ever taught in class, she just confusingly rambles. I spent more time on this class than any class I've ever taken. I went to her office hours and felt absolutely belittled. She makes this class way harder than it needs to be. Prepare to read
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Stay away. Grades make no sense, nothing is organized well, the TA's don't follow the rubric, SO much work for absolutely no reason. She claims the class is "front loaded." No it's not. It's the same amount of work all semester. She just rambles all class, therefore leaving you even more confused. Could not tell you a single thing I learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is fairly simple to get an A in. She gives tons of extra credit opportunities. Attendance/participation is over half the grade in the class. That being said, no class has ever been as mind numbing, confusing, disorganized, stress inducing, and overall terrible. The syllabus is over 12 pages long and the course is horrible to navigate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Avoid this class at all costs. Prof. Brock is a nice lady, but she runs her class horribly and grades way harder than she needs to. She acts as if the class is super interested in the Amish and assigns things with HORRIBLE directions. You can't skip class, even though the lectures don't help you with the actual, important, assignments. Not for me.

This class was enjoyable for me. There was a lot of work outside of class but she was very clear in her instructions. She likes things done a certain way so if you follow directions you will be fine. There are a lot of extra credit assignments and she gives long and helpful feedback on papers. Participation definitely matters.

If you're a STEM major taking this course because it counts for humanities, writing intensive, and diversity credit I have one piece of advice for you, take this class pass fail. This class will be time-consuming and difficult enough without having to worry about it dragging your GPA down. Which it will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class isn't that bad. Her instructions are extremely unclear about half the time, but just make sure to skim over the assigned readings and make some notes. For the papers- the way she grades them is super particular so if you want the highest grade possible then do the optional zoom meetings with her. She gives lots of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework
