reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Crozier is by far the worst professor I have ever had.  He does not care for any of his students, and he makes rude comments to his students throughout lectures.  The class is graded off 3 exams and attendance.  He will not offer extra credit, even if the student is struggling.  I would recommend any class other than his.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I went into this class under the impression it would be an easy A, but apparently not with this professor. His online exams are super hard even if you read everything and go to all the lectures. There are questions over things he says once in class and aren't even important. Take this class with anyone but him and you should do well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Literally love this man with my whole heart. I've taken three courses with him and haven't gotten anything below a B. Would recommend to anyone.

If you need help understanding a concept, he will gladly help you and clarify the content. Makes a boring class entertaining. The songs he plays before class are entertaining as well. I do recommend reading the chapters and taking notes on your own before class. It helps understand the topic more. I totally recommend taking this class!

Professor Crozier is a funny dude who keeps sometimes boring lectures interesting.  He grades very easily, almost to the point where you can get a solid B if you just show up and pay attention.  I have never asked him for help, as I don't need it, but he seems to be happy to help and answer questions in class.  Definitely recommend this class.

He's very nice and laid-back guy, until you rudely interrupt him in class then you see his other face (which is totally understandable!)  Your grade  Clicker points (20%) + 2 midterms (45%) + final exam (35%) You gotta read though to get full credit for clicker questions. If your answer is wrong you still get partial credit..... EASY A !

He's a terrible teacher. His grading method is one of arbitrary means. He provides no suggestion for improvement other than "refer to guide" as help; the guide is an example essay and outline tool. I duplicated the format and sentence structure of the paper he used as an example and did terribly on it. He doesn't grade on content.  Pick anyone else

This man is literally the best teacher I have ever had. Yes, he is tough when it comes to papers, but in the end it was definitely worth it. This was the second class that I took with him, and if I could take another class with him I would. IF you take this class you won't regret it !

This is an interesting course, but do NOT take it with this professor if it can be avoided. She knows what she's talking about, but does not accept any dissent during class conversations. If you take this course with her, go to office hours and ask questions. The exams are written and she looks for very specific answers (her opinions).

Graded by very few tests and a big semester long, group project with a vaguely worded rubric. Canvas was kind of also kind of a mess and there's no electronic note taking allowed in class. I did enjoy most of the guest lectures though. Her own lectures were just okay. She's definitely not for everyone, but it's not hard to pass if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has a lot of opinions in her class that she will talk about and if you don't agree with her it's hard to say anything in the class

Dr. Mislan was a good teacher. She's incredibly intelligent, and I felt supported by her. My main problem with her course Gender and Media were the people in it. Don't take this class if you're not ready to be judged if what you say isn't liberal enough. The people were so intense and I had classmates who were afraid to speak up because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the worst professors on the planet
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Canvas is confusing (there is bonus points for students who create test questions for her, something she never mentioned), and grading has no rubric basis. Genuinely a bad person as much as she is a bad teacher. Uses situated knowledge and the intolerance paradox to legitimize berating students on their opinions. Drop this class genuinely.

Cristina walked into class every day with her coffee, a nice outfit, and a clean purse every day while telling students they are bad people for having a heteronormative race and sexual orientation. Told my close friend in class that she could never feel the oppression Cristina has felt in her lifetime, while she is living below the poverty line.

Confusing multiple choice tests with vague answers (and no source or textbook to prove which is correct). Told  student in class that he should not speak because his ancestors enslaved hers. As a journalism professor, told white students they cannot cover black stories. Genuinely disappointing. Talked down to and belittled students constantly.

This was the worst professor I have had at Mizzou. I am progressive and open-minded, and she still offended me many times. She was cold and off-putting every time we would ask her for feedback on assignments. Every class was just political rants with zero neutrality. When talking about Gaza she referred to the group that 'runs and owns everything'
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am appalled that the Missouri School of Journalism allows this professor to teach at such a prestigious institution in its field. Not only is the class unorganized, this professors behavior should be categorized as unethical and be investigated by MU.

I was excited to take this class because DEI is a passion area of mine and I know the importance of examining my own biases. Yet this professor made me HATE the topic and I now have limited desire to learn more. She is disorganized, vague in her grading and inaccessible to students. She picks her favorites and everyone else can go pound sand.

This class was disappointing. Mislan had a negative attitude, stating she "doesn't give an F*** about journalism." The course was disorganized, with vague lectures and little guidance on exams. Materials/rubrics weren't posted on Canvas. There was favoritism and a lack of support, making it unwelcoming. I recommend avoiding this class.

TAKE ANOTHER PROFESSOR FOR THIS CLASS. I was looking forward to this class and its content. She is too unorganized and not interested in teaching students, just giving her opinions. She doesn't provide detailed direction for tests, assignments or projects and refuses to answer questions when asked for details. She is just awful.

Unorganized, opinion based (and I'm liberal!) no feedback, no clear direction given for assignments, projects or tests, even when asked. Refused to meet with students during office hours after midterm tests or help students learn what she is looking for when grading tests, cancelled all office hours until students just gave up. Worst class yet.

This is the worst professor I have had in my time at MU. The 1st day of class she told us that she didn't give a f**k about journalism students. She had clear favorites in her class & those were the only students she would call on, had unclear grading expectations & would refuse to meet students at office hours or to clarify tests & assignments.

“Most people here are upset that they have to confront complex systems of harm in society.” I think this sums up the problem. There is a way to go about confronting these issues that is not shaming students. The tone of this comment is condescending; so was this class the entire semester. Justifying political bias because you agree is ignorant.

Worst class I've taken. Dr. Mislan bans laptops, lectures are disorganized, and exams are overly complex with no rubric or feedback. Grades hinge on 10 assignments, with one group project worth 50%. Her teaching style demonstrates her need to be "heard." Take this course with another professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
AN HONEST ONE:

Christina is not that bad. Most people here are upset that they have to confront complex systems of harm in society. Yes, Christina is a leftist. Yes, she's gonna call people on stuff. YES, IT IS OVERBEARING AT TIMES. Overall, these people are dramatic. You'll like her course if you're smart and take journalism seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is essentially how to virtue signal 101. Class content is not found in the syllabus and test questions were not based on objective book content (or had any research whatsoever to back them up). If you are willing to be extremely performative and pander in the exact was Professor Mislan likes, you will do well.

As a black woman of color, this class was completely unbearable. Cristina attempts to be as performatively woke as possible while simultaneously holding and voicing biases against impoverished and disabled individuals. Placing black and brown individuals on a pedestal while ripping apart others in class is not acceptance, it's dangerous prejudice.

This class was awful. She is incredibly biased and makes her students feel anxious and scared about the state of the world. No optimism at all. She doesn't even teach herself and just brings in random guest lectures. The exams are also very difficult. She seriously needs to be fired because the way she teaches is simply unethical.

She should be fired. She doesn't even teach her own lectures, just brings in guest lectures to teach for her. She shows up to class a minute before it starts or late, but expects students to stay after class. She is also SO INCREDIBLY BIAS. I'm a minority who has experienced racism and I fail her tests. Please make that make sense.

I attended every class this semester, took thorough notes, made a study group with other students, and still struggled with her exams. Does not care about the success of her students, gives no feedback and is not open to challenging questions. The first half of classes was wildly different that the second half after she knows students cannot drop.
Do not take this class. Most of the time rate my professor pages are just students with bad grades complaining but Cristina Mislan is a detriment to the J-school.
Never rolled my eyes so much in a class. WORST PROFESSOR EVER.

Easily the worst professor I've had. She rambles about her own opinions instead of teaching journalism, posts no materials, and grades are a mystery until the end. Mizzou should seriously reconsider her place in the program.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The day we had a fire drill in class was the best day of my life because I got a 5 minute break from her class.

I have a different perspective than the other students commenting on here. I am a Jewish student on campus and feel unsafe in Professor Mislan's class. Her discussion of Palestine as well as research she published in 2019 were both blatantly Anti-Semitic. Really disappointing to see coming from someone who wants everyone to "examine their biases".

To describe Professor Mislan using her own words: situated knowledge superiority complex with a heavy victim mentality. I am as liberal as they come and she was so extreme it was hard to listen to. Showed a film with a scene that portrayed sex trafficking in the LGBTQ+ community and she praised it as acceptance. Seriously disturbed professor.
one-woman cult with a syllabus
If I had a nickel for every time Professor Mislan aggressively put down or shamed a student's opinion in class, I would be able to pay my semester's tuition.
I feel guilty getting an A- because it means that on some level this insidious human being agrees with what I say.

Professor Mislan was the worst teacher I have ever had at any level of education. Teaching extremist opinions is not journalism. Shaming and retaliating against students publicly in class (as well as when I went in for office hours) was completely uncalled for. I have written to administration about her and hope that Mizzou wakes up and fires her.

Definitely the most frustrating class I've taken in college. Instructor was overly opinionated and was very self-righteous, often interrupting guest lecturers (which we had one pretty much every day-this lady had maybe 5 lectures the entire semester). It's a required course at the J-School, so take it in the fall to get the better instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mislan should NOT be a professor at Mizzou, she is unorganized, incredibly biased to her extremist pov, (coming from a liberal myself). Dr. Mislan teaches on a soapbox and doesn't allow for any expression of other ideas. I've never been in a journalism class where people were afraid to speak up until now, because of how she bullies students.

Dr Mislan is one of the most disrespectful teachers I've ever had in my life. She actively shames people in front of the class and will call you out if she doesn't agree with your answer. She only calls on certain students and her lectures make no sense. I would genuinely hope for every class lecture to be from someone else other than her.

Dr. Mislan was so rude. While I agree with so much of what she says, she presents her ideas in a tone to make students feel bad for not knowing it. I would recommend anyone take this class in the fall with Dr. Porter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As another student said, I gave Professor Mislan over half of the semester a chance - I showed up to nearly every class, and have been uncomfortable due to her teaching her opinions and her attempts to indoctrinate students. Half of the class hasn't been there due to her opinionated lectures as it is a waste of time. Avoid and take with other prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I tried to give Mislan a chance, but she was unbearable. She doesn't post slides, doesn't give back tests, doesn't allow any technology and will call you out in the middle of class if she sees you with your laptop/phone, and lectures are unorganized. She's extremely difficult and agonizing to work with. Take this class with Dr. Porter if you can.

If the School of Journalism has any respect for its students and it's reputation, they should fire Dr. Mislan. Christina is a nightmarishly awful professor. I'm actually shocked she landed a job at one of the most globally respected journalism schools in the world given how terrible she is at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mislan is, no doubt, the most ineffective professor I have ever encountered. She wastes class time on soapbox speeches, shows no depth in teaching, creates a hostile classroom environment, and is rude to students and guest lecturers. For the good of School of Journalism, she must either dramatically improve or show some respect and resign.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'll save you some time with what this teacher "teaches": Don't be racist in journalism :/ By the end of the lecture you'll feel like you know less about journalism than going into it. It's clear MU forgot that they're still paying Mislan to stand in front of students and rip apart their chosen profession for an hour and 15 minutes. Disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The MU J-School needs to consider removing this professor. As a student with excellent journalism performance, I had to withdrawal from this class because the exams were so poorly graded, despite me receiving a 98% on the final project. I have never had a worse teacher in my whole academic career. Her teaching has 0 relevance to journalism.

Where do I begin? Cristina's inability to teach is astounding. 2/3 of classes were guest lectures (her former students) & movies. Makes prejudice claims in class saying, "there is research to back that up," and then never gives any actual research. Creates a toxic class environment where by the 2-3d week no students wanted to answer her questions.

I wish that Professor Mislan would practice what she preaches and examine her own biases. Beyond that the class structure is just plain bad. Lecture slides with no sources, zero reference to the text book beyond syllabus week, and a vague completely subjective group project. Cristina is a genuinely bad person as much as she is a bad teacher.
Wish Profes

I really do not appreciate how one-sides Dr. Mislan is. You have to be a teachers pet journalism major and suck up to her in order to get a good grade. Come to class so you can take notes for the test, but be prepared to not get a good grade because if your a normal person like me and not a try hard smart student you do not go "in-debth" enough.

I generally thought that Professor Mislan was a fine teacher. People that are talking about her "trying to indoctrinate" her students clearly just don't want to examine their own biases, which is 90% of this class, in my opinion.

I've yet to finish the class, but I will say that the final project is fairly vague, but that isn't wholly her fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Biased- doesn't care about teaching the required materials and only wants to get her opinions across.

Worst teacher ever. Stay away. Completely and utterly biased, does not teach the content and instead teaches her opinion rather than fact. What could be such a cool class was turned into a period where she ripped on people that didn't agree with her views. Upset with the MU Journalism school for hiring her. Wish I could give her a negative -100.

I struggle for words to describe Professor Mislan. A complete lack of empathy towards disabled and lower class individuals combined with her vehemently constant racial prejudice against white members of her class is astonishing. Class is execrable without her biases, following no structure, syllabus, or book. Final project grading is subjective.

Dr. Mislan was an excellent instructor in Women & The Media. She did a wonderful job leading insightful and culturally relevant class discussions. This class gave me a strong theoretical foundation for feminist reporting that will stick with me for the rest of my career. Highly recommend for anyone, but especially those seeking a fresh perspective.

Rude, disrespectful, and has a habit of either ignoring or make the process difficult in terms of fulfilling people's disability accommodations. Not a good professor and makes a mockery of the serious issues discussed in the class with her deeply unserious approach to the class curriculum.
I didn't wear my seatbelt on the way to class in hopes that I die on the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Mislan takes what should be an incredibly important class and turns it into an inessential one. She rarely talks about the practical uses of these issues in journalism. Instead, she tries to be "intellectual". However, if you know truly anything about the issues, her lectures provide no new info and if you don't, you won't learn anything.

I wish I had read this page before I took the class, I would have dropped it so quickly. Cristina is a bad teacher and grades based on views rather than facts. Mizzou did the J-school a disservice by hiring her.

Professor Mislan's situated knowledge superiority complex makes this an unsafe space for constructive discussion of topics affecting journalism. She only calls on people who agree with her extremist agenda and shames students (including name-calling) who disagree. Most of the class is afraid to raise their hands in fear of retaliation. Stay away.

Professor Mislan is the worst teacher I've had at Mizzou. Her class was disorganized, and she put little to no thought into her lectures and constantly talked down to and vilified students. Someone in the journalism industry should understand that using racially prejudiced rhetoric to propagate her own opinion is completely unacceptable.

I was excited about this class it became clear that there would not be any constructive discussion surrounding Journalistic Inclusion and Culture. Professor Mislan used racially prejudiced and outright disrespectful rhetoric toward students with different perspectives. Only perpetuated the "single stories" she claims to be fighting against.

I took this teacher last semester and thought I would warn other students. Professor Mislan referenced the textbook less than 5 times in total. Tests were on her personal views rather than facts in a class where she publicly mocked and made fun of students who held different views. Discourages open discussion and is condescending towards students.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class requires that you attend regularly, but the professor also offers office hours and is understanding. This is an important class, and we need more like it!

Lectures matter in this class, but the subject matter is important to journalism. J2000 teaches students to identify power structures and the role the media plays in either challenging or reinforcing harmful narratives about people and places. Dr. Mislan is an expert in this field, and her lectures are always interesting.

Dr. Mislan's research is really as a professor is interesting, and she clearly cares about students and the topics she teaches. She respects diversity and values multiple opinions. She challenges students to think beyond their worldviews and understand their unique situated knowledges. Students can expect to read and discuss in this class.

Professor Mislan's biased views were damaging and discriminatory toward students. Used prejudiced rhetoric that excluded dissenting options and discouraged open dialogue. Does not follow the textbook and instead tests solely on Professor Mislan's ideology. Ignorant class policies show she cares more about indoctrination than success of students.

After reading other comments, I am glad I am not alone and that I share the same sentiment. Cristina Mislan maliciously alienates, vilifies, and disparages students with differing opinions. Take this class with another professor.

Do not take this class. Professor Mislan puts little to no effort into her students and over half the class was guest lecturers. The classes where she lectured were essentially ideological indoctrination. The final project is half of the grade and the rubric is not helpful. Does not allow technology in class and does not post lecture videos.

Professor Mislan's bigoted views and cynical attitude toward students made this class burdensome. Called students extremists for challenging her lecture points that were solely based on personal ideology. I would consider myself a liberal but her mistreatment of students based solely on political affiliation was astounding. Do not take this class.
Course material and topics were all over the place. Poor professor with powerful biases towards students.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mislan openly disrespects students in the class based on their personal views, in a class where she preaches a 'safe space'. Her condescending teaching style makes learning extremely difficult. Take any other professor for this class if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mislan is one of the worst professors I've ever had. The class was extremely unorganized and she was extremely unhelpful when it came to the final project. She didn't even have a rubric for a long time. Her tests are ridiculous because the answer choices are all basically the same. I went to every lecture and still did badly on all the tests.

If I could give Professor Mislan a zero, I would. She is extremely condescending and has no time for differing opinions. The final project was worth 50% of the class grade. I had something like a 93.7% in this class before it. I received an 89% on the final which dropped my grade to an 89.8%, and she refused to round it up. Avoid her at all costs.

If you can take this class with any other professor (even if it is a different semester), do it. She talks down and belittles her students. The class does not feel like a safe space for learning and discussion. Her multiple choice tests have the same four statements re-worded four different times so it is impossible to find the correct answer.

I have never disliked a class so much. She is passive-aggressive to her students, her tests are purposefully confusing, she doesn't allow any technology to write notes, she is not flexible at all, and her students are afraid to speak up or ask questions. I would 100% recommend finding another professor for this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Moral indoctrination upstaged objective learning in every lecture the entire semester. Only 3 exams and 1 group project make up 90 percent of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Discussions often veered towards moralistic shaming rather than learning about journalistic inclusion and issues. Students who held different views, or spoke up in disagreement were openly mocked, being called "a**holes" and "fascists" by Dr. Mislan. Personal views were tested rather than objective questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wish I had dropped this class at the beginning of the year. Professor Mislan is one of the most biased and outright disrespectful people I have ever met. She ignores people in class who have different views than her and actively alienates students in class. If there is any other teacher for this class, go to them.
Very few grades and confusing test material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unorganized. Lectures the entire time. Final project is worth 50% of your grade.

Professor Mislan grades based on personal ideology rather than objective facts. I was really excited about this class but her grading and the way she talks down to students is a massive power trip. Avoid this course at all costs.

Cross-cultural journalism is an extremely important topic, but this class felt like a waste of time, and more like checking off a box than anything productive. Dr. Mislan is not flexible, and lectures are pointless when it comes to encouraging critical thinking and discussion, and yet also unhelpful for the extremely difficult/subjective tests.

The class structure is awful. Very few grades that are all worth a lot of points. The tests are probably the worst I've ever taken. Super opinion based and all of the answers basically mean the same thing. The average on the final exam was a 53%.  Doesn't count attendance but bases the tests on one thing she said in class weeks before.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I felt like she didn't really care about the success of her students. The last 4 weeks of class were all guest lectures or documentaries and she didn't do anything. She loves writing answers on tests that all mean the same thing but written differently. The class average on the last exam was a 53% in a class that should be easy.

Dr. Mislan has honestly been the most politically biased professor I have ever had at Mizzou. She does not teach, she pushed her political ideations onto the class. She is rude and snarky to those who do not agree with her. I do not recommend taking J2000 with her at all.

If you are a visual learner, I would not recommend her as a professor. Although phones are banned in the classroom, I'd recommend secretly trying to take photos of the Powerpoint slides to write down later and use class time to write everything she says. Most of the test questions are about one sentence things she says. Tests are trick questions.

If you have the option to take J2000 with any other professor besides Dr. Mislan, do it. What is supposed to be a lighthearted but serious class was turned into something completely different because of Cristina Mislans attitude towards topics and students. She is awfully arrogant and passive aggressive. Talks to students like we are babies.

Tests in this class are so confusing. Questions are worded poorly and the answers are way too similar. She doesn't allow technology in class, and notes aren't as good as they could be if I were to type on my laptop. There is absolutely nothing on the canvas page that would help if you were to miss class.

I really enjoyed Dr. Mislan/her passion for the class. What so many people are perceiving as "cynicism" or "radicalism" is simply just the display of someone with a deep knowledge and understanding of the injustices that so many people face. A great class to learn how to think outside of yourself, something so many MU students apparently need
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst part of this class is not Mislan's opinionated lectures, but rather her cynical attitude towards life in general. Most days, I feel hopeless about the state of the world after leaving this class. The course content is important, and Mislan is very smart, but it shouldn't be mandatory that we have to learn about every injustice ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There's no room for nuance or debate in this class--what Dr. Mislan says is essentially canon. At times, the subject matter is very tailored toward white people and this seems a bit insulting to non-white students who have to sit through a basic lesson: how not to be racist. Also, Dr. Mislan makes students use/purchase three streaming services.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am as leftist as they come, but I couldn't stand this class. It just felt like we were being taught to be as performatively "woke" as possible. Discussions were useless and Mislan was quick to shame people who had valid questions. Makes you watch movies that you have to pay for and includes questions about them on quizzes which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: J2000 was an interesting class I took this semester. I actually enjoyed the various topics that were covered in class despite the many papers we had. Dr. Mislan is very knowledgeable and you get a sense that she does extensive research. I thought she could sometimes be "unapproachable" and I would usually ask my question to the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Attendance was not mandatory but she claimed to know if you came. I did skip occasionally and was fine. Some lectures are interesting, others are just her forcing her opinion on you. I would only take her again if I had to; I dreaded the class because of her attitude. The content was not bad. I did well on all tests solely studying the night before
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are weekly quizzes. Some readings can take you a while. Be prepared to read a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you use a laptop or recorder to take notes, look elsewhere. No electronics are allowed in class. Mislan just came off to a lot of the class as very quick to snap, and her viewpoints can turn off many people including me. Not the best choice for a class based off of different controversial topics. Wasn't always looking forward to come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mislan is a hypocritical, close-minded person. She started the class by saying that the room was a safe space to discuss anything. We had one discussion the entire semester and she didn't lead it. When one kid tried correcting her on an incorrect stat she practically shamed him in front of everyone. The only thing I learned was from a guest lecurer

I enjoyed the topics of this class. I enjoyed the guest lecturers. I wanted to like Cristina. The issue is your opinion is valued only if it lines up with hers, which is problematic in a class that is based on opinions of how different controversial topics are seen/covered in media. The plethora of guest lectures were the saving grace of this class

On the first day we were told the class would be open to any and all ideas. Just as long as the all mighty Christina Mislan approves. The same woman who cites "Everyday Feminism" over any credible news outlet. She talks at us like we are dogs and cannot understand tone. She is out of touch with the culture of the class and needs to be replaced ASAP

A flawed class handled by Dr. Mislan fairly well. The course identifies social justice issues and connects them to journalism coverage, but it rarely gives practical advice for making the industry better. The lecture style doesn't suit the topic well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is the most passionate teacher I have ever had. I wish everyone at Mizzou was required to take this class. The tests are all essay and true/false but if you go to class (which you should because it's extremely interesting & informative) and do your readings you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Teaches only one side to the argument. If you disagree with her, your ideas actually do get labeled as sexist or racist. Exams are based on opinions that are taken from movies and class material, so not actual facts. Also she provides minimal noteworthy material. Avoid this teacher.

For a class about remaining non-biased, respectful and fair in journalism, Mizzou has hired a stubborn, one-sided individual who has no respect for her students or the subject.  It's her way or the highway, despite the fact that she promises that her class will be a safe place for understanding different viewpoints.
Her examples are misleading and bias, and she does not foster two-sided conversation. One of the worst teachers I've ever encountered.

Mislan was a very passionate teacher and I honestly thought she did a decent job of teaching this course though it is very obvious that she has an agenda (she admits it too).  The lectures were long, theres a lot of reading and the tests will destroy your hand but in the end I learned a lot from this class that I definitely need for the future.

Reading these comments made me question whether or not these were all people I had a conversation with. Everyone took the words right out of my mouth. I only hope her superiors read these and fire her. The class content had the potential to be amazing. The best thing that's happening to this class is that she will not be teaching it next semester.

Mislan is biased. If you don't agree with her, don't raise your hand. This class has the potential to be AMAZING,  but her teaching methods are pathetic. She just states her opinion with some John Oliver videos to back them up. Turn stuff in on time, make your group project something she'll gush over (i.e. her opinions given back to her) & bam, A.

She constantly says that objectivity is the best policy, yet she clearly has a side on every issue and treats students that disagree with her like garbage. She is condescending and undermines anyone who opposes her views. The tests are hard and reference both readings and tons of documentaries. Just don't speak, bite your tongue, and go to class.

If you don't agree with everything she says, she hates you. This class is meant to open minds up to tolerate and embrace the diversity around you, but Mislan needs a lesson in that herself. Also, the group project is ridiculous mainly because there are 10 people in one group.

Not the worst. The thing about Mislan is: she's funny, and she's passionate about things like racism, queer theory, class politics, etc. But her delivery needs some fine-tuning. She's very critical of those who don't get on board with her ideas. ALSO, THAT GROUP PROJECT.  For as lengthy as her instrutions were (5ish pages) they weren't very clear.

She likes to repeat that this class is not about our personally opinions yet she contiunusly expresses hers and will shoot down any opinions that don't agree with her. Tests are pretty much just to check if you go to class. Final project is vague. My advice would be to go to class, don't speak, get a B and never look back.

Honors journalism student here  She is the most passive-aggressive professor I've ever had. My friend described it well when he said, "It's like she thinks we are dogs and can only interpret tone. Does she know if she says really condescendinghurtful things in a nice way, it is still condescendinghurtful?"

2 Essay tests, each 15% - very toughly graded.  You have to go to class and you need to know concrete examples of what was said there about each topic.  Online quizzes every week about homework readingsfilms.  Huge semester long group project.  Common sense topics but overcomplicated to the point where it's hard to get an A.
Does not grade assignments in timely way. Does not provide feedback. Seems angry and insecure. Not the best professor. Avoid if you can.

I absolutely LOVED Professor Mislan. Her lectures make you evaluate your own beliefs and see things from different perspectives. She brings up topics that are difficult to talk about, but that need to be discussed. Mislan shows great videos and articles in class to lead the discussion and they are always relevant and helpful.

If you make the mistake of giving insight that doesn't align with her personal opinions, prepare to lose your head. Also, the project instructions (there are three in the semester) are extremely vague. Try and take this class with Perry if at all possible.

Sometimes her lectures are one-sided; she claims that she wants to emphasize the importance of not a single story about an issue, but many different stories, when sometimes in the way she presents issues, she only provides one story. I think if she cited more credible sources with her stats, it'd be a lot easier to understand her point of view.
The group work's instruction is really unclear. Online quiz every week-read the material and watch the movies
He is funny and gives good lectures. He grades assignments incredibly slowly and does not give a clear rubric for those assignments. He does not grade very harsh though.

LAW 2010 was for my Pre-Law path. I enjoyed the course, but it took FOREVER to get back grades for assignments. There are weekly readings that you need to do, and you may be called upon in class to answer questions. He allowed cheatsheets for the Midterm and Final, and he drops your lowest grade. Good class, but he needs to lock in on the grading.

Took this class for pre-law and was left feeling confused. Professor is very knowledgeable about topics but class is paced horribly and assignments was graded haphazardly and took months to recieve back. Funny guy but I wish it was more organized because going to lectures seemed to lack structure.

This class was a rollercoaster to say the least. I took this class to introduce me into pre-law, and I was instead given 2 equally upset friends, an extreme lack of communication from the professor, and waiting months for grades to be dropped.

The professor is VERY knowledgeable. And be prepared to be cold-called on something insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is funny and knowledgeable. Respected in the law field. Readings once a week and he outlines people he will call on, so you know. 3 papers, 2 exams. Essays were graded kind of weird but if you hit all you need to you will be fine. Exams are tougher but he does drop one out of the 5. Small extra credit, and does Iclicker which affects grade.

I love Crouch but he seems to have a strange fascination with AI. Additionally, it doesn't feel like his lectures are particularly well organized, and I often found myself disengaging in class. Luckily, CivPro and professional responsibility are easy enough.

Really passionate about what he teaches. Course is bleeding-edge and covers current events. Encourages participation in lectures, although he can get sidetracked easily. Not a lot of assignments, but he does drop 1 grade out of 5. Assigns reading material every week, but the amount of reading is usually less than 30 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pay attention and stay on task and it will be easy. He doesn't know canvas too well so be prepared but a great teacher

Crouch is a nice and funny guy, but lectures can be very unorganized and hard to follow. Assignments are not posted when they are supposed to be. You can do the class online. Attendance counts towards your gradeSeveral speakers come to speak from various fields of law. 2 tests (final is optional), 4 600+ word essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the class is a little unorganized, anyone who is truly interested in internet law would love this class and him as a professor. The memos were very easy and quick, and there were so many interesting speakers that he brought to class. He doesn't post a lot of material, but the midterm and memos are simple if you pay attention in class.

Overall the course itself was not difficult. (I was not a pre-law major, or anything related to that.) The class was extremely unorganized. Crouch rarely used Canvas, deleted the syllabus after 3 days, and gave little notice or insight about the midterm, final or assignments. Be prepared for frustration and a lack of communication.

Grading criteria is not clear for this class. The instructor told me she expects us to be in the class a minimum of 18 hours per week. She also monitors when you read the textbook,type assignments, etc. Every assignment I turned in is a struggle for a C, and I have never had this issue in any other class before. Heavily accuses students of using AI

Do not take this class or any other class with this professor. Very ironic how the class is "Human Learning" but it feels like everything they do is set up like a "gotcha". I agree with the other comments about the baseless accusations and low-grades on high-quality work. Very inconsistent grading.

She grades extremely hard! On assignments I spent hours doing, she would give me a D. I have been an A student my whole life and have never received such hard feedback or grades. DO NOT TAKE if you care about your GPA.

This instructor has a significant fear of AI that leads to baseless accusations and zeros. 

0/10 teacher, take Human Learning 4115 or 7115 with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor has no care for your personal life. miss a lecture? Sorry, write a 2 page paper to make it up. she thinks the world should revolve around her classes. I am infuriated. She is so picky with grading. Has made me cry on many occasions out of pure rage. Changed all my work to make it her own. I'm fed up. I'll never take her class again.

Mikaela did the teaching, but Marci did all the behind the scenes, when emailing her she was always helpful, and she prioritizes students who haven't gotten as many opportunities in the class so that they can catch up and get more from the course. She seemed to care, but she also had some disrespectful tendencies, and we never actually saw her.

Zero respect for student time. As a prevet student, I spent more time on this 3 credit elective than my 4 credit physics & 3 credit organic chem class combined. The excessive group work outside class was beyond unreasonable. I love horses & was excited to work with sale foals in the next course, but the coarse load isn't worth it so I never did.
No respect for student time. Nice and respected most of the time. Will set off if you do something a little too wrong. Grading for this class was horrible.....just never gets done.

Marci's tests can be difficult and detail oriented, but otherwise she is a passionate and enthusiastic teacher. She gives what I feel is a reasonable amount of homework and can relate to student's lives. She expects students to participate in class and be professional in their conduct. Be prepared to put a little effort into her class.

I was very excited to take her class, as I have a lot of experience working in that field. She's a good teacher who's understanding/easy to talk to and I liked her class a lot. However, her tests were very hard as they are all written (no multiple choice) and she expects your answers to not only be dead-on but be very specific. Fun but stressful.

Marci's expectations of her students are very clear. It is not hard to understand what material is most important and how to do well in the class. I think a lot of the issue lies in the fact that people don't like "hard work" but Marci is a good teacher if you actually go and listen to the lecture.

She is a terrible teacher. She is not understanding or helpful. She has a "power" issue and has to have control. She talks down to her students and treats anyone that doesn't have a passion for horses like crap. She is absolutely terrible. I still received a decent grade in the class but I hated every day that I had to listen to her "teach."
Tests are poorly written.

Dr. Crozier is a great lecturer. The excitement he has for the subject matter he teaches is infectious. He expects you to participate, but he is a caring and understanding professor. The two exams were difficult, but everything else was graded leniently, and class was fun. I mean, our final was a pizza party, that's a fun class
Such a nice and fun guy, really easy on people

This class was fantastic, Crozier is wonderful at keeping your attention. He doesn't care if he looks a little silly in order to more firmly plant memorable information in your mind. This class was by far my favorite this semester, and although I found it easy, that's probably because I enjoyed it, as I've found classes that are boring are harder.

I thoroughly enjoyed Dr. Crozier's course, and this course was one of my favorites. He is passionate about what he teaches and makes class fun. Lectures are very information heavy, but so long as you pay attention and take notes you'll be good. I cannot recommend the class and Dr. Crozier enough!

This course was one of my favorites. The lectures were full of information, but he made the lectures fun and interesting. I would recommend to complete the required readings and take good notes because the exams can be a little tough. Overall it was a great experience and I would take a course with this professor again.

Crozier was by far my favorite professor of the semester. His lectures were mandatory for participation, but he always made them interesting. Every once and a while he just called off the lecture for the day because it was nice outside. The course is heavy on reading outside of class, but there is no homework besides the reading.

Professor Crozier runs a fantastic class, even though it was completely online this semester. His lectures are information-heavy (expect to take a lot of notes!) but he makes them fun, fascinating, and an absolute riot to listen to. He is clear with his grading and posts grades consistently. I highly recommend taking this class.

Greek and Roman lit online (self paced) you must read about 1300 pages altogether and every ten days or so (x10) submit a 3-4 page paper. 3 exams that are HAND-WRITTEN and each were about 7 pages of writing so if you don't want to read 1500 pages of greek lit and write 50+ pages you need to find something else. grading on format only, not content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Hes a really cool guy but he makes the online tests impossible to do well on. You only have 1 minute for each question and there are questions impossible to look up that were never covered in lecture. I prepared differently for each test and got an 85/86 on every one and a B+ in the class. Youre better off taking a class w real tests in class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Crozier gives you reef points, and huge attendance "extra credit" points. He was hilarious, and made lectures interesting. The only thing was he grading scale screwed me. 94 and up is an A/A+, usually it's a 92 i believe. Got a 93, ended up w an A-, which sucked. All his tests and his final are all online which gives an advantage. Study beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is the easiest class ever. If you are looking for a friendly and hilarious professor, he is your guy! If you do the readings, it's an easy A. The readings in the book are so interesting, it won't even feel like you are studying for a class. AND the exams are online. so woohoo! Totally recommend it!!
Super chill guy, super easy content.

This was my easiest class of the semester! Didn't have to show up to class because every quiz and assignment was online. There also is extra credit you can do. He's very easy to talk to and a good teacher.
This is the best and easy class would definitely recommend!! The guy teaching also seems very nice.
I attended his class once, I got an A. All the work is online, no official final. and he is lowkey fine.
He is so nice and cares a lot about what he is talking about. The tests and labs are online but that doesn't mean you shouldn't go to lectures. He's so nice and if you have him be grateful.
He is a great teacher who really cares about his students and course.

This was a very fun and easy class. The online labs are pretty fun if you actually take the time to think about them and do them honestly. Might be the easiest A of my whole life but that doesnt mean the class is useless
Dr. Credeur is very passionate about what he does, and you will learn a lot if you go to his class. Getting an A is quite easy but I would still recommending going to the lectures.
Gives great lectures and coursework is fairly easy and same thing every week.

Amazing guy, he knew my name in less than a week, which is hard to find at Mizzou. The lectures can get a little boring from time to time, but I found that being because I just wasn't interested in the exact thing we were talking about that day. The next day was a different story, very intrigued.
This class was such an easy A. Just do your 3 assignments for the week and you will be fine. It's really just a participation class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: At the very beginning of the semester, Professor Credeur said that the class would be an easy A and it really was. Some of the assignments can be very time consuming as with most other college classes, but they were simple. Professor Credeur was very laid back and was flexible. One thing that I disliked was how hard it was to get into contact him.
Good lectures and easy class
Cost me a letter grade over a file error on Canvas and gave poor communication over how to fix it. Would not take again.

Literally such an easy class if you just do the work (there isn't much) and do the work on time. Whenever I asked a question at the end of class, he always answered it clearly and in an understandable way. If you consistently put effort into your work, you can a few skip lectures and still get an A. The lecture content was actually interesting too!

If you try to reach him, he's not gonna answer to any emails, don't even try. Lectures are dry, everything can be found online and the exams are open note. If you're considering taking NEP 1330 with him, don't. Waste of time, he doesn't know what he actually wants to teach, lot of dead time in class.
I went to class probably three times. Everything is on the Internet so if you need an elective, take this. If you plan on transferring elsewhere, credits from this class do not transfer anywhere.
Lectures were dry and many not necessary for assignments. Would take it again! Take online if given the option. Class is very easy.
He was average, i did enjoy his lectures though
Very personable and easy professor. Loves what he teaches and is very knowledgeable on the matter. Easy class for anyone needing a NEP elective.

He was my most boring prof. I would never go and passed with a B+. Tests are tough if you dont study and he just talks in circles about things that werent on the test. If you are interested in working out, it wouldnt have been boring.

Attend lectures!! Take notes on everything. You will need to review your notes and the book often. The class is graded on a curve. Difficult but very engaging class. I'm glad I had a professor like Dr. Cutkosky or else it would have been terrible. I would take another course by him if I could.

Difficult course, but what can you expect with abstract algebra. I wish Dr. Cutkosky had made the class a little more interactive because I sometimes felt lost in lecture. The homeworks were deceptively long; a four question assignment could really be more like twelve proofs, all of which take quite a while to do. Dr. Cutkosky is a nice guy.

Lecture notes online are ok, but his in class lectures are horrendous due to his atrocious communication skills. Goes over very few examples and expects you to just get everything. When you ask a question he usually says "well I've already went over this multiple times" and doesn't answer your question. You might as well never ask. Worst Miz prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Matrix Theory with this guy was a major struggle. He didn't do many examples in class and expected us to learn the material based off of typed up notes we would get online. Wouldn't give all answers to hw problems, even thought it wasn't graded. Hard tests. Got frustrated when you asked questions in class. I had to work really hard to get  a B+.
Does very little examples in class. Never provides the solutions to more than half of the HW problems. Unless your an expert in Matrix Theory stay away from this class!

Overall, he is a very chill professor that understands what it is like to be a student. He does his best to make sure you don't ever have to worry about his class, while still doing a good job at teaching it. While attendance isn't mandatory, its really easy to fall behind if you don't go.
Very great professor, wants you to actually learn than just memorize things.

He is really nice and understanding if you can't make it to class. He recommended a textbook but you really don't need it everything you need are in his lectures. The tests are straight from the notes so pretty easy as long as you make sure to get lecture notes.

I really liked his introductory bioethics course. Mr. Culak was super helpful and genuinely cares about his students. His exams and assignments are all open note, not a hard class but makes you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All of his quizzes and exams were open note and online. He is willing to send you the lecture notes if you miss a day. There is a T/F quiz every week, but he drops the 3 lowest at the end of the semester. I would go to class so then you have the notes and understand, just because philosophy can be tricky.

He perfectly understands how difficult his class should be, because he knows that most people do not take this  specific class for their major. Great at explaining things, kind, very respected by his students. You can skip class, but the wording of the questions on the quizzes and tests (open note) will force you to learn the material either way.
Very good at lectures, cares about students and wants them to do good. All quizzes and exams are online. No homework and just a true false quiz a week
Great Teacher Weekly Quiz. But they are super easy take notes and you will be fine
Super arrogant, entitled, and rude! Do not take him.
great teacher

He's cocky, arrogant, and sometimes he really doesn't know what he's talking about.  His favorite phrases include, "This is easy, you just have to make a few key assumptions" and "This is easy, okay?"  To his credit, he does push grad school and he does know a lot of stuff, but he's just very hard to deal with.

My favorite professor I've had at Mizzou! All of his IT courses are similarly structured homework wise and does a great job teaching the material and provides lots of resources to succeed. Super nice guy in and out of the classroom and really cares about his students.

Dr. Culmer clearly has put a lot of effort into giving students plenty of resources to learn the material. He uses a flipped classroom setting, so many of the readings are provided on the canvas page and we go through examples in class. I feel like the pacing of the class was good but maybe too slow at times.

I think he was a great professor, most people who rated him badly generally were doing bad in his class and didn't listen. He as well as being a teacher told me his story and it was pretty cool to hear. He teaches well and is always ready to answer any questions you may have. Overall in my opinion, he was a good teacher.

He is a really nice teacher who obviously really cares about his students and helping them understand. Every concept in the assignments had an example in class, so those were pretty easy. He was very accessible through email and discord. 
The Canvas page was somewhat outdated, which led to a lot of googling, but that was still fine.

Kristofferson is super great! I'm taking 2040 online but it's literally been a breeze with his material. He has video of himself doing it, resources, and overall it's super efficient you ACTUALLY get to learn! There's a couple of scattered quizzes but everything is in a set in stone routine which I LOVE!

Professor Culmer is a great teacher. He does a great job of actually teaching us concepts and working through them with us. Unlike other professors at this University that teach coding classes, Professor Culmer actually shows us not only how to program but how to clearly structure and think about our programs.
Professor Culmer was very helpful outside of class and seems very passionate about both his craft and teaching.

Last year Culmer took hours outside of class, one-on-one with me and on his own time, to help me with a problem with my VS Code. No prof has ever gone that above and beyond for me. Class was easy and he had clear instructions for all the assignments. Always helpful in class but doesn't always reply to his email...
Love Professor Culmer! You can tell he really cares about his students. Needs to check email more often though and go deeper with the material in Database Systems.

The professor put little effort into providing decent course materials for learning. Rarely, if ever, was the appropriate material provided prior to starting a project and it was up to you to just teach yourself how to do it. If I wanted to teach myself how to program a language framework 10 years out of date I wouldn't of paid the university.

Ok yes, I did get a B+ but that's only because of the exams... The projects and standard assignments were easy A's so that means you got to also try on those exams otherwise you'll end up like me. SQL is a new "language" to most but very logical so it should be easy for you to pick up after seeing some examples. Always put effort in this class!

Professor Culmer is a fantastic professor! He is very accessible if you need help on the course and provides straightforward lecture material that gives you all of the necessary information to work on all of the projects and challenges within the course! The content learned from this course will definitely be useful in the industry!

Absolutely love Kris and his courses offered. Very easy going and ready to help at email's notice. This class in particular is no where near the heavy coding classes such as 1040, 2040, or 2830. It's more learning how software engineering works in the workplace via terminology and group projects. Assignments all group work based.

I mean this in no offense but he was basically a stand in puppet. Dale co-teaches this class with Culmer, but your not being taught anything accept to watch YouTube videos and visit links. I did learn some stuff in this class but it was just so boring. The most fun I had was doing the Final Project. This is a req, so just bare with it, you'll pass.

This class was good, but the projects were vague and getting your team members to agree to a time was hard since the class was entirely online. I hope he is working to improve on the things I did not enjoy, but this class did teach me things like Agile and Scrum that I was able to use during my internship over the summer. Reach out to him for help!

This class may be my favorite class in the IT program. Teaches you databases which I found super interesting. I missed out on the opportunity for the class to be in a live lecture format as it is now, but I still was able to take away key concepts and apply them later on at Mizzou. Final project is a little vague, but he will help you understand.

This was my first time learning any programming language. This class was a great intro and made me comfortable. I especially appreciated the discord channel, help from PLA's via zoom to look over projects when needed, and the lectures posted for later watching. Those who waited until 5pm to start projects would get frustrated -were due 11:59.
Decent teacher willing to help students

This class is a group project class where you are assigned to a scrum team to work for the semester. The coding projects we did were in python; The structure of the assignments were vague and It was difficult to get all of my teammates to be useful for the group. I do wish there was more content from the professor instead random YouTuber channels.

Main think is he grades like an iron fist. Especially when it comes to the final project, he will fail you just because you had something similar to another person. If you use something like Chegg, you better know how to change it up so it looks completely different. Had an A+ in the class until I got a 0 on final project. Avoid him if possible.

If you want a professor that gives minimal effort, this is your guy. He posts a couple articles a week and expects that that will be enough "teaching" for his confusing homework. He barely does any instructing himself and in order to get help you have to go through a confusing discord channel where you're greeted with TA's being rude half the time
2040 was pretty easy. If you understand C# and Linq it should be a breeze.
Tough grader. Gives good feedback. Must master the readings to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Thumbs up!
Excellent teacher! Cares about her students and listens to them.

He is one of the best, well-spoken teachers on campus. He explains points thoroughly and he makes interesting points. He makes everyone feel comfortable, even if they have differing opinions about sociological standpoints. You can tell he is well-educated, and is eager to pass along his knowledge to those who want it. SAGrader homework, easy tests.
He's very comfortable in front of a crowd and does a very good job explaining what he needs to and getting people to participate.

Homework is online and you can complete it until you get a 100%. 3 exams, no final. Have one big paper but I emailed him mine, he gave me corrections, and ended up getting an A. Easy A class if you go to class, do click points, and fill out the study guides.

Reading the book may not be necessary but it helps if you need more clarification or just to make sure you get an A. There are clicker points everyday which is the only reason I went although the class is pretty interesting but the powerpoints are online anyway. Assignments you can just take things directly from the book. Def recommend this class

Pretty good teacher. His class wasn't bad, just long to sit through. Clickers count as attendanceparticipation points. Assignments not hard (i got 100% on all of them). LOTS OF EXTRA CREDIT. 3 tests not final. I got a C on every test and still got a A in the class. Take his class.

Dr. Frisby is so passionate about the content she is teaching. These topics in this class were genuinely interesting. I struggled with an assignment and she went out of her way, above and beyond to help me and make sure that I understood. I cannot say enough good things about her!!

I would HIGHLY suggest taking the other professor for PR Capstone. I have learned nothing in this class, and this is my last credit before graduation for my major. I wish that she had more organization and clear grading criteria. It feels as though she does not necessarily care what we do and our client is one that she is doing for her own job.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had. She responded to 1 of my 11 emails the entire semester and that response was only to tell me she was offended by me asking a question. Easy class but take it with anyone else if you want something that resembles normalcy in an academic setting.

Dr. Frisby was a great person and a very entertaining teacher. There were a lot of discussion posts we had to do and comment on, and random essays throughout the semester that were really long and needed you to do real research/data collecting which didn't really go with the class. She left all of the grading up to TAs, who didn't grade fairly.

This is the most disorganized, structurally confusing class I have ever taken. My TA graded papers and discussion posts very hard. The quizzes were confusing even if you read the textbook. Content is interesting and Dr. Frisby really cares about it. She gives out tons of easy extra credit, which is the only reason I kept an A.

Dr. Frisby I an AMAZING professor. She is real and cares about her students. She wants you to learn and loves feedback. She gave so many extra credit opportunities, that if you're failing this class or have under a B it's your own fault. She LOVES what she does and you can tell. If this woman could be my grandma it would make my life.

I'll start off by saying I took her J2000 class years ago, and we still talk about how bad it was. Disorganized doesn't cover it. She claimed to "research" what she taught. She played a scene from a Spike Lee movie and claimed it was a real racist insurance commercial from the South, and that was only the tip of the iceberg.
Professor Frisby is amazing. I don't know about her other class but her J2000 lectures are of absolutely high quality and absolutely inspirational.

As a person she is great, super friendly and loves talking to her students. However, as a professor she can be extremely unorganized. This did NOT work for me. We never knew what our deadlines were or what she was expecting from us. It was beyond frustrating by the end of the year. That said, it was an easy class and you never used the textbooks.

I honestly enjoyed this whole class. I do not think anything should be changed with Dr. Frisby's teaching style. She made me feel very open to share my ideas and was consistently excited to be in class. She was very helpful for writing assignments and I really appreciated how she taught. I would recommend participating in class.

SHE IS THE BEST!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! AMAZING TEACHER. She is there for you when you need her, and she understand how students are. Shes nice, kind, and very intelligent. Probably one of the best teachers I've ever had in my life.

DON'T TAKE HER! Extremely unorganized. Not clear with assignments. Says one thing one day and then something completely different when you get the grade. You won't learn anything from her or this class. Never uses the textbooks.

Frisby is very kind, and she makes her class fairly interesting, but a lot of what she says is rather vague. I received a B+ in her class because she took one point off of one of my essays (she couldn't explain why I had 149/150 points on my three essays combined). Do yourself a favor and participate in class, because it will reflect on your grade.

I don't know why people think Frisby's class is hard. She drills into your head everything you need to know, and if you come to class and read the book, you are an idiot if you don't walk out with an A. She is quite the prima donna, however. She thinks a lot of herself and good luck getting to her office hours.

Dr. Frisby is an awesome professor. Yes, her tests are challenging, but if you read the textbook (multiple times) and make study guides and go see her during office hours, you can definitely do well in her class!!! Definitely don't talk during her lectures because she gets very angry at people who do this. Overall, I learned a lot from this class!

unclear makes a simple topic (principles of strat comm) and turns it on its head. says to read the book all the time instead of teaching. Tests unnecessarily hard. Gets angry if u email her about ANYTHING. I dont understand what some ppl c in this women. I'm ok w/ hard teachers, but this woman is just NOT a good teacher. how has she stayed 4 15 yrs

Frisby has several problems, all relating to the clarity of her teaching. I think that fundamentally, she means well for every student.  However, her class is confusing, unnecessarily difficult and she constantly contradicts herself.  She constantly refers to a book (which she helped write) which is equally confusing.  Overall, not a fun experience

Frisby was really helpful and definitely a professor I will keep in mind for letter recommendations. To get on her good side, show up to class and speak up. If you do that, she seems to be more lenient in grading.

I absolutely LOVED Professor Frisby. She was very fair with her grading (maybe even TOO lenient) and clearly outlined exactly what was expected. She did surprise the class with a 10 page paper assigned only a week before the deadline, but it was completely manageable. I found Dr. Frisby an inspiration and hope to take MANY more classes with her.
Tests what she teaches, and never dull. Challenging. Good teacher.

I had the worst experience with this class. She does not lay out her expectations at all nor does she even give grading criteria. I was extremely disappointed with the about of time she spent on certain subjects while leaving out others even when she tests over everything. If you have to take this course do it in the summer when it is shorter.

Dr. Frisby is unclear, contradicts herself often, and you can guarantee that if she "promises" that if you listen to her you will get something right, you probably wont. Her resume project is a joke and everyone I've talked to says to change your resume after you make it for her. Probably the worst experience and biggest disappointment yet.

This was one of my worst classes. She does not listen to students and constantly contradicts herself in class. I would not recommend this class to anyone who does not want to be told they are wrong. Save your grade and your sanity and enroll with another teacher.

Very difficult to get personal help.  Tough grader!  Has very high expectations.  She's fairly interesting in lecture but getting a decent grade is alot of work.  Class content is valuable but some of her methods are frustrating.  Good luck with exams, the study guides are massive.
Teaching is passable. Often contradicts herself. Class content is sometimes interesting. Doesn't listen to students.

Dr. Frisby is an incredible asset to the J-School.  She has a completely engaging lecture style- it's never boring!  She is very helpful and accommodating if you have questions outside of class.  Her class is a lot of work, but it makes you a better student for it, and you are better prepared for an advertising career afterward.

She seems crazy and fun, then you realize her tests are impossible. She used to give lots of extra projects to boost you grade, but has cut back which makes tests more valuable. Expect more than the study guide to be on the test, and know the study guide forward and backward!
She is an evil, cold hearted, manipulative women.  That is her personality base.  Her teaching is satisfactory.
Worst class ever
She's great!
No Comments

She is an inspiration. You look at her and think BEAUTIFUL and STRONG, and then you learn that she lost, like, 100 pounds. She's funny, and sweet, and I love her. Plus, her class was pretty easy for me.
Great prof, great class.  Don't expect to snooze through this one and do well, but you'll learn a lot if you put forth some effort.  Also--she's got a great personality and is a lot of fun.

Dr. Frisby is a great teacher if you take the time to be a good student.  She likes people who make the extra effort, and will make the extra effort to accommodate you.  Her classes take work, but she is very fair.

Great, engaging professor.  Her classes require work, but so do all of the other classes in the J-school... It should be expected.  If you are concerned about your grade and go talk to her, she is willing to listen and help you out, but she does not make all assignments clear
She is not a very good teacher, and often repeats herself in class. Although she seems friendly in lecture, she is not as friendly in person. I wouldn't recommend her.

The outfits and Elvis stuff is just an act. She pretends to be helpful and open to suggestions, but watch out if you ever question her tests. She frequently contradicts herself in lectures. The act gets very old after a while.
Easily one of the best profs at Mizzou. Truly cares about her students. She loves Elvis and wears leather. What more could you want?
Super easy grader. She also cancelled class a lot which depends if you like that or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: TAKE HER CLASS!!!! She is amazing and you will more than likely get an A as long as you do your work. She is a pretty easy grader and is willing to work with you. Also, it was normal for a lot of class to be cancelled. I highly recommend her.

Class time is not proportional to the time spent actually teaching. Lots of talk not a lot of learning. She chooses books and movies without viewing them beforehand which leads to bad movies and books, but its easy enough to get good grades.

Dr. Reeser is pretty rude and condescending. She is way too proud and is concerned more about her pride than teaching her students. She was pretty unclear in many of her assignments and grading and did not really care to help.  She would tell you what she was looking for but then take off points on the things she corrected.
I did not like the teacher. she does know her stuff but she dosent seem like she cared for her students. difficult teacher and somewhat rude.

Dr. Reeser is not a good instructor.  She is rude, and appears to not care about her students' success at all. She claims to be fair when it comes to paper grades, but it completely depends on your TA. Anyone who may have been interested in this major will definitely change their mind after her class.

The book is the only way to succeed on the tests and papers. Her lectures cover a very small portion of what the tests are over. The grade you receive depends on the TA you get (so hope you get a nice one). Directions are very unclear so don't be surprised if you have to rewrite papers. Prompts are terrible.

While she can be slightly rude and offensive, I felt she was very interested in students learning. The TAs are great and extremely helpful! Go to class and to lab, and this class isn't bad at all. The writing intensive component is annoying because the papers are due on Saturday nights and there are two quizzes almost every week.

The grades you get on your paper are all due to which TA you get, so hope to get a nice one. The test are pretty straight forward, but COME TO CLASS, you get a lot of points for showing up and using your clicker!
She's kind of rude and the content is boring.

The material covered itself is not at all difficult. Most of the grades are paper based. Hardly anyone receives As on these papers so make sure not to slack on tests or attendance points. The class is not out of very many points, so make sure not to miss points on careless mistakes, and you should be fine.

I took this as a writing intensive, and that it was. 3 papers make up a huge majority of your grade in this class, and they are no joke. If you include what you are asked, you should do fine though. She uses clickers to gauge attendance and you can only miss 2 classes to get full credit. If the topic interests you it is a worthwhile class.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had. The class itself was mostly common sense. If you skimmed the book and read the terms you would ace the tests. She has fill-in-the-blank notes to try to make people come to class because it is unbelieveable boring. Be prepared to receive a bad grade on your first paper and the best grade on your last paper.

Dr. Reeser is a wonderful teacher and you will get a lot out of the class. But you must attend. She expects her students to be mature, so some things may be hard. Just pay close attention and read the material. Ask questions if you don't understand. T.A.'s are helpful. Expect to work hard, and come prepared for class and labs. Not a blow off class.
Interesting style...expects a lot of her students.  Be ready to work

The class itself is boring. She goes off topic. Half the time, I don't even think she knew what she was talking about. Lectures have nothing to do what is on the exams, but you need to go because she has in-class assignments. Lets just say it was the longest hour and 15 minutes of my life. Read the text book and you'll ace the exams.
Dana is nice, but she is not organized
She grades very very hard and is a bit on the meaner side.

Probably the most immature teacher at Mizzou. She yells and makes students feel dumb when she disagrees with them. Didn't grade assignments for 10 weeks - no exaggeration. I didn't know if I had an A or a D. Mandatory class MWF but also a mandatory film each Monday from 7-10pm. If you have to take the class, it's fine but I wouldn't if not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers
