reviews.comment: The best prof I've had at Mizzou so far! Professor. Miller truly cares about every student, even in the 300+ person lectures. He has a very engaging teaching style, and I always looked forward to his class. Homework through InQuizitive isn't too bad, and tests are heavily based off the lectures. Overall amazing professor with a super awesome class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dennis Miller was my favorite professor. He really cares about his students and lectures are enjoyable. It's easy to take notes during class if you want to but he usually posts the slides. As long as you show up to class and pay attention it is an easy class.

I'm a sophomore and Dennis Miller is the best professor I've ever had. He's just an amazing guy, and really cares about his students. I'm literally a journalism major and have very little interest in the subject, but this became my favorite class because of him. Wish he could teach all my classes. Super easy, so fun, very nice and funny.

Professor Dennis Miller will be missed at The University of Missouri - Columbia, I really enjoyed his lectures and how laid back he was. Wherever he goes next the students there will definitely enjoy his class

Dennis is for real one of the best teachers I have ever had. You can tell he really cares. Come to class and do the clicker questions and inquizitives and you will get an A. Also, his tests are online and you have near unlimited time. I wish I could take his class again, I am going to miss him :(

Professor Miller is one of my favorites here at Mizzou. His lectures are very well organized and paced, making it easy to absorb information and take notes. Be sure to come to class and participate with the clicker questions, as it's a decent bit of your grade. Exams are open note with no time limit. InQuisitive is a great way to learn the content.

Dennis is my favorite professor ever! If you show up to class for clicker questions and do the inquisitive homework, its an easy A. Tests are open note as well and no time limit. Dennis cares about his students and I thought his lectures were super helpful to better understand a lot of the material! Take any class with him if you have the chance!!!
Super friendly and has a great class set up.

Dennis is such a nice person and I genuinely enjoyed coming to his class. He was always really interested in what he was talking about and it was nice to feel like he cared about his students. He cares about mental health and his class is easy. Would 10000% take another class with him.

Mr. Miller is probably my favorite professor this semester. He always has the greatest lectures and really makes sure you understand the material. There are textbook readings every week, and the exams are open book, meaning it's very easy to get an A. I would take him again if I had the chance. Highly recommended.

Dennis Miller was a great professor for PSYCH1000. He uses quite a few iClickers in class, but his lectures are very entertaining and all tests are online as well as open note. The class follows the textbook pretty closely, but a lot of the reading is gone over in class.

his lectures are really amazing! You get points for participation and answering questions during the lectures so participation matters. He is so caring. His exams are not difficult. you take the exam online and he gives you 4 days to complete which is super amazing! I would definitely recommend his course!

Class is basically participation based, you just have to turn everything in and you'll get an A. There are a lot of things to turn in though, there are soo many Learning Curve assignments! Only thing that was graded for real was weekly quizzes but they're open note. No tests or final exam, only a final paper. Everything open note.

He is so entertaining and well spoken. I went online, but I know he really appreciated the students who went in person. Very genuine, helpful, and good at answering emails. I would take a million classes of his if I could. A lot of the grade is participation, and the final essay was fun! I fully recommend him.

Great professor. So nice and has really interesting lectures. All lectures are recorded so did not need to go to class in person if you did not want to. Very understanding and wants you to succeed. Class was fairly easy, definitely possible for everyone to finish with an A.
Dennis is MY MAN. Class was so easy and lectures were interesting. Gen ed class but top notch guy. and No exams :)

Easiest class ever. Took during COVID, so there weren't any tests. There were daily quizzes, but they were easy even if you didn't watch the lecture. Basically, if you do the homework and 2 other assignments, you'll get an A.

I found spacing out in his lectures and his teaching method of just babbling on and on without any interesting connections put me to sleep. He also showed a Ben Shapiro clip unironically because he mentioned a psychological study?? I eventually just stopped showing up honestly.
Keep track of your grade throughout the semester, go to class, you'll pass. I barely paid attention and still got an A! Perfect for 1st year students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DENNIS WAS THE BEST! he is so interesting to listen to! you can tell he is passionate on this subject. his tests are kinda hard, especially if you dont study. He does clicker questions, but gives easy points.

Most interesting class ever! Prof. Miller makes it really clear what you need to know for the ONE exam!! YES, ONE EXAM! The chapter assignments are easy and the dream journal is actually really fun to do! Take this class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice guy and easy A! Best way to study is the old tests- a lot of questions are the same! Must study and pay attention but it is not hard. Have to show up for class bc he does clicker everyday. Make sure you do all inquizitives (online textbook helps with these) and study participation or it will bring down grade a lot.

Dr. Miller is a GREAT professor. He is enthusiastic, and formats his lectures in a way that appeals to any type of learner. His tests are incredibly easy (he uses questions from prior tests) and are only worth 50 pts each, so there is no reason that you should get below a B. Show up for clicker questions, do the online HW, and you'll be fine.

Dennis is a good prof if you want an easy A, but I didn't like him. He talks to the class like we're little (e.g. uses euphemisms for sex, dumbs everything down). Also he skipped the Sex, Gender, and Sexuality unit entirely. He is clearly kind of religious and I feel like that was reflected in his teaching. Very nice, not my favorite prof
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Come to class to get participation points from clicker questions. You can pretty much do the weekly homework during class and still take notes from the lecture, too. Easy class, some light studying is required before tests but nothing to stress about. Tests are only a portion of the grade. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hands down my favorite professor so far! He is passionate about psychology and his classes were always engaging. He is also very approachable and really cares about your success in his class and you as well. Go into his office hours and he is happy to help you out! Fairly easy gen ed class but is also very interesting. Great job Professor Miller!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Great Professor! He really cares about his students.

Take Psych 1000 with Dennis! He is so kind & really wants every kid in his class to get an A. Weekly homework easy, 3 exams, 1 comprehensive final, lots of iclicker points! Go to class on the days you expect no one to be there, he will give a lot of extra credit through iclicker.
He does lots of clicker questions so make sure you go to class, but he gives the old exams to study from so it makes the class easy to get an A.
Mr. Miller is a beast. He brings so much passion and energy into each and every lecture and is funny. Gen Psych was my favorite class this semester, thanks Prof. Miller!
Great Prof. he's funny and the lectures are posted online. Theres like one homework assignment a week. The test aren't too bad either. :)
He is very animated and sweats a bunch!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOVE LOVE LOVE Dennis. One of the best professors I've ever had the chance to meet. Helped me truly enjoy psychology to the fullest. Just make sure to go to class to get your clicker points. Inquizitives are also necessary.

Dennis is a man who doesn't aim to be the funny guy, but he is hilarious. A chunk of points comes from clicker questions, so make sure to attend lecture if you want those points! Every week there is an online assignment that you may need to read a chapter for. For this class, you must participate in research studies or alternatively write papers.

He's super friendly and funny! I sat in the front row and we would make conversation everyday. 2 years later when I see him around campus he recognizes me! Make sure you do the research participation (SO easy) and do the inquizitives (even easier). They're easy points!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Super chill. If you do the homework and study participation youll be fine.
This is the best professor you guys will ever get, please take this class!

I love Dennis Miller. Classes went by fast because of good lectures and fun videos. He posted all the previous exams on canvas - which if you study those, you'll do great on the test. Wish more prof's were like him.

Miller loves clicker questions. A lot. As long as you go to class and complete the online homework on time, you should be fine. The best way to study for his tests is to review his old tests. His has them all on Canvas and he uses a lot of the same questions on his tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I found Professor Miller to be a good teacher and I enjoyed the class. However I found his class to be the most difficult of the psych 1000 classes as the other sections had easier exams and less homework
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Love Dr. Miller! As long as you read the material, tests are a breeze. You have to come to class to get points for participation, but if you have to miss, he's very understanding and willing to schedule office hours if you can't make it to his regular times. Great class too, the material is interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller cracks lots of jokes and is knowledgeable and passionate about the field. A *decent* amount of work (readings, online homework) but simple, straightforward teaching style and content. Fair tests, all multiple choice. Offers Tegrity lectures but also requires Clicker points. Easy A with little effort!

Class requires more effort than some other 1000 level classes, but grading criteria is clear and the work is very manageable. Class participation, research participation, homework, and exams make up the grade. Very caring and relatable teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: BEST PROFESSOR AT MIZZOU!!! This class is very easy as long as you do the homework and come to class to get the clicker question points. Tests are straight forward. He is very passionate about his job and truly cares about his students' success. You will not find a better professor here than Dennis.
We love Dennis.

First, he's an amazing teacher and makes lectures enjoyable. You can tell that he genuinely loves his job and cares about your success in the course. There are clicker questions in class that are part of your grade (go to class!). There's 1 or 2 online assignments due every week. You'll do good on the test as long as you pay attention in lecture.
Best professor at Mizzou. Loved him.

Miller is a seemingly nice guy, nothing really stands out that much. He glosses over some stuff pretty often and if you're prone to spacing out, you'll come back into it with an incorrect clicker answer (he relies on those A LOT) and being pretty confused about the topic. I wish it was more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Blandest of the bland psych1000 classes, beware falling asleep at 9am.

He does clicker questions where there's a right answer and you lose points if you get it wrong, so you have to pay attention to the lectures, which are easy to listen to and take notes on. The best part is the old exams he posts which is all I studied because he uses the same questions and the answers are highlighted. Super easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sleep and Sleep Disorders is a hidden gem at Mizzou. It's easy, interesting and actually makes an impact on your life. You'll end up taking this class for the A, then after reading the first couple of chapters in the textbook, you'll end up taking this class for the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: great teacher and gen ed class. tests are combinations of old tests which makes it really easy to see what the tests are like and what to expect. He uses clickers and in the end they can have a big impact on your grade so i would recommend going. He also has Sona credits (research participation) which can get you 7 extra credit pts in the end
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Four multiple choice tests straight from lectures and text book. Online inquizitive homework due weekly. Good lecture personality - easy to follow. Sometimes can get repetitive. Uses clickers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor very passionate about the subject and getting students involved. You must participate in research studies outside of the class, don't put it off and you can get into some cool experiments. Tests are very similar to prior exams so be sure to review those. I never used the book for the homework b/c you can guess until you get it right

Easiest A. As long as you take the weekly quizzes and show up to class for clicker points, there's no reason why you shouldn't have an A. He posts old exams online which are pretty much identical to the ones he gives you in class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Go to class! There are clicker questions worth points. It's easy points for just listening. Complete the SONA research ASAP, so you wont stress about it later. He's a very nice and understanding teacher, and I feel he cares about our grades. Make sure to study for his tests, psych may be easy, but some things are tricky.

This class is a great intro to psych course! He is really enthusiastic about psychology and brings in real world examples, instead of just reading from the powerpoint slides. He does use tegrity, but I wouldn't recommend missing that many classes because he does use the clicker. pay attention and complete the study guides he makes, & u will do good
Loved him!

Great professor!! Loved his class. He always made it fun and I looked forward to coming to class. Has clicker questions so participation isn't mandatory, but it is if you want points. I hope to take one of his classes again!

Hilarious teacher who really cares for what he does. 4-part grading, and every part except for the exams are easily obtainable and don't require too much studying. He's a great first professor for anyone nervous about the switch from high school to college.

Your grade comes from 4 categories - exams, in-class clicker points, research participation credit outside of class, and Inquizitive. Dr. Miller gives plenty of help with finding research opportunities and makes lectures easy to understand. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you miss class, you'll miss the clicker question points for that day.
Explained things clearly, although sometimes beats a point to death. But if you attend class and pay attention, you'll understand the material and pass easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved his class! I strongly recommend him as a professor especially if you haven't taken a psych class before. He makes everything clear to understand and he has detailed study guides . Just make sure to go to class he has a lot of participation points and do the homework and you will be fine. Good Luck!
Sweetest teacher, LOVE HIM!!!

He's an amazing guy! open to questions anytime, and always helps with grading issues if there was any problems. Material was heavy but he tried to make it easier as much as he can. Funny, helpful and accessible.  Totally loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's really important to go to lectures. If you go to class and do the homework, you'll be okay. Look at the old exams he gives out because some questions come from those. It isn't difficult to get an A.
Awesome professor. Easy A if you come to class and study for tests. All homework is online and should be easy 100%.

Miller was such a great professor that he inspired me to minor in psych. His lectures were informative with a dash of humor here and there. Do your homework, don't procrastinate on research credits, and study a little sparingly throughout the semester and you're almost guaranteed an A. You'll actually learn a lot of good stuff, too.
You cannot skip class or the research labs. Lectures were unorganized, but if you do everything you are supposed to and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very easy class. Show up, get your participation points, do research studies, and you'll have an A. His lectures are very well-structured and informative, although he sometimes does an extra lecture at the end (how alcohol affects the brain, Parkinson's, etc.) that is never on the test and wastes thirty minutes.
My favorite professor. Actually made me want to go to class.

Professor Miller was really funny and obviously cared about how his students felt. He was great about calling on students and asking for personal questions. In a class of 400 students, I felt like if I needed to ask something I could. It's important to go to class though, a third of the points come from clicker questions answered in class.
He is an amazing instructor. He is very caring and his test is not a big deal if you study exactly what he told you to. I thank him very much !

Dr. Miller is an exceptional professor. If you come to class and pay attention you will do just fine. He puts clicker questions throughout his lectures which not only helps you get easy points, but ensures that you grasp the concepts he is teaching in lecture. Take this class! You won't regret it!
One of the best professors I've had thus far. He is really amazing at explaining the criteria and actually shows his passion for it.
Super easy class. All online except for two proctored exams. Take the quizzes and read the book and it is an easy A.
Really great guy, cares about you and the subject matter. Big points from Inquizitive hw (super easy points) and participation via clicker.

Dr. Miller is a great professor.  He seems very passionate about the material that he teaches, and is extremely clear.  The tests are straight forward, but can be tough if you do not spend enough time with the material.  The only downside is his heavy reliance on online homework, which is tedious.  However, Dr. Miller is always there for questions.

Miller teaches at a very nice pace and is willing to answer any questions. The HW is online and lets you keep going until you get 100%. Tests are all multiple choice and have study guides, so if you study you will do just fine. He uses clickers so you have to go to class. Overall, a pretty easy class with interesting material and a helpful prof.
Great class and great professor. I had to take his psych 1000 class for a pre rec and it was an easy A. If you go to class, listen, and do what you're told then you will with out a doubt get an A.

interesting class and he makes lectures interesting. you have to be in class to get clicker points. he grades on a point system so really every single point matters even clicker points. chapters are long but worth reading. paying attention in class pays off

Study the study guide that he gives you. Read your book. Go to class to get the clicker points. Do the research studies (Go to them or you wont get extra credit in the end of the semester) Go in during his office hours, he will highlight what is on the test.

The test are easy, just do the review sheet and look at the practices test. He repeats questions from the practice test sometimes. Do the homework and go to class for your clicker points. His lectures are pretty interesting. He is really helpful if you come see him.

Majority of the homework will come from SmartWork. Come to class, the clicker questions are basically your attendance and are worth points. You have the choice of either participating in research or writing essays on topics that he gives you. The tests aren't that bad as long as you study. The final is cumulative.

Honestly, he would be fine if he didn't not excuse absences, especially when you travel for the University. I did, several times, and missed out on his stupid in class points and he said he has no excuses for missing. If you're even remotely involved with the University in any way in terms of extra curricular, don't take this psychology class.

This teacher is great! He's friendly and NOT annoying. He teaches at an understandable level as long as you listen at least 80%. Some people didn't like this class because of clicker questions, but if you come that isn't an issue. Put in the work and you will pass. It's that simple and that easy. He's always open to help and interactive in class.

Dr. Miller is awesome! The majority of the points come from SmartWork where you can use open book. Tests are kinda hard, but he gives you a clear study guide and gives you access to previous exams. He is dorky but he's a really sweet guy. Only thing is that he uses clicker points, so you can't skip class a lot.
The study guides are the test. You don't have to read the book. Do the research experiments as soon as possible to get them out of the way.  I am now a psych major because of this class.

He has the material there for you to pass you just have to make sure you do it. He does use clickers to make sure you're in class and every week you have at least one assignment due online. If you study tests will be pretty easy.

Loved this class. Prof. Miller was very clear in his intentions for the course and I was never confused on grading criteria or material. He had plenty of office hours and really wanted his students to succeed. If you show up to class and do the homework, you will do well.

Dr. Miller was incredibly helpful and nice.  He knows the material well and makes jokes in class.  You also get to watch videos during lectures.  He does use iClickers and if you don't show up to get the points you'll have a harder time passing.

Professor Miller is an amazing teacher, his lectures are very interesting. He uses a clicker, so I recommend you go everyday. I did, and I did not regret it. He uses a points system, homework is worth about 13 of grade which is an easy A+. His tests are difficult, but if you the study guide you should be fine. He's helpful and offers extra credit.

I really liked this guy. First semester at Mizzou and he is my favorite professor. He jokes, knows the material, and is really down to earth. Online easy homework, and possibly the greatest thing is that he gives study guides for tests! I recommend him for psych 1000
Great guy, great teacher. Tests really aren't bad if you pay attention in class and study a little bit.
Really nice and dorky guy(: Loved having him as a teacher!!! Tests are hard but there are enough other easy points to make up for it... He actually made psychology interesting!!

Love Professor Miller! He is such a nice guy and is very helpful. His exams follow exactly what is given on the study guide, so are pretty easy! Each exam is only worth 7.6% of your grade and the rest comes from homework points. Very easy to get an A in this class. Dennis really cares about each student and wants us all to succeed. Great professor!

He is a really nice guy, but most of the things on the test are mentioned in passing between subjects.  Avoid if possible.  Exams are ridiculous.  Studied til 6am and got a C.  Half of the stuff, I felt like I had never heard.
Good lecturer. Cares if students learn. The tests are tough but the homework is easy.

Dr. Miller is a very good teacher. His exams are hard but he had enough other stuff that you can still get a good grade without doing extremely well on the exams. We did in class question that were 80 points of your grade so attendance isn't mandatory but will definitely help your grade.

Great professor.  His tests are really hard but they are usually curved by about 5 points.  Homework is a huge portion of the grade so definitely do it.  Read the book, study the lectures, and you should have no problem getting an A.

Great Professor. Really knows what he's talking about and likes what he's teaching. I loved the class but the tests were HARD. He puts the old exams on blackboard and I would recommend definitely studying those!! Pretty easy to do well

Literally the worst teacher I've ever had. He's a nice guy but does not teach anything that appears on the tests. I was up until 3 in the morning studying for a test and got a 50% on it because he test you on the most unimportant details that you would never even think are important. I love psychology but not with him. Take with someone else!

Go to class!! The iClicker points can really help boost your grade and they are easy points (as long as you read the chapter before class). The tests are not that hard because everything comes from lecture notes and homework. The lecture itself is boring but essential to go to.
Dr. Miller is an amazing teacher. His lectures are very interesting. An A or B is very doable as long as you do all of the homework and attend class. Great guy, very passionate about what he teaches.
He's super awkward and weird but a super nice guy. Tests are very difficult but not impossible-he makes up for them in easy homework. Getting an A or B is entirely doable.
Great class, very interesting, go to class.
Dr. Miller's lectures are very clear and helpful and he does a very good job of helping you understand everything. It is important you read the textbook, because you will get behind if you don't.

Great prof and he really knows his stuff but I felt he was unreasonable with the homework.  There would be online HW due before the next class begins. He makes it clear that he gives no extensions on HW. On exam days, it made it difficult to both study for the exam AND finish HW. I don't think it's right to have HW due on the same day as an exam.

I had Dr. Miller for Drugs and Behavior, and it was by far the best class I have taken so far. He clearly states expectations, and yes, you have to read the textbook and do the homework to do well. The textbook is really interesting though, and Dr. Miller explains all concepts with clarity. I would highly recommend this class for anyone!!!

Awesome professor! Miller made class so interesting and did an exceptional job of involving students while in lecture. Good balance of textbook use, powerpoint slides, videos, and discussion. I would take this class again in a heartbeat!

He was the best lecturer I had this semester. His lectures were easy to follow. The majority of the grade is homework on the computer. As long as you do it until it is all right, you will get a 100% for the homework. His tests are hard and he will tell you that himself. You will need to study for them.
Do all smartwork, go to research participaton, and do semi-okay on the tests (C or better) and you will definitely pass the class and get an A- even! He's great too and can even be slightly funny.

He is a really good teacher and really nice! I just didn't like how he would push us to read the textbook (which didn't make any sense and was so complicated) and then would base our tests off of lecture and homework. Overall, if you have interest in the subject he's teaching, you'll do well!

This class is interesting despite Miller's tendency to be repetitive and ramble in his lectures.  He definitely cares about student learning, and what's more the class is very easy. All lectures are recorded on Tegrity, and a huge percentage of the grade comes from online homework and study participation. He utilizes videos and clips into lectures.
Covers a tremendous amount of material and exams are very hard,.  But homework and research is a big part of the final grade.
Really nice guy and very helpful

Interesting Class, you don't need to show up to class because all his lectures are on tegrity. Tests are extremely difficult but he gives you a ton of homework and research points to make up for it. Overall, not difficult to get an A

This class was impossible. All lectures are on Tegrity but that's the only plus. You have to put a ridiculous amount of work into the class. For example, the final covered the entire book... all 16 chapters

good professor, but the exams were too difficult for the class.  After all, the class is a 1000 level.  The teacher is credible, but the tests are just too difficult for the people taking the class.   Mostly non-psych majors
I rarely attended class, all the lectures are online. Just read the book and use the study links provided and you should have a good grade.
He is an awful professor. He tests you on things that you would never think to be important. He power points are not informative at all. Basically, he sucked.

knows EVERYTHING about psych. amazing teacher. classes are very interesting. his tests are very hard, but all the test put together are only like 30% of grade. if that. all points are in easy homework and participating in psych experiments.

I thought Miller would be easy at first so I took the class since it applied to nursing. He recorded his lectures this year on Tegrity. Both his lectures and textbook are on the exams. It's hard and a lot of info is covered. Online homework is easy. He even has a cumulative final. The exams require some hard core studying in order to do well.
He is great! His tests cover a lot of material and can be tough, but he is always willing to set up additional office hours.

Great professor, very interesting lecture, very high knowledge about drugs and the brain.  Book is only necessary for online quizzes, virtually everything on exams is pulled from his lectures.  Highly recommend him.

This class was very interesting I felt like I learned so much. I am going for pre-med so all that I learned really feels like i will apply it in the future. Going to class is vital so that u get the notes that is what majority of exam questions are over, You still need book to do the online homework assignments which are worth quite bit of points.
I took his Learning and Memory class. He seems like nice guy, but sucks as a professor. The classes are boring.

Mr. Miller is awesome! He definitely knows what he's talking about (he used to work for a drug company!) and the things you learn are so interesting! I would definitely reccommend taking his class! I looked forward to it every other day!

This class is set up really well. You have weekly homework that is online, easy, and worth a TON of points, 2 online tests (also easy), and 2 in class exams. The grade cutoffs are reasonable and he is a very helpful and available teacher. You should definitely go to lecture because you need to take notes on the slides. The stuff you learn is cool!
Mr. Miller obviously knows what he's talking about. If you don't understand what is said in lecture, he is always willing to help you during office hours. Great guy and teacher!
Dennis was awesome!  He made the material very interesting.

He's a great prof. He takes the time to make things  clear, and the course has a good format (no cumulative final, good lectures, online quizzes, online lecture notes, tells you what will be on the tests).
Dr. Miller does a great teacher.  He does not make the class too hard to do well in it.  The tests are very straightforward, mainly from class notes.  The subject matter is also quite interesting.
this class was interesting and Prof. miller did a good job on the subject.

miller's awesome. definitely one of my favorites. he gets flustered sometimes in lecture, but delivers great lectures and gives fair tests. great presentation of material and very interesting subjects. dennis is great!
Dr. Eggener is currently at University of Oregon. He is an excellent professor. I hope that his current department apprecaites him and his research interests.

Good professor overall, lectures can be hard to take notes in since there aren't many concepts and its more stories of the history but if you pay attention there's no need to memorize terms. About as fun as art history can be to a nonmajor.

Ridiculous perspective on art, Suggests everything artists do is based on greed for power. Suggested that Michelangelo designed one of his greatest works that went against the contemporary style to show that he could get away with it. Seems like hes reading the same unscholarly textbooks he gives students.

Prof  Eggener has the ability to make long lectures fun and engaging. He's brilliant and has a likable, approachable personality. I found out that he's won awards for his teaching, and it shows in class. There's a lot of memorization involved in the midterm and final but he's a forgiving grader and just wants to see that you've processed the info.

Eggener knows what he is talking about! I learned so much in this class and loved the material. If you aren't interested in art, it probably isn't for you because you have to memorize up to 50 paintings for the midterm and final. I loooved it though! Take it!
really nice - also my advisor... really helpful, answers questions as clearly and concisely as possible, actually apologized for the course i took not being as good as he had hoped!
Very gifted professor and delightful to interact with.  A major asset to the art history department.  Very cute personality and incredibly sharp.
Brilliant, funny, critical, challenging, articulate, sexy. A terrific combination to encourage learning!
Best professor I've had so far!!

She's the best professor I've ever had! Super nice, extremely helpful and very approachable. The class challenged me (a lot) but in a good way. The lab let me apply my genetics and ecology knowledge really well. I loved it! Be sure you know your genetics before taking this course. But seriously, this was the best class I ever had! PS: Didn't use the book, but it was a good reference.
A wonderful instructor, one of the best I've ever had.  Clear, concise lectures, great labs.
Dr. Eggert is an exceptional teacher, I recommend her to anyone even remotely affiliated with the Biology department.

I rarely attended lecture, there was no attendance kept. The material is fairly basic if you've ever had ecology before. read the book, you'll do fine. Labs are different. never, ever, ever miss a lab. be prepared to write some long, boring papers.
Pretty easy once u understand how the tests are set up, def study using the outline to save time. show up to every lab so u can fall back on that a little if you need to

Tests are every other week (7 tests in total plus final) which felt like a lot but they are all multiple choice and 15-20 questions. Main lectures were videos online and not super long, with 2 homework assignments per week. Lab is every other week! Attendance to the main big lectures is mandatory and you will have to sign that you attended.

This class uses a flipped classroom where most of your learning is done outside of class time. You attend no more than two of the lectures a week and have lab every other week as well as a test. Liscum himself was nice and personable. He seemed to care about his students and his work. I just wish that there was more feedback given on work.

Liscum himself is a good professor. The structure of his class was rather odd and it feels like you were learning about three aspects of biology at once. He has many online tests, but they are rather short and structured the same way as the homework. The lab procedure was simple enough but the layout of the lab itself was like a maze

Odd class set up. Test's aren't too bad just look over online learning assignments. Test were all online and multiple choice. Usually only 1 lecture day per week. Hw graded on completion. Labs every-other week with some online labs. Don't talk about normal intro biology class things.

Lipton doesn't deserve these negative reviews. I was terrified to take her course because of them, but proved dead wrong by the first day of class. She's nice, professional, and self-aware of her teaching style. She's totally flexible, understanding, and DOES give clear grading criteria. Do your work and don't be fooled by those on here who didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Do not take this woman's courses. She provides complicated and very unclear explanations for her many papers. Very much to read and it's not interesting. She has an unreal standard of expectations. What you submit to her will never be good enough. Do not stress yourself out for a semester.

Professor Lipton is certainly a difficult grader, but she does a good job of making the subject matter interesting. My writing improved immensely throughout the course, and she has high standards because she wants her students to succeed. The subject matter might not interest everyone, but her courses are worth taking, and she's really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Lipton is kind and knowledgable. However, be prepared for little to no explanation on her grading policies, grading inconsistencies, intense reading material, and massive exams. Number of papers is large but not unusual. I will do well but this class was still a nightmare because of the lack of clarity. Reading material is dull.

This teacher is an extremely hard grader possibly because she doesn't think anyone is as good as her in her profession. She doesn't explain assignments thoroughly and in turn gives you a low grade because she was looking for something different. You can email her a thousand times and she still will not help enough to get a great grade.
This is one of the smartest women at Mizzou, and she is interested in helping you learn.  It's not an easy A, but it's easy to be inspired by such a thoughtful, insightful, beautiful woman!!

She is a difficult grader, and when you think you've done exceedingly well, it turns out that you've gotten a low score. She will review your paper with you, and still give you a C even when you've fixed everything and the some. Don't take the class, even if you are great at English because you will NOT get an A...or probably even a B.

Emma Lipton is ridiculous. She expects your whole world to be one class. I am usually an A student and was shocked to receive a D on one of my papers simply because she did not like my topic. I talked to a few other students; apparently she pulls D's out of her...yeah. No point system, harsh grading, no positive feedback what so ever. Beware.

Emma is absolutely unavailable for you to talk to. She is a very harsh grader and the class was very very boring. Her lectures are uninteresting and her tests are always memorization of the lines from poetry or the assigned readings.
Well, she's average at best. Mostly uninspiring, which is the norm with Mizzou's literature professors.
My favorite professor at Mizzou. He is so passionate on the subject and made the class so enjoyable. Generally a pleasant guy and made the already interesting content even more engaging.

Everybody loves Jim. Taught the material so well and was always willing to review content not presented well in the lecture section. This guy genuinely wants you to succeed and will work with you to see that happen. As long as you put in the effort, Jim will make it worth your while.

Jim is an absolute delight. His lectures are very captivating, and I love his personality. He was just as intrigued by the content as I was, and I love it when my professors are fascinated by the content that they teach. As long as you show up to class for your attendance grade, and do the study guides for the exams, it's an easy A.
Grading is unclear, barely responds to emails, and the class feels unstructured. Most assignments had no rubric, an unclear assignment explanation, and no submission comment explanation.

Dr. Elman's passion for health humanities is evident, but the class lacks clear instructions and structure. Assignments often had vague guidelines, and criteria changed unexpectedly, making it hard to keep up. I valued the class topics, despite Dr. Elman's political views.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is a joke and a waste of your time. Syllabus wasn't followed, assignments not graded until the end of the semester, the assignments themselves were busy work and not college level assignments. She also does not follow the rubric she gives your grading. If I could make one wish it would be to go back in time and unenroll from this class.

Dr. Elman care about the success of her students. She is real + direct. She encourages critical thinking about deeper topics. I learned more in her class with 0 exams than my 1st bio class that had an exam every 2 weeks. All healthcare degrees should require health humanities. Assignments were easy if you payed attention to lecture.
My lowest grade last semester simply because she didn't put a single thing in until the day everything was due, I had a zero in there until dec 15
does NOT follow syllabus and grades everhthjng the last day of the semester
Same this everyone else has said about the grading and not organized

The course itself is not difficult, but prof does not follow the syllabus, doesnt enter grades until they are submitted at the end of the semester, grades things LATE, wont reply to emails and occasionally would change classroom locations with no notice, due dates are not clear whatsoever, and she just didnt seem to know what she was doing… ever.
Was not clear on grades and did not follow the syllabus.
She didn't know what she was doing and we never did either
Easy but I didn't like her texting and grading strategies
Unclear on grades in health humanities
This is not the class I had her for but she's not good at running a class and communication
She's very sweet and class is east but unorganized. I wouldn't take if you aren't a liberal or if you're a type a person because assignments and grades are not well organized

Had her for health humanities and she's sweet and class is easy but if u care about gpa or are type A person, don't take because u won't know ur grade or know exactly what u need for A. There's no tests either which is nice

She does grading by contract and she is very unclear about it. You have no clue what your grade is until the day grades are due. I read the syllabus lots and even had a convo with her about it and she assured me that if I met those things I would have an A and then I didn't end with an A. She can basically just choose whatever she thinks u deserve
Dr. Elman is very understanding of any personal matters going on in your life. She also notices your participation in her class, and she will thank you for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Flexible, understanding, always willing to compromise with students. Friendly. Funny. Great at explaining and digging deep into difficult topics with students. Attendance is expected, but she'll understand if you have valid reasons to miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Elman is very smart and clearly cares about her students. She grades papers extremely strictly and doesn't seem to give out grades over 94%, even if she has no negative feedback about the paper or suggestions for improvement. If you're used to understanding why you lose points on your work, she's not for you. Also, reading is very demanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: An incredible, intelligent, accommodating, and approachable professor who always takes time to help students. Probably one of the hardest 1000-level courses offered, but it's immensely rewarding and worth the hard work you'll put into it. I would absolutely recommend taking at least one class with Dr. Elman before graduating.

the grading is impossible without going to office hours. no tests, there is just tons of reading of outdated articles and lots of writing. You have to write for your TA so know what they specifically want to hear.  if youre taking this class for fun, dont.

Incredibly intelligent and simply amazing. One of the best professors I've ever had by far. Go into her office hours to let her know that you care and the class is much easier. Make sure to do the readings so you can participate in class, because if you don't it can be easy to get lost. I'd recommend her to anyone.

Incredibly well-rounded and intelligent. Challenges students and values lecture participation discussion. She doesn't use electronic grading system, so asking a teaching assistant is necessary to know your grade. She assigns weekly readings, but they're incredible and relevant. Don't leave lecture before class is up, it makes her uncomfortable.

Professor Elman is extremely intelligent, and it shows when she's lecturing. The writing assignments are short, but make sure they're well thought-out and show you read and analyzed the texts. Then, participate in class. Her knowledge is your reward!

She is a very caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. She puts real effort into her lectures, but her teaching style doesn't always make the material easy to understand. The workload is light with only 3–4 easy homework assignments, and the midterm and final are manageable since they are similar past exams.

Worst lectures of all time. Luckily, practice exams match exams nearly perfectly so it's easy to get a good grade in the class. The two or three homework assignments she gives are easy and a decent grade booster. Labs are easy. Not good at teaching whatsoever but clearly cares a lot and class was easy to do well in, so I can't give lower than a 3.

Dr. Sazia Eliza is a very knowledgeable and caring professor, but her teaching method isn't effective enough to convey the material. You will have to do more reading and figuring stuff out on your own in order to get a good grade. Grades on very few topics discussed in class.

I admit that she is very smart and a nice lady, but she has absolutely no idea how to teach a class. Lectures are very concept heavy with little chance to apply what you learn with examples, so nothing really sticks. Class organization does not reflect a college level class. She is consistently late and unprepared, and cancels classes very often.

She's a sweet lady but is extremely disorganized.  She cancels a class almost every week (we meet MWF) or sometimes turns it into a Zoom lecture. She would talk about concepts the whole lecture but not give us an opportunity to apply them, so by the time we got homework we had no idea what to do. Everyone in my class was confused and frustrated
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's nice and appreciates feedback. Class was only 50 minutes long, so exams are going to be 3 questions basically every time. At this level of engineering, most circuit problems take 25 - 45 minutes each, so yeah... if u mess up once during an exam you will be hit hard.  She also is quite a tough grader which makes it even worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She was constantly late to class, usually around 7 minutes or so. Her lectures felt very unorganized, and if you asked a question that she did not have written on her lecture notes she would have no idea how to answer it. She changed our final exam question several times during.
TLDR: Class organization and professor preparedness sucks. Good luck.

Easily the worst professor that I have ever had. Nothing is ever graded so it is impossible to know where you stand in the class. Exams are unnecessary difficult and unorganized, usually consisting of 1 or 2 questions. One time, she even changed the one and only exam question 30 minutes into an exam 4 separate times. Usually, about 10 minutes late.

Eliza gives little partial credit on her exams, you have to protest in order to receive any. In class she doesn't do very many example problems, she talks about concepts. Her exams reflect this, she has one question that asks you to explain a concept. She tends to do the same lecture for a week straight. She is 5-10 minutes late to most classes.

If I could rate her with a 0/5, I would. She managed to turn an electrical engineering course into a history class, and just stands right in front of what she writes on the board so no one can see it. Also, she always uses her inside voice so better sit at the front.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't let some of these reviews scare you. The class is not hard at all. You simply just need to go and participate in i-clicker questions (which she gives you the answers to in class). Cant be on phone, but its really not that hard because each lecture is a different presenter. Theres two test are from lectures. Offers plenty of extra credit.

Somehow manages to be unpleasant and passive-aggressive, without even teaching material (based on guest lectures). Condescending material and tone with students. essay is on CliftonStrengths personality test and meeting with advisor/interpreter, utter waste of money and time- yet rubrics/guidelines are strict. Highly encourage other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Makes disabled people feel more like a burden than most of us already do. Makes it seem like she wants you to succeed as a group but when you ask questions personally she seems to get upset and acts like you weren't paying attention in class my biggest recommendation is to transfer to another school to take this class and then transfer back.

Has been one of my least favorite professors in college so far. Doesn't treat students the best and expects students to know extreme specifics from lectures for pop quizzes throughout the semester. Was very difficult for an intro level class and would recommend trying to take it with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took the easiest class at the university and did the absolute most for no reason…for a class she doesn't even talk in.
Probably the most boring and waste of time class that I have ever had to take. I literally feel like I am a 3rd grader by the way she talks to students in this class
literally hate her she's terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't get on your phone at all or you will get a zero for the day. You have to pay attention in class for minute papers/pop quizzes. She is lowkey rude to all of her students and doesn't treat them with respect at all. This class isn't hard but I wouldn't take it with her

This class is a primarily a mind-numbing waste of time. The professor talks to everyone like we're grade schoolers, and chooses boring people to come in and talk about whatever (some were good). Write down everything in paper for the pop quizzes. (which you get notes on, and can't leave early for). Not good, but could be worse. (ENGI_1000).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: if you don't write every word on the slide you will have a bad grade. you have to go no matter what. huge waste of your time but you never have to study. you have to read a book and know small insignificant details. memorize stats on the slides for exams she will you specifics. if you go on your phone she will track you down and give you 0. beware.

I hated the lack of compassion that was shown for students in this class. Attendance is I think 30% of your grade and there are no exceptions for things like Illness or family emergencies, the doors also lock 10 minutes after class starts and you will not be let it, so take that into account. The class isn't bad but take it with Tracy Scardina.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: bad, doesn't teach, will give you a 0 for being on phone

This class is a huge waste of my time. Even if you take good notes, the pop quizzes ask you word for word what the slide said, which isn't how students should take notes. The minute papers aren't hard but also a waste of time. Instead of assigning homework to show our knowledge, we do surprise assignments where she gives you 8 minutes to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awful teacher, doesn't do anything but have people come in and do slides and quiz over it. Doesn't allow technology and is super strict. Worst part is she forces participation, you have to go to every class or you may miss a quiz or minute paper.

You have to go to class because you never know when you will get selected for a minute paper or a pop quiz. You can drop two minute papers and two quizzes. The material isn't difficult, just participation heavy. No technology allowed in the class; all notes are paper/pencil. She will dock your grade if she sees you on your phone.

Only grades in the class are surprise minute papers over that day's lecture, pop quizzes, 1 essay, 2 exams, and class participation. Minute papers/pop quizzes aren't hard if you take good notes during presentations. Technology is banned, the professor will call you out/ kick you out of class if she sees your phone. Not bad, just follow her rules.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mahler does not teach this class; it is taught by guest speakers in different fields in healthcare. This class is a breeze as long as you show up to class. Mahler seemed to have an attitude with us everyday though, so that is why the rating is low. Pretty strict rules regarding the class and NO ELECTRONICS ALLOWED! Sign up with caution.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's really not bad at all. I never had a problem with her once. Most people don't like her because she won't let you in class after 10 mins have passed or if you're on electronics but that's because this class is strictly presenters leaving their job to willingly come and speak to students. The pop quizzes are open note too!

This class is amazing in helping guide you to a healthcare career, but definitely taught by guest presenters, not Professor Mahler. There are many quizzes and minute papers at the end of class so be prepared to stay late some days. Attendance is very mandatory and she will push for the class to ask questions after each presenter

Was not respectful of time and would always run over and then assign work, therefore I wouldnt make it to my next class on time. Many times I had to just take the F because I couldnt show up to my next class late. She is rude about random things but overall you dont interact with her very much because its all guest presenters.

She doesnt teach the class, its all guest speakers. I personally did not like her and she was always rude about one thing or another. But, liking her wasnt crucial for this class because you didnt interact very much. Just overall not helpful and would get mad about random things, and just took everything way too seriously.

Emily Mahler doesn't teach this class, it's mostly guest speakers. But thank god because she is on some sort of weird power trip. Overall just unpleasant and does very unnecessary things. Like, this class is not that serious.. Chill.

Emily Mahler takes this class so much more seriously than it needs to be. She is not even the one teaching the class yet she has all these ridiculous rules in place in a COLLEGE class. Not worth the time, would not recommend her as a professor.

Her class information is easy but such a rude person overall and will make your life so much harder than it needs to be. Will kick you out of class if you show up like 5 min late and is just on some type of power trip. Would not recommend taking her class!!

Professor Mahler isn't really a big part of this class. It's all guest lecturers. If you take notes/pay attention the quizzes are easy. Attendance is HUGE. You never know when you will have an assignment so you have to show up every day or risk losing points. Other than that it's not a hard A. Exams are easy.

One on one, she's amazing. I've had great conversations with her. However, the strictness of her overall class is so frustrating especially with it being an intro class. She won't let you use your phones and lectures go over time so after a minute-paper I'd be running across campus to my next class. She also DEMANDS the class to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is run by her, but taught by guest presenters that are mostly entertaining. GO TO CLASS! Attendance is necessary to pass. There is pop quizzes over lectures, but you can print out the slides before and use them - easy 100%. Minute papers are randomly assigned but easy if you pay attention. One essay, and two exams, but overall very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Mrs. Mahler is very nice overall, but when it comes to class, you have to stay off technology. She has surprise minute papers and pop quizzes. You have to take a Clifton strengths test and then write an essay about it. Make sure you follow the rubric. MAKE SURE YOU DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Everyone says Emily is a hard professor but she doesn't even teach this class; it's all just guest presenters. Class is super easy if you attend class because there are "minute papers" and pop quizzes. Overall, an informative class. There are also multiple extra credit opportunities.

She was a good professor, but I think she took it too seriously. I know that the other professor did not require in class attendance. I do think I should have been allowed to miss more than 3 classes. Overall, this class was interesting, but she is a little strict.

reviews.comment:
This is a 1000 level class but she makes things way more difficult than it needs to be.

I truly think she's a narcissist, she definitely cares more about their job title than her students

reviews.comment: I read the other reviews, but in 2023 you get two quizzes and two min papers dropped, so you can skip class somtimes and not lose points if you miss one. reviews.comment: Rude, stupid, g@y.

The classroom structure is set up for health professionals to be on-time and respectful during guest lectures. reviews.comment: Emily Mahler is rude. This class is treated like a court room. If you are late, you get kicked out of class. Speak to a classmate, kicked out of class. reviews.comment: Professor Mahler just isn't very nice or helpful.

When I took this course, it was during a covid heavy time and there was no remorse for anyone who was sick and missed class in protection of their classmates. If you missed a minute paper she assigned that day, regardless fo your situation, there was no way anyone would cut you slack.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She really doesn't actually teach that much, but the class is SUPER helpful if you know you want to go into the medical professions, but don't know what you want to do. ATTEND CLASS. You will have random pop quizzes and minute papers that you have to be in class to take and receive credit for. Not very understanding of extraneous circumstances.

reviews.comment: if you're not a health science major and are taking this class for easy credit DONT. it is the most worthless class I have ever taken. if you miss a minute paper and quiz you already have an A-. I just think its hilarious that she can miss as many classes as she wants but we don't get to have excused absences. she and her class are a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Avoid this teacher at all costs. Besides doing no actual teaching, she will not be helpful if you have questions or concerns. My least favorite teacher I have had in all of my years of school. I have had two classes with her and she would rather nitpick at things and take points off (without any reason) than ever give you useful critical feedback.

The class is only out of 100 points, so do not slack off. Don't skip class, it will somehow be your day for a minute paper (you can miss a certain amount). There are only 2 exams. Read the books and lectures for it and you will get an A. Always do the extra credit, every bit counts.

reviews.comment: she's nice but you rarely ever hear from her in class, the whole class is basically guest speakers. 2 exams and 1 writing assignment. POP QUIZZES. reviews.comment: This was probably the worst class I have ever taken here at Mizzou. Professor and teaching staff are rude and constantly call people out for doing absolutely nothing. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Grade is based off very few things so every assignment is heavy. Grading criteria is very vague and does not provide clear answers to questions regarding assignments or clear grading criteria.

reviews.comment: Basically, all speakers so not much to say on professor. There are 2 exams and 2 essays that rely on the books and lecture material so make sure you're going to class. Interesting information makes going to class fun and easy though.

reviews.comment: Emily is a great person and professor. I highly recommend this class because it shows the different professions in Health Care and although it can get really boring, it's totally worth it.
show up to class and take notes on the lectures, can use notes on pop quizzes and quizzes. if you dont show up you wont pass.

In order to do well on the tests, you need to read the novels assigned, but overall there's not a lot of work outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The lectures are boring, and this should be a once a week optional course. You have to go to class though because she gives pop quizzes every single day. Easy enough because that's all we're graded on.  She seems like a nice enough person but is a stickler about texting and being late to class. You will be asked to leave if you do either one.

She tries to make this class an actual "class" when it really isn't.  There is no need for tests in this class, yet there are tests.  They are SO easy, but its dumb that there need to be any at all.  The class is a seminar, there is no curriculum.  You get to hear from a lot of people from a lot of different health professions which is nice.

Professor Endersby is very passionate about what he teaches. reviews.comment: Dr. Moore is easily the best chemistry professor in the department. She is a very fair and lenient grader, and her lectures are not too boring to sit through. Chemistry, in general, is a hard subject but she makes it very digestible and easy to follow and she is not judgmental at all if you need additional help or you don't understand something.
Dr. Moore's classes do demand time and effort for preparation, but she is highly skilled and offers numerous resources to support students' success.

Moore is very understanding as a professor. She is very passionate about these topics but recognizes that not everyone is and that they are hard to understand. She offers several homework assignments and extra credit to help boost your grade. Though attendance isn't required you will want to attend since lectures are not always posted virtually.

LOVE Dr.Moore. She is the most amazing professor I had as a chem major. She explain the concepts and the mechanism that are easy understandable. She does uses iclicker although it does not count for any points. She is hilarious and easy to talk to. She does give out extra credit opportunities at the end.

Best chemistry prof I've had. Clear, understandable lectures with practice problems that actually resemble exams. Orgo 2 is a tough topic but she has lots of practice options and explains it so well. Has a few extra credit opportunities too. Can tell she genuinely cares about students and is always willing to help with questions.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ellen is my QUEEN!!!! She made organic so fun and easy to understand. I also had her for Chem 1 and loved it! She's super knowledgeable and genuinely wants everyone to succeed.

A truly great professor, she makes such a hard subject so manageable. To be successful, study early and ask for help early on. Everything continuously builds onto itself so make sure you don't slack. Her exams were tough but manageable. Lots of extra credit opportunities and you could drop one of the 5 exams. The homework sucks but you gotta do it.

Kind, easy to reach, and the most supportive professor I could've had for such a difficult course. She is a genuine person and cares for your success. As annoying as it may be, that's why attendance is required. Most students cannot be successful otherwise. Though she may seem "fluffy" for the subject, she knows what she's doing, and respect her.

i love ellen moore. she is kind to her students and very engaging in class. she gives you all the materials you need to succeed in a hard class like orgo and is always available to help. recommend her over any other orgo teacher at mizzou. i love this lady :)
Dr. Moore is an amazing professor who cares so much about her students. I would take any of her classes again!!!

Dr. Moore is the best Chemistry professor you will find at Mizzou. Some other people say shes a bad professor, but they just dont understand Organic Chemistry. She is always willing to help with any questions you have. Its Organic Chemistry, you have to put in the extra work to succeed, so dont expect the class to be a walk in the park.

One of the best professors I've had! Presents material in a way that holds your interest and makes sure you understand the content. Always answers emails promptly if you have questions. Funny and fair!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore is one of the best professor's I have ever had. I can tell she truly cares about her students and our education. She is very patient when someone doesn't understand a concept, and is very thorough in her explanations regarding different topics. I have enjoyed the content in this class as well as the atmosphere she creates in the classroom

Love her, shes caring, smart, & witty. Lots of positive energy esp for 8am. She has iclickers everyday so go to class for participation points.  However her exams were unpredictable on content. Sometimes they were hw heavy other times no hw questions were on it etc. Didn't love that some chapters we had no slides or hw over so it was hard to learn.

I took orgo 2 with Moore, and she's great at making a tricky subject understandable. It's orgo, so you do have to work to understand the material, but tests are straightforward and mostly multiple choice. Occasional participation assignments, so go to class! Her iclickers are also helpful practice to make sure you're understanding the content.

Dr. Moore is an amazing chemistry professor. This was my second time taking orgo 1 and she was able to take the content that was so daunting to me the semester before and break it down in a way that was easy to understand and process. Orgo is naturally a hard subject but it soon became one of my favorite classes. I highly recommend taking her class
Really good professor for an entry level college course. She knows what she's talking about. Offers lots of extra credit and the drop exam is super helpful (only 3/4 exams count towards final grade).
Dr. Moore was fair in grading subject matter is just naturally difficult.

Teaches great using a combination of iclicker and lecture slides. The people saying these courses with dr.moore are self taught are just coping with the fact that they cant understand something the first ever time they see it and actually have to do work outside of class lol. Dont blame her if youre not an Einstein or not willing to put in the work

She actually wants her students to succeed unlike professors that take pride in watching you fail.  The class is difficult but she makes it manageable and passable.  So organized and gives students so many resources to help them prepare for exams. I LOVE HER!

Dr. Moore really understood chemistry and how to break it down to you. She provided study problems that would directly prepare you for the exams and gave you all of the objectives it would cover to make you most successful. Labs went along with what we were doing in class which was helpful.

Dr. Moore is a 10/10 professor and so funny! If you show up and do the homework, you'll do fine. Extremely easy course if you've taken any chemistry in high school. The extra credit adds up to around a 6% grade boost at the end of the semester. One dropped exam. The exams are much easier than the homework.

The outline and structure of the course were very clear and organized which made it easy to study for exams and do the homework. If you read the content before the lectures, it will make the class a lot easier. Do your work and you will be fine.
I need a time machine to go back and appreciate her. 2 days into the semester with the new guy and im miserable.

If you have 0 fundamentals about chemistry, this professor might not be for you. She uses slides and just reads them, so you have to be prepare yourself for self-study. But, she gives a LOTS of extra credit opportunities. And the max score in each exam is not 100, but 110. The problems that are solved in class are similar to ones in the exam.
super helpful and approachable
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I wish I was able to take every STEM class with Dr. Moore. Her class policies are very fair, as she offers a lot of extra credit and ways to earn points. Very caring and understanding professor. With effort, very able to pass her class.

Dr. Moore made chemistry simple. Even if she read off of a lot of slides she gave a lot extra credit and offered exam reviews that practically gave away what to study. She did not make it difficult to succeed in the course.

She was amazing. She took the time to star a ton of notes within each lectures and straight up telling us what to expect on the exams a majority of the time. She is very lenient on grading and even rounded labs it to be fair when comparing to everyone else's. Gave out TONS of extra credit and gave an extra 10% on every exam and one dropped exam.
Good prof, lots of material togo thru. Do the assignments, go to class, read the textbook, easy.

If you don't know much about chemistry, I wouldn't recommend it. This class is very self-taught; all she does is read the slides off canvas. I never knew what to expect on the exams because the tests were nothing like the homework or study guide. This class took up a lot of time outside the classroom.

This class was very self taught. I never went a day without being confused. I exhausted all of my resources including Dr. Moore. Homework problems and study guides were nothing like the exams and a waste of time. The only thing she did was read the slides that we were going to get in canvas anyway. No teaching at all. Take her at your own risk.

She is the best chemistry professor that I have had at Mizzou, and I would highly recommend trying to get her for any chemistry class. I had her for both Org 1 and 2, and she is more than fair with attendance and grading. I had two concussions during Org2 and still managed to get an A. Fun lectures and has good jokes.

I thought Dr. Moore was good! I think she made Chem 1 pretty straightforward and easy. Her lectures were decent and the tests were much easier than the homework. I didn't have to study much to do well. Not a lot of homework. Do the book problems to study for exams. 

However, in-class assignments are random, weirdly anxiety-inducing group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellen Moore is the best teacher to have for 1320. She's great for outside of class communication via email or in person. Tests are very lecture heavy and make sure to attend lecture to get all of the points. 4 exams, with one dropped. Typically one MC assignment and one DSM assignment per week, as well as the labs.
Love her so much! She makes jokes during lectures and is very real. Sometimes she goes over material pretty quickly, but she makes up for it by providing several study materials.
She an opp

Dr. Moore is probably the best professor for 1320. You have 4 exams total and your lowest one gets dropped and doesn't affect your grade. would often hand out extra credit. Every exam has 10 extra credit points. If you did decent in high school chemistry you could finish this class with over a 100

Dr. Moore is a good professor. She is really nice and often hands out extra credit. You have 4 exams and one can be dropped so it doesn't affect your grade. You also get 10 extra credits on every exam. She has to be the best professor for 1320.

Ellen Moore is a perfectly fine professor. She teaches the material, has good slides, and keeps a good atmosphere in her lectures. The labs, however, are REALLY difficult and involved at times, and there aren't any off-weeks for labs during the semester.
I don't like her teaching style -pretty much all she does is read off of the slides and give us auto-graded textbook assignments. Some people like her so good for them

I would say that having a background of high school chem was helpful for this class. A lot of the class was a review for me, but there were a few difficult topics, so I would just teach myself. There isn't a lot of hw and her lectures explain everything. I never read the textbook. She gives random extra credit. Dr.Moore is also super funny.

I had a rough start for this class & thought I could just go about it like hs. It took me a few exams to realize that I have to put in the work and that it wasn't going to be as easy as hs. I had to learn to study & how to do it right. It's a hard class but its doable. Put in the work by skimming the book doing practice problems& doing crap on time
The lectures are so unhelpful and the homework program is not very useful for learning. You will have to teach yourself through the textbook.

Dr. Moore is an amazing chemistry professor. Her passion for the subject is contagious, and she excels at simplifying complex concepts. She's not just a teacher but a supportive mentor who genuinely cares about her students' success. Organic isn't as bad as everyone says.
Love Dr. Moore! Best professor I have had. She cares so much about her students and making sure everyone has the tools they need to learn and be successful.

Dr. Moore is a great professor. If you had Ganley for 1320 and cruised through it, this is a bit of a wakeup call. But put in the effort and you'll do great. Excited to have her for orgo 2.
(I'm a chem major so if chem isn't your thing then this class will be challlenging)

I had Dr. Moore for 1330 and after taking her class, I can absolutely say I'm excited to have her again for Organic 2. All deadlines were clearly communicated, and we were all aware of what to expect on the test. Attend lecture/lab, read the book, do the HW, and it is impossible to fail.

she is condescending and did sneaky things like surprise in-class assignments then not posting the panapto before the due date of the assignment for those who missed class or cutting the recording and giving exam hints to ppl there. homework, lectures, and study guides were not helpful to exams at all. have to use the txtbook and teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore cares about her students. The work you do in lab correlates well with what you learn in class and homework is beneficial and a great tool. She moves fast through content but takes class time to review with students. She offers times outside of class to work with her and other TAs. I want her to be my prof for every chem class.

I LOVE PROFESSOR MOORE! She cares so much about her students. If you are struggling go to her for help! She wants everybody to succeed and is so cool. She made organic chemistry not as scary. Would 100% recommend her for any course you take. She was the first chemistry professor I liked.

Ellen,

May the word I speak about this amazing young professor, I believe she may have the best physical science teaching ability of all chem faculty. She is very understanding and will help you out with any questions you may have. Really really fun lectures.

Exams are all multiple choice, homework can be tedious but isn't difficult. Very kind and understanding professor. No quizzes, iClicker is required for attendance. Textbook not necessary, but recommended. One dropped exam. Relatively painless compared to other organic chem classes.
