His spanish is very easy to understand, and his tests are very fair and easy if you come to class and study what he tells you to study. I would recommend him for any class he teaches. He is unbelievably nice and he cares so much about mizzou and his students.

Excellent professor, the best I've ever had.  Very organized, always enthusiastic about teaching.  Returns all graded papers the next class.  I highly recommend Professor Fleak for any class.  You will learn a lot.
I LOVE this teacher.  This was my only class that I truly enjoyed coming to.  He loves MU and his students.  THe class is very easy, I would definitely recommend it.

Show up to class and you'll do great.  He gives you practice exams which are exactly the same setup as the real exams. No homework really other than 3 papers and 3 presentations (got an A on everyone).  Class gets off topic a lot...will find yourself talking about the Mizzou Tigers EVERY day in some way.  The guy loves his sports. Easy class though

Bob is a really nice guy, but do not recommend for Intro to Religion or other large classes. He doesn't allow computer notes and does not use slides, and it is hard to keep up with or hear him and his speakers while writing notes. Study guides are basically the test itself, but it's hard to memorize everything he wants. Honors section a lot of work
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bob is a great guy.  This class is discussion heavy.  You are graded more so on your discussions in class than on papers.  The discussions are great, you leave a better person than you came in for sure.  He is very generous and an enjoyable teacher.  When he actually lectures the whole class though, it can be a tad boring.

Bob is a hilarious guy who isn't afraid to spark meaningful discussion. His class isn't an easy A but if you put in the work it isn't hard to do well at all. I've taken two classes with Professor Flanagan thus far and both have been incredibly influential. 10/10 would definitely recommend.

Dr. Foulkes is a nice person, but not a great instructor. The class was not clearly organized. He would start several minutes late almost every day. Class was lecture-heavy, and he stumbles on his words or speeds through concepts frequently. Grades are due in a week, and there is still almost nothing in the gradebook. Not overly difficult, though.

Quite possibly the worst professor I've had the misfortune of coming into contact with, and I've had some doozies. There are so many other qualified and more caring professors in the geography department--so my advice would be to avoid his courses at all costs. He never replies to emails and doesn't care about the well being of his students. Yikes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He sucks! Doesn't reply to emails, can't understand anything in the class and I'm barely getting any help. After talking to some other students, I realized that I wasn't alone in this situation.
Textbook read like an encyclopedia but dont let that deter you. Very smart knows a lot, hes kind of forgetful sometimes. Tests are not too bad. multiple choice, short answers

The classroom atmosphere is laid-back, so you wouldn't expect the exams to be as difficult as they are. The material is interesting, but there's so much of it that it's difficult to memorize it all for the exams. Lots of reading assignments and small group discussion. Lectures are engaging.
Urban Geography--Great professor! Very knowledgable and interesting. Also very helpful. In the end, really enjoying this class!
No Comments
What an incredible professor!  His class was so entertaining it was like watching game seven of a World Series!
Lectures are so entertaining!  He has such a way with words that its hypnotizing, not too mention his butt is like a ripe apple ready to be picked off the tree!!!

I took the honors humanities sequence and had prof. Folescu as my discussion instructor. They are very nice and personable but can sometimes be confusing with their analyses. They can be a tough grader so it was hard to get a good grade since pretty much the only assignments we had were a midterm, final, and a paper.

They were really sweet but I found their lectures mostly boring and nonlinear. I took Philosophy of Film with them and they picked good films but their analysis was confusing. There was a reason that barely anyone showed up to class in the last month. No tests just in class papers. I did well on them but feedback I asked for was not too helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was really tough. Professor Folescu is super passionate about philosophy, but the course was confusing to keep up with because we got so off track at times. However, there are no tests; only papers. If you go to her office hours, she will give you feedback and help you improve your papers before you submit them.

Professor Folescu is a super personable teacher. I took logic with her and she did a good job making sure people understood the material. With that being said, it was a tough course, and I don't think I would have gotten an A if I didn't go to her office hours. If you show her you are making an effort, she will be more forgiving in final grades.

Dr. Folescu is very passionate about what she does. She does a great job of writing down what she lectures on so we don't miss any of it. There are many times where the class can get boring though after a long lecture and she tends to repeat herself a lot. There are only 3 grades so participating is a key value to your grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment:
Pros:
He is quite knowledgeable in his field and an amazing lecturer.
Answers all questions posed by students (even if off-topic).
Is able to artfully redirect whenever the class deviates from the discussion at hand.

Cons:
Attendance is graded.
Can be a bit too lax at times.
The weight of assignments is not outlined like in other courses.

Very good at lecturing and a nice guy. Did not like the class set up. Professor doesn't grade your assignments, your TA does. 3 different TA's in my class and some grade easier/harder than others so the grading isn't too fair. There are only two exams (one midterm, one final) meaning so much content is covered on each one. Completely written exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hate how this course is set up. There ar two huge exams and he gives a study guide the week before the exam with 200 terms to memorize and know. The exams are all short response. This seems a bit much for an introductory course. I would've much rather had it broken up into more exams with less information.

Craig is a good professor. I am not a fan of his class style though. Your grade relies solely on a midterm, paper, and a final exam. No extra assignments, no attendance. Class not mandatory but he does not post notes online. Very sweet man
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is easy, but you do need to attend lecture in order to get information as he does not post lecture slides online. In other words, you should attend, but it isn't required. The tests are short answer and essay in a blue book format so it isn't terrible, but you'll need to know and understand lecture material.
Written exams with blue book but he does a good job to prepare you.
Was a really cool guy. Very few assignments and tests were really simple and straight forward. Made the class as enjoyable as possible :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved the content and found the class enjoyable. I took an online HIST 2210 over the summer. Clear syllabus which broke down work for each day. Good routine and could work at my own pace each week. 2 essays and a discussion post each week, not too much work considering the course was only 4 weeks. Each day he gave about 1-2 hours of work.

Absolutely loved having Craig Forrest as my professor. His lectures are actually interesting and very good at keeping your attention. His slides are perfection. They have all the basic info and I knew many people who only took notes off the slides alone and did alright. He is sweet and good to talk to and often ends lectures a little early.
Loves what he teaches but goes fast on notes and gives a lot of information. Tests can be hard as they are written but if you like history the class will be a breeze.

He's not a teacher, rather someone with a degree that responds to emails. You have to read through lessons online and then complete lesson assignments that are long and waste your time. On tests, you have to write essays that fit the 5 paragraph format you learned in middle school because "an essay is always five paragraphs". Joke of a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really chill professor who makes the material easier to understand. He is really approachable, but attendance is mandatory because you get on just showing up to class. He is our TA for the class and he just leads discussion once a week but makes it fun to actually show up to class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Craig Forrest brushes over important historical events. He teaches that slaves were not treated "that bad" and that Native Americans deserved the treatment they got. He said that women being placed in the household was meant as high praise to women. You will be graded heavily on tests, which are written, and if you're like me, you'll be mad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Forrest is a great teacher but with very few things that get graded for his class. If you mess up on one assignment be prepared to have to work extremely hard to revive your grade. Lectures are dull but very informative and he gives you clear information. Take notes and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is unorganized and his Canvas page is a labyrinth of documents. No clear due dates on assignments or rubrics. Basically, he will tell you to write a paper and that is it. As stated, he rambles....a lot. It makes lectures hard to follow. 3 class periods now he has said we will watch a video, but instead just rambled on about some mundane topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took as a WI course. Attendance is mandatory because if you don't show up you won't have a clue about what's going on. I attended every class & still didn't. It's 2018 & he's used slides from 2011. He's extremely unorganized & rambles on about things that have nothing to do with material & then he assigns papers with very unclear instructions.
Rambles, in a good way. Project expectations are never clear, but he grades pretty easy. Interesting course material.
Very disorganized

Dr. Flinn is a cool dude. That said a cool dude does not equate to a cool class. This class is a mess. There's documents all over BB from 2008-2012. ITS 2015. Assignments are literally thought up during the class he assigns. Do not write from his grading rubric that requires you to restate all of your writing but also states NO FLUFF. Weird class.

Dr. Flinn is world renown in Anthropology. This class was very informative: the EVOLUTION of our bio-sexuality.  Those complaining are looking for easy As, didn't read the course description, and are likely not intellectually prepared for such a course. His anecdotes are intended to help the many lay MU students try to understand basic science.

Genius of a man but a little condescending. Probably the most well respected professor in the school but he seems like he thinks he''s better than everyone. He does like to teach and wants students to learn but if you ask a stupid question or don''t know the answer to something you''ll be embarrassed. Better to figure things out on your own.

Professor is extremely intelligent. However, this class is extremely unorganized, his blackboard is a mess. None of the assignments were clear. The TA's grade very differently from each other, and when I would go in for help none of the TA's were prepared.
Class was not what I expected. Focused more on evolution than sexual behaviors of humans. Papers are extremely difficult and TA's grade very differently.

Dr Flinn is an intelligent guy. He truly knows the subject matter, I can attest to this from attending his office hours but his lectures are hard to follow & boring. He gets off topic & rambles, sometimes I feel like crying bc the lectures are so painful to sit through. Also this course is mostly human evolution & lightly touches base on sexuality

Do not take this class. He rambles and he even admits to going on tangents that will not help you at all. As of me writing this, there are three/four weeks left of the semester and only 10% of what I have learned so far has been about human sexuality. Also the TAs are not helpful at all, sometimes they don't even know what they are talking about.

Not exactly sure what the other posters are talking about, but this is one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. Dr. Flinn is not a good teacher & I've been in this class for a month & half and have yet to talk about humans in HUMAN sexuality. Find another WI class.
Very knowledgeable, but SO UNORGANIZED!!

Very interesting class!! For a writing intensive it is an easy class and you still learn a lot. He is very enthusiastic and loves what he does. The papers are graded pretty easily but they do take a bit of time to write. Highly recommend this class!

A really committed and knowledgeable professor. Truly knows what he is talking about. I highly recommond his human sexuality class. He is not only entertaining but also is an accomplished scholar in his field. Only problem is re-learning scientific analysis. Asks provocative questions. Accessible to any deep-thinking students of any major.

Favorite teacher I had all year, definitely one of the most intelligent. Really concerned with every student comprehending the material and thinking creatively. The class was mildly labor-intensive (maybe because I took it WI). The final was optional.
Best professor I ever had. Though he sometimes (often) strayed off topic and his requests ambiguous, I learned a lot and it was an easy A.

In his Human Sexuality class he was good at tying the topic into day to day life which was interesting. However, a lot of the information in lectures was repetitive. Not very specific about assignments. I actually missed one because it was so similar to another one we were being assigned. Fortunately he does offer a make up final.

Took him for Human Sexuality. He's nice and well meaning and very informed, but sometimes it is hard to pay attention in class. Sometimes, half of his lecture will be a re-lecture of the material he went over in a previous class, which is frustrating. material was interesting, however, and the class was relatively easy if you went and did the work.

Flinn is great at leading discussions and is willing to let students explore their own ideas, even if they end up going out on a limb. If you prepare for class by reading the material AND thinking about it, you'll probably enjoy his class.

he was a horrible teacher. he didn't even put up the lecture outlines until after class, and it was impossible to copy down the notes during class. it was also very boring. his notes are very contradictory. don't buy the book, its useless.
He was terrible. Seriously, it was like hell going to class. All he talks about is when he used to live on an island. He flys through the outline, so I hope you like learning on your own.
The most interesting ideas in any class I ever took.  He makes you think really deep.
I learned a lot in this class.  The tests weren't too bad, all multiple choice.  He made sure that we understood everything and was very nice.
This professor was awesome.  He explains things well, and is always willing to help his students.  If you get a chance, take his class.
Had her last year, feel bad for everyone in her class this year. Drop while you can, she's a devil witch
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: loved service learning, hated her.

Truly an evil woman. Failed me for being sick twice, but cancelled class multiple times for her own allergies. Acts so loving & philanthropic, but couldn't care less about students. Hates opinions other than her own. Makes you read 1 terrible book every week, volunteer 30+ hours, and essays she won't accept 1 second late.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. Stone cold, has no sympathy or human recognition for students.  There are no slip ups allowed- and even week you're expected to read a (sh*tty) novel, volunteer 35 hours, + perfect attendance. She failed me after I did all that. Even if you're interested in Service Learning, avoid AnneMarie at all costs.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. The class required reading 1 horrible novel every week, 35 volunteer hours, and perfect attendance- no slip ups allowed. She was stone cold, views herself as a saint, & has no sympathy or human recognition for any of her students. Even if you're interested in this course, avoid Anne Marie at all costs.

Dr. Foley crammed 5 books and a kajillion papers into a semester. Not to mention you'll spend 20-30 hours "serving the community" and only receive 3 credit hours for the course. Dr. Foley kind of irritated me- she interrupt students answering questions she asks, and she didn't put much effort into giving feedback at all. I did enjoy the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She will not work with her students, so be prepared to do things Foleys way and without any leeway. Its Foleys way or the Highway. Even if youre a great writer, she will find reasons to not give you the grade you deserve. I made an A in Foleys class and I had to work hard for it, and she still didnt give all of the points I believed I deserve
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Foley is no doubt one of the greatest people I have had the luxury of meeting. She truly cares about everyone at the University of Missouri. I did not like her class however, as it requires lots of reading and writing papers over the readings. I am not much of a reader and wouldn't recommend it to people who do not like to read.

THE. ABSOLUTE. BEST. Dr. Foley re-ignites that world-changing fire in everyone she talks to. One of the most passionate, sassy, funny, inspirational, hardworking persons I've ever met; by far the best professor I've had. Lots of reading and essays, but the content is fascinating and eye-opening. ALL students should experience her/her classes at MU.

Dr. Foley is the best professor at Mizzou, hands-down. She is wise, cares for her students, and cares about bettering our society. She is hilarious and also knows what she's talking about. The lectures are engaging and I looked forward to going to them. I think that every student should take a class with Dr. Foley. She is AMAZING!

honestly hated this class. mostly because i hate reading but i looked up summaries of the books and still did well on all the in class writing.. go to lecture before spring break or christmas thanksgiving break because you get extra credit. it sucked but i got an a

Dr. Foley is one of the best professors on campus. She will force you to think critically about yourself and the world around. Every student should have to take her class. Your grade depends on 5 in-class writings and 6 longer papers. This class is a lot of work, but read the assigned books and take the writings seriously, and you can get an A.

I loved him as a professor, but I want to put in a warning about the class itself. Here Be Monsters is a medieval literature course, which focuses heavily on narratives concerning Christian men. I read often for pleasure, and I still struggled to keep up with reading assignments. It's worth your time to participate, can help if you need extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved having Professor Foster's Honors Humanities course. I felt that I was challenged by the course, but I was still able to perform well. I took this course online and still found it quite engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Foster is a brilliant, verbose, quality teacher. Learned a lot from him, school and life-wise, and he puts a lot of effort into his job- but this makes for A LOT of work for students too. Would NOT recommend this class, unless you're content with crazy unnecessary amounts of work. Decently interesting content, however- LOTS of lit analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster does expect a lot out of you as a student, but he makes you WANT to work for it. He clearly loves what he does, and he instills in each of his students a desire to learn on their own. You do need to be ready to work--there is a lot of reading and writing, and he is a tough grader, but also note that it's never busy work. Great teacher!

My 4th and final Humanities sequence course and by FAR the worst professor I've had in the series. Smart but a ridiculously hard grader, only one person in class got an A (and an A- at that!) on the two essays, tries too hard to prove he is intelligent. One group project. Take basically ANY other humanities professor and you'll be happy you did.
Dr. Foster was really understanding and great. He was flexible with due dates and offered extra credit. The coursework was hard, but he was always avaliable for extra help.

I've had Greg for almost two years in class and he is by far the best professor I've had during my time at Mizzou. The coursework is challenging but doable and Greg is extremely understanding with due dates and such, so I've never had a problem. He's really brilliant during discussion and always keeps the material interesting.
Wonderful Professor, very passionate about his subject matter and the success of his students. Very fun class!!
A great, insightful man.

Prof. Forrest was by far my favorite professor at Mizzou so far. 4204 was my favorite class, and she was a big part of that. She was always encouraging and inspirational, even if it was clear that your ideas needed some work. I am taking her even planning course next semester, and I cannot wait to have her again!
AMAZING!  Truly cares about all of her students and works exceptionally hard to make sure they succeed. Will definitely take a class with her again!

Professor Forrest is amazing. She is so down to earth and really wants her students to succeed.  She knows what she is talking about and her labs are awesome.  Highly recommend her.  Plan to take future courses from her for sure.  If you can get into her section, take her!
Jen is such a wonderful professor! Took her N2200 class with Sue and it was amazing! It was a pretty easy class, but their main goal is to prepare you for nursing school.

I had her for Nursing 2400 and they changed the class and honestly it was so boring and horrible. This IS required to take so you have to bear through it but be ready for 2 hour long lectures that will have you falling asleep. They start you off with a group project at the beginning of the semester which is so annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jen is a phenomenal instructor and experienced clinical nurse. Honored to have had her in multiple classes. So patient as you learn!!

The best professor I have had. She is an awesome professor who truly cares about your success. She has prepared me for a career in agricultural safety and health. Would recommend students to take her online class.

Enjoyed this class. Everything is online. Well organized and laid out. Easy to read and understand. Instructor wants her students to succeed so she is willing to help you out! I would definitely take this class again.

Great professor! I took AGSM 4020 as a psych student, without ever taking an AG related class in my life and still got an A+. Just do the work. Her assignments have a lot of videos and reading materials, but just take the time to do them (and write about them) and you'll get an A+ too.

I took this class for fun! I got behind in this online class and Professor Karen was willing to work with me. She cares about her students and wants them to be successful. Shes takes agricultural safety and health seriously; which its a bad thing. Take this online class and you can expect to get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Funkenbusch cares about students. Great teacher that knows how to teach. Understands that life happens and is willing to work with you. Has high for students in this class. If you read the lecture materials, follow directions, do the discussions on time and try on weekly quizzes you will do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Online class. Weekly reading with an assignment. Also have weekly discussions based off reading materials, internet sites or video clips. I enjoyed the weekly discussions. Very fair professor who is willing to help you out. Enjoyed the class and would recommend it to others.

Professor Funkenbusch is amazing.  I'm not an Agri major, but I highly considered it after her class.  She is a wealth of information, and is more than willing to help you in anyway possible.  If you put forth the effort you should have no problem getting a great grade!  I would recommend her to anyone, and would definitely take her again!
Smart and kind man. A little hard to understand, but great teacher.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Marissa was a great teacher. She expects work done ahead of time, but is fair in grading. It will teach you a lot. She is very funny, and treats you like an adult and not a college kid. She doesn't have patience for slackers. Do your work your grade will reflect it. She is very insightful and one of my favorite teachers.
Took "Writing about Literature" with this professor. The reading list is great and the assignments are extensively thought out. I'd recommend Fugate's classes in a heartbeat.
Great, funny teacher. She does a great job at what she does. Not too hard of a class, in part because of how prepared you are (if you are there everyday). Also very attractive.

Over the past couple of months, Dr Foley has become a major role-model. As a director, she tackles a lot, but is always wanting to hear about students. I had a community service class, that was heavy on presentations, but she made the room a safe-space. Never afraid to speak on her passion, human rights, and ask students to think and act critically

Doesn't answer emails, doesn't upload grades until a month after grades are due, is admittedly passive-aggressive to students she doesn't like, and will make you cry on a study abroad trip in a foreign country (happened to me). Worst 8 grand I ever spent. She really shouldn't be a teacher let alone director.

Taking into account the hours spent ready, studying, listening to lectures, volunteering, and writing, this class was one of the hardest in my academic career. Foley seems like a nice enough teacher, but to take her class you have to have a lot of resolve and drive
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I was really excited to take this class & participate in the service aspect of it. Let me tell you, you can do the service on your own. Ann Marie Foley is demeaning, demanding, and disrespectful. I found her to be incredibly self-centered even though she's "all about service". Her lectures are stressful and she's rarely available for her students.

Took her for Community Engagement (formerly HCCIP). Wanted to volunteer, but bit off more than I could chew with this class. In addition to volunteering, you must journal about each experience, read about 4 books (and take quizzes on them), and right a final paper of 12-14 pages. Lots of work that I did not expect from a volunteer class.
Best class of my college career!  Learned lots and had fun doing it!

Dr. Foley is the best instructor I've had at Mizzou. She'll give you a new perspective on issues, and life in general. All of her lectures are eye-opening and insightful. I want this woman to write a book on social philosophy. She's amazing. I would recommend that you stay away from HCCIP if possible. Try another one of her classes.
she does not reply to emails

Dr. Foley is probably the best teacher I have ever had at MU.  She knows what she is talking about.  The class isn't too hard, but you have to get your work done to get a good grade. Classes like these should be required.
I haven't learned quite so much from anybody else as I have Dr. Foley. Oh, and she's fun.
best teacher i've ever had
Halarious woman. She has a genuine interest in opening her students up. I would recommend any of her classes.

I feel like a better human being after taking HCCIP, and I am certainly much more educated about social issues that plague the world. Dr. Foley is wonderful. She is passionate, and she is caring. Take this class! It's easy, it's rewarding, and it's life-changing.
The most amazing, inspiring teacher I've ever had the pleasure to LEARN from.  Absolutely wonderful! I think everyone at Mizzou should have to take one of her classes!
A very hard-working and driven humanitarian.  She likes students and is always willing to help.  I had many great experiences in the course and learned a lot.

She's not particularly easy, I think she just wants all of her students to excell. I think she's extremely insightful and knows a lot about the ancient works we have studied. She also keeps everything quite interesting. I'd take a class with her any day

She's not very clear on how to do your assignments, but it doesn't matter because she always gives out A's.  Her classes are interesting, she's a nice lady, kinda hippie-ish. Easy A, good cause, take this class.
my favorite teacher at mizzou thus far

She is a ridiculously boring professor who loves to hear herself talk. She has obviously had a hard time getting students to join her classes because I keep getting emails about availability.  Just a  warning...stay away.

Wonderful professor in a very difficult class. She is very knowledgable about literature in general, and she brings pizza and cookies to her students. I really learned a lot from her, and I got an A, so that was always good.
No Comments

very easy class to get an A. he explains well, accent can be hard to understand at first but you get use to it. 15 labs that you can work in groups on, 4 exams, midterm, and final. that's all there is for assignments. and he throws out your worst 5 labs. highly recommend!!
Damiano is a wonderful teacher.  He teaches very clearly and his tests are easy to understand.  I would highly recommend him!!!
No Comments

While she has a lovely personality, she is a not good professor. I have taken two classes with her and passed with ease, but there is almost no point in going to lectures as she is always off topic and does not make any sense.
isnt a hard class at all. tests are open book and lab is a breeze. only thing is she gets off topic easily and can get behind in teaching bc of it.
LOVE DR FRUEND!!!! Unorganized at times but she cares for her students and is very understanding when you have issues outside of class/miss class. Take her class!

I love her, she is so sweet and helpful if you come by office hours. But if you took APES in high school, don't even bother taking this class bc you will learn nothing new. She grades stuff super late, and I think just gives you a 100% as long as you do it.

Overall she was very nice and cares a lot about her students. As a teacher though, she sucked. Out of the whole semester, I went to class less than 10 times and I am passing with an 87% because of a few missing assignments. Her lectures don't have any words to copy down, so you have to write as she talks and she usually doesn't make much sense.

If you want to learn anything, don't take her classes. She didn't teach me about anything relating to sustainability and talked about her kids the entire time. I don't know why she's still allowed to teach
Super disorganized, but also nice and caring. Easy class.

Dr. Fruend is a great and fun person that I enjoyed being around, however she is the most unorganized professor I have ever had. Consistently unprepared for class, after I submitted the final, nothing had been graded since August. Once grades were put in it seemed as if she didn't even look at the assignments and gave random grades. Easy grader.

Dr. Fruend is a wonderful human being, but she's incredibly disorganized. This semester, when finals week approached, I had no exams or labs graded for the semester. I had gotten no feedback on any assignments other than automatically graded Canvas quizzes. I don't recommend taking her if you are looking to engage with material in a meaningful way.

Fruend is super sweet and empathetic, but this class was not organized. She's new to MU, so hopefully in future versions of the class she'll have figured stuff out. Several lectures were just looking at videos that were kind of? related to the textbook. She assigned an essay during finals week while our exams from September still weren't graded.

Decent professor though he made all of his students buy a book that he wrote, making it seem like a money grab and profiting off of students. We did this book assignment where we had to read the whole book and write a report on it, I feel this was made so it didn't seem like so much of a money grab for him. Please stop profiting off of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The exams are basically impossible. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very frustrating considering this is an entry level class and he makes it 20,000 times harder than it should be. Don't bother emailing him, he won't answer even though in his syllabus it says he will and he's all about the syllabus. I will never take a class with this man again. I pay your salary bro, maybe be a little nicer.
Dr. Frank is a good professor. He is always willing to help students when they attend office hours.

I LOVE Dr. Frank. He is a very kind/passionate instructor who made a GenEd class interesting. He provides EVERY possible exam question in his study guide. It's very possible to earn an A if you study properly. I zoned out for many of the lectures and did not read the textbook, but prepared extensively for both exams and got an A. Attend each class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought his class was kind of dumb because he makes tests harder than they should be. He does tests in an essay format over 7 random vocab words but it's out of 50 words to learn. So basically you have to learn all of them and be able to write a really good paragraph about the random vocab word to get most of the points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Be ready to study. He gives 2 tests the whole semester and if you don't study you will not do good. They are completely doable, but it takes a lot of hard work you gotta be willing to do if you want an A.

I really enjoyed him as a professor even though I had little interest in the topics, he made it interesting. It was an online class because of Covid but he still tried to make connections to the students.

Frank is overall a decent teacher. His lectures are pretty interesting, coming from someone with little history interest. I read every assigned reading, but if you skip one or two you will be fine. We have 5 point quizzes due before most lectures. Your TA really matters because some are harder graders. Show up for discussion!

Jerry Frank is very interested and knowledgeable in his subject, which makes it way more interesting for his students. The material and tests are hard but if you go to all the lectures and take notes and read at least some of the material, its not too bad.

Dr. Frank is extremely fair and caring with his students. His lectures are rather interesting and he does an extremely good job of getting the point across. Show up to every lecture, take notes, read the assigned chapters, take the online quizes and you'll do just fine. Tests are essay based so focus on memorizing historical details.

Dr. Frank is a wonderful professor, and one of my favorites! He keeps class interesting with his sense of humor and funny comments! His tests are essay based, but you have the prompts well in advance of the exam. His honors section is not easy, but if you are willing to put the effort into preparing for class, you should do well.

Dr. Frank is a nice and sweet professor.  Also, willing to help if you ask for it.  It is not the easiest class to receive an A in especially if you're in the Honors section.  The test are essays and you must be extremely prepared and detailed to score well.  Yet, if you like history and are willing to put in the effort required you should do well.

Hard grader. Don't take the honor's discussion. He's the instructor for it, and he, while funny, is mean. He has a very one sided view of history. He sped through the world wars like they did not matter.

I LOVE JERRY FRANK! He's the sweetest guy & really cares for the students. His lectures are fairly interesting. He doesn't put his lectures online, but going to his lectures isn't bad. There are no assignments, only online open book quizzes, & 2 tests, & he gives you a study guide. Loved the class even though I really hate history.

Fred is a great professor and a very kind, funny person. He's approachable and gives genuine feedback with your best interest in mind. He can be a bit particular about some style rules, but as long as you pay attention during lecture, you'll do fine.
Writing-heavy course, do the work, take his feedback and you'll be fine. He is kind, funny, and makes an effort to connect with you. Pay attention in class, you'll lose points for improper AP style.
Super kind and understanding of missing class etc. Hard grader but worth it because you get great feedback.

This was one of my most challenging classes, but it was also one of my favorites. Dr. Frank is incredibly knowledgeable, and he wants his students to succeed. You need to read the discussion readings, the textbook (less important), and always attend lectures. If you're confused just talk to him, he's a super nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the worst professors I've ever encountered. When this man teaches he's unengaging and MIA outside of class unless you are doing well. During discussions you would think you could get help from the TA but surprise surprise he was the TA as well. I was a genuine historian now I question what I actually know. I do not recommend!

Such a wholesome guy. However if there was a gun to my head and I was asked to take this class again the gun would go off. The exams are pretty hard, there's an essay and about 40 "ID terms" from the study guide, 8 on the test, which are basically just terms from each section that you have to be a master on to get even a 70%.

Loved Dr. Frank!! If you take history 1200, please get him! He loves teaching and he is very passionate about the material and genuinely cares about students and wants them to show up. I have skipped classes for other subjects before and I never missed one of his because it was something I actually looked forward to.

While Dr. Franks exams can be tough if you aren't prepared, all material is clearly laid out through his engaging lectures and textbook reading based discussion sections. Attendance is mandatory as he doesn't record lectures, but you'll always want to show up because of how engaging and informative they are. He's a very passionate teacher, love him

Dr. Frank was extremely kind and good at teaching. The part of this class that really screwed me over was its harsh grading and extremely writing heavy tests. If you're like me and don't do well on essay exams, make sure you can memorize 40 terms and write a detailed paragraph about each one before signing up for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. Frank. He is a very kind/passionate instructor who made a GenEd class interesting. He provides EVERY possible exam question in his study guide. It's very possible to earn an A if you study properly. I zoned out for many of the lectures and did not read the textbook, but prepared extensively for both exams and got an A. Attend each class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dr.Frank. He does give pop quizzes though. He goes really in depth during his lectures so if you decide to skip his class good luck. His exam are all written, but aren't extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Best history professor I've ever had. Very tough grader. He holds his students to very high standards but I think its' worth it, because it gives a higher quality of learning. Let's just say he's tough, but fair. And the lectures are wonderful! I wish I could take this class all over again. Thank you, Dr. Frank!

I would not recommend hist 1200 with Frank. This class is so hard for being a gen ed. You have to write essays for the exams and the average grade is a C. I've heard the other history is much better. You usually have weekly readings from the textbook and you talk about it in discussion.

This class takes a lot of effort for being a gen ed. There are pop quizzes and his test average is a C+. Your exams are based off of textbook material, but his lectures aren't about the textbook, so you have to teach yourself. The discussion section doesn't really help either. Not my fav
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor was amazing at conveying the material.  Very understanding and made class interesting.

If you're a freshman, prepare yourself thoroughly by reading the syllabus. I had no idea when assignments were due, nor what the professor really wanted. Class was too big to ask directly, and discussion leader didn't help either. Great lectures, love the material, but goes way too fast.

One of the kindest professors at Mizzou! He doesn't take attendance, but you have to show up to class in order to pass. Notes are very interesting and he's very passionate. Test format is short answer and essay, but he gives a study guide. Your grade largely depends on your TA, show up to discussions. Easy A if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Frank was very knowledgeable on the topics covered in class, however, he simply does not know how to teach a class. He tries to facilitate discussion that falls flat, explicitly tells students they are wrong and leaves no room for critical thinking. If you aren't thinking exactly what he thinks you'll barely pass this class. Very arrogant too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Frank is passionate about history; his lectures aren't boring. He is good at relaying the material. He doesn't post his notes online so attend class. There are weekly online quizzes on book readings. Tests were two days, one term ID portion and one essay. This is not a blow off class, but it's doable. I have an A+ currently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. It is obvious that he loves history and has lots of knowledge in the topic. Your tests are graded by TAs or if you're in the honors college by Dr Frank. His lectures are extremely engaging and I am never left bored. Their is no technology allowed, which I personally liked. While his tests are challenging, I never got below a B+

Very very very unhelpful. One of the worst teachers I have ever had. No technology is allowed and it is very lecture heavy. To review the lecture for tests (which are very hard essay based) you must rely on the textbook and your hand written notes. His lecture powerpoints he will not put online for review and is close minded to the use of Tegrity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Frierdich is one of the most knowledgeable professors that I have had at Mizzou. He really cares about students and wants them all to grow and deepen their understanding of American politics in his course. I would definitely recommend if you are looking for a discussion based government class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Frierdich is very knowledgeable about both current issues and about general history and politics. The class focuses mainly on the founding and how that ties to current day. The papers and projects are clearly described and you should know what is expected of you. He is very helpful and will work with you to help you so you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Frierdich's class is not for you if you want to learn a list of facts. He is "big picture"/concept focused, and you won't be tested over most of what you read. Read the readings, since you'll probably be discussing them in a circle of a few students. He likes to ask open-ended questions. 2 papers that require creativity, 1 essay test, 1 project

Dr. Frierdich was one of my favorite professors! His class is easy but not too easy, he's clear about what we need to prepare for class, his assignments allow you to get creative even if they're papers, and he's overall a super supportive guy. Attendance isn't counted, but you get a participation grade, so it is important that you show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Frierdich very clearly cares both about his subject and his students. He does hold you to a high standard, but he gives you plenty of time and resources to excel. Almost your entire grade is based on participation and projects, so do the readings, go to lectures, and start projects early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice, personable guy who clearly cares about the class and enjoys our time together. His teaching style is mostly just running through problems together as a class. Pretty hard grader and gives out a good amount of work but if you want to learn he's a great professor for it.
Lectures are mainly pointless, but all exams come from the labs. If you go to the labs and make a good binder for the open note and you will be fine.
He is excellent professor.Understandable and caring professor in our university
Great teacher, you'll learn a quite a bit.  And I agree with the positive comments above.
No Comments

Prof. Solbrekken was about as good as a prof can get for teaching a subject I really didn't look forward to!  We did one project in particular that was VERY cool and fun.  Very clear, helpful, and an extra is that he's a really nice guy.
Prof. Solbrekken really cares about his students and is an excellent lecturer.  You can tell that he really likes his job and he works hard at it.  I learned a lot from his class.

He is a nice guy and an engaging lecturer but often fairly disorganized. His exams are hard but he curves them a lot. He is not super flexible or accommodating to students (especially with late assignments or missing class) and can be kind of a "gotcha" professor at times. He will like you more if you go on the Colorado field trip.

Paco is obviously very knowledgable about all the things he teaches but it makes it hard for him to tell when other people can't understand the subject matter. He is not very well organized and may take a while to respond to communication. He's brilliant, but a very disorganized teacher, he posts the slides but they don't make any sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was FAR more difficult than I anticipated. Paco is a fun, interesting person but lectures were hard to follow. Tests were unnecessarily difficult and hard to prepare for, but there is a generous curve. I found the lecture skeletal outlines and recorded lectures helped with test prep, and I recommend taking physics before this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Paco is a sweet, caring, funny guy. He is very willing to help you if you ask for it. He's passionate about geology. Only thing is he loses his train of thought and it can be hard to follow his lectures. This class is really difficult, so take easier classes when you end up taking it.

Paco is a sweet professor who is very clearly in love with geology and teaching. I oftentimes struggled to follow through with his lectures and had to resort to the online "textbook" that he replaced with the traditional textbook. I do appreciate the notion of wanting to save his students some cash, but the online replacement was subpar at best.

I love Paco for his personality but this class is DIFFICULT. If you are an Environmental Science student who is required to take this course I HIGHLY recommend taking PHYSICS AND SOILS FIRST. You will much better understand a lot of the content. Paco is caring but this class isn't easy & he's not great at lecturing. You will need to study a lot.

If you have not taken physics or calculus yet I would recommend doing so. A lot of the homework and a few exam questions involve math and physics that he expects you to know even though physics isn't a requirement for the course. You can get by without it but you'll likely struggle with the math/physics topics. His office hours are helpful though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Funny but disorganized. Extremely accessible outside of class and replies quickly to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Paco is an OK professor. He is hard to follow and I dislike that he refers to a lot of physics topics as "elementary" considering I have never taken physics and am an junior in college. He is discouraging for students who may be struggling, however he does try to help/ is accessible outside of class if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He has a hard time staying on one train of thought during lecture and is therefore hard to follow. The labs were disorganized as well but our TA helped a lot. Definitely go to office hours if you don't understand the homework because there are physics questions and he does not review in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Paco is almost too smart for his own good. He understands the concepts far beyond the undergrad level and therefore has a hard time making it more accessible to those who have not been introduced to the topic. The tests are hard but curved, and hard to prepare for. My advice is take notes off the outline and review homework. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was a hard semester due to having half the class online, but you could tell Paco tried really hard to make it a meaningful experience for students. The labs, Homework, and Tests were typically very hard, but Paco gave out points where needed, and made sure no one failed. Definitely a lot of work, but I loved the class and Paco.

Extremely nice and passionate guy who loves his subject. He is sometimes too much in love with it and all over the place which can be hard to follow, but overall, this class wasn't so bad. All the notes were online and able to print but you still must go to class because he likes to test you on little things that he says in class, but does curve.
This guy is an Expansion Theorist.

He is the best professor ever. He has a great teacher heart. His lecture is interesting and his grading is really reasonable. He tries to make students feel good with the subject and help them to pass this course with a good grade. He is so helpful and inspirational professor.

This should have been an easy A for me but I missed the second day of class. His lecture style is very easy to digest. Grading is generous – one quiz grade is dropped – but you should plan on attending all classes. Keep past in-class assignments and quiz questions. They will reappear on successive tests.
Extremely unorganized, asks questions on quizzes from one little specific question buried somewhere in the book or lecture that no one ever read. Horrible...
you can either go to class and not read the book, or skip class and read the book. you can bring your laptop to class so that's a huge plus

I read the book and it helped me a lot. He also posts lectures online which is helpful. For the final, look over the previous exams and there will be some of the same questions, word for word. Overall, generally easy class and I actually found some of the stuff interesting.

This class wasn't too bad. Although prof. Gomez isn't really that helpful, everything is pretty organized on blackboard making it easy to keep up on things. I studied about 2 hours for each test and about 8 hours for the final and got a B. Take that for what you will.
Worst teacher ever. Absolutely horrible class. Doesn't care about the well being of his students and doesnt give them the time of day when approaching for help. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!! EVER!!!

Not disorganized, quite the opposite. Each lecture is carefully structured and intended to illuminate the reading, not be a mere substitute for it.  Quizzes really help to prepare for exams, though they are not easy.  Grades on a curve.  Responds to emails quickly and is available outside of class. Easy on the eyes.

Geol 2400 - Seemed unorganized.  Lecture outlines didn't match slides and neither matched lecture.  Had problems with equations.  Homework was sometimes long and too hard, others too easy.  Very nice and friendly and helpful outside of class.
the tests were way too hard
a little unorganized but very smart and funnny

He was a little tough, and the tests weren't the easiest.  In comparison to a lot of classes though.  It was pretty straight forward.  All of the notes were on powerpoint and easy to copy.  Overall, I think the class was fairly easy.  I'd take it again or choose him in future instances.
Absolutely hated the class.  I thought he was a terrible teacher and I basically had to teach the material to myself.  I would not recommend this class.

Paco is very clear in his teaching of the concept and principles.  His quizzes are kind of difficult, but he puts practice quizzes on-line that help out a lot.  Tests are difficult and require a lot of "reading in between the lines." The lab is
Prof. Gomez is really, really great about explaining things and actually taking time to help his students. His tests were a little hard, but he was really fair. I'd definitely take his class again.

He is a nice person with a lot of interesting takes. But his writing prompts, rubric, and feedback are not very clear, which can make it hard in trying to figure out what he wants you to write. He can be a bit of a tough grader if you strive for a high A. It is not a hard class but you will definitely need to put in effort to get far.

I have for Creative Writing and he was a friendly guy! The class is chill and there's not much assignments. The thing I dislike is how we have to review every reading for the final but they can be manageable if you take your time and know the theming like CNF, Fiction, and Poetry!  Best part is he before the finals, he offered us donuts 🍩
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Scott Garson gave barely any assignments, then decided that we were going to have a final exam about all the readings from the semester. I had an A the entire class and then I got a C on the final. Legit played favorites and wasn't helpful with writing. I had him for ENGL1500 but that wasn't an option
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is way harder than a gen ed English course should be. If you do not enjoy history, do not take this class. It feels like you're in a film appreciation/ history class. You will be required to watch many films about war outside of class and write about them. He is a very hard grader and instruction is very unclear for essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Garson knows his stuff and definitely makes you a better writer, but for the most basic English class necessary to graduate he is too hard on his students. His grading is reasonable in terms of being more professional, but it shouldn't be as hard as he makes it to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Garson is a really nice professor who cares about his students, but for an English1000 class he grades way too hard. I would suggest taking an easier English1000 class unless you are really good at writing. I found the class to be very boring, and its hard to do good when 4 papers make up your grade and he doesn't grade easily.

Garson never likes to give grades higher than a 94.5. With a cutoff for an A being 93.34, it may seem like it is difficult to earn an A, but honestly if you don't turn in any garbage papers you'll likely end the class just above the cutoff. All assignments in the class are based off the American Dream, which I honestly did not find interesting.

Scott's really cool but it's difficult to get an A in his class. Three papers make up 87.5% of your grade with the threshold for an A being a 93.34%. However, he's really accessible outside of class and he seems to get lonely during office hours so if you put in the effort to talk to him he'll give you good feedback. You can do well if you work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Scott is a terrible professor. Three essays make up 87.5 percent of your grade, which is only an A if you get above a 93.34, and he doesn't believe in giving good grades; the highest grade in the class for the first paper was a 94. He doesn't use class time effectively, doesn't explain essays, and gives no writing freedom. Terrible.

Garson was an awesome prof. His class is very war based so if you're interested in that take his class! The class was based off of 3 essays, the lengths get longer as the course goes on. If you're having trouble getting something done on time, he'll give you an extension. Very easy going, passionate prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: great teacher!  english 1000 was pretty easy. we had 5 papers the whole time and other than that NO homework and NO tests!! he's funny and if you talk in class he'll like you. just pay attention to what critiques he gives about papers and you get a B+ to an A every paper

I definitely recommend participating. If you talk in discussion, he will like you and help you succeed. My class was based on the Vietnam War and we watched a full movie, numerous clips, speech, and read one novel. He doesn't waste your time, he cuts class early. Lot of days off. Awesome teacher who gives great feedback if you take the to ask.

Laid back while still professional. His description during class of what he is looking for  in the paper is way more helpful than the rubric. Available for feedback and offers extensionson papers  if you ask ahead of time. The theme for the class was the American Dream. In all an enjoyable class even for a non English major like myself.
GREAT TEACHER
Easy class. No homework, 3 essays. Don't buy the text books. Rent the quiet american from the library and share with others. Huge waste of money if you buy them. Great teacher, great class.
Over all easy class. You have to write four papers and he gives you the opportunity to resubmit them. Everything is about the vietnam war though.

If you are looking for an easy, English 1000 class to earn an easy A in, this is not the class for you. He's not awfully hard, however, he isn't the easiest grader. The topic behind this class is really boring as well. Pretty much, all you discuss is the Vietnam War.
The topic is a little boring, its all about the Vietnam war, but he's a really good teacher and really nice and helpful!
Class is centered around Vietnam War, but is still fairly interesting. He is extremely helpful and knowledgeable. Normally sympathetic on late work too. Overall great professor.
He loves the Vietnam War, but really helpful and cool.

He is obsessed with the Vietnam war and everything that you do is about it, but if you just follow the direction in the assignment for the papers, you can usually get a pretty decent grade on them. He is a very fair grader and a nice guy. He is also good about letting people turn stuff in later without penalty.
Decently interesting class. 3 papers which are a huge chunk of the grade. Pretty easy papers, though. No tests, rarely any quizzes (which are super easy). Overall a great teacher.

This class is a lot more slanted toward Vietnam than actual English rhetoric, etc. Very interesting stuff but only if you're into history/films. Really easy to work with and accessible but his grading is debatable and he's not precise in laying out how he grades papers. Talks a lot about "earning points" but never mentions how. Fun class though.
Good teacher! Very helpful with essay writing. cancels class sometimes and doesn't make you stay till the end of class if everything on the syllabus is done for that day! Fairly easy grader too!

Great teacher, he earned my respect by not keeping us in class when there was nothing else for us to. He often let us out early on Fridays and makes you turn in a rough draft for corrections on each paper which is very helpful. He was very sweet and enthusiastic about his subject.

Did not enjoy this class. He enjoys "fluffy" writing, so basically if you just blab on about nothing in your writings you'll get a better grade than if it's actually good. He doesn't use proper English in his e-mails which bothers me because he's an English teacher. Slow grader. Doesn't use blackboard. Failed to tell me my grade when I asked.

Very good professor. You will do alot about the Vietnam War, which isnt that hard. And the three essays you will write arent bad at all. You can tell he really enjoys English, and it shows in his teaching. Not a hard class, would take another class with him if given the opportunity. Oh and his daughter is ADORABLE (if he brings her in)

I enjoyed having him as a teacher but truthfully it was more of a history class than an english class. We learned so much about the Vietnam War. :S It was a fun class o attend and he was not only easy to get a hold of but also fun to talk to. But truthfully i didnt enjoy his choice in assigned writings..a little confusing
No Comments

Great teacher. A lot of fun but doesn't like technology much and doesn't use blackboard.  But he's really passionate about what he is teaching and really wants his students to learn.  Fun class. I really enjoyed it.
if you study the problem sets he says will be on the test and go to class you'll do fine. he's a great guy and wants us to succeed. take advantage because barely any other chem profs are that way.
Great professor.  Funny, clear, teaches at a nice pace.
Great teacher. Clear, concise, easy tests. Just like the practice ones.
Hilarious teacher, informative class, aceable tests.  What more could you ask for in a chem class?

Dr. Yao is a really nice guy and helps out a lot outside of class. I would often email him for homework help at 11pm the night of the due date and he would still respond and help out. Lectures are a bit rough as far as retaining information and this class is lot of just learning by failure, but Dr. Yao is extremely helpful along with his TA Samuel.

I had no experience with coding before this class, and he made it easy to learn. It actually helped me to decide on my track. He answers emails almost right away and is super helpful if you encounter any questions about assignments. Make sure to read assigned readings and pay attention in class, and you're good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was definitely very hesitant to take this class online, but it turned out well! Dr. Yao is very responsive to emails and I would highly recommend asking him (or the tas) any homework questions you might have! I did not have any programming experience before this class, so I did get the textbook. It was definitely helpful to explain some concepts.

Pretty good class for an online programming course. Didn't have any MATLAB knowledge before taking this class and I did fine. Homework is very important for your grade, he and his TA's both give good feedback if things are incorrect. 3 exams, usually pull questions from the quizzes he gives. Not a bad class, do well on the homework.

For an online set up, this class is very easy to stay motivated. There are multiple lecture videos per week, but each are less than 10 minutes and are very easy to understand. There were only very few times where I was lost on how to do something. Assignments and tests follow what have been taught in lectures. Very nice professor.

This man is so nice and always willing to help you understand the material! The lectures were recorded which was nice. He helped me discover an interest in programming, which I knew nothing about before taking this class.

Was a really nice guy and took the time to make sure you really understand every step of the coding process. He wanted me to succeed and would take as much time out of his schedule to help me when I needed. Tests weren't terribly difficult but not the easiest either.

While the class might've been easier if I had some previous experience in coding, there were very few times I knew what I was actually doing. I constantly felt lost during the class and the explanation he gave as to why things were done this specific way were very minimal. If it weren't for my other classmates I 100% would've failed this class >:(

I came in with no programming experience, and had no problem with this class. His recorded lectures were concise and easy to follow, I had no problem with understanding his accent. Definitely work heavy (HW takes up a lot of time) but I found the class enjoyable and challenging! Just make sure you keep up with the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had some programming knowledge beforehand, so my review of the class is a bit biased. I thought it was a moderate difficulty class, def put in hours for the homeworks and used a lotta googling of code. That helps a lot. Dr. Yao is approachable after class or for office hours as well. Very-mild mannered and patient. I like him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great class and i learned a lot

A very friendly guy with a moderate accent which can be distracting to the untrained ear.  The weekly HW takes about 3-4 hours depending on whether you do the extra credit.  I had trouble with the exams as you had to program under time pressure which is a double whammy.  Strongly recommend the help sessions & the HW should not be done alone.
Very helpful in understanding material. Really knowledgeable on class topics.
Great person, I think he is better than the typical professor being he is a lawyer. Likes to talk but lectures were good.
Gives great examples and prepares you very very well for the exam. Tells you everything you need to study. Learned a lot and made the lectures interesting when the topics can be boring
he sold my 4.0
Amazing professor, great guy, would love to have him again. Uses a lot of good examples and personal experiences to make things easier to understand.
George is a cool guy

George is by far the best lecturer I have had at Mizzou.  He is very passionate in what he teaches and makes his lectures entertaining.  The exams are difficult but he does prepare you well for them.  There is a group presentation but it's relatively easy.  10/10 would take a class with George again.
George brand is a great professor! His lectures are informative and about as entertaining as they can be. His tests are tough, but given the course material could be a lot worse.

Professor Brand is a great instructor. This is a tough course, and he manages to make it digestible. I truly recommend this class especially with brand because he gives you everything you need to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, review lecture slides and quizzes and tests are fine

Great class, George is an outstanding professional who challenges students to excel. The tests are tough, but using the "Half-baked study guide" to create your own will set you up for success. Attend class regularly—George's teaching style ensures you earn your grade through effort.

George is one of the best professors I've had during my time here at Mizzou. He is extremely knowledgable about what he is teaching in this course and he is also accessible outside of class for any questions/concerns. The class is tough but if you study and apply yourself it's not bad at all. Go to class.

Loved the class with Professor Brand. I wish there were opportunities for extra credit as the tests were hard. The tests have a curve which helps somewhat but if you don't study you will have a hard time passing. Professor Brand did a good job of keeping me engaged during his online lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Excels as a Business Law instructor, has engaging and enjoyable lectures with great explanations and examples of legal concepts. One of my favorite professors to date and I am a junior. Although some exams have a ton of content, making it a bit overwhelming at times. Still highly recommend his course!

So far at Mizzou this has been my favorite class, and Professor Brand has arguably been my favorite professor. His passion for teaching and his background as an attorney make his lectures engaging and creditable. Engaging with students, he creates an environment that encourages questions. Put in the work and go to class and an A is very attainable

Great professor and actually practiced law before coming to teach it. Mr. Brand is always prepared, and engaged, and keeps things relevant and interesting. Great class, great exams, and great energy. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lowkey kinda cute

I took George Brand's Business Law course last semester and it was a very rough class for myself and many of my peers. His class is mainly based on the exams and the exam answers could be almost any of the options he lists. He gives you the option to challenge his questions/answers but never takes them into consideration anyway.

Professor Brand was one of my favorite professors. He cares a lot about the students and wants to be the best professor he can be, so he's always asking for student input and is very reasonable/professional. His slides in class are very clear and he explains things very very well. Not a blowoff class, but study & you'll be fine. go to exam reviews!

Overall a great professor; requires lots of reading but puts most important material for the exams in his lecture slides so if you study those notes you have a great chance of doing well on exams. Very well respected professor who I would gladly take a course from again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: George is awesome! I took B Law with him; it was his first semester teaching, but had he not told us that, I would never have known. He cares about his student's success and is extremely knowledgeable. Recommend reading the assigned chapters before attending lecture. 10/10 recommend and I am excited to take a class with him again next semester
Professor Brand was a very nice professor had him for his first semester of teaching and he was very funny and taught engaging content

He's super passionate and presents the information in a really interesting way. There's no homework and he gives you a cheat sheet on the tests that basically has everything you need to know on it so it's super easy to get an A.

I loved this professor, the course was very interesting literally because of him. He is a really passionate teacher and actually cares about his students and the course. I would definitely buy the textbook just because you do use them during the discussion posts. overall a great class, however he is ant-technology so buy a notebook!!!

Gesiel was one of my favorite instructors. Lectures are interesting and easy to listen and follow along to. There is no home work, only a few optional readings. Participation is worth 20% of your grade. He makes it easy to participate, at the end of each class you will answer a question on a note card and turn it in. Cannot recommend Gesiel enough.

I absolutely LOVE Gerri. She is charismatic and understanding. I was working a full time job and she was very understanding of that (I took the class over the summer). JMC302 is a homework and lecture heavy class because it is just research, but she makes it easy to understand. She gives great feedback, and is helpful with writing and researching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gerri is a well-spoken and cares a lot about her students. The class was well planned out and had a lot of ways to earn points easily. The only thing that's difficult is the error spotter that's due each week, and it's not necessarily hard, just tedious. Overall, I would recommend.
Takes up the entire lecture time, when other professors teaching the same course do not. Gets carried away in conversations very easily, be prepared to online shop for an hour or two.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Geisert is hilarious to listen to. His labs are amazing and very fun, but his lectures can be a bit scattered with slides not matching to the handout. He is one of the best to talk to if you are struggling with the material, he is always willing to help. He is retiring so he isn't around much, but snag him if you can.

Dr. Geisert is literally my favorite professor ever. If you are a student who cares and does well, he will let you know. His exams are fairly easy considering you can predict a majority of the questions he asks based on how much time in class he spent on each section. It is easy to get a good grade if you just tried.

Dr. Geisert is one of the best professors I've had at Mizzou. He really seems to care about how you do in the class and he goes over and above in terms of review sessions and making the class as fun as possible!

Do not take this class. First of all, the class is literally ran by TA's, you never actually even see the professor. You are only graded on three tests and 12 labs. The labs are worth 5 points each and nothing is weighted, so if you don't do well on an exam, your grade in this class will suffer. You basically teach the material to yourself as well.

AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS. The grading outline is horrible and unclear. Your tests and in class labs are weighted the same (meaning if you bomb a test you're screwed the rest of the semester). Half of his TA's don't even want to teach the class and overall this lab is a horrific mess. STAY AWAY FROM THIS COURSE.

I had Dr. Summers for my WI Invert Zoology class. He is funny and engaging, despite not knowing the "lingo" of the students (as he would say). He uses slides for diagrams and important concepts, so you need to pay attention. I had a paper due almost every week and exams biweekly. He got to know the class by name. I definitely recommend him!

You will never meet this man, the TAs run the class. Labs were confusing and didn't teach you which makes studying for tests extremely difficult. Your grade is made up of three tests, if you do badly on one, good luck. Our TA said that they noticed three wrong test questions, told Dr. Summers and he was like "just have them take the test" WHAT?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm lucky in that I'm a science minded person and also that the TA I had for my lab section was pretty alright at teaching, however be warned that unless you have to make up a test for something, you won't see Dr. Summers at all. Labs were chaotic and sometimes confusing because he makes his own lab manual, and tests can be confusing at times.

Dr. Summers is a great teacher. I had him for both my capstone and invert-zo. He is very passionate about the material he teaches and tries to keep discussion open and light-hearted. The exams in invert-zo are difficult, and you really need to come to class and try to take detailed notes, my notes always saved me when preparing for exams. Recommend

There is a writing assignment every week if WI course. Content can be boring, but he makes everything fun to learn about. Tests are not the easiest and are mostly short answers, also grades semi-harshly on papers. Lectures aren`t mandatory, but most exam questions come from in class. He's funny and passionate, so I enjoyed this course requirement.

This class sucks. I've never had this big a problem getting a good grade on an exam since entering college. It's led by TA's who don't do that great of a job teaching, seeing as all the exam scores average around 35 (70). There are 3 exams and then lab work worth 5 points a week. You get no instructional help on the labs until after it's done.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Being in Dr. Summerss class has been extremely frustrating, as he has not taught us a thing, literally.
