All semester it has been only his TA, who is not a teacher nor an education major, teaching us. He has done nothing to benefit me academically, and quite frankly, because he isnt the one teaching us, I do not know what he does with his time.

Dr. Summers is an amazing lecturer! He will hold you attention and keep you engaged! The course material was interesting and I learned a ton. The class was writing intensive, so there were 10 papers, but it's nothing too crazy! This was the best biology class I took at Mizzou!
I had this man's course all the way back in 1990. He's still there ! He's a good man.

It's a lot of work reading papers and writing about them. Make sure you take good notes and talk in class!! He jokes around a lot and is a fun professor. Just make sure you show him you're trying and you should get an A.

Dr. Summers is an amazing professor. His informal lecture style held my attention every day. He's the least pretentious professor I've had and the easiest to approach. The lab is difficult, but not impossible, and the WI portion is kind of a joke. I don't know what the people leaving negative comments were expecting, it's a 3000 level course.
Very rude individual. He enjoys throwing his weight around and intimidating students. Very sarcastic to his students. I would advise trying to find another professor....avoid!

Dr. Summers class wasn't bad. He likes to keep his lectures informal and jokes around a lot. His tests are very fair if you have good notes. The lab of this class has tons of taxonomy but not impossible. The WI portion is fairly easy. Overall Dr. Summers was a fun professor to have which makes Inv. zoo fairly interesting.
Dr. Summers is hilarious and so nice. His class is REALLY hard but he's wonderful. He's a real stickler for grades though.

almost IMPOSSIBLE to pass his class, let alone the lab that goes with it. Made students uncomfortable and intimated to approach him. He thinks everyone in his class is a bio major, and should just get everything. GOOD luck if you have him, i took this class my freshman year, and it was the hardest class i ever took at this school.
This class was very easy. Prof summers was always helpful and flexible with letting me have extra time for my tests.
Quite possibly the best teacher I have ever had
He made class interesting, even for such a dull topic.

Exams are very difficult. Questions will always throw you off by asking something obscure. One question per exam will be worth 33% of your exam grade and it'll be over one slide from lecture. Every time I went for clarification on anything I left more confused than when I started.

Exams are truly all that matters in this class. There are four assignments and one group project, but they can only hurt your grade or keep it the same. She is very strict about talking and about phones being out. The lectures are posted but a lot of the information is not on them. She uses iClickers but will never discuss the correct answers.

This professor clearly does not want students to succeed. She is extremely strict about phones and talking to people around you. The grading in this class is strictly based on tests, one project, and iClicker points. The professor doesn't even go over iClicker questions in class. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't want her students to succeed, and it's evident in her grading and teaching. If one kid does something wrong, like cheating or taking the test in a different location, she will punish the entire class even if she knows who the student is. She even said in one of my classes, "I would really like you guys to pass my class, but."

She is a harsh teacher and makes the class one I dread going to. A lot of the times she asks us what we know about the topic before she teaches it and gets frustrated when we don't know even though she hasn't even taught it to us yet. The whole class is tests so if you do poorly on all of them that is your grade.

The definitions that professor provides for terms presented in class are usually very different than the definitions that are in the book. She seems to not understand anything about the concept she is teaching, several times she gives false information about common sense topics (such as listing the 5 senses as touch, taste, hear, see, and pain).

Professor changes the syllabus many times. The entire course is graded off of 4 exams and 1 "mini project". Each exam covers 4 chapters of the textbook, each class period covers roughly 2 chapters and is presented on a Powerpoint that we are not given access to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for both chem 2 and organic 2. He is very organized and overall does a good job. He tells you what to prioritize when studying for exams, keep in mind these aren't the easiest classes altogether and do require extra study time outside of class but as far as a professor goes he's one of the best in MU's chem department.
I love Dr. Reynders! I have had him for chem 2 and organic 2 and he is a great teacher and is willing to help students understand material! I like going to his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very well structured and as long as you show up and do the work you will be good.

I took his class directly after I took chem 1 and passed, I dropped chem II midway. Reynders was my chem II professor. His lectures were difficult to understand, he jumped around a lot and I ended up going to tutoring for every homework assignment in order to learn the content. He is difficult to work with if you're disabled.
Very hard professor, the exams are tough, but the homework is pretty easy.

Very much lecture heavy, but all information given is important. Tests were multiple choice and homework is easy with unlimited attempts. Go to office hours if you are confused, they help a ton. He is very understanding, especially if you go to office hours and keep in touch. Just be an active learner and go back through the slides after class.

His class (Chem 1410) is very easy if you get 100 on all the homework (infinite attempts) and participate in all the in class iclicker quizzes because they are most of your grade. He is a mediocre lecturer but this is only his 3rd year so cut him some slack. He is very strict about grade rounding, he wont do it....ever.

I took CHEM1320H the semester Dr. Reynders started at Mizzou, and it was clear that he was uncomfortable lecturing in front of a large group of students. His lectures were never super engaging, and he often skipped over vital points (while focusing too heavily on minor points). The labs were doable but had to be changed because of incorrect design.

He's is evidently new to teaching but he cares and is very approachable, I would recommend studying well for his exams using the material he gives in class and for homework. Labs were okay but nothing to write home about (as I imagine an intro chem class will be).
Great if you're okay with going through material fast. Tough but manageable if you're not into that.

His lectures were confusing and he admittedly taught the class backwards. He struggled to fluently answer questions, and although I got an A in AP Chemistry last year, I managed to get a B- in his class. The textbook was not helpful and labs were poorly thought out. They mostly consisted of watching water boil, and the TA was consistently confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lecture were difficult to follow with not many thorough examples to break up the slides. He was extremely passive aggressive in answering questions even though he continuously asked if anyone had any.

Gil was an interesting man. His lectures were very long and hard to follow, especially outside of class. He never used a mic so it was hard to understand and he made everything so complicated and didn't explain things very clearly. Passive-aggressive with crazy facial expressions but he's a nice guy. Do the homework and study and you'll pass

If you've taken chem in high school you should be fine, but if not good luck. His slides are impossible to follow when your trying to study them on your own. He overcomplicates simple concepts. Seems like he does know what he's talking about, but he does not know how to teach. And his tests are like quizzes so missing 1 question will give you a B.

I learned nothing in this class. I had to receive outside tutoring for this class for every test. If it wasn't for my tutor, I would have failed the class.

It was Chem 2 class but 50% of the material is Organic Chemistry 2 information. My chem major tutor didn't know half the stuff. Class average on majority of the tests were 50%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Reynders is a nice professor and answers emails quickly. We had to purchase a digital textbook which we never used. It's basically there if you want to understand concepts better. His slides are sometimes hard to follow along with and some lectures were fast paced. Exams had very few questions so missing one question quickly lowered your grade.

Dr.Reynders is not good at teaching. His slides are impossible to follow outside of class, and there is never a clear definition written in the slides. The tests are so short missing one question can bring your grade down 9%, and the labs never line up with class/have new material. I only did well because I learned this material before.
This guy is a good researcher, but switching up the way exams are taken halfway into the semester and what you're tested on doesn't help anyone. The average for all 4 exams was 68%.
I can tell he's passionate about what he teaches but he constantly rambles all class and it's so hard to retain any information. I still did decent because he grades relatively easily.

This is the best, most caring professor at Mizzou. Dr Gibson is very evidently educated and intelligent in philosophy and intellectual thought behind the founding era. The class is engaging and fun. You walk away from the semester understanding the background thought of so much. 
No homework, seminar style, two 500 word essays, and 2 exams.

Gibby is truly awesome! Taken two classes with him and have yet to get tired of him. He does love to talk quite a lot during his lectures but its all information that helps with his papers. He is a very relaxed grader and offers a ton of feedback on your papers. In both classes I've had with him there is a group project but it is not too difficult.

Even though this is only a 2000 level class, don't take it if you're not well-versed in political journalism/commentary. Even though he claims to be open-minded, Gibson has a bad habit of taking points off of assignments if your views don't directly align with his. He also doesn't respond to emails, and his critiques on papers are barely legible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gibson has by far been the highlight of my time in college. Be sure to really pay attention to his lectures because that is where the papers will come from. He truly loves his students and what he is teaching and it is obvious. He does tend to ramble and go off topic, however he offers very deep insights to all of the topics he teaches.

The highlight of my semester fr. I know very few people who are half as knowledgeable and intelligent as Prof Gibson. He's so passionate about his field and about helping students engage critically with democracy-related subjects. I always looked forward to his lectures, and how he related them back to student experiences.

Literally one of my favorite professors ever. Super sweet and gives great feedback. Just make sure to listen, take notes, and participate in lecture. It will help you immensely during essays, especially for the midterm and final. He was really good at pulling out deeper analysis from students through his questions. Wish I had more classes with him.

One of the kindest male professors ever. He cares so much about his students and genuinely wants to hear from everyone. He pays attention and is so extremely educated. Show up to class and participate. Take notes during his lectures in your own words that you'll understand later. It will help you with the papers. LISTEN TO HIM.

I really enjoyed the way he lectured. You can tell he is very passionate about the topic and allows for students to discuss topics in an open environment. I would recommend Mr. Gibson and Poli_Sci2860
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor absolutely loved him! Always gives good feedback and will allow the discussion to naturally progress. Lots of reading but always willing to help after class with papers. If you have the chance absolutely take a class with him.

One of the nicest professors I've had, genuinely cares about his students. Provides readings for free. Essays are difficult but he offers feedback and guides you through the process. Traditional lecture style, doesn't use Powerpoint so can be hard to follow at times. Hard work pays off in this class, work for him and he'll do the same for you.

I think Professor Gibson's class was very informative, but her lack of lesson planning and condescending behavior made it hard for me to participate in her lectures. There were several classes where she "didn't feel like teaching" but kept us for the class period talking about topics that had nothing to do with the class. Felt like a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I absolutely loved my time in class with Dr. Gibson. She is a joy to listen to and interact with in discussions. She definitely rewards creativity. 
Frankly, any hiccups came from students being unresponsive, inattentive, or unwilling to go with the flow. 

You have to go with the flow. 
Adapt or die. 
That's life. 

Thesis: you WILL be fine, TRY!

Dr. Gibson is one of my all-time favorites at Mizzou. I took all 4 of the honors humanities classes with her. Her classes can be difficult, but I ended up being super proud of my work and she pushes you to be your absolute best. Extremely kind and personable. Cannot recommend her enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Gibson is incredibly passionate and inspires students to look beyond an assignment as just an assignment... I had a challenging semester and she met me with kindness and patience. Truly such a unique and fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gibson was amazing! I love her grading style; it places emphasis on creating something you're proud of and take interest in rather than conforming to a certain standard to be graded on a set scale. It's just the class I needed to feel more confident in my own creative abilities. She is always willing to talk with you about improvement.
If someone told me I had to take a class she taught again I would rather drop out of college.

She is very disorganized. She only gives a few assignments and they pop up randomly, none are listed in the syllabus. Classes drag on because it doesnt seem like she prepares anything. Grading is the worst, she never actually grades anything and takes forever to give any sort of feedback. I will never be taking her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pre-March 2020, I would have already given Dr. Gibson high marks for her absolutely amazing lectures. I am an easily distracted person, but I never found myself obsessively checking my phone or the clock, and the class would fly by. After students were sent home, she did an amazing job adapting the class to be online-friendly!

This is not an easy class at all!!!! You do not have any homework to pad your grade. Only tests and quizzes so if you fail any of them you are screwed. If you do not read all the chapters and don't go to class you will not even be close to passing. Tests and quizzes are worded very weird which makes them very hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Gibson was a fantastic teacher, she is funny and extremely upbeat. She is always willing to answer your questions, and meet up with you to help you better understand if you were struggling. If you are even the slightest bit interested in music history its a very interesting and fun because your listening to music through most of it. All Great.
Had trouble learning from her techniques. Tries to make it fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gibson is all over the place. She repeated th/o the semester "I don't know what I'm supposed to teach" & "oh, they won't let me teach that" and the lectures were sloppy. She made the whole class uncomfortable by staring at us daily during discussion. We had no idea what the lectures were even about.

Gibson was hilarious throughout class and made the subject matter interesting. As long as you don't sleep in class, she is pretty chill. Honestly, you can either read the book or go to lectures. The quizzes and exams cover both.

I skipped maybe 2 or 3 classes, studied hard before the tests and finished with an A-. I loved the course content- very interesting and I personally enjoyed learning and studying about it all! Dr. Gibson was also funny and her lectures were great. Go to class, pay attention, ask questions, listen to the music and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is honestly one of  my favorites. If you are not a music person, it will be hard. You need to take notes and read the book but as long as you study it will be ok. It's not an easy a, but she does try hard to make you succeed. If you know little about anything related to music, I suggest not taking this class. will be hard but I love it!

The following is proving to be a problem: Rigidly opinionated thought process; her naturally confrontational and insecure emotional nature obstructs her ability to convey a clear message of the material, create an intellectual space or offer anything valid for discussion; she's disrespectful of student opinions and ideas and is not very self aware.

She's an amazing person. She really cares about you as a person. Just pay attention and put effort in. I would take it again for sure. There are a TON of books that you can find online or at a local library. I didn't read half the time and I was fine.

This class isn't the "easy A" that I thought it was.  It's barely an "easy C"... the least she could do is put the lecture slides online so we can review, but that would be too nice.  Instead she leaves us with the book which is way too broad for her specific test questions

Loved this class. She honestly cares how everyone does in the class. She set up study groups and gives you lots of opportunities to ask questions. Makes you want to learn and do well. And who doesn't love to learn about music. Attend all lectures and take notes and study and you'll be good. Didnt really read the book.

I really regret taking this class.  To be honest, part of me took this class for an "easy A", but I'll be darned if I get higher than a C.  Gibson is very energetic, and, at first glance, seems like a fun, helpful professor, but after about two classes the novelty wears off, and you are left with a very unaccommodating woman.  Undergrads beware.

One of the best classes I have ever taken! I learned so much and she had a great attitude. She was hilarious, informative, and always positive. Tests were easy peasy, and if you love music you'll love this class!

RUN... RUN FAR AWAY. This class was the worst one I've taken. She makes the class way harder than it should be. Questions on the test look like they are designed for failure. My class's average grade on one of the tests was a 60%, that should speak for itself. Don't take this class unless you like to get bad grades after studying for hours on end.

Gibson is really annoying as a teacher. The textbook is necessary and expensive. It's not hard if you go to class and take notes. Your grade rides on the tests and quizzes, so be prepared to study. She gives vague ideas of what to study but if you didn't come to class and take her notes, you'll miss a lot of what she asks for on tests and quizzes.

Trust me when I say this: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I thought this class would be interesting but it's hell, it should be called Jazz Pop and Race because that's we hear about. Tests are horrible,  there's no assignments so your grade is left at the mercy of the 3 impossible quizzes and test, and the final. Please just steer clear, it's not worth it.

She is a very interesting character. She is lively and joyous, and can be very funny at times. She likes it a lot when students participate, she kinda thrives on it to make class go smoothly. The topicssongs are boring at the beginning of class, but get much better throughout the semester.

I really liked Dr. Gibson. She was very funny and very animated and kept class interesting even when it was a boring subject. At times she was unclear about topics and got confused. She also puts a lot on her slides and it's hard to know what is important. It's pretty important to attend class to get her notes. But I really liked her as a person!
this class is awful, she refuses to put notes online and the only grades for the class is a few quizzes and exams. doesn't give updates on blackboard. hard to get better than a C in this class
Worst teacher I have ever had.  Rude and condescending.  Tests are nearly impossible.  Told our class we should all be happy with a "C" grade because that means we are average.
Professor Gibson is a great teacher! The class in interesting and you can tell she loves music. Make sure you go to class because there are clicker questions! I would recommend this class!

Maya was awesome and pretty easy. Classes are straight discussion, not really a need to even take notes. You go to 6 concerts for free and then write a review about them. The tests/papers are graded a little stingy, but it's not so bad.

Reynders is a great professor! I love his teaching style for orgo 2. He has pre planned slides and fills them in as he goes through lecture. He's very open to questions during class time and has plenty of office hours. Also he is very quirky and awesome!

This professor is very monotone in his lectures he talks at 20 miles an hour and acts like you know the material before you ever see it. Classes feel like a speed run of so many slides. He's a fine person just so hard to learn from.

Dr. Reynders is a great professor. Adjusting to his lecture style make take a class or two but if you attend class and take time out of class to work on the material you're set. Office hours were very helpful and exams weren't difficult if you put in the effort to understand the material.I would take another class with him teaching, very cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Wasn't that bad of a class, but you will probably have to go back over lectures and stuff, all the tests had mostly homework questions on them.
He's a good professor. He's young and makes sure you get the information. Holds extra office hours to meet for exams, and makes attendance easy to achieve.

Better than Keller for sure. Somehow the honors section was significantly easier than the regular section because Keller is simply that bad. Lectures were passable, tests weren't terrible, just an ok class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: dont take honors if u dont have to. i miss my cheat sheet:( he is much better than keller but i liked ganley the most. attendance is ur best friend or worst enemy. he loves "none of the above" as his exam answers (one exam was mostly those it was rough). he cares and is sweet but lectures don't directly connect to hw so ur on ur own for hw

He's not a very good lecturer, I was usually pretty confused by his lectures and had to teach myself a lot of material. The tests were mostly predictable though, all questions you'd see on the homework with a few exceptions.

Very much lecture heavy, but all information given is important. Tests were multiple choice and homework is easy with unlimited attempts. Go to office hours if you are confused, they help a ton. He is very understanding, especially if you go to office hours and keep in touch. Just be an active learner and go back through the slides after class.

I'm pretty bad at chemistry but Reynders made it rather easy to understand, his exams were very fair. Sometimes the delivery of the lectures was a bit monotone, but if you pay attention and study using his slides you will do well in his class

Reyenders wasn't an awful professor, very monotone and reads off slides. You can attend class, do iClicker via zoom. Homework should be 100% if you do it on time, multiple attempts allowed. 4 exams, and cumulative mandatory final. No notecards. I thought the tests were ok, there was challenging content and you have to really know it for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are effective and he's extremely good at answering/explaining questions

VERY lecture heavy and monotone, but he gets all of the important information out. Very clearly structured class, and attendance via iClicker is important. Tests were all multiple choice and the homework wasn't too bad.

He does a lot of talking and not a lot of demonstrating. if you are a visual learner this might become a more difficult class. He tends to rush over important things for the exam. he also talks about topics that aren't even relevant to the current material. He is also an extremely fast talker so taking notes and following along becomes difficult

Test problems and homework problems not clearly explained during lecture. Very quickly skims over large concepts while still expecting students to excel at them on exams. Lectures seem unorganized and hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Like with any class, you need to understand the prereq to do well. He is very willing to help students understand the material and has supplemental sessions + office hours. He gets annoyed when people don't pay attention but I think that's fair. The hw is not overwhelming. Test heavy but it forces you to learn &  easiest hw questions go on exam.
All lectures are posted online and practices given in class are like the tests

Pr. Reynder's class started out normally with introductions. Then he went on to the lecture portion, and it all went down from there. He does not care about his students. This is shown through his very few outside of class resources, failure to adapt his teaching style or slides, and his lack of instructions to lab TAs. Wouldn't take again.

Reynder's speaks very fast and talks about topics like we have a background in them. Office hours are rushed too. He quickly answers questions and doesnt go into the depth needed to understand. His lecture slides are confusing and do not transport to canvas/ powerpoint correctly.
Hard to understand what he was teaching as he didn't teach it like a GENERAL chemistry course.

He was an "OK" professor. This was his 1st year. Often times, a student would ask a question in class and he did not know the answer. He is sassy and will not curve your grade at the end of the semester even if you have an 89.9%. His 1st and 3rd exams were easy but study hard for the 2nd and 4th exams. The final is cumulative but it wasn't awful.

the worst part was his lecturing. He spoke pretty monotone and read off slides that were hard to follow. Most of the time i had no idea what was going on in class and had to reteach myself on my own. His exams were all MC which was both a blessing and a curse bc yes you can guess but they were short so missing a few questions tanked your grade.

Dr. Reynders is not good at lecturing. His slides are impossible to follow outside of class and he never gives a clear deffiniton. Labs and HW don't match with the current course material, and tests are so short if you miss two questions your grade is in the 80s. The only saving grace is the material is easy and often done in high schools.

Dr. Reynders is very disorganized when giving his lectures. He often changes his slides while lecturing because the information he has written down "isn't correct". Not only this, but the information he often relays to us students is often wrong, which he catches by the next lecture or forgets to tell us until the last minute prior to the test.

Professor Reynders isn't a bad guy, but his lectures are mostly just him reading off of a power point in a very monotone voice. His lack of expression makes it very difficult to focus on what he is saying, as he reads everything in the same tone. He uses iClicker to take attendance, but you can use zoom to attend if you would like.

Heads up. His course setup is extremely hard to keep up with in general. The labs aren't in sync with the lectures but rather cover topics of their own so make sure to read ahead of time. Do not look at the due dates as when they're due. His exams cover homework due after the exam so get used to doing the homework as early as possible.

He rarely teaches anymore, but if you end up seeing him teaching a class. I would say run. He is absolutely hilarious, but his exams are literally an LSD trip. Study the Taco Bell menu more than the lectures. Had to fight demons for my grade. Told him I had ADHD & Dyslexia during office hours and he said “DAYUMN'

He is extremely rude and condescending to students in a way he poorly attempts to disguise as humor, and bad at teaching. He constantly rants during lectures and draws illegibly on the chalkboard instead of using his slides. Be ready to commit a lot of time to teaching yourself the material, and you will be fine, but it will not be a fun semester.

Constantly said: "I don't care about your opinion, I don't care what you think is fair, I will not remember you." Talked down to students he didn't like, curves heavily for his favorites. Office hours are important but he is very vague don't expect actual answers. He makes you take "hypothesis elimination" quizzes every week that most people fail.

Professor can be blunt, but go to office hours - he'll remember you and be more helpful. Utilize Unstuck AI and the free textbook to stay on top of this challenging course. Worth the effort for the generous curve.

My biggest advice: 
- don't let him intimidate you at the beginning, you'll fail before you do well 
- don't worry too much about your grade, he curves majorly 
- go. to. office. hours. regularly. 
- make sure you have adequate time to dedicate to this class 
- utilize his accommodations, he's very respectful of them! 
- don't take him too serious

This professor was rude and condescending. He basically just told everyone that they were not going to make it into medical school without taking his class and then proceeded to take most class periods talking about drinking and his love for spiders. He only favored you if you went to office hours, and curved the grades favoring those who did.

Dr. Garcia is the professor version of Dr. House. He leans into his poor reviews, making people think he is a horrible professor. In reality, Garcia cares about his students and wants them to learn and be successful. (class avg 3.4) If you actually want to learn and be successful, you should take his course, but you NEED to go to office hours.

Generally rude, other than with his favorite girls. Brags about only looking over slides 5min before lecture. Consistently stated "What is impactful to you, will not be impactful to me" and "I will NOT remember you". Huge ego& belittles you. Talked about getting drunk during class/OH. Interesting content but can't stand this guy. Academia's worst
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is hard as well as the exams. However, the weekly quizzes that are offered help you prepare for the exams. Don't let yourself fall behind and go to office hours frequently. I studied maybe 1-2 days before each exam and still ended up receiving over 100% after the curve. It's a doable class, you just need to put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The teacher was unapproachable for any type of question. The tests are non-descriptive and based on movies. His curves can be nice unless you are average because he grades based on the standard deviation. My year he dropped the final test and averaged the other 4 tests for the 5th test score. The teacher also comes off as rude and impatient.

reviews.comment: 100 weekly quizzes+400 reading quizzes+500 tests (5)1000 (.7*lecture)*(.3*lab)grade. The hypothesis questions he puts on the end of quizzes and the tests are incomprehensible. At the end of the semester I still had no clue how to answer the questions on his tests. I knew the information well for tests and still did bad. He does "curve" each test.

This class is insanely hard, but Garcia knows that. His curve involves taking the average for the exam, adding the standard deviation and thats max score for the exam. Don't be scared if you have him. YOU MUST GO TO OFFICE HOURS. Literally once he knows your name and a little about you, he's great. He will make fun of his favorite students in class

His officer hours werent any better. He regularly mocked students questions and didnt foster an environment conducive to learning. Best way I can describe him is jerk

Avoid this professor if possible. Exams are difficult and unnecessarily strange and confusing. He tries to use a movie plot as a framing mechanism for his exams, and he ends up getting more in depth in the narrative portion of the exam than he does in actually giving useful information to answer the question. Take different prof if possible!

reviews.comment: Considering this class was at the capstone level, he was the most amazing professor I've ever had. Honestly understood that we're busy seniors and made my life a lot easier. The class definitely lived up to expectation material wise; I learned about what I was interested in just for the enjoyment of learning it for once.

reviews.comment: He is very used to joking with his students. On the anniversary of my best friend's death I had this class. He tried joking with me several times & he could tell that this made me really upset (I was in a bad place and did not want to have to engage in class) after class he pulled me aside to be supportive. It was really genuine.

Worst teacher ever. Only class I have ever failed in my life. Insults students. Friend had to sue him. The worst. He begged some of his students to rate him positively on this site, so beware of the nonsense.

One of my favorite professors I've had. Going to class is like going to a comedy show. This guy is hilarious! The jokes he tells are all relevant to the material and help tremendously in remembering it. My TA, Scott, was also very helpful and nice. Great professor overall! Definitely my favorite Bio class I've taken, probably due to him teaching.
Tests were difficult, but he was funny and good at lecturing

Took this class after receiving a W in Dr. Zhang's class the prior semester. On that note, AVOID DR. ZHANG AT ALL COSTS. Dr. Garcia is the absolute funniest teacher I have ever had. His lectures are very informative and he won't move on until everyone understands. He encourages you to ask questions and is available for additional help through email

He was an interesting teacher. He kept me engaged. Although attendance isn't mandatory, I would recommend going every day. I wouldn't trust that you'll be able to understand someone else's notes. He goes completely off lecture. If you can get ahold of old tests, that would sufficiently help you. Garcia is a teacher you should really get to know.
Tests are ridiculously hard.  He deliberately tries trip up students.  He can be extremely rude to students if they annoy him.  He doesn't mind embarrassing students in class.

If you want accurate information about him, look for posts made after the beginning of the semester.  (e.g., after the beginning Feb 2014); i.e., after the first test.  He bribes students with extra credit to give him a good rating BEFORE the first test. Some decisions, such as changing test dates, are hugely unfair to the majority of students.
gud stuf
Dr. Garcia is like a younger, more distinguished version of George Lopez.
If you have to take this class, take it with Dr. Garcia. Your life isn't complete without him in it. Go ahead. Take my word and sign up for HIS class. It'll be your best decision yet.
Dr. Garcia is the best professor I've ever had!
Good teacher. Teaches well.
Dr. Garcia... SO fly
One of a kind professor.
Dr. Garcia is hilarious! If you need a dose of laughter, his class is the place to go. Not to mention his wonderful sense of style. Enough said!
He is so interesting I could sit there for 2 hrs listening to him read the dictionary.

Mr.  Garcia is like a catalyst.  He increases the speed of which I learn.  His lectures are very informative, insightful, and I am grateful that I have him as my Biology professor.  For all he does, he should demand more... but like a neutron, he has no charge.

There are truly no words to describe how much of a genius this man truly is. He is brilliant, dresses like a Greek God, and keeps the laughter coming in class. His class is A1 like the steak sauce. There will never be a dull moment. Who knew learning about biology could be so fun? I dare you not to have him as a teacher.

This guy, is the bee's knees. The cat's pajamas. He does with Cell Biology what Da Vinci did with the Renaissance, makes it his... being of lesser value. He dominates this field like the Seahawks dominated the Broncos in the Super Bowl. To top it all off, he does it better than a comedy routine by Gabriela Iglesias.
What I have learned from Garcia thus far: Don't raise your hand.

This class should be renamed Cell Biology - Marine Corps Style.  He insults you to break you down so that you can feel better about yourself when you do something right (which isn't very often!) Fun class!
Dr Garcia makes his class extremely entertaining and fun to go to!

If you took the looks of Enrique Iglesias, the funniness of Will Ferrell, and the brain of Albert Einstein and then fused it all into one superhuman person, the result would be Dr. Garcia. What else would you want in a professor besides hotness, funnies, and brains?
This guy makes his class interesting. He tries to be funny but overdoes sometimes. All in all, great class.
Professor Garcia--a doctor of Biology, a captain of industry, and a king among men.

Dr. Garcia is the pinnacle of Latino intelligence in the biological field! The combination of his powerhouse level of knowledge combined with the driest of dark humor make the class enjoyable to attend.
This Cell Bio Connoisseur only enhances his charm with his sassy commentary that elevates his class to the entertainment level of SNL.
Is a tough teacher, but makes each class extremely interesting and funny.

I absolutely despise going to this class, it's the worst hour of my day. I went to his office hours but they werent helpful. He talks to fast and if you ask him to repeat something he will sarcastically repeat back the few words you said. I honestly can't wait until I'm done with this class and never have to deal with him again. Stay away.
Don't be scared to ask for help when you really need it. He will try to help however he can.

great professor, funny in class and helpful as well

Great teacher. Very clear and helpful.

Garcia's classes are both informative and entertaining.
I enjoy the lectures; he definitely keeps them interesting and explains things well. If you work hard and seek help instead of thinking it will just come to you, you should do well

Very sarcastic which I liked. Honest in his opinions of what you need to know. I was genuinely interested in what he had to say.
Very fun professor! Important to go to lecture everyday

Fun professor with interesting lectures.
He is a good teacher and presents his material very clearly.
He was great!
Very entertaining and interested in student learning. Only complaint is that he gave a practice test for the first exam but wouldn't discuss the answers so it was not very helpful.
Fantastic teacher. Truly cares about student leaning and very available for helping each individual succeed if they want to and have the drive. One f my favorite professors here.
He says it how it is. You actually obtain and learn information every class. His lectures are more like comedy hour with some biology thrown in the mix.
Go to class, take notes, ask questions, and go to his office hours.
Favorite BIO class thus far
Seems like a good guy. Genuinely cares  about students learning. Will answer any questions and offer help at office hours. Funny guy too.
Good guy, seems to genuinely care about students doing well. Willing to answer any questions and offer help at office hours. Funny guy too

make sure you go to class everyday! Go to his office hours from the start of the semester.

GO TO CLASS!! ask questions if you're unsure of anything. I like his teaching style. He tends to talk fast so compare notes with someone after class. Don't buy the book.
He is a great teacher, but beware of his "jokes"

I love the class, he is great.

He's a good teacher but very hard study and you will do well
Good teacher. Keeps the lecture very interesting and is treats us all like the adults we should be treated as.
Not an easy class, but he is always available to answer questions
Tough but cares that you do well and earn your grade.
Overall Great teacher, very hard tests but has a nice curve. Must go to class and take excellent notes and really understand the material not just memorize it.
Funny Professor. Just like all other classes, must work hard and know material.

Ask questions and work to understand the concepts instead of memorizing. Makes you think instead of just remembering. Great professor who creates an entertaining classroom dynamic.
