I took this class my freshman year in spring of 2011. If you can get past the "tough-guy" act, you can see that Garcia class is interesting. TAKE EXCELLENT NOTES. The book isn't necessary, so don't bother. Tests are hard, but there's a generous "curve" since lots of people tend to struggle. Try to beat the average (~60's on tests).

I cannot say enough good things about Professor Winter. She is so kind, caring, and fun to talk to; I'm so glad I took this class. There are zero tests which is very stress-relieving, just short papers here and there and some attendance-based work. The course content is very interesting and educational. Highly recommend this course and Dr. Winter!
Paper are graded pretty harshly, but the professor and the TAs are incredibly helpful and responsive.

Lectures were very interesting and relevant to the class and had all the information for the tests. The SIMS assignments were fun too! She gives great feedback on papers and has the bare minimum needed to be a writing-intensive class.

Dr. Ramseyer-Winter is the type of professor who truly cares about people doing well in her class. She doesn't make things too easy because she wants to challenge you, but she also takes into consideration student feedback and tries to teach the best she can. The content is very relevant and the class is not too hard at all. Highly recommended.

She is a great professor. Her class was one of my favorites. The class was discussion based, which was great because it really gave me the opportunity to learn from my peers and hear other viewpoints on social and economic justice issues. I came out of the semester feeling so much knowledgeable about the world around me. I'd def recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes at Mizzou. I learned so much in this class and how to apply it to my future career! I also enjoyed the service learning aspect, too! All Mizzou students should consider taking this class. Bonus: there are no tests, just a few papers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is writing intensive but there were only two papers and as long as you go into office hours and work on your papers with Ginny then you will do fine. Only had a midterm and a final and they were EASY! Ginny is awesome and super nice and always wanting to help. I highly recommend her class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Winter is the nicest teacher I've had on campus. She's very helpful and truly cares about her students success and personal issues if needed. Her class itself is interesting, but not easy. There is a lot of writing assignments that she grades fairly, but will point out mistakes. Only have a midterm and final, which are pretty tough. Great prof.
This was very hard and i did not like it
so bad i missed my cousins funeral to study the exam never take this class i promise you dont need it

This could be the worst class I've taken in the past 3 years. He is totally unorganized and almost schizophrenic. I do not understand what he expects of us for exams, or for projects. Totally lost. Thank you for nothing. Sorry.

(8420) Wow. I cannot believe how much content is in this course. We have 2.5 hour in class lectures and then he uploads hours of statistics lectures which are covered by exams. He is very vague about exam expectations. This feels like he doesn't know what he's doing or this class is new. Hardest accounting class I've taken in 2 years.

(DATA) Participation points because it's required by the uni. Talk about short articles for 2 seconds no time to contribute. Class hits 6 different software in depth. Too many to remember or learn. Lectures are 2.5 hours, he RUSHES because there's too much content. Class needs reorganizing. Projects are much harder than assignments/lecture work

I LOVE Professor Glendening! His class was incredibly well-structured and informative. I learned a lot and enjoyed his lectures. He is clearly passionate about his work and is highly intelligent while also making the concepts accessible to those without his knowledge. 

The exams were very difficult, but the curve he applies is very generous.

Said if it were up to him he wouldn't be giving exams then proceeds to give the hardest exams in the entire accounting department. Quizzes were harder than the other sections (to my best knowledge). Homework was pretty time consuming and only worth 2.5 points.

Glendening is a very smart guy, and is incredibly knowledgeable. Class is mostly taking notes from note packets. Study the quizzes for tests and be ready to sit the entire time to take those tests. Curves pretty hard, so passing the class is achievable, just go to class, pay attention and take good notes.

Dr. Glick is phenomenal. She is so helpful when approached with questions and she truly cares about her students, which isnt common at a university. She offers a ton of extra credit and goes out of her way to ensure that her students succeed. :)
She's a difficult grader and will take off one or two points on every assignment without explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor. Her gender freedom class was my favorite class ever. Unfortunately, it had to all be done online this semester due to the pandemic, but Dr. Glick made it as accessible and easy as she possibly could. Her lectures were very engaging and she facilitated class discussion so well. Would definitely recommend her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Glick is a very nice professor, but if you don't agree with her, say what she wants you to say, or interpret the text in her way, then you WILL lose points. Her grading criteria is shoddy and she lets her personal opinions get in the way a lot. She does seem to care about the topics, but it isn't worth the exchange when it's her way or the highway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was constantly taking off points if I wouldn't say exactly what she wanted to hear in the discussions. It was seriously every week she would find something new to count off for. You will have to read a lot of various articles, books, and watch different videos. Not that hard of a class, she's just extremely picky.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Glick really knows her stuff, which is admirable, but there is seriously so much reading. It's a little ridiculous for an entry class into gender studies. Also, she can make you feel a little dumb, not on purpose, but just because of the looks she sometimes gives and how much she knows about the subject. It made me not want to participate.

Love this professor! Totally devoted to literature, well versed in the field, and is super compassionate about both the subjects she teaches and her students. Discussions are a blast, and welcoming for everyone to join in and speak up. Class was so fun that we arranged an after-semester get together for pizza to chat and say our farewells.

Dr. Glick was knowledgeable in LGBT+ issues but lacked in other areas. Papers were graded inconsistently and not returned in a timely manner. The final had topics that were never discussed in class. While she claimed the classroom was a safe space, I often found her judgmental to people who may not have been aware of every LGBT+ term.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Elisa is very fun and energetic. Her class is enjoyable, even when the content isn't the greatest. She always made you feel intellectual when you spoke up (which is a must for her class). She tends to stutter over herself quite often, but I think it's because she gets excited--it's cute.

Prof. Glick is the best professor I have ever had. She is brilliant beyond compare. She made even the most difficult material accessible and fun. I enjoyed going to class and learned a lot. I also think Elisa is hot.
Amazing professor!  My favorite of all that I have had at MU.  Highly, highly recommended.
Elisa is a great teacher. She's smart and HILARIOUS. The work load is what you would expect from this type of class. She appreciates hard work and interest and grades accordingly.

Elisa is incredibly brilliant in her subject and encourages her students to think outside the box. There was a hefty and intense amount of reading, but it was FUN and INTERESTING material! Hard work but fascinating stuff and one of my favorite teachers at MU - spunky, well-read and disarming.
She's a great teacher. Really challenged my beliefs, and introduced me to so much new information. The courseload is hard and demanding, but she grades pretty easily if you try hard.

Elisa is an amazing professor.  She will challenge you to think in new ways and has a wonderful classroom demeanor.  She encourages everyone to give his or her opinion and makes the class as much about her students' views as her own.  She is certainly one of the best professors I've ever had.
She does not think her students are smart.  Because of this, she will crush your ego and do serious psychological damage to you.  In her eyes, you will never be good enough.
Elisa is an amazing teacher. She's pretty difficult, but it isn't overwhelming. It feels like she's actually challenging you to think, which is a good thing in my book.
Worst professor and show less care about student problems.

He is very accessible outside of class. He also tries to make the class fun. He should provide more examples. You need to study this daily. There is a lot of difficult material in a short amount of time. I studied for his tests for 10-15 hours. The practice tests were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: While his lectures were helpful, I learned more from the textbook. He is a nice person, willing to help you, but the material is tough. The practice tests tell you exactly what you need to know, so you can do well if you focus on those. Lectures are long and he may say that attendance does not matter much, but it made a big difference on my grade.

Very helpful and enthusiastic. Somewhat limited by time constraints for a broad topic. Gives good study material for tests and grading is straight-forward. Most who struggled relied too much on TAs instead of going straight to the source. Really enjoyable and has written me great recs since.
Professor Rainer Glaser teaches me how to submit a paper, and I can prepare my  manuscript   by myself. So I think the class in ucas is wonderful.

Dr. Glaser is very smart and a wonderful teacher. He is available for outside help and very enthusiastic about chemistry and made the class fun. Highly recommend this prof. He is a nice person and has fair exams.

Smart guy, poor teacher.  Test questions are random, unclear, and do not assess knowledge of the subject.  He cannot field questions.  I learned more from 30 min. with a textbook than from all of his lectures combined.
Just plain awful. He uses overheads to much for a graduate class. Furthermore, he just cannot teach. He trouble to connect the content in an explainable manner.

Teaches too much in too little time. Makes bad jokes and goes off on tangents about unrelated topics. When I asked about how I could improve my grade, he said study more, when I mentioned I had other classes to study for as well, he said to stop sleeping. He also didn't notice the copious amounts of blatent cheating that took place during tests.
He was an excellent teacher. I really liked him. He was available after class and didn't talk down to me.
Very very bad. 2-3 chapters per test and then 6 chapters of new material for the final? Please, don't take this guy if you can help it. He really is that bad.

I'm retaking this course even though I got a B.  we learned very little.  he shoved a bulk of what is supposed to be learned in orgo 1 into the final 2 weeks of the semester.  he recycled old tests instead of actually testing over relevant material.  his ego is enormous.  do yourself a favor and do not take one of dr. glaser's classes.

if you are taking organic I,  DO NOT take it with him...you will not learn what you need to know for orgo 2.  you will skip far too many chapters.  If you do take it with him, then be prepared to teach yourself a lot of orgo before taking orgo 2 because you wont be ready.

Thank as replguy didn't even grade our first exam, so it screwed us even more!  he spent too much time hitting on the hot girls in our class and even said that he should watch himself before he gets into trouble.  Tied, with Sharon Ryan, for the worst professor ive ever had.  Like I said, thank god he was removed and we got prof. greenlief.

I had Glaser for chem 210 and have now failed 212 because I got NOTHING out of his class.  He spends so much time on projects and newspaper articles that you don't learn any mechanisms you need to know for 212.

This guy SUCKS! He doesn't teach the material that you need to know for the exams..instead he spends lecture time talking about things that are irrelevant (how far it is from here to Saturn, and the national debt). He's seriously the WORST professor I've had to deal with at Mizzou!

He doesn't help you prepare for the exam.You basically go into it blindly. There was stuff on the exam that we barely covered and we never work with any of the concepts that are taught in class. He says he "knows what [he's] doing". He doesn't know how to teach an entry level course.

Professor Glaser is a terrible teacher. He is impatient, condescending, and rude. He actually has the audacity to refuse to further explain things that are unclear, and has no problem yelling at our class if they don't comprehend a concept immediately. He's one of the worst professors I've had.

So far all the negative comments reflect my view of this guy. He is probably the worst teacher I have ever had besides deanie neff. His tests are over material that he never tuaght and his explanations suck.

Worst professor / course ever.  If you are supposed to take this with Glaser - take the 2 semester option with other professors.  Any other option would be better.  He did not teach what we need to know.  The peer reviews are unfair.  I also wonder  where the positive reviewers are - I have never me

He doesn't teach the material that you need to know for 212, instead he spends most of the time on the stupid newspaper articles and group projects.  This will inprove your grade, but will not learn what you should.
Arrogant and condescending.  I wouldn't be shocked to find out he wrote the good reviews posted here. Run from this class, run and never look back

I had Dr. Glaser for both Org 1 & 2.  He has high standards standards, but they are obtainable.  If you want to learn organic and to be challenged, this is the man. No matter the actual text, I suggest Wade, 5ed.

2nd semester organic is about as dry and difficult as it gets, but Glaser finds a way to keep you awake. Cool group asst's, lab points, and even a few take home tests help curve the class and keep your grade up.

The good doctor Glaser was a challenging and stimulating professor.  He was demanding, but if you held up your side of the bargain you got a lot out of the class.  I love organic chemistry and thoroughly enjoyed his class. Excellent work!
The worst teacher I've had at Mizzou, and that's including the other orgo/chem profs I've had.  If you end up getting Glaser for a class, drop it and take it later!!!

One of the best chem professors I've had! Makes lectures interesting and easy to understand, especially for such tough content. Textbook needed to do well; requires lots of extra studying. Posts lectures online - a godsend! - but sometimes gives test questions out in-person only, so attendance is suggested. Exams are multiple choice but tricky!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great, dedicated teacher!For finals week, he dedicated all of his Sunday night to a review session. The curious tidbits in lecture he drops makes learning in class room relevant to the real world. Don't skip lecture! You never know when the computer is down and thus the online lecture lecture won't be available...

He's a great guy. I studied a lot and still didn't get the test scores I wanted. For him, it is about really knowing the information and how mechanisms work. Don;t think you can get through this class just by memorizing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Organic 2 is extremely difficult no matter what professor you have, but Glass makes it sting a little less. You still have to put in the work but he's really good about taking time to answer questions & make sure you understand what's going on. Generous curve at the end of the semester, but be sure to start studying at least a week ahead of tests!!

Class was difficult, which he acknowledges. He aims for the average grade on a test to be 60%, but he changes his grading scale so that 65% is a B. This is the class that made me realize I don't understand chemistry.

I really enjoyed Glass for Organic Chem 2, he makes it a little easier but don't expect an Easy A or B. He'll only write rec letters if you receive a B or higher as well. Class is based on HW and 4 tests which is rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Glass is a good professor and makes you really have to learn and memorize your stuff. With that being said the averages are around 60% each test, but you need a 65 and above to get a B which is pretty easy to achieve if you put some effort in. I do hate the multiple choice tests though. Class i had to take so wasn't too bad. Expect to put work in.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of my favorite teachers and I regret not getting to know him better, so go to his office hours. He does tegrity, but it doesn't work 10% of the time. Organic II is hard, but it's not Glass's fault at all and he will help you as much as possible. Start studying at least a week in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Glass is by far my favorite professor I have had. He is probably one of the smartest people at this University, but completely lacks an ego! He is the best. His lectures were interesting and I enjoyed the class. His exams are hard, but if you study as much as you should (orgo is memorizing and applying), you will do well. Also, he doe tegrity!

Glass is awesome. Definitely my favorite chem prof at Mizzou so far. He sets the curve for the class after the second test, so you know exactly where the grade cutoffs are. For our class, a C is above 45%, a B is above 65%, and an A is above 85%. He provides tons of past exams, wears awesome sweaters, and gives fun tidbits in class.

His exams can be harder to prepare for than other chem professors, but his lectures and grading curve make up for it. Gives "tid-bits" during lectures to show real-life examples of the reactions you are learning about (from DNA mutations to making appliances). Very nice guy, first chem professor I had who didn't have an inflated ego.
This guy rocks! Don't have to study much to get an A

Glass has amazing lectures and frequently provides juicy "tidbits," relevant applications of the chemical topic discussed in the lecture. He doesn't go as in-depth as the book, so read the book if you'll be doing more orgo in your future. That said, he only tests on concepts discussed in lecture. A few questions are ambiguous but most are fair.

This class was pretty demanding. I put in about 50(!!) hours of studying for each test and came out with an A pre-curve (A+ after), so I expect it's entirely possible to do less than that and still get an A. That's just to put it in perspective. He usually does tidbits during class, which makes them a lot more interesting and enjoyable.

Dr. Glass is a really nice guy and he's lectures are interesting! There are only 4 tests, which pretty much decide your grade (there are a few homework points, too). So, it is very important you do well the tests. There is a nice curve on the class, which helps. I would take another class with Dr. Glass because he keeps lectures interesting!

Very good professor, obviously interested in the subject and makes the lectures enjoyable. Tests are very very VERY difficult but the curve is very generous. Important to go to lecture or at least watch the Tegrity videos.

It goes without saying that Dr. Glass is BY FAR the best professor I have had in my (almost) 4 years at MU. That being said, his class is rigorous, in every sense of the word. Although he is quite fair, his exams are among the trickiest I have taken in college. They are incredibly humbling to say the least. Be prepared!

Dr. Glass is a fantastic teacher. The curve is very generous but tests are difficult. He says flat out that there will be questions you don't know but should be able to answer. GO TO CLASS or at least the review sessions held by the TA. The review sessions are VERY helpful.

Absolutely amazing professor. Very funny, interesting, and knowledgeable guy. Attendance is not mandatory, BUT I strongly suggest you go. Tegrity doesn't always work for him, plus going to his class is a blast. Tests are very hard, but if you keep up daily you should have no problem getting an A or B+. Absolute favorite professor I've ever had.

Glass is amazing. Best chemistry professor I've ever had. You will learn A TON. Great prof choice for MCAT preparation/knowledge. Also, genuinely NICE guy who cares about his students. The material is that hardest I've had in college thus far. Do NOT underestimate the work involved.

Dr. Glass is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about student learning. He is always available for office hours, and can even work around your schedule. Studying almost everyday is mandatory if you want to receive an A, but the class is very manageable if you put a lot of effort into it.

Dr. Glass is an incredible teacher. He clearly loves doing it, speaks well, and gets students. That being said, you will have to work extremely hard if you want an A. His exams are the most difficult I've seen (class average ~60%), but the curve is fair enough (~84%) for an A. Tests are straight from the notes. Study hard. Learn a lot.

Awesome professor. This class is a measure of work ethic, thoroughness, and some critical thinking. Study a week before exams and take good notes because this is one beast of a class. Dr. Glass simplifies every mechanism to the best of his ability, and takes breaks during class to show modern day relevance of what he is teaching!
Beautiful. So beautiful. Glass is a great teacher. But it's a hard class. Gotta love those wolf sweaters.

The material is presented clearly and he makes class interesting. Some days are a lot of material, but he gives breaks and I actually enjoyed the class. YOU Cannot get behind and cram. Make sure you keep and begin studying early for his tests! Very do able :)

Dr. Glass is a great teacher that deffinatly cares about student learning. He does his best to make class interesting with "tidbits". His tests are very hard so keep up with you studying and pay attention in class! Cheers!

Dr.Glass is a very helpful teacher, and he is not an ordinary mizzou professor; he does care about student learnings. He will bring up new scientific issues and teach us the up to date  info in class. He's also interesting in class, he's very devoted into his research and teaching. The best teacher I have for chemistry, I am bio major.

A very difficult class, but Glass is an excellent teacher. He cares and wants his student to do well. Keep up. Study as you learn the information. ALL mechanisms and many appear the same, so try and keep them all straight. It is possible to do well in this class, but it takes a lot of work.

Glass is a good teacher--very organized, fun to listen to. Great lecturer. The class is very difficult, though. KEEP UP WITH LECTURE! You cannot cram for his exams--start studying early. Study the practice exams + know lecture notes, and then some. He's tough, but he's a good teacher and is willing to work with you. Very approachable.

Organic is a tough class, but Glass does a good job at relating the material to some real life situations. He can also make the class laugh from time to time. I suggest keeping up with the reading, doing practice problems, and going to the TA review sessions. It will help.

Very difficult exams which tested over the "exception" to chemical reactions, rather than the "rule".  Glass was fun to listen to but did not make learning easy, and tested at a level of detail which you would never be expected to know in any professional or graduate school.  A great class for those majoring in organic chem but not anyone else.

Great teacher, Hard tests!!! Glass's tests require at least a week of studying if you want to do well. A's and B's are attainable, but take effort for sure. Test averages are usually in the 50's and 60's. You definitely need to go to lecture to understand Organic 2, its not easy! But Glass is an awesome guy who keeps your interest in class usually

Interesting guy, tries to relate useful information to what we are learning.  Expects a lot: know all the reactions backwards and forwards and you will do fine.  All multiple choice tests, pretty lenient with the curve.

One of the best teachers so far! Very interesting lecturer, and seems very knowledgeable. Tests are VERY hard tho. Attendance isn't mandatory, but going to lectures is only way to learn - textbook is useless when it comes to his test. Pretty big curve tho (I had a 75% and still had an A)

This class was retarded. The tests were not indicative of what the students knew because it was just a guessing game with the multiple choice. Glass is a great lecturer and knows his stuff but terrible in his evaluative techniques which just doesnt motivate students to learn. The class grade cutoffs...A-70%,B-54%, C-37%,which is pointless.
HARD tests, but if you are willing to put work in and learn the material well, he's more than willing to help you. He wants the students to learn, and he's very fair with his grade scale.
orgo is hard in itself but he's an amazing professor to take it with because you don't mind going to classes...his tests are hard but do-able but expect to study your head off
Writes quickly and expect you to know every reaction inside and out. Expect to study hard and feel disappointed with your grade

Organic II is a pretty tough class in its own right. Dr. Glass is a great lecturer, and does his best to make obscure material a little easier to understand. His tests are rough and make up your whole grade, though, and there is no opportunity for extra credit.
She was so accessible and passionate. Sometimes if people weren't responding to her she would get flustered. Grading really depended on your TA. Mine was great.

Honestly the worst class and the worst professor I have taken at Mizzou. She is condescending, unhelpful, and disrespectful towards students during class, and even called out students with disabilities for having them multiple times in lectures. Treats the entire class as if it's made up of first graders rather than college students. DO NOT TAKE!!!

This was one of my least favorite classes I have taken. I did not feel welcomed or comfortable since I was not a theatre major. I also felt very uncomfortable when she would single out individuals, belittling them in front of the whole class. I really wanted to like this class, but I did not what so ever, and would NOT recommend it.

Did not enjoy this class at all. The plays that were required were either offensive or poorly put together. She lost my respect when she picked on students. Nothing hard has to be done. Be sure to attend class and write down EVERYTHING she says for the lecture short writes. Would not recommend. Only plus was that there weren't any tests.

This class wasn't for me. She seems a little preachy and quite frankly I found myself not respecting her authority on the subject matter. The class itself was like a free for all yogaP.E class, but then there were thesis papers that she graded incredibly tough.

Only two test, a midterm and a final, but they're both difficult. Have to attend four shows and write essays about them and they're not the best (TAs grade - mine was tough). Lectures can be fun, but can aslo be boring, it just depends. Have to read 6 plays and textbook. She is nice enough, but the class is too difficult for introductory theatre.

Her lectures are very long and boring. You need to show up to class though to get participation points. You're assigned a learning team (group project) for a few weeks. I took the honors section, but there is NO DIRECTION AT ALL. You have to beg for clarity (different professor) and it's still not helpful. Class content is interesting though.
One of the worst classes I have ever taken.

Structure of class sucks, lecture notes are all out of whack and do not correlate with each other. Just wait & see. Many have to redo this course. Have to pass with a 73% of average tests.. doesn't seem like that would ever be a problem, right? Think again.

There is no class organization and the class as a whole is pretty pointless. The class time is used for a group project and you teach yourself the tested material. The tests vary from impossible to easy, there is no consistency. You only go to class every other week but class is long and dragged on. The group project could be done in two classes but you have the whole semester. I HATED this class

It's mostly taught online. I took the honor's section of this class and it was nothing too remarkable. It's a prereq for nursing so there's no way to get out of it. It's not too difficult but it's nothing too exciting.

1 of the worst teachers I have ever had. Doesn't teach, you'll learn by Tegrity. She is always contradicting herself. When u go to class it's to work on a pointless group project. Tests are hard & don't make sense with the material she tells you to study. Claims she is too busy to meet indiv for office hours. Too much work for only 2 credits
Weekly online quizzes and monthly exams. I read every chapter of the book and look over his notes, but still cannot find half of the information asked for on the quizzes and exams.

Make sure you find out which edition of the book he is using.  I bought the latest edition because that was the "textbook."  He said that we could use any edition and he assumes that the editions are about the same.  They are EXCEPT for 4 chapters which differ significantly.  Quizzes and exam are based on edition 7!

The class was very time consuming, but I enjoyed writing the 3 papers and learned quite a bit of new material. What I DON'T like is his poor organizational skills and his grading scale. I got an A on all 3 papers but still received a B+ in the course because of his weighted grade system and the fact that you have to get a 90.9 percent to get an A!
The online class isn't too bad. They outline everything you need to do for the papers pretty well. the weekly quizzes are a easy way to get points. the clss is just time consuming!

I thought this class was going to be really hard, but it is not at all. There are online quizzes every week and only one test which is the final.  There are 3 papers, but if you correct your rough drafts you get really good grades on them! Highly recommend this class!

Dr. Goel is okay with letting her two exam averages being very close to the cutoff (72% and 70% when C- = 68%) and a final exam average of 47.3%. She is okay with failing the average student with no mention of curve or changes to the grading scale. She is rude after exams when students score low and she dislikes questions she deems bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goel was difficult to learn from. Asking questions in class was difficult, as she would take offense or just be disrespectful as if she wasn't the professor trying to help us learn the content. I question her professionalism and maturity. Despite this, I went to most classes and felt as if they were a waste of time unless she did example problems.

Her handwriting is difficult to read and she only lectures on the chalk board without posting her notes. Everyone did poorly on the first exam and instead of curving it she gave a bonus quiz for 5 points and graded it harshly. She also graded harshly on exams and expected you to know what she wanted from a question without actually asking.Very rude
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Goel is condescending and overall unhelpful. The course is structured so that the 2 exams and final are worth 70% of your grade, meaning that in order to perform well in the class you must do well on exams. Unfortunately Prof. Goel grades extremely harsh. I would rather take Calculus 1-4 again before taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goel is definitely one of the worst professors I have had. She acts rude to anyone asking genuine, applicable questions, and does not lecture well enough for anyone in the class to be prepared. The lectures are extremely boring and very hard to read. The exams were mostly unlike the homework. Prepare to have any attempt at a proof marked down a ton
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the rudest professor I have had at Mizzou. She is super condescending when you ask basic questions and is a super strict grader. The homework is almost nothing like the exams and do not prepare you well. She blames the class for doing bad on tests rather than taking any accountability, if the entire class does bad it might be the teaching .
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Goel is a very tough grader. After exam 1 she locked the grades and after exam 2 she's seem to be very angry with the class all the time because students didn't do good on the exam. The homework is much easier than the exams as its multiple choice which isn't engaging enough for students to get good at proof writing or memorizing definitions.
Extremely rude person, and grades very irrationally. Just one slip up in your proofs and she will dock all of your points regardless of getting the correct answer.

Hard to understand, and her handwriting is difficult to read. Speeds through notes way too fast, also doesn't post notes. Very rude and demeaning when answering questions or when you try to argue points back, and gives almost no partial credit. Exam 1 grades were so bad that she locked the class grades, which have stayed locked for over a month.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Goggins is incapable of teaching any topic, no matter the simplicity. Attending lecture will only leave you more confused than never attending. He is bad about giving feedback to students for labs. Lectures primarily consist of him getting corrected by students after he guessed what a slide meant. Overall, a likeable guy, but can't teach.

He gives some confusing, cobbled-together lectures that make it look like he hasn't taught this class before, even though he has many times. It's hard to understand what you should be studying. You won't get much from this class, but at least he's a lenient grader. He's very easy to talk to in class, but was not there when I went to office hours.

The first 2 thirds of the class consisted of confusing lectures and easy labs with most covering what you've already learned, but the last third contained 2 much harder experimental labs covering poorly taught/uncovered material. Currently this class is an easy A, but you will not learn much.
Pretty chill professor. Easy to reach out too.

Extremely disorganized throughout the course. He used other prof's slides and didn't seem to understand half of them: he would read verbatim and was unable to answer questions about stuff on it. Tests are unnecessarily confusing and he occasionally had the wrong answers. Fortunately his grading is lax, but I will still avoid him in the future.

Goggins assigns work that is extremely unclear; almost no one in the class has any idea what they're doing. It's not that the assignments are hard, it's that there's a huge lack of direction. It seems like Goggins forgets about the class as soon as he leaves it every day. It's intentionally vague and frustrating.

Unfortunately SE is a required course. Its unfortunate because Goggins teaches this course. You probably won't know what is going on, the lectures are almost random and the homework assignments were difficult only because we have no idea what to do. Oftentimes does not respond in his own discord server for the class. His communication is asinine
Youll get an easy A but you will not learn a thing.

Lecture content and assignments are extremely vague. The course organization is messy and confusing. One day, a student had to teach him the basics of AWS, which he was supposed to walk us through. Left almost every class period unable to recollect something I had learned. Only redeeming quality is that you get to work with others.
horrible at teaching, often didn't show up to class. Helpful outside of class, but the class itself was the worst I've taken at mizzou

Professor is good at lectures, but he is not good at assignments. Instructions were often vague or outdated. There are a lot of group projects, and the complexity of the final project in particular does not feel supported by the course. Overall though, I've learned a lot from lectures - Goggins knows his stuff and tries to make class interesting.

Class was generally a train wreck, it was very difficult to understand what you were expected to do and when. Had no feedback/grades for the first month or so which didn't help confusion. Thankfully had a good group for the final project.

Sean Goggins has a great heart and I appreciated how much he makes himself available to help students. CS 4320 is just a bad course. Some of the assignments expect you to understand things without actually covering them in the course. The biggest example of this is the final project, which seemed to be way over everyone's head and was too complex.

Class was a total train wreck. Almost no video lectures so the only way to learn is 75 page PDF "optional reading". He was completely absent and unreachable for the first and last 2 weeks of class. Vague grading criteria, everything is group projects, deadlines are hard to follow. Was lucky enough to have a good group so I got an A
His CS4320 was a catastrophe.

Goggins sets it up pretty similar to internships I had. You have to build something as part of a team. Its not hard to do well if you pay attention to the details and go to class. Attendance is not required, but you miss a LOT if you miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Most of my classes are boring. Professors make us study a list like we are in grade school. This class made me think. I think some of the things I learned will help me get a job.
Its not what i expect from a CS class.  But I did learn a lot, it just took more time than I think it should have. But that might be me.

Exceptional. Its the first CS class I have had where I got to use actual technology that looks like at least 70% similar to the tools I used in my internships.  First class I have had that is not so abstract and useless I wonder how anyone survives CS.

This is the first CS class I have had that made me solve problems that ended up being fun.  I admit it was terrifying at first, but in the end, Dr. Goggins really put it all together. I didn't appreciate everything I learned until I started applying for jobs, and realized that a solid 75% of things that excited employers I learned here.
His class is a joke,he doesn't know what he's doing. As I'm typing this about half the class is complaining about Him to the dean

Most of my classes are very easy to study for, and also very difficult. I am a computer science major. Dr. Goggins software engineering course forced me to figure out how to deal with the slackers in my program. I hated the group work, but I was in a decent group and it turned out ok. I should have gotten an A. But my group crashed at the end.
This course is really tough, but he's a great teacher and HILARIOUS!

Dr. Goggins is a great guy, but this class was a disorganized mess. Requirements for assignments were incredibly unclear, exams had topics that were never discussed in class, and they were too long to be completed in time. He barely scratched the surface of the topics, then graded like we're supposed to be experts on the assignments.

Take this class with Dr. Goulomb if you need a Writing Intensive credit! She is so sweet and a great professor that grades fairly. I turned in a lot of the assignments late but she was very accommodating and rarely took off any late points. The material is very interesting and engaging and there's also bi-weekly Socratic seminars in class.

I took Dr. Golomb's Genetics and Society WI course, one of my favorites at Mizzou. Her lectures are engaging and filled with current topics. She's not very responsive over email but is helpful in person. The workload includes short papers, quizzes, seminars, and a final paper. The class isn't too difficult, and she grades fairly leniently.
Absolutely amazing professor, took her for my biology writing intensive and literally received a 100%. I worked really hard but she gives credit were credit is due.

Professor Golomb is an amazing individual that is clearly passionate about her subject. Grades were based on effort for lab notes, 9 problem sets, and one lab practical. The lab activities themselves were super cool and very hands-on. My only complaint was that grades for problem sets weren't posted until the very end so I don't know my grade.

Loved Dr. Golomb! She is ready and willing to help if you need it, and just wants everyone to have fun and learn. I took her genetics lab class and loved it. She is passionate and one of my favorite professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Something that stood out to me about Dr. Golomb is her open-mindedness and desire to learn. She encourages students to explore topics that excite them and left room for us to think passionately and independently. Upon leaving this class I felt competent. I developed stronger investigative abilities, reading skills, and deepened interest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors Ive ever had. This class was a ton of work but it was interesting. She assigns lots of readings and the quizzes will take you 5+ hours of nonstop work if you leave it for one day. Golomb is a fair grader, quick with feedback, and incredibly understanding. She wants you to succeed and will help however possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Golomb is the BEST! I enjoyed learning from her and I felt like it was worth all of the time I put into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Microbiome class, super interesting. Knowing processes, being able to put in own words is key in this class, esp. immune system. Quizzes are killer, they take a couple days, make sure to copy to a word doc bc Canvas likes to lose your work. She likes to hear unique ideas, so include in answers. Tough, fair, overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who certainly knows what she's and is passionate about what she's teaching. Class is not very challenging: 5 homework assignments that each take a few hours to do, 5 discussion posts, one exam, and one big project at the end. As long as you watch the lecture videos on pace you'll be fine.

Class was super interesting! Teaches both concepts and math for things in our solar system (i.e. Hohmann transfers and flybys). Lectures were a bit dry, but after I made myself sit down and listen to them, I learned a lot. Hearing about her experiences in the space shuttle program was also super neat!

The way she runs the class can make you want to terror your hair out. The homework assignment are every other week and are "50 questions" but with the multiple parts of each question it can very well turn out to be 200. On top of that there are multiple tries for each question but you lose half the points if you get it wrong. Have to put the workin
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are dry. You can get a B if you don all the homework and submit all the labs. Multiple choice quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's an astronaut which is very cool but her lectures are super dull. do the readings and do the homework and go to class. i really like astronomy but didn't love this class because she didn't make it interesting. cool topics but not a great lecturer.

ALL power points from lectures are posted on Canvas for this class, so you only need to show up for clicker points, 5% of your grade. I only opened the book a handful of times, lectures and book material overlap. You get to use 2 pages of notes for the mid term and final, which is a godsend, and the final was curved extremely nicely for my class.

LInda is such a sweet lady and genuinely cares about all of her students. She is very passionate about this class because she used to work for NASA. Her slides are hard to take notes off of sometimes. The labs are very interesting. As long as you stay on top of your homework and notes, you'll do just fine. (You have to work for a good grade!)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Way to hard for a introduction course. Super hard Test. Crazy amounts of homework. Not recommended. Must study very long hours for quizzes and test.

I absolutely hated astronomy but I will say if you have to take it, take it with Prof. Godwin. The class material is insanely hard and she's super nice and tries to make it interesting but it's so boring. You can't even read the textbook because it's literally rocket science. The only good thing is she curves the class really well at the end!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: NOT AN EASY SCIENCE/LAB. This class is far too difficult for an intro class and it is near impossible to pay attention to her boring lectures, but attendance is still mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She dumbs down physics too much. Going in, I had a strong background in physics and she tried to keep physics down to a minimum. The online homework is tough but the tests and quizzes are really easy. All the powerpoints are online so attendance is iffy.

Godwin is just not a very good lecturer. She talked about the class and all the elements of that class liked she expected others to know about the material like certain details would not be explained.  Her tests were pretty difficult and there were so many assignments for that class that were not explained very well.

Sweet lady but the way she presents the content is just impossible to understand. The book is fairly easy to follow along but concepts are on the difficult side if you're not good at science. You can use book/google answers for HW so that's where I made up for all bad tests/quizes. Tests/quizzes go off of her lectures not the book so you're screwed

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you want an easy A. She is a very sweet lady, but lectures are impossible to follow, and the quizzes are some of the hardest assessments I have ever encountered unless you are an astronaut. I am doing good in this class only because you can use a cheat sheet on tests.I have learned basically nothing in this class.

She's a really nice person and is very likable but her lectures are so horrible. The labs are fairly easy and you can just google the answers for HW if you need to. Try and go to over 50% of the lectures so you get participation points, you don't have to pay attention, just be there.

The lectures are super boring, and you won't pay attention at all. This is a mistake because then you will have no idea what is happening on tests and quizzes. You will fail miserably and ask yourself why you decided to take this class in the first place because it will not be easy like you thought it would
I would not recommend this class. I thought it would be an easy lab science class, but it certainly isn't. She takes attendance with clickers and doesn't answer questions clearly.

She is an awful teacher but a nice person. I took this class because I heard it was interesting and an easier science class but ended up being my hardest class of the semester. Do NOT take this class!

She definitely knows what she is talking about, which means she can kind of lose you sometimes because she talks at you without really making sure you understand. Other than that, she's really nice, she was an astronaut (which is super cool) but make sure you have a pretty effective study method because nothing is highlighted or preferenced.

My advice is to not take this class unless you are certain you want to be a Physics major, otherwise this course will not count. However if you are interested in physics, astronomy, or space I would definitely recommend this class. It is an easy going class, so take this if you have a pretty difficult schedule.
She knows what she's talking about, extremely reasonable with grades and homework.  Very interesting material.  SHES A FREAKING ASTRONAUT!!!! How can you not love the class?
Absolutely terrible teacher. This was the worst class I have taken so far at Mizzou. Linda Godwin is completely boring. I suggest that you NEVER take this class.

Linda Godwin is the worst teacher you can take. If you like teachers that don't know how to teach and are terrible at adjusting microphone levels, take her. Most BORING person on the face of the planet.

Very simple class. She goes over the details that need to be on the test repeatedly.  Lectures can be boring, but she tries to keep students paying attention.  She teaches because she loves the subject and it is obvious to see.  While the class was slow at times, the information was simple.  it counts as a Lab science which is awesome.

No matter what you think, do not take this course! Try to avoid it if at all possible! She no longer has open note tests and her lectures are boring...she uses iclickers so attendance is mandatory but still pointless. She is the only astronaut that can make astronomy completely boring...I didn't listen and I wish I would have...you've been warned..

A very nice a reasonable lady. She is extremely boring, regularly goes over things in excruciating detail. She is not technologically literate and often spends ten to fifteen minutes trying to figure out how to use her iclicker software or mac.
I thought she would be interesting because she was a former Astronaut, but no she is really boring. I hate the class and the only reason I went every day was to get attendance points.
You will think this class is going to be awesome. and you will think the fact that shes an astronaut is cool. that will ware off quick. incredibly dry teacher. boring as hell. assignments suck

She's a former astronaut so she really know's what she's talking about and it makes the class a lot more interesting.  Tests were challenging but also open note, so not impossible.  The class is definitely doable if you read the book and pay attention in class.
She is honestly the sweetest lady and always will to help. Your allowed to use your notes on test as well as a study guide.
Awesome. She is extremely knowledgeable. However, if you don't already have an interest in physics and astronomy, this class can be difficult to understand and maybe even to get through.
I loved this class I learned a lot and he made me laugh

I loveeeddd this class. Dr. Neimeyer is great, very interesting guy and his lectures are very interesting. There is a solid amount of work, but work is due every two weeks and he leaves all assignments open until the end so if you fall behind its ok. I would definitely take another class with him!

Lectures and material can feel a little scattered and repetitive but otherwise it's a pretty easy and enjoyable class. His lectures and videos are interesting, he's occasionally quite funny, and clearly very knowledgeable in his field.

I enjoyed Dr. Neimeyer! His lectures were engaging and funny at times, I learned a lot in this course. My only beef is he doesn't respond to emails fast, it took him 5 days to respond to me. But other than that this is an easy and interesting course with no real deadlines, you just have to have work in by the end of the semester.
Best class ever! It is focussed on eating disorders so there are alot of interesting lectures and interviews that make learning fun!
Really love him

This post prod class was probably the most useful film class I've taken so far. Anyone can teach you how to technically edit, but he will go above and beyond to ensure a deep understanding of the thought process behind every cut you make and ensure you are set for any video production in the future, whether or not you want to be an editor.

Exceptional teacher. He will give you opportunities in class that you will not get anywhere else- seriously. He is a working filmmaker with films on Netflix and an array of Oscar/award-winning filmmaker legends. If you are even slightly interested in documentary or film, take his classes. This class made me switch to the documentary track!

Very manipulative, demanding, and heavily picks favorites. Makes students compete against each other for trips to film festivals. Didn't really teach me anything outside of the basic definition of documentary. He thinks his class is the only one that matters. Talks about students behind their backs, to other students. Extremely unprofessional.

Actual class was LINGST/ENG 4420 - Historical Linguistics. Easiest grader ever. Not concerned with giving bad grades but with actually ensuring you understand material. Zero homework this year and onward as AI accessibility has messed with her ability to fairly grade assignments, so that's a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is great! She goes super fast through the slides but if you listen and participate she will reward you in your grades. She gives lots of practice and examples. One of my favorites for sure. Gives more than enough material for quizzes and tests. She says they are pop quizzes but she tells you when they will be and what is on them lol. Love her.

The class was interesting but it felt like she was throwing in random group projects for fun. The grading was very vague and she kept asking for "more" information, yet didn't make that clear during the actual assignment, such as the midterm exam. Fun professor though! I just wish there was more structure.

not a fan of her or her class at all. she goes super super fast through all of her powerpoint’s and doesn’t allow enough time for people to stop her to ask questions. very sassy and passive aggressive when answering questions. one of the hardest classes i’ve ever taken. would not recommend. if you can take another class, take it
Fantastic person. Very intelligent, caring, and helpful. Perfectly balanced workload. Made me love realize I love linguistics.

Rebecca Grollemund is so nice, friendly, and clearly has a lot of enthusiasm and passion for Human Language. There are only quizzes and she gives students more than enough material to study for them. She loves to give extra credit to those who participate! She also is more than happy to help you when you aren't understanding something. Love her!

Dr. Greenwood is a good professor. He definitely cares about his students, and the weight of the assignments I really liked. However his exams were very difficult, and his study guides aren't helpful whatsoever. The group project was kind of bad too, but he is a nice guy.
Good lectures, annoying group project that felt really detached from the rest of class and 4 difficult tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Greenwood is great. I really enjoyed his lectures, he makes the content interesting. Hated the group project, would have been much more enjoyable to do it individually. His exams are very hard and study guides aren't particularly helpful, but if you find a study method that works for you then you will do fine.

Horrendous class, great professor. I feel like Keith did his best to make class interesting and give us the information needed to pass. I went abroad for two weeks in the semester and he was one of the few professors I had that communicated with me and made sure I didn't fall behind in his class. He was super chill and I really enjoyed his efforts.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor with difficult exams that will make or break your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests in this class are incredibly difficult for J-School tests, very detailed! Not a lot of other assignments so how you do on the tests really makes or breaks your grade. He is a good professor but tough grader.

Great professor! I was shocked to see any negative reviews. While the class is not the most exciting, he really cares about his students and tries to make it fun for everyone. I would definitely take a class with him again!

Gives really good lectures that are interesting- don't worry about being bored in a history lecture. He is fun! There's a semester-long group project and 4 tests and a weekly discussion board, but that's it. Easy but interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the homework is fairly easy and accessible, we had multiple readings a week that were 15+ pages. The lectures weren't very engaging, but they had a lot of good info. He posts the slides online if you don't go to class which is nice. However, he would post the study guide for our exams the night before, making it hard to prepare in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Literally the most boring teacher I've ever had in 18+ years of school. Makes 1hr 15 min classes feel like they're 6 hours long. Spends the majority of that time droning on and on about useless topics. I always thought I enjoyed history and Greenwood's class has ruined that for me.

I took the 4-week summer class for J3000. Greenwood was a great professor and made sure everyone got involved in class. He failed to give us feedback on our first three writing assignments, and so he decided that he wouldn't grade us down on them due to us not ever getting advice on how to write better. He really cares about his students.

lectures around the actual topic in every way possible. includes every single minute detail, making the class incredibly boring. class itself isn't too difficult, but professor greenwood draws everything out so much as if he's just desperately trying to fill the time. he gives a strong impression that the content hardly excites him or interests him
Could give much more engaging / interesting lectures. Each class felt like 5 painful hours long

Dr. Greenwood is a very knowledgeable expert and a good teacher. He is fairly strict on grading academic papers, and the classes I have taken with him demanded hard work, but they were very rewarding in the end.
Feels kind of weird to "evaluate" someone on a public forum, but seriously, no rating at all for such a great instructor like Dr. Greenwood? Just couldn't pass by without leaving something.

Hands down favorite professor at Mizzou. He makes lectures enjoyable while also insuring that all students understand the material. It is important to go every day as there is a lot of hard content covered each class. While still one of the harder classes offered, Grafakos makes 4700 a class that you look forward to going to.

I felt that Dr. Grafakos was very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. The class is difficult, but if you show up to class and try your best he will notice. He made an effort to learn the names of hard working students. Put in an honest effort and you'll be okay.

calc 2 is rough anyways, but prepare to study in this class. hes not super open for office hours/likes to throw curveballs during exams. beware that on multiple choice he often changes the format on the correct answer and wont give partial credit for correct answer in a diff. format. DO NOT SKIP RECITATION. ended w an a but rough road to get there

Loukas Grafakos was an exceptional teacher who explained things very well and was very passionate about math. He was very understanding and caring in all my interactions with him and went out of his way to congratulate people who did well in class. His course was exceptionally difficult, but that's a common experience in Calc 2.

Class is the hardest thing I've ever done in my life.  Professor is knowledgeable about the subject but sometimes doesn't explain enough what he is talking about.  He goes very fast making it impossible to write good notes, and the tests are simply impossible to get a good grade.  Teacher is very nice, but the class is impossible to get an A.

Dr Grafakos has tests that will be quite difficult but nothing utterly unfair. He likes to cover the more difficult problems in class or on one of the prior tests. You can tell he's passionate about Math but sometimes the lectures just didn't cover the material clear to me. Problems from the textbook and practice webassign was super helpful.
The tests are pretty difficult. His accent takes some getting used to. The first 2-3 weeks of class are review and super easy. Don't skip the recitations, they are very helpful.

If you enjoy math, understand calculus and know how to study for understanding, you will do perfectly fine. However, one CANNOT simply memorize how to do the problems correctly because he takes examples which can be solved using the same concepts but not the same patterns as his in class examples.

His lectures were full of proofs and more to show what I'm supposed to do. The quizzes are easy, the exams are medium, and the homework is difficult. However, he rarely allows for makeup exams. This class was challenging, but not impossible. The challenges of this class were great exercises for my maturity and my ability to think outside the box.

This is the worst class ive ever taken. He is so hard to understand and fly's through lectures. It gets to a point where going is not even worth the time. His exams are just unfair. They are 10x harder than homework and example problems and he gives you nothing but an exam from 10 years ago to study with. DO NOT take this class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are usually very different from the homework and the exams. He does the proofs for every concept, which is useless and confuses everyone. I spent weeks before the exams studying and received B averages, but the grading was harsher than it should've been. The final was even worse, with foreign concepts. Do not recommend this professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He clearly understands the material very well, but he is not good at communicating why or how it works to the class. he does his lectures very quietly, even with a microphone. His examples are unnecessarily complex. his exams are also very focused on edge cases, with a class average of 50-60. his curve is also hard to understand. 

cool guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams are tricky. Class exam averages are usually in the 50-60 range. Besides practice problems from the book, the only other thing you will have to aid your studying is one practice exam from 2011. I wouldn't recommend the class.

He always says the test will be simple and easy if you know the material, but that's a lie. Ive gotten an A in every math class i've taken but im sitting at a C in this class right before the final. It could be a B with the curve but his curving system is so unnecessarily confusing so I don't even know. Also you don't get study guides so have fun
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid Dr. Grafakos's course at all costs. He's a poor lecturer who fails to explain topics properly and his incomprehensibly low volume destroys the chance of understanding anything he says. Even worse, his exams are BRUTAL—weeks of study aren't enough; you will NEVER be prepared for the difficulty of some exam questions. YOU'VE BEEN WARNED.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Calculus II is already a very challenging subject, but the professor makes the class even more difficult. His lectures are fast, quiet, and very confusing, he has a weird curve system that nobody understands, and his exams test edge cases and are way harder than any of the limited study material we receive. He also weighs exam problems weirdly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would put my grade but I don't even know what is with his curve I just wanted to write this to save any future student to never take his class. The biggest thing for me are the tests he gives you practically nothing to study with and the tests are extremely hard and confusing. He does give a curve but yet again I still have to see if I pass.

Talks very quiet making it difficult to understand what he is explaining. In such a high math class it is easy to struggle when lecturing is all muffled. It is evident the professor is very well rounded in the content, but sometimes so much so he skips several steps within problems containing new concepts thus leaving students behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are hard to follow and can be really complex at times. The exams are much harder than the homework and practice exams. The questions on the exams can be weirdly weighted so you could get the 5 questions right but only get 15 points and then miss one question slightly harder and lose 20 points.

Concepts are challenging and not taught in a great manner. He is passionate, but can only teach at his level, not at the students level. Says that exams are easy and proceeds to drop the Putnam Exam 2: Electric Boogaloo. If you can't write at the speed of light, good luck taking notes during lecture!

Test are extremely hard. Our class average on exam 1 was mid 50s. I do not think we are prepared well for the exams speaking its all free response. I spent 10 days straight studying and received a 65. Do not recommend!

makes tests unimaginably hard. you could know how to do everything in the book/quizzes but you're cooked on the exam because he will throw in concepts that are foreign. impossible to succeed unless you have a third eye for math or can guess well on the test
bruh i cant do ts

Loukas is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about math, but he has a hard time explaining himself sometimes. He is very uneducated when it comes to technology, so online classes were interesting. The exams are difficult but fair. If you do the homework and practice problems, you should do well

He is good at answering questions. He is also excellent at drawing graphs in his examples. He does not record lectures so make sure to not miss class or you will fall behind quickly. His exams are excruciatingly difficult!! They are all free response and he puts lots of curve balls on them. To pass, I suggest about 1.5 hours of studying every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This guy is really passionate about math and seems like a great guy outside of class. However, avoid taking his class at all cost!!!! His test and quizzes are the toughest I have ever had and he will go out of his way to try and trip you up. Complete and understand all of the homework and practice problems. Not a lot of partial credit.
Not a terrible teacher, but did very little to help students prepare for his difficult tests (his study guides were almost completely irrelevant )

Gives practice exams from a class he had taught 13 years ago, with half the examples not relevant to the current material. Gets tripped up sometimes on easy questions. Overall disappointing class, the only thing that kept me from switching professors was the TA.   Fall semester 2015
Quite possibly the cookiest professor i've ever had.  Lots of offbeat, thought provoking examples kept Calculus surprisingly upbeat.  Prepare for spicyness.

Funny guy and explains things well for the most part, except at times he gets really into detail and it's not needed. Tests are hard because he offers all short answer with no partial credit for the first section of tests, this only occurred on last two tests however

Great teacher, knows the material crazily well. Sometimes gets a little tripped up in his explanations but overall clear and good for an eager learner. His handwriting is excellent and his graphs look like they're actually to scale!
Very interested in student learning. And some of his explanations are just hilarious! Hilarious but helpful!

The test are about 18 problems long, first part the questions are 3 points each and no partial credit, any partial credit you would get for the rest of the test is based on whether you did the problem like he wanted it. He will take points off if he messes up on the test AFTER the test has been handed back.
Amazing teacher. Extremely clear and precise.  This teacher obviously enjoys teaching and knows the subject matter like the back of his hand.  Also has good handwriting on the board!
Pay attention in class and you will receive an excellent education on art, with very manageable A's. I am an engineering major and found this course extremely helpful in understanding the world.

Professor Guzman is one of the kindest people you will ever meet! She is so passionate about teaching and cares so much about her students. She literally brought candy into some of her lectures. I definitely recommend taking this class, not just because it is easy, but for the overall good vibes.
This class is an easy A. i would take it again. Most classes are a lecture the whole time, sometimes it can get boring. we would occasionally have a class or group activity.

Mariana is extremely nice and passionate about her subject. The material is very interesting and fun to learn, however she skims over slides VERY quickly, and grades VERY tough on her exams. Make sure you are doing all the assigned reading and taking careful notes about things that may not even seem important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great and caring professor, she really cares about students and the learning environment of the class. She loves the topic and is very passionate so it makes lectures more fun. All exams and quizzes are online to do over the weekend and open notes making them very easy. She is a generous grader and attendance in part of the grade.

Her lectures were very captivating and even though I had no prior knowledge of art history, I learned so much from her class. She is a passionate and kind professor who allowed us to think about societal evolution in a new light. She cares about her students and her studies, and it shows. I have recommended this class to all of my friends.

Prof. Guzman is one of the sweetest humans I've met so far. You can tell she is genuinely excited about what she is teaching, and is stoked to talk about art and what it means. Her class shows so much about art, and you'll not only learn tons of genuinely interesting stuff. Attendance is graded, and some of the quizzes are mean. But shes the best.
Extrenely hard

Lectures can be dull, but she is easy to follow and makes everything easy to understand.  She is always available for extra help. The tests were pretty hard, so make sure to do many practice problems to prepare.

Prof. Gu was very straightforward in class. If you needed help on the homework assignment, she walked you through every step and would check your work to make sure you got it all right. The class is based on exams and homework, so it helped.

Gu is a very timid lady. Goes way out of her way to be helpful. Random student: "Hey, those powerpoint slides. Can you print them out and give them us all next class?" She did it. Very sweet lady. She was incredibly boring, however, and talked in circles. She taught as if we hadn't ever taken an Econ class before (so much review). Bad experience.
Great proffesor!

Professor Guo was very passionate about Astronomy and it made his lectures enjoyable and interesting. The class was not difficult as long as you took notes or read the textbook AND did the homework. Great class for people that want to get an easy and interesting lab credit.

Dr. Guo is funny, nice, and loves his subject. His course is pretty difficult, but it is physics. He tries to make it as understandable as possible. There is homework every week that takes a couple of hours to complete. There's several quizzes and one exam at the end of the semester. Reading the textbook will help you out a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Guo is very sweet and obviously very passionate but his lectures are not well structured. The labs are very time-consuming and harshly graded. Quizzes and exams are super difficult because the wording is so awkward and confusing. I learned some stuff and it was interesting but it was so much harder than expected.

Dr. Guo provided great lectures with difficult topics simplified. Homework can be quite long, but is given two weeks in advance. His exams are difficult but the lowest grade is dropped. He offered 6% extra credit to be added onto our final grade at the end of the semester. He is caring through office hours, makes great jokes, and helps when needed.

Dr. Guo is so sweet, and really cares about astronomy and just wants to share interesting stuff with his students. I really enjoyed it even though I don't really care about Astron. There is a fair bit of homework but you can find all the answers on quizlet, there is no reason not to get an A in this class.

Teaches subjects in class that isn't going to be on the tests and continues teaching past a test unit. Students are expecting to remember ongoing lectures while studying and remembering past lectures for unit exams. Labs are vague and homework can be extensive. Don't recommend this prof!

As it is blatantly obvious by everyone else, this professor is the worst I've had at Mizzou.  I'm sure the topics would actually be interesting and a lot more engaging (which is why I originally was drawn to this course) had it not been for his confusing lectures and terrible grading.  Really wish I would've come here first before making up my mind

I have so many thoughts about DeSouza and this course (all of them negative). In fact, my last review I left for him got deleted because I broke the guidelines. Long story short, don't take this class or any taught by him. He is a horrible professor, and this class really should be 6-8 credit hours. It's just not worth your mental health...

When there was an issue regarding low grades in the class, he once said "its rather because of the students, the class (material), or the degree program". Little does he seem to realize, it was because of him.

Horrible, and every other synonym you could think of. Gave a final project to potentially replace an exam score, but no grade was ever put in (this is also true for the final exam). Any friendly demeanor you get on first encounter is just a facade. Don't ever take if you can, don't be like most of us early on thinking naively "its not so bad".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are not perfect (which would include reading his mind) then he will treat you like a child. Beware he blames students for his mistakes and errors, even when there have been repeated instances back to back. He single-handedly caused me to go back into therapy within two assignments, so have extra cash on hand for that

I don't often write rate my professor scores, let alone negative ones. I do not say it lightly, this is the single worst class and professor ive taken at Mizzou. There are no redeeming qualities about this class. He expects work that would be acceptable for a 6-8 credit hour class. Lectures were chicken scratch and incomprehensible. Avoid all costs

Do not take his class, he make it very hard.

DO NOT TAKE COURSES TAUGHT BY THIS INSTRUCTOR.

DeSouza made this course much harder and more stressful than needed. He's bad at effectively teaching the material and isn't helpful in class or over slack when students don't understand something, often responding in a snarky manner instead and sometimes shaming them. Avoid at all costs.
