reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. Gives no feedback for any homework or projects. Uses three different websites for assigning work, collecting work, and communication, one of which is his own amateurish website. No recorded lectures and only handwritten notes to go on if you miss a day. Condescending, sometimes outright mean in lectures. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Interesting class material, unfortunately there is no way to learn it inside of lectures. Desouza's teaching method does not make things stick, and if asked to clarify anything he rarely does. Recently he also exploded at a student in class and insulted them multiple times. If you want machine learning do not take it with him.

The course is not great but Dr. DeSouza is worse. He is condescending when asking him questions and the other day in lecture he screamed at a student repeatedly calling them stupid and dumb in front of the whole class. There is a big long list of what is wrong with this course and it begins with DeSouza unstableness. Just avoid him and this course

WOREST CLASS I HAVE TAKEN IN MIZZOU. The textbook was published in 20 yrs ago and is useless for this moment. Lecture is difficult and courseload is heavy. Quiz, exam, assignment, mini-project, final project, final exam. Be ready to spend lots of time for meaningless stuff and gain nothing, as well as a bad grade if you are going to take this.
Get ready to teach yourself the class because lectures and homework are unrelated. You also need lots of prior experience that is not listed, or covered in the previous classes.

reviews.comment: his class is just for students who have attended his course before. the ppt of lectures are handwritten, which is kind of hard to read.
Lectures are confusing and he doesn't explain well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are reading off of online notes. Does not release examples of any solved problems.

The teacher was absent from class for three weeks, and when he was there he seem to not understand the material. He had office hours but would not explain a subject. His reason being if he helped you he would have to help the other 40 students. Teacher failed 22 of 40 students in fall of 2017.
Lectures make no sense whatsoever, worst part is it's impossible to take notes about his rambling so you leave the lecture not remembering anything. Be prepared to learn from the textbook.
Its quite confusing. Lectures Material is soo messy. Lab incompatible with the content explained in class

Nice guy, bad teacher. Quickly reads lecture sides at the class and criticizes the class for not understanding, claiming that "its easy guys." Tests are ridiculous, nothing like the homework. Told us to study everything for the final, because everything will be on the final and proceeds to make half the final over a subject that wasn't even taught!
Better plan on spending all of your time on whatever class he teaches

Test are extremely hard and especially frustrating since the homework is simple. Average class grade on first exam was a 35%. Doesn't explain anything well and his labs are the most unorganized assignments you'll ever work on.
Good Luck.

Took this nwolc 2016 of the fall semester. Nothing on the exams correlated to what was given in class. Exams were multiple choice by the way and wanted you to derive snippets of code and other stuff not taught. TAs never helped much and were yzal. If you went to class all he did was just go over random irrelevant snippets of code, good riddance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good at getting across entry-level CS topics, but the labs were never in-step with the class. Pop quizzes had asinine trick questions.

Lectures were interesting even when subjects weren't. He's pretty funny. Labs aren't too difficult and really help boost your grade. He gives extra credit a lot but those points tend to be harder to get. Only problem was that he made it kinda hard to study for tests (practice problems didn't come with answer key) but lab grades balance that out.

I eventually stopped coming to lecture because his teaching was pretty scattered and didn't help me to understand more than the most basic concepts. With some outside reading/help from friends on prelabs, lab sections are pretty easy. I left the class with minimal understanding which was corrected in the first weeks of the next class in the series.

Professor Guilliams is an amusing person with reasonable expectations. He is knowledgeable enough to confidently answer most all questions during lecture. There's easy extra credit on labs and HW. My only problem with the class was the large number of "trick" questions on exams, some of which seemed to test relatively insignificant syntax issues.

Prof. Guilliams was an amazing first teacher to have in the CS department! He truly cares about his students, and he wants to see us succeed in this field. I had never done coding before, and I was challenged in the first few weeks but GO TO OFFICE HOURS/LECTURES. This will help a lot! I ended the class with an A+. Test are challenging but do-able.

Professor Guilliams provides excellent lectures that are a mix of important information with enough off-topic rambling to be entertaining. The lab is a very large component of the class, my TA Andrew Wise was great and made the labs easily doable. Guilliams is very approachable and is willing to make the class for honors credit if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was disorganized and his communication with TA was poor. Everything was rushed and he went off topic alot. Labs and homework had errors that weren't corrected until close to the deadline. If your program doesn't compile, you get a 0 on the assignment. Pretty harsh for small mistakes. Not recommended for people without coding background.

He doesn't seem to really care about students. His lectures are often dragged out while he tells ridiculous stories that lack relevance to the course. He is clueless over what the hw covers and leaves it entirely to the TAs. He lacks the ability to design an efficient course from all angles - I would go in full detail, but there is a character limi

This guy is awesome.  If you don't like him you must not have done well or cared about Computer Science.  He's an excellent teacher with clear course outlines and objectives.  You know what you have to do from day one to get a good grade.  Tough but fair.  I learned more from this class than any one I've taken at Mizzou.  Excellent.

Phenomenal and QUALIFIED (dude has done some big boy  stuff) Professor. He really got me interested into CS and IT. I originally thought it was going to be a boring class because of the material but he brings a lot of energy to the lectures (which really helps in the mornin). Labs are pretty hard but clicker points will boost your grade at the end!

Professor Guilliams is an amazing speaker and conveyor of information. His lectures include solid information while still being entertaining. The information is fairly straightforward and easy if you stay on top of it. Everything is comprehensive. The TA you get for labs will affect your opinion, I had Chantal Lewis, who was a phenomenal TA.

Very realistic, easy to follow, passionate professor. Class was challenging but very enriching! Be willing to work and don't hold back on questions if you don't get a part of the material, just make sure you know what your asking.

Couldn't have been happier when I registered for CS3380 and saw Guilliams was teaching. Although it was his first time teaching Database in a while, this has been one of the most valuable classes in my CS career. The content can drag on at times, but Joe always makes it interesting. This class left me with a great understanding of IS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was Guilliams first time teaching Database in years, and he did a great job. Loved every lecture and he makes sure that you have the knowledge to actually perform well on tests and projects.   One large group project at the end.

He is a horrendous teacher. Terribly uninformed and uneducated in his own field. Pop quizzes and tests are designed to make you fail and don't accurately test a student's knowledge of computer science concepts. I've met plenty of undergrads who have a better grasp of computer science theory and programming than this joke of a professor does.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Joe is a very down-to-Earth guy and does a pretty good job explaining the material. My biggest problem with this class is that it is incredibly difficult, and there is very little room for error. If an assignment is due at 5:00, then it better be turned in before then, or it goes for a 0. Assignments in this class are the hardest I've ever done.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is funny and tries to make the lectures enjoyable. There is lots of quizzes and you will fail every one of them. But if you try hard in the labs and homework and actually do good then you will be fine. Also go to every help or study session, like all of them they are super helpful!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a very difficult class if you do not have any prior experience in programming. There are many pop quizzes that test you over material that you just learned even before you get to practice using it. Even with going to every lecture and doing all the homework I am going to receive a C- in the class. Homework programs have many typos.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good teacher but his test suck and never make much sense even to people who have already had the class or other Professors in Computer Science, they often refer to them as unfair to the students. He's more than will to meet with you and explains things. Dont take this class as a gpa booster!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is designed to make you fail. Most of the TAs are pretentious and grade harshly. The TAs also create the error-filled homework assignments. Quizzes are sporadic for attendance.
He gives 11 quizzes but drops one. Had a couple homework assignments that were actually educational . Tests are fine, he has a review that helps a lot.

He is so passionate about computer science and really does well explaining concepts. The course was pretty tough for me, but I knew absolutely nothing about coding. Lecture can get a little boring but he did his best to keep your attention with small jokes or stories. If you work really hard and put in the effort you can get an A
He's amazing. He knows the material and loves it. He will help you and he will do whatever it takes to help with anything. Amazing teacher. One of the best I've ever had. Take this class.
One of my favorite professors.

I'm not a cs or IT major (or into it), and I had a very rough time in this class. I've never spent more time doing HW and studying for a class. He is a great guy and pretty clear and there to help. I dont rec taking this class "for fun" unless you are a huge IT/coding nerd.

Joe is a great teacher. He provides plenty of comedic relief throughout the class too. Unfortunately, his classes are early in the morning so no one's awake to laugh at his jokes. Great guy. Good teacher. His classes aren't for everyone. If you're not a comp sci major or IT then i wouldn't recommend his class because it can be pretty challenging.
He's very good at teaching the material, the labs and homework are fair.
His class is so much fun. He is clear and passionate about the topic and he makes learning the material fun.

Joe's class was the highlight of my week. I had him for both 1050 & 2050 and I've learned so much from him. His lectures are entertaining, informative and easy to follow. The labs and homeworks really help to learn how to be the best programmer you can be. He tells a lot of his stories over and over again, but I enjoyed having him as a professor.

LOVE GUILLIAMS. Seriously. He's the best. All you have to do for an A is pay attention in lecture, and then just review your notes before class for the potential quiz. Write down what he says, not the slides unless it's a list or super important. Interact with him, it makes it fun! I honestly wish I could take this class again. No book needed.

Joe is easily the best teacher I have had. He is passionate, knowledgable, and he cares. He enforces attendance with pop quizzes and labs can be challenging, but he is straightforward with what he expects, and it is possible to get an A in this class.

Joe is a great guy, and he sure knows his stuff! He makes lectures enjoyable. He does give a quiz every other lecture, but it is a great way to make sure you understand the material. Weekly labs are intense. He gives four homework assignments which take about 6 hours each outside of class. I found there was way too much work for a 3 hour course.

Guilliams is AWESOME. A really funny guy who really cares about student learning. 2050 is WAY more difficult that 1050, but he extended several labs and curved the second exam. He also explains tough concepts in such an understandable way. I've enjoyed having him for 1050 and 2050. Wish I could have him for every class.

I loved Joe's class! He made everything easy to understand, even for a novice programmer. His lectures are always entertaining and interesting. He gives quizzes every week, so don't miss class. Exams aren't too hard, but they're meant to trip you up. Get a lab section after both lectures and be on your TA's good side, labs are most of your grade.
Easily the best professor I've had yet. I actually enjoyed going to class, even in CS1050 when it was at 8am.
Great teacher knows his stuff and can convey what he knows to students very well if you pay attention in lectures and practice coding.
Joe is the best professor ever.  His lectures are enjoyable, relaxed, and very helpful.  You can tell he wants to get to know his students and truly cares about us.  Very smart funny man!

Joe is an awesome teacher.  He keeps the class challenging, so you are always learning something.  Outside of class, he is a very nice guy and super approachable.  I had him for CS 1050 last semester, and I'm currently finishing up his  CS 2050 class!

Joe did a really good job teaching complex ideas to the class. This is still a relatively difficult class, especially if you don't have prior programming experience. He is very passionate and will kindly and enthusiastically answer questions in class, despite it being a 300 person lecture. Attendance isn't "mandatory" but he has occasional quizzes.
Joe is a great teacher.  Make sure to go to class though, since he likes to give quizzes.

The lecture portion of class is very straightforward. The quizzes and tests, while not exactly easy, are very doable if you keep up with the schedule. The real key for success is getting a good TA for your lab section. Labs can be difficult and  comprise roughly 1/3 of your grade. A lousy TA will make for a challenging lab experience.

Joe is a good teacher and relates well to his students. His tests are strait forward and the labs are usually not too hard. He is a little disorganized since he lets the TA's run the show. He does tend to waste a lot of time trying to scare students about future classes or the job market. I enjoyed the class but wish i couldve gotten more out of it
Ruh-roh. Guilliams is hard to pronounce, but not his class is not that difficult most of the time.

fantastic teacher. EXTREMELY willing to help when you make a mistake (especially missing tests). Excellent at explaining complex ideas in CS... all around awesome teacher. I personally did not use the textbook once, his powerpoints come straight from the text.
You can't spell Guilliams without GUI.  Perfect for CS.

The labs are a little difficult but the exams are fine. Guilliams really knows what he's talking about. If you can motivate yourself to actually learn and listen you shouldn't have a problem in the course. A lot of help is available so make use of it when needed and you should be good.

Dr.Guilliams is a very good professor; he is very knowledgable in the field and knows what he is talking about. However, I found this class to be kind of difficult. If you have no programming background you will likely struggle.
I actually really understood and enjoyed his lectures. He's a really good professor and is really talented in the field as well. He makes you excited about programming.

She is amazing. But, that doesn't mean it's a super easy class. Do the reading and prepare to be challenged with essays and exams, she does expect what you write to be good. At times essay grading is a little confusing, but nothing to be super concerned about and conferencing helps.

Dr. Harper is my favorite professor during my time at mizzou so far. She, alongside Dr. Rymph, made book club exciting, adventurous, and fun. It is a lot of reading but the memoirs were very interesting and easy to read. And it's only around 6 students. She was always kind to me and gave me support.

Dr. Harper is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's incredibly caring inside and outside of class, and she's someone that it's easy to be comfortable around. She can be a hard grader when it comes to papers, but I think she just expects a lot. You don't need excellent papers to do well, though, as you have other easy grades!

While attendance is not mandatory it enriches the class ten fold. The class is always involved with reading, however as long as you are a fan of mythology (or Percy Jackson) you will find enjoyment throughout the entire thing. With mostly forgiving grading the class is more focused on discussion and development of characters rather than memory.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This is a class to be a writing tutor, so you have to want it. Dr. Harper is very constructive and helpful, but tough, which makes you an excellent writer. It is a HUGE time commitment between tutoring practice and writing assignments. However, Dr. Harper is everything - super knowledgeable and keeps it fun.

Dr. Harper is a fun person and passionate about the honors humanities sequence. However, she grades essays very hard, and several of her prompts are very vague. I would recommend conferencing with her on the papers before the deadline. And stay ahead on the reading! I know its a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I have never loved a professor more. She made everything we read fun and relatable while also making us understand it on a far deeper level than before. Amazing all around, definitely the best in the entire humanities sequence
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Love her in a purely admirational-aspire-to-be-her-someday sense.
Dr. Harper is an incredible person. She talks about must-have professors that teach other classes, but she is one herself.

Rachel was one the best professors I have had! She is one of the nicest people and is really understanding if you have to prolong a deadline or miss class. She has a true passion for the subject. At times, she may have been a little bit of a hard grader but in the long run pushed you to your best. Plus her end of semester dinner was amazing!

If you have one of Dr. Harper's classes, count yourself lucky.  She is a talented and compassionate teacher, and if you put in the work she will help you become a better writer.  She does not assign an unreasonable work load, and her assignments and grading are fair.  Period.
She is an absolutely amazing teacher! Even though she is kinda hard, she is willing to work with you to get a better grade.
A tough grader, but an outstanding professor!

Rachel is such an amazing teacher and person! If you need help with any of your papers, she is willing to help as long as you just go into her office. I have learned a lot from her class, and I highly recommend it to anyone who is thinking about taking one of her classes in the future.

I've found Rachel's Honors class to be challenging, like people have said.  Her grading is tough, sure, but it ultimately makes you a better writer.  Compared to Greg Foster, who co-teaches the class, Rachel isn't condescending at all.  Greg is a pretentious ****, haha. But I'd reccommend Rachel any day- very willing to help u out!

In four years at Mizzou, Rachel Harper was far and away the worst professor I had. She was confusing, condescending and narrow in her approach to the subject.  She graded papers on a whim--praising you for something in one paper and marking you off for the exact same thing in another-- and provided little help during office hours.
Expect to work in any class she teaches, but expect to come out a better write.  Always ready to meet, help, and have a laugh during class--taking any class with her I can get

Worst Teacher Ever! In my other English class, my teacher suggested I should become an English major. Then, I took her, and I went to her office about 3 times a week and learned nothing except how to be completely confused about how to write a paper. We had class once a week and learned nothing in it. She is conceited and degrading in her grading.
I had her for two different classes.  She has a very sweet disposition.  I found her to be helpful and well-informed.
Rachel is amazing.  She is, honestly, a person I would model myself after!!  She is a phenomenal person and a great mom.  Take her class!!

A VERY good teacher, but she assigns entirely too much work, and a very harsh grader.  A very nice lady, especially if you meet with her a lot.  I would take her again, but only as a thirs or fourth option.

Rachel is very friendly, informal, and enthusiastic.  She knows how to teach a class.  Her essay grading can be kind of harsh until you get used to the system.  DONT mess up on the midterm, it will kill your grade for the entire class.  But overall I would definitely take her again.

Very difficult and sometimes ambiguous grading.  While she is only on campus 3 days a week, still willing to meet with you.  Class meets once a week and is set up well.  Take if you are a serious essay writer and want to become better, if a newb, tread elsewhere.

Not the english 1000 to take in my opinion. She grades very hard, so dont expect an A. Her comments address specific sentences in your work but not how to fix the whole paper. My grades didnt improve much from 1st to 2nd draft, which was frustrating given how much work i did. Too much work and you dont get the grade.
She grades hard in my opinion, but seems to be helpful.  Also, only has us meet once a week for a 3 hour course!
very nice and helpful, but a boring discussion class.  other profs in this class offer a lot more than her.  she just asks lots of questions, and is not able to get good discussion going.

Great guy, always eager to answer any questions inside and outside of class. Focuses a lot on proofs and theorems in class. If you do the practice exams and attend office hours sometimes, you will do well in his class.
Very organized lectures. Exam reviews are usually ten times harder than the actual exams. Lots of practice opportunities. Soft spoken.

Decent teacher I would say. I ended with a C+ in his class I couldn't understand his lectures very good so I just taught myself how to do everything with youtube videos and with Chat gbt giving me lots of practice problems. He does give a lot of partial points as well.

Very fair grader and good at explaining the lectures once you get accustomed to the accent. Exams are very similar to the reviews given the week prior. The final was very challenging and the reason I didn"t get the grade I want, but the rest of the class is one of the easiest Calc's at Mizzou.
Was a little difficult at first to get used to the pace of lecture, but taught the content very clearly and understandable from about week three on.
Probably one of the best math professors I had, the first thing I noticed at the start of semester was how well he explained how things were derived.

Very kind professor and is always happy to answer anyone's questions in class/outside of class. HIs lectures might put you to sleep but he asks questions sometimes to keep class engaged. Grades very fairly on the exams, which helps because of how hard the content is. Just need to know the concepts well to score decently on the exams. gpt the hw

Han knows the content, but has a difficult time teaching it. I often had to try to learn the content by myself on the homework. There was only one homework assignment per week, but it was lengthy, taking me around 2 hours each week. There is a quiz every Friday, which never was too long. One benefit is that Han gives out lots of partial credit.

Many of the concepts in Calc 3 are hard to understand, but Prof Huang did a good job towards the end of the semester giving examples to build intuition, though his note-heavy lectures are quite boring. The homework is entirely online. It's not worth very much of your grade, but if you want to pass the tests, you have to do them. He's an easy grader

This class is all about doing an assigned reading and then discussing it in class. The readings varied on difficulty, but a lot of them were interesting. There's not many things that go toward your grade. You have a participation quiz every class, 3 exams, and one essay. It's an easy A as long as you prepare for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class and Prof. Heckel was amazing. She's very kind and helpful, both in class and outside of class if you ever need her. She understands that not everyone has a philosophy or writing background, and grades leniently with constructive feedback on your writing. Her lectures are interesting. She expects participation so be ready to talk.

Difficult class, your midterm and final are a huge portion of your grade. Her feedback on your writing is non-specific, and it can be tough to make up assignments if you miss them. Reading is very important in the class, but the texts are dense and complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Heckel is great! I was super worried about taking a philosophy class, but she is so understanding and kind about your papers. I met with her at least once for all three of my papers, and even I could see the massive improvement from the first paper to the last. I wish she would teach more lower-level courses so I could take more of her classes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor in general. She is extremely student-centered and it really shows. The only class I have that I really look forward to. You are graded by three papers but she will meet with you and tell you exactly what you need to improve on. Great professor and great person!

I LOVE HER. She is weird in a cool way, and funny. Very kind and caring as well. She does a good job explaining difficult concepts, and of catering to people who have never taken a philosophy class before. The lectures are fun because they are super discussion heavy and there aren't a ton of notes. You're only graded on participation and 4 essays.

Dr. Hall is an amazing professor who clearly loves his job his lectures are funny and entertaining and unlike some of my other professors I feel like I actually know things about him which makes him feel an actual person while my other professors I couldn't tell you anything past their occupation and first and last name
Dr. Hall seems very motivated to teach, even if sometimes his stories get in the way. He is super positive and tells everyone hello when we walk in. Be ready to handwrite essays!
He does not post the lectures and the only way to get the slides is to attend lectures. Discussions have tests worth 10 points every discussion

Honestly, the best class I have taken at Mizzou. You can tell he loved to teach students and wants us to do well; he provides extra credit on exams to help us out. My only downside was my TA, but of course, that is out of his control. As long as you show up to class you are set

Dr Hall is the best professor I have had. He genuinely cares for his students. The lectures are fun! Test grading truly comes down to who your TA is as they are the ones that grade. Attendance isn't mandatory, but the slides aren't posted so I do recommend going. As long as you go to class, take notes, and read the readings, you will be fine.

Grade is mainly determined by exams and weekly quizzes (hard). Exams weren't super easy, but Dr. Hall gave us the answers to many questions. Need to go to class to get the notes (no posted slides). Dr. Hall truly is such a caring, funny professor, who made this class incredibly enjoyable. I learned so much from him, so def take his class.

Dr. Hall is an absolutely excellent professor. His lectures make some very complicated topics much more digestible, he is so energetic and fun, and he does a great job at making you feel like you are capable of understanding the content. I plan to take as many classes with him as I can!

The class is not very difficult as long as you go to the lectures. He has a policy of never posting the slides so be ready to either go to class or get notes from someone else. Tests are 40% essay but as long as you know the topic you will get points. He is a very funny guy and he keeps lectures entertaining.
I can see why he's everybody's favorite professor. Cares about his students, enthusiastic about teaching, extremely helpful, never boring.
Very fair grader, not difficult if you study and don't get behind schedule. Clear expectations, lots of helpful reminders. Super helpful prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Self paced.Proctored exams.Essays and quizzes.Harsh grader with high expectations. If you are amazing with writing papers, this class might be for you. If not,DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. You have to know all the material and study very hard to do good on the exams. This was not an easy class even though this was a beginner philosophy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not recommend this class or this professor. Tough grader. There are two page essay and a quiz with every chapter and there are 14 chapters.  Will need to study hard, do the readings to do at least decent job on the proctored exams. It is probably one of the hardest and stressful classes based on how he grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall kept class very entertaining and allowed students to express themselves freely. He is very caring while keeping everything professional. Attendance was mandatory as the quizzes in the discussions went over the lectures from the week but the questions are not overly complicated. Overall a nice guy who wants his students to succeed.

Super interesting class. Make sure you get the easy points from discussion attendance/quizzes! You have to go to lecture since he doesn't post the slides, but he makes it entertaining for a 9 am. 3 exams, like 20 multiple choice and one essay question. As long as you understand the content and can explain it, you'll do well

Dr. Hall is confident, but definitely not a narcissist. I think he just has fun when he teaches, and it's obvious he cares about his students. Most professors don't use their sense of humor as much when they teach, but Dr. Hall does. He is a pragmatist, not a relativist--they are not the same--he talked about this in Environmental Ethics.

I really enjoyed this professor, his lectures went by super quick. I think he has a great sense of humor and good personality. He cares about his students a lot. The only negative thing I have for this course is that it is only test and quiz-based. If you are not a good test taker, do NOT take this class!!!
Awesome class!

Dr. Hall is a legendary teacher and one of the most caring professors I've had. He always has lots of energy (helpful at 9 a.m.!) and is willing to meet up and talk about anything. His classes ARE in depth--who cares if he doesn't publish--he's here to TEACH us

Very good professor!! 
Dr. Troy is super funny with an amazing personality and it makes his course way more entertaining!! He cares about his students and is very helpful with helping them succeed.
His classes arent in depth and he thinks very highly of himself considering he doesn't even publish any writing.

I really enjoyed Dr. Hall and his course. His lectures are always entertaining and easy to grasp. He doesn't post slides so you have to go to every class and take notes. Your grade was based on 3 tests and the weekly quizzes. Make connections with you TA, they are very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Hall comes off as a bit unprofessional, but he's a very chill and relaxed guy and you can tell he cares.

The course requires discussion with a TA. Discussion topics are controversial and political to the point I stopped attending. Such as our TA believing population control is an ideal solution for environmental sustainability.
This class was pretty easy. He says you need the textbook, but you don't.

I love Dr. Hall, I had him for medical ethics and ended up taking environmental ethics the next semester because I enjoyed his class so much. He cares so much and makes his lectures so interesting and hilarious it keeps you focused the entire class.
Great guy, very smart, but kind of a narcissist

This is an online course, so it's mostly reading, quizzes, journals, and exams. Dr. Hall is not the easiest grader, but he gives you feedback on your journals, and he always gets right back to you if you have a question or problem. If you don't do the reading, you won't do well on the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall was a very good professor. He cared very passionately about Environmental Ethics, and about the views he's gained from teaching. He was even able to help me outside of class when I needed to give some information to my advisor.
Dr. Hall is an amazing professor. He is funny, accessible, and fair. I would highly recommend taking any of his classes.

If you've taken other courses from him, prepare for it to be different. Some part of the difficulty may come from it being the first time he taught it, but also being incredibly dense compared to his other classes. However, Dr. Hall made the course really interesting. Really important to read the textbook (several times) and to come to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
This was the first time Dr. Hall taught 3500.

Dr. Hall was obviously unprepared in how he organized the course. The exams had atrocious questions, and despite the heavy workload, only the exams actually mattered for your grade. Good guy, but that class was awful and his "fix" for it was 15 points of extra credit which were irrelevant.

This class is very reading-heavy, but Dr. Hall makes it 1000% better. Despite the tough reads sometimes, he makes discussions accessible and enjoyable for students. He cares a lot about what people have to say and explores ideas at great depths while still keeping it interesting. Dr. Hall is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hall's a legend. He's funny, he cares, and he does everything to make a 9 a.m. class tolerable. You have to take notes and read and come to discussion. If you do all of that, you should be good.

Expects you to be able to pull quotes out of 2 different books from weeks ago for a online proctored exam for an 1100 level class. The average on the midterm was a D. If you can take this course somewhere else you should do so. Out of every ethics class I have taken, this is by far the hardest one only because of the midterm/final and how he grades

Dr. Hall is not a bad person, but I have not found his class enjoyable. Lectures are slow and sometimes feel unnecessary. His TAs are extremely tough graders, which would be fine if they could adequately communicate what needs to be improved to do better. Attendance is mandatory unless you want to get notes from a peer. Overall, good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Hall as a professor. The class has tough topics, and I really appreciate how he approaches both sides of issues. The discussions were a waste of time, but count as points. My TA didn't know how to answer questions that were asked, which was frustrating. Overall, I would recommend this class, but I wish he did the grading, not TAs.

Dr. Hall is an amazing professor! This was my 3rd course with him and definitely the most challenging. I'd say not super beginner friendly but still worth the effort. Highly recommend taking a class with him if you're at all interested in philosophy, just be ready to put in some work.

Long, draining lectures. Material really wasn't interesting at all and the discussions are horrible. The tests are insane and a lot of preparing is required. You have 50-60 minutes to answer 20 questions and write 800-1000 words which is extremely difficult in that time frame. I think unless you want a certificate in ethics do not take this class.

Dr. Hall is by far one of my favorite teachers at Mizzou. Dr. Hall gives very enthusiastic lectures and tells great jokes. Attendance is not taken/mandatory, but he doesn't post slides if you miss class. There is a short 4 question quiz each Friday during discussion. The first exam was 20 questions, and one short essay response question.

Professor Hall is one of my favorite philosophy lecturers I have had the pleasure to study with. He is kind, caring, and incredibly intelligent. One of his best traits is the ability to make the complex concepts of philosophy accessible to everyone. Although going to his class is optional, showing up is always rewarding.

Dr. Hall is by far one of my favorite professors i've had. In fact im taking a class next semester he is teaching because he is so awesome. He is very funny and easy going and goes above and beyond to make students enjoy his class. In addition to being so funny, he is also a good teacher. He is a fair grader and cares about all of his students.

Dr. Hall does get off track a lot, but never excessively. He always makes lectures great to sit through. The exams are not difficult at all if you study. If you attend all the lectures and take good notes, you'll be totally fine. I did none of the readings and studied the night before every test and scored very high. MAKE SURE YOU GO TO DISCUSSION!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Live laugh love Dr. Hall. He's so funny and incredibly smart, but never makes you feel dumb. I learned so much in the class, about the material and about myself. He doesn't make you do too much work, just lots of reading for the class.

I loved the teacher, however do good on the quizes. The exams are long and kind of hard, but only worth 20 points so sometimes its hard to good on them. If i had gotten more right on my quizes then i would have a A, but i have a B.

I don't know what the haters are talking about. If you go to class, take notes, and do the readings, you can't mess this up. His TA's are tough but fair. And I for one don't mind the fact the dude makes jokes and tells stories. He actually cares.

Great guy but don't take the class. He tries hard to be engaging and funny but its hard to do when your lectures span the whole class period and are honestly pointless. The TAs are very hard graders with no feedback. The class is test heavy with very difficult exams. Lectures can not be accessed outside of class so attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor.  His lectures were phenomenal and easy to follow.  I would highly recommend taking his classes.

If you are not good at taking tests, you will not do good in his class. Exams are 60% of your final grade which makes it hard for you to do well. However, he is a very funny guy and very interesting to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall was easily the best professor I've had. Every day before class started, he made sure to brighten our day with something positive or funny. He was engaging, lectured very well, and thoroughly taught every side of the argument on topics such as abortion. He was enthusiastic about philosophy and it rubbed off on his students. I will miss him!

I have really enjoyed Dr. Hall's lectures. He is a very engaging professor who genuinely cares about his students. The class discusses heavy subject material but Dr. Hall does a fantastic job of navigating those topics using personal stories as well as throwing in a few jokes here and there. I would gladly recommend this class to anyone.
tries too hard to be funny. grades the essays way too hard with no instruction on structure.

Funny guy but not the best professor. His TAs are very tough graders and the class is hard to follow at points. He seems to talk about nothing sometimes. I definitely think there are better ethics courses that you could choose to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: super super smart and really funny, gets the class talking. sometimes talks for a while without letting students get a word in, but I don't mind because he's entertaining and knows what he's talking about. assigns next to nothing.

I was actually in Troy Hall's 4 week medical ethics class (GN-HON-1030H). The class was a pass/fail grade and attendance was mandatory. I really loved his lectures and he's super engaging. I learned a lot about philosophy in this class and walked away feeling like I retained a lot of what I learned! Highly recommend!

This class was very challenging for me because I had never taken a philosophy course. Dr. Hall was so fun to be in class with and you can tell he is extremely passionate about what he teaches and he has lots of fun stories. Notes have to be done in class or you can get them from a friend but they are never posted, so it is good to attend class.

Great class! The material is really interesting and valuable. The required readings weren't really necessary and the tests weren't too hard for essay tests. However attendance is definitely required. He doesn't share slides or record lectures which I see as a big accessibility issue. But other than that I really recommend this professor.

Hall was one of the best and most entertaining professors I've had. Textbook is required for reading but I never did any of the readings and came out with an A. There are 3 tests with multiple choice and an in class essay but they are graded fairly. You have to go to all lectures and discussions to get the information and attendance credit.

He is so welcoming. Always wants to talk about coffee. He is incredibly respected within the Honors College faculty and gives incredible lectures. His discussion class was fun and exciting, I always felt safe to make mistakes and come up with new ideas. Be prepared to read but also to be able to talk about every reading and how it applies to life.

Dr. Hall is an amazing professor! I had him in my first semester of my freshman year, when I was incredibly daunted by the thought of interacting with professors. Truth is, he is genuinely hilarious and laid back, but truly cares deeply about his students. Don't be afraid to talk to him! He is always willing to talk and give you feedback!

the funniest professor I have ever had. Beware the three tests basically make up your grade and you really need to read the readings but he is so enjoyable to listen to. I had an issue and he was very understanding and kind. Would take another one of his classes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hall's class is very interesting, but it is extremely test heavy and the tests are not easy. There are no homework assignments or anything to get your grade up, so make sure you do good on the 3 tests throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell Hall loves his job and cares for his students which made going to his class one of the highlight of the week. Be prepared to read a good amount in the text book and to attend every lecture; his powerpoint are not given out. Exams are fair and he and the TAs prepare you well for it. I recommend taking any class that Hall teaches!
Dr. Hall made lectures so interesting, and he is such a great guy. I really enjoyed this class! The TAs are also so helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A great guy with a really great personality, but the class was hard to follow at times and professor feedback was rather vague. I feel more philosophical now that it's over, but the entire semester I was stressed about my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hall is great! He is so funny, and is lectures were even interesting via online class. The tests are somewhat difficult, but if you stay caught up with lectures, you will do fine. The discussion sections matter and there are 3 point quizzes, which kind of take a toll on the grade sometimes. Definitely make sure you are participating!
By far the best professor I have had at Mizzou. He makes class extremely fun and makes it easy to remember the information.

Dr. Hall is a good Prof. Even with Online classes he was able to show how much he really liked to teach. His TA's were brilliant this semester too. It is almost impossible to fail this class. The tests are essays, and I didn't do well on the first one but I figured out the right formula to get an A and after that the class was a breeze. Read the bo
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Troy Hall is the only professor whose lectures I went to willingly. He is very funny and makes his class content very interesting. There is a lot of assigned readings and the exams are quite tough but they are very fair. If you do the readings, you will be able to do well.

hilarious, entertaining lectures & light for the topic-doesnt post slides, discussion with Christian is great-3 question quizzes & points for participation, tests are multiple choice/matching/essay-time is hardest part-make sure you can talk about main topics & know info & examples from lecture, skim through readings he talks about important stuff
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: ONE OF THE BEST! Troy is hilarious, caring, enthusiastic, has lots of good points to make and stories to tell. Easy A. Little work, a few short readings - but make sure you keep up! Doesn't post lectures or notes; must show up to do well. But he holds your attention; class flies by. One of the few classes I was genuinely always excited to attend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall is very funny, but if you do not agree with his views, he does not give you an alternative side. Medical Ethics with him was amazing but avoid Environmental Ethics at all costs. It is beyond boring unless you want to discuss the feelings of trees,.yeah.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Hall is a stand-up guy. He begins every class with a joke or observation form the day before. He really gets his students engaged and is not afraid to get to know his students. Lectures are great, but the exams are quite difficult. (10 multiple choice, 10 T/F, & 1 essay)

This teacher really keeps your attetion. Ive never had a philo class and was worried but the TAs and the professor are really good. I did not do the readings but I took extensive notes and to prepare for the tests I made sure I had opinions and reasoning to support or not to support all the different authors. The T/F is killer so memorize basics!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Troy Hall is the best teacher I have ever had. His lectures are amazing and you get everything you need for the tests if you attend. He does not simply read off the slides, he puts life into it and makes it actually interesting. People attend this class who are not even enrolled just because the lectures are so interesting!! Tells great stories!

Medical ethics was awesome, and I loved listening to him because he is so funny. Class goes by really quickly. The exams are fairly tough, and essay score heavy. The only down fall is the discussion class at the end of the week. You HAVE to participate or you won't get your points. The TA's do not cover the same material and do not grade equally.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I LOVED going to Medical Ethics. I didn't even consider it a class. I was just listening to a funny guy talk, and I would take notes on it. Honestly Professor Hall reminded me of the gay guy off of Modern Family, which is kind of funny because he was a teacher too! Overall a great teacher and I wish I could take more classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A quiz every week, lots of reading assignments. just a few exams and they're really easy. He's super funny and tells a lot of stories. Sometimes they are hard to believe. Like how does one man know that many crazy people? But he's a cool dude, would recommend taking him over any other med ethics teacher.

Troy Hall is probably one of the funniest professors on campus. He engages with his students before class and loves to tell stories off topic from lecture. Assigns a lot of readings but material is interesting. Great class.

Honestly he does a lot to help you succeed, and his lectures are very interesting. There's no quizzes or homework, so just exams. The exams are 20 mc, and an essay question, which you can choose from 3 questions. You have a lot of reading assignments, which will help you a ton on exams, but if you go to lecture you don't have to read. Great class!
Joan is the best professor I've ever had! She is so understanding and truly helps and cares for all her students! Love her!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I strongly disliked this professor. As a sociology professor for more than 20 years, I was appalled by her clear display of ignorance and overall lack of competence related to complex race, sexuality, gender and other issues. Her lens is rooted in her straight, white experience. I would not take a class with this professor again. I felt tokenized.

I took Social Inequalities and I found Dr. Hermsen's teaching to be lacking depth and sometimes problematic. The class is cross-listed as both Sociology and Black Studies and I thought her commentary on the black experience was ignorant (white prof teaching black studies). Because the class is surface level, tests and assignments are easy.

The material was pretty easy, but she tended to go off topic and follow long, rambling tangents pretty often. Prof Hermsen is open about addressing her mistakes, but she just isn't equipped to speak on POC's experiences. Don't expect to learn anything new.

I enjoyed this class a lot because of the content & knowledge I gained from it. It's not too hard either. I didn't attend many lectures, but still did decent on the quizzes & tests. I would definitely advise doing the weekly readings though. There's weekly discussions posts, which aren't hard, and she does drop the lowest few quiz grades. Easyish A

Dr. Hermsen was a great professor overall. To be fair, I never attended any of the zooms or in person lectures and yet I still got a B. The quizzes are 100% found in the readings so I recommend you do them. I love that she offers extra credit and drops your worst exam and a few of your worst quizzes.

Dr. Hermsen was a great professor. She really cares about her students and seems to genuinely enjoy her work. You have to participate in the discussion boards and complete quizzes to keep up in the class. Textbook is absolutely required. Attend class and take notes and you'll do fine!

really nice & caring woman, attendance isnt graded but its hard to understand material from just looking at posted slides-download slides before class and write her explanations on them, tests arent too bad, group project takes some time but not too hard, weekly online quizzes on readings(pretty easy just skim material for answers)

She seems to be a caring person interested in the lives of others, but she just cant stay focused as a professor. She tends to talk loudly, goes off on tangents, and the information can be confusing at times. Easy class, but I dont recommend taking if you are interested in actually learning something new.
I found Dr Hermsen to be a very caring person, who took a lot of interest in each student. Research Methods is a dry topic, but I enjoyed the heavy use of group work in this class

Loved this discussion heavy class. She really wanted to hear a class of 200+'s opinions which I found really neat. Had good lecture material. The tests are SUPER easy even if you don't go to class very much. The only bad thing is she doesn't use a mic but instead yells to speak which is fine but if you sit too close it can become too loud.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: So helpful in a tough research based course!

Dr. Hermsen is a very intelligent and kind person. She goes out of her way to help her students. She expects you to show up to class and attendance is factored into your grade. There were no textbooks or tests in this course, we were graded on evaluating articles and the research we conducted, most of which is done as part of a group.

Classes are terribly boring and I felt like I didn't learn anything from her. I learned everything in lab because her TAs were awesome. You HAVE to go to class (I missed 4 days and got 58% on attendance). She comes off as unapproachable and if you want to do a project she doesn't like, she won't help you. Just stick with your TA and you'll do fine.

The class was alright, it's a boring class no matter who you take it with. Instructions on assignments were sometimes vague, yet grading was very nit-picky. I appreciated the fact that we weren't tested over various research methods and that we were actually graded on the research we conducted.

Easy class. Show up and there's random extra credit. Quizzes are easy. I skimmed the readings while taking the quiz and used google and got As on most quizzes. Class is straightforward. Not my favorite subject but it's easy. She's redoing the class so nex fall or spring it's going to be different.
She is really nice. The class is pretty straight forward. If you do the quizzes and extra credit and study for the exam a bit you'll pass. Classes are interesting but not mandatory.
Extremely easy with extra credit up to 25 points and print out power points class is not mandatory

You do not have to go to class. Quizzes are based off of readings and are taken at home and there are only two tests: midtem & final. A lot of extra credit. Very nice lady. Posts all the class notes on Blackboard. If you're looking for an easy class I would recommend this. No one went to class and still ends up passing

Not difficult, but incredibly boring and uninformed. Repeatedly referred to a yarmulke as a yar-mook-ul. Every time we discussed poverty, she used African Americans as examples. The books she selected for the class were dry and uninteresting. Unless her class is required, I'd recommend avoiding it.

This class was not very interesting. Exams are hard. Read THOROUGHLY. She gives out a TON of extra credit, which is one of the only reasons I attended class. If she notices low attendance on a particular day, then she will give out 3 points extra credit to everyone who came that day. She's awesome, except exams are impossible.
Lots of opportunity for bonus...content is interesting. At least try to half-ass the readings.  Study guides are given. Good teacher.

I had Dr. Hermsen for an advisor and as a teacher.  She is great!  She is very smart and a superb teacher.  Her classes aren't that hard as long as you put in at least a little effort.  I definitely reccomend her!

I thought this class was amazing and I loved it. It's not hard and you can get a lot of extra credit. Some of the readings are annoying and take up a lot of time. There is no real textbook, so the bulk of information is given in lecture. The review sessions are very helpful too. I really liked the class and I really recommend it!

Easy class. Like other raters, I didn't go to class 2/3 of the time, but between doing the light homework and going to the reviews, I did fine. Class is interesting and informative, if a bit depressing.

Learned a lot from Dr. Hermsen's class, very interesting stuff.  Go to class, keep up with assigned work and it's a pretty straightforward class.  Leads very engaging class discussions.  Good professor overall.

B-O-R-I-N-G. I stopped going to the class and still easily got a B+. Her online discussion assignments are easy to BS, as are the papers. As far as the tests, just go to the reviews and you'll be fine. I admit I slakced off majorly in here, but I EASILY got a B+... so why not?

This class was very interesting and Prof. Hermsen helped to keep everyone interested by having class discussions and showing relevant movies.  She is very cool and lets the students discuss pretty much anything.

An easy class to conquer- she spells out what's going to be on the test during review sessions, and if you actually try to do well on the reading responses, you'll be fine. The final turns out to be optional, and the two papers are very easy to write. She is a fun lecturer, and I liked material alot
Not a very difficult class, if nothing else.  Still very boring, seems misguided on some points, and takes forever to get anything graded.

Dr. Hermsen class was interesting and she didn't have ridiculous requirements of the students. The worse part of class was the discussions and opinions of students.  She is definitely worth taking and offers extra credit.

This professor was horrible. You spend an entire semester being told you're evil for being white(if white) and male(if male). The discussions get out of hand, and only disrupt the class. She refuses to answer in class questions, by either answering the wrong question, or dancing around the question.

Her lectures are very dull and unstructured as someone mentioned before.  Although the topics are interesting, the way in which she presents them are not.  The class as a whole is pretty easy however.
She teaches very interesting topics in her class.  Her lectures are somewhat unstructured, but at least she tests over the reading.  She allows for a lot of discussion, but a lot of it is unecessary.
excellent teacher, extremely fair

Didn't grade any of my projects until the last week, provided next to no feedback and was completely unreachable by email. Didn't even bother to grade over 100 points worth of assignments at the end of the semester and ignored my emails about it. Not worth the time or the $300 textbook she teaches directly off of
Super easy course work! Would have never passed had she not been my prof. BUT GO TO CLASS!!!!
Was easy asf. Gotta go to class though.

I didn't appreciate her enough when I had SPAN 1200 with her. I wish she taught 2100. I had an easy A in her class, and right now I'm struggling to keep a B with Mulligan. She was happy to schedule office hours to help me out. I even skipped Spanish 1 after not taking Spanish for 3 years, and she convinced me to stay in the class.

Professor Heston is a very caring professor. Always smiling and in a good mood, she is very approachable and will help you succeed in, and outside of classes, she is very dedicated to helping students. Her class in Methods for Foreign Language Teaching was very interesting and inspirational. A lot of reading, but the grading was fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She was easily one of my favorite professors I've had. She made it very clear from the beginning how to succeed in her class. Attendance isn't necessarily mandatory, but you get participation points in class. She's very passionate about teaching Spanish and I was never scared to say the wrong answer with her. She was always willing to help.

I had Prof. Heston in the middle of the COVID-19 and she was amazingly caring, flexible and concerned about us as people and as students. Class was challenging, but she is very available, a good teacher, encouraging, and supportive. Treated us like adults capable of being responsible for our own learning. Did not correct pronunciation enough, IMO.

A lovely teacher who made Spanish one of my favorite classes. Deeply cares for student and keeping them accountable (no bonus points), but she will help you whenever needed. Always available and response to emails ASAP. Explain material well; however, she is a little tough on the grading element. If you try, she will help yo along the way!

Such a great teacher. As a non-native speaker, she definitely understands where people who are just learning Spanish are coming from. She speaks clearly and slowly enough to understand, and without too many complicating terms. Any problem I had in class was answered quickly and with little to no error. A real gem.

Senora Dawn was a great professor. You need to attend her class in order to do well but if she sees you struggling she will reach out to you. I strongly recommend going to her office hours, she will answer all of your questions and concerns. She does not believe in extra credit but if you do all her assignments, you will make a good grade.

She's very kind and cares about students, but doesn't give any clear guidelines for how things will be graded and just deducts points as she feels like. Tough on participation grades, and the bi-weekly homework assignments are more like quizzes graded on accuracy. Doesn't offer any kind of extra credit.
Sra. Heston was always looking for ways to help and made me feel very comfortable speaking Spanish aloud in the class. I wish she taught Spanish 2100 so I could take her again.

Dawn was an incredible teacher. She genuinely cares for her students and she treats her students with respect. I can't recall her making more than 1 or 2 mistakes during the class and they were miniscule. She knows what she is talking about, and as a non-native speaker she can definitely relate with you as a student who is learning Spanish.

Sra. Heston was very energetic and understanding that non-native speakers aren't, and shouldn't be, fluent without mistakes. She does not always upload assignments to Blackboard, but hands back tests quickly and is more than willing to calculate your grade for you.

Sra. Heston is an excellent teacher! She really knows how to communicate with non-Native speakers because she is one herself! I learned so much in this class and felt very comfortable asking questions. She speaks mostly in Spanish, but is willing to explain really difficult concepts in English, which I appreciated.
Great teacher! She is very helpful and integrates a lot of practice into class time which helps a lot on tests. I WISH she taught Spanish 3. Definitely take her if you can.

Dawn is fantastic. She is very easy to understand, doesn't speak too fast. Very flexible & helpful, willing to put in extra time with anyone who wants it. With the way she teaches though, it's almost not necessary! Liked her so much i'm taking an early spanish class next semester so i can have her again. she is worth waking up early for!

What a wonderful teacher! She is extremely knowledgeable in Spanish and translates it well in class. Easy to understand and she is funny too! She really wants here students to succeed and you can see that. Best class I have had at Mizzou so far.
Very interested in how well her students do. Much emphasis on conversation.
Was overly helpful for anything. Teat are pretty hard but if you study you should be ok. There are alot of chances to make up points besides exams

The entire class is taught in Spanish, but she keeps the class engaged and doesnt move too fast.  She's very helpful and though young, really seems to grasp the language.  Definitely did a good job of working with an intro class.  The homework is also very manageable and useful.

She is cool and very understanding. If have taken a different language it is hard to transition and she will be kind. She also doesn't care if you are a little late. Don't test that a lot though. Buenos dais!

She was a great teacher. She spoke clearly, and was patient with all the students. There are a variety of assignments including presentations, compositions, etc. . .The class is not necessarily easy, but if you do your work, you'll be fine.

good teacher but i was surprised that someone so young without experience in a spanish speaking country was teaching 4th semester spanish.  my high school spanish teacher definitely knew more than she did.
Class is conducted entirely in Spanish, but she speaks slowly and clearly enough where you won't have a problem. Patient with people when trying to speak. Great teacher.

Honestly I'm not sure why most of his reviews are bad. I'm in person but I think he's nice and he cares about the topic and gives good examples. The tests are literally not hard as long as you go through the optional smartbooks. I haven't read the book at all and got a B on both tests taken so far, and that's without even finishing the smartbooks.

I cannot recommend this professor due to the excessive number of exams (six in one semester) and their unreasonable difficulty. The focus on minor details over core concepts hindered learning, and the professor offered little support. Consider the impact on your GPA and well-being before enrolling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hegger is not very good at what he does. His lectures are horrible, and you can't even pay attention after 10 minutes because he just sounds like a textbook. The syllabus basically says there is no excuse for missing class unless your dad is dead. I think he makes it pretty clear that he is only there to receive a paycheck every 2 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The entire grade is based on a few tests. It can be unclear what will be on the test, so make sure to read the chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's hard to rate online professors. His class was the basic McGraw Hill mumbo-jumbo. The tests were relatively short. Super unengaging overall. He does have very strict rules when it comes to Honorlock, but I essentially broke all of them and was still okay. Take it if you have to, but not if you actually want to learn.

Easily the worst professor on campus. Dude has his head so far up his rear end, i'm genuinely surprised he still has a job. . His online classes doesn't have lectures he just posts slides and bases his tests off of the textbook because he's too lazy to teach. He's not a professor, he's just a guy who updates canvas.
He was the worst professor I had at MU. I do not need to elaborate why. He does not understand that not all students learn the same way (regurgitating the textbook)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is no HW, just 5 terrible exams. They are honor locked and you are never sure what the test material is because there is a lot of information and you are never told what is important. I honestly don't suggest real estate program at mizzou if Hegger is teaching this course because it's unnecessary stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this guy for a summer class to graduate early. Emailed him several times about different issues and never got a response. I hope he sees this: I cheated on every single exam and homework because he wouldn't lift a finger to help anyone. Worst professor at Mizzou.
He is quite possibly the worst professor at Mizzou. He is not available for help if you are confused after his boring, monotonous, non particip

If you can, do not take this class. You have to have a fantastic memory to pass, because there are no study guides for the tests. He puts information on the test that is on homework due AFTER the test. 

He will give you a zero if you talk to yourself during the test or if your eyes move wrong. That is in the honorlock warning he makes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 6 Exams in this class and none of them drop. None of them are that hard if you have a test bank but l
He barely has lecture classes throughout the semester and you never know what the questions on the exam are gonna be.

This professor teaches a lecture-style class. We almost always got out of class 30-45 minutes early so the information was very digestible and not too much at once. You can do every problem until you get it right so you can get 100% on every assignment. Overall, I enjoyed this class.

I honestly was expected way worse based on what ppl said about him but he's actually overall not that bad at all. As long as you show up to class and try to go to his office hours the exams are pretty self explanatory. Also the homework and quizzes are online, the only thing that isn't are the 4 exams so its really not awful just put the work in
Expects his students to memorize over 100 different formulas without allowing a cheat/formula sheet for his midterms. Utterly insane

Gives a midterm the class AFTER a chapter exam which is unheard of, only told us about the midterm the class before. Does not give you any material to prepare for the tests and they are nothing like the homework and quizzes. Will laugh at you for trying to get help. Not accessible out of class. Exams are insanely hard & have to memorize 50 formulas

Everyone on here said he was terrible. From day one, he was straightforward. Got two skips, didn't round, and offered an opinion on how to succeed in class. His tests weren't terribly difficult. You were fine if you studied more than just the day before. Starting to think the people who hated him just didn't bother to show up or pay any attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You get two skips. The lectures are not informative. Lectures are short but listen to some things he says because they're important. The second exam was very easy but 1, 3, and 4, were very difficult. There are only about 25 questions on the exam but worth they're 150 points. He's a nice guy that has set rules that he follows. No extra credit.

He is simply a bad teacher.  Does not explain work problems. Lectures are short and not informative. He is difficult to ask for help and be accessible outside class. Learn more from Chegg/ online homework than from him. The class is easy if you work hard and study, but he did not contribute to my learning. Take this class with another professor.

I took Finance 3000 with Hegger and I got a C. I spent hours studying and doing the practice problems. I also asked him for help outside of class, and all he said was "Just keep practicing from the book". His exams are nothing like the homework, and he is rude and disrespectful to students. How is this ok?
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hegger is honestly not the worst. As long as you go to class consistently, you'll do fine. His tests aren't hard if you did the work and he is honestly a caring person if you take the time to go to his office hours. However, if you plan on missing any class, do not take him or you will be so lost and honestly never recover.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams were quite difficult, and nothing like what was taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far one of the worst teachers at MIZZOU. The summer course was expectedly going to be difficult, but the prior expectation of prior knowledge is dwelling. I would advise anyone to avoid taking this course with Joe. I am beyond surprised with as many withdraws and horrible review an academic investigation was not set.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Currently taking Hegger in summer online section, his lack of resources is making some homework impossible. Questions over material not explained in book or Hegger's slides. Doesn't respond to emails asking for help. Everything learned so far I've taught myself. His Panopto videos help slightly, but too drawn out and difficult to navigate.

THE REAL: Treat lecture as a study hall (easy participation points) and "learn" material while doing the HW. Exams are a bit tough but are heavily curved and quizzes are all online. Don't let bad reviews scare you the class isn't that bad. HW will take a WHILE to complete but is the best preparation for exams.

Honestly go to class or else. I mean either way you're basically set up to fail this class. There are strict rules on the syllabus and he doesn't take late work. ALSO the grade is locked until the end of the semester so you don't know how you're doing in the class!

This set me up to fail by not teaching the basics. He was rude to students during lectures if they had genuine questions. 6 exams be prepared to teach yourself everything in the course. I only passed because I got 100s on the quizzes and HW. Be sure to know how to use the BA II plus before taking this class a lot of present value problems.

I struggled in this class because the professor skimms through long notes every class. There isn't enough time to write everything down and he doesn't go in depth explaining many topics. My best advice: print out the slides he posts to fill in quickly in class. I wish he took time to work out problems in class.

He basically reads from the slides, and doesn't teach how to actually do the computations so you are left to find the HW answers on Google/Quizlet/Chegg. He's also kind of a jerk, not very nice and not flexible or accommodating at all. Try and take with another professor if you can.
Definition of "fine". If you read the chapters and do the homework you'll be fine. No exception grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had a midterm 5 days after the Unit 2 exam. Goes through the slides too fast, but doesn't teach the calculation problems so get ready to learn them yourself. Slides on Canvas are not the same as he presents. Get ready to memorize equations, he refuses to give them on the test. Very unreasonable and does not accommodate if you can't take a test.

He only reads off the slides, doesn't elaborate on anything to make it easier to remember, and kind of expects you to have already studied somehow for the class before you have ever gone. I had to do around 8-12 extra hours of looking on top of homework and other classes in order to get any questions right or understand anything. Use Kahn Academy.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! This professor does not care about his students. The class is supposed to be 75 minutes, but we are let go 30-40 minuets early. Sounds nice, but he does not show any examples of math problems. He only reads the slides that the book provides. Smartbook allows you to study concepts, but does not help on the exams.
How is he still a professor at mizzou? This class sucks and so does he

6 exams total. exams vary from difficulty. some are hard and some are easy. lowest i got was a 60% and highest was a 100% 

your grade you see in canvas is NOT your actual grade in the class, which he inputs at the end of the semester. so go TO class. (attendance is part of grade).

intelligent guy, but not the best professor.

Egomaniac. Honestly, this man also made me drop my business minor. Lectures aren't great and doesn't cover math problems which are most of the exam. You have to teach yourself everything out of class. Don't forget to sub. to chegg because you will need it. He says it's not his responsibility to tell you what's on the exams. I got an A and anxiety.

Very smart professor, but you will have to do a lot of learning outside of lectures. Lots of exams, but that's better than fewer exams for more %.  He writes the exams very fairly and I am usually not surprised by what is on them. Exams will sometimes be on Mondays, which is rough.

I would rather watch myself cut my hands off than take this class again or I'd rather play cross roads on Stadium at rush hour on a Monday. He offers zero help, and will make sure to plan the tests at the absolute worst times(the Monday after homecoming). If you are thinking of taking this class just don't.

One of the worst humans I have ever been in contact with. This professor is not only a horrible teacher in lecture, but has no respect for his students. Very unprofessional, and honestly very immature and rude.

This professor does not care whether his students succeed or not. He is agitating, annoying and simply immature. I have not heard one person talk positively about him or how he teaches. Very rude and unprofessional.

Lectures usually didn't take the full 75 minutes but does not cover enough of the math that you need for the homework- which takes hours. This class is the reason I had to subscribe to Chegg. Horrible professor.

Most of these reviews have summed Hegger up pretty well. Incredibly full of himself, intolerant towards people that learn differently, and has a complete lack of understanding on how to conduct lectures. I have had professors like this but only in engineering classes. Hegger is probably the worst teacher in the college of business.
Extremely unhelpful and does not care about students.

He gives off a rude first impression and is a stickler for literally no reason. You have to study extremely hard and essentially reteach yourself the course material before every exam by going back over the old homework. Homework can take hour's if you don't use chegg.
