I don't recommend this class if it's not required.

This class has 6 tests that account for 7/10 of the overall grade. Don't be weary if you bomb the first one or two, there is time to make the grade up. The midterm and final are strictly math. Hegger isn't very sociable, he likes to brag on himself quite a bit but if you ignore his boastfulness he does know a lot about the subject.

Dude loved to gas himself up. Kept talking about how he left his last job where he made so much more money just to bless us with his presence. This course had 6 exams, all were formula heavy but no cheat sheet. He does curve the exams and if you do the homework and the extra credit it can help. Class sucks, but if you try very hard it's not awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awful
literally don't do this to take this if you care at all about your mental health

Gives you minimal knowledge in lectures but good luck trying to do the homework without CHEGG... Never had a professor make the homework this hard without showing or giving you the resources to complete it on your own...

His personality reflects a lot of disappointment in his life to the point he might be apathetic towards helping others. He genuinely does not care about the learning outcome of any student. Exam Preparation in my experience is worthless because the questions are unfamiliar and impossible to plan for.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily Worst teacher I’ve ever had throughout my entire life. Doesn’t care at all about you as a student. Be prepared for hw that is very loosely related to test material.

I ended up having to drop this class because of how much trouble I was having. None of the material covered in lectures or really the book helped with homework/exam. The professor himself has a personality issue and acts like he doesn't actually want to help you or makes you feel stupid. If you can please just take this class with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not super approachable, but he is available. Gives a strict, somewhat rude first impression, but the class itself is manageable. He tells you what to do to do well on the test and mentions some specific topics in lecture. Do HW problems and read the book, you'll be fine. He gives a large curve. Lots of tests, so there is room to redeem yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hegger is pretty great. This is one of those "do all the work and you'll get an A" type class. There is a decent amount of reading and lectures to do on a week-to-week basis, but overall, I really think this guy does a solid job. Everything he tells you need to know for the exam somewhere in the lectures. I definitely recommend this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I should have dropped this course when I had the chance. Unfortunately, Hegger's section was the only class that fit into my schedule. He is disrespectful and arrogant and refuses to offer additional help to students. He told our class that it "wasn't his responsibility" to tell us how we should prepare for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's the worst. Not going to sugarcoat it. To top it off he isn't just difficult and a run-of-the-mill lecturer, he's also rude. The first time he said something nice to us was after exam 5, of 6 exams in the course. All of which were difficult. Also first exams of each unit are definition heavy and the second exams were formula heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is easily the worst professor I have had. Avoid taking a class with him at all costs if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 350 characters is not enough to describe how bad this professor is. I have been to three schools across 3 different regions. I have studied abroad in different countries and have been around the world. I have never met a worse teacher. He is by far the worst and proves how bad the tenure system is to us. He should not be a teacher here or anywhere

Heggar has easily been my worst professor throughout my entire college career. He's constantly doing the bare minimum, and could care less about how you. Heggar told our entire lecture hall the first day "I don't care if you were at your best friends funeral in St. Louis, or anything else if you weren't able to complete an assignment it's a 0."
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor you will ever have. This guy has no bedside manners, thinks of himself as a god amongst his students, and will not help you in any way. "I'm in no position to tell you how to study so never ask me for any help related to studying". I advise you to either put off this class as long as possible until there's a new professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever had! Not only does he wait till the last minute to post assignments, or has to be reminded Monday morning they still arent posted, he is rude and doesnt care AT ALL about his students. My mother-in-law passed. Her services were the day of an exam (fully online class) and he refused to give me an extension

Where to start? Everything below is completely accurate! I understand teaching a course this large must be hard, but it shouldn't be the students responsibility to teach themselves this much just because he doesn't adapt to different learning styles. Lectures are pointless, homework is hard, test are stressful, yet somehow I currently have a B??
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The way he has his class set up needs to be fixed in total you will have 7 exams in the class which is a ridiculous amount for any class. He doesn't give any good study tools besides a book and your past hw. the hw also only prepares you for 1/2 of the tests as there is basically no concept questions and are just math questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Can see why people don't love the huge FIN3000 setting but I had Hegger for 4 classes, the smaller ones were great and about as easy as 3000.
Too many exams

Honestly terrible. He spends half the class talking about hating students needing help, he believes he's too good for that. He refuses to curve or improve grades, yet his exams and quizzes are so short that if you miss a question you practically lose a letter grade. Many nights spent crying trying to figure out what to do with this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most frustrating courses in my college career. He doesn't go over any word problems that may be on the exams and he expects you to memorize a ridiculous amount of content. I don't think he knows that we take more than one course per semester. Get ready to teach yourself.

Prof. Hegger is literally the worst. As a straight-A honor student, I got a B+ in this class by the skin of my teeth. He spends 50% of his lectures talking about how much students suck and how great he is. All assignments are auto-graded, tests are auto-graded, lectures are pre-recorded in 2019, he makes getting help hard. What does he even do?

I got a 100% on my final exam and finished with a 889.75/1000 points available in the class. I was a .25 OF A POINT off of an A and he decides that there is "nothing he can do" to change my grade by a fraction of a point. Absolutely ridiculous class rules and grading policy overall as well. Highly don't recommend.

His lectures are chalked full of good stuff, and he is a really nice guy. If you email him asking for help, he will respond in the next hour. Reading the book isn't completely necessary, but skimming through it and finding definitions and equations helps a lot. Take decent notes and pay half attention and you will be fine.
Hegger is just a terrible teacher who thinks he is better than everyone. Not a good person, and should not be a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class isn't the hardest in the world but Heggers rules are ridiculous. In an online course exams were open from 7:30 AM to 9:45 am. With 6 exams and 4 quizzes that means youre waking up early 10 times for no reason. Also, exams took 75 minutes to complete but if you started after 8:15 AM you wouldnt receive full credit. Big ego. Dumb rules.
The class is test heavy, but the lectures don't really help. The lectures are vague but the book will help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: not too much work homework wise. actually learned a lot. however his lecture slides are often wrong (and he doesnt update) so you will have to rely on teaching yourself anything revolving numbers. will not be open to making accommodations for you. ego
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the worst teachers at Mizzou. Lectures are a part of your grade, there are SIX exams, and tons of homework every week. His lectures are dull, surface level, and you will not learn much. Twice, you will have back-to-back exams in the semester. Take this class with someone else. It's clear he does not want to and will not teach you anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I studied on average 4-5 hours per test (6 tests total) but since the Corona hit I barely studied, but still walked out with a B. I feel like the average person could read a book about basic finance / economics and retain actual useful information unlike this class were you're doing pointless calculations you'll never use in your life again.

The man cant decide whether this is an easy or hard class. In his lectures, he goes over pretty basic material but doesn't go over harder material. He teaches the concepts, but never goes over how to do the problems. He then has easy questions for attendance, so you think you know it till you get to the hw and don't know what you're doing
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am over all a good student. I do most of my readings. I take notes and show up to every single class. I have over a 4.5 GPA. This class is only 2 weeks in and is already the hardest thing I have done in college. I am a senior and have already taken accounting. Get ready to try to teach your self on calculations.

Spent 50% of the semester talking about the good old days when he wasnt a professor and made a lot more money (?) He was great with extra credit and dropping our lowest exam (also no final woop woop) Pretty boring lectures so most of the semester was teaching myself the material & didnt do too bad

He is a very easygoing and knowledgeable professor. As long as you show up to class and you somewhat pay attention, you should get an A. Lots of room for error with his grading system. He also has some pretty good dad jokes. Professor Hegger is just a cool guy.

Going to class sucks but it makes the homework a lot easier. thinks he's funny but it sometimes just comes across like a jerk. TA's were super helpful outside of class with homework and preparing for exams.

His homework is extremely tough, especially since we don't go over it much in class beforehand. Highly recommend using Chegg. For exams, they aren't that bad - use LearnSmart through the homework to really help you out. There are not as many calculations as you think there will be on exams. If you show him your work on HW, he will give you credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Extremely rude, calls students out in class for minor things just to show his authority over the class, makes others feel small to make himself feel tall, very unprofessional, uploaded online lecture due to cancelled class and used a 2015 syllabus in 2019 to tell us about upcoming exam-wrong date and time on it. Does not help students in any way.

Prof. Hegger is witty, wise, and genuinely wants to help his students do well in his course. The course itself req. way more than BA15/2500 to do well, but if you attend class, do the hw, and 1/2 prepare for the exams then you can get an A. Pro: VERY accessible office hrs for HW/course. Con: STICKLER FOR ATTENDANCE, and will NOT answer silly emails
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class consists of several homework assignments - at least 1 per week and 6 exams. The exams aren't too difficult if you actually study and he does usually curve them. This class was more annoying than it was truly difficult. As others have said, Hegger himself is some one who thinks he's very funny, but is really just full of himself.

Worst professor ever. Does not give out study guides. I understand that he wants to make it more realistic, but I have to prioritize my time trying to study for 4 other classes so at least give some sort of guide. Also refuses to tell you how many questions are going to be on the exam. He's arrogant and sucks, be prepared to teach yourself.

Amount of homework and exams is ridiculous! Homework 2-3 a week on top of 6 exams throughout a 16 week semester. Going to class is a must because it is part of your grade. If he didn't make it mandatory no one would go because his lectures are the most dry and boring thing ever. Overall I hated his class with a passion.
Show up, breathe, and get an A. Then take higher level classes and realize you have no clue what's going on. This class was a waste of time, and didn't give me what I needed to take other classes.

This class is not actually taught my Hegger. You will never see him, but he writes the tests. The whole class is taught by the Graduate Assistants. The Grad Assistants dont actually know whats on the test until a couple days before it. They dont explain how to do the equations very well, and I found myself teaching myself the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Hegger is a good professor. Easiest finance courses I have taken have been with Hegger. Very informative, can go off into tangents sometimes from previous work experience, but tests are easy. Tells more dad jokes than you are prepared for. Overall, easy A, but you learn a lot in the process.

He takes lecture attendance at the beginning and end of class. Lectures are fairly disorganized and not super useful. Exams are super straightforward and just like the more advanced homework problems. He's kind of obnoxious but not terrible overall.

Hegger is a great professor. He is one of the more laid back professors. If the University didn't have him, I would assume half of the students wouldn't even attempt to study finance (because all of the other professors are really hard). His classes are straight forward. Do the equations, tests are easy to study for.
Awsome teacher better class, id recomend taking every class he teaches

Yes there are 6 exams but they are short and not difficult. All you have to do to get an A is doing every homework assignment until you get 100%, show up to get participation points,  and master the homework assignments before each exam because the exam is basically the homework with new numbers. Plus, Hegger is hilarious! 10/10 would take again

Class was taught by grad students which we didn't find out until the first day of class. 13 quizzes (1/wk) and 6 exams total. Exams are written by higher ups, not those who actually teach the class. Poor organization (Accounting is first unit and it's not a prereq) & lots of busywork via MindTap. GA Ryan Ulrich was very helpful and well-prepared.

Very informative and experienced teacher who gives at least one example for every topic. downside is that he has 6 exams in a semester, but the exams are easier because there is not a lot of information per exam. Really funny teacher who keeps class entertaining

Really bad teacher as far as being organized and explaining concepts. Always talks about how past students complain about his teaching style and unfairness in grading. Very inconsistent in all aspects. Does offer a large extra credit opportunity, but it requires you to skip other classes which means you're out of luck if you have an exam that day.

one chapter a class, and six tests total. He is one of the few professors who really answered the e-mail, and he also gave several chances for generous extra points. Tests are really not hard if you read the textbook.
Best teacher at Mizzou

He is one of the worst teacher I have ever had. He is awful at explaining the material and goes way too fast. When we ask him to go over things in class he doesn't write any of the work on the board. I had to take this for my business minor and I suggest taking Accounting first and avoiding Hegger. Text book is needed to do homework, lots of exams.

He's your stereotypical finance man and extremely boring for an 8am lecture. However, the class is a piece of cake if you actually read the book and understand the homework questions. The homework problems are identical to exam problems just with different numbers. Anyone saying it's hard, needs to put in a little more effort outside of class.
Back to back tests twice (exam 2 then midterm and exam 4 then final).  Unorganized and bad at explaining the material in lecture.

One of the worst professors I've had.  He goes way too fast in lectures and doesn't post them online.  He is very disorganized and gives more assignments than necessary and assigns them at random times. In addition, there are 6 exams this semester, with a regular test and a midterm (as well as a regular test and a final) in back to back weeks.
Great teacher, if you want to learn.

Hirni is by far one of my favorite college math TA I've had so far. He explain the material clearly, goes over it again if asked, and has a sense of humor when teaching. He's a great TA and would recommend him to anyone taking MATH 1300
Get this guy out of Mizzou, he is genuinely a terrible professor in every way possible.

Horrible professor, I would consider any other course before his. He's doesn't care to help his students. Trying to email him and receive any type of help is almost impossible. Please don't even subject yourself to this horrible professor.
Yikes. This guy has no clue what he is doing.
My main problem with Mr. Hirni was the class. It sucked and the course head was not good. Mr. Hirni is funny but really green, so he wasn't always that helpful.
the class is challenging, but if you lock in during class you'll be fine. she really cares about you and wants you to pass, so if you genuinely make an effort to improve you'll be fine.
she's such a nice person!
I enjoyed my time with Prof Hiles. It was J1300, so there was obviously a lot of writing but she was clearly knowledgeable and wanted us to succeed.

I was really struggling in her class initially, but that really turned around later in the semester. She stuck with me and helped me through it, and was willing to meet outside of class to discuss my grade and what to do about it. She was very supportive. Though her feedback was lacking at times, she made up for it by being a solid lecturer.

Professor Hills expects entry level students to write at the level of an experienced journalist. The feedback given on assignments is minimal at best, lacks description, and is contradictory. She's unfamiliar with the curriculum she's been given. Despite her teaching flaws, she is a nice person but I would not take her class again.

Do NOT take Science Writing unless you have a serious interest in science. Sara does not teach. She relies on guest speakers to do her job for her, yet she expects stories to be on a professional level. She doesn't give clear feedback, her edits are usually very condescending. She will make you pull your hair out. Avoid taking this at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved having Sara for Investigative. She really helped out my team even after class ended and we were in the middle of summer. She is one of the most passionate, caring, and enthusiastic professors I've ever had and I'm so glad I had the opportunity to have her. If you work hard, stay on top of things, and stay engaged, you're fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is run through Google Drive and you will not receive any grades until the absolute last week of the semester. She leaves unclear editing marks that often contradict each other. She also will ask questions about content that is clearly present, so her reading comprehension is lacking. She rarely teaches, instead bringing in speakers.

If you didn't tear your hear out before, you will when you start taking this class; the course load doesn't seem too ridiculous until you receive your first round of edits. Hint: You probably will probably have to rewrite everything because directions remain unclear. I would have had an easier time understanding someone speaking fluent Mandarin.

2200 is very fast-paced and gets into the material on day one. Prepare to struggle if you are given a bad group. Fortunately for me, my group mates were hard-working and collaborative throughout. The peer evaluations are a great way to hold members accountable. Initially disliked the course but found myself liking it toward the end. Prof is kind.

She was super nice and clear with expectations throughout the course, but it felt like way too many projects per week for a 2 credit class. I think she's great for the higher Strat Comm classes--she knows what she's doing--but for J2200 there was a strange mix of projects and busy work in the schedule. 

She did not round my 93.96% up to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just took my final for this class and was excited to hop on here and brag about her! Attendance is required, but her lectures are always engaging, memorable, and entertaining. If you just want to pass, show up to every class and take decent notes. If you want an A read the textbook! Great class for all directions of strat comm.
Great professor, very engaging classes and lectures. Classwork was relevant and helped me grow in my major.

Prof Higginbotham has some of the best, well-structured lectures I've taken in the J-school. She's always very well prepared for class. Attendance isn't required but I very rarely wanted to skip it because her content was so interesting. The group work can be tedious but that's standard for a strategic communications class. I highly recommend her.

Holly was an amazing professor! Organized and very intelligent. She is my favorite professor I have had so far in the J School. For an online/ async. class, she was very engaging and interesting. Her lectures were clear and included useful examples to help make the concepts understandable. The class is easy, just time-consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Holly was hands down my most organized and clear professor I had during the fall 2020 semester. If you do your work and you end up with a good group for the group projects, then you will do just fine.

Loved Holly soo much, she is the nicest person ever. The class is pretty much all group assignments and quizzes. As long as you have a good group you will get an A. Everything I learned is applicable to my future in PR.
Group projects can be graded harsh so just include as much detail as possible. She cares about students but lectures can be pretty boring, just go to every class because group work is random.
Clearly one of the most competent and prepared of the J-school professors. Made lectures dynamic. You have to go to class and study, but expectations were straightforward.

Holly is wonderful. Overall an awesome lecturer. Lots of relevant and interesting examples. Group projects in class about once a week so make sure you go to class. Like some said below, I didn't read the box except when studying for tests and did well in the class. Tests are not hard if you attend lecture and take decent notes.

Great lecturer and professor, and she made the topics seem interesting. Lots of guest lecturers and surprise group projects. I got by without reading the book, but you definitely have to go to every class. Exams were very easy and straightforward. She was very friendly and willing to meet outside class.

Holly is the best professor I have had at Mizzou. She is so knowledgeable about the subject and it is very evident that she genuinely cares about her student's learning. Her tests aren't super easy but if you show up to class and study a moderate amount you'll be fine.
This is a great class. Holly is very fair on exams and group work - if you show up and you know what you're doing you'll be fine. It's not a stressful class but you learn a lot.

Holly is a good lecturer. Group work days are at random so be prepared to go to every class. Although I never used my class notes, I absolutely read the book. Lecture notes were just a repeat of the book material. Holly is a well-spoken, caring professor.

Holly is amazing- you can really tell she's passionate about what she does. There's random group assignment days throughout the semester and she doesn't tell you when so you have to show up every day. Most of test material is straight from lecture and only a tiny bit from the book, but she supplies study guides.
I really enjoyed this class with her! Lectures were informative but to-the-point and exams were a breeze.

I had her for Strategic Writing 1 Lab. She is awesome! Very nice, very helpful. I felt she was a fairly easy grader, and she was just very helpful with ads. I felt like I knew exactly what needed to be improved in each ad. Also she was a good communicator through e-mail, etc. I would highly recommend her!

Hilda is a good person and outside of class she is very caring and helpful. However, I didn't learn anything new in her class and even though I made an effort to talk and participate every day, I somehow still got terrible participation grades. I don't think my Spanish really got any better. I like her, I did not like her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Must keep up with readings and participate or you can't pass (but this is true of most Spanish classes). She seems a little tough at first, took some warming up to her, but by the end our whole class loved her! She has high expectations, but only b/c she truly cares about your learning and improvement. Not hard to do well if you put in the effort.

Hilda has great intentions, but she does not realize how rude she can be at times. This particular class had many students who were avid about Spanish and could actually speak it pretty well. Regardless she still would scold you if you got a question wrong. Also the class structure is confusing so you have to talk to the other students in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: At the beginning of the semester, I wasn't very fond of her but she really is a cool person. Shes very opinionated but she cares about her students and she loves to teach. The homework problems are the same as test problems and she can tell who did the homework so do it. The vocab can be tough but try and she will reward the effort and dedication.

Easily the worst professor and teacher I have ever had. She makes fun of students when they get answers wrong, even threatening to jump out the window when someone made a grammatical error out loud. She is rude, condescending, and mean. I would NEVER EVER recommend her as a professor. She is HORRIBLE. DO NOT take her class.

One of the worst Spanish teachers I have had. Be ready to work hard everyday in class. She expects a lot from her students and she becomes angry when her expectations aren't met. She is not very clear with what she wants, so most of the time it is a guessing game. Strongly suggest a class GroupMe to discuss what is going on in class.

Hilda is an awesome professor, although she took some time to get used to. She is strict on attendance and participation. Homework every day, but nothing you turn in (but do it because you go over it and that counts as participation). Tests are tough, and essays are not bad. She is very helpful if you take the time to see her. Also very funny!

My favorite Spanish teacher that I have ever had. Although the tests are hard, she does give points to you and tries to boost everyones' grades. She is so nice and really made my decision easy to become a spanish double major.
Fennel is generally sweet and grades pretty easily. She can be a bit unorganized or unclear with directions. Overall I enjoyed 3160 and would recommend this course and Professor Fennel to others

Professor Fennell is one of the best Spanish teachers I have had at Mizzou.  She is really funny and a really easy grader.  The course was slightly disorganized but she keeps it interesting.  You mostly talk about current events and have debates instead of just reading Spanish lit. stories.  Most of the homework is just reading an article.

She is the worst teacher I've ever had. I literally dreaded coming to class. She is not very helpful she ridicules her students constantly. Frequently kids were crying in class because they raised their hand and said the wrong answer. At all costs, avoid having her as a teacher AT ALL COSTS!

Fennel is assuming and harsh, and belittles students in class and through emails. Her directions are unclear- she's submitted 8 different syllabi to us, and changes directions at the last second. Our participation grade depends on how much we talk in class; however 70-90% of class is spent listening to her talk about her life.

Senora Fennell is one of the most fun spanish teachers I've had at Mizzou. She really cares about you learning AND getting a good grade. She is funny and always willing to meet with you to help you understand a concept further. My only complaint was how unorganized much of the course was, but she was at the mercy of the Spanish 3 course coordinator

Things started off rocky with Hilda but at the end of the day she is looking out for your best interest. She will try and help you in the best way she can but YOU have to put in the effort. Email her, meet with her, and definitely PARTICIPATE! She'll appreciate it!

Participation points are pretty important, I participated nearly everyday and receieved a 27/50 for participation. I had friends in other spanish 3 classes and they claimed their class was pretty easy compared to this one. I agree you will need to get on her good side right away.

I had Senora Fennell for Spanish 3. Sometimes it is hard to understand her english, and her she speaks in spanish very fast. The best advice I have is to get on her good side from the beginning. Sit in the front, participate and pretty much just suck up. If you know the material, you're gold. I received a B which I was happy with. Good luck!

He has great lecture content, optional homework that was helpful, and a list of textbook problems he recommends doing. Doing the recommended problems and practice exams was enough to get good grades on the midterms. He is by far the best calc 3 prof you could take if you're trying to actually learn and understand the material.

I took the honours section of Calc 3, and like other ratings, I feel like there is not a better professor for it. Hofmann is extremely knowledgeable and has great, lighthearted lectures, though tests are really demanding (but he does provide good practice exams). Honours section is hardly different than regular. Optional, but helpful, homework.

There was optional homework and difficult exams. Attendance is not taken, but if you miss a class, you miss the notes as there is none posted on Canvas. No note cards for exams, but you get practice exams that are sometimes helpful. The averages on his exames were very low, but ended up getting curved.

Mr. Hofmann was very knowledgeable and would answer all questions that were given to him. However, throughout the course it seemed as if he would speak in higher language than we understood yet. It made it very difficult to follow along in class as well as ask questions since there were times that I didn't even know what question I could ask.

The class is very well laid out and he is incredible at teaching the material. The homework annoying but helpful, and he is very knowledgeable about general math (helped me with some more advanced questions about the concepts). Take this professor for calc 3 at all costs if genuinely learning the material is important to you. Exams are rigorous.

Dr. Hofmann was my professor for the honors 2300 section and I could not be happier with who I was given. Great guy who is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Lectures are very important and are a must to stay caught up in the class. But lectures were always fun with a lighthearted tone. Practice exams were quite similar to actual exams.

I took the honors section of this course and Hofmann was the best choice I could've made. The course is structured with 3 midterms, a 1-1 exam where he asks you questions and you answer by working it out on a blackboard, and the comprehensive final. He makes everything a lot smoother by giving you practice exams, would recommend for honors students

Hofmann is a great teacher. His lectures were great to listen to and follow. He also had a light and fun attitude during class which made a hard class feel more bearable. His homework extra credit was great practice and a good help to my grade. Would recommend taking his class.

His lectures were funny and kept some harder topics light-hearted. The review sessions before each test were an absolute must and were somewhat entertaining to go to at times. Overall, one of the top math professors at Mizzou. However, attending class is a must otherwise the material will be really hard to catch up on.

Professor Hofmann is a great teacher. His lectures are sometimes a bit difficult to understand, but that is due to the theoretical nature of the material. Furthermore, the optional hw and practice he assigns really helps for understanding the material. His tests are not extremely difficult as the practice tests are very similar to the actual test.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall I think that professor Hoffman is a pretty decent teacher. His lectures were alright, you definitely will have to do a lot of learning by yourself. Prof Hoffman will not hold your hand. There will definately be a curve at the end of the semester. He is a lot better than the other teachers that I heard about at mizzou.

Hofmann knows his stuff, but his lectures are difficult to understand. He doesn't really explain what he's doing or why he's doing it, and he doesn't post his notes online, so try not to skip his lectures. Exams are kind of like the sample ones, but really be ready for anything on those things. Try and take a different professor if you can.

Professor Hoffman is awesome. If you do the "optional" homework, nothing on the tests is going to be a surprise. As long as you keep up with the lectures, nothing will be too difficult. Way easier than Calc 2. He has limited office hours but is still willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was fairly difficult, and I nearly dropped out after a couple weeks, but I stayed and was able to pass. 3 midterm exams and 1 final. He had a grading scale for each test based on class performance. There is a class curve, The only problem is that he doesnt change your test grades until the end of the semester.

Had Steven Hofmann for Calc 3 and in his lectures he goes really fast and makes us write down a lot of formulas, not mentioning where they came from and then after he explains a certain topic (which he does horribly)... when he explains a topic he uses very complicated terminology... he doesn't let us try some practice problems at all

Does not use the grading criterion given by the Mathematics department. Speaks a math "language" higher than the typical calculus 3 professors.  As a major, his grading dropped my g.p.a slightly. He curves each test but you yourself never know your real grade, even if you ask in office hours.

Uses his own grading criteria rather than the math department's. The homework on webassign was optional, if you did it, it could only help your grade but he wouldn't count it if it hurt your overall grade. 3 midterms where he made up his own problems so do the homework and hope he made the tests manageable. He did curve each test based on everyone.

Hill was a great professor. she's caring and understand we are not doctorates in anatomy. she doesn't treat or teach us like we've been doing it for 20 years. you could fail all exams and if homework is all done still get a C. she's very understanding and funny. she does do iclicker for points so go to class!
great professor def taken again!

This class was a total waste of my time. Lectures are useless because the professor does nothing but yap and draw awful "diagrams" that are just lines. Worst professor and class I've taken so far, I do not recommend it at all unless you want your entire life to be about studying for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took the lecture in conjunction with the lab which helped. It's flipped, but attending lectures helped with understanding because she draws and does iclicker questions. She gives out candy even if you answer a question incorrectly. content is just insane bc its anatomy but shes does a good job. the guided notes were definitely the most helpful.

She talks and laughs during exams. She expects you to do work before the semester starts and her lecture videos are annoying because she's got load of spit in her mouth when she talks. Fast paced so there's not a lot of room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Talks during tests and laughs. Very annoying. She spits in the mic and her lecture vids are either really quiet or loud. She doesn't seem like she's mean but it's frustrating how the class is taught. You have to do lectures/study stuff before the semester even begins at least for spring semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She creates a very distracting test environment such as laughing and talking to the TA or another student. She makes you start class work before the semester even begins and her lecture videos are very annoying to watch (she spits in the mic or the noise will be quiet and then loud). She's not mean but I wish she would have been better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was not super involved with students, other than just providing lectures. Classroom was flipped style which can make in class lectures better if you keep up with the work.

A very content heavy class, but is doable. To get a good grade you will have to study and do the homework. There is post class quizzes and pre class homework due each week. It is a hybrid class, so you learn from the online lectures posted each week.

There's a lot of material too cover, but it is a doable class. You watch pre-recorded lectures on your own time and in class lectures are mainly just about diseases. For tests study the study guide and the slides. I didn't go to class much, but prof hill seems like a great person. She gives out candy and you do jeopardy before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Try not to be intimidated by the class. It is tough but completely doable. You are going to have to study if you want to pass. Dr. Hill is funny and does give out candy for answering questions. Study the terms and diseases, that's mainly what's on the tests. There are pre-class homework and post-class quizzes, so there are lots of points available.
This class was not too bad. You have to study and memorize because you don't really know what will be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: All material is online. Pre-class and post-class homework. Overall, just a lot of material to learn and understand. Lecture is just a review of the material that is being covered for the week. I really liked Dr. Hill and she seemed to genuinely love anatomy.

I liked Dr.Hill! I found the layout of the class to be easy to follow and understand, as the class uses a flipped lecture structure. Exams were not too difficult, just study and go to class and you'll be fine. Not an outstanding professor, but I liked her overall.

Alot of work, but that's to be expected with anatomy. You just watch pre-recorded lectures on your own time, so it's hard to grade the prof but she seems nice. Expect to memorize a lot of stuff, but overall just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You absolutely have to watch the lectures and study for the exams. There are only three exams and you have to do good on them or you won't pass. You don't have to go to class, but study!

Dr. Hill wants her students to succeed, and she ensures this through providing lots of resources, reminders, and checkpoints throughout the course. She is great to interact with and will offer to review your exams with you or help you with studying tips to get to where you want to be. This isn't to say that you don't need to do work to succeed

She was a great professor. The class setup is a flipped classroom, which I didn't love, but she made the most of it and used many examples that helped us learn the material. She was accessible and very passionate about her subject.
In person lectures are not very helpful, you can pass the class without going to them. The class is kind of self taught so make sure you can keep up. Watch lectures ahead of time

I would highly recommend taking lab and lecture together, as they cover the same material but are listed as separate courses. I think what makes this class hard is how fast-paced it is: you have to keep up watching lectures to understand the material, but if you do that and study, you will be just fine. Dr. Hill seems to really love anatomy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She's not friendly and seems unhappy to be teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are online and in person lectures are a joke. The in person lectures count towards attendance through iClicker. Make sure to take notes and study hard on her online lectures. She gives mid level advice on how to do better on an exam. I'll have to retake the class again, but I won't be doing it through her or the school.

Her in person lectures are kind of a joke, they didn't really help me learn anything. Make sure to watch all the lectures and take good notes. For the tests, I would definitely do the study guides she gives out because they really prepare you for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom. Fast-paced regarding the amount of material to learn for each exam. Lots of memorization. Weekly pre-class homework and post-class quiz. 3 exams. I studied for each test at the very minimum of one week in advance. Dr. Hill gives a lot of supplemental material for extra practice which is helpful for studying.

She is so passionate about anatomy, and is super accessible outside of class which helped me a lot. After each exam I met with her to review the problems I missed, which was very beneficial for me! I really enjoyed this class and loved how it was set up.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There is so much information that it is incredibly fast, detailed, and hard to keep up with. If you are not self motivated and work really hard you will not do well, high school anatomy isnt going to help enough in here. She makes you work for the grade and doesnt do extra credit. She is a great person who happens to teach a really hard subject

Anatomy is just a difficult subject. There are only 3 exams in this class and the rest of the class is graded on homework and quizzes which are pretty easy. Each exam is over 3-4 units, so it is difficult because of the amount of information. I got a better grade on each exam.

To start, anatomy is a very hard class, but Dr. Hill works very hard to give her students all of the tools you could need to pass the class. She provides practice quizzes, review sheets, she records every class, and gives tons of practice opportunities. The lectures are short and concise. She is a very good teacher for a very difficult class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't think she is necessarily the worst professor. I went to office hours and she did give me advice. But, I did the most in this class and barley got by. The test are very hard to study for, I didn't do well on any of them yet I put weeks into studying. I would think this would be way better to take in person. Good luck.

While Dr. Hill is extremely intelligent, she is not good at teaching, just telling and letting us fend for ourselves. Its normally a flipped class so it was half online anyway, but with the pandemic it was all online. I basically taught myself this entire course. She is understanding but there is no extra credit and will not bump any grades.

Flipped classroom so you watch the lectures on your own time then do activities in class once a week to get points. All memorization but still was not very hard. If you study, you will easily get an A.

I took this course during COVID and that was the wrong choice. Theres a lot of material/very notes heavy. Hill (and TAs) give what advice they can but also have difficult exams that average low. Begin studying as you learn the material and dont fall behind. Class size is large but Hill is okay at responding to emails (her TAs are even better)

First professor I had at MU and she left a great impression! Most organized canvas page I have ever seen. She will meet with you to go over your test if you want. Held review sessions. Keep up with power points, lectures, homework, and quizzes and you'll be fine. This class was only hard because of the content, she tries to make it fun and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Where do I even start? I had an 86% going into the final exam, bombed it, and now my grade went down to a 79.76%. I sent a respectful email to maybe see if they would round me to a B. But, she instead sent out a mass email saying "We won't responding to emails about grade rounds". She ruined my GPA and doesn't deserve a lick of respect. Peace.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory (2 points per lecture) and do a lot on iClicker. Really helps if you do show up consistently. There is pre-homework and post-homework (super easy), and if you do it on time everytime get lots of cushion for the tests. Mine was hybrid, which watched lectures online and did homework and then did less in lecture, which I liked.

This class was basically online. The face2face were not helpful but it was required for you to go to get your 2 points. There was a lot of online quizzes and homework to remember to do, but the answers were usually on quizlet. If you want an A, read the book and make study guides. Cherry Hill sounds like a nice lady but her instruction is helpless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mostly watching online lectures and self-teaching, so you have to be willing to keep up with the class on your own time. Lots of info in short time, but not too hard, especially if you've had previous exposure to physiology or anatomy. Mult. choice tests. Dr. Hill's weekly lectures are necessary to do well on exams. Straightforward & funny!

Lots of memorizing. If you keep up on lessons and don't fall behind it may be easier, but I didn't. There are two test and the final so each test covered a ton of information. The test were't weighted much, but this is definitely a class that you need to study a lot just get a semi-decent test grade.  Quizes and extra credit bump you up a bit.

Class was a hybrid, basically tought yourself online, which I particularly liked. I found looking at the powerpoints multiple times really helped my grade. Class is all memorization, and isn't hard imo. Kept track of attendance by clickers, also gave extra credit this way too. Covers clinical situations in class which you will see on test.

Taking anatomy as a hybrid class didn't really work for me. While Professor Hill is great and funny, I don't think I've gotten much out of this class since each chapter is about a 10 minute online video. It might work for some, just didn't for me and found that it made it much more difficult. Having the lab as a separate class also made it worse.

You show up to class once a week and Dr. Hill reviews the material from her tegrity lectures (flipped-hybrid course, so it feels like you kind of teach yourself). She does clicker points during class, so that helps your grade. Tests aren't bad - study your notes from her tegrity lectures.

Professor Hill was a good instructor and taught the information well. She was easy to understand, despite the information being specific and difficult. Attendance is once a week since the course is hybrid and I honestly would not study until the day/night before and received mid 80's on all three exams. An A is definitely achievable.
Really chill and most classes get out 20-30 minutes early for J1300, at least for my class. Really nice and gives super good feedback, grading kinda harsh and to the point he doesn't mess around

Engaging lecturer & generally pleasant. I am definitely a better writer now than I was before I took his class. He is happy to review your work before you submit it, and he gives great pointers. If you ask for help, your grade will improve.
It's easy to get a good grade just by going to class and turning in the assignments. You have to be on top of the projects though, he won't give you a million reminders.
Boring lectures and unclear assignments at points.

Dr. Hutchins is the best professor I have ever had. Organic Chemistry is not an easy subject, but Dr. Hutchins goes above and beyond for her students. Her office hours are very beneficial and she has even offered review sessions via zoom the evening before exams. In her class, make sure to take advantage of her resources.

Dr. Hutchins cares about students' success; utilize office hours!
Unlimited attempts on HW assignments and extra credit offered for an extra 25/650pts (675 max.).
3 exams + mandatory final.
IMO, exams struggle with content + occasionally construct validity but it is what it is.
"Honors" = short paper on a molecule of your choice. (easy)

She's very nice and will help you if you ask questions/go to office hours. Orgo is still a hard class and she lectures quickly. Graded on hw, a project, and the final. She offers extra credit if you do the ALEKS modules, and there's usually an EC question on each test. Go to the lectures and use the slideshows and resources she posts to study.
Kristen Hutchins is truly a godsend. I think if I didn't have her for orgo I would have dropped out. She is so nice. It's a hard class but she does everything in her power to help us get through it.

Dr. Hutchins is amazing at supporting her students with the difficult subject material. There are tons of opportunities to ask questions/get clarification with her zoom Q&A sessions and office hours. In my opinion, THE BEST CHEM PROFESSOR Mizzou has. If you don't get a good grade it's because organic chem is hard not that she isn't a good teacher.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Dr. Hutchins clearly has never taught undergraduates in a 50 minute setting, and she fails miserably in this class. Every exam was WAY too long for the allocated time and includes numerous questions meant to trick students. If you are going to take this class, and you aren't religious yet, pick a religion and start praying.

This professor consistently made demeaning comments and created an uncomfortable class environment. Tests were unnecessarily long and nearly impossible to finish. The course felt disorganized, and she seriously needs to reevaluate her teaching style. I STRONGLY would not recommend this class, if you want to be happy ever again!! STAY AWAY

This is the worst class I've ever taken. She requires 500 words for the silliest assignments. I just had to write an 800 word essay about dumplings. So unecessary. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The biggest waste of my time in my college career.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: honestly, this teacher was the worst experiences I've had. There were constant quizzes, and doing poorly on just one made it hard to recover your grade. The workload was overwhelming with tons of homework and assignments (way more than my major-related classes). I wouldn't recommend taking this class as there are way too many assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class just started and its already an absurd amount of work and basically all self taught. Very few vague instructions on how to complete assignments and the main sources of information for the assignments (that are ridiculously writing heavy) are online and you have to go through an insane amount of work to learn the content. DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Laziest teacher I've ever met. Doesn't actually grade the excessively long, irrelevant papers she makes you write, just uses AI to grade. Doesn't actually know anything about course content and won't be able to answer questions. Don't waste your time with her, take this class with a professor who actually cares about their job and their students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class as a finance and econ major wanting something easy for an online course to fulfill a humanities requirement. To my surprise, this class was full of lots of reading and a lot of writing. Every assignment you complete aside from quizzes are writing intensive. The grading is all by AI and there is no work put in on her part.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Most immature professor I have ever had. Unclear about due dates, Sent screenshot proof of assignment having no due date. She would claim she doesn't "know how to read a screenshot". Received extremely rude/hostile emails from her in all caps. Had A all semester, received one zero, went to a D-. Had a higher authority check her for fishy grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class has been terrible. There is an outrageous amount of writing for a freshman non-WI course. This class is full of busy work that takes no critical thinking to complete, and doesn't connect to the course. I wholeheartedly regret taking this class. Save yourself some time and frustration. Take a different class.

Took this class online and never actual met her. Everything goes by the book and Is graded through Packback's AI. I don't think she takes the time to read/grade anything. Never received any feedback on how to improve and felt like she didn't want to talk to me when I would email her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I signed up for an easy-A food class that wouldn't require much, as it's my last semester attending the University. Instead, I come across a class that has more to do with writing countless discussions, papers, and more papers, demanding much more than that of any writing class taken. Unless you like writing about nonsense, don't take the class.
There definitely are a good amount of assignments but they are all pretty easy, including the writing assignments. As long as you keep up with the basic criteria, this class is an easy A.

You can get away with not reading the textbook thoroughly for the most part. I skimmed specific sections for certain assignments but never read an entire chapter. The grading is very tough, especially considering your only learning materials are a textbook she didn't write and discussion posts from peers. The class seems harder than it should be.

By joining this class you will get nothing more than arid readings and super difficult writing assignments. She is a tough grader and there are no lectures at all, you have to read the book and summarize all the information yourself, which is very time-consuming. Unless you're interested in intensive reading and writing course, don't take her class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She wants you to fear her even though shes just a little lady with too much useless education. Only teaching youll get is from the book so youll need to read. Weirdest part about her is how she doesnt even communicate with us directly instead all communication comes from the management so yeah I have no respect for this lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Hudson's lectures. She does a good job keeping them interesting! I thought all of her tests and assignments were fairly easy and straightforward. As long as you study some, you can get an easy A.

I got an A in the class, but it was no thanks to her. To get good grades on her quizzes, you have to read all of the assigned reading. Some of the test questions can be confusing and if you argue one with her, you will lose. She is very unapproachable. She did occasionally give extra credit, though.

Avoid this class if possible, definitely one of the worst I've taken at Mizzou.  Tests are ridiculous, she expects you to know things she never explains in class, and lectures are long and useless.  If you can, buy a book and teach yourself.  It's much more bearable that way.

Worst teacher I've had. Went into her office hours asking why I missed exam questions and she said, "You don't know that answer?" or "That was a fairly easy question". She makes you feel like you will never succeed. She expects WAY too much out of her students and thinks our lives revolve around her class. RUN AWAY! SAVE YOURSELF!

Does not know how to write a test. I really think she wants to try to break her students. If you try and talk to her about your grade she pretty much tells you that you won't succeed in a health related field if you cant do really well in her class. This was the feeling of many students in her class this semester.
If you have to take this class chose the online summer course.. It's a lot easier than the class during the semester... There are open book quizes online every week but no final!

This class is hard, however you just have to learn to play by her rules. For me, the info was very interesting and I enjoyed learning it, but her tests are hard!!! The best advice: USE THE BOOK! She gets her questions from the text. Highlight notes in the book, they are word for word! She isnt pleasant, but the class can be done with hard work.

Diet Therapy: I highly do not recommend taking this class unless you are required to say for nursing. She does not want her students to succeed at all. She gave two online exams, which had higher scores than in class exams. She then gave us a lecture on how we are all cheaters. The 2nd in class exam was meant for us all to fail. Highest score 72%.

She's really full of herself. When anyone asks her a question she acts like they are the dumbest person she has ever met. The first day she told us not to email her because she thinks it's rude not to talk to her in person. Her lectures are point-for-point from the book, so if you can read and comprehend then you really don't have to go to class.

She totally sucks as a professor! She doesn't make student expectations clear until after the whole class gets a bad grade on an assignment! She also contradicts herself a lot! It's her way her the highway always even if that means driving on the wrong side of the road!

Clearly well-educated on the topics teaching, but not good at articulating the knowledge needed for exams. In a class where the average exam grade hovered around a 50%, it was tough to know if we weren't learning the right things or not being taught the right things.
Fast-paced, math/matlab-heavy. From what I gather, very easy to pass with a C-, very hard to get an A.
Challenging but fair. Homework assignments are long but easy. Make sure you know them by heart for exams.

One of the toughest classes I've taken, but also one of the most rewarding. The material is dense—expect to work hard—but the professor explains everything with clarity. If you put in the time, you'll come out with a grade you're happy about. Expecting a B+.

Dr. Nassar is an infuriating professor. He makes assignments very easy and then absolutely destroys everyone on the exam. He takes no accountability when students do terribly. The averages have been in the 40s. He continues to blame the students instead of reflecting on the idea that the exams should actually cover class material.

Homework and projects are easy. Tests are extremely hard and take too much time. Exam averages are in the 40's with no curve. Mind you, this is a sophomore-junior level class, so none of us in there are dumb. I will say his lectures are fine, but the class kinda stinks :(

Hussein Nassar is the worst professor I've ever suffered under. By his own admission, his exams are only 60% material the class has seen before, putting the class average on every exam in the high 40%'s. Almost every student in the class is on the verge of failing, and he does everything he can to rationalize his choices with no accountability.

He's chill, his lectures are like meh but I think that's just because not many MechE's care about coding so no one participated (also at 8 am). The grading for the class used to be infamously hard but as of Fall 2024 it was very fair and honestly hard to not get at least a B. The TAs are really bad though and didn't know what they were doing.

The new grading scheme is MUCH less intimidating! There were chances for extra credit on both midterms and one of the projects. While this is still a demanding course, It is much more accessible now. Nassar is also very easy to listen to in lectures, and it is clear that he has an incredible knowledge of the subject. Funny guy, too!

New grading policy is much much better than past semesters. The course is still very rigorous but he is more than willing to answer questions/accomade students and the TAs are also very helpful. Pay attention in class and complete all the labs and you'll be fine.

Notorious professor for mechanical engineers. His grading system was more standard compared to his old system. The class content is difficult and will require heavy repetition. He is way way way more helpful if you go to office hours. Lectures can be very confusing but one on one is much better. I recommend doing practice exams at least 10 times.

Condescending in class. Nassar is one of the people that loves to see students fail. I have no idea why he is teaching at all especially an upper level course where I actually wanted to learn the content. The grading system is wild, I should have a way worse grade than I got. Be prepared to be frustrated and suffer.

Average grade FS21 was 2.3, 49 students got C's. Search "Mizzou grade distribution"
Take pass/fail or online in summer.
Grading system makes sense in theory, falls apart with implementation 
Zero partial credit, miss one semicolon, its a zero.
No clear expectations for exam content, past exams or sections covered are given.

Best of luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nassar posted one 10min video that was completely unrelated to the material in homework's. Without student run zoom meetings where we had to teach ourselves how to complete homework I would have not learned anything. The grading was vague and very hard. The book was the only spot for info. Buckle up because you're in for a ride with this guy...

I wouldn't recommend you waste your time with this professor. He likes to make sure that his class is what you spend all of your time on. He does make himself available for help, in fact it seems as if he wants students to come to him for help in order to do well in class. Assignments are difficult and grading is subjective. Spare yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Nassar seems like a nice guy. He cares for his students and seems like he wants them to succeed. But between the complex weekly assignments, difficult quizzes, and final project worth 50% of our grade I no longer want to look at MATLAB again. I think most of my peers in the class would say the same, which is unfortunate because it is useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He doesn't respond to emails, and if you ask a question, he usually just answers with "just read the book." An infuriating response when you DID read the book. I had an A in the class and ended up getting a D because the final project was vague in its grading criteria, extremely difficult, and set up so small errors snowball and destroy your grade.

This comp methods class is very challenging. However, Professor Nassar is always readily available for help. He is very flexible, if you simply email him to set up a zoom meeting. He genuinely wants students to grow and learn in this class. The problems are difficult, but you're never left astray if you apply yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This is by far one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Although at face value H seems to care about his students, he has left us out to dry on just about every assignment. Everyone is struggling to understand and he refuses to hold lectures to teach us how to do anything. The level of difficulty far surpasses that of other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Class content enjoyable, exam/lecture structure is terrible. Mind numbing lectures that are half filled with irrelevant research papers. I don't expect a study guide but there was never any clear detail what would be on these “mini exams”. AKA, full on exams that you only get half the class to complete then she forces you to stay for LECTURE after

Probably the pickiest and most questionable grading I've came across in 4 years of college. Also takes the entirety of the semester to grade some assignments. She is a nice person, but this was one of my least favorite classes I have taken. Exams are average difficulty-wise, and you can do well if you study a bit and pay attention in class.

Easily the pickiest grader I've ever had. She's a nice enough person, and she is knowledgeable about the content, but the nit-picking for every point gets old fast. The class load is also full of busy work that isn't relevant to the exams (which she has named "mini-exams", though they are essentially full on tests that she lectures after).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is honestly one of the best professors i have ever had. There is a good bit of homework but it's not very difficult. You can tell she cares about the subject and teaching, she gives fun lectures that keep you engaged. Great personality and brings up the vibes of the whole class. Overall she's just a great person and great teacher.

Very nice, and she cares a lot, but there is SO MUCH BUSYWORK. This is a senior-level class, and the level of mindless homework is aggravating. Her tests questions can also be very long, making it hard to finish. If you go to class and turn things in, there's no problem making an A, but it is frustrating the amount of busywork.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She treated the whole class as if we were in middle school. So much homework, so many little assignments, in-class participation, and random pointless busywork. Anything she grades will have 0.2 or 0.5 off randomly. She is picky and frankly annoying. She cares about what she is teaching, but a lot of us were seniors in college NOT middle schoolers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, best I've had at Mizzou so far. Very helpful, and teaches well, she doesn't just read straight from the ppt. like some teachers, she actually talks through what she's teaching. The grading is very fair, 9/10 just do the work and you'll get an A. exams are pretty straight forward as well. I loved taking her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Went to her multiple times about how I could do better on her tests. All she will say is get better sleep. She will not listen to any feedback and she will not have anything graded until the week of finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Humfeld really cares about conservation and I didn't think it was hard as long as you kept up. There was a lot of busy work (multiple small, easy assignments through the week), and her tests could be challenging because they relied heavily on application and weren't worded very clearly, but she curves so you'll be fine. Plenty of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She lectures straight from the book. Her tests are so difficult. She says she wants feedback, but doesn't actually take it to heart when it is given. She rewrites test questions in the middle of the test. More than half the class with struggle with a question and she won't curve it. Although she does curve in general, so that's nice. Be prepared.

You should definitely attend all of your classes, do not allow yourself to get behind in the tegrity's. Attending class is so much more helpful and she does in class group work that counts towards participation.
Weekly homework

She was one of my favorite professors at MU. I only opened the textbook once or twice (but you have to buy it  for the homework. There are weekly homework assignments but they ant that hard! Just remember to do them, they help! ( iforgot about 2/3 and my grade dropped 3%). Her lectures cover EXACTLY whats on the test. GO to class it counts for EC

Dr. Humfeld is a wonderful professor! Sure, learning about biology isn't all that fun to everyone, but she makes it very interesting. You can tell she loves teaching and cares about the well being of her students. She offers so much help. Her powerpoints are very visual, and she interacts a lot with the students. The info is semi-hard, but doable!

Dr. Humfeld is not a bad person. She's nice to most people if you talk with her and at some points I found her helpful. However, she's just as likely to pretty much tell you to go look yourself. The class itself is horrible. Literally every student hates it with a burning passion. People say take the professor not the class, don't take either.
If you go to class you need to read the textbook. she give weekly homework which are easy points. she is very student oriented. she is always available for office hours.

Dr. Humfeld is an amazing teacher. She is very clear and easy to understand and she gives lots of examples and homework, which isn't a bad thing. All the homework is online. She really cares about her students and loves to meet and talk to everyone. She truly, truly, cares! Take advantage of her kindness!

She is a wonderfully kind person and is extremely passionate about science. The only real downfall to this class is the work load. Multiple upon multiple assignments due weekly. If you love all aspects of science, I highly recommend this class.
Dr. Humfield is very nice but her class is hard. The homework never matches the lectures and the tests are long and challenging.

Dr. Humfeld is a very sweet woman who is very passionate about biology. The tests are a little difficult, but as long as you go to class, you should be able to get at least a B, no problem. Plus, sometimes you get candy.

Dr. Humfeld is a kind woman, but her class is a challenge. The tests are probably the most difficult aspect of the course. In order to earn an A on an exam, one must study the material intensely, and be able to apply it to concepts (ones you necessarily have not seen before). Take another instructor if given the option.

Show up to class and pay attention, you'll get an A. Her tests are very straightforward. She is kind of a tough grader on little assignments you do, but nothing awful . She also does in class notecards, which help your grade or hurt it depending on if you go to class. Take hers, its the easiest bio 1010 at Mizzou
she's an extremely hard grader. and her tests are so hard. avoid her for bio 1010

Do NOT take this class! Dr. Humfeld is incredibly sweet, but this class is a massive headache. Instructions for many assignments are unclear and the in class quizzes are very difficult. They say this class is for "non-science majors", but honestly, just take intro bio if you need a lab credit. Save your sanity.
I was told this was for kids who didn't like science.  That was a lie.  She grades as though you are a science grad student and doesn't clarify what she wants from you ever.  Also grades unfairly.

She gives out note card assignments randomly, so class is fairly mandatory. Test are straightforward and everything is from lecture. Open-book quizzes weekly. Very nice, enjoys her subject, and is willing to help students.
Sarah is a nice lady. Go to class, participation taken. Slides from class are exactly what is on the test. Uses Tegrity. One group project where she chooses groups randomly, but fairly easy.

Sarah is an incredibly nice lady, who is very passionate about what she does and that comes across in her lectures. She may give a lot of little assignments and her tests may be a little harder than one would think, but she genuinely cares about all of her students and helping them succeed.
Her notes are very clear cut.  If you know the lecture notes you will do well on tests!

She's a good teacher! As the semester goes on the tests get harder. She also is a little weird because she studies frogs but she's cool! You need to go to class because she has several participation assignments but they help the class go by faster.
She's a good professor. Loves what she does. As long as you pay attention, and do the work you should be fine. She does a few group projects but they aren't bad.
She's a pretty tough professor but she's very enthusiastic about the material but she won't hand you easy grades (but plenty of small assignments to bring it up)
She makes the class seem easy but the tests are much harder than the material covered in class. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR THERE ARE MUCH EASIER BIO 1010 CLASSES!!

Dr. Humfeld is a very nice lady who is very passionate about her work (especially FROGS!), but for an into bio class, the material she covers borders on absurd. Tests are crazy and rarely cover the material covered in class. Insane amounts of out of class work causes neglect of other classes. Avoid Dr. Humfeld.

I was told that "Warm Little Planet" is "science class for people who are bad at science". Not true. The material is interesting, but it covers such a broad range of information that it's hard to study. Additionally, you're somewhat expected to have background knowledge, which I didn't. Lots of busy work/projects. Humfeld is okay, not the class.
Awesome professor! Very interested in student learning. Always available to help. Makes class interesting and unstructured/discussion based.

Humfeld is a very sweet lady and very enthusiastic about what she is teaching. however, i HATED the class. it requires a TON of out of class work and a semester-long group project. it was terrible. unless science is your life, don't take it.

I thought she was great. A little excentric at times, but still informative, slightly quirky, and very helpful on papers and projects. These other comments tht people have made were while she was pregnant, so that could easliy explain their animosity towards her.

ridiculously hard.  Will literally take off .05 for papers.  You will never get a perfect score.  Everything you turn in will be ripped apart.  I spent at well over 10 hours on each weekly homework assignment and never received an A.
she brought her baby to class, and breastfed during office hours while you were there. not to mention she was hard.
Had her for Warm Little Pond. Thought she was a good teacher, but did not like the class. Would not recommend it unless you absolutely love science.

I absolutely loved Dr. Humfeld. She's very helpful and extremely nice. The class isn't very easy, but as long as you show up to class and start working on assignments early instead of one day before, the class is extremely manageable.

I had Dr. Humfeld for warm little pond. It was a class for journalism majors, basically science for kids who aren't majoring in science. I hated science before taking this clas, and while I still don't really like it, Dr. Humfeld made it bearable. She is a very nice lady and very passionate about what she teaches. I'd recommend her for any class.

She isn't too hard but I took AP Bio, never went to class and didn't study and got a B+... my other friends would always go to class and study and ended up with Cs... so honestly I don't know?  I thought she was pretty clear though
if you have this teacher i would suggest to find another one.
she gives regular internet assignments and in-class assignments. she cares way too much about bio, but if you go to class and pay attention like you should, its simple

I'm a non major and I didn't feel that the class hard at all. Attend class (she does random in-class assignments) and do the assigned reading: The tests are straight from the books and lectures.
