Her lectures are slightly boring. I've never had to go to office hours but she is slow on answering e-mails.

i cant believe the postive comments about this teacher, only because i frequently would ask for help email show up to office hours* where she was not at most of the time * and she would not return emails and completely blow me off!. i am a bio major and this class was terrible. Terrible teacher, get another bio1010 professor

-this teacher repetitively did not return emails -tests were ridiculously hard to the point that it was more about how many times you can be tricked in the test.  -Material was way above non-major biology class -Seemed as though this professor was more concerned with her personal research than teaching the right material for the section.

Teacher is really nice and willing to help whenever she can. Tests were easy and mostly straight from the notes. Lectures typically very clear and organized. Semester project and in-class assignments kind of pointless, though.

Wow I don't know what you guys are talking about. Yeah, the tests aren't the easiest in the world, but they come from the notes almost word for word most of the time. She's a great teacher... except that she teaches to the dumb people... but I really don't mind.

tests were ridiculous, they often had nothing to do with classwork or reading. i had friends in other bio 1010 classes with different teachers who would laugh at how hard the material i hard to learn was compared to theirs.
Tests suck!! Nothing on the tests matches the notes and reading in the book.
The class isn't hard, however for bio 1010 (non majors) she expects way too much.

She is a nice teacher, but the tests are horrible. I am normally an A and B student and I have gotten a D on every single test. You can study, and still do poorly on the test. Nothing will completely prepare you.

I thought the course content itself was pretty interesting and applicable to the real world. That being said, the lectures themselves were pretty mediocre, and even with some coding experience this was a challenging course. Content should build slower and be more inviting to students from degrees outside of CS/IT since Data Vis applies everywhere.

This class was hard without a coding background, especially in Python. He assumed that everyone came in with different experiences in coding and let you do what you wanted, but if you didn't come in with any experience, that made it hard. 
Some of his assignments were vague, but he tried to be lenient with grading ambiguity.

Assignments are worth 70% of your grade and there is a group project as the final. Some assignments were rather time consuming and difficult for someone who didn't come in with a strong coding background. Hurt was rather rude and stubborn at times, on top of never answering emails whatsoever

This course makes statistics much easier for me to understand. The lessons were clear and organized. The pace worked well. I liked that we always saw how the material related to real engineering problems, so it never felt pointless.

Dr. Kim is arrogant and unhelpful in every sentence. He shows clear enjoyment in embarrassing students in class. His lectures are useless but required. His quizzes and exams are over material we've barely touched. His grading on reports is rude and unconstructive. He is over-reliant on AI and occasionally uses it in grading.
Professor Kim is passionate about challenging students to think critically and apply concepts independently. His lectures encourage active participation, which keeps the class engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kim does not explain concepts very well, especially the math portion which you need for the quizzes and exams. He'll cold call you in class to ask you something that has nothing to do with lecture and then make fun of your answer in front of the class. Also everyone tends to average about a C-on all the quizzes and he sees no problem w/ it.

Dr. Kim is a fairly nice and energetic guy, but not a gifted professor at all. His class tends to follow the lines of "study for my class 24/7 and maybe you'll pass." He is horrible at explaining concepts and his processes, especially when it comes to his math portions of lectures where he skims over everything you need to know, leaving you lost.

reviews.comment: He still has an old-fashioned technique to "study hard" for exams. His interaction with students is fine but sometimes he makes inappropriate comments. reviews.comment: Ergonomics was a very interesting class! No homework, but instead there are five big papers due throughout the semester. Focus on these and make them the best you can. Pick a good topic for your project, it will help in the long run. Quizzes every Tuesday, so go to class to know the material. The second exam is the hardest. Great class overall.

reviews.comment: Kim is high energy which I like a lot, but this class was just not fun. The homeworks take forever, Chegg will be a necessity for them (will still take 5+ hours). He will call you if you skip class, so go. Content is not very interesting and his slides come straight from the book. Exams were challenging but doable. Lectures were long. Work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is genuinely one of the best professors I have had. She is very good about responding to emails with any questions you have. The structure of her class is very easy. Does not take a lot of effort/stress to pass this class. Truly the easiest writing intensive I've taken. Would recommend this class for anyone who needs a writing intensive credit.

Everyone told me this class was gonna be super hard, but it's one of the easiest I've taken.There is an attendance question each week plus a couple of assignments. Most of the assignments took like 20 minutes if they weren't for the research paper. She also gives 100% on all assignments and you get to drop 4 so you don't even have to do all of them
DO NOT TAKE!

I honestly don't know why there is so many bad reviews. She has been super nice, and never once was demeaning over zoom meetings discussing my research paper. The workload is not bad, as attendance is as simple as replying on canvas how you are doing. Besides an occasional weekly short assignment, the one research paper is the bulk of the class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!!!!!
Terrible.

reviews.comment: Don't take this with her

Not the easiest class to take, but not difficult either if you keep up with the material.  She is a bit hard to understand due to her Korean accent, and also does go a bit fast on presentations.  Participation is important for in-class discussions.  Exams are also hard if you don't review the material too often.  Does curve grades after finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: So bad. Do not take her. She is arrogant

She asked us to rate on her on this website. I think that goes to account for her cockiness. She is a poor professor. She is belittling and disrespectful. Sometimes I don't think she means to be, but her lack of proper English fails her. I do not recommend this class or her as a professor. As a person she seems okay. Not sure why she had us do this

The worst professor I have taken at Mizzou. She is very rude, has zero communication. She doesnt give students a rubric and will take off points for random reasons. She doesnt speak very clear English and uses the communication barrier to her advantage. She is TERRIBLE. Hopefully she is fired soon. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. Her TA doesnt ever email

TERRIBLE! WORST TEACHER EVER! Honestly should be removed from all teaching roles forever. Is not helpful, doesn't teach anything useful to the assignments you actually have. Is confusing, talks fast, and acts like you are so stupid if you don't understand anything. I would give a 0 if I could.

I respect the woman but her class is structured more for graduate students than undergrads who are used to more organization. As a student with a learning disability, I do not recommend her class if you struggle with note-taking because she talks too fast and cannot pronounce English words well.

Dr. Pearce has been publishing her work on feminism for decades before any of her students were even born, and it shows in her lectures. She has the best examples and makes class very enjoyable. As long as you have an interest in whatever topic she is teaching, this class will be a great experience.

This woman is one of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure to have. She would sometimes give two or three hours of reading a night, but I quickly learned that coming to class prepared (and coming to class, period) was the best way to go. Dr. Pearce is sweet, insightful, informed and engaging. She's a must-have for any sociology student.

Dr. Pearce is brilliant.  She is tough and demanding, as one would expect from someone of her intellectual caliber.  Serious students should absolutely take at least one of Dr. Pearce's classes.  You just know that you are sitting in the presence of an intellectual powerhouse with a unique perspective.

This is not a class for the light-hearted. There's a lot of reading, and her teaching method is more classic(mostly lectures, no powerpoint) But it is extremely interesting and she makes the classes enjoyable (and chooses really good books/articles) Grading based on exams, a term paper, and a group project. Highly recommend for serious student

Dr. Worthington has a pretty good class. I took him for Ancient Western Civilization, and it was not too bad. He had 1 midterm test that wasn't too bad, it just consist of some multiple choice questions and an essay, and 2 papers due at the end of the semester for your grade.

I took Dr. Worthington's class on the Hellenistic world. He is highly intelligent and knowledgeable on the topic and grades fairly. It is quite reading-heavy and lectures are important. I found this class to be intimidating at first, but finished with an A. Dr. Worthington is funny and gave great lectures. I feel like I learned a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worth the time of you need a mandatory history class! If you're there and do the reading you'll be fine. Essay exams can be a little vague, but he allows you to negotiate outside of class about your grade. He's willing to listen if you are. Overall: very rewarding.

Most rewarding class I have ever taken. He expects you to do the work and know your stuff. He is hilarious (very dry sense of humor) and very, very smart. This is clearly his area of expertise. Loved him, one of my favorite classes by far! Highly recommend him but be prepared to put effort in.

Alexander the Great Online course was terrible. Not only are the questions extremely vague, the requirement doent match the grade. Hint: if you ask for a 400-500 word short answer, don't say 'too short' at 480 words and 'too long' at 540. He clearly doesnt read your sources and copy-pastes in comments on your essays. Hardest B- ever
Teaching all things ancient western world. Angry welshman.

technically, he teaches history courses. in reality, the knowledge you gain is in egotism and conceitedness. worst professor i've ever had which is unfortunate because he's highly knowledgeable.  unfortunately, that doesn't translate into even the slightest ability to make the material interesting. never again will i take a class he's teaching.

intelligent but thinks way too highly of himself. not everyone has hours of free time to spend reading the "suggested" readings, which he then holds against you and hurts your grade.  if the "suggested" readings are that crucial, make them required.  and get over yourself

Ancient Greek World and philip the II and Alexander the Great classes were both upper level and very strenuous. He loves his subject and you must too to succeed. I'm a history major and have received B+ in both classes.

Excellent professor. People may complain about getting callled out for questions but it's part of the class. He challenges you to learn not just the material but WHY it matters and how it applies. Answer a question. Back it up! He's not being mean when you say something completely incorrect he's just challenging you to back it up, or do the readin

Awesome class! It was an interm class that only lasted 10 days, but I wish it was a semester. He is truly entertaining and extremely knowledgeable about the topics at hand.  He challenges his students and I feel that it has helped me examine how I approach all of my classes. Not enough room to say all that I want to say, I highly recommend him!

This professor is one of the BEST professors I have ever had.  He is a fantastic teacher, but you had better be prepared to give before you can get.  Do your readings and go to class; he is not afraid to drop you for not showing up.  He can be intimidating, but his welcomes students into his office and is willing to give you one on one help.
Despite exceptional knowledge of topics, he is rather rude towards students. I wouldn't recommend his office hours because he is the definition of an unapproachable and arrogant person.

Very obnoxious opinionated professor who can be downright abusive to students.  Asks stuff like whether you went Number One or Number Two when you come back from a bathroom break.  Juvenile sense of humor. BUT....really knows his stuff and challenges you to think.  Glad I took the class but will.never.take.another.from.him.

One of the few professors that actually, God forbid, expects the best out of his students. Not a hard class if you do the readings (and you are expected to do them). Very informative, really knows his stuff, & is entertaining while he teaches. Genuinely cares about his students and their learning. Don't expect an easy grade, but do expect to learn.

He's a fantastic lecturer, but if you are in the honors section of this class, you'd better know the reading, have an opinion about it, and be prepared to back it up. If he learns your name, there is a possibility that he will randomly call on you during lecture, and he will certainly do so during discussion if you don't volunteer an opinion.

He is great in lecture, but if he knows your name you better make sure you know the info. In the honors section you better be sure you read the material and be prepared to back up anything you say. He will try and make you go back on your claims but he likes you to stand your ground. He grades papers tough based on writing style, not on history.
Worthington is a great professor. He has a great sense of humor, but can also be very intimidating and sometimes rude if you say something he doesn't want to.
Works you hard but awesome teacher, the best yet.  Got great sense of humor, he could be a standup comic easy. God help you if you walk in late.

this prof is brilliant and not for the weak of heart, and you can kiss an A goodbye if you dont want to work, but you come out of his classes feeling challenged and inspired if you put in the work -- and he is kinda cute too:)

worthington is  a very smart  man and knows his stuff. He seems like an **** in class, but if you go to his office hours, he is really great and very personable. If you are not up for studying, do not take this class.
No Comments
No powerpoints must come to class to take notes in order to pass.
Super laid back teacher if you did the online quizzes and studied the vocab it was a breeze
Tests are tough because there is a lot of information and its over a lot of chapters. Lectures are long and boring. No homework was given except for online quizzes

Doesn't take attendance but go to class and will pass just fine.   Subject itself is interesting, power points have good / entertaining examples.  He's not that bad, voice dry and monotone, but not a big deal.
Very dry. Not helpful. Hard to hear. I regret not using this website before taking his class. Enough said.

I read some of these reviews, and I imagine Ian has as well, because the class is different now. You have to do research participation, 14 easy homework assignments, and 7 exams. You have 8 exams, so the final can be dropped. You don't need to go to class, but the notes are exactly what's on the study guide and in turn exactly's what's on the exams

The most boring teacher at mizzou. The tests had unfair questions and his lecture was right from the textbook yet he never knew the information. took way longer than a human ever needs to to read off a couple slides in an hour and 15 min class. would avoid him as teacher

Ian is a nice guy, don't get me wrong. But I recommend avoiding. Did not go to class, read the textbook. As mentioned, there is no longer extra credit and the lectures are a disaster. This class is also not a cakewalk either. You will have to read the textbook in order to get a good grade. And the curve is the only thing that saved my exam grades.

Zimmerman was boring in his lectures, and he doesn't round the final grades.  He had to curve every test around 15 points in order to have any students pass.  He tells you that the tests are mostly about information from the lectures, but in order to do well you must know the book materials front to back.
Take psychology from another teacher you have been warned. Class used to be easy but now is a awful to take. Boring lectures with little help for tests.

After curving each test my test average is a 59.5%. I go to all of his lectures and have completed all his homework assignments. Test are nothing like the practice test he gives you. If you have him contact a tutor as soon as possible.

He says the tests are mostly from the notes, but its not even close to that. I read all the notes and the book are STILL got C's on all the tests. His lectures are boring and he awkwardly brings up sex a lot. Do NOT take psych with him!! He doesn't take attendance, but he makes you write notes and doesn't put them up on blackboard.

He has extremely boring lectures and no longer offers extra credit, so don't listen to past ratings. Test are very hard, but he curves them so that helps. I wouldn't recommend taking him. Psychology can be so fun, but he's too boring.

This class was so easy I never came, read the book the night before the test and got an A+.  However as a pre-med I actually did need to learn something for my MCAT and as I I am not at all prepared.  I wish he had actually taught something worthwhile.  Also his lectures were exceptionally boring and he was a little awkward.

He's very difficult to work with. I was in the hospital on the day of a test, and he wouldn't let me make it up. At the beginning of the semester he said that if you have an excuse for missing a test you could make it up the week before the final. When I contacted him about making it up, he wouldn't let me. The worst, take psych with someone else.

Don't even worry about going to class. The tests are straight from the book, so if you read the chapters and look at the power points he puts on blackboard which he "goes over" in class, then you'll do just fine. Take the extra credit opportunities seriously because I ended up with over 80 extra credit points and passed the class with over 100%.

Really boring, awkward professor but knows what he's talking about. Sometimes unintentionally funny. He makes extra credit questions off random things he says in lectures. Know he hates steep bridges and wasps. Might come in handy. If he offers extra credit for doing more studies, do it.
Terrible teacher, feel like I learned nothing from the class. Tests were somewhat difficult but extra credit helped. Switch teachers if possible.
I never went to class. As long as you take notes from his powerpoints he posts and read the chapter you'll do fine. The connect option was helpful too.

Unlimited extra credit from taking part in extra research made this class an easy A. After reviewing the lecture slides online, I would usually get a B on the tests without studying or going to class. There are 7 tests, each covering only 2-3 chapters.  If you really want to learn, have initiative or take another teacher. Zimmerman is nice though.
The easiest class I have ever taken. I only went to class the first day and for the tests and I got an A+. Cake Walk

The class isn't bad. It's just really boring. I quit showing up because I would rather spend my time reading out of the book or going over the power points online. If you do that you should be fine. He has a good sense of humor and, overall, he is a good teacher, just needs to make it more fun.
His lectures aren't interesting, but he has a very good sense of humor, which always helps.
Very boring class, really not what I wanted out of Psychology. gives extra credit though. tests are very standardized and out of the book.

Not a very interesting class. He makes a funny comment every once in a while. Test are based more-so on the book than the power point. Test are easy to get an A or B only if you have a clear understanding of all the vocabulary.

He's really boring and dry. I stopped going to class and just self studied since he puts everything on blackboard. I only show up for test days. It's really easy to get EC in this class though. Any extra research points you do after the required amount is 5 points added to your grade. I currently have 60 points EC so it's a pretty easy A.

I recommend reading the chapter and then doing the LearnSmart review online. It helps a TON! There are bonus points on the exams for things mentioned in the lecture, so go to class and get the easy points. Some questions on the exams are really insignificant details. Zimmerman is kind of boring, but really not that bad of a professor.
Somewhat boring but overall easy A

Coming in as a psych major I was very interested in the course material but Ian made it very hard to stay interested. He simply read verbatim off of the powerpoint (which he later posted on blackboard) which made going to class pointless. I got way more out of reading the textbook myself. I would definitely recommend taking it with someone else.

This guy is so boring. Psych was originally my minor but after this class I changed it. Occasionally he makes funny comments but he usually just reads powerpoints. If you take the initiative to read the book on your own time you'll do fine. Also attendance is optional - I rarely went. It was torture. Get another prof!!

Your average Calc 3 professor. Exams/Quizzes is what makes most of your grade. Also don't forget about the final exam! This is a difficult class so be ready to grind. I don't think he curves too in which he should. He just reads the slides and expects you to know everything. Pretty challenging to communicate with.

Had him for cal 3 in-person and he read from slides from the textbook every lecture. I didn't learn much from this teaching and I wouldn't recommend him as a teacher. 90% of the time he is standing in front of the class reading from the slides that we get on Canvas. Although the homework load was pretty light which is nice, only one a week.

Dr. Verbitsky was a very straightforward professor. He gives you 2 dropped quizzes and 2 dropped homeworks. He definitely understands how difficult the course material for Calc 3 is. All of the tests and quizzes had very straighforward problems which we had either done in our homework, or in class notes. Would recommend him over other Calc 3 profs.

I think Mr. Verbitsky is kind of dropping the ball in a virtual setting. I had him this past semester for 2300 and it was certainly the worst math experience I had in my life. My main problem is that he did not allow you to show your work for partial credit on every problem. He will not slow down in a lecture even if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is an older professor and seems to be caught up in teaching in his ways. My least favorite math prof so far. He teaches fast and strictly writes on the board in chalk and does not post any sort of notes online. This makes it hard to follow him when he is talking in class. Definitely be prepared to use your textbook and to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was my first experience with college, since I'm actually just a high-schooler that's ahead in math, so I was mildly intimidated at first. But Prof. Verbitsky is very straightforward and teaches difficult concepts clearly. Do your homework -- there is no time to "figure stuff out" on the tests. Quizzes on Fridays. He grades fairly.

I had Imler when I was at MACC and he's fun to listen to. Everything's a lecture but it can totally be fun if you participate. Plus it's philosophy. Idk how you'd get that without lectures. He's also nice and pretty fun. I'd recommend for a thought-provoking class.

He likes to have students participate in his class. He often puts people into groups and have them discuss class material with others in the group. As for grading, he's somewhere in the middle. He's not going to give you a good grade just for doing the work but he's not an absolute really hard grader either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unlike previous comments, Mr. Imler was awesome and clear. Take his class.

I had MR. Imler as an online teacher. He was unclear about assignment details. He did not respond to student emails. He tested over materials not yet covered, and tested repeatedly over the same material.

Took online during summer semester. Hw, labs, and tests were equally weighted so you could do well on everything but tests and still do well in the class. Lectures were recordings that were mostly understandable. TA was mostly available on for help/questions throughout the week. Course was on Canvas, except for hw and exams. Only exams were timed.
Dr. Kosztin and his wife are awesome teachers who make online classes so fun and pretty easy! They are very accessible to help you and want to see you succeed :)
Very demanding, moves quickly. Do your work ahead of time and be ready to study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Presents material in a way that is easy to learn and study.  Definitely the guy you want teaching you physics.
A pretty cool guy. He does some fun demonstrations in class. Romanian, I think. Short temper though, so definitely don't bring your laptop or let your cell phone go off.
Good teacher.  For the amount of information in the class, I believe he did a very good job at teaching it, although probably not quite as good as his wife.

The course material is somewhat tough, but he doesnt teach it very well. It seemed like I did everything on my own, out of class, which is very irretating. His curve is very good and hes pretty leniant, but he just cant teach very well.

Awesome professor!!!He is like a friend to me!!!Never have had a professor like him in the college before!!Best professor ever!!Definitely taking his class and guarantee you an A if you ask a questions and go to class!!! Funny guy!!!!
Hands down the best math teacher I have ever encountered, and probably one of the best teachers I'll have at Mizzou.  I highly recommend taking anything by him.
He's amazing..take advantage of his office hours, you'll learn ALOT

he is a great professor. he makes sure that you clearly understand what he is saying before he moves on. he does give hints and his practice tests are extremely helpful. i've never had a teacher who was so determined to help his students succeed.
it was the easiest class in college I would only go to class mwf and I got an A without doing any homework. Great guy.
Great teacher!  Teaches math like it should be taught.

Alex is really interested in the student's success and he teaches really well.  He recommends not memorizing anything, which suprisingly works.  However, the test can be challenging, so keep up with homework and definitely do the practice exams and ask questions.
Alex is one of the best professors I've had...he's a very fair teacher and if you at least try in the class, you will not fail.  He's a great guy, I definitely recommend taking his class.
No Comments
Best math teacher I've ever had by a long shot and he's a good guy too.

Most clear presentation of calculus I've experienced at MU. Class was ok, it was math, but he introduced fun. He also expressed disgust for the much hated mathematica labs and gave us full credit for them if we scored 50% or higher on them. Keep up!
One of the best teachers I've had... you will learn a lot AND do good on tests if you keep up with the work and go to lecture.  He's also pretty funny.

He brought in a lot of guest speakers, where attendance is required, but other attendance is optional. Tests are heavily based on lectures and guest speakers. He is clearly very passionate about what he teaches, and tests were based on wherever class discussion would take him. Moot court was a lot of fun, and it was not hard to get an A.

His online lectures are not helpful. He's all over the place when he talks and stays on one slide the entire time. You can tell he's kind of just making it up as he goes. But then on the exam he expects you to know these details that he glanced over? Also no study guide. Only key terms sheet, which didn't include half of what would be on the exam.

My favorite class by far the semester I took it. You can tell Prof Horner is incredibly smart and loves to teach. Lecture heavy-- tests are based of of lectures and guest speakers, but I enjoyed it. His guest speakers are amazing. The lectures and assignments have real-world applications and the discussions reflect that. Great prof!

One of the best professors I've had at miz, his lectures are interesting and informative. Attendance isn't required every day but you should go bc all of the test material is from the lectures. For the last month, you are placed into groups for mock trail. Essentially an intro to law school, you read cases and then grill each other on them.

Prof. Horner gives good lectures and is the most enthusiastic of the 3 professors for POLSC1100, but the setup of the class with online lectures and an ultimately pointless discussion make it a really easy, but boring class. Weekly quizzes that I recommend taking as you watch the lecture. 4 online tests and an online final, all multiple choice.

Dr. Horner brings a fun, light-hearted energy to every class and he loves what he's teaching. Idk about these other reviews but 4220W is an easy A. Only 2 papers which are long, but the tests are online and open-note. Attendance not required, but extra credit given randomly if attending.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was online lecture and one discussion class on Friday's. You have to watch the lectures to get a good grade on the test. Over 75% of the questions on the tests will say "According to lecture,....." Although the lectures are long and boring you just have to watch them. Overall easy class.

He taught the third unit of the online. You need to watch the lectures to pass the exam. His powerpoint slides are not helpful at all and he puts content on the quizzes that is small and minuscule. Attendance is mandatory for the in-person discussion's even though they are pointless.

There were online lectures every week with one discussion day, easy online quizzes every week based on lectures. Discussion was pointless but you got graded on attendance, online open note timed tests were somewhat difficult.

I love Dr. Horner. His classes remind me why I love political science and why I am majoring in it. Dr. Horner doesn't just spit information out at you, he tells you his honest thoughts and is really funny. All he asks is that you show up to class and try your best. He even remembered me from class and says hello to me whenever he sees me on campus!

He taught the 3rd unit of this hybrid course. Lectures were engaging and grading criteria was clear. Only critique is that his powerpoint slides weren't all that useful and would put very tiny details on quizzes/exams that weren't talked about much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Horner is awesome. I took his online class Poli Sci 4120 in Fall 2021. I was very easy with just a couple exams and straightforward papers that you just need to be sure to cite the material. I highly recommended this course.

Prof Horner was awesome. He's a cool guy, & my only issue was the lectures were sometimes super long. It's not hard to do well if you watch the lectures, do all the assignments, & get your participation points.
Took his class in Fall 2020 and loved his lectures out of all professors. He made it so interesting and easy and understandable, definitely recommend taking his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was a self paced course and there are no video or audio lectures, only reading, assignments, and tests. Commentary assignments are easy and you'll think you're prepared for the test, but you aren't. Tests are the most difficult tests I've ever had. You'll need to rely on getting good grades on assignments for your final grade in the class.

Professor Horner is one of the best in the political science department, his classes consist of him lecturing over the course material there is no outline for what you need to know just go to class and take notes.
He was a good teacher, but didnt specify a lot. Hes also that type of teacher where I had an 89.9% and he wouldnt raise it to a 90 for an A-.
Professor Horner is wonderful, and his online class PS 4120 is super easy, enjoyable, and highly recommended to all.
Professor Horner is super nice, but his class is fairly confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher. By the book but fun to listen to.

Horner has been great for the online classes Ive taken, but I regret taking him for an in person class. His feedback didnt pertain to anything I wrote, so he clearly didnt read the entire paper. Also, hes extremely busy so meeting with him can be very tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Online class, a lot of reading but assignments are very straightforward and exams are based on commentary and textbook. It can be easy to get behind because it is self-paced. If you stay on top of things you will do fine. Also took POLSCI 4120 at the same time, course was set up pretty much identically and the same things apply. Easy grader as well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is a great professor, but he relys heavily on the book material which I didn't like because there were so many chapters to read. This class was very challenging but for the final he makes it all extra credit so I would suggest this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class itself is not all that bad. There is a lot of homework which is to be expected when it come to an online class. The problem is the homework didn't really prepare you for the test. I felt like an idiot when I was taking the test. It was like I never even studied. Which I had it was just the fact that nothing you studied was ever on there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Horner is my favorite prof from freshman yr. I hate history, but his class was my favorite because of his humor and enthusiasm. There is a lot of extra credit, so come to class. I've heard bad things about other POLISCI profs, so if you are going to take POLISCI1100, take it w/ Horner - you won't regret it!

Attendance matters. Only way to get material needed. Didn't do the readings was fine with understanding. Pretty lengthy study guides, but if you do them and know the material, tests are pretty straight forward. Tons of extra credit opportunities. Ended the class with over 100% and didn't even take the optional final. Pay attention and study Easy A

Attendance matters in this class. This class has 3 exams and an optional final that is for extra credit. Horner only has lecture outlines which makes it vital to go to class. However, he can talk excessively fast making it difficult to comprehend the material. The plus of this course is the amount of extra credit given.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was interesting and I learned a lot, but it was also one of the most challenging I have ever taken. The homework was pretty easy. The exams were extremely difficult. There is no study guide and the exams are very specific. Over all, he knows his stuff and I gained a lot from the class. If you want to be challenged, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is pretty hard compared to most general eds. I generally had to study 10 hours at least for each test and the study guides are way too long. But he makes class interesting and extra credit opportunities can make up for hard tests.

The exams are 30-40 short answer questions that are so specific and a lot of them are from the text book and not the online "lecture" and terms. He grades entirely too hard and does not answer any emailed questions unless you're asking to drop the class. Dont take this class It will ruin your GPA, however I would try to take him in person though
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horner is lots of fun! As long as you pay attention during lecture and take good notes, the class really isn't too hard.

I took this online, and if you're looking for an easy class this isn't it! It was almost impossible for me to get a B+ in this class since there are only 3 exams and they are ALL written response questions. He is an easy grader when it comes to homework and grades very fast, so you always know your progress in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and Professor Horner makes the lectures really interesting. He can get off topic quite a bit but I didn't mind. One thing I didn't enjoy was that he never published an overall grade throughout the whole year. Offers quite a bit of extra credit.
hes awesome

Online class was super easy, mostly everything you need to know in the commentary. Only some easy little chapter assignments and the 3 exams. 2nd exam was NOTHING like the study guide and he never replied to my email when I inquired so that was kinda annoying. The online class was fine like forsure take this route if youre gonna take this class.

Tests are entirely short answer but as long as you read the online lectures and some from the book and feel comfortable with the material (including details) youll do fine! The question are pretty much either you know it or you dont, so his grading reflects your studying. Super cool, well respected guy! Loved him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed taking American Government with Professor Horner last semester! Although he doesn't show the slides, but luckily, I had a notetaker for the class so I was able to keep up with the lectures in class. Also, it's important to go to every class since he gives attendance quizzes. There's extra credit and a curve applied to each exam.

This was BY FAR the hardest class I've ever taken in college. The exams are around 40 questions SHORT ANSWER and he shows no mercy when grading. The homework assignments were the only reason I did not fail the course. I have never done so poorly in a class before this one. I hope that you heed my warning and DO NOT take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: People who have Prof. Horner in seat love him. I took 3 online courses w/ him and thought the tests were ridiculously, needlessly, stupidly hard. I got As on most if not all assignments, but test questions were weirdly specific on things I wouldnt have thought all that important. Ruined GPA, but I legit know the content. Test me right now.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His exams is where it'll get ya. The homework couldn't be easier and the reading is actually interesting. Be sure to cite your answers or he'll take off points. Test 2 is the hardest and will be the determinant for your grade at the end of the semester. Create study guides for tests based on the vocab words, study questions and homework assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Horner was WONDERFUL. It is so rare to see a college professor who is actually passionate about teaching, and Horner made his love of the subject matter clear. Course content was difficult because I was one of the few freshman in the class and was taking basic Political Science 1100 simultaneously, but it was a great class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Love this guy.

horner is one of the best and most laid back profs at mizzou. attendance was only mandatory on days that we had guest speakers. sometimes i felt like his lectures were kind of hard to follow, but he always reiterates himself to make sure you understand. you can tell he really loves what he is teaching

Super easy mandatory-government-class. Horner makes it interesting, and he gives you extra credit practically weekly for doing absolutely nothing. You're graded only on multiple-choice tests. You do need to come to class every day though, and at least skim the readings. But come to class, get the extra credit, and leave with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Horner is very experienced and respected in the poli sci world. He gives good feedback and insight in his commentary. Sometimes he can come across biased towards republicans but still a fair grader. Good course overall as long as you read the material and can make inferences.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Horner is a very nice and fun professor. There is a textbook, and then another book of political documents. Both are awful but you have to read them to test well. The class was canceled a lot as he is a busy man, but accessible. Lots of extra credit, so show up to learn about that. Lectures can really drag if you aren't into the topics. Smooth ride
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE!!! It will ruin your GPA. The exams are short answer questions and he is a hard grader. I failed the first exam and did well on the next two and ended up with a B in the class. I'm a good student and this was a hard class. I asked for any opportunity to gain extra points for my grade and he denied every attempt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really don't know a whole lot about government, but Horner made it kind of interesting. You definitely want to show up to class, but as long as you're taking notes and listening to what he's saying, you'll be fine. He's one of my favorites at Mizzou (and his shirts are always really fun). Just like any other class, if you study you'll be fine!

Interesting material that is pertinent to issues in society today. Very eclectic teacher who has done immense research on the subject and published many books. He even interviewed many A-list celebrities that he shares in class. Tests are comprised entirely of essays but if you comprehend the material than it is easy to get an A. You will learn
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class online. There's 3 exams and each one is 40 short answer questions from 5 chapters worth of reading. Unless you're a perfect test taker, you'll probably spend at least 5 hours a week preparing for these tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I would not suggest taking this class from him. Lectures are very boring and I had a hard time following them. A lot of the test answers come from the book and readings so make sure you do those.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This man is by far the best professor at Mizzou. He cares for all of his students both grade wise and emotional. He is very passionate about his work outside of class. He gives a lot of extra credit but don't use him for the extra credit. Read everything and you'll get a super easy A+.
hes trash. they lose your quizzes and then blame it on you and wont let you prove you took them. very forgetful and very condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I love William Horner as a person, he's personable, funny, and accessible. However, his lectures are fairly auditory based, so if you're an auditory learner, congrats this is the class for you! However, if you're more visual like me, lectures are extremely hard to follow and understand. He doesn't use slides at all, so just keep that in mind.

For real my favorite professor. Truly cares about what he teaches, incredibly funny, good at explaining. Hell always answer questions during or after class. His lectures are straightforward, and hes really engaging. I love this guy.

Very nice guy who is very knowledgable on the subject. There are 3 exams, one big assignment, & 5 attendance quizzes. Tests are easy if you actually study for them. If you take good notes in class, it's easier to fill out his study guide. A curve and extra credit are added to each exam. I didn't read at all and did fine.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, who knows the subject well. His tests are difficult but if you study for them then you should be fine.
He's super hilarious, and I've gotten some of the easiest extra credit I've earned in this class. Definitely a very good first professor. You'll like him.
Dr. Horner is one the greateast professors at the University of Missouri.

Dr. Horner made the online section of this class virtually impossible to do well in. Homework was lengthy but helpful. Tests, however, were another story. They consisted of 35-56 short answer/essay questions that made doing well extremely hard despite days of studying. In addition, he refused to round my 89.6 up to a 90 at the end of the semester.

Holds students to a high standard, if you are involved in extracurricular, DO NOT TAKE Horner's Classes. Tests are most of your grade and is very ambiguous about what will be on the test. Ex: gives 20 possible essay questions covering several chapters, only picks two on the test. GOOD LUCK
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Horner is a fantastic teacher. He does a good job of keeping the class interesting as well as informative. Even those who don't find American Government particularly interesting would enjoy this class. He offers various opportunities for extra credit throughout the semester. About 12 pop quizzes are given as a way to track attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In class he is very hard to follow because he talks a lot and just uses a lecture outline which makes it impossible to follow. I never knew what was important information. There is very minimal grades and the tests are so hard. He gives out study guides that have enough information for all 3 tests  together so I never knew what to actually study.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hes fine to listen to in lecture. He only puts up outlines, so it's hard to gauge what is important to write down, cause he just rambles. Attendance isnt mandatory, he gives pop quizzes on W/F ususally, and you want to be there for those.  His tests are nearly impossible. He gives you a huge study guide that is no help, you have to read to pass..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Horner is a really funny, & interesting prof. You have to go to class bc he does attendance quizzes but he makes it easy to pay attention in lecture. I found myself studying lectures and reading the textbook the day before exams and got A's on all 3 exams. Just go to class and semi study and its an easy A!!

Professor Horner is a pretty good guy. His class consisted of lecture with a VERY basic outline and there was 12 random attendance quizzes throughout the semester. If you love history, you'll get along great with this guy. (Also, he wears Hawaiian shirts nearly every day.)
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really like prof Horner, I've taken him twice. Definitely not boring, kind of like that care-bear military dad that helped coach your little league team.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His T.A.s are really tough graders when I took the class. Something you think was good when you turn it in will be ripped apart. They have very strict ideas on what they consider cheating and will give you a complete zero even if they only think you were. Interesting class but unfair grading.

Poly Sci students will do well here, other than that, you need to work for it. He has a good sense of humor, but you need to put a lot of effort into taking notes because he doesn't help you there. Tests are big and hard, you need to study a lot.
He's a pretty funny guy. His lectures are hard to follow because there's no slides to go along with them. Grades are based on tests, small pop quizzes, and one other assignment.

Bill was an awesome teacher to say the least. His class was interesting for those that are interested in current events and how the government works. Participating in class is a good way to get on his good side. I rarely used the textbook, but that's because I already knew most of the material. The study guides don't really follow the test.

Interesting and fun for the first couple of weeks, then I started to hate going to this class. It is so boring. He stands up there and talks forever with no slides or anything. Tests are hard, be prepared to red the book because I gained nothing from his lectures. Yo have to show up because you never know when he'll give pop quizzes.

I really enjoyed the class content, it was just a lot. If you don't do any of the readings, you can't get higher than a C+ on any exam or in the class.  Pop quizzes were 5 questions and open note. Study guides are somewhat helpful. Would give extra help, but only if you went to office hours. Overall this class was interesting, but difficult.

Professor Horner is honestly terrible. He does not care for his students in any way. The study guides he gives before tests would take about 4 days to fill out if you actually did it. His grading scale is very messed up too. Don't be surprised if you get to the end of the semester and your grade is actually lower than what you thought. VERY BORING.

Really great professor and class! I enjoyed coming to class everyday and Horner was really knowledgeable on the subject of media and politics. Gave a lot of extra credit and pop quizzes that were really helpful, as long as you came to class. Would definitely recommend!

The class is called "American Government" not "Missouri Government". Makes an entire lecture and half of the test questions about the specifics of the Missouri Government as well as the Missouri constitution when the class is supposed to be about "American" government. Not appreciated as an out of state student.

Tells you at the beginning of class that you don't need to memorize years, then on the test it is based on solely memorizing the years. Miss a class? You most likely missed it on the day he randomly decided to give a pop quiz, which aren't even an easy 5/5, more like a 2/5. Gives a study guide but it doesn't matter, everything is on there.

Pros: tons of extra credit, tests are curved, lecture isn't boring, easy pop quizzes that are basically 50 free points if you show up to class Cons: tough tests, the important topics he covers really fast, essential to read and the readings are very long

I'm a Poli Sci major and got an easy A. Horner is a really funny guy and knows what he's talking about, and I enjoyed it a lot. Attendance isn't mandatory, but go because he only gives note outlines on blackboard and you might miss a pop quiz. He also puts more stuff on the study guides for exams than what ends up on there. Overall 8/10

Horner is a nice professor. He's funny, interesting, always has a positive attitude, and seems very interested in the subject. However, his study guides are NOT helpful. You have to dedicate 5+ hours on reading the textbook & online reader if you want a B+. Maybe. His tests are rarely ever on the lecture, and also about the reading. He's okay.

I absolutely LOVED Horner. His lectures are all oral, so you have to pay close attention. However, he is so enthusiastic, funny, and really knows what he is talking about. His tests are specific, so make sure you read the book, and show up to class, and you will do well.

Horner's class is incredibly easy and for me, incredibly easy usually means boring. However, this was not the case in this class. Lectures are interesting and Horner is a really fun and interesting professor. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him at some point :)

Horner is very entertaining but it's very easy to fall into a habit of skipping his class. Attendance isn't mandatory or all that necessary if you can get notes from someone else. He gives quizzes about every five days, usually on a Wednesday or Friday (if you have the class MWF). He does go quickly in the lecture so try to pay attention.

Really cool professor! Before having him I was worried because of his reviews, but he's really funny and educational. He includes SNL skits in his lessons & gives out a lot of extra credit. The tests have a lot from the book which I never read but still did good on the tests! Definitely recommend taking a class with Horner. FYI, he hates talkers.

I took this class online and it is EXTREMELY easy. My only problem was when I submitted my first progress evaluations, he said I needed to cite my info that was provided by the commentary & the textbook. When I asked him politely to show me where it indicates this, he completely disregarded me & only replied with "cite & you'll get full credit."

Horner doesn't want to help out the students in the ways other professors usually do. He study guides for tests, then makes the test have less that 50% of what the study guide had. Bad teacher but cool guy.

He puts maybe ten words on an outline and talks for the entire class. He told us at the beginning  that we weren't responsible for knowing years because the class is not a history class, but the second test consisted of pure year memorization of years. Poor use of time, unclear lecturing, stupid test questions, pointless pop quizzes.

Horner is an awesome guy, but the test reviews he gives have absolutely NOTHING to do with the test. His final study guide was about 10 pages long and he asked trivial questions on the test. He usually curves 5-10 points. Lots of quizzes and some easy extra credit.

Horner is a great professor. He's entertaining and a favorite by many students. There are 3 tests each worth 25% of your grade, and pop quizzes and one assignment make up the other 25%. If you write your name on the quiz and show up, you should be fine. Easy AA-.
He is a great lecturer and a really funny teacher. His tests can be difficult if you don't pay attention or don't study, but it is a class you can look forward to
Good lectures - very clear. Very kind and willing to help. Great professor - he opened my eyes to the PoliSci major and how much I would enjoy it.
Great lecturer, supremely knowledgeable, funny, very clear, but when I was in a leave of absence, he was so incredibly unhelpful. Just don't have complications and you will be pleased.

you HAVE to pay attention or you'll be lost. very entertaining, good guy, and knows what he's talking about. notes are all oral and you need to understand what hes saying cause he doesn't put any notes up to copy. he never mentions them in class but READ THE ONLINE TEXTBOOKS. we never discuss the subject matter in class  but its always on the tests
BEST PROFESSOR EVER. As an incoming freshman I had no interest in political science but his class was actually enjoyable. He made lecture fun, great speaking voice and was very knowledgeable.

Dr. Horner is so great. He loves him some SNL skits (which is what he researches for a living.) His lectures are entertaining and I never missed one even though attendance wasn't recorded. Such a cool guy. EC opps too!

Dr. Horner is the best! He really is a great guy! I'd say the most important thing is to GO TO CLASS. There's always a pop quiz and half the time it's just writing your name on a piece of paper and turning it in, so essentially free pionts. Tests are hard, but the quizzes and EC should help balance your grade out.

His class is easy IF YOU GO TO CLASS AND LISTEN. Pop quizzes are nothing more than basic info he repeats multiple times in class. Tests are difficult, but not over the top. Study the notes, skim the textbook and reader, and you'll do just fine. Pretty easy A for me

He only does oral notes, and talks extremely fast. If you miss what he said youll never get a chance to catch up. His tests are so difficult, & his study guides are no help at all. Its alot of readings and A LOT of memorization for tests. Hes seriously a nice guy but dont do it, save yourself and gpa the pain!
Easily the best Poli Sci Professor at Mizzou!! Horner ROX!!!!!

Professor Horner is an energetic person and its not to bad showing up to class. He tries his best to come off clear with what he teaches and usually does a great job at it. He will give random pop quizzes. You do use the book quite a bit. The tests can be difficult if you dont have a firm grasp over all the concepts covered (which is a lot)!

He was a great teacher. Based on his teaching alone, I would take many more classes. However, you HAVE to do the reading, and I wasn't a fan of the book's format. The test are difficult; they're a lot of memorization. He's a fast talker, and he doesn't post his slides online. He does random quizzes. Each of 3 tests is 25% of your grade

The textbook is extremely convoluted with about 5 typos per page.  My english professor father and I couldn't make sense of it.  In addition, he isn't helpful at all with people who are slow note takers.  If you miss the information in class, it's gone, too bad.  Overall, this class and teacher are awful.

Very nice and considerate teacher. His tests are very hard, even with a lot of studying. Most lectures are interesting, but sometimes they seem a little long. Overall, I would take the class again with him!
Horner was an awesome teacher and I never wanted to miss a class! He is really passionate about political science and we get to watch short videos almost every class!!

Overall, I think Horner is a good professor. I enjoyed going to classes, and I learned a lot. There is a lot of information to study, but it's not over-the-top, crazy mind-blowing. The tests aren't a breeze. I thought I did well on the first test, but only got a C+, but on the second I thought I did bad and got an A-. Oh, and I didn't get the book.

Easy class for the most part, tests have a few hard questions. I really enjoy him as a professor and think the class is interesting. If you have to take an American Government class, take this one. Not too much effort and high grade. Plus it's relatively interesting with all the SNL skits.

Horner is great. Haha Hawaiian shirts every day to class plus an SNL skit shown almost every class...not to mention he actually makes this material interesting and fun! I went into this class having a horrible background with PoliSci and hating PoliSci classes in the past and he completely changed my mind. Truly, a great professor.

Lectures are clear. He speaks a little slow for my taste, but i could speed him up on tegrity, which was nice. He IS technologically challenged, though, so be wary of tegrity with him. He wrote a book on how SNL skits effect politics, so be ready for lots of SNL videos as examples of his points. They added some color to American Government.
Soooo much material on his tests. Also, speaks way too fast in lectures. Nice guy and all but this class isn't a cake walk.

In my opinion, this class was one of the most ridiculous classes I've ever taken. I studied for hours for his tests and it never mattered because I would receive low grades. His lectures went no where and I grew tired of watching SNL sketches after the first week. His study guides are impossible and may help, if you can study 17 pages worth of info

Easy class. Recorded for tegrity so going to class was not mandatory. Don't watch tegrity until study guides are posted, then watch tegrity and fill out the study guide. The test is the study guide. I received an A+ (104%) in the class.
Interesting teacher, test are easy if you go through the study guide and pay attention in class.

Great Teacher. If you go to lecture and do the study guide you'll be fine. The grade is made of of three tests and one other small assignment that took me an hour. I hated poli sci in high school, but really enjoyed this class and his lectures are really interesting and he's a funny guy.
If you have to take political science, take Horner. Easy tests, directly from notes. Funny guy, keeps class fun.

I hate PolSci but he made it interesting. The trick to getting a good grade in this class is to really study the study guides (they're long but worth it). 1st test, I didn't study the study guide much & I got a C. 2nd test, I followed the study guide & got a 98%. During one class he set up a flash mob for breast cancer awareness- it was awesome!

Yes, Horner's tests are difficult. If you're not going to put in the effort to study and go to class then don't take this course. However, Horner is easy to listen to, a good teacher, and cares about his students. He also gives lots of extra credit and curves grades. Other students have told me they wish they had taken Horner. Happy Studying!

SUPER HARD CLASS! Unless you are a poli sci major, I would not suggest taking this. You have to know EVERYTHING! Including his lectures, the textbook, reading articles, and current events. Exams are extremely unpredictable.
Take a different class. trust me. unless you want to memorize every concept and word from the book and his lectures.

I would not recommend this class to anyone. Horner is an extremely difficult teacher who does not follow through with his exams and what he teaches. He also doesn't round up under any circumstance. Keep that in mind.
I had the absolute worst experience of my college career in this class. 38 page reviews, unrelated information on exams, hundreds of terms that are never seen. STAY AWAY! My only C ever.

This guy is horrible. He creates a 9 page study guide, which contains the broadest terms he could have possibly find, just so that when he kills you on the test, he can say he put it on the study guide. The only people who do well in this course are the ones who have nothing to do but watch the new and read the book. Take with someone else.

Great instructor. Interesting and cares about what he's teaching. Gives extra credit that really helps grades. Questions are straightforward and he is upfront about grade expectations. Outlines/notes are a little vague, but gives thorough study guides. Talks about his kids alot and does funny things for them, like wears weird hats to class

Class is just 3 or 4 tests, all multiple choice. Go 2 class 2 get notes & do study guide. I didn't touch the textbook until I saw study guide, then I'd go to textbook terms & study them. EASY CLASS. keeps class pretty interesting, & all notes/study guides on gradegenie.com w/ only slight variation. Fill out study guide & memorize & u will get A

It is extremely important to go to class. There are only 3 tests, 60 questions each/semester. The test cover a lot of material. H/e, if you keep up on the reading and listen in class. Prof. Horner summarizes the readings, highlighting important events--TEST MATERIAL. Also, if you go through the review sheets throughly the tests are not bad.

If nothing else, he's a really sweet and human guy. The tests ARE hard to study for but its an avg. 2 and a half pages of terms, NOT 9! Take notes, look up the glossary in the book for terms and you'll get a B on the test. He's the kind of guy that when you leave class you're still smiling to yourself over something he said or did.
Tests are impossible. 9 pages of just words and concepts to define. Only 3 tests in the class.. not curved. The hardest 1000 level class I've ever taken

Super easy tests you can memorize the day before hand, but you have to go to class and take good notes to make sure you have everything or make a friend and split up the notes. he is incredibly bias ultra conservative, and good luck trying to get your grade changed!

After reading all of these reviews, I thought I was in an interesting and fairly easy class. Interesting, sure. But good GOD. Definitely not enjoyable. My study guide for the last test was 27 pages of nothing but definitions and lists and an unbearable amount of material to memorize. 75 m/c questions. It made me want to spoon my eyes out.

Funny, Interesting Teacher.  Testing material is comprehensive, and studying takes a lot of time, but generally easy class day-to-day, aside from the three tests.  He plays saturday night live on mondays if there are political skits!

AWESOME Class! Very funny guy and knows his stuff! Keeps the class going. TAKE NOTES! Biggest advice. You can skim the book and do pretty well. If he has write-ins those are pretty hard, but 2/3 tests were all MC - easy!

Funny professor... often strays from topic... tests are very hard... I took poli sci in high school as an AP class and wasn't prepared at all for what Prof. Horner had to throw at me.  Study study study!
Awesome professor my favorite this semester, test are hard, studying harder than you think for the first one, but I really really enjoyed his class!Is funny too
Great lecturer, high enthusiasm, funny, couldn't ask for more! I wish I had him in a class of 20 rather than 500.

Great professor! Definitely recommend. Readings are extensive, but if you take notes and pay attention in class, you'll do fine. Second and third tests are easier than the first. Only 3 tests in the class, no graded homework, no comprehensive final.
He's good!

Very good teacher.  Very knowledgeable about politics, could probably go comment on it on TV and do well.  Easy class as long as you go to lecture and do the assigned readings, and take notes on them.  Related the class well with the election.  Pretty laid back.  We watched a lot of SNL skits in there to open class, and he was a Cubs fan to boot!
He is awesome! He knows how to make classes fun and keep your attention, as well as makes things clear about what to study and what is on exams. I highly recommend him.

Decent teacher, but doesn't like to find time to meet with you to talk over your grades.  Grades exams way too hard for what the class really is.  Lectures too fast and does not repeat, hard to take notes.
love love love love love love love him.  He's a great teacher.
If you read all assigned material and know everything on the study guides, you will do fine.
Rambles but is knowledgable in what he teaches.  Tells funny stories.
It was such an easy and interesting class. He gives study guides for everything and if you follow it to a T you get an A. He is kind of funny too. Great class and great guy

Very knowledgeable professor.  He knows what he's doing and has a great organization of notes.  Easy multiple choice exams.  HATES cheating.  He was mad when 32 exams went missing.  Btw, he changes his exams every year.

His class was awesome!! He is an excellant lecturer: he doesn't skip ahead, he knows what he is talking about and he explains everything. The tests are tricky, but if you make sure that you know the material (and reading) you will do fine.
Great guy, great teacher.  The class is not hard at all, either.

Great professor, really able to keep my attention.  The class is pretty easy as long as you show up for lecture and do the assigned reading.  If you have to take this class, try to get into his section.

Tough class, but Dr. Horner does a good job of explaining the important stuff and stressing that.  He doesn't make you memorize dates, which is always good.  Tests are tough, usually 40 multiple choice and 10 fill in the blank.  Definitely read the book and the Dow Reader and you will do well in his class.

Great teacher and a great guy.  He tests the important concepts from a class, not insignificant details.  He is always willing to talk with you if you are having trouble, and he's very educated on his subjects.  My only problem with his Writign Intensive class was one of his idiot TAs.  She was awful...ALWAYS give your papers to Horner directly.
only 3 tests

Great Poli-Sci instructor.  Knows what he's talking about, keeps up with the news.  Very good at discussing politics without injecting his personal bias. Tests are a little tough, but you'd probably do better if you read the book (I don't).  100% Recommended.
He's a great teacher. Understanding him is easy, assignments are reasonable, and so are tests. He makes the subjects interesting and times them together. He treats students like people.
i like him, funny, really enjoys what he does. tests are hard but he's a good guy
Know what he's talking about, easy to listen to, funny. Tests are pretty hard though
Good teacher knew his stuff. State Gov. PolSci 2100 is actually a fun class.
Good Educator. However, is a bit boring.
great great teacher.  Smart guy, funny, and isn't boring.  Doesn't spout his political views, just teaches the course. I recommend him.
Very funny!!
No Comments
So funny!!
he definately knows what he's talking about, and he's really funny!
No Comments
I am in his class right now, and he seems to be really into Political Science. He is funny! ANd the baby pictures are soo cute!!
Awesome teacher, he is completely passionate about polisci!

If you take notes and do quizzes everything on the tests are word for word. You do have to go to class for the clicker questions, but its all super easy and I just wrote down what was on the slides then played on my phone
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super nice, the class was super easy. It is unfortunate that this basic a class is required to take other art classes, since the content is not great. Not Bethanie's fault, though.

She's literally the sweetest, most caring professor! I think she understands that many people are not pursuing artistic careers but still makes the class enjoyable! The weekly quizzes are EASY! The study guide is exactly the same as the exam which is super helpful! The sketchbooks are really nice instead of taking notes as well! TAKE THIS CLASS!

This class is so so easy. The quizzes and tests are words for word on the study guide. Her lectures are interesting but can get boring. You have to show up for this class for attendance pinots. At the end of each class, there is an iclicker question for attendance. There are 2 group projects but they are super simple. This class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is basically mandatory as you have clicker quizzes after every class to get points. Tests are word for word definitions from the notes. This class is a very easy A. It can get a tad bit boring, but she is a good teacher. Take this and you will more than likely pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you take all the notes and memorize, the tests are almost completely word for word, and a very easy A. Irons is a good professor, she has some videos to show but most of the classes are just notes and she talks a LOT, there is an iclicker question with points at the end of every class, even artist presentation days to ensure you come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is awesome. I took Stat 3500 online this summer. I recommend taking Stat 3500 over the summer if you can.

Dr. Z is okay. I took STAT3500 online and she really just gave a 15 min lecture and expected us to learn the course on our own. However, homework was typically easy and it isn't hard to pass the class if you do well on the homework.

Dr. Zaniletti is an amazing teacher! It is super important to attend all classes or you will fall behind. If you keep up with the content, it is not hard to get As on the exams. Dr. Zaniletti is always prompt at replying to questions via email and will answer your questions even if they're dumb! HIGHLY recommend her-- plus she's entertaining.
She is nice, pretty and she is also the best Prof. in Stat department. Take her class and you will love it.

Best statistics professor I've ever had, she's funny, very enthusiastic as well as knowledgeable. The best part is I learned A LOT. She gives ample material to study with, study guides, etc. - you won't be needing the textbook.  I added Statistics as my second major because of her encouragement. She's excellent, I can only hope I get her again.
Izzy is great! All-around fun teacher, If you hate Stat take it with her, she makes it painless!

She is crazy, fun, energetic, and what was the weirdest thing of all: enthusiastic about statistics.  I am a stat major and I dont even like it.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND HER!  She makes it almost impossible to fail, if you care just a little bit, you will get an A.
I absolutely love this course! Dr. Ispa is really sweet, knowledgeable, flexible and down to earth. Be sure to show up to class and do the simple homework each class period and you will be golden!

This class was a good writing intensive course. It provided a lot of opportunities to observe and apply your knowledge to what you are observing in paper form. The tests were not easy but writing assignments in class were helpful if you actually go to class! Dr. Ispa was good and interested in student learning!
Dr. Ispa presented very interesting information in a meaningful way and I thoroughly enjoyed the course.
One of the worst classes I have ever taken.  The amount of assigned work was WAY TOO MUCH and the assignments didn't teach you anything.  Avoid if you can.
Professor Linn has been my favorite professor in college so far, super relaxed, doesn't assign too much homework, and makes instructions very clear.

Great class, lectures are engaging and homework assignments are the same every week and are easy. Gives points for attendance and exams and quizzes are all online. Hardest part of the class is recording coaching assessments but he provides a private gym to record it. Overall would really recommend this class for everyone

jacob linn is the best professor at this school. he cares about his students AND the content he teaches and is knowledgeable about it. quiz/exam questions are given if you go to class and it's easy to make up points if you miss. assignments and lectures are FUN bc HE makes them enjoyable to learn. cannot recommend enough 100/10

This is not a difficult class, despite the other reviews I'm seeing. The tests are open note, you just have to pay attention during lectures, which are engaging. Dr. Schroeder is fun. Just don't forget to do the weekly quizzes.

Like everyone else critiquing Schroeder on this site, his exams are really difficult. He is a good professor that's clearly dedicated to the subject of communications law, but if you just take care of the weekly quizzes and iclicker outside of class then you shouldn't bother attending his lectures.

Jared Schroeder is one of those professors that kept me wanting to come back to his class. The tests are hard, don't get me wrong, but the class content is interesting and professor Schroeder makes it really engaging. As long as you take notes during lectures, and make a study guide, you will exceed in this class.
Go to class. Schroeder does a great job with the lectures, you just have to set yourself up for success by attending class and taking good notes.

It is so refreshing to take a class with a professor who clearly cares about the material. Dr. Schroeder is such a fantastic lecturer, pulling in real-world examples for all the content. Also, for the 3 tests, just study, bring your notes and prepare to actually apply what you've learned, and they aren't bad at all

I know everyone says that the exams are tough, but I think it's just because the tests are application-based, which I feel better prepares us for real-world application instead of memorizing cases or definitions to just forget after the test. Show up to class, think about the lectures critically, and you shouldn't have a problem.

The professor is funny and nice as can be but his tests are impossible. You can study for hours and write every single word that comes out of his mouth into notes and the test will still be nearly impossible unless you can find out exactly what trick he's playing throughout each of the 50 questions within a 1 hour and 15 minute time frame.
The tests are way harder than they need to be and I am pretty sure he does that on purpose. The questions are created to trick you. He seems like a nice guy but the exams are just nuts.

I REALLY LIKE HIM AS A PERSON!!!!! I enjoyed his lectures. 
But the exams are way too hard and have to much content on them. They are online but they are really difficult. This class was really interesting but I wish instead of 3 exams we would have had more tests with less content.

Tests way too difficult for the information he gives you in class. I'm convinced anybody getting more than 85% on these exams is cheating. Stopped going to class after test 1 and my grade was nearly the same on test 2. do the iclicker from home and just set an alarm, save yourself the trouble of actually going to the lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The ratings here are not wrong, his exams are difficult & they did account for most of the grade. But, his man is hands down the best professor I have ever had.
