If you have ADHD, this is your guy. I took so much real-life knowledge away from this class & what the other reviews aren't mentioning is that he gave back 50+ points on the final exam.

The exams were very difficult. Because of this, earning points through attending class (iClicker) and doing well on the quizzes is very important to earn a decent grade. His lectures were okay, but he would often go off on tangents. He tried to fit in so much information during his lectures, so sometimes they felt rushed.

The lectures were fine/infromation but the three exams were INSANE. Questions were either extremely unclear or long/ too specific. Many of them were set up as "select all that apply" and then listed a slew of terms and court cases that were difficult to choose from with the vague question. I feel battered and bruised after this course.

I'll give him the benefit of the doubt in that it was his first semester teaching here and his extra credit policy & guidelines are completely fair. However, his exams are unbelievably brutal and demand significantly more out of you than he lets on, nor did I enjoy his lectures. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if there's a better alternative option.

I found Dr. Pasley's class very fulfilling. He is clearly passionate and hilarious if you can appreciate dad jokes. Some segments of the class did drag on (1820s MO politics aren't always interesting) but when Pasley reaches a high point, his lectures are phenomenal. His grading is also consistent and fair, assuming you follow deadlines.

he is passionate about what he teaches, I just don't personally care. i never went to class and still got an A. he gives study guides for all 3 tests and the papers are pick your own due date. its lowkey a perfect class if you can stay self motivated.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of people like to hate on Professor Pasley genuinely because they did not put enough effort into the class as they should have. It is clear from the start of the class in the syllabus the weighting of each category and the due dates for papers. Pasley is very knowledgable and it did not seem like he graded too harshly.

his lectures are very boring, gave us two huge papers and the second half of the mid term was a huge paper that took me 4 days to do. i would recommend taking any other history class the only reason i got a b was because he had to curve his midterm. please choose another history class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you have other options. There are only 2 papers - one 10+ page, one 4-6 page - that are research-heavy. The study guides for the tests are a list of every term from the slides. Tests include: writing a paragraph about 6 different terms, at least 5 map identifications, and 3-4 essay questions (3-4 paragraphs each).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are hard to pay attention to, his slides have way too many words and are difficult to follow, and the tests are formatted in a strange way. He also does very little to prepare you for tests and it is extremely unclear what you ACTUALLY need to know on exams. There are also essays required in the class that just seemed unnecessary.

Where to begin...This man frequently shows up late; he has the most boring possible lectures he can; he doesn't help students prepare for their exams in his class much at all, and when he does, it's either last minute or not helpful. Good luck if you have a question and decide to email him because there is no chance he will get back to you.

Dr. Pasley was a very nice person to talk to one on one, and he is very knowledgeable about Missouri History. In lectures, he was sometimes quiet, and his deadpan tone might throw off some students who weren't expecting it.

His class was horribly boring and he focused too much on topics that were not on the exams. His powerpoints and study guides were horrible and gave me headaches because of the formats. You will go into the final without knowing your grade because he grades so slow! Do not take any of his courses-not worth the time or anxiety about grades.

Worst class I have ever taken. Condescending towards students and dismissive when asked questions. Grades based on criteria that is not clear, the amount of work is ridiculous compared to the way he grades. Classes always go over the allotted period, didnt take the time to learn how to use Zoom effectively during COVID, overall horrible experience
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wasn't too bad, easy A if you go to class and the movies, didnt read one page of any of the books. Has one midterm and one final in class, both with essay style questions. He is funny though, especially because he closes his eyes when lecturing, but clearly opens them when he looks at the board behind him.

Terrible class, information was confusing and had lots of little detail. Teacher kept going down rabbit trails. He would keep students as long as possible, sometimes going over time. Talked with his eyes closed. He never recognized me from class, didn't even know I was his student. Didn't give much feedback on papers.
Prone to temper flares, dismissive, condescending. Not a fan.

I took the Conspiracies class...sounds interesting right? It is...if you enjoy lectures about mucking around on the internet by a social outcast who has his eyes closed. I wish Mizzou would hire a different professor to teach this class. It would probably be great.

Easy-going, smart, presents good and very organized lectures of which outlines are projected overhead with interesting maps and pictures to illustrate points. He has great respect for dedicted students and is kind with his time.

This class sounds fun but guess what...it's not. He lectures straight from the books.  After a while, I just stopped going and read the books instead...if you do that you'll get a B. I had a friend who never read or went to class and made a C.

TERRIBLE! Unclear, gets angry when questioned. Asked for help on paper, he said he didn't recognize me from lecture, therefore I'm a skipper and undeserving of help. I said I sit in back (true) ask my TA, he said slackers sit in back. Lost temper at times mid-lecture b/c of shuffling or people entering/exiting. Got A; consider it independent study.

Don't go to class, a waist of time.  Use it to instead read the books.  I never went and never read and still got a C.  Some good stories but way out there most of the time.  His lectures are too incoherent to make them worth sitting through.

How fun is Hist 3?  This professor's strength is in his conspiracy class.  Dr. Pasley is helpful, witty, and his lecturing style is simply more off the cuff than written down.  In higher level classes, you WILL need to go to lecture, but he makes it f

you can go to class if you want, but its not like it'll help you on the test...horrible lecturer - i counted in class one day that he said uh or um 350 times! all you have to do is read the book and you'll be fine....
Her comments on graded work are blunt, but most students still get A's. She's old-school, but you'll actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took her for Phil 2482. Guess my last review was too hateful and got taken down. So, I'll give it to you as nice as possible: Intelligent person, abhorrent professor. 10 weeks in: not one grade in the class. Modules posted late every single week. Save yourself the headache and just take it in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She graded 200+ assignments less than 12 hrs before grades were due. She also uses her own grading system that is not standard and not listed in the syllabus, really making it difficult to know your grade. She does not post materials in time. She does not respond to emails. Too much work. Never again

PHIL2440 Online

Every week included 1-2hr video lecture, 10 discussion posts, quiz every other week. Course load is heavy for 3 credit hours. Nothing was graded until finals week.

Material itself wasn't hard, but an extremely tough grader. Didn't publish modules on time and wouldn't answer emails in a timely fashion either. We had 2 papers worth 30% of our total grade; neither of which were given a rubric for until after we had submitted the paper, making it impossible to know what she wanted. STAY AWAY FROM HER

Didn't grade anything of mine until the last week of class. We had mandatory 10 discussion boards a week, all worth a whopping 1 point each. Awful at responding to emails- didn't even respond to the ones I sent. Posts material late every week and seems super disorganized. Don't take her if you can help it, she sucks.

Was one of the worst teacher that I have ever had a class with. Does not provide a grading rubric for the papers due which are 30% of the grade. Post assignments late and expects them to be due two days later. At least six discussion posts a week as well. DO NOT take her class.

She is a very good teacher, but she did not provide good resources to succeed in this class. We were assigned work to do, and it was due the very next day. There was tons of homework that was not unrealistic with deadlines. She also only did mp3 files and no visual lectures. I would not take this class with her.

Professor Janasz was very knowledgeable about Philosophy and was great at teaching it, but she grades painfully slow. Its hard to know how well youre going throughout the class when you arent getting feedback in a timely manner.

Prof Janasz is a great teacher & person, but the class wasn't at all easy. There's a lot of homework on Tophat, which is easy, but the tests are pretty long and difficult. Be prepared to take A LOT of notes & do a lot of probability stuff, and you better have a thorough understanding of the material before taking the test or you won't do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Milyo is fantastic; his class is demanding but fair. Grading is clear, and he knows his content super well. Homework is optional but should always be done, as it looks exactly like the test. He has a dry sense of humor and makes economics interesting. So long as you pay attention, take light notes, and do homework, you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found Prof. Milyo's lectures pretty entertaining and found his style of teaching much more engaging than endless powerpoint lectures. But lectures are not recorded though so you NEED to go to every lecture. Also keep up with the optional homework and readings every week, I did so much better when I kept up with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Milyo is great! He's knowledgeable, super funny with great humor, and a prof that really cares about his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Milyo is a great professor who's clearly passionate about the subject. Attend his lectures (which are engaging and funny) and do the "optional" homework, because you will be tested on all of the content. The tests aren't easy, but preparing a detailed cheat sheet can make them much more manageable.

Professor Milyo is very funny and engaging, which I feel a lot of teachers/professors fail to do. Make sure you really understand the graph, either that be putting the exact graph in your notes and understanding what each variable represents and their relationships, or by memorizing the graph. Do the homework not required, but none of them are busy

The class is 300 points spread across 3 exams with no curve. Other than that grading system he is a very funny professor and has very entertaining lectures. If you show up to class every day, take notes, and write a good cheat sheet you will definitely pass. If I didn't lowkey owe him $14 I would definitely take another course with him

Overall good professor, very intelligent. He runs class the 'old-fashioned' way -- chalk on chalkboard, minimal slides, handwritten notes. Hardest part about the class is the grading -- for 1014H, only the tests were in the grade book (and an optional 5 point paper). If you think you can handle it, I'd go for it. Very nice guy once you meet him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof. that cares about his students. The grade is based on three tests and an extra credit paper. He gives extra credit on all exams. He is open to talk after class or in office hours always. Pay attention because he gives students money, I got 20 dollars.

If you procrastinate, this class will not work. Grade is 3 exams. Yes, his lectures are cool. Dr. Milyo tells it like it is and likes to use econ-speak (externalities, utility, opportunity cost) to talk about life. He knows and loves the subject. However, I think I would've learned more if I'd been paced with deadlines and/or accountability.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Students are given little opportunity to succeed, all that goes towards your grade is three exams across the semester. he gives optional homework that doesn't count for your grade and zero assignments or projects, which for me personally made the information a lot harder to grasp. Bad test takers beware.

There are only THREE grades that go in for the entire semester. Everyone I know dropped/withdrew from this class. Counselors all say they've heard many complaints about this class. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you miss a lecture you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my second time having Milyo and he's just as amazing as ever. This section was Political Econ, and it was VERY text-heavy. Be prepared to read 40+ pages of journal articles before each lecture. His presentations are always entertaining, and there are no tests; you are graded off participation (37.5%), two essays (50%), and 3 HW (12.5%).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeff is a fantastic professor. The course is hard, but he makes sure that you have all the tools you need to succeed. Many fail his first test because they don't believe that lectures don't cover all the material (like he always says), but grades improve a lot for the subsequent tests. He's also hilarious, and makes coming to lecture a treat.
Best professor I have had up to this point. His lectures are entertaining and funny; which are vital attributes if you are taking his 8 a.m. section. Tests are straightforward but difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't be afraid to ask questions and go to office hours! It feels intimidating (bc it is) but you can't let that faze you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeffrey Milyo may grade harshly, but the material is pretty "you either know it or you don't." Make sure to participate in class, as this is often rewarded. He has a sense of humor which appeals to everyone no matter your political stance and gives lots of resources to help with studying. Just make sure you use them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Milyo is funny, which makes his econ lectures enjoyable. This class is difficult, but it's because Dr. Milyo wants you to know the material well. He expects a lot from his students, but he's a gem of a professor and brilliant guy. He also responds to emails quickly and really does care about his students and wants to facilitate their success.

Lots of chances to earn extra credit because he understands the class is pretty tough. It's definitely possible to do well but I feel like he made it a lot harder than it needed to be. Material wasn't too hard, it was just figuring out what you needed to know. We didn't receive enough practice for problems that would be on tests. A lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Jeff Milyo is a remarkable person. His classes are funny and insightful, and some of his lessons will blow your mind. I ended up with an A+ in this class even though I thought I was failing the entire semester. Take the writing intensive section and he'll help you out along the way.

Great class if you're up for a challenge. If you complete two optional extra credit papers, you can raise your grade by as much as 6%, and most exams have a few extra credit questions on them as well. Average score on the first exam was 60% and a lot of students dropped, so the class is difficult.
Absolutely fantastic professor. The class is hard as hell, but his lectures were really interesting.

Milyo's dry humor, extensive knowledge and desire to teach not just textbook info, but info that applies to the real world, were the best parts of the course. The worst part was its difficulty. If you are interested in Econ or want to be challenged, this is a great class to take, but if you're just trying to meet the req, it's probably too much.

Sensational professor, knows his stuff. Could easily see this guy being in the top decile of econ professors. The course will allow you to understand the colossal world that is healthcare, and you'll apply its lessons in real life. One of the most valuable classes I ever had.

This class is invite only but if you get the invite then take it. First half of the semester is all guest speakers. Some speakers are good and others aren't. The second half of the semester is economics after dark. You talk about some controversial issues but with an economic mindset. This part is wholly discussion but it can be pretty entertaining

Dr. Milyo is a very good professor. He has a unique sense of humor that is best received by economics majors. He does well at dumbing down tough concepts. This class dealt with some controversial topics (drugs, race, abortion, etc) but these were handled in a purely economic mindset that made I had not previously considered. Very interesting.

Milyo is funny and has a clear knowledge of Economics. His teaching style is very mathematics-based and most homeworks and exams are applications (not just repetition) of the concepts covered in class. No PowerPoints, just 1.5 hr lectures 3 times/week. Covered 36 chapters and had 3 exams. Felt like I needed an intro to this intro class.

A really interesting class, and, while concepts are sometimes difficult to grasp at first, the actual grades are easy. The tests had study guides, and there were no surprises on the exams. He also graded the essays very leniently. I highly recommend this professor and this class. Only downside is there's a lot of reading, albeit interesting reading

Jeff is a great professor. The class is not easy, but it isn't hard. If you go to class and read the textbook you should be fine. The homework is a joke. He'll give you half credit if you just scribble words on a piece of paper. His tests are straight out the lectures so take good notes.

He knows a lot, and conveys it clearly in class. It's a lot of work, though, as the course covers a lot of material. If you want to succeed, take note of everything he says and writes, ask any questions no matter how stupid they sound in your head, and re-write your notes when preparing for exams.

He is extremely mean in giving credit, does not curve even when the highest score is less than A. The test is so hard and we have really not enough time to work out that much, and the average of the scores above 60 is around 70! Even you can learn much in this class, you will regret if you attend it. It really drives you crazy if you want an A!

Damn near the best professor I've ever had. Smart as hell with a dry nerdy humor. Seriously, between health care, law and politics I don't know what subject this guy isn't knowledgeable in. Sr. Fellow at the Cato Institute too... Though he is still a pretty moderate guy if you care.

Difficult material and high standards, but an excellent professor with a exceptional command of economics and ability to take difficult concepts and explain them at a basic level, in addition to relating concepts to everyday examples. His expectations are straightforward and he is very willing to give extra help.

A really hard class, most students did poorly on the tests. Milyo cares about student learning though, giving practice exams, a little extra credit, and is always available to talk to outside of class. Milyo's curve is pretty generous as well, but you definitely have to do the reading from the book which is really time consuming.

Don't listen to all those other posts. Professor Milyo is a great teacher. Yes, his class is very difficult. But if you attend class, listen, take good notes, the tests are simple and straightforward. He no longer grades his exams on a bell curve. Also, he does a good job at relating the content to relevant issues.
Great Teacher who actually cares about teaching his students useful information and not just what comes out of the textbook.

Even though Econ 1051H is definitely a difficult class, Professor Milyo is an excellent teacher.  He taught in an interesting manner and the amount of material you learn in a semester is astounding.  Just make sure you keep up with the assignments and study well!

I simply would not recommend this professor.  Asking questions got me nowhere, as I felt belittled for asking anything and the answers were not satisfactory.  Class average on exam 2 was 52%.  Curved, but still a bit ridiculous.

The course material is tough, but Professor Piao is one of the best teachers I've had. He is very passionate about his teachings, and therefore, his lectures are always amazing. He is very approachable and cares for his students. I would definitely recommend him as a professor.
He was awesome.

Best core accounting professor I have taken.  Material is difficult, but he is very willing to help and break things down for you.  He makes an effort to know every student.  Spent a lot of hours studying, but he grades very generously at the end of the semester.  Take his class if you can!
Great proffesor, gives out letter grade on scale based on the grades for the rest of class. Most students get either a B or A, he said you have to try to get a C.

VERY difficult class, but Jeffery definitely tries his best in explaining each concept. Very punctual when responding to emails. Has many handouts to provide examples in class. Exams are tough, but the handouts, HWs, and take-home quizzes show good examples of what to expect on the write-out portions of the exams (typically 16 of them).

The best professor I have ever had. Knew everyone by name and although Financial Accounting 1 is a difficult class, he made learning as easy as it could be and enjoyable. In class examples, engagement with students, and the feedback given on handouts were all amazing.
my guy! amazing prof

This is the guy you want for Financial I. He understands this is a hard class and does his absolute best to help you learn the content. Loves a good joke as well. Pay attention as he will randomly call on people in class. My favorite accounting Professor yet.

You can tell Jeffery really cares about teaching. Goes out of his way to learn students' names, always approachable, and makes a VERY hard class a little bit more bearable. Homework and quizzes are take-home and open-note. Exams are closed-note and covers a ton of difficult content, but he gives you lots of materials to use for preparing.

Jeffery is a great teacher and great guy. His lectures are very good and organized and he makes sure to get the important points across. He also goes out of his way to make personal connections with students and is very approachable. Highly recommend.

Jeffery is an amazing professor! He knew each student by name and made such an effort to ensure everyone understood difficult concepts. The tests were similar to the quizzes and I always knew what and how to study. I would highly recommend him for Financial I.
The class was very difficult but Jeffrey made it worthwhile. I would recommend his class from my experience

Jeffery was an exceptional professor for Financial Accounting 1. He utilized great in-class examples and truly cares about students. He knew each student by name. Paper homework. Exams are similar to in-class problems. I would highly recommend Jeffery when selecting a professor for this course.

This is not his profession. Examples are meh and he doesn't go into enough detail to promote success. You will be left to drown. If you are struggling in 1050 swap degrees asap or your gpa will get tanked by this guy like everyone else I have seen. He is a red flag.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are entertaining and class content covers assignment topics; the course is relatively easy outside of exams. On strictly multiple-choice exams, I'd say that about 60% of the questions are tricks. Even the first exam over only a month's worth of content was very difficult.

My favorite prof. OS was my 6th class with him. I'll admit he used to be stricter and some classes were better than others (he gets more lenient with higher level classes), but overall he's always available to help, open to criticism, and gives entertaining lectures. Just make sure to study a lot for his tests--both lecture slides and examples.

This is the second class I've had with JimR. His lectures are entertaining. He has lots of "trick" questions on exams. If you've ever written any code before then this class will be a breeze. Assignments only took 10 minutes to an hour. If it weren't for the exams I would take again. No coding class should have exams that are only multiple choice.

He is a very funny teacher, but he was not able to teach it to students who had never coded before. Many tests had very low averages because he would make the tests too hard. Weekly assignments were not too bad, but were lots of steps that overall made them hard to complete.

JimR is a chiller, very knowledgeable. Would be difficult if you've never written code. Class is basically just an intro to python, not much actual data science. Exam #2 was hard. Weekly assignment are manageable, but are not graded for weeks. Just ask Claude to generate pratice questions based on the material and you'll be chilling for exams.

He is very charismatic, but I found this course extremelyyyyy challenging. The exams always felt tricky, and one exam had a class average of about 60%. The weekly homework was demanding and difficult. Students without prior experience in Python or coding will find this course especially difficult.

He made class enjoyable, I went probably 90% of the time. However, he is LAZY. He rarely communicates out of class and everything gets graded by TA's. The exams are always meant to trip you up. Almost always code with a million steps that you can't keep track of without writing each step down. I took 1300, not 1050, but that wasn't an option.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Despite maybe not being the best fit for 1050, JimR's CS knowledge IS a perfect fit for OS. Fun in lectures, assignments are a good difficulty - start early + expect to spend a few hours per week on them. Only negative is that TA's took a while to grade stuff and you wouldn't get feedback until you'd already messed up the next few assignments.

Alright, hated him for 1050, much better fit for 2050 and beyond. Clearly very knowledgeable, but doesn't care if you can't make class you're losing iClicker points anyway. Much easier to understand when he's talking about higher level concepts than 1050, I think he just struggles to dumb it down, honestly. Beware of Lab 3 my god.

Don't get what's so "bad" about him. It's a tough class but it's not hard to pass if you put in some grit. DO THE PRELABS AND ASK QUESTIONS!! Definitely a weed-out class, but if you're passionate in CS, you'll be fine.

Unfortunately he is kinda the only teacher that does this class. As said with other reviews his tests suck and you are essentially taking yet another weeder class. Lots of classmates are incredibly frustrated with Mizzou's comp sci curriculum at this point.

JimR is my grandpa if he could code. He's a cool person, but not a great teacher. His lectures are interesting, but sometimes unclear or off topic. Labs have clear expectations but horrible practice material ahead of time. Tests are a nightmare where everything is a trick question. He also doesn't decide if the class gets curved until the end.

The assignments are needlessly stressful with no direction at all. You're expected to code massive programs that you know nothing about because lecture is hardly related: you don't learn how to code anything in class. They aren't even useful for exams. I've spent less time outside class on 5 credit hr classes. JimR knows its hard, but doesn't care.

Class is designed to fail you. My free public school and community college classes were more challenging and your effort reflected in your grade. Tests trick you, and there is no way these labs are acceptable for a 1050 course. I finish the labs fine but I know 5 other languages and I leave them perplexed that anyone thought they were acceptable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took a lot of advanced CS in highschool and community college. Even I would say this class is wild for a 1050 course. Textbook is surface stuff relative to his tests. Needs more outside programming work if he wants his test questions to stick. This class NEEDS to priortize getting students aclimated to C rather than drilling them out the door.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are really hard to prepare for and the average usually ends up being around %50-60. The exams are trick questions only instead of vocab or testing your understanding of how things actually work. You can get 100s on all the labs but fail the class because you get trick questions wrong on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Its honestly crazy to me that JimR is getting so much hate. Hes a good professor. If you have good test taking strategies you will pass his tests.
Challenging intro course, but the professor is helpful. Attend lectures, use the free textbook, and leverage resources like ChatGPT and unstuck AI for study prep - it really makes a difference.

JimR, starts CS1050 off by making it feel like an introductory course but it quickly becomes a challenging weed-out class. Exams often feature tricky so called “JimR Questions” designed to catch students off guard/trick you, and the review guides don't help. The course's structure and testing style make it unnecessarily difficult and frustrating.
I've always really liked JimR as a professor, and this class is no different despite it being the first/one of the first times he's taught this specific course. Would recommend!

JimR is a great professor that is knowledgeable, funny, and cares about his students' success. If you go to class and don't procrastinate on the assignments, you will do just fine! I had him for all four core algorithms courses, so I feel like I can vouch that he's a good professor and just generally a great guy to communicate with and learn from.

Are you ever at a point where you impulsively want to throw a toaster in the bathtub while you're taking a bath? I was. You have failed the generous God King Ethan, and for that- you will perish in the eternal flames of darkness- forever! Fear the end, mortal, because you have done a great sin to our God King!

HEIL

#JusticeForTheGodKing

CS1050 is an extremely difficult class which inherently means there will be a lot negative feelings towards JimR. However he is a kind soul and an effective teacher. Doing prelabs are a must as well as reading the textbook and watching youtube videos. If you put in the work you will succeed but it is not for the faint of heart.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Horrible professor

JimR is genuinely a good person and is really funny. It's just that the exams he gives are extremely difficult especially for an introductory class.The review guides slightly prepare you for the exams because JimR asks really difficult questions on the exams that are designed to trick you. Expect to get a low score on the exams (40%-70%)
JimR is a solid professor.  Very sociable, and you can be assured that what he teaches is exactly what is going to be on exams and coding assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To pass this class you definitely need to attend lectures. I've taken other computer programming classes in the past and I thought this would be easy, but I found this class to be hard, even after attending most lectures and doing all of the optional prelabs. JimR does try to make lectures entertaining best he can from the already boring content.

Really nice guy, and so knowledgeable about coding! Wanted to help kids whenever he could, and responded quickly to emails. The labs were worth a lot, but very similar to the pre-labs if you did them. The exams are notorious for being hard, but following along in lectures and trying out things on your own and being curious really helps.

If you are taking him for 1050, beware that his exams are quite difficult. If you want to succeed expect to study C syntax in-depth, as the hardest questions on his exams are "What will this code do?" and "Which code will output what I want?". If you learn C syntax then his exams are fine

JimR is a very nice and engaging guy, but I think a side effect of his deep understanding of computer science is that he might expect a bit too much from his students. His lectures are good, and labs are pretty easy as long as you attend them, however exams are a different story. As far as studying for exams goes, be sure to read the textbook.

JimR is a great guy but the class is setup so horribly it doesn't matter and this mixed with poor teaching methods make it very hard to succeed in this class for most people. Its too fast paced, the labs are way to hard, and then tests are even harder, in almost every assignment the class average is failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really like JimR as a person. However, unless you've been programming since the Kindergarten graduation you will have a very tough time in this class. Lectures are incredibly hard to follow and understand. He often goes on very long tangents. All exams and almost every lab had a failing grade. There definitely needs to be a change to this class.
Frustrating. Assumes you have a bunch of programming experience before coming in. What is the point of an introductory class if it relies on this assumption? Reflects poorly on Mizzou's CS department
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You need previous experience in C before taking his class. Very confusing test questions that he will state, "I should have gone easier on you" upon review of the test. Ta's practically just read the lab and when asked a question, they give the vaguest answer. I do not recommend him for beginners in coding.

This is for cs2050 and was his first year teaching the course. Could tell he was unprepared for the course. You could tell during lectures that it was his first time reading the slides himself since he reused uhlmans. The labs are fairly easy as long as you use chatgpt. Ta's don't help much. 2 exams: the midtern was difficult, the final was easy.
Not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Often went off on tangents unrelated to course material, meaning we had less time to learn stuff we actually needed to know. Worst part of this class by far is the tests and how heavily they're weighted-- he writes his own and the questions are poorly worded, cover too many subjects, and are too complex.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
My complaints are: trick questions on exams, not very accomodating, and lots of content. 
Aside from that, he's a good guy with lots of industry experience and his lectures are interesting.
Verry hard on grading, almost no way to fight any grades. Accuses students of copying way to easy and reports anything he deems fishy to the provost without asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor isn't the worst ever. If you've never taken a college course before the class can seem like way too much but you'll need to be proactive to succeed if you're not already an expert at coding. He has a very welcoming attitude which makes it even easier to talk to him after class and attend office hours to get help.

When taking this class as a person that has never coded a single line of code before, it was very challenging. Jim unfortunately teaches like this is a upperclassman class. This class can be easy through attending lectures, office hours, and self-learning. Tests are difficult and the study guides help very little with how the test will be written.

JimR is a very tough grader. From personal experience, this class is not challenging in a good way, it's really exhilarating to be a part of. No matter how good you are at coding, you will not end up with a satisfactory grade in this class. The tests are not practical at all. You have to be a human compiler to get a good grade on these tests.

He is a decent teacher. You need to take responsibility for your learning in this class. If you read the slides ahead of class, go to office hours, ask the TA's for help, etc. then you will be set. The TA's for this class are usually really good.
JimR is a great guy and you will learn a ton in his class, but exams are difficult and filled with trick questions. Stay on top of your lab work and you will finish the course in good shape.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: most of the people who hate jimr did not attend lectures. the labs & tests will be difficult if u dont go to class, but if u go to class & office hours when u r confused, u should be ok. also, theres a textbook for the class not that many people know about but reading it is worth it! sometimes labs were def way too hard, but he has good intentions!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: terrible attend lecture or else you are screwed labs are unfair and expect you to code like you wrote code since you were out of the womb. Tests are full of tricks and no clear-cut answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of my friends struggled in this class, I thought it was fine. I enjoyed the lectures a LOT, to the point where I found it easy to wake up in the mornings and get myself to class. My rating was brought down by the awful test questions and labs that are occasionally much trickier than the prelabs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures consist primarily of example programs and rushing through the slides. The material is reasonable and labs are fair, but some test questions are unnecessarily difficult. The professor is clearly very knowledgeable on the subject, but isn't fully suited for an intro class it seems.

While JimR is a great guy and is super personable, this was an insanely difficult course. This is in no way an intro course and i would definitely say you need previous coding experience to  do well. The labs are not terrible if you do the pre labs, but the tests are awful. PAY ATTENTION IN LECTURE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will contemplate changing majors at least once taking this class. The course is fast pace and all concepts build on top of each other. The tests are insanely difficult, there is no way to prepare for the tests. Labs are fairly easy and you can get a pretty good idea on how to do them based on the pre-lab. Jimr is a funny guy but rambles a lot.
Professor Ries provides interesting lectures and is always ready to ready to answer questions. Incredibly experienced in his field he is an asset to anyone interested in computer science.

He's a really fun person, but unfortunately his class structure doesn't work well for someone who has never programmed before. I learned 90% of how to code OUTSIDE of his class. There are very few grades, and if you mess up once, you'll be struggling the rest of the semester. Tests are just trick questions and very difficult. Tough intro course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't absolutely need this class for your major, run as far away as possible. Tests are absolutely brutal, labs are WAY WORSE. Be prepared to work extremely hard and probably fail this class the first time around. At least its easier the second time you take it! Godspeed!
Jim Ries is the most professor ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny guy, worst teacher I've had in my life. I love programming, but no one else has made me want to change majors sooo bad. We get a lab every week, three exams that are made entirely of trick questions, and that's it. Horrible intro class- feels like he assumes you already know everything, and goes off on random, irrelevant side tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: JimR isn't a bad guy, he's actually pretty awesome but he is indeed a awful professor. His class layout sucks. Having your life on the line every week for lab is one of the worst feelings I've been through. Class is portrayed as entry level but is the farthest thing from it. By the time you hit week four he will start to pick up the pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jim Ries is a very nice person but when it comes to teaching, he is not very good. He rushes through topics and will often go on side tangents about something that is not related to what is being taught. If you really want to peruse computer science, for the love of all things holy PLEASE LEARN C PROGRAMMING BEFORE YOU TAKE THE COURSE

JimR was great.  He gave plenty of live examples of code so that we could see exactly how stuff works, which was very helpful.  He was passionate about what he was teaching, and always answered questions clearly.  I'm excited to hopefully take another one of his classes in the future!

JimR's knowledge of the material and his sense of humor made lectures a joy to attend. Warning: the quizzes and tests had several trick questions and hard questions. We all struggled with the assignments; some people gave up completely and turned nothing in. Don't do that! It is possible to get a good grade if you just make this class a priority.

Jimr is a phenomenal teacher however the labs can prove difficult near the end of the semester. If you are getting ready to take this class, please please whatever you do do the prelabs. It makes the labs 100x more doable. The two labs I did not perform well on were due to a lack of attention to the prelab.

Jimr is really smart and there probably isn't anything this man doesn't know about C, but it doesn't translate well at all to the assignments he gives out. Some of the later coding assignments take an insane amount of time to do properly, and it really shows when the average grade on the last one was around a 40%. God speed and good luck with OS.

Does not teach the class like it is an intro class. Nice enough guy, awful awful teacher. Sure maybe I know the code definitions, but even after all his lectures, you will likely still have no clue how to write, apply, and manipulate code.

DO NOT TAKE without learning another language prior.
To make this easier learn C ahead of time, however, Python, C++, C#, Java, and/or JavaScript Should translate well. 
Exams are not graded over what you practice, rather you are graded over passing comments he makes in class.
Be sure to make sure you lab compiles or you will get a zero.
CS 1050 is all about writing code. The class is only graded on weekly labs and 3 tests. The tests are full of trick questions. The class is almost impossible to pass without any coding background.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: JimR's a great, fun guy. He's not a good instructor though. This course is the first programming course many CS students take at Mizzou, and as someone who had prior experience going in, this is far too difficult for an intro class. Expect to need help on labs. His exams are terrible too, with many trick questions.

Had to take this course for a second time to pass. Took as a freshman and was not mentally prepared to put the time and effort in to actually learn the material. My fault. If you go to every lecture, read the textbook, and do the prelabs, you'll be fine. Spent about 15 hours a week studying hard and had a great time. Also, JimR is a cool dude.

I went into this class with experience with 3 different programming languages, and as someone who has much experience learning programming, this isnt an intro class. Labs get unreasonably hard at the end and the Exams are by far the worst ive ever taken. 60% of questions on the exam are made to trick you and dont test your actual knowledge

He only provides labs and exams. It's a hit or miss class. The TAs also wouldn't help a friend of mine, rather than encourage and help him. They adviced him to drop the class. Which is very telling of the class overall. Sad thing is I went to every lecture and still got a 69%, which is 1 percent from passing. Literaly wish to wipe my memory of JIMR

Only homework provided are Labs. So if you don't understand them, tough luck. Grades are only given through exam and labs. So you're bound to fail if you dont get them completed. Teaches as if everyone has computer literacy. His teaching methods suck and the majority of my classmates either failed or withdrew from his terrible class. I never skipp

JimR is a nice guy, but not a fit professor for an intro course. This class is not appropriate for students who have no prior experience programming. This class will make you want to change majors and many people do because of it. Thankfully there was a 10% curve, but theres no guarantee for a curve each semester. All I can say is good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: They found an issue with people cheating online homework. So they tried to ramp up the difficulty. The made it so difficult that over 50% of the class is failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you take anything from Rate My Prof at all, do not take this class with JimR. If you are a computer science major recognize that this is undoubtedly a weeder class. His TAs were awful and rarely available. Study hard and be prepared to grind on this class. IF YOU ARE NOT A COMP SCI MAJOR, take the 1040 class instead!!!
The right person if you are looking to spend your thousands of dollars of tuition learning trick questions for quizzes, or if you are looking to waste a good amount of time.

Only take this class if it's in your major, do NOT take it for "fun" if you don't have any prior experience with coding. If you are confused on the prelabs (one every week), you aren't allowed to ask the prof or the TAs questions so good luck. It is very hard to gauge what you are supposed to understand in this course until it is too late.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. This is not an intro course whatsoever. Unless you have a strong background in coding I would not take this class with JimR. Your grade is essentially based on how you do in labs so... good luck. I wish I could rate him a 0

JimR gives clear expectations for the weekly lab. His lectures are good, he seems cool. The exams are my only complaint about this class. There are questions that seem like hes purposely trying to trick us, which I guess is fine because you do have to notice the tiny details if you work in the CS industry. Just pay attention and you'll do good
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is a class in DESPERATE need of quizzes and homework. The tests are extremely hard with no curve, using concepts that you never get to practice before the test. The average grade of the semester before me was a C+. That is not a joke. If you haven't coded before, be ready to put double the time in this class than any other for a worse grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class starts off easy but jumps WAY up in difficulty at about the halfway mark. If you don't do the prelabs you are literally trolling. Tests are all multiple choice but are still tricky. Stay on top of things and or you'll get stressed out real quick - trust me...

JimR was a super sweet guy, but the quality of teaching was not there for an intro course. I had background in programming going in and I always read the textbook to learn the content, so the class was super easy for me. Objectively, though, the lectures definitely don't teach you the content as good as you need
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: JimR is a solid CS teacher. Overall, I find his lectures more helpful than just the slides he posts on Canvas. Pay attention to any exceptions he outlines in his lecture, because they may be on the test. Labs are hit or miss. Some are very easy, but others are quite challenging. Be ready to study hard and do the Pre Labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'd say JimR is a pretty solid teacher. If you have never coded before in your life it may be tricky. The tests are pretty hard, the average was around like a 68% but I've heard pre-covid it was around a 50%. Tests are trick questions. Not a big fan. Labs can be pretty difficult, but if you don't fall behind on the weeks material you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class introduces the basics of C programming and gets more complex as the semester goes on. Jimr teaches the content well. A large potion of the grade is based on labs, but it you do the prelabs you should be able to do well on them, and on many you can get extra credit easily. The tests are pretty hard but the extra credit makes up for it.

jim is not a good professor. whole class is based off of labs which are very unreasonable to complete within the given time. tests are extremely difficult as well and many questions are made to trick you. he offers prelabs for the labs but they arent taken for any credit (which makes them not worth doing). if you take his class rip

If you're looking to start computer science at Mizzou with no prior coding experience, don't expect this class to help. Grades are based solely on programming labs (which is timed) and tests - nothing more. You are better off learning coding concepts through youtube than through cs1050.

Jimr was an insanely nice guy, BUT his class was super difficult. I was not the only one struggling. Many other people I knew in this class were in the exact same boat. The whole class was solely based on Labs and Tests, no quizzes or homework. I hardly learned a thing. The whole "you don't need any prior coding experience" was such a lie.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While Jim Ries is an extremely nice person, he is by far the worst professor I have ever had in my academic career. Labs in his class felt impossible some weeks even though he claimed no coding experience is required for this class. Tests were also extremely difficult with many tricks questions. If you get Ries as your prof, I pray for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have no experience with C or another lower level language, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I have prior experience with C#, and was being tutored by a friend who is a software developer, and I still struggled with this course. The lectures are dry and heavy, labs are made to be obscure/difficult, and 90% of test questions made to confuse/trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely ridiculous amount of reading to do. Show up to the lecture? Nah. You won't learn a thing. You're better off watching a YouTube video or reading the book because good ol' JimR will NOT be much help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Operating Systems was probably in the top 3 hardest classes I took. Ries had fantastic lectures that got information across well - it's just unfortunate that essentially none of it covers how to actually apply the concepts at the code level for the assignments. The quizzes were a bit challenging, but the assignments were insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: JimR is a good teacher & cares about his students. If you do the prelabs & watch the lectures you'll be fine (he records lectures). Labs at the end of semester get hard & it's easy to lose points on those. He does like to get tricky with exam questions (all MC, normally 40 Q's long) so don't expect A's on them unless you study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jim Ries as a person is a great guy. I really like his personality and his enthusiasm over the topics he teaches. You can clearly tell this man loves CS. However, his assignments are simply unreasonable. The File Systems assignment is widely regarded as the CS killer. Be prepared to spend no less than 40 hours a week on that or take the grade hit.

Unfortunately you must take this class to graduate with BS in Computer Science at Mizzou, and he's the only one that teaches it. You shouldn't take any other hard classes during this one if you can help it. He won't show you much of anything you need for the very time consuming HW. Not sure why he decides to teach, better off doing something else.

JimR is very knowledgeable about coding and showed us impromptu examples and taught important things that wasn't included in the textbook. Lectures are very dry and it is hard to focus; you will often learn a lot in one class. His labs require a lot of preparation, meaning do the prelab and practice coding what you learned in lecture.

reads straight off the board, which is all put online in advance. labs are extremely difficult and i feel like i never learned half of what the lab was about and had to ask my TA a lot of questions. felt like i knew what i was doing until the exams. did very well on labs on homework and the tests were not accurate of my understanding of CS

The labs were nerve wracking, but doable; that said, complete the prelabs or you are going to fail. Also, his tests were terrible, but manageable. I spent many hours on his class every week. He is a great guy, but be aware that his class, despite being introductory, is not what I or most others would consider to be "easy."

This teacher should not be teaching an introduction class. He knows what he is talking about but does not know how to teach whatsoever. I've always enjoyed computers but this class made me want to completely drop my major. JimR couldn't teach me how to wipe my ass properly even if he tried.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: JimR claims that 1050 is designed so that even those with no coding experience whatsoever can pass. That is not true. This class is unreasonably difficult and if you're coming in to this class with no prior coding experience, prepare for a world of hurt. Also, the lectures and pre-labs don't prepare students for the labs or at all.

JimR doesn't know how to teach students with no prior experience. The prelabs don't prepare for the labs AT ALL, & the lab assignments are impossible to finish within the allotted 2.5hrs. Even the TAs said they have trouble doing the assignments. Lectures arent helpful & exam material is never covered in class. Take IT1040 instead of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: After pointers, it spiraled. Had multiple labs where people gave up early and almost none of us could get the task done. During lectures, he just says what was in the book, word-for-word sometimes. Exams are 50% of grade (2 midterms + final), labs are 40% I love CS and am majoring in it, but I considered dropping due to this class, a prereq for all
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: JimR is a great person and is hilarious but his class is ABSOLUTELY Horrible. I have learned absolutely nothing from the lectures and the tests are AWUFL
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Jim gives very boring lectures. They are somewhat useful, but your success in this class will entirely depend on your commitment outside of it. Do the pre-labs and the labs aren't too bad. The exams were kinda rough. Not terrible just be ready to teach yourself some.

This guy is a really, really, horrible professor. If you can find someone else. He doesnt teach you. He uploads homework that would be totally doable, (After you spent 8 hours on stack exchange learning on your own), but he makes you do it his way, and his way only. Prepare to not come to this class, and prepare to do lots of studing on your own.

Like others have said, he is an awesome person (some of his stories are the most hilarious I've heard from the CS field), but I will have to say that he was absolutely the worst professor I've had. I get that OS is a tough concept, but he even joked that it should be split into two semesters, and that really hurt because you know he doesn't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: JimR shouldn't teach. Lectures were awful, same 30/150 people showed up every week. Labs and homework were tough. GO TO THE TA's, they are much more helpful. The tests he gives are stupid and are designed to be hard as can be, the average was failing. Do your prelabs. This intro class felt more like an experienced coding class. Nice guy, bad class.

I liked coding so it wasn't as bad, but I felt sorry for the people who didn't. Jim is a super nice guy, but not cut out for teaching. When I did my lab assignments, it never felt like I had actually been taught the material, and the tests don't seem to test actual coding knowledge. Lots of opportunities for extra credit though - it's doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is basically a self taught class, you wont learn a thing going to lectures. Your best bet is to go to the TA office hours and make sure you do the pre-labs. Tests are way too hard and made up of trick questions. Good luck in this class cause you will need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jim Ries is actually a pretty nice guy and is very approachable. However, he is not a good instructor for this course in any way. It is way to vigorous for an entry-level programming class and if you don't have any programming experience, good luck. Some labs are easy, some are WAY too hard, and homework is too complex for beginners trying to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I honestly don't know how anyone new to programming is expected to pass this class, as it moves very fast and JimR is not skilled at teaching intro. The book is not recommended. Its a horrible way to teach programming and its arduous and extremely time consuming. Put the time you would have spent reading, into coding and youtube tutorials instead.

Liked JimR as a person, but really not a great teacher. If you go into office hours, he really tries to help you out, but he seems like the type of teacher that is used to teacher higher level classes and does not know how to explain concepts in an intro class. Got a C on every test even though I got perfect scores on the labs.

Perhaps it was this class being at 8am, or the lecture hall being very dark, or that I already knew a lot of the material, but I got very little from Mr. Riess lectures. Often, Jim would go on side tangents for 10+ minutes to figure out what some obscure detail of C was, which would be fine if it didnt take forever to get there. Light 4 / 10

Terrible lectures. I feel bad for all of the people with no experience walking into this INTRODUCTORY level class. He did not prepare any of us for the unnecessarily hard tests. I do not recommend this professor whatsoever for any class

JimR (brace yourself for a lot of this) was the worst instructor I have taken. He spent his lectures proving that he knew the material rather than teaching it. He wrote the tests intentionally with questions he knew were beyond our understanding. Everyone ended up teaching themselves, which was a huge disadvantage to the novices in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Jim is a nice guy, and he's good at coding. However, the grading is seriously flawed and the labs expect you to be able to understand concepts that are outside the scope of the course. For example being able to code calculus sequences in a freshman level course. I felt it was unfair with the grade, but I did learn a lot. A lot of people dropped it.

Ries is definitely passionate about what he teaches and he does a decent job of explaining things. Also gladly accepted feedback from students. I didnt think exams or quizzes were too bad since the questions were usually covered by what he taught. Projects were insanely difficult and took WAY too much time to complete. Due every week.

Terrible teacher. Tests are impossible, the avg on both tests was 50% for 250 students. Lecture is not helpful you end up teaching yourself the coding and fail the tests because they are questions that make no sense.

Jim Ries is a bad teacher. With a dilapidated schedule and unrealistic expectations it is no surprise anyone I've talked to about this professor has had something bad to say. I understand this is a difficult class but I have found my time is better spent learning the material by myself than in Jim's so called "lecture."

I gave Prof. Ries a bad review for his other class, but he was MUCH better in OS. The material is very interesting, and he explains concepts well. The homeworks were very challenging, especially the file system. Test/sample code files were changed multiple times sometimes hours before the due date. Exams were straightforward and based off lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ries taught Operating Systems for the first time this semester and did a great job. His explanations were spot on. But the homework for the class is a lot. Projects are long and worth more than the exams. Go to office hours early and often.
Terrible teacher. Had a major hard on for anything Microsoft and didn't seem too keen on anything else. He taught the course like it was a intro course. Overall bad.

I was disappointed with this class. Many of the lectures were over deprecated or irrelevant material. The class was both too high-level and too low level at the same time. He would jump around from a broad concept to a coding example without much congruency between them. He's very Microsoft-heavy, but we could have covered so much more.

Jim Ries is not usually a regular professor - he also works at Veterans United Home Loans. Jim Ries is smart; however, this class essentially became about learning various Microsoft frameworks and deprecated web technology. His lectures are unorganized, uninteresting, and uninformative. I would not recommend taking any CS course with him.
Great teacher, especially on co-ops issues.

The class was easy as long as you showed up. A large portion of class time involved guest speakers that were ok, so I did not feel like I learned as much content as I expected. The course was helpful for preparing for the career fair, but overall I hoped for more direct instruction and engagement from the professor. Hard grader if not liked
Just show up and you will do well
Jill is a good teacher and a great person. Always willing to help with career development.

Prof. Moreland was the instructor for my non-WI section of ag marketing. She was easygoing but sometimes felt detached from the class. Her presentation comments were insightful. The course content was fairly easy, but the final paper was worth 275 pts and working in a group setting sucked. However, I don't think this was under her control.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved her! She will do anything for you, as long as you are willing to try in her class!

This class was awful. She grades hard especially if she doesn't like you. I learned nothing from it besides that group projects still suck. So many different speakers that are sometimes interesting or will put you to a deep sleep. Only positive thing is there was no classes on Fridays usually!
Best professor I've ever had
Lovely class.

Dr Spain is the GOAT. One of the most caring (and entertaining) professors you will ever have. My one minor complaint would be that he prefers to have assignments submitted on paper which is sometimes inconvenient.

Dr. Spain is a great professor who goes above and beyond to make sure each student connects with the material. Each lecture is interesting, and class participation helps make boring topics seem less bad. Overall, it was a 9/10 experience. Some content was boring, but that was not at Dr. Spain's fault.

Dr. Spain is one of the funniest, most caring, and understanding professors out there. You write a research paper over the semester that he gives great feedback on. He brings in experts in different fields of ag to give fun and interesting lectures. He makes a study guide for the quizzes and exams and if you pay attention and work hard you'll be ok

Dr. Spain is hilarious and cares about every one of his students. His class is built around the student's suggestions and not set in stone until after he hears from the class. There is a big semester paper, but he gives plenty of time to write and revise it. Beware of him when he drinks coffee, he gets VERY hyper.

Dr. Spain is a lot of fun, and while I didn't really enjoy the class as a whole, I loved his lectures. He's so funny and personable, and he's always down to chat about dairy (don't ever get him started on nondairy milk though). He gives great advice on research papers and is good at helping students understand how to use feedback effectively.
Easy A

Best professor by far! This man is so funny and truly cares about his students. He is always available outside of class and works hard to make class entertaining. He gives great feedback on assignments and papers. You should get an A or B if you complete all the assignments.

He is so understanding and truly cares about his students. Awesome professor! Highly recommend. Animal Science 2111W focuses on one research paper throughout the whole course so it is fairly straightforward.

Dr. Spain is an amazing professor, if you are good at writing papers and like listening to informational lectures about agriculture then you will love his class. Attendance isn't mandatory but he takes some form of attendance everyday. Overall an amazing professor.
Only Fantastic

One of my favorite professors by far! So funny and such a friendly person willing to help you in any way possible. I have had him for AniSci 2111 and part of Ruminant Prod 2165. He reviews the material you need to know for his tests and quizzes before you take them which is very helpful. HIGHLY recommend him!!

Everyday you listen to a lecture from a different guess speaker. They want you to be actively involved and pay attention in class. This is a writing intensive course so most of our grade is a research paper that we work on all semester.

He is the best professor i have ever had! Hilarious and actually cares about what he is teaching and the students he is teaching! The material can be tough but he makes every lecture fun and exciting!
Wonderful teacher. Hilarious. Makes class worth coming to.
Dr. Spain is amazing! I love his lectures. He knows his stuff, is passionate about the dairy industry and Mizzou, and cares deeply about teaching and his students.
Who doesn't love Dr. Spain? He's my favorite animal science professor and I have loved every class of his I've been.
Awesome teacher and guy in general! Very personable and rateable to students. He is the best!
This guy is the best professor I have ever had. He really cares about his students. I learned so much but never felt stressed. He is a superhero!

Honestly one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. He deserves every great evaluation he gets. Very straightforward about the material you need to know, great sense of humor and fantastic teaching style. He also makes himself very available to his students if they need help. Honestly changed the way I write and approach problems. LOVED HIS CLASS!

I loved him as a teacher. He was funny and kept things interesting, even in a subject I had no interest in. He set you up for success by being clear about what he wanted you to know and what would be on the test. He gave you the information in a way that has practical use in and out of the classroom. I would go out of my way to take his classes
Very friendly and caring teacher, willing to help, funny, enthusiastic, get's to the point, gives many chances for extra credit. Take any class he offers!
He's a great teacher and very enthusiastic about his job and his students.  He wants his students to do well and does what he can to help them.

Professor was engaging. Teaching style unorganized and unclear. Would be better as an online class. The material is taught using online texts which I found to not help in learning Spanish. Turn in homework on time and do the extra credit to do well in the class.
Do not take this Professor! Very unclear with her directions and contradicts herself when asked to follow up on assignment instructions.
She subbed in my class for a few weeks and was very helpful, fun, and clear. She's very high energy, so if that's not your thing, be forewarned.

This woman is awesome! Very eccentric, outgoing, and passionate about Portuguese. She really loves to immerse us in the Brazilian culture--we even had class at a bar a few times. Learning any language is difficult, but if you put time into it and PARTICIPATE in class you're golden. I've learned more in 1 semester than all 4 yrs of HS Spanish.

Sra. Hartleip is awesome!!!  Her class is tough and requires work, but she makes it ineteresting. There was never a dull moment. She helped us with anything we had questions on and was a great teacher.

Wow, if she didn't have such a distinct name, I'd think I'd had a different professor than the one everyone's been rating on here! Srta. Hartleip was fun, helpful and always tried to make the best out of teaching a class primarily filled with students just hoping to fulfill their graduation requirements.
Such a difficult class. Hours and hours of studying. Fast paced. Would suggest just taking Spanish for 3 semesters compared to the 2 semesters of Portuguese.

People who think that she is a bad professor are those who did poorly in the class and that is NOT is professors fault. She is an AWESOME teacher! Of course the class is hard, it is a foreign lang. It does fill the lang. requirement in 2 semesters and the professor is very down-to-earth, open, fun, and understanding. She's the best teacher i've had
Avoid at all costs.
No Comments
From course policies to communication to mutual respect, this is the worst experience I have ever had in university.

THE WORST PERSON ALIVE. I WOULD REMOVE HIM FROM THE FACULTY IMMEDIATELY. I was verbally assaulted in his office, provided zero help or insight, had extreme class difficulty, and was way too nitpicky on simple coursework and lab reports.
Jian Lin is not a good professor. His exams are incredibly difficult and often have questions on them about topics that were never covered in class. Please try and get someone other than him.

The only positive I have for this class is that if Dr. Lin can teach it, anybody can. Real talk; the exams were worth 40% with nobody getting an A on the last one, he said he would curve if needed but I guess he forgot to do that.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Lin can't speak English well enough to teach effectively. He does not answer questions effectively and writes problems that have either ambiguous answers or multiple answers. On multiple occasions he miss graded multiple students assignments. When you ask for a correction or a clarification he gets upset with students. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Segert for two courses last semester and she made it so easy to know what you have to do every week, there are tons of options for extra credit and if you keep up with the work the exams are very simple!

I have had three psych courses with Dr. Segert, she sets you up for success. Watching the lectures and taking notes will give you an A on every exam. There are a few exams, discussion posts, and no final. There are a decent amount of extra credit options which are super easy. I am ending PSYCH 3830 with over 100%. Take her classes if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is best if you want to spend majority of your life studying the brain.

Dr. Segert is amazing! Online courses can be difficult, but she sets them up in an extremely helpful way. She lets you drop one quiz, and provides extra credit about every other week. She has office hours set up at frequent times if anyone wants to ask questions, or just chat with her about anything. She's an amazing professor!

I have taken professor Segert for all of the Psych courses I have taken at Mizzou, she always keeps things interesting and I never got bored in her class. My favorite of her classes was Drugs and Behavior I would highly recommend it. Lectures are recorded and test are online. Loved taking her classes, I wish she offered more.

If you get the opportunity to take an honors section of any of her classes, definitely do! It's clear that she has tons of faith and trust in honors students, and the relatively easy tests reflect this. Her lectures are never boring. She's clearly very passionate about the subject and knows a lot of stories that help you understand the material.
She is a great teacher. She speeds through powerpoints so you have to be a fast writer or typer. Her tests are kind of hard. She does give bonus points on tests.

Segert challenges you- her lectures are very interesting, but she flies through the slides - pay attention and type fast! There is literally no work in the course- only three tests. The tests are difficult, but if you can swing Bs on each of them and not miss class, the attendance and  exam extra credit points will cover you- I stll got an A.

2210 with Professor Segert was awesome. She gave out 60 extra credit points this semester just for showing up to class on random days. Tests are identical to lecture material, however she doesnt post anything on Blackboard so take good notes because she moves fast. This class has alot of interesting material and is definitely worth your time!

Segert's 1000 class was awful and I hated it and I somehow managed to end up in her Mind, Brain, and Behavior class and I absolutely love her! She gives over 100 points in extra credit and rewards you for coming to class. Very interesting content and she always keeps it current!

If you get the opportunity to take an honors section of any of her classes, definitely do! It's clear that she has a lot of faith and trust in honors students, and the relatively easy tests reflect this. Her lectures are never boring. She's clearly very passionate about the subject and knows a lot of stories that help you understand the material.

Professor Segert is by far one of the best professors here on campus. Her style of teaching is fun, engaging, and interesting. She incorporates current events into her lectures (i.e. Vacination debate, Ebola, etc.) and keeps you interested. Tests are easy if you come to class, take notes off the powerpoints, and pay attention.
Super passionate about what she's teaching. Always kept class interesting and fun, yet informative.

She is very interested in the material and she tries to make it relevant and interesting. You get extra credit points just for showing up on random days. She is approachable and friendly. My only complaint is that she tends to speed through her powerpoint slides which makes it hard to take good notes. Either learn how to write fast or paraphrase.

Ines made Health Psych bearable for me, as I had to take it for my degree and it seemed like one of the least painful options. She is very personal, friendly, warm, and entertaining. She makes even boring material interesting and I didn't have any difficulty understanding the concepts. She's great!

Going to class is crucial, as she doesn't put anything on tegrity and the notes are identical to the tests.  She also gives out 30 extra credit points throughout the semester that are based solely on attendance.  Somedays were extremely interesting, and somedays were so boring you couldn't wait to leave.  Regardless, the class was a fun, easy A!

Professor Segert was pretty great. She absolutely loves teaching what she does and you can really tell. Tests are super hard though. No assignments or quizzes, and the only grades are from the 3 exams. Her lecture material can be difficult, so go to class and take good notes. She is a good teacher. And she offers a couple extra credit quizzes.
