She's so nice and SO smart.  Mind, brain and behavior was a pretty hard class but it was still the most interesting class I've taken in college thus far. You cannot skip this class because she covers so much material, and be sure to read the articles she posts in the syllabus.
Excellent professor, excellent notes. Made me love psychology.

Dr. Segert is the best professor I've had at Mizzou. She taught me so much valuable information in the field of psychology. Dr. Segert is very helpful. In her capstone class you are allowed to miss 3 classes, but you won't want to because the material is very interesting! Best capstone class, I highly recommend Segert!

Professor Segert is by far the most fantastic teacher that I have had at the University of Missouri. She uses current information, provides ample study material, clearly explains test expectations, and offers extra credit. Plus she plays awesome music and is hilarious.
Mrs.Segert can teach me psychology any day of the week ;). Very hot teacher and total babe.

Professor Segert is very knowledgable about the subject and has a lot of experience. Only downside of the class is the required experimental participation which is a hassle. Each test has at least 50% of past tests questions on it so try to obtain exams from previous semesters. Overall very clear cut and easy course.

An extremely easy class. I missed quite a few lectures and pulled above 100% on every test (she does give EC questions during lecture). Can be a bit boring and oversimplified, and expects too much class participation. An easy credit and fairly interesting.

Incredible! After high school psychology I never wanted to hear the word again let alone take another class. Because of her, however, I'm now a Psych minor. Go to class (the exams are directly from her lectures), study, ask her for help if you need it (Because she is more than willing) and you should have no problem getting an A+
Easy, easy, easy! Exam questions come straight from lecture. She's so sweet & nice. Class was great.

Although it isn't necessary, I would suggest going to class because if attendance is low she will give extra credit quizzes or answers to test questions. I went to every class, but put in minimal effort, and got an A+
It's not a very interesting class, but I did end up with a 103% with minimal effort.

Segert is great, she has done a lot of research and you can tell. Her lectures are clear and she is always willing to stop and go over something if you don't understand it. The class isn't easy but she made it a lot better.
SUCH a sweet teacher. Makes the class interesting and easy to follow. Not trying to trick anyone or make the class difficult. I absolutely loved her and recommend her for Psych 1000

This was "Human Sciences Sequence I: Personal Identity." There is a lot of reading every night, but the conversations in class were always interesting. Ines is so sweet and so smart, very easy to get along with. I recommend this class.
good professor, terrible at writing tests

Prof. Segert is one of my professors in college I will never forget! She is crystal clear during her lectures and I recommend to my friends that they take at least one her classes. Her tests are straight forward--she doesn't try to trick you. You either know it or you don't sort of class. I learned a ton. And she's extremely kind and attentive.

I loved Dr. Segert. Okay, I can see why people say her lectures are boring, but if you pay attention, her stories that she relates back to the material are quite interesting. She is VERY straight-forward on her tests, especially if you actually go to class and take good notes. I want to take more classes of hers!

I was really excited for this class but only a few weeks in to the semester, I found myself not going to class. I found Dr. Segert to be incredibly boring. I only showed up on test days but I kept up with my reading. I barely studied for the tests and I got a B in the class. It's easy but definitely not worth the time to actually show up to class.

Dr. Segret is awesome for Psych 1000. Sit in the front of the class and she will know your name if you participate. Read before class and do the homework for the easy points, also the Clinical labs. Exams are pretty easy if you go to class and take notes.

This professor was not helpful at all. Her lectures were hard to follow and boring. The test questions are confusing and tricky. The class average on the first 3 test was a 67.8% . The one easy thing about this class is the homework.

Very easy class. Show up to lecture, pay attention, and you'll be golden. The "textbooks" were a few small health novels. They're not necessary for the class, but interesting and easy to read. She is always enthusiastic and open to class discussions about topics.

This class was very boring, it is mandatory to come because she dos not post her notes or provide them if you miss class, there are only tests, 40 questions, 120 points each. Make sure you know the research studies and you should do well, the book was not useful to me.

WONDERFUL teacher. She teaches a lecture but still tries to take the time to learn everyones name. She genuinely wants you to do well on the exams. She gives a study guide for each exam as well. You don't need to go to class, but if you take down her notes word for word- there aren't many notes- you'll surely pass the test.  LOVED her!
Nice teacher, but definitely not the easiest Psych teacher. She says her tests are "not tricky," but in reality they are pretty tricky. The lectures are directly from the book.
Slightly boring class. Lectures were boring. Very intelligent professor though. Memorize experiments from lecture and you'll do well on the exams.
Not a tough class at all, but then it is Psych 1000. Either read the book or go to class and take notes, she doesn't post them online. Plays music at the beginning of class which is kind of awesome.

Pretty easy class with this professor. As long as you read your book, you'll be fine. Attendance isn't necessary, but it helps with EC. She talks about being open-minded but she seems closed off, which is ironic. The class helps with GPA for sure.

Fantastic teacher. Grade consists of participation in psych experiments, online homework assignments due before each test that are very short and you can guess till you get it right, and 4 tests. The textbook is extremely helpful but I learned best from Segert herself in lecture. Gives out answers to EC questions in class that will be on the test.
Good professor, but I don't see what these other people see. She wasn't the best I've ever had by far but it's not terrible. I think some people click with her, and some don't.

Best teacher I have had! If all of the professors at the University were like her, students would learn far more and actually enjoy attending class! I can not thank her enough for everything I have learned this semester, I just wish I would have taken her other courses!! Amazing and inspirational woman! Keep it up Dr. Segert!

She is the best professor I have had here at school so far. She is very intelligent about a wide variety of topic and incorporates them very well into class discussions. Just be sure to go to class for the quizzes because it will definitely help you at the end of the semester!

Took one class from her and couldn't help but take the next! Absolutely loved her teaching and enthusiasm and while she's hard at times she really pushes you to think outside the box and analyze what you're actually reading.
loved Dr Segert--- I had her for at least 3 classes, and I loved them all.

A-MA-ZING professor. literally cannot say enough good things about her. Extremely helpful, passionate, compassionate, and funny. She is an amazing professor, in it to teach, not to fail. Hands-down the best professor/teacher I have ever had. Love Professor Segert!

Professor Segert is so great. She is so incredibly smart and insightful. Makes class interesting. The material itself IS challenging, but she enjoys it so much and is so clear cut about what is relevant that it makes the test easy. She loves to help students and will always make time for you.

Great discussions. Appreciates student input. Positive. Wants to make it as easy as possible to get an A while discussing great topics. Wants to make the class as relevant as possible. Absolutely great.
FABULOUS

Although nice, she is scatter brained and the notes she takes in class are all over the place. The tests are easy, but the class - eh, she takes notes on a projector and hates powerpoint. And I always had missing info on my notes b/c she just skipped sections of her notes. I wouldn't recommend her. Pretty dull class too.

GREAT PROFESSOR! She is a delight to listen to and learn from. It's a shame she is no longer teaching Mind, Brain, and Behavior. She cares so much about the students and teaching. I HIGHLY RECCOMMEND HERRR!!!! easy A!

THE NICEST AND SWEETEST PROFESSOR YOU WILL EVERY HAVE! TEACHING SKILLS ARE AWESOME! CLASS IS VERY INTERESTING, ESPECIALLY IF YOU ARE INTO HOW THE MIND WORKS. EXAMS ARE EASIEST YOU WILL EVER TAKE.   DEFINITELY TAKE THIS CLASS!!
Made class interesting and fun, basically study the study guide and easy A on tests, she makes the class easy, favorite professor
simply amazing love her clothes and she went to freaking PRINCETON seriously loved this woman would take another class with her in a heartbeat also she tries to learn names it is super sweet
Loved coming to this class! The daily music choice and her excentric outfits were enough to motivate me to go :)
This class is hard. She is really nice and funny but the material is not easy at all. The good thing is that she gives you a lot of extra credit!
best teacher ever

I can't believe anyone would think she is scattered and boring. If that's how someone really feels about this class then it was because they probably didn't show up that much and simply didn't take the time to learn. She is one of the best teachers I have ever had, she gives great notes, and does an excellent job teaching. The tests arn't hard.

She is great! A sweet and really wants her students to do well and rewards them for coming to class.She went to Princeton and really knows what she is talking about!!She is so sweet, I love her! I like that she talks about her fam its funny

She is a nice person, but she is super boring and scattered. I can't understand her and the way she teaches. It's all over the place. If you took psych in high school DO NOT take it again... I don't like it anymore.

Took Psych 1000 - Prof. Segert is nice, but she is completely clueless and scatter brained. Her class is easy, but death boring. Notes really aren't that clear either. She hates powerpoint, so she uses a projecter (bad idea). But she doesn't even fill the outline she provides u with, she only does like half the notes. Very Disorganized.
If you want to hear about the history of the Segert family, please take this class! That's all she talks about, her husband Yawn and her two kids. I don't like this class.
LOVE her and the class. Super easy...tests are very straight-forward and just about word-for-word from the lecture. Very interesting as well! Definitely my favorite class this year.
Amazing and interesting professor! You will fall in love. My favorite teacher ever!

LOVED her. I took the honors section and it was a great class that was actually interesting. She's extremely fun to listen and talk to-and she treats you as equals in the classroom and remembers you outside of it. Hard to get a hold of sometimes, but the class was 5 papers, no tests-all on stuff you actually didn't MIND writing about...go figure.
She keeps the class interesting
She's amazingly sweet and she knows what she's doing.  The class is easy, but very interesting.  I looked forward to going.
She is very interesting to listen to, and gives good examples to relate to the topic.

Professor Segert is a breath of fresh air! She is always straight-forward and willing to answer questions in great detail. She is different from many instructors in that she combines a good sense of humor with passion for her field. I cannot say enough good things about her. She's also not half-bad looking!
AWESOME!!!! Take her every chance you get!!!

The best teacher I've had yet.  I really enjoyed this class with Ines, and felt like she really cared about the students on top of being very knowledgeable.  I recommend taking any class with her, if for no other reason than to see a great professor.

Dr. Segert is possibly the easiest teacher ever. Her tests are straight from the notes and assigned readings. She also gave out a rediculous ammount of "extra credit" which was basically filling out a survey for her other psych major students.I ended up with over 110%, so I have no sympathy for anyone who doesnt get an A in her class.

Prof. Segert is by far the BEST professor I have had at Mizzou so far! Her classes are extremely interesting, her tests are straightforward and pretty easy, lectures are easy to understand and interesting, and she is a fair grader. I'm not even a psych. major and I have taken as many of her classes as I could. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!
She was definately one of my favorite teachers at Mizzou. She actually makes the class want to learn the information. She was really fun! If I get the opportunity I will take her again!
Best teacher I've ever had.

This is the best teacher I've had. She mad the class so good that it was the only one i looked forward to every teusday and thursday. she convinced me to switch from a journalism major to a psych major. highly recomended.
She was the BEST professor I had at Mizzou.  She genuinely cares about her students and she's very knowledgable in her area.  I wish she could have taught all of my psych classes.
I thought the class was very interesting! She shows a lot of videos and her outlines were always posted onlines. Plus, she hosts a review session before every test. She is a very good Professor!

Prof. Segert is amazing. Listen in class, take notes= get A. Very simple study guides and exams are exactly like them. She is very clear in her expectations, occasionally extra credit for coming to class. I wish I could take every one of her classes.

Dr. Segert is the best professor I have ever had.  She teaches interesting subjects and has an enojoyable fun lecture.  I have taken 3 of her classes and will take more if I can.  Tests are just like the study guide, so study!! *You do have to study a little to get a good grade, but there is always a curve!

Prof. Segert is a fantastic professor. She is easy to follow, and willing to help you if you need it. You learn a good deal in her classes, the material is generally interesting, and as long as you go to class you're sure to get an A. I also had her for Psych 2220.
She is a great teacher. As long as you go to class and get the notes the tests are easy. You would honestly be just fine without a textbook. Probably my favorite professor so far.
love her!!!
Dr. Segert was a great professor. Always straight forward and at times funny. Great teacher.

Love this prof!  She is without a doubt one of the finest teachers at MU.  Take her classes.  You will have to do your work to do well on the tests, but if you ask her she'll offer you any assitance you may need.

She is the best teacher ever.  Classes are fun to attend and never keeps you the whole time.  Don't buy the books because she doesnt put questions from there on the test. If you study the notes taken from class, you will get an A easily.
Very lovely lady who clearly knows her stuff. If you attend lectures and study a little, you will do fine in class.
Really cute, and EASY! When she says she doesn't like to be tricky, she is telling the truth. Just be sure to read what she tells you to, because there WILL be questions on the (easy) tests from it!

Prof. Segert is one of the best teachers around. She loves coming to class, knowing everyone, and never keeps you the whole time. She will adjust her teaching schedule and throw notes out if there's not enough time to cover them. She has 3 multiple choice tests that are straight forward and taken from notes. Take her class if you can!

Professor Segert is the coolest professor I've had this semester. She relates everything you are learning about to something cool and she's a total genius. A good class to take and an EASY A! I'll definately be taking more of her classes later on.

She isn't a fashion queen...that's for sure, but she is a GREAT teacher.  She makes class very interesting and genuinely wants people to enjoy Psychology, and she does a good job.  She's very straight-forward, and isn't out to get students at all.  I LOVE the class!
nice lady. pretty good teacher for an interesting subject. pretty likable person, pretty awkward lady tho socially
This professor makes the class interesting and fun to attend.
Dr. Segert is one of the nicest and sweetest teachers at Mizzou, she is extremely helpful and really knows what she is talking about!

Prof. Segert has to be one of the best teachers in the whole world.  When she says her tests are straight forward, she isnt lying.  They are normally word for word right out of the study guide or your notes.  Her lectures are always interesting, I dont see why you wouldnt want to go!  I <3 her!
This class was sooo easy....the tests are an easy A plus she gives extra credit periodically!!! The lecture may be boring at times but it is interesting.  Take this class it is a definite A!!!

I went in during her office hours to talk just because she was so knowledgable and cool, even if I didn't have questions.  Her lectures are fascinating, which makes it easy to get a good grade.  A great person, professor, and class.
Soooo easy.. definatly take this class!!!  I hardly studied and got an A.. doing the experiments sucks though.  She's super nice and the class is easy.

Extremely easy class...seriously, I think I got over 100%. She can be boring at times, but the material is interesting, and she'll show movies that take up a lot of class time. Probably my favorite class so far.
Very smart woman.  Most stylish teacher I have ever had bar none.  Kind, helpful, and brilliant.

Very interesting class, some may say she is easy, but it's mainly because she makes lectures easy and interesting.  Her tests are exactly what you should be studying, and she even gives review sheets that help out greatly.

Dr. Segert is a great teacher!  She always presents interesting topics and unlike many other professors, she does not make the class so hard that no one can do well in it.  If you take a class of her's you will not be disappointed.
She puts the notes online and you just copy her writing from the overhead for notes.  Tests are pretty easy and reading is light.  Not a bad class and a very interesting selection of material.
easy A
If all teachers could be like her....that'd be great. The class is a good intro to psych, easy but very interesting. She shows movies to make the knowledge relevant. Study the notes and definitions.
Segert is great! She is a great teacher, who knows alot and is very interesting.  She makes note taking really easy and doesn't try to trick you on the tests!
Her tests were extremely easy and the lectures were very interesting. I can 't think of one bad thing to say about her. Overall great teacher!!!

She gives detailed outlines of her lectures so it's really easy to follow and study for tests. The only thing I don't like is that she talks about her days at Princeton and UCLA a bit too much and she dress a little too young for her age.
Good teacher, knows the material and works with the students.
Very soft spoken voice, but very genuine and nice.  I like her alot!!
Challenging class, but enjoyable.

Her tests were unbelievably easy, just look over the notes and it's fine.  I suggest that you take her if you are interested in psych and want an easy time with it.  I don't know how she compares with the rest of the psych teahers though.

Segert is quirky and interesting. She was great to have in class, because you never knew what she was going to say. The class was easy, the video clips were a nice addition. It was an appropriate intro-level class, and I really enjoyed learning the matieral.
No Comments
shes really cool and a great teacher. she makes the class fun. if you pay attention its an easy class.
No Comments

The movie clips were an excellent addition to the lectures.  Sometimes the hour and 15 minutes go a little slow, but she lets us out early every now and then.  The tests are straighforward, but a little book reading is needed.
She was really funny and showed some interesting movie clips to make her points. Also there is lots of extra credit, often for just showing up.

She's SUCH a great prof-if you can take a class with her, do it! She's interesting, a great lecturer and willing to work with students. She's very passionate about what she does. I wish I could have taken more than I class with her.
fun teacher that makes you think.  her tests are straight forward and she gives good examples with everything.  great class
Probably the best professor I have had so far.  The class is very interesting and she does not make the tests very hard...if you go to class and pay attention they you will do good.
She is funny and keeps the class pretty interesting for the most part.  She is very clear and the tests aren't very hard.
She is a pretty easy teacher, but she is incredibly absent minded.  Her notes don't make a whole lot of sense, but the tests are really easy!

I thought she covered some very interesting topics.  She was a little goofy and absent minded in class, but oh well.  She did let us out early just about every class which is sweet.  Oh yeah, definitely did have a hot bod, gotta appreciate that.

Her teaching is interesting but not very helpful outside of class.  She doesn't give out her office phone # b/c she says that e-mail is the best way to get ahold of her & then she never replies.  Her test ?s need work, they have bad sentence structure
Excellent teacher, easy to approach with questions during office hours and after class. Very well versed in subject.
She is one of the best teachers at Mizzou.  Not that it matters, but yes she is hot :-).
She was great in both courses!  She is so helpful and understanding!
No Comments

I've had her for two other courses, and I can tell you that she's one of the best professors at MU!  Princeton-educated with a body that puts mine to shame, girls and guys alike love her classes and her enthusiasm.  She's awesome!!!
Great teacher!!! hot!
No Comments
She's very enthusiastic.

Good communication with students, and gives clear study guides for all tests. Only complaint I have is that he becomes very condescending to the handful of students that actually attend his lectures, when they don't raise their hands to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was a complete waste of time. McDonald lectures on the most random topics. Do not take this class if you know nothing about mythology going into this class, you won't learn anything. Easy A, but don't expect to learn anything useful.

The lectures are hard to understand sometimes and its easy to miss important information but he gives you a lot of good study materials including a study guide that literally tells you exactly what's on the test so it's pretty easy to pass. He assigns a lot of readings but you don't really have to do them, just look at the TA notes and study guide.

Prof. McDonald gives the vibe he thinks he's better than everyone. Any noise on exam day will cause him to tell the whole class to be quiet and stare at you like it's your fault the chair squeaked. Don't go to lectures, don't buy the books, don't do the readings. His study guides are basically verbatim of the test. Study it and you'll do fine.
Would be a difficult class but the study guide is near identical to the test. If you study that for a few hours the days before the test you will do good in this class.

While the class was interesting and well taught, John seems to think he's Jesus Christ himself when he comes to Mediterranean Studies. He yelled at multiple students in class for talking and he once yelled at the entire class for standing up to loudly to pick up our tests. Highly recommend taking with different professor.
YAWN #boring. Hate this class more than life itself. Would not recommend. Do not take this class. Take online if needed.

Professor John McDonald didn't just teach me—he broke me down and rebuilt me stronger. Every lecture felt like a Nolan film: confusing, emotional, profound. His PowerPoints? Art. His grading? A divine mystery. He doesn't curve grades—he curves souls. Take him if you want to see God.

It took me a while to succeed in this class, the only thing that got me through was TA notes - a saving grace because Prof. McDonald does not put any words on his slides, and the TA notes would interpret them for you. Readings also helped a lot. If you just memorized & studied the exam study guides, you could get close to 100% on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMS 2070 is probably the worst class i've taken at Mizzou yet. McDonald doesn't teach the class and when he actually does talk, it's nonsense. We talked about horses for a week straight, no joke. He makes you buy 4 books for this class, and you barely read any of them. Don't go to class, study guides posted are almost word for word the tests.

This class was hard for me at first as I was not interested in mythology and just needed the credit. At first, I was super overwhelmed but after I put in just a little bit of effort my grade completely changed and I became interested. He wants his students to succeed and makes it very clear what your coursework will look like for the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty much no point in going to lectures as he posts a question-by-question study guide before each test that is literally the exam in the same order as the test, so just memorize the that and you'll be fine. Quizes before every test but are graded on completion but doesn't give out much homework to make up for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures do not matter. Textbooks and assigned readings don't matter. He'll post a study guide about a week before the test just memorize that as it's basically the test with different wording.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory, lectures are long and sometimes boring and he expects you to remember everything hes said when he asks in classs questions. He posts a study guide before every test which has basically all the test questions on it. Easy A just takes memorization.
Greatest Professor I have had

No slides presented during our meetings for AMS 2070 and we were expected to listen to him blabber about random things and go on a tangent about something that had nothing to do with the material.We had quizzes every class based on assigned readings,but often we wouldn't get to the material covered on the quiz, but we were still expected to take it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Can't miss any class, easy teacher, but very boring. McDonald rambles and lecture attendance is required, but the study guides are just like the tests. Easy A, boring and huge classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is not very difficult at all. The only grades are basically attendance and tests, and your lowest test grade is dropped. The hardest part of this class is sitting through the lectures because he is constantly rambling and yelling at individual people in a class of 400 people. I would not take this class again.

The study guide is exactly like the exam. So if you do the study guide and attend the meetings, you are going to get a good grade. No homework for this class. There is assigned readings but you do not have to read them. Test heavy. He does rambles on during lectures. Lectures are not recorded. Do have to attend all meetings to have a good grade.

The class is only graded on exams and attendance Lectures are just him rambling abt stuff not on the test. The only way I passed was by teaching myself the material. He also has an ego problem and got so mad about my response to an assignment that he sent a whole essay about me to my advisor
Do yourself a favor and dont take any class with this man
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most negative experience I have had in 3 years at Mizzou. As someone who had interest in this topic and taken many courses through AMS, this course has ruined my interest. Class is exam heavy and McDonald chooses niche, misleading, and unimportant questions on exams. Lectures are mandatory and drawn out. TA's are rude. Avoid at all costs.

If you miss a single class kiss your grade goodbye. He puts one thing on each slide and then rambles very fast for ten minutes. Lectures are not recorded so if you miss one thing then there's nothing you can do. What he teaches is different than what the other mythology teachers teach, it's like he makes stuff up just to see if you are listening.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've had John for a few different courses, and I was hoping that his teaching style would improve if I took a non-language course with him (it didn't). He will ask frustrating questions in class in the most convoluted way possible. Honestly, I think he's a great person and researcher, but he is very stubborn and unwilling to ease up on test format.

McDonald is the worst professor that I have ever had.  He isn't engaging at all and goes off on random tangents in the middle of lecture.  Make sure to pay attention in class because the study guide has nothing to do with the test.

lemme start this by saying that dr. mcdonald is for the girls and the gays who went through a percy jackson phase in middle school and never left

11/10 loved the class content and format (lectures, mc exams, that's it)

I took this class as one of my first semesters at Mizzou. He was a pretty fair teacher and knows a lot about the subject. Beware: the class sizes are very large and so grades wont be done over night or sometimes even within a week.

John is the rare professor who will make you want to better yourself in a class. He cares about all his students and wants everyone to succeed, but you do have to show that you want to succeed. He, without fail, will help students whenever they need it and helped me grow as a Greek student. No day was dull, but all were beneficial for us students!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. McDonald is one of the best professors someone can have. I was struggling a bit in class and he approached me to help my Greek. Ive had him for three classes now and Im thoroughly excited for the fourth. Hes a nerd that loves to have fun with his students and knows everything!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a very understanding man and only wants to see you succeed. He challenges you in order to better yourself because he knows you can do the work. Also, he wants you to use your brain and become an intelligent human being! He seriously is one of the sweetest and most understanding professors in our department.

McDonald is one of the best professors I've had at Mizzou. He does make the class tough (A lot of homework) but I'm better at Greek and a better classics student for having him. Not an easy A by any means but he knows his stuff, cares about his students, and will do his best to help you however he can.

After studying abroad in Greece with Dr. McDonald for AMS4100 I can say wholeheartedly he has been one of the best professors I have had the pleasure of studying under in my time at Mizzou. He is always willing to talk with his students and productively with them to insure they are both learning and thoroughly enjoying the course curricula.

I studied abroad in Greece, and John McDonald was the faculty leader. He is so knowledgable, but also kept the trip light and fun, which our entire group appreciated. He was extremely caring and positive, and you could tell that he genuinely loves his job and students. I would definitely recommend going on a study abroad trip with him!

Luckily I had the great opprotunity to study abroad in Greece. I got even Luckier to have John as my professor on this trip. He is a great person and very respectable of his students. I learned so some much about ancient Greece and had a lot of fun along the way. If you have the opprotunity to take this class do it, especially if John is leading!

One of the most impactful and invaluable teachers in my 5 yrs at Mizzou: John makes learning fun by explaining why topics are interesting + relevant/important, and teaches you HOW to learn ANY material effectively. He has an inspiring positive attitude and is extremely patient and accommodating. He is well spoken and clear on all class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Always ready to answer any questions you have, meet with you after class, very understanding. You can come to him with any issue and he's ready to help. His classes largely focus on discussion so be prepared to talk and share what you know. Make sure to actually do the readings and def prepare what he tells you to ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: John was always available to meet outside of class if the material was getting a little difficult. His lectures were engaging and full of group discussion. The format of the class allowed me to see the material from multiple points of view, both from classmates and from John. If you read what's assigned you'll learn a lot and have a ton of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: John McDonald has been one of my favorite professors at Mizzou. As a professor, he cares for his students which is seen after class when he takes the time to answer anyones questions or to clarify something from the lesson plan. The readings he assigned were interesting and he explained in great detail what each one was about. Great class to take!!

I have never met a professor who is so caring towards his students! There was never a moment that he would not stop class to explain the complicated language that is Ancient Greek!! Dr. McDonald was always available outside of class and worked enormous hours to ensure that his students felt appreciated and were given the proper tools to succeed!!

Prof. McDonald is a GREAT teacher. He's fun and optimistic, and gives very consistent feedback. As long as you do the work and participate, you'll be totally fine. He clearly cares about his students and tries very hard to make the class worthwhile and engaging for us.

We get it John, you know big words. You can put the thesaurus away now. If you want a teacher who will literally ramble to the point where you have no idea what is going on, take John's class! His tests require too much information for the time allotted (almost half the class didn't finish in 1 hour for the midterm) and there's so much reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: He knows the subject, but he likes to ask questions in such a way that no matter what you say, hell say youre wrong to try to prove a point.

John knows the subject. However, he makes his tests too long for the fifty minutes allotted, especially for students who have only started learning Latin a few months prior. This is labeled as a Beginner's Latin course, but make no mistake, you'll be ready for Latin III by the time you are done.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is very simple and you work in groups to film and create fun projects. Melissa was helpful and gave advice on what to do. There isn't much quizzes or stressful assignments but you don't always have the most time doing projects in class but you can edit in your own time. The best part is that, Melissa gives room spaces to do our projects!

Amazing Professor, Couldn't recommend her more she's super caring and super real. Be honest and respectful and she will be lenient and respectful back. She has the experience to teach you so If you're interested in this pathway I would definitely pay attention.

I took this class more for fun, not thinking it would be as heavy as it was. Professor Jolly is a good lecturer who does well to cultivate a nice, chill environment for the class. I wasn't huge on how the class was structured, but she doesn't have much control over that.

I loved this class! Melissa clearly cares about her students and is very engaging. She is happy to help when you have questions and genuinely wants her students to succeed. I learned so much from her and would 100% take one of her classes again! There is a decent amount of editing work outside class but that is to be expected in this subject area.

Jolly is very kind and knowledgeable with a lot of first hand experience in film making and especially editing. She does approach class with a production emphasis so if you're in another focus that's something to keep in mind, but I really enjoyed it. She is a benevolent grader and always has good feedback and suggestions. Really fun class.

Melissa is great and clearly loves what she does. She can be a little hard to contact as she works on film projects outside of teaching, but she tries her best to get back to you. Her grading is very simple and is based on the effort put in, not on the end project.

Jordan Thomas clearly cares about the material and wants students to learn it. He offers a lot of extra credit opportunities and explains material in a way that is thorough and easy to understand. Tests and quizzes are slightly challenging, but fair.

For repro phys the lecture grades are 3 non-comprehensive exams and 6 quizzes. You get one dropped quiz and he averages the rest of the quizes. There are two lab practical exams, 5 reading, and 5 dissucsion assignments. There is an extra credit book worth 25pts and the class is only 500pts. He also gives plenty other extra credit options.

One of my favorite professors at Mizzou. Would highly recommend him as a professor and the classes he teaches. Grading can take a while and don't always get feedback but if you ask you can get feedback. Accommodating when things come up, fun class, and I have memories from this class I will never forget. No textbook required!

One of the best professors, very caring and always hilarious. Dr. Thomas is always willing to talk through topics and work with students to improve their grades. He is one of the sweetest people out there and an amazing human being. Highly recommend taking one of his classes.

You'll read about six books over the course of the semester. No finals, no big tests, you're only graded by a single presentation + a weekly quiz. Professor Wigger gives very interesting lectures, everything from baseball and drunken riots to airplane hijackings. As long as you read the books and take notes at lectures you'll get an A.

As long as you read the books and pay attention to what you are reading you will do fine. The class has weekly quizzes on the weeks reading and lectures they are not difficult if you pay attention. Lecture slides are posted so review them before the quiz and you should do great. He doesn't lecture on traditional history topics which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There is no textbook, but the entire course consists of reading 5 or 6 different nonfiction books and taking quizzes on them every week. Attendance isn't required, but if you don't look over the lecture slides or go to class then some of the quiz questions will be hard to answer. You also need to present once in this discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hit or miss on whether you'll like the style of the class, not a good fit for me. Reading is 6 books throughout the semester with weekly reading between 100-200 pages, followed by a comprehension quiz on reading and lectures in your discussion group class. Not much connections between books and lectures. Good if you want less known US Hist topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting. NOT your typical boring history class. LOTS of reading tho, like 42 chapters of a book in a week. i do recommend u atleast have a general detailed description of book majority of quiz questions come from the reading, and quizzes are your ONLY thing put in the grade book for the class. This class is good for history haters
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very much down to earth and in these classes of around 30, he isn't afraid to answer any and all questions. There are no exams or finals, the only assignments are 5 question open response/multiple choice weekly quizzes and an easy newspaper assignment. He is very understanding and is a great storyteller. You will have to read a good amount.

This class has been very easy and simple. He is a very solid lecturer; although he isn't very engaging at times he moves at a perfect pace and manages his content well. My only criticism is that this really isn't a general History class. He has a specific perspective that he uses this class to subtly but persistently promote.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, 6 books for the semester. Only grades were weekly quizzes over the books + lecture and participation points in discussion. Keep up with the readings and it's and easy A. Wigger is a great lecturer and always makes it interesting. Class content is also really cool and insightful.

No exams in this class, but for discussions you have to read around 6 books for the semester. Books and quizzes aren't hard, but if you don't read you probably won't do great. The quizzes are like 5-10 questions depending on your TA but he is a chill professor and makes it clear in the beginning of the year what is expected to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: super chill dude
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Too much reading. I did not have the time to read 150 pages of a novel every week and my grade suffered as a result. Wigger seems interested in history and a nice guy I just don't like reading. The lectures also don't mean a whole lot because there are no exams. If you don't like reading, do a different class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wigger is the best, I took him my very first semester of freshman year and now, going into my junior year, I still talk about stuff I learned from his lectures. The discussion section is reading heavy, but the TAs are awesome and the reading is always engaging. Just participate and take notes and you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor, just blows through his lecture slides way too quickly when students are trying to write everything down. The discussion part is veryyy reading heavy and will take up a lot of your time. If you get Thomas Stacy as your TA for discussion, good luck, he is a tough grader and not a good TA at all.

Take him if you can get him for History 1200. My friends had endless quizzes and tests from their profs, and somehow I learned more from him with no exams and an easy weekly reading quiz. He contextualizes race incredibly well and is super engaging. The only readings are awesome novels. Show up to lecture, read the books and you'll pass easily!
Reading heavy, but most of the books picked were interesting.

Professor Wigger is seriously one of the best history teachers I've ever had. He makes lectures interesting and you learn about events that aren't typically taught in an American History class. You typically read a half a book a week but I thought the books were very interesting and connected to what we learn in lecture. Take HIST1200 with Wigger!!

You can tell that Dr. Wigger really cares about what he is teaching his students and you can also tell that he wants all of his students to do well. Dr. Wigger would find ways to make his lectures interesting and entertaining.
Dr. Wigger is an awesome lecturer, and all of his TAs are great. He legitimately made US history fun and engaging. There is a lot of reading for the discussion section, but it's definitely doable.

Professor Wigger is very caring and charismatic about History. His lectures were always interesting because they covered topics we don't normally cover in American History courses. Would recommend doing Honors so you can have him as your discussion leader as well (he grades nicer than the TAs).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: he's great but the discussion section isn't with him, it's with a TA. make sure to get a good TA because that makes all the difference. Dr. wigger is great though.

One of the most interesting classes i've ever taken. Professor Wigger manages to keep you engaged throughout the lecture & makes the course engaging. You usually read half a book a week, and then take a quiz over the lecture & book every Friday. Only grades are weekly quizes & weekly assignment where you write about a newspaper article you found.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Wigger is amazing! Fun lectures that he's genuinely passionate about. No textbook, but you do have to read some books throughout the semester. I was nervous, but the books were interesting. Only graded on participation and 5-point weekly quizzes in the discussion section, with an optional final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wigger is great! The class is set up much differently than any other history course. If theres any advice I can give, it's to READ the books. If you're like me and don't want to read, READ!!! Dr. Wigger is a freak for planes, and he loves chatting about oil too. Make sure you have a good TA too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wears the same two fits Eddie Baur black and khaki pants and a black shirt  hes fantastic!!! This class was sweet and hes lowkey funny

In history 1000, rather than reading from a textbook and memorizing dates, Dr. Wigger sets up the class in a style that’s awesome! You will read six books, they are all very well written, and bring a different outlook on history that you didn’t know you could explore. Great class! I would take it again if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Dr Wigger! Super passionate about history and managed to make each topic interesting. Any quizzes we had were in our discussion sections and based off the 6 novels we read as well as the week's lectures, but the books were all good for the most part and the quizzes are easy as long as you read and pay attention. Would definitely recommend!

Great professor, easy class. You read 6 novels so there's a lot of reading (100-150ish pages a week), but there's no writing or other projects. Weekly quizzes are super easy, keep up with the reading, go to lecture and you will easily pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class has two lectures a week and one discussion section where you take a quiz over the lectures and the book for that week. You read half a book a week which equals out to 6 books a semester. The final is optional. The only grades in this class are the quizzes and participation. You cant miss discussions that is where all of your points are.

This is a great history class if you're tired of learning from a textbook. The books chosen were really interesting and easy to keep up with if you pace yourself well. It's also a really easy honors credit course. Quiz every week over lecture and book material, not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I usually think history is boring, but I loved taking it with Dr. Wigger! You can tell how passionate he is about the subject. The only downside was that we had to read 5 novels, but they were actually good reads for being about history. As long as you go to lecture, take notes, and keep up with the reading, it should be a breeze.

Gives "pop quizzes" every week with questions from assigned reading, but also wanted students to be able to identify different types of airplanes via photo (unless you know a lot about planes, good luck). Really nice guy and was considerate towards students, some quiz questions were just not realistic for those without prior plane knowledge.

Wigger has a lot of really interesting stories about flight. Took this as my capstone and I do not regret it at all! We had so much freedom on assignments and the course load was very light. I would recommend this option to anyone! I never knew flight could be so interesting and fun. It was a nice break between my heavier classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wigger taught an amazing class. I initially thought history 1200 was going to be the hardest thing ever, but it wasn't. I would say if you know you're not going to read the books, don't take this class. There are reading quizzes every week in discussion over what you've read during the week and it counts towards you grade. & go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wigger is such a great professor, and he's funny too. He's passionate about history and you learn a lot from him. The only downside about the course is that you read a lot of books, but it's not too bad. As long as you attend lectures and keep up with the readings, you should do fine.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at Mizzou. Prof Wigger is an ex-pilot, making him an incredible story teller for the History of Flight class. He brought in incredible guest speakers and talked about wild airplane stories and conspiracies. He gives weekly reading quizzes which are easy if you go to class and at min google the chapter summary
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was beyond boring and although Dr. Wigger is a nice guy, he was monotone which made class even worse. There was only a midterm and a final and a couple quizzes in the discussion class. There were 7 assigned books you had to read and then you had to write a 6 page paper over one of the books. Both exams were short answer and essay based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Wigger is an excellent professor.  Although the lectures can be long, they are very straight forward, similar to the exams.  The specific class that I took of his, HIST1100, relied heavily on your assigned TA.  If you attend these discussion classes once a week, there is no reason why you shouldn't earn an A.  Great class; great professor.
Wigger is really nice and his class isn't too hard. Attendance is recommended but not particularly needed. Tests aren't too bad but his lectures can get long sometimes if he gets off topic.
Great professor. Very enthusiastic and makes lectures interesting. Reading the books is mandatory to do well and exams are written, but it is not too bad. Great class

Wigger is super nice! He is very enthusiatic about history and it makes for a fun lecture. There is a discussion every week. Your TA literally makes or breaks you. Mine was really cool but a tough grader, so I won't get as good of a grade as my friends. The books you read are really interesting and relevant - he doesn't believe in textbooks.
Professor Wigger is a really great person and professor.

John was a great professor! Notes were very clear & well organized. A lot of reading is required for this course & you take pop quizzes in your discussion group. Your TA means everything in this class. Mine was a hard grader, but my friends had TA's who weren't as tough & got better grades. Don't take this class if you don't like essay based tests

Loved this class! If you attended lecture, skimmed the novels assigned to read, and attended discussion it's an easy A. Keeps his lectures interesting & the tests are very fair! One of my favorite professors.

Best professor I've had yet, he is super helpful, ask any related question in class and he will answer it. I went to his office hours just to get suggestions on history classes I should take in the future and he was genuinely interested in helping me. Take his class for sure
Favorite teacher. Nice and charming man. Funny and interesting class.

Professor Wigger is a very sweet man. He knows a lot about the subject and presents the info clearly and concisely. However, your grade in this class largely depends on your TA who grades all your work. Talk to them and make sure you know what they're specifically looking for. The midterm & final are the only exams and they are both essay-based.
Really nice guy
Wigger is a good professor. Moves quickly in lecture but is clear with what he presents. Make sure you get to know your TA well and ask for their help!

If you don't do well on tests with all written answers don't take this course. It only takes one bad exam or paper to mess up your grade for the entire semester. Also the course moves very quickly, so don't get behind at all.

Professor Wigger is the nicest man ever! He is very soft spoken but very dedicated to seeing his students succeed. He is a great man with a lot of interest in his subject. The tests are very easy to prepare for, he gives you a study guide with every possible question on it! And there's only the mid-term and final. I highly recommend this class!

Class is large lecture; doesn't take attendance but you need to be there because lots of notes are taken and his tests are from the notes. No textbook but expected to read 4 or so books only mildly related to the subject of lecture. Discussion classes once a week- quizzes on books each week as well. Easy-ish; Wigger's notes are key.

Sweetest man ever! Lectures are clear and to the point, and his midterm and final are very easy to prepare for and do well on. The readings correspond well with lecture. I would highly recommend taking the honors section if possible, it's great. Prof Wigger is seriously the cutest little man and he really loves the subject. Definitely recommend him

I really enjoyed Prof. Wigger's class.  He's very nice and makes US history simple and easy to understand. The midterm and final are easy if you study (he gives you all the possible questions). Definitely recommend him!

Dr. Wigger wasn't the most fun professor, but it was as painless as a history class could be. Gave notes in lecture form (they were always crystal clear, too) and then there were two exams (a midterm and a final) and one paper. The exams were all essay, but he gives you all of the questions beforehand on a study guide. Not a difficult class!
pretty much what you'd invision as the typical college professor; nice guy with a passion for history that is practical and willinging to help if you go see him during office hours
good
He is awesome!  He is a nice man and very helpful.  I personally think history is really boring and he made it as interesting as possible.
He's really very knowledgeable on the subject matter and is very helpful.
He is amazing!
No Comments

If you've had American History before, this class should be easy. I went to less than 5 lectures and still got an A. Just go to the discussion setions and go to the lecture on the day he passes out study guides.
Very intelligent on the material, presents information pretty well, tests are a little difficult but the study guide has all the info.
No Comments
The class was at 8am and he talks in a monotone, which makes it very hard to stay interested in what he has to say.  Very BORING!
I took his honors class.  It was a really easy A and interesting too.

He makes the class very easy to get a good grade in, providing plenty of review before tests and homework problems that are nearly identical to test questions. I typically don't enjoy math classes much, but he makes the class as easy as possible for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Miller is one of the most chill professors I've had, I really struggled with the material but he would always patiently answer my questions after class and during office hours. if you show that you care about the class he will help out how he can. Would definitely take one his classes again.

Hilariously bad handwriting but otherwise he was fine. The way he explained the concepts seemed a little heterodox at times and I could see how it might be confusing to some. Probably among the easiest math courses Mizzou has to offer overall, though.
Taught the material well, was helpful and responsive in Emails. Should be the standard for professors, but sadly isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For a basic college algebra class, he explained it worse than any of my high school teachers ever did. Tried to make material easy to learn, but instead, ended up over-explaining + complicating the subject. However, he is very nice and all of the homework, quizzes, and tests are easy. Clearly said what was on each test so you knew what to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He looks like Peter griffin from family guy. He's more interested in telling you why it works vs how to do it. Has the worst handwriting for a teacher that I've ever seen. Be ready to teach yourself everything.
super clear with his expectations and prepares you well for tests and quizzes. very fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Professor Miller is a great teacher, he grades fairly and his exams are similar to the homework and lectures. I've gone to a few office hours and he is always available for questions. If you pay attention in the lectures you will do fine.

Also, he's pretty handsome. I'd give a few chili peppers if I could.

Calc 3 isn't necessarily an easy course, but Miller does a great job making it as easy and simple as possible. Useful lecture videos, always available for meeting, great feedback, and always cared about his students. Exams were similar to the practice exams, and it was made clear what to expect. He often used problems we had already seen in lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Justin Miller is one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are clear and concise, and he genuinely cares for your learning. Quizzes and tests are fair, and he doesn't throw curveballs at you like other professors. He makes sure all your questions are answered and wants you to understand the content.
Made learning calc easy and fun

Very Good Professor. Didn't grade exams harshly and gave a lot of partial credit. Made good use of lecture times and expressed content in a manner so every student could try to understand. Would recommend taking his coarse again.

Lectures are clear, organized. Do not miss class or be late -- critical practice examples at the start of class. Doing homework is CRUCIAL too. He is also a nice grader and a nice person. Once I got partial credit even though I didn't know what I was doing. You get points as long as you write something down. He is also accessible outside of class.

I took Calc 3 online this semester and he made it easier online than most online teachers I've had in the past. His office hours were based off of our requests, his lectures were easy to follow, he is a fast replier, and is always posting announcements with resources and advice on how we can improve our grade.

Despite failing this class (it was my fault I stopped going to lectures) he is genuinely one of the best math professors I've had! He clearly breaks down concept and examples, gives as much partial credit as possible on quizzes on exams, and is always prompting for questions. I hope to get him when I retake it.

I took Calculus 3 online (a complete mistake) and didn't commit enough to it to earn the grade I should have. I struggled due to a lack of commitment, but Professor Miller's lecture videos were straightforward, and he was enthusiastic about helping during office hours or scheduling a time. Wish I had him in person instead, amazing guy.

Did I cry almost weekly about this class and deeply wish a campus shuttle would hit me on my way to it? Yes. However, she is a great professor that is knowledgeable and passionate about Cuba and Spanish, and you will come out with an appreciation for it. She can be rude and off putting at times though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: After reading these reviews I was terrified to take her class. Although some of these comments are valid, I don't believe they are all true. YES she is strict and CAN be rude, but she is also extremely passionate about what she is teaching and she is extremely smart. Do the readings and you will be fine.

I took her this past semester and was really scared because of past reviews. However, the class was just watching her documentaries (which have English subtitles), reading poems, and talking about discrimination in Cuba. She was so kind and quick to laugh, which I was not expecting because of reviews. Mini presentations and short essays.

I see a lot of negative reviews here, but I have a Spanish minor from Mizzou and this was the most informative Spanish class I have taken. She IS pretty intimidating at first, but she really cares about her students and you WILL get better at Spanish in this class. She is a really easy grader if you turn in the work. Don't be intimidated!
Does not keep you updated on your grade. Is harsh with you if you don't interpret a reading the way she wants you to. Just generally rude to students.

Expects you to read & interpret the stories more in-depth than any English lit class I have taken. Even if you read, she expects you to remember every little detail and will call you out if you can't. She also totally plays favorites with students when it comes to grading. Ended semester 2 weeks early & added 3 night classes. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is demeaning and harsh. This class will make you want to cry often times while you are sitting there. It is extremely hard and makes you almost worse at Spanish, the readings are for Lit majors. She is one of the most intelligent people that you will ever meet though, I just would recommend taking her class when you have an easy semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her class ruined my life. 80 page readings expected to be done in a day with total comprehension. This professor will make you lose sleep. Do not take any class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Cordones-Cook is the most knowledgable professor I have ever had. Her course is very rough but you will learn more about the language with her than you will with anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I was in her Lit 1 and it wasn't that bad but Lit 2 is a whole different story.  The 1st half focuses on plays which was not too difficult but half way through we transitioned into poetry which was a nightmare.  She loves poetry but didn't realize that it was really difficult for us.  Half of the time we were all lost and she didn't notice.

Professor Cordones-Cook is one of the most academic professors here. She is very valuable to her profession and takes what she teaches very seriously. She expects students to have a flawless knowledge of Spanish, i.e. no grammar or speaking problems. Class is interesting but very, very difficult.  If your speech and writing is not perfect, beware.

Dr. Panchanathan's anthropology course was extremely educational and engaging. He gives hilarious and consistently interesting lectures, and assignments are mentioned well in advance. If possible, please take a course with Dr. Panchanathan!
I absolutely loved this professor! He made the class very interesting, and everything he talked about was on the exam, no surprises!

Professor Panchanathan's anthropology course was an excellent view into other cultures that allowed me to see beyond what I thought was normal. He also gave fantastic lectures that drew me in and excited my desire to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are fun and entertaining but his tests are difficult but it's manageable if you study enough or manage to create a study group to nail the tests. If you are falling behind, Karthik offers extra credit for his students. It's not an easy A but his lectures and the pacing makes up for it! He also listens to our concerns and feedback!

He is a great professor who clearly cares about what he does. Offers a lot of extra credit. The classes are fun to attend despite being a lecture hall. His exams and book reports can be challenging, but if you put in enough effort, an A is easy to get.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and person! But this class is NOT AN EASY A!! The exams are the hardest tests I've ever taken. But he offers a lot of support and extra credit. He is a great professor, but this class itself is just insanely hard. If you just need a humanities credit and don't have an interest in anthropology, another class would be better.
He is actually so approachable and reasonable. Lots of opportunities for extra credit.

Dr. Panchanathan is a great lecturer. He makes the lectures seem fun and engaging, even though this is a lecture hall class. There isn't a textbook, but you'll need two books for two different book reports.
Exams aren't too difficult if you do a bit of studying before the exam. Readings are short and interesting. Class is fun to attend.
Great teacher. Actually engages with class and is very funny. Class was enjoyable, a little bit hard but nothing crazy. Tests are mainly study guides but they are mostly short answer questions.

He's definitely passionate about what he teaches, but the exams are so difficult. I've never studied so hard for an exam just to hope and pray to pass. Definitely not a class you should have to be doing allat for but whatever. Exam grades are curved though which is nice. Just beware of the exams and lots of content. Good class structure though.

I took Anthro 2030 because a friend of mine loved the class and the teacher. Dr. Panchanathan is fun, kind, encouraging, and wants his students to succeed. Honestly as long as you show up to class and take notes you'll do well. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities so take advantage of those.
He was amazing!

He is so funny and interesting to learn from. He makes the material more digestible with fun stories or videos. It's pretty lecture-heavy, but he tries to make it fun and entertaining, and we also watch quite a few movies throughout. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, going to class provides so much additional info, plus extra credit.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class. Karthik is very engaging and I loved attending his lectures. This was my first experience with anthropology and I am considering adding it as a minor now. I will say that a majority of the grade is based on tests so if you aren't a good test taker you might struggle. The rest comes from essays and a project.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My goat. He genuinely cares about the content, which shows in his lectures. Just stay on top of the essays, even if he does push back the deadline (which happened both times), and you'll be fine.

His lectures are good, he is a very interested person and you can tell he knows his field very good. Everything in class is posted online. Personally, I found the tests were pretty difficult. All outside assignments were pretty easy. There is 20 points extra credit or so in the class and exams are usually curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Just a great guy. Cares about his students no matter how difficult the coursework is. Plenty of opportunities for points and extra credit. Encourages participation and always goes in depth about every topic covered.

Karthik is my favorite professor at Mizzou after taking his class. Lectures were extremely engaging. Course materials were extremely comprehensive, and no textbook was required. If you put in effort you will do well and enjoy the class. One project was pretty useless and time consuming (costed ten bucks too!), but he got rid of that.

Great professor and class. Attendance is not required, and he posts all the necessary information in the lecture notes, but the class is still worth going to because he's a good lecturer! He really seems to care about his students, even in a bigger class where things can feel anonymous sometimes. Tests were also very straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Anthropology 2030, which had very interesting content. Karthik frequently got off track from lecture notes from student questions, which sometimes meant we couldn't finish the scheduled content. Tests are difficult with both short/long answer and multiple choice.

Really interesting class that I enjoyed more then expected. He's a super cool guy that really knows what he is talking about and has actual passion for his job. The tests make up 60% of the grade so you have to study hard for those but other then that its a really great class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just take his classes, incredibly intelligent and personable, probably my favorite professor at Mizzou. His lectures are actually engaging and fascinating, he uploads all notes too in case you're sick, but really worth going to class just to learn from the guy.

Dr Panchanathan is very kind and wants all his students to understand and feel comfortable discussing the material. Attendance is not required and he posts all of his notes so you really don't have to go to class if you don't want, but he makes it a great experience!
There are 2 book reports and you watch a lot of movies in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It was obvious that he truly cares about his students. Lectures were long but interesting for the most part. If you don't want to put in the extra work, show up for the lectures and take notes. But if you don't, he posts his lecture notes and bolds the key details that show up in the exams. Study those and do the weekly readings and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: amazing guy. super funny and lectures are very interesting! was not excited for the class when signing up but it is my favorite class by far! make sure to read the readings and pay attention to the films becuase there will be questions on the tests. book reports arent hard, community project was interesting and 3 tests that are writing intensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Karthik was awesome and his class was so interesting! He had 3 exams and two papers. One project took less than an hour. You have got to study for your exams but there are plenty of quizlets online. I really recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Test heavy

reviews.comment: GO TO CLASS! Its not mandatory but you get SO much more out of the class. I thought it would be boring but the content was super interesting. Karthiks lectures go way above and beyond his lecture notes (which are posted on Canvas if you skip). Tests are not easy but if you went to class or read the notes/slides on Canvas youll be okay.

Take this class. I learned something new every time I stepped foot in his class. The lectures are incredible and he puts both the slides and his notes on Canvas if you can't make it but you should attend every class just because his lectures are so great. He is charming and funny and you will enjoy learning his material.
Such a great professor that's incredibly passionate about Anthropology. Great lectures that make you want to attend class. Not an easy class, but an enjoyable one for sure.
Hes legit so funny and his lectures are great

I really liked this class and the professor. Beware though, if you don't go to class and rely solely on the slides you will not do well. They don't give you the info you need. The class discussion helps the most. The tests are mostly essays and application of knowledge (from the class discussion). No homework, just reading and 3 projects/papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Panchanthan is super nice and knowledgable about his subject. There isn't homework, but there are required readings that can take some time. The tests involve quite a bit of writing and can be a little bit tough. There are two book reports, but they are not long.

A very kind professor who actually cares about his students. His lectures were always very fun and engaging, and he does his best to relate them to modern-day and pop culture. Three tests, two book reports, and one project, but those are the only assignments.

Great teacher, the lectures were really engaging and you get to watch 6 movies throughout the semester which is pretty fun. Papers are difficult but not impossible; be prepared to study for the exams. My advice for this class would be don't skip class because you will get behind.

Dr. Panchanathan was easily one of my favorite professors during my time in undergrad. His classes were always very discussion based but it never felt forced. Lectures were often very insightful and tests never threw any curveballs. I could tell he really wanted all of us to learn and get something out of his course.

Make sure to do all of the readings before class. You don't have to take notes, but he won't let you BS your way to grades. Make sure to have good discussion questions to turn into Canvas; they're a decent part of your grade. He is very good at giving feedback, so make sure to take into account what he says over the semester about the 15 pg project
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have 2 book reviews, outside project and 3 exams. Each exam is 20 percent of your grade and its all short answer exams with maybe 10 multiple choice. I don't recommend this class unless you are extremely passionate about Anthro.

I like to consider myself a good student. I pay attention, do the homework, etc. This i the first class I have ever really struggled in. The tests are almost all short answer and he tests on very specific content. I feel that I am tested on irrelevant details rather than broader ideas. If you aren't an anthropology major, don't take this class.

This guy is very smart and interesting, but the entire class he really seemed like he did not want to be there. It's not fun from learning from someone who has no interest in teaching the class. Tests are thorough but graded by the TA so not as difficult to do well. Essays graded pretty harshly. Have to do a weird outside-university online project.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is easy if you study for the essay oriented tests, take advantage of all the extra credit being offered, and write good essays. There's a ton of extra credit opportunity throughout the semester for the easiest tasks. The lectures were always interesting and both Karthik and the TA were extremely helpful and accessible throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Panchanathan is one of my favorite profs I have had at mizzou. He is extremely knowledgeable and his lectures are engaging. You don't really have to go to class, since he posts his power points and notes online, but if you do go he often gives extra credit. The tests are a tough format, but if you know the material you'll be fine.

Such interesting lectures and the way his lectures are set up are unlike any other professor Ive had. Keeps you engaged and interested at all times. Loved this class and he is extremely knowledgeable on the subject!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great guy, lectures are helpful but not mandatory as he posts all notes online. "Pop quizzes" are announced at the end of class to be completed online so you don't actually have to go to do them. Test are strange format but easy to study for after you have the first one.

Dr. Panchanathan is the quintessential college professor. He is one of the smartest people I have ever encountered, period. Knows his stuff and can convey aspects of anthropology to the class in a manner that an average student can understand. The course is perfectly outlined in the syllabus and the lectures are engaging and chock full of knowledge

Karthik is a great professor. His lectures were engaging and interesting. The readings we did in the textbook went along well with his lectures in class. You have to study quite a bit in order to do well on the exams, but it is nothing too unbearable. I loved him and I loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Karthik is one of the coolest professor's I've had.
