By far one of the worst classes I've ever taken in my life. While he is a really nice person, I can't say the same as a teacher. He assigns long, tedious, and useless work for pretty much all days of the week. His IClicker polls during class take forever and his video lessons are long and boring, am not a fan of the flipped classroom style.
He doesn't stop talking and assigns a ridiculous amount of useless time filling assignments

Really nice and funny guy. But there is just so much tedious work in this class. It gets very repetitive and old really fast. Usually at least two video lectures each week that are about 30 mins long, and then the same info get repeated in the actual lecture. Tries to continue teaching as the time in class is over.

Super nice and understanding guy but the class is repetitive and boring. The video lessons are long and the info is just repeated in class again. All he talks about is his neurodivergence. There is also assigned seating! The projects are long and \career oriented which as an underclassman doesn't really apply. I switched my major after this class.

I'm not going to go into too much detail, but just don't take this guy if you want to have unnecessary assignments every day, assigned seating in a lecture hall, and get kept late after class by up to ten minutes to hear his preachy rants on politics.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was easy, but VERY lecture heavy and repetitive. You have to do online lessons before every class, and the class itself just repeats the online lecture. There is iClicker every class, assigned seating, and a lot of group work during class. Professor Klien was nice and very understanding, but his in-person lectures were hard to follow.

He is a funny guy who actually cares about students success. He offers so many extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. There are weekly video lessons to complete, and a midterm and final, which he actually gives you two chances to take, because he wants you to learn the material and succeed. Overall, great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Klien is a huge nerd, but it is clear he cares a lot about what he teaches. Just show up and do your work on time and you're totally fine. The best thing about his class is that you get to take tests twice and they are open-note. So I wasn't trying to spit out information I heard, I was actually absorbing information and applying that.
Would not recommend this instructor to any student.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Klien is a funny man. The class is super easy, and he gives lots of extra credit/ is never strict on his agenda. He always pushes stuff back and eventually we will get around to it. There are video lessons to complete each week for points as well, but they are not bad. There is just an online midterm and a final so not exam heavy

I've taken professor Klien before for COMM 2500 and both times I really enjoyed his online classes. There are weekly assignments, but as long as you keep up with them, you won't have any issues. He does a great job of organizing everything and making criteria crystal clear. Also very responsive! Overall really great prof and would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Klein was an awesome prof for public speaking! He's very enthusiastic, which made the class less scary for me. His grading is fair, but you do have to put a lot of work into your speeches to do well. Attendance is also important. The class teaches skills that are beneficial for any major, so I highly suggest both the class and Dr. Klein.

Dr. Klein is a good professor -- very nice guy. However, he is a little unorganized. Lectures are interesting, but he lectures until the very last second of class, so schedule accordingly. The class isn't too difficult, but it requires a lot of work outside of class time. Good class for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: It's extremely obvious that Dr. Klein enjoys what he does, and he cares about us as students.  The issue is that he really makes you work in his class.  He gives more homework than all of my other classes combined. Requires almost 30 minutes of HW for an average class. Combined with a paper/speech due every month makes this entry level class p hard

Klein is an interesting character, takes a few lectures to get used to him. But, you'll learn he is really interested in his students doing well and working hard to do it. He allows a cheat sheet on exams, and is very clear about grades and wants to ensure each student knows what they need to do for a good grade. Funny guy, strong personality.

Klaric is a lazy, uncaring professor, which is a shame because it seems like he knows what he's talking about.  Slides are pull word for word from PSQL or PHP documentation offers further insight into concepts. And you can forget about him answering your emails.  I learned a lot, but it wasn't because of his teaching ability.

Klaric doesn't care at all about your grade or your opinion about your assignments. Fails you on labs for small mistakes. He will fail the entire class if necessary. For the group project, he doesn't care about your concerns of group members, one of my group members didn't do a single line of code and still received the same grade as me.
Dr. Klaric is awesome!
Expects you to learn how to do the labs on your own time and minor mistakes in the labs result in massive point deductions
Not helpful or understanding at all.

It is only a few days into the class but this man is single handling making me think to change my major. He tosses you into the deep end and expects you to be able to swim....you will not be able to. Good luck
Overall good teacher.
Meh.
He doesn't care much about his students' grades and isn't at all understanding if you have a conflict with a certain lab project.
Doesn't seem to care about students or want to help them
I think Dr. Kline is a great teacher, for her first year (and compared to other chem profs) she did great.  I went to most of the classes and utilized office hours,  great class!
She knows her stuff and is a good teacher. For her first year I think she did pretty well. The tests are directly from the notes. But the material can be difficult to grasp.

This was her first year as a professor so she was still obviously getting the hang of things. She's a nice person, but doesn't know how to teach yet. I didn't learn very much, and relied on my instincts from my AP Chem class, which made all of the difference. Very heavy in note-taking. I recommend going to her office hours; she's a lot better there

Dr. Kline is very straightforward. She is better than the other chemistry II professors. The infomation is very clear. It comes straight from the book. I like that she doesn't teach us random irrealvant fluff.

Usually have to teach yourself a little. She doesn't do much but fly through examples and notes without a really clear explanation. That being said, if you study a lot you can get an A. She curves so that an 85 is an A
she literally reads the text book to you during lecture
Test averages were 64, 70, and 57%. Instead of the text supplementing your lecture, the textbook is your lecture. Have fun!

She teaches and reads right out of the book. Lectures are very boring and not mandatory, so just stay home and watch tegrity. She doesn't communicate with the TA's very well, so they don't always know what is going on. Tests are relatively easy as long as you do the book problems.

Professor Kline's exams are easy compared to other chem professors. I would definitely recommend her for chem 1320. Others may not like that she teaches straight from the book, but I think it's the best, especially for a chem course.

She is very lackadaisical in her teaching and doesn't not provide much clarity with anything at all. She copies examples from the book onto the projector and thats about it. She is very nice, but unconfident. Read the book, use tegrity, and don't bother going to the lecture.
She is a horrible teacher. I never go to the lecture hall because it is honestly so hard to pay attention. She is not helpful at all, and it is way better to just learn it from the book.
Difficult class, better to learn from the book.

Katrina is a nice person, and pretty understanding if you actually go to her office hours and ask her to explain something. Her lack of confidence hinders her lecturing ability pretty dramatically. Be prepared to work very very hard for an A.

dr.kline just stands infront of the lecture hall and basically does what the book does, she doesn't clarify information at all. This is her first year what i have been told. you'll be better if you read the book and do hmk problems from there.

Dr. Kline knows her stuff but has no confidence in her teaching abilities whatsoever. She stands at the front of the auditorium & copies down the answers to the examples word for word without much explanation. Be prepared to put many many hours into your studying for an A! Read the book...it's just as good or better than her explanations.
"Dr." Kline is completely unhelpful. At the beginning of class, she always asks, "any questions?" but then when you ask she barks "Come to my office hours!!" It is ridiculous.
legitimately the best teacher ever, he cares about his students and gives them the best methods to succeed. Tries to make lectures as interesting as possible. Helps the student out whenever he can.
the best teacher i've had at mizzou, bro was a goat. if you can get him for any of your math classes i'd definitely recommend enrolling in his section.
bro was awesome fr

Mr. K has been by far my favorite professor at MU. The way he explains the material in his class is extremely easy to understand. He's the type of teacher who wants his students to succeed, and it doesn't go unnoticed at all. He gives amazing and useful tips for every quiz and exam. If your taking finite and you have him, YOU ARE IN LUCK!!!

japheth honestly is just ok. not great. not awful. he takes forever to grade stuff. there is only a midterm, a final, and a 5 page paper due for the whole semester and the only thing that really matters are the discussions bc he grades in attendance. he posts slides on canvas but basically just reads off of those. wouldnt rec. not a fast grader

He has been one of the worst TA I have ever had if you have a chance to switch from him please do, he takes forever to answer any emails and makes excuses about all the work he has to do. if I fail this course because of not knowing my grades in time I would honestly give him most of the credit.

Took this class as a general Ed and my TA Japheth was seriously frustrating. Hes 10/10 the WORST at putting in grades and he makes a LOT of excuses. I currently have NOT ONE grade in canvas. Its Dec 16th. Dont know what my grade is and grade cut offs are tomorrow at 5pm. I just emailed to see what it was. He said I had to wait till 5pm to know...

He never once put in a single grade and complained the entire semester that he didn't know how to work Canvas because it was "broken" when it works for everyone else. We didn't even know our grades until he emailed them to us in November. He also gives way too much info about topics which doesn't help at all when asking a question.
It's not that he's a tough professor, but he is so disorganized that it's hard to know what's coming next. Very frustrating--don't take him if you can help it.

Professor Knapp is so cool! He can be cynical, but its all good-natured. You get two big books at the beginning and he assigns short stories to read from them. Read, submit discussion points (nbd) and participate in class. Participation matters. Also, he showed us how to use Special Collections in the library which was helpful. 10/10

Great entry level class. Travis is a funny professor and doesn't hammer hard assignments on the students. With that being said, take the time to do the easy point assignments bc they can drop your grade a lot if you don't. Overall, he's a funny guy and the papers aren't overbearing. Use the writing center for any additional help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Loved Mr. Knapp! He understands that Eng 1000 is something we are required to take and makes the class as easy as possible. I only had 3 papers and a couple short writings, and he gives a lot of time to complete all assignments. He is also funny and makes class bearable, even when talking about an incredibly boring subject. Definitely recommend!

I'm a person that believes if you are in an entry level course, attend class, work your ass off to improve your writing, attend office hours, then you should be given some form of credit or at least guided as to where to go next.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Fair grader especially if you are someone like me who hates writing.  There were 3 main papers and for each one he had you turn in a rough draft, then peer review, then one-on-one with him review before finally turning it in.
Fantastic teacher!  He made great jokes during lecture that helped to keep all students interested.  His paper assignments were reasonable and useful for any students of any major.

Klein is the worst professor I've had at my time at Mizzou. I e-mailed her asking for assistance and requesting an appointment to meet with her for help bringing my grade up. She didn't respond for weeks. I spoke with her after the next exam and mentioned the e-mails, and she blamed me for my failure and basically told me to drop the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I loved Klein's personality! The class was tough, and sometimes things were too fast-paced and confusing. However, she will drop one or both of your tests and add the weight to the final exam, whichever way makes your grade the highest. The tests are really tough but the final was easy so I am able to drop the two exams and get an A.
Nice lady but I suggest taking econ 1014 with someone else.  Tests are worth 80% of your grade and they are HARD

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. Her lectures are incredibly hard to follow and they do nothing to prepare you for the exams. Midterms are only 33 questions so they're easy to fail. By the time the final came I had to teach myself everything because I leaned nothing from her. Also emailed her 4 different times and got a response once.
Only 2 tests and a final so If you do poorly on 1 or 2 if screws your grade over.

She teaches the class like she's talking to Econ majors. Her lecturers are incredible complex and boring and if you don't understand something little then the rest of her lecture will go over your head. Don't take unless you already have a solid econ background.

It's honestly the easiest class I have taken in my college career. Most of the bad reviews are from freshmen in non-stem majors. Read the book or ask her questions if you don't understand something. It's your own fault if you do poorly. If you understand graphs and the rhetoric associated with them you will get an A.

This teacher's very difficult to learn from. She doesn't post any study guide online and doesn't post any lecture notes online. In class she writes minimal things on the board, so in order to do well for the exams you need to go to class & be able to write quickly. She doesn't use the text book either. Tests are only based on her words in class.

Honestly, one of the worst professors I've ever encountered. I would urge anyone who is considering coming to Mizzou, don't, because you could have her, and thats not worth the price of tuition. Econ 1014

She seems like a good lecturer but not really.Even if I've gone to every class and studied,I still screwed up my second midterm.U must be very good in taking notes to nail this class. She speaks fast and expects you to take all notes down.And, she tests you on what she said. She does not write all the important points down for you. be prepared.

I don't know why others complained about 3229, but I thought the class was great. She made everything clear what was going to be on the exam but you must learn to take notes on your own, because she does not write EVERYTHING down. Just listen, and you should be fine. Exam mat'l are straight from notes!  She is very kind & funny. Recommended.

Sounds like the 1014 students got it easy. For 3229 she's terrible. You don't get to drop any tests and half of her notes on the document viewer are totally random. She actually posted a long terms list for test 2, which helped me study. Too bad none of the questions were on those topics.

An Econ teacher that speaks English! Hooray! I loved this class. She is funny and very nice. She told us the first week, "The tests come only from what comes straight out of my mouth." - And that's the truth. I understood everything really well, as long as I attended lecture, payed attention and took good notes. Great teacher!

Sandy Klein is a very good lecturer- she's engaging and funny. However, this class kind of sucked. The tests cover tons of material that she doesn't cover in class, and at the same time, the textbook and the lecture differ in significant topics if you're not careful. Sandy's good but the class could be organized better.
she is pretty easy, she doesnt seem like she knows the material, she just has the book memorized. the exam set up is nice because you can drop any or all of your exam scores if they hurt your grade
Sandy is the eteacher you want for micro-econ. She wants you to get a good grade!

I had her for Econ 1014 and loved her!  She was well organized and always gave good notes.  So I expected the same from her in Econ 3229.  Maybe this was the first time she taught it.  In the beginning she was organized, but later her notes got messy and it was difficult to keep up.  Concentrate on her notes when studying for the exam.
material was difficult; expectations were clearly defined; tests were moderately hard, have to study; good personality, lively teaching style
Crazy, but dismissed class 3 times
No Comments
Not helpful at all and very rude when it came to answering (or should I say NOT answering) questions. She usually had no idea how to explain anything.
The the lectures aren't bad, but the review sessions are a waste of time and the tests are unexpectingly hard compared to the material covered in lecture.

Taking econ with Sandy Klein was my second time taking it.  I have to say, she is DEFINITELY way better than my other prof. I think she is very clear in lecture, and her examples are very helpful.  The lab didn't really help with my learning, but then again I already knew the material when I went to lab. If you have to take 1014 be sure to get her.
The material she always went through in class in no way reflected what she was asking of us on any of the tests.

She's a pretty good teacher i ended up with a 78 in the class but econ is just naturally a terrible subject.  She is def the easiest out of all the other 1014 teachers...there really aren't any formulas and crap you have to mess with...Sharon Ryan's class however is diff...if you have to take the class take it with Klein
No Comments

Weird lady...tells weird stories, but has good examples for class concepts. Do not agree w/ many of her personal opinions, especially politics. Haha. I didn't think the tests were as hard as some of the other reviewers. Overall: easy class, and teacher is not terrible, but not wonderful.

She was pretty nice, but if I had it to do over again, I would have gone in for office hours at least once. Go to class, it's boring but it'll help. Plus she says you don't need to bother reading the book but I think it was helpful to my grade. Boring lady, but the class is do-able

I would have to say that Klein is an interesting teacher. Even thought the tests suck, and the questions are worded with a little confusion, your final grade is computed VERY fairly. So even if you fail your first 2 exams, if you get an A on the final, she drops the exams and you get an A.
I had a hard time even wanting to stay in school after taking this class. The lectures wernt that bad but the tests were nearly impossible....and no curve!

Tests were much harder than expected. But lectures weren't that bad because she is funny, but pretty random. I learned everything for this class in my lab. But I hear she is a more delightful teacher than Sharon Ryan ever will be.
I hated this class, lecture was alright but the tests were the hard part. the class just sucked

dr. klein makes econ. tolerable and it's something i actually dont mind getting up for. I have actually walked with her to her office and she was/is very helpful.i wish i could say all my teachers were as good at teaching and making it fun as she has done
No Comments
No Comments
"ffttt" the sound of that flavored water every morning
Sandy's a really funny person, but she is often scatter-brained and doesn't use class time wisely.  Be careful, her multiple choice tests are always worded in a tricky way. Overall, she's ok.
The grading system is great.  Ace the final and ace the class. No problem!
This is an easy class.  Professor Klein is humorous and good-natured; econ. 4, however, is a an extremely dull subject.  I think Professor Klein made it as enjoyable as it could be.
No Comments

Dr. Klein is a very funny lady.  That's how she keeps us interested.  Just be prepared for a lot of randomness.  Her occasional side tracks make going out of your way to have her as your prof. an essential.  Plus, I hear that Dr. Ryan sucks. Good Teacher!

Dr. Knapp is super laid back and a great guy. He is extremely knowledge about what he teaches. As long as you do the lab reports and what you discuss makes sense, he will grade you very fairly. I would highly recommend him!
Dr. Knapp is an awesome professor. He takes attendance and there are occasional pop quizzes so just show up and you can have an easy A. Tests are over almost exactly what was presented in class.
He's somewhat of a tough grader. I though it was incredibly easy and interesting but I ended up with a B (probably because of the final)

Interesting information, eye opening. Relaxed teacher, but no phones. Easy going, not tedious work, not much homework. Occasional reading assignments. Tests are not scantron, essays, multiple choice, truefalse, and short answer.

Professor Knapp knows a lot about forestry and natural resources. He has random quizzes so it is smart to show up for class. Not a lot of grades. Tests aren't too hard but you need to know basically everything from the notes. Overall good teacher
Sarah went way out of her way to help me follow My artistic vision. Tons of respect. She expected and rewarded hard work which in return encouraged me to push my ideas further than ever before.
Very good professor. Enjoyed using non-digital photography.  Willing to go out of her way to help students who want to do better.

Sarah's a great teacher if you want to be pushed to achieve something with your photography. Her standards are demanding but understandable. Don't take this class if photography is only your hobby. Her Beginning Photography class is for those who consider photography in a fine art sense.

Sarah is a somewhat demanding teacher with all her students. It's nothing to fear but some do. I really liked being pushed to achieve the best possible results from all my photography this semester. If you need help, she's more than willing to provide it, but you do have to at least ask. Fantastic class, enjoyed every minute.

She is a very enthusiastic teacher and knows what she is talking about. She gives a few extra credit opportunities, and if you're a good student, she'll pull some strings for you when it comes to additional extra credit opportunities. You have a reading response due each class but they are easy. She grades easy and engages the class. Loved her.
She is so confusing! Never updates the grade book! I have no idea what I am going to get in the class and we have no more class/final left.

One of the BEST teachers at Mizzou. Values your personal opinions on the readings and genuinely wants you to succeed. Participate in discussion and do the readings/assignments. She makes it enjoyable!

Knezevich is sweet and somewhat shy, but always interested in her students. She wants you to learn something and to do well. The work is not difficult, but takes some focus and some interest. This class is not exactly a challenge, but definitely an excellent prerequisite and a good freshman transition class.

Pretty easy class, just do the homework.  Gives you some breaks throughout the semester and watch a movie at the end.  Definitely take her English 1000 class if you get the opportunity.  She is there to pass you, not fail you.
Not bad for a required writing class. Expects a lot from you but spends a lot of time working with you too.

I think it's weird that he still tries to stay in touch with students when he is no longer at this school. MU is much better off without him. The directors we have now are better teachers and less moody. Dr. Knight also had a habit of staring at people, which is kind of creepy.
I thought that the drill was too easy this past year for a college marching band, and the whole thing was really disorganized.
http://www.columbiatribune.com/news/2010/jan/05/sorry-mu-trumpets-about-bands-mix-up/
If you want to be a part of the worst university marching band in the country, join his band. What a disgrace to the state of missouri.
A free class with a great conductor and teacher. He doesn't hate kansas as a state, just all of them as individuals!

Dr. Knight expects a lot out of you, but is great at telling you what he wants done and what exactly he expects. He is a very understanding professor who is willing to put academics in front of Marching Mizzou, which is very endearing.  He's an all around good guy and M2 is great!
Great teacher, very exciting
I love Dr. Knight. He always says the best quotable things!!! Especially when it comes to football teams!!
dr knight rocks
No Comments
woo hoo! Dr. Knight is rockin!
Never seen a better director, for marching or concert band. Wonderful personality, challenges students, loves his job.

Seems like a nice guy, this is his first year directing here and my first year marching. For his first year I think he did a good job, and I see him doing better with these kids in the future. I can tell he loves this job.
stumbo was a lot better

He is an ok director. Sometimes he is unclear on what is going on. He tries though. Overall, there are things he could improve on but for his first year as Marching Mizzou director he is doing well. He needs to think about his students when doing drill.
Expect to do a fair amount of work, but the time in class is fun. She gives great feedback on every assignment.

I just don't get why her rating is so low. She is very friendly, and by far the most honest professor I had when it comes to expectations over the assignments. The only problem I had with her was reaching her outside of class because for some reason she doesn't check her email at all. But even so, she gave me lots of career advice and support!

She was very clear about class expectations and always made sure we knew how to contact her for questions. Timely responses too! She is VERY big on participation, so not the best class if you're quiet. Just go to class and do the work and you'll get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 1200 is a discussion class and Donna is a good leader of discussions. Very easy class and she makes it pretty easy. Lots of feedback on everything.

Mert is the absolute best! Highly recommend his class for circuits 1. He's easy to reach outside of class and genuinely cares about his students. Do the HW, quizzes, and labs. Go to class, pay attention, and you will do great on the exams. The practice exams are very similar. Enjoy!

Dr. Korkali is a chiller. Biweekly open note quizzes and homeworks. TAs that ran the labs were knowledgeable and let you leave early, not a single lab ran the full 2 hours. Exams are a carbon copy of the pratice exams, with questions coming from the textbook. Do HW and textbook problems and you're chilling. Drops lowest of 3 exams.

Had his class after another professor got fired, and he picked up right where we left off. Very nice and willing to help you out, make sure to ask him if you have any questions about the course material!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: do homework, do practice exams, do labs, and you will get an A. He is very nice and explains things well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had her a couple years ago and since then she's become much more chill and will rearrange deadlines according to class needs, cancel quizzes if enough people show up, and give you insights into what she wants to see on written assignments. Overall, she's very insightful, just a bit scattered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Dropped this class so early on because she would assign hundred plus page readings on Tuesday due Thursday, She was really nice and had a lot of great things to say but lectures were unorganized and hard to follow and reading Moby D!ck over TWO CLASS PERIODS is bonkers!

Professor Konkle is smart but her lectures consisted of rambling which made it incredibly hard to pay attention. The books chosen for this course were decent but we had to read large amounts of text before coming to class. Every time I answered a question in class she shut it down and made me feel silly for even trying...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid if possible, lectures consist of her rambling for an hour about who knows what. Doesn't give clear reading schedule but gets mad when we don't get as far as she apparently wanted. Feedback is unhelpful & she is hard to access for a meeting to discuss said feedback since she hardly responds to emails (when she does, she is super condescending)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Assigns SO MUCH WORK! You need to be prepared to read an entire novel (that you have to buy) basically every week, and write at least 2000 words about it. The feedback she provides is basically useless, and she uses a snarky tone when addressing students in announcements. I unfortunately have to take another class with her this summer :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class was actually ENG 1000 but she does not usually teach it. She can come off as harsh but she really does just want the best for all of her students. attendance was not mandatory due to covid but she really appreciated when her students would show up.

A considerable number of repetitive lectures may adorn the class as a waste of time. Surprisingly, there is a plot twist: all the assignments are so basic that anyone could complete them in a couple of hours Dont let bad rates fool you, as I was Besides caring for her students, she's flexible with dates and will understand if you need more time

Konkle is a nice person, but all she does in class is lecture. The lectures are typically long winded and rambling, and any attempt at discussion is usually one sided and aimless. Most the grades are just from papers and her grading criteria is vague. However, she usually grades fairly and gives chances to revise papers.

You don't learn anything in this course. She just rambles for the whole class time, then gives you stuff to read and you write a response to it. There's no point in going to class except that she takes attendance. This should just be an online course. And she gave a 6 page paper due a week before finals, then our final was another 6 page paper.

One of the worst professors i've had. She seemed like a very nice woman, but could not focus on one subject. It was very hard to take notes because she would often jump back and forth from several unrelated subjects. When it came down to quizzes and papers, she provided study guides that made no sense. She didn't connect with students at all.
Konkle does like to stand up and lecture for the entirety of every class period, but you can tell she knows her stuff. If only she could complete the majority of her thoughts...

Avoid. Seriously. The lectures are hard to follow, extremely dry, and she repeats herself several times from week to week, using the same examples and writing the same things on the board. This is NOT an engaging or interesting course, and will likely cause hatred of several great American classics. Take something else if you can.

Maureen may have been one of the worst teachers I have ever had.  She didn't require attendance, and if you were there, you were allowed to have your phone and computer out. The only positive to Maureen is that if you did poorly on one of her assignments, she will let you re-do it for a better grade.  She isn't strict about due dates. Not the best.

She can't keep a structured lecture, is very unclear about expectations, and only grades for attendance and 3 assignments.I have learned next to nothing in this classroom other than she's annoyed with the stereotype of Indians being "doomed." Also- she's writing a novel and has no time for this class. Don't take her for an instructor she's a wreck.
Her class was fantastic, and although lectures were sometimes muddy and hard to pick through, I thoroughly enjoyed having her as a professor. She really knows her stuff, and she is really kind.

An easy grader and offered lots of extra credit. Gave detailed outlines before each exam, but the rest of the lectures were unfocused and difficult to follow. Not the typical attitude you expect in an English class -- little discussion and more a memorization of her framework.

I was threatened for using the restroom ONCE, during her class! She told me that she would go to the Dean if I did it again, and if I did it any more times after that I would be kicked out of class. Also she is spacey, unfocused and a joke. Poor teacher Material.

WARNING: Do NOT take her classes!  She's horrible!  She rambles on about absolutely nothing for the entire lecture and usually everyday is the same thing.  It rarely relates to anything we are "supposed to" be learning.  I learned absolutely nothing in this class, it was just a pain because of her unclear instructions and ridiculous assignmnets.

DO NOT, i repeat do not under any circumstances take one of Konkle's classes.  She has no idea what she is saying half of the time so getting anything out of her hour long rambling excuse for a class is next to impossible.  Boring, hard, stupid, gross, and dumb.  That is her class in a nutshell.
The worst. Something is definitely wrong here. I got a decent grade, but there is no excuse for a low energy term like the one I had in MKs class.

HORRIBLE TEACHER. This is not an English class, she says so herself. She was late every day and treated us like 7th graders. Assignments were unclear and unreasonable. Grading was inconsistent. I am scarred for life from having to listen to her monotone voice every few days for a whole semester. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES!

Maureen Konkle insulted journalism students on the first day of class for writing short paragraphs.  She regularly insulted the intelligence of many different groups over the length of the course.  She does not grade hard if you read the work but she is very mean and seems offended every time you come to class. I am petrified of her.  DON'T TAKE TH

Have you ever though Anne Coulter could teach??? Well she looks like her, and her class sucked! I ran out of there with a B+ and was satisfied, but often frustrated with her grading, teaching, and tardiness. It was very tiring to have to hear her TALK for 1 hour and 30 minutes, but of course she claimed it would make us "better people". Not really.

Class was very unstructured, gave 5 page papers on a half a page poem. Changed assignments after we had turn them in. No realy notes, but expects you to know what she does. Always late and not helpful at office hours. She is passionate about her subject, but should not be teaching lower level courses.

Maureen has a wealth of knowledge to share even if the classroom can drag her down a little. Her office hours are wonderful resources and should be used. I enjoyed her classes and would not mind taking more for fun. Definately a + for students.
She IS a little spacey, but if you go and talk to her after class, she's wonderful.
No Comments
Worst angry troll of a prof ever.Terrible readings, boring off-topic lecture.

He has a very strong accent and not very good handwriting, so his lectures are a little hard to follow at first. His exams and quizzes are very easy, the questions are taken directly from in class examples and he doesn't try to trick you. He also gives a lot of partial credit and extra credit on exams.

his lectures were very straightforward, he did plenty of example problems for each concept, every once in a while he would crack a joke. his exams were very straightforward, no curveballs, and no traps. I feel that with a different professor Calc 3 would've been much more difficult. Excellent professor overall.

He went through all the relevant material in his lectures, and was pretty funny too. You could supplement by reading the textbook if you'd like. Tests were worth a lot, but surprisingly not that hard if you had studied the material. Homework assigned every day but not ever collected or graded, just for practice.

I initially had my doubts about Koldosbsky, but oh man.... it is impossible to not like this guy; the exam material is crystal clear - no curveballs - and the lectures, besides being occasionally humorous, are strictly based on what you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is a funny and intelligent teacher.  He will teach you things in a different way than learned in high school.  Most people went to their TA's for help instead of him.  His accent is hard to understand so sit close to the front of the room so you can hear him and see the board.  Online HW assignments are annoying,  the tests aren't too bad.

He's a hard to understand but after awhile you'll get used to the accent. Actually really funny and cute (in the old man sort of way.)  DEFINITELY sit in the front because if you can't see the chalkboard you'll be so lost.  Tests are super easy but the final was extremely hard.

I love Koldobsky! I think his lectures are clear and he gives great examples. Make sure to do the assigned homework even if it is not graded. It really helps for test preparation. I would highly recommend him.

He's probably one of the better calc. teachers out there. He's Russian, but he speaks English very well, and is easy to understand. He sometimes, goes about things the hard way, but if you need any clarity the TA's are there to help. He's very straight forward with his exams, nothing "surprising" and also somewhat easy. He has has a sense of humor
Was a good and funny teacher that is liked by many across campus.
Very good Calc professor. Perhaps the best math teacher I've had (I went all the way thru Diff EQ). He explains concepts very well and has an excellent sense of humor.

Great math professor. Go to lecture and do the math problems and if you need any help ask you TAs and you will be set for the exam. Also some of stuff he goes over seems way over the top he does not end up asking it on exams so no worries everything is the main concepts of what you learned no tricks.
TERRIBLE no reviews nothing just assigned problems from text get the SOL'N manual only thing that saved me
Great professor.  Challenging, but very good class.
Koldobsky is the man

lectures are a must. get ready to take pages of notes. he's russian but fairly easy to understand. all around nice guy and pretty funny in class. tests are VERY hard. make sure you do the homework and you should be ok. take the lecture that has Dany Basil as the TA. hes pretty much awesome.

A huge lecture, but the curve is EXTREMELY GENEROUS.  If you can't understand him, it's not his problem, just look at the board!!! He's hilarious!!  You can tell he is very smart, but you better be prepared to do your part because he can go really fast in class!  Overall, a moderately hard class with a really great curved score.
Difficult class, not clear
Difficult class, difficult to understand
Did not learn much from him, easy tests though

Absolutely hilarious. If you're having a bad day, go to this class and he'll make you laugh. He breaks chalk like it's going outta style. He knows what he's talking about and has a lot of fun teaching the class. Probably the coolest Russian ever, and you'll pick up on the accent pretty quick.
Crappiest class at University...
He's a crazy cool russian

Great teacher and funny.  Makes calculus much easier than expected.  His tests can be pretty tough, but if you show most of the work you can get at least a B on the tests.  I was able to get a pretty strong A without doing a lot of homework.

i love this guy! hes so funny. he breaks like 5 pieces of chalk every lecture haha... you get used to his accent, he presents everything in a very clear and organized way, highly recommended...easy A...
Great teacher.  Keeps you very interested and makes the topics easy to understand.
Very good!

Dr. Koldobsky was a great professor.  He's Russian, but easy to understand after you get used to him. If you do your homework, you'll do fine on the tests. I hardly did any homework, and I made a B. Just remember that you can always switch recitations if you don't like your TA. Some TAs are pretty crappy.
No Comments
No Comments

He was a very good teacher and vas very funny, as funny as you can get for a math teacher.  He was Russian, but still pretty easy to understand.  For the final, just make sure to review all old exams and it should be pretty easy.
The professor doesn't grade anything; I haven't been able to see my grade since the first day of class. Doesn't explain any of her assignments. She treats her class like a part-time job.
WORST PROFESSOR EVER.
Very hard grader. Lowers your grade for missing class more than 3 times and is not very understanding about excuses.

Great class and teacher if you put in effort! She is genuine  nice & more than willing to help if you actually go to her office hours and ask for help. I went to her office hours before every speech I gave and had her look over my speech. She will give you individual feedback and critique to help you earn a better grade! But tests are hard, study!
Good luck

This was my first time writing speeches and speaking in front of people. The midterm and final are very unclear. She grades extremely hard especially when you are giving your best effort towards all tests and speeches. As time went on, the students in class lost respect for her. I would choose a  different professor if I were you.

She's really obnoxious. I've always loved public speaking but she nitpicks so much. Considering this was the first time some people had to do this sort of thing, she graded really harshly. Midterm and final were incredibly hard and very unclear. (yeah you have written tests too.) If you have the chance, get a different teacher.
She is more of a high school teacher. Really tough grader. Anal about using technology in class.
She was very helpful and easy to talk to, and she expected a lot out of her students.

This class is fairly easy if you pay attention in lectures and do practice exams. Lectures are certainly a change of pace from typical teaching and his jokes keep them engaging if you find him funny. Content is a bit hard to grasp conceptually but actual problems are much easier. He gives great practice exams and allows notes to be used for exams.

Grade was determined by somewhat-weekly quizzes, bi-weekly homework, and 3 exams and a final. Mostly explained things well, except for a few concepts where I had to turn to YouTube. Difficult problems on some quizzes and exams, but gave a lot of partial credit so it was okay.
Lectures are not helpful and not worth going to. Exams are very similar to practice exams. Final was hard.

He is very smart but is not great at dumbing down the content. The class is test heavy but he provides lots of studying material for the tests which is nice. He's a nice guy and if you go to class you will better understand the content.

He makes the content of the class harder than it has to be, he provides good study material for the exams, and you're allowed to bring in notes to the exam. Exams aren't hard if you have been paying attention in class.

Class was definitely test heavy with 75% of the grade being tests and the final. All quiz, test, and final questions are taken directly from the textbook. Makarov could be a little hard to understand to begin with, but as the course progresses it'll get easier. Makarov is really funny and publishes all of his notes so 100% participation is ok

Professor Makarov can be really hard to understand at first, but once you can get past it hes insanely smart and funny. He understands the difficulty of the class and dropped the lowest 2 quizzes and homework. Prepare long ahead for the final as its insanely hard and worth 40% of grade.

I don't think Makarov is a bad teacher, but his approach to online learning is very frustrating. Maybe it would have been different if we were in person, but his exams (a huge part of the grade) were for little-no partial credit, meaning any algebraic mistakes meant NO POINTS for that question. You can still fail, fully understanding the material

I don't recommend taking calc3 or any other class with Makarov. All of the exams were on Webassign, meaning the answer has to be EXACT and there's hardly any partial credit. In terms of lecture, I stopped going because it wasn't helpful to me at all. If you take his class, expect to rely on Youtube videos to learn the material.

Don't even bother going to his lectures because you're going to end up teaching yourself everything anyways. Calc 3 is not a hard subject, unless you take his class. No partial credit given, and he seemed shocked when people were asking for it after getting 30% on their exams. If the only other option for Calc 3 is an 8am, take it.

If you are taking his online math class, don't. I can see how he could be an eyeopening teacher if you could get to know him, but not over zoom. He is not a good online professor, lack of organization, not great at explaining concepts, tests are hard and partial credit (showing your work at all for huge math problems) is rare,

He makes his tests extremely difficult for no reason and does not give out partial credit for the most part. Not only this but his class is the hardest out of all the calc 3 classes. He likes to brag about how no one ever really fails his classes but thats because of how big the curve is that he gives everyone because the average grade is so low
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I LOVE Konstantin. His class is definitely harder than other professors, but it was so worth it. Hes a literal genius and his jokes are hysterical (mainly because of their randomness and his nonchalant attitude). Make sure to keep his handouts and stay on top of the homework and youll be fine. I almost switched my major to math after his class.
I thought he was pretty clear cut. The test questions are always from the book. Pretty funny guy, and easy to get along with.

Didn't find his accent to be a problem. Seems to be a great guy and enjoyed him as a teacher. If you do the homework problems, you'll be fine for the test. He gets all of his test questions straight from the book. He has some pretty funny jokes. Glad I was in his section. If you do the work, you'll earn a good grade. That simple.
He was alright. Even though he has an accent, I could understand him fine. His homework problems are very similar to his test problems. I've had him for two classes, and they both went okay.

he has a thick accent. he makes some jokes and is pretty funny. sometimes he gets carried away and goes deeper into the subject than needed. overall the class is pretty hard and i strongly reccommend doing the hw. his tests are a LOT like the hw problems too.

I would say he is a pretty good teacher once you get past the accent.  He tries to lay out the material in a way that is easy to understand.  His tests are always problems straight from the book, and he gives you a practice exam before each test that has problems extremely similar to those on the test.  Plus he is actually pretty funny!
Russian, difficult to comprehend. Teaches extra material than other sections and the tests are more difficult. Confusing on what/why he choses to test on certain topics.

Makarov is the worst teacher I have ever had. He is impossible to understand, just reads the book to you, and his exams are nothing like the homework. Your grade will solely depend on how he is feeling at the time. I learned more calculus from youtube than attending this guys lectures. DO NOT TAKE HIS SECTION!!!
Took this class online during the summer, and that was the best way to go. But the homework would take an hour even using photomath.
I had a TA teach me for this class but she is just as horrible as when I had her in 1100, she sucks and doesnt help at all.
She sucks, never responded to my emails, doesnt care, and doesnt teach.

If you have basic math skills, you'll be fin since most material is high school review. I skipped lectures and learned from Canvas without issues, but some exams are reportedly tough for others. Not a bad class overall, but if math is a struggle, attend lectures.

I had to email a different professor in order to communicate with issues in my class or other things like that. Not the best at math but she made is way more harder than it needed to be, literally just read from the textbook and that's it. Taught myself basically.

Does a good job of explaining the concepts and offers resources if you didn't understand. Class flies by because you're just working on practice problems the whole time. But homework can take a while. The tests are the exact same as the practice tests so just memorize those and you'll be good. Would 100% take again.
Not 1100, but helped me out. Nice person!

so many in class assignments. i clicker so class was mandatory. everyone has to take this class so really no way to avoid it. as long as u do the i clicker and in class and homework your grade will be ok
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I've never been that good at math and I did very well in her class. I just had to pay attention to the lectures. Highly recommend taking the practice tests she provides because they are very similar to the tests.

If your reading this as in incoming freshman for next year or just in general. I wouldn't  have Kristina Hahn as a teacher she constantly complains about the class size she speeds through the lecture and doesn't really explain the material well. Online homework is 50-70 questions. I basically had to teach my self the material this whole semester.
If you commit the time you will learn so much.

This class was frustrating. In high school math was my strong-suit and my highest grade. I genuinely think I left the class more confused than I'd ever been before, in a subject I was previously super comfortable in. She also gets mad very easily and yells at the whole class OFTEN. We're just college students.

No discern for if her students are struggling. I am strong academically and the math isn't necessarily complicated, she moves on so quickly without explaining what she writes. Gets annoyed when students need her to slow her lecture down. Just help your students to succeed- you don't get paid extra for making 18 year old feel meritless.

Doesn't explain things at all. Makes office hours weird times so it's hard to get to them and assigns a ton of homework in little amount of times and tests are close together. Doesn't prepare the class well before exams.

teacher is rude, seems annoyed, talks to students like kindergarteners, is bad at teaching, the corse isn't even hard she's just bad at teaching, i do not look forward to her- or the class. this is the 1 and only time in my entire academic career that i have ever had below a b in math- im good at math. she is a terrible teacher and she irritates me

Do not take this class. Teacher seems constantly annoyed, and ta's are condescending and rude to students. Weekly homeworks with 50-100 questions each, except each question has 10+ parts. Uses iClicker so attendance is mandatory.
Quickly moves through topics without full understanding from her students. Doesn't help students that need it. Seems annoyed/ shows no interest in students or their needs.

He's a great, pastoral professor. If you want to truly be pushed, he's the guy. Easy? No. He's best for students who want to grow and be challenged. He will encourage critical thinking. If you ask for help, he will work with you to get you to where you want to go. Even with other classes and career advice! A professional, tough uncle kinda vibes.

Tough teacher, but one of the best. Made me a better film maker, taught us to really edit analytically. Hard class, no denying it, but it was worth it. Just go to class, ask questions (he expects you to), and be open about how much you know.

Most knowledge and caring professors Ive had. He will meet with you for help, advice, issues with other classes, and career goals. He always asked me if I was okay and will give you more time for deadlines. Caters class time around what the class wants to learn. Do extra work out of class, the practices/ readings & talk to him or you wont learn!

This guy literally wasted multiple classes just talking about how much he loves DaVinci software over Adobe. A third of the way into the semester is when we actually started working on projects related to the class. To sum him up in his own words, "I'm not a teacher, I'm an artist."

I usually do well classes, and I did, but i STRUGGLED.  I'm in 2 4000 level chemistry classes, and this class alone took more work for the A-.  Most unfair grader I've seen- he  doesn't try o give you credit, he tries to take points off.  The rough draft paper highest grade was an 85%, even though he said the whole point is to improve.  Avoid him

I'm usually a straight A student and struggled insanely in this course. He was very biased in feedback and graded hard to the point it was nearly unattainable to earn an A. Every student that I have spoken to that has taken this course agrees with these statements. If you can avoid it, please do not take this course with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ryan's a fun guy, but the class is graded on too few criteria for a philosophy class. If you mess one test up (easy to do) then your A is screwed and you won't get it back. The wording of multiple choice test questions is not clear-cut and leaves a lot of decision making on the table about which answer to choose even if you know the content.
The topics we discuss in class are really interesting and I liked the discussion aspect. You definitely have to go to class to get a good grade. He is annoying but he cares about his students.

Ryan is very passionate about what he teaches, takes student feedback, and is accessible for help. Even though this class is only graded on exams, participation, and quizzes, if you read, take notes, and go to class, it is not too difficult. He also offers extra credit. Not an easy A, but if you put the work in, it is easily attainable.
Attendance is mandatory, he does not post the notes, and you have to read philosophy papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kulesa is full of personality and passionate about what he teaches. I never once dreaded going to this class because it was always positive. We have open discussions about different topics and it allows us to be open minded. Grading is clear and he provides great feedback. He is understanding and allows makeups.

Great class. Ryan is an amazing lecturer, and always made going to class a great time. He connects with his students very well, and allows for a great time for discussion in class. The class can be hard, and it's not easy to just slack off. If you want to take this class be prepared read outside of class the articles, and pay attention in class!

Ryan is very passionate and unbiased, which makes him an excellent philosophy instructor. He was funny and engaging each day, and class was always interesting. The readings he assigned were challenging, but relevant and interesting. A bit of a tough grader, but rewards hard work. Don't expect an easy A, but his class is worth it!

This professor was a very enthusiastic to come to class everyday. He chose topics in which are super relevant to today and encouraged group discussion among the class to create an environment for students to actively learn the material. Attendance is mandatory and a huge part of understanding with the course but it is also intriguing and fun.

One of my favorite professors ever. He actually made me look forward to a 9am class. He made all of his lectures super interesting with good notes. Definitely cares about his students, and wants them to do well. Gave us extra credit at the end as he listened to our feedback. 10/10 guy

Ryan was such a great instructor. He made me look forward to class every day, and the content was super interesting. He was funny, involved, well-educated, unbiased, and made an effort to connect with his students. The grading was fair and the class was challenging, conceptually, but definitely manageable if you put in the work and do the readings.

I really enjoyed the way he taught because he engaged very well with the class and made lectures interesting to listen. However, the only things that go into the grade book are exams, weekly quizzes, and papers so it is definitely not an easy A class. He also really listened to our feedback and adjusted as needed which was very kind

Ryan was super nice and cared for students. Course material was not too difficult but reading the readings definitely help! The readings are super long though! The exams were pretty difficult. They started as select all that apply multiple choice which every hates and were eventually moved to normal multiple choice. Was not any extra assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kulesa is very nice and cares about his students. However, your grade is based on only quizzes, multiple choice exams, and essays. If you are looking to fill your philosophy elective requirement and want an easy A do not take his class.
If I could give a 0/5 on his rating I would. He refuses to help students with any assignments and your only grades really are the tests.  Don't ruin your GPA by taking him.

Brorsen was clearly new to teaching undergraduate chemistry in Fall 2021, but he tried and was very nice. This is rare in many STEM departments at Mizzou. His tests were based off the ALEKS homework, and he posted review guides on ALEKS, so just do the homework and you'll be set. Even if you're bad at tests, he weighs ALEKS heavily, so you're ok.

This class is less about learning chemistry and more about learning ALEKS. Exam problems are pulled directly from ALEKS almost word for word, so if you master that style of problem you're fine. Attendance is not mandatory, lectures are recorded and slides are posted.

I audited a graduate course with Dr. Brorsen. He is amazing. He cares, answers all your questions, appreciate you reading the book, takes time outside class should you need help, practical teaching, a normal and genuine person, focused, helpful, and wants you to learn and succeed in the course and life in general.

Dr. Brorsen is a great professor. He's very approachable, kind and knowledgeable. Attendance isn't necessary, but watch the Panoptos at 1.5x to save time. Tests are 100% off ALEKS homework. Don't bother reading. Labs don't relate to the rest of class, but weren't bad. Don't take the first lab of the week as materials/procedure were often unprepared
Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Brorsen is an excellent professor for first year students. He's laid back, casual, approachable, and kind. His lectures are easy to follow and he communicates them in easy-to-understand terms. He's clear about what to expect on exams and the homework helps you master the content. Would totally recommend this professor.

Chemistry is not my strong suit, but Dr. Brorsen did a great job covering the material. He was always happy to help during office hours, whether it was homework or re-explaining a concept I didn't understand from the lectures. My advice: don't procrastinate ALEKS homework and don't take the first lab of the week (materials weren't always prepared).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Brorsen is passionate about what he teaches, and the course structure was simple to follow. Make sure you do the ALEKS homework because that's all that makes up the tests. Reading the textbook and paying attention in lectures is helpful for understanding the material, but doing ALEKS hw is a MUST for a good grade. Labs were all straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brorsen does his best with the material but doesn't make it clear what students should spend time on. Aleks will be 100% of your tests and therefore most of your grade, meaning as solid as his lectures are they don't help much. Labs also have nothing to do with the lectures so get ready to feel like you're taking 3 separate classes.

Dr. Brorsen is a wonderful person who teaches with the intent to have his students succeed. The homework is done through a program for credit, but helps you really learn. The class structure is not too hard and the lectures are easy to follow. If you are in the Honors Program and get put in his class, I promise you will not regret it.
Dr. Kurlowski is very funny and relatable. We were only graded by online quizzes and in person exams. He keeps lectures fun. I would definitely take one of his classes again!

He had no power point and read the lecture of a piece of paper every day. It made it very difficult to know what was important and made tests seem very hard because you never knew what was going to be on them.

I took his American Political Thought course as a senior, and it was a nice class to have.  I don't know why people think his class is so difficult; its the same as with any university course: show up, read, participate and you'll do just fine.  Drew was great, I would definitely take other courses with him if I could.

A very hard class for entry-levels. Tests are almost impossible. He make lectures interesting but doesn't have notes on his powerpoint. You have to read the textbook and really study. And yes he is (probably) the MOST attractive man on campus. So it is really up to you to get lost during lectures or to be motivated to study...

What ever you do, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS! His quizzes are based off the book. His lectures barely have any notes (he doesn't like people taking notes because he says you're not actually learning ). His tests are pretty much based solely on lecture. Some of the questions are even based on HIS OPINION. If you're at mizzou, just take it online. RUN!

One of the nicest and most interesting teachers that I have had at Mizzou thus far.  Every lecture is so interesting and easy to follow along.  I studied harder for this class than any other and made many study guides but still could not figure out how to prepare for a test.  It seemed like the test had no correlation to his lectures whatsoever,

Dr. Kurlowski is a great professor. His tests are not nearly as difficult as everyone says they are. If you show up to class, actually pay attention and read the book you will do fine. He does actually make you work for your grade, so you can't just scrape by. His lectures are very enjoyable and he has a real passion for politics and educating.

It's really not that hard. Lecture material rarely shows up on the test. Read the book, take notes on the book, and you'll be golden. Kurlowski isn't a bad professor, but his lack of experience shows. He once showed John Oliver in class though, so he's cool in my book.

Passionate about political science and hilarious in lecture.  Basically a grown up frat star.  Lectures are 100% irrelevant to the tests. Powerpoints are pictures, not words.  You barely take notes on what he says cause it doesn't make sense or apply.  Need to read chapters for tests and quizzes. There's only 2 tests and the final, which he curved.

Kurlowski is clearly passionate about his topic and can sometimes make the lectures interesting but they're mostly tedious and mind numbing. The tests and online quizzes are worded horribly and can be confusing, if you do the reading you'll pass though. Told our class every exam would be graded on a curve and never followed through with it.

I expect a 3.0 average for each semester, until I took this class. His class is pure lecture (little PowerPoint notes) and come time for the exams, he distributes no sort of study guide. The final is cumulative and worth 35% of your grade. If that doesn't keep you away, I don't know what will. In other words, if you aren't seriously motivated, run.

It's a basic government class, much like the one you take in high school. Most test questions come from lecture, with a couple from the book. Online quizzes are easy A's cause you can take multiple times. Lecture's can be boring but if you talk one-on-one with him he's helpful and quite funny!  (just cause I know you read these, yes you're cute.)
One of the hardest classes I've taken. Lectures put you to sleep. Tests are really hard. He can be funny at some times but that doesn't really make up for the class being horrible. 0 stars.

Dr. Kurlowski is one of the coolest professors I've had so far. He really wants everyone to have a deep understanding of government by the end of the class, and you can tell that he cares about the students. He's pretty young to have a phD and be a professor so who knows, maybe one day he'll be president or something. Overall, it's a good class.
Really great class and made class discussions really interesting. Would love to take this class again!

I'm an engineer major so I figured it would be an easy course. It is not! I went to lectures and listened, he did keep them interesting however the exams are crazy hard. Crazy questions that come from a tiny corner section of the book are on the exams. If you like this stuffmajor you'll do fine, if you don't good luck and study  hard.

Prof. Kurlowski is a great person. His class is always entertaining and intriguing. Don't listen to the people that say his tests are impossibly hard!!! If you go to lecture and read the book, you'll do fine. In his words, "I spent years doing scholarly work and getting a PhD to be judged by 18 year olds by how hot I am."
People are overdramatic about this class

Class if fun and easy to understand. You do not have to take tons of notes in class. It is however important that you read the book. There are online quizzes but you can take them over and over until you receive the grade you want so those help and are not very long.
He's an alright guy but he puts things on the test that are like nothing covered in lectures. If you decide to take this class I wish you luck. You are going to need it.
His looks are AWESOME! but his tests suck so stay away. Far, far away. I studied all the time and only managed a B. :(

Though he was attractive don't let his looks fool you, his class is super hard. Even if you read the whole book and take notes like I did you will not get the grade you want. You really need to pay attention to do well in this class or come in knowing pretty much everything there is to know about politics.

Knowledgeable (and extremely attractive) professor who is passionate about government. Weekly quizzes and 2 heavily weighted tests is all you get but if you attend lecture and thoroughly read the book you'll escape with a B or higher. I never missed lecture and he is even the reason I considered changing my major.

You have an online, open book quizzes for each chapter. However, they're only 15% of your grade. I received a 100% on each quiz, and it still did nothing for my grade. You only have 3 exams. They're all multiple choice, however, they're very specific. They're not so much about fact as about reasoning. "Why did we stop at 435 members for the House?"

VERY tough class. Power points have just pictures on them so you have to listen very carefully and be attentive. doesn't follow the book either. Weekly online quizzes that do no good for the tests. It does help that he is nerdy cute
I liked him a lot! Gave very interesting information, wish he was clearer about what was on tests. Helpful if you ask for it.
His test are extremely hard and way too specific.
A good lecturer but he makes the tests next to impossible. No amount of studying can prepare you. Seriously.

At first I thought the class was going to be awesome. He covers topics in class very clearly & I study ALL THE TIME. I study before every test, usually starting a week and a half prior. I took the first test thinking it wouldn't be that big of a deal. I got a C. Never in my college life have I done so poorly. Same with his other tests.
Tests in this class are very hard!! Way too specific for how many topics you cover
The test answers are not that clear. At All. the answer could be any of two and he even says that. Other than the tests he is an awesome teacher and a great speaker.
He is great! His class if my favorite because he makes sure the class understands and is always available for questions. Cute and Funny
AWESOME Love his class and it definitely helps that he is mega-attractive in a dorky kind of way.
He is an amazing teacher who actually has a passion for what he does! LOVE going to his class!

Drew was a pretty great teacher! He moved quickly with notes, but if you pay attention, he emphasizes important points! Online quizzes were easy points, text book is NECESSARY! Not to mention...he is SUPER ATTRACTIVE and intelligent. Which made it so much easier to pay attention ;)

There's plenty of reading and writing involved, but in small, manageable proportions that require you to think about the material. Dr. Kuchinski is also very responsive, and quick to acknowledge issues with grading or schedule changes. Her lectures and class assignments promote organized, healthy discussion for even the most controversial topics.

This class really made me open my mind! I really enjoyed this professor. She was open to hear different opinions during class dicussions. She wasnt a hard grader and the test followed what she taught. She was the nicest and most understanding professor I had this semester ! Would def take again!

Anthropology isn't the most interesting topic but she made it interesting. There is a lot of reading and you have to do a one page summary on each one, but it is not too hard and she is an easy grader.

This class was pretty standard. Although you can get a high grade pretty easily, to make an A you have to have a really high grade. Read the textbook, the reader articles, and show up for the pop quizzes and you have yourself an A. I went to less than half the lectures and could guess when the pop quizzes were, so lectures help but aren't important
VERY BORING!

He's a nice guy, but the exams look nothing like the homework or study guide, he's first teacher I've heard of where majority of the students agree studying is a waste of time. Do not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is awful. DO NOT TAKE. Tests are so much of your grade and its truly impossible to do well. Review guides give you nothing for the test. The lectures are scattered and so hard to follow as his explanations are literal chicken scratch on the board. Only reason I passed is because he curves the exams- because everyone does HORRIBLE.
He is a great guy who is passionate ab
It is impossible to do good on tests. He doesn't teach or give any hints to what will be on the test.
The test are impossible he had to curve by over 30%

He is a nice guy, but this is the worst class I've ever taken. His exams do not match anything he teaches in class or any of the materials he provides to study. He said we are "supposed to fail" exams and that it is nearly impossible to receive anything above a C in the class. Do not take him
No reason to even study for tests.
Great guy but has tests that are wildly hard and do not look anything like the homework or study guides.

He was a great Professor; he explained things in detail and wanted people to ask questions. He is always willing to listen to your argument on a question and may even give you credit for it. Overall it's a challenging course, but I would recommend him as a professor.
Kyle was my discussion instructor for stats and he was a beast.
I suck at math but Maddox made it slightly less painful. The grade curve saved my life.
Kyle is a good dude! Calculus is hard and math sucks, but Kyle gets you where you need to be as painlessly as possible. He is a fair grader even if there's not a lot of detailed feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kyle is one of the most devoted Math profs. I have ever had. He uses almost every type of teaching style to help accommodate for each students success in the class room. Never makes me feel behind or stupid for not grasping a concept. Is dedicated to every student's complete understanding of topics and materials. Very inclusive & fun to be around

I've had Kyle several times as both a TA and a professor throughout my math sequence and he has been the best professor I've had at Mizzou. He genuinely cares about his students and is very knowledgeable regarding the material he teaches. I would not consider myself a "math person" but Kyle made calculus approachable and sometimes even fun.

I've had Kyle for Pre-Calc and for Calc 3. He is by far the best math teacher I've ever had. He really wants his students to succeed and he will help you even if it means he has to go out of his way. He would hold review sessions for his students that would actually help and the practice exams would match up well with the exams.
the best instructor i've ever had! smart and funny dude who knows the material.

Kyle makes math more understandable. He consistently explains things in a way that will make sense and make you want to come to class. Hes funny and cares about your performance, so you can expect a great class.

Kyle somehow manages to turn a difficult class into an enjoyable and engaging experience; I've never met an instructor that cared so much about the academic success of his students. The quizzes are simple and the lecture material is relevant and clear.
Math kinda sucks, but he made it suck less. Basically, as long as you follow his advice about what parts to study and do your homework, you'll be fine.

I was always bad at math until I reached college. I failed and subsequently withdrew from my first college math class, but the teacher of my next math class was Kyle. Kyle single-handedly made me good at math. He was perhaps one of the most caring, funny, and skilled math teachers I ever had.
Hardest class ive ever taken, a lot of time and work is expected. Impossible grader, do not recommend if not wanting to put in the work. Quiz every class.
Hardest class of my life and best class of my life.

He is absolutely one of  the wisest, the most awesome and helpful instructors I have ever seen. He is really an expert in this area, and he has the insight of identifying and telling students what their advantage, disadvantage and potentials are, and he is good at encouraging students and promoting his students. I benefit a great lot from the class

Greeley is an extremely demanding professor, but you will learn more from him in one semester than you have in the past 20 years of your life. He's a great guy and will help you with whatever you need. Don't lose hope in B2... When you're approved to the station, you're life will be stress-free!
the best professor I've ever met

He is the single most valuable asset of the entire department.  Why? Because he has an ability to make you ask the tough questions about yourself and whether you want to be in this field or not.  I've never had a professor before him or since, that forced me to ask myself the hard questions and then, forced me to answer them with incredible work
No Comments
No Comments
Firm, very firm, but fair. Charismatic guy
Okay, he's the only faculty member I almost flipped off in class. He's ruthless, but yet he's the only one I remember. Learn from him at your own risk, but you will learn. Oh yes, you will learn.

I learned an exceptional amount in Greeley's class, namely that I do not want to be a reporter. He's a good teacher and he doesn't take any excuses, and I appreciate the fact that I've been forewarned about the downsides of reporting. Greeley, thanks for everything, and summer '04 B1ers have fun!!

Greeley changed my life. He is the most involved professor I've ever had. If you want to become an ethical journalist, take his class and really listen to him. Let him push you beyond what you thought you could do. He is the best journalism professor at Mizzou.
Greeley grills you but its only for your own good..he's very paternal in his advice giving.. and wants you to come out the J-school THE BEST!!!!!

Stop whining.  Greeley kicks your butt so the real world won't have to.  If your grade's not what you wanted it to be, you were obviously one of those "out of the station by 9" types.  If you want easy classes, go be a business major.

Greeley taught me to run...run fast...from journalism.  If the real world is as hard as his class...NO THANKS. He ruined my GPA and my life for a semester.  I worked my a** off and all my grades suffered because of it. I learned very little!
No Comments

Excellent classes. Really, deeply cares about students learning outside the classroom and at KOMU. Commanding presence, will make you a better reporter while learning all the nuts and bolts you need to be ready for KOMU. You'll work hard - but keep going.
He is the worst teacher I ever had in my life.
