He failed to teach us anything but technical skills that you would learn in a trade school.  He taught us little about *journalism* i.e. good writing, crafting compelling stories, etc.  More interested in good camera angles than good journalism.
If you like self-esteem, this isn't the teacher for you.

Dr. K is a nice man, but a little difficult to work with course-wise. His assignments have weird due dates (e.g. post in discussion board by Friday and reply ON Sunday) and is never hesitant to knock off points. I sent an email to him and the TA about it and he still tried justifying it, but ig it's his class. The TAs he picks are also quite sassy.
My fav professor ever was Dr. K! He was super caring and gave great lectures

Heavy workload, with quizzes, group projects, and essays due constantly. Cares less about the quality of the work, and more about the accuracy of APA formatting. Lecture heavy as well, resulting in the class average of his midterm exam being a 68%. Doesn't post lectures on Canvas, so whatever you're able to scribble down in person is all you have.

Took over the summer. Heavy work load. Quizzes every Sunday, two discussion boards, and two 1-2 page papers every week, plus the readings for everything. Most of the topics for the papers were interesting so it was bearable. Definitely do not recommend if you do not like writing papers. The topics that were covered really made up for the workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He has weird participation requirements and odd assignment schedules(at least in his online courses) for things like discussion boards. I've taken online courses for several semesters now and he does things pretty differently than most. Other than that the course load was fairly light and the information was interesting.

Took online during the summer. No online lectures. All reading. Book was very interesting to read, easy read too. Ten question quiz every Sunday. Two discussion questions each week. 1-2 page papers double spaced each week.  Easy grader. Put A LITTLE effort and you'll get a high A!!

Overall he's average. Had him for Psych 1000 & a few HP courses.  Barely read the book because he pretty much copies from the text. Attendance wasn't serious. Grades oddly because he picks out random things. If your assignment is worth 20pts you might get 17-19 normally. Doesn't really follow syllabus... peculiar guy. 2.5 out of 5 rating

This class is easy. His power points are directly from the book, and the exams are super easy if study the power points. He tests over the general info. He does use Clickers to take class attendance, but the questions are easy. He's a nice prof. that wants you to succeed and learn the material. I would study for about an hour the day of the exam.

Awful. Reads straight from the book. 55 page powerpoints he doesn't teach and expects you to know for the test. Makes students give presentations so he can sit in the back and text. Attendance is mandatory even though he reads straight from the book. could be sued for plagiarism, seriously. BAD!

Awful. Lectures are read STRAIGHT from the book, could be sued for plagiarism. Makes you do presentations so he can sit in the back of the lecture hall and text so he doesn't have to teach. Tests are straight from the book and there is so much information, almost impossible. 55 slide powerpoints he expects you to know without teaching any of it.
DR. K is the best. He truly cares about his students and loves to teach. Don't piss him off or take advantage of his niceness, because he will stop his pleasant behavior and become very hard.

Dr. K is a decent teacher but his tests are full of random and tiny facts from his lectures and because of this tests are quite tricky. My biggest problem with this professor is that i received .12 off of a letter grade higher and he, under no circumstances, would round up. Make sure you go to all studies bc write ups are graded harshly.

Attendance isn't required, but I would recommend going because the class is entertaining, there a bonus questions that come from in-class discussions on the tests, and his real life examples are helpful. The tests are pretty easy and doing the research credits is fairly interesting. I would recommend this course with this teacher.
i found him to be extremely interesting and easy to listen to. i always had to study for his tests. study the review guide he gives you
Easy A..... Attendance isn't necessary.  Read the book, do the mandatory experiments, and get an A

Kuhnert is a funny, respectful, knowledgeable guy. He has real world experience.  If you pay attention with an avid interest, you will have to study little.  He essentially goes over what is in the book with stories of his own. You have several tests with 52 questions (2 of which are bonus, go to class for answers). The final is the same as the oth

Extremely easy. Going to class wouldn't be necessary except for the fact that his bonus questions come from examples he uses during lectures. Just take notes and review them a few days before the test and you will do fine.

Prof. Kuhnert is amazing! He definitely knows how to keep the class paying attention and entertained. He basically tells what is needed for exams and such. And sometimes reading can be a pain in the butt, but if you read and pay attention it is an easy A!

The most terrible Psych teacher I have ever had. My roommates and I dread going to class. I've sent him e-mails only to be e-mailed back with short, rude, and demeaning responses. This man thinks he is absolutely hilarious, but with all respect teaching a class of 500 is a difficult task, but if you cannot do it efficiently stick to a class of 30.
Class is very entertaining and actually fun. Notes are directly from the book, so you don't have to read it. He's probably the best psych professor at MU! Dr. K ROCKS!
He makes everything extremely easy to understand, and he's a pretty funny guy. Plus, he gives out tons of study guides before a test.
he is the best professor ever. so funny, engaging, and really cares about students success and interest in the class. no need to facebook in this class!!
AWESOME teacher and class...he really made it a lot of fun. VERY interesting and hilarious
Dr. K is great! I really became interested in psychology after taking his class. He's is really funny because of all the corny jokes he makes. His tests are really straight forward.

This class is ridiculous. He uses power points form the book, so you can either go to class or read the book (which is a horrible text book that is not only out dated but flat out ignores social reprecusions from studies done by the authors)Sure he is an outgoing guy, some may say funny, but I didn't learn anything from him.

Kuhnert is so cute and funny! I love his laugh and he always tries to make class fun and entertaining. After taking this class, I definitely love psych a lot more. He uses great examples in lecture and the notes are all powerpoints. His tests are VERY easy if you study for them a little. I recommend kuhnert! (good, interesting blowoff class)

He is a cool guy who likes to wear bright button-up shirts to keep people's attention. It's not critical to go to lectures but that's where he gets the extra credit from for his tests. Tests are managable but require @ least 2 days of studying
You could pass without attending this class as long as you got the notes from someone, but I choose to attend because he makes it interesting.

I LOVED Dr. Kuhnert. He is the sweetest man and because it is so nice it is impossible not to laugh at his jokes. Pay attention to his stories in class because that is what he bases his extra credit on. If you go to class you will greatly decrease your study time but you still need to read the textbook. Dr. K made me want to minor in psych.

This class is very easy as long as you do the reading and take notes, but you do not have to do both if you want an A; it just helps you out. The tests are very easy, but are very hard to understand at times. (You would think a Doctor could write a better test.) Overall class is o.k.

Unnecessary/boring lectures. Just fill out/memorize the study guides and you will do fine- not too difficult tests. He is nice but he tries to tell a lot of cheesy jokes. In response to the message below me, the answer is C because it's an attitude not an action (I thought it was a poorly worded question too).

I got an A but Test questions are poorly written.Example: Which of the following is an example of prejudice? A) Phil and Sue do the same job but Phil gets paid more B)the other boys won't let Juan play b/c he is Hispanic. C)Stand becomes angry when he sees a mixed-race couple. D)Valerie wasn't promoted b/c she is Korean.  C is the right answer. hmm

I went to 5 classes: the first day, 3 tests, and the final. Everything I needed was in the margins of the text book. He posts power points still, but omits huge chunks of information to try and get you to come to class. I studied about 45 minutes for each test, which was just skimming the margins, honestly. Got a B with no effort. Yay!

Easy A.  never missed a class, never opened the book.   Attend class and you will know everything on the tests.  Hell, you don't even need to take notes, just DL the powerpoint.  I don't know what ppl are thinking when they say to skip and read the boring textbook.  It's good discipline to wake up for 8am classes anyways.....

Not an awesome teacher - he just reads notes from the books off a powerpoint presentation, but a good guy nonetheless. Going to class is pointless - just read the textbook and make flashcards from the review posted online, memorize it, and you'll get an easy A.

I don't know what these people are talking about . . . the man is not funny. He tries REALLY hard to be, and sure thinks that he is . . . but at 8am, it's just painfully annoying. Not that it's a really bad class or anything, it just irritates me. Went to maybe 20% of the classes, got an A. READ THE BOOK! DO THE OUTLINES!

He was a very nice man but going to class was pointless and you had to read the book and use the study guides to get a good grade. LOTS OF WORK. But once you figure out how to study for his tests it's not so bad. : )
i found his class somewhat boring, but it wasnt hard. as long as you read the text you will be fine.

Dr. K is awesome! He loves what he teaches, and he is really funny. He almost always lets us out of class 15 minutes early. After taking this class I decided that I wanted to double major in Psychology
Fun and easy tests
This is an extremely easy class if you read the books. Never used my notes or went to class.

You have to read the text to do well on his tests. Going to lecture helps a lot too. I didn't think he was that funny and he wore the same purple shirt EVERYDAY. But I found the material interesting. The study sessions for the test are worthless but I filled out the review and read the book and ended up with an A.
The man is very funny if you ever go to class.  Tests are hard because most of it is examples instead of definitions.

Dr. K is amazing.  Class is extremely easy and Dr. K makes it worth your time to go (he's so funny!).  I'd suggest taking Intro with him as well Abnormal Psych (which I'm in right now) or whatever Psych class he's teaching.

Sadly, thinks he's a lot funnier than he is. Quite often, the study guide had nothing to do with what was on the test, and tests questions seemed to be purposefully confusing. However, the final was easy, and his grading scale is pleasantly weird.
No Comments
Hardly a dull moment in Professor K's class. He always has a funny anecdote or example ready to explain what he's talking about.
I never went to class and got an A. Be careful cause sometimes notes don't end up online but if you just read the chapter and memorize terms (doesn't take long) you'll get an A+ no problem.
Funny, easy class, just memorize all the bold words in the book and their definition, you'll get A's. So easy, the guy enjoys being in front of all the people.
He would probably be a better psychologist than a teacher but overall he does a good job.

Dr K basically read his lecture from his power points, which were available online.  Attendance was optional, and obviously so after the first week.  80% of the multiple choice tests were from lecture notes and the rest was from the text.  Answer the study guide questions and you'll do fine on the easy exams.

He is a poor lecturer and seems to only know what's on his slides. That said, the tests are easy. Just study the terms on the review sheet (make a list of them and define them, I promise this is the best way to study) and it's a piece of cake.
Let me take my final after sleeping through it... great guy.
Great guy!  Fun lectures... well as fun as lectures can be.  You dont even need to buy the book!  Just look at notes online!

He did have really bad jokes (a bit ****ed at times) but overall he was a good teacher. The only problem that  I had was that you had to know absurd amounts of detail from the book to do well on his tests.
awesome class, great person, straight forward teaching
I never went to class. I got an A+. This class is horribly easy. And somewhat interesting.
easy class dont have to go to lecture, he posts his notes online, and dropped lowest score
Hilarious, Sexy, and Interesting, what more can you ask for in a man?

Good guy, nice sense of humor.  Multiple choice tests straight from the study guide.  I don't know how you couldn't like this guy.  Could easily skip lecture and do fine on tests by reading but I go just because it's my only lecture I can stand.  If you have a choice between professors go with him.

I'm not sure where you guys are coming from. Ks sense of humor is annoying, he is a poor lecturer and is not very knowledgeable. He thought that people urinate out their sphincters, for one example. I wa surprised at the high ratings. I strongly dislike him, as does everyone else I know in his class
Dr. K is on of the best professors that I have had so far at Mizzou.  He is halarious and even though there are 7 tests, if you study and go to the reviews given by the TA you'll do great on them!
Great class.  Dr. K. is awesome.  He makes class fun.
really funny guy and a GREAT class.  everyone should take his class.. but there are 7 tests that come and go very quickly.  great guy that loves to teach

I took her Feminism in Sci-Fi Literature class, and Trudy is great! There is a lot of reading, which can be kind of daunting, but all of the material is very interesting and easy to read. You can quickly become one of her favorites if you answer questions in class and give thoughtful insights. She is always excited to hear everyone's opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Lewis is one of the kindest and best professors I've ever had. She is very understanding if a situation were to come up during the semester. I would have her every semester if I could!

Prof. Lewis is amazing at what she does! Though it's required a significant amount of work from me, I couldn't recommend her class more. She is respectable, encouraging, and gives great feedback on your assignments. Expect to spend a lot of time writing, but it's entirely worth it. Take her classes if you get the chance, you will absolutely learn!

I took her class last fall, and I picked up on her irritation with male students without even reading the comments here. Apparently she has openly favored female students for quite a while. I have no problem with strong women; it is a matter of wishing to be treated fairly by a teacher who is supposed to accomodate all students -- not just females.
She teaches from her heart and with her soul. What more can we ask?

Trudy is awesome.  However, if you are a man that is afraid of a feminist or a strong woman, steer clear.  Although you could learn a lot from her.  She facilitates excellent discussion and provides a great introduction to criticism.  Her class is never d

Trudy is a good teacher; however, her opinions are stilted by her ueberfeminism. While she may be very learned in the art of writing in the English language, she is failing in the art of social skills. Don't try to interact with Trudy outside of class!

Dr. Lewis is my hero! And her book, well at least her story collection (b/c that is all I have read), is wonderful as well. Trudy challenged me and forced me to look at many sides of a situation plus she was always supplementing the text w/ commetary.

she cared more about her book (and her female students) than she did the three or four guys in the section...she is arrogant and self-serving and not much help outside class....avoid at all costs, seriously....plus I read her crummy book...she is a hack!
Trudy is the best!  She is a genius and always pushes people to do their finest work.  Also has a great sense of humor.
10/10 professor. Nicest professor ive ever had.
Great professor. She gives clear guidelines on all assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An incredibly kind professor. Even when I would mess up in 1 of the 3 oral exams (the exams were very easy and only lasted 10 minutes), she would help guide me and give me a good grade. It is super easy as long as you learn the basics on the "quizzes," you'll do well in the class overall.

Dr. Lee was an amazing professor. Her lectures were short but comprehensive. This was nice because I was able to spend more time coding then taking notes. The quizzes were extremely helpful for assessing how I was doing, and had infinite attempts (this is essential for learning to code). The oral exams were 15 mins long, and conducted well.

Dr. Lee teaches a the senior statistics capstone and she did a great job. This class is writing intensive, but honestly, if yo do the work it's graded easily. Attendance is worth 20% of your grade, so it is important to show up to class. There is also a semester long group project, but it isn't anything too extensive, and nothing to stress over.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Not clear at explaining most things. almost easier to work through lectures on your own. Quiz for every lecture and homework once per week. Hard to actually learn because there's so much to do.
She is really sweet and helpful!

She is very difficult to understand. She is a nice enough lady, but does not really know how to teach. This class should have (and could have) been easy, but she had only one way of explaining things, and that one way usually made little sense.
Statistical programing - terrible class.  Incomprehensible.  The only thing I learned in class was an anecdote about Fishers exact test.  The provided book was the only saviou

Dr. Lee is very nice but her teaching style is disorganized/unclear.  She literally went by the confusing book, hardly gave examples, didn't explain terms and her test questions seemed to come out of nowhere - probably not designed by herself.  Her grading on BlackBoard was never correct and she changed around things last minute from the syllabus.

Horrible teacher, nice person but the worst teacher I have ever had.  She doesn't know how to TEACH.  She tries to explain things that she doesn't need to explain and makes you even more confused in her explination.  I like math and I'm really good at it, she makes me HATE math.

Dr. Ries is a good lecturer and his slides are straightforward. There's a 10 question homework every week/every other week. There are quizzes 1-2x a month, but they're short (12 questions) and reflect the homework. There are no exams or finals (but there are 2 cumulative quizzes). Textbook is optional, but he posts the key terms from each chapter.

I took this course online, and had taken stats in high school so I was kind of familiar with everything already so I ended up just throwing on the Panopto lectures and doing other things. Course will be easy if you know how to use the equation sheet to your advantage.
If you go to lectures and do the homework you will do good in the class. He is very accessible outside of class and wants all his students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 85% of the grades in this class are quizzes, so once you get a bad grade you're cooked for the semester. I got a 66 on my first quiz, and a 75 on my second, then proceeded to get all 100's and 92's and still didn't pull out an A despite turning in all the homework. Teacher is super monotone, but other than that he's kind of funny.

He was, overall, an outstanding professor. The tests are worth 80% of your grade. I did badly on our first test and have been playing catch-up ever since. I feel as though he should make an exception like other professors, and drop the worst grade since it is so test-heavy. Overall, he teaches the material really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hell. Do not take this class if you are a bad test taker. 80% of your grade is based of quizzes that are 12 questions and you only have 30 minutes to do it. He is also extremely rude when you email him and he makes absolutely zero exceptions no matter what.

This class was my living hell. If you are a bad test taker do not take this class. It's 80% based off quizzes which are only 13 questions so if you aren't really good at every single thing you learn you're screwed. He is also extremely rude when you email him and make absolutely zero exceptions for anyone no matter what.
Homework was easy but tests were so difficult. I did great on stats in high school but this was the hardest class I've ever taken.
You get one bad grade on an exam and you're done for basically, there are no extra credit opportunities, and he doesn't round up grades no matter what.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class isn't difficult if you watch the lectures (either in-person or online) and stay caught up. The homework and quizzes are usually short too, which is nice. Because it's such a big class, it's probably best to stick to asking questions in your discussion section instead of during class.

I actually can not stand the way he talks, half the time he sounds like he is yelling. Attendance isn't mandatory and he posts everything online, so I just watched the videos. There's weekly homework and quizzes every other week. He has grades set up where quizzes count for 80% of your grade and they are only 10 questions.

The class wasn't bad at all. I took it online and kept up with lectures on my own. However, the quizzes count for a ton but are very easy if you study for them. He was kind of rude whenever I emailed him. I mixed up the chapters in the email and he made me feel very dumb.

Dr. Reis was very boring in my opinion and did not teach the class well. He does post all his lectures and attendance is not mandatory. The grading scale is way off with 20% of the grade being HW and the other 80% being quizzes. Doing badly on one quiz will wreck your grade and Dr. Reis doesn't make many if any accommodations.

Dr. Ries is really nice and good professor! Attendance is not mandatory, all lectures are posted online but I recommend to watch absolutely the lectures! Homework assignment every week or every other online, quiz every other week online.The professor tried to make lectures interesting and easier material. 
PS. He does not give any extra credits
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Stats1200 isn't a difficult course. However, I couldn't stand his voice, he tries to hard to sound like a game show host. It made it difficult to pay attention. I eventually just got annoyed enough and stopped going to in person classes. Also he is very egotistical, I wouldn't recommend emailing him with any questions, he is extremely rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was overall easy but the professor is very unforgiving. missing a single quiz will leave you with an almost failing grade. All of the quizzes are weighted so heavily that it doesn't matter how well you do on the homework. Missing more than one question on the quizzes would also get you a low grade because of how each quiz was graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ries was overall a good professor! I didn't put much effort into the class because of my overall course load, but it was easy to pass! You do have to do the homework and study a bit for the quizzes, but as others have said, it's an easy class, and he's nice!

attendance is not mandatory, all lectures are posted online, homework assignment every week or every other online, quiz every other week online, very short quizzes and homework, overall very easy class, he tried to make lectures interesting

This man is unironically hilarious. Had him for 1200 on top of a STEM course load. The class was still a breeze. His grading scale is 25% homework, and 75% quizzes/tests. Everything is available online and if you need this to fulfill your major requirements, then take it with Ries. He's definitely a no bs guy, so don't slack and then beg for EC.

Pretty boring class but it's probably difficult to make stats a fun topic. Only complaint is he is pretty short with people. In class announcements if he had to repeat himself he would get a little mean.

FOR STAT 4510/7510!!! He was okay, nothing great, no huge complaints, class wasn't super difficult. My only complaint is that the way he has his exams set up makes the grading very subjective, with the questions being very open ended and short form, but wanting very specific things in the answers.

He has a fairly easy class. You dont have to show up and his lectures are recorded online. His homework system is really nice and you can get help on every assignment with Tiger Tutors. He's really loud so don't go at 9 AM. Nice guy and easy class, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable about what he is teaching but very boring. I took the course online and it was pretty simple. There is homework every week and a quiz about every other week. The course is very lecture heavy. The lectures are good but like I said, he is sometimes very boring and monotone.
Such a great guy who genuinely cares about his students. Keeps lectures interesting and posts all lectures online. A pretty basic intro to statistics.
This class was fine, but nothing special. Don't email him with urgent questions because it will take him forever to respond.

I'm not a math person, and stats is not exciting to me, but Dr. Ries made it fair and manageable. He posts videos of all his lectures which is helpful if you have a reason to stay in your room instead of sit in a classroom. For me, it was more work than my other classes, but despite the work and stress I still earned a grade I was alright with.

He is a great teacher! There is webwork each week and then a quiz every other week and that it is. He gives great lectures with examples on how to do it. You also don't have to go to class as he has recorded lectures for all of them. He also lets you drop your lowest 2 webworks and lowest quiz grade.

The class is mainly online and the test are pretty easy. The only thing is the testing website has many errors, and reaching out to him doesn't help. If it's an error on the test, I definitely think it should be fixed since it is vital for your grade. But he seems very nonchalant and not caring about it.
I ADORE him. Super great teacher, very manageable class

He does not budge outside of his office hours. I tried to reach out multiple times asking for a different time and he just referred me to a TA that did not help. I work full-time while online school part-time and they do not offer much evening or weekend help. I had to end up taking time off work just to meet with him for help on subject matter.

I didn't really personally communicate with him, but he was very forgiving by dropping a few of the lowest quiz scores (which probably saved my grade) and did a great job of clearly laying out the schedule and what he expected of you.

Because this class was online and asynchronous, I didn't get to know him personally, but overall this class was what I expected. He ended up excusing an additional lower quiz score at the end of the semester, which definitely helped my grade. As long as you stay on top of the lectures and work through the workbook, you'll do fine in this class.
Very boring professor but his exams are quite easy. There is weekly homework which is tedious but it boosts your grade. If you do the problems in the workbook, you should be fine

He's straight up mean. He has no idea how to treat people, especially during a global pandemic, and does not extend empathy at all. I emailed him to dispute a grade I was confused about (it turns out I just mistook a 6 for a 9) and he was extremely rude in the email. I realize it was a stupid mistake, but he treated me like a moron.

He's not a flexible professor at all, especially during the pandemic. Everything is based on chapter quizzes, 3 exams, and a 25% final. The book does not help with understanding the material so just watch his lectures, he records them. When you email him, you'll either get no response or it'll be short.

I took his stat 1200 class before/during the COVID-19 pandemic. not only did he add on a bunch of work, but he also gave no extensions, extra credit, or makeups. You would think during a global pandemic, he would be a bit more flexible. if you want an understanding professor, look elsewhere

I took his STAT 1200 class as one of my gen ed courses. Probably one of the most straightforward classes I've ever taken. 5-10% of students show up for lecture and lab. Material is easy enough as an introductory level course. He can get weird sometimes with questions about foot fetishes, but it's fine for the most part.

Dr. Ries is a great professor. He explains stat concepts really well and everything he explains is easy to understand. He posts lectures online so you are not missing out on material if you can't go to class one day. I would recommend going to the lectures because that was very helpful for me. I 100% recommend this class!

Have never even seen Lawrence as this was entirely taught by a TA. That being said, the class is super easy and you get a formula book to use on tests. I have barely been to class this year and will be getting an A. Homework is also pretty easy, not much of a time commitment.

Never went to his lectures and did pretty good on the tests, but you have to watch the videos to do good in the class. You have online assignments every week that took awhile sometimes. He gave a lot of example in lecture and use the practice tests to study for exams.
Is very clear in lectures and is good about uploading all lecture material online.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Lewis's class structure facilitates a healthy learning environment where all questions are welcome. She frequently asks for feedback on her class and is willing to make changes to the syllabus to support our learning. She's always willing to laugh, joke around, talk, give advice, and have serious conversations with her students!

Dr. Lewis was incredible! Her lectures were detailed and she is very passionate about this class. I missed a lot of school due to illness and she was so accommodating and caring. Course was not easy but not overly difficult. Come prepared for discussion every class. Every professor should be like Dr. Lewis!!!!!!!

Dr. Lewis is a great professor who is passionate about what she teaches. She's patient and understanding of any problems or questions you may have, and is very accommodating in my experience. As long as you watch the lectures and do each weekly assignment, you should have little to no problem doing well in this class.

This is one of the best professors I have had at Mizzou. She is so caring and works so hard to do what is best for each of her students. If you ever have the chance to take her classes, DO IT. Absolutely loved her and her teaching style. Amazing professor. 10/10.

Prof Manion is one of my favorite professors. He expects you to participate, but nothing about his class is difficult if you do the reading. He tells you everything expects. He is funny, easy to talk to, and understands. I'm only upset he isn't teaching a class I signed up for anymore. 10/10 would take again!!

I had Lee Manion last semester as a freshman for Honors Epic Destinies. He's amazing and the quintessential college professor. I cannot recommend him enough! He was so funny and engaging. Discussions are mostly student-led. I read 1/4 of the texts, but I still got a 100% in the class. If you participate in class and take notes you'll be fine.

LOVE THIS PROF! Very kind & flexible. His lectures are entertaining, engaging, and funny (which is hard to do in a middle-age-English course) He leaves amazing feedback on essays and grades very fair. The only issue I have is that the grade has been locked on canvas the entire semester. However, the accessibility of the canvas page makes up for it
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's one of the best professor's I've had at this school. His lectures are funny and he's great at putting complex ideas in a simple way the class can understand. He always has an interesting perspective on the reading we do (although there is A LOT of reading). He's accessible outside of class and really personable too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Santoro is an amazing professor and leads some awesome discussions with students taking the spotlight. Loved talking with her outside of class about various historical topics. I can tell she loves her work and talking with students, and even though I'm not a history major or anything adjacent really I wish I could take more classes with her.

Dr. Santoro is a really nice and caring person, but as a professor was not for me. Be expected to read a minimum of like 20 pages every day for her class. There aren't many grades in this class, so be make sure you do the readings and participate a lot in class. Even when there are assignments expect to not know what you are being graded on.

Dr. Santoro is a really nice and caring person, but as a professor was not for me. Be expected to read a minimum of like 20 pages every day for her class usually it was even more than that because there were multiple readings. The bulk of your grade is participation, so if you are in a class full of people who talk a lot, good luck getting points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures were basically review sessions. You learn the topics before class and he just goes into it more. Lectures mandatory and not recorded. Does provide a review sheet and practice exams which are really great, a few past exam questions were used.  I am just not a fan of his teaching style.
Hard tests
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about his students. He gives all the answers practically with his quizzes, practice tests, and homework assignments. He also is really willing to adapt to the classes needs, and is an entertaining teacher. A lot of reading, but if you pair the reading with his lectures you will do well and understand.

He's a fairly good lecturer and truly cares about his students being successful. However, if you want good notes on the lecture, you will likely have to go back and look at the slides after class. Other than that, the tests are pretty straightforward, and he provides plenty of material to prepare you well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Liscum is a good professor who cares about how his students do. It is often difficult to keep up with notes in class because he goes extremely fast, but there is just a lot of material to cover, and the slides are posted after class. The tests are easy as long as you study the learning objectives and take the practice quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, exams are based off lecture slides. Iclicker points are important for this class. He gives plenty on review materials before each exam. There is weekly reading and homework assignments on Pearson.

While I wasn't a very big fan of him at the beginning of the semester his dedication to improving the learning of his students was deeply appreciated. Half way through the semester he gives a mid-semester survey for students to give their input and he goes through and reads each on and discusses what he will do differently based on the responses.

He is nice, will sometimes get agitated if there is no class participation/lots of talking, which is fair.   Majority of the tests are from lecture and the lecture slides.  The practice quizzes are often helpful and even sometimes will have extremely similar questions.  Just pay attention, study the lecture slides, and you will be fine.
Amazing professor, genuinely cares about his students.
He was an amazing teacher and wanted nothing but the best for his students. Although he was tough on the students in his class, he does this out of wanting the best for his students.
The structure of this class is not good. Tests are very hard to understand and you will spend everyday of the week working on homework. For this being a freshman level entry class, it was ridiculous.

I actually enjoyed Dr. Liscum's class. It is very homework heavy (online video and worksheet twice a week) and you have around seven tests per semester. However, the vidoes are very helpful and he does a lot of group work and review during lectures. As long as you study you should be fine. He is very easy to approach so use his student hours!

He is absolutely terrible; his tests questions are so hard, and the test questions does not make any sense at all. The structure of the class is terrible, and it feels like you are teaching yourself. Do not take his class!!!!

This class feel irrelevant to biology making it difficult to understand, the tests are extremely difficult and the final will most likely break your grade in the end because each question has such a high point value your only able to miss 5-6 on a 50 question exam to maintain the grade that is wanted.

Online lecture 2x a week. About 30 min of video & short worksheet (You will always get full credit on this). In person lecture is "active learning" for the online lectures. Tests are an application of knowledge, pay attention to lectures and do the worksheets, you'll get an A. Liscum is a pretty chill and interesting teacher.

The professor was all right, he did not teach anything. The tests are way too hard for an intro-level biology class, and the questions tend to trick you. discussion and lab are beyond useless for course material. You're expected to learn strictly from online videos and tedious worksheets, meaning the professor never teaches anything.

Overall one of the rudest professors I had this semester. His attitude towards the students and the class made lectures something I did not look forward to. The class it self isn't the worst. The weekly assignments are time consuming but they're easy. The tests aren't great and are way harder than they should be.

One of the most rude profs I've had. Very unpleasant during lectures and genuinely makes my day worse. Homework was pretty easy although time consuming, but doesn't adequately set you up for test success. Be ready to spend a good amount of time studying, the tests focus on application and not how to execute what's learned in class. Try to avoid.

The material itself was very easy, it was always talked about multiple times and ways, so it was easier to understand the concepts. Dr. Liscum is extremely easy to approach and have a conversation with, and has office hours almost every day of the week. What I didn't like about the class was group work and structure, but the professor was amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although the material was not very tough, Dr. Liscum made it hard. His tests questions were difficult to understand. Don't even bother seeing him outside of class because he will not care what you have to say. During test week, you will have lab, discussion, a Simbio lab due, and online homework due, so you barely get anytime to study.

The structure is a flipped classroom where the actual lectures serve as an "active learning" day. He believes heavily on applying what you learn instead of memorizing. His tests can be viewed as difficult because of his styling of questions. Attend office hours as they can be extremely helpful to hear from the professors and other students.

Professor Liscum is awesome! He requires you to be responsible for your own learning, and his class structure is flipped and test heavy. However, there are a total of 7 exams every two weeks that cover very little material compared to other science courses. This makes getting an A easier. Attendance is mandatory and lots of group work. Cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There are 7 tests and a final. You will have to do a lot of studying. It is flip class so all the lectures are outside of class and you review the material in class once a week. The labs are awful, not at all related to the course. Liscum is a good professor and explains material well but the structure of the class is horrible.
Professor Liscum is very approachable and I enjoyed his class although sometimes it was a little boring because it was rather easy.
i loved this class. mannie can be a sassbox at some points, but he truly is knowledgeable. he is not the only professor though. sara bush and her husband are also heavily involved in this course.

This course is a TON of work but it was one of the courses at Mizzou that I walked away from feeling as though I improved as a writer and student. He fosters quite a bit of class participation so that you are consistently engaging with the material. He also is good at giving you adequate feedback about what you can do to improve. Genuinely cares!

Looooong online lectures and mandatory attendance to lectures that are largely useless since we learn all content asynchronously. Group work every single class is the worst part. Seems like a genuinely cool person, but the course itself is absolutely horrible in every single way. Would take another of his classes. Very passive-aggressive in emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I thought that he was overall a pretty good teacher. The thing that was bad was that a lot of the online lectures were around 40 minutes twice a week. Super time-consuming but, if you took notes you'll do fine. You don't have to go to one of the class periods which is nice and I thought his in-class lectures were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lecture, discussion, lab, and online lab do not correlate with each other. Skip class and watch your grade tank. I calculated the average for all tests combined. 78.6%. He will blame the class for the grade. Dude, if the average for your tests is a C, YOU are the problem. Homework graded like a childs T-ball game with participation trophies.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Two long online homework assignments per week, along with 7 difficult bi-weekly tests not including the final, long labs every other week that don't correlate to anything learned in lecture, and you'll mostly be teaching it all to yourself. There is little feedback given on tests and none given on homework assignments, leaving studying difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bi-weekly tests are short(13-18 questions) along with 2 short homework assignments per week. Lab component which can either save or ruin your grade(attendance is a big part). You'll learn and retain a lot of information which will help you out on the final. You'll also be in a group of 3 other people so hope you are social. Overall fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is extremely well organized. Bi-weekly tests and mandatory attendance/ online assignments (for participation) dictate your grade more than labs. Lecture can be a little dry and repetitive, but he is very fair and accessible outside of class. No extra credit is available.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: What to say besides you will have to do a lot of work to understand the material. Almost all of the class is group based and there are 7 tests excluding the final. You don't have come to class everyday but, when you expected to be there, he takes attendance. There are also a lot of labs but none of the lab information is included in the test.
He is a great human and really cares about his students. You have to do the work to get a decent grade but it is not too difficult. I would definitely take another class with him.

I loved taking this class with Dr. L! He is a very funny and personable guy, and although there is a lot of homework and work to do, he breaks it down into small pieces and makes it pretty simple and easy to understand. He responds to emails quickly, and is available for help often. I liked the group structure of the class as well.

Get ready to teach yourself. The class revolves around dragonflies and geese. He wasnt the best at explaining how those two subjects correlated with what he was trying to teach. There is also 7 test and a final, and the test are difficult because they dont pertain to what he taught

There were seven tests and a final that were challenging and I never felt very prepared, even though I attended most to all classes. I normally do well in science classes but this was very hard and Dr. L was not always helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It doesn't matter that your only grades will be 2 quizzes and 3 tests. The lectures cover everything you need to know and aren't difficult to follow. The practice questions he gives (have to go to class for!) are very similar to the exams. Also, he's the funniest person ever and really cares about his students. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yanguang's class will not be a source of stress for you. Graded solely on 2 quizzes 2 exams and one non-cumulative final. All of these will have clear expectations on what you'll be tested over, and they will be problems you've done before in a lecture or in a review. There's not much to say, watch the lectures and you'll get an A.
Great professor, homework is optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Come to class , write the notes and understand it you get an A
He asked a kid if our test was easy, after he responded saying no he proceeded to laugh in his face about how hard it was. Literally prides himself on the difficulty of his exams.
Horrible.

Definitely one of the hardest classes you'll take if you aren't an economics major. That being said, unlike most of the classes at Mizzou, you actually have to work for an A in this one. He is incredibly knowledgeable and if you can force yourself to listen to his lectures, you'll learn a lot about the stuff that happens every day in our economy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you show up to class on a regular basis you should be fine. He'll occasionally give out xc just for showing up (he likes to give extra clicker questions and points on Fridays as well). As for exams, so long as you study the practice exams and the hw you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is by far one of the most challenging courses I have taken at Mizzou, but also one of the most rewarding.  A lot of people complain about this course- they're just unwilling to work for their grade and will be in for a sorry shock when they hit the real world. Dr. Thomas is a phenomenal professor with tons of knowledge that is very important!

Dr. Thomas is a phenomenal professor. His class was extremely challenging but very rewarding. Dr. Thomas really cares that you comprehend the material- it is very important stuff! He has a deep knowledge of economics and passion for finance. Incredibly smart guy who deserves much more credit.

This is literally the worst class at Mizzou.  Professor Thomas is extremely smart but does not understand how to teach economics to non-majors. His class is boring, as he just basically lectures by speaking at you.  His exams are next to impossible, and  l find a way to ask 4 questions in just 1.  Homework is nearly impossible.  He doesn't care
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Thomas's class covered a substantial range of material; however, tests and quizzes were multiple choice and always included opportunities for extra credit. Slide material was up-to-date (usually  to the most recent month) and useful for studying for exams   Dr. Thomas is opinionated but well-reasoned, respectful, and available for extra help.
Lectures are the most important thing.

Dr. Thomas is no doubt an expert when it comes to Economics- especially the recent financial crisis. He has a very firm grasp on the subject matter. He is probably the most intellectual professor I have had to date at Mizzou. That being said, his class was also unnecessarily difficult. The amount of material covered in class was insane.

Horrible. Lectures are impossible to pay attention to, powerpoint are less than useless, and as a teacher he is utterly incompetent. He has admitted himself that his quizzes and tests are impossible. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. It will wreck your GPA and your soul.

Awful Experience. There was no clarity as to what was going to be on the tests. Not to mention the tests were nearly impossible. Lectures dragged on making it difficult to pay attention and the PowerPoints were more like books filling up each slide to the brim with information. Would NOT recommend taking Econ with him.

She is one of the most caring professors I have had at Mizzou! The tests are straight forward and open note. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and shows that. Her class is extremely engaging and easy. I definitely recommend her has a professor

Kind and cares deeply about her subject. Class was all lectures and notes with no homework. Lectures are detailed and easy to understand. There are random one-question attendance quizzes. Biggest criticism is that on the 4 tests we took, I got 3 As and one C. The C dropped my grade by 6%, so the tests are weighted heavily; it wasn't even the final.

Neier is the most preachy professor I've ever had. Class includes constant reminders that students should be 'learners, not just finishers'. Content quizzes are open notes and questions come from the lectures/materials. She claims students should spend 9 hours a week JUST on her course, which is insane bc there is 0 writing or discussion posts.

This class all sounds made up, and she repeats everything she says, which is essentially a whole lot of nothing. I can't complain because the online class is really not much work. But we have 4 online quizzes which are just annoying. She pulls from like 15+ sources, gives too similar of answers, and writes dumb questions.

Professor Neier has never taught in a classroom herself, but she sure has a lot to say about how we should teach. This class was so hard to sit through, she talked about the same thing over and over again. What could be said in 5 minutes, took her over an hour to cover. Take this class online, or with someone else to save your sanity and time

This class was extremely easy but I really wish I took it online. Professor Neier talked in circles the entire class. 
The content is easy to understand, but I always left class irritable because I felt like I had just wasted an hour and 15 minutes of my time. All of this info could be googled and found online in less time.

Professor Neier's class was kinda intolerable. She talks in circles the entire class and NEVER gets through the slides. I almost fall asleep every. single. time. She is very outgoing and passionate however, I don't think I learned anything. All of the info given can easily be accessed online and is base level. She is lowkey passive aggressive. ew.
Very kind and helpful!
Dr. Neier is great! She tells you exactly what you need to know to pass the class and improve as an educator. She made an effort to interact with every student personally, which was really sweet!

Had Dr. Neier for both LTC2200 in person and LTC1100 online! She truly is passionate about what she teaches, but having to sit through a 75-minute lecture about the same information over and over again makes it easy to zone out. LTC1100 was easy, but you're only graded on a few things so it's important to remember to do the weekly assignment(s).
Very enthusiastic about the profession, but hypes everything up too much. Technically, attendance is not mandatory but they're many attendance checks throughout the year so go to class.
Dr. Neier is my favorite professor at Mizzou! She is enthusiastic and full of energy which makes the class fly by.  I wish all my professors were just like her!

Even though I was online she was an amazing professor. Provided plenty of information and materials needed to complete assignments. Mainly reflection assignments and a few projects. Always available for questions or concerns and is SUPER friendly. Definitely learn a lot and enjoy the class.

She's full of energy and really cares about her students. She can definitely talk for a long time though about things that do not matter for the class. There are a lot of readings but honestly I didn't do most of them and still got an A.
BRO SHES SIMPLY NOT GOOD

Let me tell YOU Dr. Neier is a firecracker! She is full of energy and obviously loves her job. Personally its a little too much. She requires attendance which sucks because this class felt like it went on forever. Every education major has taken this class, so if you have any questions just ask them and theyll be happy to help :)
Easy ONLINE class!!! Dr. Neier is something else, and youll see it in LTC 2200. Shes very energetic online, and is pretty easy going.

Could take me out with one punch. Makes 15 min feel like 2 hours. TOO Enthusiastic!! Loves using quotes ON EVERY SLIDE and laser pointer. Pretends she knows everyone's name, will ask you your name every time you participate ("what's your name again?")
Super sweet and caring great class
I have never had a professor like Dr. Neir. She is rude, can be unprofessional, and is a very poor communicator. Doesn't seem to be the best at juggling multiple things.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class could have been enjoyable, however, she was rude. Many people in my class had a problem with her. She was very unprofessional with responding to emails and would get mad at students for not doing what she wanted, but could not do because of the lack of clarity. She was not understanding and never accountable in any way to her students.

She has an easy class, but is so rude and constantly calls out her students and calls them unprofessional when she is the one being unprofessional. She NEVER answers emails or messages sent to her, and then gets mad at students when something isn't finished because she never answered the question asked in an email. horrible.

She is so mean and takes every chance to call out her students for everything they do wrong. She is not approachable at all. She called like half the class unprofessional when she is unprofessional by never responding to emails. She was the worst professor I have had. Do not recommend.
shes super chill and so sweet loved this class
Despite it being a lecture class, it feels more like a discussion class. We often fall behind on our class content and lecture notes because we never end discussions during lecture time.

Honestly hated this class along with LTC2200.  Her lectures contain information that could be covered in a 15 minute period, but are more around at least 30-50 minutes. She makes information seem more complex than what it is, and is extremely boring. On a positive note its obvious she cares about her job and students and the classes are very easy.
Such an awesome teacher! You can tell how much she loves teaching and how much she cares about her students. Overall one of the best teachers at Mizzou!

She is my favorite! I feel like other professors are just bleh, but she hops on zoom excited and welcoming. She is a breath of fresh air, and her class content is awesome. Anyone who is in college of education, she will be your fav, and her class content is super interesting!

I took this class and LTC 1100 with this professor. I had only heard good things about her. I am sad to say that I am very disappointed. She made the class content purposely seem harder and complex for no real reason. She did not handle criticism well. Also, this class was not about learning, it was about reciting info back to her.

Before I took her class i never heard a bad thing about Leigh, but there has got to be a difference between having her in person and during virtual learning. A lot of us had bad 1 on 1 experiences with her and her lecture/rubrics are unclear and hard to follow. Shes either the nicest person ever or kind of insensitive and passive aggressive
I dropped out of the College of Education because of her classes. The material could have been interesting and taught well. Could have. Also, I'm not the only one who changed their major.

Leigh is, hands-down, the best! She is always so welcoming to her students and makes sure they're taken care of. Her class also has lots of good content that she conveys so well. I genuinely can't say enough good things about her. If you have the chance, take this class!

Leigh is extremely caring and personable! Her charisma kept her lectures interesting during in-person classes and she went above and beyond to accommodate students during the transition to online classes at Mizzou. Even though my class was large, she was always easily accessible when I had questions or wanted to know more about a topic.

Leigh is super amazing. She makes class interesting and is very knowledgable about student health and well-being. However, all of the homework is online and you do not need to attend to get an A. If you do the homework you WILL get an A.

I LOVE LEIGH! She is the sweetest professor I have ever had. So pure and caring to everyone. This class is required for education majors but I would take any of Leigh's classes. Attendance is pretty mandatory but it's not hard to make up if you miss. No tests and some days off for extra work time on upcoming projects.
The kindest most understanding professor on campus. No doubt.

Leigh is an amazing teacher. She is very helpful with everything and gives you many chances to make up missed points. She does do random attendance checks, but I missed class a few times and never missed one. All tests and quizzes are online and if you take good notes are super easy
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has such a booming personality and is so nice and really connects with the whole class, its amazing how she teaches.

Leigh is the brightest person in the room most times! She engages with everyone in the lecture hall, and brings in researchers, members of school administration, and the local community. Leigh truly cares about you as a person, and it very clearly shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Neier was an amazing professor and really helped me grow as a future educator. The classes are fun. She always is so helpful and cheery, it really sets the mood for your day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is obviously passionate about the class, but there was not a lot of "important" information discussed. The content was very repetitive and was very elementary and obvious.

An actual angel. The most giving person in the world and cares about her students so much. Even though she teaches education courses, some non education majors take her classes and she tries to include them and their majors as much as possible. She tries to make everything relevant and is super understanding and compassionate.

Simply amazing. She absolutely loves what she does, and it is apparent every single time she walks into the classroom. If you didn't already want to be a teacher before, she will completely change your mind after one lecture. I truly hope I get to have her again as my professor. You learn a lot about how to teach, and how to care for your students.

Leigh is the sweetest most caring person ever. She puts you as a person ahead of you as a student. SHE IS AMAZING. If you get the opportunity to take her class definitely take it. There are in class points and you need those to pass the class, but they are easy easy easy points if you even slightly pay attention.

Leigh is probably the most passionate person I've ever met. While she's still professional, she feels like your bestie. She always goes the extra mile to make sure that her class is working for you. She understands the life of students and accomodates stress by moving test dates, letting class out early during midterms and busy weeks in general.

Caring and motivational. Crazy passionate about education and used relatable, engaging lectures to teach. She wants to know each student by name, even in a lecture of 100+ people, and always makes time to respond to students in/out of class.

Leigh is an amazing professor. Her classes are interesting and she always has good stories to tell that keeps the class interested. She is flexible and her tests are all open note but they're pretty simple if you do the out of class readings
She is the best professor I've ever had. She is always in a good mood and very willing to help. She is passionate about what she teaches and it shows in her attitude during lectures.
She is the ultimate GOAT

Attendance isn't really mandatory, per se, but she takes random attendance checks throughout the semester that are worth points. She's very upbeat and positive every single day, which is refreshing. Also, she is very willing to move things around and be flexible if it's really needed. She cares about her students wellbeing.
Leigh is just amazing. She really works to make class interesting and tries to get to know all her students. Go to class and you'll get an A!
Leigh is one of the best professors I have had. Very well respected in the education department. Her lectures are interesting and she does her best to make students laugh. Leigh is truly caring.

Legit the BEST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. Leigh is so enthusiastic and happy every single day of class. You can easily tell that she loves what she does and this class is soooo easy. I ended up getting over 100%. She does take attendance on random day so you do have to come to class, but trust me ITS WORTH IT

Leigh was an amazing professor! She really engages with everyone in the class. You have to go to class if you want a decent grade but you'll want to go to class anyways because Leigh's lectures are amazing. Would take every class she offers.

-LTC 4085 School Health & Student Wellbeing  -Leigh has a positive attitude and makes lectures exciting -This is the number one class of the day I looked forward to -No textbook but she provides resources on Blackboard that you will use -You will learn how to care for your students needs in order to help them better succeed with curriculum
best professor ever. gives lots of chances if you miss points. tests are online with no time limit. she cancels class a lot.

Leigh is probably the best professer I have ever had. She is the most positive, outgoing person out there. Everything about her classes are perfect, not many assignments but most are simple. She is extremely intelligent when it comes to her subject matter.

Leigh is a wonderful educator and one of the kindest human beings I have ever met. She truly practices what she preaches! She made the hour fly by, and never ceased to be enthusiastic and well-prepared. The class isn't hard and very easy to get an A in. A MUST for any education major!

She is probably my favorite professor so far. She's funny and super friendly! There are no exams of any kind, just easy little open booknote "checks" on TopHat. She also takes attendence pretty regularly through TopHat as well. Would definitely recommend for all students even though it is an education class (I'm health sciences and I enjoyed it)!
seriously one of the best professors ive ever had

I don't think I've ever enjoyed a lecture as much as I enjoy Leigh's! She always keeps it interesting and engaging. Her lectures are very interactive. The course doesn't have any exams, but there is a heavy use of the app TopHat for attendance checks and assignments. I love this class and would definitely recommend taking a class with her.

Ms. Neier is so nice! She is always willing to help you if you miss class for a good reason or need help. She does take attendance, but her tests are easy and the lectures really aren't all that bad. Super enthusiastic. Would take again!

She gets you so engaged in the topic and loves to tell stories. The class is interesting and so easy. Final is optional if you like your grade and the exams are super easy. She does 10 random attendance checks but going to class isn't a big deal because it's actually interesting.

Literally one of the best people I think I've ever met. She is so passionate and knowledgable about everything she teaches. She is so nice! She works hard to engage students and to get to know them on a personal level. And the final is optional but you'll most likely have a good enough grade you won't have to take it. Leigh is honestly the BEST!

LOVE LOVE LOVE Leigh! and the class! She is so helpful and is truly interested in you doing well and understand the material! Super easy and fun/interesting lectures. Go to class and you will get an A! Definitely try and take her section. By far the best professor I've had at Mizzou.
Leigh is so nice! Her class is so easy just make sure you go to class. She tells you when you need to be there though for her in-class checks so she even helps you there.

Leigh is a great teacher! She's easy to listen to and you can tell is really interested and cares about what she's teaching which helps to keep you engaged. I didn't use the text book once so it's not necessary but pretty much show up to class and you'll have an easy A!!

Show up to class (attendance taken) and have a ratable IQ and you will get an A in this class. SOOOOOOOO easy and actually engaging. Neier understands what education is about and its not about tricking ppl into getting bad grades!!! So easy, no worries, try to get Neier-love her! Very professional and great person
Leigh is awesome.  She cares about students and keeps class entertaining. Would love to take another class with her. Easy A if you ay attention to powerpoints and lectures.

She is amazing. She really cares about her students. She is very enthusiastic and very flexible with everything. The class is very easy. There is a lot of class discussion and she loves hearing everyone's thoughts.
The class was so easy and she was very nice!
Leigh is awesome!! Her tests were very clear and straight forward. I really enjoyed her classes and enthusiasm. I wish I could have her again for another class.

He's nice enough and tries to have a good rapport with students, but he's just not a good lecturer. He goes off on random tangents and told us to write notes on what he says and not what was on the slides. He also didn't set aside enough time at the end, and we had to teach the last unit to ourselves. Uses iClicker every class for attendance.

Mandatory attendance for a 9 AM class. If you email him with an excused absence he will forget to change it in the grade book. All the tests are on Canvas and he does not go back and check to make sure the computer didn't mis-mark something as incorrect. Lazy teaching style.

The best professor ever! He loves teaching, he explains each topic clearly and with passion. He doesn't care about grades that much, very easy grader, if u explain your case he just changes your grade to whatever you needed. Exams are online.
Great lectures. Very easy grader, all tests are online and open note. Funny guy too. Attendance does count for points, though.

When I was in his class all his exams are online but they do have a time limit. He does have mandatory attendance but it is flexible, you can miss like 10-15 classes. He does have some reading but he provides it.
Takes attendance on Iclicker daily, all tests and quizzes were online but don't be fooled, they were somewhat tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor cares about the topic material and students. He uses Iclicker religiously, but that can be navigated around. All the exams and quizzes were online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Lord is a good lecturer, especially with topics he particularly enjoys. He is understanding and wants his students to succeed. The class content is fairly straightforward, as long as you go to class. He does take attendance via iClicker and if you don't go to lecture you will miss material not on the slides. Quizzes were fairly easy.

Dr. Lombardo is a great professor, but thermo is hard. His exams are just like the homework's for the unit. You are able to opt in or out of the homework, but homework was best way to study. During lectures, he reads slides then does example problems that are posted, but he does not post the answers so you must go to lecture to see the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy. Thermo is a hard class and he really tells you how to succeed. Just study and come to class and ask questions if you don't understand.

The material is hard, but he does a good job teaching it. The exams are all very similar to homework problems. He's super funny and makes lectures pretty tolerable. The textbook and homework are 100% the best resources to do well on exams.

Lombardo is a G. However, 4 exams make up your entire grade. Thermo is no easy course. If you do the homework and know how to read the tables, you'll be fine. Don't half-ass this course because you won't pass. Mad respect for Lombardo though; great guy.

The class was pretty simple and exams were pretty much just like the homework. With that said 28 percent had to withdrawal and many more failed. This is due to exams being worth nearly all the points unless you opt in to homework. The exams themselves are very straightforward if you do the homework.

Lombardo tries to make Thermodynamics fun and applicable to the real world. He might not have the best lectures as he just reads off the notes he has posted on canvas, but he tries to crack a joke here and there. 95% of your grade depends on your exam scores and the other 5% is homework. 25% of the class with dropout or fail, you have been warned.

Now this class is not a cake walk but Professor Lombardo definitely makes it a little bit better. He's probably the funniest professor I've had so far. Make sure to nail down the materials from the first two exams, if you do not learn this material, I can almost guarantee you will not pass the class so make sure to study.

Lombardo is a hilarious and very nice dude. The lectures themselves are enjoyable and can give you a base to understand the material, however  you will definitely have to do a lot of learning outside the classroom. He is very strict with grading and wouldn't round me up 0.3% to get a B+ however so get ready for no extra credit or rounding.
Thermodynamics is no easy class. Dr. Lombardo was an amazing professor with lots of jokes. He helped me not only pass the class, but enjoy it too!

Dr. Lombardo is a lot of fun in class during lecture, so he makes Thermodynamics a lot of fun. But it's still a thermo class, so you need to be ready to work for your grade. Exams are very similar to the homework, and Lombardo is really helpful during office hours. Make sure you go to class and complete the homework, and you'll be fine.

The tests were remarkably difficult, and there was a clear distinction as to whether Lombardo graded a question versus your TA. (TA's were reasonable, Lombardo slashed points off at every place possible).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hands down the WORST teacher I have ever had. He prides himself in how many students fail or withdraw from his course. Avoid taking this class at all costs. The grading scale is 93% exams (which are impossible to complete in given time) and 7% homework if you opt in for it. If 40% of students are not passing the class, we are not the problem..he is
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lombardo is engaging during lectures and cracks lots of funny jokes. Although the class is insanely hard. Your grade is almost entirely based on tests which is 12 questions in total throughout the semester. If you do bad on one, you need to really good on the rest and he takes off lots of points. Hardest class Ive taken at Mizzou so far.
He isn't the best at the actual teaching part.

Dr. Lombardo is a very nice person. Homework was not required but I highly recommend it. That is where the good stops. Does not give a lot of partial credit on tests. 93% of your grade is based of tests. Be prepared to spend many hours out side of class learning the material on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unfortunately, Dr Lombardo gives NO feedback via homework or quizzes throughout the semester on where you need to improve or focus your studies. Your entire grade is based off 12 problems, timed, and they are random. Worst professor/teaching technique I have seen thus far at MIZZOU...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares about your learning, and he makes it fun to watch his lectures!

Lombardo is a really chill teacher and all but his class is very difficult. He doesn't give many points out and usually spends more time going over how to find the equations used and doesn't put up many examples. But wait there's more, your entire grade for the semester is based on 9 questions, so if you mess up on one of the tests you're screwed
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Lombardo is a very good teacher overall. He gives homework hints and does some of the problems in class.  His tests are all open book and open note, but you have to prepare still or you will not have enough time. Do no cheat and use the solutions manual for the homework.  He will catch you and report you to the provost.

Very challenging class, there must be a better way to teach it. There is no way the homework should be expected to be doable without online help. Class doesn't quite translate to the tests. Really learn ch. 3 and 4. Was his first semester teaching it, so may get better. He changed the way tests were weighted to help in the end.

Where to start. The lectures were rough, she didn't voice the vocab ever, and made you guess what was going on. She was very personable and kind, but the class wasn't structured well. Most of the weekly homework was a Youtube video that she wanted you to watch, and sometimes she would forget and give the same one multiple times, it felt disorderly.

She's a nice lady, but her class is very homework heavy. Instead of four lectures a week like the class is listed as, half of the lectures are replaced by large assignments, including dense youtube videos filled with vocab that “you may have to watch multiple times.” I'm learning ASL, but it's an exhausting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Incredibly uncomfortable contacting. She is a nightmare to get in contact with and actually work out the class. Pacing is too aggressive, and too many signs with no practice. 

Fine if you DO NOT have a disability, but she often tramples over it & other departments if you do, because they can't touch her. Infuriating and rude.

Logan is a fine prof, but there's so many tests. You will have two exams over different things in the same week. It's not too hard to pass her class with a good grade if you go to all lectures and do your hw. I had to practice sign a lot outside of hw and studying because I am slower learning new languages. You will be teaching yourself a lot.
Great teacher
Her camera quality is scary bad and she does not voice/ write many of the vocab words on screen so you have to guess what she's signing most of the time, just not a very good teacher but cool person.

Dr. Logan was a great prof. She is very caring and is great at reviewing any signs you aren't sure of. I will say that the receptive exams are not horrible if you do your homework, but the written ones suck. You have to read word-for-word what the book says in that unit. If you need a language credit I would suggest ASL.

Logan is okay if you do not have a disability.  Throughout my semesters with her, I have had to continually provide proof of my disability and it is definitely not an easy road.

As far as her teaching goes, she is not the best ASL teacher, but if you have a background in ASL you will be fine.  Just be prepared to learn the language on your own.

Dr. Logan was my favorite teacher at Mizzou. I took SLHS 1000-2150 and enjoyed it so much. It was my hardest class but it was so amazing to learn sign language with Dr. Logan. She genuinely cares about her students and will always offer extra help when asked. I don't think I would've enjoyed learning sign language if it wasn't for her.

Dr. Logan is very kind and cares very much about all her students. The class is tough but she wants you to succeed.
