This was my first class with her that had graded attendance and that was a little rough but I understand why she does it. You need to pay attention in lectures and do all the homework if you want to pass.

Dr. Logan is an amazing ASL teacher! If you're needing to take a foreign language, I highly recommend her class. There is a fair amount of homework, but there's enough assignments that if you forget something or do poorly on a test, it won't affect your grade as much. She is very caring and genuinely wants her students to do well.

If youre new to asl this is a very hard class to learn. Most of the lectures dont matter much as you learn mostly through the required text book and dvd. The lectures are mandatory and might be helpful if they were in person. She didnt do very well with covid and structuring the class with it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very kind and well-liked throughout the University, however she is a bit of a stickler in class. Attendance is mandatory and she doesn't take excuses very often. My biggest pet peeve about the class is the group work she makes us constantly do. I feel that nobody learns anything from these. Good teacher but needs a better teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stephanie is my favorite professor; she cares a lot about her students, and she makes the 8am Monday through Thursday class worth it. Attendance is worth points, there is homework every week, and I highly suggest starting your Final Performance Project as soon as possible. I encourage anyone and everyone to take this class!

Professor Logan is absolutely wonderful as an educator. She is clearly knowledgable and passionate about what she teaches. My only gripes are the mandatory attendance with little wiggle room (unless you have a doctor's note or a serious excuse, you will lose points). Also didn't love having to get up and interact with others everyday at 8:00 a.m.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great Prof! Amazing human being, that actually cares if you learn the language. She gave out her personal phone number on the first day of class, and there are always several TAs available. There is no reason to get anything but an A in this class. I highly recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Logan is the best professor I have ever had. She actually cares about her students. If you have the opportunity to take any ASL classes, DO IT. Just go to class every day and you will pass the class.

Dr. Logan is absolutely amazing. Sign Language has been my favorite class the past two semesters ( ASL 1 and ASL 2). She is funny and engaging and has a personal relationship with each of her students, even to the point that previous students who have graduated come back to visit! There is homework each week but as long as you do it you will pass
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I had her last semester for ASL 1 and plan to take her ASL 3 class. She cares about the students and the material. Class is fun and you learn a lot in a semester. There are homeworks and outside of class activities that make it impossible not to pass!
Dr. Logan is amazing! She really cares about her students and what she does. There are a lot of in class activities and out of class homework assignments. Overall, great teacher and great class
She is the best professor I have ever had!

Absolutely loved sign language last semester. Very helpful and really cares about all her students. Final seems scary at the beginning of the course but she makes it fun. Attendance is mandatory, and you basically get "free points" for going to class everyday and turning in the homework. You will not pass if you skip class.

rare breed of professor who actually care about each and every student. I had a sketchy classmate who missed class for like a month because she was "sick" and got out of performing her final on the first day and ended up performing the last day; now i don't advise that, but I'm sure even her grade was fine. she's here to help her students, really!
BEST class. Sign language made very easy to long and creative project at the end of semester
So amazing and really cares about her students.

She is an awesome awesome awesome teacher who genuinely cares about every student, their wellbeing, and how well they do in the class. If you put in effort, you can easily get an A in the class but it requires doing homework, attending study groups, and reading the book.

Mar was a fantastic, engaging professor, and I was excited to come to every class! I learned more in this class than any previous Spanish class. She clearly explained difficult to understand plot points & literary devices. However, she gives no partial credit on multi-select Canvas homework that composes 20% of the final grade. An A was a 94%.

LOTS OF HOMEWORK, BE PREPARED TO READ. Homework 2x a week. She will dock you points if you don't at least participate twice per class day. Heavy on projects. Had three projects due in one week and a final the next week. Goes through material very fast. Take notes and you'll be fine. Very fun and happy while teaching though. Wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Mar is by far the best Spanish professor I have had at Mizzou. She is always excited to teach class and makes you feel comfortable to learn and participate. Her homework can be difficult at times, but if you participate in class she will generously bump your grade at the end of the semester. She is an amazing person and educator!
Mar is a wonderful teacher, and person in general. She is very enthusiastic about teaching spanish, and will keep you engaged in class. I have only good things to say about her

Mar is by far the best Spanish professor Ive ever had. She is so sweet & engages the class really well. Shes very approachable and understanding, and communicates well with her students. Though the class is difficult, she makes it interesting and doable. I truly cannot recommend this professor enough!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Im a native spanish speaker, though spanish classes are hard for me because I didnt grow up learning textbook spanish or how to conjugate. When I tell you Ive never been so frustrated with how she grades-her instructions are never clear, hw is weighted heavier than tests. Basically impossible to get an A, let alone a B.

In 8 years of spanish classes, Mar is the best spanish professor I've ever had. She is sweet, funny, and loves to connect with her students. She assigns some tough readings and projects that seem daunting, but she is super accessible outside of the classroom. She even helped me prepare for a job interview. Get ready to work hard but learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic, always has a smile on her face! Not a super easy class but she explains concepts well and makes students feel comfortable asking questions when they don't understand something. As long as you're prepared to do the homework and go to class everyday, I definitely would recommend taking this class with her!

She is very enthusiastic about what she teaches. Had fun in her class and learned quite a bit. Not a tough grader but you need to do your homework and cannot miss class. Participation is very important too.

Great instructor who is very engaged in class and grades somewhat easy. You have to go to class and only get 2 absences total (whether they're excused or not). If you participate a few times each class you'll be fine. A few papers and one group paper/presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Huneycutt was definitely knowledgeable, but the class was poorly designed and by the end of it, we were about 3 weeks behind the syllabus. Reading assignments for the week were huge and we were expected to talk about them in depth in class for points. Not hard to get a good grade in with effort (extra credit!), but frustrating and stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Huneycutt is clearly very knowledgable in the field but is not equipped to teach. She is nearly impossible to reach outside of class, the syllabus changes drastically with little to no notice, and loads of reading is assigned the night before discussion. Grading takes FOREVER and overall the class is conducted poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very well educated and always happy to discuss any time period in history. She also loves giving valuable feedback.

In general, the class seemed to be structured horribly. She never seemed to post assignments, so if your grade sucked, you were kind of stuck with it. While the lectures may have been good, it didnt make up for the fact that there was hardly anyway to show what you had learn. Also, she was very hard to reach out to outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Huneycutt is an entertaining lecturer and you can tell she is passionate about her field. Outside of class, expect to read a lot (especially for the honors section), as well as use the textbook to fill in gaps from lecture. Also, show up to lecture for occasional extra credit. Three papers, short quizzes, and discussions determine grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I worked harder in this class than in any class I have taken in two years of college at Mizzou. Her lectures are challenging and assume youve done the assigned reading beforehand. She demands a lot of writing, but gives excellent feedback and is willing to read several drafts. When I finally got an A on my third paper, I knew Id earned it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor doesn't use canvas or put grades online at all. Rarely gives feedback and grades essays really tough. Rarely gives out A's on assignments. Lots of papers and extra readings. Way too much work for a 1000 level class! Would highly recommend choosing a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's an engaging lecturer, though since she rarely uses visuals it's sometimes tough to gauge how important some bits are. Quizzes are extra credit, and 75% of your grade comes from the three term papers. The remaining quarter is from the final, which is basically just a rehash of all of her previous quizzes. Go to lecture, read, and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Super nice professor. She lectures with no visuals which can get boring if you go to class. Gives 5 pop quizzes through the semester that are for extra credit, but are super hard and you need at least a 60% to get any. They can be hard but she reuses them on the final. 3 essays fairly graded, final half reused quiz ?s and an essay.
Medieval classes are great

Really fun class with well-chosen readings.  It is just clear that this professor loves her subject and likes interacting with students.  She spends all Friday afternoon writing letters of recommendation for students; everyone wants one from her because she truly cares about helping students and their futures.

I took Prof. Huneycutt's England Before the Glorious Revolution class and loved it!  She does not use powerpoints which is a bummer but for me her lectures kept me interested.  She is really the nicest person and is willing to help anyone who asks for it! Offers extra credit too

The class was great and I learned a lot.  I really liked the textbooks and the outside readings were well-chosen.  There is a no make up policy for quizzes but only 50% of the points count for your grade; the rest is extra credit.  Lots of opportunity for extra credit made this class easy to get an A in.

The professor is a huge stickler about grammar and rambles alot.Class is interesting but disjointed.  Her attendance requirements for quizzes are excessive there are no makeups no matter what the excuse. Avoid her class.
TA a horrible grader. Teacher knows here topic but way to much work for a 1000 level class.
Professor really opened my eyes to the premodern world. Challenging readings, but really worth the slog.  I would pay to hear her lectures.  Oh....I guess I did, lol!!!!!!

If you have honors college status, take this class honors...it's way better than regular, imo...be ready to write... Honestly, though, I only read about 75% of the books and 0% of the textbook and got an A, if you can bs your way through really good papers and know how to complete an essay exam study guide, you should be good. she is unorganized
Knowledgeable but unreliable. Consistently shows up to class late and forgets things all the time.  She was enthusiastic but just did not seem to put any effort into the class.  Frustrating at best.
Awsome person, extremely knowledgeable and helpful.   Great scholar and teacher

She is definitely a great teacher and loves what she does so it's more fun for the students. Watch out for the T.A. that grades the papers... I'm pretty sure she just likes color with her pen because her critisisms are mostly unfounded.
Extremely boring lectures, difficult to follow, monotone and annoying voice. Avoid all classes taught by her.
I thought that she was very good professor.  She knew her stuff and kept the classes interesting.

Wonderful teacher with lots of enthusiasm for the subject.  Easy to talk to, great anctedotes to help clarify confusing topics.  Her lectures are entertaining, focuses on the necessary "in depth" stuff, but also puts in the lighter side of it.

Someone said she was very organized.  Apparently that person has never been to her office . . . She is a very energetic professor who really enjoys what she does.  Her class can be somewhat difficult to follow because she doesn't give outlines or notes, she merely talks and you have to go from there.  However, her papers are very interesting to write and her readings are usually quite good.  She is very knowledgable about the material, and what she lacks in organization she makes up for everywhere else.
Great teacher! Her papers are actually interesting to write!
Obviously a brilliant woman, very organized, very fair.  Just cite your sources in your papers like crazy, and don't write based on general assumptions.  She hates that.
She's a little flaky, but the class is well organized and the books were well chosen.  So your work and this will be a good class.
No Comments
Great lectures. Do the readings, turn stuff in on time, get an A!
Excellent professor.  Great historical anecdotes to go along with in depth lectures!!!
Great history lecturer! Knows her stuff.

She really restructured this class this semester. I loved her! Her lectures were engaging. I loved the group work. She related course concepts to real life which I appreciated. The class is far better now than it was previously.

Very condescending and belittling towards students. If you ask her a simple question, she makes you sound dumb and almost humiliates you in front of the entire class. She doesn't seem very professional. We've been in this class for weeks and can't tell you one thing she's taught us.

I'm sitting in the first class right now, and this class already feels like a joke. What is actually going on. So unprofessional and not helpful at all. Mizzou Journalism School, why is this a professor for a required class?
She often made me feel stupid instead of helping and was disorganized and very very late in responding to questions.

Monique Luisi was my least favorite professor I've had at Mizzou. She often called out my group when we made mistakes to be a "learning moment" and made us feel stupid. She wanted my group to retake the class so we could correctly do the class next time. There were also no examples of the assignments and were left confused.

Luisi is the worst professor I have had at Mizzou. She does not open up the modules until class time, so it is difficult to be prepared. She grades based on how she is feeling that day, not her rubric. If you ask for help during Zoom, she will take at least 40 min. to come to the breakout room. Take another teacher if you can.

Instructions on assignments were super unclear most of the time, and grading was unfair. Whenever anyone asked a question or didn't understand something, it seemed like she got frustrated and impatient with them. She talked a big talk about wanting her students to succeed, but when it really came down to it, her actions said differently.

Honestly, it's like hanging out with one of your friends. Group work is a guaranteed A as long as you show up. She will change up class - ask your opinion or just have discussions - if she finds it interesting/conducive to the class's learning. She literally invited anyone who had nowhere to go to her house for Thanksgiving! Most caring prof ever!!

YOU NEED TO TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. Dr. Luisi is easily one of the best professors at Mizzou. I looked forward to going to that class each assignment was fun and interesting. She truly cares about the well being of each of her students. (She invited students who had nowhere to go on Thanksgiving to her house in case they wanted a homecooked meal)
Super kind and wants to help you do well. Also, she's pretty funny. Go to class, participate, you'll be fine.
overly complicated introductory course. Not an easy credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: exams very hard for why

Everytime I have reached out to Dr. Lupo he responded within a few hours with a very helpful and insightful message. While I am in an online course and have not met Dr. Lupo in person, his patience has been very appreciated and it seems he genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ugh!  Dr Lupo was too political.  Obviously a staunch conservative and Trump supporter as he would go off tangent during his lectures ranting and raving about liberal wokeness and border security, blah blah blah.  Sign up with a different professor if you can when taking any of these course.

Sometimes I thought I was back in political science instead of atmospheric science because he would get rather right-wing political and MAGA.    Not the worst professor I ever had but certainly not one of my favorites.   Choose another professor for this class if your can is my advice.

I've never met him as I've only had him for an online class, but the tests are incredibly weighted and there's not much to help yourself with besides the textbook; hopefully you can understand content then. There's no lectures, just some extra notes on the modules. So, really, I don't know... Meh.
Do not take this class unless it is your last option. Entire grade is based on three proctored exams. Not a fan at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an extremely understanding individual when it comes to events and special circumstances. The tests are VERY difficult, but lots of extra credit is offered. I can't complain too much at all, he is very friendly that's for sure just do your best to get full credit on the quizzes and case studies and you will be fine.

Unless it's your last option, avoid at all costs. Proctored exams make up 65% of the grade and are incredibly difficult. It's an entry level course and the amount of technical jargon makes it extremely hard to understand. If you have to take this class, use AI to teach you. It's way better than this teacher will ever be.
He's gets way too political mixed into his lectures.  Always gloating about how he's a proud NRA gun toting card carrying professor.  Please just teach and keep your political ideologies to yourself.

As a history major, this was one of the most difficult classes I have ever taken. A majority of the grade is based off of proctored exams that are incredibly difficult. Would not recommend to anyone unless they have a passion for science, because it the content is incredibly dense and requires in-person learning for any success.

I missed 2 tests and he let me retake for full credit and on homework assignments if its clear you got something completely wrong hed give it back with a nudge in the right direction for some points back.

Took the self-paced online intro meteorology class. Quizzes and case studies are easy, but the exams make up the vast majority of your grade. Make sure to study and read the textbook for those. Overall not too bad if you're just looking to get a science class out of the way.
Dr. Lupo is a great Professor. His lectures can be long-winded, but he cares about the students and loves to teach Atmospheric Science. The exams are fair and all information is available on Canvas.

Took the self-paced version of intro to meteorology. It wasn't bad... tests are a huge part of the grade, though, so be sure to study (that was my mistake). Homework/quizzes were easy enough, and tests are right out of the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great guy, really funny, wanted students to do well, and was very clear in his explanations. Made class worth going to just for the jokes at times. Was very understanding, it's a shame if you don't get to have a class with him. REALLY knows his stuff too.
Great teacher but tests and labs can be really long or confusing. He will always help you on them if you have questions, but they are unnecessarily hard
Great teacher!! he is so funny and nice, and tries to make class interesting. Wants to help you learn, wants you to to do well. Just go to class and test reviews and you'll be fine.

Dr. Luo is nice, but her canvas page is autorius, she puts everything under files. She grades based on points instead of percentage which is really great, it took me from a B+ to an A- at the end. She does grade on very few things, 4 tests, 12 (2 dropped) article summaries, and 4 one point attendance checks. All tests are open note though!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Luo is a great teacher, and a kind soul. The class is fully online, yet she is always quick to respond to emails. She is a very reasonable lady, and would take our feedback into account and apply it. Her lecture notes were helpful, and she allows a drop exam. I would take this class over again, especially with her!
I liked this class and I liked Yuyan. If you showed up to class and took notes over what she said, you would do well. She does her grading based on addition, not percentage.

She is a nice professor. She's always willing to answer questions and talk with you after class. It's a pretty easy class. All of the tests are open note. There are 12 article summaries that are easy to do and you only need to complete 10. There are 4 random in class assignments so that's why I said attendance is necessary but there's wiggle room.

She is a tough grader. She doesn't explain what she's looking for in short answer questions, only afterwards if you set up an appointment with her after receiving a grade for your test. However, she is very enthusiastic about the topic and going to class is a must so the lecture slides make more sense by taking notes of her verbal explanations.
This is my 4th psychology class and I've never had one this hard. She knows a lot and expects you to know a lot of details, which is very challenging

This class was the worst! Hard to understand her English and she moves too fast in the class. She makes the exams very difficult to pass. If you take it sign up for presentations EARLY in the semester. That will save your grade. I wish I never took her class. Was not a fan. Avoid her if you can!

As a senior, I've have never regretted enrolling in a class more than hers. Her exams are truly impossible, and it's tough to get presentation spots. She is a merciless grader. Do your GPA a favor, and don't click the "enroll" button on this one.

I really enjoyed this class. She is very knowledgeable and interesting to listen to. I thought that this class was easy, attending class is very helpful, but not necessary. I didn't use the book at all for class. I've heard a lot of people complain that her tests are hard, but I thought they were very easy as long as you actually pay attention.

Luo is really cool, but her class is extremely hard. She is a notable researcher in the field, so she knows a lot, but this also shows up in her tests and lectures. If you want to pass this class, you MUST do presentations in class, because her tests are just so hard. Going to class is required, as she only posts outlines on blackboard.

As a person she is super nice, but as a professor she is the most difficult on I've had. Her tests are HARD. Going to class everyday, and studying for hours on end only barely got me a C+ in the class. Her powerpoints are posted online with blanks in the slides as to make you attend class. No complaints other than the difficulty of her tests.

She speaks very well English for having grown up in China. Her grade is based off of three tests but if you study the power point the questions are a no brainer. She posts slides on blackboard so class attendance isn't essential. neither really is the book. Pretty easy class and the topics are interesting to anyone who likes kids.
I love Professor DeSouza! Her lectures can be quite fast, but you learn to keep up. She is so funny even if it is early in the morning; she is always cracking jokes.

Sweetest woman ever!  She wants to make sure everyone understands the material and provides many ways for help if your struggling in the class. I am not good at math at all but the class was easy if you pay attention and do your work!

A lot of homework and quizzes but you get multiple tries, class isn't hard; Luisa is a great professor and really wants students to understand the material. If you're bad at math I would suggest going to the office hours if you have time. Luisa doesn't give you the day off after exams but she does allow a day off later in the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Desuiza is a very sweet woman. Lectures are mediocre-good. Tests are not that difficult if you pay attention and do test review before hand. There is a good amount of homework.
Even though I suck math and I got a C. Professor Desuiza is a kind, funny woman who helps you. SHe answers emails quickly and tells you exactly what you need to know.
NOTA GREAT TEACHER. LITERALLY DID NOTHING ALL SEMESTER. STUDENT TEACHER SUCKED TOO. DO NOT RECOMMEND FOR ANYONE ACTUALLY WNATED TO LEARN.

The best Comm professor at MU by far. I'm a senior and have never enjoyed a teacher and a class more throughout all my years of schooling. His lectures are fun and very interesting. Lots of groupwork in this class. Papers instead of tests, and 4 missed absences a semester. Great teacher and great class

Dr. Luisi is amazing. He cares about his students and is very knowledgable in his field. One of the best professors in the communication department. This was my third class taken with him, he is AWESOME! Make sure you show up to class regularly and you will get the grade you desire.

Dr. Luisi is without a doubt one of the best professors in the communication department here. His lectures are very organized and provide great insight. I took two of his courses and they are both ran in a similar fashion with a big focus on group work. If you show up to class and do the work you can be sure that you will get the grade you want.

Luisi was good at conveying material and gave us plenty of resources to be able to fully understand what we are learning. There's a lot of group work and the semester project sucks because of having to work in a group because people will not pull their weight, but he grades just tough enough. The mini assessments were so nice in place of exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Luisi is a great professor, and his lectures are easy-to-understand and enjoyable. He uses iClicker and there are mandatory discussion labs. He's pretty flexible though and easy to reach via email. You actually learn real-life skills in this course and he helps prepare you for future job interviews and workplace scenarios.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Many lecture and discussion days, reletively understanding to different students circumstances, respected professor and spoken of very highly

Dr. Luisi is a great teacher who is very flexible and caring. He will give you an extension if needed and there is little homework No exams, but heavy on the 3 speeches you do for the semester. He's very clear with grading and its an easy class to get an A+ if you put effort into it.

Dr. Luisi was a great public speaking professor! He is very nice and cares a lot about making us better public speakers. Class was engaging with no busywork, and his grading was very fair. I hate public speaking in general but Tim's class was the highlight of my day. Absolutely take his class if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tim is a really understanding and caring professor. He is super flexible and always has something good to say after students voice their thoughts. The class content is interesting and he keeps it really relevant to us as students. Every once in a while, he would let us leave class super early if the energy was low or it was a Friday. Great dude!

Dr. Lucy is hilarious and his lectures are very fun to go experience. He was my favorite professor this semester. He knows how to immerse students very well and he cracks jokes all the time. He usually has a pop quiz on Fridays that go over material from the week. 
His lectures are very hormone heavy so be prepared to study that.
This has been the best professor I have had so far. It was especially helpful when you posted lecture slide shows ahead of time and brought visuals to lectures.

Dr. Lucy has such a dry sense of humor and its great. He has such a passion for dairy cows and will be at every single lab. He knows dairy is hard, but does his best to explain it and give visuals to help with retention. Overall I love Dr. Lucy and would love to take a class with him again

Dr. Lucy is a very fun teacher who gives a lot of examples and involves the students in class. He covers a lot of information fast, though he records the lectures and posts them online. He does provide a study guide for tests. Very fun guy who adores dairy cattle.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lucy is absolutely amazing; he's super fun and friendly, and his lectures are fairly easy to understand. He's approachable both in and out of class, though he's not very good with computers, and it may take him a while to email you back. Be aware, though, he may go off on tangents, and you may become an unwilling volunteer in his conversation.
Dr. Lucy is a very funny professor. He is very entertaining during lectures and keeps your attention. If you need any questions answered he's an approachable professor.

Dr. Lucy's section on dairy is the hardest in BAP, but he is so funny and makes class very enjoyable. His labs are very well organized and easy to follow. You can tell he is passionate about dairy and is happy to answer any questions you have. Creates study guides for quizzes each week. Overall just a very nice person and easily approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Lucy is an amazing professor, his lectures are always educational and entertaining and he clearly cares about the subject matter. His section in BAP is by far the hardest, but he explains it well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this teacher. If you struggle with Spanish she makes this environment very hard to feel comfortable. Everything is 100% Spanish even questions, so students never feel comfortable to ask anything.

Instructor is almost passive aggressive and intimidating. It is understood that the class it to be taught and engaged in with only spanish but she insists that every single question be asked and answered only in spanish. after a whole summer with no spanish, jumping into this environment is not okay when other professors at the same level arent

I would recommend requesting a change in professor. Poor attitude and not understanding of students differing knowledge of the language and expects only Spanish to be spoken at all times which prevents students from asking questions.

If you miss class for any reason, including death of a loved one, you will lose attendance points. Even if you do the make-up assignment, she still deducts points. What's the point of the make-up assignment? I have had "below-average" professors before and she does not come close to comparison. She is very rude; I don't know how she got this job.

Professor Perea was a decent professor. The online homework is a lot at times and there is an exam about every other week or so, the class moves very fast. Multiple times she emailed our class about an assignment due for the next class the night before it was due. However, Luisa is personable and you can go to her with questions you have in class.

Many people struggle in SPAN 1200. Test averages are generally pretty low. The homework is meant to "teach". If you put the work in, take notes, and DO the homework, it's quite easy. Homework is not on Canvas, it is on a separate website. Required textbook-- and buy it before the first day of class. She is quite caring and understanding though.
She hasn't updated her lecture videos since 2020. For a class that uses software that is updated yearly, that is unacceptable.
This class is very hard and you have lots to do. Suprised I got an a
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lyria is fun and very cool. best teacher i had in college

Lyria was amazing!! Her class was very fun, and she gave us the freedom to do just about whatever we wanted as well as the opportunity to be creative. At the same time though; she was very critical and helpful in her instructions. Not only did she help me with my projects for her class, but she also gave me great advice for the future!
Not better than Movshovitz
Memorize what he is saying word for word in the lecture or you are wrong. It doesn't matter if the answer you provide is right, if it isn't EXACTLY what he is looking for then you will not pass.

Everyone else hit the nail on the head. He knows what he is talking about. Study the vocabulary for the exams as they can mess you up later. Quote him exactly he doesn't care about the textbook answers. Don't miss class or you will regret it. Extremely arrogant.

Lyman is obviously good at what he does and he knows it and expects students to memorize every word he says. The Lab is good and WILL boost your grade so definitely take it! He grades his tests really severely and not completely fairly. His office hours are at 7am and class is at 8am usually. However, this class is required for the major.

If you can't memorize every word he says EXACTLY and be able to barf it up on the tests, then you're screwed.  He doesn't make you feel like you can come to him with problems, either, and when you do, he makes you feel like you are interrupting something more important.  85% of our class failed the first test.  I strongly discourage his classes.

It's really not a bad class, he can be intimidating but you really learn the material, just go to class each time. I also recommend the lab if you're in 2020. The tests ARE ridiculous, I got a 56% on the first one, but a 97% on the second.
No Comments
I concur with the previous person's comments. He's arrogant and expects you to repeat what he says from his notes (which reads from legal paper and guard's in a manilla folder).

Dr. Lyman is a great lecturer, but he is arrogant, and his tests are ridiculous.  Because he is a good teacher, students understand the subject matter well, but the tests do not reflect this.  Prepare to give word-for-word answers; he doesn't care is you understand or not.
Professor Kraxberger is very kind and smart. She'll work with you if you need help.
J1010 is useless. The professor tried her best given the lack of content.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easiest intro Journalism class there is. Show up to class and do the online assignments and you will pass. All there is to it.

This class is so boring. SO BORING. You have to take it for the J-School so it's a requirement but it's seriously the worst. Don't take notes, just buy the TopHat and you'll be fine. Also it's a pass/fail and, besides the fight to stay awake, is extremely easy.
No Comments

I took this class as an independent study. There was a lot of reading and writing, but this professor is passionate about the subject and expects her students to be engaged in the study as well. I worked hard and received an A- which I felt was fair. Work hard, review your syllabus/learning contract often, and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is everything, in my opinion, that you DO NOT want to see in a "Professor".  Quick to judge, rigid, and just overall not understanding.. of anything. Please, if you have a chance to take anyone else.. do. Not a person I would like to learn from (putting it mildly) Never.. EVER have I received an F.. she was the first, and the worst
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am taking a class with her and the experience is horrible. She gives far too much work to meet her ridget deadlines and offers no helpful feedback. I reget taken this class, not beacuse of the material but because of the unnecessary amount of stress and pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Truly an awful experience. An exceptionally large amount of work was given out. The work was not returned with comments in a. timely manner on anything but the response papers. She was a very difficult professor to deal with and if you demonstrated true knowledge of her subject she seemed to take it personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was decent at best.  Lynette is knowledgeable but her teaching style is very scattered. The three hour lecture was used very inefficiently. Class discussions were the best part but the information from those was hardly usable on tests. It would be a much better class if it was better structured.

I am in class with her this semester and I find myself rolling my eyes the entire class. She doesn't seem to know anymore than the students and makes us write journals for every class on the reading and then dont even go over them. The class is just busy work and is pretty useless. It would be better is she were more knowledgeable.

Can't really BS your discussion questionsresponses. Tests are tough if you aren't using the tegrity lectures. You also really need to go into depth when explaining your answers - include as many definitions as possible. She was so helpful in virtual office hours and genuinely wants to see you do well. You can get an A if you work for your grade
Easy to understand and learn from. Somewhat interesting course. Easy A if you go to class.

She's a really great teacher. You have to be there and be willing to do the work, but it will pay off. Also she will assign readings now and again, but make sure you keep up with assignments so you can understand what the next class lecture is going to be about. She's very clear, she can even go over stuff with things you don't understand.

Overall awesome guy and deserves all the respect expected day to day. Tests are very frequent and vocab intensive, but he helps you understand the things that confuse the average student. I recommend if you want to take Spanish as a secondary language credit, you have him as your professor.

Great teacher and chill guy. Loved the class, NO EXAMS, only formal 5 minute interviews which he gives you the questions ahead of time. The final is a paper turned in a week before exams, also one oral presentation is required.

I love Professor Martin! He is a very easy grader and helps students out very well. If you don't understand something he will realize before you ask him and will teach you the correct way to answer. It is ok to miss a class here and there, but it is a 2.5-point penalty every time you do.
Great professor with fun and engaging classes. Doesn't give busy work so it's a nice class to take the pressure off. Would 100% take again!
Professor Sveum is a great lecturer and goes strictly with the textbook. Go to class and take notes and you will be fine!
Very knowledgeable on topics such as ag. economics and sociology. His lectures are to the point and good to retain info.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He didn't round up my final grade to an A even though the syllabus says he'll round up within 0.5 of the next grade level.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He doesn't explain anything different if you don't understand a topic, lectures will literally put you to sleep, and he set up the course to have extra credit being your grade down. Would not recommend. If you have other professors that also teach this course, choose someone else.

LOVE THIS PROF! HE TRULY Cares and explains the material well. The material can be a little boring if you aren't a fan of economics but he is very engaging. Studying for tests has never been easier. The notes pack for the class contains exams from previous years along with practice exams, and worksheets over topics. Also has fast communication!

Clearly explains topics in lecture but also very boring. Does a lot of in-class activities so you should probably go to class. Doesn't have a rubric for his papers so he will take off points just because. Not too difficult for a capstone class.

Good professor.  Easy to communicate with, accessible, understanding, and will work with you.  Lectures can be a tad boring, but that could very well be because I'm not an economics fan.  He explains all the concepts very clearly, the homework isn't difficult, and the tests are reasonable if you pay attention and study with the provided materials.

Do you love roller coasters? Do you love assignments changing at the last minute without any notice and after you have already done the work the syllabus called for? You will love this guy then. Always check your grades and the comments because he lacks attention to detail and will reduce your grade for his mistakes.

Dr. Sveum was an overall good professor. His expectations are clear, and the workbook provides everything you need for exams. The study guides are basically the exams with different numbers plugged in. His lectures could get long and boring, though, but this could be due to the 1.25 hr lectures and subject material. He clearly explains all concepts

AG_EC 2225 Statistical Analysis. Sveum will be happy to help you outside of class, always responds to emails, takes student feedback seriously and is fairly lenient. It would be in your best interest to show up to class though because he doesn't post all notes and often gives bonus for attendance. All in all fairly easy class and hes a chill dude.

Prof McMillen is a good guy saddled with a not great course. The assignments in J1200 leave a lot to be desired, but McMillen still makes the course fun and engaging, and made an otherwise difficult class manageable.

Travis is such an amazing professor. Seeing the reviews that call him too harsh in his replies is so funny, he isn't harsh, he's just humorous and gives great advice. He's such a down to earth guy and is fun to be around. He thoroughly helps you learn the softwares and how to make edits on them. I would 100% take his class again!!

probably my favorite professor! In terms of grade distribution this is by far the most challenging section of 1200, but so worth it. WILL prepare you for harder, upper level journalism classes, I feel miles ahead many of my peers. Imo, you get the grade you deserve. Gives really good constructive criticism, especially if you take the time to ask!

These ratings are so harsh! I took his J1200 class last fall and he was just funny and easy to talk to. He isn't mean, he gives feedback, and when I approached him about it he provided more detail and told me how to improve. The work isn't too heavy, but it gets you out there (interviews/photography), and that's what you should expect at J-School.

I had Travis last fall and am giggling at these reviews. He's nice if you actually engage with him. I only got a B because of missing work. 1200 is a class designed by a course coordinator, so the projects arent his fault. If you actually do your work your grade is fine. He can give harsh comments in class but online its just about the rubric

Travis is genuinely the meanest professor I have ever had. While in class, he was nice and personable as well as sarcastic and funny, but outside of class his Canvas comments were rude and gave little to no constructive criticism. I don't think he understood that freshman take this course and don't understand how fast it's pace is.

Prof. Travis is an easy going dude. If you go to class and turn in homework, you will get an A. It doesn't get much easier than that. I found this class pretty easy. He is pretty chill and funny if you get to know him.

Travis inspired me to change majors. Missed one class for the Sports Journalism boot camp and dropped my grade by two letters. Also super judgemental regarding student work, however, is a light grader. Most of his lectures are him just yapping until the very end as well. Didn't help that my class was in between most club activities.

It's the fourth week of class and I have decided how this guy works. I gave him the benefit of the doubt but it's not needed. On assignments he'll leave words for you in the comments but don't always assume they'll be helpful. I've conferred with multiple students on grades and there is no way I would accept a C for a grade based on HIS standards.

I took him first semester my freshman year and he was great! I really enjoyed his class and his humor. Definitely a little unorganized, but it makes him understanding. He really takes in consideration the effort you're putting in. Definitely talk with him and ask for help if you're confused and you'll do fine!

Travis is a fun, good professor. He gives examples of all the assignments, helping you know what to do. The rubrics are pretty clear. There is a lot of homework/busy work and you definitely have to have storage on your phone for it. He can be a little unorganized, but that is probably what makes him understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dont get me wrong, he was very polite and fair when it came to grading, but is not a very skilled teacher. Often he would reveal that he never planned to teacher and never made an attempt to be prepared for our lectures. Often we would ask him questions about assignments and he would say one thing and the rubric would say another.

Travis is very rude to students in front of the whole class. He makes very snide comments every day to people who don't know what they're doing since they haven't been taught anything by him. He has been very rude and disrespectful to me and some of my friends in the class.
So Dr. McFadden is a good proffessor but there is very little room for error in this class. you can only miss 20 points to keep an A, which is impossible because the only grades are quizes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the most disorganized class I have ever taken at MU. The instructor did not follow the syllabus, and structure and order was absent. Final grades were not even submitted until

I won't be the only person to say his class structure is not the most organized. He makes up for it by being very accommodating and understanding towards his students. He is always available to help students before and after class and lab. He takes feedback from his students and genuinely wants us to succeed. Put some respect on cow guys name

Dr. McFadden is the most caring professor I've had. The class can be a bit disorganized but he is always very accommodating. He is very passionate about what he does and wants every student to learn. He's always willing to stay after class or lab to talk about anything. If anyone does poorly in this class, they did not reach out to him for help.

This professor, though nice and funny in class and labs, gives lots of empty promises (and lies) for due dates and assignments, no transparency. You don't get any grades or critiques on papers until your already writing your final paper (all papers = 50% of grade). This behavior is consistent for all aspects of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken, would never take his class again except I have to to graduate. Every single assignment and paper grade was put in two days before the final, ZERO FEEDBACK on any of the papers that you use to create the final paper that was worth like 40% of the class grade. He actually forgot to post our paper assignments twice. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was super nice and very accommodating. Exams were multiple choice with essay questions. Exam questions were very random, minute details you wouldn't necessarily think to study. Quizzes were online at first but he made them in person after test average was 30%. Long lectures and LOTS of information- keep up with the info or you will get behind!

Very nice and funny person. As a professor, he is very...laid back...to put it. Most due dates change due to falling behind or because he forgot to post it. Don't have an interest in the dairy industry? Do not take this class. If you do, take it for WI b/c you have to write the paper regardless, but you get more points towards your final grade.

Due dates may change, but works to be very flexible because of those changes. Lectures seem more laidback, but good notes are important because the tests are more challenging. If you study the slides all the information is there. Expects you to know specifics from labs, but he makes it clear. He is willing to help everyone pass. Very approachable.

Please rethink your course selection. This is the most unorganized dumpster fire of a class I have ever taken. You have no idea what content will be on the exams, he talks about having papers and quizzes due but never actually posts them (which made me check every 12 hours). I seriously think he forgets that he is in charge of a class sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: def one of the best professors. clearly states his topics and makes it easy to connect. the discussion work is a bit tedious but it does pay off when it comes to tests
Took the class honors so had Prof. McFarland for my discussion group leader. Was very good with answering questions, and was very responsive outside of class if I had any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Phenomenal lectures that truly make the class content very interesting. I wasn't expecting to enjoy this class as much as I did, and I always looked forward to the lectures. The quizzes, midterm, and final are very straightforward; he tells you exactly what you should expect and gives you generous study guides to prepare.
Very good lecturer, very passionate, clear requirements and generous grading policies. I really liked going to class, would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No comment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I learned so much about Middle East relations with the U.S. in this class with Professor McFarland. He is very knowledgeable in the topic, and has written a book on the oil crisis from material brought up in lecture. The weekly reflection assignments and quizzes are pretty easy and help your grade. A great online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor McFarland was a great professor. When I first decided to take this class, I was unsure whether or not I would like the subject. He changed my mind completely through his lectures and I truly enjoyed his class! A caring individual who really wants the best out of his students.

Victor McFarland is a great teacher. His lectures are purposely slowed down so that you can adjust the speed based on your preference. His lectures are straight to the point with great details. You have to attend the labs to get points. A few papers and weekly quizzes. The quizzes are open note and the answers are in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: McFarland is a cutie! Not only is he extremely well educated on the topic, he is caring and always open to questions. I loved how much he took the classs opinion and concerns into consideration. I will say the material is very heavy and confusing. Attending class and reading will help you succeed. Otherwise it would be easy to get overwhelmed

Harder than necessary for entry level. Grade depends on TA. Must go to discussion, lecture not mandatory but highly suggested. Study a lot for tests, it is basically your whole grade. There are a couple quizzes and a paper as well. Memorize terms and have very well thought out, specific answer for essay questions.

Lecture can be skipped if you're good at reading and retaining information. If you skip lecture AND don't read, you'll fail. Tests are challenging, difficult for a survey class. Discussion section was okay, and you do have to show up for it and for the quizzes. I didn't love the way the class was organized, but l would try a different class w/him.

Personally I thought this class was easy. You're only graded on quizzes, the midterm, and final and a paper. The quizzes are over the key terms in the book so only know those and your fine. he gives study guides for quizzes and the midterm and the final and always reminds you about things and gives sample papers for the paper you write. Nice guy

4 quizzes, midterm & final, one essay, participation points for attending discussions. You can only miss 1 discussion but lectures are optional & posted online. Honestly if you didnt take upper level history in high school then dont take this class, definitely required background knowledge. Difficult quiz & tests. Nice guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: lectures are optional. The discussions are not. You get participation points. Although he covers the material in class I would recommend reading the text book. It helps you better prepare for the tests. There are 4 quizzes, a midterm, a paper, and the final. This class requires work, a little difficult for a survey level class. Interesting though.

Dr. Mathews is by far the best journalism teacher I have ever had the opportunity to learn from. He genuinely cares for each of his students and reminds us daily to "Be kind to yourself". The class itself is very easy as long as you attend the lectures. Minimal online homework, and lenient policy on dropping bad grades. Wish I could take it again.
I love this man. Take his honors portion; easy A and engaging. Very sweet person who genuinely wants students to succeed. Amazing lecturer. Easy class as well.

He is the most caring teacher I have ever had. He makes an effort to get to know every student personally. On tests he doesn't try to trick you with questions and everything is very straight forward. 100% recommend.

Dr. Matthews has been the most passionate, kind, and inspiring professor I have ever had the privilege to learn from. I always left his class feeling confident that I made the right choice to pursue journalism at Mizzou. He teaches with so much passion and care for his students and our futures and can make a 200 person class feel like a community.
He is very passionate about journalism and truly cares about each and every student of his.

Dr. Mathews is the best intro to the J-School one could ask for. Even if you aren't a journalism major, I highly recommend this course - engaging material that applies directly to current issues. Mathews is so hilarious and genuine, and clearly cares about every one of his hundreds of students. I can't say enough good things.

Incredible lectures, you leave the building ready to go out in the world and make a change. Really cares about his students, & he greets everyone outside the hall in the mornings. Go to his coffee hours.
this is the best professor i've ever had, if you can take a class with him, please do it
Amazing guy and professor. Truly wants the best for his students. You'll learn a lot if you listen.

Great guy, so engaging to listen to. Exams follow the material we learned in class and aren't overly difficult. I'm not a journalism major, and this is still one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. Highly recommend!! Textbook "required" but I never got it and I'm doing great in the class so far!

Dr. Mathews was one of the most engaging professors ever. I wasn't a journalism major and had to take this class as an elective credit but it was one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Mizzou. The class isn't too bad and everything is online-based, so if you just take computer notes from his slides you will do very well.
As long as you don't take advantage of how easy the class is, you will learn so much about Journalism. It is the perfect first Journalism class to take as a freshman.

I loved Professor Matthews' lectures!! He did such an amazing job at making the class feel smaller than it was. My class had a full house, so you definitely didn't know every one, but for the most part he knew you by name. He makes class fun and engaging, but also productive at the same time.

Made lectures very engaging, and you can clearly tell he is passionate about teaching journalism. Make sure to attend his coffee hours. Exams aren't too bad and he gives plenty of chances to make up for bad grades with extra credit and grade drops. He really cares for the wellbeing of his students and overall it was just a really fun class!
Love this guy.

Professor Mathews makes a big class feel small. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches and keeps the students engaged. He makes the content enjoyable and is HILARIOUS!  He cares about every student's well-being and success. The journalism school is lucky to have someone as intelligent and compassionate as Professor Mathews.

I was so obsessed with this class. Professor Mathews gives the most engaging lectures and has the best stories. He cares so much about the success of his students and is always willing to talk about anything journalism related outside of class. Tons of opportunities for extra credit and tests that you'll ace if you pay attention in the lecture.
I did my J1300 profile story on this man and he is super awesome. He helped out a ton! I appreciated his readiness to answer questions.

Edit: Completed it, and I absolutely loved his J1100 course. He does a great job of lecturing in an engaging, enjoyable, and most importantly MEMORABLE way. He manages to pack a solid amount of content into his lectures without making it feel like he's been going on for hours. Super supportive, great at teaching. Would totally recommend.

Take this course PLS! Dr. Mathews is awesome and he really cares about his students and making learning easy for everyone. There are lots of assignments every week, but they are not hard and very immersive. Love his lecture style and his coffee hours.

Amazing not only as a teacher but as a person. In a 500+ lecture hall he was still personable and easy to get along with. Offered about 20 points of extra credit and was very adamant about taking breaks and making time for yourself and being kind to yourself. Engaging classroom and humorous. 100/10 would take this professor again.

Mathews is an amazing teacher. He was very accessible and it was fun attending his class. Through his lectures he applied the material to pop culture and every day life. He made the big lecture hall feel more of a small classroom which helped me a lot.
Nick is a great teacher! He was super receptive and fessed up when he got something wrong. 10/10 would do it again.

Mathews is an accomplished journalist, which makes him a great professor and lecturer. J1100 is very easy, most people just do other classwork during lectures. There are quite a few weekly assignments but they are easy. He is funny and wants to build relationships with his students, he has coffee hours where you can meet him in a small group.
Such a fun class and a amazing professor!

Despite being new, Matthews is a great teacher and knows what he's talking about. He's engaging and makes a boring, mandatory class more fun. Attendance is essentially mandatory but the assignments, exams and content is far from difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Matthews is an AMAZING professor. The class is big but he makes the effort to talk to every student. He cares deeply about what he is teaching and it's obvious through his lectures. The lectures are entertaining and engaging. Attendance is taken. There are 3 weekly assignments but they are not difficult. HIGHLY recommend!

He is new at Mizzou but is more than qualified. Very engaging in lectures and tests/quizzes are all online and open book/note. Only thing is there are three weekly assignments due Saturday and the following Monday, so deadlines sneak up on you. Attendance is taken but he is very lenient and drops a few at the end of semester.

The material isn't that bad but the way things are graded is horrendous. The biggest exams and projects are worth only 10 points and everything else is 5-8. These grading antics tanked my course grade to the point where my 4000-level psych course is easier. Make sure to do the extra credit, it does matter.
Don't mess with her

Dr Murph holds her students' group projects (which replace lectures half way into the semester) to higher standards than her own teaching. Her grading makes no sense, and all assignments are worth so few points that a single discussion post is 5% of your grade. Her attendance policy is strict for a redundant and unengaging 8 am.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her teaching is just reading slides with no insight, making lectures a waste of time. She promotes "creative freedom" in projects but docks points for not meeting vague, unstated expectations. When questioned about this, she blames us for lacking effort. We're paying for education and getting an audiobook with attitude. Scam.

Strict attendance policy. If you miss more than one 8 AM class, your grade drops 1% per absence, which can be difficult for students with jobs/ other responsibilities. Lectures often shift focus from music to broader social topics, which sometimes can feel off-track from the course material.
She is very passionate about the topic which made it very interesting. I really enjoyed how she presented the information, and I liked all the projects we did. She is a very kind professor as well.

This professor primarily lectures and doesn't engage the class in any sort of discussion or critical thinking. Quizzes largely based on rote memory and do not actually let you demonstrate your knowledge. Does not treat students as adults and often grades subjectively without a clear rubric, even if you go in for office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For this class, I have no issues with the teacher besides the Attendance policy.  Since Dr. Murph only lectures by reading PowerPoints already available on canvas, all of the reading and studying can be done entirely online.  Therefore, having attendance as a grade is simply redundant and impractical, especially for an 8am class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her classes. She's thoughtful, fair, and understanding. She expects quality work, so handle your business and you'll be fine. Dr. Smythe knows her stuff and she expects her students to put in the work.
Did an amazing job of drawing people out and stimulating conversation, especially from the guys.
she only cares about herself. trys her best to make you feel bad about yourself. always condescending.

While I thought I would enjoy this class, she was possibly one of the worst teachers I have had in the communications department.  Her classes are completely biased and grades have been proven to be completely subjective.  If you are on her good side, good for you, but your grade will suffer if on her bad side.  Working hard will get you nowhere.

For a writing intensive class, I did not find J1300W too stressful. He is decently fast when it comes to grading and gives helpful feedback. There were several times when he regraded assignments to be a completion grade because we had not received feedback for that type of assignment yet. Would pick him as my prof again! He is very chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Throughly enjoyed his class, made it very engaging and was one of my favorite classes this semester. He was very chill and laid back...very easy grader.
Great class. You do a lot of your writing outside of class so there is homework, but he typically gives you in class time. He is a great professor and will help you if you need it, just ask.
Great professor especially if your new to Mizzou and the J-School. Class was chill as long as you do your work.

What was expected from you was very clear. If you actually put in some effort, it's an easy A. Exams were basically based on her lectures more or less. Textbook recommended, not required, I didn't read it. Not open note exam, but one dropped. Wasn't a comp final. Class attendance was extra credit. Has recorded lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are long, but easy to stay engaged. Dr. McSteen is very knowledgable, but explains things well. Exams can be tough even if you study and think you understand the material.

Dr. McSteen is a really great professor! There isn't attendance required, but if you go to most of the discussion meetings you can get extra credit. She is pretty generous with extra credit and will remind students about it and how to calculate their grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super fast-paced. If you skip class, you will probably have no idea what is going on in the next lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory, but iClicker is bonus points, and so is discussion. Test averages are usually below a 70. I barely studied for the first test and got a 50% and then studied super hard for the second test and got a 30%...

Dr. McSteen is a dedicated professor who is very passionate about her subject. The lectures can be long and heavy, but participation is important, and iClicker activities count for extra credit. The textbook is helpful for practice/details. The exams are tough, and there are weekly group quizzes, so staying on top of the material really matters.
Passionate teacher, very knowledgable about genetics, moves fast and weekly quizzes (good study tools).
Great professor! Tests and quizzes are difficult, but are open note, so are very fair. You must attend lecture for extra credit points & can get more extra credit from other various assignments.

Her lectures can be fast paced, but she's often available outside class for help and gives you lots of resources. She's very kind and truly wants to see her students succeed. The class is hard simply because of the material, but with her support, it's definitely manageable and doesn't make you feel bad. Just takes some effort outside of lecture!

Dr. McSteen is one of my favorite professors that I've ever had. She's super passionate about what she's teaching and it makes you want to learn the material. She is super caring and accommodating. She gives opportunities for bonus points, but you can do just fine without them. As long as you participate and put forth some effort, it's an easy A.
The tests are pretty difficult and the lectures are boring. Just make sure to do the work and it's not too awful.

nice lady, dont need textbook, goes fast but posts recordings-print & write on slides!, attendance isnt graded but clicker questions for extra credit, tests are completely written and pretty difficult-make sure you understand example problems & PROBLEM SETS, weekly quiz over problem sets for extra credit-they go over some questions in discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: nice lady, dont need textbook, goes fast but posts recordings-print & write on slides!, attendance not graded but clicker questions for extra credit, tests are completely written and pretty difficult-make sure you understand example problems & PROBLEM SETS, weekly quiz over problem sets for extra credit-they go over some questions in discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Attendance isnt necessary, but she offers extra credit if you attend which can really boost your grade. Shes entirely reliant on vocabulary/problem sets for tests so make sure you know how to do the problems! Shes not a very interesting lecturer and not great at explaining. Discussion is a joke though; I personally never really found it helpful.

Lecture was hard to pay attention to because it was very boring, but the clicker questions were worth a lot of extra credit and bumped me up a whole letter grade. She gave online quizzes and practice exams each week that helped focus on what to study for the exams. I went to every lecture, recitation, and even tutoring but still struggled.

I struggled in this class, because lecture was very boring and unclear. Even though I went to lecture and recitation consistently, I was still unclear on the material. She does offer a lot of bonus which helped my grade. In general she just isn't a great teacher, so be prepared to teach yourself.

Dr McSteen is a young professor, that said, while I think she really cares about teaching students, she is a little inconsistent in method.  3/4 tests were really easy and keyed to problem sets, the last was ridiculously tough and kind of unfocused.  Hit the ground running, don't fall behind, go to class - clickers and quizzes worth extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. McSteen's really nice, but she poorly prepares you for exams, making it harder than it should be to get a solid A in her course.  The discussion section with the TA is not necessary at all (no grades rely on this), and she gives extra credit for percentage correct with clickers at the end of the semester, so showing up to class is worth it.
Really awesome professor, easy grader, makes her lectures interesting and relevant. Granted, I'm really interested in genetics, but she makes the content easy to understand

Going into the semester I did not think I would enjoy it. Much to my surprise, I actually looked forward to going to class! Dr. McSteen was pleasant and willing to answer questions without making students feel dumb. I learned a LOT and I would definitely recommend taking this class! Clicker questions & homework get you extra credit so go to class!

I went to every class and she just didn't really know how to give a good lecture. She follows slides obviously written by another professor and when you ask questions in class she almost always turns it into a question back at you. Clicker points are extra credit and it was up to 25 points of extra credit, but don't expect to earn all of them.

Great teacher. If you have to take genetics I very highly recommend you take her class. She is very helpful in class and is extremely fair on all her tests. No tricks, very straightforward. You can tell she really wants all her students to succeed.
She is an okay teacher. Lectures are hard to follow even with tegrity and recitation to help. The problem sets help on test. Good luck

As first year professors, Dr. Braun (husband) taught this with her.  The class requires A LOT of work but it is certainly not impossible.  GO TO LECTURES; valuable clicker points.  GO TO RECITATION; attendance points and problem set clarification.  BEST ADVICE:  YOU *MUST* DO THE PROBLEM SETS.  If you do not understand the sets, you WILL fail.
Nice lady, but doesn't explain things very well. If you take this class you must definitely pay attention to practice problems...those are always on the exams.
Does not know what hes talking about
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doug isn't the best lecturer.  The exams are really difficult but he does give more than generous curves.  The semester long project is confusing at times but he's more than willing to help along the way.

one of the worst profs ive ever had, gives wrong advice for the simulation, talks super slow and for entirety of class, confusing/bad explanations, his grading system is slow and confusing, p chill final presentation grade, but FAT final- he recommends you take at least 3 hours (its another simulation). bro also has assigned seats

It's insane how bad his advice is for the simulation. I was on our finance and listened to him; we underwent an impossible to recover from catastrophe and received a grade so low it hurt my insides. This was all his fault and I felt completely misguided and alone. Thank you professor.

Whole class is based on how well you do the simulation, but his guidance is faulty and you're pretty much thrown into the fire. Feel free to google as much as possible. Lectures are long and he grades stuff as late as possible because he doesn't have a TA. Not his fault + hes nice but this isn't what I thought capstone would be honestly

Doug is just not a good professor. He talks for the entire hour 15 and doesn't stop. He will give advice on the capstone simulation and if it doesn't help, he just says whoops. Also the final takes 3-6 hours usually. Nice guy, just really bad class. Take the other professor.
Doesnt communicate well with students. Doesnt understand how to use canvas DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

Prof. Moesel is very thorough in how he grades assignments. It would be a challenging task given that he grades something like 70 students' assignment s himself without a TA. The class is so so and most students would go through the motion anyway but he showed good work ethics.

Professor Moesel is a great professor - nice and interested in student learning. He's also dept. chair for the management dept., so he's pretty busy, but he will make time to speak with you. Lectures are filled with information and tests are heavily dependent on texts, so make sure you read them!!! His study guides are extremely helpful as well!!

Any given day he has 50-70 slides to go over that are FILLED with concepts. A typical test consists of 100-200 different concepts and theories. He speaks in circles and it's extremely difficult to follow or understand what you are to take away from lecture. Test quetions are dense and 3-4 sentences long. Other capstones are not like this at all.

Slides are FILLED with text, but they're online. He's boring in class, but the videos are helpful. His study guides and essay guidelines tell you exactly what you need to know, but there is a lot of info.

Tim is a great teacher if he likes you and you inflate his ego. If he does not like you, be prepared for passive aggressive comments both in person and when getting graded. 

The material is fine, but the slideshows get stale after awhile. Be ready for a lot of memorizing.

I have taken courses from Moloney several times. This last time, his teaching style was different. In the past, you could truly tell he cared about ALL students. Now, it seems he has picked select favorites and pushed the rest of the students into a 'lump.' Disappointed, to say the least. Maybe he was too busy with extra duties to truly care?

I took 2215, wasn't an option when selecting for Tim. I loved him. I did fail every single ID quiz, but if you put in the effort on homeworks and his 2 big projects, and show up to every class for his pop "insta quizzes" youll be fine. He gives really good feedback on everything you submit, I've never felt more seen as a student than by him.

Professor Moloney is a very caring professor. He makes class entertaining and interactive, and gives lots of fair ec chances to take advantage of your grade if you struggle with quizzes. It does take some memorization work, but I do recommend him. Knows his stuff

Tim is a great guy!  Your grade will depend upon your projects and the tests.  Tests are super easy, didn't study and got good grades on them all.  Pay attention during lectures and you'll be fine.  Grading is super reasonable, and he always gives feedback so you know how to improve.  He cares about his students, he still remembers me by name!

Really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. I've had him for 3 classes and have enjoyed every one. For all of his classes, as long as you stay on top of your learning and complete your assignments, you will succeed. Skipping classes or missing assignments is trouble. If memory isn't your thing, commit extra time for Woodys
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious
