reviews.comment: This is an ID class-lectures and participation matter. There are some assignments to help boost your grade, but it's important to stay on top of memorization or it'll hurt later. He's a great professor who cares about his topics and really wants everyone to succeed, creating EC opportunities in struggling classes. As long as you try, you'll be ok
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He likes to pit students against each other.  Most assignments do actually help learn the content, but some assignments seem like they were designed to really inconvenience and burden students.  IF you are taking him for site-analysis be forewarned that the final is about 20% what you learn in class and 80% making a scale model which is a waste of

8-week course so slightly fast paced, final project will take you a while to do so do not procrastinate unless you have no other finals or projects to do and can concentrate just on the project. He is super helpful and friendly and will do everything to help you succeed. I have enjoyed every single class of his that I have taken.

Loved this class. I already knew some Spanish so it was a breeze but even if you know nothing, you learn from the ground up. Very easy to make up missed attendance. I think if you take the honors section you actually get Rosa as your prof and not a TA

This class is very heavy in class participation. You will have to answer a lot of questions in front of the class but Professor Morales doesn't make you feel bad if you don't know the right answer. Her lectures were engaging and went by really fast most of the time. She does give her instructions in spanish sometimes which can be confusing.

I have taken low-level Spanish before, so take this review with a grain of salt. Professor Morales cares about her students. If you participate and show genuine interest in learning the language, then your experience will be even better. Sometimes the locations of assignments in Canvas can be unclear, but if you ask she is more than happy to help.

It is much easier to learn Spanish if its taught by a native speaker, which is true with Prof. Morales but sometimes she speaks only in Spanish during lectures which is hard to understand. You WILL answer questions in front of the class and work with your table/partner.

As an instructor, Rosa was lively and always came ready to teach; however, I had a very personal emergency that required me to go home and miss a week of class. While I did not expect any sort of special accommodations, I did expect some degree of understanding. She completely lacked sympathy in the matter and was not understanding whatsoever.

Rosa is a lovely woman! She really cares for each of her students and is happy to help if you are struggling. The homework was a drag but it's all related to what you learn in class. Didn't like the 7 HW assignments sometimes assigned but she's funny and loves to encourage her students to practice!

Professor Morales is very kind and a good teacher. The class moves fast and has plenty of homework, plus a test every couple of weeks. But she prepares you well for tests and lessons are very clear. The textbook is EXPENSIVE but it's not the professor's fault.
Wonderful woman and great teacher. A little hard to catch up if you've never taken spanish but she is always willing to help. As long as you attend and try your best you'll do great

Solid class and professor. If youve never taken Spanish, you might feel behind in the beginning but its easy to catch up. Attendance required. Homework and tests are pretty easy. Just pay attention and do the work.

I had Rosa for Spanish I-Honors. She was very helpful and seemed to genuinely care about students. She was able to clearly teach me about the Spanish language. She graded clearly and fairly, and I was always able to understand what I was not doing correctly. I would definitely recommend taking Rosa for Spanish!

Spanish has always been difficult for me, but the online textbook, homework, and professor Morales really helped me. Yes, I worked hard for my grade (like really hard), but it was not impossible. Prof. Morales is so sweet, funny, caring, and personable. She will always help you! If you have to take spanish, take it with Prof. Morales! Seriously!

Rosa is super sweet and appears to genuinely care. It's very hard to keep up especially if you have little to no previous Spanish experience. The textbook says it is mandatory but she also put all of the activities from the book on the projector. The tests are a big portion of the grade, especially the final, and the homework is taken for accuracy.

I had previously taken two years of Spanish and struggled to keep up in this class. Subjects advanced everyday, and I don't know how people with no knowledge of Spanish kept up. Homework everyday, but it is not challenging. Rosa herself is very kind and is always available for help. Graded mostly on tests, but she is pretty laid back in grading.

If I was rating Rosa solely on personality, I would give her 6 out of 5 stars! As soon as she noticed I was struggling (comparatively to my classmates) she did everything in her power to help me succeed, including checking my classwork and clarifying any confusion after class. Very occasionally, I had trouble understanding her English.

Rosa is okay. She gives good feedback on papers so you improve your writing skills. The class is not very hard, the tests are more like quizzes. I like the class set up, but it is difficult to pay attention and the content is very boring, although I know that's not he fault. Overall, it's an okay class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rosa was a great professor. She was so so funny and kept the class engaged the whole time. Vocab tests were really easy if you studied the material and went to class, tests were composition heavy. The only thing that was hard was that she can sometimes get to speaking very quickly, but she really helped my conversational skills.

Extremely caring and interesting. Class is almost exclusively in Spanish, which is understandable. She is easy to work with and reviews the material well. As long as you show up and are trying, she will work with you and help you out. She is also extremely funny and lively in class.

Lovely teacher, I actually looked forward to spanish everyday (which is saying something). Extremely lenient grader so long as you genuinely try. Actually cares about her student. Honestly, after the first class I was freaking out because she speaks quickly - but trust me the class is worth it!

She doesn't know how to explain concepts clearly. Gets confused easy. A LOT of homework 3x (+)/week. Takes favorites. Has mutiple times made me look stupid in front of the class... coming from someone who has taken 6 years of Spanish and gets A's on her exams. Makes no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. She makes the class really interesting, if you try to be involved. Rosa is very nice, and likes to have positive interactions with students. You get out what you put in. She likes to have fun and laugh. My favorite spanish professor so far.

Rosa was amazing. Though we did have a little complications with clearness every once and a while, she always did her best to help us and made sure we always understood. She is hilarious, takes her time to know her students, and makes class fun! Wish she would teach higher spanish so that I could have her again!

Okay, I really liked her. She was a less harsh grader than my last Spanish professor and, if you listen closely to the things she says, she is really freaking funny. If you're paying attention, being kind, and participating, then she'll like you. It's that simple.

She is tough, but nothing out of the ordinary. Her instructors were good and class was easy. There is a lot of homework though and she does not accept late work. She is a tough grader and not very lenient. Just get all your homework done on time and SHOW UP. Also she doesn't excuse absences unless you have a sick note or something.

Prof. Murillo can often be a bit strict/blunt, but she does a decent job explaining concepts and cares about her students as long as they show that they care about the class. Keep track of the calendar ahead of time, communicate, participate, and you'll enjoy class. (Note, I took the honors version of the class with a smaller class size)
She does not care about you or your wellbeing.
She's strict but you'll learn

In my entire school career, I have not had a worse professor. We were technically a "hybrid" course which could explain for some of the issues. You are expected to check the calendar every day and if you miss an assignment, tough luck. Do all of the HW and you should pass. Do not take this professor if you want to actually learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The professor was caring, but sometimes went away from the questions she was asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Communication is important with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Love her!!! Does a great job of making class enjoyable and fly by. I looked forward to this class, which was nice because it was 4 days a week. You can tell she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I highly suggest taking this class with this professor.

She does not help struggling students , and is in fact downright rude to them. She focused on the negative parts of all my assignments, which just makes you feel bad about yourself. She doesn't care that I actually improved a lot over the semester, just that I wasn't where she wanted me. When I asked for help, she basically said to work harder.
Probably one of the best teachers I've had. Classes were well done and informative. Office hours were easily accessible and he is good with managing time and answering questions.

Scottie is a great guy, and if you are looking for some cool things that can apply to your everyday computing life this is a great class. I still use some of the applications that we discuss such as VM's in this class that I did not know about before.

Scottie is a fine professor, he can get lost in his own world sometimes haha. HW can be unclear sometimes but gives plenty of time to get it done and will explain it if you have questions on discord or next time in class just don't wait. Lecture can get bland and boring sometimes. He does care though and tries to engage the class.

Mickey Mouse class. Could chat gpt the entire course. There is no lectures its a textbook that you follow. Theres a project at the end that is full stack development but the grading is fairly easy. Another easy scottie Murrell class im not sure how the university lets this slide.

Scottie Murrell is a really good guy who is always willing to help you with the concepts. However, he doesn't teach anything. Nothing he says makes any sense. His lectures and slide shows somehow leave me even more confused than before. He basically expects you to already know everything he is talking about. Good luck in his class.
I really liked this class. We got to do some really cool stuff. The lectures sometimes got a little boring but overall it was ok.

Scottie seems like a great guy, was always available to answer questions and extremely knowledgeable about Unix. However, some of his lectures or assignment requirements were very incoherent and unrelated to what we were learning in class or doing for an assignment. Midterm + Final were honestly drastically easier than smaller weighted assignments.

Pretty much completion assignments all the way up until the last 4 weeks of class, which is a final project, that no one understands and he expects you to know/learn full stack development on your own.
IT department needs to do better.
Take any review of this guy over a 3 with a grain of salt, as it's most likely fake. I would not recommend Scottie at all. Avoid him at all costs

The assignments were fairly clear and easy for the most part, except for this one that had me up until like 5 AM banging my head on the wall. The final group project was a bit tough, but I had a smaller group than others, so that may have contributed to the difficulty. Overall, not too bad.

The lectures were at times incoherent, but he was always available to give help (and I mean always, he's answered my Discord messages at 1 AM). The course itself had semi-challenging homeworks but open book tests, and all questions came from the end-of-week quiz banks. Make a Quizlet with your whole row and you've cracked the code to an A.

Has us learning about the concepts necessary to complete the final project up until the week it's actually due; nobody in my group understands how to do the assignment. Switching over to Zybooks did not help his class structure whatsoever.
Some one definitely has it out for Professor Scottie because I have taken his class and he may not be my favorite professor his class was easy
90% sure Scott added fake reviews to pad his rating...

Genuinely surprised this guy still has a job. Lectures are incomprehensible, very hard to follow. Get ready for ChatGPT to be your teacher and to spend hours watching pointless lectures to find snippets of code you need to do your assignments. Can very confidently say I've learned absolutely nothing

retweet: Yikes. For an introductory-level course, it's surprising how poorly this guy taught Unix. Assignment instructions are poorly written, and when confronted, he lashes out at students. Very unprofessional. The only upsides are his availability outside of class to answer questions, and that the assignments are fairly easy.
just never-ending pain and suffering

This class is so unbelievably bad it's incomprehensible. I took Web Dev 1 (2830) with Scotty previously and it was a decent class, pretty easy to follow. This class picks up from a completely different spot and I am entirely lost as to what's going on. Video lectures barely pertain to assignments and I'm on the verge of having to drop the class.

This is my 3rd class with Scottie, and I'm not sure why I keep torturing myself. He is the most illiterate professor I have ever had, and his courses are also completely unorganized. His lectures are hard to follow, and the homework is only half related to them. Sadly, he is the only professor that teaches 2 of the core courses for the IT program.

This class is incredibly unorganized and poorly structured. Each week you'll watch a prerecorded video of him just skimming through completed code, then he expects you to write an assignment half-related to it. Basically required to teach yourself all of the material. Final project is over material we have done ZERO assignments for. Would avoid.
Learned a lot from this class. Was easily approachable and responded to questions even at 1am

The class is too easy if you go into it with any web dev. experience. The assignments are typo-ridden to the point of incoherence. He just shows code during lectures and barely speaks. He refuses to correspond through email; you must join the Discord server.

The professor made the class fun and he seemed extremely knowledgeable about the course material I was able to contact the professor at anytime to get help as well as outside of class time he would take time out to help me. No other professors would make themselves available the way he does. He is my really good professors.
This course starts off easy and works it way up. You learn full stack development
This course was online but fun to learn
This course was challenging but usefull
Well informed about the topic

A few assignments throughout the class, all were not bad, including the final project. The main issue is how he goes about grading these assignments. He refused to regrade a project worth 20% of the grade when the fix took 1 min. 0 partial credit for any of the parts that worked including extra credit. My group received a 50% because of this.

The final project for this class is insanely hard compared to other assignments. and is worth 200 points.The lectures at the end of the class make no sense, there is just lines and lines of code and he explains only bits and pieces and expects us to know how to do the rest. I honestly don't know how anyone was able to do the final on lectures alone

Not that great. Reads off slides word-for-word during lectures. Assignments are really poorly worded and unclear, although if you can decipher what they are asking for, it's not that hard. Has (sometimes) weekly quizzes that are open note and pretty easy. Final project is trivially easy.

Yikes. For an introductory-level course, it's surprising how poorly this guy taught Unix. Assignment instructions are poorly written, and when confronted, he lashes out at students. Very unprofessional. The only upsides are his availability outside of class to answer questions, and that the assignments are fairly easy.

Currently working on final project. Lectures are poor quality. We are doing a final over things we have not done any projects over. Expect to be required to do things for a large amount of points that you have done no work on prior to in the class, with your only reference being poor lectures that hardly cover what is actual required.

I wanted to have faith in this course, but the reality is that it is structured all wrong. I really think Murrell is a nice guy, he just needs to change up the lectures heavily. The current lectures offer random bits of code and little helpful explanation, and our current final project is full of things we haven't previously done projects on.

New professor. He seems chill, but his coursework is horrible. If I didn't already know what we were learning in the class I would 100% fail. His assignments are sporadic and uncorrelated. He seems to not know what he is doing yet, and figuring it out while trying to teach us. Mizzou jus needs to do better in IT. Not enough qualified prof  in IT.
Seems like the professor talks about the same thing everyday at such a slow pace that it's impossible to pay attention and learn

Avoid classes by Murrell if you can. No teaching happening, won't ever know your grades. I am writing this review in week 11 of the semester and still haven't received my grade for the homework from WEEK 2! The lecture videos are him switching through completed code, not explaining it in depth at all, and then expecting you to do it yourself. Awful
Not helpful and is very sarcastic

Gives pre-recored lectures in which he quickly switches from tab to tab of already completed code while loosely explaining what it does. This was then followed by links to use to teach ourselves what the new topic was that week instead of him doing it himself. THIS was then followed by an assignment that asks you to do something you haven't learned

absolutely loved her! one of my favorite professors thus far. she's very easygoing and patient if you have any late work. as long as you put in some effort, you'll do fine. class discussions were fun and I was rarely bored. 10/10
She is awesome and grades easily as long as you put in effort. Nicest professor I have had in the English department. Take ENG3700 or any of her classes!!
Literally do the work and you will get an A. If it is late, tell her and she will understand. She was super nice and cared about what we had to say. Class was super easy and fun.

This class is a lot of reading and writing, but it's all interesting. Muller is very understanding with late work and really cares about her students! The class will prompt unique discussions and really promotes critical thinking. Generally, as long as you come to class and communicate with her, you'll do well. Grading was also pretty easy.
best professor I have had in college. She is passionate & is always willing to offer help, it is not hard to succeed in this class at all. She is also the most caring prof.

Virginia was an angel! I loved everything about this class. The only inconvenience is the Monday night movie, but everything you watch is very interesting and she does a nice job of tying the articles and movie together. You do weekly summaries over 2-3 assigned articles and have some minor projects throughout the semester. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Hilarious

reviews.comment: best professor I have had in college. She is specific in what it is she wants/needs from you in the class for you to get a good grade (& it really is not much.) She is passionate & is always willing to offer help, it is not hard to succeed in this class at all. She is also the most caring prof I've had and cares about your well being & offers help.
She's very nice and she would answer any question you have. Give back good advice for paper

I think she is just an amazing professor, very specific with what she expects and a good grader. She makes the class so interactive and helps you think about things you never thought off. Easy papers and feedbacks are really helpful.
awesome teacher
Amazing English teacher. If you put forth the effort your grade will reflect!

She was seriously so sweet and made this class really easy to do well in.  She grades really easily and if you follow her corrections and suggestions she's sure to at least give you points for improving the paper. She's so nice and actually kept me interested for a relatively boring English class.

I loved Prof Muller. She was incredibly encouraging of discussion, & constantly asked questions to provoke thought. One thing - she really allows students to go off a tangent, and that can be annoying sometimes. Attend class for the pop quizzes (I missed a couple, hence the grade), and do the readings. Her tests are easy (&easily graded).
Favorite professor by far. Speak up in class because she loves a good discussion. Don't be afraid to be opinionated. Great class. Highly recommend it.

DO NOT take this class by any means she makes it impossible to do well. I remember spending hours trying to make the perfect paper going off her corrections as well as several other peoples input and she still would not give me an A. For an english class you can definitely find a better/easier teacher than this
Kinda boring but its not that bad, im sure there aren't that many teachers much better for an english class. overall pretty good teacher

3 essays, 3 drafts each, and a fun finals week project you'll enjoy. thats it. no tests. not quizzes. fun class. interact as much as possible and you'll get an A. office hours for extra help on you essay reviews will guarantee A+.

one of my favorite teachers. ever. obviously cared a lot about making sure students were comfortable, etc... most of the negative comments on here are coming from english 1000 students, and almost every english 1000 teacher is viewed as "awful", and so on. she is AMAZING.
I didn't want to take this class.  I was glad to have her as my teacher.  She was helpful and nice.

god awful teacher. She is overly biased toward male students and holds some subtle communist viewpoints. Very Unhelpful then blames you for not understanding what she wants. Horrible teacher. Avoid like the plague!
She was awesome for world lit. She graded very easy. You just had to do the readings and participate. I really enjoyed the class discussions!
Nice person, Terrible teacher

She was a terrible teacher. Her teaching actually hurt my writing more than it helped it. She doesn't believe in technology and it's all creative writing. Do not under any circumstances take English 1000 with her.
She is very unclear about what she wants and expects and tends to be a biabia

this is the worst class i have ever taken.  She sucks as a teacher!  You go to class to sit there and do nothing, then when she revises your paper she tells you a bunch of s&%t that doesnt help you when revising it for the final class.

It was challenging, but in the end I think I learned something about myself as a writer.  I need to keep in mind that I will not create my best paper the first time, but I was able to improve my paper when I rewrote it and I was given props for that.

This class & this professor = both originals. Truth, this school = not ready for her & the hard work she asked. I transferred here from UIC & forgot what it was like to be in a class where I actually learn. Honestly the racism & disrespect from some of my classmates was next level & she quit teaching here. But she stayed the term & did not run!

This professor seemed to be nice at first, however as the class progressed she expected you to do work in her class every single day. This included weekends. She would check to see when you were active on the class page and how many hours you were active as well. Very tough grader with no rubrics and very vague grading criteria.

Tons of reading. Be prepared to spend all of your time reading and creating discussion posts that will take up your weekend. Not enough time given between assignments. 2 discussion posts and two papers due in one week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I love Prof. Murillo! She makes you work, but it pays off. She's great at explaining concepts and gives you lots of in-class practice. You get participation points and attendance points, so go to class! There's also a decent amount of homework, but it really helps you understand the topic. As long as you do the work, you'll get a good grade!

Prof. Murillo is the best! I wish I could take every college Spanish class with her. Lots of homework, lots of studying, lots of work, but you WILL learn Spanish. She is hard to read at first, but so fun and helpful once you get into the semester. Her exams are tough, but you'll be fine if you study. I'm sad that this was my last class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Murillo is AWESOME. I had to work hard to do well in her class - lots of studying, lots of homework, lots of big ticket assignments - but she gives great lectures, is easy to work with, and will give you the grade you deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The first couple of days she is kind of rude in class but the rest of the semester she is a lot easier. Her class isn't overly difficult but she does talk the majority of class in spanish so be prepared for that. Overall not a bad teacher, and she is a nice person.

This class was extremely easy. On the first couple days of class, she comes off as kind of rude but after the initial week, I absolutely loved her. She is really funny and asks a lot of questions to start funny debates. Absolutely love her.

He was good but be prepared to get called on in class if you arent even ready. If you miss class be prepared for your participation points to go down. Can be a tad bit unorganized but overall hes a really good professor but grades so insanely hard! Really cares about the students but if you dont go to class be prepared to not pass the class
Not too much homework but calls on you in class if you're ready or not. You have to prepare for the lesson if you don't catch on well. Really nice and explains concepts really well.

Martin Mulligan is really one of the best Spanish teachers I've had. Sure he can be a tad unorganized but he genuinely cares about what he is teaching as well as the students. He's always available to help and is an easy grader if you show you are working hard. Im so bad at Spanish but he made it really easy to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Martin was a good professor. He would occasionally  digress in lecture, but he was respectable. He didn't always catch students' mistakes, so they wouldn't learn from them. I wish he would make connections among grammar tenses. A lot of  times I did not know which one to use, so that's something he could improve on is going over each function.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's a little unorganized.  You have to check Vistas once or twice a day. He never announced when we had homework. He was lenient on grading in some areas like accent marks. He's always enthusiastic about the material but goes off track from the lesson plan sometimes. He goes over everything on the test in class. He's a tough grader on projects.

Martin saved my grade several times throughout the course of the semester.  The class isn't easy, though.  All of SPAN2100 at Mizzou covers a lot of the "subjunctive" tense, and since we don't have it in English, it's hard to get a handle on it.  Martin explained the subjunctive pretty well, and gave his students handouts to help remember the rules

I studied much more than usual, but got "B"s on tests because of a few missed accents, not because I didn't understand the concepts. The online homework is usually posted 3 times a week, but there isn's any sort of alert system. I missed 1 assignment all semester because he posted it the day before it was due, and it dropped my grade 3%.

He is very early in his teaching career and has yet to find what exactly works. He leaves out little details that I only found out because I read the text book. His tests are pretty difficult and while lets english in the class slide, he often speaks entirely in spanish using words that I have never heard of. Very helpful out of class, however.

Dale is honestly a great professor, the final was due for this class early in the morning and I missed it and he allowed me to retake it later on in the evening get full credit. Honestly, one of the best professors ever.

Took this class online and overall a pretty solid class! I like an online class that has clear structure and this class is that! Notes and Quiz boom you're done for the week. There is a midterm and final test AND project but it was nothing crazy at all. A super solid online course if you're someone like me who prefers online!

Professor does not respond to students, however I hear that he is responsive on LinkedIn so there's that. Easy class overall though just don't expect to get any help from the professor, only the PLA's.

The entire course is online with modules coming every week. The grade for coding assignments is for participation and not if you did it correctly. The Quizes and Exams are extremely easy. If you have half a brain and can use chatgpt you will pass this class with an easy A.

Really well-formatted courses. He provides a lot of documentation for every module and grades weekly assignments based on effort. Reading the documentation takes a while but makes the quizzes a lot easier. Quizzes and tests are open note, with no time limit. Stay on track with the work and the course will be easy.

Extremely easy course if you already know Python - otherwise, you might have to do a lot of self teaching. Weekly workload was only about 30mins - 1hr for the first half, and then picked up to ~2-6hrs/week for the second half. Only complaint is the lack of consistent communication from Dale himself.

Dale is the best professor I have ever had hands down. If you have the chance to take a class with him definitely do. He cares about the students and actually wants us to learn. This class was completely self paced, as long as everything is completed by the end of the semester. He grades quickly and fairly and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you have the opportunity to learn Swift with Dale "The Alpha Male" Musser, you've gotta do it. This course, albeit online and asynchronous, is a step up from other CS and IT courses offered at Mizzou. Dale makes it a point to make sure you learn to program well and have fun while doing so, which is something that few professors manage to do.

Compared to its predecessor this class is a walk in the park. There is not very much content in the course and the assignments were reasonable which made it an easy A+. Thankfully there is not as much documentation to read as 4405. I liked how Dale created up to date lectures for this course and how everything was due at the end of the semester.

This class seems to feature almost no lectures from Dale. The content is fine for the most part. My only issue with it is that some of the quiz and exam questions are outdated for the version of Python we used in the course. People claim that this course is a cakewalk but I disagree. It is a high workload. It was a great class and I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: 100% online self-paced course using Swift programming language for FS '22. Mostly graded on whether or not you can implement code into a given challenge/assignment. Online lectures are straightforward and he gives you the code afterwards as a sort of reflection

Lectures were completely optional and homework is easy if you know how to use Google or have any prior Python experience at all. If you don't know how to do something, look back at the resources on Canvas or ask the PLAs for help.

I didn't find the lectures very useful. I had to ask PLAs a lot of my questions which sometimes helped. It took months for me to receive feedback on my assignments/projects. The class is organized well, but not always executed well.

Dale has done a good job of structuring this class; I feel like I learned a lot of material. He has made it very straightforward and simple to do alone. Most of it is you teaching yourself so I feel like I didn't get to experience a whole lot of him, but during his online lectures he is very knowledgeable about Swift and good at explaining things.
IT 1040 was a pretty easy class. Dale was a good teacher and a lot of the material that you need to succeed in the class is online and on the homework he assigns.

Had to drop the class because he simply refused to respond to emails. I received a 0 on an assignment that I asked for an extension on because I was in the emergency room. I received several 0s that did not make sense to me; when I asked about them, he never responded. Absolutely unacceptable behavior. Your job as a professor is to help students.

Intro taken in python. Assignments, projects due every Friday. Class isn't very hard if you pay attention and study. You can't read an article once and know how to code. First few projects are way too easy then it ramps up so just study a bit. My TA was the only reason I got a B, had an A all year. Dale provides adequate material to study and learn

Class is difficult if you don't have a background but you can work to be good in the class. PLA's were useless on discord, don't even bother. You have to work for the grade and if you don't understand the initial projects you are screwed. If you can't understand the work in this class, switch majors.

Great for those with programming backgrounds, but tough for beginners. Material was easy to follow for the first 1/2 of the semester before it got difficult. Dale is a great teacher and passionate about what he does. However, he is in CA so it can be difficult to make a connection with him. The PLAS are easy to contact via Discord for project help.

This class is okay. I didn't know anything about programming before this course which put me behind. The PLTA's are alright and Musser tries his best but I hate that everything is online. As many students have mentioned, everything gets pretty difficult after midterms. Make sure to hammer out the basics of python. Test your skill often & study them
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dale Musser is an absolute king. Programming is challenging so be prepared to take awhile on the assignments but he and his TAs are fantastic. He is very relaxed but can ramble sometimes. Pretty much everything is on Canvas and is mostly assignment based

To simply put it as this, Dale is a nice guy but the assignments he give can be hard especially if you don't have much experience with programming, but that's not to say the assignment are impossible it's just that you'll have to put a lot of effort especially for a 1040 level course if you want to succeed

I can see how those without any prior programming experience may have had issues with this course. I have a decent amount of experience programming and I feel as though that has given me some advantage. Around midterms, things get more difficult, but the goals are realistic and attainable with some clever thinking.
If you have never used python or any coding language this will be difficult. First weeks are easy and then very hard.

The first 3 weeks were easy, but everything got much harder. You ask PLA's for help, and they don't even respond at times. I have never coded before this class and the PLA's don't really care because they expect you to know everything. During class he shows us coding that doesn't even relate to our assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Musser is a nice guy but his class is hard for anyone that doesn't have much experience with Python,, just like the other reviews say, the class starts off easy (your printing our basic statements, creating basic functions that'll do things like calculating volumes of cylinders, etc) and then the class all of the sudden gets hard

INFOTC 1040 starts with basic programming which is what you expect at a 1000 level class. Near mid-term's, the class goes in a complete 180 degrees and projects become extremely challenging. The professor is really nice but the class is brutal if you don't have the slightest experience in python programming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: You either get 0's or 100's on the homework and the midterm project. Good luck, you'll need it.

I had Prof. Musser in three classes here at Mizzou, and I look forward to each one because everything is clear and concise. There is a weekly plan to follow and I like that there's a choice between visual and reading learners as I'm a reading/note taking hands-on learner and sometimes videos are a waste of time to me. Loving all I'm learning!

For a basic 1000 level programming course, I didn't expect the work to be more harder than it was supposed to be. Before you attend any lecture, you must read the links Musser posted for that week or else you won't understand any of the material (since this class is very fast paced). Adding on, you either get 100 or 0 for assignments no in between

Currently in INFOTC 1040 with Musser and class is a mess. Someone is basically projecting Musser from a screen (since Musser is in Cali) so while this class is listed on the schedule as in person most of the work like homeworks/quizzes is done online also while the content isn't the hardest there is lots of studying you have to do outside of class

Worst professor in my four years at MU. Sent him multiple emails asking for help through the semester and got only one response saying hed get back to me in the morning (obviously I never heard back). Even reached out to other faculty to help me get ahold of him and they had no luck.

It is like being given the parts to a car, but with no manual or prior knowledge of how to assemble everything. Horribly setup class. Believes it is most beneficial to you when you make a valid attempt. I do not have the luxury of trial and error without counting against my grade. I need all the information the first time to learn and excel.
There was no partial credit, so you either got a 0 or 100, grading was late, never knew why I would given zeros when I tried and 100s when I did not. A serious mess.
Awesome Professor, I wish he would teach in person still. His classes from what I have had are structured similarly with weekly assignments and two large tests.

One of the best professors at MU and the reason I stuck with the IT major. His class structure and grading methods helped to take off the pressure and help me focus on developing my coding skills. Failing was okay in the class and I think that idea of failing and learning from it is what should be focused on in college.
Great teacher, good at getting information across.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Like all of Dale's classes, the structure of the class is given weekly. Each module beginning on Saturday morning. I took this class the summer of 2020. I would not recommend to take this class in the summer, as the semester is quite a bit shorter than a regular semester. Learning a new code structure in the short amount of time is tough.

Lots of reading to do for this class. TA's were very helpful. Wish there was a video lecture form instead of reading. Definitely a step up from 1040. Was very accommodating with COVID even though nothing changed with the delivery of this class.

SP20 was the first time Dale did a live lecture for any of his classes since he left for San Francisco, and he's still got it. He offered the live lecture or the traditional way that he normally teaches his online classes. Learned so much more from watching the live lectures. Wish he did this for more of his classes. Highly respected and liked.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Musser is always respected here at the University of Missouri. He is a very easy grader, and it is apparent that he truly cares about his students' learning. His lectures were online via zoom and always wanted to answer any question asked. Using the internet, this class will be very easy.

Dale Musser is one of the extremely few professors at MU that are very easy to work with and genuinely cares about his students learning. His assignments do take some time to work out, but aren't overly challenging to the point of banging your head on the wall. He's also one of the 2 professors that showed compassion for the COVID-19 pandemic. A++

Dale is a good teacher but since he isn't on campus/doesn't respond to emails (TAs do though obviously) it makes the class feel even less personal than most online classes. I took his 2040 class too and it feels like we do readings that don't help and watch barely coherent videos. Despite that I gave a good rating because overall his class is good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved the course! Definitely take his courses if you are going into IT. Everything is online and grading is based off of effort and participation. As long as you do all the work, you will succeed and get an easy A. I'm looking forward to his IT2040 course in the fall!
He seems to care about his students and their success. I wish he was teaching on campus.

Professor Musser is regarded as the one of, if not the best professor in the Computer Science department. I passively learned more from watching him code in class than I did in most hands on classes. His teaching style and approach to learning is phenomenal. He made databases a breeze. It is a shame he is leaving the school and will be missed.

He's a great professor. He gives tons of feedback and really cares about his students. I've taken every class he offers. The classes are definitely easy A's but it doesn't subtract from learning the material. He gives it to you without the convolution.
His SQL databasing class has to be one of the easiest in the Computer Science program as long as youve been paying attention in previous classes. Just show up and listen and youll do fine.

I would argue Dale to be the best professor at Mizzou. He makes his lectures interesting and explains things very well. He makes some great jokes and is not to intensive with assignments. He will give you real deal and no bull. Classes are interactive and very easy to follow. Seriously, take one of his courses and you will agree. He is the best!!!

He is a hard working professor at the University of Missouri-Columbia. He definitely cares for his students, and their success. I have specifically tried to take every course that he teaches at the school, simply because I enjoy his teaching style so much. He teaches with live code! That's one of the best parts!

I enjoyed every lecture in Musser's class. He covers a wide array of topics/viewpoints on Software Design, and explains concepts incredibly well. He encourages students to explore on their own and think outside the box when learning. His classes are an easy A, and you will learn a great deal.

Dr. Musser is one of the best professors at MU. His lectures are super easy to follow and learn from, he greatly cares about students, and he truly enjoys teaching. His OO class is impeccably structured. All of the requirements are clearly listed, and the assignments are great and obvious representations of the core concepts. 10/10 would take again

I took this class as a requirement, and I thought I was not the biggest fan of Shakespeare. However, she made this course so fun and got me to love the subject! I learned so much, and she is so passionate and knowledgeable about the material. I have such a good time taking her course, and I would definitely recommend any of her courses!

While I have no doubt the professor is knowledgeable about literature, I would not recommend taking her class if you are not an english major. The lectures were interesting, but she nitpicked through all my papers and finally accused me of plagiarism at the end of the semester, which I did not do. I'm too much of an idiot to plagiarize.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Anne is a genuine person who is extremely flexible and always willing to meet a student half-way. She makes sure that assignments are communicated clearly and everyone is on the same page. If you need help, she will go to any lengths.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Myers is such a great teacher. Her lectures make 17th-century British literature interesting, which is saying something. She genuinely cares about all of her students and is always willing to help. Best professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Myers is a very caring person who will work with you on anything you need help with. She is so approachable and makes learning about dull topics interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had; I don't know why she doesn't have a 5.0 rating on here. SUPER nice, very funny, genuinely cares about her students and loves what she teaches. It's an English class, so you have to read a lot and actually MUST read to do well on the quizzes, but she is a very fair grader and always available to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you do the readings, you will do well on the quizzes and tests.  All the quizzes and tests include extra credit questions that are easy.  Overall, the class is a lot of fact recall, but the readings are very interesting, and class discussions are too.  Her feedback on papers isn't particularly helpful though, and she grades papers a bit harshly.
Clear grading, the readings kinda suck but you can get away with not reading everything.
This class was dry and HARD!! Hardest class I've ever taken, but Milton is a tough author. Myers is a very nice, knowledgeable professor. Take her for something other than Milton, though.

She grades a little more strenuously when looking at papers than most professors-- it is really helpful to take advantage of her office hours to discuss your paper topics with her prior to turning them in. Her lectures are interesting, and you can tell she really enjoys her subject.

Content isn't really difficult, but she can be hard to follow in lecture,not always clear about her expectations and really difficult to write a paper for. She is really strange and not a terrible teacher but I would avoid her if you can

Prof. Myers gets so excited about what she teaches that she does prat falls and stomps around. It's strange at first, but you grow to like it.  Discussion was not mandatory as she always had interesting lectures prepared. She's also good at deflecting stupid comments and dealing with those few obnoxious students in every class. Three cheers y'all.

I'm gonna miss her. Thermo 1 was a pain but she made it manageable and I even found myself enjoying it in my bettter moments. I'm sure the new Thermo 1 prof is wonderful, though. Thank you for your work, Dr. Myers.
Best professor ever. Very smart and great at teaching. Also super funny.
Thermo 1 was the hardest class I've ever taken so far, still, Dr. Myers made it approachable and taught it well. Go to her office hours and you'll be able to succeed. (Don't underestimate any test!)

Thermo is a tough class, but despite the toughness Dr. Myers is one of the best professors I have had. She is always willing to help and clearly wants her students to succeed. Her class is designed to be tough though so you will have to work for it especially if you want a good grade.
Dr. Myers was an AMAZING teacher! She is very interested in her students learning and will help them at a moments notice.

Dr. Myers is simply fantastic. She's helpful, knowledgeable, and a fair grader. You can tell she loves the students and really cares about the direction MIzzou's ChemE department is heading. Take a course with her, you won't regret it.

Dr. Myers teaches very well, is a fair grader, is extremely knowledgeable, and conveys information well.  There were only two instances during the semester that I felt I was lost, at all other times I knew what I should know, or I knew what I should be able to do, but I couldn't necessarily do it.  The course was difficult, but I learned a lot.

This was a dual-taught course with Pinhero/Myers. Dr. Myers is incredibly intelligent. She teaches applicably, which really helped us students to understand the material better. She throws you to the wolves and have you struggle, but will then bring you back in and discuss what went wrong. I couldn't have asked for a better Thermodynamics course.

Dr. Myers is an absolute joy. I am so grateful to have been her student. Truly invested in her students, cares about learning, and is always available for help. With hard work, I understood everything in this class and felt confident about the work I turned in- that's how a class should be. Very challenging and rewarding. Best prof in chem eng.
Prof is very engaged in student learning. She will happily retrace her steps to cover things one or a few students don;t understand. Very clear expectations for what material needs to be mastered.

I love Dr. Myers - she really wants her students to succeed and was a pleasure to learn from. She knows her Chemical Engineering very well. Her tests can be tricky sometimes, but she helps round out the trickiness with a wealth of opportunities for her students. I wish I could have her for every class in this major. One of the best teachers I know.

Myers was very unwilling to work with my accommodations through the university because he felt it would get in the way of my participation. The grading is very strict and attendance is mandatory. Would not take again.

Noah is a Pompas Jack. Does not take feedback well and talks down to you. The class started with 21 there was only 8 of us at the end. All making C at the end of the class. Very labor intensive and uses multiple outside programs to have our work done. If the app or program isn't working, it's all on you to figure it out before your deadline.

Noah is very kind, but for such a young professor I wish he would be chiller. Sometimes he acts like an uptight strict old man and does not give much slack. But he teaches very well. He is very funny and teaches his class all in Spanish but makes you understand what he means with movements and he is hard but if you want a challenge he is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

He teaches out of a textbook from the 1990s and the material is extremely outdated. On top of this, his lecture notes are hand written and terribly difficult to follow when studying. He provides little resources for outside class learning and the homework problems are very different from what is learned in class.
Dr. Noble puts a good amount of care into a class that it would be really easy to phone it in for. Term Project can take a long time to do if you put care into it, so start early

Very difficult to replicate his work. HWs that require the use of a softwares he never walks you thoroughly. Expect hours of study by trying to understand his messy class notes. STUDY HARD and beyond! Tests are tricky and conceptual questions may seem vague sometimes. Honestly, I was expecting more from the chair of the IMSE department.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He brought many people to tell their career stories. Some were inpirationals while other not so. Most of the class time was spent with mentors and other TAs, only saw Dr. Noble once per week. He wants people to pass and this class is not strenuos. All the homework was online and the deadlines were good enough to get other homework finished

This class was fantastic and Dr. Noble taught it very well. You truly learn a lot of good IE material in this class, however, it is a ton of work. Six homework assignments, three midterms, discussion posts every other week, a presentation with a partner, read a novel and write a review, and a final project. Great class taught well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Noble was very good in this course. He was a very nice guy with a good sense of humor. He cares about his students and wants them all to succeed. The homework was actually fun at times as he has some great intro to IE topics to explore. There will be 3 group projects, get them done early and work with your group! End of semester project is long
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Absolutely brutal class. Extremely boring material and his expectations of the class reading between lines and having random accounting and finance knowledge is ridiculous. The lecture literally puts you to sleep. his quizzes are bogus and good luck arguing a test score. Except the fact that this class is going suck really bad

This professor teaches a boring subject and is a bit quirky from a personality standpoint.  His appalling delivery only heightens the mind-numbing nature of the material.  Stay clear of Noble for any reason you can rationalize doing so while meeting your degree requirement.

I wasn't even going to rate him but I had to couter balance this persons great score they gave Dr Noble. He cannot teach. Granted the material is insanely boring and there no point for engineering students to be learning about finance. His class is boring, its only twice a week so its 80 minutes of painful lecturing.
Great prof!
Terrible teacher, didn't have a clue on how to relate information.

He doesn't use Canvas. You don't have a clear idea of what your grade is until the end of the semester. You have to physically print papers and walk them to his office, and there's SO many papers even though it's not a writing intensive. Heavy reading assignments every class. He's very nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course was a requirement for me but I wish I did not have to take it. It is completely online and the set up of the class seems disorganized. There are many readings and the tests are not easy- make sure you remember every little thing you read. Pretty heavy grader too so make sure what you do is perfect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If one is a full time student and works 40 hrs, his class is near hard to participate in. It is a fully online class, and the set up is frustrating, as is the process for turning in materials. Syllabus is on Canvas, bigger papers are published in assignments not modules, all work turned in via email, except for discussion posts. So much reading.

I had Noah for my capstone class and he was one of the nicest and most approachable professors I've had at Mizzou. He definitely expects a lot from his students, but once you learn how he grades it isn't hard, and his feedback is always helpful. He's knowledgable about the subject matter, and if you do the readings and come to class you'll be fine.

This class was very challenging; lots and LOTS of reading and papers, but it was a writing intensive course. He's kind of intimidating, which makes participation hard. Sometimes expectations aren't clear, so I had to email him often for clarification. The other students in the class made it a fun dynamic and Noah loosened up a bit by the end .

Professor Heringman assigns an intense amount of work. He could probably tone it down. However, he's is passionate about his subject and really wants his students to succeed. He fully expects participation in class and will embarrass you if he knows you haven't read. The works he assigns are interesting and relevant. An intelligent, kind professor.

Assigned 200+ pages of reading almost every day.  He wasn't clear and mumbled.  His syllabus was confusing.   His grading was all over the place and his comments weren't helpful.  He wouldn't even really teach class and had other students lecture instead.  I won't be taking another class with him again.

Very knowledgeable and personable professor.  He's pleasant and his lectures always bring up fresh perspectives, BUT ...his standards are very high for both exams and written work.  91% is a B in his class.  Very challenging, but enjoyable if you can just press on and work your butt off.  Read every word of his syllabus!
The man is psychotic. He'll tear apart your work with a smile. He maybe easy for lower level classes but my capstone was hell. STAY AWAY!
Noah is VERY knowledgeable on the subject; however, he honestly challenges his students to do the absolute best they can do, and his expectations can be set quite high.
Very sharp scholar with a broad knowledge base. Very approachable, excellent lectures, and solid texts.

Dr. Herringman is one of the few professors I have met who actually wants to share his passion for the subject with you.  He is very patient and makes a lot of effort.  He took a lot of his time to answer my questions outside of class as well.

I had fun in this class due to my awesome classmates, but there was WAY too much reading for a mortal to accomplish per class, and then, on top of that, we hardly referred to the reading at all in discussion.  He also seems to have different standards for each student.  His instructions aren't very clear, nor are his comments.

Heringman is interesting and definitely knows his stuff. But he is hard to literally HEAR sometimes (he mumbles) and he's a bit...odd. I really do not enjoy British Literature, so I got very little from the class. He's pretty basic, though.
No Comments
No Comments

Noah was a decent teacher, though his tests were supremely unspecified, and as a result you had very little idea as to what to expect. Also, he continuously brought his political beliefs into class where they absolutely did not belong. He trashed particular groups, and offended some people.

By far one of the best professors I've had here. If you follow the outlines for writing essays, you'll do fine. He even goes over your essay with you before it's due. Attendance is mandatory but it's not the end of the world if you miss a class or two. Very chill and funny guy I definitely recommend choosing him to be your english professor.

this dude's an absolute legend. super casual and open with his students, made the classroom way less intimidating. also offered great feedback on papers and was very lenient with grading. all in all, really solid introductory english course that also introduces you to MU resources for writing future papers. 10/10 would take again

Professor Siela is my favorite professor Ive have had in college so far. The class was pretty easy and was essay based. He wants everyone to get an A and he will help you get it. He gave great feedback on how to improve your paper before you would turn it in. He is halarious and empathizes with his students and is just all around a great person.

Professor Siela has an easy class, for sure. I did not get much out of it, though. He was nice, he likes to tell stories, and he does not grade terribly hard. Have something decent to turn in, and you will get a good grade. This class did not challenge me, but it did not hurt my GPA either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think we wrote 4 papers the entire semester and the entire class was out of 100 points. Prof Siela is literally so cool and I couldnt have asked for a better professor. He is such an interesting guy and is so laid back! Has conference weeks and tells you what you need to do to get an A on the paper. Take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I was nervous going into this class because I am not the best at writing. Professor Siela has helped me so much to improve on my writing and english based skills. He is so fun and is super understanding and really just wants for us to succeed. Some readings, a few essays that he gives tons of help and feedback on, and about 15 in class assignments.
Professor Siela is super layed back.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Siela was easily the best professor I had my freshman year. He was super accessible outside of class and was sure to answer any questions I had and would be understanding for any problems I had. He is caring for students and wants to make sure you have all you need to put forward your best work. He's also just hilarious.

Prof Siela was super easy on grading and very easy to contact if there was a problem or you feel you need an extension or extra help. He's very funny and chill. I would definitely take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Siela is truly one of the best professors I have had at the university. His lectures were engaging as we were learning way more than just 'writing' but the news happening in the world. Siela cares about his students like no other and has a great sense of humor. He helps develop you as a writer and doesn't stress his students out! Amazing Prof!

This class with Siela was great. The class consists of 3 papers and a project along with participation and little grade bumpers. Siela was a very funny guy who cares a lot about his students. The only thing I did not like was the use of politics throughout the class. Overall, this was a very easy gen ed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Fascinating lectures with a sense of humor. Lands enthusiasm for art is contagious. I looked forward to his class and wish I couldve taken more.
Dr. Land is incredibly brilliant when it comes to his class--he's very passionate about art, and is a nice guy. Sit near the front, as he is hard of hearing--and speak up!
He knows what he's talking about and has good interest in the subject matter. His tests aren't particularly difficult. He is a good teacher.
I had little interest before taking his intro to art history, long story short, I'm an art history major now and absolutely love it! He is very inspiring and loves what he talks about.

Norman Land is a great Art History Professor. I had him for 17th Century italian art (baroque) and part of western art 2. If you like art history, you will love him. It may be a little difficult, however if you arent that familiar w/ art history. His passion for the subject shows. I suggest baroque, and not western art though.
Great, enthusiastic professor...but very dry lectures and determines grade from two multiple choice exams only.
I think he's a good teacher. He is very knowledgeable and seems genuinely passionate about what he does.

You better be interested in art history otherwise you're screwed.  Sit in the front otherwise you cannot understand him and he can't understand you.  Hopefully you have a good memory as well otherwise drop it.  If you have all of those things then go ahead and take his class.

Great teacher!  Made me decide to become an art history major.  He is extremely knowledgeable on his area of expertise and I find him to be hilarious.  His classes require lots of memorization, so if you don't have a good memory, don't take his classes.
really nice man... tries hard to crack jokes - just laugh, he'll love you for it. memorization is key - doesn't require a lot of effort if you just take the time to do the readings and memorizing

Professor Land is a decent guy. He tries to make jokes sometimes, but many arent that funny. His lectures are ok, but i find art history to be boring. I hated the tests because you get 60sec per slide ID and little time to do the essays. overall, hes a decent teacher.

He is a pretty cool/funny teacher. It is hard to pay attention in his class but you don't always have to go. And sit in the back if you plan on leaving in the middle of his lecture. But overall he is a pretty awesome teacher.
His tests are pretty easy.  He's a nice guy.

Dr. Norum has trouble making her lectures exciting. She is fairly monotone and it can be hard to pay attention sometimes. There are 10 or so homework assignments throughout the semester, some of which you must go to a store to complete. The tests are online so use that to your advantage, although they can be difficult. Come ready to do math
This class isn't too terribly hard it is just a pain because attendance is random and for points and the tests aren't necessarily easy. You need to study and pay attention.

Class is not mandatory but she takes 10 random attendances. The cyber assignments are really easy but if you don't make As on the test then its really hard to get an A overall. You'll get at least  B if you take the class and pay a little bit of attention

I took this class towards my minor and it ended up being HELL. The tests are impossible and she is so boring. I've always thought TAM was an awesome field, but she brings nothing to the table with this class.

She was soooo boring!!! I came into this class thinking it would be my major, but she made the material completely uninteresting. Also, shes kind of out of it sometimes, she counted me absent even when I did a presentation that day....
she is really hard to take seriously because she pronounces a lot of designer names wrong but overall its really easy
She was kind of boring and talked about her kids alot but it was an easy class altogether
Great professor! You will learn a lot. It is challenging, but you are given every opportunity to learn and do well. It is sad that so many business majors dislike economics so much.

Extremely enthusiastic and really wants her students to learn. However, her teaching methods need to change. Her class is hard -- even her TA's didn't understand her homework half the time. She will give you an insane curve if you show effort. Go to class & sit near the front. Go to walking hrs. I ended up failing the final but got a B+ on MyZou
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Lee is a good professor and truly cares about her students. She loves getting to know as many as she can over the semester. Going to all lectures is a necessity if you want to get a good grade, and there are usually clicker quizzes every morning. It's a difficult and time consuming class, but with hard work, a good grade is very possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's more difficult than most of the freshman level class. You will need to go to class, take thorough notes, and read the book in your leisure time. Professor Lee's class gives you in-depth understanding of Macroeconomics, but the time and efforts you will need to devote to this class is no joke. However, I still enjoy her class. She's awesome.

Explains what concepts are, however the math on the in class quizzes is not covered or explained. Very hard to understand. Quizzes and exams are quite difficult. She yells and screams at 8 am. The "extra credit" she provides are walking hours usually during my other classes, so I am not able to get any of the extra credit. Avoid at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are mandatory but are very informative & descriptive. Lots of extra credit offered for attendance throughout semester. Tests are very difficult, but attending class, doing ALL of the reading, working diligently on quizzes & homework will help you prevail. This class required hours of studying & hard work but an "A" is definitely attainable
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have ever had. 1. her English is difficult to understand. 2. She is not accommodating with technological issues. Will not get back to you in a timely manner and if she does it is rude. I believe she is legitimately out to fail every student she can and would not recommend her to anyone! Especially if your GPA is hurting
She is hard to understand in class and the quizzes she assigns are tricky as well. She does not work with you on clicker points or grading matters.

Professor Lee is a wonderful human being. She can talk a bit fast sometimes and she REALLY speeds through the slides but if you come to class focused and pay attention you will get the information you need. Most importantly, make sure you do the readings or you'll be lost!

Gives out homework, does not explain how to do it until you turn it in. Same with quizzes. Tests are very difficult to complete in the given amount of time. Talks extremely fast and not clear all the time. Just read everything and you might be okay.

The worst class I have taken at the university. She doesn't allow the use of laptops in her class and she speeds through every slide. It is also very hard to understand her. Be prepared to teach yourself all of the information. I highly suggest that you do not sign up for her class.
Go to class and you will be okay. She gives extra credit take advantage of it. Study a lot for the exams and quizzes.
Enthusiastic teacher but has terrible teaching methods. Her class can be confusing at a lot of time

worst teacher i have ever experienced. She hardly speaks English which makes understanding the content that much more difficult. I would not recommend taking her class unless you want it to Decrease your GPA. Overall worst experience I have had at the University.

She is super passionate and knowledgeable. The exams are not that bad. There is a lot to study for so don't wait until the night before. Go to lectures since attendence will be taken and sometimes there are extra credits. Huge curve- I got a C on the final, had a B+ with homework quizzes and extra credits, and eneded up with an A on MyZou.
One of the best teachers I've ever had. She is passionate about her subject matter and truly cares about her students.

She is the best teacher I ever had.  She loves her students and teaching and is clear on her expectations. Don't expect a special treatment or break from her.  She sets the rule of the class and follow it through.  She treat you as a responsible adult. A tough lady but treat everyone the same.  Blame yourself if you do not do your part.

Dr. Lee as a person is great. She's really nice and approachable and her lecture can be funny but wow her tests and quizzes were hard. I would study about 16 hours over three days for a test and after curve still only get around a 78. If you skip you will fail. Try your best to keep up on reading even if it's a bit unrealistic.
Takes awhile to understand her.  She will treat this class like it is the only one that you have, and will pile it on.  Definitely don't take her class and just take it over the summer if you can.
I didn't like her at first. But then I find her class is very good! And she takes care of her students!
Class was tough. You really have to study. The quizzes are very difficult.

She was a good teacher and she meant well by a lot of things that she did but her tests are terrible I studied night and day for those things and never got over a 70% constantly I saw 3 right answers on the test but it was just which one was more right overall a extremely hard class but I also do not like economics very much.

Most difficult class I've ever taken. Dr. Lee is great teacher, and she is funny. I like her, but her tests are insane. I (and most of the class) studied day and night for her exams and still did poorly. She curves because half the class would fail if she didn't. But as long as you go to class and make an honest effort, she'll make sure you pass.
The lecture of this class is very boring and the exams aren't that difficult, but the final is next to impossible.

Myoung Lee is by far my favorite professor on campus. She genuinely cares about her students' success. However, you must attend all of her lectures otherwise you won't understand what is going on and you won't be able to take advantage of the enormous amount of extra credit she gives.

I'm not refuse to be interested by any professor. Lee just failed to interest me. She brings bad parts(instead of good parts) of Asian teaching style to classroom. Lee also let us subscribe WSJ, but she didn't use it at all. Just FYI professors can get benefits from WSJ if certain amount of students in the class subscribe. Google WSJ for professors

I loved Myoung-Lee. I know she is one of the more hated teachers but she is seriously one of the best at Mizzou. She is enthusiastic, goes out of her way to help everyone, and is a unique and eccentric character. Like how could you not love her? Oh yeah, when someone doesn't try or do well in a class, they blame the teacher. Myoung-Lee is great

This class is seriously not that difficult.  Yes, the tests are hard but she curves them and gives a LOT of bonus points towards the end of the semester just for attending class! I ended up with a B but she curved it to an A- because I only missed one day.  Really nice lady and really passionate about Econ. Don't be afraid to take her. Go to class.

Love economics but this class was DIFFICULT. Hard to understand her at times and questions can be worded vaguely where you can misunderstand what she's trying to ask. Advice: Pay special attention to her lectures and read ahead in the book. Many times I found questions for assignments and quizzes hidden in future chapters. Good Luck... she curves!

Dr. Lee obviously loves her job and is interested in preparing her students, yet her methods are not so effective when dealing with a 400+ lecture hall. Her accent is difficult and takes getting used to. If you want a good grade(B or above) you must dedicate at least 50% of your effort Shes nice person, but inefficient as a professor. Do not take!!

This has been the worst class I have ever taken at Mizzou. You can't understand her and her exams are ridiculous. After learning new material, we are having our cumulative final the next class. Please tell me this does't make sense. Try to avoid her at all cost. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES
This is, by far, the worst Professor that I've had while attending the University of Missouri. Her tests, quizzes, and homework were as unclear as her accent.

She made the first exam super easy by taking exact questions off of HW and Practice Exams, but then for the second exam, she changed it up completely and mostly everyone failed. She quizzes you over stuff we hardly covered and I had a really hard time understanding her heavy accent. Don't take this class with her! She makes it so much harder.
Basic economic concept can be ruined by her. I tried my best to follow her on class but the way she taught made me feel like Macro Econ is the hardest course in the world.

I love Econ, however, after taking Prof. Lee's class for Macro, I almost dropped it as a minor. She is a really nice person who cares about Econ, but she is not a great teacher. She is extremely difficult to understand & she manages to muddle basic concepts, two things that are not conducive in an economics teacher. Be prepared to teach yourself.

This teacher is the most insane I've ever experienced. She is incomprehensible and has requirements that just make my blood boil with anger. I treat you with respect and dignity as an adult, I respect the same in return as an adult.

This is possibly one of the worst teachers I have ever had. First of all you can't understand a word she is saying! She talks down to the class & her outlines are horrendous. Only B I have received in college. I was in hospital 4 two weeks & went to her office hours and she literally said "too bad, cant help u, drop the class" - she should be fired

Possibly the nicest teacher on campus. She loves economics, and is so accessible outside of class. You'll get a little extra credit for attending class/office hours/walking hours, but you will not get bumped letter grades at all. This course requires you to heavily read the textbook, ace the quizes and homework, and study hard for the tests.
I had her for Macro and Intermediate Micro. She's a great teacher and is definitely passionate about the subject. Go to class and she'll boost your grade.

I had her for Macro and it was my least favorite class. I didn't even deserve to pass but she pushed my grade up to passing. Yet, I got a B+ in Micro no problem. Granted, she offers help when needed but I went to the TA for HW help and did worse than when I did it on my own.

Had for two classes. How can you hate her? Oh, yeah. That's right. People who hate subjects they have to take but don't want to (like Economics) blame the professor. Here's what's up -- If you don't like Dr. Lee, you're prob. just not smart enough for economics. She's brilliant, one of the nicest ladies I have ever had, fair, and a great teacher.
More interested in handing out candy than teaching. Makes simple concepts super confusing. She also incorrectly taught game theory. AVOID

Class sucks. It is seriously the worst part of my day. I'd like to ask questions in her class, but she shoves her microphone in your face. Honestly, a B is doable, but the amount of workload you have to do to get that B is unbearable.  Everything about this class will make you mad
