A waste of time. On the rare chance you understand what she's saying then she's lecturing on topics you've already been tested on. Terrible teacher.

A lot of people have trouble understanding her, but I didn't have any issues. She's very energetic and definitely passionate about economics. Dr. Lee loves seeing her students outside of class and I highly recommend taking advantage of her walking & office hours. Read, use the workbook, & take diligent notes - don't expect to slide by in her class.

20% of her questions on her test ask you about what she said specifically during class when everyone was busy copying down her notes and physically unable to lister to her and comprehend what she said at the same time. I got over 100 in Sharon Ryan's class and got B's on Mrs. Lee's tests...

At first she is very very difficult to understand. By the time you figure out what she is saying she is already weeks behind. You have to read the book and take a quiz over what you read every week and then she lectures over it two or even three weeks later. And by that time you have already learned 2 more chapters and taken 2 more quizzes.

Class was a total waste of time. She requires attendance if you want to get a good grade. I got an A in the class and slept through all her lectures. She's annoying and her voice is whiny. If you want to do well in this class you'll actually need to read the book. Beware she does use lecture examples on the tests though. Overall it was awful.

Don't go into the class thinking it is easy because it does take work to get a good grade in this class. You can not slack off and expect to get a A. Mrs. Lee is super helpful and is willing to do anything she can to help you achieve a good grade in the class. She is fun and energetic, which really helps keep your attention throughout the class.
Dr. Lee is very helpful if you go visit her in office hours. She is nice and enthusiastic. Keep up with the work and you will do fine.
hated it
She is so nice and so funny.The class is worth the money.Exams are not easy but if you study hard you will get the result you want.

This class is not easy. I studied so much for the tests and still did poorly. She expects so much out of you that you'd think this would be the only class you'd take in a semester. On top of reading, study guides, homework, and quizzes, the amount of time devoted is unbearable. I've worked so hard for a grade that's going to be a detriment to my GPA.

The class itself is easy, and well structured. However if you have to ask her to help you with anything outside of class, she always says she's too busy to do so. The Korean accent is easier to understand than you might think. I will probably get a C+/B-.

This is an extremely easy class. Three things to remember. Go to class and take notes, Read the book, and Take the practice exams online before the test, there's normally two. The test is 75% from those practice exams, word for word. If you do that an A will be no problem
Hard to understand i just gave up and started listening to my iPod

If you took micro, don't think you're going to be able to fly through macro...it won't happen. GO TO LECTURE (she gives pop quizzes) and make sure you do the practice exams because they will help. Lecture is fast paced and she is VERY hard to understand, but she's nice. Tests screw a lot of people over...study hard and read EVERYTHING she gives you
No Comments

If you can get past the fact she can't speak english and just copy whats on the overhead youll survive. Personally I would take this at a community college and transfer it in. I studied forever from the book, notes, and old exams for the tests and still only got high Cs and very low Bs, very frustrating
She is just to hard to understand. Her tests are terrible and she does not prepare you enough. She is just not a good enough teacher for a college class.
Her lectures are incredibly simple, but very fast-paced.  Her exams are very difficult and complicated!  Try to take this class somewhere else!!
No Comments

Be prepared to have a major hand cramp at the end of the class: there is a TON of note taking involved. Always refer to the old tests. I would honestly take this with another teacher, if one was available.
tests are difficult; very available out of class and will help you; material covered in class isn't always clear

She is very dedicated to teaching and classes are entertaining b/c of her bubbly nature.  The class material isn't something that comes naturally to most.  OLD EXAMS ARE THE KEY TO THIS CLASS...use them and it helps a ton.
She is better than Sharon Ryan . . . which isn't saying much
No Comments
No Comments

Myoung is hard to understand and is more concerned with getting through a certain number of chapters than making sure her students understand the material.  My best advice is to memorize all of the old exams and practice exams because a lot of the questions are repeated.

I originally had Myoung as a TA a few years ago. If it hadn't have been for her, I would have failed. She is still very passionate about her classes and tries to keep them lively.  You will have to work hard to pass the class, but you learn a lot of worthwhile information in the process.  If you want to use your money wisely-take Myoung's class!

At the start of the semester things are pretty easy, its mostly review and the material isn't too hard, but after that second test it starts getting really hard and Myoung stops making any sense at all- my advice- KNOW all of the practice exams!!!!

Some of the previous commentors are unfair to Myoung. She is very smart, and tries very hard to help students to succeed. I think an econ class could be A LOT worse. If you sit in the front, Myoung is much easier to understand. Do all the assigned readings, and look at old tests and quizes. Go to class, too.

Professor Lee has exceptional knowledge of the subject, yet does not know how to convey it to her students sucessfully...and the thick Korean accent doesn't help. She does, however, make every effort for her students to succeed.  Best advice:  study old tests, read the book, and go to lecture (she rewards those who go to class).

this class wasn't easy and she made it very difficult to enjoy the class. you have to go to class and read the book. the work load in that class sucks and even then you aren't guaranteed a good grade but if it wasn't for her curves i would have gotten a C and instead i got an A so i can't complain too much. good luck.

Myoung Lee is the worst teacher i have ever had. Her annoying voice made me want to rip my ears off.  Hopefully she will get fired so nobody else has to suffer through her class.  I honestly studied for over 20 hours for one test and still got a B-.  She wants people to fail and she gets a sick pleasure from doing so.

this teacher is from Korea and speaks poor English.  her classes are boring plus with the language barrier it is very difficult to pay attention.  the only thing you can really do in order to get a good grade in the class is read the book and look at her previous exams online.  wouldnt reccommend this class
could study for weeks and get the same grade on the test

I have never studied so much in my life, yet done so horrible.  The class might have been easier had she known how to speak ENGLISH!  Tells stupid jokes, is annoying to listen to, and doesn't help students.  The only reason I don't have an F is because of my TA.

Horrible teacher.  Her tests are hard, you can't understand her, and she doesn't have her students' best interests in mind.  She's only concerned with quickly covering the material she has to, and sounding like an idiot in the process.

Listen to headphones during class because your brain will hurt trying to listen to her lectures. Weak grasp on English, terrible examples, and difficult tests. Booed 5 straight classes for being so sucky. Doesn't cancel class during day with a night test. Want to gouge my eyes out every min. of lec.
the tests are incredibly hard and ridiculous. her pronunciation is unclear

I don't know why everyone is giving Myoung such a hard time, she's really not that hard. Yeah, you're probably not going to pull out an A or anything, but you do your work and read the book and you should get a B or B+. Also, she doesn't know what a pronoun is, always Myoung does this, Myoung that.

Tests were ridiculous!  What is it with economics teachers and their tests?  This is supposed to be an INTRODUCTORY course and it shouldn't be this hard.  It is also unfair to give pop quizzes in an 8am class.  The readings weren't bad, it was just the tests that sucked.
Test does not reflect what is covered at all...makes me want to change my major.  It is just frustrating that I study so much and understand the material, but do poorly on all the graded work.

This class is hard becuase no one can understand her. She lacks good English skills. On exams she throws in trick questions along with stuff hardly covered in class. Avoid this class if at all possible.
Not such a great class

Myoung dropped our two lowest quiz scores and our lowest hw assignment to help us get our grade up..I had her class Winter04 and she is very easy to understand and she has jokes..She curved our 3rd test up 7%!!!Haven't got my grade yet though..Will inform

I hate this class.  Myoung totally sucks as a teacher, and I definitley learned everything in that class from the lab.  Her tests are total B/S and she adds in trick questions, as if the material isn't hard enough already! AVOID THIS CLASS!!!
No Comments

Myoung Lee does not at all excel with the english language.  She covers about a third of the material and then pop-quizes us on what she cannot get to due to her lack of english skills and her snail-like pace when covering the chapters.

This class isn't as hard as everyone makes it out to be.  It's just a lot of reading, and every now and then she'll throw out a pop quiz during lecture!  Labs are really easy, and tests are all right (just be sure to study hard!)
Myoung is a joy and a sage. She is witty kind and helpful. She even brings candy. I like her a lot.
Myoung lacks clear english skills...the class is very difficult to stay focused in.  Expectations of students and testing procedures are not well-defined.

He's a really solid professor, just the amount of reading is uh, near impossible to keep up with. I think I was most impressed by him when we switched to online for COVID-19: he made it a point to ensure all of us were doing okay (not just in his class, but mentally) and went the extra mile to help any way he could, he really showed he cared.

As an honors teacher, Nudell really pushed us to think abstractly. It was easy to participate in class discussions, but the readings were always extensive so this class had a lot of prep work. The one time I missed class he emailed me to make sure I was doing okay, which was really nice. He was good at communicating also.

I will never understand how this dude got to teach a whole class about Alexander the Great. After a few weeks, we were just grasping for anything at all to talk about. It was extremely difficult to write 1,500 essays on one question. Also, the assignment description is nothing like he ends up grading you on. Basically prepare to fail the first one
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would never take this class (or any) with Nudell. This is the second time I have had to endure such a hard grader who gives barely any information on the topic. Unfortunately it was the only option that fit in my schedule. Nudell puts minimal effort into teaching and doesnt care about student success whatsoever.

The online lecture material was so slim that the writing assignments actually required a larger word count. Idk how Im supposed to write more words on an assignment based on this amount of information. Nudell is stuck up and a horrible communicator. Dont ask him for any help, he will just tell you you are wrong. God help you in this class!

This class absolutely sucked! If you dont already have an extensive knowledge of Greek history, do not take ANY class with Nudell. The worst part was you got grades based on things that were not included in the assignment description or rubric. He is not willing to work with you at all and does not communicate to students. Ever.

Professor Nudell is AWESOME. As a history major, I am thrilled he is in Mizzou's History department. I had to miss his class due to an interview for an internship and he went above and beyond to keep me up to speed on what I had missed. Provides EC, is available during office hours, and grades fairly. Weekly online quizzes & take home assignments.

She graded all of our exams, and unfortunately, I find it strange how I received the same grade on two different exams. She was a very tough grader on essays, even if you have all of your facts right, she will still find something wrong about it if she doesn't have the same viewpoint.
Amazing class would take again!!

Attendance is required but you don't get points unless you participate in during class, which would be fine if there wasn't 30+ people trying to fit their thoughts into a 50 minute class.Her grading system makes no sense, they are supposed to be 60% of the grade but effect your grade less then participation. When I asked about it she gave attitude.

Alice was a nice TA, however, she graded the essay portion of the exam extremely hard. I am typically good at writing as well and I found that she took points off for very minute things. It was unfair as I heard other people with different TAs doing so much better in this course and felt it was easy as well. Not an easy A class, should've been.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is an absolutely amazing instructor. If you go to his office hours he will absolutely go out of his way to make sure you know your material. He does have a lot of reading quizzes which is a downside, but he actually wants you to get something out of his class. Very passionate about his line of work, had his class 3 times already. Great guy

I absolutely loved this class. All you really have to do is show up and listen to him. Very simple. I actually learned a lot in this class just by showing up. You have weekly quizzes over reading material, 2 exams, and one group project. There's also extra credit opportunities, so I suggest doing those to get an even better grade.

I've taken both SOC 1650 and SOC 2200, and Gummi is by far my favorite teacher! He does require you put effort into your work, but if you show up to class and listen, you will get an A. He is interested in your learning, is very fair in his grading, is eager to help you and offers a lot of extra credit, making it hard to fail any of his classes.

Easily one of the worst professors I have ever had. Rambles about absolutely no course material through class, yet makes attendance mandatory. Any thing you learn will have to come from reading. Only upside is the ton's of pointless busy work he gives you, (weekly quizzes, discussion board, group project)are helpful grade boosters.
I loved this class. He's super helpful and funny as well. Lots of reading and you will actually have to do some studying! Nothing to worry about though.
Great guy. Very interested in the subject and will take time to explain things that do not make sense. Taking a class with him again just because he's a great professor.
had him for social deviance, super fun class and good teacher! cute and so nice! easy class if you do the work
He is a great teacher, he is quirky and has a dry sense of humor. He makes class interesting and will always make you laugh and he is great at explaining things. I would recommend to anyone.

Best math teacher I've ever had. Show up to class, ask questions when necessary, and you'll understand the material well. Tests are straightforward and fair (and easy if you know what you're doing).  Class average is always in the A range.  Plus, he's always available for extra help, and has a subtle sense of humor. Definitely recommend.
Super chill professor. Pretty easy tests.
Wonderful Teacher! Perfect and easy.

Dr. Okonkwo was possibly the best teacher I have ever had. For senior seminar, he assigned readings and music that allowed us to think critically of the world. He is funny, nice, and only asks that the students stay caught up with the reading. If I could take him again, I would!

Dr. Okonkwo is the best professor I've had at FSU. He is SO passionate about what he teaches, and it shows. He's goofy and his lectures are interesting. He was more than willing to help on essays, welcomed us to come to office hours, and understood the times when we didn't read the whole assigned text. He gives good feedback, too. Take his class!

This prof seems like a really nice guy but the class is insanely difficult. I have higher level courses that are writing intensive that are easier than this. An 8 page paper is worth 40% of grade alone, and we only get to write 2 and do a presentation. Does everything via email, no canvas. Nice guy, intense class. Would not take again.

Did not use Canvas the entire semester, gave everything via email, syllabus, assignments, grades, everything, but ironically never responded to emails. Assignment descriptions were vague at best. He had a really great personality, but in almost every class he showed long YouTube clips over zoom that were impossible to hear. No feedback on grades.
Professor K is amazing! His teaching style is so laidback and simple. Loved his lectures and he gives you every possible opportunity to succeed. 150% recommend!
Very knowledgeable. He is a good lecturer, so nothing comes off dry or dull.
Passionate and kind, great at making students feel comfortable. Very engaging lectures.

He's great! You WILL have to work in this class and he's a pretty difficult grader, but he knows a lot about his subject and is very dedicated to student learning. He has been one of my favorite professors at Mizzou. He's so funny and really cares about his students.
Really passionate about his subject. Will NOT respond to emails. Come to all the classes, and STUDY FOR THE MIDTERM because it's crazy hard. Otherwise, everything is easy and fairly interesting.

An awesome teacher that takes the time to explain the material. Very cool personality and quite hilarious. Only way someone could get below and A-B range is if they never read or attend class. One of my favorite courses in college be far!

He is an incredible teacher, extremely knowledgeable and fascinating to listen to. He expects a lot from his students but is very reasonable. He wants that his students succeed and takes a personal interest in their education. The coursework is fascinating and I highly recommend him. I got an A- in his class and am taking a second class from him.

He is knowledgeable, cares greatly about his subject area, and also cares greatly about the success and learning of his students. Yes, the work is hard and frequent, but the experience is worth it for anyone wanting to take a meaningful class that will broaden your literary horizons. If your a lazy student, don't waste the enrollment space.
MAKES OFFENSIVE JOKES AND VERY UNORGANIZED!!! STAY AWAY!!

Does NOT answer emails, unorganized, arrogant, and INCREDIBLY hard grader. This class is NOTHING like i thought it would be, I sacrificed sleep (took an 8 am) to take this class, and I am DISAPPOINTED. He thinks he's funny, but is very dull.
Speak up as much as possible, he emphasizes and grades participation. Read closely too, he likes to put specific names of do****entaries, characters of stories, titles of plays, etc on exams.
interesting class, but challenging.  fair teacher but makes you work work work

Honestly, he seems like a pretty cool guy. However, as a teacher he sorely lacks the ability to tell if his students are actually learning. Lectures feel unstructured and blown through, and he will race through an example problem so fast that he is erasing the problem before you get a chance to copy it down. Only passed because of test corrections
Go to class and you'll be fine

Don't do it. He's disorganized, jumping all over the board during lectures making it difficult to take notes, without mentioning what section you're in. He assumes you know information and likes to tangent on things that aren't necessary until later math. 30 minute warm ups every day from previous sections, and then furiously rushing to finish.
very good.

Sometimes he may not be clear about what he is discussing, however he is really nice and if you are confused about something he can definitely explain it better if you ask him in person or attend his office hours.

IF you MUST take this course with her, I HIGHLY recommend doing all of the extra credit she provides. It almost impossible to pass the class without doing at least some of the extra credit because her tests are ridiculous. Lectures and book are completely different. Avoid this professor.

At first, I thought she was intimidating because of her strictness, but she is really easy to talk to during office hours if you're honestly interested in understanding course material or things beyond the course. She looks at Anthropology from a holistic perspective and presents many different topics. You can't use technology in her class.

I thought the class was interesting and worth the time! She appreciates class attendance. I never felt talked down to, I just think its her personality. If you read the material you will ace the exams. Plus extra credit is enough to get everyone an A.

You must attend class, and read the book. She does not like redundant or "stupid" questions, and will make you feel stupid for asking them, however she offers extra credit and if you go to her office hours she is a lot more friendly and willing to help you then. Overall her grading system, and what/how to study was unclear.

If you are taking your anthro class with her, drop it. She is extremely condescending and makes you feel stupid every time that you step into her class. She really doesn't care about her students and acts superior to them. She begins to make you hate going to class every day. If I had to do it over again, I would never have taken this class.

Very rude and arrogant. She could care less about how her students are doing. Lectures are boring and usually have nothing to do with the material in the book, she just shows irrelevant pictures and words. There is NO guidance for exams, even though her lectures and the book teach us two different things. Probably the worst teacher I've had.

Dr. Okamura is one of the best in his field. He is also very eager to explain anything if you didn't understand and a pretty easy grader.  His lectures are in a very traditional style, so much that he still uses an old overhead projector.

Larry is my favorite professor I've had at Mizzou. Very nice guy, fairly entertaining lecturer. Takes attendance, but you don't really need to pay much attention. 4 exams are all of the grades, and he's a very easy grader. Sends out study guides that help so much.
Nice guy, knows and loves the subject matter. The problem is, is that he has such a traditional lecture style, that it is hard to pay attention to.

DO NOT take HIST 1520 with him. I am going into a career in ancient history and I could barely sit through this class. He is clearly smart and cares about what he's teaching, but his approach to the material is unbelievably dry and ineffective. Literally the only reason to take this class is because it's an easy A.

Awesome teacher. Tells you what will be on the tests, so studying is not a problem. Very interesting. Offers excellent insight into historical topics. If you have any interest in history of the ancient world, this class is a must.

Professor Okamura is extremely intelligent and clearly knows what he's talking about.  He keeps class fun and interesting with his personal anecdotes and gives a review sheet for every exam.  He's genuinely interested in his students' learning.  One of the best teachers I had thus far.
Nice guy, very knowlegeable. Lots of reading assigned but not really used. Traditional lecture style class so if you are not an auditory learner this class will be difficult for you.

Good teacher, gets off on alot of tangents. Wants you to read alot, but it is relativly unimportant. He talks contiuously about what he wants you to know and what youll need to know for the test. Overall a really interesting guy.

I've had several classes with Professor Okamura and can't imagine a better professor. He is a wealth of knowledge and is interested that his students are learning. He's also very approachable for questions and will make office hours to suit you. I wish all professors were this good!

He was a nice guy--but not the greatest professor, ESPECIALLY for this course. It's reading intensive and there's a LOT of material, but he didn't go over the main parts for the final. The important material gets snuck in with random information, so its hard to pick up on. Even if you read, obtaining the info needed for the test is hard work.

CHANGE YOUR SECTION LEADER if you get him in ancient world. he is very eager to help, but a complete failure as a professor. the worst part is you can tell he knows what he's talking about, but it is not being demonstrated properly.

I had him for discussion and wouldnt pick anyone else. He makes class interesting, even if he has a hard time covering all the material. An easy grader to boot, he is simply the discussion group teacher to get. I guarantee you will get a good grade and laugh throughout class.
He is very knowledgable about the subject matter and he keeps it interesting!
Not impressive.  AT ALL.

Excellent teacher, he really knows his stuff and is a very nice man.  He was genuinely interested in my performance and did a great job covering course material.  He had funny little stories along the way.  English is (or might as well be) his native language.
A remarkable man and a genuinely nice person to boot, with a fairly sassy sense of humor.  His classes are quite enjoyable, you'll learn more than you expected and leave with more than just facts.
Great teacher.  He's like a modern day Asian Indiana Jones.  Very interesting class; he actually likes his job and it shows in his teaching.  Tests are essay and recognition, very fair.
A tendency to ramble on, but when he does you learn the most interesting things. He is absolutely brilliant in his field, and is very helpful in office hours.

Very fair, unbiased, and promotes a positive learning environment. Never singles out students for ridicule because they don't agree with him, and was a fun teacher. This is a rarity in the history department at MU, and I'd recommend him to anyone.

I really enjoyed Jude's class. She is very knowledgable about her subject, and a passionate lecturer. The main grades come from tests, which can be hard. It definitely helps to come to class, but attendance was not mandatory.

Dr. Olzewski is a very passionate and intelligent professor, but her class isn't very well structured. You are graded on three tests and one extra credit assignment. If you are good at testing and studying, you should at least get a B. She is a new teacher, so be kind to her; she will improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams worth 60% of your grade and a group project worth 25%. The class is so poorly structured and disorganized. DO NOT TAKE THIS AS AN EASY ELECTIVE. you will hate your life, exams are so hard no cheat sheet given, barely any extra credit. 1st year teacher I went to every class and actively participated and took notes and I'm praying I end with B
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As this was my first semester at University of Missouri, I was expecting a lot different for courses and how they would make the students think more clearly. This was not one of those courses. If you want to feel like you are in middle school again and filling out worksheets in the only way the professor will take it then this course is for you.

Prof. Watson is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. She really cares about her students and will do anything to help them out. Could not possibly recommend taking comm1200 with her more, overall fun class and easy to get an A if you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Olivia two semesters ago & she was great. I saw her recently and she remembered my name, my speech topics, and she asked about a hobby I had talked about. She truly cares about her students and I don’t think I appreciated that enough when I had her. I wish more professors at Mizzou took such an interest in their students success!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He really wants you to do well and he gives you every opportunity. Always available for extra help and clearly loves what he teaches. Great TA!

Mr. Olson was the awesome, not only did he show his determination to the field of History. He pushed all of his students, he limited those that would run the conversation into the ground and gave everyone an equal voice. His determination to show make us all succeed went beyond the classroom. His extra credit (Not BS) wanted us to succeed. Amazing!

mr. olson is a freaking legend! he's passionate about the subject of history and makes it real interesting and fun. he's always going out of his way to make himself available outside of class and he really tries to help you understand the material. mr. olson makes history feel like a story instead of just dry facts. i would take any class with him
Very unclear expectations. Not consistent. Confusing directions.
Very helpful professor.

It's all online except for the first class and exam days. Watch her tegrity lectures - they're vital to doing well on the exams. I took the Honors section - it required a project over a specific area of nursing. You don't need the book. There are weekly quizzes online - info comes from her tegrity lectures.

All online! Only seen Dr. Oliver once at the beginning of the year discussing the syllabus. Her lectures are all online and long because she does not have inflection and also does not make the material interesting. However, paying attention to what she says and what is on her powerpoint is vital for a decent grade in the class.
Good teacher with a great grasp on the topic. Was able to articulate the information to us in a way that was interesting, yet very consuming. Great teacher and wish I could take the class again.

This teacher does not care about his students, he thinks every opinion is wrong but his. Class is not helpful and useless to go to because he doesn't use technology, doesn't have a description of what he will be lecturing over, and just asks questions the whole time. Very unorganized, and I ended up teaching the class to myself. AVOID!
Excellent teacher that knows his stuff. Has high expectations  for students and pushes them to think, which is a nice change.

This was supposed to be an intro class that surveyed all topics in soc but we didn't touch on all of them. As a soc major, I was disappointed. His essay prompts are confusing and hard to dissect (he asks you to answer three essay Qs in one) and his assignments and instructions are really ambiguous so you don't really know what you're suppose to do
Take the online version of the class. So much easier.

Had him 4 Sociology - Orgs & Institutions. He's a young grad student & good prof. Interesting & fun class w/ cool discussions. 2 exams were multiple choice & study guide he gives is VERY thorough. there R 4 papers, 3 of which are VERY short. 2 short many said. 1 neg - Sometimes hard 2 make connections of discussions to sociology terms & thoughts.
Awesome professor who always makes you laugh. Not too tough, but it is a foreign language so ya know

Olaf is by far the most eccentric and hilarious professor I've ever had!  He is one of a kind, if you get the chance take his course.  You will have a bunch of homework and tests/quizzes but if you study you will pass no problem.  He challenges students often but it makes them better.  Class is easy, it's what you do outside of class that matters.
Olaf is a great guy. come to class. study a little before all quizzes and you will do well. participate.               ----get that A :)

Olaf is great; he really wants his students to pass and if you ask him for help, he'll do his best. German definitely isn't easy, so be read to study, but all of his tests are pretty easy and even if you get an answer wrong, he'll give partial credit. He's hilarious and tells lots of great stories. Great guy, take him if you have the chance.

Olaf is the funniest teacher I have ever had. I had him for 2 semesters German 31803190. He is also a really nice guy and wants you to pass. I'll give you an example, if you get a multiple choice problem wrong on the test, you get 1.52 points. Come to class, it's super fun and your Deutsch will be Ausgezeichnet. Highly recommend Herr Schmidt.
No textbook required. Stick it to the Man, Olaf!
Simply put, Olaf is the man. His class is great and you really do learn a lot. Probably my favorite professor so far
Great teacher, makes it easy to have fun

(I have taken about 8 German classes at Mizzou and None of the German studies teachers post grades on black board. It's just a department thing) SO I CONCLUDE THAT: OLAF IS THE BEST PROFESSOR IN THE GERMAN DEPARTMENT! (AND THE BEST ONE I'VE HAD AT THIS UNI!) I've taken 2 of his classes and enjoyed both immensely! HE'S A HOOT!
Great teacher
Olaf's a great guy, great teacher, and he's really funny...my only complaint is that he doesnt post scores on blackboard...
Yeah, take as many classes with him as possible.  Best professor in the German department BY FAR. he wont let you down
Olaf is an amazing professor! He is absolutely hilarious! Take as many classes with him as you can!
Fabulous teacher, a majot asset wherever he ends up.  We miss you Olaf!
No Comments
No Comments
Wonderful teacher, makes German easy and fun.

Prof. JT is great guy, but he isn't a good professor. He showed up late to class every day. Lectures were all over the place, and were always very vague. He never communicated outside of class. And he took forever to grade. As I am writing this, he has only graded the first paper, which I did 4 months ago. The actual papers are not difficult.

He is a very nice man and cares about all of his students. Lectures could be a little long, but that was just how the course was set up. They were not mandatory but were still helpful. Only had four papers all semester and he was a pretty easy grader. Highly recommend taking his class.

Very easy English class and not very demanding. 4 total papers the whole semester spaced out evenly and he sets up time outside of class to conference with him. As long as you turn in everything on time and meet the requirements you will get an A. You don't need to go to the lectures but they can be helpful. Attendance not mandatory.

I wrote harder papers in high school than for this class. the papers for my class were: body narrative (1st person story ab your life), rhetorical analysis, research paper, and a remix of a previous paper into a poster, video, podcast etc. Just follow the rubric and you're good

Very easy to get an A in this class as long as you turn in all of your essays and assignments on time. If you do not turn in even one thing on time you risk getting below an A in this class. There are very few assignments so each one holds more weight towards your overall grade. Just turn in everything and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Orejel was one of my favorite professors. Keith is a stand and lecture style professor, but he is very in-depth and will make sure you know about each subject covered in class. He always posts the notes to BlackBoard. Keith is good with communication and answering questions. His exams are semi difficult but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Keith definitely has a passion for history, which is clearly evident in his lectures. For the most part, my experience with him was positive. He spoke in depth & fluently about each subject. Although I liked his 'stand & talk' lectures, others did not. He puts notes up on the board & online, but was not as good about it at the end of the semester.

Very knowledgable. Lectures are very interesting and easy to keep up with. Only 2 tests the whole semester: midterm and final. Clearly states whats going to be on both exams and very easy to study for. Enjoyed a lot. ;)

Dr. Orejel is a very long-winded young man. He is very knowledgeable about American History and gives long detailed lectures about the subject matter. He does move through slides rather quickly, but any material you may have missed, your TA will cover. Also, I've only read 1 of 5 books and I'm making a B+, so yeah, he's pretty chill.

Only gave 1's because 0 was not an option. Will never take a class that has Dr. Keith Orejel as the instructor.  His slides are not very helpful as he keeps talking and going into depth about the main topics on the slide while students are copying the slide. Which am I supposed to write down? ALL TESTS ARE ESSAY QUESTIONS.
Lectures sound like he is reading from the textbook. Impossible to take good notes. Long and boring lectures.
Awesome teacher! I took an online course, he was truly helpful and gave extremely insightful feedback!

He gives a lot of practice examples for the tests in class and also helps you see the applications of the math in real life, so you can get a good grade and actually use the material to your benefit. I liked how he taught and he was a nice guy. Tests were all multiple choice which was nice for a math class because I didn't have to study as much.

I think he's a TA/Grad student. He's passionate about math, but seemed nervous to teach a class full of students. He's actually a very good teacher, often restating concepts more than once. He clearly links two concepts with plenty of examples. He's genuinely a nice guy who is interested in our success. Good teaching methods, good guy, easy class.

He's a basic College Algebra Teacher. Pretty sure he's a TA. He does his best at teaching, and most of the time it isn't hard to understand. But it's math. He has office hours that you can go to and he will help you as much as you want. A nice guy.
best TA i've had

Not much homework for a math class. He makes it really easy to get a good grade and you usually get out of class early. He doesn't always give a lot of examples though so you might have to study extra. The only problem I had was applying material to real world concepts because he knows most people don't care and rushes past that stuff. Nice guy

Prof. Orf is one of the hottest and smartest proffesors I know. If you take good notes and listen to his gorgeous voice, you will not need to study for his tests. He also has a big heart; he is pro-student, especially with athletes (he is kinda of good at volleyball).
Andy Orf made me switch my major from Finance to Statistics.  If that doesn't say anything nothing will.
Andy was super cool.  If you go to his office hours before lecture he will literally make sure you get all the homework questions right. Best TA I've ever had.
Professor Orf Rocks! He's a hard grader but really fair. Let's just say he doesn't give the other team any free balls, but I heard some of his exams are easier than a roll shot.
SUPERB!
Mr. Orf is a really swell dude. He was a Division II athlete and is super strong. I think he works out A LOT. He also is a really good singer. You should ask him to sing the fight song some time.
Great
Pain to understand at times. TA was cool. Did well in class.
Doesn't tell what exactly is expected on assignments, will change grades if enough people complain.
Could not stay on topic.  Wandered off on her own interests.

The man is overqualified to teach. MacroEcon is is strength. I loved this class. I knew going into each test just how well I was prepared because he did such a great job teaching. I really enjoyed the way he taught and he was a very nice and understanding guy. I would recommend taking any of his MacroEcon classes. Don't fear him, ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The questions on the exams are extremely specific and worth up to 30 points apiece (!).  So if you mess up on one thing, you're done.  If you want an A, you have to literally do everything--rewrite notes, read the chapters, go to class.  The final is much harder (due to no general study guide): entered final with an A+ in class, left with an A-.
Easily worst professor I've had at Mizzou. Not sure why I had to pay this guy when you have to teach yourself everything out of the book. He was useless.
He knows what he's doing, he's just the most boring professor I've ever had. It's incredibly hard to stay attentive during lecture.

I know that Mr. Otrok had good intentions. However, I'm not sure if he was fully prepared for the transfer from Virginia. I can honestly say that I taught myself more than I learned. I hope that he develops a more sensitive adaptation for new and foreign surroundings. But hey, some years are trial and error. This was one of them.
Absolutely awful! Nothing else to say about him!

Worst Professor I've ever had. His lecturers are SO boring and he takes them straight from the book. Might as well just read the book and not come to class honestly. His class is based on two midterms and a final that is worth half your grade. The tests are not impossible, but you're definitely going to have to study. Wouldn't suggest his class

He gets his powerpoints from the book and reads directly off of them every single class. He is boring and does not seem passionate about the subject at all with makes it impossible to pay attention. He skims over complex information. The final is over 12 chapters.......

Man he is a boring lecturer. He also says "um" or "uh" every 12-15 seconds. I counted one class, in 67 minutes, 307 times. So hard to listen to, but if you pay as much attention as possible and look at the study guide before exams, you'll be fine.

Awful teacher. This year was his first year at Mizzou. I asked him what he recommended I focus on while studying and he said everything. There was no practice exams to look at. Homework only counted for 2 points and hardly made a dent in my grade.

Professor Outlaw was super cool but made the class very difficult. A lot of students dropped the class after the first exam as the class average was not very high. After the third exam the class average was 55% causing him to curve the class which didn't help many students. Overall his class was great but the exams were ridiculously hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Outlaw is an amazing professor! For organic chemistry which is really hard, he did an amazing job of making it as easy as possible. Tests are multiple choice and really easy if you study. He's a very knowledgeable guy and the class was extremely fair for such a notoriously difficult class. He even gave everyone extra points at the end 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take Organic with Victor! He is friendly, knowledgeable, takes his time covering the material in lecture, tests fairly, and the homework and book are fantastic (and well correlated) resources. I wish he could lead my Organic 2 class

I was so thankful to have had Dr. Outlaw as my Orgo 1 professor. There is a lot of lecture material but he takes the time to go over everything (lectures are a bit slow if anything). Graded based on Wiley hwk (you get a 100% as long as you complete), 4 exams (1 dropped), & the final. Gives practice exams that are very similar to the tests.

While Organic Chemistry is a hard course in itself, Dr. Outlaw provided us with many resources and awesome practice exams that really prepared us for the real exams. I also found the homework to be helpful and you always get a 100% as long as you complete it. Hamza, his TA was also a huge help when preparing for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Outlaw provided a lot of resources so that the material could be understood. This class is still hard and very lecture heavy. His practice exams were exactly formatted like his actual exams and he posted videos explaining every problem in-depth for us. I highly recommend him for organic chemistry because he truly cares about all of his students
Literally the best professor I've ever had. Definitely take this class especially if calculus is only a pre-requisite and you're not a math major.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. He explains concepts more clearly than I though was possible for Math. Really makes you enjoy it too - he clearly loves Math. I went into Calc 1 hating Math and knowing nothing about it, but by the end, I had decided to do Math minor because of Dr. Oveys and his class.

Dr. Oveys explains things super clearly and really wants us to learn the material. He's the best math teacher I've ever had! There's not too much HW and his lecture notes are all you need to study. His exams are tough though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely aweful teacher. I had the best math teachers at NYU until I had Hesam Oveys. I don't know what kind of PhD's they give out in Missouri but this guy is not qualified to teach in NY. He is a big F!
Best professor for MFE1&2 at NYU by far. Just study his lecture notes and you're done. No textbook required. Really helpful during his office hours, definitely recommend professor hesam.
Took Math for Economics I at NYU. Great professor, very clear explanation of concepts, accessible during office hours. Recitations are useless. Do the homework and you're fine. No textbook needed.
Great teacher I reccomend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. Class is very straight forward. He absolutely knows his stuff. If you're taking Diff EQ with him, know your Calc 2 identities well.

One of the best calc professors i have had. He puts your knowledge of math  to the test however he doesnt test you past anything you cant do with the material he as taught. Not an easy A but you will know the material when your done if you pass

Hesam Oveys is the best teacher I have EVER had. Not just at Mizzou, and not just in math, but in my life. Wish I could have him for every class. His way of explaining things is just so thorough, and he really cares about what he teaches. Take him if you can. He's not an easy 'A', but you'll definitely know how to do everything if you pay attention

Hesam is an amazing teacher. He's probably better than most professors and hes not a professor. I had him for calc 2, and he made what was a hard subject come easy. He tells you exactly what you need to know. He makes calc 2 understandable to students and gives off his techniques and leaves out any unnecessary bull.  Recommended.

Hands down best teacher I've had at Mizzou. Everything is very well explained, he is very helpful, and makes a hard class a lot easier, as long as you're willing to work. Warning: he will constantly tell you that you're almost "over the hump" of Calc 2 and you never actually are until it's over

Fantastic teacher. I love math and it comes very easy to me but having him there was great and very reassuring. He knows exactly what he is talking about and offers his skills to the students in an extremely understandable fashion. If you have the option to take one of his classes you would regret not doing so.

He's probably the best teacher I've had for during my math career. (calc2 specifically). His lectures are spot on, he will tell you what to expect on tests and quizzes and if you go see him one on one during his office hours which is what I did, there is no way you can go wrong.
Awesome teacher. He really understands calculus at a fundamental level and can translate that understanding into his students. I highly recommend.
Hesam is a good teacher. There's nothing that he can't explain makes everything straight forward.
great teacher- very clear and helpful!
Awesome teacher
Really really helpful. Explains things easily.
Hesam is better than the actual professor for Calc II.

Calc is either easy for you or it's not, but after hearing from others in Math 1400 Hesam seems to be the best.  His students normally scored well above the department average and he was easy to follow in class.  Two thumbs up.

Very passionate-not great teacher. 90% lectures and little discussion. The entire first 1/3 of class was just learning about niche poetry classification and terminology. Gave a lot of us the same grade and copy/paste feedback. Communicates few expectations, but grades harshly. We had 3 essays and 2 exams, a class presentation and attendance.

Class was really confusing at first. The whole semester is group projects every week. Would critique one group on something & not even mention he was looking for that in the criteria when grading another group's work. Asks openended questions that I dont even know the answer to in English & expects an answer. Will joke around & be funny sometimes.

So he started out with a grading criteria but kept changing what he was looking for. This class is only group presentations discussing and papers but you can do different jobs in the group. No tests. His grading is difficult and we were confused on what he was looking for to the end. You also talk about controversial topics in this class prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Otabela is very knowledgeable but most classes are just memorizing a powerpoint. He's a funny guy that seems to care, but he's tough to contact outside of class. Easy grader but some of his exam answers were incorrect and he never listened to our complaints. Some of his powerpoints looked a lot like the wikipedia articles about the same topic.
This class is honestly terrible. We hardly go over anything in class, the online homework is so tedious and picky and goes over stuff he didn’t teach us. I would not recommend it or him to anyone.

You can tell he really cares about you learning Spanish, but my class had a lot of difficulties with him changing grading policies, the syllabus, and assignments. There is definitely a language barrier as his English is not great and we weren't at a point to communicate what we needed to say in Spanish yet. Overall he is a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Keep up and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man does not have clear criteria whatsoever. Will not change his viewpoint, even if the whole class disagrees and is confused on the subject. Show up to every class. Don't ask questions because he will be mad you don't already know it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take class with this man. I have never done anything wrong, I go to class everyday, and he still is the worse professor I have ever been with. He doesn't stick to his syllabus and doesn't even seem to know what he put on the syllabus. He encourages students to ask questions then yells at them for not knowing the material. Avoid his classes

Grades slightly hard, but will tailor to your specific class if you ask. Would highly recommend going to his office hours even if you dont think youre learning more from them. With this, he is much more apt to round your grade up at the end of the semester with the extra effort shown.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent semester in Doctor Otabela's poetry and drama class. For sure one of my best Spanish professors at Mizzou. Take this class with him! Nice and funny!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my best Spanish professor at MIZZOU. He is passionate an cares about his students

The worst Spanish teacher I have ever had. I got an A in the class but it was difficult. He asks open-ended questions but expects your answer to be the exact same as his. He is confusing and has very high expectations that he does not explain at all. He is also sexist, so if you take him get used to hearing a lot of outdated stereotypes about women
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Otabela is one of the most genuine teachers I have had in my life. He is a fantastic teacher that will be willing to do whatever it takes to help you understand and gain a general interest in the material you are learning. He loves his students, bringing the same enthusiasm and desire to teach to every class. Take Otabela, he is an amazing man.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: SPAN 3160 is an advanced Spanish course. Prepare all your readings and be prepared everyday. Otabela is amazing and a very good Spanish Teacher.  improved my writing and speaking skills in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Otabela follows his syllabus closely. Every week is repetitious, with a lot of confusing reading, discussion consisting of him talking mostly, and a few essays. He does not grade too hard on the essays. Submit them to the writing center for editing. He's intimidating and does not answer questions well. Tests are challenging and count for your grade
Take this class with him. He knows what he's talking about... and he's funny! Amaizing class at all. I really enjoyed!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my best professors in Spanish

SPAN 3160 is an advanced composition class. Otabela is a very good professor, one of the best I've had in Spanish at MU.  The level of difficulty is grammar. Be prepared on topics like imperfect and preterit, ser and estar, the use of subjunctive, etc. The readings and discussions are goodand the teacher always tries to link them to our daily lives

Otabela is the worst Spanish professor I've had so far at Mizzou. He's very unclear about what he expects the class to do and gets angry when the class doesn't do it and is confused. He spends most classes talking at you, which doesn't leave much room for improvement and learning. He also asks really personal questions  in class all the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: SPAN 3430 is a spanish literature class focussed on poetry and drama. At the beginning the class is somehow difficult. But Otabela makes it easy. I don't like poetry, but this professor explains so well that I finally enjoyed the class. Grading is fair. Overall this is on of my best Spanish class at Mizzou.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Solid professor. If you've skated by in every Spanish class prior, you're going to have a hard time - for example if you participate by saying things like "Yo, like, um, hacer algo fun this fin de semana." But show up, speak up, do the work and you'll do well. Pro-tip: connect the readings to current events in essays - he likes that when grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Once I got to know him better, I liked him more as a professor. Many of my classmates were discouraged after the first test, and he also is a tough grader on essays. The course content is difficult because it's Spanish poetry. He gets grades back to us quickly.

Professor Otabela makes learning fun! Unfortunately, he does not really give you clear outlines on what exactly he wants. It's like a guessing game; he says one thing, gives you a prompt for another thing-- when you seek clarification, you don't really get that either.  Great guy! Love what he does and is passionate about his craft!

Professor Otabela is an excellent teacher.  Spanish 3160 is Advanced Spanish Composition, and nearly all of the bad reviews for him in this class are because those students were not at a high enough level of proficiency to be taking the class.  The tests are not hard; it's all information that you should have already learned in a lower class.

This teacher was unwilling to help. His tests were crazy hard, as though he was making them impossible on purpose. When you made a mistake speaking, he was rude in the way he corrected you. He would argue for almost the entire class when our interpretation and opinion about a story was different from his own. 10/10 would not take again. Ever.

Honestly perhaps the worst teacher I've had in my entire life. He is very rude and his tests are verging on IMPOSSIBLE. I am good at Spanish and I enjoy it but I hated this class. If you can take this course with ANY other instructor, I 10000% suggest you do that. Three people dropped and took an F instead of dealing with this guy for one more day.

Dr. Otabela is great professor! He really cares about his students, and he makes sure that everyone understands. He strongly encourages class participation, and homework is an absolute must. Overall, I enjoyed this class.
Horrible class.  Gives little to no instructions for major assignments.  Speaks in circles and repeats himself in order to fill class time.
I liked this class with Otabela. He is clear and you can revise your grammar mistakes for extra credit. Very good teacher.
Dr. Otabela is amazing! He is without a doubt one of the best professors I've had during my time at MU. I've had him for several classes now and I strongly suggest everyone take a class with him.

In taking this course, I did not know much about African literature in Spanish. I admit that this course has been of great importance to my research. I learned a lot of things that radically shaped my research project. This is a boon for our university to have this kind of teachers

Very good teacher! My best spanish teacher at Mizzou. He likes literature and explains it the way that you will like it. At the beginning I was afraid because I don't like poetry, but Otabela made everything easy. Go to class, participate to make sure to get a good grade.
Very dedicated and excellent teacher.
I really enjoyed the semester. I liked the stories we read, and I also liked the way he explains theory. He knows what he's talking about
I really enjoy the course. Nice professor.
I liked the stories and Otabela makes it easy. He's very good explaining theory and analyzing the stories. He's a very good professor, nice and funny. The course is enjoyable.

Not a bad professor. A little harsh at times, but always fair. Allows re-writes on essays and corrections on tests to earn some points back. Show up to class and getting a B is attainable. Getting an A is difficult, however. He expects a lot of you.
I like the readings and the intructor is very nice and funny. The class is enjoyable.

Otabela is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He makes the course enjoyable. I learned a lot about African culture and Equatorial Guinea. From what I learned in the class, something should be done to help the people of this country.
Good teacher, very nice. I don't like literature, but with him, I really enjoy the semester. I like the stories we read, and I also like the way he explains theory.

This class helped me a lot to know about African culture and specifically Ecuatorial Guinea. We read a variety of authors and texts, and we even had a skype interview with one of the most important writer from this country. It was also enjoyable the the discussion on immigration of Africans to Europe. I learned a lot from Otabela in this class.

He's a decent teacher. The class was confusing because we read and discussed stories in class, but the exams were on grammar. He does give you the opportunity to correct mistakes, though. You definitely need to go to class. He's funny and likes teaching, but he doesn't take criticism well even though he asks for it.
Take this class with him if you like Sanish and Latin American Literature. He's very good and funny.

Professor Otabela is a very good and funny teacher. He makes learning spanish fun. He is the best spanish teacher I've had at Mizzou in 6 semesters of spanish. I learned more from him this semester than the other semesters combined.
Otabela is the best professor in the Department. He makes it enjoyable to come to class and encourages participation.
I really enjoyed having him as teacher in this class. He knows and he likes Spanish Literature. Take this course with him... He's funny. Grades are good and fair.
I like the stories. I like the way Otabela explains theory and the stories. Take this class with him.
I enjoy the class. He's funny. I like him.

I really enjoyed having Otabela as a teacher. Key is that you HAVE to go see him in his office. If you are willing to show that you want to learn, and go to his office hours w/ specific questions, you will do fine in this class. People complain that he's difficult to understand-I never had a problem. Allows retakes & homework is minimal.

The course is enjoyable... The syllabus is clear and at any tim you know what you have to do. Follow all the classes, do all the homeworks and quizes... and you will have a good grade. I enjoyed the class, I like Joseph, and next semeter I will take amother class with him.

Guys, he's really awful. In a nutshell, I have .5 away from an A, had attended every class, met with him outside of those, did all the work, emailed him regularly with questions, and he refused to round up at the end of it all. I had to go over his head to the department head and it ultimately worked out - but I had a terrible experience with him.
I like him and I enjoy the class.

I had him for Spanish Conversation. Drop this class if you have it with him, it was awful.  Nearly all the class got low grades on essays, he said points didnt count yet gave them out, and overall had a rude demeanor in class. Not a good experience, besides the fun of anticipating his safari outfits!
Good teacher. I like the way he explains poetry

Very nice and intelligent professor. He loves Literature and you early notice it the way he explains the stories.You cannot do poorly if you do the reading and speak up in class.He really cares about her students.
I like this teacher. I really improve my spanih and I enjoyed the class.

I like him. He's nice, fairly easy, but you still manage to learn things if you're actually interested. His accent is a bit weird in Spanish, but I don't have any trouble understanding him. I had him for intro to lit, and I always loved the way he approached lit, always getting into the historical context. All in all, he's not too bad. :)

Had him for Spanish conversation.  All we did was listen to an oral presentation every day and then discuss it.   I don't think he even knew my name by the end of the semester. Great class if you don't want to anything; not so great if you want  to actually improve your Spanish.  He is very nice, though.

He is from Africa, but lived in Spain so his accent is nuts, and he stutters...so good luck understanding him at all!  Participate in class!  GO TO CLASS or he will fail you!  You will get a kick out of hia authentic African elephant outfit!  GET OUT of his class if you can!!!
No Comments
Other than some occasional trail offs, he was a good professor. Communication with him was very good and easy. Some of his lectures trailed on, but outside of that he was great.

Absolute legend. Entertaining lectures and he made everything about the course easily accessible and understandable. My only fault with him was the class itself, a lot of the things included in lecture and exams seemed pointless.
He is great
Shared teaching with a few TAs, overall a really cool person with lots of experience both in journalism and other things. Speaks Mandarin which is pretty impressive. Engaging & insightful lectures

Chad is a wonderful professor. I love coming to class because of his energy and passion for his job. He really cares about students and our success. The class material is great and easy for students to understand. It consists of quizzes, discussion boards, and assessment surveys that all can be easy points as long as you show up to class.

He is fantastic! I look forward to his lectures. He is kind, personable, and connects with students. His lectures are engaging but he gives lots of homework. Discussions, responses, and quiz, and an assessment survey every week. He had lots of guest speakers this year but I enjoy his class the most when he teaches it! I definitely recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Vajk is easily one of the smartest people in the physics department if not at the University.  Sure, his test are pretty difficult and the class is very fast-paced, but he is ALWAYS willing to help and teach you a little more.You could ask him any physics question and he would know the answer.Absolutely brilliant. I aspire to be like him.
He's brilliant and very available to help students.(If you have him for quantum, you will need a lot of help). His exams are fair, but difficult.
No Comments

Class seemed very daunting at first but Dr. Parsons breaks everything down in a way that feels like taking middle school algebra. Useful class to take before the more rigorous econometrics coursework as it lays a solid foundation for the more in-depth stuff you'll do next.

i took intro to applied economic practice with her (econ 3271) and her syllabus and grading style was AMAZING. she respects her students time and treats us like adults.

Attendance = 10%
Homework (One Drop) = 48%
Case Study One = 8%
Case Study Two = 10%
Case Study Three = 10%
Case Study Four = 10%
Case Study Presentation = 4%
Late Work = 20% Off

Professor Parsons was really easygoing and helpful. The lectures were very clear and all the homework assignments were the same as the notes we took in class. The case studies she does seemed hard at first, but once broken down, were super easy. She also offers good feedback and is a super nice grader.

Covers using Stata and econometrics in a very gentle and easy to digest way. Homework and projects are most of the grade and the expectations are clear. Great class to take before taking upper level econometrics

This class was by far the hardest class I've ever had to take, but if you ask if for help and show that you are truly trying and doing your best, he will see that and do what he can to help. It is very important to go to the extra study sessions and ask him for extra help. He notices those things and it is so very worth it in the end.

Don't get me wrong this course is difficult. I struggled with a lot of the unit material. But when I expressed my worries with Dr.Parrish he helped me, and actually cared. He is the only reason I ended this class as strong as I did. Truly one of the best professors I have had at Mizzou!

Hands down, the hardest class I've taken at Mizzou. I had all A's up to this point, but I got Ds and Fs on the first two tests after attending all classes and office hours and spending my weekends outside of class studying. You get one dropped exam, but the course is exam-heavy. However, the prof is very caring, and because of his help, I passed.

Well this sucks to write because I actually like the guy a lot, but I would not wish taking this course online upon my worst enemy. If you have a job over summer or have trouble will online lectures do NOT take this class. It is very lecture intensive and many days will have you watching nearly 2 hours of lectures, and that's before note taking.

Took for 3202 and 4204. 3202 sucked--but due to Hanft, not him. 4204 has been a ton of fun. He's a good lecturer, though often has tangents, and wants everyone to learn. However, not in a gatekeeping sort of way. He respects grades as things for scholarships, etc., so doesn't try to aim for a class average GPA of 3.0 or any crap like that.
Very accessible outside of class, gives great lectures. Exams are difficult, but you won't have much homework and the homework grades boost your grade a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was difficult. The lectures while fine were unhelpful. Tests and lecture materials didn't align. Tests were comprised of questions that had never been covered or expected students to make rash assumptions about the material. Funny guy, but class was dense and he didn't know what to focus on enough.

Highly recommend going to office hours as Dr. Parrish is very personable and reviews everything lectured about. He is pretty funny and overall a great lecturer! The course has some difficult content as there is a lot thrown at you, but I am so glad I had Dr. Parrish for it!

Pretty easy and manageable course. Dr. Parrish is clearly enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the subject, but he does not always express his thoughts clearly and I find him hard to follow. He kinda bounces all over the place.
Dr. Parrish was very knowledgeable on the content in this course. I found him easy to approach for extra help and questions beyond the course content. He is also pretty funny

Dr. Parish cares about your success! Great guy, loved his lectures. Very knowledgeable on the topic and explains material in a way that is easy to understand. This course has a lot of "padding," so your performance on the exams isn't the only thing that determines your final grade.

Dr. Parrish is extremely knowledgeable and wants to help his students learn. He was always accessible outside of class as well. In phys, we watched the lectures online, then came to class to discuss what we watched, which I found super helpful for truly learning the material. He is approachable and helpful, so I definitely recommend this class!

the tests are definitely difficult. they often had errors in them (even if just grammatical) or questions that weren’t clear. i didn’t really find him approachable for extra help. his lectures were really detailed and thorough, though. exams are about how well you understand/can apply material, less about memorization.

I had him for physiology, but really got to know him in pharmacology. Seek him out. He is very knowledgeable and understanding. He loves helping his students and gave hilarious pharmacology lectures. He had regular lecture classes and then one class a week was more of an in-depth case study day. It was really challenging and fun.
He teaches the first half of the Physiology course. He is great. I absolutely loved when he was teaching the course. He is extremely nice and will go out of his way to help you. Loved him.

He teaches the first half of the course very well. I found his lectures to be very interesting, or as interesting as they could be at 8 am when you are way too tired to actually function. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches, and it is super respectable. He teaches at a good speed which makes this super rigorous course easier.

I absolutely loved this professor. He just wanted his students to do well. His exams are difficult, but if you study hard you will not have a problem. He cracks the occasional joke in lecture. Attendance is not mandatory, but I would recommend going because he does say what you do and do not have to know for the exam. He also posts a study guide!

AMAZING. If you have to take physiology take it with him! I'm not a strong student, but if you study the slides and follow the study guides he provides you will score GREAT on tests. Lab for this class also makes up a huge percentage of points and helps your grade. I cant say enough good things about this man and his class.

I LOVE MARVIN! He can be kind of rude at times but if you go to class and study hard, you will be just fine. His lectures are actually pretty engaging and interesting to listen to. He's hilarious. You get graded by like 3-4 exams but if you really study and go to class, you'll pull out with at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. I respected the way he conducted class, and felt that I had learned more because of it. You must do all assigned readings, know everything he has said in his lectures, and then some, to do well. I would not say I am blessed in this subject, but with a solid work ethic, I got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If you are good at memorization and have an interest in politics, you will be fine. However, if you are looking for an easily passable class without doing work, you will fail. He is very tough and you have to study heavily for the exams. There is a lot of information and it takes a lot of dedication to get through the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: To reiterate a former post, Overby gets a lot of hate that he doesn't deserve. He will make you work for your grade, and he will make you smarter.
Great teacher overall you will learn a lot if you attend the classes, the whole class is based on four tests, take good notes, review the notes very well before the test and you'll be alright

His lectures are pretty interesting and he's good at keeping you engaged on a boring topic. The reading is not really necessary but be prepared to miss a few test questions if you don't do it (he assigns like 50 something pages a week, not worth it). Overall, he's a good professor if you try in class and study hard for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is one of the worst classes that I have ever taken. Do not take this class. The professor is rude and will use profanity throughout the class. The exams contain so much material that it's ridiculous. He will not let you withdraw with an F. He does not care what you are going through.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Overby is one of the best teachers that I have had at Mizzou. He does make you work for your grade, but he has a wealth of knowledge that you should take advantage of. This class is very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I feel like Overby gets a lot of hate that he doesn't deserve. He can be an ass but you can tell he loves what he is taking about and genuinely cares about you getting a solid education. Every class is a lecture and he doesn't take attendance, but if you miss the lectures you will most likely fail the test. He is always helpful during office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are very interesting and he teaches very well, however the tests are difficult and make up your entire grade. As long as you are ready to study, you will do okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As long as you pay attention in lectures and do your reading (while taking good notes), you'll be fine. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The worst class I've taken at Mizzou. Your grade is determined by 4 extremely hard exams that seem to have nothing from his lectures. There is reading outside of class and most of it isn't helpful. If you go to him for help, he is rude and not helpful. Take this class with a different prof. He makes this class way harder than a 1000 level class.
Good teacher, but tests are ridiculously hard.

Will keep you engaged for the entire hour and 15 min.  Somehow makes a lecture with just him talking extremely interesting.  Not an easy class, you have to show up every lecture.  Quizzes every week, tough tests, and an essay.  Extremely knowledgable.  Take it if you are a poly sci major.
One of the best professors at the University of Missouri. Overby is "Going to make you smarter"

Tests are ridiculously hard and don't seem to have anything from his lectures on them.  The whole class is graded out of four exams that are very hard to get A's on.  Do yourself a favor and take this class with a different professor.

Overby is tough but like everyone said very knowledge.  As this is an upper level class with poli sci majors, most people in class really respect him and enjoy the class, although it is very tough.  You will learn a ton, but weekly quizzes are hard and you must attend every class or you will miss vital notes as there is a lot of material.

Tests are very hard, Slim to no extra credit. Lectures go the full hour and fifteen minutes. He is very picky about phones in class. You will need to go to every lecture + additional 10 hours of studying to get a decent grade on the exams. Good luck
Good lecturer, and well informed. Hard class, but you learn a lot.
Marv is amazing. 'Nuff said.

Professor Overby is by far one of the greatest professor I have ever had. He is fun and friendly towards students. He jokes around during class but always remains on topic and makes it very interesting for students rather than a tedious nightmare as many professors have the tendency of doing.

He is going to talk, and you are going to listen. You aren't going to Facebook or play with your phone, because he will break your electronics. You will attend all classes and remain focused. You will learn much more than you expected. You will be rewarded with an A for  doing what is expected of you as a college student.
Overby is extremely knowledgeable and his lectures are interesting, but his tests are extremely difficult. If I could take this class again, I would take it a different professor.

Amazing professor! His courses are more challenging than those of his colleagues, but they are much more rewarding. He really cares about his students learning and is more than willing to help. Take diligent notes and review them before the weekly quizzes and you should do fine.

Marvin is amazing. Not only is he incredibly funny, but he knows what he's talking about. His class is so interesting and lecture style so conversational that I never wanted to miss class. Tests weren't too difficult, readings not necessary IMO. Just go to class and take notes. His upper level courses are a must for PS majors.
