Wonderful, challenging professor who drives his students to their strongest capabilities. Anyone who gets the chance to take his class should jump at the opportunity. He is a wealth of knowledge and a wonderful instructor.

He could care less about making sure people pass. In a class of 500, on the first test the average was a 52% no curve because we should've tried harder to do good. Terrible at explaining and never lets people ask questions in class.

Professor Overby is extremely rude and unhelpful. He tells you at the beginning of class to not even bother going to his office for questions or help. He is very arrogant and the exams are extremely tough. This is the worst class i have ever taken. Avoid taking this class if possible.

The teacher is a really cool guy who knows his stuff, but this class was horrible.  I would spend most of my week and all of my weekends studying for the tests, and I still made Ds and Fs. I attended all the lectures and took great notes, I read the books and still did not do well.  Do not take this class.

Overby has been one of my favorite professors of all time. He's absolutely hilarious, and he knows just about everything there is to know about Political Science. His class is nothing like high school government; it's really in depth, and not easy at all, but if you study hard enough you'll be fine. I would recommend taking this class, I loved it.
Overby is an amazing professor. If you are a Poly Sci major his class is a must. Be prepared to work hard and learn sooo much.

I learned more about American Government in a week than I did in an entire semester of high school American Government. He makes everything very easy to understand, and his study guides are helpful. The first exam was difficult because I didn't anticipate such detailed questions, but I learned from that and did well on the remaining exams.
He'll challenge you but it's a good thing. He wants you to know the material not just learn it for the test. Keeps lectures interesting most of the time. Very good professor.

This class was interesting but exams are ridiculous. I attended every single lecture and studied for every single test and failed all but 1. I don't know where he even gets test material because they're not even covered in class. Don't take this class if you want to get a good grade.

I love the guy, but his tests are impossible. I went to every lecture, studied for the tests, and participated in class, and I still only pulled out a C-. If you want your grade to suffer, take the class with Marvin...if not, stick with any of the other lectures. From what I've heard, Marvin is the only professor who makes this class at all hard.

This class was extremely difficult. I went to lectures,studied hard, went to study groups, went in and asked questions but when it came time to take the tests I was at a loss. The tests are hard and specific. You can tell he is passionate about the subject but the tests are impossible. I would avoid.

If you can avoid taking Overby, it'd be in your best interest to do so. His lectures are nothing like the exams, in which the exams are extremely difficult. Not once did he personally try to help me. Every time I asked, he directed me to a TA. I've never gotten a C on a transcript, let alone a D, but now, I have one. Thanks for the 'D', Overby!
do not take this class if you want to die. His tests are impossible. I go to class do all the homework and still do poorly!!!

LOVE Marvin's attitude. He's hilarious and is always willing to help you if you ask him personally. That being said, you will definitely need help at some point. His tests are ridiculous (thank goodness for curves) and there is a lot of content, but if you study hard and take good notes, you should be fine :)

i like the guy but christ the tests are hard.  I went to every class, took notes, did the readings, and studied more for these exams than any of my classes and this was my worst grade of the semester.  I miraculously pulled out a C after getting a D- and a D on the first two exams (half of the course grade).  I'd try to get someone else if possible

4170 is the best class I have taken at Mizzou. I never ever considered skipping because I loved it so much. Yes it was hard, but because it was so enjoyable I didn't mind. Marvin really knows what he is talking about, and if you go to his office hours and get to know him, you won't regret it!
Overby is probably the best professor in the department if not the university. Class is enjoyable and informative.

He is a great teacher. But his quizzes are all over the place. You must attend class on Tues bc there is a quiz every Thurs covering material from both days.  His quizzes sometimes cover only the lecture, or cover only the book.  So you must read the book.  He gives a study guide with the essay questions.  .  But this is not an easy class to take

He is a great teacher.  I really retain a lot of information from him.  But his quizzes are all over the place.  You must attend class on Tuesday bc there is a quiz every Thurdsday covering material from both days.  His quizzes sometimes cover only the lecture, and other times cover only the book.  So there is really no way to get around reading th

Hands down the best professor in the PoliSci dept. If you are a PoliSci major and genuinely enjoy learning new things about the history of the American political system, you MUST take at least one class with Marvin before you graduate. You will learn more in 2 weeks of Marvin's class than any other complete course in this department.

Ignore the comments from Poli Sci 1100 students. The class is required and nobody really likes a class they have to take. For those interested in Political Science, Overby is an engaging and knowledgeable professor. Lecture notes are vital; readings not as much. He actually wants you to retain what he teaches you and is not there to waste his time.

One of the best profs I've ever had. Extremely engaging and knowledgeable lectures. Isn't an easy grade, but if you go to class, take good notes, and study a moderate amount, there is absolutely no reason to not get an "A."

Marvin is one of the best professors I have ever had.  Ideologically I think that we are on opposite ends of the spectrum, but he does a good job being objective. He is a little tough though, just go to every class If you stay caught up then the tests are not very difficult.  I got an 'a' last semester with no reading and am in another class w/him.

Overby was one of the best teachers I have ever had.  He is an incredibly engaging speaker and obviously knows the material inside and out.  He can seem intimidating but if you go to him for help he will do his best for you.

One of the hardest classes I have ever taken. I do not advise trying to take this course over a 4 week period. If you want an A, prepare to study furiously. Your best bet is to memorize your notes before tests. He never asked questions from the books. If you regurgitate what he says, you will pass.
Very interesting lectures, but the exams are nothing like the lectures.

He's a complete jerk BUT he know what he's talking about. He definitely challenges you to do your best. And he is willing to help you if you have the guts to ask him for it. The only reason I'm giving him and average rating is because he was too arrogant and said the F-word at least once a class period.
Kinda arrogant.  Pretty charismatic.  Overall, thumbs up.
Would help if he actually put stuff we talked about in class.

Exams very hard, teacher on an ego trip. Going to class won't be enough to pass this class, studying might not be enough either to get through these tough exams, take this class with another prof., and maybe you'll actually enjoy it...
Great teacher. He loves political science. Very engaging in class. One of the only professors who gets interaction in class and makes it engaging
Overby acts like this class is upper-level. He really knows his****, but he's arrogant, and quite an ****. The good thing, he's very smart, and KNOWS he's a jerk. His tests are very challenging.

Overby is horrible excuse for a professor! His test are rediculus for an enry level class and he needs to get over himself and realize that he isn't the greatest politician that walks the earth. If you have Overby as your professor, I suggest you rearrange your schedule and get a decent grade.
Basically people who can't do...teach. He needs to stop crying about all the little details and start helping students understand American Government like we pay him to do.

I dont mind a challenging class...but please give me a teacher who is more worried about actually helping students learn and be successful than finding ways to trip you up just to show his "expertise".
He needs to get his head out of his ass and make an exam that is over the material WE talked about

Ok, Marvin needs to have a ****ing reality check.  He is full of himself and needs to realize that the universe does not revolve around him.  He believes he is the greatest thing in the world and tells you that you will respect him by the end of the class.  I didn't respect him and I never will!
Yes, Overby is a challenge but he's willing to help you out.  I don't know where this negative feedback comes from because he helps anyone who asks.  He's even helping me land an internship.

Overby needs to get over himself. Loser. Good luck not allowing your ears to bleed during the first day of preaching about honor code and about how he is so high and mighty. Also, if you can get past being threatened and belittled constantly, then you'll still fail because of his crafty "exams".

You absolutely must be prepared for his tests by really thorough studying of notes. You should also attend class as often as possible. The TAs are not helpful, so you have to focus in class. The tests are very hard, but with studying are do-able. Overall, I actually really liked this class.
did not try in any way to help his students understand. too long inbtwn tests and the class avg on the final was a 55% and he wouldn't curve b/c 'we didn't study enough'. i studied for 4 days...
this class was horrible. knowledgeable professor, but tested on too much material for the tests

For those who aren't interested in politics... this class is really gonna suck.  But if you really study... it's still gonna suck.  There are questions on the test that you've never heard of, he tricks you on the exams, and your grade is based on 3 exams.
covers a TON of in-depth material w/ at least 5 pages of notes/day. very knowledgeable, but is hard w/ almost 2 months inbtwn the 1st and 2nd tests.

he is pretty tough and there are a TON of notes between the first and the second midterms, but if you study hard enough you can pass.  just make sure to pay attention and go to every class.  and he does not believe in extra credit so dont even try to ask.

He is a very good speaker and his class is interesting to sit through. He doesn't give extra credit, there are only 2 midterms and a final. He always says that you should never go to him with your problems-go to the TAs. But isn't he our teacher?
No Comments

He is a very good speaker and knows what he is talking about. There are only 3 tests in the and this man does not believe in extra credit. make sure you bring a pen threre are a lot of notes. Not a bad class to go to but study really hard for the tests!
No Comments

New the material well.
Graded fairly.
Was good at teaching and answered questions well.
Tests are curved to heavily favor students.
Funny, felt comfortable in his class.
Negatives:
Could have been a bit better at paying attention to students with their hands up.

I enjoyed taking his class. Practice tests and quizzes were just like the practice, an easy class to pass with no homework. As long as you study the reviews, there is no need to attend class. Was easier then any math class I've taken at Mizzou (compared to all the calcs, matrix theory, etc)

reviews.comment: Tells the best jokes. Test are exactly like his practice test and he genuinely wants you to succeed. I love his organization and how he moves through the course.
Dr. Pivovarov is awesome. I really enjoyed attending class. Often he asks questions to the class. He is very nice and has a good sense of humor. I learned a lot about proofs.
Learned a lot from the class because I was forced to study a lot.

reviews.comment: He was very kind and funny during lectures and bumped my grade up at the end of the semester! He was easily approachable and open to help. Lectures can be kind of grueling sometimes but so is Calc in general.

He is a solid teacher but was boring, every class i found it difficult to pay attention because it my mind drifted. He doesnt grade too hard. His notes are the definition of okay. He is better than my last college math professor so i guess thats good.
Moves really fast, but that's expected for a high level Math course. Speaks really clearly and always knows what he's talking about. Never saw a problem or question from a student stump him.

reviews.comment: poor teaching skills and doesnt take feedback well

Good professor, taught the subject material in a way that was easy to understand. Sometimes had to rush through things but mostly because of snow days. Asked class if they understood before he moved on to a new topic.

He didn't turn around to answer questions very often. He also answered questions too deeply to the point of no longer understanding the answer. He did though teach us the content and he did not expect anything unreasonable. Overall he was alright.

Overall one of the smartest math professors I have ever had. I am a math major and took through calculus 3 before even getting to college, however I really struggled with this class. His tests were too long, the class content was way to difficult, and the lectures were taught as though we were already supposed to understand the information.

reviews.comment: Professor Pivovarov taught very linearly and would often teach an entire class without participation if no one had questions. His tests were challenging, but always graded fairly with attempt to give as many points as possible. The vast majority of the class was based on tests that were challenging if you did not do the comprehensive practice exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He goes through content very quickly in lecture and doesn't take many questions. He makes exams very difficult, but grades fairly and I really enjoyed the class. Probably the hardest math class I've taken.

Peter on average turned around to see if the class was still there maybe twice a class. Tests were pretty tough and he was always very vague on what to study for them. He also provides very little resources online or outside of class so basically you are on your own for studying.
Great guy and great teacher. Class was most difficult class I had ever taken but he was still a good teacher and had fun doing it. Really helpful and there for you if  you seek him out.

One of the most well organized classes I've taken.  He is very clear in lecture and you're never caught off guard by the difficulty of an assignment or exam.  The subject is challenging but not nearly as hard as it's made out to be, and if you're genuinely interested it's so much fun.  I wish it had been more rigorous, but I loved this class.

Dr. Peck is actually the best! He is so incredibly kind and supportive of his students, and even though he is incredibly smart he does a good job of teaching undergrads. Very lecture heavy and has pop quizzes, but the material is not too tough if you keep up. Wish I could take him for every biochem class!

Dr. Peck is one of the kindest professors you will meet. There are weekly pop quizzes, but they are incredibly easy. There are ~15 homework assignments for the whole semester and three exams. The exams are easy; however, he does grade them tough. He cares about his students inside and outside of class and is extremely understanding/accommodating!

I took Dr.Peck for 2480 and beware of pop quizzes!!!! He will hint at when they are but you have little idea when they will be. Because of this he expects you to be in class every day. The class is so lecture heavy. All written exams. He does care about his students and is really approachable outside of the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was thankful to have MS. Pfuhl this semester, especially with the craziness going on with the outside world right now. She is incredibly understanding of any issues you come across and is very approachable. She kept class fun and is easy to work with. Do the work, and you should have no problem getting an A.

Such a nice teacher! She's a grad student so she understands student's struggles. No busy work, but sometimes the homework is a lengthy and tedious. she helps a lot if you're struggling. She keeps class interesting which helps if you don't like English courses that much. Do your work and you'll get an A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor.  She is early in her teaching career but very helpful. Writing intensive class will require papers but she will walk you through and coach you on how to make YOUR specific paper a lot better.  Ended with an A+. Missed a couple assignments but if you participate in class you can pass easily.

Okay, it's obvious she is being review bombed due to her recent tweet re: the fires in California (Jan '25)
So Imma be truthful.

Karen is a solid teacher, her classes were straight forward and she is good to talk to, whether you agree with her politics or not. she is an open mind and mouth, and I think that is important for growing minds.
Spent most of our time watching YouTube videos, and not actually learning. Lots of pop quizzes, and she can be inappropriate
Yuck for the class

reviews.comment:
Very judgmental and actually did not hide that she enjoys someone struggling because of differing beliefs.

I was very pleased that I did not suffer like other commenters about having to see "too much skin", I have enough leather at home.

reviews.comment: I took British Literature: Black and Asian Studies. The one thing I appreciate is that she extended the due date to multiple assignments. My complaint is long response times to my emails, many quizzes and journals for the books we would read, and only watching youtube videos.

Very nice woman but I wouldn't take this class unless you want to be told how to think regarding politics (which should never be the objective of any teacher), and sit around and watch videos all class after taking a pop quiz over the extensive amount of reading.

She spent each class confused and was extremely vague. She often completely mixed up characters and stories. She told our class that we would be doing a research paper and then later seemed confused and told us that we shouldn't need to do outside research for the papers. She also made inappropriate jokes when we read stories about sexual abuse.

I thought this class could be interesting, but no.  The books were good, the teaching was terrible.  This was a Women's Writers class turned anit-Iraq and anti-Bush class.  Regardless of your opinion, it's not literature.  Furthermore, I saw way too much of inappropriate parts of her body in class (accidentally, of course).  Ditto to above remarks.

I loved this class!  Piper is fun and high tech.. she mixes it up with video clips and power point and great readings by authors I'd never heard of before.  But if you don't like talking or presenting, don't take it!

Well, if you'd rather watch Google videos about nothing for an hour and fifteen minutes than learn anything about British lit, take this class. Occasionally, you'll watch a Power Point about something marginally related to the class or the novels. And you'll read some abysmal excuses for literature. But you might get an "A." You decide.
Very difficult class and the tests are insanely hard with no where near enough time to complete them.

This class is a baptism in fire, he's incredibly passionate during lectures and all around amazing but the course itself is incredibly confusing and forces you to go to the PLA/office hours. It was fun though and most came out better.

For a first semester class you are expected to know a lot of chem/calc, and without it you will constantly be left behind in the lectures. The homework's are made unreasonably difficult having to sit in office hours with the other students for 3+ hours a week. This class should be more introductory like the other intro to engineering classes are.

Professor Pinhero is an amazing professor! His lectures are really interesting and he is a super nice guy. His homework is extremely tough though. I had to go to office hours just about every week to keep an A, but he gives extra credit to make up for it. I also wasn't sure what my grade was until the end of the class, which isn't ideal.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pinhero was always very dedicated to seeing students succeed, however his homeworks were often incredibly overcomplicated and in order to pass you had to attend office hours on Friday nights that lasted 2-3.5 hours. Pinhero is a genius, but often left us as students in the dust when it came to lectures. Overall, a great man and ok prof
Great class
Awesome class
Awesome teacher that cares about students  learning.
Awesome professor!

Dr. Pinhero is a tough teacher but makes you learn your stuff. He dual taught the course I took with Dr. Myers and overall it was the most challenging class I've taken in college. Even though it was difficult, I learned a ton. He challenges you to really solidify your knowledge and is great with helping 1 on 1.

The course was dual taught by Dr. Pinhero and Dr. Meyers. Specifically Dr. Pinhero is a great professor, a little tough yes but he is truly interested in student learning. He may seem intimidating at first but is very approachable and knowledgable about the subject. I look forward to taking another class with either professor.

This course was dual taught by Dr. Myers and Dr. Pinhero.  Individually they did a great job, however there were some instances when both would try to lecture at the same time and that was less productive.  No course has challenged me like this one has.  I worked hard to learn a lot.  Overall an extremely informative and extremely difficult course.

Dr. Pinhero is extremely intelligent, and conveys information very well.  He is perfectly happy to let a student run down his own rabbit hole before correcting him, but he ultimately makes sure students understand the material.  He helped me during office hours a great deal.  His class was difficult, but I learned a lot.

This class was a dual-taught class with Pinhero/Myers. Dr. Pinhero is easily one of the smartest men in our department. He works conceptually, which is different for engineers, but altogether useful. You have to study hard, but he is almost always available to help. I couldn't have asked for a better Thermodynamics course.

Dr. Pinhero is a great professor and I got a lot out of thermo. The material is very confusing, but I think he did a great job organizing it and getting it across clearly. He's very interested in student learning, and the project was helpful. I feel confident leaving this class.
Smart guy who really knows his stuff.  The class is hard and can be confusing but that is due to the material more than the professor.

Dr. Pinhero was borderline genius.  He knows his stuff but sometimes had a hard time dumbing things down for his students.  Tests were difficult but reasonable and I learned a lot from his class though most of the class was based on theoretical science.

Dr. Pinhero really knows his thermo, but sometimes didn't do a great job of communicating the concepts to students. Because of that, some of the questions on his test seemed to come out of left field. Definitely not a dull prof though, a lot of his classes were pretty entertaining.

Hes class is awful. Lack of organization. Making mistakes frequently. And his tests have nothing to do with his lecture. Never be able to answer your questions clearly. Hes the worst teacher ive ever met
I took element

Veronica was a good teacher and knows Spanish well.  I personally didn't have an issue with the class as long as you attend, do all the assignments and participate.  The tests are usually straight forward and same with projects.

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Go to class, pay attention, participate, do the assignments are you're set. Perez-Picasso makes the language easy to understand and a fun class to be in.

Very chill professor, very fair grader. There are a ton of "busy work" assignments, but if you put in even a little bit of effort, you'll get full credit. She's also flexible about due dates and tries her best to help you succeed in the class (required conferences for essays, peer review).
That entire class felt like a fever dream. The work was easy though. Wow. Just wow.
very nice but and lots of participation points but the essays were graded harshly

NEVER take English 2010 with her. Each assignment requires a million little ridiculous hoops to jump through. The amount of excess work required just to write what should be a simple essay is absolutely absurd. Not to mention, the class is dull and somehow makes fairly easy concepts seem difficult.

reviews.comment: she gives you the illusion of choice then makes you spend half of every class trying to guess what she wants. anyone who has taken an AP lang type class will be bored out of their minds in this one. she doesn't grade quality of writing which would be great in any class except this one (a required intermediate comp class for future english teachers)
Best class I have ever taken. Free money. Don't listen to anyone else.
Very understanding with college students and their lives outside of school. Very flexible with making adjustments to the schedule to best fit everyone's needs.

reviews.comment: Penny is a very nice person & she means the best but the class is not enjoyable. It's an insane amount of busy work and long projects/papers. I rly wanted to like this class but couldn't. Don't expect to learn how to write, as we never get specific feedback. She creates an open space for sharing, but the class can often get political.

Was pretty turned off by all the negative reviews but Penny ended up being a solid professor. You can't skip class and have to take part in at least a few class discussions. Overall it's not difficult to do well if you show up and complete the writing assignments. I could definitely tell she wanted us to improve and succeed as writers.

Penny is a funny & cool person who really wants students to succeed. That being said, this was the hardest class I've ever taken. Every assignment had lots of tedious "writing process" activities. Participation/discussion board points are easy & worth a good % of your grade. Got an A, but worked SO hard and wrote what I knew she wanted to hear.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS! By the second lecture with her I knew I would hate her class, its so boring and the task are useless. Instead of allowing us to give a final product she gives these stupid mini tasks in between. Her grades fluctuate like CRAZY. The way she teaches is just confusing and annoying. Save yourself the time and avoid her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is just so boring. And she makes you do assignments in parts instead of just doing the final product. Remember being forced to do graphic organizers in elementary school? She makes you do stuff like that before you write a paper, except they're harder than doing a basic graphic organizer. It's so pointless and a waste of time.

The first day of class she explained the course very well and in detail, and she puts a cool spin on the traditional English class. She gives great feedback on your papers and drafts and is always willing you help with any questions. She really wants her student to succeed. She's also pretty funny! Definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I was going to wait until the end of the semester to write this, but I am just so fed up.  The amount of extra assignments that she makes the class do, not to mention an entry level class, is ridiculous. She grades so harshly on things that take hours to finish. She was the only teacher left for English 1000 during registration. DO NOT TAKE THIS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Screw this professor. Completely over the top and forces you to watch Star Trek. Never organized. Very rude. Treats students like children. 0/10 would not recommend.
She is literally the worst teacher I have ever had. She doesn't help at all when you ask for help and makes everything 10x harder than it should be. Do not take a class with her!!!!!
Penny is a great lady, but she should be teaching an upper level English class. She makes the class harder than necessary for a gen ed.

She knows what she wants, and has a hard time explaining it.  All assignments were very specific, but was worded weirdly, so it was hard to understand.  It was very hard to get a clear answer out her if you asked a question.  If it is not her opinion it is mostly likely wrong.  However, if you do the work it would be hard to fail.

Like a lot of others have said she is smart. Her grading is just so tough and her essay assignments are difficult and unclear of what she wants. I attended class every day and still could not understand what she wanted.
Most confusing teacher I've ever had.

DO NOT TAKE!! She is an extremely smart individual but she uses her entire class time forcing you to participate in discussion. The assigned papers were super specific and if it did not fill her exact expectation then do not expect a good grade. The class workload was overwhelming and unnecessary for an entry level English class.
DO NOT TAKE. She is really smart, which would normally be a good thing. But she spends half of class trying to get people to say what she wants say. Not helpful. EXTREMELY tough grader.
DO NOT TAKE. VERY unclear and confusing, wayyy to much busy work, any other professor is a good idea. Easily the hardest class I have taken here. SWITCH OR RUN.

She was very confusing about what she wanted. The class started out pretty well and simple, but when she got more into depth later in the semester. She only repeated herself and couldn't give a clear answer for questions. Avoid her... also she showed a power point of student comments who loved her class on the first day, it was kinda sad...

Overall good teacher some of the paper topics were difficult to understand but if you show interest she is willing to help. if you show up to class and look like you care she will give you a decent grade.

Difficult to understand at times, however a very rewarding class to take if you have the time and interest.  Mainly a gender/culture oriented curriculum.  She is a very intelligent and engaging professor.  Pre-J students would benefit from taking her class as it gives important outlook and discussion on subjects relevant to current events.

One of the worst teachers at Mizzou. I did show up for every class. She was not helpful during her office hours. When you would go to her office hours, she would treat you like you're mindless and stupid. Her teaching is unclear. She's the reason I have to take the class over again.

Professor Smith-Parris was nice, intelligent, and more than willing to assist students in their learning. HOWEVER, she was EXTREMELY unclear with the ideas and concepts she presented in class to the point where asking for help seemed useless. She assigned way too much work and went way too deep for a 1000 level course. This class made me cry. Avoid

I took Brit. Lit. with Penny and it was my favorite class this semester. She does not grade hard and is crystal clear on what she expects. She is very understanding and extremely nice. If you are willing to put in the effort, it is not difficult to receive a good grade in this class.

Class is easy for the most part. Shes an easy grader and will extend due dates if you need it. The material is somewhat interesting, but she gets way too into it to the point where everyone is confused. She isn't always clear on what she wants & get used to working on 2 papers at a time. But I BS'ed my papers & still got an A. Just go to class
This class is just flat out terrible. She stresses too much on obscure cultural questions but never explains. Shes slow and not fun to look at. Don't waste your time.
Brit Lit 1200 was an enjoyable class with Penny. As long as you keep up with your readings, this class is very manageable. Take notes during her lecture and participate and you will be fine!
Just run. Thanks all I can advise after taking this class... Switch teachers

This is a very difficult class and I found myself dreading every Tuesday and Thursday because of it. The material is boring, but comprehensible. This professor is more than willing to help with any questions I had. If you use her advice and go to class, you won't do bad. However, this class is very hard, so try to find a different teacher

Extremely har class. Was clueless on all papers, reading quizzes and finals as to what she wanted due to her lack of explanation of each. Requires a majority of your studying time over other classes. Do not take this class unless you have nothing better to do or want to go above and beyond a challenge.

Terrible teacher! Drop the class! She has no idea what she's teaching and my entire class was completely lost the entire time.  I'm a really good student and always did my homework but I honestly have no idea what she wants in this class.  Homework and papers are completely unclear.

She is by far the worst teacher I've ever had.DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME/MONEY TO TAKE HER CLASS! She gives reading assignments out for quizzes daily and the quizzes will be nothing from the reading. I literally got up and walked out of her class during her lecture and dropped the class the day I got a "0" for not doing an assignment to her specication

I had to put 120% into this class.  I had to sacrifice all my other classes to get the B grade I needed to get into the J-school.  Unless you are really good at reading someone's mind, I suggest you find a different teacher.
Terrible teacher. Class average is the lowest of all of all the english sections. Pointless assignments, and tests on every reading assignment. DROP THIS CLASS!
She grades ridiculously hard and isn't clear on what she wants at all. Pretty sure she just enjoys giving out bad grades because the class average was in the low 70s. Terrible.
She is unsure of herself and contradicts instruction leaving students guessing. Not sure what she is teaching Eng or what she choses.  Do not take this class, find other class.

She does not teach very well at all.  She does not make anything clear and is not very good on letting you know what to read for class.  All the assignments she gives are pointless and have nothing to do with the essays you are required to write.  She's boring, and should be fired.

the assignments were stupid and not explain well.  she gives a lot of side work that is no help at all.  if you actually take this class do all the readings because she will give quizzes. she is boring and i learned nothing in this class.
This class was useless.  All of the assignments were extremely abstract (compare the oedipus cycle to 9/11, etc). Didn't learn english, i learned to hate the class.
Do not recommend this class unless you are very interested in politics. Papers are your analysis of political readings...very boring lectures/discussions

Just really an awful class.  This class is required but I would recommend that you pick a different teacher.  The things that she teaches in class has nothing to do with the homework.  The class is slow paced and boring.  Just a total waste of time.

He is a really cool and kind person with a more sarcastic sense of humor. If you have any difficulties email him and he is really helpful. He did give lots of busy work and there were times he randomly added extra assignments mid-week but consistently extended deadlines and was more than willing to take student feedback. READ THE SYLLABUS.

Cannot say enough, STAY AWAY. During the week, you had 4-5 busy work assignments (more than my online class, which is perplexing). Sometimes, he'd add more assignments mid-week as an "experiment" (he made us write an essay on what we want to research in 3020, but you don't do research in 3020). You could do less work with a diff prof for same grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wood genuinely cares about you and encourages everyone to ask questions and clear up any confusion with him. He responds quickly to emails and has consistent office hours. You do need to at least skim the textbook to learn what he doesn't cover in the lecture because there will be questions from it on the test. Tests are online!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment:
Phil is truly a nice, caring professor. He enjoys talking with students and often walks around the room in order to encourage more interaction.
Personally, I struggled with hearing him at time, but you can always talk to him after class, and he assigns homework that is actually helpful, even though it seems like a lot.
He bumped my grade up for no reason other than he said I deserved better. He brings snacks to class and class is optional. A great professor cannot recommend enough.

He was incredibly smart and really cares about the success and wellbeing of his students. The content of this course was challenging for me personally but I definitely chose the right professor to take this class with. Some assignments could be a bit confusing. Especially if you don't always come to lectures, keep a close eye on the Canvas page.
He's very clear if you studied ahead. He's kind of funny too. He knows SO much what he is talking  about, one of the best classes I've taken.

Funny. Class follows book and handouts. Lectures pretty open-ended. You need to ask questions, because otherwise he tries to use the lecture to "make things interesting" by extending things. Homeworks help, project paper can be done which will help for your research or thesis.

Knows his stuff, but the course is harder than any course I've had. Genius grade, but thinks that because he knows what he's doing that we all do too. Probably smarter than most of the faculty but seems to want us to go out and be smarter than our advisors. Learned more than I have in any other class, though.

If you're wondering about taking this class, do it, provided you're willing to work hard. Dr. Phillips is by far the best professor I have had at Mizzou. Yes, this class can be time consuming, but it is absolutely worth it. The frequent feedback and exam tips are helpful. Show up, participate, and learn. It will pay dividends in the future.

Caters to pre-professional students. Felt like I didn't exist. Keep up and do the work or you will be hopelessly lost. Try to find a way to organize notes as quickly as you can. Helps to take pics in lab - buy the atlas - it will save your life in lab. He is arrogant and talks about Harvard/MIT quite a lot...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had him for premed fig. Hes very knowledgeable & provides a lot of resources for you. He can answer all your questions & prepares you for the future. He set up many informative guest speakers & med school tours. There are some assignments but mostly just talking about the medical field. He can be intimidating but put in effort & you will be fine.

I've never left a rate my professor, but I loved Dr. Phillips and I felt highly compelled to recommend his class. Throughout all of my University studies, he was my favorite professor. You are going to need to show up and engage, but he definitely puts the extra work into his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Must take it seriously and be willing to work hard and do lots of independent study, but it is by far the best class I've taken, with my FAVORITE professor. Both the class and professor are very helpful in preparing for med school; beyond worth it! He likes to act tough, but he is the most caring professor that would do anything for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor at MU. Those that don't like him aren't willing to work hard or don't take his warnings about pace/difficulty seriously. You have to earn your grade, but he gives you EVERYTHING you need, goes above and beyond to help you learn/succeed, and is a FANTASTIC mentor and asset for professional growth. The work is WORTH IT, I promise!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He cares about you learning the material and remembers students who come and don't come to class. The tests were never ridiculous, but they tested your knowledge and application of the material. Overall very good instructor. Do the homework!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: STAY AWAY. He will make your life miserable

This professor is horrible. Terrible lecturer and very condescending towards students. None of the instructions are clear as to what he's expecting instead he grades you're work based on what other students included. Unless you're good at reading minds don't take this class

I am yet to meet another professor who cares so much about their students' success. If you give him the chance, he will invest in you, ensuring you succeed in class and beyond. Take his class, but only if you are a hard worker with a desire to learn. If that describes you, it could be one of the most valuable opportunities of your college career.

I took his Cell Bio course over the summer. It was pretty challenging especially since the pace is ramped up for summer course, but his notes are very clear and he's always available for help during office hours. He's also very helpful when it comes to things outside of the classroom like questions about post grad programs and medical school.

There are a lot of essays but those can save your grade. If you do bad, you can re-do it to make up 12 the credit you lost (more if you go above & beyond- go to office hours!). The tests were usually hard, but he lets the students write the questions sometimes. The make-your-own final was great- just make sure the essay is good! Class ranks suck

His words on the final, open-ended essayexam: "If you can't find two cell biology topics that you feel are really interesting... you should reconsider your major or career aspirations." Well Mr. Phillips, I consider it a testament to my deep-seated scientific enthusiasm that I was able to consistently withhold myself from storming out in disgust.

I learned more in Histology than any other class in undergrad.  It has certainly given me an edge now that I'm in medical school.  Dr. Phillips goes above and beyond for his students, but you aren't going to get an easy A out of this class. You have to put in the time.  Take this class if you are pre-med. It's worth it.

Phillips was a decent teacher and cares that his students learn the important stuff. His grading is a little annoying. Overall, you learn a buttload of material, but you will also be forced to work for it. This is not an easy A type of class. I highly recommend it for pre-professional students. Don't let yourself be intimidated by him or others!

Dr. P loves no 1 better than himself & loves the sound of his voice. He likes to embarrass people & u sometimes have to wonder if he has a heart. Class is not challenging. Just bulk memorization. Learned a lot because TAs are awesome. Will be helpful for medical school. Don't let him scare u, his tests r not hard, u just have to put in the effort.

Teaches a difficult course where students are responsible for a large load of material.  The main problem is his grading, which is highly subjective. Also plays favorites, and will grade the students who brown-nose him higher than those who don't. Thinks Connely scholars are a godsend, and seems to have an inferiority complex.  Not humble.
He's tough and intimidating at first... but he's probably the best teacher I've had and REALLY cares about his students :) Even if he doesnt make fun of them!
good lectures, relatively easy tests, but incredibly nitpicky on assignments. Expected honors work from an intro class. Gave extra credit options to the honors class, but not the regular section.
I feel as if my speech has improved a lot after taking this class. I do not get as nervous anymore when giving speeches.

The class was hard but the assignments were fairly graded. He gave helpful feedback on the assignments and they all kinda built up. The lectures often had me confused but I went to office hours and did well on the papers and debates.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Bombed the first speech, went to office hours and did much better on the second. Classes usually ended 5 mins early.
Very tough tests. Expect lots of reading and quizzes. Enthusiastic. If you struggle, go to office hours and he will help a lot.

He is very clear on what he is expecting and is also very fair about assignments and such. He gave quizzes but they were small 5 point quizzes that really were there to help your grade. He even gave everyone 100% on some of the impromptu speeches we did to alleviate added stress. He is a great guy! If you give him respect, then he will reciprocate!

This guy isn't an actual teacher. I think he enjoys the subject matter, which means he's way more into it than you will be as a student. He talks really quickly and is somewhat spastic. He's very off putting from the very beginning. He reminds me of someone who was made fun of a lot as a kid, so he became a jerk in order to "get back" at those guys

I feel obligated to declare that this TA has an ego that gets in the way of his students learning.  If I had to make an analogy of his teaching style it would be relative to a horse with blinders on.  He is clearly trying to get his doctorate and move on.  Therefore, great care should be used when the university allows him to practice as a TA.

Talks about himself and topics that have nothing to do with class too much. I've never found his classes useful. Grades too hard on ALL assignments and always says he does it because people grade HIM hard in grad school... not my fault!

He was so full of himself and could care less about teaching actual helpful material. He was one of those "power hungry" teachers who had no clue what he was doing.  Hopefully he has changed, but I doubt it. I would highly recommend not signing up for any of his classes. (He also thought leap year included every month with 31 days)
It takes a little while to get used to him, but after you get used to his style it becomes pretty easy. I improved quite a bit as a speaker from the beginning to the end. Exams not that hard.

I liked him, he certainly tries to help students out when they need it. He also offers extra credit, which allowed me to get an A. The first part of the semester was kinda boring because of all the reading, but when you start really speaking, it's a pretty good class.

I thought he was a good teacher. Talks very fast but once you get used to him and his teaching style its not hard. You just have to put in effort and do the work. Can be a tough grader but he gave us an extra credit opportunity that really helped. Overall I have a very positive experience in his class. He's a good guy with a good sense of humor.

It was his first semester teaching last semester, so maybe that is why he was so terrible! He is not helpful and is very arrogant. If you have him for Public Speaking 1200, SWITCH NOW!! Saying this in all honesty!

I dont know what was wrong with the other two responses but he actually is a great guy. Great sense of humor and helps a lot. Just have to be willing to ask question and he will answer anything for you. Great Class. I had fun doing the speeches! Only bad part was the reading but I didnt do much of it and I did fine in the class.

If you can get out of this class do so as soon as possible. Huge jerk. thinks he is the creator of communication and that he has been teaching for years. super arrogant. if you are looking for a easy comm class for a pre req DONT TAKE THIS its just a huge hassle. waste of my time. he probably wrote the other review himself.
Hard grader and a lot of reading in the class but could be manageable.

Dr Powell is knwoledgeable in regard to theatre but it seems like in this class she was much more interested in learning about you then you learning about theatre. She is very understanding and thoughtful, but beware of the personal questions and the standard theatre type agenda to be pushed a little but. Regardless, this is certainly an A class.

Extremely nice, makes it clear that she cares about you as a person. Participation points but as long as you speak once per class you'll get 100%. Ends class 10 minutes early which is nice. The study guide is exactly like the notes. Only a handful of assignments and exams.

She's an inspiring teacher, kind to every student, and always looking to bring attention to underrepresented voices in the Theatre world. Most of her classes revolve around participation, so don't be too worried about your grade, just by showing up and paying attention.

Professor Robbins is passionate about philosophy, but his teaching style is often unclear and indirect. Even with prior knowledge of probability and statistics, the way he structured problems was confusing. The course also covers technical terms that you will never use in your life again. I would not take this class with this professor again.

For: How To Think.
Given the option, personally would not take again.
The actual content is fair but the
execution was poor - in my opinion.

very lecture-heavy and he's not great at teaching the material. Tes where medium difficulty until the last one and it was nothing like the study guide and very challenging. Would not take again as I don't like his teaching ways and the class was too difficult for an elective thats supposed to be fairly easy.

Professor Robbins is very passionate and knowledgeable about philosophy. That being said, this class is so hard for no reason. I really gave Professor Robbins a chance but his lectures were too confusing and rushed. He will go on and on about a topic all class and then realize that class is almost over and rush through the rest of his slides.

He understands that philosophy may not be everyone's strong suit and tries to make sure material is explained clearly. He talks pretty fast sometimes and it can be difficult to understand him if you don't catch what he says, but discussion groups help. Would recommend going to discussion. I probably won't take another PHIL class, but he was cool.

Requires lots of readings. Doesn't answer emails. Both lecture and discussion session require attendance. Very knowledgeable and can answer questions. Grades pretty hard on papers and short answer exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The course is a subscription, TOPHAT. It was very easy to comprehend and enjoy. The slides provide no help and even get off topic at times. Homework was fair as well. Exams are confusing like any PHIL class so be on guard for mentally challenging questions. Multiple choice is also easy, but the free answer questions are graded poorly...

Dr. Robbins does an excellent job explaining and articulating concepts. I had heard some complaints about him, but I found him to be pretty fair to his students. He was also extremely helpful during office hours before exams, he walked me through several long and difficult problems and prepared me well every time I stopped by. Great prof imo.

Prof Robbins talked a lot in his vids but never really got to the point, however, in TopHat, as long as you read the passages, you'll get the home work questions right. Easy class, not as good of a professor.

i have dr robbins for moral psychology right now, and i really appreciate how helpful he's been trying to accommodate for pandemic living! his main concern is his students understanding the material, so keep that in mind if you're lost and need help. he Will go on tangents about things that may not seem connected tho lol. he's just super nice !

really nice guy, tophat textbook & easy weekly homework online, attendance & participation in lecture & discussion for grade, discussion is useless-avoid Sukhvinder Shahi, 3 tests-multiple choice & written questions but can use 1 page cheat sheet so pretty easy, gives extra credit assignment to raise grade 3%, gives good examples but can get boring
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Robbins is a bit of an odd duck but he's very passionate about what he teaches and is good at explaining to help you understand. Attendance is counted and he asks about 3 in class questions for credit a day so showing up is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is not the best professor in the world. He thinks that he makes the class and the concepts easy but he teaches it only in a way that appeals to him. He talks super fast and just assumes that everyone knows what is going on. It is more of like a statistics class and there is some hard math involved which made it harder for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yikes. I took his class for an entry-level philosophy course. He talked himself in circles without ever getting to the real point of any of the lectures. He seemed incapable of explaining or teaching any of the concepts in any digestible way. Grades too harshly for topics he didn't explain well and has poor communication with TAs on grading.

Had a rough time in this class and trying to understand the importance of diving so far into theories that only exist in the class itself. Basically you dissect logic and reasoning. It's way easier to look at the overall problem and figure it out using common sense rather than using the methods in this class.
cool concepts but a lot of information. didnt mind this class at all. papers are rough and tests can be difficult but basically you just have to work hard for it
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher- he's occasionally amusing but he's no good at explaining anything. Grades harder than he probably should. I headed into this class loving philosophy, but now I dread it. This class has made me question taking any philosophy class again.

He knows what he's talking about, and that's all I can say for him. He rambles until he's confused himself and seems incapable of understanding well-worded student input. This is a small honors discussion class- or it's supposed to be. He treats this as soapbox hour which would be great if he could articulate himself at all. NEVER TAKE THIS TEACHER

Not a great class to take. Robbins is nice but is much more of a critical grader than he needs to be for a 1000 level class. I wasn't expecting the class to be easy, but in a class full of pre-med and pre-law honors students, this shouldn't have been our lowest grade when all of us worked really hard. He does offer extra credit which helps.

Overall nice guy, good sense of humor. Very knowledgeable about philosophy and seems to love the material he's teaching. Very hard grader, especially on essays. Feedback can seem more critical than constructive. Not too strict on doing the readings, offers a few extra credit papers. This is a TOUGH course, not really for freshmen. Not recommended.

As a person with a writing disability this was not an easy class to take. It was two long essays and two full writing tests. While taking the class I absolutely hated it because I really put myself in a hole. But looking back it wasn't actually too bad. I've heard phil 1200 is the way to go so look there first.

I took this course as an elective to raise my GPA and it ended up being more difficult than I'd anticipated. Robbins is a cool guy, but his grading rubrics are ridiculously strict and he tried out a new program TopHat that was not benefitial. There's only 2 tests and 2 papers so don't take those lightly!

Very clear about what he teaches and is very unbiased. I am still not completely sure about his stance on some topics. Gives reviews for tests before them and weekly quizzes comes straight from the notes. Corny jokes and video clips easily makes attending class worth it.

Great professor. Not biased, even when discussing religion he gives both sides, and allows student in a lecture hall to point out arguments against the suggestions he makes. Very fair. Book is kinda worthless, just go to class, definitely go to discussion groups. Tests are written and kind of difficult, but papers are fairly straightforward.

at first it seems impossible because the quizzes are so difficult. Keep in mind though that they are only 20% of your grade and the 40% of your grade that is 2 papers you will get a high B or A on more than likely. Also there is 5% extra credit!! bottom line: go to discussion, study for the exams the night before, don't read the textbook.

He was a pretty good professor. Had only 2 tests and 2 papers for the semester. There was weekly quizzes over the material learned that week which weren't always the easiest. The tests are essay so be sure to study really hard. If you pay attention in class and ASK QUESTIONS you should do just fine.

This class was pretty easy. You only have 2 exams and 2 essays for the semester, each make up 25% of your grade. If youstudy its a piece of cake. He is interested in teaching and the TAs are great. 5% extra credit added to final grade if you go to the non mandatory section meetings once a week. I'd recommend this class.

Had him for Intro to Ethics. Definitely recommend! The teacher is well-informed, clear, and unbiased. He uses movie clips and references to modern culture to aid understanding. There were only four assignments in the class (two tests, two exams), but they are easy if you do the readings and/or come to class. Very interesting, definitely recommend!

Professor Potter was easily the best professor I've had at Mizzou. I took his Comics and Cartooning, and despite being a journalism major, I had so much fun with this class. I received in-depth feedback that helped me refine my art. Potter is one of the most caring and intelligent professors at Mizzou and I highly recommend any one of his classes!
Excellent faculty member. Should be the go to for DST major students.

Probably the best professor I've had. Genuinely cares about his students, and was VERY understanding if you had to miss a class for a good reason. Rather than tough grading and strict rubrics, he believes in giving students detailed feedback to encourage real learning and self-improvement. Fosters creativity, discussion, and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is one of the only teachers I have had that I believe truly cares about me and my learning. I never got below a 100% on an assignment in his class, he cares that you learn and actually try on assignments more than how well you match a rubric. He is an amazing professor and I would recommend this course to anyone I know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Potter is energetic, motivated, and responsive. He genuinely is passionate about what he teaches and makes an effort to adapt the class to his students needs. This course might be difficult if you don't already have a basic understanding of digital programming and media editing. Homework is reading heavy in the beginning and shifts to media later.

Potter's the bomb. Take all of his classes. They're all so cool and you'll become a better writer. And a better artist! You gotta read, watch, and play a lot of digital content but it's all pretty compelling. He's god-tier in the DST department and he's hilarious. and super cute. and he really likes k-pop.

Nick is the best professor I have ever had. He's super down to earth and chill. He understands that life happens and school is sometimes second priority, while still holding people accountable. Not to mention, the "textbooks" we needed were video games. Easily my favorite class ever.

You're going to work for your grade in Dr. Potter's class, but you're also going to learn SO much. I took his course as a random elective because it sounded interesting. I didn't expect much. I came out of the class with more academic growth than I've experienced in any other course at Mizzou. He's a wonderful professor. Definitely take the class.

Nick is an awesome professor at Mizzou. He's wicked smart, funny, and doesn't take himself too seriously. There is a lot of reading but it's all mostly relevant and helps you think critically. You won't get away with surface-level analyses for the papers so think creatively and put in the effort. Overall, I loved this class.

Nick is SERIOUSLY the best. He's my favorite professor I've ever had. He expects a lot from his students, but don't be discouraged. The effort required to excel in his classes is totally worth it. You'll learn so much, you'll grow as a reader, writer, and artist, and he'll make you laugh the whole semester. Take. His. Class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nick introduces you to new material and makes you think outside of your comfort zone. He is interested in your opinions on the material he assigns and genuinely wants to hear from you. I learned a lot through reading and experiencing new mediums.

There is a ton of reading but it is all helpful to your writing. He is a fair grader and gives really helpful and honest feedback. He keeps the class entertaining and makes us feel comfortable with each other. He made my whole class mixtapes once and that was really cool and nice. Writing the longer short stories was really fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The Eng Dep is really hit or miss when it comes to professors, but Nick is one of the good guys. Knows his stuff, unpretentious, and easy-going.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: In the Digital Storytelling Department, many of the teachers are like splitting hairs to find who is best at what. Hands down I cannot amp this guy and his classes enough. He is funny, nice, and helpful. If I could take a whole semester of classes with Nick, I would. He is human and understanding and knows how to get you excited to be in his class.

Showed very little enthusiasm for material, lacked organization and readiness for class, denied disability accommodations, rude and unforgiving, strict grading despite no clear instructions on big projects, inability to learn from mistakes, bad communication, and arrogant. This professor was fired from Mizzou in 2022 after 1 year of employment.
Doesnt really teach much besides lectures where he just reads the screen. Class is primarily TA. Brian Arends is a great TA.

The lectures weren't very helpful for the assignments. The textbook is what teaches and tells you what to do, but it's a "teach yourself" kind of class. The TA was occasionally helpful. The exams were difficult because they are hard to prepare for and a decent portion of your grade. If you miss points on assignments, you don't really get feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Truly cars about her students and is very fair in grading.

Absolutely love her. She really cares and wants to hear everyone's opinions and makes it clear that her class is a safe space for everyone, even if your opinion differs from hers. I actually look forward to the discussions that we have in class. It's a super easy A, all you really have to do is show up and participate.

I actually took WGST 4600 Women & Health with Dr. Prasad, and it was one of my easiest classes of my senior year. The majority of class time we debated about different women's issues, so prepare to be in a political environment. Regardless, Dr. Prasad loves to hear everyones opinions and is lenient about due dates which is helpful!

I learned so much in this class and really ejoyed the class discussions. She always wants to get everyone involved and hear everyone's opinions--and she also shares her own which is cool. Easy A if you do the readings and just come to class.
Is unorganized most of the time. Very one-sided, opinionated lectures about her liberal/feminist feelings. Has random outbursts of anger for no reason.

Acts like the class will be easy take home midterm and final papers, no exams. Irrational grader. No clear with her expectations at all. She doesn't prepare for lectures. Plays youtube videos of people reading out of books (only first row can hear). Takes attendance. Has 5 question TF reading quizzes, she never knows the answers.
Good person. Great educator.  Fun and thought provoking class as long as you enjoy discussion.  Highly recommended for all considering going into health care.
ADORABLE teacher. EASY CLASS just pay attention and do the work ... easy A!!! LOVE SRIRUPA!! This is my second class with her and will take another if possible!

She knows what she is talking about and has great resources for class. Her class is a breeze as long as you pay attention and try. After taking two of her classes I think it is inspiring to see a teacher to invoke discussion and debate in such a passionate way to fully enagage students into the course work!
If you have any respect for yourself avoid this woman...because she doesn't respect anyone.  She treats everyone horribly.  By far the WORST prof I've had at Mizzou.  RUN!!!!
She was the worst teacher I've ever had in college. The class was horrible and worthless; I didn't learn a thing.
No Comments
he was really helpfulout of class but exams are a littlw harder than expected
He was a good teacher, and the class wasn't too hard. He was also pretty helpful out of class when I had questions
Would be fair to say that he cares less about the learnings of the student and more about his syllabus. So, basically he crams in as much as he can and spouts it on students.
Mr.Edara was a good teacher that helped me understand civil engineering in a better way then prior. His tests weren't to difficult if you just payed attention in the lectures but are too long.
Best teacher I have ever had
great guy

Felt like this might be a career path I'd be interested in. Dr. Edara convinced me otherwise. Very condescending. Exams were long and could not be completed in the allotted time. He acted like he wanted feedback regarding exams, but didn't change anything all semester. Promised bonus points for listening to presentations, didn't reward students.

The class was pretty easy to follow if you attended. The tests were a little long, and most of the time couldn't be done in the time permitted. The attendance wasnt mandatory but he did do random in class assignments, that were done in class and due before the end of class usually.

Very knowledgeable in the field and you will definitely get a lot out of this class if you show up to the lectures -- they are a drag though, u can get away with not going. Cool guy too, always had a smile on.

You do seed labs and some of his own created labs throughout the course and a few easy short answer written assignments. TA's graded fairly
i have no idea what's going on in this class 99% of the time

I took three other courses when I took his course. All the other courses together didn't require the collective efforts and pain I had to put in this. It's not that you would learn something cutting-edge. He would just dump all the projects he takes up for money and make students do free labor for him. Just awful
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Calyam is very knowledgable on the material. He makes class engaging and expects students to participate. This class had easy assignments but complex lectures. Some of the labs were frustrating because of random errors, and the exams took a long time, but I still got an A on everything. The group project is a lot of work and not well-organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were hard to understand, scattered and contained unrelated concepts that are vaguely related. Labs took 8 or more hours to complete and often had unrelated issues that took hours to resolve. Exam formatting of around 8 pages full of written response questions and diagrams was expected to be completed within the class hour for the exams.

This man is despicable. His response to the global COVID-19 pandemic was to create a midterm exam that took 5 hours to complete, not change any of his assignment due dates to accommodate students, and to also assign a final exam that takes no less than 9 hours to complete. Personally, the final took me 16 hours to complete. This is irredeemable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of assignments and they each require 6-12 hours of work to complete, this course should probably be a writing intensive. Sometimes labs would not work on my machine because we were asked to use obscure tools without community support. Went to online (covid) and the Exams were a nightmare. Grading criteria is the farthest thing from clear.

This dude makes learning anything an absolute chore. His in-class problems don't make any sense, you have no idea how to answer any of his questions, the GENI labs are like trying to build a house out of sawdust and duct tape, and the professor himself is very arrogant and snobby. The whole class is also just buzzwords with no other substance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nothing in the course really fits together; lectures, homeworks, and labs are all only vaguely related. Content could be really interesting but the course goes all over the place without a real sense of direction or any idea concepts relate to one another. Also tedious labs and homeworks as well so start early.

I would have to agree with all of the answers here. While I ended up not enjoying the content of the course as I had hoped, Dr. Calyam is still very enthusiastic about his class and wants his students to do well. The labs and homework are tedious as others have mentioned, but as long as you follow the guides for each assignment you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr Calyam is a real deal His class is very interactive and expects his students to be really involved in the class Too many home works,but they are neatly organized and enough time is given to complete each assignment,and he is easily approachable You can ace midterms and finals if you prepare thoroughly from the course notes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Calyam is overall a great professor. I have never heard someone laugh so much during lecture. He pushes a lot of homework and tedious labs, and the documentation is not the best, but as a professor I cannot say anything bad about him. Good resources and genuinely understanding of conflicts and problems that students encounter. Tough, but good.

He has very high expectations for students. He truly wants his student to be dedicated outside of class to his coursework and learn the material. This is great but it can get very tiresome. First 3 weeks of class and I believe I have spent over 24 hours on a couple of assignments. He is very intelligent and has good lectures, but is he very tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: this class was way too difficult for a gen ed requirement. Shelby was never clear on instructions for our large projects and in class we would do activities that were not much help for our assignments. her explanations for assignments were lengthy and did not make much sense unless you are very knowledgeable about the topic.

This class was way too rigorous for an intro level English 1000 course. She is a tough grader and has very unclear expectations for her papers. The "lectures" are very boring and attendance is mandatory. The majority of my time spent on this class was spent trying to figure out what she wanted me to do. Do not take this class if you want an easy A.

If you are looking to complete your English requirement without fuss, don't choose Shelby. It felt a lot like being in an honors section. She fails to explain projects in great detail & overcomplicates things that don't need to be so confusing. She doesn't give feedback on final drafts and claims C's should be the average. Don't waste your time!

Shelby is the worst teacher I have EVER had. She wastes time by MEDITATING before every class. She grades really harshly, for just a gen ed class. She also NEVER gives feedback on assignments, so you never know what you did wrong. She also NEVER replies to emails. Pls don't take her class if you have a choice, you'll hate it.

Mrs. Preston grades insanely hard for a basic gen ed class. She says it is average to get a C and good to get a B in her class. She got upset at our class for asking questions about what we were doing and is overall not a good teacher. She also responds late or not at all to your emails.

We had to meditate and "ground" ourselves at the beginning of every class. She would keep going until everyone participated, it was a waste of time and VERY annoying. She expects so much out of a gen ed class yet she never replies to emails. The main issue is she NEVER tells us when assignments are due. Please stay away!

No proper student teacher relationship was established and at some times she could be very chill and fun but then her mood will switch on a dime. Little to no feedback was given on essays and if a zoom conference was missed for reasons that weren't the students fault it was automatically a zero on the assignment.

The professor is a very freindly and kind person but there are a lot of flaws in her style. She doesnt respond to emails, she is too friendly with the students and doesn't establish a proper teacher student relationship, and she hasn't been the most organized this year. Overall I would say she isnt a bad teacher but I wouldn't retake her class.

She was not prompt at ALL about responding to emails. She gave me the same grade on every one of my papers with little to no feedback. Some of her grading philosophies were annoying and unbending (ex. Missing a zoom call, because website was crashing and getting half credit after asking to make up for it), etc.

Attendance is not mandatory, but a portion of your grade comes from class participation. I took the Honors section of this class and I felt that it was pretty good. Professor Shelby was always open to feedback and our course work was clearly divided into separate units. 

We had plenty of time to work on our drafts and conduct peer reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit, which was appreciated. She was passionate during class and never made it feel like a 75 minute lecture. I missed a handful of lectures, but never fell behind in my work.

This professor was by far my favorite professor this semester. She didn't respond to emails well but was a very forgiving teacher. Due to COVID we were all online and I only spoke with her twice. She is very lenient on deadlines especially if you ask. She was consistently very nice and respectful to her students. I would recommend her as a prof.

This class was fine but she expected a little too much for a gen ed class. Does not reply to emails in timely manner (or at all sometimes) and doesn't seem to care much about student success. Discussion boards twice a week that could be finished in 5 minutes somedays but a couple hours others.

Great teacher, but the exams are MASSIVE. When you write out all the questions you need to know the answers to for an exam, before you've answered any of them, it's a 12pt, single spaced, 5 page document. They were online this semester so it worked out fine, but he's considering putting them back in person and has mentioned that several times.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Tests are 90% of your grade, with quizzes being 10% the quizzes are easy as long as you take notes and do the readings. I would recommend printing out the notes before going to lecture, that way you just need to write down what he says. 
Rough class, not what I was expecting, but not awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher while the class is lecture heavy there's no other way to teach it and he does a good job of making sure to engage students. There are pop quizzes but they're never really a surprise he always gave the warning to make sure that you do the reading when he assigns them. Overall a good class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really loved this class. Lectures were engaging and coming to class was very important (especially because of pop quizzes). Not a lot of points, but the actual exams (3 total) were all online and open note. Also provides detailed plans concerning exactly what is covered in each lecture, which is available to students at the beginning of semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of information you have to know. Not a lot of points so make sure you show up to class and take the pop quizzes. He does curve test but it is a linear curve. There is a lot of information on slides and he kinda goes fast so I suggest typing out the slides before class and just fill in the blanks in class or print off the slides
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hard content, graded off of quizzes and tests. Not very accessible outside of class. LOTS of pop quizzes.
