reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pete REALLY cares about each and every one of his students. He makes an effort to get to know his students, and he understands that a lot of hist students can be discouraged by the difficulty of the content. He spends so much extra time making examples and helpful packets for students. He checks in often and sends motivational emails. love him!!
10/10 would recommend
He is a wonderful professor who truly cares about his students.
Will not quit until you understand the material.

Pete is the best TA  I could have ever hoped for. His weekly review sessions have helped me go from  being 10 points below the average on the first exam to 20+ points above the average on each exam since. I cannot stress this enough how helpful his review sessions are.

I cannot stress this enough, Pete is INCREDIBLE.  He was my T.A. for Organic Chem 1, and he saved me.  He made sure that he knew me by name, and would give me a little word of encouragement before exams, as well as checking up on me throughout the semester.  Unless the material just comes to you naturally, GO TO HIS STUDY SESSIONS.  He is great!

Pete was just a T.A. for 2030 with my professor being Rainer Glaser. Without Pete I definitely would have failed this class. He has weekly sessions for help and makes his own tutoring sheets. During the sessions he goes over every problem and explains to you exactly what you're doing. A little difficult to understand but definitely helpful.
Awesome teacher, clear and concise.
Personally I found her sort of hard to follow, though she was willing to help more and always help study sessions on her own time.
She's hard to follow sometimes, but very willing to explain things if you get lost. You get 9 free days to miss class before she takes points off.
Professor is a nice guy. Genuinely interested in the subject he is teaching. Class was quizzes based on readings, an in class midterm, and take home final. Would take again

I've had Quirk for a couple classes now. Really nice guy, and knows what he's talking about. Has a genuine interest in the material he teaches. Classes aren't difficult. One of the best in the english department, in my opinion.

He's genuinely mediocre...there's nothing terrible you can say about him, but there's nothing good you can say either. Your experience in the class depends on how interesting you find 19th century lit, not so much on this guy...he's bland in a good-natured way.

I have liked this class so far. I don't think it is terribly hard, can be boring if you aren't interested at the time though. Haven't taken final yet, quizzes are alright if you have read the stuff you were supposed to.

Dr. Podgursky is a funny guy who is knowledgeable about the topic. He can get off track easily and slow down during lectures which was annoying, but you still get in the info you need every day. There's class the day after the exams (which are tricky, go slow). Read the book ahead of class and take good notes. Hard work is key. Study old exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This man is the best thing to happen to economics since tofu.

Podgursky is the best Econ professor I've had at Mizzou. Econ is difficult in general, but Podgursky makes it fun and thoroughly explains material and has helpful homework and practice tests that help prepare you for exams. He also is open to office hours for one on one help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Podgurksy's an interesting professor. His tests are extremely difficult, but please, don't let that discourage you from taking him. As long as you study, attend class and actually care about the class, you'll pass with zero issues. The dude does have an obsession with tofu.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Podgursky is really an awesome professor. He has cheesy economics jokes, which are kind of funny. He makes his lectures interesting and explains concepts thoroughly. Econ 1014 is not an easy course, so attending  lectures and doing the readings are the best way to get a good grade. Exams can be tough, but you do get a one page cheat sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super difficult tests, attendance based on clicker points, however class is curved
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Podgursky is a good lecturer, I would love to hear him lecture on something that I actually like. He talks about tofu in ever example he gives, which can get pretty funny. The tests are super hard, but there is a pretty big curve. DO the reading and homework. And read the book.

Podgursky is a good professor and occasionally funny. His use of real world examples is helpful. However, if you do not read the textbook you will most likely not pass the class. Understanding concepts is key, so if you need to, go get help at the econ help desk.

It's clear that Podgursky knows his stuff, but his lectures can be kind of dull and sometimes confusing. Reading the online text book is very helpful. His tests are extremely difficult, but don't worry because he gives a huge curve on the tests and the class. He makes a ton of references to Tofu.

Dr. Podgursky is a great professor and really wants you to succeed in his class. Make sure to go to every single class and form your own study group!! It helps a lot. Reading the textbook is also a must. His class is tough,  but you learn a lot.
I really enjoyed his class. He loves econ and if you try you can pass.
Podgursky was the man.  I really enjoyed his sense of humor and the effort he put in to the class.

He's an overall good and smart professor but you need to have an excellent handle on the content to be able to apply it to some of the tests. Teaches lectures well and I feel like I understand the content but the tests are just brutal.

He's passionate about his subject and willing to help students, although you need to take initiative and seek him out during office hours. Hits the highlights of his readings in class and is making an effort to be more technologically adept. Tests and papers are no gimmie, but if you do the readings and can write coherently you'll succeed.

It's very important to not miss class.  Being an 8am, I missed a lot and therefore paid for it.  He's tough, but fair.  Everything is straight from the book.  Tests have HUGE curves, so don't freak out when you don't know everything

Podgursky doesn't believe in easy classes, so naturally you can assume how his class is. If you show up to lecture, go to the study sessions, and read the book you will be perfectly fine. I'm only a freshman, but his class has easily been my favorite.
The tests pose a lot of hypothetical scenarios and are hard to pass. The class as well as the tests have a huge curve due to the difficulty of the material.

Michael is a goofball. It is honestly worth showing up just to hear what random things he will spout off. Read the textbook. The textbook is equivalent to the bible in his class. It is more important than showing up to class.

Podgursky is a nice guy, but is awful technologically. He will never update blackboard so you will know what type of grade to expect and don't expect him to get back to you via email. Expect lots of references to tofu and Justin Bieber. He likes making jokes about journalism students so if you're a j-kid and fairly easily offended, steer clear.

This class made me love econ. The tests are completely reasonable and can be aced by rereading the chapters and coming to class and taking good notes! Even if you miss class, all the material is in the book. Great professor. Hard work gets you an A. Great jokes too

When he tells you at the 1st class to read the book, he means it. Do it before class, because that way when he discusses it and does examples, you'll already have an understanding. I was consistently behind in readings & suffered for it. He's a great professor, knows his subject, the tests will be hard! Hardest B, but most satisfying B I've gotten!
Funny guy and a good teacher. Goes on tangents a lot though.
Lecture mostly the same as what's in the textbook, sometimes doesn't know what he's talking about. Tests are fair and overall not a hard class. The final paper is annoying, though.

Best professor I have ever had! I had no interest in Econ, but I took his 5 hour honors class and wow! He is hilarious and teaches concepts in a memorable way. The class is a little difficult, but no more so than regular econ. You can bring up your grade with the final paper, which is nice. TAKE HIS CLASS! You will learn and you will like it!

Econ 1051H was my favorite class last semester. Podgursky's lectures are fairly easy to follow and he answers questions in a helpful way. Plus, he is hilarious. If you do the reading and pay attention, you'll do fine in his class.

Basically: Professor Podgursky is a very knowledgable economist. The course content itself is difficult (hello-learning a new language here) and your grade will reflect how much effort you put into it OUTSIDE of class. Lectures reinforce your learning. This course is what college is all about-he won't spoonfeed you, take responsibility for yourself

I was in the Honors econ 1051 section. Professor Podgusky is very knowledgable and gives interesting lectures...if you listen. Prepare for class by reading text material ahead of time and you will be fine. Tests are difficult, but doable. Stay on top of your work and you will be all right!
Mocks student questions, very sarcastic, does not TEACH concepts well, expects WAY too much on tests, very hard.

Podgursky is not a very good teacher.  He IS a pretty well known economist, but he is just bad at communicating to his students.  I asked a question at the beginning of the year and he physically made me walk up to the front of the room and ask the question to the class in order to make a joke out of me.  Hardly anyone else has asked a question.

VERY sarcastic when answering questions....deters people from speaking freely because they might get grilled for any little question. maybe two people know what is going on at any given point. the foreign TA is a better teacher...out of the entire class, i probably understood 2 concepts that i didn't have to teach myself
Does not explain at all...very hard to follow, knows the subject but not how to teach it
Definitely Reccomend.  Easier than the poor Micro and Macro teachers.  Podg expects a lot and the time of the class is poor but it's an easier A than the other two classes in my op.

I loved this class.  Podgursky is so witty and sarcastic that it's worth it to get up for the 8am class.  It's challenging, but if you study and ask question you can learn an incredible amount.  He also brings up current economic issues, which helps you understand what's going on around you as well.

Podgursky's sarcastic comments toward those who do not want to enter the field of economics are not appreciated.  His tests contain "joke" answers that are designed to make fun of students.  He represents all that is evil and wrong, and I don't think he cares if students learn or not.
The class was hard, but he is a great guy and he's incredibly funny.
He is probably the most absent-minded professor I've ever had and he gives very hard tests.

This is prob the worst professor in the econ dept... and he's the chair!?!  He taught an ENTIRE lecture wrong and at the end of the lecture, he noticed that he was wrong and just said, "Oops, I'll post the right lecture on the website."  WTF
He's funny and a good teacher, but it is a tough class.  I am glad I took it though.
No Comments

I'm just not a big fan of his sarcastic wit, plus he makes hard tests. I wish I hadn't taken his class, and I got an A in it. That should tell you my impression of the man and his teaching style are not favorable.
He's so friggin hard.  He's tests are like impossible.  But then again, the class is designed for Honors students.  It's Econ 4 and 5 together. But it sucks ass!
No Comments
he is literally so sweet and genuinley cares about what he teaches. he always makes sure to ask if anyone has questions and wants us to suceed on the work. just show up and it makes the class easier!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very respectable and knowledgeable professor. The lectures are easy to listen to and as long as you pay attention and take good notes it's a fairly easy class. He is clearly passionate about the content. I would love to take another class from him.
He is a really nice man and his class is pretty easy if you show up and pay attention. He is also available to give you the lecture in his office hours if you miss class for any reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's very passionate about HDFS

I love Marks so much!! If you ever have to take a classics or latin class TAKE HIS. He really understands when students are struggling and will always try to help curve exams and quizzes so the class can do decent. Definitely a lot of memorization for the weekly quizzes and occasional exams, but he is super clear with what you will need to know.
I looooovveeeeeeeeee Ray Ray Marks. So funny and kind. Good at balancing letting you off easy while still teaching you what you need to know. Super chill guy.

Not a hard class, but definitely time consuming (homework each night was translating about 30 lines of Latin to discuss the next class). Dr. Marks was super helpful and very knowledgeable on his subject.

Professor Marks is my professor for Latin1100H and I have really enjoyed his class. He is such a nice guy and very well-versed in the subject. The language is hard, but the activities we do in class help me to understand it better. I would highly recommend Professor Marks as a professor and am sad I won't have him for Latin1200H next semester.

Took this class to fulfill my gen ed requirements. Early in the semester I attended every lecture, but the slides were really boring as someone who isn't that interested in history so I started to skip class. As long as you know everything on the study sheet he posts you could get an A without ever going to class. He dropped my lowest exam score.

Class is very lecture-based, if you miss a lecture you'll have to go to office hours to catch up. Your entire grade is made up of 3 big tests which are all multiple choice. Overall I think you get out what you put into this class. Lots of names and dates to remember. If you're a bad test-taker I don't recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Engaging teacher, sometimes likes to make off-color jokes. Attentive to detail and very knowledgeable about his subject. Be prepared to answer grammar questions in class and for tests. Attending class/doing the reading is necessary. Somewhat of a harsh grader but very willing to help you if you need it. Definitely visit him during office hours!
Awesome!

This is a very interesting class! Roman Culture and Mythology are must have classes at Mizzou. Dr. Marks makes the class very interesting and he's very amusing. Always available for a chat. Passionate about what he does. =]
Roman Culture: interesting material, but tests are difficult.  Memorize all the details and don't mix anything up.  Great class, but very difficult, should be a 4000 class instead of a 2000 level.

Age of Augustus - The class was fairly easy.  I only read the first 2 books of the Aeneid the whole semester and I ended up getting a B+ in the class.  He goes over everything you need to know during lecture.  You know exactly what's going to be on the tests, so there's no surprises.
Marks is an amusing teacher, and very willing to help.  The only reason to not get an A is difficuly of the language or lack of memorization.
Very engaging and cares about her students. Assignments are strait forward and not too difficult. If you show up and pay attention it should be an easy A.

Dr. Ramirez is soooo great! lectures are never boring and she really goes in detail on every subject.She has great real world examples. Material is easy to learn quiz are also easy. For my class we had to make videos to show our understanding and they where really fun to make and she gives great feedback. She does do random attendance.She is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Ramirez is great! She's very understanding and funny. She does randomized attendance and most of her lectures are interesting. Her quizzes are easy and the material is very easy to follow. There are a few in-class activities that are in groups but they are all relaxed. Students will conduct an interview which is the main part of your grade.

Reggie is honestly the goat. This is a very tough class, and since he has been teaching for so long, he understands this very fact. There are 3 exams, all 2 hours, and very difficult. The homework requires a lot of thinking and time each week. In this class, you will find many people starting to discover if this major is what they really want.

Reg is a great professor.  You can tell he loves what he does because of how well he teaches the subject.  Mass and Energy Balance can either be a fun class or a hard class based on what professor you have.  As long as you show up to every single class and pay attention to what Reggie says, then he will make this class fun and worth your time.

Diffidently some tough love, but only because he wants you to grow and build skills that are useful outside this class. If you're having any sort of trouble school, personal, otherwise he wants to help. Just be willing to go see him talk. Work hard, make sure you understand material, practice and you'll be fine.

There's five exams and they are weighted 80% of grade. 4-5 questions on each exam and they are hard. No shortcuts in this class even on homework bc its all about understanding material and processes. I had to retake it twice and dropped it both times. Nice and understandin guy. He says use your intution but it's a beginer class? Too much pressure

Takes pride in a low grade.  Almost treats the class like it's his entertainment and doesn't seem to remember that his student's education is more important than trying to entertain yourself. Loves to be open ended with his explanations rather than go in depth about a topic because that's more mysterious. very corny so beware. adds layer of stress
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super sexist. If you're a girl in his class good luck. All these other ratings are probably written by men. He gives all the boys in his classes his phone number.

He's a bit intimidating at first, but he's honestly a really good professor. When going over problems, he breaks them down in a way that makes them very easy to understand. The tests are quite difficult and can make or break your grade, so make sure to study hard and prepare well for them. Try not to miss lectures either.

Reg is a great teacher and a caring individual. He wants his students to do well, but he wants them to put in the work to earn it. I've learned a lot in his class, but I've also cried a lot over this class. It's very tough, but he is there to answer any questions whenever you need. Be prepared to be pushed to your limit!

Reg is really good at what he does and is one of the best professors I have had. He is always willing to help and  wants his students to succeed. This class isn't easy, but if you put in the work you will learn a lot and enjoy it despite maybe struggling a bit more than other intro chemE classes.

This is probably my best experience with a class and professor so far in college. Reg truly cares about each and every one of his students. He wants you not only to learn the material, but understand it and be able to apply it in a group setting. Work hard in this class and you will grow immensely as a ChemE.

Reg is one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He will push you to the very limit, his class made me want to cry at times, but I learned a lot and Reg was very approachable when I had questions. When COVID-19 forced us all to go home, Reg was my only professor who went above and beyond to make sure we all did well and continued learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Reggie is an all around great professor, who cares about his students. He is available for help outside of class and gives good feedback when you go into office hours. His lectures include lots of group work in addition to discussions of real world scenarios. He gives plenty of time for exams, and his exams always have an fun theme to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The class is easy yes but it can get bery boring quickly. I think Dr. Rivera has her moments and can be nice but other times she can be passive. She is particular about everything. There is a ton of extra credit so the intense grading can be over looked. Also dont walk into the wrong door on the first day of class, you wont hear the end of it.

The 5/5 difficulties and 1/5 quality ratings on this page are from people who clearly didn't try/show up for this class. Dr. Rivera offers an ABSORBINANT amount of extra credit (+- 70pts). You can comfortably get Bs on all exams and still get an A plus. Take advantage of extra credit, GO TO LECTURE and STUDY and this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading is extremely frustrating and overly strict, often resulting in poor grades. Additionally, the evaluations are highly inconsistent, and the explanations are vague and difficult to understand. She heavily relies on guest speakers to do her work for her. An elective class should not be taught by her.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. The professor doesn't teach the class and her exams are all gotcha questions. There's an insane amount of info given in this class and any of it could appear on your test. There is no textbook and no study guides so good luck figuring out how she wants you to study. Your only resource are your own notes.

Bunch of extra cred is offered and material is super easy. Prof is very difficult, doesn't teach her own class -gets other people to speak. When she does lecture, she's fast and hard to understand. Said course is "designed for her" and that's clear. It's repetitive and she's horrible giving feedback on assignments she took points off for no reason.

She is absolutely terrible at giving feedback. It seems more like she's not comfortable giving out good grades so she takes off points that are not justified. She is never willing to help and does not even give lectures herself, and thank goodness! Because she's also a terrible speaker. She goes too fast and blames it on your notetaking abilities.

One of the worst professors at Mizzou, and that's saying a lot. Exams are all gotcha questions, grading system is broken, and the information expected of students is totally unclear. Other people teach the class for her, she just sits in the back and watches. Students are blamed for having difficulties in the class. Super paranoid about cheating.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. Quizzes at the beginning of every class made it so that in-person attendance was mandatory... during a pandemic. During exams, she made students leave their bags outside the room. Her grading rubric on the syllabus makes sense until you turn your assignment in and she docks you points for absolutely nothing. So awful

Dr. Rivera is sweet and funny. Class is mostly guest lecturers, most of which are pretty interesting. Often bring in animals! Have to come to class and take good notes to do well on exams, but it's a VERY easy A (or A+). Crap ton of extra credit available. Cool service site choices if you take the Service-Learning section.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing professor for Operating Systems. Very engaging lectures and connects class topics to stories from his experience. Assignments can be tough though, but he provides tests that show exactly what your grade would be, so as long as you start early its hard to not get an A.

Awesome as a person but bad professor. Sometimes would not post the prelabs until the day before the lab. When asked about practices exam he would say that he doesn't have any since he hasn't been teaching the class for too long, but he wrote all the exams from scratch. This is not a proper excuse.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's the reason why I'm changing majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor

He's one of the funniest and most engaging teachers I've ever had. He knows how to get students engaged and gives a lot of examples to really get you to understand. The labs start getting a bit hard but not really as long as you do pre labs

This was my second go around at 1050 and to say the course was WORSE my second time around is an understatement. Ries is an ok professor and the lectures are helpful but the class is very test-heavy. There's 3 tests and 12 labs. Grades really hard on labs and tests make up a majority of your grade. Study the ins and outs of C to pass.

tests were extremely difficult and was truthfully a luck based game. There was never a clear cut answer and you left the test session not having any idea what you got on the test. You almost have to be an expert at C to get some of his questions correct because some of them entailed 'What error will this show' on a piece of code NO ONE would write.

Professor Ries ("JimR") is a solid professor for CMP_SC 1050. His lectures are clear and focused making learning much easier. If you like dad jokes or the St. Louis Cardinals, you will like JimR. The course itself on the other hand is a different story. Tests make up the vast majority of your grade, if you do not test well, you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved professor Rice, she was understanding and kind. I did notice that the students who talked during lecture or didn't do the readings tended to complain about her as a professor because she requested the same respect she gave. she offers redo's on her essays. Follow the instructions, write like a college student and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor was amazing at giving feedback and always making time for meetings when they were needed. However, this was not an easy course. She definitely makes you work for your grade and it is a very heavy reading course. 99% of this class was probably spent reading and the readings are quite confusing. However, the professor did a good job.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: There are lectures every class, but honestly reading the textbook was sufficient for learning the material that would be in the weekly quizzes and even the midterm. The "essay deconstructions" were a little work because of the very broad prompts, but she was very fair with grading, gave good feedback, and was always willing to help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. C gets a bad rep, however, her class is easy to pass. She has numerous homework assignments, in-class worksheets, attendance papers, and quarterly projects that everyone gets 100% on because she doesn't actually read them. The exams are the hard part; they don't quite correlate to what is on the lectures and study guides, but overall super easy

Dr. C gets such a bad rap, but she is truly a great professor. Her class is hard, yes, but welcome to being a biochem major... If you are organized this class really doesn't require more than 3-4 hours outside of class each week. The skills learned in this class are necessary for any research/lab work. Dr. C wants to see her students succeed.

Dr. C is an amazing professor that really cares and tries to relate the material to the real world. The midterm and final were somewhat hard, but she gives out enough extra credit so it doesn't matter. She gives out a lot of practice and teacher material that is relevant and important in the real world.

This was a great introduction into the world of biochem labs. Lots of extra credit at the beginning which helps a lot if properly taken advantage of. Dr. C speeds through her lecture slides; however, most of the material isn't on the final, and she posts slides online. Go to PLAs with lab questions since her office hours are "by appointment only".

She has the expectation that freshman will be able to perform an experiment at the level of a tenured professor on the first try. Just was very negative and would constantly talk down to us. Gives extra credit at the beginning to justify being such a picky grader.

Dr. C is a somewhat ok teacher. However, her labs are never straightforward, and you will constantly be asking the PLAs questions due to everything being extremely unclear. The amount of work is ridiculous. If you are an organized person, prepare to be angry. Her entire course is unorganized and makes you want to crawl into a hole.

SO MUCH HOMEWORK!!! her homework will take you hours and the PLAs will grade toughly! Her tests are ridiculously short for the amount of work she expects you to do and then blames it on your time management. She a great lady but I would not take one of her classes again.

This class is an easy A, but I feel like I learned nothing. Dr. Chaudhary is not available outside class or by email. The PLAs make or break the class. The lectures are confusing. The assignments take forever but teach you nothing. Having taken the biochem class that comes after Dr. C's, I can say that this class does not prepare you for it.

She gives a LOT of extra credit, so as long as you do the extra credit & spend a little effort on the labs, you can bomb the midterm & final and still get an A. Doesn't respond to emails for weeks. Terrible at explaining things clearly, worksheets & labs are super confusing. Prepare to spend HOURS on the homework. The class sucks, but its an easy A

He's a great professor, and his lectures are genuinely interesting. However, do not take any of his courses if you'd freak out when your GPA inevitably drops because you get an A-. Because you will get an A-. He also gives no feedback on anything you submit, so you'll never know why you keep getting a 9/10 instead of 10/10.
My absolute goat, taken his classes like 4 times and signed up for another next semester.

This class was more writing than I had anticipated. I wouldn't say too much work, but more than I expected for an elective. The grading felt random and strict. He never gives 100% and doesn't give any feedback. Ramsay is a good professor who cares about his students and class discussions were fun but I had to work for an A- which will drop my GPA.

1. I have taken him for 2 semesters and have never received a 10/10 on an assignment, not a super hard grader but will almost never give a perfect score
2. Often cancelled class, or during class we did something chill like watch X files or have discussions, never work in class
3. Great movie choices, smart, funny, great teacher. I would recommend.

He rocks!! My class was fully online and he was still great about reaching out and making it as enjoyable as possible. I definitely recommend taking him in-person if you can though, just because he's cool. The class was also pretty simple, with the only assignments being weekly discussions, weekly film summaries, and two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Even if you aren't into film, you will enjoy his class. Ramsay cares about his students and chooses movies that he thinks they will like. The honors course is not much harder than the regular one. The classes are for discussions, not doing work. All assigned work is to be completed outside of class. I plan to take more of Ramsay's classes.

Professor Wise is definitely the best professor I've had here. He made every class super enjoyable and it was actually a very fun environment. He's very passionate and knowledgeable about the movies we talk about. The homework, papers, and exams aren't difficult, either. Would definitely recommend to anyone looking for an easy/enjoyable course.

Ramsay Wise is awesome. I took his honors film course and had a lot of fun with it. We had to do some questions and a small writing prompt (250 words) due every week so the work was extremely manageable. He's a bit of a goofy guy, but it's because he enjoys teaching this course so much and he just has fun with it. HIGHLY recommend!

One thing I really admired about him was how much he loves what he teaches. He was always so excited to talk about the film of the week and didn't mind at all if a topic got switched and went down a completely different road. His criteria was so interesting and he really inspired me this year to do what I love.

Unless you like to write do not take this class. Every movie is old, hard to find, boring, and requires a 3 - 4 page paper, plus there is a 10 page paper at the very end of the course. Find another gen ed because you will need a lot of time and effort to finish this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Despite never meeting him (quarantine class), his grading criteria was 100% clear. It required lots of reading and discussion posts and 2 big essays, but it's doable. And if you love film there's nothing better than the Major Directors class. TBH not super involved since there's no lectures, but good class, could recommend as a high level one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wise is a great professor, he knows a lot about film and loves what he teaches about. I would definitely recommend!

Prof. Wise's Film 1000 class online is a really cool experience. It was a great opportunity for me to learn more about the film, and having it online taught me to be more productive with my time. Ramsay is an awesome online instructor :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great teacher. If hes available, take him. Maybe not an "Easy A" but very engaging and strives to see students improve. He likes to focus his classes on fun, less serious material, which is great for engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the coolest film teachers I've ever had. He definitely knows his stuff, especially pop culture references. His class is extremely laid back, and the in class conversations were so much fun!

He is amazing! He makes everything fun in class when you have class. He understands that as students your time is valuable so if you are able to do something on your own time he cancels class or lets his students leave early. He is always available through email or after class and is so helpful! If you can't make it to class let him know no biggy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DO NOT PROCRASTINATE! Each lesson has a hefty paper analysis. I managed to forgo watching the movies and wrote my papers based on IMDB analysis, trailers and his long synopses. He tends to grade each paper in the same range. I'm convinced he skims. Remember, no more than 3 assignments can be submitted in a 7 day period-don't let this screw you over

The man is a legend. Prof. Wise will easily go down as one of my favorites. Not only was his class completely engaging, but it was also fun and enlightening. I would definitely recommend him if you are looking for an organic, conversation-based class with a great film selection. Lots of quizzes and a few writing assignment, but it's all cake.

Each lesson you had to write 3-4 page papers, but the course is not listed as a writing intensive. The movies he chose for the lessons were very old and hard to find. The lessons weren't very clear on what to do and were sometimes repetitive. Would not recommend this course or professor!
If you see him in the list of teachers please take him. You will have an amazing experience in English. I do not like English and he made it interesting.

I look forward to this class every time. Dr. Wise is laid back but knows his film. I swear, you could make any reference and he would know exactly what you were talking about. You will learn a lot and enjoy his sense of humor!

I'm taking his trends in world cinema class, which  I thought could end up being dull. However Ramsay is very passionate about film which makes lectures more interesting. It doesn't hurt that he's pretty laid back and hilarious. He always has the class cracking up.  There's a lot of reading but it is manageable. I hope to take another class of his.

I took an online film class taught by Prof. Ramsay. He was a fair grader and extremely quick in returning papers (sometime's I'd get my grade back within a couple of hours). I would definitely recommend him if you have the chance to take his class.

Literally the best, coolest professor I've had all throughout college. He's hilarious, does South Park impressions, and is super passionate about film. He seriously knows his stuff and he encourages creativity. In short? He's really awesome.
Best teacher I ever had
He loves what he does and it shows. Just make sure that you go to the showings and engage in classes and you will do well. It doesn't hurt that he's good to look at.

I took his film class. From a student's perspective it's a great class because there's barely any material. Wise doesn't have much material to teach and it shows - so he calls off class a lot, and the classes he doesn't call off, he shows video clips just to fill the time.  All he needs is a 20 minute class period in addition to the screening.

Ramsay is a very laid-back and nice professor. He's one of the best professors I've ever had at Mizzou.  His class and tests are easy.  He is also very funny at times and facilitates discussion in the class very well.  His teaching style makes students interested in the material.
excellent discussion leader, easy going, and lets students speak freely.  I would put money on every one of his classes being informative and interesting.

He is such a nice guy and really cares about the subject and his students. Keep in mind that just because you are in a film class doesn't mean that you are not going to have to do any work--keep up with the reading and do research on your own time. A class with Ramsay is definitely worth taking.
I liked his class a lot.
I loved Ramsay. He was funny yet informative. I learned a lot and really enjoyed the class.
I really enjoyed his Hitchcock class. I've had Ramsay for two semesters now--he's very enjoyable and laid-back. He loves the subject and it shows.
No Comments
No Comments

I had no idea what t expect going into this but I liked the class.  Maybe back when it was 91, orwhatever, but I thought Mr. Wise did a good job of discussing the material.  It made sense when he went over it.  I thought the class was pretty good.  I learned a lot.
I don't disagree with his politics, but his rants had nothing to do with the class, and should be directed elsewhere. It's not professional.
it was a lot of fun and the books he picked were excellent.  So what if he takes a political stance.  At least he stands for something.  Bob Marley
This was an enjoyable class and he was very interesting. The main advice is to read the books according to the schedule because the quizzes are the main part of your grade. Overall nice and fun guy.

I'm confused by the negative political comments.  I'm  a conservative future teacher who, in my student teaching at least, has found that taking argumentative and contrary positions is one of the best ways to stimulate actual thought about issues - not just knee-jerk, party line crap.  GREAT CLASS!
Just another socialist blowhard who likes to shoot his mouth off.
Enjoyable.
A fun TA. Is really laid back and lets you talk about the films freely.
He is a good T.A. He likes to have fun with his class and helps the students if they need it. All around good class and T.A.

All the films were political, it's unavoidable!  I never got the impression that Mr. Wise wanted us to believe any certain thing.  I didn't always agree with him, but he never seemed confrontational or anything.  I liked the class.
Opinionated, but well informed.  I like that he gets involved in the films and is willing to be personal.  Talks a lot, but then again, the class wouldn't talk much.  I enjoyed the class.

Does not create a positive learning environment for students. He makes it clear that he dislikes Republicans and America by making contemptuous comments, and seems to have dropped hints he is a Communist/Marxist. Unfair and left-wing biased, terrible T.A.
No Comments
Very nice and really funny. I thought he was really hot too but he has a girlfriend ;)
No Comments

This class is just a difficult class for some people to understand. Don't be concerned about the past reviews from when he first started teaching. He has gotten much better and listened to his students on what to improve. The exams are not doing to be super similar to the practice exams, you do have to understand the material (do the HW/discussion)

Professor Roland is a very kind and intelligent instructor! You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches, which honestly helps a lot. ASTRON1010 was a fairly easy class with pretty simple labs. Overall, he's a very organized and helpful professor, even if his lectures are a little boring at times.

Prof Roland is a fun, helpful, and intelligent guy, but lectures could be convoluted with difficult proofs. 5 relatively easy exams throughout the semester, no final, and plenty of help between office hours, Tiger Tutors, and TAs. Posts notes online, extensive formula sheet for each exam, and gives two nearly identical practice exams for each exam
he is amazing.

I ended the semester with an 89.45 and he wouldn't round my grade up .05 percent to give me an A. His lectures are boring and he talks way too much about the proofs and meanings behind the concepts rather than how to solve problems. It sucks because you can tell he's a really nice person and is really interested in physics but this class is no fun.

prof is genuinely super kind and always willing to help during office hours. my only gripe would be that the lectures are very proof heavy and not super helpful for applying to problems/studying. genuinely go to his office hours if you are struggling, because he is seriously super knowledgeable and kind. focus on prac exams/discussion for studying

Lectures are fine, just a lot of unnecessary proofs for equations. Best part about the class is the practice exams, they are very similar to tests making it easy to study. Homework and discussions are not very similar to tests, so just be familiar with the concepts. Prof Roland attended honors discussion and lab which was helpful.

Heavily recommend his teaching style. As for class difficulty, there were 5 curved exams + provided cheat sheet for each + no final, each exam having 2 practice tests pretty much identical to the actual exam. TA/prof office hours open every weekday. Slides and expectations were so clear, don't even need to go to lecture.

I don't understand the hate. This class was perfectly fine, 5 exams makes it easy to mess up and still be okay. Practice exams matched real exams just fine, lectures were solid and helped. Full notes on Canvas. Must be a giant improvement from last semester, test averages hovered in the 80s this semester, heard they were much much lower before.

i took this class in fall' 24, so it might be different now, but my experience was not good. so much homework and lecture notes that barely correlated with the tests. I eventually gave up sutdying for this course realizing it was a waste of time, and i got the same results on exam 4 and 5 as i did on 1(curved) 2 and 3 which I studied for

Compared to what I heard about his first semester, he did better in Spring 25. Practice exams are similar to the tests, but make sure to look over the lecture slides and review slides too. His lectures are full of proofs and unnecessary content, so you get little information about what to actually learn for the exams. Ask TAs for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Roland is a nice guy but his class was not run well. Examples he did in lecture were extremely basic compared to what showed up on exams, making it nearly impossible to study effectively. The exams were graded harshly with absolutely no rubric and he refused to curve them, only curving the first one after many students complained about the 40% avg
Have you ever played a game where you knew you would lose no matter how much you prepared? That's what taking his tests feel like.

Physics 2 is such an interesting field of study but this guy made me hate it. He zooms through the lectures (which have unnecessary content), and he makes you do homework and labs that don't prepare you for the test. His tests are extremely confusing. When the entire class failed the first exams, he didn't even care and acted like it was normal.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was awful. The professor failed to teach us the necessary material needed for the exams, homework, and labs. Exams were a joke in that there was no way to prepare. Even if you do the exam practice and review homework problems, it does not help. Our first exam average was a 41%. And he was not going to curve. This was a reoccurring theme.

As this was his first Mizzou semester, I'll give him some grace. As the semester went on, he definitely made some helpful adjustments. He did come to the honors discussion and lab section every week which was awesome! The lectures lacked practice problems which made test prep more difficult.

As it was his first Mizzou semester, I'll give him some grace. He is helpful in office hours and came to the honors discussion and lab section every week which was definitely a plus! However, the lectures lacked practice problems which made it more difficult to prepare for tests. Things did get better as the semester progressed.

Professor was really nice but since it was his first year of teaching he didn't really know how to teach the content. Exams didn't match the exam reviews until later on. Test averages continuously dropped with no curve. Recommend people to take this course over the summer!!
he was nice guy but does not know how to teach well. lectures had no practice problems and you're better off just reading the text book. his test averages went down with each exam we took.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was completely fine. The lectures could've had more practice problems and the discussions need to be revamped to match this new professors style (they are old discussion problem sets from the former 2760 prof). The exams were medium difficulty and you always will have enough time to finish them since they are not very long problems.

He's a very nice guy, but nothing he gives you prepares you for your exams which take up most of your grade. I've spent hours going through the material in the lectures only to take tests and find most of the content foreign. A lot of the homework is time consuming and pretty foreign to the test content.Lectures dont teach you to solve the problems

Friendly guy however...was better to go online and find the content than to try to decipher what was important through the lectures. Lectures had next to no good practice problems. Exams were okay-some problems were much different than what was practiced in discussion. Most exams to WEEKS to grade.

It was easy to get a high grade with an extensive curve applied to each exam, extra credit opportunities for each lecture attended, and extra credit for giving a five minute presentation to the class, but I didn't learn anything. The lectures were messy and frustrating. She didn't give any indication that she knew the content she was presenting.

Tests are all multiple choice which may sound easy but they are not, every single answer sounds right. Quizzes in recitation (not open note). Calls on u randomly in lecture. Forced to do 1 group presentation, attendance is mandatory through iclicker.

Go to class to get extra credit; it is worth it. Dr. Angelovici was kind, but it wasn't easy to communicate with her. Tests could be difficult but manageable. The lectures were hard to follow, so re-visit the slides after class. If you study and go to class, you should perform well. I am not quite sure how much I actually learned, however.

She's kind and tries her best, but an awful professor. Speeds through lectures and refuses to post lecture slides. I genuinely don't think she knows a word that comes out of her mouth. There are extra credit opportunities and tests are easy but if you are looking to actually learn cell biology, DON'T TAKE.

She made it impossible to take any kind of notes in class, written or typed, and went way too fast. like not the amount of content was fine but you could not learn anything in class because there was no time to take the notes needed. Also made every person in class do an in-class presentation over the semester.

Most lecture slides came straight from the textbook, and often the test material did come from the slides. Some lectures were fast, though, that is the nature of upper-level biology courses. The class will not be difficult if you put in a reasonable amount of work, I did not do any crazy studying and was successful.

Probably the worst professor I've had. Lectures are rushed and don't make a lot of sense. Exams had lots of typos and sometimes there were questions on random things we didn't cover. Extremely disorganized. Assigned us 3 units to do on our own. Got a good grade because she adds lots of extra credit in the end, but I don't feel like I learned much.

This was probably one of the worst teachers I have ever had in my academic career. I would not at all recommend taking her class. She is horribly disorganized and really has no idea what she is talking about. Her slides are copied from the textbook and some of them just have word vomit all over them and she spends like two seconds on the slide.

She seems like a nice person, but the organization of this class is so frustrating. Does not post slides before class, flies through them, and talks fast/all over the place so it is difficult to take notes and follow along. The tests are doable but you will be teaching yourself the content most of the time. I would avoid taking courses with her.

I would not recommend. Her teaching style is a little all over the place, which makes the information dense lectures difficult. The grading/syllabus for the course has been changed multiple times already as of early November. The tests are doable if you study, but the multiple spelling errors and straight up informational errors are frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a bad person wants people to succeed but. Test haves spelling errors and multiple choice answers not in ABC order. Talks fast during lecture write quick. Not many grade in grade book test and quizzes Changed grading scheme three times and we are halfway into semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: shes nice & helpful, dates & questions are kind of inconsistent, lectures have tons of info & take a while to get through, weekly quizzes not too bad, quizzes during discussion are harder-write down what TA says beforehand, extra credit for attending discussion, tests are hard & specific-doable if you study & summarize info, everything's open note
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was very boring, but she offered extra credit clicker questions that brought my grade up a whole letter grade. She did not give a clear idea of what would be on the tests, but did give (unhelpful) practice exams a week before the test. The tests had too many spelling/grammar errors, which made them even more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I said attendance is non-mandatory, but there is extra credit for you if you go. Her tests are fairly straightforward from her lecture slides and the book, which is far better from the other cell biology teachers from what I've heard.

This was Angelovici's first semester teaching this class. Unfortunately, she does not communicate what is really necessary for the exams. She uses slides directly from Pearson (the book company) which have far too much information. Tests are not terrible, but her expectations are very unclear.

Professor Smale is charismatic and kind. In Colonial Latin America you would never expect to have so much fun. His eccentric teaching style is all tangents and fun facts; its super engaging. His assessment style matches this perfectly as he only asks you to write what you know. I recommend this class to everyone especially aspiring educators.

I took Social Revolutions in Latin America, and it became one of those classes I was genuinely excited to attend because the lectures were so fascinating! Professor Smale brought this vital history to life with the stories he told, the readings he assigned, and the questions he encouraged. If you pay attention and do the readings, you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A gem of a man, but loves his tangents and goes over time more often than not.

This class is a great history elective that has interesting topics while being fairly easy. The only things really graded is attendance, short reading quizzes, and short comments. The lectures are definitely all over the place, but he is a super funny guy. Only complaint is that if you took his colonial class, its super repetitive for first 5 weeks

Definitely one of my favorite professors this semester! He shows his passion for history through his lectures and it really makes you want to learn. His PowerPoints are mainly just pictures emphasizing what he will talk about, however, he is not hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Smale is so awesome. He gives energetic lectures that are seemingly scattered-brained, but absolutely educational. All you have to do is provide strong short comments every week and take easy quizzes... if you read/ skim the texts. I did not read everything but definitely read my fair share. Take Smale!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Smale is a very interesting and funny person. His lectures, all though required, are interesting to listen to. Beware, he does not have bullet points for you to copy and he definitely is all over the place, but he means well. The class is super easy, normally a reading quiz that you do online and a short comment. Plus, he gives feedback

He is very nice and caring when it comes to his student and is always wiling to meet to discuss grades, assignments, etc. However, he does get distracted very easily and sometimes takes up the whole class time discussing something that is not on the syllabus. Be prepared to be all over the place, however it will be rewarded with a good grade.
He is an amazing professor and clearly loves his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The assignments all have a heavy percentage behind them and most follow the same guidelines. This makes it easy to improve and maintain a good grade with this professor. The professor is also really easy going.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: WORTH walking across campus to attend his lecture. Smale not only teaches in a clear and diverse way; he also makes sure students are active and keeps material interesting. A TON of reading, three textbook and endless article and online support; HOWEVER, the topics are interesting and the reading are relevant. ONLY down side is he HATES canvas.

Dr. Smale is one of the best professors I've had at Mizzou. He's absolutely hilarious and if you put in an honest effort he will always help you out. He does do pop quizzes for attendance, but as long as you do the reading and show up you'll do well. There's weekly readings but nothing too bad. Take his class!
Professor Smale is an amazing professor. Extremely passionate about his courses and student ideas.  He really cares for his students success and well being

As a history major, I was already looking forward to this class. Professor Smale was an AWESOME teacher who explained history in a fun and contemporary way that anyone would enjoy. 50% of your grade is short essays you turn in about every week and it's easy to get almost all the points. Also- no midterm and the final was NOT cumulative!

Dr. Smale is a wonderful professor. His lectures were interesting and thought provoking and he was very knowledgeable. The organization of the class was different than most classes as all assignments were written comments on assigned readings. Only drawback is that he does not post any grades on blackboard or even use blackboard very much.

Probably one of the best speakers I have ever had in a professor.  His lectures were not only thought provoking but, entertaining. Also, although he does not take attendance, all the information on the exams is presented at the lecture therefore, you have to come to class to pass.

Smale makes you want to go to class, that's how interesting he makes his lectures. If you do your assignments and show up, you should do well. I seriously considered becoming a history major because of him. He knows so much about what he's teaching, ask him any questions and he'll tell you all he knows.
He was awesome!
Smale was a fantastic professor, and is a relatively easy grader. He's also funny and very enthusiastic. I highly recommend him to any History major needing the credit.

A great teacher. Phenomenal at turning seemingly boring lectures into intriguing historical stories. The second lecture on Cortes' conquest of Mexico was the only time I've ever seen college students show up early to make sure they got a good seat to the lecture.

Prof Smale was really great. He made a topic that might have initially seemed very boring (Colonial Latin America) very interesting through his storytelling ability (much of the history is in story-form, like Cortez and the 'Aztecs'). Smale is not only incredibly kind but is also one of  the funniest people Ive ever been taught by. HIGHLY recomend.

To be honest, I'm a history major and this class still scared me to take... I mean... Colonial Latin America?? Turns out it's the best class I have this semster. You HAVE to go to class if you want an A or a B, but it's totally fine because the lectures are actually a lot of fun! He's a very funny man and I'll be taking more of his classes!

I had to take History of Latin America for my gen eds and was NOT looking foward to it. Smale's enthusiasm, humor and reasonable expectations made the class one of my favorites this semester. Not hard at all if you put forth a little effort.

I took 2 classes w/ Smale- Social Revolutions in Latin America, and Colonial Latin America. I loved that he was always so enthusiastic about everything he taught; he kept the class interesting. By no means is he an easy teacher - quite the contrary - but any class taught by him is well worth taking. He's cool and he really knows his stuff.
Dr. Smale is easy to get along with and provides extra help if you need it.

GRAD STDUENTS: Not as bad as her undergrad. Her feedback sometimes reads like a dissertation. You'll still write & read a ton. Meet deadlines & be detailed. She says she wants short, precise work, but really, she wants everything covered or you'll lose points. Reach out if you need to. Her assignment instructions can be confusing so reread often.

This is the worst professor to ever step foot in a classroom. She was removed from the Capstone professors as she finds pleasure in failing students. She lives a sad life and feels the need to project her pain onto her class.

This professor genuinely thinks she is the smartest person in the world. Her teaching method is horrible and I have learned absolutely nothing. I highly recommend taking any professor but her. She should not be a teacher anywhere
Buy the book and save money, be smart. The class consists of PowerPoints summarizing the book.
It's okay
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The coursework is completely grade based and the online material is full of errors.
Tough class, labs were ok but the quizzes were very difficult.

He is kinda confusing and his tests are hard. He is a good teacher if you pay attention but people sit on their laptops. I think he thought we had all taken Calc 2 (didn't matter- cheated on everything). he's really nice personally & really funny. I just can't take this slander, the class is just set up badly! Please he's cool & cares!

Very smart, guy. Bed teacher. You'd have more fun dingdong ditching his house, than taking this class... so do yourself the favor and don't take it. Take a higher level econ class with Tabitha or someone else, this class isn't worth it.

Awful, awful, awful.  If I could've given 0s I would've.  Save yourself and do not take a course with this man.  He is very knowledgeable in economics, but couldn't teach if his entire life depended upon it.  I would rather slide down a razorblade into a pool of alcohol than take another one of Rudy's classes.

It was a rough course for me because out of the first 3 classes, he cancelled 2 and showed up 10 minutes late to the other. By the time 3 classes had gone by, it was too late to change courses. I did not like him as a speaker and felt his Powerpoint lectures were too long and uninteresting to understand. He was as unorganized as one could be.

Professor always cancelled class for various reasons and never showed up to lecture. Not responsive to emails. Exams are quite difficult but often curved 20%. Did not grade assignments until the end of the semester. Take another professor.

Definitely one of my favorite Professors I've had in college. I would definitely take more classes with Dr. Chacon. The material is hard but he teaches it well. He does go a bit fast in class. I think recording in-class lectures could help students look back. I get not wanting to post those sessions because students will skip class.
Professor Chacon is great. He is organized and regularly communicates with students through email and announcements. The exams are a little difficult, but he provides extra credit as well.

Professor is straight forward. Grading is straight forward. Easy class overall. Attend class for free test questions (typically gives you info that you specifically need to know and market updates). Extra Credit is a game changer. Tests are multiple choice. Calculations are simple. Only draw is his class is at 8am. Go to class, get easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great teacher... Made a lot of good analogies and broke things down in a way that was easy to understand... and cute :)
Great professor, learned a lot in his class, really seems to care about the students

I honestly can't say enough good things about Dr. Thomas. His class was inspirational and challenged me to think about journalism in new ways, but the biggest impression he left was due to his kindness and easygoing teaching style that made class fun to come to. One of my best class experiences at Mizzou.

Professor Thomas is great and has a cool accent. His lectures are interesting and he involves the class in the discussion so it's never just him reading off a PowerPoint while students take notes. His class is fairly simple to get an A in, there's always the same homework every week and nothing special is thrown at you. Lots of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Thomas gives good lectures that are easy to follow. Every week there are three assignments due but they are easy, especially if you go to class. Your lowest exam and assignments are dropped. He wants students to learn and also succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a large lecture hall but he makes it a great class. Plus, his Welsh accent makes it easier to listen to lectures. There aren't a lot of assignments (short quiz, discussion board, and simple learning audit each week, which in total takes about an hour). The textbook is required but TBH you can get by without it, I never used it. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There are lots of great professors in the j-school but Ryan deserves credit for being the nicest. He is funny, positive and laid back, and just comes across as a really good dude.

He is a really good lecturer. The smallest parts of info will show up on tests, take good notes. If you do, then the tests are okay. Make sure to take your time because they make up all of your grade. He drops the lowest score (out of 4 tests) which is nice, but don't rely on it. Get ready to spend time on the videos. You have to be self motivated!

He is a really good lecturer. The smallest parts of info will show up on tests, take good notes. If you do, then the tests are okay. Make sure to take your time because they make up all of your grade. He drops the lowest score (out of 4 tests) which is nice, but don't rely on it. Get ready to spend time on the videos. You must be self motivated!

Thomas is a great teacher. This class has a lot of content so if you want to pass you really need to get down just about everything he says. You really have to work for it in his class so pay good attention, he's a really smart guy and easy to work with but you have to be able to keep up with him to do well in his class.
All his lectures were straightforward. All the exams were directly from the notes and since it was open book, it's an easy A. He also gives extra credit. Look at quizlets for his class as well.
Helpful, cheerful, beautiful

An amazing professor who really cares about his students. The course was easy and interesting and gives a solid foundation for journalism students. He also has some very cute dogs and a Welsh accent that honestly makes the lectures nicer to listen to.

Great instructor. Very nice guy who was clear about what to expect in a given week, so while he often gave out a lot of work, it was very easy to work around since it was pretty easy to figure out what was due, and I never felt overwhelmed with the amount of work assigned. As long as you watch his lectures, you'll do well in the class.

Dr. Thomas was my favorite teacher this semester. He always has a smile on his face and genuinely cares about his students. Weekly schedules are predictable and easy to manage. Content on tests/quizzes are clearly outlined in the lectures, so there's no surprises. Watch the lectures and you'll do great. RUN to him if he's an option for your course.

Prof. Thomas is a great professor. The class is based on weekly quizzes and discussions, and 2 exams and 3 Reflections. He does really well at teaching students the beginnings of journalism. Some quiz/test questions will test your knowledge though. You also have discussions groups every 2 weeks. Overall, he's funny, and the class is a breeze.
Lots of homework. But worth it.

I took undergrad and grad classes with him. He is the best. The kindest, most genuine professor I had at Mizzou. He came to every class with a smile on his face and made time for any student who needed it. Also If you can get him on your thesis committee, do it.

Ryan is an awesome professor and a fantastic lecturer. I dont think I wouldve liked the course as much as I did if he hadnt taught it. Has a great sense of humor too. Show up, pay attention, do the readings, and youll be a-okay.

The course itself is kind of boring, but Dr. Thomas is a very funny, British man, who makes it a lot more interesting. You can probably get by without doing the readings, but I would suggest doing them anyway, just to get a grasp on everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class isn't a cakewalk and you need to stay on top of reading quizzes, show up for events quizzes etc. Thomas is a genuinely nice person, always upbeat. Lectures are organized and interesting, only complaint is that there's a lot to cover and sometimes toward the end of the period he rushes to fit things in.

Ryan Thomas is a wonderful professor! The only thing I would change from this course is the time in between exams. We did not have our first exam until the middle of October, which is a lot of material. Our second exam is the week before finals week, then a cumulative final during finals week. There should have been less time between exams.
read the book for the weekly quizzes, set alarms if you forget homework easily bc if you don't do one thing your grade will SUFFER.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Slow down during lectures, people cannot write as fast as you speak.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Thomas was my favorite professor in the j school and the first name I recommend to incoming masters students or friends considering applying. His attention to detail is unreal. A genuinely kind and supportive person, great teacher and even better adviser. And HILARIOUS. My experience at Mizzou would not have been the same without him.

If you have the option to take one of Thomas' classes, do it. He's funny, handsome and a fantastic lecturer (his accent is music to your ears ). The class isn't that hard, but if you forget to take an online quiz or an in-class current events quiz, you're pretty much screwed. And don't skip the lectures. Seriously; you're missing out.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class itself is kind of boring and logical. Ryan Thomas was by far my favorite professor this semester. He made this a class I looked forward to. (He has the coolest accent EVER... it makes the lectures go by much faster).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ryan James Thomas was a great professor. At the beginning, I was really worried that I wouldn't be able to pull out an A. As long as you actually try to do the readings and know your current events, you'll be golden. Going to class is essential as a lot of what's tested comes straight from the lectures. He was nice enough to offer extra credit.

good guy & super funny but requires a lot of work and material seemed somewhat repetitive and unclear. lots of reading and so many quizzes but that means a lot of grades so also a good thing. reading quizzes once every week online and pop current events quizzes in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Thomas is a very funny professor whose exams are straightforward and easy to study for. The hardest part of the class are the pop quizzes on current events - you'd better know all of the headlines. He does let his liberal politics show a bit when he teaches and with articles he assigns to read however, so those on the right may feel a bit attacked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The Welsh Wonder. Ryan James Thomas is your classic British academic, but hes funny and makes a dry class interesting. There is a LOT of reading for this course. Its a bit repetitive, and its all theories and broad concepts. There are pop quizzes. Very few total points available. But Thomas is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I feel bad reviewing him for the trainwreck that was J2000 as a whole, but that class was seriously a mess. Lots of high school-type hand-holding, and the guest lecturers were insufferably dry. There are required in-class quizzes at each lecture, but you can do them remotely online. I attended all of three times that semester, and passed with a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's frustrating because he was an excellent professor for 1100, but J2000 has been a mess. He is a v. talented lecturer but has given up almost all of the actual teaching in this class to guest lecturers - some are great, some are awful. Having had Thomas for 1100, I was hoping he'd play more of an active role. Disappointed.

I've taken three classes with him. He really is one of the best teachers in the j-school. The level of organization, preparedness and attention to detail he brings is unreal. He'll drive you crazy with how picky he is on your papers (you'll never want to see another rubric again) but he's a really nice guy with lots of good research advice.

The class is tough mostly because there are only 3 tests that make up your whole grade 2 tests worth 25% and a cumulative final worth 50%. You have to study A LOT. Everything he goes over in lecture is on the test. The lectures are really long and its a ton of writing. I got an A on the final but I had a C all semester before that.

Ryan Thomas is a nice Welsh chap with a pleasant accent who gives fairly interesting lectures. Class isn't hard -- tests are high-stakes, but if you take decent notes, borrow the ones you miss, and review pretty thoroughly before exam, you'll do fine. I got an A and I definitely didn't go to all classes or read the textbook.

He does his best. He seems like a nice dude. His T.A's / guest speakers often don't know how to lecture, which can lead to frustrating classes. I never opened the book once, and got a B- for the class. I probably could have pulled off a B if I did a few things differently. I never missed a class and took exceptional notes, which helped.
By far one of the nicest and most supportive faculty members in the j-school. He made a potentially dull class (theory) really interesting. Really prepares you for the thesis process.

Honestly, the MOST important thing is to come to class and pay attention/take good notes. As long as you do that, and read some/most of the textbook you're solid. If not, you're screwed. He is hilarious and his lectures are really interesting and he does a really good job of facilitating discussion/participation. (Plus, awesome accent! :)

Dr. Thomas, known for his Welsh accent, is a pretty good prof. J1100 can be only made so interesting, and he does a pretty good job of it, incorporating lots of fun videos. He can be a little long-winded sometimes. The only grades for the class are 3 exams, and the exams are pretty tough (40/450 got an A on the first). The books are must-reads.

The class used to be based on more than just 2 tests & a final but now that that's all it is it is very hard to get your grade up. I'm hoping to get a high B but man those tests are hard. He said if you came to class and studied you would do well but that's not the case. I studies really hard and those are probably the hardest tests I've ever taken

We were an experimental class. There use to be assignments, quizzes and papers in this class. But now they have taken all of the assignments out and your grade is SOLEY based on two exams and a final, THATS IT. So it is very hard to bring a grade up. However, there are tons of opportunities for extra credit if you participate in research studies.

Very motivational lecturer and really gets his audience involved, however he told the class before one of the tests that if you have been attending the lectures and reading the book that it would be an easy test. He was wrong. I did both of those and still didn't do very well. Just make sure you study the book cover to cover.

He is hard to figure out. Sometimes he is very friendly and personable, other times he can seem remote and distant, like he's not really interested in what you have to say. It's hard to tell what he's really thinking. Gives very good written feedback though.

Ryan is a nice guy but not a good teacher. He is funny, that's true, but I always felt like he used that to disguise the fact that his lectures were really long and repetitive. He talks a lot about history and law and ethics but I don't feel like I learned anything hands-onpractical.

On the plus side: Uses lots of clips and examples. Presents material in a clear way. Makes you care about the subject. Strong sweater game. Quirky British accent. Really blue eyes. On the negative: Very hands-off with his TAs, who vary in quality (and they do the grading, not him). Grad student guest lecturers sucked. Useless with technology.
He's hot and he has a nice accent, but I was always exhausted from listening to him talk.

You definitely will want to go to every class, but you'll begin to actually want to because he makes the content exciting (as exciting as the history of journalism can be). He's funny, and uses memorable videos and memes to really drive topics home.

He's very easy to follow, adds his own input to make the subject matter more interestingapplicable, and funny. The exams are not too difficult, but you definitely want to know specific examples and remember what guest lecturers talked about.

Not only a great professor but a great person. Goes above and beyond in the help, detail and feedback he provides. I went from someone with no idea about research to feeling totally prepared to write my thesis. Very funny too.

Dr. Thomas was an excellent instructor. He was helpful, encouraging and his lectures were incredibly interesting. He is very intelligent and well-spoken.
