He typically teaches upper-level graduate courses, so he knows what he's talking about. Additionally, he has a great Welch accent that is sure to make class more entertaining.

very funny uses pop culture references, memes, videos to keep lectures interesting kind of a hard grader, but gives a decent amount of feedback so you know what you need to improve upon always has at least one "free" question on a test where the answer is obviouscommon sense

The class gets irritating because the same ppl answer questions all the time and Thomas doesn't try to vary things. He's very quick-witted and I wished he would have used that to cut down some of the frankly stupid things some students said. TAs were terrible. Thomas is good at lecturing on course concepts though.

Thomas is good about lecturing over the test material, but there is such a small amount of points that missing anything is detrimental. TA's sucked. They took off points to impress him, probably, in the two papers that were pointless to the learning process. You have to go to class to know what's going on.

Solid lecture prof and a really nice guy but way too laid back in managing his TA's. Assignments were returned really late and the whole process was vague. He seemed very "hands off" in this aspect, which was disappointing
Super enthusiastic instructor. Students love him because he's a really nice guy-  direct, easygoing without being a pushover, straightforward and fair in his expectations.

Good prof. You'll spend the semester either loving his accent or wishing he didn't end literally every sentence with "so, uh, yeah". But an all around good guy, passionate about the subject and super friendly and approachable.
His lectures are great. He's really funny, goofy sense of humor. Ridiculously good looking. Exams are a little tricky.
He looks like the tiredest guy on the planet but he's a super enthusiastic instructor and a genuinely nice guy. The guidance and feedback he gave really helped me in planning my thesis.

I was a bit skeptical at first because of how young he was, but Ryan turned out to be one of the best teachers in the grad program. Knowledgable and dedicated - really goes out of his way to help. He also has a bit of a fan base in the student body.

J2000 isn't a cakewalk, but Dr. Thomas handled the class well. He's funny and the content of his class is important. Guest lecturers vary in quality and the tests are hard, but the final project is spoon fed to you. Seriously, if you have any sense of deadlines you'll be fine.

I don't get the Thomas hate below. My project group are doing okay. It is not that hard - there is a lot of work though, probably too much for a sophmore-level class. Dr. Thomas is a VERY handsome man and his accent is adorable.

Dr. Thomas is a good professor and quite funny, however his tests are somewhat difficult and the TA's who grade them are even worse. There is a lot going on at once, which is manageable, but the TA's are so fond of docking points that any little slip up will cost you a grade.

A classic case of good professor, bad class. And by bad I mean an absolute nightmare. Useless textbook, horrible politically correct content, a final project that is a waste of time and paper, unfriendly TA's who grade hard to suck up to the prof - UGGGHHH. Thomas seems like a nice guy but he can't compensate for how AWFUL this class is.
Great lecturer and super funny, keeps you engaged with goofy stories. Doesn't require the textbook and was great about posting PowerPoints and video lectures online
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far my fav teacher, he is super funny and his lectures always kept my attention.  Class and reading are not a must, due to posting of notes on Blackboard, but i would really go to class just to hear his stories and jokes.  Gave a ton of extra credit in class, so much i didnt study for the final and still got a B in the class.  LOVE HIM!
Excellent professor. His lectures are always interesting and he's really funny. No assignments or grades apart from the midterm or the final, so it dosen't take up a whole bunch of your time.

Dr. Rymph is knowledgable about the history of the US and a good teacher. Her class is all lectures and three bluebook exams total. Each Sunday a textbook quiz is due and there are 4 chapter book quizzes throughout the semester. The class is not easy but it is not impossible. Show up, pay attention, and study hard for the tests to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was not a great lecturer, content that could have been interesting was exceptionally boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Go to class, it's a must. lectures are full of information you would not get by only reading the textbook. textbook readings are mandatory. She talks quiet fast so I recommend taking a laptop to lecture and taking notes that way. she is also monotone sometimes so lectures can be boring most times. But the lectures can also be very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredibly interesting, and Dr. Rymph is very clear and intelligent. You'll want to take very thorough notes and stay on top of readings. Copying my notes outside of class once was enough studying for me to get high As on her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was not a fan of the teaching style. She talks super fast for the entire class time, and sometimes she appeared annoyed if someone asked a question. The lectures were boring, but the material was interesting. The quizzes are easy if you did read. There's no need to read the textbook, just go to class and taking good/detailed notes is important.

Lectures were fast-moving but very informative and interesting. Rymph does a great job of connecting the material with past and present day events. The class was challenging but worth it. She gives easy quizzes over assigned books but they are worth the read and relate to class material. Awesome professor!
Really great historian, the class is tough however. Your final is worth 40% of the overall grade, and book quizzes matter a lot.

Not a lot of opportunities for grading, so quizzes matter. You have to read novels in the class, which sucks, but the material is really interesting. She has good lectures, but you can't just copy the powerpoints--you have to get the spoken information as well.

Good professor, I would recommend attending lectures but missing one or two is not a big deal. She has a lot of information and not all of it is on the powerpoints. Few grades in the class so all tests/quizzes really count! Overall enjoyed the material and Rymph's teaching

Dr. Rymph is a smart woman, but she doesn't have good teaching methods. She has a powerpoint to serve as a guide but a lot of the time it doesn't have the information that is most important on it. She lectures for the whole class period and it is hard to retain and get all the information because she throws so much at you at once.

This class was AMAZING!!! I took it as a freshman and loved it. She speaks really fast, but all of the information she gives is very interesting. You definitely have to study and know key dates, and people to do well, but this is a class WORTH taking!

The tests are hard, blue book multiple choice, short answer, essay. If a question is about lets say the cold war, then you need to know people, places, movements, etc. You have to read books and take quizzes on them, and on the quizzes the questions are details from the book. I would NOT recommend this class to anyone...only if I hated them.

She is very smart. She knows possibly everything about the last 100 years of History, but she is a very quick speaker. Have to go to class to fully understand all the notes and concepts covered each day. Tests are short answer/essay, pretty hard, so you have to study a lot. I actually learned from this class though. She's worth the challenge.
Surprisingly engaging

Really smart, REALLY knows her subject. She's a quick speaker, but I've never had any issue with taking notes. Her exams are mostly short answer/essay, but they aren't too difficult if you study a decent amount.
so hard

She keeps this course very balanced and manages to cover 100 years of US history effectively and objectively. Take good notes and you won't even need the textbook. She takes questions during lecture?don't be afraid to speak up if you get confused. She IS a quick speaker; her PowerPoints are generally a good guide, but don't rely on those alone.

Like others mentioned, she's quick! But she definitely knows her stuff. Be prepared to learn more than you ever wanted to know about American History. I thought she was a great teacher and I loved the class, but I enjoy a challenge.
She is fairly pleasant to listen to, does move fairly quick with notes though.  Projects were interesting and quizzes were straightforward.  Very clear about concepts.

Interesting class, but you'd better bring your laptop to class to take notes--she's quick.  Keep up with your reading, go to class, make a good outline based on the test study guides and you'll pull an okay grade.
She really tried to make lecture interesting. Just pay attention and read over your notes! Her exams are BLUEBOOK. :(

Teacher was one of the worst I have had in 4 years.  She spoke way too quickly, tests were essay and graded subjectively.  They made up reasons to grade people down so that they had enough C's, B's, A's, etc. to make thier bell curve look right.  Also, class doesn't cover US history, it is history of liberal movements.  Do not take this class!!!!!!

This was a great class that was very interesting and that made the material relevant to current events. The assigned books were very good, as well. My only complaint is that she talked too quickly in lecture. I learned a lot in this class and got an A.
pretty good class. lots of notes, but the essay tests arent hard if you outline them in advance.
She was a lousy Prof.
Very good... if you're taking a history class on the feminist movement in America.
Extremely clear and smart.  The best professor of the semester BY FAR.
she was a pretty easy teacher but she rambled a lot in lectures. She also moved too fast for any one to take notes in her class.
she has a good knowledge of subject matter but comments on my papers were very snide and unhelpful...quite a few people were put off by her bad attitude and favoritism to certain class members
WOW! I've learned so much from this teacher. She taught me more about history then anyone I've ever known...wow
very good prof

Very well prepared at all times. Though the info wasn't always interesting, he made sure that the class understood. Clearly wanted the students to learn and succeed and explained things well. Straightforward review and testing, online homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Don't bother taking Fin 2000 with anyone else, really. His exam reviews are extremely helpful, he writes the exams and tells you what every single question will be on. His lecture outlines are visual and organized. Even when most people were on their phones in lecture he would still be very enthusiastic. My friends other sections had it much harder

Ryan Ulrich is great.  He makes detailed study guides, goes over specific test questions and is more than willing to provide additional help.  He is spectacular and all should definitely take his class.  He explains things clearly and simply and really wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: ryan is one of the best teachers i've had. for finance 2000 he gave us very detailed lecture notes and outlines and before every test he would tell us exactly what each question would be about so we didn't have to waste time studying things that wouldn't be on the test. he is willing to meet any time and responds to emails so quickly.

I personally was not in his class, but I'm always hearing my friends talk about how he is always lecturing them. They says that he spends the majority of the class talking. They've told me he is always making rude and unnecessary comments.

He was a TA in my Medical Ethics class. I guess I would say he's a tough grader, but I'm not really sure because he provided no feedback. For some reason I just received bad grades on my essays that he graded. Expected all students to participate every discussion class, yet he himself spent 90% of the class talking. Too talkative for a discussion.
He's a TA and is annoying and thinks he's funny and wastes a lot of class time on things that have nothing to do with the class. He's a tough grader and doesn't help students out that much

What you get from Dr. Sexton's class is what you put into it. Do the readings and pay attention to the lectures and you'll do just fine. He doesn't grade his own students' work now, but he has TAs (some from  The University of Oxford). 

Dr. Sexton is extremely knowledgeable in 19th century studies. I looked forward to his classes each week.
Learned something new every class. Every history major should take Jay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Sexton is a very captivating speaker whose lectures are informed by his vast knowledge base. If you pay attention and keep up on your reading, you will definitely be able to do well in this course. Plus, if you're a history buff, you may receive extra credit if you can answer questions in class pertaining to mid-eighteenth century history.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sexton is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to the Civil War. I found his lectures to be very interesting, and he was always up for answering questions or repeating information if needed. There is no homework for the course; however, you're expected to stay up to date on your readings, as there are weekly quizzes. GREAT PROFESSOR!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Genuinely amazing professor!!! His lectures are hilarious and very easy to follow if you do the readings on schedule. Only hard part are the quizzes but they're light work if you show up to class.

Styled the class similarly to an AP History class. Very good at keeping me engaged and interested in the topics being discussed. Genuinely makes the class so much more enjoyable just because he is the professor.

Jay Sexton is an amazing professor. He clearly knows his history well, as he has very in-depth lectures with a lot of interesting stories in the mix. He does not allow technology at all so you have to take hand-written notes but that just makes you pay attention more. He gives a lot of in-class and out-of-class extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Sexton is truly an amazing professor, he is incredibly smart and has an amzing ability to share his kowledge in a fun and informative way. I honestly did very little of the reading, find summaries online and pay attention before quizzes and you will do fine. All tests are in person now, but they went well. Try your best and talk to the TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Sexton is hands down one of the most interesting professors. Very funny, a little strange, but wants nothing more than for his students to learn. Be prepared for long essays and once a week quizzes. Pro tip: when you're writing an essay, SHOW THE TA THE OUTLINE! This can genuinely make or break your grade. Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Sexton is the greatest professor I have ever had. His lectures are amazingly interesting and complemented by his unique personality. While there are a ton of assigned readings, I did very little of them and still did great in the class. One must also be aware of pop quizzes that pop up as well, furthermore, you should attend class regularly.
Jay Sexton is the Dark Souls of professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Gives a little quiz once a week will drop the 2 lowest grades at the end of the course. Honestly did very little of the course reading.

Sexton is smart and wants all his students to succeed. He drives his students to grow no matter where they are in their academic career. Great teacher, great TAs, and great textbook readings. Show up to all the lectures because there are pop quizzes and the answers are often found in the lectures and readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best professor at Mizzou, hands down.
I did not like my TA I was given but highly respect Professor Sexton and hope to take one of his classes in the future.

Dr. Sexton was a truly amazing professor this fall. I loved his course on the American Civil War and the lectures he did. He explains things fairly easy and the additional readings in the class definitely help. I would take another class from him if I could. 10/10

Jay Sexton is the professor that everyone wishes for but few get to have. He is truly invested in his students, and wants the class to be structured so they get the most of it. Be sure to do readings, as he will give pop quizzes to hold you accountable for them. But I guarantee you this; Jay Sexton doesn't want to teach, he wants you to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This man is a straight baller. There is a lot of reading and a quiz about once a week but if you actually did the reading you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Sexton REALLY wants to help you succeed. He's brilliant, but he keeps his ego in check and is very receptive to his students' input. He's very nice and can be hilarious. While his lectures and content can get dense, he tries hard to explain everything and is a VERY nice grader. I learned a ton, but be ready to do the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pablo is passionate and understanding about late work, but assignments are not entered into Canvas, so students must track deadlines themselves. Grades are often posted weeks later or right before finals, and the grading criteria in the syllabus does not accurately reflect how work is graded, which caused stress for many students.

Pablo is a funny professor but he is also very pushy with his politics. He takes a long time to grade and I didn't have a single grade in until week 9. Also for a Spanish class at this level, he talks a lot in English which is annoying. The assignments or due dates would change and he wouldn't really tell us.

Pablo was a great professor. He made class very entertaining and gave us plenty of time to understand concepts. I didn't like how the homework wasn't displayed on canvas, so it was easy to forget. He was a tough grader, not curving even if the highest grade was 85%. Also, he can be a little pushy with his political stance.

Pablo really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. This class will really help diversify your vocabulary and is a great balance of quizzes, exams, and projects. His class encouraged me to declare a minor in Spanish and he was extremely helpful in this process. I would highly recommend this class.

Pablo is very kind and caring towards his student but I was extremely frustrated this semester being completely unaware of my grade in this course. Toward the end of the semester, there were still tests and presentations from September that had not yet been entered. I could've been failing the class for all I know and I would have no idea.

Lots and lots of vocab quizzes and the homework takes a long time but you get at least two weeks to do it. Is super funny and nice. I honestly didn't learn anything though so it was weird to have tests on topics. Most of the class was just talking about stuff. Overall though, a super great and nice teacher and gives great feedback on essays.

Pablo is by far the best most awesome professor ive ever taken!! He is kind funny and cares about all his students. He also makes himself available for students who need help outside of class. If only he could be my teacher for the rest of my spanish classes!!

Pablo is my favorite professor at Mizzou. The first day of class, when I found out it was taught entirely in Spanish, I freaked out. I went to his office hours and told him I wanted to drop the class. He reassured me and told me that it would be okay. Three years later, I completed a study abroad program and I'm now fluent in Spanish. All bc of him

Listen. Pablo is the GOAT. He's one the best educators I've ever had. If you come to class, ask questions, and engage in the course, you'll do well. He's hilarious too. It makes coming to class easy! Pablo, in my opinion, is the best teacher at Mizzou.

Everything I hated about this class was out of his control. My biggest gripe is that as an ECON major I have to take 3 semesters of a foreign language. This class takes up too much time I could be spending on other more relevant work. I have taken 3 semester of Spanish, I know as much Spanish as before I took 3 semesters of Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's literally the best. He makes learning and practicing Spanish really fun.

Pablo is easily my favorite Spanish professor I've ever had! He is also hilarious, and makes the class fun. The class is easy if you participate and do your work (about 1-2 homework assignments a week). He gives your essays back for revisions before you turn them in for a final grade. I loved this class and hope I get to have him again!

Pablo is of the sweetest most caring professor ive ever had. I dont find spanish interesting (i was only taking the class for a major requirement) but I never minded going to class because he would always show up happy and ready to help you succeed. My grade in start of semester was bad (D+) but you learn how he grades and I ended with a B+

Pablo is one of the best professors I've ever had! As a Spanish major, feedback is really important to me to improve my language skills, and Pablo gives really clear feedback into what you need to work on! The course load for this class was also very manageable (without it feeling like it was too easy). I really hope to have Pablo again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is fun and unlike some Spanish professors at Mizzou he doesnt make you feel dumb for asking questions or saying something slightly incorrect. Revises essays for you before you turn them in for a grade. First professor Ive ever had that really made me want to go out of my way to take another class he teaches

My favorite Spanish professor at MU. Pablo truly cares about his students and their success. He encourages conversation and is very courteous when it comes to correcting any errors. He shows up everyday with a good attitude and a fun story to share. 3 class presentations, a little bit of HW and lots of talking. Easy A if you just try.

Pablo was awesome! He's hilarious and his classes are genuinely fun. Show up to his class and participate and the class really isn't too hard. Lots of discussion but he keeps it light and pretty simple.

Pablo is a great guy but a tough grader. If you put in the work and go to his office hours, it pays off. I learned a lot with him and he has been my favorite spanish teacher so far. I do recommend taking his courses
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Anyone who's able to land Pablo as their teacher should consider themselves incredibly lucky.  By FAR the best Spanish instructor Mizzou has to offer and AMAZING person.  Spanish is tough, but if anyone could REALLY make you learn and do well in class, it's him. He's caring, he's inspiring, he's funny, and he'll even sing for you from time to time.
He was one of my favorite teachers so far at Mizzou, genuinely cared about his students and their spanish

Pablo is definitely the best teacher I've had at MU so far. He is super funny and nice, but I also learned a ton in his class. He gives a ton of homework but I would definitely take his class again because he is an incredible teacher. One of my favorites, for sure. He tells great stories and has great insights on Spanish culture. Take this class!!!

Pablo is easily the best professor I've had. Extremely caring, helpful and funny. Unlike some Spanish professors, he wanted to help me improve at speaking the language and genuinely cared about how I was doing in life.

Great guy, but definitely be ready to work in this class.  I had an hour of homework each night and he was a difficult grader for sure.  But he really cares about students and he's a really funny guy!

Pablo is an awesome teacher. The lecture can be long but he's super funny, energetic, and keeps the class entertained. He is one of the best teachers i've had at mizzou and if your taking Spanish i would take his class. He is clear, helpful, and easy to understand. He is always willing to help. If i could have him for all my Spanish classes I would

Pablo is a wonderful professor. He is really willing to work with every student and while Spanish 3 is difficult, he makes it bearable which is really refreshing. If you need to take SPAN 2100 for sure take it with him

Pablo's class was by far the best experience I have had in a spanish class. He is really engaging of the students and has a great sense of humor. This class focused heavily on conversation, so mostly oral presentations and class participation (NO TESTS). Very manageable to get an A and no worse than a B.

I'm about to receive a poor grade of about 65%, but I didn't care as long as I passed. I hate Spanish. ABSOLUTELY HATE IT. However, with that being said, Pablo is a good instructor and keeps the class from dragging with humor. Some don't get his humor, but it helped keep me interested. I could have had a far worse instructor for Spanish 3

Pablo is easily one of the best professors I have ever had.  He is a very funny and nice guy.  This course takes some effort which includes weekly online homework assignments as well as participation in class.  As long as you show effort and respect Pablo, you will see he really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed.
Pablo Serna was one of the most passionate teachers I've ever had. He loves his job and students and it shows. He is a tough grader though.

Pablo is such a nice guy. He's a picky grader, though. Make sure you're paying attention during lecture because the different verb tenses can get confusing if you don't know when and how to use them. But Pablo is good at explaining concepts, and he's extremely approachable. Just make sure you're showing up to class and participating.

Pablo is extremely fun and insightful. You'll never have a dull moment in his class, which is important because you'll have him every day. He's very helpful and understanding, but his class IS very challenging. You must, MUST, participate and attend class to be successful. If you put in the effort, he'll be one of your favorites for sure.
Best professor I've had at Mizzou.

Pablo is a great teacher! He tells you want you need to know and makes sure you understand it. The class isn't easy, but Spanish is a foreign language. You will do fine if you put your time and effort into it and listen to Pablo! He's super funny and cares about his students doing well! Best Spanish teacher I have had at Mizzou so far!
Terrible. Try not to take class with him.

Pablo is really a great spanish teacher. He engages you in class, and makes sure you learn rather than just telling the information to you. He's funny, and makes class enjoyable. He's also always willing to help if you need it. Definitely the best of the 4 spanish teachers I've had at Mizzou!
Funny man, but he can get down to business when he teaches. Good, clear instructor who's always willing to help.

Pablo Serna was an absolute bro. I loved this guy's energy and humor and he was always interested in what his students were doing outside of class. He was very nice and very helpful. His class isn't hard but he is a little bit of a stingy grader but not as bad as most in the department. Absolutely take Pablo if you get the chance.

TOUGH grader. Really nice guy, but pretty inflexible. He says it is what the coordinator requires, but other teachers for 2100 are more flexible in grading. He really appreciates when he can see someone making an effort. Doesn't speak Spanish the entire class like other 2100 teachers, which is a plus and minus.

I difficult but great teacher. He is a tough grader but an amazing teacher. Very thorough in his explanations. He definitely cares about his students. He is tough though, requires work to do well in his class.

Great teacher!! Most laid back professor I've ever met in college. Very willing to help and work with you. Simply be attentive in class and try and you'll do fine. Tests are a little difficult but they come from the course director. His stories always add to the class and give you a cultural perspective. Very enjoyable class overall.

This professor doesn't expect much for homework as it is just weekly ALEKS assignments and frequently extends the due dates. He expects a lot on test. They are difficult. You can put in lots of time and there will still be a struggle. He provides some practice problems but not much and most of them aren't related to the test.

Makes what he expects out of students very clear, but he does expect a lot. ALEKS every week and frequently extends the due dates for them. Tests are very difficult, usually around 13 questions with two free response and an extra credit question. It is totally possible to get an A if you work hard and study for the tests.

Professor Sewell has been my favorite professor in the chemistry department at Mizzou. He expects a lot out of his students but if you put in the work you will succeed in his class. If all the studying you do is the homework be prepared to get a B at best, if you want an A you need to go the extra mile and do a ton of problems out of the book

He's tough but clearly cares about the subject matter and his students' success. If you go out of your way to ask for his help, he will and he's happy to. Mizzou is incredibly lucky to have someone with his background teaching freshmen.

This class is fine if you are prepared to dedicate a lot of time to it. I had to spend a ton of time with tutors and looking up Youtube tutorials to get through the ALEKS assignments. Almost all of the assignments are through ALEKS, so be prepared for that. The lectures never felt like they lined up quite right with the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Sewell is very intelligent and offers a lot to learn. However, I never felt that his tests were accurately assessing my knowledge. I always felt I knew the material well, but his tests seemed to test my test taking skills rather than what Id learned in class. Although he did curve a few tests really what saved my grade were the labs and ALEKS.

Prof. Sewell was very smart. His lectures were very well organized. The tests were tricky as they would only be about 20 questions so if you got one question wrong you'd be docked 5% already. Some of the questions were written that you could get partial credit on. Make sure you do the labs for points and the homework problems for review.

To the people saying they enjoyed the class, they either 1: only had this as their one hard class or 2: they're lying. Sewell was a former researcher at Los Alamos, so I have no clue how he became an intro chemistry professor. If you have multiple tough classes, don't give yourself an extra burden with this guy.

Sewell gets a bad wrap for his level of difficulty, but he is extremely caring and understanding under the surface. He has taught us well, but people do not put forth the effort. Most people complain when it really is not that hard to do the work that he asks for. I recommend taking him if you want a good chemistry education and a manageable A.
Get ready to do ALEKS every single week.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best professor I had in undergrad. Fantastic lectures and very helpful outside of lecture time. If you slack in his class, you will probably fail and pchem 2 with him is almost completely conceptual. If you try to get by with memorization, you MIGHT manage to pass. Also a tough grader. He puts alot of effort in on his end and expects the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Sewell is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures were well-organized and blended well with the textbook. The homework assignments were hard but helpful for the tests. Tests were at night so you always had enough time to think deeply about problems. Our final was conceptual. I left feeling comfortable with quantum mechanics!
This class was by far the hardest class I have ever taken. Went to him for help and was very rude. Tests were extremely hard and hardly like the old tests. Good luck!
Whatever you do, do NOT take this professor. He doesn't explain well at all and is not clear.
Good teacher for the class. Nature of the class makes it extremely difficult, but Sewell does a thorough job of teacher important concepts.
He is very smart and sometimes is hard to follow, but thats just the nature of the class. As long as you go to class and pay attention you should do ok... Thats kind of the same with any class.

He is very passionate about his studies and what he shares in class! He rambles a lot, but he always catches up to where he needs to be. Loved his class this semester and thought it was easy! Very light work, weekly quizzes and 2 essays, and 2 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super passionate (rambling at times, but interesting nonetheless), weekly quizzes, and lots of note-taking, would absolutely take another course of his.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My class was actually AMS2100, wasn't listed. His lectures are great, he's clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about the material and it shows. My one gripe is that he is extremely harsh when it comes to grading on essays. The rubrics are usually pretty vague and if your paper isn't nearly perfect there's a good chance you will get a C-F.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall he makes himself fairly open. Provides recordings of each lecture in full detail. The only complaint is that it takes a long time for him to respond to emails
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Waits until the last min to grade essays, and then grades them harshly. He only opens the essays the day they're due and expects a professionally written 6-page essay that should be front and center of the New York Times. The finals are super easy, but it's only two essays and two finals, so your grade rests heavily on his lazy essay grading.
Not too hard of class. Sometimes the lectures would go over 50 minutes which got annoying at times. The essays are graded kind of tough. If you do the readings and lecture you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was difficult for me due to the whole Latin thing, but the professor was very accessible and eager to help. You will use the textbook everyday, and there will be homework every single day. Most of the grade will come from quizzes that happen every two days or so, and you have to do well on tests. There is a small amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Go to class, his tests are based off what he talks about in class not what is on the powerpoint
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Taking this class feels like you're being ragebaited on a daily basis. Exams have nothing to do with lectures and are only based on the homework. He'll make one statement in lecture on the material that actually shows up in the homework. Canvas assignments are posted in the most inconvenient possible way.

TA office hours were very helpful to understand the homework! And tests were entirely based on the homework! The lectures were okay, but definitely got more rushed towards the end of the semester. I had not taken dif eq or bme 2080 as pre reqs and this was not an issue, I just wish I had a better understanding of enthalpy.

He's awful at lecturing and none of the content relates to the homework. I bought the digital textbook and he never linked it in Canvas even after several emails. The TA hardly knew what to do with the HW solutions. The content is so specific that no YouTube videos can help you. I've considered switching to ME because of this prof.

Horrible at lecturing. Hard to know how to apply lecture material to the actual homework. But if you figure out the homework or find the answers somewhere, just use those answers to study for the exams and you'll be good.

Terrible at lecturing. Stopped going to lecture after a week or two bc it had nothing to do with the hw that the exams are based off of. Go to TA office hours to learn how to do the hw. Study just the hw and nothing else for the exams. Hard to contact him via email. Terrible class that I learned nothing in, but at least it's not terribly difficult.

Dr. Sengupta is a really nice guy, he just isn't the best at clearly communicating the course material. He's super smart, he just doesn't have a very concise course plan/layout. The tests are basically straight from the homework and he posts homework keys. Lets you use a cheat sheet on tests. You won't come out of the class having learned much.

I dont understand the other comments. This is literally one of the easiest classes you will have as a BE student. I went to 2 lectures and got like a 99% in the class. Yea he's not the greatest lecturer but he's a REALLY nice guy and he'll help you out. Seriously if this class is too difficult (regardless of the teacher), consider switching majors.

Literally awful teacher. Does not teach jack and expects you to do impossible homework problems when he does nothing related to them in class or even close. I'd say don't take him but, you have to. SUCKS
Worst teacher i have ever had!

Hard to understand. Doesn't use sufficient examples, expects too much from students, not available for extra help,... The text is copied material from other indian-british books which are extremely hard to understand and overall horrible professor don't take him.

Professor Scardina is one of the best professors you could take for a 1000-level course. She is incredibly kind, genuine, and truly cares about her students. Her class is easy and enjoyable if you put in the effort, and I would happily retake it a million times if I could.

Great teacher but you must go to class, you have minute papers or mini quizzes 8 of them randomly throughout the semester in class. 2 Tests are based of a book you read and 2-3 lectures from guests. The class is just guest lectures, of different degrees and programs at mizzou. easy A if you put in a little work.
the dumbest class ever. it was so hard for no reason

You can print slides for pop quizzes, but if you don't you will do poorly. The answers are taken verbatim from the slides, so it's not easy to do well on them. Tests are also pretty challenging. Overall, all of the questions in this course are hyper-specific. Nothing against Traci just didn't like the course. Also, super boring course.

Traci is the nicest professor ever. For the intro to health professions class, we had a different guest speaker every single day so it is very helpful if you do not know what you are going into. This class will not stress you out at all.

reviews.comment: His lectures are AMAZING and he's super knowledgeable about the field. 10/10 recommend if you like geology.

very stand up guy, always provides resources and gives extra information to anyone who is curious. all lectures slides are put online as well in case you miss class, which is super helpful. gives respect back to his students in regards to communication and time management. jim is a very understanding guy, rating of 29/10 :)

James is a great professor. I feel the class has a bad reputation because of the difficulty of the material. He is aware of this and gives a very healthy curve because of it. Jim is hands down one of the best professors out there. For one, he has so many cool and relevant stories, but keeps students engaged and focused while entertaining them. I wish he was my prof for every class. To reiterate. LITERALLY .THE .BEST . Also very accomodating to my test taking needs.

reviews.comment: Absolute dude. 10/10 best professor at Miz.
Laid back, fantastic lectures that clearly lay out the course material, as well as the tested material. Never had to study a single time outside of doing the weekly homework assignment.

Can't type enough about how great and knowledgeable Jim is. Unfortunately, there's a lot of disconnect. Low D average on exams, he considers "pretty good." Lectures are incredibly dense with information, then come exams you basically guess on what material will be covered, only for the questions to ask a Hawaiian term for a special type of magma.

This class was a nightmare. He teaches the class as if were all majoring in geology. Studied for hours on end just get terrible grades back on exams. Offers no study guides. for the amount/type of questions he gives u think he would allow open note/book. Im convinced he gets a kick out of watching students struggle. Stay away if you care about gpa

For a general Ed, this class is a ridiculous amount of work. His exams are are extremely extensive and oddly specific for this to be an into course. On top of that, he offers no study guides. The amount of hours I studied for the exams just to get a poor grade back is ridiculous. Nothing is open note, open book. Just stay away from this class.

Jumps around during lectures between the slides and stories. Often hard to follow. Great guy, just kind of hard to follow. Be prepared to study extensively for a good grade on the exams regardless of the quality of your notes. Quality and difficulty of the lab depends on your Teaching Assistant
Fantastic professor with a great sense of humor. He incorporates his humor into his lessons to make the subject matter more enjoyable to listen to.

He is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He talks about personal experiences on the field and in his research, rather than always teaching out of the book, which makes class so much more interesting.

Flies through slides, Clicker points every week, lab section is easy
Really enjoy this class!

Overall he was a great instructor! Very informative, easy to talk to, and made all the material feel very approachable. If you need a less stressful capstone, I'd reccommend this one. He was very compassionate and clearly cared about his students' well-being, however, sometimes this could impede his ability to make it through lectures. I appreciated his anecdotes and knowledge of the field, but I feel like the course could have been more focused.

Todd was a great professor. The grading scale was lax but since he keeps a physical grade book, it's hard to keep track of what grade you have in the class. Lectures weren't mandatory and sometimes confusing but overall helped with understanding. Chill class, recommend for honors credit

todd is one of the best professors i've ever had. he truly cares about the subject he teaches and about the success of his students. this was a great class and he always made discussions interesting. i hope to have him for another class in the future.

reviews.comment: Shannon Breske could not possibly care less about her students. She was extremely difficult to work with, was not understanding, and overall just should not be a professor. In four years of college, she was my least favorite instructor and I would advise everyone to stay FAR away from her. She is rude, disrespectful, immature, and condescending.
Very unfair grades, vague rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Tell me how someone who has never worked in a business is supposed to teach us about Business Communication. Anyways she tries to be all genuine and upbeat, but its fake. She literally was telling us how much she loved money in class. Way to be an example for your students! Ask the registrar for the equivalent course 2nd grade Phonics. Avoid!

Terrible teacher, lectures are absolutely useless. The TAs take off for every little error on a paper, even though it's something you just learned about. The grading system is so unfair. Spends too much time going over non-relevent stuff, like her personal life. Lecture doesn't help with the assignments at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Shannon Breske is the worst professor I have ever had in my four years of college. Not only is her class the biggest waste of time but it is incredibly difficult to do well on the assignments even after visiting the writing center or the TAs. The University of Missouri shouldn't be paying this lady to do anything above teaching a 3rd grade level.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Shannon talks too much about her personal life in class. Lectures will not help you much on the paper assignments. Although the grading is tough, my TA is a nice guy. The only thing I learned is avoiding passive voice in business writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The idea of teaching Business Communication is great however Shannon is not well suited to teach this course She has worked in School Administration her entire career and has no idea how companies communicate internally and externally She talks about Sweating the small stuff yet makes mistakes that she would deduct 20% of your grade for HORRIBLE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Her grading is ridiculously difficult. If you make one grammar mistake you can lose nearly 20% of your grade on a paper. I used Grammarly and two English majors to proofread my papers and the TAs still found an excuse to mark off on grammar. She lectures like she is teaching 1st graders instead of college seniors. Avoid if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Shannon seems like she really is happy to be there. Unfortunately, no one else is. She treats us like we are in Kindergarten. Her lectures are pointless but attendance is mandatory, you absolutely must go to class. She makes the TA's grade VERY harshly, you're probably going to get a C no matter how much work you put in. Avoid taking her if you can

Shannon and her TA's have one of the most messed up grading requirements I have seen at the University. She talks too much about her personal life and problems that the students simply do not need to hear. The average grading on the writing assignments are a 70% even after you ask your TA to make revisions. Worst class I took at Mizzou. So unfair!

She is not genuine at all. Her lectures are pointless and she deducts so many points. Im sure her grade distribution for this semester will be so low. If this class is offered by another teacher I suggest you take it . She swears the small stuff and you loose a ton of points. I never write reviews but this one I have to warn you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Treats us like were kids, easy class. Attendance at each lecture and they're very boring. Reminds be of BA 3500

She's a little annoying but means well. She just dumbs things down too much and wastes a lot of time in lectures. The class itself was pretty pointless but required (for me at least). Tests are online and easy. No need to study. Labs are better and more interesting than lectures but my instructor was great, so I'm sure that helped.
OK so BA1500 is a breeze. The lectures are only offered on monday nights which blows, and they are pretty boring. The lab however was awesome, definitely don't skip lab.

Shannon obviously cares about our success as students, but I found her often treating us like children. She is very enthusiastic about TCoB and the subject. BUS1500 seemed unorganized and lacked a specific point and reason for taking. The assignments were easy, and the grading was easy. Lab class was participation based.

Amazing attitude throughout the whole semester. Wanted the whole class to understand all material and greatly prepared us for our online exams. Labs once a week, which were a breeze if you attended that weeks lecture. Not much homework until towards the end of the lesson.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A very fair and organized class. If I remember correctly, there are 4 exams, but only your highest 3 count towards your grade. I completely bombed my first exam (D). TAs are readily available outside of lecture and are more than willing to help your understanding. Ended up with an A+. Just take the material seriously, and you'll be fine.

Sharon Ryan was a fantastic economics professor who worked super hard to ensure you actually learned the economics material. Tough but fair. Great teacher. Truly enjoyed the class, her lectures and the challenge of the course. I also majored in economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Really helped me understand economics. Best professor yet!
SO, amazing I have no words.
N/A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sharon Ryan was a terrible teacher and I wouldn't recommend her to anyone. Also, the TA's were not very good at leading the class and only confused me more because I couldn't understand them and they even got confused sometimes while teaching.
if you are enrolled in her class DROP IT NOW!!!!! she is the worst teacher i've ever had and I dreaded going to her class everyday. the devil in disguise no joke... save yourself now and drop

despite what most people say, I did not find Sharon Ryan's class to be incredibly difficult.  Go to class, do any homework or optional practice problems and her tests are no problem.  The final is worth almost 40% of the overall grade so you can make up most of your mistakes and pull out a decent grade if you try

The worst teacher in the history of the human being race. If you're considering going to mizzou. I strongly consider not going, because of the most worthless, arrogant, and no soul teachers that they hire. Sharon Ryan wants her students to fail.
I don't wear my seatbelt on the way to class in the hopes that I die before I get there.

Sharon Ryan really isn't all that bad. Just go to class, do the weekly reading and quizzes, and study your butt off for exams. That's all there is to it- just put a little work in and it should be no sweat.

Economics is really hard for some people and really easy for others. Everyone who really really hates her are just not that great at economics. I didn't think she was the best professor ever, but econ is something I'm good at so I didn't have any ill feelings towards her. I like how the exams are curved like 12-20%.

There have been several times where I understand Sharon Ryan's teaching assistants better than her.  Her examples aren't always helpful or relevant, and quite frankly they make concepts more confusing for students.  She is making this class unnecessarily hard.  Even after reaching out for help, she just brushed me off to someone else.

Sharon Ryan is an awful professor. Learned absolutely nothing in her course. Hardest class I've taken at Mizzou by far. I stopped going to lecture after awhile because I wasn't learning ANYTHING. The tests were impossible. I pulled 2 all nighters for the final and still didn't do good. I hated this class. Take at a community college if you can.
Yes this was a hard class but if you put in effort and didn't just whine the entire time you would get a good grade! Received and A+ in her class
Sharon Ryan gets enjoyment from failing students. Avoid this class at all possible.

This class is hard. However, it's not impossible. Sharon Ryan is a bright individual ... but she doesn't make it easy for her class. You have to read the textbook cover to cover and memorize every key point within it. Do all the homework (it's optional, but do it). Tests are extremely difficult. STUDY. But don't fret - she curves significantly.

You have to actually put in the work for this class and you'll be fine. I don't understand all of the horror stories. Yes, her tests are demanding but they are doable. You have to put in some effort though. Dr. Ryan is a good professor and explains things well, but there were a lot of people that didn't come to class and expected to get an A.

Professor Ryan isn't as bad as everyone says she is.  You just have to go into the class with an open mind and willingness to work hard.  Come to class, read the book, study for the exams and you'll be fine.
The class is poorly organized. Study the quizzes and learn her tricks.  Homework is helpful, too.  Strongly recommend taking this elsewhere.

Don't take this class here or if you do, take it over the summer with one of her TA's. She doesn't define things very well because she wants you to read the book but even then things are not very clear. I've never had to re-take a class in my entire life until I took this class. Make sure you study because her tests are tricky.

I don't understand the complaints ---maybe because I didn't take this as a freshman, it didn't seem hard. This class is super easy, Dr. Ryan explains the concepts like you're 5. YOU HAVE TO READ THE BOOK. PERIOD. Homework was easy, but weekly and annoying to keep up with. If you read and understand the book, and pass book quizzes, this is an easy A
MEMORIZE THE BOOK AND QUIZZES. then you will get an A. and look over the graphs and make sure you understand them 100% because that is the entire exam

Dr. Ryan is not that bad. Just make sure to pick your homework up every week and really pay attention during the Friday lectures and this class is cake. People complain so much because this is one of the first real classes they take in college that actually takes some work to get a good grade.

I had a 4.0 until this semster and got my first grade lower than an A in this class...a D.  I am the best test-taker around and her exams are impossible no matter how hard you prepare.  She does not care about her students whatsoever.  This class is a GPA killer and I would take it at a community college if possible. SHE IS AWFUL!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Just awful. Sharon Ryan's lectures are confusing pointless. Read the book and review quizzes before exams. Easy concepts are made confusing and difficult. I'm an A student and I attended every lecture I squeaked by with a C+. Class is a GPA killer, she does give large curves though! Avoid this class if you can.
By far the hardest class I took at Mizzou this semester. Her tests don't make since shes just an all around bad teacher

Lectures are straight from the textbook. She posts notes online that make it easy to learn the material. Attendance wasn't required, so I rarely went to class. Her exams are based on the lecture notes (which are mostly material from the book) and similar to questions from quizzes/old exams. Easy A if you put in any effort at all.
Regardless of the horror stories, this class really isn't that bad. Go to the M/W lectures and READ THE BOOK! Study old tests and the online quizzes before the exams and you'll be fine.

Everything she teaches is straight out of the book. Read the book and you are gold. If things aren't clear attended class. Gives very generous curves on tests. If you work hard it shouldn't be too hard.

Dr. Ryan is tough but worth it. Take the online quizzes at the end of each section to prepare for exams but don't expect the numbers and figures to be verbatim, she'll trip you up that way. Always over-prepare for the tests but you can reassure yourself if you did poorly that there is always a large curve.

I was told horror stories but it best to come in open minded. You have to do the reading prior to class. If you are focused and paying attention you will do fine. She is helpful during office hours and uses lots of examples...Only thing is she wont bump if you are short of an A she wont help. I was .01% short of an A but I learned a lot

If there was one professor who doesn't deserve to teach, ever again, it would be Sharon Ryan. She is a terrible lecturer, creates unfair exams, and is hardly ever available. If you can, take this class elsewhere. I hope the University takes a closer look at her. She doesn't offer evaluations, either. Just bad all around!

Sharon Ryan must think we're all idiots.  She consistently uses a 4th grade level when with her class and talks down to us.  She also wrote the book used in class and follows it word for word.  Don't attend lecture; it's pointless.  Also, her lectures are repetitive and she spends half the class reciting the later half of her previous lecture.

Not as horrible as everyone says.  She is incredibly smart so goes over everything in tons of detail. There are always TAs to help, especially the day before homework is due.  Content of the class is repetitive but not too difficult.
She wrote the book. Literally.

Dr Ryan wrote the textbook she uses in class. I only attended lecture a handful of times and got one of the highest grades in my class. Read the book thoroughly because the tests almost always consist variations of given examples.
Class is pretty easy but Sharon is an awful teacher. Has no idea what she is doing
take this class at a community college. this is a class you either are really good at and pass, or really bad at and fail. this class is ridiculously hard.

This teacher can teach that is true. The only problem is that the book is poorest thing you will ever read. Unorganized material. You have no idea where she is in the book. Without the book to help you learn, tests and quizzes are hard to pass by yourself. I know that majority of people take quizzes together and also memorize the book for test.
Show up to class on Friday. Read the text book, and do the extra credit.

This class is not that hard at all. If you read the book and do the homework and online quizzes you will be fine. The tests are very similar to the quizzes and worksheets she gives you. She makes a hard subject easy to understand. I don't know why everyone is complaining.

Don't know why everyone is complaining, this class is stupid easy. Skip class on Monday, turn in your homeowkr and leave on Wednesday, and show up to class on Friday, do all the homeworks and online book quizzes, and you'll AT THE VERY LEAST get a B. Really not as bad as people are making her seem.

Professor was always prepared and had clear examples of what she expected. Nothing appeared on the test without her covering it. Econ is difficult for people in general and they take out their struggles on her rather themselves. Class is fair and seemed wiling to help before and after class along with office hours.
She wrote her own book for the course,so her examples are bad in person and in writing. NO power-point and has foreign TA's teach on Friday's. Not helpful

Would you rather stab your own eye ball 50 times with a rusty needle.. then pull your finger nails out with your teeth....... OR take this class. I choose the first option. There is an online quiz every friday and it is the most frustrating 20 minutes of my week. examples in class: yeah, makes sense. quiz questions: ummm what...?

This is a hard class, and an easy GPA killer if you are the typical student who just wants to get a gen ed out of the way. If you want to actually learn about econ with a very knowledgeable prof, take this class. She is clear, efficient, and totally willing to help you. Attend all EC opportunities and ask questions in lecture and you will succeed.

Economics is not an easy subject to grasp at all but she is very clear in what she says in lecture and repeats concepts several times while she is going over them. Class attendance is required as well as the extra credit reviews(which not only enforce her teachings but you get extra credit. She is always willing to stop and make sure YOU understand
Lectures are almost impossible to follow, she starts a subject and then swiftly changes to another topic. Her tests are hard and the material is uninteresting. Prepare to study, a lot.

Sharon Ryan is not as bad as people make her sound on her. The class is hard but since test's are really all that matter, you can do well if you go to class. Her questions and wording are the hardest parts of the class but if you look at her HW's and her quizzes you can get a hold of her. She is hard but the TA's are the real a**holes

Do not take this class what so ever. Sharon Ryan is here to kill your GPA and to discourage you from asking for help because she always have an attitude. I seriously recommend you do not take this class here. Avoid by any means!

I felt like this class was really difficult...It's economics... but Sharon Ryan makes the subject as easy as possible.  She provides a lot of study materials on blackboard and TA sessions and extra credit opportunities.

She knows her stuff, but not how to teach it.  "Tutoring" sessions are just slightly smaller lectures with the head TA teacher.  Even though these "tutoring" sessions suck I'd recommend them - the TA is a better teacher and they're worth extra credit.  Bottom line: thank God she curves tests.

Lectures are important, tutoring sessions even more so. Class is completely manageable if you do your work. Plenty of Extra Credit opportunities, basically a course in common sense. Use her practice quizzes on BB to study... 50% of exam questions come from those. Easy A if you complete assignments on time.

Don't spend your money on the book, it's not used at all. Also, skip the lectures. They're worthless. This is not the type of class that can be taught in an auditorium. Go to the tutoring sessions instead. Read the stuff online and you'll be good to go.

People need to chill out. She knows her stuff and teaches in a very clear manner with examples. If you stay on top of your work, pay attention in class, and pick a good TA, it will be a breeze. Don't bother buying the actual textbook, I never even took it out of the plastic.

Sharon Ryan is a know it all thats only purpose in this world is to ruin the GPA of mizzou students. The only relevant thing she has ever discussed in class is nueticals and its relevance alone is feeble in itself. Dont take the class. Waste of time. Decays your GPA.

Sharon Ryan knows her stuff! I learned a ton in this class. She is very organized and is very clear with her examples in class. People complain, but she is a very good professor. This isn't an easy A but if you do the homework and understand it, you'll do fine on the test. All of the material you need to know is on the homework.

Econ 1014 is a course in common sense.  At first I was worried about this class, but Prof. Ryan was great! Tests were extremely fair, and everything was curved up. The weekly tutoring sessions were extremely helpful, and the online quizzes were really good study material for the final.

Had her for Micro Econ last sem. Although the homework and quizzes were enough to drive you insane, her teaching methods and tests I found to be intriguing and balanced. I'm glad I had Professor Ryan.
sharon ryan!!!!

I had Dr Ryan for Labor Econ.  I have nothing but good things to say about the class.  Sure, it was difficult, and she challenges you, but if you are interested in economics, she definitely prepares you.  Her class requires you to use what you've learned and apply it to the real world- which, at least in my view, is what makes an econ class great.
Had this class a couple years ago, but she was good. She told us what we needed to know, and I did well. People complained because she's strict, but I never had any problems.

The online section of the class that she runs is terrible. Don't do it. I've found that she does tell you everything you need to know for tests, but she adds in a bunch of useless info you don't really need to know. The homework basically is the test, so understand it, and you will do well.
no help at all.  try to get another professor for economy if you can.
this teacher is a moron who cant teach.  How she hasent been fired yet is incomprehendible.  Mizzou is just wasteing its money on her.  she is so stupid

Everyone complains about Sharon Ryan but she is a GOOD professor and the class is totally manageable. The people who complain about this class are the ones who never go and don't do the homework. If you are a good student, you will get a good grade. And Sharon is a fine professor.

I have no idea what everyone else is complaining about this was THE easiest class I took freshman year. The homeworks are the tests, and there are LOTS of extra credit opportunities. The hardest part is making triangles and finding the area. Just go to lecture and do homework and you'll do great. At first it may seem hard but it gets loads easier.
hated it

She makes a class that should be easy enough into a task between the 30 minute exams and the fact that her lectures lags behind the quizzes, just be prepared and do all the practice work and you should get out of there with a passing grade.
I'm sure this woman is a great economist, but she is a poor instructor. I felt she had very little interest in her class actually learning. She was cold and intimidating.
boring teacher and very restrict
Sharon Ryan has become a Mizzou legend for her hard classes.  I earned a C+ and that was almost impossible. If you have to take econ, take it with someone else!!
Great professor! Lectures were very organized and well put together.  Millions of online lecture notes and study guides and bundles of opportunities for EC!

How does one describe evil? At Mizzou all one says is "Sharon Ryan" and it is enough. Granted, the subject she teaches is hard. But I have had advanced microbiology and pathophysiology courses that ran smoother and better. Avoid her.
reminds me of my high school statistics teacher(btw-that class helps with econ) she is really interested in her subject and is always in a good mood
Sharon Ryan sucks as a person and should never be able to teach seeing as she apparently has no possible idea how to teach.
Utterly disgusted in the quality of this teacher (not professor that would mean that they met my standards of a professor).

She was the most organized teacher I have ever had and it made this class one of my favorites freshman year. She posts all of her lecture notes online (very helpful!), exams are very similar to written homework, extra credit GAMES are given online(Do these they are worth your time), online quizes are harder but can obviously be done in groups.

Sharon Ryan is a good teacher. If you attened most of the lectures and all of your RSD classes it isn't hard at all. The exams are EXACTLY the same as the written homework she gives, so as long as you do those you will do well on the exams. She gives you all the material you need to do well and even a couple of extra credit assignments.

Relies heavily on online Aplia system to teach. She eliminated RSD sessions, which did not turn out to be a good move. If you prefer a human to teach you econ., instead of a computer, then don't waste your money on this course. Utterly disgraceful.

Worst class I have ever taken. Avoid at all costs. When you are handed exams, you will not know what to do. It saddens me that the university is still employing her. I will be taking similar course elsewhere - after a semester in econ. 1100 I have no basis of micro. econ. (Do not take course online, she runs course). I went to all classes & reviews

Useless lectures, impossible online quizes.  While the exams are not impossible the half hour time limit is frustrating and causes students to work quickly and make mistakes.  Partial credit rare.  Do not take this class.

Material covered in class may not always correspond with exams. 30 minute time limit on exams can prove both stressful and detrimental to many. Although Dr. Ryan would disagree with me... she could at least send out reminder emails for the large amount of online work she requires. NO STRUCTURE (as RSD was eliminated)

I transferred from Northwestern and my advisor suggested I take this class. Her lectures were unlike anything I have ever experienced. She spoke a mile a minute and always had an attitude if you came to her office hours. My TA was ridiculous, condescending,a not very helpful at all. For the sake of your sanity and your GPA, do not take this class.

Sharon Ryans lectures have absolutely no structure and are very very difficult to take notes off of.  Go to all RSD classes and make sure you very clearly understand the homework and you might be able to pass with a B. Maybe.

Sharon Ryan is a fast paced professor but is very easy to understand. If you pay attention to her, you will be able to learn the material easy. Tests can be hard because of the time limit but take advantage of the E.C. games because they can be a life saver. Take all the optional stuff: quizzes, hw, and test! A's are possible.

Hardest C+ ive ever earned. Ryan and TAs were NEVER on the same page which made meeting with her for help useless. "Help sessions" are a huge joke-1 poor TA in a small room with 10+ frustrated/desperate students while Ryan refuses to open her door (the NEXT ROOM btw) The quintessential "evil" college professor.

When taking this class, I constantly finished exams thinking I had done wonderfully. Too bad, however, that they always came back stamped with a C or a D. Only because of the RSD did I manage to do well. It's pretty pathetic when you do 100% of the work and studying, and are in the top 5% of your class... and STILL can't get an A.

well... sharon ryan is undescribable. i worked my ass off went to every class and still got a c thanks to the curve. thank god for the RSD or i would have not passed. go to class and do all the work and take every opportunity for make up work. the tests are all written and graphs. she goes off on so many tangents and circles you cant understand her

I just finished Sharon's course this semester and with the help of a tutor I passed with a C. I have to say that I put no real effort into studying so I'm sure with effort I could have gotten a C. Do the hw and u can do the test. Study the MC she puts up for the final. She takes your highest scores and lets you drop a test. All in all...not bad.

Her lectures are VERY clear. If you attend lectures, study for exams, you can at least get a B-.  The course material is hard, but Dr. Ryan goes over it multiple times to make sure that everyone gets it. It's my second time taking Econ. Took it with a different instructor: that class sucked! With Ryan it made complete sense.
hate her, her class consists of making random facts up
hard

Not hard material to learn, but hard to get a good grade in this class.  You study for hours and think you'll do well on the test and when you get it back u dont do so well.  Even straight A students like myself are surprised and still get a c or so on the exams.  doesn't explain topics in great detail and yet still manages to repeat everything
Terrible, avoid at all costs.
Nooooooooooooooooooo....don't take this class.

You will go to class and she will talk at about 1,000 miles and hour and after you are able to comprehend her, it all sounds pretty good. You will study for the tests and look over the material she has given you and then you will get and F or a D on the exam and you think to yourself "what the hell I am a 3.2 student!" Trust me, avoid the class....

Ok, I'm going to try and clear up some misconceptions here. The course material is not exceedingly difficult. The work load will not devour hours out of your days. And the tests... well the tests on the other hand will probably make you want to cry. Even though the material in 1014 is rather simple when you take a minute to work it over on your own
Horrendous, worst teacher of all time.

I'm a 2nd yr. student, I get A's, I try in all classes & study 4 EVERYTHING. I did all the hmwk,study sheets, practice exams, read every page of the book,&got a B- after the curve. Her TA's sucked 2. Mine hated me from day 1, & once I got a 2/5 on a quiz, and she handed it back to me,and smirked, and said "maybe you should consider studying"
worst prof in my history of being an MU student
bad girl ,he mama would hve taught her some manners....baaad puppy
Don't take this class
if you go to mu you've probably heard how bad her class is, but then it fits into your schedule perfectly or something and you'll say "oh it can't be as bad as everyone says" ...well it is.
none of her lectures have anything to do with the exams practically, its stupid. if do the homework well then you will know the test. she isn't a good teacher.

This women teaches that free trade is good and tariffs are nice. Ummm... contradictory? She never teaches whats on her tests and I have learned from a foreigner TA who barely speaks English on what I am tested on. Avoid her like the plague, or clap, or ebola. Horrible.
if you go to mizzou you already know.... its bad.... good luck
She is undeniably hard. I didn't attend ALL her lectures but you REALLY need to read the book and MEMORIZE the hand-outs that she provides. GO TO LAB! Follow these and you will do fine.

Really not that bad. Even if you do really bad she curves the test in your favor 99% of the time. Do her practice tests to get a feel for the exams. Her personality may not be the best, but you can survive. Attend class and you'll get the material

Horrible professor. She is a pure example of how not to teach a class. What she discusses in lecture, isn't on her tests. The curves do help, but she is just awful. If I was to do it over again, I would have not taken her class.

I braced myself for the absolute worst and it turns out the bark is much worse than the bite. She gives massive curves on each test (nearly 20 points for some). I don't think she was really all that open if you need help but the TAs are. The last exam was completely different than the the other two. She smirked evily during exams.
Ryan was one of the most practical and straight forward professors that I've ever had. The horror stories about her come from freshmen newbies that are not accustomed to college classes yet.
So I took this class and it was super-easy.  I have no idea what everyone else is talking about.

Honestly, even though this class was super hard, Ryan makes herself very available for help. Despite students labeling her as a notorious ****, she's seriously pretty nice. I missed my final by accident, and she was cool about it and let me take a make-up exam even though I had no real excuse. Pretty sweet, ended up with a B+!

It's easy to say she's a bad professor because her class is hard, but she really explains the concept well, and her expectations aren't unreasonable. I did very poorly on my first test, but I hadn't studied well. I talked to my TA and prepared more, and I did much better. Take advantage of all the online quizzes and the massive curve.
assignments were horrible
do NOT take econ from sharon ryan. you WILL regret it.

She was TERRIBLE! this class is required for most students...so there's really no way around her. I went to every lecture and lab and still barely passed. After putting her academic probation, you think this school would wise up and fire her! This was by-far my worst and most hated class. I pitty anyone who has to take this class with her!
No Comments
Her class is not that hard if you read the textbook.  That is all you have to do, no attendance necessary.
She is the honestly the worst teacher I've ever had. She is a total **** and has no clue how to teach. You can study for hours and still flunk the test. She's awful!
grrrrr
All she does is discuss real life applications on economics, read the book to do well on the tests.

AWFUL teacher her idea of being a good teacher is making the test so hard that all of the students fail and she has to curve the entire class, in lecture halls if 400+ she takes attendance which is of no benefit to the student unless you attend every lecture done take her class!!

Her class is extremely hard. I often understood the notes. I did the multiple choice online and the practice problems. I also had a tutor. I'm an A student and I strugged through this class. Often her test seemed completely different or drastically manipulated from the notes. I squeaked by with a B after the huge curve.

Sharon was GREAT at explaining concepts clearly. To do well in her class, you MUST attend every class, otherwise you will quickly get behind. At the end of the semester, she will boost you to the next letter grade if you've attended most of her lectures. She also posts her old tests online, so DEFINITELY use those. I highly recommend her.
for the tests: read the mc online and know how to do all of the problems from recitation and you'll do well...going to class for that EC and doing all extra surveys helps too.

I tempted to rate my TA instead; she's the only one I learned anything from. I went to a lecture once, it was pretty worthless so I'd say just go to all of your labs, do the online quizzes and study with friends for the tests. It's really not a hard class.
