Very very very sweet but assigns too much work
The course was so easy informational. It was self paced so I finished in like 2-3 weeks. There is a quiz after each section so make sure you take notes.

Took this course online and all of the lectures were great! There are assignments to go along with each lecture so I do recommend taking notes. That being said, the assignments are pretty simple and easy to get 100% on. This class was a self-paced eight-week class that I got done within the first two weeks of the class.

Took this class online over the summer and enjoyed it. Dr. Sharpe would respond to my emails usually within a couple hours. If you just read the materials and ask questions when you have them you'll pass.
Dr. Sharpe WILL NOT let any of her students fail the class, unless you have the inability to show up to. Just put in your best effort, ask questions when needed, and just trust that you will be fine.

She is a great teacher overall, however, her assignments are so much work and she gives a very little grade. There is so much reading involved and booklets you have to purchase. reviews.comment: Dr. Sharpe is a great teacher. I actually enjoyed going to her class. However, she assigns a lot of writing assignments, and it is hard to stay on top of assignments. She is extremely approachable, she even puts her personal phone # on the syllabus. She just makes the course more work than it needs to be.

Sharpe is one of the nicest and approachable professors at MU. However, here classes are no walk in the park.  Exam average were 58, and refuses to curve! However, she does off extra credit, but it is incredibly difficult.  She does want her students to learn, but will make her classes harder than they need to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Sharpe is without a doubt the best professor at Mizzou. Ive had her for a few classes now and she will go above and beyond for any of her students. Wonderful woman!
Most helpful teacher in the department.

Very helpful and nice.

Very good professor. Professor Shin was super funny, gave really good feedback on every assignment, and overall just made class enjoyable. I took English 1000.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy English class, you have 5 excused absences.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Srinivas is easily my favorite teacher. His content is engaging and he has a way of teaching that makes me actually want to learn and pay attention during class in general. He works very well with students, slowing down when needed and repeating slides or info when students aren't picking up concepts. I have always disliked coding until this course
It was one of the best courses I took at Mizzou. I feel well prepared for the job market in analytics.

Eng Quality Control was a university level class that prepares you for your IE career. Prof. Srinivas has an amazing way to deliver his lectures. Successfully explains complex concepts in simple words and really cares about your learning. Constantly gives you feedback at the beginning of every class. Be ready for a Python analytics group project!

Systems Simulation was an interesting class that helped teach the Simio program. However, lectures were focused on data and stats, so Simio was only learned in lab. Group project is tough, need a large amount of data for it. No rubric for final report or presentation. Class structure is great. Sharan can be tough at times though so work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The whole class is notes, so study the material sooner for the exams. Exams aren't difficult if you put in the time. There is no homework so the class is graded on the group activities, attendance in discussion and the exams. Your lowest exam is dropped and he curves the class. Overall, he's a very nice guy and wants his students to succeed.

You can pass this class, but will need to do outside work. In the most respectful way possible, he is hard to understand and I found that impacting my learning. I would sit front row and still found it hard to undestand him. Glazes over confusing concepts. Make sure to go to dicussion-helped me lots with understanding. Exams are not too hard.

He is really nice and funny. His accent is not super hard to understand. There's not any homework for a grade. The class is exam heavy, but they're not hard. There's a lot of content but if you study you'll do just fine. Compared to what I've heard about the other genetics teachers, he sounds the best/easiest. Does give extra credit.

Shiu is a great professor, he is not hard to understand, the tests are very easy, and there are many opportunities to prepare for exams. People fail his class because they don't study, then resort to racism and blame his accent for their bad grades. Good luck premeds who apparently expect to never have a mentor, colleague, or patient with an accent

Overall a great class, would definitely take him over the other genetics professor (what I have heard from friends). People who say "I can't understand him" are ridiculous, his english is fine with a slight accent. He has extra credit points EVERY lecture if you answer questions. TAs are also of great use in this class!

I love dr. shiu. he is such a kind man and really cares about his material and students. He's very funny and approachable. idk why people say he has a heavy accent because he doesn't. the class is test heavy but the material is strait from the slides, so if you attend class, take notes, and study the slides you will be fine. seriously love this guy

Shiu cares about you and your grade. He is difficult to understand, however, if you take the time to see him and the TAs, you will be fine. He is super fun and outgoing. The class is basically just graded on the tests, which is hard because one mc question is 10 points, so you must know your stuff!

purely test based grading. Fail your test=fail the class. Though they are curved but you dont know youre true grade till the end of semester past the W period so that causes a lot of stress. I feel bad ratin him "ok" because he is super nice but the lack of question on the test (~17) make it so even if you knew >70% taught things u could fail

Shiu is hard to understand, and there is basically nothing more to your grade than exams. TALK TO YOUR TAs. You don't know your grade the ENTIRE time you're in this course until after finals which gave me extreme anxiety. Very lecture-heavy. Exams are so detailed and sometimes over very minute things. Gotta have. big work ethic.

His lectures felt like he was reading straight from the textbook. There was a lot of unnecessary jargon and it was hard to keep up with. The tests were hard and worth a lot of points, but he drops the lowest score and grades on a curve, so I managed to keep a solid grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can teach yourself, you'll do great. His lectures are awful - he's very hard to understand and he simply just reads off the slides. The discussion section was a lifesaver and his TAs are a godsend. Overall the course was just 4 tests weighted 238 points each. If there's another teacher available, save yourself and switch.

Dr. Shiu is an amazing professor, his classes are exciting and you can tell he cares about the material he teaches. 90% of the class is graded from tests. Ensure you study well and understand the concepts for the first few tests. You have one dropped exam. also, the top 25% of the class gets an automatic A- if u don't have an A already

This class is mainly about memorizing a ton of slides. Grading criteria is not clear. The only good thing is the TAs; they're helpful, so make sure to ask them for help. If you want a good grade, start working hard from the beginning. Honestly, if you can, avoid taking this class with this professor. It might save you some stress.

It is so much information to learn for a singular test. This class is not just memorization. You have to actually understand the concepts along with memorization. Make sure to go to office hours if you want a clear understanding of everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is all memorization of hundreds of slides. The grading criteria is not clear, you do not know your grade. The final is actually the last test and a cumulative final, so dropping a test doesn't really matter. The TAs are the one good part about this class, lean on your TAs if you want to pass.
The only points in this class are for tests and attending discussions. The material did not make sense to me.

Professor Shiu is a fun teacher who obviously loves genetics. The class is very lecture heavy, however as long as you keep up with the slides and attend discussion, you do not really have to go to the lectures. Exams are not too bad, but they cover a large amount of material.

The lectures are really detailed but the tests are pretty easy. Just know the overall ideas and concepts, don't focus on the small details. Know how to do the examples and problems he does in class because those are usually the ones on the tests. The TAs are so helpful in preparing you for the test. Participate and go to class, easy A.
the lectures are so boring, he reads word for word off the slides the tests are very easy if you pay attention in discussion and study he is a funny guy, just teaches boring material

Dr. Shiu was awesome. The class is just memorization of the slides and it is about 120 slides of memorization per test. He is a funny teacher and helped me through rescheduling an exam due to health. Super great and the tests are easy if you study week before the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class. His lectures are very traditional with lots of slides and pictures, you must watch them before the tests. The tests are a little complicated but you just have to apply the notes. He's funny and passionate. But, you're only graded on tests and participation in discussion, your grade depends if you're in the top 25% of total point

He is a super funny professor and adds weird pictures in his lectures to make you laugh. His tests are somewhat hard. You will definitely need to study. The discussion portion of the class was EXTREMELY helpful when it comes to his tests. If you study all of his lectures slides, you will get a good grade in his class.

Dr. Shiu wasn't a good teacher. His tests were confusing (he gives you the notes, but he asks very about very minuscule things and there is SO MUCH material to learn). He doesn't like when people ask questions as he thinks he's the best. ever. Every time I asked a question, I was looked at like I was stupid. Take a different professor, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Shiu is a funny and nice guy. I wish I could like him as a professor but he has a terrible teaching style. He is very difficult to understand. GET A TEST BANK. His tests are absolutely ridiculous and he will ask questions over a minute detail that you think is completely insignificant. Be prepared to teach yourself. Easy enough to get an A though.

Shiu for genetics over anyone else. He is the easiest professor for the subject. His test literally is just memorization. To study for his test just go over the problems he provides in class and go to TA office hours. They really help. Go to discussion it is easy points along with the few bonus points. Easiest test was #3, don't take final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Shiu is knowledgeable of Genetics, but I felt the class was structured in a way that makes it difficult for students to succeed. Material is tough to remember, so make it a priority to memorize your notes. Tests are usually /248 points, 120 being m.c., the rest being short answer and other questions. Lab is taken for grade, so try to go.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not a good professor but the notes that he hands out are good enough that you can teach the materials to yourself. Tests are just memorization of the notes.

The way he teaches does not engage students because he is hard to understand most of the time. He gives all the notes on handouts before each class period which minimizes how much students pay attention. His lectures are boring with the exception of maybe three lectures. His grading scale is strange and you won't know your grade until the last day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Shui was a class that you needed to memorize the lecture notes basically. All of this stuff is espically important when studying for the MCAT. He went into great detail to go over the specifics and things that are important. It is ALOT of material, but it is worth it overall. Also at the end there is a good curve that happens.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Shui is a terrible teacher and could care less about his students.  But he's easier that the other genetics teacher, and as long as you understand the problems, you should do fine.  But he's really so apathetic about teaching :(
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: For the first 3 tests, study the powerpoint slides from in lecture & you'll get an A.  However, the 4th test is paired with a cumulative final (optional) and is much more difficult.  He gives extra practice problems in class that are almost exactly the same as the ones on the tests.  Go to recitation, my TA was great at explaining key concepts.

Shiu gave you what you needed to pass the class. He provided notes each lecture and the tests were solely lecture-based.  Never really used the textbook, except for animations sometimes. Discussion really helped clarify certain topics, so don't skip! Also, take pictures of the LGS questions when he puts them up, because they will likely be on test!

DONT BUY THE BOOK. Lecture based lass, no need to waste 200+ dollars. I made the mistake of doing so. Literally in class problems are the same as the tests so it made the class easy. All TA's ive heard are good and chill.
DO NOT SKIP CLASS , there's no tegrity classes. DO NOTBUY TEXTBOOK, study the lecture slides he prints them out for you, never used the textbook.

He prints off his lectures and hands them to you in the beginning of every class, there's usually 12 slides done per class, but rarely it's 24. The discussion is where you do most of your learning, and that's where there's attendance points. There's 4 tests and the top 25% of the class gets an A, but it's not that hard if you start studying early.
I would highly recommend Dr. Shiu for genetics. There is no reason you should not end up with an A or B
He gives you all the notes on a worksheet before every class.  As long as you study those you will do fine on the exam.

His class really wasn't that hard if you studied his lecture notes and went to RSD.  He usually tells you if you have any problems go to RSD and ask your TA. The first three tests weren't extremely hard, but the last one is combined with an optional final which is very hard.  The in class exercises don't count for anything, don't worry if you miss.

Dr. Shiu is going to begin the semester by telling you how hard his class is going to be. Don't let this fool you! He is one of the easiest genetics professors at Mizzou. The first three tests are super easy (class average around 80%). The last test however is really hard (STUDY!). He does give a lot of extra credit, but it won't make a difference.

Shiu is a pretty decent professor.  I didn't use the book at all and still got hundreds on the tests.  He reads word for word off his powerpoints so going to class is kind of pointless.  Definitely go to discussion.  My TA was really good about clarifying the concepts on the exams.  It's definitely possible to get an A.
Overall class is interesting. You don't need to go to class but go to discussion the TAs are very helpful and will explain how to do the problems better than he can in lecture.

Genetics was a hard course and Dr. Shiu was a good teacher. The reason he " read off of his slides" is because he has to cover an enormous amount of material and can't sit their and read all slow. As long as you studied the notes, and read the book, the exams were no problem. For everyone else complaining UMC isn't about teachers spoon feeding.

Genetics with Shiu was awful! Funny guy but the class is difficult because he does not teach AT ALL.  Only reads off of slides and TAs teach as much as they can. Make sure you get old tests or take with John David.

Terrible class. Shiu spends every lecture reading directly off of power point slides that are also available online. You never have to open the book or do any of the optional homework because your T.A. will do all that for you in RSD. Point distribution in test totally screws you over--250 point tests with about 15-ish questions each.

Genetics was easy with his slide printoffs.  Tests were hard only if you did not review the slide prints. Make sure you get the slides either from a friend or going to class they are all that matter.  Occasional hard question with actual work thrown into exam.  Shiu is hilarious though in front of the class.

Shiu is funny and kinda goofy at times, but i feel like I taught genetics to myself. I would def go to lectures, but all he does is read off slides and you write in words. RSDs are key to learning. He is hard to understand, tests are difficult, but A's are possible if you study your slides hard! Not too bad of a class.
Good teacher, kinda funny.

I was not impressed by his style of teaching. He read the powerpoints and had a hard time just understanding students questions. I basically taught genetics to myself. Also, when he reviewed for tests, he would go back over the slides and say "know this...yeah, you  need to know that..." =pointless. class wasnt too bad and i ended up with an A.

Pretty good for his first semester teaching.  All the test information came straight from  the notes, so I never read the textbook once, and managed (easily) to pull off an A.  As long as you're not lazy, pay attention in class, and look at your notes a few times a week outside of class, you don't even need to do the optional homework to get an A

Dr. Shiu is actually a really funny guy. It was his first semester teaching and all he did was read us the powerpoints which were summaries of the textbook basically word for word. I pretty much taught myself Genetics. His tests were either really easy or really hard. But, the final is optional which was nice.
great professor, very knowledgable, tough grader, be prepared for exams and papers, very supportive, amazing lectures
amazing lectures
tough grader but amazing lectures
I thought he did a great job of demonstrating the culture and history of North and South Korea throughout the class. He balanced the large-scale history with his own personal experiences really well.
Fun lectures, helpful in and outside of class, enthusiastic about her teaching

This is one of the easiest classes you could possibly take. She is so sweet and gives perfect scores on basically everything. I didn't read a single harry potter book and was fine, you can look up most of the answers!

I absolutely loved Dr. Cohen. She is passionate about the topic and really makes you think beyond the pages. If you haven't read the series yet you definitely need to read the books weekly. Grade based on weekly assignments, discussions & EC, and a final project. The class is really fun and stress free. She cares about her students a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: There is up to 225 points of extra credit given in the semester. Each discussion board is worth 50 points and each assignment is worth 100 points. You also get to go back and redo up to two assignments. The easiest class I have ever taken. Loved the professor, she was really nice and very accommodating.

Dr. Cohen is so so nice. She puts effort into every lecture and, while lectures can feel very long, it takes little effort to do well in the class. She wants students to do well and grades papers mostly on effort and thought. Lectures can feel boring though, especially if youve read the books before.

Professor Cohen is amazing. She cares so much about her students and gives so many chances to redo papers that you may have received a bad grade on. She makes class exciting to come to and always has a great attitude. 100% would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Some people may ask "Why take a Harry Potter class?" I'll tell you why: it's a good GPA booster and there is so much cool behind the scene information you wouldn't otherwise know about. She's super friendly and has a magical way of somehow being in class one second and in her office the next!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is absolutely wonderful and Dr. Cohen is very informed and understanding.

Dr. Cohen makes class very enjoyable and is very knowledgeable about the topic. Be prepared to do a lot of reading. She gives excellent feedback on papers, and is willing to meet with students outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: love Harry Potter and love this class essays are kind of a drag to grind out but graded pretty loosely

I never read a Harry Potter book but was an extreme/avid movie watcher and I got an A in this class. She offers several extra credit opportunities and adds those points onto paper grades. Not many grades in this class... 60% papers (3), 10% attendance, and 30% final. If you love HP, take this... if you don't... don't. Super fun prof and passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is the second class I've had with Dr. Cohen (World Religions was first) and in both classes she is an exceptional professor. She is extremely knowledgeable and her lectures are both fascinating and entertaining. She will work with you if you need help and really cares about her students. Strongly recommend, would take her again in a heartbeat!

Her teaching is enthusiastic and knowledgeable, and her interest in the topic comes through clearly. Her lectures are interesting and always have new information, but don't crowd you with useless things. If you pay attention in lecture, you can pretty much pass the class. The books assigned are VERY needed, as they are the focus and you need them.

The class itself wasn't too difficult but Dr. Cohen gave out more extra credit than any teacher I've ever had combined. Every time there's a lecture in town she gives you 3 extra credit points if you go and write her summary. I went every one and ended up with over 80 extra credit points on my papers and final. You have to try fail.

LOVED THIS CLASS! She knows her stuff and is super helpful. 3 short essays, a midterm and a final. Go to class (it's a really cool class anyways) and pay attention and there's no way for you to fail. Offers a TON of extra credit.

I took Religions of the World 2110 and have no regrets. The grades in this class are 3 essays, the midterm and the final. Neither of these is really difficult  and she gives out tonnes of extra credit opportunities. She's always open to questions and is genuinely interested in helping those who are struggling. 1010 would take class again.

AWESOME professor. This is the second class I've taken of hers and I am so happy I got the chance. She really knows what she's talking about and she makes it interesting. She's a great person. Easy to talk to and ask for help.

I LOVE HER. This class was amazing. Easy A for sure! Easy grader and she allows rewrites on papers and gives extra credit opportunities. I hated missing class because her lectures were so interesting. GO TO CLASS because it will help you SO much with the papers. Overall I don't recommend if HP isn't your thing because you have to read all 7 books.

Very sweet and cute little professor. It's fun just to listen to her accent as she lectures. However, she does lecture, the entire time. Even when taking a Harry Potter class, I would get bored after a solid hour of note taking and really no interactive participation. But the class is good, the assignments are easy and I'd take another class w her
I  love this class. She is a great teacher and very knowledgeable.

As long as you go to class you will be fine. I felt the class was boring because this will never help me in my future. She repeated herself a lot. She was very helpful when I went to her office hours and you can tell she is intelligent and knows her stuff. Overall I don't think I would take this course again because I'm not a huge fan of HP.
She was my favorite professor at Mizzou. Her class was always interesting and you learned a lot of information. Her stories are well worth going to class for!
Great professor! I took two different classes with her, and she was fantastic! Very clear, helpful and obviously very knowledgeable. Very easy to contact and work with. I highly recommend her!

She was so nice and truly interested in the class (Harry Potter: Magic and Religion). Obviously don't take the class if you haven't read the HP series. Otherwise the class is ridiculously easy, pretty interesting, and the notes are all given online. Extra readings weren't needed for good grades. Cohen was a great professor.
I had Harry Potter: Magic and Religion with her and she was awesome.  So sweet and helpful.

I took her World religion class and liked it so much I went on to take her Hinduism course, which was amazing. She is extremely knowledgeable about the religion and even lived in India for a few years. My favorite part of class was when she would tell stories from the Mahabharata and the Ramayana and other Hindu texts. I absolutely loved this class
If you go to class and pay attention you should be fine. The final was comprehensive so it was mostly just a lot of material to retain but very interesting. Always enjoyed class.
Very pleasant and thoughtful. Excellent prof and class.
good teacher
Good teacher, lots of information.   This class was really interesting and overall enjoyable.

She is a really good teacher, she makes the class worth going to.  There is a lot to know in this class, but it's all really interesting.  She takes attendance every day, and there are only 2 tests.  If you are looking for an interesting (but not blow-off) class, this is highly recommended.
Very good teacher.  She is very interesting and keeps the class intertaining.  It is not a blow-off course.  It is work, but very good and worth it.  I highly recommend her as a teacher.

Sipe is an unreliable professor and is often arrogant and mean. He accuses students of cheating when their written French is different from their spoken French, gives very little information about assignments, grades late, and is extremely passive aggressive in communication. He expects a lot from his students but doesn't put a lot in himself.

He was easily my favorite professor of the semester. I had prior experience in French, but he made my desire to continue even greater. I mean, he literally skateboarded for all of us. Doesn't get much cooler than that.

Monsieur Sipe is fantastic! He has a strong passion for the French language, and it really shows. He genuinely wants his students to do well, and will do a lot to help you succeed. The VHL textbook assignments are a pain, but they do help you learn. If you show genuine interest in learning French and participate, you'll have an amazing time.

Sipe is such a great professor. He will definitely call you out if you're not participating but it's only because he cares about helping his students improve. As far as grading papers he gives good corrections and for speaking exams he picks out a mistake and has you correct it. If he likes you he *might* let you talk in English occasionally.

He's a good teacher, passionate about what he teaches, and genuinely wants his students to do well. The only thing I really have is that he's very disorganized and doesn't like to take responsibility when he forgets things. He can be intense one on one; he is not afraid to single people out. But on the other hand, he's a really nice, positive guy.
Dan Sipe is an amazing teacher! He really cares about his students and takes the time to help. Ask him what "nosebox" means for extra credit.
Dr. Sipe was one of my favorite French professors!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: professor sipe is a great professor! he can be kind of intense one on one (i once balled uncontrollably in his office) but he genuinely believes all his students can succeed with out any excuses. he pushes you out of your comfort zone sometimes but only enough to challange you which is what sets him apart from other teachers.
Le meilleur des professeurs!Prenez ce cours et allez visiter la France, un tres beau pays!
Great professor!  Incredibly helpful, very humorous always cracking jokes.
Cares about students and well being.  you must put in effort to succeed, including reading,  can be a pushover if you demonstrate need whether it be true or not is irrelevant
Great prof.!   Extremely difficult but worth one's time and he's not that bad to have to look at
Very enthusiastic and makes funny jokes, however, you must take the class seriously and work on grammar!
Daniel Sipe is an excellent professor. He makes class interesting and worth going to. He enriches the French experience.
She gave lots of cheese in my class with nuts in them. She told me to do the math and I go do them.
I thought she was a good teacher.  She was always there for help and she graded pretty easy.  She was easy to understand, and helped out on the difficult subject.
The class material is very hard but the teacher is a fox so its very easy to make it to class.  She is very nice and always giggles in class.  Her European accent brings grown men to their knees.

I had him at a different school that isn't listed here for an online class, Media Literacy. He didn't give great rubrics for grading and when he did, his grading did not match the rubrics listed. I felt like I was shooting arrows in the dark. His recorded lectures weren't very concise and wandered a bit, making it hard to reference in assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He clearly cares about Journalism, but tends to have a condescending attitude. You feel less like he wants to teach and help you learn, and more like he wants to make you feel dumb about what youve made. I dont recall feeling like he taught me, but rather just criticized my work. It was very discouraging and not what you want from the #1 J school

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. I had two panic attacks due to the material. However, Judd is a great teacher who guided me and my classmates through all the stress to make us better students. Grateful for the opportunity to have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Had him as a professor for 4804 & 4806. Incredibly knowledgeable and really wants his students to succeed. Don't try to just skate by though - put in your best effort and he'll give you his time and guidance in return. Spend time in the lab outside of class and come with questions. Is willing to go above & beyond and help you in any way he can.

Judd gave good feedback, and I learned a lot, but most of the time he tried really hard to be funny when I just wanted to know what I did wrong. No clear grading criteria; you'd turn in a project, be torn apart in front of the rest of the class, then receive a grade a few hours later with no explanation as to where exactly you lost points.

Judd is by far one of the best professors I've ever had. He's a tough grader, but gives great feedback and pushes you to be better. I took the mobile section, so Judd had more freedom to structure the class however he wanted. Class atmosphere was laid back and fun. He even took time one day to teach us about resumes and the future in the j-school.

One of the best profs I've had (I also took 4804). HOWEVER in 4806 Judd is so focused on corralling the 4804 kiddos that he will rarely go out of his way to check-in/help you like he did in 4804. Go out of your way to update him about how your newsrooms are going. Required quizzes/blog/portfolio site are just busy work unfortunately.

Has a big ego and is a tough grader but really teaches you a lot. I thrived in high school journalism, but was torn to shreds in this class in the best way possible. He knows what he is talking about and gives awesome pointers beyond the general topics. Left this class feeling ahead of the game as I continue in the j-school.

Judd is by far the best teacher I have ever had. If you want to be a the best possible journalist you can be, you have to take one of his courses. You will learn more in one semester than you will in your entire four years of college.

This man quite literally changed my life. He is an extremely tough grader and has very high expectations, but he will help you if you show and effort and ask for assistance. He really knows his stuff. Listen to him and you will go very far in the J-School. He's also not as scary as he likes to think he is ;)

Judd is extremely helpful. He really, really knows his stuff. He is and knows he is one of the hardest teachers in the J-school. He's a bit of a temperamental ass sometimes, but other than that, he will really help you grow.

HARD! Maybe the hardest grader I've had at Mizzou. Gives extra credit at the end of the semester, which helps. Learned more in this class than all my other J classes so far, so it was probably worth the pain. He explains a lot of stuff in class and is always around in his office to work with you. Tries to be funny. Doesn't always succeed.

I absolutely love Kani!! He is the absolute best. I was a summer student and worked with him in the lab and I had such a great time! He is such a good listener and is great at explaining things. I have learned so much and this is the most fun I've ever had working in a lab.
I was a summer research student and loved working in the lab with Kanishka!
Kanishka rocked was the best TA for Chem 1320 and the only reason I made it through the course.
Kanishka Sikligar is one of the best people in the chemistry department. Thank you for all your help.
Very helpful & an amazing professor! One of the only professors that can make chemistry make sense! So grateful to have had this professor over the summer.
He is so thoughtful and actually cares about his students. Will do anything to make sure his students are learning the material and goes the extra mile no matter what.

My favorite TA ever! He truly cares about his students, loves to talk and help you learn. I believe he would make any upper level Chemistry class bearable. He is good at breaking things down into simpler terms and making boring and difficult concepts fun to learn.
A fun TA that is always willing to help

Angel Kani was my favorite TA/Professor I've had in any level of schooling. The actual Keller lecture was insufferable but at least every week I got to look forward to actually having fun in my Lab. It's not just about fun though, I learned more valuable information in my 2 hours a week than I did the entirety of the lectures from Keller
I would give this man a 100/5 if i could!!! He is not only the most helpful and TA but he is just so easy to talk to and ask questions!! he is probably the only reason i dont entirely hate chemistry
Kanishka is awesome! 1330 with Bernskoetter was very tough, but Kanishka made it bearable. He is so kind and wants his students to do well. He's a lot of fun to be around, 10/10 would recommend!

Great professor. Explained difficult topics in chemistry and made connections between units more easily understood and accessible to students. Will break down any topic into the simplest term so that anyone can understand the material.
Awesome TA. Loves to help his students learn and is reliable. Would 100% recommend!
Kanishka helps foster a sense of community within his classes and he goes above and beyond to help his students understand the material.
Absolutely amazing. Goes well out of his way to connect with students and makes sure everyone understands content for labs and the topics discussed in lectures.

Kanishka is AMAZING! If you dont take his class literally just quit. He makes sure you understand all the content as well as reteaching is the content in lecture. He truly cares about each one of his students and tells us everyday. He wants you to win and be successful and that helps so much in pushing you to do your best. Take Kanishka.
Kanishka is amazing! I have had him for two semesters now and he is the only reason I can somewhat stomach chemistry (lol). Definitely take his class if you can!!

Hands down best TA at Mizzou. Helped my lab section survive Kellers Chem1320. He knows when students dont understand something and does a great job explaining material. Also truly cares about you as a person. Simply an amazing teacher.

Kanishkas goal is for all of his students to love chemistry and he makes that clear from the beginning. He understands that the material is not easy, but does his best to make sure that his students grasp the concepts with clarity. His lectures are interesting and he loves class participation. Hes a fun guy and I couldnt recommend him more.

Love this man so much. He truly wants his student to succeed and learn, and will do  everything he can to help them. Idk if he wants to teach long term but he has a true gift with students. Would recommend him to anyone who has a chance to have him as TA
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The best TA at mizzou. Not only does he understand what he is teaching, but does everything he can to help you learn. He was always willing to stop and make sure we understood. He an amazing teacher but also cares for his students, he wanted to get to know us and we became friends, I can't wait to have him again next year.
The most goofy TA I've ever had. I love him so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Kanishka genuinely cares about each and everyone of his students. I am a biology major and went into the lab thinking I would hate this semester. With Kanishka, I was able to challenge myself while still learning to enjoy the different material as well. I enjoyed going to lab every week and I highly recommend you take a class with him if possible!

Kanishka really cares about his students and wants to help them in anyway you can. He's one of the best TA's I have ever had. He makes chemistry easy to understand and sends you notes about what he covered. Be ready to goof off a bit in lab with him. He's very understanding and is a pretty easy grader. Just label your stuff and put some effort in

Kanishka is one of the best TA's I've had. He's super helpful, wants you to do well, and will respect and build a relationship with you if you try to do so with him. He wrote me a fantastic letter of recommendation for my program.

Seriously the best TA Ive ever had. He essentially adopted me because my TA was bad and he treated me as his own student. Provides so much help and is widely respected by all students. He always provides great practice problems. He truly cares for his students and is a very effective teacher.

Kanishka is a true gem. In the struggles of chemistry, Kanishka provides valuable feedback and is always willing to help a student. Between studying for exams, preparing for labs, and understanding the lecture, Kanishka provides ample practice problems and exams. He is a real angel.
Angel
Most amazing TA I've ever had, so smart and helpful. Makes going to lab not totally awful. 10/10 take any chem lab with him.

Great TA! He absolutely loves chemistry and is so passionate about teaching, I've never seen anyone enjoy a subject as much as he does. He grades fairly and wants to help everyone reach their full potential, going above and beyond with handing out extra information and practice problems. Great person to talk and get to know as well.
fair grader, always had fun life applications for the lab. best chem TA

He's a beautiful soul who makes you feel comfortable by wandering around and gossiping with students. It's hilarious to watch because he'll go to group 1 and speak with them, then flutter to group2 and talk with them about what was said in group1, and down the line. I've never particularly liked chemistry but he has made me enjoy it.

Kanishka is the best TA ever! Not only is he very passionate about chemistry and is good at explaining each topic, he makes class/lab fun! He is usually an easy grader as long as he sees that you know the material and wants the students to do well. He gives extra practice problems before the exams that make it easy to go back and apply concepts.

Kanishka loves chemistry more than anyone else I know! He really takes his time to explain and break down complicated topics for students and even sends his notes to everyone after class. Hes always available at any time if you have trouble understanding the material and he makes chemistry fun and easier. Best TA Ive had in any class ever!

Kanishka was probably the best TA I have met for a chemistry class. He takes time to make sure you know what is going on, he ACTUALLY listens to your concerns, and most importantly he cares about the well being of his students.  Yes, in his section there is more work than others, but it is never pointless work and actually helps.
On a lot of the labs he doesnt make you do the last trial that other TAs do make you do. He emails all of his notes so if you dont understand something you can always go back.

Kanishka is hands down the best TA I have had during my time at Mizzou! He is absolutely hilarious, and truly wants his students to succeed! He wants to get to know his students, and finds fun ways to explain concepts! If you get the chance to take his labs or courses DO IT!!!

Kanishka is the best TA I have ever had!! He genuinely cares for his students and wants them to succeed. He is passionate about what he does and excellent at delivering the necessary material relating to lecture and lab. He is also willing to help with any other academic or personal problems students may be experiencing! Highly highly recommend him
Kanishka is by far the best TA Ive ever had. He thoroughly explains everything we went over in class and makes topics much easier to understand.

Very interested in and engaged with students. Brought chemistry alive with specific real life examples and historical narratives on important chemists. Always well prepared for lectures, and gave practice problems almost weekly and held exam reviews that were helpful in preparation for exams. One of the best science TA's I've had.
Cares a lot about his students in and out of class.
Very enthusiastic about chemistry, but even more so about wanting his students to succeed!
He's a great TA. Makes class interesting and always explains concepts with applied matters. Always walks around and makes sure we under stand the lan. He should be President.
He is awesome
Slane discourages questions in class. She is often late to her own classes and sometimes didnt show up at all. A waste of tuition.

Slane's classes are hard and the expectations are a little bit ridiculous, but if you know that going in you can prepare and be fine. She's incredibly intimidating at first, but fairly personable if you give her a chance. And she's always willing to help or clarify. Warning though: her finals are cumulative.

Class expectations are unrealistic. She did not narrow down any of the slide identification. Therefore, for a midterm and a final you needed to know 150+ slides. Do not take a class with her. If you do, go and talk with her for extra clarification, especially for papers because she is a tough grader.

Professor Slane is extremely intimidating. At first I thought she was really mean, but after a week or so I realized that she was just sort of brusque. She's helpful, but the expectations for her classes are RIDICULOUS. I have experience in art history classes and I still found hers extremely difficult and time consuming. Avoid at all cost.

Having graduated a few years ago, I can safely say that in retrospect, this woman was flat out the worst instructor that I ever had. It can't even be put into words. The only way to truly understand the pain is take a class for yourself, but don't. I wish I could take back every last second of it all. The lowest point of my college experience.

I loved this professor. I had her for Intro to Personality. She was super easy and really sweet. She was a bit nervous standing in front of the class, but she was easy so who cares! The lecture was boring, but again who cares if you get an A.

This professor is so sweet and easy. I took her class my freshman year of college, did not know how to study, and got an A with barely any effort. I was just looking at her reviews and saw that they were awful so I had to put my good experience in here!  I would really recommend taking her, her lectures are a bit boring but the class was good/easy.

She''s a pretty nervous professor and is obviously uncomfortable at the front of the room. Lectures are long and boring which is weird for such an interesting subject. Powerpoints are online so you don''t really have to show up for class. There was rarely more than 7 students in class. Prepare to die inside during lectures but still show up.

She has no idea what she is talking about and can never make sense of her own PowerPoints. She creates study guides based off of material not discussed in class. Exams are not based off of study guides. I do not know how anyone could fare well with her as a teacher.
I know she's speaking plain English, but I can't understand her, because she speaks in pop culture references.  Don't take this class, it's not worth your time.

She does not know the material she teaches.  Much of her time is spent reading the powerpoint slides word-for-word, processing them, and not being able to clarify them. If I didn't already have many classes in genetics (and work in plant genetics) I'd be in trouble.  Her examples are as dimwitted as she is.

He grades very strictly, with most exam points from short answers. Missing a lecture or pop quiz costs significant points. Lectures are 40–60 slides read word for word, making the class about memorization, not problem solving. It focuses on herbicide families and barely covers modern, more environmentally friendly techniques. Also study EVERY fact
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests often include very random facts from the slides that you would never have memorized. Writing intensive section is poorly structured
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smeda is a fine professor, but a little old school. It seems like he wants to make his class as difficult as possible and overwhelm you with information.

He is a nice guy but I had him for Plant sciences 2370 and he co-taught with his wife.They organized several field trips off campus for us but did not arrange any transportation while requiring attendance which was annoying as a student without a car. He would only teach at lab and most times would not go to lecture, only his wife would attend.
AMAZING professor. Smeda has amazing stories that apply to the materials he teaches
Smeda is a good professor and clearly explains topics in class. Take good notes though, because he won't post the slides and the exams are all short answer. Lab is usually not too difficult.

Smith is a great professor. She is well-versed in everything she teaches and gives good feedback. She goes out of her way to make herself available to students for help even given her busy reporting schedule. She is both an effective professor and a legitimately good person.

She would say we had a had a workshop day but then she would continue to talk for the entire class. The class would be given examples of what was expected and would work with her one on one during office hours where she would help edit but then still receive a low grade. Assignments took weeks to months to be graded.

Becky is an amazing teacher! She is very easy-going and funny! Some people may struggle with J1200's large amount of homework, but she is always willing to help. She also gives you the opportunity to revise your work and give you back your credits. She's a reporter working in KBIA with a lot of experience. You really can learn a lot!

In my experience, she has been kind. Her class is also very organized. Attendance is graded both directly and via in-class activities that cannot be made up outside of class without extreme circumstances. Actively engage in the class at least sometimes and do your work, then you'll be fine. The group projects can be tedious though.

professor is understanding and willing too work with students who communicate. all expectations are clearly defined in videos and documented step by step tutorials. People saying they got bad grades or that she grades too harshly, just didn't watch or READ ASSIGNMENT INSTRUCTIONS. Assignments are really EASY but can take a while

She is the nicest human ever, she makes it SOOOOO clear what needs to be done when, and what's expected. The class itself was not my fav ever but for it being a lab credit it really wasn't that bad. Follow the instructions to a T and do the extra credit.

I cannot stand this class or professor. It being a TAM class, it is taken too seriously. Extremely tedious work (which takes hours from your day or week) and the grading is tougher than my classes that are actually applicable to my major. You will lose points for everything, even if you followed instructions.
Just no. The professor thinks that taking off a million points is her job. She forgets she's a TAM teacher. Tries way too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst class and professor ever. She is so picky and is NOT flexible with students at all. It's a TAM class, not a technology class, yet you get points off for tech issues that are out of control. Worst online professor I've had.

This is time consuming and pointless class. You have to make 206 samples fo a book on video the entire time and it takes about 7 hours. Not only this, there is continuous weekly labs where they take hours and she grades harshly. She takes points off for stupid reasons and tanks your GPA.

I honestly don't understand why ratings for Professor Smith are less than stellar. TAM 2200 is not a difficult course. Folks who have complained about rigorous grading criteria have failed to simply read instructions. Every single step is clearly outlined in each assignment. There is AMPLE feedback. Failure is hard unless you just don't care.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor I have ever had! Super organized and makes everything super clear and transparent for students. Feedback on assignments was very in depth and helps make changes for final projects.

Assignments themselves were pretty simple, but submission requirements were excessive and strict. No understanding for technological mishaps. Had to download 3 apps and get editing software. Had to drop $200+ on supplies for an online class, half of which were barely used and unnecessary. Do not take if you are not a TAM major. Not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: BEWARE this class!! The content of this class is not hard but all the assignments are very tedious. The professor is also a very tough grader, but not for the reasons you think. It's nearly impossible to get a 100% on an assignment because she constantly takes off points for technology errors (ie: the way you submit things).

She takes off points for the smallest details and is very particular about the way everything is done. The class is a lot of work but easier than most labs, so I would say to take the class just with a different professor if you can. She offers extra credit often which is nice, but it can't make up for all of the points lost from her harsh grading.

The way you turn in your assignments must have been set up by an infant child or someone with half a brain, I have been at Mizzou for 3 years now, and have never taken a class as bad as this. The amount of stupid little rules you have to follow when turning in an assignment blows my mind. The stupid classes are always the unnecessarily hard ones.

Smith is pretty nice and offers a lot of extra credit. The content isn't difficult, but there are so many unnecessary rules you have to follow when submitting things that the class is significantly harder as a result. If there's even the smallest error with submitting, you get a 0. Can't recommend for that reason alone.

Every assignment is graded way too harshly, and I'm not talking about getting a question wrong and wanting the points for it, I'm talking about having to submit video assignments and if you "embed" your video on canvas instead of "attaching" your video on canvas you get a 0/10. If you joined this class for a quick credit get out while you still can
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was clearly designed by someone who anticipated technological hurdles, and then made the class incredibly tedious instead of rethinking their process to be more student friendly. There are so many rules to follow for assignment submission, and too little room for error. Smith is not at all fit to teach this type of class.

He seems terrifying, but get on his good side by participating in discussion & following his instructions to the T. If you don't participate he will single you out, so make sure you're always prepared & on your toes.

Pro Tip: after finishing the assigned readings, form a few comments or thoughtful questions beforehand so you're always ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Excellent section professor if you like a challenge. Very dry humor. Speak up in discussion or prepare to be singled out. Sends grades through email and doesn't input them in Canvas, so it's hard to keep track of your cumulative grade. However, there's opportunities for extra credit and the assignments are very structured and don't sneak up on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He challenges his class by: calling on people randomly, asking about outside knowledge, and questioning peoples' assertions. At first I struggled a lot with his grammar/punctuation based grading system for papers, but I adapted over time. He asks difficult questions about the reading that force you to think. Pro tip: show up and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Our essays and the midterm were graded with no rubric or standardized system and those were 60% of our grade. Discussion sections were stressful as they were graded and I always felt like I needed prior knowledge to understand what we were talking about--even though I had read. He also did not put a single grade in Canvas until the end of the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's the worst. Expects outside knowledge from his students with stuff that doesn't relate to the class. Rants about philosophy in the middle of the lecture. Honestly, he is extremely pretentious and arrogant.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The guy takes everything personal and is relentless when it comes to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He definitely comes off as rough around the edges at first. I'll be honest, the first couple weeks I wanted to drop the class, but I found that though he may be gruff at times, he actually really does care about your learning and development. Participate in class, appear intrigued, and ready to learn and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Can seem a little rude at first, but he does care about student learning. Do the readings, there are quizzes over the material. He asks A LOT of questions in class. If you participate, he respects you more. Tests are heavy on essays. Go to class, take good notes, and read over them occasionally. You'll learn a lot!
You will learn more about the early Middle Ages than you ever imagined. Do not think this is a course where you can show up and sit in the back row and pull a B. you will work for every point.
His approach to teaching history is interesting and his lectures full of captivating information. A really great prof for students who love history.
He is a great teacher when he can keep it together, but he takes students' attendance and participation a little too personally.

I wish I had this class before I took my SATs because I would have scored a lot higher in the vocabulary section.  Professor's motto seems to be never use one syllable when four will do.  I learned a lot in this class even some about history.

Lecture were super important since he didn't teach from the book. his discussions were the hardest thing i have ever been a part of. he was extremely condescending but kind of helpful. If you have another option, go for it. but it isn't too bad.

Math4140 not 1400, overall awful, lectures did not flow in any way and were very hard to follow. She refuses to work out the examples in the slides she presents for lectures. She always says "I expect you to work these examples on your own" every time an example comes up in the slides. She also refuses to curve, even when the average is in the 60s.

Smita was an incredible teacher of calculus. She explained everything clearly explained all topics in depth. The class is very straightforward. You have homework due every Tuesday morning and four exams. If you go to class and take notes you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hardly responded to emails or allowed the opportunity for an exam to be relooked. The entire 1300 department was difficult to deal with when it came to rounding or showing enough work even while my answers were correct. Probably will have to take it as credit, but if you don't, please don't. This class is very unnecessary in my opinion.
Difficult to work with, not flexible or helpful whatsoever
Hi, I'm glad to have a professor like her.

I had her for finite math. She was able to present the material in a very easy to understand way. I would often learn ahead of the class, but the material didn't really solidify until she walked the class through it. I would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took him for 4710 there was not an option for that wasn't bad just a really boring class.

His lectures are good and engaging, so its important to go. However, he doesn't really prepare you for the exams. He makes you buy his 110 dollar book and lets use it on the exam, but there are way too many pages and formulas to keep track of. He randomly selects obscure problems to review. You have to read a lot on your own to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was just a weird class. everything from the lectures to the structure of grading. The teacher was ok, but theres gotta be a better way to teach statistics.
Make sure to write down any practice problems covered in class, they are very useful when studying. Go to lecture.

Solid professor. Has open book exams that are very straightforward if you pay attention in class. Teaches pretty well but he was largely unavailable outside of class, didn't answer emails in a timely manner and was often not present at his own office hours.

He was a nice person, but not the best teacher. Expectations for assignments were unclear. Would skip through the lecture slides and tell us that we can look at them later. Told us we should not email him because he probably won't see it. I left class feeling like I did not learn anything.
Nice guy but terrible class. Everything is based on his opinion and he likes to get mad when people don't respond in class. He has good intentions but not the most convenient class to be in.

My favorite professor I've ever had at my time at Mizzou, he was so passionate about the class and more than willing to learn from students which I thought was so personable and amazing. I was actually so upset when the class was over, after we finished our final he fist bumped or shook hands with every single student- I LOVED HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Daryl is the best professor I've had at Trulaske. His classes are not only teachable and able to be applied to real-world situations, but he makes them fun. Throughout the semester, he makes students comfortable with the class content and encourages discussion with our peers. Come to class & you will get an A! Best professor ever!

Multiple instances of saying one thing and never delivering in relation to due dates, posting assignments late, etc.  If assignments were posted late, due dates were not extended.  Rarely ever replied to emails. Video proctored exams requiring full recording of the entire room pre test.  You will miss assignments because communication is unclear.
Great professor who is enthusiastic about the topic. He cares about his students and his lectures are always interesting. Would definitely recommend

Proctored exams, closed book/note. Exam dates promised the first week of semester but not given. Continually forgot to post assignments and then had them due within a couple of days. All exams (5) were on weekends (3 holiday and 1 spring break) Unprofessional communication with students. Rarely replied to emails. Not good online professor.
Very professional, caring, and knowledgable!
One of my favorite professors I have had during my 4 years. I wish I could take him for my other classes

Professor Smith is a great teacher with unique experience in the field. In class, student participation is important while discussing each topic. I feel that he mixes a nice level of speediness and intrigue into each lecture. I would recommend his style of teaching to nearly anyone, as he is able to accommodate for the needs of his students.

I truly enjoyed class with Daryl Smith. He is a fantastic professor, and even though the material is not relevant to my major, I still enjoyed learning about the material. All business majors should take this class to go over basic HR policies, as well as the chance to have class with Professor Smith. His classes are truly a joy!

Prof. Smith is an amazing professor. He cares about all his students and is passionate about teaching them. Lectures are entertaining and engaging. He provides many real-life examples to clearly explain the content. He is very approachable and always willing to help. Prof. Smith is very inspiring and I encourage other students to take his classes.

Definitely one of the best professors in the business school. He is very relatable and easy to talk to. If youre having a problem he will work wit you to get the outcome you want. PLEASE go to class, lol, you need the participation points and the info from lecture.

Prof. Smith genuinely cares about his students and goes above and beyond to prove it. His lectures are actually interesting and he encourages participation (participation points can help your grade at the end of the semester). The best professor I've had at Mizzou, highly recommend!

Professor Smith is hands down the best professor I've had in the business school. His class isn't a walk in the park but he wants you to succeed. He is able to speak from real world experience and is passionate about the topic. By all means take a class with him! As long as you go to class and engage, you will do fine on exams.

Whether you are a management major or taking 4020 to fulfill some other type of requirement, I highly recommend taking this class. In addition, Daryl Smith is an incredibly kind, knowledgeable, and engaging teacher. He gives good feedback, fosters fun participation, and really explains all of the class topics well. Definitely take it with him!
Daryl is THE MAN! tests are open note & open powerpoint slides so they arent too bad. attendance is mandatory but as long as you talk in class and pay attention you will get an A

Professor Smith is amazing. There are not enough good things to say about him. I have now taken three courses with him and enjoyed every one. Make sure you attend class, but honestly... youll want to.

Best Professor I have had at Mizzou. If you want an A you will have to work for it, but he is a forgiving grader. Super funny, super nice. Regularly finds his students internships and jobs outside of class just because he can and knows people. Big on attendance. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. Sparked my interest in HR and found me a summer internship.
Best professor I have ever had! He truly cares about his students and their futures

Professor Smith is great! This is one of the few classes that I felt I actually used the contents in the real world. As long as you show up, prep for the test like he says, and put in effort you'll do fine! His classes have a lot of discussion which made it interesting as well. He even helped me get in contact with employers for after college.

If you read the book, participate, and do your work, getting an A or close to it should be a simple task. Very laid back class where the professor doesn't always lecture at you, but has an open discussion class setup. Easy and comfortable but you're expected to do your best. Not a class you can blow off.

As long as you go and participate in lectures youll do just fine! Lectures are actually interesting and fun! We had very fun discussions and Professor Smith always makes it a safe place for open discussions. Hes very understanding and helpful. Ive taken two classes with him and hes definitely one of the best professors Ive had at Mizzou!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor and he does a great job with lectures and powerpoints. He really cares about students learning and taking away something from each class. He tells you from the moment you walk into his course to think like a CEO, and you really learn a lot about human resource management.

One of the best professors at Mizzou! His classes are very engaging and discussion based. You can tell he enjoys teaching and helping students. Very genuine, funny, and caring professor. Tests are open note but you have to study! Easy grading on homework. Always willing to help outside of class with career search and everything. Love his classes

Vasey Academy was a great opportunity. Professor Smith has so much knowledge and connections throughout the university. This class opened my eyes to great career possibilities. Professor Smith is truly a gem at the University and I am glad I was able to meet him.
Awesome, definitely recommend people take his course!
I'm an international student and prof. Smith show us enough respect. He is very friendly and easy to communicate.

This is a professor I would love to have again. Professor Smith is passionate and engaging. His lectures are more of a discussion with student input and feedback required. Show up, participate, do the homework and you will be more than fine. With real-life examples and recent events stories, Professor Smith has no issues relating the course to life
I really like this professorhe is vey intresting and very care about all the students He care about every students thoughs and what they think. In his class, I learned lots of things.
He is an amazing professor. He really cares about the students. I loved his class, I learned so much about diversity and integration. I definitely recommend taking this class, you won't regret it.

He's an amazing teacher! His lectures were really interesting and he made his course easy to understand by using real situations and events to put things into perspective. He very approachable so don't be afraid to ask for help or even say "hello" if you see him outside of class. Plus he's really funny; I actually looked forward to going to class.
He a is very nice and helpful professor.

Daryl is incredibly helpful and approachable in and outside of class. Class discussions are interesting and engaging. Attendance and participation are key in his classes. He makes sure his students are treated fairly and with respect. Highly recommend this course as well as Management 3700.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Daryl makes sure that his students succeed in his course! He makes class fun and interactive as well. The homework and quizzes are short and straight to the point so that the students are able to take away important information!
Classes are interesting. Tests are open note and there is one paper assignment but he grades it very easy. Attendance is important but the class is somewhat interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: good

Prof. Smith is a great professor! With substantial HR experience, he is an expert teaching HR management. He made efforts to inspire students in class, and he respects every student. He is a very nice and polite person, he is awesome!!

Cool class, so long as you go to class. Daryl is passionate and really enjoys everything HR related. Lots of reading and quizzes almost every other week. Can be an easy class so long as you follow the syllabus.

Professor Smith is so helpful.  The Vasey Academy is definitely a class worth taking.  Professor Smith is invested in students and he cares about your success.  He has a lot of experience in business and has a plethora of knowledge.  I would suggest him for any class.

Daryl was awesome!  Always had a great attitude and showed he cared a lot for his students.  His stories helped me learn the material a lot (he's VERY experienced and has worked for a lot of cool companies, like ESPN).  The class is very achievable and he lets you use notes and PowerPoint slides on his exams.

Daryl is the best professor I have had during my 4 years here. He looks out for his students and will do whatever he can to help them succeed. Took hr management and collective bargaining with him and would take any class he taught if I could! Tests are open note, he uses open discussions and real life stories. Doesn't feel like you are in a class!

Dr. Sowers is possibly one of the best professors at MU. I have NEVER had a professor be so amazing at giving lectures. She makes material easy to understand; she is extremely passionate about what she teaches, and that passion makes an imprint on the students. If I had Sowers teaching all of my classes, I would pass every class with an EASY A
BEST professor on campus! Very knowledgeable and always willing to help her students. Puts you out of your comfort zone to actually learn something.
The best professor I have had. She is an amazing professor and truly cares about your success. She has prepared me more for my career in one class than I have received in any others.

100 percent easily the best professor on campus and CAFNR is lucky to have someone as talented and caring as Professor Sowers. I have taken two of her classes and getting ready to take a third next year and I have to say that she has really helped me become an impressive individual when it comes to placing myself in front of future employers.

Professor Sowers is the best professor I have had while at Mizzou. She cares about students and is the first one to lend a hand in times of struggle. She allows you to come into her office and ask questions before tests as well as lets you know what you personally need to work on. By far the best class and professor I have taken at Mizzou!

Professor Sowers is one of the most amazing teachers I have had in my 4 years of college! Her class was so beneficial for my post-grad endeavors and I will take these tools into my work life forever. You definitely have to put time and effort into it, but she grades fairly and you will actually learn and retain the material.

Fundamentals of communication was the most challenging and MOST REWARDING class I have taken yet at Mizzou. Sowers is absolutely incredible. Everyone should have her as a teacher. She cares about you as an individual and wants to see you succeed.
Linda Sowers is the absolute BEST professor I have ever had. After taking two of her classes, I can truly say that she is incredible and is really trying to help students get a job in the future.
Enthusiasm!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Linda is a professor you must take one class with, even though after one you will take ALL of her classes. This lady is INCREDIBLE!!!

Linda is a great professor. This class was easily the most beneficial to me. She teaches you real world stuff that you actually need to know. The grading on papers isn't too hard but her tests are a little difficult and there is no good way to study for them.
Ag sales is the best class I took in undergrad.

I took her golf etiquette class and if you are in CAFNR take it! It is a great class for experts and beginners. The final is to go and play 3-4 holes of  for free! She teaches you the basics and how you could use golf in a business setting! It is a passfail class but it is an amazing class to take!
IF you  miss class you wont' get the homework and you fail!

This is the second class I have had with Linda and she is the best teacher I have ever had. She not only cares if you pass but also about helping you get internships and jobs after you graduate. She is one of the most caring professors that I have ever had the chance to have.

She is one of the best teachers at Mizzou.  I wish she taught more Comm classes! I would take any class of hers.  She is so helpful and really cares about the students.  (She knew all of our names by the second class)
One of the best professors you will have in the Ag school. If you attend class,you should get an easy A.
Awesome teacher who really knows her stuff. Class is moderately boring but it helps that she is passionate about her job and subject. oh... and hot!

One of the best classes I've taken as an undergraduate.  It was so good, that I'm writing this comment after a year of graduating.  Course concepts are VERY practicable to real world situations.  If you actively participate in course, you're able to walk out of ABC's "Shark Tank" with a deal.
Honestly an easy A if you can skim the book and remember the assignments. Can get boring at times because she uses the book's powerpoints but overall very helpful and a great reference for resumes.
This is the best class I have taken so far in college. She is a great teacher and is very aware of the agriculutre industry and sales within it! I highly recommend this class!!

Professor De Souza means well but this is a really difficult class, mainly because it's all online. There isn't much actual teaching during class time and there's a LOT of homework. You get very little flexibility on late work and tests impact your grade a lot.

The class is 100% in Spanish. We spend a lot of time in class doing little assignments that mostly everyone just looks up the answers to on Quizlet to be able to answer. If no one knows we will just sit there for minutes until someone answers. The first part of our exams is via zoom and she talks so much as if we don't only have 1 hour  .

this class is taught almost totally in spanish, which is typical, but it's harder when it's online. she spends most of class having you complete little assignments without teaching a whole lot. participation and attendance are really important and there is a lot of homework.

The lesson lecture videos are 100% in Spanish.. it is up to you to essentially interpret the lectures. She is quick to say that you are cheating when posting in discussion boards. But, when the lectures are in Spanish, how else am I supposed to comprehend what I am hearing? There is typically 8-10 hours of work a week and test are proctored.

The teacher's personality was good, but her teaching styling wasn't great. There is so much work a week and the instructions weren't clear. Sometimes they would say one thing in Spanish and another in English. Everything was touched on very briefly before you were tested on it. No extra credit was offered. Quizzes and tests hold a huge impact.

I have never felt so lost in a class. I felt like I was always one step behind. Based on my peer's expressions and questions they also felt that way. There is a ton of homework, several exams, and a few projects. There's a lot to be graded on but class material is fast-paced and difficult so it's hard to do well. Take Spanish in person.

The course was chaotic. While the professor speaks fluent spanish, she is not able to teach it in a cohesive manner. The class was unorganized and constantly changing and incredibly unclear with all instructions. The lectures were difficult to discern as she spoke quickly in spanish.
A lot of homework assigned, wasn't clear with instructions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Taking a class with this professor is miserable. The expectations for papers are incredibly vague and no examples are given. Grading is biased. When asking questions, responses are rude and not helpful. Some of the questions on the quizzes have multiple correct answers so it's a matter of guessing what she's thinking. Wish I would have checked here

Carol is one of the worst professors I have ever had. SW7720 is only out of 100 points total, so any slip up can cost you a letter grade. Group project IN GRAD SCHOOL ONLINE is a bit much.. Disrespectful and EXTREMELY critical at grading papers. Quizzes were reasonable and you can take them twice. Avoid her at all costs for your own sanity.
