She was clear in her written expectations around when she would be available to respond or meet with us. I appreciated that we could take the weekly online tests twice. Very biased and inconsistent in her grading of papers. Honestly felt like she was trying to weed us out of the program. It's very clear that she primarily operates as SSW Director.

Hands down the worst professor I have ever had. She is a narcissist who puts assignment instructions in multiple places, changes them frequently, then denies doing so. I did not feel supported in any way. In fact, this instructor is the singular reason I will walk away from this program and my passion.

Unethical, uncaring and rude professor. Grades without justification and valid reasoning. Can be very unprofessional at times if she thinks she is right on something. Avoid at all costs if possible not worth the stress

Carol is the only professor in the department that I didn't enjoy. Virtually universally disliked among students. I did well in her class but still felt her grading was erratic and opinion based. Her ego is huge and her lectures are boring. You could read the assigned book and never attend a lecture and get more out of it than I did this class.

Carol is literally the worst professor in the department. She is unapproachable, grades based on what she thinks is correct rather than considering that ethical decision making is fluid and may have multiple acceptable courses of action. She gives you the majority of your grades and feedback after course evaluations are due. Do not take her.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!! Grades unfairly and with unreasonable expectations. Rude. Elitist. No empathy. Does not care that you are an adult with a life outside of school. If anyone has a choice whether or not to take a class with her, DO NOT.
Her expectations are unrealistic and computer like.  She has a hard time empathizing.
very critical & not supportive. has an elitist attitude. forces her perspectives on SSW. probably has learned a lot, but has been isolated for a while & is now on a power trip.

Carol doesn't teach any courses, but is the director of the Social Work Program.  I wanted to inform anyone reading this that she is not supportive in the success of her students and seems to secretly want them to fail.  She is arrogant and believes she is the almighty God of social workers.  She doesn't not give chances or excuses.  Good luck hah!
Very good. Interested in Student learning and participation. Very interested in discussion. Abstract.

Best grad student teacher I've ever had at mizzou. Better than any of my senior level professors. Loves stats & always willing to help his students learn & succeed. He made complicated problems seem simple and straighforward -- made sure everyone fully understood topics. I wish more professors at Mizzou were as courteous and knowledgeable as Snyder

Amazing professor. His grading is extremely fair and he never "tricks" students on tests. Puts his notes on canvas, and gives homework assignments that will actually help you on the test. BEST statistics professor I've ever had and I would definitely take a class taught by him again. Plus he's hilarious and very approachable.
Hands down best Graduate Professor in the department. Will make you learn the material to the extent that the exams are easy.
Teaches intro classes like they are capstones!

This is the worst professor I've ever had. He reads directly from his paper for notes which he reads quickly through so its super hard to take notes. only 3 grades midterm, paper, and final. He grades hard on all of them. He told his class how he failed papers in college bc of his professor and he basically wants revenge. Do not take his class!!

Easily the most boring and monotone professor I've ever had. I've never even came close to failing a class until his class when I DID fail. He is absolutely awful and reads lecture notes straight from a piece of paper. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.
He is unbelivably boring and not very willing to help. Also he never uses blackboard so you never know how you are doing in class.

He is a terrible teacher. The lectures are not helpful at all. This class is about reading the book and attending RSD's. His PowerPoints are completely useless. He will have terms on a slide and not even talk about them. It was extremely hard to stay awake in class and if you did get up to go to it, you were sorry you went. Read the book.
I love history but he is extremely boring.
Lectures are extremely boring!! Very unclear on what to take notes on, hard not to fall asleep. Exams don't come off as being to hard but the grading is extremely strict!

Spoltore is the GOAT. I found his class to be very entertaining when discussion was active, not so much when it was quiet. With this being said, discussion made up a big part of the class. Attendance isn't necessary, and you can do the HW without it, but his in-class commentary is great. Dane is very caring and hilarious. Absolutely recommend. 5/5.

Dane is super nice and a chill professor. He unfortunately takes forever to grade and doesn't always give feedback. Sometimes the assignment will not be posted on time. He does accept late work. The syllabus does not have any deadlines, but the project outlines will. It was not a hard class; there were only 3 full papers and then a revision paper.

This instructor was so disorganized. The syllabus provided at the beginning of the semester didn't have any due dates. Modules weren't updated regularly and major assignments were frequently posted a few days before the due date. He provided no feedback and graded without a rubric. This class was easy, but frustrating and a complete waste of time.

He was okay, work was easy to complete. A lot of in-class peer work which didn't do anything and was pointless. He takes FOREVER to grade, like, after finals week all my assignments were finally graded. "conferences" are unnecessary to go to, all he talks about during the conference, is all on the notes he left on your paper. Fine professor
Professor Spoltore (Dane) is very kind and he is a great instructor. He is just a graduate student and I think he's doing better than a lot of my other professors. Great guy and a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hes a really nice prof and really young. The class isnt hard at all and he accepts stuff late. Id take him again, its definitely my most relaxed class this semester.

I was in this class for the 2023 spring semester. He was AMAZING. He made sure everyone understood the topic at hand as long as you spoke up for yourself. He would make time aside from his office hours to give extra help before exams or just any other day. His tests were problems we had seen before on hw or study problems.

I really liked Derek. He explained things well in lecture and made sure we understood it. Weekly homework that varied between 15-50 questions so make sure to start that asap. Weekly quiz in discussion over homework. Easy to keep an A as long as you do the homework and quiz. Didn't go to lecture much and still did fine in the class.

Derek is not the best at explaining the course content. I feel as if I could have done far better if someone else had been teaching the material. Moreover, in my experience, he seems to be more concerned about his paycheck than his students. In his email to me, he basically called me lazy and stupid hidden under a façade of professionalism.
A teacher that really cares about students and their education. Quizzes were few and far in between. Final was longer than expected, but still reasonable. Always willing to help out if you ask.

I had Dr. Spain as a professor for the honors BBQ tutorial. He's a funny, caring, and passionate teacher. His lecture on livestock ethics is my all-time favorite. At times he'll make the whole room laugh and other times he'll leave you deep in thought. Take his class if possible.
Hes the real MVP. He really makes an effort to get to know his students.
Dr. Spain is phenomenal, I looked forward to his class everyday. He really wants you to both learn the material  AND get a good grade. I only wish he could teach all of my classes!
Everything you could ever ask for in a professor. Helpful, encouraging, and genuinely cares about his students. Wish I could take every single class with him.

Dr. Spain is exactly what I look forward to as an instructor. He has wonderful jokes and interacts with the class. If you need any help or have any questions, you can email him or ask him before/ after class and he is more than happy to help you out.

Had him for Sophomore Seminar and he was one of the best teacher I have ever had. He kept lectures interesting and was really helpful if you need him. Disscussion were always a blast no matter what day it was. He has a great sense of humor and is very organize and straight to the point. He get things done and like the same. Overall a great teacher!

I was a TA for his 11 course this semester.  I find that he seems to have a true passion for teaching, and wants his TAs to be effective - although I didn't find all the TAs willing to go the extra mile to learn.  Dr. Spain seems to take a true interest in having students learn!  It's refreshing and something you don't see too often in professors.

The best professor I have ever had in college.  He was hilarious and knew what he was talking about.  When you were tired and sick of doing something he could always spark up some interest in the class.
GREATEST POFESSOR IN HISTORY!!!!!!
He's wonderful! I want to take all of his classes that he teaches!
Dr. Spain was great. He was alive when we were dragging as a class. His delivery kept our classes moving.
The best!
Dr. Spain rocks
He was a great teacher. He was also very funny, which made class fun to attend.
Definately the best animal science teacher I have had.  Really great person.  Funny, and he actually cares that you learn something!
No Comments
He's a really good teacher.  He has a sense of humor as well.  He really cares that you understand the material.
great teacher, great jokes

His feedback on my first draft essay was very discouraging. His ONLY advice was that my essay would basically need to be rewritten. I pressed him for more specific feedback, but he left it at that. Dropped the class after that. Syllabus also had errors, particularly regarding dates.

Sperber is a genius.  I absolutely loved this class.  You really have to work to get an A in this class, but it is totally worth it to try.  I learned so much through the assigned readings and his incredible lectures.

His classes are like story time in kindergarten. His lectures are so thorough and detailed, its like you are there in Germany! He is an expert of all-things-Europe, and he uses fantastic graphs, charts, tables, and pictures to exemplify his lectures. The books he assigns are some of the best I have ever read in college. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!

Hands down the most intriguing class at Mizzou. Dr. Sperber is an expert on 20th Century Germany and inspired me through his lectures to seek more information on historical events. Attendance was never mandatory, but skipping class will make you feel guilty that you've missed one of his amazing lectures. It is a very tough, but rewarding course.
Decent class; attend class every so often and spend time on the papers, and you should't have any trouble.
Great Teacher makes lecture interesting. World War II was by far the best part of the class
Very good professor, knows his stuff inside and out.  Class is not as easy as it seems

Fun guy. He likes to tell a joke before starting class. The workload is acceptable. His TAs provides very good comments and suggestions when returning first drafts. Not hard to get an A if you write your papers seriously.
Shes the best person ever ( ( (

She's a pretty easy grader, but the workload for the class is kinda hefty. Class attendance isn't necessary, unless you're turning in work, or there is an in class writing (I think there were 4). Study the book for the exams; there are very few questions from lecture. Overall, easy A class as long as you turn in all the work and appear interested.
Very nice and made the material very interesting. I highly recomend this class for all mass comm majors. Very easy to follow along with the material and she is a VERY easy grader.

I loved this class. Attendance in lectures isn't mandatory and if you read the textbook you would probably still be able to pass, but I found the lectures really interesting. We had three tests and they were all two essay questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you want to cry every class take this course. he writes so much on slides and goes way too fast that you will never get any notes down. doesnt share them either, not even with the TA. your notes will all be half done. there is no other grades than exams so you better be good at long essay test questions. would not reccomend!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Squire is a very knowledgeable professor. With that said, his class was definitely the biggest pain last semester solely for the fact that he does not upload slides to Canvas. His presentations go fast, so if you aren't paying attention, you'll miss out. The required readings come from his books, which are well written and not too wordy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Actually had no interactions with prof squire but my TA was Joseph Harrison and he was very good at explaining things. It was an easy A I just got lazy but less than a B is basically impossible in my eyes. Very easy going graders just listen to lectures and you should pass very bare minimum class and interesting!

Squire is really laidback and gives your average lecture. Tests are tricky so make sure you study in advance. Overall, if you know the material youll do fine. Lectures almost always got out early which was a big plus! Your pretty standard course that most students will do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a professor, he is a great person. The course content is interesting if you're interested in political science. There are 4 tests, which are 90% of your grade. It's great preparation for law school, but can be challenging to study for them. He also doesn't post any lecture material on Canvas, so you must come to class and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whole class is just 4 tests. Go to lecture and it will be a piece of cake, otherwise youre going to have to read a lot to make up for missing his explanations. Really interesting topics and you usually dont go the full lecture time. Tough grader depends on the TA
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You have to go to class to get a good grade in this class. The lectures aren't posted on Canvas and the material is only shown during the lectures. The professor is amazing and he is very good at explaining concepts. The only negative thing is that the exams are 90% of your grade. The remaining 10 percent are participation in your discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I basically rewrote everything on the powerpoint and studied that information until I knew the key concepts and a fey details about them and I received an A on almost every exam and I have never been a test taker. Very easy concepts to understand too

I've had Professor Squire before and all I have to say is he is absolutely brilliant.  He has a sneaky humor that you will only catch if you are paying attention, and you can tell he knows his stuff (especially about state government and the legislative branch).  He is clear on what he wants and is no-nonsense.  Read, go to class, and pay attention
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Squire has an air of professionalism and knowledge that commands respect, but he is also funny and approachable. The class was focused on examining broad trends in comparative state government backed by specific examples. The only downside of the course was that the tests (90% of total grade) are essay with somewhat nebulous grading protocols.

He's definitely dry. Sometimes, the material can be interesting depending On your interests. Must be able to write notes at super speed. Tests are straightforward; it's wrapping your head around the subject matter that is challenging. Buy the books, DO the reading.
The only grades you get for the class are three tests. If you fail one, you can't come back from that. His lectures are long and boring, and don't help you on the test.

This guy is the best professor at MU. Take his class. He is halarious, always something funny to say. If you take 2100 make sure to go to the state capital lecture, he has a great way of talking about Florida's state capital. His information is just great. I must warn you, he is dry. He cusses at least once a lecture and will drop the f bomb.

He's pretty plain but not a bad teacher. He occasionally adds some humor. Do all the readings! Ideally, go over vocab words and concepts with others to help prepare for tests. Grades take a while to get back because of TAs, but this class is passable. He also wrote the textbook which was expensive and I was not able to sell back.

This class is very easy if you A) have background info about American Government already, or B) Pay attention in class. My girlfriend didn't take a single polisci class in high school and managed an A-, I did and managed an A with relative ease. All of the exams are the same and easy to B.S. Pay attention in class and don't miss any. You'll be fine

I really liked this class. He really knows his stuff. Basically there are two trains of thought for this class.      1 You can go to class and not buy the book(which is what I did)                         2. You can buy the book and not go to lecture   Either way its a good class.
Awesome guy and knows what he's talking about. He wrote the book so you can't go wrong!!!!!!!!!!

Totally dry, but if you pay attention he has a very dry, very funny sense of humor and usually has one golden line per class. (Ex. Calling some historical lady a "Bar Ho"). If you take thorough notes then reading isn's totally necessary. Definitely harder tests than the other professors teaching this class

He's pretty monotone and it's easy to fall asleep. This semester, the tests consisted of defining and stating the significance of five terms (from book) and answering one of two essays (worth 55 pts). You need the book. He wrote it, which I think it pretty pretentious, but you will need it. I don't go to lecture, and I have an A, so it can be done.

Attend the lectures! He does not post the notes on Blackboard. Lectures are somewhat monotone, but he's not a bad teacher, some of what he says is actually interesting. Read the book! It's a lot, but it really helps! Know how the terms apply in the real world. There are 3 essays and a midterm, right now I have an A but we'll see at semester.

Everything about his lectures being monotonous is completely true.  He is extremely dry, and seems to drone through class, but you can make it through with a good grade.  He is no nonsense, and his tests are essay.  The essays are very predictable.  Attending discussion is an absolute must! Average Overall for 2100...I'd hate to have him for 1100

State Government is hard with Squire. He is the smartest person in the room and has known such for a long time. He believes in the bell curve so dont expect to get an A. and expect to learn about the Squire index for legislative professionalism quite a bit.

While he is a very dry teacher, he knows what he is talking about.  Only take this class if you are truely interested in congress and legislatie policy. His tests are essay, but a little easier than I expected.  Its a hard class, but go to class and do the readings and you'll get an A/B

Not interesting, very monotone. The best way to pass this class is to skip the lecture and read the book. Make sure you know the key words and how they apply outside of class. I took this class during the 2008 election, and he spoke nothing about it. What a waste.

He is a very intelligent man, but the WORST teacher ever. I went to class, but he put me to sleep! He also wrote the book for his class, so you have to shovel out money and pay for it, and I didn't even use 2 of the books he made us buy. I greatly disliked, HATED, this class and if you want to pass a general requirement, then take something else.

Professor Squire will not baby you, but he is a brilliant scholar and if you actually do the work, have a shred of intelligence and aren't planning to skate by the next 4 years (for most of you complaining I should say 5 or 6) you will be fine and be happy with what you have learned.

This man thinks he is God's Gift to Political Science. Little to no sense of humor compounded by a monotonous, almost accusatory tone and a permanent scowl make lectures miserable. They are irrelevant, anyway, as the textbook is his baby and is easier to follow than his sermons. His examples are typically involved, yet ineffective. Avoid.

he is dull, his final worth 50% which is soo intense and u need to read a lot. he wrote the book, so if u read it u really dont need to go to class unless for a nap. his tests are all essay questions...bottom lines i would not wish this for my worst enemy

Don't do this to yourself. Take with another teacher if possible. Lectures dull, strangely structured; same content as text (which he wrote). Cumulative final worth 50% of grade, other 50% from 2 tests. Can put in tons of effort and still do badly. Might have once had personality besides jerk, but not anymore. AVOID.

I went to all the classes, did all the reading (which is extensive),and STILL got a C on our first test. I went to talk to the TA about it and the TA basically said he hates Squire and that his teaching/grading method is ridiculous. When the TA couldn't do anything, I tried to meet with Squire who basically told me to f*ck off.He hates students.

He is very charasmatic. Easy to understand and so far, the tests have been pretty easy. He wrote the book so all of his lectures come straight from it. Come to class and you should have a good experience.

He's passionate about what he teaches and knows what he's talking about. Lots of group work! He's very nice and wants his students to do well, but he has high expectations. If you're willing to keep up with class and participate, you'll do well. Class isn't mandatory but he expects participation and engagement. This was my favorite class!
It would be nice if he didn't talk down to people. We get it you are 35 and almost a doctor but you are also unclear and just not very nice. I have had few ruder teachers. Class is also very boring.

Dude sucks. Honestly my least favorite teacher. Taking this class dragged my GPA down and I regret it. If you forget to complete reading responses or ever miss class you can kiss a good grade goodbye. He's also a tough grader and doesn't want students to get good grades. Save yourself the hassle and avoid.
Matt is awesome! He really loves what he teaches and wants his students to do well. He is also pretty funny. Take Comm1200 with him! It will be worth it!

Dr. Srinivasan's class is taught much more like an upper level proof-based course than an introductory course. She is a fine instructor for someone who is slightly familiar with the material, but her class will be VERY hard as a first look at matrices. If you are a science/engineering major, consider that the class will not be applied math.

Do not take this instructor. I took her despite the reviews and it was a mistake. Please do not repeat my mistake. She is a nice person, but it will not set you up for success for all the reasons other reviews have listed. Find a way to take it elsewhere, there are better options.
Could have been better.

For someone whose USP is being such a wonderful and kind person, she sure gets very defensive and very rude when questioned about questionable grading practices, at the very least asking to see her grading, and her well known and questionable practice of having many typos and serious mistakes in problem sets and exams.

Wish I would've trusted these reviews & dropped this class when I could. She is a very smart and kind lady, but I feel like I learned nothing in this class. No homework, grades were mostly determined by exams (+ some quizzes worth little points). You have to teach yourself if you want to do well. Received the lowest grade of my life in this class:(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Srinivasan seems to think that all of her students understand math as quickly as she does. Once she tells you about a topic, she acts as if you fully understand it. Her slides are extremely technical, but you barely have time to time to take notes. She never takes time to explain concepts, yet each test had conceptually-based questions.

Prof Srinivasan is very helpful, but the way she taught the material just did not work. Still not sure if going to lectures was worth it or not. HWs were doable & she'd give plenty of "insights" onto what is/is likely to be on tests. Had some extra credit available too. Also gives plenty partial credit & is very forgiving about arithmetic errors.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Srinivasan is a sweet lady, but she is fundamentally incapable of teaching. She teaches as if everyone has had a proofs-based course and is familiar with linear algebra before. Her slides are as long as the textbook, and she offers no substantive insights to make things more digestible. She is the antithesis of what a professor should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Content is hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hema talks way too fast and writes even faster; it's impossible to learn anything from her. You MUST read the book and self-teach. The homework isn't even doable and she changes the questions every year. Wanna Chegg some answers? Good luck. Don't even think about memorizing the review-the test is completely different. Avoid Hema at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Everyone seems to be complaining about her lecturing style, but it's really not bad at all. The important thing is to use the book in conjunction with her lectures. Read the book, THEN go to the lecture with it in mind, then read the book again. Ask if you still have questions. Despite these comments, she is helpful and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If possible, avoid taking this class. She is friendly and enjoys what she is teaching, but it is incredibly easy to get lost in her lectures. She goes very fast and writes a lot. I find myself with multiple full pages of notes, having learned nothing, at the end of each class. Her office hours don't help much, and the homework is incredibly hard.

This class was by far the most challenging course I've ever taken. Two of my friends also took this course with another teacher and told me it wasn't that bad. I would avoid her if you can. She goes way too fast I couldn't pay attention to what she was saying I just worried about copying what was on the board before she erased it.

I have had many great teachers at Mizzou, and several bad teachers too. The Math department seems to have a skill at finding the worst teachers. With that said, Srinivasan is the worst teacher I have ever had. She is very nice, but her teaching style is the worst it could possibly be. Trying to learn from her lectures is impossible.

Took two graduate level courses with her and didn't learn a thing.  Very glad I had seen the material previously in my undergrad courses.  She does not explain things very well and isn't good at answering questions.

I don't think she's a great teacher because of her handwriting and office hours aren't all that helpful.  Her handwriting in her office hours was kind of hard to read and she didn't let me copy down what she wrote.  So I give her a C-.  And to me, teachers are only worthy if they have a B+ rating or higher.  so there.

As taking this class, I felt that I fall into the hell. The instructor went too fast, nobody could interprut her and asked a quesiton if he/she confused what she said. Only if you hate to get an A, you may enjoy her class. Although you can get all A or A+ in calculus 1,2,and 3, suceeding in these classes don't guarantee you can survive from herclas

This is a review for Basic Algebra, a preparatory course for qualifying exams. The teacher kept randomly jumping from topic to topic, and she wouldn't pay attention to the needs of the students. She would keep talking and talking. The homework was too long, and useless for the quals. It would help if she slowed down a bit.

Scott was my absolute favorite editor at the Missourian. He was really easy to work with and had reasonable expectations given that this class was a first time reporting class for many students in it. He was very fair and if you put in the work, he could tell. Honestly, probably my favorite teacher I have had in the Journalism School so far.

Scott is the best. His lectures are valuable, he will not waste your time. He will absolutely make you a better writer, but you have to be willing to work for it and take risks. His dad jokes make him a real gem. He struggles with Canvas, but is understanding and will re-work assignments to ensure fairness. Take Scott! You won't regret the decision
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Scott is the best J2100 Lab Steacher!!! He is so knowledgable and he wants you to succeed. He will stray from the syllabus a bit, making the schedule work the best for the class. He is so flexible and reliable - will reply to emails within minutes. He never speaks in a condescending way and doesn't assign crazy amounts of work!

If you have the chance to take a class with Scotty Swaff, DOOO IT! He's the actual best – he is really lenient and really helpful, you actually feel like you are learning and he makes class interesting. Also I'm pretty sure he knows every single person in Columbia, which is really helpful in terms of finding people to interview.

He's a tough grader but that's because he knows what he's talking about. He has tons of real-world experience and really wants you to succeed. By far the best j-school professor I've interacted with so far.

Scott is the best journalism professor you could ask for at the J2100 level. He's got a world of experience, though that means he has extremely high standards for your work. This class will be extremely tough, but if you love journalism and writing, you'll enjoy every minute of it.
He is the best editor at the Missourian. If you want to remain sane and have the ONLY nice editor get him! Just do your best reporting and he'll give you a good grade.

Amazing editor. Extremely helpful and nice. Best editor at the Missourian-- most sane too. Work hard enough for him and he will write recommendations for you and be very helpful to you for the rest of your time at the J-school!
Lectures are incredibly boring and have nothing to do with exam material, half of the time he just talks about his past career work. Didn't learn a thing but easy class with the lab adjunct.

I enjoyed his lectures and that he was an easy going guy. He can talk your ear off, but I can't say anything bad about the guy. He's open with talking about his life so it's nice to hear during his lectures. Class was sometimes a little dull, because the slides seems to be repeated.
Mark is an interesting guy. I enjoyed him all semester until the last few weeks where he made some uncomfortable/sexual jokes that weren't really necessary. Knows what he's talking about.
Mark is a funny dude. He gives lots of his field experience stories in lecture which helps supplement the material. Although lectures sometimes drag on, his lectures are interesting most of the time.

His lectures are interesting but long. Tests are half lecture, half test. He splits the lectures with Frank so it's an interesting class set up. Only two tests and they aren't even the majority of your grade- your lab is. Interesting class.

I never write reviews for teachers on here but I must say that Mark is probably the best teacher that I have had in the journalism school.  Strat writing II is the hardest I've ever worked in a class but it's well worth it because of how much you will learn from him.  He gives great feedback and is always looking out for your best interest.

I don't post on these things, but I figured if just one aspiring creative saw this it'd be worth it. Your grade should be of no concern. Put work in, get into Writing 2 and by the end of the semester you'll have a book that could potentially land you a gig in the industry. If he made the class easy, it'd be a disservice to you. Lucky to have him.

Lectures are usually short and not necessarily mandatory. You can buy an older edition textbook no problem and for cheap- so read that. The 2 tests are really easy and straight forward, especially if you read the book. Hard not to get an A. Go to lab, do those assignments and you'll get an A pretty easily.
Awesome class, easy lectures. If you just read the book, you'll be find. But I definitely suggest going to class, they're easy/funny and usually short.

Mark is the best, obviously has lots of industry experience and teaches with a sense of humor. Most of the work is done in the labs but the lectures are well worth attending. Some weeks have you put on the spot to come up with ads and present them (embarassing accents may be mandatory.) Award for most pop culture references in a single lecture.

teaches Strat Writing 1 & 2. Had him for 1, which was easy. 95% of work is done in lab (he doesn't teach it). Lectures were entertaining & he's witty & knowledgeable. Not sure I learned whole lot though. Good class, just wish there was more substance 2 the lecture! Swanson also realizes tho that it's a degree where u learn by doing (u do in lab)

Mark is a really nice, funny guy. The problem is that none of the strat comm professors seem to talk to each other about the material they cover because his course material is basically a watered down version of principles of strat comm. Easy, but kind of a snooze when it's all super general. Lab on the other hand was extremely helpful.

What a guy... He's extremely insightful, knowledgeable about the business, and has a great sense of humor.  If you're looking to be a creative in advertising, you basically have to take his class, but it's completely worth it 100%.  Mark does a great job helping you build your book.

She is currently teaching in Washington and Lee university and is definitely one of the best professors there. Really passionate about what she teaches and is incredibly humorous. She never grades students hard in her intro class. There are lots of chances you can take to put theory into practice in her class. Love her so much.

One of the best professors I've ever had.  She was enthusiastic about the course which made it enjoyable to attend class.  Even though this was her last year at Mizzou I would recommend her for any class!! Amazing person who wants her students to succeed. She is also hilarious and her tests are easy just go to class and do the readings

Alecia was a great professor. Her wealth of experience in the field made for some great stories in class, and she was a great resource for advice. She was straightforward, but made an effort to engage the class.

Although she is grad student, Alecia is one of the best instructors I have ever had. She applies her real world experience to make the class super interesting. She genuinely cares about each student and their success not only in the class but in the journalism field. I HIGHLY recommend taking a class taught by Swasy!

Alecia is an awesome instructor. She's a grad student but has worked at some prestigious publications and knows a wealth of knowledge. She is always available to help - even if it has nothing to do with class. She wants each of her students to succeed in the class (including getting stories published) and helps with internships. Get her if you can!
Very knowledgeable about creative writing and a great instructor. Good comments on workshops. A little bit eccentric so that sometimes you're like, "Wait...what's going on?" but still. Good teacher.
Yeah, she's cool. Unorthadoxed maybe but studly all the same.
She was really nice and forgiving about late assignments.

I think Larry is an overall great professor. He goes over the readings very effectively in class (our class was discussion based so doing the readings was important) and tries to facilitate discussion. He gives very in depth feedback on essays, which can feel daunting but is very helpful. He obviously cares about his work and his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Svabek taught 1/3 of my online POL_SC1100 class. He did a good job explaining concepts and seems unbiased. The class is overall easy and boring due to the online lectures and ultimately useless discussion section. Weekly online quizzes that I recommend you do while watching the lecture. 4 online exams and an online final, all multiple choice.

The class is graded by very few things (3 essays and attendance) but the criterion is extremely clear. The classes feel more like insightful discussions than lectures and are amazing. He cares a lot about his students and how well they understand the concepts. I would definitely recommend him for any of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had Carlos for my Civil Engineering Legal Issues course (online). He was great, very engaging with students and passionate about work. The exams are a little harder than expected, but the rest of the coursework is very straightforward.

Teaches online courses. Ive taken three classes with him at this point and its always pretty good. The lectures are pretty easy to understand and the material is usually not too complex, but its almost always interesting. Exams are notorious for being worded very strangely but they are not actually too bad. Overall great.

Dr. Sun is a professor that expects student to know a fair amount of material but is sloppy on presenting the material. The first test is a unexpectingly vague/ open ended  question and asks your opinion on a design. overall you need to review it.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Respected guy, everyone likes him as a person even if you don't like the class.
Lectures are dry, tests are basically just the book.  You have to know EVERYTHING.  Take it online if possible...
Prof. Swenson is a really great professor.  His lectures were actually really interesting and the exams are straight out of the notes. Just pay attention in class and you'll do fine.

This class is not hard. Swenson has law experience so he knows his stuff and always has examples from his cases to help clarify the material. Go to each lab, do the homework, and do the practice exams and study notes before each exam to do well! Exams are worth a lot but not difficult if you do those things. He is hilarious and I enjoyed the class.

To be clear this is John Swenson from Mizzou, not Duluth. Great teacher, uses very good examples. The book and notes are very straight forward and easy to study. Very interesting in the smaller class but less enjoyable in the big lecture hall.

Terrible, would not recommend. He is no help at all if you go to his office hours. The book is your best chance to learn anything but still reading alone you will not do well in the class. Possibly one if not the worst class I have taken in Duluth.

If you read the book, and outline the chapters you'll do fine on the exams. Lab in worth 20/200 points of your grade so its pretty important that you do well in lab. There is no such thing as "studying too much" for theses exams. The material is interesting, but the tests can be tricky. I went to class once the entire semester and did very well.

I found this class super easy. I never went to class because the book is the exact same as the notes. Outline or read the notes and know the definitions and you will be fine. The study guide questions for the lab are also helpful. Memorization is the key in this class, know how to apply the terms too.
Go to class, and you will get an A. It's not hard at all. Just pay attention and you will get a good grade. Don't miss lab, it's worth 10%.

Wow, if you are not required to take this class, DO NOT take it!! What started out as an elective for me (I liked MGMT 3540 BlawI) turned out the HARDEST & MOST Difficult class for me... Seriously, studying is useless because the tests are too unnecessarily specific and hard and tricky. I am not exaggerating either, I am a hardworking student..

I love BLaw and Swenson. His jokes are funny. He uses good examples to help you understand. His tests are hard but college isn't supposed to be easy. He challenges students to actually put forth effort if they want to succeed. I'm have a large amount of respect for Swenson. Great professor!!

DON'T TAKE BUSINESS LAW II!!!  He's a nice guy, but he forgets that its a MANAGEMENT course and not a Law School class.  Its unnecessarily specific, and the tests are ridiculous.  I studied 2 weeks out and he still wound up curving 10%+.  Trust me, take another class if you want to save yourself the headache.

not that bad a class either take the notes or get a group and rotate days to get the notes, study practice test and notes a little before test and wont be that bad, test depends on how bad the TAs are
Very very nice professor.  Always smiling and always wanting to help students.  He gives an outline of notes which is very helpful.  But his tests aren't as easy.  Study hard for the exams.

He's test a MC, but very comprehensive. If you're like me and cannot memorize stuff by just hearing or reading it once, you'll have to read your notes over and over again. He reuses his tests, the final is more difficult than midterms. But he's organized and teaches well. Some funny stories from his practice are a bonus!
No Comments
Doesn't care if you fail or not, and unless you have an iron-clad memory, you'll fail.

Not the easiest class since law can be confusing, but the terms are usefull for our daily lives.  He is friendly, easygoing, and very organized (which I love). His powerpoints are easy to follow and take your notes from so you can study.  It's basically written like laws.  Excellent teacher and lab.
Awesome teacher.
Good teacher,good guy. Tests are mostly MC with some short answer and are usually very tough. READ THE TEXTBOOK.
He's a good guy and knows his stuff, but only curves 1 point.
Great class, clear on work and on what needs to be learned.

Dr. Tanner is a great professor who explained the topics very well, but some lectures were lengthy in material because of what we were learning, but he made them entertaining and relevant. Tests were very similar to the homework and easy if you studied. Notecards were allowed for test. Lowest test dropped and extra credit for attendance at the end.

Hard because of the concept so you have to study a lot. Lecture was him reading and elaborating on slides for an hour straight making it hard to focus. Wish he did more practice problems/drawing out molecules in class. Having a PLA in the class was a life saver because she did in person office hours. However, he is a funny and unfiltered guy.

Really enjoyed tanner! Switched to biochem my sophomore year-so I took this primarly freshman based class my 2nd year, and this class really ensured that pursuing biochemistry is what I want to do. Allows cheat sheets on all exams, he also posts past exams to help study and I found that very helpful. Attendance is required but lowkey you should go

Great professor. Lectures are hard to follow only because concepts are harder. I recommend going back to watch them as well as studying the homework. Test are easy to understand but hard. His office hours are great for clarification on topics he's super helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Tanner has long and tiring lectures where information is constantly thrown at you. No point in memorizing specific terms, you will need to know the entirety of the concept. You really have to be on top of studying. You get 5x7 notecards for all exams. Final exam is optional. Definitely a weed-out class. Find a solid study group very early on
I know you are reading this Tanner

Dr. Tanner is honestly a great person. You can tell he genuinely enjoys the subject, but sometimes that makes it really hard to understand what he's saying. He goes through lecture slides pretty fast. You get a notecard and he drops one exam including the final. Its gonna be hard, but that's biochem for you:)
Easily accessible outside of class, enthusiastic during lectures, passionate about teaching, and extraordinarily knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tanner was a great 1090 professor! He goes a bit fast during lectures, so for me around 10 hours of studying a week outside of class was necessary to do well on the tests. He grades extremely fairly and often extends deadlines for homework if he notices people struggling. The slides are easy to follow outside of class. Would recommend him!

Dr.Tanner is good at lecturing. He goes a little fast at times, but if you pay attention, all the material you need is on the slides. His slides are also very easy to follow outside of class. He gives a lot of materials and examples, and you can use a notecard on tests. Overall he is very kind. Homework is always harder than tests.

For biochemistry, John Tanner is a good professor. Notecards are allowed for each test, which is a huge help for biochem. Attendance isn't specifically mandatory, but he does use iClicker questions for participation points. The online homework can also be grueling and tough at times, but overall his class is taught well for the difficult subject.

For BIOCHM 1090, Tanner was a pretty great professor. I had no problem with him at all and he is very capable of clearly explaining rigorous material in a way that makes it easy for students in an intro-level course to understand.

Make sure to attend lectures, he often does iClicker but does not give points off of correctness, only participation. He tends to just read off of the notes without translating it into his own words. This class is homework heavy that can range from 10-50 questions with three of four assignments for each chapter. You can have notecards on the exams.

Yet another iClicker class, but Tanner's sense of humor makes waking up early almost worth it. You can tell he has a passion for the subject and wants students to succeed. Lectures are fast-paced, but everything is recorded so you can review it later. Exams are challenging, but not impossible.

Great professor with a good sense of humor. Beware, he truly flies through the lecture slides at times, but he does record them for later viewing. Exams are not that difficult if you put effort into studying for them and do the hw. Some of the topics can be a little tricky to grasp at first, but the PLAs are super helpful.

Funny guy. First biochem class and made it a semester and decided it wasn't for me. Sometimes he is hard to follow and goes off on tangents about random things. Overall good teacher, but would use the tutors on hw problems.

participation matters because in the lecture he covers mostly everything from the textbook and you get points for your participation and answering questions during the lecture. His tests are not that difficult, if you do attend all his lecture, understand the concept and do all the homework given, you can get even 100% on the exam. He is so caring.

Great guy, I had him for 1090 during the pandemic and he was super helpful and understanding. I didn't read the book and passed because I attended all of his lectures but this might not work for everyone else. His lectures are in-depth and comprehensive though so if you're a auditory learner, he's great for you.

Dr. Tanner used the document camera during lectures and zoomed in on his writing. Whenever he trailed off bottom of visible page, some guy would always holler "PAGE UP!!" Made my day every time. There's LOTS of memorization and solving easy CHEM 1330-style questions. Dr. Tanner's voice is amusing on Tegrity double speed, I highly recommend.
Tanner is a very good teacher.  The class is difficult but you learn a lot.  I love his method of teaching and he has a witty sense of humor that makes every class enjoyable.
Great class, very challenging. Do the homework problems and you will be fine.

I really like Professor Tanner. He has a witty sense of humor and does a great job of explaining concepts. Tests are difficult but with lab points, extra credit, and a curved grading scale the class isn't too bad.

Coming from a straight A student, this was the hardest class I've taken at Mizzou thus far.  I'm actually retaking it with a different teacher and passing with an A+ at the moment.  Not helpful, tests are ridiculously hard, and he is extremely rude if you try to contact him.  Worst teacher I've come into contact with.

Dr. Tanner is a good teacher. However, his test are unreasonably hard. It was really difficult to know what study for the exams. Stuff that was not covered in class ended up on the exam.  In addition the exam averages were very low.

I ending up doing alright in this class and recieved an A-. I definitely had to work for it though. Labs grades saved most people and the class averages on tests usually ranged from around a 45-55%. The best advice I can give is to do every single practice problem in the book. Things never discussed in class often showed up on tests.

Terrible Chemistry professor. Lectures were taught straight from the book. Does not show many example problems in class so you're pretty much on your own for that. Asks lots of questions about exceptions and random things.

I came out of the class with an A but i really had to work at it. His lectures help clarify what you read in the book and the calculations that you must be able to do for the test. Know the odd balls of what you read he tends to ask questions about those.Do the recommended problems in book to help prepare for exam. Also gives extra credit quizzes.

Good teacher, Good lectures.... Challenging tests. Average test score was around a 60%. Labs will save your grade though.  Three extra credit quizzes given, if you attend class. I would say take this class only if its needed for your major or your have an unexplainable love for chemistry in which case i would assume you're a chemistry major.
Best Chemistry professor I've had in school, made everything easy to understand. The tests were somewhat difficult, but if you know the material he doesn't try to trick you.
Good professor, keeps the lectures entertaining. He posts all his notes online so if you miss something in class, you aren't screwed over. Tests are challenging but fair.

He is an average teacher. His lectures aren't great, and I had to do alot of reading and learning on my own outside of class. If you study a lot, the tests are manageable, and he gives a little bit of E.C. which is nice. Chem 3 is pretty much all math, so if you like math, you will be fine. Just make sure you take go to class and esp. labs!!

HORRIBLE teacher! He definitely does not care one bit for his students. I made a couple appts with him for help and he missed two of them, came late to the 3rd and basically just sat there and said I was stupid. The TA was a lot more helpful. I don't know why he chose to teach bc he has no personality, worst teacher I ever had. He was just rude

Tanner did not care about his students very much. He missed a lot of class and had a TA teach instead. He made fun of individual students in front of the whole lecture. His grading was fair, but he really didn't know how to explain chemistry to students. Take this class from Robertson instead.

Tanner is HORRIBLE!  He's one of the worst profs I've had.  He missed a great deal of class.  His lectures are very haphazzard, and he does not know how to explain things more than one way.  Either you get it or you don't.  I learned everything by reading the textbook.
Tanner was not the best teacher. It appeared he didn't really care about the students at all.
Not a bad teacher. The class was an appropriate difficulty and his grading scale was fair.

Seems like a smart guy, but not really interested in how much students learn.  I think that he thinks Chem 1320 should be a weeder class.  He's probably here more for research than teaching.  I didn't really realize how bad he was until we had Adams as a substitute (Tanner was gone for 2 and a half weeks).  Sometimes he has his TA teach.

This class takes a lot of studying. Tanner is very smart and definitely knows his stuff, but sometimes he doesn't dumb things down enough. He doesn't do a lot of practice problems in class. If you are really good at chemistry then Tanner would be a perfect teacher for you, but if you aren't so great at it then it might be kind of a struggle.

Dr. Violet is fantastic! Her class is discussion-heavy, but easy if you keep up with readings and participate. She's flexible as long as you communicate and genuinely cares about her students. The class involves readings, discussions, and weekly mini projects, some as group work. 10/10 would recommend!

Dr. Violet is fantastic! You can tell she really cares about her students and the accessibility of her class. She actually works with her students to get them through the course. Genuinely one of the best, most helpful class I have ever taken. A lot of eye opening information with genuinely enjoyable assignments.

This professor is PHENOMENAL. She values accessibility in homework and will accept late work at full credit weeks after due dates, Fantastic lectures and class discussions, one of my favorite course I have taken. Only one large project and it was optional to do it in a group. Just quite a bit of academic reading outside of class.

She taught incorrect and outdated information, including some that can be downright dangerous about livestock guardian dogs. She lectures very fast and won't stop if you're confused. She tries to make the class participate, but her questions often fall flat. She also brought in goats for lab that had active Orf infections.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My only problem with Tawnie is she goes through her material very fast and I would usually have to revisit the lecture notes after class. She like to engage the class by asking questions and having you talk to the people next to you. I loved Tawnie and the material (small ruminants) that she taught

Tawnie is a very nice professor and her lectures are very organized and interesting. I thought her labs were a bit tough but doable. Very approachable and happy to answer any questions you have. Her quizzes every week were pretty easy for me. Overall I really liked the sheep and goats section she taught.
The funniest and most interactive teacher I had in my first year. You will be asked to read a ridiculous amount, but he makes the class much better.

Tarkow is the MAN! He is an amazing human who genuinely cares about the success of his students. His lectures are always up to date and include plenty of humor, something important for a 9 a.m. class. Topics were a bit confusing for me at times but it was a great class I would recommend to anyone!
Great professor. Lectures were fun. The reading was all interesting. Study for the tests but they aren't too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took the first class in the Humanities sequence with Tarkow and loved it! He's very funny and entertaining with his lectures, and makes sure you understand the material. A couple of essays and tests in the class, but not too difficult. Just make sure to do the readings and you will do just fine. Excellent teacher, 10/10, would take again.

My favorite professor I've had. His lectures are great. He knows what he is talking about. This class is VERY heavy on reading, but the rest was pretty easy. He grades papers fairly but gives tons of helpful feedback. Quizzes are easy. If you read and pay attention to the lectures you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tarkow is such an amazing, passionate, and funny professor. He truly loves his subject and wants you to love it too. Class allows students to be very creative with their two projects. Tests are not incredibly difficult. You also get to read several plays and poems, including the Odyssey, and discuss them. Fantastic teacher and class!
Fun in class, knows what he's talking about! Helpful outside of class and cares about the success of his students.

Ted Tarkow is the ultimate professor. He's endlessly funny, lectures in a way that is interesting and informative, and always has time to help out a student in need. I've spent the semester raving to my friends about his classes, he is just that good! Tests are difficult and he can grade tough, but if you pay attention, you'll do just fine.

Professor Tarkow makes any topic interesting. I had him for two separate classes, and it was obvious that he really cares about his students and his classes. He can explain any concept and make it easy to understand, but he also pushes you to discover things for yourself. You get out what you put in, so definitely do the required readings.
Ted - He's a legend. The man is hilarious and an amazing story teller. Struggled with his essays, but he was always willing to help. Got to that final ready to ace it! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. He's great!

One of the greatest professors you'll ever have. I took Ancient World with him, a class that I wasn't particularly interested in, but he made it relevant and interesting. I would've loved a higher grade but I don't regret taking it b/c he's an awesome person to know (Dean of Arts & Sciences) and REALLY cares about his students. Take his class!

Tarkow is the best professor I've had at Mizzou.  He's really funny and is very open to different ideas and interpretations.  He is a relatively harsh grader, but if you do the work and pay attention in class, you should be fine.
Taking Greek Classics in Translation with him.  Super fun teacher.  Mostly lectures, with some discussion.  Interesting.  Fair grader.
he doesnt use blackboard, or powerpoints, and is pretty hard to follow while taking notes. you kinda have to adapt to his style.

One of the greatest teachers I have ever had. Tarkow is able to take student's comments at the beginning of class, and weave his lecture around those points. The discussion is always deep, but never tangential. He has a wonderful classroom presence. He's a picky grader, but he gives you all the tools in class you could ever need to do well.
Tarkow is a great guy. Some of his jokes get a little old after a while, especially his comparisons to Wal-Mart and MU sports teams. Eager to help and enjoys what he does.
No Comments
the best professor i've had so far - makes mythology fun and easy to remember. i will never forget the voices!

He's really a nice guy, someone you feel comfortable chatting with and going to with concerns about the class.  It's definitely not an easy class though, myth. contains a lot of information and it takes a lot of studying time to be successful on his exams.

Tarkow is hilarous and tells jokes that are actually funny. Extremely personable. His summaries of myths are incredibly good, and he knows a crazy amount.  The tests are fairly easy if you are willing to study. I highly suggest his classes.

Ted Tarkow: The Man, The Myth, The Legend.  He is seriously the single best professor I've EVER seen.  Uses humor, acting, and craziness to help ANY student learn the material.  Ted Tarkow is THE MAN!

Professor Freelin is amazing. The course is extremely easy and not a heavy workload. She is great at answering questions and providing feedback to help learn more. This class is an amazing class to take with Professor Freelin
Pretty easy class if you have any sort of knowledge on social workers. Lots of guest speakers during class, not a lot of homework. 1 chapter in the textbook a week.
Freelin was an extremely good professor. The amount of work in this class is extremely reasonable. Don't let the writing intensive part scare you, it's not much writing at all.
She wasn't bad, but she wasn't good. She never answered my e-mails throughout the semester. I don't think I paid attention once, and still got an A.
Professor Freelin is extremely nice, and this class was very easy, but also very helpful. Would absolutely recommend it to anyone!
LOVE professor Freelin she is amazingly nice and the class is super easy. Would totally recommend it!
Extremely easy class, taught by the Student Services Coordinator for the MU School of Social Work. She's very helpful with questions and fairly forgiving for missed classes.

Dr. Safranski was an amazing professor, and it was so much fun to take swine prod with him. You can truly tell just how much he cares about the swine industry through the way he talks and teaches about it. I took it non-writing-intensive, but I've heard from friends that the writing-intensive portion is not that hard either. Highly recommend!!

Does not take any submissions online, even when having computer or printer problems. Hand writes notes, hard to read. Let's you use notes on exams but not on quizzes. I never wanted to come to class was not a joy to be present in class.

Dr. Safranski is one of the best professors I've had. He's incredibly knowledgeable and gave us so many chances to learn outside the classroom: labs, field trips, real-world examples. His class was challenging but fair, and he truly wants students to understand and succeed. Also super personable and friendly! Exams are really hard but open note.

I took an online course with Dr. Safranski he did not grade anything until less than a week before out last day of class. We had to email everything to him instead of turning it on canvas and he lost assignments and did not take responsibility to that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You can tell Dr. Safranski genuinely wants to see his students succeed. If you like swine and know a bit about them, I would recommend this class. The assignments are easy so take the WI version. My only complaint would be that his lectures are pretty unorganized. I wish he went over more specific scenarios, similar to the questions on the tests.
Great teacher willing to help you just have to ask
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This instructor is a top 3 worst instructor in my life. She makes you watch an insane amount of boring lectures that are very very long, and then will create the most impossible quiz & exam for it. You genuinely can't miss a single word she says in your notes, otherwise you are screwed and you WILL fail the quiz/exam. Why TF are her quiz's so hard.

This is a very poorly managed professor. I understand being strict, but Tiffany Alexander takes it to another level. Absolutely no exceptions for late work, not understanding at all and is an all around poor example of a caring teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really had high expectations for this class, unfortunately for Tiffany she did not have a fantastic semester personally. As the marketing department had to take over this class, this became debatably the worst course I have taken at Mizzou. It was incredibly unorganized...I hope they get their act together for those who are required to take it.

I actually really liked her until she made everything confusing and complicated. Test was insane and no one felt confident. She disappeared and didnt respond to ANY of my emails spanning over 2 months. Graded us on our major final assignment with no rubric or feedback. Shes a great person but a terrible prof.

I'm a senior at Mizzou, this class was the worst experience of my college career. Attendance was taken inconsistently, grades weren't posted until the night before the final, the major group project was so disorganized that everyone received full credit. The professor disappeared halfway through, the replacement made things worse. Avoid this class.

The class isn't overly difficult but has significant issues reflective of Mizzou's marketing department. It was disorganized with unclear instructions, tests drawn from a 500-question pool, and the instructor disappeared mid-semester without explanation. Unless you're pursuing the Sales Certificate, I wouldn't recommend taking it.

There is no structure, and she is BEYOND unorganized. She will randomly call on students to answer questions or role play but doesn't even teach or lecture - yet there was over 100-points on the midterm (which no one knew anything). I still don't have a grade; she says there are extra credit opportunities "hot topics" but hasn't given any
Tim Langen is the reason I study Russian. He cares about his students and his subjects.

He's an angel. We love him, all of us in the Russian program. He is so kind. When I took Russian 2 last year and was sidelined by a brain condition, he was very understanding when I missed class. He is legitimately so sweet. An angel again. Take his class.
The course itself was designed to make you work for your grade, but I appreciated that Prof. Langen put forth effort to help make us better writers and thinkers.
The class makes you read a ton of books and is very fast paced but he gives few assignments. Discussion is 2-3 times a week and attendance is mandatory.

Professor Langen is super enthusiastic and tries to spread his love for Russia, but unless you have an intrinsic fascination with the Eastern European state, you will dozing for a lot of the lecture time. He tends to, not necessarily ramble, but repeat himself a lot, covering the same topic to its death. His TAs are pretty proficient, as well. :)

Langen works you hard. He assigns a lot of work and is strict on making sure you understand the concepts. But he grades easily. He makes you work to actually learn the language but doesn't penalize you for not being an amazing test taker.

His passion for Russia is obvious. His lectures are a little hard to follow but he has powerpoints. He is VERY helpful when righting the paper because although they are in depth he will meet with you to discuss until you understand. Russia isn't extremely interesting to me but he made class interesting.
He is an amazing lecturer! If you have him as a section leader, he grades fairly hard though.
Very hard class, very difficult teacher, incredibly disrespectful, work hard and you can get an A

He may the rudest and most condescending professor I have ever had in my entire life. He makes his own bizarre questions and rarely taught the work, he just expected you to figure it out. He made very disrespectful comments to the students. He expects a lot out of his students, but doesn't provide a foundation to allow the student to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Difficult and work-heavy class, yet I am so grateful I took it. He teaches you to be an independent thinker, a true problem solver, and cares deeply for his students. He appears intimidating and is a harsh grader, but is so for good reason. Once you can confidently solve a Dr. Reilly problem, you can easily work your way through any other problem.

Dr. Reilly has an exceptional lecturing style. His lectures were consistently engaging, and I found it much easier to retain the material because of his approach. He frequently calls on students during class, which motivated me to stay on top of the material and be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tough grader. Rude and condescending. International students feel uncomfortable. Asides from my terrible experience in his class, many others share this feeling. This is your first writing intensive course if you are following the approved biochem major plan - so why does he insist that every single report be perfect, publish-ready work?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: There was no option for it but I took Dr.Reilly for 1094. He is very intimidating at first. But he really does care about his students in his own way.  He also gives a lot of extra credit and take advantage of it!!!! He makes the class way more intense than it should be but it will prepare you for the other biochem classes you take.

I learned a lot in Dr. Reilly's class but he is a ridiculously tough grader. Your lab reports had to be about perfect and his exams were ridiculous too. He even said that he has been told every year that the midterm is way too difficult but he won't change it. Disrespectful and degrading when you ask him for help, total know it all. Don't take him.

Dr. Reilly's class is super tough. However, I don't think I have learned more in one class ever in my life. Dr. Reilly is so passionate and knowledgeable and wants nothing more than for his students to engage. If you put in the work, you will get so much out of this class. If you really care about biochemistry, you have to take from Dr. Reilly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Was nice at first but not accommodating during the pandemic. Was my only in person class and not easily approachable. TAs were great tho at explaining the stuff. HARSH grader. Midterm was very hard. Study a lot I recommend study groups. Doesnt post panoptos only brief slides. Take detailed notes & write very fast!

Dr. Reilly is one of the most intelligent people I have ever met. He was extremely rude to me on one occasion but never again after that. He is a very tough grader and the midterm is way too hard but I learned more in that class than I have in any other class so far. He is very knowledgable, the labs are fun, and you get used to how he wants papers

Dr. Reilly is a great professor and is helpful in succeeding in this course. The course is tough, and there are a lot of concepts that are difficult to grasp. Dr. Reilly is very approachable outside of class and is always willing to help with lab concepts, journals discussed in the discussion class, or any other question dealing with biochemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment:
HDFS 3050** 
Professor is SO kind and nice, lectures include random in person assignments that you need, so go to class as much as possible. Content is easy to follow, she's very thorough and answers all questions, 3 exams that weigh HEAVILY, she usually offers extra points for going to office hours, there is a group project, but it isn't too hard.

You have to work hard to do well and there are lots of papers, but professor is very accessible outside of class. She was very willing to help clear up any concerns and help you improve your papers. I loved the class and the professor!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes! If you are at all familiar with psychology you will be totally fine in this class. It is writing intensive, but only 4 essays and relatively easy to write. Awesome teacher-shes super helpful and wants you to succeed! Loved it!

Prof. Thomas had interesting lectures that I thought were very enjoyable! He was able to break down abstract concepts into simple terms. If you show up to class and raise your hand a couple of times during the semester, you can easily get an A. He's a clear grader and you'll know what to expect from quizzes and tests!

His lectures make no sense. He goes very quick over the slides and says too much to even take notes on. If you wanted to try typing your notes to keep up with the fast pace lecture, NOPE you must use paper or he will take attendance points off if your computer is even open. Overall, I would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yes the lectures are heavy, but there are attendance points that help your grade keep up and we had weekly discussion posts and quizzes ONLINE that are easy points! There are only three exams in the class, but he posts study guides and has a review day basically saying everything that will be on the exams. I am taking another class with him now!
The worst class I've taken so far, this guy should not be teaching. His lectures are difficult to understand and make no sense. The grading is also very hard.

This guy is not a joke. His lectures are so confusing, as a high gpa student who's a pre-med, this class was slamming me more than my STEM classes. The lectures are so fast-paced and lack structure. Additionally, there are only three tests in the whole class and if you miss one question on one test your grade drops 4%. Dont take this class .
Weekly quizzes and hard tests but overall easy

Called Title IX Thelen. Earned it. You don't know what to actually study--just how to listen to him go on about corn. So. Much. Corn. It's his research, so it makes sense, but you will end up crying because corn was discussed instead of whatever insanity goes into making his tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Thelen is clearly knowledgeable, but he tends to skim quickly through slides and read off them verbatim. He is a tough grader, but exam performance tends to improve over the semester. Office hours help if you come in having a basis about the material and questions at the ready.

Overall not a horrible class but a little tough, exams are very specific and account for most of your grade. His lectures are really fast in person with a lot of information on each slide, but posts lectures pre-corded online that are helpful. Readings are really long but helpful. Homework load is light. Attendance not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for my first fall semester, and he was the only class I had an A in. The textbook homework is due after the tests, and there's no final.

Dr. Trull is a really nice professor! I ended with a B (88%) in this course which I think was good considering that I attended a little over half the time, never really read the textbook pages, and etc. He does randomly do extra credit for students who show up to class (which I did get all 3 times he did this). He is overall really funny!
Easy class. Do the homework and exams will be easy. Dr. Trull is a great guy and I would recommend taking at least one class with him.

Dr. Trull is awesome! If you have any chance to take his class, especially psychopathology, do it! I showed up to pretty much every lecture and received some extra credit for showing up. His lectures can sometimes go a little off-topic, but the stories he tells and his sense of humor are top-notch!

I LOVE TRULL! This is the easiest class ive ever taken tbh. Homework is on cengage and is very direct. Tests are questions pulled from homework too. Attendance isn't necessary but he occasionally gives out extra credit if you show up. Hes so funny and so understanding. If youre looking for an easy A, definitely take his classes

I overall liked Professor Trull. He provided really useful information about the course subject. I thought some of his lectures felt a bit long, but others were really interesting. If you complete the homework (there isn't a lot of it) and pay attention during lectures, you will almost definitely get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Best professor at Mizzou easily. His lectures aren't too boring and he has recordings of past lectures online. The homework doesn't take too long and is rather easy to complete. The tests cover 3-4 chapters and aren't difficult either. If a majority of people get a question wrong, he will admit fault and give the point for that question.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was very easy and he makes classes interesting. Homework is on Cengage and easy to follow. Tests are all online on Canvas and open note. I would recommend this class to anyone because it would be hard to not pass with a decent grade

Great class to take and you do it at your own pace! Homework is necessary and helps a lot on the tests. His lectures easy to understand but feel. very long with the amount of slides covered. Easy A if you put just a little work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: loved his class. homework could be heavy sometimes, but its very helpful and simple. he has a fun personality, likes to make jokes and is very knowledgeable about what he is teaching. gives quite a bit of extra credit as well.

Great professor. Very funny and approachable. Enjoyed his lectures just because of how much knowledge he had about each topic. Attendance isn't required but I recommend going if you want good notes for the tests. The online homework is also a huge help when studying for the tests.

Trull's lectures are long and dry. He had too many guest lecturers and the material dragged on. Complete MindTap on time and try to get a high score. It's worth a good portion of your grade, but he doesn't submit until the very end of the semester. Tests are easy-use practice tests. I'm pretty sure he was high at a lot of the lectures.
He taught in a way that kept your attention and made you learn what you needed to. He is also very passionate about his field which is great to have in class.

Trull is a great guy! Super chill, quirky, and funny. Though I can't really blame him for this, the course was a bit too easy in my opinion. Psychology is pretty much all vocab memorization/common sense. Never went to class after the first few weeks and got As on all but one test just by doing the homework and studying quizlet...
