Mindtap is heavily used! Extra credit is given for attendance a couple times over the semester. He is funny and makes lecture enjoyable!

Dr. Trull is great!  I genuinely enjoyed going to class, though you really don't have to in order to do well.  He gives a ton of extra credit, though, and usually only if you show up, so I recommend going.  Informative, but easy.  He wrote the textbook, so it's a must-have.

Dr. Trull is an absolutely wonderful professor! I have always been interested in psychology and had been leaning toward changing my major to it, and this class sealed the deal. Attendance is not necessary, but Dr. Trull makes class fun. Overall, it's incredibly interesting and informative, but it's also not difficult to get an A in.

Great topic and gives a ton of extra credit! He wrote the textbook so it is extra helpful to read it as that is where the test comes from. Attendance is not mandatory, but he does give extra credit for going  among other things. Great professor and very kind and understanding. Homework is 40% and all online.

Dr. Trull is by far the most entertaining professor I've had.  He's very friendly and approachable, and extremely knowledgable.  He gave E.C. on 7 different occasions when he thought it looked like many people weren't there, so go to class.  Great guy, highly recommend for Psych.

Dr. Trull is hilarious and makes going to class fun. He wrote the textbook, so the test are straight from the textbook. Had a T.A. help him out and she was awesome. Overall, I really enjoyed his class and if you put in the time you will get an A.

Dr. Trull is HILARIOUS. Some of the funniest lectures from any professor I've ever had. Makes learning the content fun and exciting. He wrote the book, so attending the lectures aren't mandatory, but sometimes offers extra credit randomly for people who attend. Never studied for any of the tests, got at least an 80% or higher on all of them.

Dr. Trull is one of my favorite professors! He offers extra credit, curves test, is super knowledgable and has a lot of great experience to offer for his students. I would HIGHLY recommend him for abnormal psych!

Dr. Trull is a nice guy who is entertaining to listen to. He is very knowledgable and has a lot of experience in the field. His class is super easy if you read the textbook since he co-authored it. Also tests are usually curved. Highly recommend him.
Dr. Trull is entertaining to say the least. He wrote the book and everything on the test is from it. Online Homework from book every week but is pretty easy.
Awesome teacher! Makes class interesting and engages student in learning. I didn't buy the textbook, but still ended up with an A simply from attending class.

He wrote the book, so don't make the first mistake I did & just rely on the notes. He takes everything from the book, you really do not need to go to class - although he is really funny and makes it interesting! Even though he is laid back, some of his test questions are tricky!
Did not go to class at all. Got A's on the tests by reading the textbook only. enough said :)

Great teacher! Related well to students.  Like most psychology professors though he was really knowledgeable when it came to the disorder he was given a grant to study at the university, but lacked in knowledge in some other areas.  For tests READ THE BOOK! and take notes while reading each chapter.  I did this and ended up with a 95% in the class.

SO HOT and very funny. Dang. A really good teacher, listens to and answers questions clearly, doesn't treat you like you're stupid for having questions or giving an answer that might not be correct. Great professor. Does require a fair amount of studying for tests, though; read notes AND assigned book readings and you'll be fine.
Two words - bonus slide!24
I love this class! Dr. Trull definitely makes the class interesting and I love going to his class! I took abnormal psychology with Dr. Trull!
Mr. Trull is a lot of fun.  He shows so much enthusiam for the content he's teaching. He keeps his lectures interesting and his tests are generally pretty simple.

Great teacher! Lectures are both interesting and enlightening. Teacher is very helpful and friendly. Does not "talk down" to you or make you question your intelligence. Content of class can be challenging, the prof. makes an effort to make sure EVERYONE is on the same page.
I took her J1200 class. Although there were many assignments, she was fair and supportive.

She taught complete common sense and then got angry at the class when no one wanted to answer a complete obvious question. She doesn't get grades in on time whatsoever, but expects you to turn in all your assignments not even a minute late. Some assignments from the first week of class weren't graded until week 16.
For an intro class the expectation is way to high.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have a very positive impression of her. Although the class is quite theory-intensive, she is both approachable and highly knowledgeable

She is hard to understand and so boring. Every class is the same material and none of it is applicable. It's just powerpoints about the same three topics, and she asks questions that are so painfully obvious. Get ready to hear about the definition of things you learned in middle school.

Professor Schnurbusch challenges you in a good way in Meat Animal Eval by teaching real skills, not just facts to memorize. Attending class is key: she reviews material, gives helpful feedback, does extra credit practice, and sets you up to succeed. Participation and quizzes help learning while helping you apply meat evaluation skills.

Professor Schnurbusch challenges you in a way, but does so with the intent to build knowledge, not create more stress. She clearly prepares you for what she wants you to know, reviews material, and is open to feedback. Her goal is student success. Just showing up earns quiz and participation points that reinforce learning and make class feel doable

Her lectures are somewhat long and may be boring if you have previous experience with animal products. She is a good teacher if you pay attention and ask questions. Lab material is what your lab practicals will be over, although they were fairly simple if you paid attention. She is blunt so be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 50% of grade is 1 lab practical and the final. Continuously states blatantly wrong information about her own content or just random things in general, very condescending toward students, does not record lectures but also slideshows are very vague so make sure to go to class to hear her yap about whatever she wants to that day. Not worth the effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: challenging and helpful.
This class was hard not because the material was confusing but because the tests were confusing and covered WAYYYYY too much material. Structure of the class is horrible.

The layout of the course is not ideal, but its the only one at MIZ. Theres A LOT of info to remember so print off the study guide and answer the questions after each lecture. You HAVE to study almost every day for this class. Meet with kalogeris weekly and go over study guide questions, he is intimidating at first but is very nice & intelligent!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: physiology will be hard regardless of the professor!! Take the time to meet with kalogeris and go over the study guide with him. He started making his own mini textbooks that follow the lecture in order and are VERY helpful. He is intimidating at first but is very nice and knowledgeable! He is always willing to meet and help go over material!

Honestly what you put into the class is what youll get out. Kalogeris comes off as intimidating at first and lectures very fast so I suggest printing off slides for lecture and writing supplement material he says in lecture. Take the time to meet with him and youll realize he is very nice, jokes around will slow things down when explaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ted is the second professor you will have in MPP 3202 and his style of teaching is different than Parrish. Make sure you pay attention to the slides because he goes fast and that you read all the materials he gives or you will fail
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken. all tests, but labs are easy points.

He is the first professor and class I have actually hated with a passion. There is no blank space in his lecture slides - sooo much info!! But, still, somehow when you do the long ass study guides, some of the answers are not in the notes but something he said during class. His tests suck. You need to know every bit of detailed information.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kalogeris went very in depth for a 50 minute class - he often ran over (don't schedule a class right after physiology - you'll be late). His exams are tough. Seriously, don't skip class. He says useful stuff that's not found on the slides that you need to know for the exams. Online homework and labs help bump up class scores, but not enough.
The tests are difficult even if and when you spend hours at the library. Do well on the first two tests because the last two are impossible. Lab points are the only thing that save your grade.

the ppt are super long, the study guide are not up to par with the tests, need to know the details for the exam, will not do well if you skip class, recommend going in for office hours.  exam are tough,.

Gives "study guides" for exams... useless. Expects you to know 10 lectures worth of information containing over 400 slides and copious amounts of information for 40 question exams - and forget a curve. Seems nice in lecture and means well but the class as a whole is not laid out well.

Although he comes off as a nice person he's hard when it comes to grading. He would say nice things to your face but when it comes to grading he would go behind your back to give you bad grades. He also doesn't believe in his students and needs to retire.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tom is who every students wants to have a lecture with. He's great

Tom is amazing. He's honest but fair. It was an online class, so he encouraged participation, but he really cares about how his students feel about the class. I learned a lot and saw things from different perspectives. We had a few quizzes, but they weren't trick questions or anything. Everything was online.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: If you are taking 2100, take it with Tom. He wants to get to know you and really cares. If you piss him off, he'll let you know, but he is just bringing the real world newsroom into the classroom. He has his dad jokes which are fun and he really knows how to make a class a community. Basically everyone loved him and respected him, he knows whats up
Kind and engaging, loved her!! Very clear expectations and straightforward grader. Also accepts any late work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Totsch was an awesome professor. This course has A LOT of writing though. Weekly discussion posts, unit summaries, etc. The content can be interesting. There is also a LOT of reading. Very reading and writing heavy even more than some of my writing-intensive courses. She does a great job teaching the content though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very easy and interesting class! Recommend for anyone needing a gen ed, she was very nice and understanding.

Overall not terrible, what you would expect from a college English course.  She is kind of rude if you have a different opinion than her, She once told me my opinion was wrong and i found it hard to participate any more in her class.  Papers aren't awful, could reuse ones from High school.  Participation and attendance are MANDATORY for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class is pretty easy, just attend every class and do all assignments and you will be great!

Ms. Toro is an incredibly charismatic lady and while you will be screwed if you haven't done the reading, her class was not bad at all. She wants everyone to participate and notices if you don't speak up- though, she is so nice that I wasn't even scared. Group project w library citations. I took her her first semester and she was great.

Nice teacher, but very sassy if you don't attend class. Film screenings are a must because of the quizzes at the end, but other than that your only other grades are 2 tests and 2 papers that she grades pretty harshly.

The material is actually pretty difficult but he gives an ungraded practice quiz before every exam that is very similar to the actual exam, so use it to study. His lectures are pretty hard to pay attention to, but anyone can pass this class with a relatively low amount of effort if you know where to look. Watch out for the final, its kind of hard.

exams are very easy, they are basically a copy of the study guide he gives us. I found most of my learning came from the homework. Lectures are brutal, they are very boring and he has horrible handwriting so it makes it hard to follow along. He can be intimidating but talking one-on-one with him he is helpful and accommodating.

Dr. Tsoi is really kind and has a good understanding of diff eq but the lectures came directly from the textbook so they could be hard to follow at points (textbook isn't great). He does give out a very helpful review packet for the exams and usually draws the exam problems directly from it. Homework can be challenging but does help you learn

The homework was difficult, but the exams and the final were straightforward and based on the lectures. He teaches straight out of the textbook and is not a very engaging professor. He didn't take the time to get to know his students, and his class was exam-weighted. He gave good review packets before exams that were similar to the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not much homework. Textbook is the worst diff eq textbook out there. Teaches straight from the book, not worth going to class. Saving grace is that exams were extremely straightforward and he was very caring when responding to emails. Learn whole course on YT from Dr. Trefor Bazett and it's easy A. I rate Tsoi high because of the easy exams.

We did the same things over and over each lecture like how to determine if a number is prime or composite (non prime) for over 4 lectures. Each and every lecture is like a summary of the first two introductory paragraphs of the book but in poorly spoken English. 95% of the homework you will NOT be taught in class. Exams covered lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: canvas website had almost no information, felt like we did the same things in class everyday for weeks without new learning

Tsoi teaches right out of the textbook, so there is no need to go to class. He "took attendance" at each class but it never counted for credit. Homework is optional and if you do it and are on the edge of a grade, he will bump you up. Quizzes and Exams were straight from the textbook but changed the numbers. Easy A if you are good at memorizing.
Goes over material super quick and literally only once. Ive had her for two classes now and Im sick of it I cannot stand the way she teachs her slides make no sense.

An awful professor that claims she wants you to succeed but makes it impossible to. Difficult grader looking for proper wording on exams (you won't get points for showing you understand the topic), required iClicker attendance, weekly quizzes, no notes posted, NOT flexible. Expect to struggle on every exam no matter how much you study

Trista is hard to approach and when you do she comes off as friendly but will make you second guess yourself when asking a question. I have reached out over email multiple times and she never gets back to you. It is very hard to communicate with her. You have to put in a lot of your time and constantly pester her if you want to succeed.

Weekly quizzes based on lectures from that week (lowkey kinda hard-ish). The exams are graded harshly bc if you don't add a specific word or mention something then it points off. Attend lectures and exam reviews. Also offers extra credit papers from reading articles/videos. Nice teacher, but grading made me mad.

She was extremely passive aggressive and if you did even one thing wrong you got a bad grade. She made multiple people in my lab cry and didn't even care about it. She doesn't care if you pass or fail and doesn't try to help you succeed. She doesn't explain her lecture slide well and doesn't spend time going over what will be on the tests.

I absolutely love Dr. Strauch. She is a great teacher and actually cares about her students. She is enthusiastic in all her topics and will help you in anyway she can. Zoology is a great class and has very interesting and cool topics. The labs are very hands on and you get to dissect a plethora of organisms. Highly recommend.

Dr. Strauch is AMAZING!! By far my favorite professor at Mizzou so far! She is very caring and wants your to pass. Although, you need to work for it, she gives you everything you need to pass, so just put in the time. If you need help she is very understanding and wont make you feel dumb!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great teacher- by far my favorite AnSci teacher here at Mizzou. She also teaches Captive Wild Animal Management which was super interesting and fun. Definitely recommend her!

As long as you show up to class, pay attention to lecture, and read the ebook, this class will be easy. Trusler's lectures can be long and slow paced but a lot of the material she covers is fascinating.
The exams can be a bit weird as the questions are wither very easy or completely random.

She's fine. She is friendly enough, and does seem to be very knowledgeable in her subject. The class is not a lot of work, the midterm+final are both online and open-note (however there are two essays for each). Her lectures can be boring, but overall the class is fine and is a mostly easy elective credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite a lot of studying for something I took as an introductory gen ed. The exam questions can range from pretty easy to super specific, but the assignments outside of that are easy (reading quizzes, 3 small projects). The textbook took a super hard dive into promoting left-wing ideology out of nowhere, and she would definitely lean into it.
Tests are easy if you study

She is the worst professor I have ever had and I've had Keller. She is disrespectful to her students, doesn't answer questions, and treats us like 5 year olds. I once asked her a question and she asked me a question back and I told her I don't know and she never helped me. She doesn't care about her students unless they are perfect.

It was incredibly difficult to learn basic concepts in this class. It was very test and lab assignment based. If you missed one or two labs you would be put back. If you bombed one test, it was impossible to raise your grade. The tests were also not multiple choice and very difficult for the amount of material taught. I would not take this class.

Makes you feel dumb, the way she teaches is not attainable to keep a steady grade. You turn your homework before class begins and then goes over the assignment, which is just vocab over the unit. Doesn't have recorded reviews for exams so if you can't make it you're completely screwed. She's an anthropology major teaching bio?
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This prof will make you feel dumb if you don't understand. She can be condescending and treat you like a child. Very frustrating canvas pages as assignments are posted on a completely different page than the actual labs. If you have a problem, you're better off figuring it out yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is confusing, especially if you do not have a bio lecture in the same semester. Complete the labs BEFORE the lectures, and there is no textbook. Made me feel stupid when I asked how I should be learning the topics.

I would not recommend any classes with this teacher for three main reasons 1) She makes you feel stupid for not understanding the material during lab and lecture 2) There are only three tests and 12 labs, so you have to do good on everything - it is hard to raise your grade after you bomb ONE assignment 3) If she doesn't like you, you will know..
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Trusler is decent at teaching. She has a good understanding about biology, but her main study is anthropology. I feel like there is a lot of information to learn, and sometimes it can be hard for her to simplify it for students. I had to do a lot of outside work in order to understand concepts and study in order to do well in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing anthropology lab professor. Passionate about the subject. Very willing to help and patient. Funny and personable. Highly recommend her. Flexible if unable to attend lab.
Very nice teacher, helps when you need it.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. It was the biggest burden of my week. He needs to give more time. So difficult. DOES NOT TEACH AT ALL. He copy and pastes YouTube links. The material is from 2021 and outdated. BIGGEST WASTE OF TIME. You'll spend 10-40 hours on a project for a 15/20. He never responds to emails. Pathetic, lazy, waste of time.
Worst professor at Mizzou. He takes months to grade projects, hasn't responded to a single email, doesn't teach, all his lessons are copy/paste from some other website.

(This is for IT2610) Probably the laziest and worst IT professor. Pretty much exclusively assigns packets with little to no directions. You gain practically no knowledge from this class, just busy work that burdens you. It feel like I could ask chatGPT to create a digital media and design class and gain substantially more knowledge.
His name brings traumatic flashbacks to anyone who's taken his classes
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Any of the 2630 comments you see are pretty accurate. The layout of the learning material is literally so confusing and out of place. And like some others mentioned he uses youtube videos from some random person? So far I've managed to just wing this class and do good. Just answer the weekly discussion and project and you're fine.

I literally have 1 semester left and this guy was my worst nightmare. I am not very good at 3D modeling, nor do I want to be because of him. I really tried my best on these early projects to model easy objects like silverware, but apparently they aren't EXACTLY like my reference image. The man expects perfection. Absolutely DO NOT take this class.

I highly suggest not taking any Michael Tompkins class. It is unorganized and the only thing he does is send you YouTube tutorials and most of them are made by someone else. He doesn't grade anything until last minute, and will leave you confused on every assignment. Spent 10-60 hours per assignment. Rendering videos takes 2-3 days, may want 2 PCs.

I was very dissapointed with Professor Tompkins and this class. I am currently taking 2610, Digital Media Design, and was actually looking forward to these topics. Half the time, he literally posts the modules for the wrong class, putting us behind another week. The class content is just taught in bullet points on canvas. Very dissapointing.

He doesn't actually do most of the lectures, just links outdated youtube videos. He's usually 2+ months behind in grading and is impossible to get ahold of for questions. Also has a very bad late work policy combined with not being able to know what your grade is months after the assignment.

IT 1000 online is trash. He posted last semester's work on Canvas, so nobody could access anything the first week. Insane amount of reading, which is just a lame collage of the internet. Wikipedia links, redneck YouTube tutorials, and no original content. Requires Discord - why? Assignments are due on Friday night. Save your money, avoid this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is primarily YouTube videos and long lectures. For whatever reason it took weeks / months for grades to be put in (...like all the other reviews...), but to be honest, it was the lack of effort from the TAs rather than the professor himself. Other than that, if you have >= a single braincell you can get 100s on all the assignments.

This class consists of a bunch of recorded powerpoints from 2 years ago. Each one read word for word in a monotone voice with nothing added. The assignments are not graded for at least 3 months, yet the late policy is very strict. The professor does not respond to emails. The game making assignment is a youtube video made by some random person.

Jesus christ his class was a mess.
HOW ARE YOU A TEACHER AND NOT GRADE FOR 2 MONTHS!
HOW CAN YOU GET AWAY WITH THAT!

Overall, a very unorganized and uninformative class. Professor has posted course materials late almost every single week and has rarely given extensions for lost days. Assignment instructions are very unclear and "lectures" are usually just random youtube tutorials that aren't helpful. Also weekly group zoom discussions that feel very forced.

Assignments are rarely posted at the beginning of the week, sometimes posted on Wednesday and due Friday. Lectures rarely work and are usually outdated Youtube videos. If you need help bcuz of this, don't expect to get it. Nothing has been graded since September and it is November as I write this. I had a 4.0 before I took this class. Not anymore!
I can't believe I'm paying to be linked a bunch of YouTube tutorials and

Expect unedited videos full of "uhh umm actually don't do that" backtracking that wastes time I could actually be doing the assignment. Speaks slower than my dead grandma and even on 2x you will be pulling your hair out of your head listening to him go "uhh" while he himself tries to remember how to use blender. Horrible lectures and worse teacher.

Do not take this class if you expect to get into any game theory it is strictly design. Weekly discussions that are meaningless, impossible to get a hold of, follow-along Unity tutorials way too long and he makes mistakes but doesn't cut them out/show the correct way. Brutally slow speaker. Don't expect to get grades until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tompkins does a decent job with his prerecorded lectures which will walk you through the assignments in the class. It's a great class to take if you want to learn the basics of animation. Make sure you have a decent computer or else your pc will explode. Animation renders take hours to complete and will kill your pc if it is not good.

He talks lots of nonsense bs in his recorded lectures, does not really emphasize what is really important. 
He hardly ever reply back to your emails. Don't forget this is also an online class, so don't expect to get a a hold of him:)

This professor seriously needs to restructure his classes so they make sense to anyone else but him. The presentations are a joke and he talks sooo slowly even at 2x. His assignments are just copy pasted across the board so expect typos and things that make no sense. You're better off watching a couple youtube videos to actually learn blender.

Like media/game arts? This class & prof will change your mind. Couldn't reliably explain rubrics or grades the same way twice, gives repetitive assignments that make no sense to anything in the course, takes forever to grade & the feedback was meaningless, & every assignment was just busywork. He's nice, but I learned more from youtube
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst class I have taken at MU so far. Tompkins wasn't there for months, no announcements or anything. Then he would give a discussion post assignment. There were 5 assignments total! I love game design and the process of design but he made a joke out of it. The assignments were very basic random aspects of gaming cobbled together. Terrible.

Professor Tompkins did a terrific job teaching the basics of simulation and modeling using AutoDesk Maya. He is approachable and will respond quickly to any question that may arise during the class. The assignments are self-explanatory and professor Tompkins has given rubrics and tutorials that will help during certain assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Game design was a great class to participate in. Weekly discussion boards to communicate and see what your other classmates have idea wise with projects. Some assignments, professor Tompkins gave me an outline that just needed to be filled out. If you like video games and want to learn more about the process, take this class!
OMG HES MY FAVORITE!! Always remembers everyone's names and makes me think about real world problems with myself during lectures
Will post quizzes due day of and not say anything. But really nice guy.

Tummons really cares about the well-being of students. He doesn't tell you what's right or wrong, but rather how to work on your strengths. To earn participation points you have to sit with a group, and there are group projects. Beware that you will take a billion personality tests that all tell you something different so it will get confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a down-to-earth and engaging lecturer. He's very clear with what he expects from you and doesn't assign an unrealistic workload. Fun class with lots of group-focused discussion and projects. Also can be quite funny at times.

It is very evident that Dr. John Tummons really cares about his students. Even though there's a lot of assignments/quizzes/tests/projects, Dr. Tummons is more concerned that you walk away from the course having learned something about yourself, rather than memorize everything there is to know about leadership. Highly recommend him!
Great professor and course. My only comment is the midterm was challenging, so studying for it even if the class is easy.

His class is so much fun, and he makes lectures very engaging! It is not you just sitting there and him speaking at you the entire time. He includes activities that help you learn the topic, along with getting to know your classmates around you - so sit near people you want to get to know. He uses textbooks, but genuinely you may not need it.
Lots of projects and quizzes, however the class is pretty easy to follow . Lectures a lot, but has very fair policies and an entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Tummons is an awesome guy. He delivers class material effectively and you also feel like you get to know him. He is very approachable in and out of class and treats students with respect.
Great guy! Will work with you, 100% recommend his class!!

One of my favorite professors! Being a larger class he tries to know everyones name! He grades all the assignments and gets great feedback! You can tell that he genuinely cares about the well being of all of his students! Besides the midterm the class was a super easy he tries to make the class interesting. He also gives a lot of extra credit!
He was a really funny teacher who was totally understanding about issues outside the classroom. I would recommend this class to any business/ hospitality management majors.
Tummons is amazing! I had fun in his class and I would reccommend any of his classes!

He is very energetic. Most of your points come from clicker questions during class. A few projects on your own, one group project as a final, and one midterm exam. Material is posted online, and is mostly common sense.

Dr. Tummons is a great teacher! I accidentally forgot to take a quiz on blackboard and I spoke to him about it and he just gave the points to me anyways! Extra credit is given through clicker points and in class assignments. 1 midterm test & group project presentation for final. Super easy!  I would take this again! He is such a nice guy.
Lots of assignments. Not many are that hard. Awards participation pointa using a clicker. Easy class just have to use a little effort. Really nice guy

I actually took Darin Tuck in "U.S. History to 1877" At MidAmerica Nazarene University (where he is teaching now). He was amazing; my favorite teacher ever. His lectures were really helpful, so be sure to take notes. He's super kind and caring, and if you work with him, you will get an A. You do have to read a lot for his class, but it's worth it!

I recommend finding a different TA. Tuck isn't absolutely horrible but he's a pain. I found him to be rude and condescending most of the time. Also, he would take off random points from assignments and give little or vague reasons, almost as if he doesn't want to give a higher grade even if you've earned it... I think it's a power thing.
RUDE. Grades extremely hard. Find a different TA at all costs.

Professor Tuck is a great guy! He is extremely passionate about history. While there are a lot of outside readings, he didn't give any other outside work, and there were no papers! However, the tests are 50% 'short' answer, and 50% essay; but the questions were not hard to answer. If you attend classes and discussions, you will do fine in his class

My boy Tucker is super chill. Tests are a pain and all the material is in the reading. Classes though, were always fun, easy, and super low-key. He won't force you to do anything outside your comfort zone, so don't expect to be challenged, but it's a good easy intro to public speaking.
Overall this class was great - lectures are easy to follow, speeches are pretty low-key, and the activities are really fun and engaging. I definitely recommend taking this class with Tucker!

Tucker is a fantastic instructor. Simply showing up to class every day & not being late is the hardest thing you have to do to pass. Every class consists of a minimal "lecture", followed by a fun in-class activity. He gives you good, detailed feedback on all of your speeches. Exams were mostly easy, only have to study a night or so before the test.
Super nice, super cool, overall a great instructor!
Great professor. Cares about students.
Cool guy, likes healthy food.
poor
Great teacher. Really fun. Had him for professional development 4201. Very unorganized. Lots of guest speakers and very helpful toward my professional career!
Awesome
There's a lot to know for the tests, but he's a really fun guy and a good instructor.
Most definitely one of the best professors in the business school.
THIS IS THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!!!!!!!
An extremely friendly, humorous professor.  Is very approachable and makes you feel comfortable in class.

Tyler is a great professor and guy in general. Gives amazing, interesting lecture and actually cares about his students. His course is pretty engaging so if you take it you will definitely end up with new friends. Would take again 10/10

extremely confusing and unclear expectations. random assignments and didn't grade anything for the entire semester until the last week of classes. hard to succeed when you don't know what to do. at any point of the class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very funny dude. Knows how to run a public speaking class by constant use of putting you in the spotlight. After a few weeks you'll be comfortable with just about everyone in the class if you just talk. The speeches can be challenging if you have stage fright but Tyler makes it tremendously easier. The petty assignments are graded generously.

He's a really nice guy and can be super understanding! He makes it clear that he expects you to do your best and has zero tolerance for people who skip his class, so this isn't really an easy-pass class. He gives great feedback if you ask for it, but he's kind of slow to grade and doesn't really keep you updated until the end of the semester.

By far the best professor I have ever had. He cares so much about his students and does the most to ensure that they succeed. He is so incredibly funny and created an environment where it is easy for every student to connect. And contrary to popular belief, I don't hate you.
Amazing!!
Tyler has been my favorite professor since I started college. He made Public Speaking super engaging, I recommend this class to anyone.

Easily my favorite professor of my college experience so far. Has excellent command of his classroom and keeps the class entertained because he is absolutely hilarious. He also has genuine concern for his students well-being and is almost always available outside of class for extra help. Should be promoted ahead of his peers, and it's not close.

Tyler was my favorite professor in college. He made me want to go to class every day because of how entertaining he makes his class. Never a dull moment. Also really helpful outside of class. He has experience with sales so he helped me to land a sales job by giving me some tips! Awesome person overall.

Awesome class because of how absolutely funny he is. Hes slow on grading so if you want to know how you did on something youll have to ask. He starts the class with a question, usually something funny and actually cares so much about his students mental well-being (shown multiple times throughout semester). Hes a great professor!

Looks like the old man from UP. Not a hard class by any means. His exams aren't bad if you know the material. There will be no surprises. There are  only 2 topics that he covers bad. Those were FGPAs and 2 address microcode. If you get these you get what he is talking about. He has quizzes once a week, they're good @ indicating how you do on exams

Will spend entire lectures explaining things that you may use in the field on down the line but does not include these things on tests, homework or labs. He has wasted entire class periods inventing a problem only to solve it and produce the wrong answer. He will confuse you. Read the text book but not everything covered is in there. TA is useless.
He is horrible.

Tyrer is overall a nice guy, but is useless as a professor.  Half this time he doesnt even know what he is saying, so he will pause in confusion for minutes at a time. I took this course at a different university and the quality of teaching was rediculously better then Tyrer. Avoid this teacher if possible.
Overall nice guy.

Testing system stupid; he will drop one of your 4 test grades (not incld. final) which helped, but tests were tricky; has a lot of part a,b,c ... problems that require you to get the first part to do the next so STUDY OLD TESTS even if you don't think that you covered it in class unless he tells you not to study. Labs are hard and worth only 10%.

This professor was horrible. He never explained anything in detail and was awful about helping students. There was about 100 kids in the class, and now about 15-20 go. I could have explained the subject better than he could.

I really wanted to like this class but he made it impossible. He is loud and obnoxious, his grading makes no sense, and he is very arrogant towards the students.  When the semester started, there were like 80 people showing for lecture.  Now there are probably 25.  No on can stand him or the way he teaches.  Seriously, worst class I've ever taken.
Loud and obnoxious.  Does not teach effectively at all.
Loud speaking. What he says doesn't make sense. Grading is strange.

he is hard to understand, and when it comes to grading a test he is a hardass. this professor dosn't know how to set a curve. watch out, because i recieved a 98/100 on a test after two minor errors and it was curved down 8% to a 90. you have to be perfect to defeat his curves, and he is arrogant
I once ran into him after hours. Unbelievably arrogant.

Puts forth excellent effort although unclear at all times. You go to lecture and wander whats going on but after reading the book you notice how much sense he was making. Very fair and tests are not tricky. Very straightforward man and class.
She's adorable and it's clear she loves what she does. Lectures are actually pretty entertaining and tests are easy.

This class was very interesting and I learned a lot. There are no tests but you do have to write three journals. The journals are kind of difficult grading wise. And there is one final project that was a challenge but that was because of who I was paired with for the assignment. I recommend this class.

Loved this class. Very imformative and interesting. Tyler really loves teaching and seems to have fun doing it. It is mandatory that you come to class everyday. She gives outlines for each lecture and you have to fill in the blanks when you come to class. Clickers are needed. Overall, fantasic, fun class. Highly recommended!

I took her Intimate relationships class... and by her lectures, you can tell she knoows what she is talking about. Details... attendance is mandatory (uses clickers) but asks pure curiousity questions which are very interesting. Her exams are a breeze if you attend class, trust me, this will be the class you won't wanna miss!
she is a cutie who loves what she does for a living

She's cute and fun and teaches the subject well. You can tell she has a passion for the subject. Go to class and do the in-class assignments. Study. She drops the lowest test grade though, so I didn't even have to take the final.

Tyler is awesome!!! She is so interesting to listen to and always makes class fun. It may seem like easy material but make sure to study because your first test grade will surprise you if you don't!! This was make favorite class I've taken so far at MU and if she taught any other classes I would enroll in them for sure!

She is great! Very fun and engaging and has great examples. The book isn't necessary to read, but you need to review. Things may seem common sense, but still study. Note: If you are in a long term relationship you will become scrutinous and may drive your partner crazy with how much you analyze it. I HIGHLY recommend this professor!

GO TO CLASS! In class assignments and quizzes make up much of the class. No excuses to miss, I was in the hospital and missed an in-class assignment and was not allowed to make it up, this kept me from gettin an A in the class. Pretty easy and interesting, though.
No Comments
Pretty easy grader, nice guy

Hack is a good teacher and a good guy. I've had him for four classes.  His Ohio State fanhood is annoying but he cares about the students and the subject. does a good job incorporating his experience into the courses he teaches. Sometimes seems like he gives busy work but he's fair and easy to work with. always willing to help me in office hours

Tyler is good guy and class is fun. Had him twice now once in huge class(120 students) didn't like it. Now in with 50 students much different. Doesn't lecture a lot uses lots of different ways and approaches in class. Keeps it funny and interesting. Does a good job bringing in his experience from the field. Definitely recommend

Hack is a terrible teacher. He doesn't lecture at all and instead makes you do group activities with no point. Attendance is mandatory with quizzes over nightly readings. Tests are nearly impossible bc he takes the smallest details from the book and puts them as questions. Offers little guidance or help. Prob a cool guy outside the class but not in

The only reason to attend class is to turn in the homework that is due every class and take the mandatory quiz. He gives a quiz every class because if he didnt, then nobody would show up.  You wont learn much, but the test are fairly easy because he strongly hints at which problems to memorize.
Lectures relatively incoherently, has free-points quizzes every class.  Exams are too much for 50 minutes, one mistake/switched sign and you're done for.
You have to attend because there is a quiz everyday,and he gives hint for the homework which is due next class. His curve is helpfull , A- from 81 to 86.

A B- on his tests is a 68%, but that doesn't mean you do not need to study.  Do the homework (which is usually easy with the hints he gives in class) and when you are done, go to his office and ask to check your answers.  He will tell you if you got it correct and if not, will help you get it correct.

His notes give good examples and he will give hints on how to do the hw. Quizzes everyday so class is mandatory. Stay caught up and you should be fine. Exams have problems very similar to quizzes and hw.
No Comments

Attendence is mandatory in this class, there are generally homeworks and quizzes everyday.  Cho is always willing to help with the homework problems, and quizzes are easy.  The tests are almost exactly like the homework and quizzes, so if you stay caught up this class is pretty easy.

*professor cho is somewhat boring during class lecture but make no doubt about it he is very clear and very very organized.  he grades on a curve* 2 homework problems are given each day of class and a thrid is taken at the end of class as a quiz*tests are tricky at times*he is very helpful!!!!!!!!!!

Great lecturer, but refuses to give any information about exams, could study for 20 hours and still get a 60 on the exam, ridiculously difficult for a intro class and does not give the materials to succeed.

The course is front loaded with work due to the main portion of the class being carrer fair prep. The main grade is carrer fair attendence, resume, coverletter, and mock interview. After the carrer fair the class consists of weekly guest speakers and one budgeting assignment. Hannah is amazing and very caring of her students!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's very passionate about her job, which is admirable. Her grading criteria is not clear at all. Two students could say the same thing in an assignment and it would be marked wrong on one and correct on the other. Overall, very funny, but I think that can take away from lecture sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Was ok in class, definitely need to study to pass the class. Was very difficult to get a hold of through email. Was very difficult on grading. Was not very gracious about things.

Will call you out for talking in lecture. Easy to reach outside of class if you need help and is reasonable about absences/make up labs. Some people feel she grades unfairly but honestly just study and the exams are straight forward. Clear she is passionate about the subject she teaches and us learning it for a reason.
almost wants you to fail, refuses to make study materials
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In her sections of this class, she lectures for the purpose of you deeply understanding the information. She invites students to talk to her at any time and makes it easy to ask her for help or to just talk to her. She understands where we are in life and that we have other things going on. The only thing I didn't like was the pointless packbacks.

Absolutely love Hannah! The animal science courses are a good mix of biology and management. Provides fill-in-the-blank notes for lectures. There are weekly pop quizzes, but I've found they help me study during the week and understand the material. She's very sweet and open to questions during lectures and makes learning very casual and fun.

Hannah is a great professor. I would 100% take any of her classes. Her lectures are fun and the labs are very hands on. Just be prepared for a pop quiz once a week. She doesn't tell you what day it is on so always come to the lecture. As long as you study the material throughout the week you will pass the pop quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes that are random, which makes attendance necessary. Labs are helpful in applying material and are very hands on. Professor Twenter encourages questions and is willing to help students if you attend student hours or schedule a meeting. Tests and quizzes are not awful if you take time to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Assignments are actual things you can use in life (resume, cover letter, budget, etc) and attendance. If you try you will pass the class. Guest speakers are kind of boring and many seem unprepared and are a little underwhelming. Hannah is great when she lectures, but only does so the first few weeks. You have to go to the career fair so be prepared

Hannah Twenter is a fantastic professor. She's often really busy, but you can tell she cares a lot about her students. Her labs are fun, and the class is structured very clearly. Attendance isn't technically mandatory but there are quizzes in class for points.

Overall Hannah is a great professor. She cares a lot and will answer any questions that you have. During one class she took off some points for something that wasn't in the rubric which is why I rated 4/5. She gives weekly quizzes, but as long as you study you'll be fine. Overall would recommend taking Hannah's classes

Hannah generally has easy lectures, but the slides will have blanks on them so take down what is on the slides. Tests are generally easy without anything that is meant to trick you. She is super nice, though she is busy so don't expect her to be in her office very often. Overall, really easy class.

Hannah is honestly one of the best professors here in the Animal Science department. While she does expect you to pay attention during lectures, it is worth it in the end and will get you an easy A+. I am happy she is one of the first professors you get here as an Animal Science major. She reminds you why you have chosen this major. 10/10 prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hannah is awesome! As long as you go lectures, pay attention, and take good notes you will be fine. There are pop quizzes every week but again as long as you study the information that will be on the quiz then you can get an A on it. She is very nice towards her students and can always help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hannah is a very chill, relaxed professor. There is a "pop" quiz every week for attendance purposes, but they also go towards your grade. They were usually given on Fridays, but occasionally she would do a Wednesday. Tests are probably the hardest part of this class, some things are on there that were not really learned sometimes.

exams are a lot and there are quizzes each week (but it usually helps your grade out so); some of the labs were pointless and the TAs take forever to grade (had things from March that were graded finals week)

The class and her teaching either works for you or it doesn't.The class is straight-forward, it's the same thing each week. There is a quiz each week. Exams take a long time to grade (like 3-5 weeks). It is a lot of content. It just keep gets thrown at you, so you don't really have time for a "break."

Hannah is one of my favorite professors I have had. She has one "pop quiz" every week but they're okay as long as you review notes before class. She realizes you're human and is super caring + understanding. It is clear she wants you to do well and labs are super fun. Definitely recommend her and I can't wait to have her for ANSCI 1175 in spring.

My grandma suddenly passed away in the middle of the semester, and Hannah was by far the most understanding and accommodating out of all my professors. Her lectures cover a lot of material at once, so taking good notes is important.

Hannah is an awesome professor. She is super funny and very enthusiastic about her lectures and labs. She is always accessible outside of class for school help or life help. As long as you focus on studying on class material, you'll do just fine on her tests and weekly quiz (which are matching, multiple choice, fill in the blank, and short answer).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hannah is such a fun and kind person. She genuinely cares about her students and is extremely approachable. Her lectures are very easy to follow, and her anecdotes were a nice touch. Labs were so fun and easy to understand. If she is the instructor for your class, I guarantee you that you will have an amazing time.
Very sweet and genuinely cares about students learning and caring about the topics. Tests are difficult but graded fairly.

Hannah is super sweet and always willing to help you! You have to study about as much as you would for any other class and her tests are more difficult than some profs but definitely manageable! In my opinion, she grades hardest over the equine portion but that's just my opinion. Would definitely recommend for any classes.

I loved taking 1175 with Hannah! She is such a fun professor and she truly cares about her students and their performance in her class. Lectures are always very interesting and you will learn a lot in her class. There are weekly quizzes, but if you pay attention in class and review material you'll do fine; same with exams. Definitely recommend!!

Such a great person and professor. She demands respect and makes you actually do work, but she has a lot of fun in class and is super relatable. She'll make time for students outside of class, and truly cares about how you're doing both in school and in your life. One of my favorite staff members at the university.

Hannah is great! She genuinely cares that you learn something and take something away from the class. She does her best to make herself accessible at all times. She grades very fairly and tests are done over lecutre material so if you study you'll be fine. There's one pop quiz every week so be prepared for those.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Hannah's fantastic. She's super funny, passionate, and teaches really, really interesting stuff. You have to show up though! If you actually show up and listen, it will be a challenging, fun, rewarding class. It's work but that's what school is.

At first, she is really dry and sarcastic. However, you warm up to her pretty fast. She tells you the information very simply and explains expectations clearly. You have to study to do well- it's not a slacker class. Despite this, the material isn't that hard to understand if you put in time.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Señor Ugarte provided my best academic experience at this university, and my most beneficial. His grading techniques are not soft, and you really have to earn your grade, but I recommend his class to anyone that really wants to advance their knowledge and skills in the language.

Ugarte is a rare gem. A wonderful lecturer.  I took a class on the 19th Century novel. I happen to find the century interesting, so I never would call the class"boring". The novels were read collectively, which eased the reading load. His assignments allow students much leeway and are very engaging. If you care about literature, take his class.

He's an energetic guy, but his class was the most boring class I've had in undergrad with an unbelievable amount of reading (and I'm an English major...) Because of this, it was also one of the hardest cause I couldn't pay attention.

By no means is Ugarte an easy teacher, but he's not stressful either. He's an intelligent, passionate teacher who loves what he does. He'll never know this b/c I don't ever talk in class, but I adore him. He's so cute in a sweet, old man sort of way. :)
I really liked Prof. Ugarte.  I thought he was fair on tests and in grading, he was easy to understand, and he was very accessible for questions both in and out of class.  I took his class in 1990.
I really liked this class and I thought he was a good teacher.  He had a lot of interesting things to say.

As others have said, this guy is unnecessarily tough, almost just for the sake of being so. His lecturing is ridiculously monotonous, and I just did not feel motivated  to be passionate about the material. He is also not the nicest or most approachable guy. Avoid.

Make no mistake it's a tough class. If you skip class you'll miss TONS of stuff. Everything you need to know is in the book and I recommend meeting with other students to exchange notes. It's a very interesting class but he's just an okay teacher

I am a geology major, so my opinion is a little bit more favorable. I really, REALLY enjoy the subject matter in this class, but make no mistake, this class is challenging. Underwood is a very bland speaker, but on occasion can be funny. He teaches from powerpoints and sometimes goes too quick. The tests are challenging, but the info is in the book

This is the worst/most difficult class I have ever taken. The lecture is super boring. Sometimes he's funny but it doesn't make up for it. His test are IMPOSSIBLE. I once spent five hours in the library before the test and still got a C. Avoid this class.

This class is a nightmare. Just please---don't do it to yourself. The subject matter is fine, but Underwood makes it near impossible to do well. He doesn't care about his students. His test questions are near incomprehensible. You DO NOT want a class with this guy!

Good luck. He won't help you much if you go to office hours and sometimes will disappear days before the test. Labs are what save your grade. Try and get out of it. Don't really bother using the book, majority of the test (if not all) is based on lecture.

It isn't to hard to get a C in this class as long as you go to all the lectures and take notes. I never actually paid attention to the lectures. Just wrote notes. My TA for labs was awesome and there were a ton of easy points there.

THIS IS THE WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN. Do not take it. His tests are actually impossible and he does not care about student learning. He is funny, but that doesn't make it any better. He curves everything but it still extremely difficult to get a good grade. Just don't even put yourself through the agony of this class.

If you want to pass you need to go to class and do the study guide, his lectures are dry but informative. I had to sit in the front row to ensure I paid attention. Write down everything on his slides and you will be prepared for the test.

His lectures are super dry, and I honestly didn't get a thing out of them since I could care less about geology. GO TO LABS!! Those are easy points if you go every week and help your grade. I went to every class and took detailed notes, and studied enough, but still struggled. Maybe it was just me, but this class was hard. Labs saved me.

I thought he was hilarious but others despised his lecture style, either way hes a nice guy. Lectures arnt exhilarating but I would definitely recommend going to every single one because he lets you know of questions that WILL be on the test in class. He,also makes subliminal political jokes which is what made him super elitist but funny. go 2 clas

He is a terrible teacher. He is teaching an introductory level course but treats it as a higher level. His lectures are really hard to follow and tests are extremely difficult and do not involve the information he puts on the study guides. Labs are not bad but not related to the lectures.
As a person, he is funny, and the classes are well organized, but it is just not ane efficient use of time. Still, if you go to class and DO THE STUDY GUIDE it should not be that difficult.
Professor Underwood was a great teacher.  His tests were word for word from the notes,and it was pretty interesting.

ZZZZZZZ.  What is he talking about.  Easy tests but do yourself a favor and skip lecture, do the study guide the night before tests and study it right before the test.  Dry humor and 55 minute classes never appealed to me.  Nice curve makes good grade obtainable.  Labs help comprehension.
He is so boring and is really unclear on tests and homework. Unless you really like this stuff take another class.
He does not give good examples of the things he is teaching.  He would be there to help you, I suppose.  His study guides are really really hard!

I took Derek's class my freshman year and it was one of the easiest/best classes I had. His expectations were easy to understand & he was very knowledgable about the subject. The weekly assignments were very reasonable and this class came to grow on me very much even though I was not pleased about taking it in the beginning.

Derek's class was by far my favorite. You definitely need to go to class for discussions but class is almost always fun. He's really helpful and focused on you improving your papers, and always willing to help.
Derek is the best! He's super funny, laidback, and extremely helpful. So glad I took his class.

Derek was such a fun teacher! Very cool/laid back. Favorite class I've had so far at MU! The course relies heavily on class discussion, so you must go to class, but Derek is pretty lenient on grading and late assignments. He's gives very helpful and constructive criticism on writing exercises and stories. He really knows what he's talking about!

Very cool teacher who cared about his students. He focused heavily on having the paper write itself, which strangely it did. He had us do peer editing so prepare for your other classmates to read your work. Also make sure you get the class book because there is a lot of in class discussion over it. This was one of my favorite classes!

There are a lot of bad reviews about Dr. Urban however he is my favorite professor that I have ever had in my academic career. Super smart and passionate about the material. If you pay attention, take notes, and ask questions you will be fine in this class. He is respectful to his students and very helpful when a lot of professors aren't. 100/10

Professor Urban NEVER graded my work up until the end of the semester, so I had absolutely ZERO idea as to how I was doing in the class. When confronted, he made excuses. Prof. Urban very rarely responded to emails. Overall, this class was terrible in terms of content and presentation. He made this the worst class I've taken @ MU, by far.

So it is the day before grading period is over and over half of our assignments have not been graded. We turned in 5 papers over the semester and only one of them is graded as of now. The final was also unreasonably time consuming. Don't take this if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I did not know my grade in this class until the final day. He assigned lots of essays but never graded them until 4/5 of them were turned in. These were assigned over about a 3 month period. So, wouldn't recommend if you need to get an A. But, the climate change simulation was the highlight of the class for sure.

Stay away from this class if you can, it is miserable. nothing gets graded until the last couple days of the semester so you never know what your actual grade is. The exams are unnecessarily difficult and he straight up tells you he doesnt care about your GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He doesn't actually teach, all he does is talk about his fullbright to china and how he loves to travel. The class is supposed to be about climate change and policy, I learned nothing new about climate change (like we talked about the carbon cycle) and to teach policy he pits students against each other in a simulation where you wont learn anything

The class is very stimulating if you prefer textbook style lectures verses laidback lectures. Expect to study quite vigorously for the exams to make an A, unless you have a solid background in Geography.  Otherwise, his lecturs are full of interesting information. If you like Geography, of course :)

I had the most intriguing  learning experience from Dr. Palmer. The only reason that I got a B in that class was that my TA was a useless piece of trash and made us do geography coloring books for credit and didn't teach crap. I would gotten a C+ in the class but Dr. Palmer knew what I was going through so he bumped me to a B and saved my GPA.
Avoid him at all cost. If he's your advisor you WILL NOT graduate.  He will go out of his way to avoid you.

Keep up with the readings and study the map quizzes pretty well.  As long as you do well on those and pay attention in class you'll get an A in the course.  He has a tendency to go on rants that get long and boring, but the class overall isn't horrible.
I loved this class. Dr. Urban is a great teacher and really knows what he's talking about.
Lectures were a lot of fun and engaging and taught at a slow pace. We only made it through 3 of the 9 sections he had listed in the syllabus. Very nice guy outside of class also.
Don't ever take him as an advisor.  Seems like a nice guy in class, but outside of class you might as well not exist.
He made geography interesting for me. Good examples, great sense of humor.
No Comments
No Comments

Dr. Valettas did a really good job balancing staying on track for the course and also checking in to make sure everyone was following his lectures. Frankly, advanced calc is tough subject, and the homeworks took quite a while, but he always managed to explain things in a way that made sense. Just don't forget to review material before exams.

Professor Valettas does a very good job of explaining where the math comes from. The course was not proof based, yet I feel like I could prove everything we covered. The grading is fair, but there are only a couple of tests, which make up a substantial portion of the grade.

In my opinion he shouldn't be teaching 'lower level' math, he taught Calc1 so broad when it is the baseline of classes you will take in college as a math or so on major. His tests were incredibly hard, I remember him putting something on our exam he had never taught before and even admitted to it after, but expected us to figure it out.
I hate this
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If your notes are only composed of what you get in the lectures, you'll have no clue what's going on. He seems to operate under the assumption that you already know what he's talking about, which I very much didn't. He also seems to take personal offense to people asking questions and would become quite mean when someone would ask. I'd rather die.

His tests are brutal and they are nothing like the homework and in class quizzes he gives every week. He barely gives any outside resources to help you prepare for the exams. And even the reviews he puts out he doesn't give the answer key to them so you are stuck figuring it out yourself. Spends most of lectures writing useless nonsense.

Exams were nothing like homework or example problems from class. He didnt't even completely work through example porblems in class. When it came to exam reviews he did not give you the answers to the review so you won't even know if you do them correctly. Drop his class or be prepared to teach yourself.

Dr. Valettas was one of the best math teachers I've ever had. He is very good at making sure we understand the basics of the course and will take time to show us proofs of important theorems. He explains everything very clearly and is also very friendly during office hours.

I took his differential equations class (4100).  He single handedly made that class the hardest one I'd ever taken.  His handwriting is so small and poor you can hardly see it from a few rows back and he seems to get upset when you don't understand his explanations.  His English isn't the best either.

He writes so messily and small you can't really read the board. Then when he asks if you have questions, he'll respond with "well how do you not understand?". He is honestly the worst teacher I've ever had. I know if I was placed with a different professor I would receive a much higher grade in this course.
Mr. Valettas was an okay professor. He gives a 20 points bonus on every exam which is nice. He never explained what was going to be on the quizzes and barely hinted what was going to be on the exams.

Awesome teacher who really tries to make sure all students understand the material and succeed. Always available for help if you need it. Exams are manageable and make up most of class grade. Also a few quizzes, online assignments, and participation. Really fun and enjoyable teacher who likes to joke around and is passionate about the topic.

Anna's classes are her reading off of a PowerPoint quickly. Each day is a new topic and every night there is hw on the reading. She rarely responds to emails and is difficult to reach. I took 3 of her classes and she still didn't know my name after 3 years. (She emailed me asking why I wasn't in class even though I asked her a question in class)

Valiavska is a great professor, feel like she is often misunderstood as a strict professor but she really just cares & wants you to care about what you are learning. She tries to connect w/ her students by using current events in her lectures. The home/classwork can seems tedious, but the papers/project help prepare you for the real world.

Very slow grader. Doesn't respond to emails. Yell's at students who are in class complaining about the student's who don't come to class. Nothing happens during class other than her reading off the PowerPoint resulting in her not going into detail about what concepts mean. I wouldn't recommend anyone to her class ever. Not approachable either.

Assigns a midterm which covers 6 chapters in a book, along with outside readings, exam is 250 points, 23% of the grade in the class, without giving study guide. Class is like a military academy in Russia. Slow grader. In class she goes extremely fast, and doesn't do anything but read whats off the powerpoint. Would NOT recommend her to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: When I had Verchota she was very unconfident and did not know what she was teaching. When I had her it was a high school coarse. She couldn't even teach high school. I failed her class two quarters in a row. All my classmates also failed her class.

She's a really great person, just not a great teacher. Most recitations were spent working out very few problems where she would go on tangents and spend valuable learning time solving material that we won't need to know for exams while spending little time on actually valuable info. Other Calc 2 teachers also provide much better review for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm aware that Calc 2 is a very hard subject to teach, but with her it is almost impossible to really understand. She will spend half the class deriving formulas with proofs that don't matter. If she simply just gave us the formula and moved on, there would be much more time in the class period to better understand the actual material.

I have never had a teacher that is so unconfident in what they do. She will get halfway done teaching something and then decide that she wants to do it a different way leaving you lost and confused. I would recommend any other teacher for Calc 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Verchota cannot teach to save her life. Math 1400 is already an upper level freshman math class so it is a bit harder, but Verchota makes learning so much worse. Honestly stopped attending her lectures because I understood the material better when I taught myself.
Not a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Everything is straight out of the textbook but when she tries to put it on the board to explain it, it comes out to be a hot mess. Calc 2 is super difficult as is but with her its impossible. She is super nice as a person but I wish I could say better things about her teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The worst "professor" i've ever had. Had no idea what she was teaching and admitted it multiple times. What she "taught" in class and told us study made up about 30% of the first test. The other 70% she didn't even mention or mentioned once. Make sure that she isn't your T.A. before you attend the first class. Drop immediately if so!

Almost everything she taught she made it known to the class she wasnt sure if she knew was she was talking about and to read the book to make sure after class. The average for the first exam was under 50% for the students. Worst professor Ive had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Seemed unsure of himself the entire semester. Doesn't know how to teach a class and lectures were difficult to sit through. 90% of the class stopped showing up by the second half of the semester. Very easy class, but you have to teach yourself.

He seemed almost scared to teach the class. There were a lot of "um" and "uh" throughout every one of his lectures. The content of the class itself is not very difficult. He does provide examples, it is just hard to get past the mumbling and filler words. I would recommend avoiding him as a professor when taking this course.
Boring and has a monotone voice.

Personally, I strongly disliked his teaching style, he stumbled over his words and half the time didn't seem to know what he was teaching. The class itself was really easy as long as you do the homework, it helps you learn better than he him. Exams are just like homework, and quizzes were super simple. Teacher wise, if you can don't take his class

Professor Vatterott does a great job offering more than required. This class isn't a listen-to-lecture type of class. You participate and have to be involved. I believe that if you take advantage of this class it is one of the most valuable classes at Mizzou. There will be times when you are pushed but you learn a lot from those moments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Vatterott has been my favorite college professor so far at Mizzou. His lectures taught content that I can implement in my future career, which has been my first class to do so. He not only preached about how to be a top sales performer, but also taught us the importance of discipline, perseverance, and passion. 10/10 would recommend this class.

Vatterott brings extensive sales expertise to the table. The course provides invaluable firsthand sales experience and emphasizes feedback utilization. Numerous companies actively participate, offering opportunities for internships or full-time positions. If you're aiming for a career in sales, this class offers a valuable head start.

Vatterott is a good professor, but can be a little intense at times. As long as you go to class and do the assignments, you should get an A. There is a business casual dress code everyday in the class that kind of stinks, but you get use to it after a couple weeks.

Awesome professor who teaches a solid class. Dr. Vatterott has a bunch of connections and he'll provide you with dozens of networking and potential internship opportunities while your in his class. If you want to explore the world of sales and like to listen to The Grateful Dead, Anthony is your guy.

I came into the class and he molded my mind and helped me raise my confidence in selling. We had a lot of guest speakers who worked at different companies come in and we always would have a chance to work with them. I would recommend this class to any student looking currently for an internship.

Different teaching approach with an emphasis on providing hands-on, real-world experience to their students. Rather than solely relying on book work and test, they understand the importance of practical application in mastering the art of personal sales. Really great course to prepare you for the real world!

His class format is unlike any class I've taken here at Mizzou. I typically take braindead lecture halls with 300+ students in class where I learn absolutely nothing. He also makes it very clear what is expected out of us and how our workload will apply to our future after school. A very unique professor and I'm fortunate for the experience.

Professor Vatterott's class was great. I came into this semester not knowing a single thing about how to sell, but this class has prepared me to feel like i'm ready to get into the field. Sometimes this class can seem like a lot of work, but it truly does pay off.

Professor Vatterott cares about your success and this class sets you up to learn a lot about sales skills. You also preform sales roles plays that will benefit your confidence and comfortability in the sales world. As long as you do assignments on time and show up to class you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Anthony Vatterott's Marketing 3410 class features unique role-playing exercises and engaging storytelling. His relaxed teaching style and fair grading offer a rewarding experience, with plenty of networking opportunities and a focus on practical skills.

This class sets you up for success after college with tons of networking events with big companies and group role plays. The group role-plays sound very intimidating at first, but they are actually a lot of fun and push you out of your comfort zone. I really enjoyed this class, and I have recommended it to my friends!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class structure and content is not like any class I've taken before. You have to do role plays which force you to get out of your comfort zone and learn what a salesperson would do in a sales meeting. The class is what you make of it, and the professor is not too serious which I liked. Lot of companies come in to speak that are interesting.
