Easy to get a good grade if you show up and complete assignments, class runs a little long sometimes, and the professor doesn't take himself too seriously.

One of my favorite classes, the teacher always shows up with energy and a great story about his past. The class is what you make of it, if you wanna have a fun time you will, if you don't want to you won't. Fair grading, and random attendance, he wants you to learn and become a better person during this class

He is a great teacher and I learned a lot from this class. The things that he has us do are very useful and interesting. He also relates class back to the real world which helps learning a lot. Overall a great teacher and he made the class very interesting.

Favorite class I've taken! The professor has a unique teaching style but ultimately, it is difficult not to be engaged. He is hilarious with a personality that some students may be turned away by, but believes in the material he's teaching. He provides many internships/job/competition opportunities. Up to you if you take him up!

Exposes you to a lot of opportunities to connect with internships and jobs. get hands on experience with sales in terms of group role plays in class that are mandatory. can push yourself to do voluntary sales competitions outside of class as well that are not mandatory. Grading extremely fair, really wants you to learn. witty guy, not too much work

The class is more oriented towards helping individuals become better salespeople and  provides numerous networking events. Go to class and do the work asked, you will receive a good grade, but be ready for the professor to go on some tangents. The professor provides multiple opportunities for extra credit, so keep a close eye on the opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall a fun class that's good for those considering a career in sales. Grading criteria was clear and I knew what was expected from me in the course, I liked that my performance wasn't based predominately on tests. Would have liked the professor being more organized, posting assignments ahead of time, not moving dates around as much.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class, fun teacher. Very easy to stay engaged because the energy is so high. Get ready to do A LOT outside of class. It is very different from any other class I have taken but ultimately I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He cares about his students and their success after college.

I enjoyed this professor and learned a lot from his lectures and class. The sales role plays were uncomfortable but helped me a lot. I had a job interview and they made me read a quick case study and then act out the sales role play. Thankfully, I was prepared because of this class because I wouldn't have done sales role plays anywhere else.

Professor Vatterott is friendly, approachable, & cares about his students' success. His interactive teaching style was a good change from textbook-heavy courses, growing & challenging my selling & public speaking skills. If you have even a slight interest in sales, I recommend this course for its networking opportunities inside & outside the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor was cool, he might put you in unconfutable positions, but it's to build the character of a future salesman, so it definitely helped me a lot. It's a fun class, and as long as you show up and do what you suppose to, you can get a good grade easily.

This is definitely the class to take if you are looking to gain hands-on sales experience. The class structure is fun but also feels like it is actually preparing you for the professional world. Attendance is also a decent portion of your grade.

Vatterott was passionate about teaching, allowed students room to grow with constructive criticism, and provided students with incredible resources and networking opportunities which often led to internships or full-time job offers. He made class fun and had us do role-plays which taught us how to effectively sell ourselves and products. He's amaze

This class offers a great opportunity to expand your communication and ability to get outside of your comfort zone when learning how to make sales. You will gain first hand knowledge and be able to meet first hand companies and what they are looking for in graduates so you can be prepared.

Great class! Helped me get out of my comfort zone with talking in front of people and getting to know new people within my class! I would recommend this class if you love to learn more on sale techniques.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a great class for gaining hands-on sales experience. The structure of the class is heavily reliant on mock sales role-plays, which help build communication and presentation skills.

Professor Vatterott was great at helping students throughout this class. He really wants his students to succeed and get an internship/ job after the class is completed. He's a great resource to utilize when you have questions about your career.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awesome class. Not your typical lectures with taking notes. He comes into class everyday excited and ready to teach. I really enjoyed his class.

Vatterott gave the class great times to network with companies. Many sales companies would come to our class to teach us about their companies and give us internship/job opportunities. Also, we did many sales roleplays, so we got real-life experience with sales. Learned a lot about what a job in sales would look like and how to be prepared.

Only thing you will not like about this class is dressing business casual! Great first selling class and you do lots of role plays in front of class (beware if you are shy). There are many guest speakers that can help you get a job or an internship. Random attendance but you get 2 free skips. He is a hard grader but there is extra credit to help!
Vatterot cares about his students. Attendance is taken a few times during the semester at his discretion.
Great introduction to what to expect in sales.

Professor Medina is amazing. She is very easy to talk to and actually wants to help you. She makes the material easy to understand and also allows us to ask as many questions as we need. She is always available outside of class as well. 10/10 recommend

Dr. Medina is an amazing professor, she genuinely cares about her students and is extremely interested in the subjects she teaches. She actually inspired me to change my degree to Sociology. There is quite a bit of reading but it all pertains to the lecture given the next class.She is a motivated professor who wants you to succeed.Take her classes!

Dr. Medina (IUS) is friendly & understanding, other reviews are right that there is way too much reading involved that usually isn't needed except for the weekly 5 pt quizzes.  She is not an easy grader either; gives useful feedback. I'm a good writer and I am not expecting higher than a B even though I tried very hard in this class. Not an easy A.
Dr. Medina was a great professor. Take her class and you wont regret it! She makes the material easy to understand and is very funny!
Now at Indiana University SouthEast, Dr. Medina is very intelectual, well prepared and organised, I enjoyed her class but be warned too much reading involved.

Didn't really enjoy her class too much. All about how anyone who isn't a white male is horribly oppressed by society. Didn't read a page of any of the assigned readings and still managed to get an A, while others read everything and struggled to get a B.

On the first day she comes off as a little scary, but eventually you see her softer side. I found her class incredibly interesting and straightforward. She basically throws extra credit opportunities at you. But she will call you out if you're caught texting in her class or you try to leave early.

I really like this class but the amount of reading is ridiculous and very little of it is ever needed for exams. The weekly online quizzes are no fun either. Luckily I took this class with a friend so I was fine.
awesome class, extremely interesting

Extremely unreachable. Every-time I contact her she takes weeks to respond or just doesnt respond at all. Tough grader and assignments did not help improve my writing or reading skills. Also she doesnt grade til the end of the semester so you have no idea what you have in the class.

This was an asynchronous online class. Only ppt, no videos and was absolutely useless. Hard grader. I learned nothing that improved my English or writing skills. Nothing inspiring to read, no skills gained. Plus you pay extra money to upload your homework to a 3rd party site (Eli review). Why should we spend more to peer review?

Super relaxed and nice! Loves hearing her students participate and push their thinking. A lot of reading though that not many had time for. The only difficult thing was the analysis assignments over the readings, to not easy for a grader for saying your thoughts. Classes are about the same structure every time. Looked up mainly summaries to get by.

I took 1020 Brit Lit. Her class is easily laid out so that you know what the rest of the semester will look like after the first week. She is understanding and knows a lot about her specialty. As long as you participate and do the homework, it is an easy class. 10/10 recommend!
A lot of work. We had homework for almost every single class. But if you do them, you are secured to get an A. Easy grader and very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Gopal teaches a very tough class. He is very knowledgable and speaks in pure theory, but if you put in the work he can make you better at reinforced concrete design
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr, Gopal is one of the best professors in the department. He cares about student learning and emphasizes not learning by rote but by understanding the fundamentals. He is available outside of the class for help. Often he addresses questions from prerequisite classes to help studnts learn.

Prof. Gopalaratnam takes student understanding and learning a priority -  regurgitation of memorised material is a strict no-no in his classes. He takes class preparation seriously and expects the same level of commitment from students.  I look forward to take his elective Prestressed Concrete class next semester.

Gopal is one of the best professors in Civil Engineering Department and offers an indepth understanding of the topics rather than superficial rote learning. Be prepared to work hard, but you will learn a lot.

He knows his stuff, but can be rude to students oftentimes. Beware of pop quizzes. You have to attend class or you will be more confused than you may already be. His tests are tough but he grades pretty fair if you can show effort. This will be your hardest class so allocate time for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One the best professor in civil engineering. Learn a lot in his courses. He expects students to attend classes. His cares for student learning and sometimes the insistence on the student knowing the fundamentals rubs studnets the wrong way. I would recommend Dr. Gopal's courses to any student who wants to learn

He's is the professor that if you show that you are working hard and work with him, you will deserve that grade. If you decide to skip class, he will give you a lot of crap the next class period. also he gives out random quizzes, you can't trust him. the good thing that I Learned from this class was if you work hard, it pays out in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Does not want you to memorize equations. Expects you to be able to answer conceptual quests in depth with just a little bit of discussion on the topic in lecture. Also, when talking to him about questions on homework outside of class it almost felt like he was being rude and spiteful at me for not understanding a topic.

Excellent professor. Gopal knows theory and practice. Presents practical reasons for design assumptions. Cares about student learning. He discourages memorizing and learning by rote. Classes not humorous but very well organized. Surprise quizzes a bummer! Fair in grading -- a little on the tough side?
Good Professor. Learned the most of any MU course.

Great teacher and very knowledgeable. Well organized and does not waste class time. I am glad to have taken this course even though it is not required. Clearly one of the teachers in the college who cares about student learning.
Not an easy professor to like. Very abrupt almost to the point of being rude.  I won't take another class with him.

Enjoying the class - demanding in effort. Useful for my career. Gopal takes the time to explain ACI code as well as provide reasons for design procedures. Better have strong background in structures and strengths. Lectures are fast in speed and not boring.

Absolutely the most useful course I have had so farould suggest regular semester offering. Gopal's combo of theory and practical application was very useful. Would strongly recommend class to all seniors and graduate students!

Gopal is passionate about student learning. I learnt a lot from this course not only on Reinforced Concrete but critical engr analysis as well. He is sometimes curt when answering student questions but I suspect it is more his style because he is very focussed on student learning. Wish I had more structures classes with him.

Very knowledgable and cares about quality of teaching. Expects a lot from students but also from himself. Gopal has a dry sense of humor and classes could be more interesting. He is available for help outside of the class. I would certainly take more classes from him before I graduate.
The best professor I have had in my four years at MU. Expects a lot from students and from himself. Quizes are easy only if you keep up with the class. Helpful outside the class too but not chatty.

I am currently taking my third class with Dr. Gopal. He is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He makes sure you understand the material and actually learn it, not memorize it. If you take note of every detail and schematic in class, then you know exactly what to study for the exam. He doesn't always seem approachable, but he actually

Excellent instruction. Cares about student learning. Dry wit sometimes goes unnoticed. Expects a lot from students but in a positive way. Wish I had him for Statics and Strengths - very knowledgeable of subject matter.

Gopal is very knowledgable and makes students think for practical solutions themselves. He is demanding but class time is always very usefully spent. Very useful but not an easy class. Enroll  but plan to work hard.

I benefitted greatly from the course. Gopal is organized and enthusiastic about student learning. His tests are demanding but fair. Lab commitments take up a lot of time. Making the course 4 credits better reflects the effort required.

Dr. Gopal is very knowledgeble and organized. Student expectations are high and I learnt a lot in this course. Would be useful to have a textbook. Overall one of the best teachers in Civil Engineering. Helpful during office hours. Writing on the board can be improved.
Shes ok but will give bad grades just because she doesnt like your answers, not because they arent correct. Really annoying and unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super nice person but a boring lecturer and VERY unclear/difficult grader

She is a very nice person who cares about her students but I wouldn't recommend her class to anyone. As other reviewers have said, she's a very unclear and unnecessarily hard grader. The lectures were also very boring.

EXTREMELY hard grader. She does not go into detail about what is expected from us on our assignments and then grades them extremely harshly. There are no exams in this class and just papers and projects. Her lectures are all over the place and do not relate to our projects/assignments.
Great personality, very hard grader

I really enjoyed taking this class with Astrid. She was knowledgable about the topic, and made class interesting and relatable. That being said her tests are impossibly hard! She expects you to do way too much in the time allowed for the exam. If you take her classes be prepared to work for it!

I have mixed feelings about Astrid. Her class was interesting at times, other times it was insanely boring. Her quizzes are almost impossible to get a good grade on, and her exams were so difficult. she's an extremely hard grader. I like her as a person and she was nice but i think she makes this class unnecessarily difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She cares about some students, not all. If you're not one of her favorites, she is not  welcoming nor friendly to go to for explanation, and etc. She has a very thick accent and it is very distracting. It was too difficult to keep up with her fast pace lectures and powerpoint slides, while trying to figure out what words she was even trying to say.
She really loves this class and puts a lot of heart into it!
Astrid is amazing!  She really prepares you for the real world and is great to develop a relationship with!

She is a really good teacher, has great knowledge of her subject and cares about the students, but the downside is she has such a thick accent it makes her so hard to understand. Hard to stay engaged sometimes, and she speeds through powerpoints. Really hard to take all the notes. Make a friend so you can get notes from them when you miss a point.

I absolutely love Astrid. I started off struggling in this class with a C. I eventually went ans talked with Astrid and she gave me great feedback ending the class with an A. She is really caring, funny, nice,  and easily available. Definitely interested in you succeeding in her course. I'm taking another one of her courses next semester!

I am in COMMN major, and I can say that Astrid is so far one of my favorite professors in MU. She cares about you, easy accessible when you have questions. Although she has some accents, which would not influence you catching her words a lot. A very humorous and nice lady. Highly recommend it!

Astrid is by far my favorite professor I've had at Mizzou. She was always extremely helpful when I was confused about anything we were discussing in class and always showed a personal concern for each student. One time, I woke up late for my exam and she let me take it later that day. She is kind, sweet, and very passionate about communication.

Loved Professor Villamil! she has a slight accent but is still easy to understand. she worked in the PR field so she has first hand knowledge about what she's teaching. Keeps everyone engaged. 1 midterm, 1 final, 5 journal assignments, and 1 group project along with participation makes up your grade. I highly recommend her and this class! :)

Wish I knew more before taking this class. Exams are 25/25/40 with only 90 total questions, plus surprise proctoring, never mentioned in the syllabus. Only a 36-hour test window, no partial credit, confusing free-response math, and homework doesn't match exams. He teaches it most semesters, so consider taking it elsewhere. Do not take it with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Impossible to get a grade. ECONOM 8413: Research Workshop I.

Dr. Trindade is a helpful professor if you care to learn the material. However, the way the class is set up is not really student friendly. Then again, an 8 week course has its obvious pros and cons. Nonetheless, I wish this class was not graded by just 4 tests. Essentially, you need to study his lectures and the book, methodically. Theres a curve!

Unnecessarily difficult, but he's genuinely interesting and I enjoyed the class. Don't expect a good grade easily, but he is reasonable and will curve if the class does poorly. You NEED to read the textbook if you want to do well. Review his study materials and email him with any questions and/or schedule to meet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He means well but the 90%/10% percent exam/homework grade breakdown is brutal. 75 questions makes up entire 90 percent. does proctored practice exams as homework assignments so you will not be getting the full 10%of that homework grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Trindade was nice and his lectures weren't bad, but each exam was worth 20% of your grade so if you did poorly on one you were screwed. He curved generously which helped. He was difficult to reach via email, which isn't great for an online class. I had to email him 2-3 times to get a response.

Its entirely test oriented which is fine, but theres only 3 exams each 25 questions, so that means 75 questions is 90% of the grade. He curves kinda, but he offers no extra credit. Also the other 10% is homework MIXED with actual accuracy graded practice exams, so you wont get that solid 10%. DO NOT take any classes with him, he's a bad teacher

I took the 8 week online version of the class, and it was one of the easier econ classes I have taken. All practice tests and tests are administered using SmartProctoring, and account for 90% of the grade. They were curved generously. He is good at explaining key concepts in lecture videos. Reading the book is helpful but isn't needed to do well.

I am poor at statistics and this class was intensive, much more so for a summer course. Prof Trindade is why I passed. He is articulate and conveys the information in an understandable way. I ended up rarely using the textbook because everything I needed was explained better in his lectures. He graded fairly and took late work. I recommend him.

I loved him! I have taken a lot of economics courses at Mizzou and his was the easiest to understand. He does a very good job of explaining topics in layman's terms and is very personable with his students. It is a lot of work and intensive, but 1) he acknowledges this and 2) you signed up for it. Pretty easy tests, too as long as you take notes..
Dont rely on his practice exams or the homework to study for the exams.
the average of each test is around 50%-60%, just think about that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Just study what he assigns and you will get a good grade. The Class average is honestly lower than it should be so maybe if you don't see yourself as a strong economics student you will struggle but he curved multiple exams and seemed like he wasn't going out of his way to screw the people doing bad over. Overall i'd recommend.

This class is ridiculously difficult. You will have to learn software, STATA, to pass this class. Your assignments will be on this program. Then you'll have tests that are all math based exams. Everything is theoretical and will be based on a bunch of nonsense. The computer program is obsolete, he'll try to convince you it isn't, but it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class is SUPER hard, please avoid this class at all cost. If this class is your capstone, Vitor would be your best choice. Vitor is the best professor I've ever taken at MU. He is a real expert and explains everything in class in such a detailed way. He made me believe Econ is practically useful. Got an A-, but really not an easy one!!!

Vitor doesn't explain the material in the lectures clearly and they are very boring. You can go to class and pay attention and still do poorly in the class. His tests are very hard and worth about 85% of the grade. There is a ton of extra credit, also do your homework and clicker questions. That will make up for some of the very difficult tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are very difficult, particularly the 2nd one and the Final. Questions are all meant to trick you and are all 2 part answers. Extra credit is very helpful and highly recommend doing it. Lectures are extremely boring and he is not very good at answering peoples questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I got an A+ in this course with Vitor. I recommend reading the book as the course progresses, getting all the reef points (going to lecture), and completing the extra credit video. Tests are difficult, so study. Gives a generous curve to the tests.

Went into the final with over 100% in the class due to the very large amount of extra credit points he offers. But then after the extremely difficult final, my grade dropped more than 10% even with a huge curve!!! The class seems manageable in the beginning but the final was so hard. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT ASSIGMENT. It saved my grade
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Prof. Trindade is the most amazing professor I had at Mizzou! He makes difficult topics easy to follow. Be prepared for a LOT of work tho! I would def take him again if he teaches another class!!

He's such a bad teacher. Very unreasonable with the amount of time he wants you to put outside of class. Homeworks do not help with test preparation either. Exams are very difficult. 0/10 definitely would not recommend. Take this class somewhere else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lots of extra credit. Great textbook. Easy class if you put effort into it.

I have learned so much from Prof. Trindade! It was a quite difficult class, but the professor broke down everything and made it easy to learn. Lectures are very clear and organized. The professor is very nice and helpful! Definitely recommend him if you really want to learn the course!

Professor Trindade is a funny guy and knows his stuff. However, he doesn't do the best job teaching it, pretty much just reads off the PowerPoint. The tests and homework are annoyingly hard, but he curves them quite a bit. Offers a big extra credit opportunity though, saved my grade.
The tests are harder than they need to be. The homework is very hard. He really doesn't teach because he just reads off his PowerPoint
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is willing to work with you.  If you have questions about an answer on a test and can explain yourself, hell likely give you credit for it.  Go to class, sit near the front, and this class wont require much outside work (other than the homework).  He never puts anything on the test that he didnt discuss in class, so there are no surprises.

VT knows his stuff and he obviously cares that we know it too. I expected Macro to be very difficult but he made it easy. Go to class and take notes and its a breeze. He sets everyone up to succeed with extra clicker points, a curved homework grade and ample opportunity for help. Only 3 tests, 2 midterms and a final so studying for them is key too.

A superb professor. He provides real-life examples with real data, and makes a dull subject like econometrics seem interesting. His tests were straightforward and based on what was done in class, but you need to truly understand the material, not just memorize figures and equations, in order to do well.

Professor Trindade was an outstanding econometrics teacher.  He provided numerous, meaningful examples in class that brought an otherwise dull subject to life.  Watch out for his exams; they are fair, but quite difficult and he will not tolerate improper use of economic terms.
Excellent professor. He helps to facilitate conceptual understanding, not just regurgitation of textbook.

he's a very knowledgeable professor. if you are really interested in economics, you should take his class. he knows a lot and he teaches well. he is very good in explaining things in different ways. but, his test is hard. i got a B even if i attended every class. his grading is a bit harsh because =>90 is A, =>80 is B and so on. there's no +/-.

He is a fantastic teacher! He is also the first instructor I have seen in my life who does not bring the textbook to class, because he already knows everything on the textbook. His grading scale is hard since he only cares about your final answer for each question on the exams. However, he will try to help you conquer difficulties to pass his exam.

Best class no, I mean club. Many amazing people and the best club at Mizzou even if it's small. The best part is Chinese New Year where everyone including myself celebrate and spread our culture. A big break from stress and we get to watch fun movies, play games, and conversation speak. 100% best.

Well, why am I rating this if it's just a freshmen interest group? Well since it's Dr. Volz, he made me feel at home since he knew Chinese. He was nice and casual, but one of the sophomores actually runs the class, and we just went on trips, and did presentations. I only took it once a week and since it's that, attendance is necessary.
This professor is outstanding! I've enrolled in several of his classes, and he really knows his material. This course involves a significant amount of reading and engaging discussions!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love this man dearly, even as someone who did horrible in this class (I was an idiot freshman year, it was 100% my fault) He would actively would check up on me to make sure I was ok, and was always willing to help me catch up. Freshman: just know, a 6 credit class is a BIG time commitment; as long as you are prepared for that you will do well.

Professor Volz is caring, passionate, and easy to reach. You can tell he genuinely wants his students to succeed. He assigns a lot of reading for his history/culture classes, but the accompanying reading guide allows you to skim while still understanding the main points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable, clearly lays out expectations and also ways to reach him for help.

Taught the material at a really good pace. There is a lot of material and the course is fast paced but if you participate in class and do the assignments then it is easy to get a good grade in the class.

Though he's listed as a professor for class, he never actually taught; he just made the schedules (which were very unrealistic). You had to learn the equivalent of 80 vocabulary terms a week; after chapter three, most of our class became hopelessly lost. We were just trying to make it through the semester. He seems nice, but new schedule please!

Professor Volz is genuinely a really nice guy. He knows what he is talking about and is super easy to discuss topics or get help from. I will say, this class (CN 2310) does rely on quite a bit of reading, but his lectures make up for it (you should still read the book though, if you can). Overall, he is an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Volz was a good professor. Chinese Civ was a fun class, though his textbook reading guides assigned for homework were time-consuming. His tests were not too hard if you filled out all the guides and paid attention in class. I guarantee you will pay attention because Volz makes sure to tie in fun stories of his trips abroad into lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Tests were a little hard (but only 3 of them), so make sure you read the textbook. 2 papers, but short and semi-easy. Cared a lot about teaching and not just throwing stuff on a powerpoint so it was very interesting material. Very soft on deadlines, as long as you talk to him before something is due! Good prof and very willing to help students.

I loved this class and learned a ton. I disagree with another recent poster that the tests are hard. If you do the reading guides he provides, then the tests are a breeze. You MUST come to class and he takes attendance every single day, so be there or you won't get a good grade. Wonderful person, glad to have had him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Michael is a great teacher. He is so passionate about China and everything about it. I took his Chinese Culture class and I learned so much. The tests are difficult and attendance is absolutely mandatory, but he gives good feedback and the group projects were actually fun. He's usually available for extra help and just a great guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Excellent professor; knows Chinese VERY well but as someone who's not a native speaker, understands how hard it is to learn. Very nice, understanding, funny. Lots of homework and studying, but it's to be expected in a foreign language class, especially one so different from English. I love Chinese, and this professor is part of the reason why.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have never learned more in my life than I did in one semester of his class. You start with absolutely no knowledge of the Chinese language, but Volz and his Chinese TAs encourage dialogue and give authentic feedback about your progress. This class is not easy, but it is very fun if you're ready to work your butt off six times a week.

Class is extremely organized.  Expect to speak, write, sing, etc. in Chinese. Super passionate about the language and tells interesting stories of his Asia travels.  The class is quick-paced, you face a chapter of the Chinese language weekly, if you're willing to work, you'll get an A.

Very good teacher, good sense of humor and knows the Chinese language very well. He can be a bit scatterbrained but always accepts full blame for losing/forgetting things. Very good at explaining grammar points and easy to communicate with. Two quizzes a week (oral and vocabulary) as well as character practice and workbook weekly. Tests are hard.

He used a lot of old articles, however my biggest problem was unorganized this class was. He changed the assigned readings on the syllabus several times and often we fell behind because we would be side tracked in our discussions. I didn't like the online discussion, especially because he wouldn't post them until the weekend before they were due.
Great teacher! Very helpful and I loved the pace of his class (A lesson every 2 weeks)

He is a great teacher and cares if his students learn anything. In addition he cares about the overall well being of his students therefore he is easy to talk to. He is understanding and helps his students if they ask.

This was a great class! I took this class so that I may learn Chinese, and I am now in love with the language. You will need to study alot in order to do well, but it's totally worth it. I am thankful that Mr. Volz was my teacher because I am learning the language so well. I hope to one day be fluent. xie xie laoshi!
No Comments

This is a somewhat exciting course. The professor is a good teacher and very helpful. This class is taught by Volz and a Chinese native Yanyan. Their both great but you will have to study a lot if you want to get a good grade. It's a difficult class but if you work at it you should be fine.

Professor Volz is an all around great guy and teacher.  He's fun and likes to joke around with his students.  I've had him for Chinese 1 and 2 and he asks a lot but it IS Chinese.  Get this teacher if at all possible.  He also teaches Chinese Film.  You'll love him.

The rudest professor I have ever met. The amount of reading for this class was ridiculous. Quizlet has all the answers for the reading quizzes so you don't have to waste your time. He shadily insults people and is just plain awful. Wish I never would have taken this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Vos is honestly a great guy. It's clear he is so passionate about journalism and it's cute how he geeks out over certain topics. Yes, this class can be dry, and yes, it's annoying that class rarely gets out even a minute early. Even so, you'll learn so much if you try even a little bit. Don't let others stress you out - this class isn't bad!

Prof. Vos doesn't get enough credit for his style. He does a great job identifying historical patterns and outcomes, but you need to do the readings (sizable but not unmanageable) before class for the lectures to be interesting and for the concepts to click in your head. You can learn A LOT from this class if you put in a little extra effort.

If you can avoid taking this class with Tim try your best. He is super super boring in lecture and uses terms that are too complex and doesn't explain things well. His powerpoints are ugly and all he does is read off them in class. There is a TON of reading but make sure you do it because all those points add up fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His reading requirements for each class are rather unreasonable. Unfortunately, he doesn't seem to realize students are taking other classes. Within any given week there could be 2 document quizzes, each over documents ranging from 15-30 pages, in addition to a reading quiz, usually over 3 lengthy textbook chapters.
Lectures are boring, but the tests are pretty easy if you study the material. Don't worry, you'll get through this fine. You'll hate it during the class, but everyone else in the J school did too.

Great teacher. The material of this class was pretty standard, but I think it's more of a weeding out class, to see who likes Journalism enough to stick with it. He's pretty funny in a nerdy way, and I really enjoyed his teaching style. You have to take notes from the slides he shows as well as read the textbook. Overall, LOVED him. Plus he's cute.

Dr. Vos will bore you to tears at some points, but you have to go to class if you even want a chance of doing well on the exams. His exams are straight from the lecture/PPT. Occasionally he is funny/witty in a nerdy way, but overall this class will weed out who is really interested in journalism and who isn't.

At the beginning, it's easy to write off Vos and J1100 in general as a bland class with poor lectures. To do well, you have to attend class, read the textbook, additional readings, and do the assignments. He knows his stuff and says "uh" or "um" a lot because he has his lectures memorized word for word the way he wants you to know it for the test.

Suffer through the class. Nothing makes this class easy to get through, because the material is awful. Tim doesn't help much. He's dry, his jokes are lame, and his lectures are slow and boring. But you need to go to class and you need to read the textbook. Memorize the phrases and follow the study guides. Suffer through it and you'll make it out.
Definitely has a dry sense of teaching, but well worth learning from! Grading was not at all as difficult as I expected.
Dr. Vos will grow on you after a while. He has his moments where he is dry but does have a pretty good sense of humor. Make sure to attend class and read the textbook before exams!
It's like he takes each of his sentences and restructures it to be unnecessarily confusing. It even seems like it's taking him extra effort to speak like that. he says um and uh. NOT CLEAR AT ALL
This class is hard- do the readings, TRY to listen in class, but he's a bore. Too bad it's required :(

This class is hard. He takes a theoretical approach that Volz doesn't... I've taken them both :( if you get the theory at the beginning-- and do allthe readings/pay attention in class-- you'll do OK. He doesn't seem condescending to me, but he does make lame jokes.

The subject matter is insufferable. Unhelpful class that did not enhance my understanding of journalism at all, just a snoozefest. Also be sure to take constant notes, and to study everything, not just the study guides. Vos is also very condescending and arrogant.

Prof. Vos starts class each semester with the assertion that "learning is not meant to be and should not be fun." This is an adequate precursor to the class, as the subject matter is extremely bland and the exams and quizzes are unnaturally difficult.
HIGHLY RECOMMEND ;)

Cool guy that makes the lectures bearable. Exam and quiz material come straight from the power points covered during lectures. Sometimes forgets to upload power points so you have to remind him via email. Probably one of the easiest Finance 1000 classes out there so I would definitely recommend taking it.

Quiz every Friday that is basically straight from power points. Super easy and covered the basics of finance. Sweet guy who is really understanding about busy college lives. You can take quizzes early if you have to miss class on Friday. Recommend if you need an elective.

Nice guy, but the way he taught didn't work for me. He took a while to post slides, and provided a ton of info, so it was sometimes hard to keep up. Hard to get in touch with. The class material was interesting, but this class was offered as non WI for first time, so only grades came from 3 tests, and was a bit unorganized. All in all it was ok.
One of my very favorite classes of all time.  Very interesting.  Vom Saal educates his students on a range of very interesting, up to the date information.  Highly recommend.
No Comments
Extremely interesting to listen to. Very enjoyable class that I would highly recommend.
Is very funny, but his handwriting is HORRIBLE. Class was moderately hard but interesting for a Capstone.
Monotone, Heavy use on book
He is fairly hard, but a very great teacher that is such an interesting philosopher and person.

He expects a lot on the exams and seems more interested in improving our critical reading skills than teaching philosophy. Seems invested in student progress - will pair up students who do poorly on exams with students who do well. Found ways to relate the material to practical situations. A good guy.

He tests primarily on the book, but never discusses it in class. Some of the tests are over nearly 200 pages of text. No discussion goes on in the class. If you want to be bored to death in a philosophy class...which I never thought possible, than take his honors section.

I have the honors section; his lectures are very thought-provoking and interesting, but he doesn't really cover what's in the textbook and ends up on the tests, which wouldn't be bad if one reads the text well in advance, portions it out and asks any question that comes to mind - he will answer questions. Don't take at 8 AM though.
Ok, hes really intelligent and really likes philosophy- but I actually read the book in that class and it was still hard!  And I like philosophy!  I learned a lot though- hes a good teacher.
Powerful. He received a standing ovation at the end of my class and he deserved it.

I almost fell asleep when he did his lectures...but he's entertaining when he comes up with story scenarios, and he's generally pretty likeable.  Tests were tough, a lot of true/false questions on subjective topics.
It's very hard for the simple minded person
He is a brilliant man- a little too intense for me at times. I found the exams in his Philosophy in Literature course to be very difficult.
Excellent philosopher.  Thinks he is hot; is not.
Low talker
He's frequently sarcastic and flexes his vocabulary, but he's really helpful

I absolutely loved J3000 with Dr. Volz! She is such a great lecturer and the topics were super interesting, with the second and third blocks of the class being some of the most compelling content. The exams do make up a majority of your grade though, so definitely study, but don't be discouraged since the project will help pad your grade.
This class in general is probably a harder class due to it being based on uninteresting topics. Additionally,
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. VOLZ! Oh my god! I'm a PhD student, and this was the best class I've taken since I was born. She is also the best professor in the history of professorship. She prepares every minute and has an outstanding work ethic. She puts all her efforts into transferring knowledge and makes the class highly engaging. She is also so invested in you.

This class was not super easy. Most of the lectures were interesting but some of the content felt all over the place. I could have studied harder for the exams, but they were really difficult for nearly everyone in the class. Most people in the class got a B. If you talk to Dr. Volz and TA's about your grade, they are very helpful

This course was really hard this semester. I think the worst part was that it is taught by another professor in the fall and he is much easier of a grader. Her tests are very, very challenging because of the memorizing she requires of you, but also the deep contextual knowledge on top of that. I studied 20 hours for the last exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her exams are HARD. If you go to class and read the textbooks they aren't as difficult but you still need to spend a lot of time studying the material. She tried to make the exams easier but it did not work. For some questions, it felt like you knew the answer but turns out you were dead wrong. Take it with ANYONE but her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Volz is a solid instructor. HOJO's material isn't the most exciting, so try your hardest to stay engaged. Her English is beautiful-you just have to pay attention. The microdocumentary project isn't too bad and could help your grade. Exams are difficult, definitely prioritize studying for them. You can get by by skimming the weekly readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is by the far the best professor I have had in J school. International student here but her English was always very clear to me. She had the classes well designed We did interviews, text-analysis and observations. Not to mention how kind and helpful and efficient she is. I have her on my committee and she has helped me more than my chair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Volz is a nice & endearing professor, but good lecturer she is not. I think I speak for most when I say J3000 is a boring class. More students stopped showing up to lectures after each week. Monotone, humorless & dry. To be honest, I think if you read the text & write your own outline notes, you could get by with not coming to class.
All these negative comments on her English are totally absurd. She has the SLIGHTEST hint of an accent but speaks great English. I had no troube understanding her. And I took her class in 2010.
The professor is knowledgable and the class is interesting - maybe because I am very interested into History. If you work hard, it would be too difficult to get a good grade.

She is very intelligent and knowledgable of the subject.  If you go to class and take good notes in addition to doing the reading, you will do well on the tests and essay.  Pretty simple.  Also, asking TAs about grades/grading helps your overall grade most of the time.

The tests are not very easy. The lectures are interesting but if you don't like history you might have a different feeling. Need to study hard to get A. To get an average score is pretty easy. Skipping class is not recommended.

Had her for HoJo. She's really smart, but a terrible prof. Class is SO BORING - prob. the most boring of my 4 years. She speaks pretty good english, but not great. Exams are TOUGH (lots of mindless studying). One 8 pg paper is kinda tough too. I got a B cuz I studied 2 long & wrote a good paper. I'd take it w/ a different prof or differnt semester!

Prof. Volz is very knowledgeable about the subject, and prepared very good powerpoint presentations with interesting visuals. Tests are hard, though, but if you use well the study guides, you will do fine.

This class is not easy.  You have to study really hard, go to all the lectures, and pay attention to every single item listed on the study guides.  The teacher is very nice and helpful if you go to her office hours.

If there is any way for you to get out of taking this class with this professor, then absolutely do so now. While she is a very intelligent person, she has spent little time in America and does not know the language well, which will be incredibly frustrating. My advice would be to do well on the 12 page paper.

The tests are hard. And the lectures are sometimes boring, especially if you don't like history... BUT if you read and study alot and pay attention, you can probably get a B. I would definitely recommend NOT skipping class tho, and get on the good side of the TAs early. They grade everything!
Terrible english. Terrible tests. Too much writing and trick questions. Be prepared to use entire print quota within first week. TERRIBLE TAs also. Worst class ever. Hands down.
This class was too hard.  She tried to cram so much information in her tests that it made studying for them impossible.  She was also really hard to understand.
Difficult to understand. The tests had too much material, the reading was boring. This class is awful!
trick questions on tests, doesn't answer your questions, hard to understand, boring!!, just a bad experience all together.

Attendance is not mandatory, but if you want to get a good grade, it is. The class itself is a difficult topic, but he teaches it well. There is one homework assignment a week, and he grades the tests VERY generously, with a lot of partial credit. The lowest two homework assignments were also dropped, which was very helpful.

Hw every week with 2 midterms and 1 final. Exams were easy as you get a group of problem and choose which ones you want to solve (couple extremely easy ones). Homework is long but doable with help. Grading on homework is very easy. Lectures are HEAVY. To be honest class was not too hard.

Don't miss lecture and take lots of notes. The hw takes a while so its good to have detailed notes. The tests are formatted so that you only answer a couple of questions from a list which is great. Out of all the writing intensive classes this one is definitely one of the better ones. I recommend taking this class with Dr Walsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Walsh took over my Calc III class after a previous professor was removed. His lectures were well worded with many examples and problems included. He was very accessible via email and was generally very helpful. Calc III is hard, but Dr. Walsh makes the class manageable and less stress inducing. Take him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My initial thoughts on this professor were wary as he used very flowery mathematical language. However, as the class went on I grew to enjoy it quite a lot, the lectures were interesting and informational. The tests could be difficult, but he posts old exams to practice with and they are very good practice at that.

Final is worth 40% of your grade so make sure you study for that. Homework can be tough and physical copies are turned in, but it helps for learning material for exams. Lectures are ok, but there are not many in class examples and they can be confusing at times. Overall an average experience.
Dr. Warren taught the linkage section of this genetics course. It was the hardest I believe of the sections however, if you follow the textbook and rewatch lectures you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's much nicer than Schnabel although he is a bit theatrical with his lectures. His section is one of the shortest so don't expect your grade on this exam to boost your grade, although you will do better than the other 3 exams. Talk to the TA if you need help, they're always more helpful than either professor for 3213.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Dr. Warrn is better than his Co-Professor I have only but disdain for this man. He teaches one section of the course and his lecture was not very engaging. He was a but more lenient, but overall is not very accessible outside class and just overall wasnt a great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teaches alongside Dr. Schnabel and only teaches one section. Explains concepts very well and prompts us to ask questions. He also grades a little bit easier than Schabel and makes his exam pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor goes with Dr. Schnabel in 3213 and unfortunately only taught one section. His test was the only out of the four that I passed with a 73% on. His lectures made way more sense than Schnabels and you could tell that he actually cared if we understood. For the most part was helpful with questions. He is way nicer than Schnabel.

Professor Wales is emblematic of a greater issue I see with every government teacher I've ever interacted with. They study bureaucracy but are in no ways a part of it so they set up imaginary gears to crush you. If you take his class be prepared to be given an F on a nonsense fluffy assignment with no explanation. Great class if you hate yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Wales is now at Clemson and I took one of his first courses here. He likes to read directly off the slides and connects them to real-world issues but his teaching style is not great. There's not much work in the class and the exams are 20% apiece.

Wales is a decent lecturer, kind of monotonous, but the biggest problem I have with him is a lack of flexibility. Don't expect him to give flexibility with due dates for personal emergencies since he "already has a late policy" (10% off per day). Also doesn't always post lectures on time. Easy class but not my favorite instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wales is a good professor. You can tell that he genuinely is interested in international relations, and that he enjoys teaching and talking about it. He can be a bit unenthusiastic at times, but nothing major. Overall, I enjoyed the class and felt like I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: genuinely awful I learned absolutely nothing and I wouldn't take this class again for a thousand dollars
She wouldn't stop talking
All of my friends hate her. Based on the stories it seems justified.
I always edged in this class, on skibidi
Greatest teacher I have ever had.

She does not teach. She will play one video or explain it once, have you practice in your notebook, and then assign an hour and a half of graded homework. Every day is a different lesson, after 2-3 days we have a test or quiz. Nobody has an A. Last year I had a 99, this year I have a 79. I've learned nothing and the class is destroying my GPA.
this teacher ruined my motivation to learn spanish because her teaching skills were not good
This will be the best teacher you will ever have.
mid ngl ong ong

At first I thought I was the only student who didn't like her, but it turned out to be the majority opinion by week 3. She grades upon criteria that are not outlined anywhere, and there are no lesson plans. She doesn't follow a syllabus and often times homework was assigned online without being announced. Couldn't pay me to take her again.

She's very sweet, but one of the worst teachers I have ever had. There is no structure and she is all over the place. It's like she doesn't have lesson plans and just wings it every single day. The assignments are weird and pointless. I loved Spanish in High School, but she made me hate the class!

All the interest that i had for the subject got washed down with her teaching. She is extremely unreliable.Her grading is inconsistent and she does not ever check the homework submitted to her. She is only interested in taking test without teaching and does not give back the graded tests on time. I will never take her class again.

I should have listened to what people have written on here, because everything here is exactly right. She is nice, but she is a terrible teacher. Hardly any time is dedicated to review, grading is very subjective, and homework is often mentioned as people are leaving class. We had substitutes for a few weeks and the difference was night & day.

VERY nice, but not that great of a teacher. Assumes you know Spanish already, and doesn't explain what she is teaching very well. Participation and homework grades are easy, tests are not, in my opinion.
She is a very nice woman. Will definitely work with you when you need help and is very patient. Her Spanish is easy to understand

Really nice lady, but do yourself a favor and find another teacher. I enjoys teaching but it isn't her strong point. I assumes you fluently speak spanish even though it it spanish 1. Her class consists of her writing random sentences on the board and not going over anything of worth. She wont remember your name either.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had. I have taken spanish for many years before this yet I still am unable to obtain an A. Her grading is very biased and unfair and her teachers methods are pathetic. She will change grades after posting them in order to give students the grades she desires them to recieve. AWFUL TEACHER! DROP HER CLASS!

Her teaching strategy is horrible bc she assumes that since the students who have taken high levels of spanish prior can answer the questions that everyone should be able to as well. She grades harshly and it doesn't really matter if you study a lot because you will get marked off for little mistakes even if you show that you understand the concept
She's an amazing person and super nice, but you couldn't pay me to take another one of her courses.

She is very nice and enthusiastic about teaching you.  She teaches in a logical order and as long as you look over the textbook and do the exercises before or after each class (10 min. tops) you will be fine. Only bad thing is that 80% of class is in taught in Spanish, but I think every professor is supposed to do that. Good professor.

Very nice, but just doesn't know how to teach. It's like she assumes we all know how to speak Spanish from the very beginning. After the first week she was trying to teach the whole class in Spanish. You will get used to saying "en ingles?" Also, she grades very harshly. Suggest you pick a different one.

Sweet teacher.  A lot of the grade is based mostly on homework and praticipation, which is good because the test are hard.  There is a lot of writing in spanish, but I pretty sure the department cordinator makes the test, so I doubt they would be easier with another teacher.
Her test were difficult because we had to write a lot in spanish, but a lot of the grade was on homework.  I thought she was very friendly.
She was very sweet but does not know how to teach at all. I learned nothing and would have received a much better grade if i took a teacher that i could understand and that actually knew how to teach

Dr. West's lectures were difficult to engage with, and the reading load was extremely heavy. Many of the assigned texts were painful to read and did not feel accessible or relevant to all students. I would recommend reconsidering whether this class aligns with your interests if you are not an English major or do not enjoy literary analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVED this prof! I was shocked at how much I enjoyed this class, and she is now my favorite professor at Mizzou! She's super passionate, knowledgeable, and caring. She made 9am classes a joy, and I highly recommend taking her courses! Her positive mood is contagious, and she is hilarious! The most inspirational and amazing professor ever!

I took her Jane Austen class and loved it! She is now one of my favorite professors, and has me, a non-English major, searching for classes she teaches to take. A lot of reading but that was expected. Weekly writing quizzes where you write about a topic previously given to you. Allows edited versions of papers to be turned in for a higher grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is so caring and genuinely wants to connect with every single one of her students. I was looking for an easy honors class and while attending class is mandatory and there is quite a lot of reading I recommend. She is very open to helping you in any way she can and as a non english major I appreciated that.
Very good lecturer with a lot of passion and experience. A little old school but always rewarded real interest and effort! I had a lot of fun, really enjoyable class.
Fantastic lecturer and very personable. There is a LOT of reading but that's to be expected with a course titled "Reading Literature" lol.

Very easy to pass if you could finish readings and simply pay attention but lectures were often filled with unnecessary political bias which also hindered the selected readings of the course. Dr. West also displayed an unprofessional reliance on her TA and an immature lack of cooperation regarding absences due to sickness and death in the family.

Dr. West was super fun. As a non-english major I was just looking for a relaxing class and I picked this one because I liked to read. I learned a lot and enjoyed most of the stories she has us read. We also had the opportunity to watch movies for some writing prompts, which was fun. Would take it again.

She was easy to listen to and had a clear lecture. The tests were so easy and I had a great time in the class. I really enjoy her class and I would definitely take the class again if I had the chance. She is also very easy to connect with. I definitely recommend taking this class if you want an easy honors or English class.
Very tough when it comes to grading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable and friendly, but does not utilize online resources. Many assignment specifications and deadlines were only mentioned verbally in class, so attendance in very important. All writing assignments must be printed out and brought to class. Lots of small group discussion. You can not get away with just reading the SparkNotes for books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. West is my favorite professor at Mizzou. I recommend that anyone considering taking a class from her does so.

I loved Professor West! You have to put in the work to get an A, but if you read, study, and do your homework youll do great. She also offered 50 bonus on our final exam, and offered bonus on every quiz (there were not any pop quizzes). Shes extremely knowledgeable & I learned a lot in her class. 10/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I would not be where I am today without Dr. West. She has been the best professor I have had in college and has made me grow exponentially as a writer and student. She encourages critical thinking and praises creativity! If you want to be a writer, TAKE A CLASS WITH DR. WEST! She will help you find your voice and hone your skills. 1000000/10!

Dr. West is AMAZING! She holds clear passion for all that she teaches (I've taken two classes with her), and she has an amazing sense of humor, and just sense in general. She's intelligent and is ready to help and encourage her students, and is very much open minded - there is no 'right' answer with her, you just have to be able to defend yourself.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Dr. West, go for it! Dr. West loves what she teaches and creates a great atmosphere for students to learn in. She is a fair grader and gives helpful feedback as well. She does give a lot of reading, but if you keep up and do your best you should absolutely be able to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She encouraged discussion and wanted students to think for themselves. She is funny and respected. While she expects a lot from students, she is available for additional help and discussion. I would love to take another one of her classes.

Dr. West is a total sweetheart! Her lectures are informative and she's clearly passionate about what she teaches. She takes grading papers seriously but is fair and gives good feedback. Anyone would be lucky to have her.

Dr. West is an amazing professor. Shes knowledgeable about what she teaches and shes also passionate about the subject and about getting students to become passionate about these topics. Shes big on class participation and creativity; she wants you to be a part of the classroom environment and enjoy the learning process. I loved this course.

This is a fun course if you like literature. You read British literature from multiple different periods. Dr. West is hilarious and makes class so much fun. She's pretty firm on some things, but completely fair. Her class was really enjoyable and not too difficult. There is a lot of reading, but most of it is pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is by far my favorite professor Ive ever taken. Brought my love of English to a new level and even made me realize I wanted to take it on as a second major. She is hilarious and really knows what shes talking about. You have to participate but the content is so interesting it wont even feel like homework.

She's amazing! She is obviously so passionate about what she teachers, which is such a great quality in a teacher. English majors will love her especially!! You do need the textbook, which is a pain in the butt, but it's actually an interesting book, so not all bad. Oh, and she's definitely funny, despite what her son apparently thinks. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. West is one of the best professors I have ever had in my 5 years at Mizzou. She is caring, and enthusiastic about the topic she teaches. She will challenge you to be your best, and makes every book you read as interesting as your favorite book, even if you hated it to begin with.

Dr. West is probably one of the best professors I will ever have. Read the books (they're actually interesting because its modern novels) and show up to class and take decent notes. Do the Blackboard prompts every week, super easy points. As long as you study your notes and the given vocabulary you'll pass easily. Got an A+ in the class, that easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor West was by far the best professor to have my freshman year. She was funny, well dressed, caring and enthusiastic. Participation is really important in this class, worth 25% of your grade. We also read 6 books this semester, so if you love to read totally take this class! The books were from the previous year, including Girl on the Train.

I completely agree with other posts: I want to be her. She is amazing, probably my favorite college professor. She is so enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and fun. It is the one class I actually look forward to going to every day. She's a very fair grader, and class is largely discussion based which keeps it interesting. And not And very cute dresser!
Love her, she's so cute! She is so enthuastic, she honestly cares about her students and subject. Knows a lot about her subject. I'll echo someone else and say I want to BE her when I grow up.

I want to be her when I grow up.  So helpful and nice in class; our group talked a lot, so we had a blast. I had no attendance problems; had to go replace my driver's license one day, went in and talked to her beforehand, wasn't a problem.  Make a good impression the days you're there and do the reading, she'll love you.  Snappy dresser, too.
She brings in a lot of enthusiasm into the class
She has knowledge about film and she tries to make lectures intersting.
No Comments
No Comments
very, very, very strict with attendance.  doesn't care if you're a graduating senior attending job interviews or not.  kind of ****y.

Weston is such a sweet lady who truly cares about her students. But, tests are EXTREMELY difficult & there's no allowed equation cheat sheets, also her TAs give graded 1 quiz every week which is draining. Lectures are hard to follow due to a funky lecture style and her very hard to read cursive handwriting that the lectures are based off of.

For the love of all things good and holy don't take Calc 2 with Dr Weston. Her notes are all handwritten with lots of mathematical shorthand you have to learn at the start of the semester on top of the course material. Also, her TA gave quizzes every week that were so toughly graded you would be lucky to get a C. DON'T DO IT ITS NOT WORTH IT!!!!!!!

All notes in cursive with strange shorthand notation that is tough to decipher; does not allow notecards/ cheat sheets for exams which makes it very difficult. Tough grader and bad lectures (watch professor Leonard on YouTube instead). I also took this class at 8am which made it tougher but I would not at all recommend taking her.

Isn't wise for teachers to interrupt kids asking questions. Doing so felt insulting to her, having a response of "you should know this! You gonna wait til the night before the exam to learn it? A week? Two weeks? No!" She goes over notes taken from the book, but expects students to understand how she interprets it. Office hours didn't help.

She was nice but not a very good teacher, she seemed like she did not know what she was really talking about and made lectures hard to keep up with. It did not help that her assistant gave quizzes every week that were impossible for no reason. Westons grading on the exams were tough but fair.

Her lectures and notes were definitely hard to understand, but I found that watching other professors lectures on youtube and reading the textbook to be an easy way to prepare for her lectures. Her tests are very fair and she gives a lot of credit on the exams as long as you show your work and use the correct notation. She's a very silly lady.

This class will have you rethinking your entire major. There is homework and a quiz every week along with a lecture everyday. There are four total exams that account for a majority of your grade. She curves the tests at the end of the semester by around 5%. She is a bad at teaching as she only has one style but she cares about the students.

This class is extremely difficult, but she does her best to talk us through everything. I found her notes difficult to understand, same with lectures, and instead the review days seemed to be the best way for me to learn. She's very nice and gave us plenty of review material for the exams, which there are a lot of.

Asks for 5 homework questions, only grades one of them (you don't know which), then take off 1/3-1/2 of the points for irrelevant trivial things. She uses doc cam and uses very cursive handwritten notes, the lighting is also bad so often hard to read. She also treats us like 10th graders when half of us have an M.A.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Lectures consist of pages and pages of cursive notes written in sentences with mathematical symbols. I prefer reading the textbook than going to lectures. There is no intuition whatsoever for linear algebra, and she focuses solely on computations rather than concepts. Do not take this class with Weston.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tough grader is a HUGE understatement. Barely gives any partial credit. Lectures are erratic and hard to follow. One bad grade will tank your grade for the rest of the semester with no way to recover. Not worth it. Take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Weston is a very kind and fair professor. She is by far one of the most fair professors I have ever had. Her exams are very difficult, but very fair, you will NEVER be tested on something you did not cover in class. She moves quite quickly so sometimes it is helpful to take notes before hand so you can just follow along while she lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I will never rate a professor who cannot give help without interrupting students before they finish giving their question.

Dana is a great professor. She writes everything by hand on the board and provides notes before class. Her writing keeps students engaged and it is easy to follow along. She will take time to answer misconceptions and questions even with a lecture planned.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Weston was a professor that genuinely cared about her students. Her tests were very straight-forward and were very similar to the practice tests she gives before each exam. She sometimes rushes through topics (saying you can always access them online) and when trying to make something clearer, she gives analogies that make it more confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Class was slightly confusing at first, but after putting my nose to the grind and going into her office hours on a consistent basis things became very clear. The better she knows you, the more lenient she is with you. She is very encouraging and wants you to really understand the material and will do what she can to help.

She's very technical and therotical when explaining concepts and she doesn't always teach the quickest and simplest method. But she is good about telling you what's on the tests and you have a decent curve. Not the best teacher, but a sweet lady who knows what she's talking about.

Hardest class I've ever taken. Went to every class and did every homework assignment and struggled for a C. She knows her stuff but can only really explain it one way. Most notes are directly from text book and she reads over them quickly in class. I wouldn't have passed without an outside tutor. Very sweet woman, but insanely difficult teacher.

Always willing to go the extra mile to help me understand the material. She cares a lot about her students. Tended to fill the entire board with notes before class and talk through them, most notes were directly out of the book. You had to work outside of class to understand main ideas. Her exams were very fair, quizzes not so much.

She's knows the material, but has a really hard time explaining it in a way that is easy to learn. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! Once she gets to know you, she'll be easier on the grading for you. Also find any help sessions, they'll give you quicker methods to figure out the solutions, but she may take away points for not using her method.

Dr. Weston was crystal clear. She treated her honors class basically exactly like her regular class. This was a pretty easy A, especially for an honors math class. She was funny, interesting, and it was obvious that she wanted us to learn the material. Overall this was a great class!

Assigns hw but doesn't grade  or provide solutions to check against.  Renders hw pointless unless you go to office hours.  Unfortunately, she is quite rude- very abrasive and interrupts a lot.  If her teaching style/lectures 'click' for you, you will be fine.  But if not, get out of the class as there's no independent study path through the course

I love Professor Weston! She is probably the best professor I've had at this university, so far. She is immensely helpful and really kind - in class and in office hours. Also, if you do all the homework carefully and pay attention in class, you'll get an A in the class.

Teaching style is very hard to follow. She knows the material, but can only convey it in one method, so if you don't understand it then you're out of luck. Even going in for office hours doesn't help, she will just cut you off before you finish your question, wasting what little time you get. Had her for Calc2 and Math3000, both poor experiences.

Amazing teacher.  By far the most helpful teacher i have ever had in my entire life.  She knows the material, has notes for the entire semester all written out for you, so that you dont have to worry about missing something.  If you study, you will get an A. I got 100% on 2 of 3 tests and a 98 on the final. She will help you and loves it.

Professor Wexler was very good at explaining concepts. He was clear on what to expect on the exams (in class/practice problems very similar). His lectures were recorded, so missing class wasn't a big deal. As long as you do the discussion problems and go to the review before the exams you will be fine.

Dr.Wexler was a good prof. He gave practice exams that were extremely similar to the real ones. Gave plenty of examples in class for the homework and exam questions. Plus he was clear about grading. Loved that the exams weren't weighted heavily. 5 exams, 10% each. He gave you notes to fill out during class as well. Hate physics but he made it good.

This course will pick up covering basic 2d kinematics identical if not easier than high school level physics. Only difficult exam was 3. It was unexpectedly hard compared to the sample exams and included a very unorthodox problem we were not familiar with. Be careful and study hard for that exam. The other 4 are easy A+ if you practice throughly.

This was probably the hardest class I ever took as an engineer so far and took an insane amount of work, but it seemed that the tas and Dr wexler wanted the students to succeed. I had to read the textbook alot but I found the lecture slides were also necessary. This course is insanely fast paced and he taught it well for what it's worth.

Very entertaining professor. You must pay attention in every lecture or you will fall behind. This class was definitely my most difficult, but it wasn't impossible to succeed. Carlos is very funny and you will find his lectures entertaining!
