Dr. Wexler is a great guy who is a lot of fun to talk to. He is clearly very knowledgeable about electronics and is always willing to help. However, it seems he thinks the material is more intuitive than it is, and there are times where his explanations can come off a little condescending. 4050 is conceptually quite difficult, but graded easily.

Wexler's nearly a complete non-factor, you're not going to learn most of the material by showing up to lecture, but from quizzes, labs, and homeworks. He will zoom and post his lectures online, if you do find value in his lectures. Class is challenging but easy to get good grade in due to the weight of labs, quizzes and homework

Prof Wexler is very passionate about physics and makes the lectures enjoyable to watch. The class is really hard and fast-paced so it is important to study outside of class. Read before lectures and go to discussions.

Very passionate about what he teachers and really tries to make what he does fun. His demonstrations for different Physics concepts are silly and you can tell he enjoys doing them. He really does respect his students and it seems the majority of students respect him as well. The class itself is hard and very fast paced but still quite manageable.

Only small issue I had was lectures, fast paced most times. Took me til the second exam to get in the flow of how he teaches. Lots of opportunities to ask questions. Exam prep was also very helpful in what he posted. If you studied what was provided, you should have no problem passing with a C. More study hours and questions from the book help. Fun

Prof Wexler is a great professor and you can tell that he is very passionate about physics. He genuinely wants to see his students do well and although this class is fast paced, he gives many opportunities in lecture to slow down and understand. This class content can be a challenge but Prof. Wexler is the best suited to teach it. He's also funny

This class follows the textbook (openstax univ. physics) very closely and it's very helpful. Honestly showing up to all the lectures isn't that important as long as you have the discipline to review the textbook, discussion problems, and practice exams. He is also very understanding and a genuinely nice guy.

I took the honors version of PHYSC 2750 and it was fairly decent. Overall, the pace of the class is fast, and lectures condense a lot of information in 50 minutes. The labs were straightforward but tedious at times. Exams were 50% of our grade but were pretty similar to practice ones. HW questions were long. I would take a class with him again.
I understand what he is saying during lectures, but as soon as he does an example problem during class whatever he is saying makes 0 sense, and he uses a technique he never even mentioned.
His lectures don't make much sense

Dr. Wexler is my second favorite professor from undergrad. I took his Electronics Lab and it took me from knowing nothing about electronics to building on my own. He is VERY passionate and knowledgeable and actually makes an effort to teach the material well. It really shows. He is also an easier grader so if you make an effort, you should do fine.

This is a tough 4000 level class for physics majors (and some engineering majors too). It is quite intense mathematically. Get ready to calculate integrals in spherical coordinates! Overall I thought Carlos did a good job adding some physics content even if the class is very math oriented (Electromagnetism). Work hard and you will do fine.

Carlos is a good guy, but place him in a upper level course that he's never taught before and it's a disaster. I feel like I know less after the course than I did before. The only way I got a B in this class was because of the grading curve. I've been earning failing test scores all semester and because homework was worth 50% I squeaked the B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher, cares a lot about us learning the stuff.  Fast paced class but he makes it good.

He's pretty goofy and a nice guy. The class is fast-paced, but it will be that way no matter who is teaching. He offers students respect, and expects the same from them - doesn't like talking in class. He's an okay teacher; he teaches much better one-on-one than in lecture. Read/skim the text book before lecture to get more out of his teaching.

I don't how people are rating him as good? He wasn't that great of a teacher. Very unapproachable and belittled people. His class was fast paced, he would pause class to yell at single individuals. The time I learned anything was on my own time or through recitation.

One word to describe Carlos Wexler: swag. The class isn't bad, just work through MasteringPhysics and the sample exams and you'll be good to go. He typically sides with the student and is just an all around awesome dude.
Considering this is University Physics 1, I think this class was awesome! Nice demos, plenty of enthusiasm.  Wish the class could move slower!  It's like drininking from a fire-hose!
Prof W is one of the best I've had.  The class is dyanmic and interesting.  Grading was one of the fairest at MU.  High enthusiasm and nice to deal with. No issues.
Good prof in the recitations.  Helpful and dynamic.  But speaks very fast!
Very good in this recitation.  Clear and nice.

I really dislike physics, but I like how the prof. teaches the course.  He is always willing to help and it is evident he put a lot of effort in the preparation of the class.  My only issue is that the class does move very fast, too fast!  Please slow down...

Avoid if at all possible. Not helpful in understanding homework or basic concepts and yells at students who dare to ask questions. Moves to quickly through topics and rearranges equations without saying why. Very confusing.
Good prof.
Professor is very dynamic.  Makes many (some bad) jokes. Class was hard through the entire semester, but not so hard at exam time.  A good teacher!!!
His latin accent is so cute!
Interesting class but you have to work work work...  I'm learnin' though...
He wants you to learn. He is much better in rsd or one on one though. You learn what you need to and do your work, but he is very enthusiastic and not at all a droning, boring prof!!
Good guy!
Good course! Dr. W keeps you working everyday whether you like it or not!!!!  (but then there is no need to cram for exams which was good).  Class was interesting, but I still hate physics.
There was a lot of hard work, but it paid off in the end.  CW gave great grades!
Physics is hard, but CW makes it interesting.  Cool class demos, cool in-class discussion.  CW makes us work hard (webct quizzes 3 times per week) which is tough but I can see the (good) results!!
Fun guy, very helpful.  Class is difficult material but he makes it more interesting.  It requires a lot of work, however, so be prepared!!!
One of the best classes at MU.  Very dynamic.  I really like the approach this professor takes.
Excellent professor, the best I've had.  I really like how he guides us through the difficult materials by making US do the learning.  Excellent!!

Class is hard, no doubt.  Especially if  you're like me and never had physics before.  One of the points of his class(at least now)is that you teach yourself rather than cramming everything into a lecture, which I like.  His tests are tough but fair and he gives a LOT of extra credit/easy points.
This teacher is very hard to understand and he does not help you during class. Try all you can to avoid taking Physics with him

Professor is unhelpful and unclear both in course materials and also in expectations from students.  Has a poor command of the English language, and mocks students who ask questions during class.  AVOID.
I'm having a tough time in the course but the professor is very good and helpful.  He even makes the lectures fun!
Nice clear lectures.  Course is hard, though.

Smart, but extremely arrogant. Exams had few questions and averaged 50%. ADA is not a priority for the course. Half of our homework platform was deleted halfway through the semester and he offered no alternative. There were times I felt personally attacked for requesting accommodations while undergoing inpatient treatment. Good luck.

Attendance isn't enforced, but it's recommended if you want to do well. Just get prepared for irrelevant tangents about his work that only vaguely relate to the material.

He is very knowledgeable and passionate teacher. His lectures are the most important part of the class to do well on the tests but the lectures are not boring. There are 3 tests and a final that has 3 short answers and 6 multiple choice and they are meant to be challenging but he curves the class to help people get a decent grade. A 75% was an A

He clearly has a passion for chemistry, but you just can't transfer an ivy level class to students who had much lower rigor requirements for entry. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is not mandatory but no online notes/lectures make lectures a requirement to do well on exams. Lab grades heavily determine the grade so your TA is important. Tests are hard but are curved based on class performance. The professor is extremely knowledgeable about chemistry.

He gives interesting and pretty good lectures, but his tests are just too tough. Around 6 multiple choice questions are worth 10% of the exams each and are all or nothing, which can really screw up your test grade. The class is heavily curved though so although I didn't do great on any exam, I was still about to come out with a good grade.

Dr. Bernskoetter lectures well, but his tests are what make the class difficult. Test average is usually ~50% and is based on very few questions. Working out the old exams and practice problems he posts are vital to do well on exams. He also does not post his lectures after, but many of the in-class problems come from the textbook.

He does not go over the material in detail whatsoever, and then on the tests, he expects us to know it as if we were professors. Also, he will post a test review, but the review does not correlate with his tests.

ATTEND CLASS. You won't do well if you don't. This class is 10x harder than Chem 1320 with Keller. He makes Keller's class feel like cake. I received >100% on Keller's exams, and ~45% avg on exams in this class. You definitely have to work for the grade. Lab TAs are confusing and not helpful. If you can, take it with someone else.

His class was difficult. Taking organic chemistry was easier for me personally, but to do well in the course I recommend always watching lectures and if you have a question, go to office hours. His grading style wasnt my favorite because your grade was a mystery until the end of the course. Spend lots of time on the material outside of class!

Basically you never get feedback. He never explains things clearly. Makes office hours only to get aggravated when people ask questions. He only gives random stats about the exams and you just have to hope you're on the right part of the curve. Although I did good, I wouldn't advise anyone to take that class, or any class with him.

Bernskoetter is the rudest Chemistry professor I have ever had. He absolutely refused to help me understand the concepts. This was my second time taking a General Chemistry 2 course as I had taken it at a previous University quite some time ago. The lowest exam score back than was a 76. I was only able to score a 40 as my highest score this time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tests are unbelievably difficult and you have no idea what your grade is until the very end. reviews.comment: Chem 1330 with Dr. Bernskoetter is a challenging class, but if you do your part to understand the material beyond the surface level, youll do fine. Very hard class with an even worse professor. He is rude when you ask for help and tests are over information that was never discussed. The class is curved on an average class grade and standard deviations. Unfair way of learning and causes stress throughout semester. Avoid at all cost.

You can tell he doesnt care about teaching this class. He doesnt give you any idea of what your grade is until the very end of the semester. Also, he put content on the final exam that he explicitly said he wouldnt teach us because we didnt need to know it.

This has been one of the worst classes I have taken. As far a lectures and homework this class is easy to understand. He gives out review sheets that have absolutely nothing to do with the test. Bernskoetter had really good lectures, and made the material very easy to comprehend. However, when it came to the test, it felt like I never learned anything. reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible. Swear this guy goes out of his way to make his tests unbelievably difficult and completely unrelated to anything in the lectures or on homework. Avoid this man like the plague, he should not be a professor.

reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

4 exams, 1 being a comprehensive Final (25% of grade). 1st 2 exams are difficult imo. Go to lecture or you won't pass. Go to office hours, even if you think you don't have to. Ms Webster is a fantastic teacher! If you like French and the culture before this class.. you'll love it after. Her class is a lot of fun and pretty easy.

Courtney is a great teacher. She has lived in France and knows a lot about the culture, and her accent when speaking French is flawless but also easy to understand. She is funny and nice, very helpful and always available for office hours. Try to get into one of her sections if possible, she'll make your life a lot easier.
She's awesome! I was dreading having to take French but she was a great teacher. Hopefully I get her for the next section of French. Definitely attend class and you'll be fine.

She lacks the ability to speak in French and instead just wastes class time talking about her personal life. She is an awful professor and prefers using worksheets and useless exercises  to fill class time instead of having conversations in french.

my king. i love him

I didn't buy the class textbook and still managed to get A's on every exam and every project. He grades very easily and also will remove questions from your exam score if most people get it wrong.

Dr. Whitney was amazing. It was discussion based so attending class was important and so was doing the reading before hand. This guy rocks. Most interesting and easiest class I've ever taken

I enjoyed this class with Dr. Whitney. He is extremely insightful, and I look forward to having conversations with him each class!

Dr. Whitney is a great professor. I look forward to his class every week. Every education major should take this class because I know I've gotten so much out of the readings and conversations we have in class. He's such a great professor! The honors reading course is discussion-based and is fairly easy if you do the work and participate in class. It's a really fun course and it helped me understand the importance of being an educator.

Dr. Whitney is an awesome professor who loves to challenge his students. He develops a personal relationship while maintaining professional expectations. His assignments and readings all make sense to the content and has a purpose. He is a great professor if you are willing to put in the effort for the class! He is my favorite person ever!!

I loved Professor Whitney's class. I feel like the bad reviews are from people who did not even try. You have to study to get an A (and the tests ARE hard), but it's definitely doable. I learned so much in his class that will help me become a great future educator.

I feel as though some of these negative reviews are unfair. Dr. Whitney's class was challenging, that's indisputable, but he genuinely cared about us students. He emphasized us taking responsibility for our own education. Those who did poorly only did so because they didn't give their all.

Dr. Whitney is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and holds them to a high standard. Great teacher. Really makes his students think deep and outside the box. Helps aid in gaining knowledge of real-life situations in the classroom. He also brings cookies to class!

I had Dr.Whitney for a reading class, and loved him. The books we read were interesting, and I enjoyed our discussions. It opened my eyes to how different opinions can actually be. He was thought-provoking and overall the class was pretty easy.

most amazing teacher I've ever had, really impacted me

not much to say he likes riding motor cycles like its a second child.

My all time favorite professor. His lecture videos are really helpful. His homework he assigns are really fun to do if you enjoy programming. You definitely need to put the work/hours in but the reward you get at the end is worth it. Take him if you can. You wont regret it.

Professor Wergeles is a fantastic professor. Yes, he gives a lot of hw, but you learn a lot. He knows a vast amount about many topics related to CS and you will definitely learn valuable skills. If you have a full class load, it can be difficult to work his assignments into your schedule, but if you can, his class is worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Notes are done outside of class, take upwards of 2 hours. Attendance is mandatory, takes 3 hours a week where questions get answered. Changes instructions on hw the day it's due. Tends to talk around an answer; everything is very wordy, including syllabus. Does not proofread hw instructions. Mandatory citation style leaves a lot to be desired.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Wergeles has been my favorite professor so far at the University. His course is challenging but if you put the work in throughout the semester, you will be successful. Lots of help is available outside the class as well. Wergeles cares deeply about the success of his students and has amazing experience in the industry. Highly recommend!

Yes, the workload is overwhelming, but that's because there's only so much time to teach all the content in one semester. You will spend quite a bit of time taking this class each week, but you will also learn so much. Very lecture heavy but he explains things very clearly. Available help is also a good perk of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is a 3 credit hour class that requires you do research and trouble shoot 20+ hours a week. At the end of it all I was proud what all I did. Yet at the same time I wouldn't wish this course on my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good professor, forces you to learn the material. He knows his stuff and still does interviews with FAANG companies to make sure he is teaching useful information. His challenges take you a long time to complete and some required material is a little silly. Overall, he's a good guy who cares about his students and I'll take more of his classes.

I liked how available Wergeles and his TA's were for the class. Having weekly available meetings and developer nights gave you ample time to learn indirectly or directly from them. The challenges aren't as hard as they are tedious to get correct, but they will take you some time. Overall, I have learned a ton from Wergeles and enrolled in 4830.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: About halfway into the semester and I've already learned so much. He clearly explains every concept and makes sure you know everything that's needed for the weekly challenges. Lecture videos could take a lot of time to get through but imo it's worth it. A lot of help is offered in this class. He also tells you everything that's gonna be on the exam

If you want to take a class that will make you question your choices about going into information technology then this is for you. And be prepared to find 15 answers to a single question that has 80 different choices. The challenges are also a joke. Tells you he is giving you 80 to 90 % of the challenge in lectures, but that is such bull.

This shouldnt be a difficult class. The material is easy and the professor is smart but he couldnt make it harder if he tried. Quizzes are so poorly worded you wont be able to answer even if you know the material. Astronomical amounts of work not necessarily hard, just way too much. 10+ hours a week and I have never had to use more than 4.

To be fair to him he knows his stuff. Very knowledgeable on the subject but he demands perfection. Have a typo in the name of your project, 0. Forget a comment in the code that he wanted, 0. Its honestly ridiculous and he requires things that are at times completely unnecessary and frankly time consuming. Cool guy but hard to have as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nick is very enthusiastic and knowledgable. There are weekly challenges that can be difficult, but if you watch all of his lectures, you'll be okay on most of them. He is slow to respond to emails, but always comes through with helpful info.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He makes it so much harder than it needs to be. The content itself is good but the amount is too much. The course load isn't difficult, it just takes time to do, he also gives like two exams for one midterm and there's 2 final exams and a final project. Just a ridiculous amount of work to do. Like even to get a B or a B+, you'll have to work hard!

Great Professor. Had him before in Object Oriented Programming. Had really good lectures and was pretty funny during some of them. Gives great sources for problems in the class and almost everything in the videos are on the weekly quizes. Not the biggest fan on the exam style. Projects were fun to do and great way to increase experience.
Best professor you could have for COSC.

Professor Wergeles is one of the best professors Ive ever had. He taught me so much and wasnt too difficult. Very understanding of his students and tries to get to know each and every one of them. I definitely recommend him.
Hes super nice. He cares for his students and he wants to get to know us. Hes an amazing professor and he deserves the best. Please go to his class. Hes amazing!

Wergeles does a good job at breaking things down and explaining them well. He is also very available outside of class for help. My main issue is that his lectures are ridiculously long and his quizzes and tests take directly from that. There are tons of questions often with 8+ choices and references to stuff not in the lab, just unnecessarily hard

Professor Wergeles was one of the best professors I've had at Mizzou. His teaching is very clear during the video lectures he recorded and they are posted on youtube. He also cares about his students! If you start early on the projects and go to office hours, you'll succeed in class! I highly recommend his courses because they help you get a job!!

Professor Wergeles is a good professor, audible and clear. He's very accessible outside of class and after lectures. He does a good job of having half in person classes and half online. Quizzes are difficult but open note/internet and have no time limit. Challenges are difficult and will take time but are useful application development practice.

Wergeles is the best CS prof that I have had so far. His teaching is very clear and gives you the code to work alongside him in lecture. He also records every lecture so these are great tools for studying later. Quizes in this class could be better, but they only make 10% of your grade and can Challenge bonus could make up that difference.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm enjoying the web development class so far! Do all of your assignments early and go to office hours as much as you can. If you wait late in the week to start, you won't get the assignment done on time and you will receive a 25% deduction for each day the assignment is late. Also, if you can't handle his courses, then CS or IT is not for you.

Expect around 6-12 hrs/wk of outside homework for a 3-credit course. Quizzes and exams are written in such a way that it is difficult to understand what is being asked. No feedback is given for incorrect answers on exams. Grading takes up to a month. Useful course material, but mostly relies on your own research skills.

His lectures are mandatory, but they're very thorough and engaging since he shows off code live and has everyone follow along on laptops. Some of the grading on coding projects is questionable, but overall very consistent and clear as to what's being asked. He communicates very well and is often available outside class for help.

Had him for 3330 and 2830 in same semester. One of the most frustrating professors I've had. Weekly projects and quizzes take up so much time, and I had to deal with that for 2 classes so it was a massive workload. I dreaded doing every one of his assignments. They were terribly worded, you lost an arbitrary amount of points, structured poorly, etc

Nick isn't a bad guy. He seems to really care and likes what he does. But his challenges are insane, be prepared to spend 6-10 hours on homework a week and then lose half your grade because you forgot a to make a small button green instead of blue. His quizzes are based more on opinion than fact so the average grade was around 65% on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Some of the material and practices are outdated. He can be evasive and difficult to contact sometimes. Lectures go by extremely slow. The homework challenges are usually good practice. The quizzes were written by a small child - every single question either has a typo, grammar mistake, or poor formatting. This was especially frustrating.

Professor Wergeles has very hands on lectures, excellent for the practical portion of web development. Compared with prior classes, Professor Wergeles enjoys web development more than Java. The class was very straightforward and what you would expect from a web development course. The quizzes often contained material not covered elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you want to do well in this class and are not a hobbyist programmer, you must step up to the plate and put in many hours outside of class. Online quizzes are open-internet and have no time limit yet most people scored 70s on them because they're poorly written. Lectures were uninspiring, though he seems more enthusiastic one on one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His voice is a total meme. "NetBeans." He is a very caring man who is available for help. He provides all the resources for learning Java. I liked the homework assignment "challenges". My only complaint is that the open note online quiz questions were terribly written and I did much worse on those online quizzes than anything else in the course.
The best professor I've had at Mizzou so far. Clearly cares about his students, stays after class for question. I look forward to having him as a professor in another class.
You will learn a lot in this class, but be prepared to show up or spend hours outside of class researching/working on homework. Cool guy though, seems to really care about helping those who want it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nick was not entirely competent with his course material. Class was painfully slow, dull, and often times comprised of irrelevant notes. Several sections of the course material were significantly outdated. Seems like a decent person, but not a good teacher by any means.

Tough but fair. He's entertaining during lecture, but be prepared to do a lot of work outside of class if you want to get good grades on his quizzes. The Oracle website is your textbook, and yes you will need it. Very interactive though, and he spends a lot of time outside of class helping students. Use his office hours and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Wergeles is a very hands on professor. His lectures are almost all hands on coding and discussion with the class. The lectures are excellent for the practical portion of java, but were lacking in the concepts. However, the quizzes are mostly conceptual. Professor Wergeles is willing to work extensively outside class with students.

This professor is the best you might get. This teacher might have hard assignments at first, but he cares. I can't believe how amazing he is compared to other teachers at Mizzou. He cares he stays after class to respond to questions and if he does not know something he is willing to learn, and respond with a positive attitude. I would recommend.
Professor Wergeles is a cool guy, always willing to help with coding issues either after class, during office hours, or his weekly developer nights. His dry humor is also a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Monotone and a dry humor but one of my favorite professors yet. If you can get passed how he talks his lectures are incredibly helpful and he is always available right after class for any questions. Super helpful during office hours as well, you just actually have to ask for help. Challenge and quiz every week, will have to work for good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cool dude, if you go for help he will be there for you. Course is difficult, but when I look back, I learned the most in this guy's class. Go get help and you will be fine.
Homework had nothing to do with the lecture material. The professor doesn't actually know anything about the topics and googles everything he talks about. Do not take the Prof for any reason
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is not a good professor in my opinion. You are will not pass if you cannot type as fast as he can. It is a live coding class and he goes very fast and does not answer questions during lectures often. He presesnt's himself as if he just woke up but in a fresh dry cleaned suit. His TA's are very rude and unintelligible on the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Can't take him seriously.

A tough course maker, yes but Prof. Wergeles fundamentally cares about his students. Always available for help and makes good use of TAs. Lectures are very hard to keep up with at times and if you don't get it down you can be kind of screwed because your program won't run. Get to know the course note taker! I had him for Java and Webdev andlearnlot
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible!

Cranky and boring most days. You can forget about asking questions before or after class. he acts bothered and annoyed when you need help or have an issue. he is prob close to retirement which is a good thing.

He is old, tiered and I feel like he should be retired. He comes to class everyday and teaches like expected. But outside of that help from him is impossible. If there is a discrepancy he will not believe you! Ugh just not a good experience. But I am not a fan of math anyway..

This class only has weekly quizzes, lab reports, and the final practical and exam. The content of the products portion is not hard, but it is a lot of memorization. Your grade is dependent of how you do on the finals. There is extra credit opporotunities and Dr. Wiegand is an engaging professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His classes are like a fever dream and always a joy to listen to. Once you take one class that he teaches you are always trying to take another. Wiegand does have a lot of other responsibilities outside of teaching so he can be hard to track down, but he is always willing to spend time with you if you manage to find him.
Good class

Definitely my favorite professor. 
His material can be difficult but he teaches it so well it makes it easier. 
He is funny, respected, and very approachable. 
Don't let any of his courses scare you, he'll make sure you do great!

Overall, it is a pretty boring class, but not too hard. Lecture is good, but a different person teaches the labs and those are terrible. Poorly run and is all over the place. Weekly quizzes are super easy. Only have a final exam which was kind of difficult. Lab practical was difficult due to the professor of that portion. Pretty average class.

Truly cares about his students and their learning. He's also really respectful of time, and won't continue to lecture just because there's time left when he finishes material. Overall, it's a pretty easy class but he makes it fun, and you'll definitely enjoy him
One of my absolute favorite professors. Very clear grading and great lectures. Cares about his students. Wish he taught all my classes.
Dr. Wiegand is a wonderful professor.
Super cool professor. Willing to help if you're confused.

Dr. Wiegand is a really really cool prof. He is very lenient and kinda lets a lot pass by in his classes, the only bad thing I have to say about him is his grading. In this class, he never posted any of our grades online, and no one in the class even knew what grade they had going into the final or lab practical. Which might I add, were really hard

He is probably one of my favorite professors, as well as adviser. He is helpful, easy to get along with and incorporates humor. Just a real cool guy. The class was pretty easy as long as you half payed attention.

This class was pretty much an easy A. Dr. Wiegand is very nice and helpful. His TA's do most of the teaching, which makes the class easier.  If you can get ahold of an old exam the tests are a breeze.

This class is all busy work, but it is not hard!! All the instructions were super clear. Just stay on top of the due dates of stuff! The professor is also very reachable by email. If you need a science credit, take this class!!

This class requires you to buy your own ingredients and cook each week, yet you don't get proper lab credit for the time or expense. The recipes are poorly designed, and the course feels more like a nutrition ideology lesson than practical cooking. It pushes vegan, low-protein meals and is a waste of time and money. As well as time consuming work.

This class is pretty silly. We have about 30 assignments due each week which are very time-consuming. Also, the professor grades very heavily on the deep dives. It just takes a lot of time, it's easy work, but it is very time-consuming.

This class isn't difficult, it's just time consuming because there is usually 25-30 things due a week. She doesn't record lectures, you just have to read the textbook, which is annoying. The worst thing about this class are the "deep dives" and they aren't really hard, just annoying. Easy enough class to get your science credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was very time consuming and the professor graded unreasonably hard for the assignments/material. It was not a difficult class but the professor tried to make it hard by taking off points for every little thing. If you like to cook this will be a good class for you.

It was fairly easy as long as you keep on schedule. DON'T forget to turn in the sheet to the self paced platform. The assignments were insanely easy. The only minor challenge is the assignments that she creates herself. She was helpful via email and I asked any question I had on the homework and she would help me all the way through to the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was just sitting in his class, an oil painting class as a hobby, many years ago. William is such a passionate professor who made an impact on me. Now I'm a faculty (in another field) and still remember how he cared about the students. He has influenced me to teach and guide students, and pursue something I love. Thank you!
I had Bill as a painting professor in 2000. It was a great experience and I gained a lot of knowledge from him.

Hawk is a great teacher, painter, and friend. He's extremely easy-going, but he wants you to be in class! You are expected to come in and paint, and then come in and paint some more outside of class. ASK FOR HELP. He is willing to go above and beyond for students, but you have to put the effort forward. Also, he tells a pretty good joke.

I loved Professor Hawk's Painting 1 class.  Hawk has got a very entertaining personality and is really encouraging. I learned many new techniques and perspectives that improved my work immensely.  Hawk's class is a lot of work, so if you aren't already interested in painting and are willing to put in a lot of time, I wouldn't suggest his class.
Tough professor but nice person. Make sure you are really into painting and really want to learn something. Otherwise it is bad for your GPA and everyday  mood.

I didn't really connect with Bill. He's a great guy, but I didn't like him so much as a professor. Very long lectures, has very structured teaching methods, long, slow classes. It was hard to understand my grades, because he puts them on his own website. Otherwise the class in general is very expensive (supply kit is $300) and time consuming.

I learned SO MUCH from this class. Everyone in my class improved tenfold. For my section there was one quiz worth 1 point and a final worth 100 (The entire thing was the exact same as the practice test). If you're not a good painter, you won't get an A. Lots of studio work expected from you, but he does help if you listen. Lots of extra credit.
Very hard on students but not on himself.  Would not recommend him.
Yeah, he's a hard grader. Yes, he is scatterbrained and incomprehensible. His final exam is crazy difficult! Even harder than my Math final!!! DO NOT EVER TAKE THIS TEACHER. EVER.

William Hawk is probably the worst professor I've ever had.  He squashes any individual drive by injecting his own aesthetic senses into every student piece in a very biased way.  He uses his professorship to inflate his underdeveloped ego and is obviously insecure about his position in life, therefore he makes classtime confusing and unhelpful.
really scatterbrained, but nice enough. Just double check your grades, he writes them down wrong on occasion. Grading is a little unfair at times but if you reallllly try, he is fair.
This class was so chill. Required.

Dr. Wintemberg is the nicest woman, and professor, I have ever had. If you are in this course, you will get an A. No exams, content is intuitive. There are some lengthier homework assignments, but I didn't even mind because of how much I love Dr. Wintemberg. Class gives good insights into health issues.
Amazing class and amazing professor. Fair grading and learned so much! Could not recommend more! Class attendance is required but the class is interesting so its not bad

Amazing prof. So sweet and cares about all of her students. Class was very easy and manegable. The only thing that sucked was the group project at the end, but even then it was fine. Clearly knowledgable about her field and great lectures.

Very sweet person. She's very helpful and shows how much she cares about teaching and one-on-one she is super nice. I don't like the attendance policy due to how many days you can miss. Her class is interesting and the quizzes/home works are always doable. She gives clear explanations over what to cover for each week and how she can help the class.

Dr. Wintemberg is a good professor and she is very nice. Her slides are posted on canvas which is nice. She does use iclicker for attendance so go to class because attendance counts for points. There are 5 "homework assignments" throughout the semester and no exams. There is a quiz at the end of each week. Make sure to stay on top of things.

She is an amazing professor and cares very much about her students. Most of your grade is in class participation so be ready to go to class! Not too many assignments and quizzes are fairly easy. Would recommend!!
she cares about her students so much. there's extra credit opportunities and projects, but participation makes up a HUGE portion of the grade. i loved her class.

Dr. Wintemberg covered a lot of important issues with health disparities in this class. She was very caring, acknowledgeable with disability accommodations, and overall a great professor. Would take again.

Great professor who cares about the material she is teaching. The class is lecture heavy but all lectures are posted online. There are opportunities for discussion during class and there are attendance points taken every day which gives the opportunity for lots of points. This class is an easy A as long as you show up. Weekly quizzes are given.

She has been my favorite professor so far. Her lectures are paced correctly and full of really useful and engaging information. We have weekly quizzes based directly off of the lecture notes (no exams). There is no busy work, just the occasional homework project that is actually relevant to my learning. I adore her. Amazing teacher.

Professor Wintemberg is great! She is very nice and has interesting lectures - her voice is lowkey soothing to listen to. If you complete the discussions and homework assignments, you will get full points - she is somewhat a light grader! No tests, either. Definitely a good professor choice for this class.
Dr. Wintemberg really cares about her students. This class has a good amount of group projects but overall, she is an easy grader.

No zoom lectures, exams, or textbook. I took her Public Health class at the recommendation of another student and was super happy with it. There are weekly discussion posts and a small project due at the end of every other week. Concepts are easy to understand and there is a clear grading criteria. I would take this class again.

Jenna Wintemberg is an ANGEL!! She is probably the best professor that Mizzou has to offer! She keeps students engaged through her presentations and even has guest speakers come! She takes a genuine concern in her students and will do anything to help them succeed! I would take her again in a heartbeat! Do yourself a favor and take her!
Amazing professor!!
Amazing professor. Very clear about what she expects and explains everything in full detail. easy to talk to and personable. attendance is mandatory, but its easy points to just show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A. Show up for class and go to office hours at least once and you'll be set.
Show up to class or get the answers to the in-class questions she asks over tophat from a friend and do the weekly tests, and you'll have an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take a class with Jenna Wintemberg please do it! She is an incredible professor and truly cares for her students.

Professor Wintemberg is the best professor hands down at Mizzou. She is so caring about each individual in her class and truly wants you to succeed. She is so sweet and I will be taking her other classes in the future. Her class is based of attendance and quizzes each week. There are no exams. Highly recommend taking this class with her!!!!

Jenna is one of the best professor's I have had. I received an A and wrote one of the best papers of my college career. She also offers extra credit for going to the writing center which is so easy. In short, great professor, easy class, but you still learn gain a lot of useful knowledge
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Jenna is the most entertaining and enthusiastic professor I have ever had. She truly cares about each students success, and is always available for help! She loves when her students visit her in office hours just to chat. Easiest A ever because there is so much extra credit.

Jenna is an amazing professor. She really cares about your success in this class. As long as you show up for the attendance points (every class), do your homework, and weekly quizzes, you will pass. She has a couple extra credit opportunities as well. She does not have tests and it is heavily based off attendance, homework etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's literally the best professor I've ever had. So caring and thoughtful. LITERALLY a gem! I would highly recommend.

Mizzou needs more instructors like Dr. Wintemberg.  Participation/attendance points are given at the end of class (freebies). Be sure to take notes on what she says that stray from the powerpoints as these are fair game for tests. It's obvious that she really cares about what she does and her students.  I would suggest getting an ebook.

I absolutely adore Professor Wintemberg. She is such a lovely, smart woman who cares a lot about Public Health! She is a wonderful teacher and genuinely wants her students to achieve. If you have her as a professor, get to know her more!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Woods is a very experienced social worker who does a wonderful job sharing her knowledge with students. She is very understanding and gives in depth responses to questions. I appreciate how Dr. Woods makes class enjoyable, a safe space while exhibiting skills we have never used before, and is willing to work with students with conflicts.

AMAZING professor! Tons of great personal stories to add to her lectures. Cool guest speakers. Very easy class, as well. Most test and quiz questions come straight from the textbook. A few very short papers. Some in-class participation assignments, so you have to show up to do well. Highly recommend, even for non-SW majors like me!

Prof. Woods is an amazing person and professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable. I learned so much and grew as a person and as a social worker because of Woods. This program wouldn't be what it is without her.

BEST PROFESSOR!!! She's very passionate about what she does. She often shares relevant personal stories, so lectures are always interesting. You have to read; she gives pop quizzes over chapter readings. Tests are easy. Overall, this was a great class and made me change major to SW. I would highly recommend this class for students of all majors.

The tests and quizzes are online, open book, and you don't have to come to class on those days they are given. She gives little participation activities in random classes as a way to check attendance. She gives 5 in the semester. The power points are online, so note taking isn't necessary.
very relevant course for the current times!!! highly recommend for anyone interested in the social side of education
She cares

Worst professor Ive ever had. We are almost done with the semester, and I am waiting on 12 assignments to be graded. Readings are repetitive and unnecessary. Would not take this Professor again, shes very irritable at times and hard to work with. Also has a no email policy, so good luck if you have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The 200+ people scandal is real. I had to withdraw after getting a 65/200 on the test. the online lectures (2/3) per week were longer than a class period in itself and the TAs didn't help at all much less the professor. It was also not fair that the first test was after the drop date so you thought it would be easier than it actually is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is hard and requires work, but it's not impossible. He really gives you a couple of lifelines and grades on an easier scale than the standard one. As long as you read the textbook and try, you'll be fine.
His tests are hard but if you're prepared (read textbook, watch lectures) then its fine

reviews.comment: absolutely awful guy and doesn't care if your graduate or not
